text:
This place is not great. 

We were stuck in a table under the stairs, the hot pink wall combined with a too strong chandelier, left us feeling like we were dining in a soviet interrogation room. 

The server took forever to come over for the first time.  I think they forgot about us since we were hidden.

The teriyaki was good as was the sushi, the rest was just plain. 

Menu is weird mix of Asian food.  Not exactly sure what they are going for.  

But the kicker for me was the prices.  WAY overpriced for the quality. 

I would not go back.

Why why why why why? Why do I continue to eat here?

It's a love/hate relationship.

Rationale: they've got a 24/7 drive-thru (I've never seen them close) that happens to be around the corner from my brother's abode. Convenience is the name of this late-night game... oh Del Taco, you're my faux Mexican booty call!

True story: I found my little dream home driving to Del Taco hungover one morning in a quest for a breakfast burrito. Saw an open house sign, wandered in, fell in love, called my parents and the rest is history! I lived in this cute little house for 4 years before moving, and now it's my brother's nest. Thanks Del Taco!

There's not too many people here as lunch is just opening.

Service is friendly and great here. The bartender mid-week today is very personable. 

I agree but expected that the prices are moderate. I wanted the wings but since I will be taking it on the flight.. it might get a little messy... I'll stick with something clean today like the Cheese Chicken and Nuts Salad. Sadly, the salad was mediocre and there wasn't anything special with it. Basically, greens with honey mustard. I'll keep in mind to order a few other items next time!

I went to this Starbucks for the very last time today. This Starbucks has not been in the area that long, (maybe 2 years), and they have raised their prices 3 times already.  My usual order (tall hot chocolate and banana bread) went from $5.81 to $6.37. The cups have gotten much smaller, but the prices are getting MUCH HIGHER.  That's it for me.  I'll drive a couple lights down and go to the Starbucks in Target from now on. The same order is  still about $5.81 there. This kind of sucks for the employees now because they will probably not receive as many tips.

Even if this were the most amazing breakfast sandwich, I could never give it above 2 stars. Why? For the egg white portion of my sandwich, dude pulled a solid, white pancake-like object from behind the counter (that was the egg white) and cut it into quarters. 

Then he nuked it in the bizarro half microwave-half monster. When it was all said and done, he forgot to add the Black Forest Ham to my sandwich. The only thing that was probably made out of anything real was the bread. I'll probably get these every morning though.

Yes, we are health freaks, but really... they have probably the best burgers and fries I've had.  I rarely eat red meat... let alone with a side of deep-fried potatoes... but I will stretch to make excuses to eat here ("I was in Vegas all weekend and still need to soak up the alcohol.... I went to the gym everyday this week, my body probably needs protein...").  Hey, I didn't say they were good excuses.

I tried the turkey burger once, which is usually my go to if I'm craving a burger... but I say, splurge for the classic cheeseburger and fries.  This is a once-a-year treat, but so worth the wait!

It's a decent sushi place, but like Meghan C. said, since they got a liquor license, the price of entry has gotten very high.  We usually can't get out of here for less than $100, for two of us.

We haven't been back in quite some time, but their sign says that all their alcohol is now half off.  I wish they'd just make that their regular price, since they really do have good rolls.  Their specialty rolls are better than anywhere else I've been, though their sashimi and sushi portions are small, and are pretty much standard fare.  Not great, not bad.

I love coming here to get my hair cut the guys here are pretty kool. The barber are pretty good barbers too if I may say so. The location is right in the plaza where the flea market is at. Inside they have about 7 barber chair and none of them are ever open there's always someone cutting somebody hair. Its nice inside and clean, they have about 5 TV's inside at ever corners. They also have a ATM inside just in case you stap for case you can ran your ass over to the ATM to get some cash and as always the barber shop gossip is always free LOL.

I have been eating subway for awhile now.(so about 8 years now) and everytime I go regardless of location, its bad or good depends on the location. 

The bread may be freshly backed but that dough must have been in the freezer for years its always hard and stale now. 

I don't need 8 different people shouting "HI WELCOME TO SUBWAY" in a depressing tone, one will do. 

every now and then my order is usually wrong but as they're asking lettuce and tomatoes? they're already putting stuff on my sandwich that i dont like. I'm sick of paying for a sandwitch that taste aweful.

No question this place has some incredible rolls and sashimi.  Definitely the place you go for the creative and unorthodox (not for the same-old-same-old sushi).  

there are 200 items on the menu and I've only had the pleasure of 10 of them.  but as I return, I will expand this review (for now, anything with habanero sauce is to die for and the baked green lip mussels are killer...but be careful, they come in groups  of five so I hope you know how to share "awesomeness").

god bless my girlfriend for introducing me to this place.  can't wait to go back for the oysters (which, fyi, can run out if you get there too late!)

I've quit, in favor of taking random yoga classes and rock climbing. Can't get over their attitude change (seeming super juiced up to me) in the past year, and there seems to be little communication between staff. Besides, i hate that the Old City location makes you walk between all the equipment and people lifting and checking themselves out in the mirror to get to the locker room. Nothing like being gawked at on arrival! And then you get to the tiny, tiny locker room, which is, frankly, too close for comfort.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
What. Fresh. Hell. Is. This?

I wish I could claim that I originated that expression, as it popped into my head as soon as crossing this dreaded threshold, but I did not. You can thank Dorothy Parker (I do, quite regularly).

If the idea of a "2 Dolla Holla" is appealing to you, come here on a Saturday. If the idea of a 2 Dolla Holla is appealing to you, I'm afraid we have nothing in common.

In closing, is where you might end up at Misery O'clock looking for a cheap beer or worse.

I'll be back on the 12th of Never.

Sweeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeet jaysus! I confess, I strayed from my beloved tart the other day because I was wooed by an array of flashy, slutty flavors at FroYo. I sampled: red velvet cake, cookies & cream, cake batter, and cheese cake. Slatterns! What the hell was I thinking? At one point, I think they all pretty started tasting the same. 

There's also a lot of topping choices (but no *cherries*). The asking price seems typical and I know plenty of people prefer sweet stuff, so if you're one of those people, you will love the slutty offerings from FroYo!

A straight-up comfy little spot, Harry's Corner is worthy of its iconic name. If a bar is named Harry, it has to be good or it needs to change its name. Simple as that. And *this* Harry's, I like just fine.

No bells and whistles here, just a Quarter corner bar with seasoned bartenders and cheap enough drinks. I've been in here when packed (Halloween) and empty. Empty is preferable if you're feeling *old and cranky* which BTW is a state of mind that I do my best to avoid, but sometimes it's inevitable.

On that note, I shall create a list of my favorite bars to hit up when in that OAC state of mind...

I used to eat here plenty back when IV was my stomping ground &  was a Santa Barbarian. I ate here recently on our last trip down and I'm happy to say that this place still lives up to my good memories. I like all their burgers and the malts are the best I've had. It's an outdoor sit down joint with okay service, they just come out and place the food trays on your table. I really wish I could eat here regularly- it beats In N Out Burger any day. It's a treat for me and my tummy so that's why it gets five stars.

OK this place is a typical Chinese buffet, but it does have the best Chicken and Broccoli of all the other buffets I have tried in town.   And I think that says a lot.   This place seems very popular so a lot of people seem to have a good opinion of it.   I have notice that there are many quality items:  the white rice here is very good--soft and moist, it has excellent steamed dumplings, and the obligatory sushi is assembled with some care.   A nice atmosphere as well.   I would rate as above average and worth a visit if you are in the neighborhood.  PS: The price is very reasonable compared to other places.

I'd like to file Vaso into several familiar categories:

1. Bars where I'm baffled that they employ a bathroom attendant.
2. Bars where they pour stiff drinks.
3. Bars you might be able to get into without getting carded because there's [occasionally] no one at the door. (Not that you are with anyone underage, it's just that your wife got her wallet stolen at the last bar, and now she can't get in anywhere with a better band playing.)

Also, Vaso is the only bar I'm aware of that fits into the following category:

1. Bars where I've seen jazz covers of some of Kurt Cobain's finest songs, and liked them.

Matteo's has gone through a couple of ownership changes and yet some of the core staff has remained from change to change so it hasn't been obvious that it has changed hands.  So far the changes have not had any effect on operations and food.  The newest change is still new - they are painting and freshening the place up.  They are going to add back some seating.  I haven't been in since they started the upgrades but have had delivery and everything is still top notch.  Consistency is key and they are doing a great job.

I am not a huge fan of fast food chains but every now and then I enjoy having the original chicken sandwich here.  But the best deal is the $0.50 soft serve ice cream cone special they are running this summer.

With me being laid off, we have had more fast food adventures lately using coupons so I have been observing them and comparing.  Burger King is still better than most of the rest.  However, like almost all fast food places I have been in, staff can be standing around and you can be the only person in the dining area and all the tables will be dirty, spills all over the beverage area and such.

Five Guys serves the best fast food burger I can order in Edmonton. And it appears that service has improved tremendously since it first opened in 2012. This location is always fully staffed, and the service is prompt. 

My only complaint is that they salt the fries a bit too much.

And if you aren't  feeling like Joey Chestnutt, I'd recommend ordering a Jr. Cheeseburger rather than a full cheeseburger. A Junior patty is nearly 1/4 pound, which means that a full cheeseburger nearly contains 1/2 pound of meat.

It feels odd to review a Wendy's, and especially give it four stars. But really, Wendy's has come a long way in the last 10 years. Why this location - because it's been updated with swanky decor, at least by the standards of a fast food restaurant. There's TVs, a (faux?) fireplace, and a variety of comfortable seating, including sofas. And it's by far the best place to get a salad for lunch in the area.

And if you do want to indulge in something less healthy, a side salad costs roughly the same amount as fries.

The burgers still taste like fast food for the most part, but the experience has been elevated tremendously at this location.

Not the greatest fast food place to hit at night.

I was driving through one night and had to stop and use the restroom and get some food. The employees looked at me with almost disqust that I was in there. Not that I'm one of those people but maybe I was the wrong white girl in the wrong neighborhood at the wrong time? Not really sure. It's pretty much almost downtown past the arch right off 70 so it was convenient. It was pretty clean for the most part as well. Just didn't like the whole vibe going on inside.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: I found a menu in my new mailbox the day after the move and decided to get some food to go for dinner.  The uni was nice and fresh,and my king crab dynamite roll was pretty good, with a slightly sweet and spicy sauce. The sauteed scallops with mushrooms was very flavorful, and the yakitori was pretty decent.  Overall, a good restaurant,although it is quite small.  I'll be back and if the return visit goes well, then this will be my new "I'm-too-tired-to-cook-so-I'm-going-to-get-takeout-across-the-street" place.

Attended a seminar here and the event facility itself was decent although the temperature was either too hot or too cold.  The hotel itself seemed rather cramped and a bit disorganized in its layout (bathrooms on alternate floors, towel carts in the middle of practically every hallway).  The attached parking lot is a nightmare, though.  It is 5 stories of narrow spots and narrower navigation lanes, which basically turns the experience into a nightmare on Elm St.  The location is nice (right in Midtown) but the venue is almost subpar.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I had the escargot app and duck entree. The escargot were very well seasoned and the duck was succulent and flavored with a hint of coffee.  A bit different but delicious all the same. The Pinot noir that we brought added a nice touch. Their wine pairing recs were right on target. The nutella pot du creme was just heavenly. Chocolate, coconut, and hazelnut creme all in one dish!  I will come back just for that alone. Service was okay but they did refill our bread basket, which was much appreciated because I love warm, fresh bread with olive oil.

Not a big fan of either the service or food.  The margherita pizza was on the bland side in terms of sauce seasoning; it was rather salty but lacked actual flavor.  My drunken gnocchi was heavy on butter and excessively salty.  The saving grace was the rack of lamb which was tender and nicely seasoned with EVOO and rosemary.  Service was very slow and we had to ask for water refills and the check more times than should have been necessary.  Portions are pretty generous.  If they cut back on the salt and butter, this place would have potential.  That is, if they also improve the service level.

This is a solid sushi place with good offerings and great service.  For lunch, the short ribs sandwich on brioche is very tender and nicely marinated.  The chu toro is very fresh, and melts in your mouth.  They don't have too many original rols but the standards, like the spicy salmon and eel/avocado are all pretty good.  I love that they have a california roll made with actual lump crabmeat.  The agedashi tofu is nicely seasoned, and the braised short ribs are very flavorful.  

The servers here are very friendly and attentive,and the ambiance chill.  A nice place for a quick and casual meal.

This is owned by the same family that runs Joy Tsin Lau in Chinatown and has the same great menu and food.  I love the crab meat sauteed with pea tips, cold plate with marinated roast beef and jellyfish, sauteed seafood soft noodle, stir-fried dungeness crab with ground pork, and the stuffed triple delight (pepper, eggplant, and tofu with shrimp).  The restaurant is huge and the service is great.  We are always greeted with a smile.  This is probably the closest that you will get to Chinatown-quality food outside of well, Chinatown.  Plus, no parking charge!  Definitely one of the best suburban Chinese restaurants in the area.

Not bad but not fantastic either.  You will find the essentials and then some at very reasonable prices, but the store itself could be cleaner and better organized.  There is a poultry stand that sells decent bbq pork and duck, and they are always more than happy to slice the pork into very thin pieces for me.  The seafood section is pretty good, although it doesn't have quite the variety as Kam Man does, or even Assi.  Nam Vang is also located inside, and they have a very good beef stew with baguette entree.  Actually, that might be my ulterior motive for shopping here.  Fresh sugarcane juice and a beef stew.  All for under $7.

If it a MCD owned/managed by "Blessed and Faith" McDonalds of Indianapolis, you will get piss poor service and they will screw it up.  They will not accept the coupons that come from corporate, or they will try to get you to buy something else.  Actually b/c of this particular franchisee, I have not made a purchase at MCD for anything in over a year.  And I don't miss it.  And since some of the "higher" end burger joints like Steak N Shake are offering cheap combos nowadayz, I get my unhealthy, quick burger fixes there.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: The BEST PIZZA and Italian food in Hendricks County. Go early because the place is not a place for ambiance and the seating is crowded and limited. However, the place is super clean, smartly organized considering the space, and the waiters are always available. No one has said much about the Italian dishes but the wife and I have tried a few different things and we were never disappointed. They offer a special everyday and the last one was a Chicken Marsala that I was disappointed that I did not order it. It looked sooooo good! But we were there for pizza and that is one heck of a consolation prize!!!!

Four stars? That's mighty high praise for a McDonald's there, Todd.  Well, the stars reflect just how outstanding the service is here. Everyone is polite to the point of ridicule. Welcome, how may I help you today is a normal thing for them. Smiles and thank you and please is effortless.  Effervescent attitudes and genuine care abounds. And they get the order right 100% of the time.

Why? What mythical training have these managers unlocked? How can an MCD this great be in the same town as one of the worst of their same brand, much less in the same shopping plaza as the worst Wendy's ever?

The shoes, T-Money! Gotta be the shoes.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Do you like beer? Do you enjoy trying local brews? Do you peruse beer menus looking for something new and different? If so, this is the spot for you. So many beers! And for a bar located right in the middle of the action, this place is always relatively empty. And it's significantly quieter than all the neighboring bars. Those are two big pluses in my book. The bartender was really friendly and knowledgeable. She was great at figuring out what we like and suggesting other options. A very pleasant experience! And all in a place that has a dive feel.

Oh my goodness.  It is a fitness miracle.  I'm still pretty new, so I can't yet speak to results, but so far I absolutely love it here (Love a gym?  Hence the miracle).

The smart-trainer machines are super easy to use, and since it is a sort of computerized personal trainer, you can follow your progress on the screen and it will let you know if you are doing it wrong.  They also offer elliptical machines and treadmills with a long list of  "coached" sessions (each 15 min).  

I really dig the website.  You can see how you did your last workout, see your totals and if you do Weight Watchers, you can see what the equivalent activity points.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
It was the end of our trip. We had been walking for days and were tired. I don't think we wanted another sit down meal, so we ordered delivery from Pizza Delicious! They were right within our delivery zone. We ordered two pies, one pasta, a salad, and garlic knots. It was all delicious. The crust was perfectly thin. I think we ordered the buccatini and that was yummy too. Just think about it, still good even after they delivered it to us via bicycle! Awesome. 

Don't compare this with like NYC or Chicago pizza. You do realize this is new orleans right?

Pizza: 5 Stars
Pasta: 1 Star (Generously)
The Margherita pizza was out of this world fantastic. Delicious crust. Each pizza is enough for 1 person if that's all you're eating.
She got the Fettucine Boschiola and I got the Penne alla Vodka. $14 and $13 respectively and we could not have been more disappointed. Honestly the worst restaurant pasta I've had, including Olive Garden and Shoney's buffet. The portions were tiny for the prices, but it was really ok since they tasted so bad anyway.
We will go for the pizza ONLY. Please learn from our $27 pasta mistake and do likewise.

I had just gotten off of a three and a half hour bus ride from NYC, and was about to get on the train for another hour to get to my parents house.  I hopped into DD to grab a donut and a hot chocolate.

The staff didn't really talk, they just stared.  But, they had me my order quickly, and gave my change correctly.  (I'm trying to find the positive in the experience.)

I got settled on the train, took a bite out of my donut, and immediately spit it out back into the bag.  That thing was STALE STALE STALE!!!!!!!!!

The mint hot chocolate was fine.  SUPER sweet, but that's how they do at DD's.

Stale donuts are the worst.

People say this is Philly's best cheapest pizza. 

Uh uuh, it's just really good pizza regardless of price. 

They say you can always judge a pie by the margarita, but what I'm learning here in Philly, it's about the "plain" pie. There's is strictly Splatter Spiral red and white. A thing of beauty and to be lusted after. 

The sauce is sweet and plentiful so choose toppings wisely (i.e. probably not a good idea to get sweet peppers and other sweeter veggies). Probably a good (GENIUS) idea to get the "Old Fashioned" a pizza sandwich if you will, with onions, American cheese and "Pizza cheese."  You can now die. You're welcome.

To make a long review short:

- It's probably the most reasonably priced and tastey sushi you can get in the area.
- Their Sushi rolls are all similar but that doesn't mean that they're not   tastey!
- Byob
- Service is good. The restaurant is small and laid back vibe to it, no frills unless you count the pink curtain in front of the women's bathroom door... 
- The spicy sashimi salad is amazing and for 8 bucks you get a ton of sashimi in it.
- Thinking about that spicy sashimi salad is making me salivate. I'm going there for dinner.

Best sushi/sashimi in the area. Typically fresh fish but the wait for takeout on weekends are abominable. Last Saturday we placed an order at 5 and was told it would be 45 mins-1 hour and it took about 2 hours.  But where else are you going to go, the city?
We typically order the mainline roll and spicy tuna. I've gotten the chicken teriyaki for the kids and admit that it's pretty good. Ordered the fatty tuna roll and you could tell it was not fresh. Husband said it's my fault for ordering as you would never put otoro in a roll unless you were trying to hide something. Haha

Not many options in the area so this place will have to do! They have everything you would need to put together a Chinese hot pot, from the condiments to frozen fish tofu.  I enjoy coming here on a weekday to pick up some asian vegetables (love my leafy greens). It's small but it has a good variety of Chinese condiments, sauces, vegetables, instant noodles etc. There is a small prepared foods section where they sell baked buns, cakes and seaweed salad (random but these are the three things I bought from this section). If you're looking for a particular Chinese or Asian inspired ingredient, this place is worth a look.

My grandmother loves this place, so I'm here more often than I'd go on my own. My late great aunt was also a fan. Since we're talking about elderly women here, I've most often visited in the mid afternoon for their early bird dinner specials.

My take: I'd give The Coastline a 2.5 if I could. I've never had terrible service, nor have I had amazing service. I have not experienced any of the bad things written about by some other reviewers. The food has always been fine, and served hot. None of my glasses/silverware have ever been noticeably dirty. Nothing to write home about, but nothing wrong with the place either.

The only time that I have been here is on Mondays. They have half priced sushi from 5p-7p. But beware I think everyone that likes sushi on the southside is there so be prepared. We used to be able to call ahead and let them know we are coming but i dont think they do that any more.
The sushi is pretty good, not the best, but definitely not the worst. We have ordered other things off the menu and have not been all that impressed. Everything is pretty affordable and the half price sushi on Mondays is a geat deal.

I stayed here at the weekend and I agree on most everything that has been said: decent value, small rooms and beds, and so on. I ordered a queen-size bed which is not their smallest room, and it was just enough room for a couple. The service was poor; although the front desk was friendly-enough, I had to call for a few things and was greeted with utter disdain, and then was told I had to get my own ironing board and iron from "guest request closets" which was just storage on the 12th floor. But overall, not bad for a nearly self-service hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Osaka's got some good sushi.  Not the all time best sushi, but very consistent, fresh, tasty sushi.  Been here both for dinner and takeout.  They make some pretty good (and strong) drinks, and the waitstaff are very pleasant and attentive.  The sushi is always made with some focus on presentation, so it always looks good.  Even when you get takeout they try make it look like a piece of art!  

I have a standard four rolls I like and tend to base the level of the sushi off those (spicy tuna, caterpillar, soft shell crab, and some shrimp thing).  They get above average marks on all and its not crazy expensive.

Liquid pixie stick, at a to-go stand.. for $8?

I wish I got more of it while I was there, I felt good after but I was also grabbing beers and a Jester while trying to stay as sober as I could for the ride home.. I wasn't driving but I didn't wanna be puking either.. (see Zippys review for puke status).

It doesn't taste strong, the way it's suppose too, hence why I wish I got another one or four.  Shame on me!

It comes out of a soda dispenser, odd.  I asked him why; well duh hello was the answer I got, they make so much of it that no one would get any if they had to make it one by one.  Good reply my friend, touche.

Incredibly outdated and almost too large to navigate or manage as seen by the lack of customer service. We had to literally ask for our rooms to be cleaned. Decent pool area when all amenities are in working order. The"gym"is a complete joke. Old equipment in need of calibration and balancing before someone hurts themselves. Selling point for active people is the 9 mile loop through several small parks and running along Snake River. You generally get what you pay for; so, I can't complain too much. I just don't think "I have no idea" should ever cross the lips of management and I had the pleasure of hearing it twice.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: this is delicious, authentic Italian food. I love the extensive menu, and when you go in with a large party, the chef usually comes out and introduces himself. The food is plentiful and the portions are sufficient. You won't be going home with tons of leftovers but you will be full and happy. This is the perfect place for a romantic dinner because it is quiet and relaxed inside and if you have room after dinner they have a huge selection of desserts that they present to your group on a huge tray. I have gone a few times in the last year we have lived in Carpinteria and while this is definitely a splurge for dinner, it is well worth it.

Kiwi has fresh, delicious frozen yogurt!   This is self serve, you pay by the ounce, it works for me. The serving cup is quite large/deceiving,  I suggest going easy on the portion, especially if your  'eyes are bigger than your stomach' (guilty as charged). They have a lot of different flavors of yogurt as well as a large selection of toppings. I always get the 'fat free, no sugar added  pure vanilla'  flavor,  then I load it up with toppings. For tonight's toppings I had fresh strawberries, fresh blueberries, a little bit of peanut butter, hard pretzel chunks and chocolate syrup,  yum !  I may be addicted.

I work nearby and decided to give this a shot based on the recommendation of Julia S.  I was not exactly wow'd by my burger.  But the atmosphere was fine and the food was okay.  The fries were nice and crispy and I left with the feeling that I'd ordered the wrong thing.  So I recommend getting a pizza type item rather than the burger.  Or if you must get a burger, get it well done.  

The beers and large bar are very nice and the place has free wifi.  Parking is super easy along the street or in the parking lot directly across from the restaurant.

This is the place to go for the *best bang for the buck* sushi in Center City. Their rolls are very decent for the price... just don't expect it to be Morimoto quality. For 10 bucks, you can get 3 rolls. You can choose from the standard rolls (california rolls, spicy tuna rolls, etc.) or some specialty rolls. They also have some cheap appetizers. All in all, you can be stomach happy for less than 15 dollars. The only bad thing about this place is that it's really small, with only about half a dozen seats or so. Many people just order take out. Simply put, if you want some inexpensive, good quality sushi, stop by Vic's!

I recently moved to Indianapolis, and I was pleased to see that there are good, local options for coffee.  I don't know why anyone would go to a Starbucks here when Hubbard & Cravens is an option.  

The coffee and espresso drinks are fantastic.  Service is quick and friendly.  It's clean, and there's a good amount of seating, and they have free wifi.  They have a decent selection of pastries, though I have yet to try any.  Even though this location is very close to downtown, it feels very out of the way.  I'll definitely continue to frequent this place.

We dropped in here during a recent trip to Reno as we were bored with the strip. Nice little dive on the corner..did not get a chance to see what else was in the strip it was on, although there was a decent tattoo shop next to it as well. Small on the inside, excellent service, great bartenders that know how to pour a drink. They were kind enough to open up their lot many of your local MC's that had some great booths and merchandise as well. We will definitely make this one of our regular spots when in town.

Gorgeous property, amazing staff, clean and enchanting and a nice place to play and stay.

But there are some surprising  misses for an RC.

If you arrive at 3, its hard to find food. At least in the summer. The lobby bar Ignite: closed. Claytons for burgers: open, if you want to wait for then ride a shuttle. Core, closed. Coffee shop: closed. Turquesa open, If you want a " very limited menu" and clamor up to the pool in street clothes. 

The rooms have power only on one side of the bed. Chipped furniture. A clock radio with an old now unusable iPhone plug. 

The patios are nice with cushy chairs. Big soaking tub is terrific!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Not too impressed. When asked what is the difference between a white mocha, a white chocolate mocha, a white latte, and a white chocolate latte the answer was "they are all the same, just different ways of saying it." Huh? 

The drink was not mixed :( I thought it tasted a bit "off" for having white chocolate, but being one who doesn't gripe due to the attitude that can lash back at times (and this particular evening I was on a good vibe and didn't want to rock my own boat) I kept my trap shut. Half way through the drink all of a sudden the drink tasted realllly syrupy. Too bad I couldn't have saved some of the syrup for my morning coffee.

Slow. Dirty. Splattered with dried, spilt milkshake.  The dining area is used for storage, the lights don't work, but my food was edible, and I didn't get sick, which was a plus.

Pretty much the last place I would choose to go, but I was starving, and didn't have time to go anywhere else.  

It would be a huge improvement if the owner fired the management, and all of the employees, as none seem interested in doing anything related to what is typically expected while employed.  After they were done gossiping and checking their phones, they did make my food. It would have been nice if they washed their hands after handling their phones, though.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
After much deliberation and a few great washes here, I decided to buy the monthly membership. $30 seems a bit steep but if you like to take care of your car and wash and vacuum it once a week, it's actually a pretty good deal.

We now have just added this to our weekend to-do's: swing by and get the cars washed. So fast and so easy!

The people who work here are always very nice and thorough in their pre-washing. They even get off a lot of the bugs and you know those REALLY tough to get off.

I've not gone to any of the other locations yet, but the membership applies to their other car washes as well- which is a convenient bonus!

I had a Groupon, a bunch of errands to run and a cooler in the car -- so I opted for the readymade treats from the front freezer.

Sugar-free butter pecan, strawberry, cookies & cream, yellow cake batter and brownie batter.

These are pint containers, which is a whole lot of frozen yogurt.

They all tasted perfectly of their flavors and saved well in the cooler and beyond . . . into the freezer.

I may mix some of these with Greek yogurt and fresh or frozen fruit. I can imagine brownie batter with frozen cherries, or strawberry with frozen bananas.

Mix it up.

I've been many times. Inside a couple times. Mostly drive-through.

They've got a double drive-through, which always makes me nervous that I'm either going to pay for the other guy's food or GET the other guy's food. But it's never happened.

The order-takers, money-takers (particularly when I'm counting out change to give them) and food-givers are always friendly and smiling.

I like to get the McDouble when it's $1. I get two, ditch both buns and have a meal for 10 carbs. Ditch the ketchup on both, and carbs are down to 6 with 460 calories. This is not something you eat in public!

They've got free wifi.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
My girlfriend and I went for lunch July 30. Her suggestion. We sat at a booth in the bar. Quite close to the restroom. Kinda a plus.

We both got the prime sirloin meatloaf, which comes with fries. I should have asked for broccoli. Fries only last for -- you eat four or five, and then you're done. They were fine. Shoestring-style.

The meatloaf was incredibly rich. It was a mound -- not a loaf. And covered with ketchup.

I was not blown away with this meatloaf. For one, it was too rich. I took three bites and was done. For two, the overwhelming ketchup was waaaay too much.

Leftovers were better, 'cause I added A-1.

I like this place because they have a fun name. Oh ee shi. OH EE SHI. OYSHI. OYYYEESHI.

Um. So, exceptional service, tasty drinksies, great lunch specials. PRETTY sushi. Great presentation! See attached picture!

The only thing I REALLY don't like is that their crab is completely shredded and chopped. It gives it a funky texture I don't jive with. Kinda mushy. So the California rolls are not my favorite....or anything with the crab, really, which is a shame because I love crab.

Cardinal roll was delish. Love that subtle crunch and savory taste of the shrimp tempura, and the delectable tuna on top. yummm.

Assholes closed early. I was told they close at 10. I try to get a quick bite at 9:25 and they've already COMPLETELY cleaned up (except for the massive discussing Coke spill by the garbage cans, clearly from dragging garbage bags on the floor and not cleaning up the spilling liquid) and both employees are hiding in the back on their cell phones. I asked if they were already closed and the rude employee just says "yeah" and goes back to fucking around on her phone. I can't believe they're getting paid right now. And I'm standing here starving. FUCK THAT.

OK. I really really wanted some coffee this morning. Since they don't have drive thru, I illegally parked (parking lot was PACKED) and bolted to the door from a good distance away only to find that the line was almost out the door. I don't care how fast they are, there was no way I was getting out of there in 10 minutes, it probably was going to be longer. 

Keep in mind, this is after 9am on a Tuesday. Not convenient and always a struggle for parking. Can they PLEASE figure out a better situation?! You let me uncaffeinated Starbucks!

I decided to give this place a shot before attending an author event next door at Parnassus. It was a pretty forgettable experience. I had the chicken habachi meal with the miso soup, ginger salad, and chicken/veggies with fried rice. I think my favorite item from the meal was the fried rice. It was really tasty! Otherwise, it was a lot of food and I boxed up the rest. The flavor was ok but nothing special. If it was cheaper I'd consider going back, but for the same price ($15.00) I can get the same (maybe slightly better meal) and a really nice atmosphere at Goten off West End.

The menu and prices are the same as the mothership restaurant on 22nd. The exterior is brightly colored, just like the other one. The interior of this one is less crowded than that one. There is actually room to walk around.

That being said, they have (just like the original location) what it likely the best lunch deal around. For $4.99 you can get a plateful of fajitas with rice, beans and tortillas. Their salsa is some of the best around. Top off your fajitas, tacos or burrito with that and you are sure to leave with a full wallet AND a full belly.

This is a very good place.  They seem to focus on their specialty rolls as opposed to nigiri.  The montecito was very delightful, light and filled with a variety of sauces.  The kiwi roll had a great tang as well from the kiwi.

The nigiri was very good as well the spanish mackarel, yellow tail and tuna tasting fresh and melting in my mouth.  The salmon on the other hand was not so great.  The wait was a bit long, but worth it.  It was a little difficult having to order through the waitress for everything as opposed to filling out a sheet.

Although I can't have pizza, I went with my husband to try Pizza Delicious for his birthday.  The garlic knots are a must.  I would order 5 orders of these and would eat every one.  

The pizza was tasty (although I had it without the cheese).  The crust was the best part.  One of the best crusts in the city.

They were a little on the pricey side.  However, the $21 for a pizza turned out to be quite a lot of pizza.  The pizza was ginormous.  

Overall a great place to go and not a bad drive either.

They are only open on Sundays.

When my furry child decided she was fed up with her normal, healthy life, she started having eye problems. Dr. da Costa had been checking her every month until her eye started having really bad eye problems.  She had emergency eye surgery that lasted over an hour.  He is a very good doctor, but he doesn't have the best bed side manner. He puts his "vet face" on.  watch out for him giving you an estimate and then adding things on after you have decided on a certain price.  He also doesn't take pay plans.  You basically just charge it.

This place is a little pricey, but it's pretty much worth it. The fried calamari is a favorite, and the raspberry caramel bread pudding is delicious. My husband and I used to frequent this place a lot when we lived in Manayunk, and we do miss it now. The specialty cocktails (jolly rancher, starburst...) are good, but they are SUPER STRONG. So, if that's not your style, I wouldn't spend your money on them. Also, everytime we went Derek was actually there. You can tell the guy is really invested in his business, and it shows.

We got some sushi take-out from here last week, and it was GREAT! 

I got to try the spicy tuna roll, yellowtail scallion roll, unakuy roll (eel), fire cracker roll, red snapper sushi, smoked salmon sushi, and the gyoza,

All of my rolls were good, but I especially liked the fire cracker roll. The crispy topping and hot sauce should be served on every roll, ever! It's delicious. 

The gyoza was a little too greasy and tough for me, though I usually prefer steamed dumplings as opposed to fried ones, so it could just be my personal preference.

Overall I was very happy with my meal here... give it a shot!

This isn't a White Castle.  It might look like a White Castle, but it's some Third Circle of Hell White Castle (minus Cerberus for fans of Dante).

White Castle shouldn't have bulletproof glass in it (note, it's next to the BP I reviewed).

White Castle shouldn't be completely nasty.  And this place is.

If a certain movie had been filmed in St. Louis, it would have been titled "Harold and Kumar Go to White Castle Only to Discover That This is an Abomination and Instead They Drive Another Half Block and Go to Taco Bell."

It's wrong.  Completely wrong.  The only thing you will crave after visiting this location is Tums and Pepto.

I mean, shoot man... why not, you know?

The Emerald is a gem!

This place isn't a typical Florida bar if you ask me. It has the look and feel of a neighborhood dive bar you'd find in Pittsburgh or Chicago. 

Smoky, cheap wood-paneled walls, worn linoleum floor, old school furniture, dusty old beer paraphernalia, old-fashioned jukebox and an analog cash register with real scrolling numbers!

The clientele is a mix dominated by the street punk/rocker or barfly in the making. Come as you are, not as you were or will be. 

4 stars for relentlessness.

INSTEAD of paying by the pound, you pay a flat rate for the cup size at Parlour, HENCE make it as heavy as you want with fro yo and toppings!! 

i actually enjoy the icier texture of their fro yo (as opposed to creamy) since its so refreshing, ESP on a hot summer Tucson day! my only gripe is i wish they had better flavor selection

i think the best two flavors i tried were the blueberry pomegranate & green tea! prickly pear was interesting but not enough bold flavor & salted caramel was yucky

NOTE: ask for sample cups, ALL the yogurts are low fat & GLUTEN FREE horray

Yup, it's an undiscovered dive but cozy and old school. Clean and well kept. I was glad to hear about it. Since it's on lower Dickerson, many people may not know about it unless they've lived around the area a long time. The waitress was friendly and the food was reasonaby priced, and really good. They're getting into live music and comedy on certain nights, which may help get some hipster crowd Gallatin Rd and 5 points establishments enjoy....kindof a sketchy area and the place is as non corporate as it gets, which the latter is what I like best about it besides the food. I'll look forward to going back.

After a slow morning at jury selection, I was ready for a lunch break, but didn't want to face the crowds of Reading Terminal Market. Lucky for me, Kabuki was conveniently located across the street and was offering lunch specials.

While the place was very quiet (only 1 other patron from 11:30am-12:30pm on a Tuesday), the fish was fresh and the service was very friendly. I found the rice and nori (seaweed) to be just a little chewy. Consider Kabuki next time you're in the area and want something different from the RTM scene.

Conveniently located just a block from the Kimmel Center, we stopped by for a pre-theater dinner.  We were a little worried about only having 1.5 hours, but our waiter assured us that they're used to the theater crowd and we'd be out with time to spare.

We started with the Ahi Tuna Rolls (okay, but needed a higher fish:rice ratio) and the Homemade Gnocchi (so fresh and delicious!).  My entree was the Short Ribs special, which had been cooked for 24 hours - tender and great flavor and served with delicious Leek Mashed Potatoes.

Terra seems to be a well-kept secret with a fairly quiet Saturday night crowd in the intimate space. We started with appetizers of Mac & Cheese (tasty with the pretzel giving a nice crunch), Spring Rolls (a little too fried for my taste), and Deviled Eggs (where the devil is mustard with a kick), which were more satisfying than the complimentary bread which we suspected had been reheated. We were very pleased with our entrees: there was a generous portion of fresh Pan Seared Scallops, and the Pan Seared Black Sea Bass was very tasty.

The Circ provides a convenient option for guests of the Marriott.  Even though it's located in the middle of the hotel, the area is designed so that you are not distracted by people walking through the lobby or gawked at by them and service is reasonably attentive.  The drink menu is a little pricey, and with the Marriott's central location to some great restaurants and bars that would give you a better glimpse into Philadelphia, I'd say check out some of the other options in the neighborhood if you have the energy to walk a few blocks.

Hey, miss?  I am a customer, not an interruption.  

The really helpful guys in the garage across from the airport where you actually pick up the car almost make up for the woman who waited on me at the Budget counter.  No eye contact, brusque.  How did she get a job dealing with the public. 

Does Budget send its counter people to the DMV for training?  To a hospital admissions office?

Y'all might want to hire some folks away from Enterprise.  They seem to have integrated customer service into their corporate culture.

Yay!! Another authentic Chinese restaurant.  They have fresh roasted duck and chicken.  And many dishes for those who are not interested in items like sweet and sour pork and are looking for something more authentic.  They actually have a special where you can order 3 items from a special menu for only $19.99 which is a great value.  The a la carte entrees are not expensive either - starting at $7 and up.  I definently think my favorite was the Seafood and Tofu Hot Pot.  The Tofu was fried perfectly and the inside was still soft and delicious.  Overall a very pleasing experience :-)

A fairly large Italian Restaurant located in Clearwater.  The server was very friendly when we sat down.  They have specials daily, and also a wide variety of entree choices on the menu.  We ordered the Shrimp and Scallops Grand Marnier and the Chicken Marsala.  The salads are quite large and fresh.  The fresh bread  and dipping oil was good.  The entrees are HUGE....it looked like I barely made a dent in my plate (plenty to take home :-)) For the chicken there were two large chicken breasts and the pasta there were a good amount of shrimp and scallops.  Overall very pleased with the restaurant!

I went into this Safeway for the first time this weekend and I really liked it.
I generally don't shop at Safeway, but I don't really have anything against it. I really like shopping here because you can see your savings. When we went here, we had a pretty big shop and we bought a lot of sale items. The receipt had our savings totalled at the bottom and it stated that we saved $26!! I couldn't believe it.

Safeway is pretty well laid out as well. I always have an easy time finding stuff and the selection is pretty good too.

This Safeway was not very busy, which was really nice. It may be a switch in my household!

Our first dine-in service for T.T. and we of course got the awesome Lo-Mein noodles for my two toddlers. They are picky picky eaters but they destroyed this dish! The chicken they use in the Lo-mEin dish was delectable-I stole a few pieces. There is NOT a lot of oil and it's seasoned to perfection.  Meanwhile, my husband and I had the sashimi boat and it was so fresh and good. Definitely will be back.  Salmon and everything was great-we usually get take out from them but this was so cozy to finally come in. They do not have booster seats for the toddlers but they have hi-chairs. TT is On point! PS. This is BYOB as well.

When I come to Edmonton on business, I either stay here or in Sherwood Park.  This is a nice Westin, with large comfortable rooms, flat screen TVs, good internet services, and a nice lounge downstairs.

I'd give this place 4 stars, if it wasn't for it's location.  In fairness, downtown Edmonton has come a long way, but it's still a little rough in spots.  I end up taking long walks to various places including:  Alberta Crafts Council, Aubrey's books, the downtown mall, Tim Horton's, the Hotel MacDonald, and down into the Saskatchewan River Valley.  As far as nice places to eat and interesting attractions, a cab ride is still necessary.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: We've been wanting to try this spot for awhile and finally were able to carve out alone time. Farm and Fisherman has delicious food and fantastic cocktails. My husband and I each ordered something different so we could sample. He had the burger and I had the wahoo fish special. We split the crispy potatoes, too. That burger was juicy and succulent. The fish???? Fresh, light, airy, and served on a bed of "fall salad" (squash, cranberries, etc.) which I could've inhaled in 2.2 seconds but was polite about. I'm seriously counting down the days until we go back.

I'd been itching to try Bistro since we moved to Cherry Hill. Everytime we walk by, I can smell that wood oven. I could practically taste the pizza on my lips.

Before we kicked off an afternoon of shopping, my Mom and I stopped here for a bite. We both had the Viennese Salad. It was... good. Just that. Good.

The pears on top were a little soggy, but the brie was warm and creamy. The balsamic was a little too sugary for me. We didn't try anything else, so this isn't too fair of an assessment. I'll be back for a full meal - at least to give it another shot.

The service was great though! 

If you don't want standard mall grub, stop here!

Apparently much nicer in comparison to other locations (this was my first).  Italian Pie has a large patio area to dine and/or drink, a large bar area with small tables, and a spacious dining room filled with natural sunlight.
I stopped in for lunch, and was pleased by the long list of lunch combos, and noticed that its a great spot if there is a large group gathering for lunch.
Great service, good food, and average prices. Nothing jumped out compelling me to return, however I noticed their phenomenal happy hour specials and I think that might just compel me.  I look forward to returning for happy hour!

This place is so easy to miss amongst all the eyesore stripmalls on Street Road.  But if you do go, you definitely won't be disappointed.
Like everyone else said, the half off menu is great.  Every roll you could possibly want is on this page-in my opinion, don't even bother with the rest of the menu!  I think the most expensive roll was like $6.50, with most of them being in the $3-$4 range.  I tried a Hawaiian roll which was great.
Plus, how could you not love a place that gives you a complimentary orange?

While Coda Rossa may not have the glitziest tasting room or a cute little wine boutique, they certainly have some of the best wine around.  For $5, you can sample any and all of their wine.  That right there is pretty awesome!  The wine is really delicious and they have plenty of variety, my favorite being Ameritage and Black Bird.
The people running this winery could not have been nicer or more knowledgable.  If you are looking for delicious wine and a cute, quaint little area in which to drink it, look no further friends!  Also be sure to check out nearby Bellview Winery.

To-yo is a pretty decent sushi place.  I've had better, I've had worse.  The fried rice is delicious.
The place is way too pricey, however.  I took some friends there, and when our $150 bill rolled in and everyone was still hungry, I thought I was going to get stoned in the parking lot.  
I had a horrible experience with a serveer there.  After settling the aformentioned bill, she came over, and annouced loud as could be that we only left her a $5 tip.  1) a tip is a tip, be grateful...2) we left her $35, she just couldn't add.  I thought that was the rudest thing I have ever encountered in my life.

Underwhelming experience.

The Average:

o  Not the freshest fish, not the worst.  Average.
o  Typical Americanized sushi menu, but decent selection of noodle soup dishes.

The Poor:

-  Friendly staff, but slow service.
-  Horrible pacing - the first entree was brought out nearly 25 minutes before the last, so one person was getting hungry while another was finished and ready to go back to work.
-  We had to wait 10 minutes to be seated.  There were open tables.

Overall, I was pretty disappointed and won't be coming back.

The location of this bar is pretty excellent. A nice patio, and rotating specials every day. Great view of that creepy dancing circle-head thing on Mass Ave.

That said, the staple menu is kind of vanilla and the plates are too small for every single dish served. I had a really hard time keeping my salad on my plate. I appreciate giving me more lettuce for my money, but it was extremely difficult to eat. 

Old Point makes their own cucumber vodka, which is definitely delicious. One question, why not garnish it with a cucumber?

The service here is really spotty. Sometimes you have an amazing girl in the drive thru who tells you that you are "dripping with swagger" despite being extremely hungover, (thank you awesome DD employee) and other times every single part of your order was wrong because the lady was talking over you while you were making your order. 

The turkey sausage breakfast sandwich is killer, despite obviously being a microwave creation. 

It really doesn't matter to me though. There's not a DD near where I live. I'm obsessed with Dunkin Donuts. I will return because coffee tastes better in a styrofoam cup.

The food was not even sub-par. It was so below par, in fact, that it shouldn't even be able to call itself Mexican food. 

I had a 2 item combination with an enchilada and a taco. The "seafood" taco is a mix of imitation crab and who knows what else. My enchilada was smaller than my hand. The rice was bland, and the beans were runny.  Our waiter used ridiculous slang and was inattentive, he was too busy making "bro" jokes with the other staff and texting. 

The patio is great, and that's probably why people go there and fill it up in the summer. Please do not waste your money on food that makes Taco Bell look like it has 3 Michelin stars.

This is a pretty great Dunkin' Donuts, especially since Brownsburg customer service is notoriously bad if you don't look a certain way. The staff is always friendly, and they don't rush you when you are trying to get through the new giant menu. I remember when they just had coffee and donuts....not the case!

I tried one of the lunch sandwiches today with ham, bacon, and cheddar on a flatbread. Kind of greasy, but really tasty for the $3. I always get a large iced coffee in the afternoons when I can get to a Dunkin. The problem is they are so far out of the way, I never get to go!

If you want cheap, delicious coffee, this is the place to be!

The Broad Street Car Wash pretty much sucks.  My car comes out of the wash and these guys run over to dry it with wet towels.  This is the first problem.  I understand you're trying to save towels or something, but how are you drying my car with a wet towel - exactly, you're not.  So, my (supposed to be) clean black car still shows the bird shit and bugs that "the wash" failed to remove and now a whole bunch of new water spots because "the dryer-guys" used wet towels and did a horrific job.  A waste of $8 (exterior only)!

Myself along with 11 other guys came to Kokopelli's for dinner.  We opted for the All You Can Eat sushi and we sat at the bar.  

The sushi itself was really good!  You could order anything off the menu except for the sashimi.  Some of the rolls that stood out for me were:

Mountain Roll
Dragon Roll
Caterpillar roll
and Ceviche roll

Service was just ok as it was pretty busy and we had to ask for refills and to have them remove our plates.  

Dont be fooled, when you walk in you think youre in a mexican restaurant but the bar area is where the sushi bar is.  

Would I come back?  Yes!

I can't imagine a nicer place to stay in New Orleans. Very stylish, comfortable rooms with excellent beds and helpful, friendly staff. Although less than 5 minutes walk from the unhinged Bourbon Street, the location (next to the Ritz) on Canal Street is elegant and not too noisy. There are about a zillion great restaurants within 10 minute walk.  It takes a few minutes to get used to the crazy lighting in the hallways/elevators and massive furniture in the lobby but it all works in the end - I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
A group of us came here on the way to the St. Louis airport.  It was dumping snow, 12" that day, and we discovered that this White Castle is a great place to camp out during a snowstorm.  

Overall excellent service. Our server was super friendly, patient, and helpful while a big group of us tried to decide what to order. She convinced us to try the chicken rings which were delicious. And I do feel slightly ashamed to admit that. She also let us customize our order to get half of each type of burger and multiple flavors of chicken rings.

I'm not sure why this place has gotten all the one star reviews. It's a Wendy's. it's a fast food place. Your expectations are supposed to be low so you can give them an ok rating. 

But to be fair, I've never set foot inside. The drive thru is my MO here. A customized soda and a chocolate waffle cone. Sometimes I'll splurge and get a burger with it. Nothing special, so maybe that's why I've yet to have a bad experience. It just meets expectations. 

They do have free wifi. It's nice to check Facebook during my whole five minute visit.

I've been here a handful of times before, and was not impressed. I never got around to reviewing them before last week's visit, and I would have given them 2 stars before. My recent visit, about a week ago, I was really impressed with the service and food, so I'm giving them 3 stars today. 

Their sashimi platter is HUGE, especially at that price. Its made for sharing. Order that, along with a few rolls, you're going to be rolling out of there happy and stuffed. 

Pro-tip: Be discerning about where you sit. If you're claustrophobic, there are a few places that make it miserable. Then there's also the booth that gets all the air-conditioning.

When clean is the best positive adjective I can use to describe you, there's probably an issue or two. 

The place is really cramped. Even the lobby and hallways. It's a tiny tiny hotel. And no one has a clue about anything. I was trying to get in touch with front desk, but no one answers the phone. Go down there and trying talking to them directly and they don't even know who to talk to/or who they are talking to, on their walkies. It was a bit of a joke.

What I really don't get is the price. It's pretty expensive for such a cramped space. This is Philadelphia, not New York. In the end the experience was alright, but far from great.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
For the price, I can't really complain, but overall as hotels go the room was a bit cramped (the bathroom ridiculously so) and I didn't dig the half-glass door on the shower, which as other reviewers mentioned, results in water getting all over the floor.

The staff are very friendly and their valet is pretty quick. Just call from your room when you want your car and they'll call you when it's out front, so you don't have to wait for it.

Protip: If you want free wifi: sign up for their free Guest Select and they'll waive the $10/day wifi fee!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
One of the best things about this Yogurtland is that it's open late.  Located on State Street, it's one of the few places open past 9pm.  But if you've been to a Yogurtland, they have a formulaic setup -- made to look like any other.  No boutique feeling here will be found.

They have a nice selection of flavors, and while I didn't count, I'd say 20.  I don't like Yogurtland that much because I find the yogurt to be more icy than creamy or smoothe.

So, although I would never say "no" to frozen yogurt, I say in a sluggish and slightly staggered and quiet voice, "Okay".

While the star count on my review is staying the same, I just want to clarify that even though the service at Sonobana is extremely slow, the servers are very nice and the sushi is delicious. 

At dinner a few weeks ago, we had such a great experience. I think if you go into it knowing that its going to take awhile, it's not as frustrating. Our server was really really nice. She made sure our sake glasses were never empty. Which is always great in my book. 

And the giant plate of sushi was some of the best I have had to date in Nashville. I cant wait to go back, and get some tasty sushi and sake.

Fresh Market is a bit like a cross between Roberts and Whole Foods. It's better as a place to pick up a few items from for a quick dinner (as opposed to walking in with an actual shopping list). They have some nice touches like free coffee and a pick your own 6-pack. Okay-ish cheese selection (Whole Foods is way better since they have a deli setup where they'll cut you a sample). On the whole, I'm very glad that something is occupying the former bookstore/funeral home, and Fresh Market does a pretty good job.

I used to go here much more often when my bf lived in the Marigny, but I don't get over here as often these days. As some of the other reviewers have noted, this is a very different coffee shop than others in the city, probably due to its stark design inside. 

I recently met some friends here, and appreciated the tables outside with plenty of chairs. We were highly entertained when watching (I swear I'm not joking) a chicken cross the street right next to us. Pro tip: If you're not feeling like ingesting tons of caffeine and get the Thai iced tea, don't be shocked when you get something that looks like carrot juice. It's tasty, I swear!

In Cali-Cali, this grocery sto' wouldn't even register on my meter. It's somewhere between the communist Russia Safeways and dingy Save Marts.

In the NO, it's a lifesaver when my body's reached it's saturation point with fried foodz. The salad bar, produce, prepackaged soup, and dairy are pricey compared to what I'm used to (I noticed that the meatz are cheap and they have quite a selection of Cajan/Creole specialty food also for cheap, if I were ever adventurous enough to try to cook in a Residence Inn kitchenette). But it's nice having a choice in what I stuff into my face.

You have a workflow here that is easy to master:

Baked green mussels  ›  joy roll ›  tuna box.

The joy roll in particular is fantastic - a rice paper roll in a nice slightly spicy sauce.  Baked green mussels are standard, and to be honest the tuna box is often too ricey.  It could use a little more finesse.  But what do I know.

Really you come here because it is right in the French Quarter, and the interior does a well enough job of Japanese minimalism with a requisite stainless steel fountain percolating under blue neon lights - like a quiet nightclub that forgot to hand out the flyers.

01.02.13

Ended up at Cafe Sierra since Rim (the all you can eat sushi place inside GSR) wasn't open.

Service was slow, but friendly.  Can't fault them TOO much since the crowd was larger than expected...but still.  I was hungry.

I had the large clam chowder and the chicken lettuce wraps.  Skip the soup and go for the wraps.  At $8, it is a steal and can definitely feed more than one mouth.

My parents each had the steak and lobster special at $17 each.  Also a steal in their eyes.

Total damage for six: $117

Ok, since I failed miserably at getting a treat for myself the other day (see my review of Dunkin Donuts), I tried again at Wendy's.  This time the treat was real and I was happy!  I've only been in the drive through at this location and its fast and the cashier and food givers are nice.  The crispy chicken sandwich I got was hot and super tasty, the fries were pretty good.  I could not believe how freekin fast I my food came, this made me happy because I was really starving.  Altogether a nice fast food experience.

I really love crazy pizza toppings and Jules really delivers.  Last night for my B-day I tried the edamame, goat cheese and lemon dressing pizza and the artichoke heart pizza, both were awesome and interesting.  The dining area is clean and modern and suprizingly not echoey considering the materials used.  Lots of babies and kiddos yet nice and quiet.  I also appreciated how there was a busy worker that came by to clean off the table and windows, nice!  Also, at around 3 bucks a slice you can have a great 2 slice dinner for $6!
Also keep in mind you can BYOB.

In this world of high-end, authentic cuisine food, the Old Spaghetti Factory (I hate that name) serves awesomely predictable Italian food.  Trust me on this, the food is tasty, affordable, filling, of decent variety and satisfying at the end.

Don't go there with expectations of a high-end Italian restaurant.  For a chain-restaurant, it does a great job!  I love their combo meal.  Comes to about $14 which includes a small salad, bread with regular & garlic butter, your main course and for dessert coffee/tea and an ice cream.  

Affordable, satisfying, weekday night-out kind of place with a decent ambience and spacious seating.

We stumbled onto this place as a result of our pick for the night being closed.  It turned out to be a pleasant detour.  The menu is small but the food was generally good - not heavy and greasy which tends to be the trend for most Italian restaurants.  Their chilled red pepper, prosciutto, and mozzarella appetizer was excellent while the seafood ravioli and veal medallions were better than average.  The panna cotta dessert was quite good though.

Was it the best Italian meal I ever had?  No, not really.  But the staff was great and I wouldn't mind going back - but I'm not sure yet if I would go out of my way to eat there.

I used to be a regular  Wednesday winger, on their wing night!  I love the wings they are great! however i am super disapointed in the service there latly!  I think they have just gotten to busy to care about everyone the way they should!  The all you can eat wing deal on Wednesdays is like $10 for all you can eat!  the problem is that i can't even get all i can eat out of it! the service is so slow! The worst part of it i don't think they care enought to improve the service!  I will not be a regular any longer!  I quit!
Elijah

the other day my brother and I order two large iced coffees with sweet Carmel and cream.  We got expensive large iced coffees from the Harleysville location.  They left my cup empty by at least an inch.  I pay how much for this stuff and you can't fill my cup?? Even adding extra ice would have been better than giving me a large cup not even close to full!    They barley put any cream in it which isn't normal for Dunkin either.   I kinda felt like they were just trying to pinch pennies yet charging me through the nose.   I also feel an attitude problem with most employees when I order.  Wawa might be my new spot for coffee.

Typical Americanized Mexican slop. I'm sure you know the drill: Huge, ridiculous menu. JUMBO margaritas. Tacos y burritos that all taste/look just like the enchiladas y chimichangas. Dry, barfy rice. 

The service was great though for our large party -- the only reason Los Vallartas is getting 2 stars instead of 1. 

Foolishly (very, very foolishly) I ordered Chicken Mole. WHY on Earth would I order this dish at a place like this? It was horrific. Lesson learned. 

Next time, I'll just get a table fulla margs!

Teeeeeeeee-rashy!  But still fun. 

You'll find all kinds here. Chicks with really bad tattoos everywhere, old men that ogle the young ladies, jocks, good old boys, grown men that send girls notes from across the bar on karaoke slips. 

I'm not sure I'd call it a dive. They have actual organized activities here and you can probably get almost any kind of typical cocktail. 

They have karaoke, of course. There were wayyy too many whiney country songs being sung for my taste. 

Also, it was smokey as hell. I was shocked to discover that you can still smoke in Florida bars. I smelled rank when I finally went home that evening....errr morning.

not bad not bad.... ordered lunch here for the shop and had it delivered.. the delivery was on time and the food decent... i had the kung pao 3 delight with chicken shrimp and beef... i've had better hot and sour soup... for around 6 bucks, the lunch specials include choice of soup, side, and rice ... the meal was tasty and didnt coat my mouth with grease... i'd go here any day over panda express... 

looking forward to the egg foo dishes and crispy half duck...  i see myself being a regular here for lunch... overall decent food and convenient lunch delivery

I do enjoy this place. I used to like it a bit more a few years ago when I use to go to school here. 

I do think the service is very good. They have someone who plays music outside, which is very soothing. 

I have had several dishes, one being the pumpkin and shrimp pasta, which was a bit rich, but had great flavors! I also enjoyed the parmesan fries with bacon aioli, another rich dish,  but still just as good! The portions are definitely ones to share. 

I can't say this is my favorite place anymore but I will always have a soft spot for this place, so many memories.

I don't want to speak to highly of this place, because I don't want to have to start waiting for equipment and parking.  But this is the best gym in the City.  They offer everything you want in a gym..brand new machines (cardio/weight), fitness classes, towel service, parking, a nutrition/protein shake bar, hot trainers, reasonable prices a place to stretch, and personal TV's on all the equipment.   The knock, is they don't have anybody clean the equipment, and some of the staff are a bunch of arrogant douche bags.  

That being said, I lost like 12 pounds.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Complaints about the thin walls and older furnishings are not unfounded but location and price is why you stay at this Doubletree. If I spent more time in my room, maybe I'd care more, but when in NOLA, the room is just a crash spot between all the activities (read: day drinking) and sleeping. 

I received excellent service from the hotel staff throughout my stay. Service is very important for me since I practically live in hotels and the level I received was comparable to much nicer/pricier hotels. Would definitely consider staying here again the next time I am in NOLA.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Not worth the $. I've been to 3 different branches & no one can cut a straight line. My son could've gone to another chain for the same price & gotten an actual style besides straight-across bangs, squared, chopped hair above the ears (Not even any grading...just a blunt chop half an inch above.) & an uneven back. The chairs always have hair in & around them, no matter the location. The stylists always seem bored & disinterested, & they don't even brush the hair off the kids fully. We won't be back to this chain.

The front desk service has been excellent. When we were walking around trying to find a place at night the sign was not lit so we ended up walking around for a while trying to find our hotel. I told the front desk receptionist and she immediately called to get that fixed. At 10:50 p.m. I called the front desk receptionist how about the massive booming coming from outside our window. I just wanted to know if there is a noise ordinance here in town. She said there is a club with very loud music that they been working on getting them to become more quiet. 
For over $200 a night I expect much more. It is a clean room
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: We stayed here for five nights and I have to say this was not my favorite place I have stayed in New Orleans. The staff was fairly helpful (especially the conceirge), however the layout of this place is ridiculous. In order to get to the quarter or wherever you want to go, make sure you plan for ten minutes travel time to get out of the hotel. The fitness center was ok but not anything to write home about and the pool was meh. This seems like it would be a good place for conventions but for vacation, I would pick someplace else.  Thanks for reading.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This is a review of the Le Nails on the STREET LEVEL of the Gallery Mall near the 10th Street entrance.

I had a mani pedi ($35 for both, $12 mani, $25 pedi) yesterday and "Lisa" at table 1 (they have 9 mani stations and 5 pedi thrones) did a nice job.

While I am still leery of pedicures and santitation, it "seemed" OK here.  They use OPI polish and decent base & top coats.  The pedi inculded a short exfoliation with scrub and a decent massage.

I would not RUN back here, but if I need a manicure and am nearby I will return.

I am ever-so disappointed with Gennaro's - and just went there again for the first time in years as it never is good.

Well, I was right - my cappucino came out with curdled milk.  Ick.
Fortunately the very kind server, Wendy, brought me another one and took it off the bill.

My close friend eats here ALL the time and loves it, but I just don;t get it.
It's never "quite right" for me here.

Friendly service, old-school digs (they need new carpeting) and a menu to match.

People/Locals love it.  Maybe New Yawk has spoiled me for Delco-Italian.

I have not been to moshi moshi in a very long time, and I needed some quick take-out tonight, so I stopped in and noticed a few things:

1.  The menu has changed (smaller)
2.  Prices went up a wee bit (but it has been over a year, I think.)
3.  My favorite Toro Ginza roll is now gone- but he will still make it, if you ask.

I ordered 2 rolls, - a crunchy tuna and an albacore & avo.  Both were fresh and fine.  service was prompt.

The dining room was very slow on a Thursday nite.  It's still OK - just a 3 star place.  Shiroi Hana is better (IMO).

OK, I'm gonna be nice and give them 2 stars - as usually McDonald's by it's very nature is a one star chain for me. 

I don't do fast food.  I just don't - but if you need a clean(ish) restroom - and the new McCafe coffee - the New Britain (old school) mcD's has been around for-eh-ver.

I think it may be about the same vintage as the Doylestown location.

The people working here are pleasant, though and that is worth alot.  Mostly CB West folks, some young adults - some not-so-young (during the day shift).

I won't be in often, but hey - it's there.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
OK - I dare not tell you when I used to walk "up town" to Nat's - because then you will know that I am older than Pink.

Hell - I coulda baby sat for little Alicia Moore and her brother - but I digress..

Nat's has been a D-town staple.  For years.
Generation after generation of Jr. and Sr. High schoolers congragate here after football games and dances to have a (greasy) slice or a "wooder" ice in the summer.

I always liked Capri's Pizza better - but Nat's Sicilian pie is still a cheesy baseline for me to this day.

God bless 'em.  They're still here.

Solid, nostalgic, "traditional" Chinese American food - with BIG portions and great values for eat-in at lunch (weekdays lunches are 5.95 - 6.95).

Lunch for 3 of us WITH TIP was $24.  Wow.

Friendly service and clean comfortable digs.

The Moo Shu Chicken for lunch comes with 2 fresh pancakes.
My 6 year old enjoyed her steamed "light & healthy" chicken and broccoli.

It's not Asian Fusion, It's not "modern" Chinese, it's old-school combo platters with white or fried rice (which was freshly made and good, by the way - loaded with pork and egg!).

NICE!

OMG, Dunkin' has taking over the universe - including Suburban Station with multiple outposts.

That said I never eat donuts, but I do occasionally succumb to temptation and get a hot or ice latte as is seasonally appropriate.

Passero's in Suburban has far superior coffee and food but is also more money - natch.

It is still cheaper that Charbucks (FiveBucks?) and they have oodles of flavors/syrups (I pass on those.)

For a "regular" cuppa joe - Dunkin or Wawa are my go-to's.
Thanks for being here when we need you, Dunkin. You are taking over the WORLD.

It's hotel food - and usually I might give a place like this 2 stars - but I am giving 3 due to VERY nice service and we lingered a very, very long time.  The main dining room was nearly empty (but the bar was hoping for happy hour) on the week night we went.

A good friend of mine who is vegetarian got the pasta with goat cheese which looked very good.

The female server was superb!  Very attentive and brought us apples and nuts (with a nut cracker) to snack on.

While there are far better choices nearby - this was a warm safe place to kill a few hours on a bitterly cold afternoon.

I am torn - the food is 4 stars but there are too many other things that need attention - mostly decor-wise - like dust-covered bread plates and a dining room that needs a makeover, stat.

The business has been around for 11 years and is clearly family run.
Shrimp scampi was very basic - but good.  I asked for it light on the sauce (oil/garlic) so that was a good move.  Frittata for lunch is a good and tasty value.

Bread was cold and dry (and sitting on the table waiting for us).
Not great.

I can cook alot of these things at home just as well.
I would return but won;t be rushing back.

Not as bad as it could have been but not great either.
I attended a conference here - ate the "banquet food" (Meh) in cramped dining rooms (The room downstairs claims to seat 150 and that is too tight.) with disinterested servers who could not wait to finish their shifts and get the heck out.

"Grab & Go" breakfast was a joke.  Awful  100% pre-packaged foods.
