Room seemed OK but now I am paranoid about bedbugs.  Surprisingly, bathroom (in hotel room) looked as though it had been renovated.  Public restroom was a high trafic area and needed re-stocking moreoften than it got.
Will let you know.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
OK, my husband (back then fiance) and I went here ONCE about 3-4 years ago and i will try to remember what I can.  I know that I loved it and he hated it, so I am splitting the difference at 3 stars.  (I'd probably give it a 4 for the Chicken Francese entree I had, and for chatting with the chefs in the semi-open kitchen.)

Service was good, but DH did not like his pizza (margarita) at all.  Too thin, too burnt tasting, too expensive.  he went on and on.

Meanwhile, i had a great time and (being fresh outta Manhattan at the time) thought the prices seemed pretty "normal".

I would like to go back and try this place again.

Friendly staff - a few of which have been there for years, and also a few who appear to be "mentally challenged".  Kudos to Acme for that.

Meanwhile, the prices are fine (cheaper than Giant) but also they do not carry certain items like Hint Water (I have to trek to Giant or the new Whole Foods for that) and other organic goodies.  They carry Reed's Ginger Brew - but want 6.89 for a 4 pack.  Ee-gads!

Anyhow, I do shop here and will continue to do soas it is on my way home from work.
But for major weekend shopping it's Giant or Whole Paycheck for me.

P.S.  Your Newman's  lemonade was nearly 3 weeks out of date in the Dairy Case.

Where my wife and I always end up when we want to relax and not worry about what's going to come out of the kitchen.  Eddie and the staff work hard to be attentive, but not smothering, which results in great service!  They have 4 or 5 daily, good sized and thoughtful specials, a soup of the day, a veggie of the day and good desserts.  The dining room is a typical restaurant dining room, but if you want to mix it up w/ the staff, sit IN or AT the bar and don't be afraid to dish it out.  Just be prepared to get it right back!

***This National Car Rental (located at the Philadelphia International Airport) features a very small but good selection of new cars and SUVs in their Executive Aisle; I also appreciated being able to rent a hybrid, which provided great savings on gas (especially since I was traveling from Philadelphia to Baltimore and Washington, DC); service was good and quick--both at the car rental agency and the shuttle that provides transport to and from the airport***

I am not sure what the parking situation is at this National Car Rental if you just need to stop in to grab something.

***This National Car Rental agency featured a great variety of vehicles in its Executive Aisle--large sedans like Toyota Avalon as well as many SUVs; it is also conveniently attached to the terminal so that you do not have to catch a shuttle (it makes picking up and returning a vehicle here very easy and quick); I did not like how the car I rented only came with a half tank of gas because trying to return the car with exactly a half tank was not easy; National though proactively refunded me for the additional gas I put in the tank***

I am not sure if this National has parking available if you just need to pick up something here.

This is a very busy and popular McDonald's. They recently remodeled the building. They completely tore it down to build a new one. They did it quickly, but now the store seems cramped.

They do have two drive-thrus now and so they get more people through faster. And they are extremely fast. Very impressive. 

Food quality is good for McDonald's. The owner is also extremely nice and is a good member of the community. He allows kids to use their water for car washes and donates things like cups to events around the community.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Fat Salmon is the 2nd sushi place I have really fallen in love with.

I'm a vegetarian, so I don't know about the fish options, but I love the Old School roll, the veggie tempura roll, and the tofuholic.  The veggie tempura roll is nice and spicy, but the Old School roll is really spicy, but so tasty I can't stop eating no matter how much it hurts.  

The Agedashi tofu is my favorite appetizer.  I once had a bite of the Deep Fried Tofu before I realized it had scallop in it, but it was fantastic.  

The only things I have found disappointing are the gyoza, and the edamame every once in awhile gets a bit over cooked if we get take out.

I felt the need to review this WD as they really seem to be trying.  I am used to their "attitudes" and the snottiness that comes with being a check out clerk in this city.  For the past month or so, I have noticed a "toned down"version of cashier "uppidy-ness".  Did they get a raise?  A good talking to by management?  A spanking?  Well, I dunno, but the customer service warrants 3 stars.  The meat department lady vacillates between over friendliness and sullenness.   I will keep shopping here for basics and staples until there is another affordable choice.

Underwhelming. Seems like a haven for blue-hairs that are pretending/trying to get out of their comfort zone and try something "hip."

My sandwich (the cuban) was good, and I definitely liked the chick pea salad served in lieu of fries/chips. My partner's caesar salad was just weird. It was a basically a hunk of heart of romaine with this weird polenta thing on the side. The dressing was nice though.

I thought the cookies at the end were good. I like my sweets sweet, I guess. Or maybe it was just that I wanted my impression of the place to be positive so I faked a positive response at the end. 

Overall, meh.

Breaux Mart is the closet grocery store to my house and therefore has become my "necessities" market. They have most of the things that I need at the last minute and I use them for that detail mostly. The market staff is friendly and the store gives you the feeling of a hometown local grocery store. Due to its size, I feel the variety is lacking from some of the bigger stores, but in most cases it gets the job done. Also due to its size, I often feel cramped in the store and become slightly claustrophobic. I like Breaux Mart , but really only for the small things.

Dinner at M Bistro was perfect. Service, food, and atmosphere were great.

The pork chop was perfectly seasoned and cooked.  The andouille mac-n-cheese it comes with is the best mac n cheese I've ever had. The filet was also perfectly cooked. Topped with just the right amount of crab sauce. 

Dinner for 2 with appetizers, dessert, and wine runs about $140 before tip. Worth every penny! 

TIP: If you dine later, Jeremy Davenport comes on at 9PM. Amazing Jazz while you eat. Can't beat that. 

Highly recommend M Bistro.

This may be the sketchiest taco stand around.  They dont speak any english not even numbers so come prepared to use sign language or bring a bilingual friend.  

They were out of ceviche, my guess is that they only make it on certain days.  We got chicken tacos and steak tacos.  Requested avocado which they didnt have.  $25 for 10 tacos.  They are served with a green sauce and a red sauce.  The green is much more spicy but flavorful.  The steak was seasoned well and tender.  The chicken was pretty bland.  I ended up pouring on the green sauce. 

I was hoping to have a solid late night quick taco spot.  This isnt it.

Service was a little slow during lunch with a single old lady busting her hump waiting every table (which she appologized for). Once we ordered food came out pretty fast. The dinning area is small with a few tables. 

The menu is typical New Orleans Poboys, fried seafood, and daily specials. I much appreciate that they offer a petite portion of their salad (which is plenty for lunch). Fried Shrimp salad was good but its hard to beat my favorite from New Orleans Food and Spirits.  Prices are decent. $2 for a side of fries, about $6 for a petite salad, and $4-$6 for a 5" poboy.
 
I would recommend this place for lunch.

I'm really biased when it comes to hotels - my preferred brand is Starwood.  When traveling for work, I don't really get a choice and I have a budget to keep.

I stayed at the Marriott at Vanderbilt University to attend a work conference.  The room was spacious and clean, but nothing that would make me feel like I do when I stay at the W or St. Regis... (yeah, I know...I'll shut up...).

The staff is VERY friendly!

The rooms could use some updating as they are looking really worn and out of date.  Price was reasonable for the location and they have a full bar and a pretty decent steak salad.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Tres Jalapenos serves solid Mexican food.  The salsa was fresh and tasty and my pork tostadas were delicious.  

This is a BYOB, but during brunch on Saturday and Sundays (11am-4pm), they provide free mimosas.  How can you say no!?  Unfortunately, we got there a little after 4pm and they were out of mimosas.  But, possibly detecting my sadness, the server offered to make us some free margaritas.  Yes!  She knows my weakness.  And boys and girls, this was not a diluted drink, as to be expected when it's free -- the margarita was pretty strong and delicious!  A perfect complement to the chips and salsa and tostadas.

Horrible, ordered off grub hub ans specifically put " no red sauce"  on my steak Stromboli , once the Stromboli arrives it has red sauce on it, so i called the girl hung up on me, i called back kept me on hold then once she picked up told me they would send another one out but i need to send the other one back, what kind of place wants food back from someones home who knows what they could have done with it, what are you gonna do with it sell it to another customer??  i told them cancel the order i didn't trust what they would do to my food i will never ever order anything from them again.

So the place is by no means the BEST sushi anywhere, but for our suburban philly world, its pretty damn good!

make a reservation, especially on a wknd.  the place gets crowded and youll always have to wait for a table.  service is good to great, depending on the night.  eaten there a million times, never have had bad service.

everything - everything is good.  my family's favorites are the salmon kama appetizer, fuji roll, clear soup, and any of the udon noodles.

atmosphere is okay, and remember - its byob!

Seems like a really cool spot as I noticed its on of those places that can be like a Cheers type of joint. Everyone seemed to know each other so I'm sure its a place where the locals go to stay away from ridiculous tourists like myself...lol

Bartenders and staff were really nice as they offered me some complimentary pizza which came in handy because I was drunk and hungry. This place is located almost on the edge of the Quarter. Nice R&B music was playing so I was definitely enjoying the music vibe here. Cool spot to hit up if you wanna get away from all the tourists in the Quarter.

Everything here was great, but I can't give it five stars. Why? Because the food came out warm, not hot. And I like my food hot. No one else at the table complained, so I didn't say anything either, but considering this is probably the best restaurant in St. Louis right now, I expected my food to be hot.

Other than that, everything was wonderful. My father in law, who has dined all over the world, loved it. I have never heard him rave so much. He had the pork chop and it was huge and he eat the whole thing (shocking, if you knew him!)

Whenever I am in the mood for a pizza, this is the place I go to.  Reasonably priced, timely delivery, and the most tasty pizza in the area. 

Unfortunately because their pizza is so good, I cannot speak to any of the other entrees on the menu.  I always fall back to their pizza. But my good friend, whose taste is almost as impeccable as mine is, swears by their sandwiches and subs.

If there is one negative I see, it is that they do not offer a large number of side items.  That part of the menu is a bit sparse.  But in terms of the quality of their pizza, Rocco's dominates.

Global Quesadilla. Bright red walls, sassy t-shirts, steady food. I like it here. I've come here with a big group before a few Arch Rival Roller Girls matches and they haven't disappointed yet. For less than ten bucks, you can get an obscenely large quesadilla or an obscenely large plate of nachos. They even throw in a handful of shredded lettuce just in case you need a vegetable side. Service has always been friendly and relatively competent. The concept may slightly outperform the execution, but hey -- other than tortilla and cheese, what more could you ask for?

Woah.  Stepped into this McDonalds looking for breakfast and it was hands down one of the most unpleasant chain location I've ever entered.  Broken seats were taped with "under construction" tape, the people hanging out there weren't even eating, and it almost felt unsafe at 10:00 in the morning.  (And as a St. Louis city resident, I feel like I'm allowed to say that.)

Must avoid unless you really want those hash browns.  And don't get your hopes up, the one down the street's even worse.

P.S.: The ATM was broken.  (Why I tried to get money here, I don't really know.)
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
I have always loved Maggie Moos, but bc of the frozen yogurt craze, I haven't been back until recently... and it made me wonder why did I not come here instead!?

The ice cream here is made fresh daily and the small is HUGE... you get sooo much ice cream! I loved the peanut butter flavor... I mixed it with dark chocolate and topped with a brownie! yum~

Also, their ice cream cakes are fantastic, got one for my dad's birthday this year and everybody was fighting over the last piece! We got the turtle flavor, it was dynamite!

Had breakfast here on an early Sunday morning since the cafe was conveniently located inside our hotel. We wanted to grab a quick bite before heading on the road back to San Jose.

Wasn't the greatest food and the menu had very little choices for breakfast food. I think McDonalds would've been the better choice. 

The egg benedict was pretty gross - the sauce that covers the ham and eggs on the english muffin wasn't tasty at all. Only the hash browns were decent. Will most likely pass on this cafe the next time.

This reminded me of the authentic chinese restaurants I've been to in other parts of the world, with flavors that are hard to find in American Chinese!

The sesame chicken is healthy, hearty, and flavorful...
The sauces are tart with vinegar.
The dumplings are packed and seasoned.
The chicken egg drop is gelatinous.
The tea is bottomless.
The staff is UNBEATABLE. Sweetest staff of my day!

A wonderful first visit in an atmosphere where you can hear your conversation. Loved it!
Also, all cocktails are under $5. No idea if they're good or not, but it's probably worth a taste!

I was able to check out this Rotolo's as soon as it opened.  Having been a fan of Rotolo's for years, I was excited to see that one was opening so close to where I live.  I got my usual: a medium pepperoni pizza with extra cheese, and of course it was fantastic.  It was big enough to split with my friend and we were both satisfied.  My friend also decided to try a bowl of their tomato basil soup.  While I was unable to try it, my friend told me that it was really good, so I will be sure to get it the next time I go back.

Not a terrible bar. I only go here because some friends of mine live about 2 minutes from the place.

Okay crowd, but it gets super packed with young people who are just there to get ripped. Ridiculously smokey and since I am being drawn more and more to places that lack smoke completely, this is a turn off.

They do have a few little bar games here that are pretty fun. Like Morgan mentioned, the skee ball is one of the selling points. All in all not a bad place if you are in the area, but not worth the trip if you aren't.

I'm going to just lay it on the line: the bar is cool, but the drinks are overpriced. Way overpriced. $8 for a beer you can get for $5 elsewhere overpriced. Look, I'm not a dope. It's the Quarter. You're gonna charge what dumb tourists are gonna pay. Can I show you my Louisiana ID and get a discount? Even if it's just a buck off? Seriously, we are on the same team here. We're all friends. $15 for two beers is a little much. It's water and barley...don't get arrogant.

Other than that, this place is cool. Cool people and cool staff. Just don't rob me.

First of all, I want to start by saying I don't know why I do this to myself. I once again ended up at a bar on Bourbon St. Gee, I wonder how it went.

Well, it sucked. It was Razzoo's without the charm. The music was pretty good and the shot girl was super nice, but the guy on stage who was pumping up the crowd needs to work on his act. It wasn't really entertaining. Of course, in places like this, you gotta take what you can get.

So, why the two stars?? Uh... $6.75 for a beer is the reason. It was Abita Amber, not some fancy import. I know it's the quarter, but come on.

Accidentally stopped in here with a friend when we were looking for another bar in the same area. Really cool space with friendly people. They were offering free mac and cheese when we came, and although we didn't partake, I thought that was nice. There weren't a lot of people and they had a little jazz band playing in the back. Ordered one Abita Strawberry and was pleasantly surprised when it was only $3, considering some other places charge as much as $5 for the same thing.

I'll be back if I'm in the neighborhood, but I think it would be a better spot if it were smoke free.

This is a fancy little place with a speakeasy feel.

I was here for an afternoon cocktail and I immediately dug the vibe: a classic cocktail bar that makes you feel as if you have stepped back in time- except for the tvs (can we PLEASE have some cocktail bars that don't feel the need to have big screens on the wall?). I got the Frenchy which was a tasty vodka and champagne concoction, which I enjoyed. They have music practically every night, but sadly I arrived too early and I wasn't able to catch the band.

This seems like the perfect place to start an evening and I will return.

This store is okay. The place had just possibly been robbed when we got here (lots of cops and confused workers), so maybe I'm leaning a little more towards the negative. 

Honestly, we just stopped in here for a wine and liquor run, so this review is going to be short and sweet. They were having a sale on Barefoot wine, so we got that and it turned out to be pretty good. They have a pretty good beer selection- nothing too crafty, but the more "mainstream" stuff is well stocked and there are a lot of choices. Aisles are wide to prevent crowding, which is awesome and we checked out with ease. We even saved $4 for using a Winn Dixie card.

Soooo it's like a tiny Shop N Save that is diorganized-prices are the same though. Its kinda skeezy lookin if I do say so myself not awful, just not nice, also the check out guy was nice, but I ended up only buying some powerade cuz I was thirsty and they were a buck a peice for the big ones. 
I firmly believe it depends what store you go to for what its like, but come on, if you own a store take care of it -especially the inside.
Overall I got the atmosphere of a crappy (yet large) conveinient mart -its better if you live near by, I think.

Why 3 stars? Because this is your average sushi experience.

   ---   ---   ---

I came here at the recommendation of Yelper pal, Christy T, who claimed Kaisen to be the #1 sushi spot in Tampa Bay. Unfortunately all I walked away with was the knowledge that our taste buds do not see eye to eye.

I went with the chef's choice sushi dinner, because I wanted to get the best of the best, and I fear nothing. Unfortunately, I found it to be rather unforgettable. 

Not to claim Kaisen, because it wasn't a bad experience, but nothing about what I ate screamed, "I must return!"

Why 4 stars? Because Publix is solid again.

   ---   ---   ---

Publix, or PUBIX as I like to call it (YAK YAK YAK) has this weird X-factor about it. I don't know why I like the store so much, but I always feel at home in them. 

I'm temporarily living in Gulfport for 3 weeks while I close on my house, and this will be the place I check into 3x a week, instead of the Seminole Heights location. This one makes me wish that the SHeights Publix would make some upgrades, but I still love it anyway. That being said, how sweet would it be to get sushi and a real meat counter in my hood?

Really freakin' sweet, I say.

Why 4 stars? Because who knew the Brandon mall could be cool?

   ---   ---   ---

Chain or not, I never expected to see a beer bar in Brandon, let alone at the mall. Be warned that Apple maps does a poor job of explaining the actual location of the BT. It's right next to Dick Sporting Goods and Cheesecake Factory. Apple Maps makes it seem like it's outside the mall area, by the Wal-mart. False, Apple... false.

Tons of beer selection here, and plenty of it is local. During my visit (Friday night) they had some really good live music, as well as a gaggle of TV's playing baseball and basketball. Basically, all of the keys to my heart.

I had to try a Mexican place called Nachos!

But its just a Mexican place with nicer decor. Prices are the same as most standard Mexican joints... $7.49 combo platter, $3.00 for cheese dip you know the scoop. 

Our server was all smiles (probably because of our thirst of margaritas and flirty eyes) and was very prompt and nice. The food was just okay. There were alot of families with ninos in there because when the food is cheap that's where the kids are! 

I'll be back to nachos, I like the decor and service but probably just stick to the drinks.

Okay so maybe it was the YELP in me, or the fact I couldn't sleep knowing my favorite dry cleaners screwed up my shirt. Finally, I went in to show the burn mark and make them aware of the problem. 

I met with the owner. He said, "If I can't get this out, I will replace the shirt, but let me try" I said fine. He said he didn't think it was a burn but a chemical stain. A few days later, I went to get the shirt. Well, look at that. He got it out. No way. 

I didn't have to pay to get the stain out and was happy I gave him another shot. 

Sorry for the 3rd update - but it's worth it.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
History has it that this was the first Sushi place in Nashville. Used to be a sushi bar with a few small tables. They have since expanded the res truant and thank goodness they did because they need the space. 

Since a new sushi place has opened across the street, these guys have really stepped it up. New chairs, I believe new carpet, and always adding new rolls.  

I feel its affordable, i like the service, its clean and quaint. Best for just 2 people though. 

I recommend: Vandy Roll, Jane Roll, Dr. Larry Roll. - Big rolls - Big pieces. Service is quick even when most tables are full.

Good clean spot with fresh good take away. They don't deliver but if I'm craving good take away Chinese, it's minutes from home and worth a trip.

Great hot soups
Fresh flavors
Flavorful and hearty veggies
Good tofu 
Plump shrimp
Brown rice which is hard to come by (?!?!)
Good noodle bowls

New items I noticed tonight and tried: 
A lean on Thai flavorsi tried the curry coconut basil veggies with grilled tofu over brown rice and it was just enough heat and very fresh!

I Would recommend them for great take away in the old NE section of town.

For early birds only!! The lobby is open straight up to all rooms and is all hard surfaces... Very very noisy starting EARLY.

The room was OK but small.  The bed was pretty nice, but a pretty crappy location really close to the ice machine and the elevator.  No soundproofing in this place at all, was the real bummer:  The room next to us had some assholes with a baby---who takes a baby to New Orleans??---and they were awake playing peek-a-boo every goddamn morning at like 5am.  We could hear them really clearly through the walls, so one morning we rented a porno and put it on CRAZY loud and went out for coffee.   PEACE OUT BREEDERS.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
On Beach Walk. Right across the street from the beach.

Staff was friendly. 
Hotel rooms are decent. 
Plenty of parking on site. 
Nice size pool.
Free wifi - good speed

Hotel has 4 floors. Has rooms with connecting doors for people traveling with others.  Rooms with frig or kitchenette.

Continental breakfast is a joke! Juice, Little Debbie snacks, and bread to make toast.

Had an issue with the refrigerator in our room. The frig was replaced within 20 minutes.

Close to restaurants and other hotels.  Restaurants deliver to the hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Got booked here via Hotwire. 

PICK UP:
You can't drive in any personal cars onto the lot. You need to park on the street probably in a no parking zone, but no one harassed us. Why'd we have a personal car and need a rental? We're vacationing and had use of a relative's car to pick up the rental for our road trip. 

That being said, the female associate who helped me was great. I didn't bargain at all but she got me a good deal. 

RETURN:
Was fast & easy. Staff were friendly & helpful. 

OVERALL:
It'd definitely be a 4-star if it weren't for that inconvenient no personal car rule onto the premises.

When I walked into this place I didn't know if I was in a hotel or in Studio 54 in New York.  White grecian marble everywhere, this place looks like it was in an episode of Pimp my Hotel.  Overall, the staff is nice and the rooms are comfortable.  Had to change my first room because the bed had pubic hair on the cover.   The free breakfast is good, you can tell that management makes the cooking  staff wait around in the eating area to make sure no one takes food from the eating area, this is kind of tacky and stupid.    Put down that apple!    Verdict, 3 stars.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
$10 ATM fee during mardi GRAS. You tell me if it deserves more than one star. I don't care what they have on tap. This is a tourist trap, and you should have known that the second you stepped on Bourbon Street. 

On the plus side (though not enough to redeem from one-star status) during the National Championship game, they sold these hybrid beer mug/funnels. It looked like a regular plastic 32 oz. beer mug, but the handle was clearly a pipe. You would unhinge the handle from the handle holder, and boom goes the dynamite; you've got a beer bong. 

No seriously this place is pretty awful. All of them.

I had the sashimi and tempura lunch special. The tempura is pretty good- i guess you cant really critique it other than i was kinda weirded out by the fried banana with the dipping sauce. it wasnt bad alone but just wasnted expecting a little sweet treat in between the sweet potato, carrot, and zucchini tempura. 

the miso soup is good but i do think that for the size and quality- its a bit pricey. 

id say this place isnt anything to rave nor complain about considering its a mom-pop type of sushi place. its just... meh!

The place has the best quality of fish. The sushi chef has a reputation that hes been doing this for 20 years which says a lot but I'm also not sure how accurate that statement is. Either way, the food certainly tastes like he has been. Their chirashi bowl is so tasty and worth ordering. I love their sushi options and their sashimi option A is by far my go to for 12 pieces (4 kinds of fish x 3 pieces each). The fish is cut in decent sizes and not small at all. The service can be a bit slow or fast depending on who your server is. Order their ramen on the cold days! It's so tasty!!!

Three stars for Rock N' Raw is right on.

The experience was just fine, not amazing. 

We enjoyed our food. We had the salmon nigiri, a few rolls, and the crab rangoon and veggie tempura. All of the food was good. 

We shared a bottle of hot sake. There was a fly in it and we didn't see it until the bottle was empty. We told the server and she took it off our bill. 

This isn't a place to go out of your way to visit but it's a fine place to eat if you're already at the casino. The food was better than I expected.

Balducci's has been a few times a year staple since I lived across the street. I like the ambience and the pizza is good quality- both the deep dish and the thin. Someone mentioned smoke and that was most certainly true a while back. It was always smoky and had really poor ventilation. However, it has since gone completely smoke free (other St Louis restaurants should take note!) and doesn't have the smoke issue any longer. They have great wine, a tasty house dressing and a decent sized menu. I gave 3 stars - if they would consider coming down in price on their pitchers, I would consider 4.

I've been to other Champps around the country - usually between flights at airports - and they are a pretty decent restaurant chain.  This was my first visit to this Champps which is located in a large shopping mall.  A friend was entertaining some of his clients and I got to tag along :-)

Our waitress was friendly and attentive.  I ordered the fish and chips and they were surprisingly very good for this type of place.  The wine list was good and I enjoyed a nice Bare Foot Cabernet.

A pretty good experience considering it was a busy Friday night...in between snow/ice storms.

Yay a new ice cream shop...which has only been open a couple of weeks. The space is small but I like the sparkly booth seats.

 The ice cream selection is small but there is definitely something for everyone. I had the peach vanilla and it was fresh and tasty. My only small point was that the peaches bits were large so they got a bit icy to the tooth. But that's probably me just being a weirdo. My friend loved her toasted coconut and it was yummy. 

The business is cash only and supposedly also has snowballs but I didn't see anyone get those while I was there.

Didn't people make the runs on the grocery stores last week?  Why is the dairy case at this store still empty?  It looks like they haven't really restocked completely after the post-Isaac carnage.

The store is small but it carries some different brands and items than the other groceries in town, so that's a positive. Every one was raving about the produce and the cheeses, since these areas were a bit depleted, I'll have to go back and check again.

Four stars for now...I've really liked Fresh Markets in North Carolina. I am surprised at how tiny this store feels.

This was probably my favorite bar on the Metry bar crawl. The decor reminded me of my aunt & uncle's rec room...all padded leather and wood paneling with big (heavy) captain's chairs. Unfortunately it was really smokey (maybe some scrubbers?)

The bartender seemed to be distracted so it was difficult to get a refill. The DJ (Saturday night only?) was playing an eclectic selection of music ...which didn't really go with the environment. I would have preferred some old school rat pack maybe.

Price point was pretty good. And I'm not sure what was going on with that meat roasting out front....

Pandemic update:
Rouses is my usual go to big grocery. I popped in midday yesterday to do my parents' shopping and pick up a few things for me too.

There as a staff person outside wiping down baskets. All employees were masked and the checkout stations have plexiglass.

Most of the shoppers were wearing masks. And the store was well-stocked, I got almost everything on Mom's list. They even had paper towels! (OK, one brand and they were the small rolls.) 

Since this is a large store, I felt like I could keep my space away from people more easily and people maintained distance at the checkout.

I just realized that I reviewed this Rouse's as one of my very first reviews and the store has improved so much in the last couple of years.  Love the produce area and the wine/booze selection.  Love all the local products, especially the Dong Phuong bakery cookies.

So why not 5 stars? The same issues as when this was a Save-a-Center. The parking lot needs better drainage. After one of our lovely NOLA thunderbursts today, I walked to my car in shin deep water. My car almost flooded...but that was really due to the jerk in an SUV and his wake. I really do wish my eyes were death rays sometimes.

Yes I'm the dummy who shows up at the airport hungry, every SINGLE time. I'm rushing around too much and don't get hungry until I get through security and can breathe. Then I'm waiting for my flight and grumbly grumbly tummy.

I was excited to see a new option on the SW concourse AND it didn't have a line on this very busy Saturday morning. I got a HUGE and yummy breakfast burrito. Yes it was airport prices but what are you gonna do.

The staff was quick and friendly and I was able to nosh on my burrito through lunch it was so big. 

I'll have to try their non-morning offerings but so far I'm a fan.

From what I understand...the Bronx Bar doesn't really open until the adjacent New York Pizza closes...or maybe there is some overlap.

The important thing is that you can buy a slice late night. And scarf it down while drunkypants and give yourself a wicked pizza burn that sends you down the WtH memory trail the next morning.  

On the particular night that I went, I was grateful to Lindsay A for buying me a slice and amused by Holly G when she stole it. And even more grateful for my 2nd non-molested slice.  

Basic pizza slices came out quick. Selection of beverages is good, but as Joel M said...the bartender wasn't really interested in us.

I liked this bar a lot!  Maybe because it was of the company I had, or perhaps the intense game of Golden Tee that was going on between us, or the unmentionable amount of beer that was consumed, I really liked it here.  I do have to mention the variety of liquor and beer that is available was rather impressive too!

Sure, it was completely dead on a Wednesday night, but I loved the inside of the bar, it was quiet, and service was awesome.  Plus, drink prices were very reasonable.  That being said, I'm happy I wasn't here with all the yuppies and sorority sisters that my fellow Yelpers have warned us about!

This was about 2 years ago, that I stopped here after everyday testing at Abington Hospital and errands at the Willow Grove Mall and heading towards the turnpike, just to get home faster, when I realized how hungry I was and did not feel like cooking or going out. I saw the Hunan Village and hubby and I both love Chinese food.  I ordered up a storm and just handed them the credit card.

Some of the most flavor-less food we have ever eaten.  I will not return for the second chance. I just wish my hunger had hit me a few miles down the road, in front of the Mandarin Garden, now they have great Chinese food!

My in-laws gave us a gift certificate for a free night at the Marriott.  We stayed there one night during our last trip.  We were upgraded to a slightly larger room.  We had a view of the lake and Saks.  

The room itself was nice.  The bed was uber comfortable.  The bathroom was good too (great shower, spacious).  The work-out facilities had much to be desired.  It was pretty bad.

We had an enjoyable breakfast.  It was a buffet of typical breakfast foods.  The service was outstanding.  We also had outstanding service the night prior at the bar.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
New east side sushi joint, Save me some travel time when I am craving for sushi, but wasn't quite a cure, just yet.

I am just not sure how to take on a place like this, Is this a place like Samurai that everything is self-serving (the way the decor) or a sit down restaurant (the price) with full table service? Okay sushi, overly salted noodles, Well ~ believe or not, it seems like the chef didn't mixed the salt in the wok so I got a bite with nothing but salt and noodles...kind of funny in a way...but wth?

I might come back for lunch sometime.

Sushi...is that the name for Japanese food? How many of you guys love go to Sushi Garden and think they have the best sushi in town? If thats whats you like and yes have some California Rolls and be merry. 
But for me..I rather have a Tuna Sashimi Bento form Samurai...have you ever had Japanese curry rice? Thats another my favorite. Only if I live little closer to this place. I can come here for dinner every night (well~maybe not) , They are so reasonable priced...places like this and Snow Peas makes single guy's life easier...and why are you still eating McDonald?

The only good thing about this hotel is that the staff is really nice.

The bad:

- The beds are so uncomfortable. You'll sink into them. I hardly got any sleep! 
- The rooms are institutional.
- The bathroom is gross. When you turn on the light, the light would flicker for about five seconds and then makes this annoying buzzing noise. 
- The lighting makes your skin look yellowish green. 
- The shuttles to the convention center are usually about 10 minutes late. 

I don't think the neighboring hotels are much better.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
When I moved to Philadelphia last year, I asked a few people where I should get my hair cut.  A couple Wharton students suggested that I try out Chinatown because "it's so cheap and they do a great job."  

As it turns out, the hair cut was indeed cheap.  But the few times that I went (yes, I gave them the benefit of the doubt the first and second times), my hair looked as if it had been cut by someone who'd been blindfolded and used dull hedge trimmers.  If someone held a gun to my head and told me to return for another haircut, I would gladly ask him to just pull the trigger.

i had such a wonderful dinner at jax! it was before things started getting toasty in t-town, so we got to sit on the patio and enjoy the sunset. we started off with a coctail (a margarita, im forgetting the name, but man was it tasty) seasonal melon salad and it was awesome! the flavors all went together so nicely. we then shared the kobe burger, which was AWESOME, and the hangar steak (my personal favorite). After one bite of the steak i no longer wanted to share it.. but that wouldn't have been nice so i did anyways. good thing too, because the burger was also delicious! the service was top notch, and we couldn't have been more pleased.

The three stars are based soley upon their chinese bbq chicken salad.  (Reeally good.  So good, in fact, that I'd risk having the snootiest service EVER just to eat it.)  This place is located in Plaza Frontenac, snootiest of snooty's when it comes to malls.  Watch out for 16-year olds having really glamorous birthday parties, and also people who think they own everything including you.  If you need to impress someone at lunch, I guess take them here.

**Note: Cardwell's original location is in Clayton, and it is still there, and has a more casual bar area where you can enjoy the chinese bbq chicken salad without snooty people.

Perhaps we would have enjoyed this restaurant if it had not been our last dinner in New Orleans - after days of heavy indulgences. Additionally, coming from San Francisco, we were not really looking for a California twist on the cuisine. Compared to the other meals we had had, no one was very excited by the menu.

The waitstaff was very friendly and accommodating to our large group, although the drink service was pretty slow. We enjoyed all of our appetizers, but I would really strongly advise against getting the duck confit main course. Everyone found the duck to be far, far too salty. I should have paid more attention to Marcy S.'s review!

I'm enamored by the fact that La Viola has restaurants on BOTH sides of the street. I mean that shows how legit the value of this place. I definitely thought that the service was top notch. The waiter was very knowledgeable and was attentive. However, they are like a little bit of a factory.... they won't change the dish really other than what is on the menu.

The food is good, but not life changing.

This is an excellent BYO, not the best -- certainly far from the worst.

I will definitely be back.... I mean they have open table .... Hello OT points??

Harry's is one of my favorite watering holes.  I love this place not for the food, which is mediocre, but for the fond memories.  Harry's is a great place to go in the summer after a softball game.  There is a rather large patio out back to sit on with an outdoor bar that is occasionally staffed.  

Harry's also has Karaoke.  If you are a fan of the karaoke, I would call first to see which day it is offered as it has changed a few times.  MK the emcee is always happy to oblige with a song if the bar isn't willing to participate.  

So let's recap this bar is great for a drink post softball or kickball, not so great for the food.

We were brought here by my sister the first time we visited her in Philly.  La Baia is definitely yummy, with generous portions of traditional Italian fare. I am a fan of BYOB, but the cash-only policy is a little frustrating (my husband had to walk down a shady side street to grab a wad of cash from an ATM after we were done eating). The restaurant is cramped, so if noisy isn't your thing this might not be the place for you. But if you can get past the screaming kiddies or go later in the evening, I could definitely see this being a cute date spot. A solid 3 stars.

I'm always on the lookout for a better sushi spot, but when it's all said and done I always come back. Try as I might to find a new sushi restaurant, I never find anything quite good enough to dethrone Shiroi Hana.

It's not that there's anything wrong with this place - the fish is always fresh, the miso is delicious, the udon's warm and inviting. The place is consistently good, but I guess I'm just searching for greatness. I don't even know what I'm looking for in particular. I always leave satisfied, but wanting something more.

We liked this place. Went to the library in the American Can building (Where some dude was checking out porn in plain view of everyone).

We checked out their booze selection (A little higher than Rouses but a good selection) and then the beers. We ended up doing a mix and match beer 6-pack they were selling for 6 bucks. While I didn't love all the beers we selected,  I loved the ability to pick and choose different kinds to try. 
The staff was great and were very willing to answer any questions we had. They weren't overly-clingy and let us do our thing. 
All in all, a really great experience.and we look forward to going back.

It's 24 hour fast food next to downtown...

The place was remodeled a few years ago & usually pretty clean.  The employees usually get the food & change right.  There is no wonder the the place is always busy.

Yes, sometimes bums are in the parking lot or in the restaurant.  However, for the general idea of "the show must go on" is accepted here.

Could it be better? Yes.  I could also eat healthier & spends more $.

Side-note is the cool create a flavor Coca-Cola machine.  Why they put it in this location is beyond me.

Midnight to 5 AM... I am usually impressed by the workers patience & attitude being 24 hour 7 day a week drive-thru & dine-in establishment.

Constant business with people in the drive-thru is one thing, but add weird people coming inside to use Wi-Fi, get out of the weather or just relax for a minute in the middle of the night has to be stressful.

It is still a McDonalds- so the food isn't completely healthy or tasty, but it is cheap & fast.  Being available in the middle of the night when most places are not makes me grateful.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Free bowling in the basement of this old shotgun neighborhood bar was the draw for a birthday party. The lanes are small and we had to get someone to set up the pins, but FREE & silly fun. I had to order the drinks upstairs because there was no bartender downstairs. 

The place is a small friendly dive. I had fun seeing some locals have a good time with cheap booze & entertainment on this Friday night. 

The draft selection is small, but they had more than standard bottle selection of beer. (plus they had Grand Ma) 

Corner Bar & Grill is a definite destination for enjoyable evening on the while on a budget in St Chuck.

Sushi was OK but service was oddly passive-aggressive.  Wasn't impressed and wouldn't go out of my way to go there.  It could improve itself simply by having a profound change in the way they treat customers.  I changed my order and I could tell she was pissed, I asked for salad instead of soup not excited.  The place was empty you'd think they'd want to offer all they could to a future prospect regular.  .  Anyway, way better somewhere I'm sure.  If your desperate for Sushi and don't care about service this might just be your place!

It's a nothing spectacular place that some how gets 4 stars.  I've lived in Seattle where there was some sushi places that deserved 5 stars, so based on that baseline, I give it 4.  BUT, this place is definitely worth going to.

The people are friendly.  Even at closing time they didn't make you feel rushed to leave, and they were very welcoming to another couple that came in just before they closed.  The chef was very friendly and struck up conversation with you.  The sushi was of good size.  Rolls were fairly priced.  There's nothing bad to say about the place.

I've been here a few times now and this is a good place to stop in and have a beer in the afternoon / evening. You can sit by the window and do some people watching or have dinner with the family or a date. The bar gets pretty lively around 5:30pm. They also have a very large dining room separated from the bar area.

Drinks can get a little expensive so if you're on a budget make sure you know the prices of those mixed drinks, and even the pints of beer like Sam Adams before you go on a bender. You might find a $90 tab in your hands when you're finished.

The Eye Bar does a great job of bringing unique European lines to St. Louis.   They have the best selection of eyewear in St. Louis, hands down.

While I have never gotten glasses at The Eye Bar (I have family in the optical industry), I have stopped in to look a few times.  They are always nice and never pushy.  

This weekend we stopped in after my boyfriend's sunglasses lost a screw.  They were not purchased at The Eye Bar, but they very happily replaced the screw.  We really appreciated their fantastic customer service.

If you're looking for new glasses, The Eye Bar is definitely the best spot in St. Louis.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
After reading all these BAD (and sketch) reviews of dry cleaners in the area, I decided to take my chance and trust this place. To my utter amazement, I loved it!

I had to dry clean a down vest and the Asian lady was super nice and fast in helping me fill out the form and stuff. When I came back, the cute little Chinese man helped me retrieve it and was very sweet.

There were people using the coin-op machines too and the lady was helping the people fold their own clothes (I assume...?) so it was nice :]

Needless to say, my vest was beautiful, clean and UNRUINED!!! I'm coming here again. Oh and it was super cheap, less than $5!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: This place rocks, went here for breakfast on the first stop on our bus tour.  The boomtown folks gave us all $5 cash and a restaurant coupon so breakfast was next to nothing.  I had the chicken fried steak and eggs with rye toast.  I'm on a rye kick right now and this was the best marble rye ever, thick and buttery, yum!  My partner in crime had the french toast which was a huge portion and perfectly made, yummy.  The coffee was good as was the service.  Our waitress was attentive and quick and for serving many drunk peeps she did her job just right!  Oh don't miss out on the country potatoes, so good!

The presentation was good.  The service was good. The spicy tuna roll was good, however why are they so skimpy on the fish????  My rolls had a lot of filler in it.  There was more rice, veggies and cream cheese than fish.   Be prepared to pay for parking because there is no free parking around.  Not that parking is expensive at all as it is very cheap, but just annoying. Imitation crab sucks.  This may be a good place for a new sushi person wanting to try it, but not for someone use to good sushi. If they prided an actual bite of fish and didnt use imitation crab I would go back to this place and give it more stars.

I had to pick a place to stay for one night so I can catch an early flight and I probably will not stay here again.  There are many other places to choose from.  I did not feel my room was clean.  I also did not feel safe as a female staying at the property alone.  There are no restaurant at the property or anything within walking distant.  I had to drive and look for food and everytime I walk in/out of the hospital, there is always someone out there smoking.  Also as of March 2012 they have a major construction going on and that might have made me feeling a little negative about the place.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This place has a really cool set-up!  I first noticed it as I was on the way to yoga in an adjacent shop.  They've got indoor seating in addition to this really neat outdoor space with tables and twinkle lights and an outdoor fire.  I love the music playing and the feeling of actually being at an Italian cafe.  I've enjoyed the food each time I visited, once trying one of the wood-fired pizzas, and another time a calzone, both of which were pretty tasty.  The service has always been really excellent and I really love the authentic feel.

I can't believe that I haven't written a review about this place yet.  It used to be my go-go place for cheap margaritas and Mexican food, with 2-for-1 margaritas Sunday-Thursday evenings!  I was thwarted on my most recent experience there when we went with a large group for a birthday on a Thursday.  THEY CHANGED THEIR HAPPY HOURS so that Thursday is no longer 2-for-1.  I was incredibly upset and disappointed.  The bevvies was the main draw of this place...if I just wanted the Mexican food, I'd probably go to my favorite taco cart on Nolensville.

Hip Hip Hooray! A Mexican restaurant literally two minutes from my house! I love my authentic Mexican food, and I've never lived so close to a Mexican restaurant. So thankfully, ever since El Sombrero has opened it's doors in the McKay's Mill subdivision, I've been very pleased. Nice and clean on the inside, good service, and the food has been great. Salsa above average but not my favorite.

Pancho's Place still is my favorite Mexican in Franklin, but El Sombrero is still a solid choice and we'll be regulars there due to convenience.

Stayed here on my honeymoon in New Orleans. This location is the best of both worlds, just 2 blocks over to the French Quarter, but you don't pay those very expensive French Quarter prices. They gave us a free room upgrade when they heard we were on honeymoon. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The rooms also had umbrellas, robes, an iron, and lots of extra useful things in the suite for their guests. We spent most of our days walking all over the city and this was a nice place to come back and unwind too with street noise at a minimum. I would stay at this hotel again and really enjoyed the week I spent there.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Parisian bistro is dark with a semi-romantic feel.  Went with a group of 5 and shared in the raw bar assortment of oysters and littleneck clams.  Go for the west coast oysters... they're tasty!   had a bit of escargot, which was uber buttery but i can say that Le Bec's escargot tops the charts.  They have a good selection of seafood entrees.  The sea bass was MASSIVE. i swear they injected something in there to fluff it up because it was thick, but light served over a bed of greens.  Could have used a touch more seasoning, but the salt and pepper was nowhere to be found on the table. Nice ambience, and the food was okay.

Great place to stop on Bourbon St.  cheap drinks, not loud music like every club/bar on Bourbon St, and the people who work there are very friendly.  My friend and I stopped here on our first night in New Orleans and learned so much about the city in just a half hour.  The only downside is like every other bar on Bourbon St. anything other than Miller Light, Coors Light, or Bud Light is hard to fine.  This place at least at Abita, the local beer.

A tip I learned from a local, have them add an extra shot or two in the daiquiris - helps downplay the sweetness

Why did I not check the yelp reviews before going here? UGH. The prices are outrageously expensive, especially for alterations. The business is difficult to access in either direction as it is located at the very busy corner of MacDill and Bay to Bay so leaving the business, you basically can only get out in one direction as there is so much traffic / so many cars stopped at the light blocking the access to the driveway. Beware of discounts not being applied correctly as the cashier does not have the ability to correct the check once it has been invoiced so it is a major hassle to wait to get it corrected. Will never return!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Probably the best distributor I've been to in this city.  Prices are reasonable, you can order cases in many instances, and Paul and his staff are extremely knowledgeable and friendly.  

Plus, you can't beat their Saturday tastings.  It's an automatic party and after going to them sporadically for a few years, my husband and I are on a first name basis with most of the folks there.

Bonus here that I've never seen anywhere else--the craft brewing take a brew leave a brew program.  Since we're bound to buying full cases, an honor-system trading spot where you can try a bottle of something someone else found good enough to buy is really great.

it's a standard, classic pub. the atmosphere has a grimy charm and it smells like old frier grease. you feel like you're in your uncle's basement bar. it's a good low-key hangout for a beer if you don't expect it to be fancy-pants. my most recent trip here we just got wings (surprisingly good) and a heaping plate of onion rings. the onion rings are served with a horseradish sauce which is pretty tasty. i'd stick to beers and apps but i'm sure you can't go wrong with a burger or other sandwich.

and FYI, for those of you who don't know, you can't really go out hard in the village. there is a no shots and no doubles policy at every bar.

in summer, this place is packed. if you can find a spot on the deck amid tourists with wandering children and the errant duck (yes. duck), i think it's really worth it. the mojitos here are really good. 

i recently went here on a cold, rainy night in november with my parents and husband. the bar was full of presumably regulars, so we asked for a table. we were treated with the best seat in the house, in front of the large fireplace. it was lovely. we just got a couple beers and wings, but the service was pretty good. 3 stars since i can't really rate the food. will update upon meal intake. either way, definitely a nice place for a drink.

Decent Courtyard. The room was clean, and the wifi was pretty solid. Seeing as this is in St. Louis, I spent more time eating BBQ than I did at the gym, so can't tell you much about the fitness center. Plenty of parking located around the hotel.

I didn't have any problems here. It does get a little dry if you have the heater on constantly, so I wish the thermostat would be a bit more sensitive so it wouldn't run 24/7. It also wouldn't hurt if they had a real bar, but the bistro counter will suffice for most needs.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This is the French Quarter shithole "locals" bar. If you want to get to know the people that live there this is one of the places to go. The interior isn't fancy and is really quite dingy but for some reason it has it's charm. Actually it's flat out dirty as shit and the bathrooms are absolutely piss nasty. Right around the corner on Decatur from One Eyed Jack's and The Dungeon. Don't go in this place unless you want to leave smelling like stinky cigarettes because it's a giant smoke pit in there, and you can handle being in a smoke filled room with metal heads and tattooed people sitting at the bar. In other words my kinda place!

I have never had a problem with the food here.  I find it to be very tasty as far as Chinese take-out goes, and they also serve very generous portions for the price.  The speedy and free delivery is the best thing about Fusion, though--good delivery is pretty rare in Reno.  If you really want to enjoy their food, I recommend you avoid the shop itself.  Although the people are super nice, it is a pretty run-down place, and certainly not somewhere that you want to eat in.  Walking in there can really color one's opinion of the food.  Just let them deliver it to you and be happy!

So the washer's on the fritz, which means Family and I have had to haul all our crap to the laundromat...ugh.

But, if anything can make doing laundry away from home bearable, it's a bar INSIDE the laundromat.  Yep, order up a Bud and play a few rounds of pool while your clothes clean.  Brilliant.

Everything here is always clean and well maintained, and the staff are very friendly.  We've never had a problem finding open machines, either.  Every regular load of laundry is $2.75, and the dryers are 25 cents for 25 minutes.  Kind of pricey, but worth it for the big-screen TV and video games.  And did I mention the beer?
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Really, this is as good as it gets when it comes to frozen yogurt.  By far the best non-fat tastes I've ever had. I would go multiple times each week, if it weren't so expensive.  The only negative is the price.  You pay by oz, and with unlimited choice of toppings, it can add up!  

But hey, you might spend $3-$4 at Starbucks every day... ?  It's worth it and I highly recommend this place!

I take all of my out-of-town friends here and they enjoy it as well!  

Tip: They have all natural yogurt for dogs as well!

Thought it would be fun to have a couple of slices while my son was here for a football party. Unfortunately ordering was impossible, I was asked to leave a table because I didn't have food.. see above problem. Finally asked for a manager and think I might be getting food but not counting on it.

Rude wait staff that was not interested in helping because they were busy. Hope the pie is great because the service is horrible.

Edit ... the manager finally got a pizza ordered and the sauce was awesome!! Added a star for quality...take out or delivery might be worth it.

Martha Hoover is one of my Indy heroes.  She's really made her mark on this city.

It seems like Gelo has been a long time coming (they were supposed to open last summer but only opened in Oct), but it completely lived up to my expectations.

This is a gelato shop for grown-ups.  Elegant, Roman, white marble decor.  Nicely curated menu.  Treats that aren't cloyingly sweet.  Serving sizes that will satisfy without giving you a coronary.

Here's my first-world problem: so far whenever we've stopped at Gelo, it's been completely impossible to resist going into Napolese first.

I'm not into frozen yogurt.  I like ice cream, the real deal.
And I'm not that into football (give me time, I only just arrived in Indy).
And I don't love strip malls.

So you'd think that a football-themed frozen yogurt store in a strip mall wouldn't be my kind of place.

However.  Huddles is at the end of a strip mall that is adjacent to the Monon Trail, and has a nice patio for sitting outside.  And it's cutesiness completely works for 86th Street.  Great for families (of which there were a ton last night).  And their frozen yogurt comes in cupcake flavors like Red Velvet.

The price is kind of high here. I ordered takeout:an inari (filler), egg sush (tamago) cause I love it, and a white jade roll.

The inari was basic, good I guess? I was really disappointed with the egg. It's usually one of my favorites. If I see the egg at japanese supermarkets, I'll buy a rectagular cube of it. I think it just wasn't sweet enough... 

The white jade was good. I forget what was exactly in it, but it was some type of white fish on the outside and then maybe salmon on the inside. This roll was good, but for $20, I was still kind of hungry.

One of the many popular Broad Ripple Avenue bars, the Mineshaft carries most of its notoriety for its Thursday pint night, where hundreds of Ripple-ites gather to slam multiple pints, run into friends and cousins, do shots with those people, and then attempt to get up for a reasonably productive Friday. 

This cozy little spot is your basic, no-frills 'drinking bar.' The place gets pretty lively on the weekends, especially Thursday nights.  Located right along the strip in Broad Ripple, it makes for an easy stop along the bar crawl route, or if nothing else, a great crowd of locals on weekend nights.

I'm usually a fan of Hertz and I still am, it's just that the Metairie branch was not a great experience.  I could understand if they were busy or were short staffed, but neither was the case. It took me over an hour to pick up a car that was already reserved for me, and I called ahead to see when it would be ready and was told at 9am that it was ready. I got there at 1:30pm and I didn't drive off until 3:00pm!!!!

They did give me a voucher for a free rental because of my troubles and for the long wait so that was good.

Delicious! We went to Criniti for my friend's birthday dinner, and we all loved it! The complimentary mushrooms they gave us at the beginning of the meal were amazing. A warning, though--you will want more, and it costs 7 or 8 bucks for another order of mushrooms. Every part of the meal was yummy. I had the chicken parm and it was the best ever! Thin and tender with lots of sauce! We were all very pleased with the experience at Criniti.
One more thing: Good luck finding parking around the restaurant! We lucked out and got a spot right across the street, but South Philly parking is not usually that easy!!

We got takeout from Ahi for the first time recently. I ordered a bunch of different half-price sushis and a raw tuna-avocado salad. First of all, when the delivery man arrived at my door, he was holding two beautifully-arranged catering-style platters of colorful food. I was so impressed by the display. The sushi ended up being very good and so worth 3-5 bucks for each 8-piece sushi. Unfortunately, the salad, which was much more expensive, wasn't as good as it looked. The greens were all arugula which I find very bitter, and the fish tasted bitter too. I didn't like it. But I would order sushi from Ahi again!

We were hunting lunch at International Plaza and Bay Street.  There were lots of options, but I was lured in with a sample of their bam-bam shrimp.

I ordered the bam-bam shrimp and a cup of the blue crab and corn chowder. My fiance had the Caribbean chicken.  The food was good; my chowder was very rich and I was glad I went for the cup rather than the bowl.  

We really enjoyed the the ambiance and decor was nice.  We were sat in this cute booth that made it feel much more quiet and intimate than most restaurants.

Had to get my car washed! Gentle touch car wash offers package deals that you can use at any gentle touch car wash. I usually go to the one in Malvern that was close to my old office. 

This was an okay car wash. You get to sit in your car while it goes thru the wash. I haven't done that in ages. The finish product was just average. My car wash deal included vacuuming and there was still crumbs in my center console. The back of of my car was still dirty, which is usually never the case. I always check my car after a wash and missed checking the back, because that's usually not a concern.

I am a big fan.  If you find yourself a couple hours early before your flight, head upstairs to jet rock. This is before going through security. I sat down at a booth and had a great breakfast burrito and potatoes for $6.  Most of the food is your standard American fare - sandwiches, burgers, fries, salads, and brews.

Jet Rock is an excellent place to go to relax, get away from the packed crowds at the terminals (germs!), and go to the adjacent clean restroom before going through security.  There are a bunch of booths available.

The only reason I gave them a two star, not one, is because I respect their selection of beer, especially for such a small place. 

That being said, the prices are freakin' ridiculous!!! I mean I get it, we're in yuppie Newtown PA, but Jesus H. Christ!!! You're going to pay at least $4 more here for a case of anything. Even cheap crappy beer. Some of the price differences for craft beer range from $10 - $15 more per case.

It's a bummer because my friends and  I would buy there all the time if the prices were better.

Came here after a haircut at Montecito barbers. Haley Jo took make at the bar and made it a soul-refreshing dinner. Goat cheese salad had crisp fresh ingredients. Lady next to me smiled like "oh look at the piggy eat, so cute". Then my pistachio pizza arrived and I thought, shit... I might have over-ordered. but the taste truly made one believe in a higher power. After crushing that and a hand wash and cold water on my face. Why not the well-placed chocolate cake in the line of sight of all food being cooked. It was so rich I had to order coffee to unglue my mouth. All and all, DELICIOUS dinner after a very productive day.

Three and a HALF stars. 
Listen, this is one of those places that people don't think to write reviews for UNLESS you've had a bad experience. And I have not had a bad experience here. The woman who works the front computer there is SO NICE!!! And very open to if you need something cleaned quickly. I wouldn't drive out of my way to get my clothes dry cleaned here but if you live in the neighborhood there's absolutely nothing wrong with this joint. They have temporary parking right in front so you can park and run in if you need to. Sweet.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
$8.95 lunch special for two rolls (limited selection)/ bento box with miso soup and ginger salad. Not bad, I say. I had the tempura shrimp and crunchy spicy tuna. My friend had the crunchy spicy tuna and the crunchy spicy salmon. Decent sushi, quick service, unbeatable price.
I've read reviews about the service being subpar, but I don't see it. During my lunch session, they offered the mailman a glass of water to go and asked a lady fi she wanted another sweet tea to go.
I'd like to return for Happy Hour (5-7pm) for discounted sushi and beer!

I came in late on a Sunday afternoon riding bitch in a tow truck with my poor car on the truck bed due to a blown tire. They were having a buy 2, get 2 sale on tires. They had a few options of tires in stock for me to choose from. Within a couple hours, I had a brand new set of tires on my ride. They told me about how long it would take and even worked hard to finish by closing time.
I was able to get picked up to run some errands in the meantime, but their waiting room is clean with comfy chairs and a tv. The bathrooms are male and female separate and are surprisingly clean.
I am very satisfied with the level of service I was provided.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
My girl took it upon herself to color her own hair after decided she wanted to be blond. bad idea.
Shes very thrifty and didn't want to spend the money to have a professional do her hair but after a few tries I took her to Regis at the international mall.
i dropped her off for a cut and color and picked her up an hour and a half later and she was beautiful as always. 
The cut was brilliant.The color was fantastic and the man that worked this magics name is Brian.
We cant thank you enough. She looks and feels amazing.
I truly recommend this salon.

Great atmosphere the outdoor dining area right on the water is cool, came here for lunch while traveling on business. I had a light lunch which was seared Ahi tuna with a cole slaw type salad. It was tasty and not to filling, it hit the spot. the people at the giant tiki bar seemed to be enjoying themselves, looks like a great local hang out spot. The service was good even though she had just started. The wildlife was nice to watch with the fish and the birds and the signs said manatee's. Next time I roll into  this part of town I will stop here for sure.

I really enjoyed this place.   The staff were all very friendly and the drinks I had (blood and sand and a martini) were delicious.  

It's not a place for the faint of liver, heart, or wallet though.  

I poached some of my friend's mussels.  I love mussels and these mussels were delicious.    Another friend of mine had a burger, and she's a burger expert.  She loved it.   I'll let her review it because I told her to join yelp. 

It's a very good place and it's so close to me so I'll be back again and again

I LOVE OSAKA.  The sushi is great.   They have a late night happy hours on weekends with cold food and drinks til 1.

On weekends it's a really good idea to get a reservation.  The crowd is your normal Chestnut Hill rich guilty liberal crowd, but at least that means that wait staff are happy because they're getting good tips.  Casual dress but not sweatshirt casual.  Jeans are ok.  

Sit at the bar (the liquor one--though the sushi bar's fun to sit at too) and be a guinea pig for the bartender's experiments.  Yummy

It's a State Store so it's grand!  This is like the super market of State Stores in Center City.  It's huge!  They have a crazy selection of wine and liquor.  It's also one of the special ones with Sunday hours! 

This is the State Store I go to when I forget to get something on Holidays and they always handle the CRUSH of people really well.  I remember being queued up all the way in the back of the store on New Year's Eve and being to the front of the queue in like 10 minutes when it seemed like I'd be there all day.

As a fatty, I appreciate the very chilled out vibe the morning and early afternoon crowds at 12th Street.    I've never been during rush hour but there are no "fitter than thou" attitudes from the other members or more importantly, the staff and personal trainers.  

It is confusing as hell to move around in (in fact I've already figured a lot of it out) but that doesn't bother me as much as how HOT IT GETS because it's an old building with no central air .

Still, I was a member of Sweat and I really like this place a lot better.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I was running some errands in town and I had to wait for another shop to open so I went in here to grab somat to eat.    I don't know how to review a ham egg and cheese sandwich except to say that shit didn't kill me so it was cool.

It's a counter with about 10 seats and you sit and wait for your food and chow down.    They do a lot of take out and delivery for the businesses but it seems like the crowd inside were all Philly locals/natives. 

I did enjoy sitting on the counter with locals and watching people with fancy jobs come in and leave straight away.

The old Poly Esters 70s dance club for locals who need to put location in perspective.  

While this place does have a pretty rocking hotel bar (http://www.yelp.com/biz/chase-lounge-the-sheraton-four-points-center-city-philadelphia).  It faces the same issues as many Chinatown hotels.  The two main ones being their proximity to massage parlors and homeless shelters. 

It is bright and clean and the lobby smells gorgeous.  It would be my choice for a hotel out of the 3 on the same block between 12th and 13th on Race.  

Until March 31 2009, they're having a grand opening special 90 dollars a night too.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Bit of a mixed bag here.  The first time I ever went it took us like 90 minutes to get our lunch.  This was a work lunch so it was a bit annoying as we were in a time crunch.  I've since been back there and it's not been that bad but first impressions mean a lot.

The food is ok.  I like this ham sandwich on a pretzel roll thing. It's kinda greasy hit the spot goodness. 

I did have a waiter when I asked for sparkling water said he didn't have any but then gave someone at the next table club soda.  I guess I should have been more clear, or he less of an idiot.  

It's a sports bar though, so I'm not sure if I should have expected more.

I'm obviously not here enough, b/c I don't know who this hot barista is that the girls are buzzing about in these reviews. 
The Orange Couch is the kind of spot I've been craving. Living in an old city that thrives on being casual and eccentric, there are not a whole lot of spots that cater to modern design. 
I remember driving by this place and i nearly drove my car into the ditch, I was so surprised. They hadn't opened yet, so I wasn't able to go in at that time. 
By the time I was able to find it again (this is very much not in my 'hood) I was extremely excited about it. Quiet. Minimalist. Clean. Modern. Mochi.

This is a typical Korean owned Japanese restaurant.. the food is ok - I mean when sushi is in 'rolls' and it is plastered with sauces I can't ever tell the difference. My second time I tried their Katsu Don and it was pretty tasty rice. But if you've noticed ANYONE OUTSIDE OF INDIANA thinks this sushi sucks... it may be the 'best' in Indy..but it certainly isn't the best sushi and way overpriced. 

Nice wait staff - a little slow (edit**I went back a second time and it wasn't nearly as packed as the first time and my friend who ordered 3 simple rolls waited over an hour!!!). 

Overall = not bad but not near to great.

i like this place a lot. their new location is worlds nicer than the old spot on seventh! i remember going there many nights before hitting the clubs, always a good way to start the night.  this is one of my preferred sushi spots in nashville, the value is second to none! my only beef is the maki seems to be rolled a little carelessly/messy (but that's what i get for ordering maki, right? lol) and both times i've been since they moved in the new spot, they haven't had toro. but aside from that, i can't diss this place at all!

eric b

Boring. 

I had dinner here when I was visiting Philly because my boyfriend had been here during his last visit and raved about it, but I thought this place was forgettable and after this visit he said he wouldn't be back either. 

The bread was cold and tasted stale. The Caesar salad was drowning in dressing. I will give them an extra star because my meal came with so many mussels. They certainly did not skimp on that. But service was slow and the place is cramped. My servers butt shouldn't practically be on my table when he turns to help the table next to us.

I try to like this place but it's just not very welcoming unless you know the people already there,  I like it when I can go into a dive bar and strike up a conversation with a random person and have a great evening. When you walk in here people act like you are a stranger walking into a house without knocking on the door...
I've made 4 attempts and the only time it was enjoyable was when I was with the "mayor" of the place. Food is typical good bar food and drinks are affordable. I just can't get past the lack of warmth.

I've said this in my other reviews of sushi places, but places like morimoto should get 5 stars, not places that serve frozen fish that are basically tasteless.  This place is fine for a quick fix though and they're BYO.  I've gotten take out from here as well because the 3 rolls (24 pieces) for $11.95 is a great deal.  The place is tiny so you've got to get there early to get a seat.  It's basically just seating at the sushi bar and it's always packed.  Like many other sushi places in the city, this place is not Japanese-owned.  I have to use a lot more soy sauce and wasabi than I normally do to get some flavor at this place.

This place is like Mizu and Vic but I have to give it a low rating because it's in a bad location and they don't deliver.  The sushi really isn't all that great but it will do if you've got the craving for sushi.  I would never get sashimi at a place like this, usually just rolls are what I'll order.  The soft shell crab was ok, the spicy tuna ok...you see the pattern here.  They give you a side salad and it's mostly just iceberg lettuce--the salad dressing is yummy (it's the usual tangy Japanese salad dressing).  University City doesn't have as many options as Center City so I'm guessing that's why this place stays in business.

I stopped by Ichiban while on a road trip. I wish I went elsewhere. While the food, service, and atmosphere were ok, I was not too impressed. The waitresses talked loudly in the background, the TVs were pointed to FOX news, the food was not too terribly exciting. I had a vegetable roll as the appetizer and a noodle soup for my main course. The sushi was ok, while the soup was nothing but a microwaved water with some veggies in it. I am not too familiar with the downtown scene in Nashville, but I am sure that there is better food to be found.

Great atmosphere.

I walked in without reservations on a Saturday night, and the host "rings/ buzzes" upstairs to the upstairs host.  He tries to get him -or anyone- on 8 different channels, in the process using the most stereotypically mobster names you can think of. It was great. He tells us to go upstairs and ask for Gino/Mario/whomever.  We do and we ask for him, he then calls BACK downstairs to make sure we're approved.  

It was great, but I don't remember the food.

I will be back though, just because the atmosphere was so out of this century.

Being too empowered a woman (and generally lazy) to launder and iron my partner's shirts, I take them to Felix.  I've tried numerous other cleaners, but this one is the closest place that doesn't charge an arm and a leg.  They're nothing special, but they're in the neighborhood.  Despite having a plant on premises, they are ridiculously slow with the turn around time (e.g. turn in Friday morning, get back TUESDAY night--aak!).  If they get their act together and get the in by 10am, out by 5pm that day (or even in by 10am, out by 5pm NEXT day), I'll give them the last 2 stars.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
I'm not sure where all the hello kitty stuff came from, it must've been a promotional thing because there wasn't one hello kitty thing in this place.  

It is very clean and they have some flavors i haven't had like "Red Velvet Cupcake Batter' it was rich and delicious.
