For froyo this is not my favorite, from the reviews we were excited about this place for the month we heard about it and drove the 50 minutes to get here.  I think i will stick to the metro east froyo.  Based on Froyo...the actual Froyo and Red Mango chains are much better, however, you won't get a frog spoon there!

It is worth trying out but not as a regular spot.

We stopped here for breakfast after being rebuffed at Jackson's.  Jackson's needs to get a lesson in customer service from these guys. 

The breakfast buffet is small, but very high quality.  The cheese blitzes where awesome. They will cook eggs and omelets to go.  The fruit jam is in some nice crystal containers and not the cheapie little disposable containers most other restaurants use. They have beautiful muffins and bagels.   And the price ($17) included coffee or juice (our our preferred diet cokes). 

The food was good, the service was great, and the price was not outrageous.  I'm a fan.

Was passing thru Dunedin and of course my daily pizza craving came upon me.  Did a quick yelp check and Tonys on Main had some good ratings so I ventured over there. However parking was non existent so I decided to just try this place instead. 
Despite the lower Yelp ratings this place makes good pizza. One of the advantages here is he does not allow the pizza to sit on the counter with the Moozzaell. He adds a generous portion of creamy Mozza then bakes it in the oven. The verdict was 2 good slices of pizza with fountain drink for $5!

Friendly bartenders!! I'm SO thankful for this!! I used to frequent bars and I never understood why people thought rude bartenders gave an establishment character. Even after we accidentally broke a shot glass the bartenders were friendly, attentive, even offered our large group a table (probably because we couldn't help party block the door.) The draft list is huge. If you don't know what you like they offer suggestions or a taste, pretty standard stuff, but it's not service you find everywhere. Always appreciated! Great spot, the neighborhood is lucky to have Fountain Porter.

Not bad to stop to pick stuff up on the way home, but I can't say this is MY grocery store.  Prices are reasonable for the city but the selection just isn't up to par.  The same goes for the produce, but the produce sold out of the back of trucks on 44th are a better deal.

No selection of fresh bread or sea food and poor selection of meat.  In the past I've called the store to find out if they had ground pork in stock.  They said yes on the phone and no once I got there.

Also, apparently the store hates fat people.  The entrance has poles every two and a half feet-ish keeping shopping carts near the door.

Go to Total Wine across the street, don't go here. We were buying hundreds of dollars of liquor for our wedding and asked about the return policy and was told they only give store credit. It would have been nice to know that before we got to the register. Why would anyone overbuy for an event just to have multiple non-returnable bottles left over?

No discount for bulk, nobody to help us if we needed it like the other Yelper mentioned.

Total Wine has nearly the same prices and gives you cash/credit back for your unopened returns. At Total Wine you can even return opened cases of beer if the bottles are untouched.

Checker's is one of those places that's just hard to find in Brandon, but Tampa people are lucky to have all over. If I'm on 60 driving somewhere or with a friend nearby, I usually can't help but stop by and have a juicy burger with some of their amazingly well seasoned fries. Their fries have always been my favorite, and I love them even more now that they are hard to come by. Sometimes eating outside can be a pain there, but if you want your food to be really hot, you may just have to do it, or eat in your car.

This Starbucks located in the Winthrop plaza has a very nice design to it. The workers inside are always friendly after I come and always quick to fill orders and make them just right. It's located close to Publix and some restaurants so it's a nice place to stop by after visiting these places. There are plenty of chairs outside for those winter months when you want to have some hot coffee and read a good book outside. Inside, the couches are extremely comfortable and people always seem to be on their laptops looking all cool and productive.

So I came here one night before the drive home from USF and was really hungry so I stopped at this McDonald's and ordered some food. The order went through and when I got to the window they had my food ready they passed it to me and then I handed them my debit card and they THEN told me that it was cash only...with the food already in my hands, I could already smell my meal and was ready to eat it. The lady asked for the food back and I handed it back to her pissed and still hungry. While I was in line before I saw someone angrily speed off and I imagine it was for the same reason.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: I think one of Philadelphia's restaurant industry's strong points is that there are plenty of BYOB's. I think La Viola is one of the better ones. The service is quick and friendly; the kitchen is accomodating and the value is close to unbeatable. I had the artichoke soup (wish I was eating it right now) and the Fish of the day which was a simple dorado fillet with black olives and tomato. It was a bit on the mild side but I think my taste buds are fading due to the abuse they receive. The place is cramped but what do you expect at a BYOB? It's also a great way to meet the people sitting next to you.

I was definitely not a fan of this place. However, I was on a date and the guy was really excited about it...Trying not to judge him for it.

I ordered kung pao shrimp, he ordered mongolian chicken. We got wontons and hot and sour soup. I really thought you couldn't mess up hot and sour soup. but you can...and they did. Yuck.

The shrimp was well cooked and he liked his mongolian chicken. However, everything was especially greasy--even for chinese food. 

While you can order from the buffet, if you order off the menu they'll cook it fresh for you. 

Just don't waste your time.

Sorry, not a fan of Oishi Sushi...

The rolls are worse than the pre-made rolls at Trader Joe's. California roll was the worst I have had. Bleh. The only decent roll I tried was the shrimp tempura. Side salad and miso soup were good, but who comes to a sushi place to order those?

The service was quick but unfriendly. I felt rushed since it was the busy lunch rush. 

Nothing special here at Oishi. If you want to try it I advise you not to try anything with their crab meat. Sorry Oishi, your name is cool, but your sushi drools.

In the way of this is no surprise, yesterday the Bella Aquila owners posted  notice on their FB page that they will be closing the permanently on December 4, 2021.  Food and service hit and miss and very much a miss since Amy and Chad took over from the founding parents.  Primo location on the river in Eagle.  I hope this space becomes home to a locally owned, chef driven, scratch kitchen restaurant and not another of the formula food chains where the focus is on bar sales not food that are increasing on this side of town.

One of the original few places I frequented when I first began eating sushi years ago... yum yum. & look at me now, I'm obsessed!!

Prices? Cheap! Quality? Great!
Fresh and good cuts of fish are served.

Decor? Well that could use some work
... we can't all be perfect though, 
& I'll take tacky cheap decor as long as the food is delish as it is.

Although I have an unagi obsession the salmon and tuna are my favorites here. And the miso soup is some of the best I've tried.


Fun fact?- This place is named after Tom (the owner's) daughter. Cute.

The oddest crowds frequent here- from bikers to half my high school during the holidays. On any given day you will find both, plus a few freaks here and there. 

Bartenders are attentive. The bar is a dirty, divey place. Girls dance on the bar, the place gets overly crowded. It smells like beer and vomit. 

...still remember the sixty something couple walking around in dominatrix outfits, complete with dog collars. Ewww. For this place, it's normal however. 

They do have pool tables, which isn't so bad on a off night where you can actually move around without being groped and not even know by who.

While I tend to patronize another independent coffee shop while I'm in Mt. Airy, I just so happened to be roaming around Chestnut Hill and had been meaning for quite a while to check out this shop.  I had reached my coffee quota for the day, so I got a plain butter croissant and sat down to enjoy it since I had some time to spare.  The environment is comfortable, calm, and features an upstairs seating area should the lower level get crowded.  I can imagine this would be a great place for Chestnut Hill College students to study or for there to be live music!

I ate here with my dad and a friend before seeing Will Hoge in June 2006 at World Cafe Live.  From what I can remember, I just ordered the basic salmon and tuna rolls, but the fish was fresh and the sushi was decent.  Seeing that it was a Wednesday night that we were there, it was not crowded at all, but since it is located very close to World Cafe Live, I'm sure it gets a lot of traffic from concert-goers before and after shows.  In addition to the a-la-carte sushi, they also offer an all-you-can-eat sushi option as well as other traditional Japanese dishes.

Great food, great service, and a nice but not overly fancy setting.  Toscana 52 has a special thing that they do, and your waiter will take the time to explain this to those who are unfamiliar, that the 52 in their name means that there are 52 weeks in a year, and each week they feature a specialty menu from a different country or metropolitan area.  Their menu, staff, and restaurant layout all serve to meet the needs of anyone who may dine there including large parties and children.   I got the Norwegian Salmon with lemon olive-oil sauce--so good I left full!

While en route to see a friend perform at the Raven Lounge, I decided to pick up some sushi to go since said bar does not serve food.  The place itself is small, but the atmosphere is great for lunch or early dinner if you have time to sit down and eat there.  They also offer a special if you buy two or three rolls from the same list.  Their special rolls are great too--I had the American Dream roll (which had mango on the outside with spicy salmon, yellowtail, tuna, and tobiko (tiny fish roe)) and a regular shrimp tempura roll.  I will definitely come back again when I have time to eat in!

Imperial is second-rate at best in terms of its customer service, but when you're craving Chinese and don't have that much cash to spare, it works.  They do deliver, but require a minimum purchase of $10 for it to be free.  On that note, in bearable weather, I've gone by foot to pick up my food.  My biggest beef with this place is that I asked for and paid for a drink, but when I proceeded to dig into my food, the Snapple was nowhere to be found so I walked back to get it.  The woman at the counter seemed annoyed that I returned, but at least she believed me when I said I paid for my drink and didn't make me pay for another one.

The pizza here is good, but it's nothing that will wow you compared to some of the pizza I've had in other shops and in other parts of the world.  They do, however, offer more than just pizza, so I ordered a mushroom and swiss burger and fries over the phone so I could come pick it up.  The straw that gets this place only 3 stars instead of 4 or 5, is that when I arrived to pick up my order, my order didn't show up on the computer so there was a bit of confusion at the counter, but I grabbed an Israeli nectar to drink, and since those are so rare, I couldn't leave without one.  Wouldn't consider sitting in to eat here, but for pickup, it works.

It's hard not to love Publix in general, but this is easily the nicest Publix around. They have a sit-down deli, an amazing arrangement of fresh sushi, and their ethnic food section is huge!! Not to mention they have a parking garage for when the weather is less than desirable. 

I walked in today and every staff member smiled and said "hello" as they walked past or stocked the aisles. The sushi chef asked if I needed anything made to order. It was like walking into grocery heaven. 

If you don't thoroughly enjoy your shopping experience at this Publix, then you're just crazy.

How can anyone ever this place hungry? I left so full that it was almost painful!

The food here is spectacular! Everything that came out was amazing. Since I was here with a larger party, I was able to have a nice tasting of practically every dish on the menu. You really cannot go wrong with anything that comes out of that kitchen. Actually scratch that... the lobster was not extra supplemental dollars. It was good but I don't think it's worth the extra $18 or whatever it was.

Looking forward to my next return.

I made reservations for Upstaires but since their heating system broke, we were seated down in Sotto. -- Strike 1

Food was just mediocre, maybe less than mediocre-- scallop/shrimp cerviche was meh. lobster ravioli was way way way too salty. bread pudding dessert - tasty, but the smallest piece you could ever imagine. -- Strike 2

Umm.. soda does not come with free refills... wtf?! haha -- Strike 3 for sure!!!

The only pros -- wait staff was very nice, the view was pretty decent i guess on the first floor, and ummm... yea, nothing else.

We got a window seat on a summer day and it was great for people watching. The pizza we shared was enough for the both of us with maybe a slice left over. We got the mushroom and pepperoni. I had a big beer from the bar and my wife got a soda. All of this for under $20. Not bad for a quick lunch. Was very packed though and it seemed like they were just letting people in to stand around while others ate, which was kind of awkward. You have these families standing by your table talking and just waiting for you to finish.

Pros: Vegan and Vegetarian friendly, and the stuff they have that is veg is really good.

Cons: The veg stuff they have is so good, they often sell out of it. 

Come on guys, if you keep selling out of something, shouldn't that tell ya you should make more?  

Vegan French toast was really good.  Hopefully one day I'll get to taste the vegan pancakes . . .

12/2010

Well the same thing happened again.  They ran out of ingredients, or didn't have them on hand, and they had just opened.  I really want to love this place. . .

Had a flawless stay here during Hurricane Irma while power was out at my house.
The breakfast is awesome with great variety. I wished it lasted later than 930 however.
My room was clean and everything worked as it should. I had no issuws with any of the staff who seemed very courteous despite other negative reviews. 
I was able to get a room last minute and then stayed another night at a lower rate. I wish I had gotten to use the pool.
If you miss breakfast, there's a Starbucks within easy walking and several decent restaurants are nearby.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I had to come back three times to get my prescription right. That alone disqualifies this chain from further business.
They always feature a bogo deal on frames that seem to cost about $70-$90. But by the time you've added all the necessary things, you end up paying well over $300, or more.
The staff is hit or miss. Some seem to know what they're doing, and some most definitely do not, especially the younger ones.
The staff optometrist seems competent, if a bit lacking in the personality department.
It took well over a month to get my two pairs of reading and computer glasses done correctly.
I'm pretty sure you could do better elsewhere.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
I would have to say, this is an in and out store for me.  The selection is not the best, but not the worst.  What saves them is the prices are on point.  This store is not as stocked on wine like RED, Grapevine, or Frugal's, however I know I can go in, get a bottle on the way home and be on my way to relaxation central.

The service is always great here.  I always find the employees to be very helpful when I need advice on picking out wine.

I feel like the place shines with hard alcohol choices and they even have a small craft beer section for high ABV brews.

Great local coffee shop!

This has popped up since I left the city a few years ago and it's a great addition to Whyte!  I love finding non-chain shops and this is a great one to hang out and catch up with friends or get some work done.  Wi-Fi with a minimum purchase.  They do have computers on site as well that involve an additional fee.

Nice seating options from tables to comfy chairs and nice table spacing.  Great mix of cold and hot drinks and a nice selection of basic coffees... loved my hazelnut one at less than $2 a cup!

How can you go wrong with that?

I ordered Needle noodle with chicken and my friend ordered Beef with chinese vegetable. Needle noodle looked like white worms. EWWW but they were actually pretty good. LOL Chicken was seasoned very well and had bean sprout and scallion..  Also had salt baked squid as well, and I think i liked it the best outta three dishes. 

The service was good but the place was sooo cold. They didn't have turn on the heater until they saw us eating with jackets on and complaining. I hear their rice dishes are pretty good as their noodles so might go back again.

I don't get the big to-do about Ralph's. I went there expecting the most freaking delicious pasta I've ever had in my life and it tasted like dare I say, Olive Garden? (Okay, I know that's not fair, but I'm trying to emphasize how bland and flavorless the food was - get my drift?) It took FOREVER to get our food, but other than that, the service was pretty good.  I thought the prices were a little expensive too, at least for some of the dishes. It seems like Ralph's has gotten lazy because of their notoriety and history in Philadelphia.

I am loving Alamo more and more every time I rent from them.  They have the best discount codes all over the Internet... this time I picked up a car for 3 days for $80 including all taxes.  Checked in on my phone on the shuttle ride over, and then used the kiosk when I arrived to avoid any up-selling.  Went to get my car and they were out of compacts and mid-sizes, so I got a full-size for the same price.  Was stoked to get a Ford Fusion with less than 4k miles on it, complete with Sirius radio and some pretty fun features.  Had a blast driving it, and super easy time returning it.

This is a fun local bar on old Tampa Bay in Oldsmar. We have our company Christmas party here each year.  They have a real tiki bar outside!  Out back, I have even seen live alligators sitting on the sea wall! The food here is not to miss. They have a the best crab cake i have eaten.  Their blackened shrimp appetizer is very good.  The hot wings are also very good.  The bar-b-que flank steak is awesome!
The staff is always friendly and quick.  Oh yeah, they have good drinks too!  Lots of locals with big $$ cars hang out here!  Fun to watch that!

So I really want to like the new Rexy's.  It is a local landmark and place where the Flyers would hang out (years ago).

It has been renovated and has an inviting dining room and bar.

Not sure whether it wants to be local hang out by the beverage selection OR an upscale Italian eatery by the prices... both do not seem to work.

The food.  Generally it is OK and have given it a few chances but other than the pizza which is very good the entre's are just average.

I will go again but unfortunately not as a first choice.

I like the concept and the menu has a nice selection of meats, fish and even vege options.  There is also a bar as you walk in in case there is a wait or you just need a little refreshment.

The food.  Overall pretty good.  The smoked tuna was very good.  The turkey Reuben was average as was the commerce burger.

My only real complaint is that i do not judge a place by the price alone. I fantastic meal is worth every penny but i do judge it by a price to value ratio and unfortunately a "nothing special"  lunch for 3 people at $75  is a bit much.

Real rating is 3.5 but in this case had to round down.

In Havertown you can't through a stick without hitting a pizza joint!  This is one of them.  I'd put them in the top 25% based on quality, quantity, and service.  It's nice that you can grab a beer here which is not true of most pizza places in the area.  There is a great cheap public parking lot about a minutes' walk down the street.

This is a full menu pizza joint.  In addition to pies you can get burgers, hoagies, Italian, etc.  Pizza is a really personal thing.  They are worth a try to see if you like their style.

NO SURPRISES is exactly what you should expect from a chain restaurant and that is exactly what I received today!

I rolled in and stood at the counter for at most three minutes before I had my order.  The guy was friendly and actually asked my name so customer service was solid.

My medium Spicy Chicken combo meal was about $7.  It was hot and the fries were crispy so no problems with the food.

I observed that the place was clean and while I was there I saw folks working on keeping it that way.

CONSISTENTCY is what I expected and I received it!

One of the nicest Italian BYOBs in the western burbs.  Nice décor however it is a little cramped.  I've been here for lunch a couple of times and each time I was smiling on the way out.  Their bruschetta is outstanding.  I know it's an Italian staple but it is fabulous here.  Typical lunch entrees are about $10.00 and portion size is quite large.  The last time I was in I tried the Penne Bolognese.  This simple dish was executed perfectly.  Just the right amount of sauce with the correct consistency.  

Fellini Cafe is definitely worth a visit if you are in this part of Delaware County.

Flying Fish Abbey Dubbel beats the hell out of $2 Miller Lites!  I stopped in and discovered that they have embraced the craft beer craze.  A big blackboard was up on the wall with 11 interesting drafts.  There was the usual "On Deck" list detailing what's coming.  Also, the bartender (cute) was quick to point out that they have just added about 20 craft bottles. 

The last time I rated these guys I gave them 3 stars and wished I could go 3 1/2.  Now I'll give them a 4.  The food here has always been solid with a huge variety and big portions.  Add tons of TVs and this place is a really decent sports bar experience.

This is one of the greatest exterior car washes around.  Why you ask?

* It's almost completely automated.  As you drive up you use a charge card (or bills) to pick and pay for your wash.  No human involved.  Prices range from $7-$13.  

* This is the type of where you stay in the car.  Just before you enter the tunnel a human brushes the extra dirty parts of your car. 

* The tunnel itself is shiny and new and the dryer works great.  

* Because there are essentially no people there is no tipping!

* They knock about $2 off the price for happy hour.

If you are looking for just an exterior wash this is a great place!

This place is the quintessential example of a suburban sports bar.  It's bigger than most.  Memorabilia everywhere, waitresses in referee jerseys, a zillion TVs, sports themed food, etc., etc.

They have a decent beer selection but mostly domestic popular brands.  Beer aficionados, this is not your place. 
 
The food is quite decent.  Big portions.  A lot of burgers, fries, dogs, and wraps.  

This is a very casual place and the dress code is anything goes.  In addition to watching a game this place is very popular before or after taking in a movie at Regal Edgemont 10.  It's a one minute walk.

If I could I would go with 3 1/2 stars.

Stopped in for a little afternoon treat. My daughter got the glazed twist and I go the blueberry donut. Both were delish! They were light and full of flavor! The place wasn't to busy all the girls working were very nice and answered all my questions. I liked the blueberry donut But it was basically a plain cake donut with blueberry buttercream frosting. It had A TON of frosting. I would have liked it to be a blueberry donut with a little glaze or just a little frosting. It was good non the less and I ate it up! I can't wait to go back and try all the donuts!

This is my go-to restaurant in Chinatown. It's not because the food is particularly tasty, but because the service is awesome. I think all Philly Chinatown restaurants are pretty crappy, so being the best of the lot doesn't mean much. Nevertheless, I always enjoy my visits there. 

As you see from all these reviews, everybody loves Cathy. She is overly-friendly and effortlessly hilarious. If I order something she disapproves of, she will simply reject it and order for me. This has happened on many occasions.

If you're in the area and are craving some Chinese, you should pop in there and say hi to Cathy!

I really enjoy going to BrickTops.  Our most recent dinner visit was for New Year's Eve.  I had one of their daily fish offerings.  They have fresh fish brought in daily and it is apparent they have experience in preparing it correctly.  BrickTops is also a great place to go for a business lunch or for happy hour after work.  They always have a great selection of wines by the glass and a number of craft beers on tap.  The atmosphere is really nice and when it's warm enough, they have a great patio area outdoors.

Wondering why Collingswood is now the place to be when it comes to fabulous dining?  Plain and simple:  restaurants like Sapori. 

If there were a 6-star Yelp rating available, I'd use it for Sapori.  I had one of the best meals of my life there, enough so that my mouth watered thinking about the food well after I had eaten there.  

I'd take anybody to Sapori - from family to friends to colleagues.  I would be thrilled to have them cater something for me.  I would feel extremely comfortable recommending it to anyone.

No muss, no fuss, no shoes, no problem.

Undertow is the standard beach bar. Nestled between two hotels, and directly on the sand, this little shack offers a lot of fun for both tourists and locals. 

The prices for drinks are reasonable, dependent of course on what you order (I feel like their premium liquor was higher than avg). The also have a late night happy hour, which is great if you're staying in the area.

Great spot to anchor the boat and swim in for a nice refreshment, while enjoying St Pete Beach at the same time...

A-OK is how I feel about this place too. The concept is good and I always have a blast, but I don't ever think it's been my idea to go there. The drinks were typical for any bar, but the prices seemed a tad high for beers. I think they usually charge a cover, but it's nothing horrible if memory serves correctly.

On the negatives, Channelside seems to have been dead for about five years. This is usually the only 'hoppin' place late at night, and parking can be a dread between paying and walking to the garages. I wish the complex had more options, but this place is fun (and very original for the area).

As I have said many times, I only review liquor stores based on their selection of whiskeys. This liquor store seemed average in most respects, but with a limited selection of whiskeys.
The prices here were higher than they are at Bluegrass, just down the street and the guy working there seemed too busy watching TV to acknowledge my presence until the way out.
To add insult to injury, all the whiskeys were mixed together - Irish with Canadian with Bourbon with Tennessee etc. 
Definitely not my favorite store

I could almost go 2 stars b/c of the snobbery. It seems so much bigger from the outside, I kept thinking there had to be another area with the rest of the food. The deli departments are great. Tons of nice cheeses, meats, and bakery items to die for. Good wine selection too. I was almost run down by a woman who had to get to the free coffee, so perhaps that tainted my experience. She was oblivious to me standing there. In her defense I was wearing camouflage, had my face painted like I was in Apocalypse Now, and was hiding behind a barrel of pistachios.  Oh wait, I wasn't.

I tend to shop at Marsh because there are so many of them, and they have a bigger selection than Kroger. But Kroger is definitely cheaper. 

Not a big fan of the Purdue brand of chicken they carry at Marsh. It's not the freshest in the world. And they're often out of limes. And tortillas? Don't come here for them. Go to Kroger. They're better and much cheaper there. 

...But they have Tyson frozen (raw) chicken breasts at Marsh, which they don't carry at Kroger. And Multigrain Cheerios--rarely see them at Kroger. Alas, I am destined to come to Marsh.

Disclaimer: I haven't actually gotten my hair done here. But when I walked in on a perfectly reasonable hour on a perfectly half-empty time at the salon on a Monday, I barely got recognized. In fact, I almost felt as if I was intruding. And trust me, this is not so upscale that they don't take walk ins.

It's obviously an Aveda salon, and offers makeup services besides haircuts and hair removal for men and women. 

Kudos for a few things: They are exhibiting some local jewelry with some really cool thick-wire charms (see picture). They're also collecting for a food drive.

The Blue Coast Burrito chain was one of my first "big burrito" experiences several years ago and has remained my favorite since then. The win at Blue Coast is the Fruit Tea and the Pineapple salsa. It's truly the best I've ever had and the other big burrito places I've tried usually have neither. 

I find that the Small Tortilla is still PLENTY to have for a meal, though they only offer it in regular flour. The regular sizes offer other flavor tortillas, but they're just too much to eat. 

I've only tried one other menu item besides the burritos, and that's the fish tacos....and I didn't like them. The burritos are the way to go!

I used to really like this Casa Gallardo, but the past couple of times I've eaten there it's made me really sick. They also only seem to have one kind of cheese now: yellow. 

That "yellow" cheese was way too salty and offensive on a spinach and mushroom enchilada. My stomach hurts just thinking back to it. My friend also felt pretty terrible after his dish. 

I will say that our server was very nice and the guacamole was good. Probably won't be back though, when there are many better choices for Mexican that don't make me ill.

If you're looking for an SF style burrito this is the place.
Located on state street, its pretty low-key and not fancy at all.
Order at the counter and pick up at the counter.
They have an array of burrito options and a couple taco options as well.
The food was surprisingly good for what it was. Namely a 7 dollar burrito.
I was slightly annoyed that they did not offer me the super spicy salsa, but upon asking for it was sorta blown away. It was like dave's insanity sauce in salsa form. Spicy as hell but good.
Anyway I'm not gonna seek this place out again, but if it were to become an option I would not kick and scream.

Workers were friendly however the lady who helped me told me the incorrect info. She said "Pick whichever car you see, the key is inside". I paused and asked "Any of these?". She replied "Yeah. Any. We are trying to get rid of them". 

Of the choices were a Camaro, 328i or Q50. Obviously I walked toward the luxury car only to find that the key wasn't in the vehicle. I walked back inside and inquired about the key. I was told by another worker that it would be an upgrade because it was a luxury. Grr..National needs to make sure not to mislead us.

*Mobile Review*

Came here for an ADEA council meeting.

Decor: 2.5/5
-You can tell it's an old building

Service: 2.5/5
-Service is alright

Room Presentation: 2/5
Overall: 2/5
-Not much to say..it's kind of crappy.
-Room was cramped and smelled like smoke even though we requested a non-smoking room. 
-We requested a king size but they couldnt match the request.
-Breakfast bagels were hard and stale
-Make your own pancakes were fun and delicious with honey, apple and strawberries
-Pastries were meh

We chose this place only because the Westin was booked. I would not recommend this hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I came here with friends since it is dog friendly and we had a bunch of pups in tow. Brown Boxer has a nice outdoor deck area, but that is about all it has going for it. 

Overall, my table's food was pretty mediocre. I was pretty let down by my meal. My fish tacos were not prepared as they were described on the menu, missing a few key ingredients, and the amount of cabbage served with them was seriously about a teaspoon's worth. When I asked for more cabbage, I was brought a very tiny "extra" amount. Considering the server told me this was one of their most popular dishes, I can't imagine what something less popular must be like.

We hsve stayed on Hampton inns in a lot if different cites. This particular hotel is all right. It's not the nicest and it's not updated as we would expect.  The pool was pretty popular but not enough chairs for parents to sit& watch kids swim. So standing room only. The pool assist handle getting into and out of the pool is broken and watch several people almost fall back into the pool due to the broken handle. We got hood at warning people if we saw them. The rooms were just ok and no fridges in rooms like advertised. I would look around for some other places before staying here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Locals love this place. I honestly doubt you're reading this if you aren't a local. Then again, if you are a local, you should already know about this place and have no need to read this. Eh either way locals love this place. I say you've gotta try it for yourself. It's cheap and quick and they even have a drive through window. I didn't realize you could make pizza that fast, but who knows! I found it kinda runny, and cardboard like, but OK overall. Now I just hope I don't get beat up for my three star review.

I guess I was spoiled going to the original location in Doylestown for so many years because this location is a hot mess. Where to begin ... the staff is borderline unapproachable and seem to be just going through by the motions with the customers in front of them. Which is fine if you are in McDonald's but not a local joint. I just that's what you get with kids these days just average service, average attention span and average pride in what is happening around them. Doubtful I'll be back to this specific location.

I'm disappointed to be giving such a low grade to a fairly cheap meal with nice staff, however my latest experience really soured me to this place. I found one of those yellow and black pill bugs in my noodles yesterday. I assume that it must have been in the cilantro leaves I put in my bowl. I asked for a discount on the meal since I hadn't been able to finish and received about 7 apologies but only 20% off. The staff was very sorry about it but I'm disappointed I didn't get more of a discount for something that would have resulted in a failed health code rating.

Stopped in today for lunch, right at lunch time, about 11:45. Ordered my usual and the service was alright. The sandwich maker behind the counter was friendly as all was well. However, as I finish my order, I ask for a large tea. She charges me for a large fountain drink and disappears. 

I go over to get my tea, which happens to be behind the fountain drinks and notice there's no tea made. At all. There also is no other fountain option than soda and water. So I ended up paying $2 for a large cup of water and there was no worker to be found to ask about getting the money back. 

I know it's a minor complaint but come on!

Great food - service too but it took 26 minutes to get a group bill and then still it was wrong - in their favor of course.  Calculate this into your decision when hosting 39 people like I did once... Danny - fix your point of sale system -- the best of entertaining is minutes when you get to say good bye to your group.  I lost all of that time with my clients because you kept changing how things should be broken up... not my problem. I lost 30 minutes of goodwill time with my clients on the last night @ over $100.00 each and missed a chance to say good bye with most of them due to the check out process.

I based my visit on some of the Yelp elites from years ago but quite a bit must have changed from fine dining (hand towels) to more casual. The service was wonderfully polite and the inside did have a homely vibe. Maybe a little too cluttered, but that's not really the 3 star rating. The sushi was simply average and not the current 5 star yelp has it at. 

I ordered a pork fried dumpling and fancy roll. Friends also had the same type of orders. No complaints, but no pizazz...just straight down the middle average.

Two visits, one was bleh and the other was pretty fun.

The crowd is age 22-30...30 is pushing it but doable. There are the famous $5 bullrides and be prepared for the line; bachlorette night is suicidal. The drinks are good and if you sign up ahead of time you can skip the cover. The bathroom cleanliness beats most crowded places I've been to. The crowd is fun and no asshats that I had to deal with. Some people would argue that this place has nothing but doucheturds but I didn't have that problem. I'd try this bar a third time.

My husband grew up nearby and firmly believes that this is one of the best pizza places ever. I do not, but I let him have that childhood memory so every once in awhile I go to Alex's. 

We definitely have had good pizza from Alex's. The last time (during covid) we had a pie in the car. It was overcooked and parts of the crust were black. The girl who gave it to him even said that they left it in too long. Still, they gave us the burnt pizza and I give them a fair rating on Yelp. Try harder, don't overcook pizza. See you soon because my husband makes me.

Their competing with all the 20 million mexican food trucks and stands here in town, and it does get a little confusing sometimes.  I had ordered a beans rice and cheese with shredded beef burro.  I would have like more beans and rice and cheese with my HUGE portion of shredded beef.  The beef was over powering the entire burro.  Next time  will order it without meat.

The staff is very friendly, the Drive thru attendant talk with me about how my days was going and we still talked for a few minutes after I got my order.  =)

It's just OK! I had heard of this place for awhile so when we had the opportunity to go to Shogun we took it. I was starving so I felt like I could eat COW, and you know what that's just what they gave me.  I had ordered the Bluogi beef (spl)  The platter was sooo HUGE I mean the Portion was so big that four people could share it.  It was almost too much to eat even for this rice loving girl!  

I am not a Sushi lover, but I will eat the Cali roll, and the roll itself was all right, but yet again there was too much rice.  Not saying we won't go there again, but now I can say I have been to shogun.

3.5 stars

Although we were already pretty stuffed from our really late lunch at the Reading Terminal, we still found it necessary to add in an extra meal, which we called dinner... but it was really like a second dinner since our 'lunch' at Reading Terminal was so late, and so... large.  Even though almost no one was hungry, we went and ordered lots of food - edamame, agedashi, lots of rolls, and even dessert.

We brought our own wine since it's BYOB.  The Sweet Potato and Crab Tempura Roll was interesting.  I think the food was pretty standard, nothing extraordinary, but it was good.  

Service was also good.  We had a good time.

Why oh why can't I go in a grocery store for what I come in for?
Because Straub's has such an excellent selection that "normal stores" do not have. (But they do not have "normal prices either.")

On my list was: Stuffed Porkloin and Citizen Kane Seasoning
What I came out with is Ciabatta and all the stuff to make Tres Colores, Miss Huitton's cake, which is to die for, Some Nice Italian Wine (which is now my fav), and these amazing little jalapeno stuffed shrimp from the meat department! 

So if your looking for different or tad bit gourmet this is the place to go. Just make sure you go on a payday.

La Bamba...Burritos as big as your head that's their slogan.  Well it is true!  They are big!  I was going to give the first reviewer a hard time about how it is great Mexican food but then I realized that he said after a night at Broad Ripple and decided ok that's fair to say.  

I came here once when I came to visit my SO's brother who lives here and after day Indy Racing.  It was still daytime but sufficient beers were drank so it tasted ok.

The best deal they have is cheap T-shirts I think we paid $4.99 for the one I scanned in the photo.

Very very nice people. However, IMO fairly expensive for takeout with little overhead.  For the price of the primo bianco pasta for 2-3 servings with bread it's like $26 with tax.  I can literally get the same amount of pasta or a huge chicken dish with a glass of wine & fresh bread at Cunnetos for about the same price or cheaper.  Pasta was just ok. Tiramisu $4 for good size piece was good even if store bought and the highlight of the meal.  Like I said super nice but price and limited menu may prevent future visits.  Will see if leftovers taste better.

Of course it is more expensive then if you order in bulk from Northern Brewer but when you are mid-batch and need something, no problem, they probably have it.  
The fat cat though...I am in love with that cat.  They had to ask me three times if they could help me because I walked in, heard a THUD and looked down and there was this big - no - HUGE cat looking up at me sweetly.  
They technically accept credit cards but have like an 11 dollar minimum or something strange so if you only need one thing, just bring cash or else you're going home with three bags of rice hulls.  Yup.

I am a fro-yo fiend and I was excited for a self-serve place to open up downtown. I love the concept, but unfortunately I was really disappointed with the yogurt itself. It wasn't horrible, but it tasted really artificial. I ate about half of it and threw the rest away. This is unheard of when it comes to me and frozen yogurt. 

If you like the self-serve idea, I would recommend Sweet Alley in Isla Vista. They have really really good flavors that taste delicious (Root Beer is my absolute favorite), and tons of toppings (even more than Yogurtland I think). They're also locally owned.

So the flavor of the yogurt here is not as good as some of the other froyo places, but it still satisfies my craving, and I can walk to it from UCSB. The toppings are fine and I think the mochi tastes like it's supposed to taste. The major downside is the cost - I usually have this in place of a regular lunch which sort of justifies paying a lot, but if I get a large with 3 toppings it costs 7.95 or something like that. That's a lot for yogurt. 

Still, I'm glad this place is here and I will keep frequenting it despite the exorbitant prices. I guess that makes me a slave to my froyo addiction.

I get really random cravings sometimes, and a few months ago I was on a chicken piccata kick. I just HAD to have chicken piccata. I looked up the menus of various Italian places around town, and Petrini's was the only one that I found that had it on their menu. So that's where we headed - and let me tell you, it definitely satisfied my craving. The piccata is really really lemony and delicious. The sauce is not too thick, and the chicken is just lightly pan-fried. It was perfect. I could do without all that fettucini alfredo, and the bread wasn't great, but I would absolutely come here again just for that chicken. Mmmm.

I think one way to tell how good a mexican place is, is by the quality of their rice and beans. Los Gallos beans and rice are crazy good. My favorite thing on the menu is a simple beans, rice, and cheese burrito. Just those three ingredients in a tortilla are full of flavor and totally hit the spot. I've also tried the chile relleno burrito and chicken burrito, and both were great. But the BRC is a classic and Los Gallos does it right. I also love their avocado salsa. The service is super friendly and the prices are reasonable. I also love the neighborhood and the fact that it's never super crowded. This is definitely a local gem!

Though my repertoire in coffee is limited, for what it's worth, this is the best cup o' joe I've ever had period. This brew rivals even good 'ole Peet. The coffee is smooth, sans burnt after taste. Stay, and they'll pour it in a generous-sized mug. Even the mug screams luxe; the handle is beefy and exudes confident index-fingering.

NPR was the soundtrack for the barista joyfully serving our legal drug of choice. Can you ask for more? 

Well... yes, I can. Saxby's, please oh pretty please close later than 6pm?

This has been a great find! We came for a late lunch and had the place to ourselves. The tuna was making and the mussels may have been the best I have ever had. Our waiter was top notch. We came back the following week for dinner because we had to try it again. It was much busier...of course. They have great choices that are unique and delicious. I was a little disappointed with our steak dish and the waiter this time was not as attentive.  Would have given 3 stars if we only experienced dinner and lunch hadn't been so amazing.

Maybe I was spoiled with Brother's over the years. All places have on and off nights.
I went to Nick's earlier and ordered a well done pie. I didn't recognize the guy making the pizza, which was odd. I brought the pie home and it was good don't get me wrong, but not even in the same atmosphere as Brother's. I've never said Brother's was the neatest pie, but this pie from Nick's was rather sloppy.. It may be a rookie cooking when the owner isn't there. Overall the place is still better than most places around besides Brother's... And that's a fact.

I personally don't like Manny's pizza. I'd give it a 2 of 10. However, many of the people I grew up with and went to school with do love it. They have a pretty beasty menu, with a lot of sandwiches. They are all reasonably priced. The Clint Eastwood is good. I've only had it once though. i don't commonly crave that kinda stuff. I think their pizza is really weak, but I've had some good things there.. I just can't remember. The staff is cool, good fast nice delivery service..Which you can't complain about. Manny's has been open a lot of years so you really can't argue that factor. People like, however I'm not one of them.

I was treated to lunch at the Villa as a welcome to my new job. There were about 15 of us, and while they really probably should have grouped our tables together differently, everyone had a good time.

The bread... OH THE BREAD!! I could eat it all day. Fresh baked and omg-delicious. So much for my New Year's Resolution. Most people chose paninis, but I went for the gusto and had the fettucini w/crab and spinach. GOOD CALL. lololol. The servings are two-meal huge, but the food is delicious, so I forced mine down. The normal people took doggy bags home.

The Apple Market will never be the place that checks everything off my grocery list, but usually saves me in times of despair. With its ever-colorful crowd, Apple Market is the place I head to when I forgot to pick up eggs or desperately needed a coke. For some reason they are also the only grocery store that carries the California stir-fry vegetable medley that has now become an essential part of my very being.  What they have to offer in the way of produce tends to be adequate but not my first choice. All in all, it's a great place to pick up those last minute items.

I know Maggie Moo's is a chain, but having never had it before I moved to Nashville, this review if for those 'not from around these parts' people. I cant think of anything better than someone letting me pick my ice cream and then letting me shove it full of any and every topping I can think of, and believe me I do just that. My favorite Maggie Moo's ice cream flavors are better batter or cheesecake; mix in caramel, brownies, and cookie dough and you have heaven in a cup. Seriously, delicious and if you don't like it, it's your own fault because you pretty much made it yourself!

I am a big fan of decades if anything because it is so horribly out of place in the Honky Tonking capital of the world. It's cheesy, it's glamorous 80s, and I'm sure it would suck if I was sober but still it's if anything a fun distraction. My one major dislike is that they charge a cover, I'm assuming in an effort to be a real club which its not, but I'm pretty sure their isn't a real club anywhere in Nashville. The crowd tends to be a slightly more interesting version of the Honky Tonk usuals, so if anything if you are looking for some variety in your Country bar hoping night Decades should give you just that.

I have to say this is hands down the best sushi place in Philly. I've eaten here once and ordered for takeout and both times did not disappoint. My fiancé is limited in what he can eat due to being partly vegetarian and even the vegetarian rolls here are AMAZING. Sweet Meadow roll is probably one of the best vegetarian rolls I've ever tried. I got the rolling fire and Mr French kiss and both were so good and nothing like I've had before. Super unique rolls here that do NOT DISSAPPOINT. No wonder the wait for pickup was like 75 minutes. Can't wait to try more of their rolls soon.

I've eaten here a half dozen times or so, and every time I look around the table to a bunch of "it was ok" responses.  Not good... not terrible.  It's convenient and popular... especially with the seniors and familes with young kids.  It's about the same type of menu quality as your average OK diner - burgers, sandwiches, a few hot plates like hot turkey platters, etc.  Prices are a little high for what you get, but not outrageous.  My vote would be to continue right past Sam's to either Tiffin or Elevation Burger in the same shopping center.

Great place to stay if you are stuck in Oldsmar, FL.  It's not a very happening town but there is a happening Applebee's right by the Residence Inn!!!!  Bonus!!!!  Happy hour till 11pm.  

The rooms here are very good, not huge for extended stay, but functional.  I had a king room with a nice sized bathroom, small TV/livnig room and a little kitchen with full sized everything (I did not cook though).  I'm not sure I'd recommend for more than one person, the "living" quarters were a bit cramped.

Full breakfast in the morning is a nice added bonus and this location has a small workout room and pool.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I don't remember the food being so great, but the thing I do remember is that they do not card you for booze.  I was there on my senior band trip in high school, and I had asked for a pina colada.  They then asked if I wanted it virgin or not.  Sadly, I had to say virgin because our band director was at my table.  I went back two years later to check it out and ordered a Hurricane and was not carded.  Hooray!  The hurricanes are delicious, but pricey...but if you want the cool Hard Rock glass and a drink with a ton of liquor in it, it's a good deal.

If I lived in New Orleans, this would be my go-to. I loved my Thai iced tea milkshake (although I had to switch to a small straw to keep from sucking it down in two seconds! it comes with a giant bubble-tea-type straw) and hubs had amazing Vietnamese coffee. 

Friendly service, and the atmosphere inside was adorable. We sat outside, though, and watched as some random chickens roamed around the sidewalk. Yep. Live chickens. Just, you know, out for a stroll.

I wish I was in New Orleans. I could use another Thai iced tea milkshake.

I used to frequent this place on certain holidays...  After a few too many visits?  I quit going.  Seems like the same old posers, over and over.   BUT this place can be fun, if you go once in a blue moon.   Felt the drinks were overpriced, felt the music to be really nice, but the same people over and over?  ruined it for me.

I suggest going there on a busy weekend, when lots of tourists have infiltrated it, and its not so "trendy".   Make sure you got a good buzz on, and you'll have a really great time.

On halloween?  beware of the high cover charge.

Don't expect a Real Starbucks. 
They told me they weren't "real " but with Hilton, but I doubted it would taste different. 

The drinks are just not the same. Why?its like going to a Stbk at Target. Not the same! The ones at Disney too. 

Ordered my usual Mocha decaf with soy, do not get how it can taste so bad as if I made it at home with a cheap powder mix. 

Sad, I want to like it.... It looks the same, the prices are the same.... Great disappointment 

Not worth the long lines, very small space tho outside area seating too

Best thing is it is next to a real Starbucks, not one of those hotel ones like down the street.
2 of my favorite restaurants are also almost next door with amazing views by the water. 
Older hotel, they try. 
Nice location by the water, not impressed by anything else.
Clientele seems lower class, lots of teens here, during the conference I come to annually 
Would stay here only if I have to, for convenience to the Tampa convention center across the walkway/bridge. 
Btw the pool is small and not inviting, like one I would have in my back yard.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Came to this place for dinner while I was on a snowboarding trip with friends.  The place is located in a rather large strip malls, and has multiple flatscreen tvs displaying the most current sport games.  Service was above average and the food came out a rather brisk pace.  Although most all you can eat sushi places are known for stuffing the sushi with a lot of rice, this place only had modest rice which is a huge plus to me as you can eat more fish.  Highly recommend this place for anyone one who is in town traveling and has the itch for sushi.

This is a pretty standard American fare restaurant inside the Grand Sierra Resort and Casino.  I actually ate here three times (one lunch and two breakfasts) because the hotel gave me some discount coupons to try it out and it was fairly moderately priced.

The food is OK.  Nothing crazy good but not bad.  The breakfast service is a little slow especially considering that hardly anyone was in the restaurant when I came down for breakfast.

All in all, a solid 3 stars for a decent menu selection, decent food and OK service. Plus, it's right in the hotel so it's super convenient.

YOOOOOOO.....this Pizza is BOMB--AFTER THE CLUB!

-Lots of toppings to choose from, big slices, and hot (they reheat for you in the oven)
-Usually run into a friend or 2 after the club/bar here (it's kinda like a guaranteed unplanned reunion)
-Staff is always friendly and works fast 
-Always a fun scene in the gayborhood, the gays at the hut are a riot--got to luv it! :-)

Side Note:  I've never actually had this pizza before 2am, and we all know most food is good after 2am...I'll have to write an update to give a more unbiased opinion

So I'm studying for a big test...and finding new coffee shops to study in has become my new favorite pastime.

This place is just NOT the business.

1.  Wi-FI did not work for me or my friend AT ALL
2.  Cash Only--I'll accept this if the establishment is offering something tremendous 
3.  Really loud/inappropriate music was playing
4.  That packman table constantly makes noise even if no one is playing

I think this place may be good to come chat with a friend in the back room.  It's too noisy to study and the Wi-Fi is too unreliable to use your computer. 

Others seem to love this place :-???--hey to each their own.

My frame of mind most nights as I leave the office: "Oh! 'XYZ' would be great for dinner. Oh, wait..I don't have 'Y'..okay, Spruce will have it.

Beautiful flowers, good beer selection, an incredibly friendly staff, and reasonable prices for a local city market.

Downside: this is not the place to go if you are looking for ingredients for a specific recipe. You won't be able to get all of your food shopping for the week out of the way, but you'll be able to snag the basics, as well as a couple gourmet finds.

Honestly - I really never understood why people would write reviews of chains like McDonald's or DD, but this is HANDS DOWN the best Dunkin Donuts I have ever been to! I stop here almost every day before work. They are incredibly fast..I don't know how they do it. My coffee is ALWAYS ready before I'm even done paying.  Food is fast and the guy who makes the egg sandwiches is legit the nicest person I have ever met and always remembers me! Five stars and two thumbs up to this Dunkin Donuts..and this is coming from a Boston gal!

So, I must admit my feelings remain mixed.

We will start with..

The Good: bar scene is unquestionably fun and entertaining. The summertime firework display at 9:15 every Friday evening really reigns in the crowds and provides a beautiful scene of the bridge from the deck.

The Bad: we waited almost 2 hours for a seat and my veggie burger with pasta salad was mediocre. I think it's more about the ambiance here, situated directly on the river, than it is about the food.

I'd bring tourists back but would probably be inclined to check out other locations first.

Blowfish Sushi is now called Jimmy's Sushi.
This is one of my favorite sushi restaurants in Pinellas County, FL.
The atmosphere is casual and quaint. Jimmy and his staff are friendly and fun- they always remember me and my special orders. 

I recommend any of the specialty rolls. They are large rolls and well worth it. 

I have been going to Jimmy's for two years at least once a month and have never had a bad experience. I always leave full and happy. The only problem is my eyes are bigger than my belly.  

If you are feeling creative- make up your own roll and they will name it after you and put it on the menu.

This is what my boyfriend and I call the "bad Marathon." 

We have given it multiple chances, but it has always failed to impress. Most of the time, the food isn't very good. 

Last time I was there I had my usual grilled chicken sandwich and the chicken looked and tasted like it had been cooked on a Foreman Grill. I love my Foreman Grill. In the winter. When I can't bring myself to light up the real grill in my yard. I expect a lot more from a restaurant with GRILL in the name.

Service is spotty. The interior is like a corporate cafeteria circa 1992. Do yourself a favor and at the very least walk to the one on 16th Street.

These kids are alright.

I used to rent cars all of the time, back when my company required it for travel over 50 miles, so I'm old hat when it comes to the rental business.

The last time I got work done on my car (FOR A MONTH), I used these guys as my rental company.  They came and picked me up at the body shop and took me over to grab my car.

The people that work there are clean-cut and professional, I've seen them resolve customer conflicts while waiting and it is nice to see a team of people know how to respond with courtesy and empathy.

Hope I don't have to rent a car any time soon, but if I do, I'm going back to these guys.

Drinking a hand grenade = one going off in your head in the AM. 

We stopped last night and I unwisely ordered and consumed a famous "hand grenade" drink. Wooo! They are extremely potent, but you dont taste the grain alcohol or whatever is in there, so be careful in your consumption. Hand grenades are also extremely sweet, so you can definitely look forward to a bangin' headache in the AM. (Trust me on this one, it was NOT pretty!)

On the plus side, the staff here is extremely friendly and there seems to be live music regularly.

I've gotta say, this place has some kick-ass fried chicken. I usually go to Crusoe's for my Sunday chicken fix, but the line was out the door when I visited. So the closest place I could think of (because Hodak's is TOTALLY overrated) was Gingham's Homestyle.  Service was brisk and friendly, and the chicken? Fantastic. Juicy and very, very tasty. I would have grabbed a piece of chocolate pie to finish up, but I could barely move after such a good meal. I think this is my go-to for fried chicken in the future.

It's hard to build on what others have said about this Planet Fitness. It's much larger on the inside than it looks, and it's chock full of machines, televisions, weights, etc.

I decided to join because I usually walk in Carondelet Park, but the weather doesn't always accommodate my needs--stop it, Mother Nature! And when the Grant's Trail bike path is full of Tour de France wannabes, it's easier to hop on a stationery bike at PF and read a book. It's completely affordable, the staff is friendly, and the space is clean and inviting. I dig it.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
It's a Starbucks, like any other one, and it's just a few blocks over from the school I teach at. There's a drive thru and a confusing parking lot, but I understand why it's set up like that. It's a busy intersection; people are going to be coming in from Belle Chase and from Terry. It's fine, just park.

There's never a wait if you go inside, although the drive thru line can get a little long. I only order maybe 3 things ever and I'm in and out. The staff is nice and polite, recognize their regular customers, and the bathrooms are clean. No complaints here.

Big fan of the remodel.  This place looks brand new.  Wendy's is always a great late night stop, this one is no exception.  Last time I stopped here there was a line nearly wrapping around the entire building.  My wife and I were shocked how quickly they were able to work through the orders.  The new flatbreads are pretty good too, but I'm still not buying their latest fries.  My wife, (who hates salt) even had to salt these they lacked so much flavor.  Other than that, I think this is a nice Wendy's location to stop by.

The guys who work here are great!  They remember you and take care of you when you come back.  That is enough to go back to this place, but on top of it, their pizza is the best around.  

I am a fan of the NY style of pizza - thin and tasty...this is the kind of pizza Illiano's has.  Their sauce is tastier than other places too.  I mean, really, who doesn't love pizza?  Its hard to complain about pizza, but its even harder to find pizza that rises above the norm and this place does it.  We always get take out, but they have tables inside.

Finding glasses can be one of the most unfun things you have to do....but the staff at Pennsylvania Optometrics makes it a bit easier.....

if you want designer glasses like chanel or kate spade, their selection is so so....but if you want some interesting specs that make a statement, then this is the place to go.....plus they are super super reasonable....i got a pair of adorable 1950's like glasses for $130 with the lenses....my friend got two pair for less than $300.....

sure lens crafters gets you glasses in an hour or so....but this place only takes a few days and you will get way more compliments....
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text: This place is super good! The atmosphere is nice, the music is good, the food is AHH MAZING! Of course it should be, your the executive chef!! It's all your own creation, you just tell them how you want it! I opted for the basic crust, Alfredo sauce, black and green olives, chicken, chorizo, roasted red peppers, sundried tomatoes, jalapeños, all dosed with a couple stripes of buffalo sauce! My mouth is watering just writing the review and I'm still sitting in the diner! Did I mention this place is locally owned?!!!!

Came here Monday night during Hurricane Sandy, since many other places were closed. Our server was very friendly, which I always appreciate when dining. I ordered the steak and my date ordered the salmon, but we ended up sharing our meals. I enjoyed the salmon, but the steak seemed a little tough to me, but my date enjoyed it. For dessert we just had chocolate ice cream, it wasnt on the menu but our waiter hooked us up! After dinner my date and I sat and talked for a long time and they didnt rush us or anything even though they were obviously closing. The waiter was really nice which is why I gave 4 stars instead of 3.

I was recommended by my fellow co-worker to get my bushing, shocks and stouts replaced here as my 90k checkup called for.  I stopped by Precision Alignment after work to get an estimate and I have never had a technician physically showed me why my car was in need to get bushing replaced.  Unlike many dealers, they are extremely straight forward.  I was told that my car only really needs to get the bushing replaced but shocks and stouts are recommended but not necessary.  They also offer a 10% discount off labor, ask them how!

Thank god, Lee lee is coming to Tucson.  I was grossed out walking around this supermarket.  All the fruit and vegetable weren't fresh.  There is no organization in this store.  Everything was hard to find and the workers weren't responsive and most importantly they don't speak English.  After shopping there once, I have been driving up to Chandler to get my grocery.  I rather drive three hours to a place I find everything I need with half the price (esp lee lee in chandler gives 15% off of your total price).  With Lee Lee coming to Tucson, I hope Grantstone can maintain staying in business.

I have met up with people here for lunch several times and so far I still remain disappointed.  I am amazed of how busy this place could get during lunch time.  Our normal 1-hr lunch break could get stretched out to 1.5hrs-2hrs due to extremely slow service.  I have tried their several menu items and I find the food here average.  Nothing special and can be easily made in your very own kitchen.   I was a bit disturbed by their green tea that was made from green tea powder and their tonkatsu sauce that is straight from the bottle.  Each item could be acquired from Lee Lee Oriental Supermarket.

Had lunch here with 2 other business associates. We all had the flounder special. It was breaded, to our surprise, and just okay. My minestrone soup was lukewarm. The waiter told us how the owner insisted they make their own bread, even though the area has plenty of bakeries around. So I was thinking the bread was going to be great!  Not. Dry, not tasty and somewhat stale. The eggplant appetizer was good. The chocolate cake dessert was excellent. The tiramisu was average. Service was on the slow side, even though it was not busy. 
Considering the price, which worked out to about $40 each (with tip) for lunch, I was expecting more.

Better coffee than Cafe DuMonde, and its only ONE DOLLAR for a 12 oz cup.

I loved how the entrance is disguised from Royal Street, you need to enter through a "Secret Passageway" to get into this McD's.

Breakfast is the only meal I can tolerate at McD's -- and this one has the "Steak McBagel" (currently not sold in California).  

I love the Steak McBagel.....its one of my guilty pleasures on the entire planet.....and my wife loves the Sausage Burritos.  

Cheap prices and a friendly staff makes this a must-visit place in the French Quarter when you need a refuge from Tourist Traps and shitty coffee.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
My friends and I wanted to eat somewhere french after Julie and Julia. We checked the menu before we went. Steakfrites! Give me steakfrites and I'm a happy gal.

We get to Coquette which was not so cute once inside. I had passed it a few weeks earlier and thought it  was adorable.

They bring a bottle of room temperature water to the table.....no ice. We peruse the menu. The only thing we are even slightly interested in is the beet salad. 

We made an excuse and left and went to Beau Monde.  Save yourself a trip!

Great place if you want to argue with the manager to get an entree that you sent back taken off your bill.

The food is mediocre. You can make better at home. My friend ordered a dish which stated fresh mozzarella.  Fresh Mozzarella does not melt as well as the cheese in her dish. It was not what she ordered. So she sent it back and did not want anything else. They expected us to pay for it!

To boot the waitress told me I could come to the kitchen to talk to the manager. Ah no? He can come over to the table. 

Please do not go here.

Oh and the artichokes in the salad are canned. And I think our waitress left her pants at home

If you're into McHotels, with no idea how to use the large spaces they have, and with lots of screaming kids while you're trying to eat your disgusting TGI Fridays breakfast after a night of getting called a f*g by a group of drunken Phillies fans in front of their security guards, then boy do I have a hotel for you to stay in the next time your travel plans send you to Philadelphia.  

They get 2 stars because of the psychotic notes I get every other day from my cleaning lady, blessing me and loving me, in the weirdest language available.  good times.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
My sister was in town and she loves going to the downtown Belleville location.  I suggested we go to the nearby new West Main location. 

We started with a salad. The house dressing and salads are awesome suace. I ordered the meatball sandwich and she ordered a French dip sandwich. We both asked about fries. The waitress explained that they did not come with fries because the sandwiches were so large. I ate half of mine one night for dinner and the other half of hers on another night. :) 

I would like if they offered a smaller sandwich and a side.

my sister picked Marcos on Main for my mom's birthday. she and her family love it. 

i think it is just ok. prices are competitive for an italian place. the food is good but almost never served hot. Warm yes. HOT no! i got their greek pizza and a bit of mom's pasta. the taste of the food is good, but i think it sat a minute because it was not exactly cold but not hot either. 

i go if someone else is paying or the rest of the group decide to go. but not a place i would choose on my own.

if you live in the area, give it a try. it is  not a place that i would go out of the way to eat there.

Usually the only time I end up at a Starbucks is when trapped at an airport terminal for a morning flight. Luckily, I don't fly often so years can pass between Starbucks experiences.

$3.95 for the largest size cold-steeped coffee is ridiculous, being that at least half the volume is comprised of ice. Watered-down medium brew at 40% mark-up over the same stuff they serve hot. 

On this occasion I had been up for over 24 hours awaiting the arrival of my first grandchild. With any luck I won't have to avail myself of week-ass cold brew and harshly hot "fresh" brew until the next grandchild comes along.

I give this place a 3.5. I have never had a pizza that reminds me more of my trips to Italy. The pizza options, the crust, the sauce all very Italy. The place itself is okay but I like that it is tucked away in an alley with outside seating. That also gives it a very Italian feel. This place isn't for people looking for an American slice of pizza because you will be disappointed. The taste, crust, and toppings of a true Italian pizza are very different than our American version. For what it is this place is awesome and it takes a cultured palate appreciate.

We stayed at the Crowne Plaza for a total of four nights, and it is a basic, upper-medium place to stay. It is pretty centrally located (I was able to walk most of the city in a day), across the street from a Starbucks (for all you fans) and several great local street-food vendors (gotta have an authentic Philly pretzel!!!!). The staff is accomodating and helpful, and they go out of their way (upgraded bed linens, sleep package) to make sure you grab a good night's sleep with them. I would absolutely stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
We arrived early on a Friday afternoon and was pleased to discover that we made in in time to take advantage of the half price sushi and two for one drinks. 

The sushi was actually quite good and fresh. The rolls were a little small but it all was flavorful. We also had a tempura shrimp appetizer and that was exceptional. We actually ended up ordering too much sushi and forced ourselves to finish. My son who doesn't do sushi (he's 13) ordered the chicken teriyaki which I tasted and it was also pretty good. Service was adequate, maybe a little slow but they were kind of busy so I'll give them a break on that.

This is a slightly below average (but not terrible) Chinese take out place. The portions are large family style portions that are served in tin foil and styrofoam containers even if you happen to eat in. The dining room has a couple of booths and is brightly lit by fluorescent lights. It's very much a fast food kind of place. The food is over cooked and very saucy. Nothing special. The menu has all the regulars you would find on typical Chinese takeout menu. 

Can't really recommend it. It would be a fine place to stop for a bite if you happened on it and were hungry for some mediocre Chinese, but nothing to go out of your way for.

Went here for lunch on someone's recommendation. They don't have a lunch combo special (like teriyaki, salad, and 2 pieces of nigiri, or whatever) but they do have all AYCE sushi. $20 for lunch. It's almost cheaper to get that than to get two rolls and an app separately, so I did it. I was hoping for more of a cheap lunch combo thing for less food and less money since I wasn't starving, but oh well. The sushi was fine -- not off the charts, but not weird and smelly. Service was nice. If you're starving and feel like stuffing yourself with sush, try here. If you want a more particular experience (classy date night, etc), branch out.

Ministry is yet another Ms. Pacman destination (pack! pack! pack!) Tucked away on a dank alley in NoLibs, you kinda have to know where you're going to get here.  But if you do, most likely it will be worth it.  They have pool tables, video games, a reasonable beer selection and a fun bar staff.  It's pretty divey which is meant entirely as a compliment.  I also like the size of their bar.  It's nice and big.  They used to have good food but I haven't had food there in awhile so I don't know anymore.

Despite it's pretentious name, it's a great local neighborhoody kind of bar.

Mama Yolanda's is a perfect example of a restaurant in which the owner should avoid customer interaction.  Sort of like the sixth season of The Sopranos when Artie starts to go a little bonkers and drives the customers away with his inappropriate chatter. Mama Yolanda (I'm assuming) who was also our server had a few too many glasses of vino and was in a bit of a state.  That and we were subjected to banter from the Rat Pack for the entire meal, some of which was racist and pretty darn offensive.  The food was decent, but it definitely did not live up to the reputation it has garnered due to its long history.

The first and most important thing I have to say is chicken tinga tacos.  They are made with plum tomatoes and "mexican spices" which I think includes chipotle...nice and smokey and all in all very flavorful.  The guac is bliss inspiring and the chips are cooked fresh.

It loses stars for the complete and utter lack of ambiance. I mean it isn't really dirty it's just overly bright, mismatched and dingy.  I'd suggest they can the gringo food and spend more effort on making the place a little more pleasant.

BONUS for the kitchen being open til 1 AM and quick delivery time.

I'd give it 3 1/2 stars if that were an option.

This Carpinteria pizza place is located in downtown along the main business section but not immediately off the 101 freeway.  The have an indoor area complete with out of date video games as well as an extensive outdoor seating section.

Their pizza is reasonably good.  It was technically a thin crust pizza but really too thick for my taste.  It had a good balance of sauce and cheese.  Both the sauce and to a greater extent the cheese were bland but did not taste processed or of poor quality.

The service was friendly but distracted and I was not 100% sure that they would get my order.

La Salsa is kind of a strange combination of a Qdoba and a regular Mexican restaurant. You order at the counter, get a buzzer, seat yourself, and bus your own table. But the food is served on real plates and they have a full bar. It's slightly pricier than Qdoba, but the food is not as good. I was excited to see the salsa bar with about 8 different types of salsa. However, after trying about 6 of them I was once again disappointed. Every single one was either bland or just plain bad. The habanero and avocado salsas had the consistency of water. I won't be back.

I have not had Chinese Food since I moved to Kirkwood and when I began craving it, I knew it was time to find a new favorite place, so I referred to Yelp.
 I would agree that it is the best American Chinese food in the St. Louis area. The Crap Rangoon comes with 6 in an order and is well stuffed, the Wonton Soup is amazing and the Beef with Broccoli has thick, juicy pieces of beef and crisp green broccoli. There was plenty of beef in the order. The price is great, especially for the portions. The only problem is that they only accept CASH or CHECK, which may be a blessing in disguise, and keep me from going there too often!

The place has mixed reviews...  and I could c that....

2.5 stars

I have been here a couple times.  (pre-Rona, and recently...  during 'Rona)

Its a good place if you have a large group, get a table and if you are lucky enough to get good service.  I have experience that before, though mostly on the negative..

I have had really bad service here before, and some of the servers have attitudes.

If they cleaned up their act and had better training across the board the place would be a lot better.  It can be hit or miss.

Delish! We went to Delmar Loop looking to have our favorite Blue Ocean All you can eat sushi.. When we found out they killed it on the weekends we decided to come here instead because we both LOVE Mac & Cheese.. And we figured a place couldnt stand alone serving ONLY Blue Boxes of the stuff.. There had to be more to it.. And it was.. Expect a slightly longer wait but that is because each plate is made to order.. and well worth the wait. I got the Philly Mac And Cheesesteak and my GF got the santa fe.. both were delicious! Will definately return!

Maxwells DOES have a strange decor! I ordered a Greek salad and it was good. Nothing over the top just a simple salad.
