Ive had better but Ive had worse. overall not a bad experience but as I sat there I couldnt help but wonder what the place looked like in (I Imagine the 1940's) when It was a house.. I ASSUME it was a house at one point.. it has all the symptoms of a house turned business. All I wanted to do was rearrange the layout and build a couple of walls.. knock a couple down.. anyhow the food was decent and if we went back I would try something else.. but I AM on a quest for Healthy food and I dont believe italian is on that list..

The prices are sky high, staff are scarily unfriendly, produce is disgusting (rotten garlic) and overpriced, but the last straw for me was my latest interaction with a cashier.

I presented a manufacturer's coupon I printed at home to the cashier and she responded with, "That's no good here."  I checked to see if it was expired (it wasn't) and asked why.  She told me it wasn't "legit" and after I asked why again she said it was because it was printed.  During this lovely exchange she made zero eye contact and sighed repeatedly.

The only thing they have going for them is their location.

I feel a little absurd writing a review for the liquor store immediately after writing about my juice cleanse, but I did buy a bottle of champagne there (which I enjoyed yesterday in Brunch Club mimosas--last hurrah before the cleanse!), so I should write a review.

I'm not super enthusiastic about a liquor store, it's fine I guess. Bright, big aisles, lots of choices. I'm more of a beer drinker, so I don't expect I'll be here that often, but it's still conveniently located. I'm sure I'll be here again, probably for more champagne. I do so love the sparkle.

The outside is a little creepy looking and if you decide to shop later in the afternoon, it attracts a rough crowd.  It basically looks like a hole in a wall type of place.  Inside, it could certainly use renovations, but for what it is, it does its job.  The grocery store covers all my basic grocery needs and at a fair price.  The cashiers are really friendly and I never have a hard time parking despite the limited space.  

I basically come here for convenience, but if it wasn't one block away from Vandy, I would definitely go somewhere else...

This was a cool place. Very unique, small and intimate but at the same time, it still felt private. This little gem is actually located fairly close to 100 oaks mall... I've passed it so many times and never knew it was here.  Really glad I tried it though. The Mediterranean vegetarian Lasagna was tasty and the Reisling made me very happy :) The waiter was really friendly too.  And the crowd was interesting- mostly middle age, stylish and maybe hipster, East Nashville/ Belle Meade type folks. It was kind of upscale yet somewhat casual.  Definitely a fun outing.

I just have to say that I am really happy that Vandy has this Wendy's right down the street!  I had cravings for chocolate ice cream and most things were closed (no Pinkberry or tasti-D lite).  Luckily at 11:30 at night, this place was booming!  And to my surprise, the cashier told me that they are open until 4AM!!!  I just love the chocolate frosty and their chicken nuggets.  And it was nice that there were a bunch of Vandy and Belmont students... mostly Belmont though.  Also, they take the commodore card!  And is it just me or did Wendy's become cheaper than it already is?

The pepperoni pizza tasted ok. It looked really delicious though (no burnt bottom). And my brother got a BBQ chicken wings sub... I dunno exactly what it was but I tried it and the spices started choking me as I inhaled... I imagine their Philly cheesesskes would be great.  Overall, I think this is a 3 star place.  And I'm not sure if this was because of the food, but I had an upset stomach afterwards... Maybe the food wasn't thoroughly cooked? Not sure....

Pros
- They have plenty of parking.  
- Plenty of seating indoors and outdoors. 
- cheap food

Cons
- The employees didnt look happy to be there.
- food was mediocre

Came here after getting a body wrap at England's hair salon.  Got chicken terriyaki with miso soup, salad with ginger dressing, and shrimp shumai.  The ginger dressing was perfect and the miso soup was pretty good.  I really enjoyed the shumai and the chicken terriyaki was OK but the chicken was a bit dry and the vegetables that came with it was too salty and peppery.  Otherwise, it was great!  

The food was delicious!  The staff were very friendly and attentive!  And the decorations inside the restaurant were very nicely placed.  I was so surprised that it was rather empty on a Friday night, especially since this place is so good!

It's pretty basic: put fresh fish on a menu, have good tamago that isn't watery, and a nutty roll selection and you're in for a good time. There's a green tea roll or white pearl or something that's stuffed with tempura tuna and topped with another fish and kiwi. Get that. You'll be happy.

But then again, when you order inari and it comes sliced up on top of some sushi rice like a peculiar brown fish, you're probably confused...and you begin to wonder if there isn't something slightly awry with the style of sushi you've ordered.

This is one of the hardest ratings I have had to come up with. My experience can definitely be summed up as hit or miss. 

HITS: outdoor seating, BYOB, the shrimp tempura, 

MISSES: the quality/freshness of fish, corking fees, service

I checked this place out because I had a groupon but don't think I will be back. Maybe I caught them on a bad night but the fish didn't cut it especially with all the other options around town. Looking at "are these photos helpful" none of the presentations for my rolls came close to those quality. In conclusion, yes I have experienced better.

This hotel is actually very well updated with modern decor and flat screen tvs and very comfortable beds. They have a small breakfast consisting of omelets, muffins, sausage, waffles, yogurts and fruit juices to get you going in the morning. Great location to stop when traveling due to there great prices, and convenient location. Staff was also very friendly. The only complaints I have is that the doors do not close properly and as a result you can hear the hallway traffic quite a bit, but I'm not sure if all room are this way or if I was just unlucky. There is a few minor cosmetic issues but for the price I really can't complain.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This walk up restaurant serves authentic Mexican food. Located half a block from Home Depot, this place gets a steady walk up business from the day laborers near the store.

The menu is a bit confusing since I don't speak Spanish fluently, but I managed. Both times I went I ordered some type of soft taco/burrito thing. Both times were with chicken, unless polo means something else. The food is very good. My meals came with a side of salsa that was spicy and delicious. 

Don't be intimidated by the appearance of this place. The food is very good. You wont be disappointed.

I don't know what the big deal is with burger chains and saying that they have the 'best burger' in the world. It was fresh and somewhat like Subway where I could choose what I wanted on my burger, but I've had better. 

I really enjoyed that they had boxes and lose free peanuts though. Very uniqe and a great salty alternative to fries. They also had free refills on drinks as well. The food was somewhat fast - for a fresh burger. There was lots of parking as well.

I don't know if I would go back - lots of other burgers places to still try.

When my mother came to visit I decided I had to get my Daewoo washed and vacuumed properly. At the time this place was on the way to work and open at the hour I needed. Let me tell you my Daewoo is a piece of crapola. It gets me from point A to B and I don't need much else, but it looks like a dinosaur egg and is dirtier than a wombat's belly 99% of the time. SO any wash is better than no washes. It looked ok after, which in Daewoo world means it looked like $100 bucks instead of $10 bucks.

In the end, I really should just do this myself...

Overall okay. 

There's a mix up with carrentals.com and advatage going on right now but at least they are responding to my emails/calls to try to resolve the situation. I suggest just booking directly with the rental place, instead of third parties. 

The woman at the front desk told me that there would be a $200 charge on my card, I've been to other rental places that have a much higher rental car 'deposit' and I received the refund for it about two days later. The drive off and the return were very easy and I had no issues with the car. 

Can't complain about $13.50 a day for a car with 3000 miles on it.

Another fine First Tennessee branch. 

This one is closest to my house and therefore I sometimes stop here for quick deposit my roommate's - I mean boyfriend's share of the rent. I believe this is one of the branches that is open on Saturdays, since if you haven't heard they've closed all but a few select branches in Nashville on Saturdays. Everyone at this branch is also alarmingly friendly and helpful. The traffic light that manages the intersection here is freaky if I do say so myself. I don't think people in the Walgreens lot realize that they should not pull out just because it's red. Be aware is all I got to say!

This is decent lil food/drink option at IND. Added bonus that it is on Priority Pass!

It tends to be a bit busy - sometimes hard to find a place to sit. But if you can sit at the bar the service is usually faster. Out a the tables it can be a little slower since the bartender has to bus them.

The food menu is bar bites mostly and some smaller sandwiches. Nothing amazing but it hits the spot especially when its free with Priority Pass. They have a pretty solid drink menu though!! Lots of local Indiana brews on tap and in bottles.

Decent Japanese place on the south side - it's not the best sushi you'll find in Edmonton, but really, why are you looking for the best sushi you'll ever have in Edmonton anyway? They have some decent rolls, they also have a pretty standard selection of bento boxes, and what you'd normally expect to find. The interior is definitely nicer than average though, I particularly like the little private tables in mini rooms where you take off your shoes at the doorway and then sit around a sunken table - great for groups. Service is generally fine and it's a great choice if you're in the area craving Japanese.

Situated in the same complex as Vegas Tapas and Lee's Cleaners in Old Metairie. This is the spot I go for my BLONDE. Christine has the magic touch. I've never left diasappointed. My hair looks wonderful each time. I've been going to her for years and being a natural brunette she does a wonderful job in the coloring process. I'm Asian and its very hard to get my hair to turn the right shade of color. She knows exactly what she's doing. Highly recommend her! Downside is parking. Hard to find and in a very busy street so beware.

This is probably one of the worst dining experiences I've had in this city. Wings were luke warm and tasted very generic. This location has recently gone through some sort of metamorphosis turning into some sort of Hooters wannabe. Even the waitresses now have to wear short shorts and similar outfits. That doesn't seem appropriate for Magazine St. And what really pissed me off, they blasted the worst shit I've ever heard, when we asked them to turn it down they wouldn't! Music was so loud we couldn't talk to each other.

Authentic, fast, and quite possibly the best Chinese restaurant in the Tampa area. Any time one of my friends wants to eat Chinese food, this is definitely the first place I think of.

It's a great, laid-back, no frills place where every dish is made with love and perfection. While everything is delicious, my favorite item on the menu is the Salt and Pepper Calamari. It's easily in my personal top-3 for best calamari on the east coast.

It's also BYOB, so feel free to bring your own libations. Whether it's a bottle of wine or a case of beer, you won't have to worry about paying $8-$10/glass of wine or $3-$6/beer.

This is Mexican for the American palate, so I am reviewing it as such.   We've been here four or five times and found the quality to be inconsistent.  We finally resolved that you'll get good food if they're not busy.  If it's crowded, the food is likely to come out slow and the quality will be iffy.   

One time we asked how much a pitcher of margaritas was.  The waitress said $10.99, so we ordered it.  When the bill came, the pitcher was actually $15.99.   We asked what happened and she said "sorry - I guess I had the wrong price."  We were not pleased.   

The service is generally not bad other than that one experience.

I found Osteria Natalina on Yelp, and it was just as great as the reviews said it would be!  The staff was very warm and welcoming, and the food was delicious.  

I was impressed by how accommodating of dietary restrictions the staff was - the restaurant is very willing to make any adjustments you need.

 We had the meatballs to start, and they were incredibly flavorful.  The special - a snapper fillet, served on a bed of spinach along with pasta (with a tomato basil sauce) - was also excellent!

I spend a lot of time in Tampa for work, and definitely intend to go back!  Thank you, Yelp, for the great find.

I came here for a sushi with my husband and friend. Reservations were easy through open table and were were seated promptly when we arrived.

Service was decent and the atmosphere is suited for the young professionals crowd. I ordered the super crunchy tuna, spicy crunchy tuna x2, and the salmon skin roll. Rolls were rather small (6 pieces each). The only roll i really liked was the spicy crunchy tuna, though the others were pretty good. Prices were okay, not as good as my favorite place in Maryland.  Overall, a pretty good place to get sushi when I'm in PA.

This hotel was rebranded as a Hyatt Centric (from a normal Hyatt) earlier this year.  The location is great (corner of Canal and Bourbon) and they have balconies that look out on Bourbon Street (got to stay in one of these over Easter).  What the staff sometimes lacks in experience, they more than make up for in hospitality.  I especially found Ben (the front desk manager) and the staff at Powdered Sugar to be very friendly.  Rooms are modern and clean.  Try and get one that looks out onto the street instead of the center courtyard.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
It's in a bit of an odd location, not in the trendy area of downtown. Don't let that throw you off, though.

The restaurant was quiet when I went, but kind of in a calm sort of way. My gal pal and I were seated quickly for lunch and had fun going through the big menu picking out all things Japanese for our midday eat.

Our waitress was great, and although Japanese isn't usually my first choice for a meal, I really liked my food. Plus the company was great :-)

If you're in the downtown area and willing to walk a few blocks off Jasper, definitely check out Mikado.

Mama Mia! One of the only fast-food style pasta places in town. Their system is so easy! Choose a style of noodle, choose a sauce (usually they have meat or alfredo - I would recommend meat), and if you would like, add a side of garlic bread of a salad (go with caesar)! The food is really good here, although it's much fresher at lunch than it is at around dinner time.

La Pasta also carries lighter meals and desserts like paninis and giant cookies. The cookies are just OK, but the staff here are very nice and it's a nice change from a lot of the other fast food fare in this mall!

New favourite liquor store. Just...the best.

I walked in on Friday night and after a few moments browsing on my own, a staff member asked if he could help with anything. I was looking for a good malbec and he showed me three different bottles at three separate price points, which I really appreciated. The middle-point bottle (around $22) was his favourite, so I went with it.

A short encounter, but definitely the most helpful I've had at a liquor store in a long time. I loved the wine, appreciated the helpful but not pushy service, and couldn't believe the selection. Go buy wine here!

This place can be really good ..or really bad 
We went for dinner and it was great. Friendly service ..good food...we really enjoyed it 
We then returned the next day for brunch and it was horrible. The food was served cold.. the service was painfully slow. It was so bad we cashed out and went to the bar so we could actually get some service. It took... literally...20mins to cash out. Absolutely sucked!
Once we got to the bar the tender was nice and right on top of things. 
I'll go back ...and just hope for the best.

My husband & I love this place. Their mussels are soooo good. The beef carpaccio was so thin it stuck to the plate but once we pried it off it was delicious. The bocaccini did not live up to its description. The service is top notch. Prices are very reasonable and the wine list offers lots of selections. There's a nice bar area you can eat in or opt for a nicely lit cozy table. We came for our anniversary and had extra treats given to us by the server/management and would recommend this place for anyone (except those damn tourists and those with kids)

My hubby & I love the selection of imported beers here. It's nice you can mix & match 6 packs so he gets what he wants, and I get what I want. The store itself is in an iffy part of town and the guys that work there sure do like to flirt it up but even if your hubby is with you. I ignore the homeless guys outside by the bus station and the creepy proprietors and run in and out grab what you want, and be on your way. Mix and match six packs will cost you over $12 but that's what us picky people get! OH, and watch the employees faces when someone comes in looking for Bud or PBR, I swear they're physically remove them if they could! : )

Okay so we got luckier last time.  The chipotle sliders were definitely better when we were here before.  Service was better.  But we had a lot of time to kill anyway, so at least it was a place to sit and listen to music.  

This time the chipotle sauce that came on the side of the sliders tasted like plain ketchup.  Burgers were dry and tasteless.  Buns not bad.  Fries not bad.  Chips okay.

Place feels like it could use a good cleaning. Prices high.  

Food choices in this terminal continue to suck.  This cafe might suck a bit less than some of the others.

Definitely smaller then other National Car Rental... I walked out to the shuttle, thankfully the shuttle came after few minutes, the bus was full... the bus pulled up and I was the last to get out and unfortunately by the time I got out, vehicle selection was minimal... either a F150, Minivan or sedan... then I found a Hyundai SUV, got in and found that the seats where manual... after getting myself situated, they brought another SUV, so I got out and took that one.

Returning the car was simple... just dropped off the car and went to the bus and in few minutes, I got my receipt via email.  Overall, not bad experience.

Let's be real here. How much can one really expect from airport food or airport establishments other than overpriced junk food and a full bar? This place is no exception. Ten dollars for nachos, add a diet coke and it's a fifteen dollar tab of mediocrity. Had the service been better and more efficient, I might bump it up a star. But having one server for over 40 seats is ridiculous. It took minutes just to get water. This is the only spot to sit, drink a beer and catch some ESPN. I prefer the grab and go counter next door.

If you're looking for a semi hand wash of decent quality this is an ok spot. Classic car wash offers the option to have a standard machine wash as well as a 100% hand wash service. Opting for the hand wash service is going to cost you  upwards of $25 dollars. Overall quality really depends on who washes your car. I've also had my car detailed here which included a shampoo of all the car mats for over $75.00, which I did not find to be a super thorough job. I likely wouldn't bring my car back for a detail here but I'll keep it on my list of places to go for hand wash car wash.

St. Mary's Mexican Food reminds of Nico's taco shop in a lot ways. The food, at least what we ordered, is on par with a fast food taco joint. It's fast and cheap, but not the greatest, in my opinion. I have not tried some of their signature items like the menudo and red chile. Out order was two tostadas, carne seca burro and a breakfast burrito (bacon, egg , potato, cheese). They were a-ok. The highlight of the breakfast burrito is that the potatoes are finely diced. I wish more places would do it that way! The line was a little long but moved fast. However, that's not always the case. You can call for pick up and that's highly recommended.

In terms of equipment, this Webster/Crestwood/Shrewsbury/SW City area gym has THE BEST and they offer a basic monthly membership for only $19. 

Up until recently, they have focused on award-winning bodybuilding programs, but they now offer spinning, yoga, aerobic classes and weight control programs/products. 

Watch out for some of the trainers though. If you get hurt doing what they tell you to do, you're screwed. They do not back up their instructions or take responsibility for inexperienced or uncertified trainers.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Cheap, friendly dive bar filled with smoke, and locals from the neighborhood.  This place is no frills, in fact the bartender sits until you hail her for a bevvie.So, if service is your thing, this may not be your place.  But, locals like it when they need a no frills gathering place in Soulard, minus the meat market and fake boobs.   I think the key words are CHEAP, familiar, and low key.  Always busy, always smoky.  The bars on the window can be a little intimidating, but don't that that scare you.  It's a pretty normal neighborhood bar.

The Neighborhood Car Wash is a somewhat economical self serve car wash that is conveniently located near Arsenal on Kingshighway.  I'm not particularly fond of this car wash, but it's okay in a pinch. They have all of the basics like self serve and automatic stalls in good working order.  The layout of the vacuums isn't great.  One vacuum gets in the way of the driveway where the cars are leaving the stalls and there are no vacuums at the automatic stalls.  the car wash is mostly unmonitored with questionable characters and the occasional panhandler.

As others have explained, Cafe Mochi looks like a coffee bar. It's a small space, with a small patio. They have an AWESOME happy hour with 1/2 price sushi/rolls. The discount is on basic maki, not specialty rolls that tend to be bigger/more elaborate, but it IS an awesome deal when you only pay 3 bucks for any sushi. 

Unfortunately, it gets so packed during happy hour. Too packed, but good news is coming! Expansion! Cafe Mochi is expanding to the building next door and they will have a second patio. So, starting in mid- August, I will be more confident about going for happy hour. Yay!

Terrible. Do not go here for tires. I went here and they only carried the most expensive version of my tires. They were rude too. I really needed new tires and one of mine was flat so they thought they could box me in.

 I went to Pep Boys across the street. They gave me better tires, free install, better warranty, and all for $200 less. Plus, they checked my brakes free of charge because I wanted to know how long until the pads needed replacing. They also agreed to mount my tire on a rim for a spare when I bring it in next time, free of charge. 

Sears was a bad experience and Pep Boys will be my place for tires from this day forward.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
this place is totally run by wai guo ren, i.e. there is NO CHINESE MENU.  what you see is what you get.

however, as a consolation you should be happy to know that this is perhaps the CLEANEST chinese take out place i've ever been to.

some things i like:

-  combo lunch plates: cheap, comes with rice, a choice of dish, crab rangoon, and egg roll
-  the hot and sour soup


what i wish they had:
-  larger sizes for the hot and sour soup

to reiterate:  THERE IS NO AUTHENTIC CHINESE FOOD HERE.  but the orange chicken is tasty.

best sushi in st. louis, by far.

the chirashi bowl is generous.  this means i couldn't finish it.  great bang for your buck.  grilled squid appetizer can be chewy, but the sweet teriyaki/soy sauce is very tasty.  

occasionally kampai has uni, which is really hard to find in st. louis.  ASK if they have it, because when they do, the heavens open up and angels sing as you take each bite.  delicious.  one day, i'll retire, buy a sea urchin farm, and spend my twilight years tending to them/snacking.

limited free parking in the garage below.  love this place.

If you want hand crafted, perfectly balanced and delicious espresso drinks, Sump is the place for you! They aim to make the perfect cup of coffee each and every time and they have achieved that goal in every visit I've made. The single reason that I don't give them a full 5 starts is simply the time it takes to get your drink. Since they take the time to perfect each order, you could end up waiting 10 minutes on a light day or more than 30 minutes on a busy day. If visiting Sump, plan on hanging out in the cool decor and comfortable surroundings as you await the caffeinated deliciousness that you will receive!

As a new resident to the area----I have never been in a Schnucks store previously.  This grocery is one of the closest to my home and I actually really like it.  It is clean, not too busy, and I was greeted by several employees during my trip there.  The produce area looked crispy and fresh and I found the prices to be better than Dierbergs.   I am very picky about meat and was eating mostly meats from the Whole Food Store in my previous city---I was not put-off by the look of some of their meat selections so I decided to try some beef and pork cuts.  I have since cooked them and they were good.

ummm okay they were nice enough here I didn't feel uncomfortable or anything and the mani-pedi was only 30.00 but I would have enjoyed a more posh situation and appreciated a little more care when doing my nails...it was very wham-bam thank you mam type place....they seem to have some happy and loyal regulars here but i'm not sure why because the decor and lay out suck and they massage they attempt to do was just in a nutshell weird.....they go thru the motions but I left without any satisfaction....they didn't get my cuticles good enough nor did they give my feet a hard enough rub with the pumice.....

i am updating my review only because I have been going here at least once a week and I am disturbed by the window up front that they have racks of candy pushed in front of and there is just wads and wads of dust bunnies and dirt and dead insects accumulating and nobody can even get to it to clean it.  I blame this on bad management....if I was in charge at the store the first impression of  that window front would be a priority to make it sparkle.....the bathroom was also so dirty that I decided to "hold it" until I got home....there seems to be a problem with cleaning as of late.....get it together Schnucks!

I ordered some take-out from here a couple weeks ago, and it was decent enough. There was a special for 10 wings and a large pizza for $18 or so - and it was definitely enough for three people to split for dinner. The pizza was thin and greasy, but did the job. The customer service here was not spectacular, in fact - a little bit sarcastic and insulting, but I guess that's the South Philly charm here. I would return again for an inexpensive bite, but I'll check out some of the other pizzeria's in the area first.

It's hard to rate a bank, since they're all essentially offering the same things at very competitive rates. However, TD stands out from the crowd for their late night and weekend hours, dog and kid-friendliness, and bright cheerful atmosphere in the branches.

I recently brought a bunch of change over to the branch, and had it counted by their animated automatic counter. When it's finished, you receive a receipt, and the teller can credit your account for the funds! Easy & fun way to feel a nice payback on your pocket change.

Thanks, TD!

Supreme is a-ok. It gets the job done better than Fresh Grocer... but you'll have to shop the specials at either grocery store to get the best deals. 

Supreme has a large produce selection, the basic deli and bakery departments, and all of your standard generic and name-brand shelf items. The size of the store and selection of items in general is the best you'll find in West Philly / University City.

I've found customer service here to be less than par, and the security guards standing every few feet throughout the "customer service" area is a little intimidating. 

I'll visit every now and then... but it's no Trader Joe's!

For local sushi, this is the best.  I've come here more times than I can count and have never had a bad meal, or service.  And my Japanese friend thinks it's good, so it must be, right?!

While all the sushi is always good and super fresh, I absolutely love their spicy tuna.  I don't know what they do to it, but it's so delicious.  

There is hibachi upstairs, and outside seating in the warmer months.  Reservations are most definitely recommended for weekend nights.  But be forewarned...if you won't be able to make your reservation, call to let them know.  They keep a black list posted by the hostess stand!

BYOB

I stopped in here because I was craving steamed veggies and shrimps after my intense workout. I was concerned that they wouldn't have any, but much to my surprise. I checked out the back of their menu, and found their diet menu on the bottom of the page!  So happy! I'm doing an eight-week healthy eating and fitness challenge, so I was very glad to see this option. This take out place is a hole in the wall, but offer lots of great dishes that I cannot have, but I'm glad they offer healthier alternatives. (Part of my #fitfood #8weekchallenge)

The menu is pretty standard. Sandwiches, Burgers, Pizza, about 5 different salads. I had a turkey club that was pretty decent,  nothing special. Entirely not enough bacon on it :(

My friends had, Fish and Chips (looked great, and the tarter sauce was really good with a fry)  and a tuna melt ( He gave it a thumbs up and a nod when asked about it).

The park bench in a grassy area is nice to sit in on a nice warm day. Some had an umbrella for those of the fairer skin...or are just sun wussies. Lots of rug rats running around and some folks actually had dogs with them.  Watch for dive bombing seaguls.

This place maybe has some of the better Korean food in town. The sushi is fine, but that spicy pork is awesome.
Interior is awkward in its size, the lights are kept low even though it's very far from a fancy place, and its strip mall is a lot dumpier than you would think for the far east side. Prices are a little high. I also called one time at 5pm on a Wednesday to try to get take out sushi (3 rolls) and was told it would take 90 minutes. Weirdness all around, but sushi places in Tucson are generally a little weird.
But definitely try the Korean food.

My veal pomodoro might have been the worst meal I have had in a long time.  That being said, the lobster ravioli was delicious, the rack of lamb was a huge portion and the roasted salmon was tasty too.

I think the restaurant is way too cramped.  It is beyond "cozy" to the point of making it difficult to get out of certain seats without having your entire party get up.  It was kind of fun, but kind of not.

They also overbook, so be prepared to wait even if you have a reservation.  I've been to way too many good BYOs in Philly to warrant more than 2 stars.

When I walked into this bar, I knew something just felt right.  After initially thinking it was just my general love of the macabre, I realized that between the skeletons and skulls adorning the place was Chicago swag!  Being originally from Chicagoland, it felt like a little bit of home.  Beyond that, the atmosphere in this bar was just cool.  As I was here in the summer, I'm sure it wasn't as crazy as it gets when school is in, but the drinks were strong, the staff friendly, and reminders of home everywhere - what more could a girl want?

I've only been here once, on a Thurs, and we were the only people in the bar.  They have $.50 beer, but only Busch light...ewww.  I had a 312 that was reasonably priced anyhow.  The bartender was really nice, and talked to us quite a bit as she was clearly quite bored with how dead it was, and the door guy was nice as well.  I think I might have a totally different view of this bar if I went there when it was busy, as it has never enticed me to go in when walking by on a busy Saturday, but since I haven't been in during that time, I'll only review the one experience I had there, which was good.

This place is fantastic.  I've been coming here for about a year and half and both my hair and I couldn't be happier.  The first time I went, I booked with Mo for a cut and color.  She is awesome.  She listened to everything I had to say and made absolutely sure we were both on the same page before she started.  Both my cut and color were fab., I've gotten so many compliments.  I've gone to Mo several times since that first visit and I've never been disappointed.  Love her & the salon, everyone there is so friendly it's really a great experience all around.

Wowza. Someone doesn't often expect any South Philly establishment off the beaten path (aka Passyunk) to serve non-food-poisoning-containing raw fish (SPTR aside).  But Hibachi2Go breaks the mold and serves decently fresh sashimi, delicious rolls and a slew of tasty salads/teriyaki, and at penny pincher prices.  Not to mention they deliver. What a score!

Don't be frightened of this place - it's legit.  Not "OMG YOU'LL DIE WHEN YOU EAT THIS" sushi, but "YUM YUM THIS HITS THE SPOT" sushi.  And for more than fair prices.  Serious South Philly score.

Note: I am not a roll fan, but try the Special Boston.

Had to start of the night with one of Tropical Isle's infamous hand grenades which come in frozen as well as on ice. It was packed the night we went in but service was fairly quick. I see now why they call it the grenade..I started sipping away and was like " oh wow this is just a sweet drink".... a few blocks later down Bourbon Street I was like " wwwwooowweee I drink this like".... Definitely sneaks up on you quick! Yes it is touristy, but resist the urge to pass it up, and join the hundreds of other walking down Bourbon with a little green cup!

this place has the most amazing sushi i have ever tasted. the rolls are unique and you can't find them elsewhere. the bill will be high, but it is so worth it. this is one of the places i miss the most because i have moved back to the bay area. and even with the unlimited sushi places here, i doubt i will ever find a place like Sakana. 

however, if you ever order take out, make sure to check the box. once, i was given someone else's order, but luckily i checked before i drove away. they gave me a complimentary edamame :-).

This Publix perplexes me. Around the corner is the Gandy Publix (literally, around the corner) and when you count, you realize there are 5 Publix markets south of Kennedy. When I moved to Gainesville for grad school, this was a pretty terrible Albertson's... maybe when the lease runs out on the Gandy store they'll consolidate to a single space. 

The store itself is pretty nice - newer than the Gandy store, and certainly well appointed. 

Britton Plaza continues on, in spite of its need for a serious upgrade.

I like having Fresh Market here, although I do most of my shopping at Publix - I stop in here for the odd specialty item, prepared food or specialty cheese that one would expect here.

Tonight I found some corn tortillas that were out of this world, and made my basic tacos simply outstanding. And a fresh ripe avocado that literally burst with flavor. Oh, and I hate them for piling up the Ritter Sport at the check out and making me buy some. Hate I tell you.

Course, I'm old enough to remember when this space was a USave supermarket - yeah... I'm old.

When I lived in Hampton Terrace, this was my Publix. Smaller than many, it replaced a beloved Deco store that even still had the original green virtalite 'wings' on either side. Honestly, they should have saved the facade and built a new store behind it - not a big fan of the Faux Deco replacement... although  it is superior to their usual bland suburban look.

Inside, the place is cheerful, with the usual Publix efficiency and a decent offering of vittles. Given the size of the joint, they are in permanent restock mode from open to close. At least you don't have to worry about anything having sat too long!

Yes, this is a motel and a little bit dated, but it was an economical solution to one night in Nashville to do a little sight-seeing.  

There is a very large flat-screen TV in the room, which was nice and a pleasant surprise.  Breakfast was meh.  Various options, but nothing incredible.  

The water pressure is really strong, which was nice for the shower.  But then the toilet flushed really strongly and loudly each time, which kind of startled me.  

We walked to the pedestrian bridge during daylight, and the neighborhood looked a bit shady.  So we took an Uber back after when it got dark.  The walk is about 30 minutes if you want to do that.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Angelo's is your typical Italian take out assortment of pizzas, pastas, sandwiches, etc. Their pizza is pretty good, pastas are nothing spectacular, and I generally default to the chicken wrap, which fills you up. The fries are pretty good, and they have some good mozarella sticks. 

Food arrives in a timely fashion, not much to say. About half the time you ask for something customized, like sauce on the side or something, they forget. Such is average delivery food. If you're looking for a cheese steak, however, Slack's Might be the better option.

This place is fly!

Seriously, there was a fly in the creamer, which I found when I poured it into my coffee.

Not a fan, although the waiter was awesome about it.  Otherwise, ate here for breakfast while staying at the hotel and it was so-so.  Typical buffet, though the eggs and the homefries were good.  Limited seleciton otherwise and the women at the front door were the least helpful and least hospitable humans I've ever seen work a hostess stand.  You had to ask them questions just to get them to seat you...they offered nothing except vacant stares and fake smiles.

I only come here for the ice vanilla coffee. For this type of coffee, they usually put 70% of milk + vanilla and the remain 30% is coffee. What I like about the coffee at this place is they give you more coffee, which is perfect for caffeine addicts like myself. The coffee is also very cheap. Medium for $2.19 and Large is for $2.50. 

Occasionally I would get the chicken nuggets. For some reason, they don't taste as good as other McDonald's...they seem drier. Deep fried to death? 

I've never been inside before and not planning to go in anytime soon. This isn't a  very nice neighborhood after all.

2013/#36
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
The food is great and the service friendly. Prices are okay. Shrimp and cream gnocci was $16 not including tax/tip. The quality was great and I wish they had a more extensive menu! Came here for a large birthday party, and they were very accommodating despite our obnoxious and loud behavior. Would definitely come back.

Food is delicious. The bread is standard (wish they had balsamic vinegar for it).  Prices are standard for expensive italian in general. Service is great. I'd give them four stars if they had more choices.

We had our office Christmas party here a few weeks ago. Matt, the manager, was very helpful and attentive with planning the event. We were placed in the big room for our party which accommodated us nicely. The food was buffet style and served quickly. The food was traditional pub food and was tasty. My only gripe was that the waitress had to come back to fill drinks such as soda and iced tea. It would benefit them more to have pitcher readily available for parties. Over all I was pleased and hope to return for a burger and a beer.

I stopped in here the other night without an appointment to get my eyebrows waxed solely based on the reviewed I read on Yelp.  After checking in with the front desk and very short wait, Jade came to greet me and fix the mess I made of my caterpillar brows.  She was extremely friendly and did a really great job cleaning up my horrendous brows for a mere $10.

The woman at the front desk gave me a price listing for all the services - the prices looked very reasonable.  I've been spreading the word to my friends and will definitely be returning here in the future for a haircut and possibly a color.

Thanks, Yelp!

Wonderful as usual. I don't know our server's name but she's the best. I had my boyfriend go and put our name in case the lunchtime blonde was working haha. 
We love this place and it's a Friday night treat for us. I was tired and just had diet coke instead of Sake and boyfriend had one beer only, so it wasn't too expensive. 
We had to wait almost 20 minutes, which was odd given there was almost no one waiting. It's not unusual on a summer night to see a horde of people outside. 
Everyone had just sat down when we arrived around 8PM during this late year heat, but it was very fast once we got seated.

Dante's is a good, easy pop-in for a quick slice of 'za off of Bourbon. The pepperoni slice was good, not greasy. Service is fast. I like the flat screen and fish tank decor here- reminds me of something a place might do near Times Square in NYC. 

Sat here for a bit, as we finished our 'za, and in walks in the Devil himself, the Imp of Imps, Satan- to touch up his red makeup, and have a potty break. Satan was nice. And nobody at Dante's blinked an evil eye.

The owner came by our table and teased us for sitting there and playing Cards Against Humanity; but in the nicest of ways. At least I think he was kidding! ;)

I took one star off after my second try at Jonny Primo's. We ordered Chef's special Osso Buco that our waitress highly recommended. I almost dropped my jaw when I saw the dish. 3 tiny undercooked veal shanks and a pile of tomato sauce pasta was a huge disappointment for us. It was tasteless. My home cook Osso Buco is much better. 

I can only assume that it was the off day for head chef. If they keep serving food like this, we won't be going back. 

Although, price is still reasonable and very family friendly. I will give it a try again in the near future.

This place is so hot and cold, I can never fully form a true opinion on it. But if consistency is a hallmark of a quality establishment, then Pizza Rustica needs to get it together! Sometimes you come in and the service will be pretty good and you'll get lucky with some recently cooked slices. Other times your so turned off by the attitudes of the guys behind the counter that you just walk out and ask yourself why you keep coming back there...sucks because its a pretty good location and I've enjoyed it once or twice in the past.

Casa Grande is definitely not horrible, and light-years beyond the "other" mexican chain restaurant down the street. I've been here twice- the first time was pretty good, the second was just.. eh. Although, the second time I was in a party of 10, so I can't really fault them for that. The food is good- the ranch-like sauce served with the chips is.. different. Not bad, but I can't see myself inhaling the entire bowl as I would with salsa. The chips are fantastic. I've had enchiladas both times and they were decent. Overall not a bad place, but considering this place isn't exactly "local" to me, I'll stick to my "local" in the Irv.

I've been here twice and both experiences were underwhelming.  The food doesn't necessarily taste bad, but it just seems generic.  The presentation is poor considering my Lasagna was served in a ceramic skillet (think Denny's) and it was just drenched in sauce and cheese.  I would imagine some people would like this, but it just too much for me. 

The new addition is a lot nicer looking than the older dining area which kind of gives off a Max & Erma's in a hotel feeling.  

Iaria's is really better all around if you're going to eat Italian on South College.

Even in my least sober state, this place barely deserves two stars.  The band plays the usual crowd-pleasing tunes (like Snoop Dogg) and stretches them out over 5-6 minutes too long.  The crowd is split between the drunken dancers and sing-along-ers in the front and those watching the mess closer towards the bar.  The beers on tap are lame and to top it off, they're ridiculously priced.  We spent $7 on Bud and Bud Light in a plastic party cup.  This place is not worth your money, but if you can get in without a cover and listen to a band for free, then why the heck not? :)

We just tried Las Margaritas for lunch today. They moved into where Rotolo's used to be. It's a very colorful and lively place, as you would expect a Mexican restaurant to be. They have seating both upstairs and downstairs. We arrived just before the lunch crowd.

The staff is very friendly and attentive. The menu is fairly large. They provide you with free chips and salsa. I got the Chicken Quesadilla lunch plate and my co-worker got the Taco Salad. Both were good.

It's a good place to go for a work lunch. They get your food to you pretty quick. We will definitely be back.

Pretty good quality food for a decent price. I wouldn't say it's the best pizza in the city, but it was really good. (I think Slice is the best.)

A friend and I had an early dinner here. It was quiet and slow when we were there, so I don't know how it gets on a busy night.

We split a House Salad and a Margherita Pizza. Both were excellent. For dessert, we split a featured special they were having that night. I can't recall the name, but they were sort of like dark chocolate donut holes with raspberry sauce to dip them in. Yum..

Our server was very friendly and attentive.

Cool place.

I like it when it's cold. 
I like it when it's hot. 
I like to eat frozen yogurt.. a lot.

This place is so yummy it attempts to turn me into a poet so I may sing its praises!

The location parking leaves a bit to be desired (small lot, narrow lanes) but it's close to home and has a great selection.

The staff is always ready and willing to offer up suggestions of their faves, samples of the new flavors and a spoon when you're ready to dig in!

No matter what the temperature is outside, stop by and enjoy some fro yo!

The customer service at this place has come quite far since I used to visit. These days they are on point with the customer service.

The flavors have always been great and now the service matches the quality of the product.

This past holiday season we enjoyed one of their holiday cakes - we did a turkey ice cream cake with camouflage colored ice cream inside. It was a hit and may actually become a new tradition for our holiday times.

Whenever I crave a scoop I head over to this spot and check out their new flavors. My latest fave is Baseball nut - vanilla with peanuts and a blackberry swirl.

this place could be so much better.  

first off, how does a hotel in the french quarter not have a lobby bar?? 

second, while i was there they were experiencing some elevator issues.  by this i mean we had to wait (literally) 10 minutes for an elevator to come.  of the 3 they have, only 1 was in order.  and when we weren't waiting for the elevator to get to our floor, we were waiting on the extremely long line in the lobby.  on our last day we had to carry all of our luggage down 10 flights of stairs. 

the room was ok, i wouldn't say it was spectacular.  definitely not worth what we paid.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Who knew shade grown, organic coffee from Alabama would be so yummy? That's probably why I drank about 3 cups of it and then ended up bouncing off the walls for a few hours afterwards (which made me productive but probably quite annoying).

Make sure to give yourself enough time and room in your belly for some of the food - the sandwiches are great. This is the perfect place to hang out for a while and get some work done - with its free wireless, friendly staff and a good vibe, this just might be my new office away from home!

I had lunch here on a recent sunny day with a friend - we sat outside, drank beer we brought from the Foodery (A Full Plate is BYO) and enjoyed the great service from a sweet waiter with black framed glasses (thank you!). The menu choices were extensive and really well-priced, but my attempt to go healthy kinda backfired on me. I got the Monster Wrap, which was, indeed monster sized, but also monster spicy for me. Yes, yes, it did say spicy sauce on the menu. Guess I was too engrossed in my conversation to pay attention. Life lesson #162 brought to you by your pal Carrie.

While I respect the 1st reviewers comments, I live a couple buildings away from the Cat's Meow and have spent a substantial amount of time there. One thing I like about the Cat's Meow is doesn't just attract one crowd...on any given night there could be a group of college kids, a couple of yuppies, a large handful of blue collars, and that mix of in-betweens. The $1 shots, cheap drink specials, and general dive atmosphere makes it a good starter location (or ending for us, so we can just stumble home afterwards). Only place in the city I can start and finish an evening for under $10.

I used to go here a lot with my family as a kid.  Went back last night for the first time in years.  Despite a lot of booths, they seem to have a mostly takeout clientele.  

It's a typical pizza parlor setting.  Nothing fancy.  Hard booths and some game machines.  The panzarotti was a HUGE pizza turnover (not fried like the original panzarotti.  But my aunt loved it.  I ordered a chicken sandwich.  They clarified (steak or sandwich) and I said sandwich.  I got a chicken cheesesteak.  I specifically said no cheese.  Whatever.

If you're in the area and need food, this is a place to go.

I am reviewing this as a venue for events - I have never eaten in the regular restaurant. 

The private 2nd floor is a completely hidden gem in Rittenhouse. It's a long room with a capacity of maybe 60, very bright, with bathrooms and an elevator. The events manager Candace really paid attention to the details with her table settings and the cleanliness of the space, which made our event (a singles event) feel special. They also made a custom menu for us. I run many events and this is one of the best spaces in the city, for sure.

This was a great hotel and great experience! It was modern (recently renovated), quiet, the service was great and they offered a plentiful complementary breakfast each morning. Plus, they had an indoor pool!  I forgot my suit, but one morning while my friend was still sleeping, I ate and then read magazines poolside and it felt more "tropical" that way! Jessica and Sheneke, in particular, were awesome and our favorite employees! -Especially, Jessica: she remembered us and always greeted us in such a friendly way each day! We felt Philadelphia, overall, was a super friendly and accommodating city!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I'm itching to tack another star onto this review just for being the only place that will deliver pizza to me until 4 o'clock in the morning, but really everything was just average. We ordered a pizza and two types of wings. Contrary to some other reviews, everything arrived fresh and hot. The pepperoni pizza was good, just not great. The buffalo and barbecue wings both tasted the same. Make of that what you will.

At another time of day, I'm sure I'd order from somewhere else, but in a 3 a.m. pinch Gay Pizza will do.

So this place's schtick is they are real-down-home cookin'.  And they pull it off pretty well.  During brunch with mum, I had something that resembled eggs in a basket (or toad in the hole) and it was pretty good.  The potatoes were a cut above and everything was done pretty well.  

The interior had that generic style of bold colors followed by knick-knacks on the wall.  It's funny how these types of places are the anti-applebees but then sort of emulate them.

I say that you use this place as some sort of secret backup in case the line for Honey's is wrapped around the block.

Oh, Lord. 

Hand grenades. 

DO NOT think you can defeat the hand grenade. This is an impossibility. I tried. Oh, how I tried. I tried five or six times, in fact, before succumbing to the liquid contained within. Keep in mind, each one has SEVEN ounces of liquor in it, so I was about a step away from full-blown alcohol poisoning before my gf took it from my hand and stopped me from drinking the rest. 

These things go down smooth; they do not come up smooth. Pace yourself, eat a po' boy, and for the love of god - don't guzzle these one after the other as I did.

The polar opposite of nearby East 8 or Spamp's, you won't find Jersey Shore yuppies dancing to a DJ here.  This place features all the necessary features of a true dive bar: jukebox on the wall, familiar beers on draft, all in a down-to-earth atmosphere.  Casmar serves this crowd well.

Their prices are reasonable and the bartenders are approachable.  They sell 6-packs to go, which is a plus.  So why 3-stars, you ask?  I can't find anything distinctly wrong with Casmar, its just not memorable or significant.

The interior has this country meets culinary kind of feel.  The white fences that line the wall are matched by the "open" kitchen that really allows the wonderful smells to breathe throughout the restaurant.

Having lived in the city, I've seen my fair share of BYOBs but it isn't often you find one that accepts credit cards or mixers to match your alcoholic drink of choice.  It's the little things that make this place a true 5-star.

Started with the pumpkin risotto cake, a unique dish whose taste was matched only by the presentation.  The GF and I both raved about our dishes.

Highly recommended for a nice date night.

Was going to Brooklyn but decided to try something new.

Picked up a large extra cheese pizza, 10" shrimp avocado pizza and the large garden salad.

The cheese pizza had tons and tons of cheese.  Good crust and good sauce.  

The shrimp avocado was decent but a little garlicky.  

The garden salad was terrible.  Looks like lettuce they put on your sandwich at Subway with some shredded cheese and a few sliced tomatoes.

Not running back but overall not terrible pizza.  Price was decent (~$30) for the whole meal.

They do NOT accept AMEX.  Absolutely no reason for this....

The food is three-star, and the service is zero or one star.
Yet another restaurant that pours all its effort into the decor, looking to lure people into a horrible or mediocre dining experience.
I went with a group of Japanese students years ago, and everyone remarked at how rude and inattentive the waitress was. I understand Japanese have much higher standards in this but even I was finding myself irritated and I'm very lenient with waitstaff.
Food was mediocre, especially for the price.
I'm not sure about Hikaru's other locations, but the one experience was bad enough that I don't care to give them a second chance.

Love the location and the design of this place. But ... The service is the worst that I've ever experienced at a Starbucks.

One friend shares on Facebook the following: "The female morning manager is an idiot, and rude on top of it all. I'll drive to the CWE to avoid this place. Glad I'm not alone in thinking this place is a cluster."

The place is gaining a bad reputation with people who would be very loyal to the store because of the history of the locatin. Unfortunately, the treatment of customers by the staff is chasing people away.

Starbucks needs to seriously get a staff attitude adjustment in place or it will probably only get worse.

I have used this place because they deliver to my building, not because they're good

I left a blazer with them to have a button sewed back on.  It fell off again after one wear.  Shoddiest repair work I ever had done.

there's this weird negotiation of when I can get my clothes done by, and the time frame is very inconsistent

Also, I think they're one of the most expensive places in the city.


2 stars for location and delivery, but no stars for the actual work product, and in the end, isn't that what counts?
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Eek! These guys need help badly! The hostess was new and did everything in her power to remind us of it, every second of the way. I recommend the "fake it until you make it" method. Just smile and do your best. 
Anyway, instead of having a hostess they ought to train one more server... you know what? Just email me... I've got tons of ideas and years of FOH experience. 
The menu looked good, but we couldn't order. It took 45 minutes to be seated, order a beer and get a check. We only saw our server when she dropped the tab. The poor, untrained hostess had to pour a beer.

maybe it was because i was really, really hungry the last time i ate at (the other) sushi garden. or maybe because i at at the other sushi garden. but this time i wasn't as thrilled. the food was still good, it filled me up, but it wasn't quite as tasty.

i guess that sounds really weird, seeing as they're the same restaurants and everything.

the service was okay. the girl that waited us (even though we got the lunch buffet) seemed peeved that i asked for white rice instead of taking fried rice from the line.

for the price, you still can't beat this though.

we celebrated my sister-in-law's dirty thirty last night. after the initial celebration, we ended up at whiskey tango on broadway/kolb.

there was a bouncer at the door who was super nice. he told us there was a $5 cover per person for a journey tribute band.

the place was nicer than i expected. actually, i am not sure exactly what i was expecting. i guess i was expecting it to be more divey. 

everyone enjoyed their drinks. there was quite a crowd in there, but lots of room to accommodate people. 

the tribute band was pretty good, they played all the classics.

Pricey Airport Starbucks

SITREP

They have the basic level 2 Starbucks products & service available at this location.

THE SETUP

I am not a fan of a Starbucks - whether it be in an Airport or a Stadium, etc. - that uses the location as an excuse to charge up to 35%-50% more for their product.

Paid nearly $3 more for the Venti Blonde & Sausage Breakfast sandwich I could have gotten for less at my home Starbucks.

THE LOWDOWN

They got most of the goods you want at a Starbucks, but they will make you pay for the "privilege" of being in an airport.

First off, not a fan of sushi. :-( I know, I know, what not to like? But I did taste a spicy tuna roll and it was pretty good. The tuna was not too spicy, just had a hint of heat. The Yaki Soba noodles with chicken was very good. Fresh veggies and small cut chicken. The Tempura Combination plate was delicious, fresh fried veggies and teriyaki chicken. Plenty of food for possibly two if you get sushi rolls too.

Very small place, but I enjoyed myself. There must only be 12 tables and 10 chairs at the sushi bar.

The restaurant is a little small, but they do offer out door seating and have a nice view. Each table is made with a tile masaic on top. I have gone for breakfast and lunch. 

Breakfast is good with their homemade beans. Tortillas are being made right in front of you if you are sitting inside. My favorite dish is the chicken tacos with the hard shell and Horchata to drink :) The salsa is very good as well. You can ask for a mild sauce if you need. Service I have recieved has always been good and attentive.

It's a nice place to go for lunch with family and/or friends.

I have been trying for over two weeks to get reimbursed for the portion of my car rental that a repair shop is supposed to be covering. I've talked to managers in person and talked to at least three different people on the phone. Each time, they say they will call me back but never do. 

All of this on top of getting a smelly, dirty car to begin with. Seriously, it was disgusting--like a bunch of college kids had just brought it back from Bonnaroo. I had to go to the Enterprise office at the airport to get a clean car. 

It's a shame that I have to write this because my first experience here was actually really great.

I have to say that this place was pretty terrible. We sat at the bar and the bartender took almost 10 minutes just to acknowledge us. We ended up getting our own menus because after acknowledging us, she didn't come back again for another 10 minutes. The other diners near us didn't look too happy either. The food itself was just okay. It's your average American food chain restaurant. The food took some time to come out (surprise) and the fries were cold, but it just wasn't worth it to complain. I wouldn't come back here by choice.

Frag out. (as we say in the Army) As a person who qualified expert with grenades I managed to easily make the throw of the grenade into the little nets that hang from the ceiling.

Of course I had to have a hand grenade or two while visiting New Orleans. And what a potent drink it is.... (at least so far as I remember) Their nachos were adequate (making up for a lack of quality with quantity).

One neat note, they have a "skinny" hand grenade now. While made from artificial sweeteners, the drink came off as less sweet than the original (I kind of liked it better). And of course it still has the same punch as the original.

As they say in real estate location is everything..

What better place to swing by after a hard run or a long ride and enjoy a refreshing beverage or two :)  The Lakehouse House become a regular stop for me after my Friday afternoon cycling and with a big salad and a delicious IPA before I head home.

Menu  and drink selections are good, service is always excellent and friendly, and although I ave never been around for the band, the staff seem very enthusiastic about the performers.  So rent a Kayak on a weekend morning then wander down for a lunch sitting and admiring Mallard Lake..you will not be disappointed :)

Someone had to bring you here first! You would miss it if you did not know where you were going. Higher Grounds is a cosy place to be on the edge of NoLibs. The mood set in here is what all coffeehouses should model themselves after. I have been here many times and never have I heard a loud obnoxious conversation or seen any rude people in general. This is a great place to have a meeting or just sit back with a book. I've escaped here for hours with my MAC wondering if I could Bonjour everyone in the place. but, no one with a MAC really uses Bonjour, so... I LOVE HIGHER GROUNDS! I chatted them up about doing some events there...stay tuned!

Vic's Sushi is so cheap that you can't help not liking it.  They deliver a decent radius around the establishment and they sell Arizona Green Tea(a big plus for me).  

The sushi here(currently) is adequate.  It hovers the exact middle ground between excellent and mediocre.  When they first opened, their food seemed much fresher, but lately things have slipped a little bit and I've been searching for replacement sushi joints.  

Don't get me wrong - this place is definitely worth checking out, and you wil get full before you walk out(without spending an arm and a leg).  I highly recommend the shrimp tempura roll and the yellowtail.

After reading reviews here I decided to check it out, mostly because it made me really hungry and start to crave all the things it supposedly had.

I was not disappointed! Lots of toppings choices and all the fruit looked fresh! I got red velvet/cake batter swirl and put so many random topping on it. It was delicious! The price is a little higher than I thought it would be but not outrageous especially when you compare it to other ice cream places where you don't get to control the amount of toppings. And the flavor of the yogurt was spot on! It tasted just like cake, mmm.

Now I am craving it again after writing my own review!

I had a good meal here recently and I 've had them here before. I can recommend Sushi Time to others. But there's nothing special here that I've tried that I can recommend over other sushi places, so it only gets three stars from me.
Sushi Time is a reliable place to get sushi. At my recent meal there I liked just about everything I tried. the shrimp was kind of bland and flavorless. Maybe it wasn't fresh. And I got an order of six mussels and one, the largest, tasty really fishy and was unusually rubbery. I had to spit it out. The rest of the meal was good.

An average liquor store. It will serve most needs for liquor purchases but doesn't seem to offer much more than a decent grocery store offers.
I went in looking for rye and Islay Scotch whiskeys. They didn't have much of a seleciton. Nothing else jumped out at me either in the other liquors.
I checked the wine selection. They have eight to 10 Italian wines that look promising. The French selection was poor (probably a reflection of Reno's tastes) and I found little to interest me among the domestic wines.
The Ben's at Lakeside and Moana has a better selection.

So, from my perspective the 2 stars i gave is very calculated.  

1 star for the out-dated rooms and decor

5 stars for the location and convenience to the airport

1 star for the price of the hotel (299 per night).  Not a great price for the value.

2 stars for the airline check-in kiosk not working

4 stars for the surprising limited noise of the planes (hardly heard them)

2 stars for the parking being overpriced!

Overall, the service was great, the bed was ok as was the room, and the stay was decent.  However, all of the other factors combined... I could stay at another hotel in town with a better location for cheaper.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I think it is my fault that I always have an uncomfortable meal at this place.  From high points to low point:

Great appetizers, fantastic Mac and cheese.  

I do like the design of the space and the cocktails are excellent.  They also get points for having an excellent beer menu with my favorite Southampton double white. 

The large portions of comfort food are very inviting for an over-indulger like myself. My advise is to proceed with caution. For whatever reason the saltiness has twice caused me to have to completely neglect my dinner plate.

Avoid the very affordable $35 three course meal unless you are seriously in it to win it.

I've only been here for drinks, so I can't say much about the food - but if you're going to have your "grand opening," I'll come visit after work and you better have some drinks ready!

Oh, what's that?  Your draft lines aren't working yet?  And neither is your credit card machine?  Okay so I'll take a bottled beer.  Oh, you only have two available.  Then I'll do a margarita I guess - which I was actually pleasantly surprised about - it filled about 2.5-3 glasses for a mere $7ish.

The work gang and I went back a few weeks later, it was a touch better but they don't have their ducks in a row.  We haven't been back since.

Ok for a sushi craving but not all that. Some of the specialty rolls are nice. I really liked the Lost Rainbow. Some were murky. The Duo, for example, had too much going on: unagi, sauce, asparagus (which was overpowering and probably would work better if it was halved). They de-emphasize sashimi, which is what I really prefer over sushi. I really care mostly about raw fresh fish. The wasabi was the weakest I have ever had, nice flavor, but no nasal kick, which I crave every once in a while. I did find a scale, a big no-no. But the staff were very friendly and it is byo.

I would give it a 2 for food but I'm giving it a 3 because I appreciated our server. I ordered 6 rolls for 2 people and she suggested that 2 per person would suffice. I don't like to have leftover sushi so I particularly appreciated this. The spciy scallop roll was ok, but the other 3 rolls all became a blur. Each had different ingredients (salmon, eel, shrimp), but because the sauces they used were similar, and many of the rolls have crunchy fried components they all ended up tasting the same. I think that more than anything else, their rolls hide the seafood rather than highlighting it.

Sometimes, I start jonesing for an omelet and a stack of pancakes. That's when I head to Gingham's. 

On first glance, the interior is kind of run down and outdated, and it looks more like a restaurant that someone stopped caring about in the late 90s. However, every time I've been there, the service was fast, friendly, and accurate, and the food was absolutely delicious. 

The last time I was there a couple months ago, there was a sign saying they'd be relocating. Not sure when that will be happening, but when it does, I'll find their new place and stuff myself silly there.

This was my first-time staying at a SpringHill Suite hotel. Pretty nice digs for a 3-star, business hotel. Leaps and bounds better than the Wyndham Garden on Baronne! I loved my room - comfortable, clean, bright, and stylish. The free breakfast was a nice bonus, although the lines and crowd were insane.  Thankfully, housekeeping did not knock on my door at 9am. A little far removed from the hubbub of Bourbon street but still well within walking distance of the French Quarter and nearby a lot of great restaurants. I would definitely stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Very basic hotel. Like outdated basic hotel. Like green carpet green couch basic hotel. Close proximity to airport is its big selling point. They also do offer airport parking which may or may not be a plus. The shuttle service runs pretty consistently but it's almost always a full boat & I've seen people turned away a time or two. The lobby recently got renovated & the restaurant is looking super nazzy, I can't comment on the food as I haven't eaten there yet. Beds are on the firm side and the blankets are very thin.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Maybe I'm just strange, but I always get a chuckle each time I see the sign/logo outside.  Kinda like Superstore, but with liquor..

Parking is plentiful around the building.

The selection here is decent but a bit lacking.  Can't blame them though as the store actually isn't that big.

One thing that did surprise me is that Superstore has their own line of liquor!  There is President's Choice ghetto-beer, and Medallion liquor (vodka and rum), served in cheapo plastic bottles.  Yes, hard liquor in a plastic bottle.  I had a good laugh.  But at least you don't have to worry about breakage.

What the heck did I just eat? Normally I like to digest my food before leaving a review but I want to clear the air on Little Alex's. 

I ate a grande primo burrito, yuck. Vegetables were sauted into oblivion and that was basically the sauce. Bad aftertaste but despite the wet burrito the tortilla is impossible to tear with ease. That is a stale store bought tortilla that only alcohol could help one eat. 

The steak was poor quality. Clearly boiled rather than cooked properly, it was a bad choice. Little Alex's is a bad choice.

I don't see the magic about this place. It's good but not so good you can't have the same experience elsewhere. It's pricey and the seating arrangement is awkward because you are literally sitting with the people next to you...

Sushi is good, I can taste the freshness. Service is a little sour at lunch but I don't think that would be an issue at other times, lunch is pretty demanding. They have a big TV over the sushi bar that just displays a fish loop video. I get the general idea but I kinda wish there was a game on instead.

One of the best hotel bars I've been in.  

Generally busy, but even when it's not, it has a lot of charm.  The bartenders can be somewhat persnickety, but if you can get past the prickly exterior, they're really quite good.

Perfect place to pre-game or grab yourself something to warm your cockles during a rainstorm. 

Alone?  Perfect:  New Orleans is the perfect place to be alone, because that's the best way to meet friends.  And no better place than at a bar like this.  And what better use of one of your free drink tickets if you're staying at the hotel than to use it on that other lone drinker?!

Food was 4 stars but service was 3. Even though I elected to sit at the sushi bar, this one server was super over bearing and refused to let me order with the chef directly. If that wasn't bad enough, she tried to remove my menu even when I wasn't done eating. I barely ordered my soup and hand roll that she was inquiring if I would eat more. WTF!! Leave me alone!!!! Remember, I picked the sushi bar for a reason and didn't sit at a table or booth! She totally ruined the experience for me. 
Outside of that, food was good. The only other complaint was excessive use of imitation crab on the menu.

This was my first visit to the Kirkwood location, and it was really good!  The atmosphere is quaint, kind of a small dining space with nothing too fancy.  The patio out front would be nice to try on a warm night.  The service was friendly and very good.  

I had the chicken special, which was two chicken breasts covered in tomatoes and spinach and a pink sauce.  It was served with mashed potatoes and broccoli, and was everything it should have been.  The bread and butter was really good, and we split a caesar salad that was awesome!  Nice italian meal.

One of the best places to eat Italian in New Orleans. The ambiance is quaint Italian and the food is delicious. Sometimes the place can get a bit overcrowded and you might feel a bit rushed with you meal. Corn Bisque is a great appetizer and you will probably leave with a hefty size go bag of leftovers. Parking is on the street, so be prepared to walk off some food going to your car. But it is a nice Uptown neighborhood so don't worry. 

Tip: Reservations are recommended, but waiting by the bar for a table is not a bad thing.

This may be Irvington's independent coffee shop and I give it props for that. And the ambiance is very nice... and the patio looks comfortable. Ok. 

But extremely slow service, mediocre coffee and poorly trained baristas are disheartening.  Tiny and disgusting bathroom was the last straw for me.

Go for the music, to meet up with a friend, to look at art or learn about the ghostly history of the area, but that's about it.

Coffee: Poor.  Untrained baristas.
Food: Ice cream
Vibe: janky
WiFi: Yes and it's fast
Plugs: Yes.

Coyote Ugly..hmm...I say a no go. I will admit it is very cool and sexy for the girls to get on the bar and dance, but when I was there, those dances weren't as sharp as your memory from the movies would make you believe...

To me this is the bar you would pre-game at before a bachelor party. Our bartender was giving belly button shots off herself, which the men seemed to enjoy, but I was drinkless. 

The clientale was a little country...I try to stay away from the word redneck, but I think you get my drift...the waitress are usually trashed and will lay on the bar and ask you to do shots off their bodies. Does that meet FDA Inspection???

Kyoto is a regular take-out stop for me, and I find quality is consistent among all locations so this one never disappoint.s I love picking up a bento box and a cone for dinner on the go, though I've dined in a time or two as well. I really love the authentic little rooms available instead of dining at a table, they're great for a more private dinner with friends. The menu is awesome, and I find the food always tastes fresh. This is excellent value for your money, and in the prairies where good sushi is hard to come by and/or outrageously priced, Kyoto gets it just right with quality and cost.

Polite staff, good prices for breakfast food and quick service.  

They have an eat in area if you so desire, however I'm unsure why anyone would desire that. 

I'm not a big breakfast fan so I didn't eat anything from here just did the legwork. However the food received no complaints other than wondering why the portions weren't larger which I guess is a good thing if people actually want to eat more of the food. I'm sure, being it's insanely close proximity, that we will be going here again. They were super speedy also.

It's not terrible but it's not good either. It's got 3 stars because of the sheer amount of food you get. But the tofu fried rice was terribly underwhelming. I must admit that yesterday I had tofu fried rice from my most favorite Asian food place ever (pho xe lua) so it made the experience here seem much worse in comparison. It lacked flavor , period it tasted like nothing. I had to add way too much chili sauce and soy sauce in order to want to eat it .

Honestly, I take back the 3 stars and give it 2.5. It wash BAD it just wasn't good either. Sigh

i had a very nice dinner here. the food was good and the waitress and owner were very nice. the dining room is very relaxing with low lights and a live paino player. very intimate. however, you wouldnt want to sit right next to the paino because it would be hard to talk to your dinner mate. also there is a theater across the street so it can get busy. the night that i was there the resturant was full and the kitchen could not respond properly because it took over an hr to get my food. we were not rushing so we didnt mind, but i would keep that in mind in the future.

Service was friendly and efficient.

I ordered a side salad for like $3, came with a lot of Mozzarela cheese, one slice of salami, olives, fresh lettuce, and tomatoes.

Friend got 1 trip to salad bar for $5.99. They have REAL bacon, carrots, beets, tomatoes, peppercinis, olives, and a lot of other choices to pile on the plate. 

We split one of the specialty pizzas that had garlic, pepperoni, peppercinis and fresh mozzerela. It was really tasty.
 The garlic was very flavorful.

Soda prices are way too high...like 2.70 or something.

Was a little pricey for what you get, but I don't regret going there. 
Not in a hurry to go back.

You have driven by Fausto's a zillion times.  It's on the lower end of Vets just a few blocks from the 17th Street Canal.  It's a small little traditional Italian restaurant.  The food and service have always been acceptable but never outstanding.  I have been here at least a half dozen times over the years.  I have always thought the portions were a little on the smaller size, I don't think I have ever taken any leftovers home from Fausto's.  Don't get me wrong, it's solid but not over the top.  A very small, quiet atmosphere and very much the opposite of someplace like Bravo.
