Let me preface this review with the following statement: The last time I ate here there was a fraternity who had taken BYO to mean BYOK- that's bring your own keg. The male members of the frat were all doing keg stands and the girls were all giggling.  

The food here is fine, it's a BYOB which is always a pleasure and since this part of the city right by Drexel has so few, it is a welcome change of pace. The food is not life changing, but they have some good standards. I would definitely eat here again, I just hope those frat kids aren't there again, that really was something.

Of all the chinese places I've tried in the area, they have to be the best. Not only are the prices pretty on point, but the food is consistently good. I also have special order items and they are pretty good about ordering to specifications (i.e. steamed, no sauce, extra sauce on side, etc). Plus their chicken fried rice is out of this world; it's my favorite, hands down, outside the city.

I order from here fairly regularly and they always deliver quickly and are always friendly. I would definitely recommend.

I stopped in today to redeem my free large 1-topping pizza from T-Mobile Tuesday.

Honestly, I couldn't remember the last time I had Papa Johns before today (I'm definitely a Dominos junkie!). I ordered online and drove about 20 minutes before going in. My pizza was still in the oven for a couple minutes; no problem.

I get my pepperoni pizza and leave. Personally I was not a fan of this pizza. The sauce is almost too sweet and then it has like a pepper taste that doesn't work well with it. The only part of the pizza I liked was the crust. It was very light and fluffy. 

Personally, I'll stick with Dominos.

We stayed here during Essence last year and it was great.  The hotel is very nice and in a great locale.  My only complaint is that my feet hurt from walking. But what does that have to do with them?  I don't know, I just wanted everyone to know my feet hurt.  

I gave this place 5 stars because the overall experience.  If this is one of your options, STAY HERE BECAUSE YOU GET YOUR MONEY'S WORTH!!!  It's a quiet hotel and perfect for long weekend's with your boo!  I'd stay here again if I'm cheating on the Sheraton.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I am a Las Palmas fan, but just not this location. This is probably my least favorite of the several that I have tried. It likely has something to do with the age of the building, but it just feels a bit dirty to me.  I don't like the layout either, and I feel like you can still smell the smoke from when it allowed smoking.  

On the plus side, the food is pretty much the same as it is at all the other Las Palmas locations.  I am especially fond of the fahita quesodillas.  They are new to the menu and are just wonderful.

This Enterprise was fantastic. The customer service was great with a representative greeting you as you got off the shuttle bus with bottles of water for everyone. They never rushed me to get to the next customer, and they they never let the line get long. When I returned my car, everything went smoothly, and even though I drove through allot of snow, and got the car covered in salt, they never gave me a hard time about it. I wasn't expecting such a good experience being that they were the cheapest, but I'm thoroughly impressed. I'll use these guys again!

The coffee here isn't that great, and their employees could use some training on customer service.

To start, they load your coffee up with more cream and sugar than you could possibly need, and forget about a smile or a thank you. They seem more interested in making sure the assembly line runs smoothly. Perhaps that's what you pay for with the prices much lower than any of the other coffee places here at the airport.

Even though the coffee was miserable, I have to give it to them for their donuts and muffins. They are always fresh, and they hit the spot. I hate to say that this probably won't be my last visit to this Dunkin.

it's as good as it gets for the Westbank. It has everything you'll need to work out. Machines are old but workable. New treadmills and spin bikes. There is a women only work out area in the back. There is also a movie cardio room where you can use a treadmill, bike or elliptical while watching a movie on the big screen...too bad they lock the DVD player so you'll have to ask someone to play a DVD.  There is no kids care area for single parents. The bathroom area needs renovation but it's workable. Don't be surprised if while you're in the men's locker room you see a female staff member cleaning the area. This place is closed on Sundays.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: I dealt with this Hotel - Colette in Sales for our photo booths and she is the best Venue sales person I've dealt with. She goes beyond her duty to make our service work.  I love the family feeling of staff at this hotel right from the housekeeping to caterers. The bed was so comfortable and I forgot to check what mattress they use. They did not have any strawberries or berries for my waffles is my only complaint!  Funny eh?  I recommend this for your economical stay and wedding venues. Please talk to these staff for your weddings! ;)
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Been driving by this place for years and found that some folks from another restaurant took it over and some friends (locals) said it was a great find for a local place.    Greta beers on draft (even Guinness ) and wine.   Awesome burger, very good fish & chips, "Great" french fries and a shepherds pie that will fill you up.  Everyone loves the chili...but they always run out B/4 we get there!!!   Clean and friendly staff & owners.  There is occasional music, a juke box & a few video games.    A real neighborhood location for cold beer & good food.   Just don't tell too many people about it!

Late September 2015 (Thurs night, 9 p.m.-ish)

Bourbon St is gross; don't go there. Having said that: we passed this place on our way back to the hotel and the music was great. There was no cover, no drink minimum, so we entered and stood inside fairly close to the door and enjoyed some top-notch R&B covers. Really good singers and band.

Why stand so close to the door, you wonder? Thanks for asking! There were definitely some grifter types waiting to pounce further in the room, in the darkness. I happen to like my purse and the ID/money within.

But..the music was best we heard while trying to run past Bourbon St.

Arguably the worst Chile relleno meal I have ever had and, trust me, I have eaten a lot of them. First one arrived incorrectly, second one was cold, third one was sufficiently warm but  was overlooked and soggy. And tasted bland. 

My dinner companions had Carne Assad's  burrito which also was cold and meat over cooked. 

Service was fine and attentive which is why I rated it 2 star instead of 1 Star. This is not a place to get basic American style Mexican food. 

Maybe there are specialty items that are good but I probably will not return.

I'm so torn on coming here. On one hand, I love their unique flavors. Not your typical vanilla or chocolate; rather, there's white chocolate mouse, vanilla bean, girl scout thin mints, and always flavors of the month. The toppings are just as great!
Where do I find my fro-yo turmoil? The service is terrible. Always really young kids, unwilling to really help you out.  I always feel like I'm inconveniencing them when I ask to try different flavors. 
I do recommend to try their unique flavors and quirky decor.

Okay, so this IS NOT my first choice grocery shopping.  However, when I was making tortilla soup the other night I needed some specialty items that I knew my favorite store would definitely not have.  They had a wide selection of dried chilies and also fresh herbs that you normally cannot find.  I had never heard of epazote before, but they totally had it.  So, go in the day time, lock your doors, and brave though the store to get those specialty items that you're not going to find at most places.. or you can just go eat at Taco Bell.

I ordered via grubhub.  I got the miso soup, spicy tuna, California roll, and shrimp tempura.  I also ordered a diet coke and didn't get it when I called the delivery boy back to tell him that he agreed to come back.

They give you 8 pieces with the spicy tuna and California rolls so it's a lot of food and good pricing.  The miso soup was well priced as well.  I wasn't a big fan of their shrimp tempura.  I didn't realize it came with eel sauce on top.   

I'm not sure if people know this but miso soup is a great hangover cure!

It was late at night, I was working overtime covering the midnight shift at work and needed food. Not much was open at such an ungodly hour. The service was quick, the food was hot and fresh.

I was impressed that the lot was pretty much litter free, which is impressive considering its downtown location. Normally I do not use a drive-thru window, so I was shocked with the speedy and polite service I received. I had a good giggle while in line for the drive-thru, the car ahead of me was actually a golf cart. He was a security guard from a nearby nightclub. 

Not my typical WC, but I'd come back for a slider or two.

Friendly staff. Can't go 5 feet without someone asking how they can help. Breakfast buffet is amazing with the omlet station and waffles station. 
Nice gym equipment in gym, clean rooms, prompt service and no smoking in any of the building. 
Gave it 4 stars Because we came back from dinner and were told we HAD to valet our car because the garage is full. How does a hotel garage fill and not have enough room for registered guests? When I said something about it he was quick to ask someone on his radio a question, then said he would valet it at the self park rate.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This place was MOBBED this Saturday. I'm so glad there is another grocery option in the area. I stopped by to get party supplies for my kiddo's third bday.

I ALWAYS love Giant's bakery items- the cakes are good and the frosting is better. They have a large enough selection that I didn't even bother ordering it ahead of time but you certainly can!

The lines were hella long- but it was 12noon on a Saturday on the last day the gas card deal was available.

There's also a STARBUCKS THERE!! I love coffee. Love.

I often have doctor's appointments out in Wynnewood, and my pre-train snack back to the city usually consists of a coffee and carrot raisin muffin from Main Line Bakery. Welp, not this time. I spied Yapple from across the station and suddenly started craving the fro.

Unfortunately, not even a 10% off Yelp check-in offer could save this one. While the topics selection was out of control, the yogurt was just too icy. I understand the concept of frozen yogurt through and through (a healthy! delicious! treat!), but in my opinion, it should be made as creamy as possible.

this place is a little expensive but their food is always spot on.  I usually have delivery and they are quick, the order is always right, and the delivery guys are really nice.  the fried rice is amazing and so are their soups.  I get the egg drop when I'm feeling like a little pick me up and the war wonton is amazing when you're feeling sick.  portion sizes are large for all their dishes.  The pad thai isn't a typical pad thai but it's tasty none-the less.  not sure what the sauce is (it's not the typical peanut sauce), but it's good.  love the crab rangoons and the sweet/sour red sauce as an appetizer.

My fiancee decided to try this place out after being frustrated with the Supercuts across the street and their hour-long wait on a Thursday morning. Not to mention I usually have to trim quite a few hairs after he goes there....

Overall he had a good experience, and didn't mind paying a few extra bucks for a quality cut ($19 before tip). He got a buzz, a little longer on top than on the sides. Not sure the name of the guy who did it, but it looks good and there isn't anything I need to fix!

He'll was pleased and will continue to bring his business here :)

Also, no credit cards! Checks and cash only!

This is a decent Safeway location.

I don't usually like to shop at Safeway because I find it's the most expensive place to get groceries, but when I'm in a bind, I'll stop here.  

This Safeway doesn't have the best selection out of the Safeways I've been to but it's pretty good.  It's one of the better ones.  

The tore is usually pretty clean and it's attached to the mall (you have to go down a little hallway) so that's nice.

Overall, it's not bad.  Like I said, its one of the better Safeways I've been to.

This is a nice Boston Pizza in the beautiful suburb of Beaumont.

I found that there was an older crowd here (and a lot more families).  It was a nice atmosphere though.  

The food was just like every other Boston Pizza so I was satisfied in that sense.  The staff was friendly too.  It was nice because I haven't had a lot of experiences with happy BPs servers.  

The restaurant itself was a typical Boston Pizza, newer.  It was nice.

I had a good experience at this location.  Check it out if you're in the neighborhood!

I do not like World Health Club.  

It's a great gym as far as equipment goes but the vibe is not a good one.  This gym has a really stuck up feel to it.  It's as though if you aren't a professional body builder or a pinup girl, you aren't welcome or you are frowned upon.  

The staff kind of adds to the stuck vibe too.  They are focused on sales  and themselves as far as I can tell.  

The facility is nice though.  They have newer equipment and it's nice to work out on.

It's really not a friendly place though.  Sorry to say.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I really like this location of Second Cup.  I prefer this location on Whyte over the stand alone location on Calgary Trail and Whyte.

The reason I like this location is because I find it more chill.  It's not as busy than the other Whyte Ave location and it's got a different feel to it.

I find that this location is less of a trendy hangout than other Second Cups.  Because it's part of the Varscona Hotel, there are more out-of-towners and the atmosphere is a bit more business like.  It's not uptight business though, it's a relaxed business environment. 

I just like it!

I'm not a big fan of Taco Del Mar.

I went here with high expectations because I LOVE Mexican food, but I was fairly disappointed when I left. 

The food wasn't as flavorful or well put together as I thought it should be.

Mucho Burrito is probably my favorite fast food place in the city so I tend to compare places to them - especially Mexican places.  And Mucho Burrito blows Taco Del Mar out of the water.

I appreciated that Taco Del Mar had some different items on their menu that I didn't expect.  That was nice.

But in the areas of taste of quality, Mucho is far superior!

This is a good Boston Pizza.

I like it because it's one of the nicer BPs but it's not the busiest.  the servers are great because they are friendly, for the most part.  And they are usually happy and smiley.  I really believe that the service you receive will make or break an experience.  And I've almost always gotten really good service at this location.

The food is the same as all Boston Pizzas so I can't say too much about that except that if you haven't had the cactus cut potatoes, you have to try them!

The parking lot can get very slippery in the winter so be careful!

I've only ever used the drive-thru at this Second Cup but I've used it a few times now.

Usually I don't have a problem.  The staff is usually not too cheery but they do their jobs.

I did, however, get the wrong drink once!  I didn't notice it until I had driven away and I was so upset about it.  I was so looking forward to this delicious drink and it was the complete opposite of anything I ordered.  

Needless to say, I stayed away from this Second after that.

But, they are a good company and a decent location in general.  The staff never seem very happy though so that's concerning.  

AND CHECK YOUR ORDER BEFORE YOU DRIVE AWAY!

Oh man, this place makes me feel like a kid in a candy shop, except the candy is precious booze. 

Ben's has a comprehensive selection of liquors. Only once they didn't carry something I was looking for (Absinthe, right after the US ban was lifted. They carry at least two varieties now). Their beer & wine selection is quite good as well. And they have about any kind of mixer you can dream up. Prices are typically cheaper than comparable grocery/liquor stores. 

Did I mention they are open late Fridays and Saturdays?

F*ck Disneyland; Ben's is the happiest place on Earth.

Well, I am glad Ernie C. was wrong and here, three years later, Strega is still poppin'. 

The energy is usually decent in here, depending on what night you go. I've always had a good time at Strega, whether it's during the Santa Pub Crawl or a low-key Thursday night. Bartenders and such can be a little slow to get to you, but the ambiance more than makes up for it. Drinks are priced decently, but this isn't a cheap bar. 

I really like that they rotate out the art on the walls frequently. Strega is actually one part house party, one part bar and one part art gallery. Solid.

Hue, Hue, Hue...Meh.

Nothing was just quite right. The experience was unorganized and kinda awkward. 
Service Ok. Things were coming out in a strange order by multiple people. 
Microwaved dinner break came before drinks with no plates to eat it off of etc. Bread was rock hard once it cooled. 

Not alot of menu choices but what was there was overpriced for the portions.

I had the snapper and my dining partner had the vodka chicken pasta dish. We both thought it was quite anticlimatic.

Sad to leave this review...wish it could have worked out between us.

Where do you go after your Trivia Team has dominated at The Melrose and you're heading back?  Um, this place was all we could think of.  We ordered 3 things, paid, got a bag she said "here's your order, thank you" and closed the window... 

opened bag, 1 thing
we had not pulled away, she came back to the window said whoops, hands another bag.. checked this time, nope... not done...
wait wait wait... and third thing...

Not horrible mind you, but the food was not quite Wendy's late-night quality... which was kind of sad.

Had a slightly less than sterile experience when I was there, but I believe it was because the place had been bum rushed by hundreds before I got there so I'm not expecting it to always be in the level of uncleanliness.

Other than the furniture being in disarray and a few napkins laying about it was your Joe Generic Starbucks.  The entire time I was there the people behind the counter were hustling, so they never got out to see, so my guess is it's generally a nice and clean place... it was not dirty, just disheveled.

Nothing wrong with it... coffee was ok and food was ok and price was too high and it's Starbucks.

Due to child's schedule we've been dropping by here for a breakfast snack. Having been to Dunkin's all over the map, I've got to say this one's a real interesting one - donuts are significantly better than average, coffee drinks are average, and the breakfast food is sort of below average.

Service speed is really good. No complaints there. 

Can't really eat outside without someone hitting you up for money or a group of people stopping and talking about various ailments of someone across the street, but meh. Really do not want to hear about infection complications while eating a somewhat tasteless breakfast sandwich, but I do.

Spirits on Jasper is my usual liquor store, purely because I can walk about a 60-second diagonally-straight line and be standing in front of their cooler. There's nothing exceptional about it at all: it's small, its beer selection is small (but has everything the average consumer might need) and its wine selection is small (and never has what I'm looking for), but it's the closest by about 20 meters and sometimes that's what counts. When you live in an area that has more liquor stores in a ten-block radius than you can count on your fingers, they all start to look the same anyway.

During the Fringe, I spent a fair amount of time in this Second Cup drinking frozen strawberry lemonades and working on my laptop, taking advantage of the free wireless internet. The air conditioning and a little area at the back with a few tables and padded seating made it possible to escape the heat, sort of escape the massive crowds and concentrate on getting my work done. It's definitely not my favourite Second Cup just because the layout offers little privacy - every seat is either in a high-traffic spot or cuddled up next to a floor-to-ceiling window - but this summer, I certainly was grateful that it was around.

The fragrance of roasting peanuts is intoxicating, and Super Value roasts peanuts on site. :-)   In addition to the delicious aroma, what keeps me coming back to Super Value are its terrific prices on the beer workhorses that the Mister fancies (Coors, Corona, Blue Moon, Sam Adams) and the very gallant staff.   Even though I am perfectly capable of toting my own beer cases, sales associates invariably materialize from nowhere to carry my selections to the cashier and then to my car.  Such service is unexpected yet very much appreciated.

Penzey's is a great resource for spices, herbs, mixtures and flavorings, and it is near the top of my list of spice shops.    Because Penzey's is across town, I do not get to visit as frequently as I would like.  Nonetheless, when I do visit, I usually gravitate to the larger quantity packages, which are always a better value than the smaller quantities.  We are big fans of Penzey's salt-free spice mixes and ground chills (especially the chipotle and ancho).    Hint:  Do sign up for Penzy's mailing list, and several times a year, you will receive their catalogues (which include fabulous recipes and coupons for free spice samples).

Went to Samurai today for lunch with a group of 10 coworkers. The service was pretty bad; it took over an hour for everyone to get food even though we all broke up into different tables. Although at the end of the meal, the manager noticed how bad it was and comp'ed everyone's meals (must have been over $300 in sushi). Glad to see someone taking care to make sure their clients leave satisfied. 

Oh and the food is good but they have no non-sushi options for my non-fish-eating friend except for miso soup and gyoza.

Its clean, cheap, and has a great location. Rooms are also quite large. Those are the positives.  Alas, it definitely has seen better days, and the amenity charge is complete bullshit. The wireless sucks major ass. Right now I'm in a Motel 6 using wirelss service from a holiday inn that is god knows where. It is 10 times better than what I had at the St. Louis Hotel. I wish I was exaggerating. 

soo yeah, decent place to crash in the heart of the French Quarter, but you definitely don't get any more than what you pay for (and in the case of wireless, less than what you paid for).
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: $14 chirashi bowl was pretty decent. Fat slices of sashimi. The quality was decent but nothing exceptional. Very sad that there was no uni included but for $14, what do you expect. They actually don't have uni, which is sad, but I talked to the owner Vinh and she says they might get some. Service was nice and friendly. Vinh also came by and gave us some fried avocado tempura which was a very nice gesture but tasted just okay. I ate a couple pieces but couldn't finish them all because the bowl made my friend and me so full. Would come again.

Good enough. With a long queue at the drivethrough, I went inside to order and pick up my lunch. The parking lot was clean and the dining room looked clean. The condiments and cutlery area was tidy and the tables did not have trash on them.

The young man at the counter took my order and filled it quickly. Pulling it together as I drove to my next stop, it was accurate and still hot. Sandwich was assembled properly and the chicken nuggets were crispy.

No real complaints, it was a good visit.

[Review 14208 overall, 1530 of 2020, number 26 in Louisiana.]

A very pleasant stay here, with a clean and quiet and comfortable hotel room for four nights. I really have no complaints at all - I am a fan of this property!

Plenty of parking, easy enough to get to from the road and after you figure out the exit, not really a big deal to get out and back on to the road. Maybe some highway noise but not that much. A Dunkin Donuts within walking distance but no other restaurants near enough to walk to.

The same layout as recently upgraded Courtyards with a nice lobby and restaurant in the lobby. Free (upgraded as I am Platinum elite) Internet worked well.

I would stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I give this place 4.5 stars.  The food is very spicy here for all you bland tongues of the world.  We ordered a total of 9 plates, so it was that good.  The Mongolian Beef was very spicy and doesn't have a lot of onions like in most places.  The sweet and sour chicken was crisp and had a lot of flavor.  The salt and pepper squid was tender and crispy.  The BBQ pork fried rice wasn't too salty.  The spicy eggplant was to die for.  The portions are large here.  We were seated very quickly and the food came out fast too.

I have had GREAT experiences at George's and NOT GREAT experiences at George's. 

I like their stuffed breadsticks with cheese and pepperoni. They are amazing. Sometimes their pizza is really good, but last time I got it, service was slow and it came out cold. 

Their chicken velvet soup is always great. They also have good salads. 

I don't like their breaded tenderloin. 

I would definitely try it out, but sometimes I have slow service. They often have live music and drink specials. The owner is often around talking to regulars. Lots of friendly people. Definitely a neighborhood spot.

Centrally located in downtown St. Louis, and a member of the National Historic Register, Magnolia Hotel St. Louis opened as the Mayfair in 1924.  Reportedly the originator of "chocolates on the pillow" and now part of Marriott's "Bonvoy" collection, guests can expect excellent service and cleanly confines from lobby to room and everywhere in between.  Offering strong WiFi and a 24/7 top-floor gym with plenty of new equipment, early risers will not even need to pay for parking as there are free street spaces available from 7:01pm until 7:59am, plus all-day Sunday and on Holidays.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Stopped in for lunch yesterday with two of my buddies.  This time, I ordered a cobb salad...desperately holding back from ordering the burger with roquefort.  There was also a guy playing jazz on his saxophone.  That was really pleasant and made the place have a really upscale feel.  I've never had a cobb salad until this day and wow....definitely delicious.  They also shaped the foil used to cover my friends leftover pasta to look like a swan..it was unexpected and pretty funny.  So far this place is 2 for 2...and I will be back again...

I had dinner here with my friends after a shopping trip for Halloween. everyone was tired and starved so i decided to go to a closest place. Well, i have a salad and a grilled calamari which were good. My Friends complained that they were salty but overall i think the meal was OK. The price is reasonable and the location is not hard to place. This place have a modern Italian twist not very cozy but nice and have enough space for you to not eavesdrop whatever the people sitting in the next table talking about. I would give this place 3.5 stars but i can't. A 4 stars is not fair cuz three of my friends were not happy with their meals.

Let's be honest: sushi in Nashville isn't very good.... however Fujiyama's sushi selection is pretty darn good. The staff is very friendly, the restaurant  has cool tatami rooms for larger groups, and the sushi presentation is beautiful! 

I've been to other more 'upscale' sushi restaurants in Nashville, and found them to be overpriced and REALLY Americanized (I even got hard rice on a few rolls at Virago.. eew). I've traveled to Japan and have lived on the West Coast, so I'm pretty picky about where I eat my Japanese food - especially sushi!

Every time I go to Grand Cru, I leave with a few more items than I intended on purchasing... and I'm proud of it!

The people who work at Grand Cru are very knowledgable and friendly. If I mention a wine that I like, someone will direct me towards a wine I will like MORE and is usually LESS EXPENSIVE. 

I have always been satisfied with staff recommendations; I know I can count on them when I'm unsure of what I want!

They also carry 360 organic vodka - Bing Cherry. Delicious. End of story.

*Don't miss their complimentary wine tastings every Saturday at Dose!*

Three words: The Feed Me. A seven course meal including dessert under $40. The entree changes depending on what's cookin' in Mr. Tony's kitchen.  My father took me here on our "date" for my birthday every year when I was a little girl. A special place for my big night out. Now my husband takes me here for my birthday every year. This place has become one of our places for special occassions. I was heartbroken after Katrina knowing that such a local landmark and special place for so many people was gone.  I am so glad they rebuilt and came back.

Once you pick a theme, run with it.  NASCAR!  There is a very impressive collection of NASCAR tchotchkes up in this piece; I felt like I was on another planet.

The food was traditional American breakfast shizzo and the biscuits n' gravy were plump n' wondrous.  My coffee cup was never empty, the service was pleasant and the omelets were full of not-too-oiled-up fresh vegetables.  

Be prepared to be ogled severely if you're a fine lady.  The clientele is about 75% male, 20% in denim shirt-plus-jeans ensembles.

Been going to this place since I was wee.  Since I am visiting Tucson, I stopped in.  Support local biz!

It's mostly Korean stuff, so being half-Korean I find it exciting.  Chapaghetti!  Bacchus-D!  Gochujang!  Chimpang!  Those peanut balls with the squid on the outside!  It's a tour of my childhood, an instant time machine to Actual Korea and Actual Korean Food.

If you get there early enough, they have good take-away kim bap and jap chae at the counter.  

It's a family-run place with videos, food, beverages, a big snack aisle and some Korean and Japanese booze.  I hope they hold it down for the midtown fo-eva.

I just went there last night to check the place out -- the flavor combinations of their pops sound really tasty.  And the atmosphere is bright and clean.

I ordered the cucumber jalapeno pop, but I think I got something different, there was no spice at all.  It was good, very good even.  Just not what I ordered.

You can't beat the price -- $3.75, for something this crafty.  Will definitely be back!

UPDATE:  I had the following today:
Blackberry Goat Cheese - amazing!
Peanut Butter Pie - well executed, my wife loved it.

I really don't know what's up with all the bad press that Buca is getting here on Yelp. My husband and I have been to this location at least three times and have left full, satisfied with the service we received and in a good mood. I will admit that we prefer the Center City Philly location. It has a certain vibe to it that the Wynnewood locale does not have. Most likely there is a higher turnover rate too because it's in a busier area, but I'd rather not pay for parking. The last time we were here, we had the Bucatini Ala Enzo and it was really good. The portions are huge and we both had enough for lunch the next day.

Shopping used to mean shopping. Now it means driving to the store, having a Pavlovian reaction to the Starbucks sign, drinking coffee for 20 minutes, and then shopping. What a world. 

I love a Target with a Starbucks. The alternative are the Target branches with the Cafe and those are terrible.
The Starbucks branch here is quite good. The barristas do a great job at moving the big lines along and the coffee is the same quality as you'd get at any stand alone branch. They also have Target specific cake pops which my kids absolutely love. 

All in all, good stuff!

I feel like I should love McCaffrey's. On the plus side, they have a lot of what I look for in a mainstream supermarket, plus a very handy hot food bar which I tend to use when I don't have enough time to make dinner. However, they are just crazy expensive. You can even get better deals on staples at Whole Foods which says a lot. Also, their selection of organic foods is really lacking, especially in the fresh produce section. They have some stuff here and there, just not enough in my opinion. In a pinch they're great, but when I have the time, I feel like my money is better spent at Wegman's or Whole Foods.

I really like this store.  The ambiance can't be beat- they have great, comfortable leather seating in a very chicly decorated space, and the coffee is very good.  My friend also says that the sandwiches and other food items are amazing, although I've not tried any.  ALSO, THEY SERVE WINE!!! What is there not to love about that?  

Williams Blvd is a bit divey for my taste and it is way out in Kenya, but if I'm ever out that way, I like to stop in and chill if I have time.  This is a nice, unexpected little gem in the heart of the Wezest, and Ioves it.

I love love love Little Tokyo, but be warned that if you want the best they have to offer, you will be dropping some cash.  Here's what to get: the burning man is divine, the chocolate city roll as ridiculously good as nola itself, the fema roll ginormous (if not so good as sushi bros), and of course the old standbys are fantastic.  The tempura dinners are massive piles of crispy goodness, the spicy edamame is phenomenal, and the seaweed salad perfect.  Service is excellent and friendly.  I always order way too much (and usually drop well over $100 for two), but damn I love waking up to leftover sushi for breakfast.  Worth it!

This is a great little Turkish market that was recommend to us by an awesome waiter in Zahav when we complained about our favorite halva brand not longer be sold in the far northeast. While the place itself is not huge they do have a good variety of items. Also the prices seem to be cheaper here than other Turkish markets we have hit up in the area. The staff was super friendly and let us try their cheese, olives and just about anything else we looked at before buying. So this place is a winner and worth the drive for us.

It seems like every other week a new Japanese steakhouse (complete with teppanyaki grills) opens.   I personally don't see the attraction of the pomp and circumstance so I typically sit at a normal table and order off the regular menu.

Hirosaki is pretty generic in that respect.  The miso soup was meh.   If you blindfolded me and didn't tell me that the salmon was seasoned with curry there would be no way for me to tell.

Service wasn't too bad, however I was there for lunch on a weekday so they weren't busy at all.

This little strip mall pizzeria seems like it should be in a much nicer area (it's almost right next to a gas station).

They make their own dough (and they must make a lot of it based on the gigantic electric mixer I saw in the kitchen) and it shows.  The crust (it must be good if it's in your name, right?) is superb.   Crunchy on the outside but a nice chewy inside.

Our server (manager?) was very nice and had an extensive knowledge about all the items on the menu.

The ambiance is very classy, yet kid-friendly.   I look forward to returning soon.

This is a pretty basic faux-Mexican restaurant.     It's tucked away in a strip mall near a big office complex so they have a lot of dinner and weekend specials to try to attract the non-work crowd.

The food is pretty much what you would expect from an American Mexican restaurant in a strip mall: crunchy tacos with cheese and lettuce, burritos, enchiladas, queso, guacamole, refried beans, etc.   Pretty nondescript, but tasted OK. 

I would never chose to come here, but the price is right and the service very fast (the food was on our table in under 10 minutes).   Better than fast food, but by no means good.

This is the 2nd location of the now-famous Sushi Club on W. 10th St.   The menu is identical (as far as I could tell).   It's all-you-can-eat sushi, but not from a buffet.   You order by marking on a dry-erase menu.   Order what you can handle (you can always order more) because if you waste too much food they will charge you extra for that.   They have a large selection of cooked and raw rolls (maki).   They also have a decent selection of regular sushi (nigiri - raw fish on a bed of rice) and a small sashimi (raw fish only) selection.

There are also some hot appetizers (soups, dumplings, teriyaki) and cold salads you can order.

I wonder what Emilio Zapata would think about being the namesake for this restaurant? 

The place isn't bad, I'm just spoiled because I can get top-notch Mexican food at all hours around my home. This was a Chevy's-level establishment with decent food and good drinks. 

The Enchiladas I had were OK, but they were really wet burritos, and I'll let that slide. The Carnitas were tasty too, though I only had a bite of them. 

Most of the menu is simple and plain Mexican, and probably the best Mexican I've had outside of California, Arizona, New Mexico, Texas and Nevada...and that's kinda sad.

This Anytime Fitness is a nice looking gym with very friendly associates.

The gym itself is a bit cramped and very limited in free weight space, and as others have mentioned the trainer had sessions going which caused a serious setback in my workout. The single bench press station was impossible to get to for what i needed, so I had to change up and use the incline bench. 

It is a good gym, but could just benefit from more equipment if the training is that popular. As usual, no soap proided in the showers!
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Super cool looking gym. New shiny grey Matrix machines and equipment set the mood here. A lot of room dedicated to free weights and nautilus. Good selection of curl bars, dumbbells, and kettleballs. All equipment new and in great shape. Cardio is limited to about a dozen basic machines, but never saw a wait for any either. The single bench however was another story as it was in constant use and also served as squat rack as well, making a serious workout almost impossible. More benches would equal more stars.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: I have never been a huge fan of marathon.  Sure the food is served quickly and the servers are friendly enough.  But, despite the seemingly tasty ingredients, the food always tastes bland to me.  If I had to recommend anything, I would recommend the salads.  I had the grilled veggies & greens yesterday (with calamari). The veggies were fresh and the barley was tasty and filling.  My tablemates all enjoyed their salads as well (quinoa and salmon and, most notably, the control freak).  So, if you want a fresh and healthy option for lunch, marathon should have something to suit your needs.

Mmm. When you have a hankering for fro-yo, you HAVE a hankering for fro-yo! Luckily, there's this cute place in Collegeville near Wegmans to satisfy your (and mine!) craving.

There is a wide variety of yogurt and toppings for you to choose from, just remember the cost (at the time of this review) is 49cents, so if you go too crazy, yes, you will end up with one expensive cup of fro-yo! The interior is designed really nicely and the staff are friendly. I especially love the fact they have a pitcher of water at the front for you in case you get a little parched.

Nice place!

Biggest Little City Club came replaced Satellite on California Avenue near downtown Reno.
Upsides for this club are a comfortable atmosphere with a cool old Reno cowboy theme, a great layout, unique promotions (movie trivia, movie nights, etc.) and cool music. The ownership is friendly and built the bar partly to help improve the offerings in downtown Reno.
The only downsides? The drinks could be a little cheaper (although I did enjoy $1 PBR night not that long ago) and the music can get a little loud because the stage is in your face. Overall, this place is a great addition to downtown Reno without being pretentious and hipsterish.

Good wash but I've had better. Much better actually.

Maybe it's a lack of full service car washes on Lower State but this places gets crazy busy. Your best bet is to drop off and eat next door. You'll have a clean car and full stomach before you know it.

Full service wash and detail available and the prices are average. The're about in the middle of what SB has to offer. The only reason I go here is because I'm in the neighborhood and don't feel like driving a dirty car to Montecito Street and Cliff Drive.

Easy place to pop in for lunch. 
Slice (cheese), salad and beverage for $5.95. What a bargain. Even with adding a couple toppings for 40 cents a pop and tossing in a buck for service, you're under $9.00 for lunch. 
4 TVs on ESPN 8/The Ocho, music and some kids crane games keep me sitting outside.
The salads are big, the pizza good and even the calzone is large. The service can be slow and it's not cleanest dive but did I mention it's cheap? I hit Gina a couple times of month for a nice slice. Nothing fancy, just pie.

Busy with market. Food for now and later.
This is my favorite location of Cuca's and it's all about the vibe. I feel like I'm in divey taqueria...and I am.

The food is the same from other locations with large portions and some seating on the covered patio. I dig the breakfast burrito con chorizo or the lunch with carnitas. Mmmmm

Parking can be a bear in the back but push your way in and give it a try. If this location is too much for you, the Mesa spot is more laid back with the same great food. Grab a burrito to-go and head for the beach. Breakfast, lunch or even dinner. This food also cures hangovers so salud!

A nice neighborhood sushi joint on the Mesa. Good quality but higher prices deserve more. There are better places that fit the bill in Santa Barbara.
Week nights or weekends finds Ichiban packed with a line out the door. It must be the location and family feel that pack um in for this, nothing special sushi house. And pack in they do with moms and dads, kids and dates all jockeying for a seat.
Standard offerings with a marginal sake menu. I find most of the waitresses are knowledgeable about the rice wine and will help you pick out the right fit for you.
All and all it's good, constant, clean and friendly but you can do better off The Mesa.

As I have mentioned before, my husband and I stay at various hotels in the city now that we live in the suburbs but still visit our friends and the wonderful restaurants in Philly frequently. I ended up getting us a room at the Club Quarters through Priceline, which was fun in itself. We were extremely pleased with the hotel. It is nothing fancy, but hit the mark in terms of clean linens, quiet rooms and location. You don't spend that much time in your room, anyway! The taps of sparkling and flat water in the libby are a nice touch.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Met my brother and sister in law here Sunday for brunch! I was glad we made a reservation because the place was packed! I am guessing it is due to the great bottomless mimosa and bloody mary deal. And yes, you can switch back and forth. I had the vegetable omelette, which was very light, filled with veggies and light on the cheese. Others at the table had omelettes too and my husband had the crab eggs benedict. The table was given amazing pita and pumpkin bread to start. Our server was very nice and honored the "Happy Birthday Month" coupon I had been sent via email. I like Derek's - it is fast, easy and simple.

Sweat, you make me kind of mad. I joined your gym last January because you are closer to my house than the one I go to near work in Wilmington. I just have a few little requests. YOUR TVs NEVER WORK. The AC never seems to be working and it was REALLY hot this summer. I do, however, like the fact that no one is checking each other out, no one dresses to impress really, and they are just there to pound out the miles or lift weights. I also like the classes you offer and the trainers I have met are incredibly nice. But alas, I think the experience could be enhanced. Can you please fix the audio and visual on your TVs?
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I like this place - it's not bad. It's just $$$ for students - which are their primary clientele. I'd come here if I want to splurge on a sushi box or a spicy scallop roll.

Generally fresh - I've had a few of their items like their salmon-based chef box (cute presentation/unnecessary for extra cost though), a few of their rolls, their bowls and more. 

Maybe because I am not a big fan of Double Knot so I don't find it super special but I think if you're looking for a quick sushi fix but don't mind spending the money, then it's the place to go.

I'm not really one to typically review a Starbucks, but this place is a cut above they typical Starbucks. The drinks are the same of course, but being next to a university, the ambience here is really conducive to getting work done. There are ample tables, benches, and seats that invite you to stay to enjoy your drink or to get some work done. 

The people who longer tend to be students, and being around students always gives me a charge of energy, as if I were still of that age as well. 

I really like the layout of this place and wish more Starbucks made an effort to creat this type of environment.

This Hampton Inn is a renovated warehouse. This is the trend in the Warehouse District/Convention Center area in New Orleans. Only, I would not have expected this place to be as nice as it is. Having stayed at many Hampton Inns previously, I was surprised at how nice this one is. However, they price accordingly so there you have it. 

The one downside to this hotel though is that it's not really within walking distance of the French Quarter (well, a mile, but that seems inconvenient for a vacation.) However, it's right across the street from the convention center so if you're in town for a function, it's the ideal place to stay.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Located on Magazine street, amid a mix of boutique shops, restaurants, and residential homes, Breaux Mart is provides convenience to people who live in the immediate vicinity and just need something quick from the market or like to make frequent trips to the market to get things fresh. 

To be clear, Breaux Mart is not a supermarket - it is relatively small. But even still, it is well stocked and when I was there I couldn't think of anything off the top of my head that I could have wanted that they didn't have. 

I think I will be a frequent shopper of Breaux Mart from now on. Whole Foods for the good stuff, Breaux Mart for the basics.

Walked in and the phone rang as I walked up,  she said one moment (to me) then answered the phone to take the order. No problem here,  it was a toss up as to who was here first. 

She looked at me to say something,  phone rings again and she answers it and takes an order.  Looks at me and says "What can I. ..", then the phone rings and SHE ANSWERED IT AND STARTS TO TAKE THEIR ORDER! ! WTF?! Put them on hold,  I was next several times.  

Never coming back.  I can get over a bad meal,  but that lack of common sense is un-acceptable.

I was expecting a lot after reading several Yelp reviews saying it was better than Ted Drewes. I was disappointed! I'm not a die hard custard fan or Ted Drewes. In fact, I went to TD for the 2nd time ever in the same week that I went to Custard Station! If we have to compare, I'd say that this is at the bottom of the heap for custard in St. Louis. 

The pros:
- Big portions
- Cheap

The cons:
The custard had no flavor! 

Sorry Custard Station, I'll drive farther for Ted Drewes or the Custard Factory the next time I want frozen custard.

Super cheesy goodness! I visited this place last night. 

Yays- 
- Lots of variety, including at least 4 for vegetarians and even a vegan mac n cheese option!
- They just added breadsticks to the menu
- Flights are coming!
- Good looking baked goods & Fitz's root beer
- Friendly workers
- Good location
- Yummy pasta - got the creamy pesto. SUPER cheesy!

Nays - 
- Furniture is definitely second hand and no ambiance to this place - just cheese!
- Expand the menu a BIT more!
- A little pricey- but this is a niche restaurant.

I'll go back!

fat city. i do not love krispy kreme.
who switches counterpeople mid-order? me and two friends went for a half dozen, they friggin love KK and finally dragged me here the day after new year's day. i was feeling vulnerable post-mummers. i said yes.

my friend asked for one of his original glazed to be hot. they forgot to do that.
the dark chocolate glazed was not good.
the dark chocolate kreme filled one way a-okay, but not at all worth the 360 calories.

it did appear clean in there though, so that earns 2 stars.

My friend and I traveled to Arizona for hiking, tacos, and sunshine, escaping the tireless Philly winter. 

What one doesn't think of, perhaps naively so, is that there is amazing sushi to be found in the desert. Sachiko was so delicious we went two nights in a row and here I sit back in Philly wishing I could go again! Perfect to sit at the sushi bar and look at the handwritten specials signs plastering the walls. The rolls were well executed and the shumai was piping hot. Get the cherry coke, you won't regret it!

something i believe must be noted for future patrons: i was aware they have a prix fix menu available, but i did not realize until i was already seated (with a reservation) that they ONLY have the prix fix menu. perhaps it was lost in translation for me.

it was still a tasty meal from start to finish, but i believe my stomach would have rather had me chosen a different restaurant. call me crazy, but i think one should be mentally prepared for a 6 course meal before committing to one! regardless, excellent desserts, pork chops, and very tasty house made vegetable soup!

30 mins before closing they had closed all their lanes and wouldn't take anyone else. The manager looked like he debated changing my tire but instead tried to upsell me on a price for next day on a tire that didn't match my car; this is the second time in a few years Goodyear turned me away 

Also they had no generic tires - only brand names for over 100 bucks

I drove five seconds to Firestone and the manager Michael saw me and 3 other people after me. There's also a Tuffys on this street so Goodyear turning people away with 4 people working and 30 mins left and tons of competition is stupid
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
The location is pretty random (at the end of a long winding road with a bunch of other hotel off of the highway with no food nearby) and the building has seen better days.  

My room featured an unclean floor, torn wallpaper, dusty bathroom vents, and water spots in the bathroom.  The hallways might remind one of "red rum" and the building itself is ugly showing it's age as a product of the 70s (as am I so I can judge).

The bed was comfortable and the room serviceable but it was disappointing as I have grown accustomed to a higher level of quality in my Doubletree experience throughout the country.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Great spot to grab a drink and watch the sunset. We've been here several times and enjoyed ourselves. 

The food is hit and miss. Do NOT order the smoked fish spread! It's way over processed and has the texture of baby food. Gross. The taco salad was passable, not bad but not stellar. The plate of nachos look like they cleaned out the walk in and just piled whatever on a plate, or possibly Emeril plated it. 

I ordered a Mai Tai once and I have no idea what she thought that consisted of but what I was served was not even close. Stick with beers and margaritas and that's pretty risk free.

I've been to Bobby Burger's Tavern a couple of times for lunch. It's your typical hole-in-the-wall dive bar, though surprisingly spacious (there's a back room with pool games). The food is pretty typical, although there are some fun variations on fries (chili, Irish, etc). It's a neighborhood bar, stocked with neighborhood Conshy people, plain and simple.

The beer menu is surprisingly craft-heavy, especially the seasonal taps, and I was able to choose from a bunch of local brews at great prices. Bonus points for the friendly bartender (Deb, I think).

Tired of the regular dining at the Palm, we caught a glimpse of this place from across the street and decided to try it out. Looked like a decent restaurant from the street however it wasn't the hustle and bustle during lunch. We were seated at a table by the large windows and had a leisurely lunch. Oysters, and more oysters were ordered, along with a couple of appetizers ... calamari and the likes. Then we went along with our pasta options for lunch. I'd say this place wasn't anything memorable, we were just curious. Nothing more, nothing less.

Meh...it's a Starbucks. What can I say. It's close to home but I've only been once and honestly I would rather drive 5 miles down Campbell and get some seriously bomb coffee.

I swore off corporate coffee a couple of years ago and every now and then I end up having to come for one reason or another. I ordered a Dirty Chai and it was horrible. Tasteless honestly. I could barely taste the Chai and there was no spice at all. It was probably the blandest tasting Dirty Chai I've ever had.

That's really all I have. No love loss here Starbuck's

There are Hilton Garden Inns around the country and they are all pretty much the same except for some minor differences.  The rooms in this hotel were clean and the beds were comfortable.  The air in the room tends to be either hot and dry or chilly as the rooms use forced heat.  

Couple of negatives for this hotel; 1.  The fitness room was a dungeon, overcrowded and dark.  2.  The hostess for the breakfast area had the personality of a prison guard and 3.  When they added the charge for the breakfast, they created another charge for the room so I have two hotel room charges on my American Express bill...very sloppy!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Since my last review I've had some pretty awful sushi experiences at Jay's... the first time my sushi wasn't that fresh I decided to give them another try and hope I ordered on a VERY off night. 

the next time I ordered, the sushi was awful. It takes a lot for me to put down a meal and opt to find something else to eat, and this was one of those cases. The fish itself was awful. The quality has gone down tremendously, which I guess is why they can support their low prices.

Since then, I have found a new sushi delivery place.

I used to be a huge fan of Machismos for the Main Street location in Manayunk and recently discovered this location.

Maybe the quality of both locations have gone down since it's been about 4 years since I've lived in that neighborhood, but I cant compare. I can say the steak was somewhat bland and chewy in the burrito I got. The flavors overall were lacking. The guacamole we ordered as a side was good, however, the chips tasted somewhat stale. 

On the plus side, if you check in while there on Yelp, you will receive a free fountain drink!

I'm somewhere between a 2-3 star review for them, but will round up with their "newly" created club card that helps with prices.

I stop in here a few times a month, usually to pick up random items for dinner that we don't have in the house. The prices are high...but its what you get in center city. They have a good selection overall.

I think their downfall is the freshness of a lot of their produce. I have bought basil (2.99!) and usually more than half of it is already slimy and browned when I open it up. I cave and buy it knowing this will happen, since I have minimal other options.

I must admit I only come to McDonald's for their $1 any sized iced coffee (caramel) all summer long and the occasional egg mcmuffin.  I'm pretty thrifty when it comes to McD and only come when I have a coupon. 

The reason I'm taking the time to review this location is because they are always pleasant and efficient. On numerous occasions when I have come through the drive thru and used a coupon the lady behind the till has cheered, "woo hoo!" and they have let me keep my coupon to be reused on several occasions.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
I've been to Lakeside twice now with the kitten I'm fostering and I have to say I'm really impressed. 

They have day, evening, and weekend appointments.  And they have office cats!  Yes, you read that right!  Adorable balls of purr walking around the office.  

My appointments have been on time thus far and the staff and vets alike have been great!  Everyone I k is who comes here raves about Lakeside.  

And access us a breeze - less than 5 minutes off the Anthony Henday west on Wye Road.

Lakeside is the purrfect Animal Clinic for all your furry friends!

I've been here for concerts as well as a closed set for filming a music video. 

It's everything you'd hope for in a country western bar.  I appreciate the multiple seating options, large washrooms, and double bar.  

Often I'm the DD and each time I've been pleasantly surprised that soda water was on the house. 

The venue has great sound and a lovely open air patio for summer months. 

If there's a country act coming to Knoxville's that you're wanting to see, don't think twice.  Plenty of room for two-steppin' & great sound! 

Until our next boot scootin' good time!

I've only ever hit up the drive thru at this location for a Happy Meal for the chitlins and a coffee for myself, but never had a problem.

It's at a fairly busy interchange so coming to and from this location can be limited depending on the time of day and the direction you are travelling.

No playspace here for offspring to burn off energy on a frosty winter's day so we'll keep the West Ed and Stony Plain Road locations as our main haunts.

Be sure to collect the sticker on the side of your coffee cup to trade in for a free medium coffee after purchasing 7 (used to be 6 but c'est la vie).
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Looooove this place.

The owner is super friendly and knowledgeable about coffee and the instant coffee machines.  He even helped us Jimmy Rig our new Keurig 2.0 to keep reading the no name cups.

Be sure to check out the clearance section in the back of the store for 50% off normal prices.

He also has a fill your carousel deal where you pick out individual K cups (24 I think) and it works out to just shy of $1 each which is awesome to trying specialty coffees/teas before committing to a full box.  

Coffee, decaf, tea, ciders, cocoa, syrups... you name it, he's got it!  The variety here can't be beat!

Brought the whole after Yelp Shops Local and what a disappointment.

First - no kids menu - blah.

We did the all you can eat Sushi and were not impressed.

Some items never came and others we watched tables receive that came in after us while we still waited for ours. 

Between the 4 of us we only ordered 30 pieces of sashimi YET they still charged us $2 twice for extra ginger and $2 twice for extra Teriyaki Sauce.  This is SUPER wrong when you've paid almost $100 and only ordered 30 pieces of sashimi each.

Also the hubs and I were not feeling very well later that night and the next day.

We love our Sushi but will never be back.

We really wanted Mexican last night and we were in a time crunch... we came here. It didn't start off all that great. We wait a few for our waitress and then after that had to wait a little bit longer for our drinks. Although the salsa was pretty tasty, unfortunately my step daughter found a hair in it.... My husband and I each ordered a variety of tacos and they were good. I especially recommend the fish taco. 

In spite of the hair situation and the slow waitress i would be willing to come back because the food was cheap and good for the price.

First I want to apologize to the staff of Twisted for not writing this review sooner. I have been there twice and I will keep coming back. My girl, Gerlaine has cut my hair twice and I'm always happy with the results. She even trims my beard!

The other staff here are friendly and like to talk with the customers. I actually stayed there for an extra 20 minutes just hanging out. The Atmosphere is pretty cool as they converted a house-type building and made it funky. 

Twisted is a perfect balance of avant garde, sophistication, and professionalism. Plus, they give you a discount if you mention Yelp.

WOW is all I should have to say about this experience. After eating at the Sakana in Summerset I wasn't that impressed but some friends wanted to go try their no location out and I am glad they did! The ambiance was nice, the chef's were amazing attentive and willing to answer questions. The servers promptly cleared our empty dishes and made sure our drinks stayed full. The sushi was amazing and I loved everything I tried I am pretty picky on the muscles and they were perfect! I am glad they opened near my house, I am pretty sure we will spend alot of sushi nights here.

Was craving Italian but was solo so I sat at the bar.  Kelley the bartender was extremely busy but gave me great service and recommendations.  Started with the mozzarella/risotto appetizer that he suggested and could not have been happier!  Creamy, cheesy, salty and in a small puddle of marinara with a sliver or parmesean on top!  Then had the spaghetti carbonara with a Stella to wash it down!  If you get a chance to stop by do not pass up the chance to sit at the bar with Kelley.  Even though he was super busy he still made treated me like I was the only one in the whole place.  Will definitely be back soon!

What a perfect dining experience. 
I went with my parents and my boyfriend. We ordered the Chef's Tasting Menu, which was definitely the way to go. Everything that came out was interesting, creative, and (most importantly) delicious. It was one of those dinners where you keep having to exclaim "THIS IS SO GOOD" between mouthfuls. Unusual food pairings (custard and caviar served in a hollowed-out egg?) kept things interesting through the 8 or so courses. The atmosphere felt very Nor Cal if you will: casual elegance, big homey wood tables, open kitchen, cookbooks on bookshelves. Totally understated, friendly and warm staff, great place overall.

I was majorly disappointed with Las Trojes when I visited.

The service was good and that may be their one redeeming quality. The food, on the other hand was bland with little to no seasoning.

I ordered carnitas which as a rule are quick fried pieces of shredded pork butt that is a staple at most Mexican restaurants. Here they are the equivalent of grilled pork chops. Not tender at all, not shredded, etc.

The beans and rice were very bland. Maybe it was an off night, but I will certainly drive past this place on my way home.

La Baia is right outside my door, which makes it a super convenient spot to grab dinner. You can usually get a table outside when it's nice out with no wait. It's a BYOB and there's no corkage fee. The staff is friendly. I only wish the food were a little better. 

It's basic Italian food. Nothing modern or fancy. And it's not bad, but it's not amazing, either. The texture of the gnocchi is great, but the pesto it comes in is way too salty. The best bet is the special of the day, which is often lamb. 

Also... this place is cash only. I almost never have any money on me, so I always have to plan in advance before going here.

I hadn't been here in years and was looking forward to trying it again. Ordered before I left work at 4 and picked up
15 mins later. The crab Rangoon was already cold and flavorless. Wonton soup for one had two wontons and no flavor. But the worst was the sesame chicken which was tough and covered in a sauce which was way too sweet and had weird other noodles in it. It was so tough to eat that I thru it out. The rice was already dried out. Basically felt like I received the lunch leftovers and paid way too much. Should have gone out of my way and gotten Panda Pavillion.

I stayed at this Hotel for one week and I did not like it as much as the Marriott Westshore that I spent the rest of my time in Tampa at.  It is much bigger and it has a much colder feel to it.  The views are better but there is a charge for parking (valet) and there is a limited number of restaurants within walking distance.

The workout facility is large and has 50 lbs dumbbells. 

I ended up changing hotels only because I found out that another project had already negotiated a better rate at the Westshore.   Maybe if I had stayed longer I would have warmed up to it.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Great find. Definitely comparable to Pinkberry or Red Mango in terms of quality, choices and overall store design and vibe. Very cool inside, a fortune must have been spent building this space out. The yogurt is actually better than Pinkberry in taste and quality.  Pinkberry mixes powder with liquid and Krave uses real frozen liquid yogurt that is more perishable. I met the owner Inga and he was pretty cool. They'll do very well and I will be back.  I had regular flavor yogurt with Cap'n Crunch, Strawberries and Coconut. Yum!

Anyone who gave this place bad reviews doesn't understand pizza.  It was absolutely delicious!!!!  The dough was fluffy and fresh, the cheese and sauce combo was perfect, and best of all.... delivery only took 17 minutes from the time of order to the knock at my door.  Totally impressed by that.  If you're home, hungry and want some tasty pizza this is your spot.  *Note, it's not thin crust pizza. Somewhere in the middle of deep dish and thin crust is where you'll find this dough -- at least for the Medium size.

I came on a Saturday afternoon and got a lunch combination - chicken teriyaki and California roll for $8.95. I was impressed with the amount of food for that price. It came with miso soup, a little salad, rice, and some kind of small appetizer type thing. I used the yelp check in offer for free edamame, too, so I was very full! I even took some of the leftover edamame and chicken teriyaki home! Service was very good. I can't speak for their actual sushi since this was my first time there - but the teriyaki was good. I would go back , especially for the good lunch deals.

This Dunkin Donuts is about two blocks from my apartment.  I usually only go there if I'm out of the coffee that I make at home and/or I'm too tired to go somewhere nicer. Well the other night I stopped in for a small coffee and a donut, but as I looked around at all the sad, empty bins, I realized they were out of donuts! Seriously, Dunkin Donuts was completely OUT of donuts. I asked the man at the counter if they had any in the back and he said "No. We make no more donuts until 4am." Mind you, it wasn't that late when I went in there...it was only 10pm. So the Dunkin Donuts is open 24 hours, but they don't have donuts from 10pm-4am? Really?

I have the opportunity to stay in a decent number of hotels (across the globe) for both  business and personal travel; My threshold of expectation is higher for personal travel   That said, even for business this is a tired and " one to be avoided" property. It is tired, worn, and in an awful location. There is a commuter train that runs just behind the hotel and blasts it's horn, interrupting your sleep. When checking in, the desk clerk joked with me: "I hope the train won't bother you"......it did and I won't be back.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Going to Sam's is always an adventure. You never know just what he is going to feel like adding to that roll you just ordered.  Which is mainly the reason I am not so much of a fan. I can be picky... especially when it comes to sushi. That and the fact that I have yet to be allowed to order miso soup with my meal. But the prices here are good especially if you are a quantity over quality kind of person. Sam's does take credit cards but just be sure that you don't leave him a tip. Unless of course you like to see a grown Japanese sushi chef flip his lid.

I'm not sure why I thought this place would be better than it was.  But we had a $2 draft coupon, so off we went. 

Since it was the afternoon, there was no cover.  They had cute T-shirts, so we checked those out.  I couldn't bring myself the spend $30 on it, though...

It was my birthday, and they made me do a $20 shot.  And I actually mean they MADE me.  It was a non-option unless I wanted to leave.  So in all fun and games, they drew on my husband (a penis joke) and tore his underwear and made it into a rambo bandana.  Funny, but not worth $20 of entertainment.

then they did it to the rest of the people at the bar.

Overrated!

I've never been the first to review something! Cool! Anyways, this is a great training gym. I went here for about a year when I lived in St. Louis and had a great experience working with Peggy. The owner really cares about his patrons and is involved with setting goals and doing assessments. 

The gym has the perfect balance between being supportive and also pushing you really hard. It is a small enough place that you get to know other trainers, gym-goers, and the desk administrators, which is nice. 

I would highly recommend this place if you have some fitness goals you need help achieving!
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Excellent location, plenty of free parking and a very workable free Wi-Fi.  Their breakfast buffet is good, but nothing really special stands out.  Staff is very courteous.  The place is very dated looking and could use an upgrade.  Old furniture etc.  I suggested to them that they need USB ports in the room.  The living room/kitchen area is very large but my bedroom was kind of small and I am not a big fan of the bathroom sink not actually in the bathroom.  As someone else noted, the toilet is a very weak flush----nervous moments!!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Casa's has consistently good food, and a great happy hour.  I usually order either a chicken burrito or the chicken Guadalajara, which are both terrific.  I love their corn cakes (my friend is obsessed with them and always orders an extra side).  I haven't had it in a while, but their fried ice-cream is especially yummy if you're in for dessert.  The service is also consistently fast and pleasant.  They also offer punch cards now; I think it's buy 5 entrees, get one free.  I'm still trying to make it sometime for their brunch on Sundays.

I really like this place. It's not overwhelmingly crowded, and if there is a wait it's not too long, you can always call in reservations too. I have to agree with the other reviewer about their Chicken Sonoma... this is one of the BEST chicken dishes I've ever had. I get it every time I go there. My wife loves their Salmon too. She is pretty picky about her fish, and she LOVES theirs. I also love that the seating is mostly booths, so you can actually have a conversation without screaming over the ambient noise.

I'm not sure why Supreme (Shop and Bag!) has such a terrible reputation. This isn't Whole Foods where your carrots are arranged in a pyramid.

They have a good selection of seasonal produce and if you go for the sales, you will NOT go broke. Bananas the other week were $0.39/lb and they were amazing. I haven't seen that price in a while. 

And the Brown and Serve sausage links were $.99 for the past few weeks... not bad!

The ladies at checkout will call you endearing names like "Baby" or "Sweetheart" and it will make your day. Or they'll just gossip, but that's ok too.

I got the spicy salmon salad and spicy salmon roll...big salmon fan as you can tell.

Came here on a friday night, it was packed but we got seated pretty quickly. The spicy salmon salad was okay, it was like minced salmon into a big circle. I was expecting like salmon sashimi ...not sure why. The spicy salmon roll was the same. It didn't come with actual salmon sashimi, it was like minced salmon. I really like sashimi so I was a bit disappointed. I would come back to try something else because it's BYOB. Gotta love BYOB places, I brought wine and soju.

this is one of the absolute best restaurants - not only in collingswood - but in south jersey. 
every dish is prepared perfectly, with great care and attention to detail. the chef comes out and talks to everyone, which is just further proof that he really cares about everyone's food!
i've been here twice, and eaten fish specials both times. screeeeamingly good. crazy good. wildly good. 
i've never been to italy but i'm pretty sure this is what real, authentic italian food is supposed to taste like.
try the carpaccio. and leave room for dessert!

I found this place very elegant and quaint. The servers couldn't have been nicer! 
My mother and I went here for lunch and were delightfully surprised at the Breakfast and Lunch only menu. She had the breakfast melt, and noted that the eggs were cooked precisely to her liking. I wanted the BLT but can't eat tomato. So any chance I can find a place willing to swap Tomato for Avocado on a BLT, I take it. Beautiful, just beautiful. 
 The portions are perfect and a choice of grits or home fries come with almost every meal. If you're on this side of town and looking for something new, give this place a shot!

Murray Cleaners is the place to go in this neighborhood. I used to go to the spot on 48th Street, and they messed my clothes up using way too much starch. And, they were not nearly as nice.

The lady who I always see at Murray Cleaners is very nice and very professional. They do a great job with my clothes, never using too much starch.

The prices are very fair. The service is great. They always get my stuff done in a reasonable time. And, they love it when I come with my baby. But then again, who doesn't love babies?
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Whenever I search for the best deals to rent a car, Alamo seems to pop up. And, they are just as good as any car rental company, so why not go with the cheapest?

The service is always great. They are quick and very friendly. I often get a free upgrade because their cheaper cars are out.

Additionally, you can usually find their cheapest rate also available through their own site. The bonus is that you can get that cheap rate even cheaper by using the prepay option. As long as you're not concerned about a possible last minute change of plans, this is the way to go.

This is a bit of a hidden spot. Just when I thought the night was over, one of my buddies led us up the stairs of The Corner. It's a small spot with a very cool 2nd floor outside deck.

When we arrived, the place was practically empty. The one couple that was there decided that our presence made it too crowed. After a while, two other groups joined the party. Still, it was not busy by a long shot.

Our waitress was very cool, super friendly. The drawback here is the beers are not on tap, which I really prefer. The waitress said the food is pretty good, so I might go back to taste it for myself.

THE place to buy wine in Saint Petersburg. My husband (a wine snob) jokes that Lee has forgotten more about wine than we'll ever know. Lee makes great wine recommendations and has never steered us wrong. I've enjoyed several wonderful wines I might not have ever tried without Lee's direction (I am NOT a wine snob). 

As for liquors, their selection beats everyone else in town. This is the only place we have found that carries Nassau Royale, a liquor we found while traveling in the Bahamas on our honeymoon. 

Prices are good. Service is excellent. Selection is superb.

I like to drink.

I like partying with other like minded individuals who aren't scared of having a good time.

I like potent frozen Hand Grenade drinks that make me feel feisty.

I like making a game of throwing the grenade toy into the basket.

I like trying to figure out the next day exactly WHICH Tropical Isle I went to and I like that the Hand Grenade is the reason why I can't quite remember.

Thus, I like Tropical Isle and hit it up everytime I come to New Orleans.  It is touristy and it is full of drunks...but I like it despite that.  Or because of it.

So I've been here twice now and think the Crossroads is an A-OK honky tonk on the lower Broadway circuit.  Actually, the first time I came here I only remember dancing to the band while one of the members winked at my brother's girlfriend.  Good times!  

This last time I remember a little more clearly.  Inexpensive drinks compared to the rest of Broadway.  Drunk tourists and locals all mingled together.  Good band.  Seats in the back.  Smoke 'em if you got 'em.  Bathrooms not too hideous.  

Bottom line: put the Crossroads on the regular rotation - this is a true honky tonk!

We had some friends getting married in the far away land of Lebanon so we decided to bite the bullet and get a hotel nearby. This one was conveniently the one where the wedding shuttle would pick up so we made a reservation!

This is your standard Hampton Inn. It's near some chain restaurants like Cracker Barrel and Such. It has free breakfast in the mornings and cookies in the PM. Check in was friendly. Rooms were comfortable and not fancy. Coffee maker and fridge in room. WiFi is available. 

Basically you could do worse than this hotel if you have a reason to stay somewhere in Gallatin.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Summary based on 1 two night stay:
--occasionally available on Hotwire as 2.5* with Amenities: Free Parking, Free Breakfast, Free Internet, Pool(s), Restaurant(s), Self service laundry, Internet access, Accessible bathroom, Handicapped parking  
--exterior corridors
--free parking in large lot that didn't seem too secure
--relatively quiet
--fairly convenient to Interstate
--unlike others, found it clean and room security ok
--typical cheapo, sugary breakfast for this class of hotel. Ok.

I'd stay here again with a good rate.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Well lately I've been trying to branch out from my typical Mexican establishments to see if I can find something special. This was not it.
