It was not Tex-Mex. I will give it that. The horchata was decent and not over sweetened like many places. I ordered Al Pastor, Chorizo, and Lengua tacos. Of these three the Lengua was by far the best. The other two were par for Indianapolis. 

There service was very good and they were excited to see me interested in the authentic qualities of the place but if you are on this side of town and looking for real Mexican food I would probably say go down the street to La Canasta.

Went Monday night for my b-day. Still our favorite place in the Reno area for sushi. Service is GREAT, rolls are very creative, and overall a solid solid place. 

Non-rice items that are fantastic: Volcano, Renee chips, Loise 13, Ahi Platter. 

Rolls that are excellent: Super Star, Battleship, and I forget the rest. 

Chefs are relaxed about making changes to listed rolls (at least for me they were). I usually add tobiko and salmon skin, sometimes yamagobo too, to some rolls. No problem. 

Still #1. (But not recommended because I don't want this place to become the new "it" spot. Selfish, I know).

Upon arriving in NOLA, we discovered that a number of places close down at or around 11pm, so in roaming around the Quarter and trying to find a decent place for a night cap, my husband and I discovered 21st Amendment.  The bartenders were friendly, and while we only caught the tail end of the live music, it was a nice hideout away from the mess that's Bourbon Street.  I had their Frenchy cocktail while my husband had the La Louisiane.  Both were good and since we were staying just down the street, it was also convenient! Definitely a great alternative to slushy frozen drinks, Hand Grenades, and Hurricanes!

OKs - not the a good experience here.  When I checked in - they had to a person training someone - but had to wait for the trainer to comeback in order to check me in.  Took like 20 mins.  Then they promised me very breakfast in the morning for all the hassle.  They never brought me the voucher.  Bad move.

Room was very outdated.  Something from the 70s.  Needs a complete remodel or teardown.  More of a holiday inn than a crowne plaza.  TVs were small and old CRTs.  Terrible.  Workout room was small with older machines.  

Not coming back.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
***A warning to others looking for Sonoran Hot Dog Goodness***

My husband and I drove to Franciscos (which during the day is called "Franks") expecting to get the delicious tacos and sonoran hot dogs - however we were beyond disappointed to find that during the daytime, "FRANKS" serves boring things like omlettes and sandwiches.  There was like one friend flauta or something on the menu.  They also gave us a sonoran hot dog but without any of the special toppings.  It was a huge let down.  Learn from my experience, and go after 6pm.

I had the Blanche Bruxelles beer which is excellent especially right out of the tap. I think of it as a summer beer but when the weather is cold outside it brings back warm memories of the summer. The Reno Public House is just getting started and they were moving new tables and benches in while I was there. I like the place though the hours are a challenge for me since they don't open until 3pm and I can usually only stop by a pub for one beer at lunch time if at all.

I'll be back if my schedule permits but right now the jury is still out.

After getting a sandwich at the Rubicon Deli, I went into St. James Infirmary to check it out since it is in the front (Cal Ave side) of the same building as Rubicon. I only had time for one beer because my phone started blowing up so I had to step outside and then go.

I like the decor and the solid selection of beers on draft. I had a Belgian Wit beer with a slight hint of apple nose. I know it sounded weird enough to me, to want to try it and I really liked it. I forgot the name of it but it was good, not sweet, just a hint of apple on the sour/citrus side.

I shall return, hopefully soon.

46 bucks and 2 minutes from Bourbon street you cant really complain, but if you plan on spending time in your room, pay the extra money and stay somewhere else. The young lady helping us was very unprofessional, she was talking about drinking and partying on the phone while we waited to check in. After she was done with conversation she showed us to out room, and it just felt dirty and dingy. The one awesome thing about the room it had a bidet. 

Bottom line is if your going to New Orleans with a group of friends and plan on spending little to no time in the room its an ideal hotel, if not stay far, far away from this place.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The food was delicious, but the wait was horrific. Made a reservation for 9:30. NINE THIRTY! WTF! and waited a full hour before we were seated. 

We had the 4 course tasting menu and ate the following: 

Foie Gras Soup / Pork Belly Chili Oil: The pork belly was out of this world. Loved it
Calamari / Octopus: Loved the octopus and the way it was charred
Meatloaf / Rabbit Pappardelle: The rabbit definitely won this round. 

For dessert, the only thing I remember was the rice pudding which bore an uncanny resemblance to the rice pudding that I loved at Aldea.

After sleeping on air mattresses for several days in the DC area (the downside of make a trip to see the inauguration), I was really looking forward to sleeping on a real bed before flying back to Oakland from PHL.

Unfortunately, due to traffic in Baltimore, meeting with friends in West Chester, an accident on a highway in the Philadelphia suburbs and meeting with more friends inside Philly, we didn't check in to this hotel until almost 1 AM.

Despite a very limited amount of time in this hotel, a king sized bed was welcome and so were the flatscreen TV's.

I only wish we were here longer.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
just not a fan. it is full of late 20's wanna be, suited, superstars, who look at you like youre lunch. then there are the girls who love them. tons of undeserved ego up in there. there is no diversity. i feel like i could never relax and have a cocktail without some dude laying some lame game on me. like, look at me. i wear a suit. i must be successful and interesting. 
it's painful to witness. the service sucked all 3 times i was there. i never had the food, but if its like the crowd, its boring. flavorless. go here if you want to hook up with a d bag. if its d bags youre looking for, then 5 stars!

Hand grenades are the devil. Incarnate. I don't know what's in these deadly green concoctions, but if I had to guess, I'd go with Everclear. As a seasoned drinker, I barely knew what hit me. 

They give you a little mini grenade with each drink, presumably to keep track of how many you've had ... no need, as I can't possibly imagine ever drinking more than two without hospitalization.

This is definitely an epic New Orleans experience, although I warn you - eat first, or you may not remember your Bourbon Street escapades!

I had the duck lomein but all I can say is MEH. It's only $7 which is pretty cheap compared to the amount noodles and duck meat you are getting. The first bite was good but I got sick of it the more I ate it. It gets saltier as you eat and the meat still kind of had that distinctive duck smell which can be unpleasant. Plus I'm not much of a duck person other than Peking duck lol. Overall, good cheap eats but not something I would be able eat by itself unless accompanied with other food. Perhaps the original location instead of RTM would have been better.

I was nervous about how they would reconfigure the space Borders wasted as a bookstore.  I'm happy for the changes! This space is a well-deserved addition to this stretch of St. Charles avenue. The staff was plentiful and helpful. Everything appears extremely fresh and there's a strong emphasis on local produce. Upstairs, a space for dining and a decent selection of hard liquor, beer & wine is available. Best of all? I can now buy Peet's coffee locally!!!! Cartwheels!!!!

Why four stars?

The parking is, and was abysmal, so there will be no rush hour shopping. If you offered delivery, five stars would be so here.

This sushi bar is located between El Dorado and Silver Legacy.  We tried to sit at the bar and order, since nobody was around to seat us, but we were asked to leave since the bar was for All You Can Eat Only.  So weird their AYCE is charged by the hour, and not by the person.  

We shared a roll and a miso soup.  The tofu in the miso soup was not cut up with care, as they were all different sizes.  The Gecko roll, their friend roll felt like a frozen or premade roll they keep in the back, and just fry (with no batter) as you order.

Not a good roll, I wouldn't go back.

I heart Breaux Mart for my own reasons, those being easy in and out for the quick 12 pack or pint of ice cream.  Otherwise my experience with this space = neutral.  

Once upon a time this was a drag ass A & P, and thank the grocery gods Breaux Mart not only took it over but gave it an almost 100% facelift post K.

The staff are friendly, and the prices can be cheap though they're likely average to above average (though a 12 pack of Tecate is just $9.99!).

Great parking lot, great location, and there's a convenient service counter at the front of the store for quick checkout or purchases of the harder stuff.

I've eaten here several times since it's close to my office, and it is really hit-or-miss.. (mostly miss).  The bourbon chicken is extremely dried out and chewy, not the succulent, tender dish it's meant to be.  The veggie dumplings were most likely frozen and were an off-putting green color.  The sesame chicken was not bad, and would probably be the only thing I would go back for if I am craving Chinese food.  The best thing I had there was the bubble tea, which comes in a variety of flavors.  Overall, a pretty underwhelming experience.

Vincent's is great for those last minute groceries. Sometimes going to the real grocery stores can be overwhelming since they are so busy and spread out. Vincent's has everything a regular grocery store has but in a much more casual space. 

The selection is pretty great and the service is always wonderful. Vincent himself is usually there when I go in for a visit. It's great to know that this store is really a family run place where they really do care about their customers! 

They also have a great beer and wine selection if that is what you are looking for.

I really like the Cat's Meow for a bunch of reasons, but mainly I like it because it's a small dive bar in my neighborhood! 

There are times when my friends and I try to figure out a place to go for a few drinks and since we are always broke we need a cheap drink spot. Cat's Meow delivers. They have cheap pitchers and really cheap "shot specials" including  an Apple Pie shot. 

The inside of the bar is very small, but this just means that everyone has to sit closer and mingle. The bartenders are friendly and they are quick. Remember to bring cash since this is a cash only bar, but they do have an ATM if needed.

You go because everyone goes there and you need something that tastes like drunken death, so....  let's get hand grenades all around!  You do it because you have to, and yet every time you visit, you do it again.  And again.  And every time, as the years go by, you may hate yourself just a little bit more, but you can't just *not* do it.  So go ahead, tough guy, get one. Hell, court death and get two.  Either way, close your eyes and think of Mother England and enjoy the rest of what you remember for your evening!

With no Yelp within an arm's reach and after a test run on the Philly Triathlon's bike course this place looked like a solid place to refuel.  The restaurant is nice on the inside and offers outdoor seating right off Kelly Drive.  Other than looks, there doesn't seem to be too much left to offer.  The food is NOT bad, just not enough to brag about.  The menu consists of typical Italian dishes but nothing worth noting.  The service was pleasant but unremarkable.  There just isn't enough for me to make a return.

After days of searching for a somewhat inexpensive hotel  for a one-night stay in St. Louis, I settled on this one.  Going into it, I knew it would be a bit farther than I wanted from downtown but in terms of travel and proximity to Interstate 70, this hotel was perfect.  The staff and amenities were great and the room was spacious.  I couldn't really ask for more for a one-night stay other than being closer to the city.  Next time, if there is one, I will definitely pay a bit more to be in downtown but if you want a nice hotel close to the airport and about 15 minutes from all the action, this is your place.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: We have been here twice in the past 4 months. We weren't over-the-moon with our first visit, so we went back. The food isn't terrible, but it just isn't great. It's no better than what I can cook at home. It's not worth going to a restaurant and spending a ton of money for mediocre pasta. The space itself is nice and the staff is great. We used to live in Montgomery County and would go to a place called From The Boot where the food would have you praising the gods with every bite. This is NOT that type of place. It's fine.

There are tropical aisles strewn all over the vicinity of Bourbon Street, but pick one.  

I consider the hand grenade a kind of passage for first time New Orleaners.  Does it taste like Pixy Sticks, Laffy-Taffy and Sweet Tarts blended?  Yup!  Does it come with a foot long cup to make you look like a tool-bag?  Yup!  Does is knock you out quickly?  Yup!  For all these reasons the hand grenade needs to be on your list of things to accomplish in NOLA.  

You probably won't want to go back for seconds, but there's nothing wrong with a one-timer every once in a while.  Right?!

Still fantastic! Free miso soup in the wintertime is amazing, and the tuna is still the best I've had. The service is fast and friendly too, a nice change from Sakura (see my review). They've been a lot busier the last couple times I've gone, so make reservations if you're going on a weekend.

However, I don't recommend getting anything with the tempura "crunchies" as an ingredient. I ordered the "Funky Tuna" roll and was less than impressed because of this unfortunate addition. They're kind of greasy and flavorless.

So the place isn't terrible and it's not amazing... I travel to this area a lot and have tried several other hotels in the area. It's at a decent location, but is somewhat hard to find if you don't know your way around.  The service is great, bed is comfortable, but the rooms are a little small for my liking.  
There's a small indoor pool and the gym is great. The eating area can get a little cramped and there is a complimentary continental breakfast.  Once in a while they'll have a pile of Clif bars (bonus!)
All in all decent...  not the first place I'll try and book, but would be content here.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This is a pretty standard hotel--small, cozy, boutique-y. Nothing too special about it. The service is good--everyone was super friendly. The rooms are small, but well-appointed. On a random note, they have those flush-with-your-foot toilets. Seemed somehow industrial and out of place. ANYWAY...

Montecito in general is very sleepy and quiet. The hotel is right near the freeway for easy access to downtown SB (less than 10 minutes). We were here for a wedding at San Ysidro Ranch, and Montecito Inn is 5 mins or so from there.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
i got the shrimp & corn soup special and the cobb salad. the soup was really good, especially when you dump a ton of Crystal sauce in it. 

the cob salad was huge and very good. the grilled chicken was just right and tasted like the grill, which i dig. i actually felt full after this salad and i can throw down at lunch. 

i would like to make it here for breakfast/brunch but i'm never downtown during the day so we'll have to wait on that. 

i would come back. they are proud of their food but prices are high everywhere downtown, at least where you would want to eat.

now that i know Chef Shun is at Sachiko, i'm gonna say it's the best in town. the variety they offer is unmatched. bluefin toro sashimi for $6.95 is unheard of. we got that, hamachi toro, spicy yellowtail roll, hamachi sashimi (which was some of the best i've ever had), and the bbq bluefin toro kama - which was out of this world. 

now, i'm a dedicated Chef Shun fan - i love the guy. he is the best around. i highly recommend sitting in front of him and letting HIM tell you what to get. after all, he is the expert. 

i thoroughly enjoyed my meal, the staff, and the atmosphere.

I was very skeptical when I was told by the receptionist that my trim would cost $60, but I was very satisfied with the cut. I recommend Chris, he gave great suggestions about products to use (and avoid!) on my type of hair, was very personable, and was very meticulous. I am giving this salon only 3 stars because the service was not at all reflective of the high prices Giovanni charges. The receptionists were not very welcoming or helpful, but the salon itself was located in a historic and beautiful building.

Bar 635 is part of a network of bars along Bourbon. I would classify Bar 635 as the crazier, drop-it-low one with frequent live rock music. They were spilling beats onto the street to lure the wild ones in. There's no better place to show off your twerk.

If you do prefer a little calmer atmosphere, the connected bar might be more of your style with live jazz. I was able to access this by going up the stairs and across. While you are on the 2nd floor, make sure to pass by the balcony. In my opinion, this was the most accessible balcony in all of Bourbon Street. Many of the others tend to be restaurant reservation type tables.

Cheap drinks, good beers on tap, karaoke, and they let you smoke inside. Word up. This is the kinda place I can get used to at 1ish in the morning coming back from wherever.

The place isn't huge, but it doesn't need to be. Diverse crowd inside, but if I had to nail down the type of crowd, I'd say... well, I dunno. You just have to go there. They're really friendly. Especially on karaoke night.

I'm a huge sucker for singing songs to strangers, aren't I?

Oh, and clean bathrooms! You can't underrate that!

Again, this place was a pleasant find amongst many overhyped and overcrowded bars in the area. Will be back.

I've always liked you, Doc's. You've been in the shopping center forever, and your selection includes a healthy mix of craft.

Then you opened your beer take-away and mini bar next door. Oh yes. Make my own six packs with a candy store level of selection? Rock bottom prices that laugh in the face of other beer take-aways with similar selection, but whose pricing always has me begrudgingly thinking "this costs almost as much as a case" when I'd only bought a dozen beers? Friendly, knowledgeable service?

Yes, please.

I visit my parents in Andorra almost every weekend. You bet your ass that I'll be visiting Doc's, too.

This place would get a fourth star, if only the service was more professional.

At 1PM there were no other people in restaurant.  We had to wait several minutes for the waitress to stop chatting with 5 or 6 guys congregating behind sushi bar.  Only then did she approach us and get our order.  Adding to this, her mastery of English language did not break the boundaries of the names of dishes on the menu, so asking about a dish is a futile task.

The good side of it is relatively good interior, decent hot and cold dishes and modest pricing.

Killing time while waiting for someone, I needed a shot of caffeine as a picker-upper. There's nothing too different from this place from any other of the 3,984 other Starbucks within a 50 mile radius.

I ordered a mocha frappucino, they made it, spelled my name wrong, it was delivered, I sipped it. I'm a rebel. I refuse to use the words "venti" or "grande" or whatever. I steadfastly ask for a SMALL.

In the meantime, I was provided with a nice clean bathroom and a comfortable place to sit and relax until it was time to head out.

I don't know, I feel like this is one of the unfriendliest Subways I've ever stepped foot in. For convenience sake, it's very close to where I work but after I tried it once, I opted not to return.  Perhaps they have had issues with other customers, but to a casual observer like me sitting down and watching how they talked and watched over people coming in and out, they acted like they thought everyone in there was about to rob them or steal them blind.  Very unfortunate, very uncomfortable.

Their sandwich making was also sloppy.

How to start off a cross country jaunt for a move back east? Why an early morning pit stop at Dunkin Donuts, of course!  If you are from the east coast, DD's was THE place for donuts, cheap and fast.

I'm boring and nearly always order the same thing, a medium coffee, extra extra (because it's gotta taste like Haagen Daz coffee ice cream) and a glazed chocolate donut. It's only 874 calories! I'm kidding. As long as you are not eating this every day, you won't die.

Service was fast, everything was just a couple of bucks, and I was fueled up and ready to drive 2,900 miles.

Got ourselves a rad little red Ford Focus - it was perfectly fine for a long, rainy weekend.  Here's what happened - three of us arrived at SBA expecting to Uber it to our AirBnB.  They quoted us $47 for a one way ride to go a couple of miles! Okay, I get it, torrential rains, yada yada yada.  We checked online and found we could find one a cheap car rental for around $20 a day - worth it to have our own car at our convenience. These guys offered to match the rates we found online plus threw in some extras. SOLD.

Perfect for what I needed and very nice people to deal with.

Conveniently located in a little shopping center where you can get gas, coffee, groceries and cash - why not add ice cream?  It's definitely a splurge - if you do the math, don't cringe because you're basically paying for the equivalent of a pint of ice cream for just one scoop.  But you are really just paying for convenience.

One funny story - my friend from Ireland was visiting and wanted some ice cream. We walked in and saw there were dozens of different flavors, which I thought would boggle his wee Irish brain.  So what flavor does he want?  FREAKING VANILLA.

He said it was the best vanilla ice cream he's ever had.

Sigh.

Been there two times.  The first time it was quiet and I got two killer bloody mary's.  The second time it was busy and my bloody mary was lame.  The inside of this place is nice and dark, picture a florists.  Now turn out the lights add a bunch of bottles of alcohol where the vases would be and remove all the flower clippings and that is what the Reno Public house is like. 

The guys behind the counter were friendly when both slammed and and not too busy.  Parking in this area can be a small hike if it's busy.  

I will probably go here again.  It's centrally located and they can make a killer bloody mary.

WOW! The 2 of us were stuffed on $12 of food including tip.

I had some chicken tacos and an endless supply of tortilla chips and salsa (AMAZING SALSA). The salsa was nice and spicy and I put some hot sauce on my tacos which helped, too. The tacos were good and tasted authentic. 

The service was speedy and they were one of the few places around still serving food that late at night (around 11:30 pm on a Sat night).

The bar wasn't too crowded and the tv's were plentiful. They had a live band, but it wasn't so great. No cover. Street parking was hard to find at that hour.

We'll be BACK!

Super attentive staff, great location, comfy bed, good room service, Illy coffee. Hotel is very small only about 10 rooms per floor. The rooms are pretty small too - like the luggage valet cart doesn't fit in closet and the king bed takes most of the room. The business traveller desk is tiny and your feet dangle as they use a bar stool style chair. The hotel is connected to a mall that has walkways to other hotels. Location is awesome, walkable to lots of restaurants and shops. All and all a decent place to rest your head on business travel. Thumbs up!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
WOW I can't believe no one has ever reviewed the Homedale Inn!  Well I used to live right down the street and this was one of our favorite neighborhood spots when we didn't feel like venturing out much.  This place has been around forever!  (since 1937 to be exact).  I am not a beer person but they carry lots of beers.

Each night of the week they host different events (darts, open mic, comedy, trivia and the famous New Orleans classic "steak night").  It's a perfectly respectable neighborhood joint bar for you to hang out at.

Ever notice how the TV show Cops always seem to be in Florida in some trailer park busting funny meth heads? Well, if they ever come out with a show called Bar Cops, this will acquire most of the raw footage.

Most reviews are right. If you have a 20 dollar bill and absolutely don't feel like walking further than 100 yards then this is your place. If you ask me what was worse, Bobby Burgers or this place, I may slightly lean towards Bobby's but not by much.

Bottom line; If you ever wondered where all of our money goes from our taxes we put into welfare, take a trip to the Casmar.

I might as well cut and paste Shawn H's review into this space....
This location is always clean and friendly but I never walk-in because it is so durn slooooooooooooooow. The drive thru is a tad better. 

Another toughie is the location, as it can be a major pain the arse to exit the parking lot with the awkward one-way and sometimes horrid West End traffic.

Now that I'm done with being Debbie Downer, I can't emphasis on how a Wendy's drive-thru can save the day every now and then with healthier fast food options for when I can't slow down. The side salad and plain baked potato are low on the guilt scale.

I really dig the overall aesthetic and epicurean selection at Fresh Market however I was really surprised that they didn't offer more vegan options at their prepared foods section. They didn't have a single dish with tofu in it and many of the dishes that could easily be vegan included cheese.

Regarding the rest of the store, I loved the curated sections of products that included a rather impressive wine and bulk candy section.  The produce selection was enticing and the staff was very friendly and accommodating. 

Prices were a bit in the higher side but the quality of brands and produce off-set much of the expense!

When I do end up here...it is at the end of a booze soaked evening but never as a starting point. Most people don't make the best choices after getting intoxicated...

This place is a lot of fun if you come with your own group or "posse" but I would never come here without a couple of partners in crime. The crowd has always been in the "college age" demographic when I have visited...so I don't really have much interest there. I can't deny that fun evenings can be had but this just wouldn't be my first choice. 

On the flipside,the bartenders have always been great and I think that the drink prices are fair. 

That's all I got.

Sometimes it's just plain difficult to find a sushi spot open for lunch on a Sunday in Nashville but I was pleasantly surprised that O'sake located in Elliston Place was.

Quiet spot with no frills but nice service.
We ordered the vegetable gyoza ($5.95) which were a great way to start off the meal and a few rolls. I enjoyed the asapragus tempura roll ($4.95) and a pickled vegetable roll (Dayang roll?) $4.95. 

Prices are fair and this is a good option if you are seeking a low-key meal without any flash. 

I will likely pay another visit or do carry-out!

TIP: If you like Udon soup, they have a nice selection of varied versions here!

You know, this place isn't bad, and perhaps I'm allowing my disappointment to negatively affect my reviews, but I think I'll be sticking with my Kraft mac and cheese thanks.  

I got the Mediterranean, because if you say goat cheese I say, yes please.  It came out reasonably quickly, and was a good size.  I must admit, I did eat it all, but it was slightly soggy, super heavy, and I just was not wowed.  I ate with a group of 7 others and we all had similar opinions despite our different orders.  Then we all went home and napped, because... what else could we do?

I thought this place had a lot of redneck charm! Especially when one of the patrons drank too much and broke his chair! 

Mom and dad LOVED the pitcher of shock top and the wings! 
The fried chicken club comes loaded with cheese and super crispy bacon but could've used a sauce to cut out the dryness of the chicken breast. The chicken breast sandwich had the same problem although the toasted ravioli is good loaded with meat sauce.
The best part about this place though is DEFINITELY the massive quantity of wings. Ask for it super spicy and it will rock out!

I was pretty surprised by this little yogurt place! I loved being able to design my on little frozen yogurt sundae with all the toppings. I chose the Kona and Cheesecake flavored yogurts with cheesecake chunks, brownies, and Nilla wafers...YUMMY! Then hubby had the chocolate and Kona flavored yogurt with brownies and white chocolate chips. Once you've finished filling your bowl, you just pop on over to the register and place your bowls on the scale. The cost is .33 per ounce....we both had very full sundaes and each cost about $4.60. Not too shabby!

We already started planning out future flavor endeavors.....LOL!

i think this place is just okay.   It's no Chatham Tap, I'll tell you that much.

The patio is about all it has going for it, really.   And it is a good patio.   if it weren't for the patio it would be a no go.  In fact, there have been times when I have come here and realized the patio was full and the inside was a billion degrees so I left and went to Chatham.

I haven't had a lot of the food, but what I have had was, like I said, just okay.   Same with the service, not terrible but not anything to tell your friends about.

I will try the nachos soon and update, hopefully with better results.

Quaint and cozy.  I drive all the way from Metairie to check out "Treme" with other Yelpers and it's a nice time.  The ambiance is very warm with two great televisions to watch whatever you want with closed captioning.  The bar area is conveniently laid out, and the conversation area is very much conducive to a good time with friends.  

What I really envision is a place a couple can go to have a nice talk and a drink when the "Treme" fans aren't filling the place up. ;-) I haven't ventured out to the pool area yet, but it looks like another great gathering area for friends to chill and have a few laughs.

I'm really not a pizza eater. I blame my college's dining halls for my overdosing on it when I was there. But if/when I am forced to grab a pie, Slice is a pretty darn good option. The pizza is fresh, thin slice, and can be customized (all pizzas can have other ingredients added to them before heating) Their choices are creative and a little higher-end in comparison to most pizza places. 
The staff is friendly and talks to you as if they've known you forever. They seem to deliver absolutely everywhere (they were delivering a pie to the Navy Yard last time I was here).

Went to Borst after seeing a Groupon for an oil change and inspection for $19. An awesome deal! After the inspection was completed, I was shown a list of items that needed to be repaired on my vehicle. This would have been great if the prices were reasonable. I was quoted for new rear brakes for $330. I kindly refused the repairs and drove down the road to another business where they were replaced 45 mins later for $180, almost 50% less than Borst. I can understand that small businesses have to make their money somehow, but overcharging for services is not the way to go.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
You'd think that in fancy pants Rittenhouse Square that a "market" would be nicer than this dump. You'd be wrong. Everything here is old. Old meat, old produce, old deli salads. The meat is super dicey, We've been burned more than once (which does call our common sense into question). But the prices are certainly what you'd expect. Convenience comes at a cost. 

Now that we have a car and can drive to the beautiful Superfresh, I would like to say I'll never be back, but let's be honest. Parking is a bitch. 

Note to self: don't buy the meat.

So far out of the three Habit's I've been to, this one is by far the best.

It's the best because unlike the others, they have a chili burger here! I can't compare the Chili to Tommy's because they're different, but it's good here and I'm itching to go back to have another.

And the onion rings are to die for. Just the right amount of onion and batter, served with ranch (and thanks to the girl I also use BBQ sauce at the same time as well).

If you're in Santa Barbara, be sure to stop in and see what you've been missing.

I heard great things about the refinery so I had to check it out! The outside rooftop seating was great, the atmosphere was amazing. They were out of several red wines that night so I had to pick between two. It was good, I just wish I had options. We started with a small plate..the pork belly, it was cooked perfectly, but I felt like it needed a sauce to pull it together. For my entree I had roasted chicken with leeks. The chicken portion was huge, I could of used another side dish and less protein. It was delicious though and the service was amazing! I would like to try again but I will not go out of my way.

I collect Hard Rock Cafe pins from all over the world. 

I had to have one from my own city! 

This place could be 5 stars easily if they were more locally involved... if they held better live entertainment. I never hear anything going on with this place so it's easy to forget it's even there. 

Unfortunately, other than the merchandise, all the Hard Rocks are the same. I wish they allowed them to be a little more unique and become integrated with the local culture. 

Hmm... maybe I'll open my own chain and do things better.

Anyways, I go for the pins

I will 2nd that the pizza here is awesome. Don't let the comment about it being a little greasy scare you - in my opinion there is good greasy and bad greasy. Jean's isn't "puddles of grease sitting on top of the cheese" greasy (ew), it's more that it's just a very moist slice of pizza. Perfect cheese-to-sauce ratio - there is lots of it but one doesn't overpower the other - and the crust is lightly crispy but mostly soft and chewy. Definitely not the place to go if you're into thin, extra crispy and "light" feeling pizza, but for those of us who appreciate a hefty, gooey slice, Jean's is full of win.

i came here all the time, and have for 3 years now. the sushi is always fresh and if i am lucky enough to get my favorite chef really nicely sized rolls. the super california is a must its a mouth full tho but whos complaining if you go try it its not on the menu though. i also like the albacore here the sauce they put on it is really good.

another reason i love this place is because they are one of the only sushi places that still give you miso free and on top of that they give edamame and a warm cloth which on a cold day feels amazing.

It took me a while to visit Samurai, because I thought with a name like that, it might not be authentic.  It turns out that this is a great place for real Japanese comfort food.  It is fast food compared to the usual Japanese restaurants, but you still wait for it to be cooked and it can still be healthy.  It's great to be able to get unagi-don, katsudon, and other dons (rice bowls) which are very simple lunch meals, but not the sort of thing I can easily put together at home.  If I worked a little closer to them, I would come every week!

The sushi here is pretty good. I always get the spicy tuna, spicy yellowtail or any of the speciality rolls when I come here. I wouldn't suggest the salmon roe though... I've had it a few times here and its always been a disappointment. The other sushi items are all pretty good. 

Every time I come here I have to get the tempura ramen. Something about those tempura flakes and veggies in the ramen.

I would give them a 4 but I really do get disappointed about the salmon roe (my absolute favorite). Oh and a plus is that they are open pretty late.

I think this place hits the right spot when you're being a gluttonous slob at home watching movies or catching up on your latest T.V. shows. Portions are generous, taste is okay, and the delivery fee is cheap compared to other places on Grubhub. I like their roast pork fried rice and their steamed dumplings. Their lo-mein is okay (fried rice is better), and their entrees are also generously portioned and above-average for takeout. 

This place is definitely not sit-in but take-out and delivery only, though dining in is probably not entirely out of the question.

The last 2 times I came here we had to wait VERY LONG for our 2nd and 3rd plates of AYCE crabs. We complained to the manager and all he did was come out with the crabs when they were done which was a half an hour later. It was one SMALL cluster with NO CLAW! I asked them to put another order in right away. My husband was so disgusted he left. I waited for my crabs, another 20 minutes and thy were partially frozen!!!! I know what you guys are doing, taylors. I'm no dummy. Unfortunately for you, you just lost a weekly customer!

Quite good...fresh ingredients.....super nice people with no language barrier....

if you are eating in house...be sure to ask for real utensils...

burrito was plenty full, and delicious....just not as impressed with salsas as I am at other places.

....of course...that is a matter of taste....and everything is obviously house made of quality ingredients.

Support locally owned !!!

I will most assuredly return !

...and they had an infomercial for "Little Giant" ladders on the tv....how did I get through life without one ??

Quintessential bar from the era of Happy Days !  While the crusty proprietor is now ensuring and enforcing correct bar etiquette at the great saloon in the sky...his legacy lives on in the form of the retro charming Red Key Tavern.

Usually an interesting mix of patrons...and excellent old skool juke box...and pretty darn good burgers...but ya won't find goat cheese or any kind o aioli offered...good ol' pre slice processed cheese like product to adorn your burger !

Great neighborhood bar with lots of history and the aforementioned charm....

Well worth a stop on your libatious travels !

I thoroughly enjoyed my time at this cute boutique hotel. The staff was super friendly, and the food and drinks at the bar/restaurant were delicious (they actually had drinks named after two of my rockstars songs: When Doves Cry and Purple Rain). My room decor was adorable. I especially liked the comfortable, king sized bed, full length mirror, sliding bathroom door, and big screen television. Unfortunately, there was a problem with my television working properly almost every night, and the broken iron leaked water all over my dress and the floor. Definitely worth a stay.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Maybe if they had been more responsive to my request for a car closer to my  house (I even offered up parking spaces, both in front of my house and in a small parking lot) I wouldn't have started using Zipcar so much. Though my neighbors are interested in car share, it seems that we  just don't live in "targeted neighborhood." 6 months later and I've used Philly CarShare once, and now they want to charge me $15 a month? No thanks. 

I'd love to support a nonprofit, but I like options and service, too. When I called to cancel their phones were ringing off the hook. Maybe they'll learn a lesson and make some changes for the better.

This place is around the corner from my house, so naturally I'd try it.  We were always getting coupons dropped at our door with some good deals, but it's not even worth the money I'm saving.  The pizza is terrible, I think Pizza Hut has better pizza and that's saying alot considering I don't like pizza from chains, at all.  Thick, white crust.  Low quality cheese, bland sauce.  And not only is it bad, but it takes so long for anything you order!  It's also sort of a shady business.  There's always men sitting around outside, sometimes around 3-4 am.  I know it's their business what they're doing, but it's still a little shady.

I love the Mom and Pop shop sushi bars - but with all the five star reviews for Vic I must have shown up on a day when the chef was hung over.  Ordered a three roll combo for 11 bucks that I might as well of gotten at a mall food court for 8... but then again shame on me for taking the cheap way out.  The real crimes were something very funky with the soy sauce and a general sliminess to all the fish.

That said I went with a regular who said it was the only bad experience he's ever had there - and he's in there twice a week on average - so I'll probably try it out again.

I'm a pretty laid back guy, but I am big on manners and etiquette. When I asked the manager "How's your day going?", his response was, "What can I get you?"  The young man also proceeded to call me "dude" multiple times, although this is a word I often use, it is definitely not appropriate for a customer you do not know. I still went back the next day to get some more work done, but found it impossible due to the overly loud, obnoxious conversation of the employees. I'm all for a fun work environment, but please respect your patrons. Nice enough people, they just need a course on social etiquette and treating customers with respect.

Criniti's is a no fuss, no muss Italian restaurant in South Philadelphia that has very good food at a very reasonable price. The staff is always very friendly, considerate, and attentive. Their pasta, lasagna, various parmigianas, and calimari are all quite good and their table bread is excellent. Street parking never seems to be too bad, plus they are located only one block north of the Oregon stop on Broad Street Line. (An added bonus, if you are going to or coming from the stadiums on a spring/summer game day is that Pop's Water Ice is around the corner on Oregon.)

Quiet with large rooms and free breakfast and free wifi

Located 2 short blocks from Burbon street in the French Quarter. So you can easily walk to enjoy the New Orleans Burbon street experience but have peace and quiet to sleep. Large clean rooms. Free hot breakfast and free wifi.

If you get lucky, they also sometimes have delicious soft chocolate chip cookies at the main front counter.

Hardworking bellhops. Nice front desk attendants

P.S. I got really good pricing for this hotel when I booked through   tripadvisor.com
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: What an awesome little discovery.  About 20 of us celebrating a friend's birthday at the beach 2 weeks ago rolled in there unannounced on a Saturday night.  There was only one bartender, Scott, and he was fabulous!  We drank $3 domestic bottles all night (unheard of for a bar on the beach on a Saturday night) and got great attention from Scott.  Wednesdays they have $1 domestic bottles!  They have a drink special every night of the week, but I can't remember that they are right now.  If you're in Pass-a-Grille, and love dive bars like I do, Shadrack's is a must!

Noodle Noodle is one of Chinatown's more established and upscale dining establishments.  It is especially know for its dim sum.  I have a friend who absolutely swears by their turnip cakes (pan fried cakes of mashed turnip with bits of pork).  I once headed there for a snack, and ended up with one of the crispiest green onion cakes I have ever enjoyed.

This is quite a large restaurant, very bright, and perfect for groups.  The menu is quite extensive, and although slightly pricier than other Chinese restaurants, the quality justifies the cost.

Il Forno is one of the city's most popular Italian restaurants.  It is rather upscale on the inside, and serves a variety of pastas and pizzas.  It is also rather pricey, so be sure to bear that in mind.  The pizzas are authentic Italian wood-fire cooked, and I enjoy the pizzas much more than the pastas. Like Jeanette, it takes a lot to excite me about a pasta from a restaurant.  They are flavourful, but like I said before, a bit on the pricey side and not really all that special.  Definitely consider reservations if you plan on going around meal times, or on the weekend.

Great selection, reasonable prices, and knowledgeable staff - what more could you want from a wine store? I was impressed that both high end and less expensive wines were available, as well as a reasonably selection of beer and other drink selections. The place has a very upper class feel to it without being snobby. There is even a sampling machine at the front of the store, some table space, and a "wine of the month" - type club. My only suggestions is to have more more signs denoting the origins of the wines - I had a heck of a time finding the ones from Argentina. Otherwise, a must-visit for wine lovers.

Stopped in here with a few friends on the way back to Edmonton from an event in St. Albert. Cozy little place, with lots of gluten-free items on the menu. I had a cappuccino and I thought it tasted great, albeit reading a bit more like a latte with extra foam, but I don't necessarily think that is a bad thing. The others at my table said the soup was really good, as was the sandwich that was ordered. There was only one person working the front counter, so it did take a while to get acknowledged as he was busy getting other people's orders together. However, I would come here again if I am ever in St. Albert and need coffee.

I discovered this kiosk in West Edmonton Mall as I was coming down after watching a movie. I was very thirsty, and thought a frozen yogurt shake would hit the spot. It did. I had my choice of flavours, and for an additional charge could have added a topping. My shake was large and thick. You can also get a float or just a cup or cone of froyo with your choice of toppings. This is apparently a Canadian company, and the "cafe" part is that you can also get coffee. The people working there were very friendly and thanked me about a half dozen times for my purchase, half of which is still in the fridge because I could not finish it! I will be back.

The AC Hotel is brand new and has the potential to be really nice. The design of the rooms itself isn't bad, although the rooms are quite small, but I would not advise staying here. There is construction going on permanently and it is loud, starting at 6am on most days. In addition to 6am noise from construction, the hotel is right next to an open-air dance club, meaning that on weekends until midnight or later, there is music pounding so loudly that you will not be able to sleep. Unless you are looking to only sleep between 1am and 6am on weekends, I would stay elsewhere.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: My poor little Ziggy got into a car wreck, the car almost won. He did not die, thank goodness, but he was pretty banged up and miserable. I took him to Value Vet post ER vet for two check ups, and they were great. The staff was good to him (that I could see), and they let you drop your pet off as early at 7 am and pick up by 5:40 pm, which is great for us working folk. The prices are very reasonable, and they seemed to care. The doctor spoke with me afterwards to explain his thoughts and was thorough. Ziggy will be coming here from now on!

I realize that I am in the minority of at least my friends in how I feel about this place. I know a lot of people really like it. I think it is lackluster and the food is bland at best. The prices aren't even cheap, but the quality tastes cheap to me. The only thing halfway decent I've tried here is the shrimp tostada, which was alright, but definitely overpriced for its size. The enchiladas are frankly no good. The chips aren't even fresh tasting, just taste like grease. The salsa is boring as well... sigh, I just don't see what the fuss is about...

We immediately smelled cigarette smoke when we walked in, which was really off-putting. It seemed to be coming from the back where the kitchen is. The menu is huge and had a lot of great options, I particularly liked that they have several versions of udon and ramen. I wasn't super impressed with the udon I ordered, unfortunately. It was a combo of egg, chicken, vegetables, and shrimp. There were maybe two shrimp, some chunks of bland chicken, and the rest was pretty basic. Overall, we were not impressed and would not come back, especially given the smoke smell.

I had heard good things about this restaurant, but admittedly I'm a bit picky when it comes to Mexican food in tennessee. The margaritas were tasty, though not too strong, great with a meal. I had the camarones al mojo de ajo (garlic shrimp), and it came smothered in garlic which I liked. It had sliced fresh avocado, which made me happy to not see crappy guacamole with mayo as so many mexican places do to cater to us gringos. All in all, I enjoyed this restaurant, a lot more than most mexican restaurants around (you'll never catch me at places like las palmas in west end area). I recommend it!

Tonight we decided to try something new for dinner.  Piada recently opened in a revamped strip mall in Carmel.  We pass by here frequently and were intrigued by the concept of Italian street food, so we gave it a try.  I can sum up Piada in very few words:  overpriced fast food.  I was expecting something really special, especially given the cost of our meals.  But Piada just didn't cut it at all.  The atmosphere and music did not help.  Electronic and sterile, I am quite certain that Italian street food in Italy is absolutely nothing remotely close to this.

Day 5 of my 6 night stay here. Overall 3/5 stars. 

Pros: 
Staff was very accommodating
Put a larger banquet table in a larger room for my boyfriend to work
Close to my conference 
Quiet for the most part
Cheaper parking was found nearby 

Cons:
Smells bad, no signature Westin scent to be found, just bad body odor 
Short staffed - like everywhere, I get it, it's COVID
Had to ask for my room to be serviced after 4 nights 
All rooms have a small round table, no long tables 
Small pool
Valet guys made me feel uncomfortable 

I think I'd rather stay at the Marriot where the conference was, but the rooms were all booked.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Small, quaint, classy ambience raised my expectations only to have them dropped off a cliff with some sort of tasteless pasta/beef dish which was so flavor-challenged I couldn't finish half of it. Server said it is made not with sauce but "gravy" from the meat. Bread seemed fresh but the dip for it tasted like some kind of bitter spread that might be served in Game Of Thrones. They serve lamb here which, in this day and age, shouldn't happen considering they're baby animals. Really no reason for me to return here as nothing else on the menu seemed appealing to me.

Chaotic registration staff didn't follow through on their promise to call us as soon as our room was ready, leaving us cooling our heels in the lobby for nearly 2 hours. Fortunately, the concierge staff were friendly. When we got to it, however, the room was nice, with high ceilings, incl bathroom and showerhead - especially tall guests would be pleased. Decent fitness room but only fair pool and mediocre hot tub, which was disappointing  The event staff at American Place (one of the onsite restaurants) was outstanding for the wedding I was attending there.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Growing up in Fishers, this was our family's Chinese carry-out staple. The staff is always super enthusiastic and friendly, and the food is fresh and quick. The Cashew Chicken and Pad Thai are my favorites. They've done some updates over the years--expanding their menu and freshening up the look of the place. The restaurant is always super clean and food is above par compared to other carryout options. They do offer seating if you'd like to dine in, but it's sort of cold and doesn't offer much atmosphere. Most people seem to dine out. But it's always busy, the food is great, and the service is quick!

I don't think their sushi is excellent but their teriyaki entrees and lunch specials are. I've been eating at this place for over six  years and I'm never disappointed by the chicken teriyaki entree. It comes with a side of sticky white rice, a finely grated cabbage salad with a dollop of the creamy thousand island dressing, a generous portion of chicken covered in teriyaki sauce and a California roll for under $15! That and an Arnold Palmer and I'm set! They do close in between lunch and dinner time, though. So, don't be surprised if you're there on the  later side of lunch time and they want get you out the door!

Eh, it's a sports bar.  I'd probably not come here at all, except that it's a nice convenient spot to grab a bite to eat and meat people before heading to the movies at the edgemont theater.

They have decent beer selections and fair prices.  Staff service has been mediocre; no complaints, but nothing that stands out either.

The only major plus about this place is it's extremely quick service with the food.  I've probably stopped in a half dozen times to grab a bite, and I'm always impressed that the apps come out within like 5 minutes (which seems...a bit too fast, but I've never had issue with the quality of the food).

Really didn't have high hopes for a second chain to open up in Goleta, as the downtown spot does super well. Boy was I wrong! The new location is huge, with lots of seating. It's spacious and very clean. The downtown location seems a bit "hole in the wall" vibe, but the new location just screams cleanliness.  The quality of the meat is similar to the one downtown, which is a huge bonus.  

Avoid coming during rush hours as lines can go out the door. My personal favorite is the tripas, which they only serve fri-sun.

Just when I thought I found my regular sushi joint...I get food poisoning! I actually figured it was the yellow tail I had. My cousin had also ordered the yellow tail and got equally as sick as I did. We were the only two who got sick out of the five of us, and the only two who had ordered the same fish. 

Needless to say living inland and eating raw fish is always a personal risk. Not sure if I can handle spending another 24 hours of my life vomiting uncontrollably. Will probably save sushi dinners for when I'm on a coast.

Awesome italian restaurant! Overall, good food, service and ambiance. 

Had dinner here last night for the first time. Started with the house salad: lettuce, cheese (provel and something else?), prosciutto and a perfectly light but flavorful dressing. For my entree I ordered the fettuccine diablo sans mushrooms. It is a tomato sauce pasta with shrimp and crab meat. 

Yes the prices are a bit high but they sure don't skimp on the portions here, and the salad alone could be a meal. Definitely plan on taking some leftovers home. 

Friendly service, although our waitress was a bit forgetful.

I was awaiting for the 42 bus to take me downtown to Walnut Street Theatre and I spotted this deli while looking for bus. I was hungry after theatre and decided I was to hungry to wait for food so I tried that night after stepping off bus. Quick Stop deli is convenience store with a deli counter where you can buy sandwiches and hoagies and lunch meat. I had turkey hoagie with provolone cheese. It was great! The prices are affordable and they are quick. Yup ! You can get 6 inch or foot long sub, plus other bread for regular club sandwich. I will definitely come back.Nice to know I have Mom and Pop type deli store a block away. !

I agree with Mike H, Cajan and Zydeco bands seem to be hard to find in the French Quarter, although the bartender at Kerry's Irish Pub said that they sometimes have Cajan music.  Strange.   The Bayou Club claims to be the only bar on Bourbon St. with live Cajan music and from my observation they are right.

We had good drinks and friendly service and we were served by a sweet kid.  There was quite a festive vibe, and the Cajan band brought  a following in to the show.  The first band was a country band (the waitress told us the singer had been asked to go to Nashville three times)!  

Good times.

Fascinating that one reviewer gave it 5 stars and the other gave it 1.  My reviews of PA Wine and Spirits stores are against others in the system and not liquor stores out of state.  The PA system is unique unto itself and usually inferior to almost any serious liquor and wine store anywhere else.

This outlet is super convenient because it is inside the Acme supermarket, but that is all it has going for it.  One of the smallest I have ever seen, the selection is poor, unless you want the basics, like Jack Daniels and a cheap pinot grigio or boxed wine.  The staff is adequate but very bored, at least when I was there.

I'm giving 3 stars for the fact I have gone here for years.  I wish I could go higher but the quality fluctuates too much for enough confidence to go higher.  The staff are pleasant to deal with and special changes are always fine.  My last experience my  be my last though.  I had gotten the cold sesame noodles and while very tasty and fresh....it had 2 pieces of plastic in the sauce.  I was really put off because other than that, I have never had an issue.  So...avoid the cold sesame noodles and the rest is good.

Pretty good burgers at solid prices.

The Calf Burger was very good, juicy and actually cooked medium as I ordered.  The cheese was as good as advertised, try the cheddar.  The steak fries were very good, thick cut and a good portion.  The Kobe Burger seems to be another solid choice, I look forward to trying it.

The atmosphere is cool and still seemingly old-school, even after the fire a few years ago.  Service was solid and the food came out fast.  Prices are great for the quality, a burger even with additional toppings and steak fries can be had for $9.

Green. It's very Green!

Light flows through the translucent geisha motif covering the windows in what I would say is a very inviting space. Well laid out, but definitely geared for couples rather than large groups because of table-for-two setup, the modern shaped black chairs stand out.  The sushi bar is very nice with barber shop style chairs. Consider that the sushi bar is the focal element of any sushi restaurant trying to differentiate themselves from the pack. 

In case you didn't know you were at a sushi place, S-U-S-H-I is cleverly spelled out hanging over the sushi bar. And I thought this place was a pizza joint!

I love this place!  I've brought several pieces for dry cleaning and they are always prompt and courteous.  The prices are decent and they are in a great location (across from ACME).  I am definitely a repeat customer!  My only gripe is that they don't have the most friendly hours during the week.  I work - so it's important that there are later evening hours - or hours in the morning that allow me to pick up before work.  Hours are 8-6 Monday through Thursday (to 7 on Friday, not sure what Saturday hours are).  If I have to pick up mid-week, I need to leave work early enough to make it before closing.  Still, a great neighborhood place!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
This place did a good job. .85 cents per pound. I got a whiff of some of that "good-good" if you 'nah mean, but if I washed clothes all day, I'd do the same thing unless I was in school.  There were a few stains I didn't notice and I gave them a towel that smelled mildewy when I gave it to them and still kinda smelled when I got it back although it was clear it was washed.

There are 4 covered parking spots and very limited street parking. I believe there's wifi.

Overall a good experience. If I hadn't found Coin Laundry on Carrollton, this would be my go-to place.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Oof.  Terrible food. Terrible drinks. I left feeling gross. So gross that I bought movie food to soak up and cover all the grossness in my stomach at the movie we saw later.

If you want a drink, stick to beer. Don't get a cocktail, especially the coconut martini if you like coconut, because it's gross and doesn't taste like coconut.

I had the salad and miso soup which were average, but the BBQ ribs and chow mein were horrible.  The ribs were too sugary and the chow mein didn't taste recognizable.

I left $30 poorer and feeling disgusting. Not how you should feel after Japanese food. You should feel fresh and light.

I like the Mexican Hot Chocolate. I also like getting four small scoops. I find when you eat a big scoop of this ice cream I lose my interest and the flavor tastes bland towards the end.

Props for interesting and ever changing flavors, but the quality is way below Haagen-Dasz.  I have high standards though, so I'll just say that ice cream is ice cream and it's still enjoyable.

Cash only!

Don't park in the lot across the street or the *police* will run you off. Not joking. CVS is pissed about their parking lot spaces being used by anyone not going there. Ridiculous. It takes like 5 or 10 minutes to get an ice cream. Lay off, CVS.

This was a stop listed on our map during the Super Hero Crawl 2012.  My friends and I walked in and were very surprised to see the karaoke set up with plenty of future American Idols.  In our state of celebration we decided to do a group performance of the Backstreet Boys - I want it that way.  I have never performed in front of a crowd before but living in the moment, I joined my friends under the spotlight.  The crowd was great...we had people singing with us, there were cheers and applause... This is a great place to have some fun!

I love this place. If I lived near it, I'd be there all the time. Thankfully, my work takes me nearby often enough for an occasional visit. I've tried plain coffee, an Americano, and a couple of their creative seasonal special drinks. Everything has been delicious. The service has been mostly amazing, with the exception of one kind of sullen barista, but since every other encounter has been genuinely pleasant, they still get 5 stars. Plus, their prices are really reasonable, and they don't seem to charge extra for soy. I love that.

Ive been to many Fat Tuesdays so why wouldn't I visit the NO one! We have been on a few trips to New Orleans and the last time was less pleasant, lots of shootings on Bourbon during our stay and people pushing you to spend money or making you feel like you shouldn't be in there bar. To find this place we were so excited. Out of all the bars on Bourbon they offered the best service. Even snapped a photo of us on our camera. Enjoyed it! Only interesting thing is everywhere in the south is more inexpensive compared to CA but this place had the same prices as they charge in Vegas. IDK. Inflation is a b$%^*

Definitely a dive bar.  It will make you feel OK about drinking in the day time until you go back inside (no windows).  You can smoke inside. I had no idea they served food...and I honestly I wouldn't touch it with a 9 foot pole.  If you are hungry stick to the pre-packaged food behind the bar.

Drinks are cheap. Patrons, slightly scary.  Lets just say Doc Martins are a trend, black eyeliner worn generously.  You will also find your common north Central hipsters with their PBRs and shots of whiskey. 

Stop by.  Its a good place to grab a drink or two,but not to pull an all nighter.

Very good quality japanese food in a most unlikely locale. The menu is quite extensive, and I was especially impressed by the dinner combo platter which includes a bento box with your choice 2 entrees and 2 choices of rolls or sushi on the side. They also have a very good selection of sake. A must try is the banana fried green tea ice cream, which also comes in large portion, perfect for sharing and an appetizer whether it be the gyoza or the beef negimaki (thinly sliced broiled beef rolled over green scallion in teriaki sauce). Its one of the rare restaurants that offer a lot for your dollar.

the genuardis market near my house closed down recently.  so i started coming here.  it's a bit far and out of the way (10-15 mins).  guess i was spoiled with the genuardis that was across the street from me.  runs to the supermarket on thanksgiving day will never be convenient any more.  this market is clean and has a nice selection.  their prices are usually pretty competitive which is good and they have good customer service and plenty of parking being that the gold's gym next door is usually empty.  it's an okay market, nothing special.

I came here again after a long drive down from NH with my brother in law.  We wanted to try their philly cheesesteaks. Well, it's not what we were expecting.  It's good when you're hungry but definitely not a close substitute for Jims or Pats.  The bread was soft but something about the beef just didn't taste right.  It was kinda griddy to me.  I don't know how to describe it.  So far, nothing on their menu has blown me away.  The food is ok but not super great.  I still like the atmosphere and its location is convenient for me.  Our waitress Jackie was really nice.

I used to go to the Duke car wash down the street.  Due to poor new management, employees stealing money, and the company reusing the dirty water from the floor, I stopped going here.  I am surprised they are still in business!!!  I saw signs for this place as I was driving by and decided to try them out.  The guys working here are nice and very professional and do a really clean job.  However, they did take longer than I wouldve expected.  You tell the attendants what you want and you go inside to pay while your vehicles makes it way through the tunnel.  5 stars for clean vehicles, 3 stars because they are a bit slower than I would expect.

I went here on a first date not too long ago. It's a pretty casual place but still has some romantic flair to it. It can be very loud at times though so don't think you're getting a nice quiet evening here.

Ordered a bottle of wine which wasn't too expensive and we each ordered an entree. I had the gnocchi in marinara sauce and my date got the lasagna..both were very large portions. The waitress was awesome and she was right on top of things even though the place was packed. Also we were in no way rushed to finish our meal so that they could seat another customer.

I came here for the first time a few weeks ago to see Tim Barry play a show on a snowy Sunday night. 

This bar is setup very nice white white leather seats and booths and the bar is able to sit quite a few people. 

They have some beers that I have never heard of, which is a good thing to me because you can only drink the same 3-4 beers so many times until you get bored. 

Tim Barry played amazing, I had a green apple wit that I was happy with and the snow had stopped just before I decided to drive home. Over all a good deal.

Holy smokes, is this place busy ... this morning while enjoying a latte and a muffin while reading the news for just 20 minutes, I saw some police officers (in plainclothes!) meeting, and two business meetings and a whole bunch of folks coming n' going.  The service was good, the latte was at least adequate (I'm not a great judge, I'll admit), and I got to sit in the sun for a while.  :)  At times I wished for an iPod with earphones to help me ignore what was going on around me ... still, I'd definitely go again.

Well this is the original location. I was actually looking to eat something else but it seems there really isn't much good in Santa Barbara/ goleta.

Ladies at the register were ok, not good, not great.. Just ok. No smiles but not rude either.

However, they guy who gave me my food was friendly and polite!

Chicken Caesar salad is good, you can also have them put teriyaki sauce on your chicken (I did not). The dressing they use on the salad was just right.

Char burger is generally pretty good. I wouldn't recommend eating it cold the next day tho... Really is the best fresh lol.

Never really been a Dunkin doughnuts fan but I must admit I do love their new Spicy Smoke House Sandwich! OK OK! now down to business..

Customer service is ok, DD is located inside a gas station so its kinda convenient if you wanna pick up some breakfast along with a full tank of gas or soda etc. Like any doughnut shop they offer a wide range of pastries along with a cup of Joe,..nothing special about the coffee just plain. 

I shall return because its very close and they have the Spicy Smoke House Sandwich:)!!

I have to agree with my fellow yelpers...this place is mediocre at best. Food is okay, I ordered the slider combo after it took 21mins for the waiter to come to my table. When I finally received my meal it was cold all around as if  it was pre made and forgotten! Once i informed my waiter she took it back only to return another 20mins later with a completely different meal...A DESERT!...really....really..?! I informed her that my lunch was over and to just keep the food!...I was never of fan of Ruby Tuesday's so this experience will put a stamp on me never coming back here..

I liked the Hyatt. The rooms were clean and the location is great.  The most annoying thing was that there was no frig. Ummm what?! How do you expect to make money if there is no mini bar...but more importantly, where was I supposed to put my Sweetie Pie leftovers?! 

One HUGE tip is that if you are driving in, don't get conned into their parking lots. Just take 2 minutes and drive around the block.  My Hubs and I saved at least $40 dollars by finding free street parking less than 1/2 a block away.  It was awesome.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Everyone told us to try St. Louis style pizza, so we did.  Ok, by everyone I meant the St. Louis natives...the Chicago transplants told us we would be disappointed.  I'm glad I tried it...I mean it's different. The cheese is really smokey, and the sauce almost tastes like it was cooked in pepperoni.  The problem with this pizza is that if you don't eat it piping hot it gets too waxy. For me, part of the fun of getting pizza is so that there is breakfast pizza to have the next day....this does not make for a good breakfast pizza.

Meh is the term that pretty much sums up this place. If you live in the building and want to quickly grab dinner this place is a decent option, but definitely not any place to seek out. The basics are fine, but some of the more rare types of fish often taste a little off. For example, I refuse to eat any type of yellowtail from here. It's just not right. I definitely recommend that you stick with rolls that involve tuna, salmon, fake crab, or tempura. If you venture outside of those options you're bound to be disappointed. The teriyaki dishes are also decent. The one time that I ate there the servers were a little rude. Note that it's BYOB.

This is basic fast food style chinese food. The only that separates it from all of those fast food places you see lining Broad Street is that it's in the suburbs. Otherwise, same kind of thing- gloopy sauces, boring menu, over cooked dumplings, salty soup. 

The reason they received two stars? Vegetarian options that are edible and they deliver.

The staff is adequate. 

If you're in a hurry and not too picky, this is your spot. Otherwise, skip it.

PS The fact that I have very little to say about it tells the entire story about the food!

Had a pretty decent stay here this last weekend. Got here through Priceline.

We were in town just of the fun of it and were pleasantly surprised at the size of our room, the comfort of the bed, and the AMAZING water pressure in the shower.
The room was set up in a strange configuration but it worked for us. And Topher at the front desk was very helpful and gave us the number for a car service instead of a cab, which each cost about the same to get us downtown.
Continental breakfast was a bit meh. When i went down, there were out of quite a few things, but the waffles were decent.

Overall a pretty pleasant and enjoyable stay.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Really has taken a turn for the worse. Ordered 3 meals last night, came to $30. Took over an hour for the food to arrive, Delivery girl was on her cell phone when she dropped it off, yelling at someone on the other end, and the food was soggy and tasteless. The Red Enchiladas were dry and are in serious need of seasoning. The tacos were the soggiest and small. And the chimichangas were probably the best of the three, but only because the salsa was good. There was not nearly enough slasa or sour cream though. Not really worth it for delivery.

Interior doesn't resemble a Max &Erma's (what the building used to be) at all!  Nice tile work; they are going for an upscale Mexican feel.

Chips and salsa are good; they also served a small dish of a ranch dressing, which was weird.  I tried the chicken enchilada lunch special, and the chicken was moist and tender.  Standard Mexican rice on the side.  

My lunch companions got ticked when they ran out of regular Coke and were brought glasses of water instead of refills.  "Who runs out of Coke?!"

The booth upholstery offers entertaining squeaks as people get on and off the benches.

hands down the best pizza in the Philadelphia area - at least by my reckoning. Pizza is like religion - no one is ever going to convince you that their pick is the best. But like a cheesesteak, or pork sandwich , its all about the bread. 

The pizza dough here is phenomenal - crispy , airy, chewy and charred. puurfection on a plate. We got the Caprese and the Puglia (goat cheese , prosciutto, arugula). These are the old fashioned size - e.g., 16" like i remember. Not a slice left over.... 

the icing on the cake is the bakery next door, do not leave without bread- you will regret it.

Good start. Outside heated seating. Wineglasses, salads and bread arrived penalty. All A+ do far. The arancia app was (2 large balls) terrific. Had to wait a while for the entrees- was not a big deal as we were digesting anyway and drinking wine. 

We had the special - veal oaobuco,- pasta de mare and clams with linguini and white sauce. All generous, all freshly prepared, and really good 

I don't go to italian restaurants a lot. Mostly because I'm a pretty decent italian cook. But these guys rocked.really - that good. 

Desserts were fab - literally the icing on the cake. 

This deserves a repeat....

I guess what I'd say is this place has figured out their target market. Mostly this is a by the slice establishment, where a slice with the topping will run you roughly 4.50. Each slice is  huge - easily a meal for one person. So I can imagine that the local university students gobble the stuff up. 

It's not bad- it's just that it's also not really good. The flavor of places like Spatola's completely eclipse what you get here. But if dough, cheese and the topping  of your choice in a large format  is what you like--Lorenzo's is what you're looking for- you can't go wrong. 

But if you're looking for real pizza flavor - probably not the place.

Pretty average hotel. Location is close the airport, but really not great for anything else. Rooms are nice and spacious. Breakfast is consistent, but pretty plain. What they do have is pretty fresh though. No omelettes most days. My only real complaint is that I called for a shuttle from the airport when I arrived, called again half an hour later, and shuttle was finally sent. Hotel is 10 minutes away, so this is pretty ridiculous. Total wait time was 40 minutes, which made me pretty unhappy at the time since I had to get up early the next morning.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Here be the facts, mateys. This place has LOADS of potential but after eating there a few times it's obvious they don't have their sea legs yet. Why am I talking like a pirate? I don't know. Could be the ocean before me. Possibly because this little place could be a West Nashville hidden treasure.  Anyway. My medium burger was actually medium, but only on half the patty. The other half was raw. They are slow as hell  too even though they weren't full. I mean Suh-LOW.  Mac n cheese is good and the black eyed peas are really tasty.

I hope to be changing to 4 stars soon 'cause I'll be back,  It's so damn cheap!

Keep trying little rabbit.

CBD is still super new to me and I was intrigued by the CBD infused ice cream options at Revolution Ice Cream. 

Their flavor menu is fun and casual, with specials listed on the right, along with their CBD flavors. 

I splurged for the $6.99 CBD Oreo ice cream. It didn't taste too strongly of CBD to me, mostly just like Oreo ice cream. Did I feel more relaxed after? Not noticeably more than the normal food coma, at least. 

Some unique flavors (and apparently an ice cream challenge?!!) to try at Revolution. Not much indoor seating but great to stop by and grab to go.

I really enjoy this place.  A small BYOB but the service, and food are excellent.
I've been here when there are only a few other folks at tables, and I've been there when people are waiting for one of the tables to open up.  There isn't really a waiting area, so you're waiting outside if you come with a few people in your group.
We like getting the seaweed salad, and we usually start with 2-3 cuts of sashimi, and a few specialty rolls.
The kids even enjoy the food here!  We all look forward to the tempura banana for dessert.

This location is the Starbucks closest to home - so when I do have a hankering, this is where I usually end up! I've always had a good experience here. The drive through can get very backed up during peak times due to limited space, so I usually order ahead and park/run in to grab my drink. There is a small but nice outdoor patio that has a great mountain view. The location further north on Oracle is much bigger, but I prefer this cozier shop that is far more manageable and well run (at least in my experience). Thanks, crew!

A large group of us stopped in here rather late on a weekday. That might have been our first mistake but in no way were we pushing the limits of their closing time either. We just needed a place to eat that would accommodate 8 people. 

We sat on the balcony overlooking Bourbon. I ordered a burger. Tasted okay going down but definitely nothing special. We were starving and this place filled the void.

Service was extremely rushed.
