Later that night the horrible stomach cramps and diarrhea began. It lasted for two days. Sorry if that's TMI but consider yourself warned!

Good location at big yet bit outdated hotel.

Highlights:
- Walking distance to funk zone 
- Big pool that has limited capacity for Covid safety 
- Restaurant with patio and view of ocean for drinks and snacks 
- Fridges in room which was good to keep leftovers in or a few cool drink 
- Bike rental and drink coupons upon check in

Lowlights:
- Bit outdated and not as nice as expected for the price.
- Couldn't make reservation for the pool so hard to plan around. Pool inset so no view of the beach from it

Was fine for what we needed for a few days away.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I'm not sure which one I like better - Froyo or cupcakes, but in any case, so excited for another froyo option nearby. 

Chill offers a great variety, just like Fro-Yo on Delmar. I stayed with old faithful (aka original tart with strawberries and M&Ms), but can't wait to try the blood orange and dark chocolate! 

Again, due to my germaphobia, I have to say that the self-serve is not my fave. Too many people touching handles, breathing on toppings, etc., but because Chill is new, it's much cleaner than Fro-Yo, and for that, it will be my preferred choice. For now.

This is my neighborhood coffee spot & I really love this place! My only complaint is for the one male staff member who just never seems to like me. I've stopped trying. He also always gets my food order wrong but I'll never say anything. I've also tried to make my order as easy as possible so as not to feel like I'm bothering him. Sometimes, if I can, I'll head over to One Shot instead of here just to avoid our awkward exchange.

The cheery female staff member is always awesome & I kind of let out a sigh of relief when I see her. She's always very helpful & attentive.

Villa Barone's red sauce is my absolute favorite!  They always have extensive meat and fish specials (though I've never tried them), and their gnocchi and eggplant dishes are my favorite from any Italian restaurant.  Also, each dinner comes with a salad and some amazing warm bread.

Unfortunately, their 3 large dining areas are always very loud.  When you're in the mood for a quiet date, it's not the best atmosphere.  During the summer, I often prefer to wait for an outdoor table, mostly because the town of Collingswood is the perfect evening setting.  

Don't forget that it's BYO!

I had to stay here for two nights - they put me in a smoking room because they were at capacity.  Bleh.  Also - there is always a wait at the front desk to check in - I noticed that this was always the case.  

The rooms are small.  The beds are low and not very comfortable.  Room service is normal.  This hotel is older than some of the nearby hotels and things just look and feel old and kind of icky.  

However, since this was my one and only experience with the Crowne Plaza, I wouldn't rule it out as an option.  The staff is very friendly and helpful and I think that they do try to do what they can to make your stay comfortable.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Since I can walk to this little store I give it an A-OK for convenience. 

I like that I can go there for essentials like milk, bread, and eggs. They also have a good selection of produce, which surprised me. As far as other items like toiletries, paper products, meds, etc. I would recommend going elsewhere because they are a tad bit overpriced on those items. They do carry local honey if you are in to that sort of thing.

Everyone who works there is super friendly and seem to enjoy their jobs, which is a welcome feeling.

I'm not much of a coffee drinker. It makes me sick. Literally. 

But I've been running on an average of 5 hours of sleep per night this week, so DD was a necessity. I've been dying to try their coffee, anyway. I wanted to know what all the hype was about! 

I like that they have a drive through. I ordered a vanilla latte with an extra shot of espresso. It was delicious and creamy. WAY better than starbucks -- there was no bitter, metallic taste at all! 

I also had a few donuts (you can't go to DD without getting donuts!). Honestly, DD's donuts aren't my favorite. But they did the trick, I suppose!

E'ville's newest wine-spirits-beer store. First visit impressions:
* Wine is mostly Californian, some high-end Napa Valley stuff, but also selections under $20/bottle. I saw some Oregonian, and a smattering of other regions, though not much French wine, at least not that I remember.
* Spirits here are mainly whiskey, prominently displayed.
* Beer, a small but well chosen selection of bottles within a stone's throw of Global Brew. I saw at least two varieties of Bell's, and four of Founders, the Founders @ $10.71/six-pack, according to my receipt.

This review is about my experience as a commuter at a two-day conference, rather than an overnight stay. There's a lot of space for events, and much flexibility in room arrangements, as I attended large group lectures of several hundred, and breakout sessions of 25 to 50, all with comfortable seating and good acoustics. The food was tasty, from informal sandwich lunch to formal plated banquet. Restrooms were adequate, and the bar area elegant. The parking lot gates weren't working correctly, prompting two visits to the front desk to get out. The staff was friendly and responsive to my requests for assistance.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: These guys are pretty expensive, but they're pretty delicious. I've pretty much only ever gone for their Sunset Nachos after a night of boozing in the Hilsboro Village area, but they're pretty fantastic. They come with this stuff curiously called "swill," but it is absolutely delicious! As previous Yelpers have described, it's like cream cheese and salsa and yummy melty cheese, and I'm not sure what else. It tastes great. And they use fresh jalepenos which is great, too! Definitely worth $10 when you want to grub on some health-be-damned delicious gooey crispy nacho delights.

If Chipotle birthed a bland, Italian quick-service baby, it would be Piada.

The food was just okay, not memorable. I would stick to a Piada (basically an Italian burrito) or a chopped salad over the bland angel hair pasta option. The good thing is that the cheese, veggie, and sauce/dressing options are numerous.

I do recommend trying one of the Piada sticks if you have someone to share it with.

I do not recommend shelling out the extra cash for the crispy chicken fritte as your protein. It was chewy, spongy, and anything but "crispy." The Italian sausage wasn't bad, though.

We have tried Plate several times - each time the service was less than acceptable and the food just fair.  This time we thought we would give "brunch" a try - and we received a gift card.

Well, as expected - not worth the effort.  Food just OK, service just OK.  There were 6 of us.  Some had eggs and waffles.  I had the Asian salad.  Eggs were cold, waffles fair.  The salad was a salad.  I ordered a bloody mary and it tasted OK but came in a little juice glass.  

Much better brunches nearby.  As another reviewer said --- if you are in Suburban Sq and feeling lazy.........

Good location, very decent accomodations, excellent service.   

Brian at the front desk was seriously one of the nicest, most helpful hotel staffers I've come across in a long time (and everyone I made contact with during my stay was friendly and accomodating).  The rooms are a little noisy, and could use updating, but they're clean, with comfy beds and nice touches like eye masks and ear plugs.

Not quite the hip experience of a W, nor the luxury of a Four Seasons, but dependable, comfortable accomodations at a reasonable price.  I'd definitely stay here again if budgets prohibited the afore-mentioned brands.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Went to Tampa recently and if I wouldnt have been here on business (and my employer was paying for it), I probably would not have stayed here. The hotel itself was decent but nothing special. It kinda irked me that I couldn't check in early. I was there two hours early and that has never been a problem....the guy didn't even check to see if the room was finished with its cleaning, he just refused to let me do it....so I had to go wander around Tampa for 2 hours with my suitcases. The parking here is free but they don't have a lot of it. Available spaces disappear pretty fast in the evenings.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Not real keen on this place for the food but I always have GREAT service.  This last time I ate there I had the fish tacos.  Formerly living close to San Diego and really liking fish tacos I decided to give these a try.  They were excellent  except for being very stingy on the fish. Moneywise, I could probably eat here for less than $10 if they didn't have margaritas......   I tried sitting at the bar once but the bar for some reason is abnormally high, or the chairs or short.  I definitely recommend the patio, some friends and a pitcher or 2 of margaritas.

Pine Street Pizza is my local pizza joint, just a few doors away from my house.  They have your order ready (really no matter how big or small) within about ten minutes, and everything is always fresh and fantastic.

Very simple pizza shop stuff - hoagies, grinders, fried stuff and pizza.  The pizza leaves something to be desired (its a bit like Domino's or Pizza Hut) but we occasionally order it in a pinch.  

The staff is basic Philly pizza joint - not the most friendly, but never snappy or rude.  It's Philly - unless it is a Starbucks, there generally aren't too many places where you will get a genuine smile, at least in service situations.

I know Milano Inn is an Indianapolis institution but every time I dine here I'm completely underwhelmed by the food. The meal starts with complimentary cold bread. The salads have hard dry croutons out of a box. The pasta sauces taste generic and nothing fancier than a store bought jar sauce. I've definitely had comparable lasagna from the freezer section of the grocery store. The pesto sauce lacks fresh basil flavor. I really want to love this place but until they get creative and add some excitement to their food preparation then I'll just be under satisfied.

Came here with my friends, wanted some good Italian food on sunday, it was pretty empty. i got a glass of white wine-their house wine, turned out to be pretty good for a cheap price.

i got the seafood one-i liked how they put salmon pieces in it! ($15) my friend got the mushroom one-i liked her better than mine even if it didn't have meat, but it tasted quite delicious. the only thing was my pasta seafood one the red sauce was a little bit too sour. other than that we got the chocolate mousse dessert and that was okay. all in all, this place is delicious!

Service was horrendous.  I was craving a drink at the moment so I ordered a Salted Dark Hot Chocolate because the Frappes and shakes weren't available at the time.  Several minutes go by and I noticed nearly half a dozen customers behind me got their order before mine.  The cashier said she accidentally missed the order.  When she handed me the drink, it was spilling all over so I asked fer to make another one for me.  It nearly took 20 minutes for them to get my order.  The staff here need to get their stuff together.

With a handful of ice-cream shops on the loop, agreeing on a location for a late-night frozen treat run can be difficult. However, Fro Yo, the newest addition to the loop will satisfy your next craving while keeping your wallets and your tastebuds happy.

Everything is self-serve, even toppings and samples! Customers pay by the ounce--for a reasonable price--and choose just how much of each flavor and topping they want. The flavors are high quality, as far as consistency and richness are concerned and offer a wide variety of flavors and toppings(cheesecake, sprinkles, marshmellows, fresh fruit,  and many more.)

This place is a big favorite for everyone in our circle.  The food is fantastic, we always love the queso dip and the salsa.....cheap too!
This wouldn't really be a place I would recommend however....the wait for a table can be quite lengthy....and the atmosphere is leaves a lot to be desired.  
There are a couple places closer in to the city for us to go to now so we haven't really been here for awhile.   We do go to the one out by Ronnies Theater and they have a much nicer atmosphere and usually less of a wait.

Stopped in on a Saturday night since we were in the area (leaving The Whiskey Ring).  They serve food really late and we wanted to try their waffles.
We ordered the blueberry waffle and a latte.  
Our bartender was nice and there was a DJ playing that night so it was really loud.  
The place is very casual and hipster with some really cool arcade games to play.  
Our waffle was good but on the thinner side....not like the fat Belgium kind.  The latte brought it down a star since it was pretty terrible.  
We want to come back later in the day time to give them another try since there were a lot of interesting choices on the menu.

Definitely the place to go if you want "well done" pizza. You can't go wrong with the traditional, but their white pizza is even better in my opinion. The coal oven gives it a nice crispy crust, but it's not burned. Parts of the crust may be a little on the burnt side, but I think this gives it character.

Be sure to try the coal oven roasted wings. They are delicious. They're a little crispy on the outside, but so juicy on the inside. I don't eat pizza as often as I used to, but when I'm in the mood, better believe I'm going to Anthony's. I'm definitely a fan of coal oven pizza.

My friend absolutely loves Italian food and is a pretty good critique in terms of food. She brought me and our other friend here and informed us that they won the food feud meatball challenge on the Food Network, so we were excited. The restaurant itself isn't very fancy. It's simple and definitely low key, good for a casual date. We got bread and clams casino as starters and they were delicious. I obviously ordered the spaghetti and meatballs after what she told us, but in my opinion it wasn't the best I've had. I might have to go back and re-try it, but my friend claims it was amazing. Service was pretty good though.

One if my favourite places to go!!! Love the atmosphere, food, price, menu, just awesome. It is also gluten free friendly so i go with my sister. my favorite is the beef maki!!! i Love beef maki and it is hard to find. Also i love their onion cakes and beef or chicken bowl. It is a nice tiny place where i go anytime i get the opportunity. I also love their sushi specials and i find that they have a great menu for ppl who have a limited diet. Great for vegetarians, non pork eaters, pescatarians etc. One of my favs for sure!

I was torn between 3 stars and 4 stars, but I'm trying to exercise some discipline here. La Viola is a small Italian BYO a few blocks off Rittenhouse. The service was very attentive. The food is solid if not spectacular Italian with a menu filled mostly by salads and pastas. I found the food to be solid but not great. The flavors are good, but textures in the food and presentation were off. What saves La Viola is the prices which are extremely reasonable. When you combine those factors La Viola makes a solid but not spectacular place to come and enjoy a bottle of wine with some decent food.

Pumpkin is one of the hot spots right now for BYOB. It's located in a small cramped space on South Street. The first thing I noticed was the small menu, it's good in that the chef tries to only make dishes with fresh ingredients, but bad in that it seriously limits your dining options. What I most remember was the good sauces that accompanied the decent cooking: my quail had a nice balsamic reduction and scallops had a saffron vermouth sauce. The wait staff was a little pushy, but all in all it was a good meal and definitely has a different sort of a menu than some of the other BYOs around.

I have decided that I don't feel like riding my bike to work this week, so I'll take the subway. I do what I want. Unfortunately, I had about $0.30 and a button in my wallet, so I needed to stop at an ATM. One Shot is usually where I'll stop, but they're in the process of moving. A friend mentioned going to Coffee House, and I pass it all the time. Why not?

It is adorable inside. A complete respite from Girard Ave. I ordered a hot apple cider, and took out some cash. The barista was really nice (and cute!), and friendly with the customers. The cider was good, especially on a cold morning.

I'll definitely come back.

Here's another fun make-your-own pizza place. Offering pizza, salad, and pasta. Pionic, meaning unbeatable, is "an artisan style pizza baked to a crispy light, airy perfection in as little as 90 seconds."
You order your own crust, pasta, sauce, cheese, meats, and veggies from the very friendly and happy staff. You can also get gluten free pizza and vegan cheese for a little extra.
The restaurant is very casual with an opening garage door to the outside patio.
I really enjoyed their pizza and all the choices you have to make it special.

We used a GroupOn coupon and enjoyed a very tasty lunch here for our first visit to Lupita's.
It's clean, brightly painted, and has friendly and attentive servers. The salsa was outstanding....one of the best I've tasted. The chips were warm. I love that.
I had the combo cheese enchilada and bean tostada, and corn tamale with refried beans and salad. All were delicious, especially the tamale that was sweet with corn. Yum.
Yes, this is Marana and we don't get up real often but when we do Lupita's will be on our radar screen for a return visit.

Having traveled far and wide and sampled what I would consider the best pizza anywhere in the world, I'm puzzled by the low reviews.  This place not be top-tier, but it is still a pretty good pizza place.  It is also open really late at night.  It has thin-crust style pizza...not quite as good as the top-notch stuff in New Haven, CT, but it's getting up there, especially among Philly's more modest pizza offerings.

Pizza can be bought by the slice and is reasonably priced.  There's a good offering of toppings, including my favorite of fresh tomato and spinach.

No complaints!

After a few stays here, I can't that I love it or hate it, but you get the basics out of this hotel.

 - The rooms are pretty standard but clean.
 - Attentive Service
 - $10 charge for wifi...who still charges for this??
 - Walking distance or short cab ride to attractions
 - Generally affordable rates off peak holidays

Worth a stay to save a few bucks versus some of the more expensive hotels nearby.  At a decent rate, you pretty much get you a hot shower, comfy bed, & close to local points of interest.  Don't any expect anymore or less.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Having grown up in Vancouver and visited Japan a few times, I am spoiled and am a sushi snob. 

Good sushi is expensive as fresh good fish is an expensive product. So from a relatively inexpensive sushi restaurant I would expect nice sized portions and their cooked dishes to be done well. 

This restaurant has good sized bento for lunch, but the food is just average and a little on the salty side. I also don't like the lack of effort in their Nigiri, the rice was tasteless the fish was placed on top rather than formed and there was no Wasabi involved. 

In all it was a place I will not frequent again.

What a great little spot.  I've been here twice now, both times with a LARGE group, and each time these guys have been more than accommodating.  

There's an incredible selection of wines, including sparkling and I believe they have tastings, which I'm sure would be a lot of fun.  Pricing seems good, nice staff, tidy bathrooms.  All in all, not bad.  

So why not 5 stars??  They need some food.  Something.  Bites, snacks, crudites.  People need some nourishment when drinking wine (or any alcohol for that matter), and my group has said the same..  Get some snacks, and I'll give you guys the upgrade!!

Ahh- the best pizza by far on the mainline! My favorite is the grilled veggie with low-fat cheese- They sure know how to make a girl who only likes string beans love veggies! Tony  the owner is the best, He always knows it's me when I call to order the grilled veggies with ricotta and hot peppers and makes it extra special. I can't help but get my favorite pizza every time but my boyfriend's family gets a variety of different pies and they never disapoint. I've had the boneless buffalo chicken tenders as well and they're great.

I happen to live near two different Rouses. This location is definitely the better of the two. While both stores have the same sales (Pick 5 deal on the meat!), the Clearview Rouses has a little bit of a better selection. The extra selection of ramen noodles (including some "premium" ones) appeals to the bachelor in me. The expanded salad bar and hot plate lunches speak to the lazy cook in me. 

While Rouses may not have the specialized selection of Whole Foods or the Old Metairie charm of Dorignac's, but the prices are certainly better on my budget.

I don't expect much from a fast food restaurant, but I do expect two important things: customer service and speed. Yes, I expect staff at a McDonald's to put on a smile and at least pretend they are happy to serve me food. It's customer service. I didn't always enjoy my time in retail but I never let the customer think that. So lay off the surly attitude and learn to interact with customers.

Second, I expect the FAST portion of fast food. Double when it's something that is mass produced and under a heat lamp. It should not take 10 minutes to get a McGriddle.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: This was a complete disappointment. I'm not expecting authentic Chinese or anything, just some decent Americanized food. I ordered the kun pao dinner special. This was the first time I've ever had fried rice that was bad. And I mean bad, it tasted horrible. I don't know if it was rice not being fresh or other ingredients being off but it was nasty. The eggroll was obviously from a frozen bag, not just because of quality but because it was still half frozen. And my kung pao chicken? Barely any chicken in the dish. I wound up tossing most of the dish and going to get a burger.

I don't expect much from Subway. At its core it's still fast food. But I expect the staff there to be courteous, attentive, and at least pretend like they enjoy their jobs and want to be there. This Subway failed to give me any of that. I get it. You're young, probably working the summer before you start the big adventure that is college. You want to be going out and having fun, not slaving away making sandwiches. But be professional and do your job. Don't take out your displeasure on your customers.

And learn how to make a damn sandwich. Don't put so many onions that's all I'll taste.

If you haven't been here you are missing out.  The décor is dark and romantic.  The servers are attentive and very knowledgeable about the menu.  And the menu, oh the menu.  You must try the grilled octopus.  The flavor is wonderful with the char that is on it from the grill.  Then there is the seafood ravioli.  It is a party in your mouth as you bite into it and taste the lobster and other large pieces of seafood.  They don't skimp on the filling.  And for dessert you must try both the tiramisu and their chocolate cake.  The tiramisu is a family recipe and the cake is perfect if you are looking for something that isn't too sweet.

I can't say I saw much of Tampa when I went there last month.  I was there on business for 3 days.  If you find yourself in the same situation, the Tampa Airport Marriott is super convenient.

You just walk from one terminal and down a corridor that leads to the hotel.  You never even go outside to get there.  No hassle and super convenient.

They have a gym(which is a plus), an outdoor pool, a top floor rotating restaurant, and a decent lobby bar that's always playing sports.

Maybe someday I'll see more of Tampa as a tourist, but for business; this hotel works just fine.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This new location just opened. It is located in the former Wendy's, then Dickey's BBQ building. 

After leaving the Ellisville location with NO product, we were en route home, when we noticed the "NOW OPEN" sign. Turning left off Manchester is a beast,  but we perservered. Now, the good news for us was - they HAD Vanilla Creme Donuts. The bad news was they were filled with less than one bite of creme, leaving a dry powdered donut. 

This is their sixth location opened, since the original one in Kirkwood. They must have decided to scale way  down on spending when converting, as it has a thrift store feeling. Cheap chairs and wobbly tables.

I got my car washed on the outside and detailed on the inside here today. And I was there for an entire hour. Thankfully it was beautiful outside so I enjoyed my wait, but it was little long. The outside of my car was fine, and the inside of my car was 90% better when I left there compared to what it looked like when I arrived. They simply could not get all the dog hair out of the black carpet. It did cost $70 which feels like a lot. I will probably come back here for my next car wash, but won't spend the money to get the inside detailed.

Dinner Feb 23
  This is our go to place for Chinese Take-out.
  Why?  
   Quality has never wavered since it opened. Food cooked thoroughly and always the way we ordered it (ie, no green peppers).  When we order a lot, they always give us something free.  And honestly, we have never had a single complaint or problem with this restaurant.
   My favorites are Bourbon Chicken, Hunan Beef, Moo Goo Gai Pan in Brown Sauce and their chicken wings (10 for like $4.55) and crab Rangoon are really good as well.
   We did try the other Westchase take-out place and found Kangs far superior!

'I've experienced better' is exactly what I was thinking while I was there. I had a good time because I was with some great friends but I would not suggest to go back there. I think that the bartenders were friendly and were serving costumers fast but overall I wasn't impressed with the bar. It was very crowded when I was there and I did get served quickly but the mixed drinks were so weak! Even the shots that were being passed around from their shot girl tasted like straight lemonade. I was just not impressed.

Great place on Main Street in Manayunk. The food is very good. I recommend the fried calamari as an appetizer. The drink menu is also very good! Try the Candy Cocktails! I had the starburst on the rocks. Yummy. My only issue I have with Derek's is the sitting in the back dinning room gets so cramped. I felt like I was on top of the table next to us but it did not ruin the night.  If you don't like dinning in tight spots I recomend asking to be seated in the front near the bar because there are a few booths. Enjoy.

This place rivals Holiday Soft Serve, though their Soft serve seems just tad bit creamier then Holiday!! But I do love Holiday too!! I wanted sugar -free & they didnt have it- : (
Only thing is Holidays I would get Child size as their sizes are Gi-normous!!

I went here on Thurs evening with friend of mine who frequents here with his wife & he loves it.
I can honestly say -Now I know Why!! Though the parking getting in & out can be slightly tricky  if you have lots of people trying to get in .

Return Factor:
Definitely..Just not all the time, be at the gym 2x a day !!

Do love my coffee, on weekends in particular. As My brunch buddy & I had to bring  it down couple notches, we came to this one, since some errands had to be around this area. The Store is busy, quite a bit people with tablets or laptops. , we ordered, and seemed little backed up, but started to move quick.I got my grande Caramel Macchiato, Yum..with breakfast sam-mich. Quite good, its nice one, Never feel rushed or the barristers are friendly, but sometimes in Philly , it can get like that, where the employees are having a bad day or something.

Return factor:
 Hell Yes-Hello Coffee Aficionado!!!

Well I'm not a fan of this location because they only carry seafood and crab SEASONALLY. Hmmmmmmm ehhhhhh huh????

I found the customer service to be great as the sandwich maker was friendly, suggestive & patient; but I just wasn't happy about the NO SEAFOOD & CRAB thingy. I mean, I'm trying to go MEAT-FREE & I just wasn't in the mood for a veggie delite, which is ultimately what I got.

I love the offers I get to my phone for discounted subs.... yessssssss winning!!!!

Ample parking.  Friendly staff.  Clean facilities.  Fair pricing.

Although located in the very heart of very busy & congested UPTOWN NEW ORLEANS...this Capital One is quite efficient & swift in transaction processing. 

I particularly like the walk-up ATM that consistently works. How frustrating to exit your vehicle to go to the $10 dispensing ATM, to only find that it's out of order... Ughhhhh!!!!!  

Parking is ample; as the parking lot borders the bank has spaces on both sides & the rear. Additionally, there's street parking. 

Friendly staff. Regular banking hours. Great location; St. Charles Avenue rocks.

I like that this branch is centrally located on the corner of Canal & Carrollton; in the heart of it all. 

I find the service to be on point. Customer orientated. Friendly. Not a fast moving as I'd like, but I understand everyone's needs are different & so it's relative. 

I like the major aesthetic upgrades they've made to this & most Capital one branches. 

The only thing that really sucks about this branch is the availability of parking & the entrance to the parking lot; it's cryptic I tell you. 

All in all, I like this branch, I've seen & know of worse.

*************************************************

This WINN DIXIE is listed twice. So here's my review AGAIN!!! 

***********************************************

I hate even giving this place 1 star!!! If I could give it a negative star, this place would get like negative 5 stars. 

This place is trash and services trash.  Apparently the people who shop here don't mind paying for & shopping in trash. 

I've gone into this store and seen half eaten ice cream sandwiches, opened sodas/drinks, open/eaten chips...need I go on?

And dare I even brooch speaking about the management.

An older store in the Lakeview Area, this locally owned grocery store serves the Lakeview Community. 

Open lanes, well stocked aisles, one can be found out perusing the aisles for extended periods, making selection choices one after another. 

I find their pricing to be more than Wallyworld, but as expected, its not a chain & doesn't have the finances of big box retail... Support Locally Owned. 

Checking out is easy, paper or plastic? Cash or credit? 

I've seen a time or two where the bagger has assisted a patron with loading groceries into their car; so like the days of yesteryear!!! Awesome!!!

This place is right across the street from North End Park which also happens to be our (Belleville Rowdies) rugby pitch. Excellent patio out back with tons of greenery surrounding a centered fireplace. Not sure how often the fireplace gets used but it looks cool.
Inside is filled with tons of old knick-knacks from years past. Its a cool place to just sit and have a beer and soak in all of the scene. Plenty of locals. Kinda divey. Most importantly, ice cold STAG on tap here. Can't go wrong with a place like that. No food served, but a decent stop for a beer or cocktail for happy hour.

While spending the night in Boise we ended up at Trillium.  I'm not going to lie...we originally didn't realize it was in a hotel and almost left when we arrived due to that fact alone.  So glad we didn't!  The service was great, our server and the hostess were super nice and attentive.  The food prices were on par with other restaurants in the area.  The Szechwan cauliflower was super tasty!  We also tried the crispy brussel sprouts and stuffed jalapeños... both were great.  I enjoyed the cheesesteak and could only eat half...so much food!  Lol  but it all was super tasty!  Would definitely go back and recommend!

Best find about Higher Grounds -- they make an amazing blueberry-almond-soy smoothie which is pure heaven, and my friend swears by their chocolate milkshakes.  Not really a fan of the Oregon Chai, but the iced mochas have always been spot on.  Service has been consistently friendly and they're quick to make suggestions if you're not the cuppa type.

Though I haven't had the time to actually sit down in the place, the environment looks cozily geek-friendly, with cushy chairs and a couple of retro arcade tables.

The place looks nice & clean, however the food is so-so & the service is kind of rude & impersonal. Growing up in the southwest I am always on the hunt not just for authentic mexican, but GOOD authentic mexican, starting with the salsa. If the salsa sucks from the start what makes you think the entree will be any better? I say work on the staff communication skills first, then work on perfecting the entrees. I urge the owner to pay a visit to Red Mesa in St. Pete or Casa Tina in Dunedin. Those places have some great dishes...still nothing like back home, but close enough.

I wasn't that impressed.  I went for lunch, and it was fairly empty, but seemed to be doing some brisk take-out lunch business. The food was ok, but way overpriced for lunch.  The bento box wasn't too expensive, but the rest of the sushi and the drinks are just too pricey.  I know it's chesnut hill, but it's not beverly hills.  The service was only so-so.  The sushi chefs and the servers were too busy talking to each about what they did the night before instead of providing us good service.  There's tons of better sushi places out there!

If you have to go to a Safeway this one is quite centrally located but unlike other Safeways (notably the two on Tanque Verde), it's old and hasn't been remodeled.. Seems small, too. What a shame since this is the closest Safeway for much of central Tucson. I'd rather drive the extra few minutes to hit up one of the other ones or, better yet, the Albertsons up the road, for meats and canned goods. Checkout staff has always seemed sluggish to me and not as friendly as my preferred shopping locale, Sprouts. I only go in here when there's something in the ad I need or for that addictive salsa of theirs.

I think one should take the other eateries in the student union into account when reviewing Sabor. If it was really so awful in comparison why is it always full? Yes, you can get a bigger burrito elsewhere and it's probably worth your while to walk to Chipotle instead, but there is one thing on the menu that stalls my steps elsewhere every time: the taco salad! Lovingly cupped in a perfectly fried crispy bowl, you may feel free to dress it up with your choice of the four salsas, radishes, onions, jalapeños and lemons at the condiments bar or just leave it plain. There's also a  "bang" fountain here for jamaica, horchata, tamarindo etc.

WOW talk about authentic? Came here for my birthday a few months back. I'd say it's the closest to Italy you can get without actually going there. Delicious fresh baked bread with hummus as a spread. Food was cooked to perfection. They do not offer soda because they believe that it takes away from the taste of the food. They also do not serve pasta with their dishes because all REAL Italians know that pasta is not supposed to be a side dish. It is supposed to be a dish on its own. Prices were not too bad for what you get. I also really enjoy the "cavelike" atmosphere.

Yes the Flyers used to hang out here in the 70s. Yes, there used to be lines out the door just to order their pizza. However, those days are long gone. I have been to Rexy's twice. The first time we went, we ordered pizza. It was good and just that. Not worthy of a long drive and not as good as some other local joints in the area. We went back again one night for dinner. I ordered spaghetti and meatballs. I don't know what it was, but the meatballs had a funky taste, and I swear that the rolls they put out on the table are from WaWa. If you don't go, you won't be missing out on anything.

Great beer bar and as others have mentioned it's hard to argue with a $5 burger.

Let's be clear, this burger is not going to change your life.  There will be no epiphany as a result of it.  You'll order one, try it and say, yep, it's a $5 burger, it tastes pretty good.  That's about as detailed as it gets for me.  It is served on a potato roll if that piques your interest.

This place can get a little crowded on weekend evenings but I've never seen it where people are spilling out onto the sidewalk.  The staff has always been very pleasant and that certainly contributes to me coming back here.  It's just a solid spot.

My first time here was for my daughter's 16th birthday. I called and made a reservation. Mentioned that it was her birthday and was told that she would receive ice cream. We arrived and no mention about her b-day for the entire meal. She even had a sweet 16 tiara on. When I mentioned it to our waitress, she said to tell the hostess. Since I told someone when I called, I chose not to do that. Lo and behold, no ice cream. 
Miso soup was tasty. Edamame was good, nothing outstanding. Enjoyed the ambience. We all enjoyed our meals, but won't be running back.

This is my first and last time at this restaurant.  I walked in here at 3:52pm and ordered dinner. The Hostess seated myself and my guess. My server came over and introduced herself to me. I started asking her questions and she wasn't too sure about the food. She brought over bread and salad and disappeared. The server forgot to bring over a knife to cut the bread with. I asked the hostess if she would and she said" I'm not on the clock yet". Finally the server came over and brought one. The knife was either dull or the bread was old. Terrible service and the food was mediocre. Go somewhere else.

My youngest sister loves this place so I went to eat here with my boyfriend in 2007. The decor was really nice and the atmosphere was very welcoming. This is probably the only thing I liked about the place. 

On the first visit, the wait was FOREVER and when my entree came, there was a HAIR in my food. I had it redone and took it to go. It was pretty good, but I was still appalled about that hair.

We went there a second time and it wasn't any better. We got a nice view of Broad Street this time but the food was still awful. I don't remember what dish I ordered but it was cold and undercooked.

It's nice to know that there's a corner of the French Quarter that isn't littered with "clean" and "safe" bars, restaurants, and attractions. If you want attitude, it's probably best found here. If you want a jukebox sporting Neurosis and Hank Williams, it's probably best found here. If you want a punk, fresh out of a Florida prison, drinking with two others who wanted to beat the shit out of him for hurling a pint glass at the bartender several nights before in this same venue, it's probably best found here.

What a great concept! Piada reminds me a lot of Chipotle in setup. You choose your piada (basically like an Italian burrito), pasta, or salad by picking a grill item (mostly meats), sauce, and toppings, or pick one of the pre-chosen combos. Go through the assembly line and tell them what you want, and voila. I'd never had a piada before, so I had to get one (a vegetarian one) and it was delicious. My mom really loved her pasta. It wasn't busy when we went in, but I was still impressed by the speed! Great value and great experience.

In general I'm more of an ice cream chick, but I like fro-yo sometimes, and Huddles time is one of those times.

The flavor isn't the strong sour taste you often find with frozen yogurt, it's more subtle but still good. I've been here twice and both times got several flavors in one cup with half their available toppings, because there were too many choices and I'm indecisive like that. But they won't judge, it's a free fro-yo world. Wonderfully, instead of charging by the number of toppings, they charge by the weight. 

Mo' Huddles mo' fro-yo. (That's their tagline, right?)

Semolina's made a big mistake with this one. Prior, they had a decent formula: huge pasta dishes, that tasted pretty decent, at affordable prices. Semolina's has since become synonymous with pasta round here. They nixed that formula for this concept. Most dishes here are served with polenta in lieu of pasta. The menu is smaller (but does have certain dishes fromt he original restaurant that they would not be able to survive without) and more expensive. Before drink my fiance and I were looking at $20 a person and some wine easily put us over $30.

You may think because this restaurant has a Broad Street address and is right next door to Ruth Chris that it is $$$$. This place is actually really affordable and I happen to love the food.

The onion rings are thick and the onion doesn't slink out on the first bite.
The hamburgers are awesome and huge. Yes they even offer bison, but I think it tastes the same as cow and cow is easier on the wallet.

The salads are also hearty and huge. You will see lots of suits here during the week for lunch. Everything is really fresh, the prime rib is perfect and basically this is every father's favorite place to go for Father's Day.

if you like sushi, don't mind a little attitude and have $20 (or hell, $10) in your pocket, you should stop in to see sam.  the shop is small, the sushi is tasty (AND CHEAP!) and there isn't any waiter, hovering over you and making sure you like your food.  waiters would be unnecessary...OF COURSE you'll like the food!

i can't attest to how this place is during the peak hours, it was EMPTY when the hubby and i dropped in, leading to a quick and filling meal.  but even if there had been a wait, for those prices, it would have been worth it.

I've always been a HUGE fan of Publix and here's another reason why! CONSISTENCY! Customer service is the best. 
The Deli rocks big time, and make you feel that you're getting personal treatment. Each staff member will say hi and offers to assist you. It shows in every Dept and at the Front End. 
I come here maybe once a week as I have lunch with my Granddaughter at Trinity Elementary and might need to pick up a beverage or special dessert for her. Publix has the same high standard in EVERY SINGLE STORE! Thank you, Publix!

All I know is this place was open when I need it most! I had just left Orlando at 5:15am. Couldn't find a special bakery down the street in Ybor open so I succumbed to Mickey D's! 
Hit the Egg White Delight McMuffin as that's the healthiest sandwich I will find with coffee that hit all cylinders and was not hot water. 
But what got me the most was the interior of this Ybor establishment. The designers embraced the 'hood's heritage and scored big time. Just check out the pics I took. The service was also good at 0' Dark Thirty in the morn when I am the most temperamental! I was a happy boy when I left so there's my 4 Stars!
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
I've had Papa John's off and on for a while. I basically stay with Sausage, Pepperoni, Mushroom, and Peppers. Stopped all together for a while then drawn by the  "Bacon Cheeseburger " pizza. Uh, you got my attention again! The construction is real beef, cheese made from mozzarella, fresh cut Roma tomatoes, hickory-smoked bacon, pickles and Papa's signature burger sauce. Personally, I think the pickles do the Jedi Mind Trick on ya! AND I love it! Don't let the looks deceive you.The magic is underneath the cheese 
. with pickles peeking out to draw you in! Yeah, I hit it tonight and had to shout out while the tastes were fresh!

Terrible. Terrible. Terrible. 

Hated to wake the guy inside running things to pay for my overpriced car wash. But who else was I going to pay? One of the guys who doesn't understand or pretends to not understand English? 

I know it's a car wash but come on!!!! When a car wash customer points to a pile of sand in the corner of the bumper that you missed, you don't understand what I mean? 

And how do you effectively dry the car and treat the wheels with one hand because you're in the phone the whole time? 

Last time. Unless this is a mob front, they'll be out of business soon anyway.

Oooo, this is a really nice new Superstore! Besides being new and shiny and clean, the thing that really sets it apart from other's is how well set up it is. Produce right directly in front of the doors, nice! And as soon as you walk in, the Joe Fresh is to your right, bright, well lit, and organized. Then all the food to the left. I do love me some Joe Fresh!! Who needs Lulu Lemon when Joe has super cute "Joga" yoga pants at a third the price (or less!) I also like that they have a plethora of self check-out machines. I will definitely make to trek out here in the future!

I really enjoyed the Felicia's Special Pizza here!  It has spinach, tomatoes, cheese, and garlic sauce.  Every ingredient tasted fresh, and I normally don't even like soft tomatoes, but these were delicious. It was a little greasy but if you got a bite of the crust with each bite of the middle, it made for a great balance. 

I got a side of fries, which were packed a bit precariously, but they did hit the spot.  Classic thin fries. 

I also thought the prices were fair, especially given the quality of the ingredients. 

I'll definitely be back!

Cozy, comfy, friendly staff, the usual for this type of hotel that caters to business travelers and vacationers alike.
Valet guys are very friendly, always saying hello, offering to help, etc. (it's kind of their job I guess). Desk staff and concierge were also pleasant.
The housekeeping staff could be a bit more thorough, nothing was gross but I could just tell they skipped over certain things. 

Overall, nothing outstanding, it's your typical Marriott. The location sets it apart since it is in spitting distance of the convention center, the marina and a couple of other places.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I used to love this place when it first changed names. It had a really affordable can't beat lunch special price! However; slowly but surely the servings sizes became smaller and smaller to now joke size. I'm not a huge person but I can down some sushi pretty well. The rice also went down in quality too. There is a place around the corner on Samson street that is much better quality that offers similar pricing but way better sushi. And if pricing is really important try Maki House sushi on 2nd and South. Atmosphere not great but 2 rolls hand or regular only $6.50! Such a Deal!

Sticky table tops, pesky flies, room temperature food-all inside this location!

I was not impressed with my visit here.  (I wasn't expecting anything near the quality of Chimichanga, just some simple dinner.)  

When we first sat down my arms were sticking to the table top. Eeww!   Then there were the flies that kept landing all over the table. Double Eeww!  

Our server sat a metal rack down to protect the table because I ordered one of those dinners on a skillet.  When she brought out our food it wasn't very hot, not even steamy!  (There was no need for the metal rack!)

I will not be going back.

On a longer visit this past weekend a couple things that I noticed that I never did before.

1. The windows. I could have sworn they were open since the people outside sounded like they were in the room with me. I stayed on THE THIRD FLOOR. I can only imagine what it sounded like on lower floors. This is a busy area so this can be a serious draw back for light sleepers (as my companion was) 

2. I know the "breakfast" is free but to have the coffee machine not work at 9 AM? NOT COOL

but all and all still worth the price for the location and rooms.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The Japanese food is added as an after thought as everything on display in the buffet window is Panda Express style Chinese food. That's ok, but why call it Maki of Tokyo? Anyway, I dare not order the sushi or noodles and stuck with what I could see.

The food was over-salted, the service a little lacking, but compared to the other choices I still stuck with this place. If you are looking for something like a real meal, and not pizza, burgers or poorly made pasta that is offered next door then your sense will lead you back to this restaurant.

I'm from SoCal and I'm always looking for good Mexican food in Illinois, funny I know. I had the chicken taco and shredded beef chalupa. The chicken in the taco had no flavor. The shredded beef had amazing flavor. My issue though was it was just tortilla and meat no sauce or even sour cream. I'm also in love with tomalito so I had to get some, but wasn't impressed. My husband got the burrito and taco and didn't even finish which says a lot for him. So this place was just ok, still searching for my good restaurant though.

I'm not a massive fan of sushi (I can just imagine everyone freaking out) but my coworkers and I visited here a couple of weeks ago.  As usual, we order the Bento Boxes.  With Japanese restos, I always have to make sure there is no shellfish anywhere in my dish.  So they accommodated me with extra tempura veggies.  That was a good touch.  

As for the atmosphere, it has a modern decor and have special rooms for larger parties with your own privacy by just sliding the door. But nevertheless, sushi is sushi.  So it's all the same to me.  I don't think there isn't an experience that would a Japanese resto any different.

Ate here last night, hubby had the fish and chips and wifey had the dueces wild 3 pancakes, 2 sausage, 2 bacon + if you order off of the breakfast menu a $2.50 Skky VODKA Bloody Mary.

This place is clean, I give it 3 stars because of a billing error and the waitress went missing for a bit, and checking out there was a long line.
The busboy was very attentive and filled my water on cue.
It wasnt my waitress's fault about the bill but it did hold us up.

Everything I saw come out looked delish.


THE GSR is my favorite in town, they offer out of great free deals and local's special.

I'm a little ashamed to admit that my office is less than a block from Tenno and it took me 4 years to try it. 

My department walked over for a little team building lunch and our large group was seated immediately.  The place was pretty empty for a weekday lunch hour, so unless this wasn't typical, waiting isn't an issue. 

At Keisha G's urging, I tried to "crazy roll" ...whoa. It's this giant roll wrapped in some kind of sweet potato strings and then fried. Intense. 

Service was fast, food was reasonably priced... It wasn't spectacular, but I'll be back for sure for a quick lunch out of the office.

Very glad to read the so-so reviews. I was afraid I was becoming a killjoy.

The lawn is beautiful, very relaxing. But the food took the shine off the scenery. Tri-tip sandwich was tough, the Pepperoni pizza ought to be renamed the mushroom immersion as it would be impossible to be more mushroomy unless you were eating your way out of a mushroom from the inside. 

The fries are very good!

My suggestion, buy a meal from another place nearby then add a soda and fries here, enjoy the scenery and smile knowing that you're eating the best meal on the property.

well I'm certainly surprised today. usually there is this one barista that is super irritated and has the "I don't give a crap" attitude and for some reason always doesn't make my beverage right and is usually rude. today though, today.... mmph my latté was def good and he seemed less rude almost like he was actually trying to be nice.  However he still had the unhappy face he usually wears. I always hated coming here bc the the guy barista could be really rude at times and it's like I always leave feeling super pissed off. but because it's convenient I would come here when I'm in the area. I hope things continue to get better from here...

My hubby and I lived here for the first two months that we arrived in St. Petersburg .. we had one of the beautiful private balcony's because this is considered their "smoking rooms".  It was perfect and for the July 1st fireworks you couldnt get any better.

Tricks of the trade ... we met a couple in for a weekend from Daytona paying 150 + a night ... we were getting corporate rate long term ... can't really tell you what we paid but they turned around and went to the front desk asking why other guests received a cheaper rate of $120 they got their stay matched .. (ours was less)

Staff was super to us we would definitly stay again!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
We ordered a sushi meal, a couple of hand rolls and rolls, chicken katsu, 3 bubble teas, and edamame. Overall tasty bubble tea, good katsu, and disappointing sushi. 

The sushi was small and flimsy. Two rolls were supposed to be hand rolls and came as regular rolls instead. And the sushi meal had a note for no crab, eel, or panko for someone gluten free. Well, the spicy roll was full of panko and couldn't be eaten. We ordered a good amount of food and paid premium prices for sushi and it really wasn't worth it. If you can't eat gluten, I wouldn't trust this place.

The Beef Bulgogi was excellent, exactly what I was looking for. The meat was pure meat without fatty gristle, and was nice and marinated tender with the perfect about of sweetness that is typical with bulgogi. I did have to ask for an extra side of steamed rice to go with it, the amount that came with wasn't near enough for all that meat. Look forward to coming back and trying their fresh sushi.

*Note; this place had a great ambiance to it...everybody knew everybody and was super friendly. This is definitely a local favorite.

I like Creole Creamery, but not nearly as much as it appears every one else does. Any place that lets me sample as many flavors as I want before ordering scores major points in my books, and I like the classic ice cream shop feel, but while the ice cream is certainly good I don't think it's the best I've ever had. It is the best I've found so far in New Orleans, though, so that counts for something. Sometimes parking is a little tricky in the neighborhood, but a long walk to and from my car only justifies that extra scoop I inevitably always order, right?

I picked up my rental car late at night on Christmas Eve, and the guy behind the counter could not have been more friendly and cheerful. He completed my check in and pointed me in the direction to get my car- when I got off the elevator, I was greeted by name by a female employee who was equally friendly. She didn't seem to know exactly what she was doing and had me carrying my luggage up and down the isle while she figured out which car was mine, but over all she was nice enough. She was a little pushy on all the upsells, but that's to be expected at car rental places. I'll definitely be using Enterprise the next time I'm in Tampa.

This place is fast, cheap, and convenient...a perfect combination for a Chinese restaurant!

I always come here for the Chinese vegetable soup when I am feeling a cold coming on - it always helps me feel a little better. I also really enjoy their vegetable mei fun.

There is an area to eat in, but I rarely see anyone sitting. I usually call ahead and my food is ready when I get there, but service is pretty fast even if you walk in and order. All of the people that I have talked to are friendly and cheerful. They also deliver! 

Definitely my go to Chinese place in Lansdowne!

4 stars for a great HH but besides that, it was ok. 

Their HH is from 4-7pm daily. This in itself is awesome. Bud lights were $1.50, fresh calamari appetizer was $5, and various rolls were $5 and $7.

The hubby and I ordered way too much food and our bill was modestly priced. 

The sushi was fine, but I felt it had too much filler (Panko and rice).  

I would like to return again when I'm not pregnant and sample their raw sushi. My hubby liked the scorched earth roll and said that with an appetizer would have been plenty of food.

Excellent neighborhood restaurant. Zerillo's from the outside is completely different from the inside. Inside it's cozy, intimate, not too big but not too small. You can tell the owners are heavily involved with the running if this restaurant. 

Our server was very knowledgeable. We ordered the chicken francese with a side of penne alla vodka. We also ordered the chicken special with linguine, mushrooms, mozzarella and a white wine sauce. Both dishes were fantastic.  

The dishes come with salad and bread. 

The portions are huge and definitely enough for leftovers. 

We will go back and next time try their pizza.

Suburbia, aka Exton, surprisingly has some great food spots. Lemoncello being one of them. 

While in PA for work, our group decided to enjoy a night at Lemoncello. We ordered a wide array of food, including a cheese/meat tray, burratta, pasta dishes and seafood. 

I went with the red snapper with a citrus glaze and it was quite tasty. Instead of potatoes I went with a side of pasta and it was just ok-supposedly the pasta is made in house, but it didn't have the taste to me. 

The atmosphere is pleasant and inviting, the service was great and the food is priced accordingly. When in PA again, I would definitely take a trip back to Lemoncello.

I probably should have drank more before I got there.  But paid a $5 cover (not worth it IMO) plus drinks were pricey and you need a $20 card minimum if you run out of cash.  

Vibe was great and music was fun (but didn't quite hit the spot).  There was a lot of dancing and young folk and it was sweaty, slimy, and gross.  

Very little place to sit if you get tired and there are A LOT of people after the usual NOLA drinking time.  It got so crowded and I got stepped on several times by really wasted people.  

If you don't mind getting swamped by people and just want to dance wasted stupid, then here's a good place to go.

I am a little surprised by the negative reviews especially since this place is always PACKED in the Summer.  I really like La Jolla the food is good and the patio is great.  I would love to say that the service is wonderful but it does fit with the casual nature of the restaurant.  The servers seem as if they are friends with a lot of the customers.  This may result in them spending a bit too much time chatting but hey your time for chatting will come :-) 

I have been in Indy for almost 2 years and I have made sitting on the patio during the Summer for lunch my thing to do.

I like going to Champps.  Its big got tons of tvs and I can get beer on draft.

This bar is standard.  With a little yuppie-ness thrown in for good measure.  This northside hot spot always has a mixture of old men in their Seven jeans and cougars looking to "casually" meet a young whipper snapper.  

That being said I love to watch the people and the bartenders are good.  Now in the Summer time especially on Wed. nights this place turns into a hump day saving grace.  Live music, beer specials, and tons of folks.

The great time I have at this location makes up for the long drive home.

So, you know how you watch tv and you see someone who has made a hotel their home?  Well the Conrad is definitely that type of hotel.  Located in the heart of downtown the Conrad has an old feel although it was just built about 3 years ago. The staff is great and restaurant attached is wonderful but  what do you think will be the talk of the hotel?

THE BATHROOM!! 

 OMG!! Spa tub..separate shower with dual shower heads...AWESOME!!  I could not imagine waking up in that room everyday because I would never make it on time for anything! 

I would like to thank you Conrad for an excellent night of sleep and a wonderful bathroom.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: We got the niku udon and tonkatsu ramen with sprouts. The service was very friendly and attentive but not intrusive. Both of our soups came with a little salad (with oddly amazing dressing) and a 4pc california roll. The udon was great, and filling. The ramen was a monster bowl. It's quite good, but I think it's pretty ridiculous that all the toppings cost extra. It was quite good, but I did add soy sauce and recommend a sploosh of sriracha. With that, it was really amazing. It's pretty much losing the 5th star for pricing and charging so much for extras. Nonetheless, it was a lot of food and very good.

One thing that St. Pete beach seems to have a ton of is ice cream shops. This one is tucked into the ground floor of the Don CeSar, in the big pink monolith's shopping arcade.  They have a wide variety of locally made ice creams, and you can get sundaes and banana splits as well. My sundae was kinda small - not that I expected anything massive for the price at the Don! Maybe I should get the sundae-in-a-sand-pail option next time.

Bonus: there's a Ms. PacMan cocktail table tucked away in the corner, and they also brew Starbucks coffee if you're craving something other than diner-quality java.

A cute little place to stop by for a quick cuppa. I'm not 100% sure, but I think the coffee is La Colombe, ie, awesome. They have a decent selection of bagels and danish for breakfast, and sandwiches/salads for lunch. I've never tried the food (other than a bagel), so I can't comment there.

Service is friendly and quick. There's a small garden area out back where you can sit and enjoy your drink (in addition to indoor seating). It's not a snobby cafe or a super hip coffee shop. It's just a place to get a good cup of coffee and a snack while passing through.

This is your basic neighborhood Chinese spot . The kind of place that seems sorta shady, but is the only Chinese place around so you deal. There is really no reason to frequent Mandarin House unless you are a Fishtown local with a craving for quick take-out. 

The sesame chicken is pretty ok, and the general Tso. The crab rangoon is very tasty. Pork fried rice is good, but the lo mein tastes very blah.

Service is decent enough for a take-out joint and they've always been pretty quick with my order. I've never ordered delivery - but then again I can't see why. If you don't live close enough to walk here, then I'm not sure why you're going.

We were in the area and looking for someplace for supper.  We decided to give it a try without looking at the reviews.  Had we looked at the reviews, we probably would have passed.  

As it is, I'm glad we stopped.  Nothing pushed this into the excellent category, but, for a cheap chinese buffet, it was pretty darn good.  The food was fresh and tasty, the restaurant was clean, and the salad bar was much more that your run of the mill salad bar.  We seldom get to this side of town, but wouldn't hesitate to stop again.

I was pretty excited about this place, and very much looking forward to trying it.

The one good thing was my salad, it was VERY good,  and well mixed.

I got an Italian sausage piada, and that had to be the blandest Italian sausage Iv'e ever tasted.  Seriously, no taste.  VERY disappointing.

My wife got a different kind of Piada...I don't recall which one...but her experience was much like mine.  She got soup and said it seemed like it was straight out of the can.

And I thought it was VERY overpriced.  2 small Piadas, one salad, one soup, 2 soft drinks, over 25 bucks.

Yeah.....thanks..........but no thanks.

I've visited here a few times.  I've got friends east, and this is a comfortable halfway point for us to meet for lunch or dinner.

Everything I've had here is well above average, but I don't think it QUITE reaches 5 star level.  It's close--but not quite there.

The breaded tenderloin is quite good, and the burgers are hearty and when I ask for a medium cooked burger, I GET a medium cooked burger--I wish more restaurants were like that!

I've had a steak here a time or two, and, again, above average.  Certainly good enough I'd not hesitate to order one again.

They've carved out a nice little niche on the East side.  Worth a visit.

I'm not sure it's quite "A-OK", it's not a "meh" either.  

When you enter the store, the produce area is large, and spacious.  The aisles are plenty wide, and you can browse without feeling like your personal space is being intruded upon.

But, once you get to the main part of the store, the aisles are probably the narrowest I've ever seen in a grocery store.  I'm not a claustrophobic kind of guy, but this part of the store just sets me on edge.  It seems I'm ALWAYS either bumping into someone, or they're bumping into me.

They have a good selections of goods, and the employees are always friendly and helpful, so that's a mark in their favor.

I love glasses, Im always looking for my next pair. This place has a great selection of good looking glasses, I dont really see cheap fillers. Cheap being the important word here. I found a pair I loved and the frame itself was $1000, gulp say whhaaaat. Well this fit my presumptions that downtown shopping is a lil expensive. The shop looked really cool and trendy but nothing i could afford. I usually spend about $300 for everything and felt intimidated in the store. The staff is super friendly but that didnt make up for the hefty price tag.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text: Rockford is an upscale Edmonton diner that has a very chic & modern restaurant design along with a fabulous patio to enjoy the too brief Alberta summer sun.  I enjoyed the classic 'Rockford Burger' which featured high quality beef that truly makes all the difference, tasty smoked cheddar cheese and crispy bacon.  Mmmm... bacon.  The drink menu hosts a wide range of options, but I recommend Double Happiness Draught craft beer brewed especially for Rockford customers.  The friendly customer service and prompt attention are notable highlights.

Who would've thought this store was a diamond in the ruff?!? 

Fantastic boutique with great pictures of little boys gettin their first haircut by Aidan.  It's eclectic and chic this storefront and in the back is where all the big boys hang.  Make sure you set up an appointment in advance to get your shave (and drink) on!

Minus one star for the pompous bitch who could do nothing but stand and sneer.

Although there was this fantastic lady working next to the bitch as well -- she was gosh darn helpful and really personable.  I wonder if those two were sisters....

Pre-Katrina this joint was THE spot to be, superior sushi and rolls with unbeatable service.  Back then, the servers actually had uniforms - all black button up shirt w/ black pants.  Now the servers seem much more lax with black shirt and jeans.  

True, service hasn't been as great as before....but it's not a huge turn off if anything.

Great thing about this location is that they have a separate Japanese style dining room in the back, complete with sliding doors and floor-cushion seating - to make it as authentic as possible.  Hence, the extra star.  

Good luck w/ parking!

Busy joint w/ friendly folks running it! 

Small is a decent size already and runs a buck!  Cheap!  

Whole boatload of flavors and probably 3 are sugar free.  They do serve yummy looking soft served icecream, but that you can get anywhere!  Snowballs are distinctly New Orleans!

Brought my three cousins all under 10 yrs and the lady was super sweet to them.  We were patient and she was a bit slow, but she made the effort seemed worth it.  

Parking is scary though -- so much traffic and ppl literally parking in the turning driveway BLOCKING entrance/exits!  I guess it's so freakin hot that only a snowball can cure.

having just come back italy, i knew that any pasta eaten afterwards could not live up to the food i had there. i now know what really good italian food tastes like and have a benchmark when comparing it to restaurants here in the states.

their gnocchi is really good. it was fresh and definitely tasted homemade. however the lobster meat inside the ravioli we ordered was a bit fishy smelling and tasting. it could mean that it wasn't fresh. but overall, i left with a good impression of this place, concluding that it is one of the better italian restaurants back in the states.

Horrible job and service.   Paid for super wash to clean interior and exterior.    They wiped the top of the dash and that was it.  I asked to wipe the obvious dirt on the console and fender.  The mgr comes out and says that is all,they are going to do. I told him I was disappointed after spending $20 and would not be back...he said fine, don't come back and learn how to read.....implying that there sign that explains all the great stuff you get with the "super wash" did not include actually cleaning anything dirty.

Excellent, personalized, first-class hair care from guys who are total professionals. I can't believe more people don't know about SB Barbers; they put all the other jokers in SB, IV, and Goleta to shame. I think I paid $17 for the haircut, but it was well worth it. I don't know what kind of gel they put in my hair afterwards, but it was quality stuff and I had a smooth look going for more than 12 hours (a student described it as "fresh"). These will be my go-to-guys for as long as I live in the area.

CASH ONLY

Grossly overrated restaurant that wastes its ideal location on Mass Ave by trotting out food that wouldn't be out of place at an Applebee's or Ruby Tuesday (not that either of those places are bad, but still ...) I get that this place is open late, but that doesn't excuse the less than stellar food. I agree with some of the more honest reviewers here that while the wait staff is friendly, it cannot save the food. Some of the food is good, but others felt like a Piccadilly or old person cafeteria. Avoid the chicken salad at all costs, as well as the quesadillas.

Lazy Daze is a great, COZY little coffee house. The place is a bit cramped, the furniture is pretty used. It's really comfortable- If you can find a spot. I usually grab something and go when I do stop here. I stopped here the other night, and some comedians were doing stand up. I was here to talk to a friend, but I love that this was happening. 

My drink usually tastes great, and the staff has always been friendly. 
The bathroom is creepy, and that's kinda cool. And they have ice cream! 

For as cramped as it usually gets, it'd be hard to grab a seat in here to sit for awhile, but why would you want it big anyway?

I don't understand the bad reviews here.  Easy check in. Clean, mostly quiet room with friendly staff.  We've stayed at many Holiday Inn Express and know what to expect.  I like to not have to figure out breakfast.  Unfortunately breakfast here wasn't that good.  We've had better.  There were a couple little things too, like there was no bath mat until our last day. There was no "I'm busy" hangtag for the door.  I did appreciate the fresh water bottles left 3 out of our 5 days.  Easy check out. They stored our luggage until our flight, called us a taxi and mailed(hopefully) my postcards.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This gym has a pretty good selection of equipment for $20 a month, and the staff is all really nice. I don't expect anything fancy from a gym, and that's what I got here. It seems like I hardly ever have to worry about waiting on equipment, since its never really that busy (I go in the morning before work, most of the time).  There's a great selection of weights and equipment, too.  My one complaint is that when the treadmills break down, they can stay broken for a while before they get fixed. But for a $20 gym, it does the job.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: This is the kind of Italian restaurant that grandmothers would love. Probably because they don't have much left in the way of taste buds, or memory of what good food is supposed to be like. The 'entertainment' was creepy and embarrassing, consisting of an older man 'singing' over what sounded like a casio keyboard. And the dinner was one disappointment after another. What's called 'home made pasta' seemed to be suspiciously pre-frozen. The tomato sauce that came on the ravioli's had an overpowering taste of tomato paste.  And they use canned mushrooms in their dishes. That should tell you all you need to know. Avoid this place.

My friends have been coming here for a few months with glowing reviews, so I decided to stop in for happy hour recently. I love this place. It's got a Mexican/Rockabilly/Gothic/Neighborhood bar feel. If that makes any sense. 

Tuesday nights there are $2 food and drink specials all night long so the tab was very reasonable. The food was good. Not spectacular, but I think the point of this place is booze. 

I get the feeling that this place gets crazier as the night goes on. I'll be back later next time to verify.

This McDonald's is brand spanking new.  All that means is that the play palace is bigger and the furniture and decor is more modern.  Everything else is the same.  I don't really like McDonald's other than their coffee... but we were at the Blues game last night and since they scored 4 goals or more we got a free Big Mac with our ticket stub.  I felt kinda odd just walking in and getting a hamburger for free so we got a soda too.  The counter attendant was fine and didn't make feel like the cheapo that I am... $1.08 for two Big Mac's and a soda.  :)
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
This is really one of my favorite restaurants in all of St. Louis.  It's one of those places where I've never received a bad meal, and all of the menu items are very well made.

This last time I split a rueben with mac & cheese, a salad, and a side of spinach.  Everything was top quality.  The rueben was juicy but not messy.  The mac & cheese was perfect... super rich and creamy.  The spinach was good too.

I used to eat here all the time.  I've kind of forgotten about it, but will be back more often.  I have been reminded of how much I like the place.

I could drink the Napoleon of the west pretty much everyday for the rest of my life! Nice smokey flavor with a perfect amount of SPICY. Its basically the perfect cocktail IMO. 

Other drinks were are also well made with fresh ingredients and premium liquors. 

I have not had dinner here, but I've been for events and had some of their snackitizers. The hummus is very good but not in anyway traditional. Its a bit on the thick side too. 

Roof Top Patio is killer though. Easily one of my favorite especially since its walking distance from work!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I've found the food at La Pasta to be ok, nothing outstanding, but definitely not the worst on offer on campus. They do a cafeteria-style pasta thing downstairs, and upstairs they do sandwiches and desserts and coffees. 

La Pasta wins extra points from me for having the cheapest lunch on campus (as far as I know). $2 for a grilled peanut butter and nutella sandwich. (Although I think it went up to $2.50 right before I finished...)

Still. This place stands out over the other mediocre, overpriced food options on campus.

This is a pretty standard TD branch. They have extended hours on Thursdays and Friday nights, as well as Saturday hours. I've never seen it too busy, although it definitely picks up at lunch time. 

One thing to watch out for is that they lock the doors to the ATMs at (I think) 10pm, although this doesn't seem to be consistent. They seemed to be having problems with their alarm and with people hanging out in there, and the solution seemed to be to just close it in the evenings. The alarm seems to go off randomly any time they're closed as well.

$20 for a mens pedicure? Tampa, I friggin' love you!

I know its Monday and its kinda slow in the shop this afternoon. I'm going to the beach tomorrow so my feet will need to look smexy (which in my vernacular means man sexy)
I'm sure you don't do too many Mans Pedis so.. release the smexy! 

Pretty good job overall but something I need to point out. In NYC they would have massaged my thighs but I'll let it slide based on the price. I gave a $4 tip because I'm the Brad Pitt of feet and I didn't want you to talk about me.. Me and my smexyness..

Tampa dudes! Support a local business and get your feet cleaned! And tip well!

Hell no.

I will never rent from Budget again. We needed to get our rental car quickly. I have plans in Orlando! I've been renting cars for decades, its usually an easy thing to do.

When I got to the Budget Car Rental there was a forever line? There was four counterpersons assisting renters, why is this process taking so long? Every other car rental place had no line, WTF?

10 minutes turns in to 50 minutes. Now I'm late and I had to switch up all my plans.

Budget Car Rental, I would have spent the extra $10 to finish the check out process quickly. 
I should have budgeted my car rental with a different car rental company.

Never again

I had high expectations after seeing this place featured on Food Network. It was good, but not mind-blowing. Very yummy ice cream (I got the maple oatmeal cookie, hubby got the salted caramel) but not the most amazing I've ever had. I really wanted to try some of their savory flavors, but they only had 2 on this particular day, and I found both to be bland. My young daughter ordered lavender honey, can't tell if she liked the taste as much as the fact that it was purple (her favorite color), but it was pretty tasty. Personally, it was a good experience, but I'd choose a spumoni or torrencini from Brocato's over this place any day.

Welcome back to St Louis Dunkin Donuts. Still working out the kinks, this brand new, from-the-ground-up store is charged with introducing the classic donut and breakfast sandwich establishment back to town.

The location is great, the facility clean and new, and the promise of good, cake-y donuts when the crack-laced Krispy Kreme donuts just aren't your thing is welcoming. Oh and the coffee is also well respected by many. 

So will St Louis run on Dunkin? Time will tell. 10 more stores are set to open in the future.

You mightn't guess that hidden behind the Hooters in a Castleton strip mall is this cozy little sushi joint. The menu, in Japanese and English, is extensive, and they seem to have plenty of weekday specials, including free miso soup. I sampled some veggie rolls, the house salad, seaweed salad, inari and miso soup--all were above average. I washed my meal down with Asahi, which was 20 percent off, making the 24-oz bottle a steal. The service was gracious, though perhaps a tad slow when it was time for the check. But by that time I was in a warm, belly-full-of-sushi kind of haze so I didn't much mind.
