I was excited that there was finally a liquor store in this area because there aren't many other options close by. At first glance, it is clean and seems nice, but we weren't greeted by anyone and the employees weren't friendly like other liquor stores in the area. Also, the employees aren't familiar with TN state liquor laws, which is frustrating because they should be experts since they are employees. The prices are cheaper just a few miles down the road in Mt. Juliet, at least for the items we were purchasing.

I've heard so many great things about this place so why did it take me so long to try it? I'm mad at myself for waiting so long. 

I came here after a dinner out in East Nashville and I purposely skipped dessert so I could grab some ice cream. The line was long, which I expected, but I appreciated the opportunity to try different flavors before I committed. Both of the flavors I tried I loved, so my decision wasn't too difficult. I picked the lemon and blueberry and the chocolate. The lemon and blueberry was absolutely amazing. Its not cheap, but I believe the quality is worth it. I'll definitely be back to try some other flavors.

The old rectory building was turned into a bar and restaurant with french country decor. The cocktails, while fairly traditional, were on point and well made and not a terrible price at about $9/glass. The food was fabulous. We tried the crispy cauliflower, brussel sprouts, smoked fish, liver and toast, and the steak. I had trouble picking my favorite because they were all so good. The portions are small for the price but it is very delicious and worth the occasional splurge. If they ever decide to add a happy hour option, I would need to empty my bank account.

My extended family of about 25 had a family style lunch here on Sunday. The room we were given was not private, so other customers were walking by and looking at our buffet table, which was kind of odd, but oh well. Service was better than great, our drinks weren't even half finished and they were being replaced. The Pasta con Broccoli was OK, but the Chicken was amazing. Large moist pieces, i went back for 2nds. Dessert was plain cheesecake and a fruit spread. The cheesecake had to be homemade, b/c store bought just doesn't taste like that. 
Overall, the food was pretty good, service excellent, space was so-so.

I dislike the Winn Dixie chain as a whole. I think the products are overpriced and their food selection tends to focus on highly processed foods. That being said, this is probably one of the nicest Winn Dixies I've ever been to. It's always clean, it's a large store, it's right next to a basketball court and art studio, and it's down the street from my gym. The parking lot is also more shaded than most are due to the trees. So I guess if you're going to get ripped off at a Winn Dixie, get ripped off at this one.

His nachos were perfection. The people behind us got an order too and said they were "Great!" My enchiladas were not bad. A bit dry, a bit bland, benefited greatly from the addition of the sauce we asked for. 

Service was pretty quick, everything was hot. We had to ask for water and ask for our check...but culturally this is pretty normal because that tends to be the norm in Mexico. 

He wants to go back to eat those nachos every week. I'm dragging my feet and wishing they had made a better first impression on me.

There's another Chinese restaurant RIGHT NEXT DOOR to my work. However, if I want Chinese I will drive to this place (about 1.5 miles away) from now on. The food (although essentially the same) tasted better and the veggies were fresher, the employees were WAY nicer, and they let me switch out my "lunch combo eggroll" for a wonton instead. I don't like cabbage. 

It's not going to blow you away, but Kang's has got better food for sure than it's nearest competitor. Bonus points for being two doors down from the fro-yo place.

Really nice selection of local beers, wine, and liquors. This store is open later than a few of the others so it's become our go-to place. The employees are helpful and the store is clean. The wine vault and bar in the basement are really cool...be sure to check that out. This location used to be the downtown Kahn's, if that helps you out at all. Parking is metered out front and there's a spot or 2 in the alley alongside the building if you're just running in and out. There's a bike parking thing right outside the front door.

I love White Castle, the taste is so unique. This location is also a Churches Chicken, however this review is for the White Castle. 
The food was hot and fresh. The staff could have been a little friendly however.They just took my order and that was pretty much it, no smile or anything. Everything else was great, the food was outstanding. The store was very clean and the restrooms were almost spotless, I do have to say, the hand dryer is really cool. It is a Dyson AirBlade, I just thought that was really cool. At any rate, I would have given more stars if it wasn't for the cold greeting I recieved at the outset.

I've been wanting to go to fat salmon for a long time, but I'm just not in that area very often.  Finally had a chance to check it out in between some afternoon drinking and a birthday party.  This was more of a snack spot so I just got a salmon avocado roll and the dancing vampire roll.  They were both really good.  I mostly eat the 3 for $10.95 roll specials, and it's amazing what a difference the good quality makes.  The salmon pieces were huge and the avocado was perfectly ripe.  The dancing vampire had a really nice spice.  I kind of want to go back again immediately.  Really wish they delivered.

3rd or 4th stop on my crawl(s), having too much fun to check in anymore on Yelp. Went here 3 times during my week in NOLA. Music super loud, so no deep conversations here.. just booze and boogie. Tall bar tables so you can rest your happy hour rewards here. Waitresses super nice and watched my LV bag--contents were still intact...THANKS!!! Many bachelorette and bachelor party people from Chicago, Tennessee, Philadelphia...Tourist fun to dance like no one's watching. Saints fans in jersey wear head bobbed all night long (locals?) Everyone was all shiny and smiley. Stop by 4 SUUUURE.

I must first say I come from NYC where there is a Chinese restaurant on almost every corner. Nothing special with this fast food Chinese takeout place.  I have had much better and also have had worse. I ordered the Bourbon Chicken combination plate.  It came with pork fried rice and an egg roll.  Actually I liked the egg roll the best.  It was hot and not greasy. The Bourbon chicken had a uninspiring sauce with little taste. The pork fried rice was ok but also with very little taste.  The positive was it wasn't the usual greasy fast food Chinese meal.  They used grease sparingly.  I would think twice before going back.

I feel as though the people that gave them 3 stars or higher might be homeless.  

This Inn was awful!  The door didn't have a deadbolt locked that worked and the chain lock was, well, was there a some point in time but is now missing.  The windows were easily opened and cracked,  I had to put my hair straighter in the jam so that no one could break in.  The room smelled of bleach the the shower only had one temperature, cold.  

This was our fault for booking a hotel the week of the wedding, which 3 other weddings were and a marathon.  

We booked the room for 2 nights but only stayed for one.  

Lesson learned, never again!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I was hungover and decided to try a cheap hoagie from here.  It was less than $3 and I guess I got what I paid for.  Bread was average, some standard turkey, tomatoes and shredded lettuce.  It's a bit dodgy inside, but maybe that's just my impression as my hungover was rendered worse by the one guy yelling at some kid that he was stealing things.  If you want to spend less than 3 bucks on a sup-par sandwich, go for it.  (Sometimes we just have days like that!)  If you want a quality sandwich and are okay with spending more, go elsewhere.

Went for breakfast.  Feel of the place is nice and homey with a sort of old-fashioned counter in the front and a fireplace in the back.  The menu is a little on the small side.  The Spanish omelette was good though I felt the potatoes on the side left a little to be desired.  We also tried the pancakes which were delicious.  My girlfriend thought the coffee was good.  All of this came to $20 so it's affordable.  It's good but nothing wowed us our first time there.  I give it a solid 3 1/2 stars and we would try it again for lunch or otherwise.

could I get some mac n cheese with my salt?!?!  What's up with STL and oversalting perfectly delicious things?!  

I had  a gruyere cheese and bacon macaroni plate and it was decent but the bacon already really had enough salt so i'm not sure why there was so much in the gruyere.  I really like the concept and think it could be amazing.  so much more interesting than a cereal restaurant or some other place that tried to channel our childhood cravings.  

Maybe I'll go back someday if a friend wants to try it and i'll give it a second chance.

We happen to stop here after a visit to Cabela's sporting goods next door.  The Sundance offers traditional American cafe food serving breakfast , lunch, and dinner.  

I was not very hungry after walking around and around the sporting goods store.  Walking to our table, we pass the salad bar; which did not look appetizing.  The only appetizing item on the menu was the buffalo wings.  The wings were a bit salty and wasn't hot at all.  Meh, I have had much better.  At least, it wasn't greasy and over cooked.  What can you expect when you are miles and miles from anywhere.

Tucson is not known as a Sushi town, and this place further drives home that point. My friend made a point to inform me that Sushi King's purveyors deliver fresh, non-farm raised fish, but honestly, when served at room temperature(!), the difference in taste gets blurred. The "special" was a rather greasy fish they were obviously trying to get rid of...not impressed. At least the sake seemed to have killed any harmful bacteria. Pretty dull, strip mall office decor. And translate "local feel" into "very casual." Not a place for special occasions.

I think we might think twice the next time we take up a place on one of the most drunken streets in all the city/state. The construction crew didn't help with the morning either.  We had only picked up on this place because of its location and low price for the night. 
Rooms are large enough, but overall kinda shabby. The bathroom had peeling wallpaper and a super dated hair dryer that blew its fuse after a few minutes usage. The beds are comfy but I noticed some brown stains on pillow inside of its cover. 
No doubt, one can do better than here.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I see Lauren G on the top floor, she is fabulous! She does the best blondes hands down in the city! She does my great length extensions for me and it was well worth the price! She also does the best blow outs for any hair type I would reccommend her  to anyone she is awesome i literally am obsessed with her....The front desk however sucks they never confirm appts or follow up with anyoneand rush to get you out. The assistants are awesome! She takes her time is kind nice and just a great person who loves her job and shows through her work!

Not sure why this gets such high reviews on their tacos.  I got 2 steak, 1 chirizo and 1 pastor.  The steak was tough and grisly.  Probably one of the worst I have had.  The chirzo was nothing special.  Now on the other hand the pastor was some of the best that I have had.  If I could go back I would order 4 pastor tacos.  They have homemade salsas that were pretty good.  The verde and picante were very nice.  Overall this was ok.  I wont be driving out of my way again to go up there.  I will hit Guanajuato the next time.

OK doubletree. Nothing really too special about the place other than the view from one side of the building. It is in a really pretty location, though it is hard to get anywhere by foot.

One of the people at the front desk seems to have major issues communicating in english and then gets agitated rather easily. Top it off with the fact that they were fully booked and completely ignored my requests to not be on the top floor, or near an elevator when selecting a room for me, and I'm not too killer about the location.

Oh well, at least I still earn rewards for it
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Walking into the breezeway that leads to this place, I was very impressed. I went to Rome last year, and it did faintly remind me of walking down the alleys and backstreets to get to little restaurants. The inside was delightful as well. However, the food didn't live up to it. I got the margherita pizza, as about an old school staple as you can get, and it was just bland. Almost no flavor, and it was a little overcooked like some people have said. My wife and our two friends were also disappointed with their meals. The one saving grace was the cannoli, which was quite good.

I'm going to be generous with 3 stars.  More like 2.5.

It's old.  A hole-in-the-wall kind of place.  A bit cluttered.  Could be cleaner.  Needs remodeled.

The food  was okay. 

The cashier/waitress speaks English well.  And they deliver, which is a rarity among Mexican places.  Prices are very good for the food you get.  Those bumped it up to 3 star. 

They've been in business a long long time, so they must be doing something right.   I oughta go back and see what their specialty or secret to staying in business is.

It shares a building and a common entrance with Miller's Pizza & Sub Shop, another dreary-looking restaurant.

This place is a mess.  They had 1 person working at the counter during the after-work rush and she was in noooo hurry to keep the line moving.  Speaking of lines, there isn't one.  It's a mass of people, some waiting patiently for their turn based on when they walked in, and others nudging their way to the front to get faster service.  While this may be a reflection on society and not on this business, the store should have some sort of simple queue system, knowing that they'll get swamped at the end of the day.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Here it is.  The famous Imo's Pizza.  The pizza, its cheese in particular, is more divisive than the AB-InBev merger.  I'm personally a fan of the pizza, and I can prove it by eating an obscene number of slices in one sitting.  I've done so at this location more than once because the service is speedy and there's always open tables for you and your guests.  If you plan on making a trip, preclear your plans with everyone in your party to make sure there are no provel haters amongst them.  They tend to get verbally violent or physically sick at the mere mention of Imo's.  That's fine though, more for me.

I've driven a fair number of clunkers and, as a result, acquainted myself with a fair number of repair shops.  Of those, Royal stands out in my mind as honest, fair, efficient, and friendly.  Most shops will just assure you that X was wrong with your car, and it's all better now.  The guys working on my car actually showed me the busted part, explained how it broke, and showed me where the new part was installed.  This might be just a minor gesture, but it goes a long way toward creating repeat business, especially since the problem WAS fixed.  My car was in and out the same day, no backlog, no waiting for parts, it was great!

I always feel like I'm imposing on the staff here as I meekly take my seat in the fancy antechamber and wait for my name to be put in the computer.  Upon entry of a potential customer, the staff at most haircut places will take a short break from cutting hair (or reading a magazine) to greet you and place you in the computerized line.  That's not always the case here.

However, once you're enrolled, it's smooth sailing.  The staff offers you a drink, a mechanical chair massage, a hot towel, and of course, a shave and a haircut.  The prices are competitive, but the hours are not.  I've gone here a few times and I'll likely go back.

I go during the lunch hours and have gone during Happy Hour in the past. The staff is great and outgoing and the crowd is nice. It's mainly local older folks, but they certainly are not fussy.  The drinks are cheap and the food is decent. I like the neighborhood feel to it earning that little extra star.

I typically get the Grilled Cheese. It's yum! The wings are decent.  The Irish guy in the front window tho' is super creepy.

This is, thankfully, a smoke free place. You can go outside and smoke and eat outside too. It's covered and I think warm all year around, but I stay inside.

Located in the Conshohocken Marriot, Shula's is a pricey option for a steak lunch or dinner.  I've been here many times and its good, consistent,  and dependable, but nothing special.  If you have family, friends, or clients you wish to wine and dine in the Conshy area, and you are thinking steak, this is your best bet. 

Service is fine, and decor is typical upscale chain steakhouse.  Abundant free parking in the Marriot parking garage, and just a minute off the 76 and 476 ramps.  Not worth the trip, but if you are in town and want to stay local then its a good choice.

Good beer distributor right in town when you need a case and some ice.  They wiffed on my Hofbrau Original (my go-to beer once it get's warm...yeah, I abide by the Reinheitsgebot and so should you...put away that hipster pumpkin ale and stick with water, malted barley, yeast, and hops), so plan B was Spaten.  Ahh, a nice Munich style lager on a warm spring day.  If you've never experienced this state of inebriation, then by all means do so.  Now, what hipsters find in PBR I have no idea, but they certainly don't know what a classic German beer is...and that, dear reader...IS what beer is.

Typical Courtyard. As with any chain, one room looks like the next. Even looking out the window is often provides a view no different from one hotel to the next. Still, this locale was convenient to the in-laws and provided us with a quiet, comfortable place to stay. The staff was friendly, housekeeping didn't bother us, and it  was quiet. Their exercise room was a little sparse. The shopping extravaganza of Montgomeryville Mall is across the street. Nothing like staying across the street from a mall on Black Friday!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The staff at the front desk was very friendly but this joint needs a little upkeep. Over each vent water was pouring down not allowing for any dry counterspace. The rooms are clean, the beds are comfortable, televisions are older, bathrooms are smaller, but AC works well. 

Housekeeping is another story, I was put on hold for a long time, but it wasnt actually hold, the handset was just placed down so I could every line ringing over and over with nobody answering them. Thennnnn you hear someone walk back, and just hang up on me. No answer from there on. Oh well. They do have cookies though.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Went back for dinner this time which was ok but I prefer the lunch much better. The much talked about corn and crab bisque was good but not worth all the hype, especially when it had canned corn as an ingredient. My party ordered the lasagna and the eggplant while I had the chicken parmesan. The best of the three was the eggplant while the chicken was just ok and the lasagna came in 3rd as it looked to not be that fresh. The lunch dish called veal napoleon was not seen on the dinner menu and that was a disappointment. 5 stars for lunch just three for dinner.

Came here after a move to calm my sushi craving and I was really disappointed. The sushi special I had last time I was here was not on the menu so this time I ended up spending almost $20 for some of the smallest rolls I have ever had. If I was really hungry I would have spent close to $50 on my sushi meal here easily.  I would have gone to my usual stop Sushi Village for the all you can eat fresh prepared deal but was not hungry enough for an all you can eat. This made me realize to get a deal on sushi I need to come hungry or dont come at all. Most likely I wont be coming to Sake Cafe anytime soon.

One of my favorite joints in the city has fallen to the surge of the AirBnB dwellers who have taken over the neighborhood. Ever since they changed to an electronic board it all went downhill from there. The slices are smaller, not as tasty and way less toppings. The rolls are also smaller when they are available. The prices are a bit on the steep side as well, a salad, ONE slice of pizza and a beer for $20, you've got to be kidding. The entree's have turned into high priced decorations that leave you hungry after eating them. Its sad the so many of my favorite places in this neighborhood has gone to the dogs.

This is one of the best groceries if you don't want to cook a big meal and want a quick grilled steak, chicken or fish all of which they cook for you for free. Just buy the meat and they prepare it for you in their kitchen so you don't have to use yours. They season everything well and do a great job in the kitchen. They have a wide selection salad bar and seafood specials on Friday, a huge BBQ plate for $7 on Saturday. Their prices on other items or up there so do your shopping wisely, but if you want a great pick up meal at a great price this is the place. Just do your heavy duty grocery shopping elsewhere.

Three stars only for hotel location and a Starbucks in-house for convenience. I've booked a month ago for a personal trip and was granted club access which I liked but was not expecting that. Club access was breakfast and appetizers throughout the day. Parking was around $45 a day and rooms were standard. What was interesting was the toilet flush handle was under the sink and the seat barely stood up. I've asked for extra towels and never gotten it. 

I was glad I only stayed two nights. Other than the location that I was walking distance to downtown, I probably would not come back.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Meh. The food is decent, our waiter was nice but this is such a "scene" place - in PHILLY. The trance/house is thumping/loud - so much that my husband and I could barely hear each other talk. The tables are teeny/cramped, and you're guaranteed to get smacked in the elbow at least twice while you're eating. The kitchen is also really slow...one app and two pastas = hour+ meal. 

The lobster spaghetti was pretty good, but the fettuccine was just ok. If you're down with trying to eat some decent Italian with "Castle in the Sky"-esque music, you might like it but there are so, so many other options in Rittenhouse.

3.5- Oh sure the hotel is nice.. but CRAZY expensive.

Stayed at the Marriot connected to the airport (seriously, you do not need to go outside the terminal to get to this place).  The hotel itself is nice and well kept.  They have cookies and lemonade in the lobby, and a pretty nice work out facility.

The low rating from me comes from the value.  Considering this room was $250+, where was the free wireless?  Or at least a business center with internet access?  $17 a day for parking?  i gave my friend the choice of where we should stay.  Next time, I'll know that this is not a place to ball on a budget.

Chuck Norris Rating- Dutch Oven
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I had a hankering for Italian and since I have a discount here, I decided to go. The place was pretty empty on a Sunday afternoon, but I guess it's alright since it was Sunday. I ordered the calamari and the spaghetti pomodorini. With a practically empty restaurant, the waitress somehow still mistaken my order for chicken parm. I said whatever and just ate it b/c I was hungry. The calamari was greasy and not crunchy at all. On top of that the fried zucchini was just pathetic looking, all thin and flappy. The chicken parm was alright, nothing to complain about or to rave over. I'm not coming back anytime soon that's for sure.

I have never had faster service. I had barely had one sip of my margarita before our food was out. And this was on a relatively busy Friday night. It was good -- not the best Mexican I've ever had, but pretty average for a vegetarian special (cheese enchilada, bean burrito, tostada). A little above average, in fact, since they use a lot of sauce. But I'd recommend it if you want to get in and get out. If you want to sit and chat, try somewhere else. Also, my margarita was really watered down, though my boyfriend says his wasn't. Maybe I'm just used to Rosepepper.

By far one of the coolest and most comfortable hotels i have ever stayed in. I was traveling with a large group and needed a place to stay in short notice and they were able to accommodate us without any problems and went the extra mile to provide great service.  

Large rooms equipped with a full kitchen, a giant bathroom with an awesome shower head and the mirror, well the mirror was HD lol  you'll know what i mean when you look lol but yeah.  a nice stay, good breakfast, fun pool and fitness room. a great get away place 

Hope you enjoy the stay as much as we (group o 40+) did!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Excellent food, excellent service, reasonably priced.

We went here back in December 2010 while on a trip to Arizona.  Jax was a surprisingly great find.  Chef Casey McQueen creates some innovative and delicious dishes.  The standout was a mussels vindaloo that was a perfect mix of spicy, sweet, and savory.  We used every bit a bread to sop up the sauce from the bowl.  The velvet cake for dessert was also a treat.

At the end of the meal, the chef came out to chat with us personally and ask about the food. Said he spotted us as new faces in the dining room and thought he would introduce himself.  Super nice guy.

Good sized outdoor seating area. Didn't make it for the sunset but I would imagine it would look beautiful. Food was ok. We ordered oysters, Peel and Eat shrimp, kids pizza, blackened grouper, wings, cup of gumbo and side of lobster Mac n cheese. Just a note...Wings were ordered mild but were really spicy...and we generally order hot wings. Everything else was ok. Service was a little slow and it was not busy. I ordered the gumbo as an app and it came out after everyone's main dishes came out. Live music added to the ambiance. They do not take reservations. First come first serve. Overall a nice spot considering it's inside a Holiday Inn.

This is your average run of the mill Bertucci's.  I went here for lunch because my Grandma refuses to eat anything besides Italian food or the Cheesecake Factory and this is closeby.  I got the margherita pizza with shrimp on top and it was pretty good.  The waiter was a bit confused and got my aunt's lunch very wrong- but he was trying.  We were celebrating two birthdays so he brought out a slice of cheesecake on the house.  Overall, I wouldn't go out of my way to go here but it's decent if I'm going out to lunch with Grandma.

Good Mexican food, but nothing too special. 

On my first visit I tried the tortilla soup and sopes. The soup was only okay - good, but not especially flavorful or anything, but I enjoyed the sope. On my second visit I had a carne asada burrito, which was warm and hit the spot. The burrito was the perfect size for lunch. Sometimes burritos in other places are too small, and that makes me mad.

I also enjoyed the salsa and guacamole. The queso was really good. You could tell they used real cheese rather than just some junk from a can.

Service was friendly, but nothing outstanding.

Another one of my stops when I visit St.Louis. Mall location with a comfortable classy atmosphere. American style menu with great salads and sandwiches. All of the entrees I have had were excellent. My favorites are the Lobster raviloi and the baby bake ribs. Bill Cardwell is a highly regarded chef and the menu refects his talent.I have always had a good overall dining experience with groups or just myself. Wait staff is excellent, bar is a happening place. I always meet people who just strike up a conversation with me. Very good price/value

Big fan of top chef, and this is actually the first restaurant of one of the contestants that I've visited.  My fiance and I made reservations to celebrate my birthday here.
It was a really fun time.  I'm pretty new to multiple-course easing (beyond appetzier and dessert) and this was a great place to give it a try.  

I enjoyed each course, but the highlight of the night was definitely my fiance's dessert!  He chose the pana cotta crumbly deliciousness.  Totally jealous I didn't order it.

A cool place, a crowded place serving good food that strikes a nice balance between familiar and fancy.

I was really torn between giving this review 2 or 3 stars.  This has always been my favorite of the Vallarta's locations here in Tampa, the service here is definitely better than the other spots.  The food is plentiful and they do offer 32 oz Margaritas.  I usually order the Molcajete, a cauldron of shrimp, chicken, beef, mushrooms, onions, cheese....it's steaming hot goodness that you can wrap in a tortilla.  The portion sizes are good and the cost is reasonable.  It will fill your belly up, that's for sure.  The food is not bad but not great.  It is just good.  And sometimes just good is enough.

Just ate there last night.  The food was amazing the drinks were flowing and all in all it was an amazing place.  

I live out in the north and made sure to go out NW to make a trip to Abel's.  The owner and staff are so friendly and sure make it an amazing time while you are dining.

Was there around 7 and it was a happening place.  Good for the people who live in Verdi and also for some authentic mexican eats before you hit the road or just to grab a bight to eat.  Very convenient location, right off the freeway and easy access back on to I-80.

We were there on Sunday, June 12, 2011. It was good, and the management and servers there are really SO nice and seem to work SO hard. It was kind of hard to believe we were in the Ritz shopping center area because it really does feel like more of a neighborhood place (i.e. not in Bore-hees) (and I live here, so I can say that). But I have ONE complaint: could you PLEASE use fresh mushrooms? Sometimes people can tell, and that makes a great deal of difference to people who don't have other toppings put on their pizza. We'll go back, but mushrooms no. Canned=not good. Fresh=good. Come on, you can do it.

Unlike the MTA in NYC ... you'll never find long lines at this SUBWAY!

When i come to fast food chain like this you come in expecting the same result each and every time for quick satisfaction. this subway does the trick.. Sandwiches are prepared with fresh ingredients and quicky made to order and in your hands in less than 5 minutes. insta satisfaction and no long lines so you can go quickly in and out and on with your day. 

the tables are always clean and even the prep area looks immaculate when ever i order a sandwich. even during the PM rush hours! all plusses in my book - keep up the good work

This place is overrated. I've read all the reviews and happened to be on the Wbank yesterday so decided to give this place a try for lunch. The only good thing about this place was the service. It was not very friendly but it was fast/efficient. Now, about food. I ordered their Philly roll and it was tasteless, mediocre at best. The person I was with ordered a lunch box which came with soup, salad, Cali roll, Chicken Teriyaki, dumplings and broccoli. It was a generous amount of tasteless food. Won't be back.

Alright, so I have a secret addiction.  It's frozen yogurt and soft serve.  When I hit the chinese buffets with chocolate soft serve machines, I tend to throw back four or more.

I have been here a couple of times, and what I like about it is the variety of flavors and that you can choose how much you want.  They also have a big variety of toppings.  I always have to get their cheesecake flavor, sometimes mixed with chocolate.  They have a variety of fruit flavors as well.  The place isn't cheap, but it is in tourist central, so that's to be expected.

Stumbled into Vinomania while in a rush and grunted "BBQ chicken, need wine." The staff was super helpful giving me three good options in the high $20, low $30 range. I went with the 2012 Californian Birichino Grenache. Found it very delicious and was the perfect compliment to BBQ chicken. It was light, but had just the right burst of flavour. Really fired me up for the rest of the day. 

I got the 25$ membership as well (it's a one time fee) which gives you a small discount on all purchases. I'll keep you posted to let you know if its worth it. 

I could get used to coming here. A fan!

Came here after work for some drinks and eats. To our surprise it was 2-for-1 margarita Wednesday. A couple margaritas, chips, and taquitos later, we were pretty happy with the place. 

I ordered the blue corn tacos, which were okay. They were pretty light on the inside - just chicken and cheese. There wasn't much to add, just some shreds of lettuce on the plate, but definitely not a lot. They were tasty, but nothing spectacular.

The refried bean dip may have been the best thing I ate. Take that to mean what you want. If you want a place to grabs some drinks and chips it's a good bet. For a full meal, there are better places.

After reading all of the shining reviews for Lupita's, I was excited to try it out.

For me and my friends, it was just adequate. My shrimp a la diabla was fine. The sauce was reminiscent of BBQ sauce almost and it tasted like it was made with condensed OJ. It was a nice flavor, just threw me off a bit.

The carne asada was overcooked and far too gristley. I realize that it isnt supposed to be a fine piece of meat, but Ive had better versions almost everywhere else.

The service was also adequate but all in all a very forgettable experience and not one worth driving across town for, for sure.

I came to a friends pre-party for the Santa Pub Crawl a few weeks ago....it was my first time in the Belvedere Towers.  My first impressions were positive and I was impressed with the improvements they made to what was once a dated hotel tower.  If I was looking to rent or lease and I worked downtown or at the University, this would be a great option.  Prices are reasonable, it has a secured entry and it's within walking distance of everything.  I get the sense that this place is only going to get better as Reno's economy slowly crawls out of the recession.

Underwhelming, to say the least.  Came back here after years away only because they keep their kitchen open late.  Wish we had opted for a casino because the food here is completely uninspiring.  I had a tasteless steak sandwich on a too-big roll with an afterthought of a side salad. The place is nicely appointed and they have big menu which might be why nothing tastes great.  Moxies has been around forever and I expected so much more. I think if you are into playing some bar top machines this place is fine but would never suggest eating here just for the food.

Boohoo for the low reviews from people who don't understand dive bars. And oh, what a dive it is! I kind of can't believe it's in Chestnut Hill. It feels like you could be walking into Oscar's in center city, so if that's your type of place, welcome home. Cheap beer, friendly clientele, darts, pool, naked photo hunt (although not official naked photo hunt so it has a different name and worse photos - excellent), cash only, and a bartender who seems really disinterested in serving you. So happy this place is in my neighborhood!

This is my favorite Publix in this area...
I just moved here 5 or so months ago...
When i go in people know me by name...
The awesome guy in the deli knows what i want...
He always asked about me or my wife if she isn't with me...
The bakery made us an awesome cake for our wedding...
I am a Publix shopper and by far this has been my greatest experience...
I am not big on giving 5 stars as you will see...
But this place is always very clean well stocked...
Always have what i want and make you feel special... 
I feel they go above and beyond...

Ah Monte Bello.  The other reviews are spot on.  This place wont' jump out at your as your driving down the road.  If you're looking for it and are in the area and you see the "open" sign then you've got your place.  Head down the stairs into what looks like an ordinary basement - because that's what it is- and you're home.

The pizza is solid.  Nothing earth shattering.  If its in the neighborhood for you I recommend it.   If like me you need to venture into the off-the-grid places then check this one off your list then head over.  

You can find a better piece of pizza in this town but as far as St. Louis style goes its a solid B.

A serviceable Courtyard Marriott, with the standard amenties and options. The lobby and common areas are nicer than the rooms, I'd say, but it gets the job done. Wasn't a fan of the door lock that only worked after 3-5 attempts, the awkward room layout, and the connecting door that in no way provides as much of a sound buffer as places without said door.

Funnily enough, the new renovation plan I'm seeing at all these Courtyards is driving me to start looking elsewhere. The new layout really emphasizes the overpriced food/bar options at the expense of non-revenue generating amenities. I guess I'm just too price sensitive.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I felt the sushi place was okay and the sushi was not consistent at all. The salmon came out and it was really really good and wanted more.  Unfortunately, the second order of fish, the fish was a little on the not fresh side.  The rice on the sushi had a lot of vinegar and tasted like the sushi at Costco or even worst. The mussels were not good at all and did not want anymore.  The rolls were not up to standard.  and looked different compared to most of the places.  Probably want to head back to circus circus and eat there.

We had a positive experience at the Club Quarters in Philadelphia.

OK, the layout is wonky, but it's an old Philadelphia building ... hardly their fault. And it's FULL of character; in the restaurant, you sort-of get the feeling that Philadelphia's elite once dined here (and may still, for that matter).

We had a suite, and it could hardly be called spacious ... but again, I'm mindful that this is Philadelphia, where a really spacious suite could ransack a good many Benjamins from your wallet every night.

The staff were top-notch and helpful in all possible ways.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: This McDonald's is a pad site (Ha! Wikipedia this term.) in front of First State Plaza. One annoyance I encountered is the pedestrian approach to the entrance was oriented in a strange direction. There is a fence all along the edge of the parking area, so one has to walk almost right up to the mall road and then back again to the door. That aside, this McDonald's seemed pretty much standard. The food was what one would expect. Service and food preparation didn't take too long, and they didn't forget anything in my order.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
This Macaroni Grill is in a strip mall off US-202 northbound. Access from the soundbound side is via left turn at a traffic light. Parking seemed more than adequate.

Generally, I'm not a fan of Italian food but I think Macaroni Grill is okay for a chain restaurant. Because I couldn't decide what to get from the menu, I got a "create your own pasta" dish, which compounded the problem by presenting yet more choices. So I got spaghetti with meat sauce and a few more items, and it turned out pretty well. Service was good too.

This McDonald's is on US-13 northbound. This is an entrance from the highway but you have to approach slowly or you may miss it. The restaurant has its own lot and parking area. I only got takeout on this visit so I didn't use the dining area or restroom, but the order area looked decently clean.  Service was okay and speed of food preparation was what you'd expect for a fast food restaurant. I would note though that food from this place was a possible cause of the problem I had later that night, although I can't prove it conclusively.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: This Burger King is at a location that is just-off-the-highway convenient, yet I haven't been here in the five years or so since they opened. My initial impression is everything still looks new and clean. The dining area seating arrangement is somewhat unusual compared to other BK locations but there is something for most groups of diners. The food is pretty much standard for BK. Service was fast and efficient, although the manager had to take over when the cashier didn't know how to apply a coupon. Overall, it's a decent BK. Not the closest one to me but I wouldn't mind stopping here again.

I really like this place but the beer selection  is pretty poor compared to other places. I do enjoy the ambience and how nice the staff is :) !

I always come back because the area is really nice and it is in a centric place at the mall ! 

They have life music on Fridays and Saturdays and that is a plus for me! I never really seen this place super crowded, but Im not sure of its a good or bad sign. In my case I like it, bcs I can find a place to sit and get my beer quicker!

Oh yeah theres no food at all tho, but lots of restaurants around, you re always welcome to bring your own food :) !!

Definitely one of the best sushi places to go to in the city for the food and for the people. The place is small, so everyone cozies up with each other and we all talk and comment on each others' dishes. The price is very reasonable and I love the tuna dumplings and sunomono along with some, hamachi, salmon, and eel. 

The sushi chefs are super friendly and if they're not busy making rolls for people sitting there, people ordering take out or delivery, he'll chat with us. They offer pretty neat special rolls, which change every so often. Tried a special roll with crunch tuna inside and eel with avocado on top. I gobbled that up so quickly.

This was not at all what I expected it to be, not even close. Now I'll be the first to admit I had nothing to base my expectations on, just what was on my mind. It is a counter in a small location with a very casual atmosphere. The choices are straightforward, but yet I still felt limited. I knew it was all mac and cheese, but I guess I was expecting more variety or just more of something. I went with the Mediterranean with sun dried tomatoes, olives, and goat cheese. It was ok, but a bit bland. All in all this place was just missing something.

A haiku for Lure Salon: 

Jenny I Love Thee. 
Dip dyed red and brown, leaf like. 
Bright, like Autumn sun. 

I keep coming to Jenny with hair color challenges and she keeps hitting them out of the park.  From platinum, to strawberry blonde, to Nicole Richie honey colored highlights, to bright as hell red, to my current dip dyed red and brown locks.  So good. So, so, so good.  I also have to mention that the shampoo bowls are super comfortable and you don't get that weird neck strain cramp when you're getting washed.  Thanks Lure!

It's older decor like 90s. The room is very large.  Has a mini fridge, microwave, two burner stovetop.  Plates in room, but no cooking pot.  Bathtub shower combo.  Sheets on one bed were pilly and rough.  Switched to other bed and they were silky smooth.  I was room 102, and it was quiet.  WiFi was slow, couldn't watch anything streaming.  Had good pillow selection with feather or fiber.  Parking is in a garage and take elevator up to lobby.  Breakfast is at the restaurant starting at 7am.  Rooms open to a courtyard outside.  Cute mini golf course in the center.  Would be good hotel with kids.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
4.5 stars.  So close...

Rouses is a local Louisiana based chain.  The Uptown location on Tchoup has recently been renovated and it's truly a pleasure to shop here.  It's also open till 11 PM every night which is pretty handy.  The meat and seafood departments at this location are almost as good as Whole Foods.  Rouses is great because they provide a great mix of local products and national brands.  

The one area I'd really like to see them pick up their game is produce.  They don't do the best job with carrying local, organic produce.  If they kick it up in this department, they could definitely be a 5 star grocery store.

Another amazing meal at La Viola. The orrechite is just DELICIOUS - I get it every single time I go. My friend got the Caesar salad, which was excellent as well. The pumpkin cheesecake for dessert was light and cinnamon-y. Perfection! The service is great, but they REALLY cram in the tables. You need to fully move the tables for people to get out. They were very understanding when the last guest in our party was 30 minutes late because of traffic and parking, which was appreciated because the restaurant was obviously booked.

The ice cream was good, but the service was not. I went with my boyfriend and we forgot his birthday certificate. I told them the situation and asked if he could just show his ID to prove his birthday and they refused. It's ridiculous - I know they are capable because I've been to other Cold Stones that were willing to make an exception. Bad customer service. I'd say I left with a bad taste in my mouth, but that'd be a lie - the birthday cake ice cream is just too delicious for that. But I did leave with a bad impression of the store.

Ugh what a terrible experience. I love Yogorino, but the service we received tonight was terrible. We went in and placed our order. I went to pay with an expired BuyWithMe deal. I requested to use it for the price paid (AS REQUIRED BY LAW). Not only did the woman refuse to accept the deal, but she was EXTREMELY rude. We paid in cash and took our froyo, but I wish we had just left it there and told her to throw it out. Terrible customer service. As tasty as Yogorino is, there are too many places that treat their customers better to return.

Rooster & the Till continues to be our favorite restaurant in Tampa. The food is just phenomenal, as is the service and the heart that the owners and employees put into their food. We decided to try a few new dishes on our most recent visit instead of always going with our favorite tried and true options. Each dish was better than the last. Hubs' favorite was the quail and mine was the scallops and pork neck. Those scallops were just perfection. The cheese and charcuterie board is always a great option, and make sure you leave room for dessert!

My boyfriend called last minute to see if anyone at Salon Bass had availability for a haircut. They were kind enough to squeeze him in, but it was obvious that his stylist was in a rush (she had another client waiting). She didn't do a good job and left a lot of hairs uncut. His hair may not be the easiest to style, but it is obvious that Holly didn't do a thorough job (she rushed) and I ended up having to trim the longer hairs when he got home. If you don't have last-minute availability, no problem...but don't squeeze someone in and do a poor job. We won't be going back.

I returned again for a gel polish change and this time had Jenny, the manager, as my nail technician. I will keep this short and just say that my nails did not look good. The color I chose turned out to be OPI gel axxiom, which Jenny said was difficult to apply. Apparently...because I had gel polish all over my nail beds and skin, which meant that the polish was lifting after a few days as my nails began to grow. They were chipped and looking ragged after less than a week. Such a bummer, especially because this was right before NYE and my vacation so I didn't have time to go back and ask them to repair.

I agree with the first reviewer that you can tell a lot about a building as a guest. I must say that I was shocked and disappointed in the St. James' apartments, especially when the exterior and lobby are so beautiful. The units were outdated (particularly the kitchens) and the heat/AC regulation is terrible. The thermostats aren't even digital! I must say that the doormen are quite nice and are eager to help, unlike doormen at other buildings. They always open the door and are quite friendly, which I appreciate. But for the price of the units and the idea of a "luxury building" these units just do not fit the part.

We had food from A Full Plate at the craft fair at Penn's Landing today. It was the only remotely healthy option available, so we decided to try it. Although we really enjoyed the food, I was disappointed in the portion for the price. At $8, I would have wanted at least 3 falafel balls rather than 2. The pita tasted healthy, which I loved, but it kept cracking and crumbling (not sure if it was the grain or that it was stale). The falafel were delicious and didn't taste deep fried like they often do. I'm guessing their food in the restaurant is really good, as was our food at the fair, but I struggled with $8 for 2 falafel balls on a pita.

My favorite authentic mexican food in SB at the moment. I may be biased because it's two blocks from my house but I'm sticking too it. Their taco's are particularly amazing especially on the days when they have homemade tortillas. I also recommend the tortas and burritos but I've never tried their burgers. Just seems wrong. The salsa bar is also good.

The tables are a little cluttered and the place is never full so I feel like they would be better off getting rid of some of them. The meat can be a little grisly sometimes as well.

This might just be the best city ice cream parlor I've ever been to overall . The only places I've experienced so far in my humble life that can compete are a couple of farmstands in Massachusetts but they're all about kiddie/candy flavors. Pear/goat cheese might not be my favorite of all time, but the fact that they attempted it and actually made it work...props to them. So yeah - tons of interesting flavors in addition to all the favorites, amazing texture (not too hard, not too melty/dribbly...juuuust right) and only $2.50 for a decent sized small!

I think it is time for me to give another update.

Balducci's serves a steak sandwich.  What is amazing is the price $9.95 for at least a 8oz strip steak. The steak comes with a garlic season on the meat.  It is also served with steak fries.  This is an amazing deal when you look at how fast beef prices has risen in the past year.

So what did I have for lunch?  Pasta.  They had a special of pasta with butter, garlic and shrimp.  Wonderful pasta.  This is a great lunch for anyone within driving distance for lunch.  Or if you prefer supper.

+ good location (right off of canal and decatur!) in a nice historic bldg. the rooms had a lot of character with odd room sizes, exposed brick, and windows of all different sizes. 
+ comfortable beds, bathrooms with breathing room. 

+/- free but slow wifi 
+/- breakfast was meh but free again. if you love waffles, you can make your own! 

- service was extremely SLOW! waited a long time to check-in. waited a long time to get our car, which is unacceptable for paying $30/night for. We called down 50 min in advance to get our car. I might come to stay again if a) I didn't drive and b) someone checked in for me an hr ahead of time.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I really like Macaroni Grill, It really doesn't remind me of chain restaurants at all. I think that the food is great! Although pretty much everything I've had on the menu turns out to be pretty heavy. I would definitely recommend showing up hungry. They use a lot of dressing on the salad (big pet peeve of mine)- so you may have to ask them to bring it on the side. 

Staff is nice and I've never had an experience where they weren't able to answer a question. 

AND you get to draw on the tables...and who doesn't love that?

I know its my own fault, but I fell for the Fresh Market's Valentines Day bait-and-switch. I went in to buy the 2 dozen roses for $30. I left with a beautiful bouquet that didn't have a price tag. Was it more than $30? Yes. Was it fresh and cheaper than a flower shop but of equal quality?  Also a yes. 

I've been to Fresh Market several times outside of Valentine's day, and it remains a good place to buy exactly what you'd expect: Fresh product. Its great for fresh fish, fruit, and veggies when a farmer's market isn't an option. But, beware, the prices reflect the quality/freshness of the products.

A locally opened coffee shop (owned by the non-denominational church who holds services there), I had a good vibe as soon as I walked in. 

Friendly staff and a hip interior greeted me, and I enjoyed chatting while I ordered. My banana smoothie was quite tasty!  Plenty of seating, both tables and couches. A band was even practicing in the back!

The church aspect itself might be a turn off for some people... in reading the literature, it definitely seemed a little more hard-core than what I would look for in a place of worship.  But for a cool drink and nice people, it was a great place to go.

Our second stay here. The place is reasonably clean. The breakfast is ok. BUT, the overall passive-aggressive quality of the management is incredible and permeates the staff. The biggest issue is the WiFi. Constant resetting is not enough; hire a competent IT person and find the problem. Don't leave the obviously dropped items on the room floor. Don't say you will have maintenance person look into something when you clearly won't or you would have way earlier. I know that the place is aging, but take care of your property.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: This is a nice little place with pleasant if dated ambiance. The waitress was very nice and helpful. The food was okay, just nothing special. I had the sense that the chef had never been to New Jersey let alone Napoli. So the eggplant parmigean was nicely fried but totally inauthentic. The soup tasted more Greek than Italian although it was good. The salad was not Caesar so much as good restaurant side salad with decent dressing and for extra cost some anchovies. The bread was a mix of sourdough and Italian, not quite one or the other. While we would come back for lunch, this isn't a place we'll frequent.

We were on our way to the Ogden Museum of Southern Art and thought we would come here for a quick lunch.  I really enjoyed the atmosphere - white table linens, beautiful art frames on the walls and wide large windows.  As far as the food, it was just OK.  After  a long weekend of indulging in delicious NOLA food, I decided to order a vegetarian dish - one of my favorites - egglplant sandwhich.  I obviously really enjoyed the bread - but that was it. The egglplant was kind of too chewy and flavorless. My husband, however, ordered a chicken sandwich and he thought it was pretty delicious.  Service was great.

Found the Green Room restaurant near the Hard Rock lobby and found it clean looking and wasn't expecting to like it as much as I did.  The garden omelet was filled with spinach, broccoli, peppers, tomatoes, onions, shrooms and cheese.  The platter was way bigger than I was prepared for.  Home fries and toast and orange garnish rounded up the meal.  Quite delicious.  Service was a bit slow but since this was taking up gambling time, saved money in the scheme of things.  Way better than the likes of Denny's, Ihop etc.

Have ordered pizza from here a few times and liked the sauce to pie ratio. Thin crust is what I grew up on so that's always a plus.  The pizza is better than most of the other places in the area. 

Have also had the calzones. They are huge and can be shared and still have plenty of leftovers. 

Only thing that has me scratching my head is, how does a restaurant, let alone a pizza place not have hours on a Friday?  

Seems my pizza cravings more often than not seem to happen on Fridays. Can only imagine how much business they lose by choosing to be closed on a Friday.

Awesome selections at great prices.  Not only do they carry a huge selection of beer, wines and liquor, they also have international foods, accessories galore, mixers, glasses and just about anything you can think of that goes with drinking.  

This ABC is located on North Dale Mabry, in the same shopping center as Sweet Tomatoes.  I often come in to browse as they have change up the inventory and often have wine or liquor tastings.  

They always seem to have the right amount of employees so never a long check out line.  Very friendly staff and clean, well stocked and easy to navigate.

This review is for the sushi.  You are in Tennessee, a landlocked state, so your fish is going to be frozen.  Best in Nashville, but I haven't tried Virago.  The salmon was real high quality fish with nice veins of fat.  A lot of reviews for non-sushi items were subpar, so I won't even waste my money.

So, for non sushi items, I'd probably check out the Cool Springs area for Japanese restaurants like Shoguns, because Nissan HQ is there.  There's also AYA sushi in M'boro.  Sonobana is also decent off white bridge rd.

I should have expected to be disappointed because I looked this place up on yelp before going, but stupidly decided to go anyway.  Since the food is usually the most important thing, I will start with that.  The actual food was fine.  Everything else, though, sucked.  The music was awful and too loud to ignore, the prices could be cheaper, and the waitress did not exude friendly vibes.  No paper towels in the restroom, no straws with drinks.  You can really tell when places start cutting corners.  It was sad in there.

Mica delivers exactly what you would expect from a fancy dining experience. I took my wife to Mica for our anniversary and it was perfect. We had the set menu and we both enjoyed each stage of the meal. Throughout the meal the waitress was extremely helpful by explaining the next course and bringing out tastings of various specials the chef had for the evening. 

It isn't a restaurant that a normal middle-class couple will be frequenting, but we sure enjoy having the option for special occasions and celebrations!

This place is still my go to on a rainy day when I want some creamy pasta and a side of soup to warm me up. The staff are really friendly and when you step inside, you feel transported somewhere else. I really enjoy their rosa sauces on their pasta, particularly the penne primavera pasta with shrimp which comes in my favorite Rosa sauce tossed with mixed vegetables. All the entrees come with your choice of salad or soup as well as garlic bread. I tend to go with the minestrone soup which does not disappoint. Their pizzas are also really tasty but I'm boring and stick to the pasta because I know I'll regret it if I don't.

Not bad, but not fab. If you need your food fast, you may want to try another place. Considering airport prices, it makes it hard to say I'm a fan. The roast beef sandwich had a hint of horseradish. It would have been nice have more of a kick. Don't be afraid to ask for more sauce if thats your thing. The gu.y serving was cool dude and had a bit of the pirate vibe going which works well with the theme. I took a long time for the food to arrive. One guy had to pack his food. 
Overall not a bad experience. Very convenient though.

Obviously a hole in the wall. But honestly this place is alright. This was the first place I got drunk at on my 21st birthday so I obviously hold fond memories of drinking shots people randomly handed me to the point even THEY had no idea what the bartender gave them.

Our bartender that night was very friendly and offered me a free drink for me and my friend, just for being brought here for my birthday. So sweet! Like Sara said it is a place for the Bud Lite crowd. Nothing fancy...

Some gross people, but that's the fun with these kinds of bars, right?

This place functions so differently than most frozen yogurt places I can't figure it out completely. All self-serve and they charge by the pound. Awkward in my eyes. I am used to a friendly staff who helps me to decide the right kind and toppings before I order to them, and there's a set price for each size with up to 3 toppings. Here, I wasn't allowed to sample and I had to wait for someone to pop out of the back room to get them to place it on the scale and charge me.

A nice variety in flavours, but not toppings. So you actually do get more from this place, but not enough for me to come back often.

I told my boss I picked Yellow Porch to try for restaurant week, and she told me it was "just okay."  Should have listened!  

I ordered paella.  Paella is tough to pull off... or at least it is usually not good in American restaurants.  But, this place had good reviews, and this was their showcase restaurant week menu, so I thought, okay Yellow Porch, I will play, let's see what you're made of.   BLLLLAAAHHH!!!  Paella was watery; bland rice in thin tomato sauce and a few morsels of meat.  Paella is supposed to be thick and gooey with tomatos, onions, cheeses, delicious herbs and spices, etc.

So in short: poop on Yellow Porch.

This is a pretty solid place to grab a coffee in Old City. It's conveniently located on Chestnut, and it's huge: inside you'll find a nice space by the windows with bright seating and the seating area expands back to feature lots of tables and space for studying. 

The prices are what you expect for coffee and the service is quick. Did this place used to be called Customs Coffee House? If so the sign now officially declares Double Shots Espresso Bar, but I believe they are one and the same. 

Note: They have a $4 minimum on cards.

This is an update for all the vegetarians out there. 

Lilly's has a vegetarian option! I got the veggie tacos (sautéed zucchini, squash, green beans, corn, sliced carrots) and they were super tasty. Add the spicy red salsa and some lime and you have a delicious vegetarian meal. I had two tacos and a bottle of water for under $5, and you can't complain about that. 

I feel like now that they are more established at this location the line is more manageable and the food comes out way faster. The seating area is still clean with ample tables. Yay for can and bottle recycling at the exit.

Just ok. Went for 2/3 roll special and ended up getting the 3 rolls for $10.25. I figured I could save some for later but they turned out to be pretty small. I also requested brown rice for which they told me they had to charge me .50 extra per roll. I hate it when places do this, rice is rice, and the extra charge is just more annoying to the customers than it's worth in my opinion. Anyway, the total came to $12.69 with tax which is a lot more than I usually spend for lunch. I wouldn't have minded if the food itself was amazing but it tasted kind of bland, and not super fresh. I don't think I will be going back.

Heck yeah! Newer hotel with a spacious king suite with a sofa sleeper for around $120. Can't beat it. We didn't want to stay in some smokey Casino type hotel so we turned to Yelp and thanks to other Yelpers we chose the Hyatt. If you want a CLEAN room with a COMFY bed this is it.
Other notes - It's really close to the airport, but I didn't hear any planes. Close to shopping and restaurants. You can take a short drive downtown if gambling is your thing. 
The sofa (that is also a bed) is big and comfortable (our kids were with us). Huge TV that can be seen from the two divided sleeping areas.
FREE breakfast.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Nice hotel with spacious, well-designed rooms and on-par Westin service.  The location isn't the best if you're not a baseball fan (up along Washington Avenue would be more in the thick of things) but the MetroLink station certainly is convenient.  Speaking of that station, why isn't there a lower-level connection from the hotel to that platform?

I'm a bit disappointed that the character of this old warehouse has been preserved only on the exterior.  The rooms might as well be new construction, save for the high ceilings and generous windows.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: The structure of this DD is pretty cool looking. It's modern and this DD promotes it's green awareness. I've had service issues several times here though. The staff seems pretty stressed and makes mistakes pretty frequently. The drive-thru line can be a mess also, with two different entrances converging to a single speaker. During peak hours, the drive-thru line will loop around the parking lot, blocking parking spots, so good luck if you happened to park and go inside. It's not the best DD I've visited, and it's far from the worst. The donuts (when I get the right one), are always pretty good. That matters most, right?

The owner of Water Toy Car Wash is usually around in the afternoons.  Surprisingly, he is a real nice guy; helps with the machines if you need assistance.  Typical car wash prices range $6-$8, not bad at all.

Why two stars?  The car wash uses reclaimed water now.  I did not realize this until I had already paid for my car wash and was in the process of getting my car cleaned.  Immediately my air vents start smelling like rotten eggs.  I can understand wanting to save the environment, but no one wants their car to smell like rotten eggs!!!

Some of the best Italian food in Tampa!  I would go more often, but carbs seem to go straight to my hips so I can only occasionally indulge.  During my last visit I had the Caprese Salad and the Ravioli Bolognese - both delicious!  The dessert menu is divine... I love the tiramisu and creme brulee so I prefer to split the sampler which includes a trio of flourless chocolate cake, tiramisu and creme brulee.

Parking is a pain in Ybor, I recommend parking in the garage.  The half priced pasta from 4-7pm and $2 martinis ease the pain of paying for parking!

We enjoyed some tasty ice cream served up by a nice lady named Ann. She told us that the ice cream comes from an Amish community in... wait for it... Sarasota. Apparently, 20000 Amish folks live down there and crank out some delicious ice cream in their spare time! 

I don't think Amish folks use Yelp since it's technology-based and all but, nevertheless, I'll go with four stars. That's because there is no place to sit in this ice cream shop except a wooden bench out in the parking lot in the hot sun. We scarfed down our delicious ice cream in the car.

Jack & coke $10.55. Wow!

I should have just waited to get a $5 drink on the plane.

I was loured in by the fun collection of Gibson guitars throughout the little diner space at the end of Concourse C.  It was like a tiny 'hard rock' with a few signed Gibsons on display. They had a menu with sandwiches and salads and such. I didn't get any food though, I was only here for a drink. I wasn't excited by the beer selection, or the thought of having to use the facilities on the plane 10 minutes into the flight, so I ordered a cocktail that ultimately cost me $12, with tax & tip.

My own fault really.

We had a great mid-afternoon lunch here.  We liked everything we tried. We loved the overall design and feel. The decor was cool and classy, you can tell they put a lot into this old building.

Of the things we tried, my favorites were the Hawaiian roll, it was more like a spring roll, but filled with coconut fried shrimp, mango and spicy tuna, and, the Geisha Ceviche which was sort of a sashimi salad served in a  martini glass. There were too many raw onions in the ceviche, but they were easy enough to pick around.

Overall, we enjoyed the food, and the whole experience and would love to go back!

I love this place! A group of friends and I were looking for a late night place to grab something sweet and some locals recommended this place. After a trolley ride and wandering around, we finally made it. The environment is really comfortable with pictures of patrons on the bright walls. What makes this place special is the homemade and unique ice creams. If you can't decide, they will let you sample a bunch of flavors. You can even get half scoops. I came back several times during my stay in NOLA!

Here's the flavors I got:
-lavender honey (my fav)
-red velvet
-chocolate amaretto cheesecake
-almond toffee

Highly recommended!

We came here on a weekend and it was not that crowded. In fact we were the only ones there on a warm Saturday afternoon. It was just after lunch time too. That said, it was great because we got to sample a bunch of flavors and ultimately chose the dairy-free coconut fudge.

The ingredients were top notch and you could taste the quality. The inside was small but had a few places to sit. The service was great and I would recommend this place. I could see it getting a bit claustrophobic if there was a long line though.

This place is definitely on the pricey side, but it has presentation, local foods, and a very skilled chef. If you're willing to shell out for that kind of stuff, hit it up. Make a reservation first.

The highlight of the summer was a pizza with figs, goat cheese, arugala and balsalmic vinegrette. I liked that pizza so much, I tried to make it at home. The highlight of the fall is an amazing pumpkin soup. They bring warm bowls with a little piece of pumpkin bread and crystallized sugar in the center right to your table. Then, they pour the soup in front of you from beakers. It's a neat show. Even better, the soup is out of this world delicious.

I think this may be the WORST Subway I've ever been to. I had some sort of expectation because 1. It's downtown and 2. It's so close to Tulane health center but I've found wrong. The servers were downright nasty and paid more attention to the small child (really, for a child in the work place why does it take four people to dote on her?) than any of the customers. They acted as though they were doing you a favor (begrudgingly at that) by making you a lackluster sandwich. The overall prices are also higher than any of the Subways in the area... To do it all again, I wouldn't have.

I lived out in Ardmore years ago and vaguly recall dining here. . . from my Ardmore days, my sister my dad and I developed a pre-Christmas tradition. .  . we have a daddy-daughter shoppinjg day. . . 

So this year we had lunch at Plate.  It has a nice atmosphere, the food was good and the beer list was decent (but over priced).  I don't think I would go oiut of may way to go back but it is a nce alternative to the "cafes" that dominate Suburban Square.

Note- if you are shopping at SS this is the only place to get an alcoholic beverage.

Not as bad as I anticipated based on the reviews. I put in a bid on priceline and got a room for under $100 on a Friday night and loved it. Yes, it's not the "4 Star Hotel Experience" with free water and whatever else one may expect but it's still a nice hotel. I typically stay Hilton and this is on-par with their service, comfort, and amenities. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and we were able to get a room with a great view of the harbor. Overall a good experience, would recommend checking this location out.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The frozen yogurt at Sweet Cece's is not bad, but just not remarkable. The toppings selection helps make up for that somewhat. The prices are a little high, so don't pack your bowl too high if you have the munchies. You know what I mean, giggling college kids!

I think the majority of the buzz about Sweet Cece's comes from people being happy to have a lower guilt option than ice cream and more colorful, innovative model than dying national froyo chains. I have no complaints, but don't think it's remarkable either.

I've been to Shiki several times, starting soon after they opened. Shiki has a large menu of rolls and nice clean interior. Prices are reasonable. I've tried both their chef's specials and individual rolls. My experience is that if you're looking for rice, something cooked, and some seaweed, you'll enjoy Shiki. If you're looking for quality fish or a large variety of raw fish, you'll be disappointed. I don't think they have the volume of nigiri and sashimi eaters to focus on those types of sushi.

The service is friendly and good, and I've rarely had to wait to be seated or for service. For the location, I'll give it 3 stars.

Love the use of reclaimed wood. And the expansive concrete bar is rather impressive and you can't miss the fire-engine red espresso machine. 

Despite all the eye-candy when you walk in, there isn't much for seating or for comfort either.  

Where they lack in warmth for furniture they make-up in super friendly staff. Since they have no food to speak of, they were kind enough to let us bring in our goodies from Companion! Score. 

In short. Awesome vibe. Not much of a lounge. Killer staff and espresso. Win. Win!

Love Love Love Montecito Inn. What a perfect place to spend a weekend away. It's quaint and cute with so much personality. The staff is so friendly and accommodating. I loved the free teas on the main floor and the binder of nearby restaurants. They know how to make one's stay easy and comfortable. Not to mention the history! Charlie Chaplin's place and retreat of the celebrities. It just felt really cool staying there for a weekend getaway. 

Just one more thing to note: The location is perfect, right along the main street in town. We just stepped out and had a ton of things to do and look at. I want to go back!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: If you've been lucky enough to visit a Pinkberry, Fro-yo might seem  disappointing at first because they don't offer any fresh fruit as a topping, but they have a variety of frozen fruits, nuts, candy, cakes, and sauces as well as different flavors of yogurt that you can mix and match yourself. There are non-fat and low-fat varieties of yogurt but no non-dairy. The smallest cup size is quite large, and if you fill it all the way you'll pay at least $5. But if you keep your creation low on sugar you can create a filling and satisfying meal. I'll definitely be back.

$8 a sweater?? EIGHT dollars?? Would love to give this cleaners a higher rating, as the staff are friendly, they've been open in STL a long time, and they do good quality work. But I was absolutely flabbergasted when they told me what my total was: $32 for 4 regular, non-embellished sweaters. Sorry, but I don't have that kind of money to spend on dry cleaning. I have no idea what their other rates are as they are not posted anywhere inside (note to self: always ask what the price is before dropping off clothes). And they only take cash. I'm on a search for a cleaners that is more in my price range.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Stars for good location and outdoor seating. They're situated right at the most bumpin' part of Mass Ave, which is great. However, they might be leaning on that high point a little too heavily.

The food is just ok, which is fine considering that it's bar food. The drinks are reasonable but not cheap - also just eh. The service is good once the waiters figure out which of them is taking your table, and this process may take a while. 

They do have some good healthier options, which is nice, and domestic bottles can be had for 2-3 bucks, so I will definitely keep going for my patio fix during the summer.

We came here twice for the $9.99 breakfast buffet. It's a great way to start your day before a full day of skiing or snowboarding. They had quite a selection of food. Scrambled eggs, ham, sausage, biscuits and gravy, french toast, pancakes, fresh fruit, oatmeal, yogurt and granola, plain bagles and a selection of pastries.

The first day we went the service was pretty good. One of the wait staff offered to toast my bagel once I sat down. I had an orange juice and it had a very watered down taste to it.

The second day the service wasn't so great. No one offered to toast my bagel, but at least the orange juice tasted better, haha.

This was a fun place to grab lunch, especially if you need something on the quick and in a hurry. After much debate, we ordered the side by side t-rav and Bahn mi. Both delicious. But I think the Bahn was the winner for me, on a sight technicality that the ragu makes the ravioli chips soggy quickly. Maybe tighten up the sauce a tad, just my opinion, I don't really know how to fix that. Great flavors and enough toppings for each chip. Be sure to grab a delightful Ski beverage, too. I'm looking forward to trying other flavors!

We stayed here in the sort-of off season (early January) and from what I gathered from  locals we got a pretty good deal on our room (booked flight and room through priceline). It was a very generous size, had a view of the Alibi Room across the street, and the staff was friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking to stay in the French Quarter. Many awesome bars & restaurants were in walking distance.

Didn't get to enjoy the pool since we were there during the cold snap (it got down to 30 degrees while we were there) but it looked nice and we were close by!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: How did no one write a review about this? Tuesday night was my first time here- it was awesome.  Inside was nice for the area, the bartender was a cool older guy, pretty generous with  the pour.  great out door patio area with a large bar and TVs.  I had 2 double vodkas with soda, and a shot and a local bought me a shot on her way out the door that turned into 2.  I was feeling awesome when I left and my bill was like 13.50 or something awesomely ridiculous like that.  It made me appreciate being home from NYC.  I would def want to come back!

I came to this Bulk Barn mid afternoon and it wasn't very busy.  I came with items I had in mind and wasn't tempted beyond them even though it's easy to be.  The prices here can be a little more but you can find just about any item you need for baking or snacking. It's a great place to go before you go on a road trip to stock up for the kids' and adults' treats! They have a coupon that you can save $3 when you spend more than $10 which is easy to do.  Also, kudos to the cashiers who usually know the codes by memory!

Every time I shop at Superstore I am reminded why it's not my regular store to get groceries. Sunday afternoon and the produce section was busy, and bins empty including Roma tomatoes. Next on my list was coffee and I went and none left of the one we buy. Most of the time they don't have everything I'm looking for and was stopping in as my sister was doing some shopping. I did find a few other items that I needed or some I didn't need but got for a cheap price.
