They do have decent prices and I did get bonus PC points on one item so that made it better.

We came on a Saturday evening just before 8 and the restaurant wasn't very busy.  There was no line up but we had to wait a short time for our order to be taken.  Since we were getting take out, we sat in the waiting area for our order.  The rice bowl was ok except for some chewy meat.  The bento box was decent for the amount of food and there was a lot of beef with the rice.

This isn't the best place for sushi, rice bowl, or bento boxes but they do have a big menu to chose from and there are numerous locations that are easily accessible if you are in the mood for their food.

Looking for cheap booze prices? Come here! When I walked in, the first aisle in front of me was the beer and pop too.  They carry many of the more popular brands but the shelves seemed a little bare in spots.  It must be a Superstore thing.  At the back are the larger cases of beer and the prices are good.  They have room for more booze to sell but maybe they don't carry enough kinds or they were in the process of trying to keep the shelves and floors stocked.

If you can find what you are looking for, it will be a good price.  If you are looking for any speciality alcohol, you probably won't find it here.

We came here for breakfast before heading out to an event.  It was a Saturday morning and it wasn't very busy with one person in front of us and there was a lot of seating in the restaurant.  I used a coupon and had no issues with that d'uh look that sometimes I get when using a coupon.  The food was ready pretty quickly too which was great.

With McDonald's you never know how clean and comfortable the seating will be.  But the tables I observed were clean and the booth we sat at was the same.  We had our breakfast sandwiches and made our way out.  This is a good McDonald's stop on the way to and from somewhere.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: I had never heard of this place until a colleague suggested we go.  I was a little leary as the entrance is in the alley but when we went in, it was decent decor.  I decided on the bento box which came with soup, chicken teriyaki, tempura, and sushi.  Compared to other places, it was average.  I found the chicken to be a bit bland and sauced up.  The tempera pieces were smaller than other restaurants.  But the sushi did taste fresh and good.  For $10, it was a decent meal and the server was attentive.  If I were in the area and craving Japanese food, I would try it again but I would not make a special trip there.

I've been to this McDonald's a few times now on the way home from a concert because that's what we sometimes do, grab a midnight snack after a night of rocking to music.  I go in and there weren't any customers in front of me and the staff is ready to take my order.  They're efficient and friendly and I'm able to use any coupon from the app easily.  

The drink area can be a bit messy but there are napkins nearby to wipe any spills.  Last time we got food to go and had to ask for ketchup but most of the time ketchup and napkins are in the bag.  It's McDonald's, you know what the food you'll get and it somehow tastes better late at night!
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
This place is just the worst. The last time I tried to come here, I was denied service because they were 'too busy'... TWO CUSTOMERS.... perhaps just tell me it'll be a few to wait, rather than make me uncomfortable and tell me you're too busy for me!!! So here I am, months later, on a weekday... figured I'd give them another go because it's cheap. The legit SAME THING JUST HAPPENED. 2 customers. WE ARE TOO BUSY. 

OK BYE. 
Don't waste your time... they aren't very good, and they are ridiculously rude to boot.

Superb Cleaners is, well, SUPERB!

Upon first moving to Avon in April, we started using Tuchman.  Well, sure they do a fine job, but WHY PAY MORE? 

When Superb opened, we gave them a shot and haven't turned back.

They do great cleaning, have friendly service, very reasonable prices and they turn clothes around quickly.  We have had dresses, blouses, business shirts, jackets and pants all handled by Superb.  Everything from inexpensive clothing to Charles Tyrwhitt to Dolce and Gabbana.

You can take all of your clothing here and feel really good about it!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
After a few years of coming here now, we've seen the service slip and the price increase.

The food is still really good, don't get me wrong.  The service is spotty, especially if they are very busy.  

Recently, we purposely ordered sushi rolls well before our entrees, so we could enjoy them.  We were pressed to order and ended up being rushed through soup and salad to have everything show up on the table at once.  Not a huge issue, but not what we were looking for.

The last couple of times we've been here it seems that the overall check has been about $30 higher than it had been previously.

My experience here last night was fine... even though the power in the area failed between 10pm and 11pm!

The style of the place is very Crate and Barrel-ish, save for the standard glass tumblers you find in hotels everywhere.

The location is also far enough off the highway to offer some quiet.
The airport is 5 miles away... so if they can the an airport location... well...
And, having stayed all over this area, at $100 you can't do better. Sorry. This is as good as it gets for $100. Some people just don't get out too often and then expect way too much? Pesky leisure travelers!!! : )
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Deceptive practices. Bad customer service from shop manager. These guys completed brake service on my car and the shop manager flat out lied about me needing tires, stating "you barely have tread on three of the tires".  The tires are barely 13 months old. I know because I bought them 13 months ago from Firestone in Chicago and have only put about 5,000 miles on them due to the pandemic. I had my brother in law call and they conveniently changed their tune. If it wasn't an emergency and I didn't have to travel the next day I NEVER would have left my car with them. If you can, go elsewhere. Happy Thanksgiving.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: I have been to Love's several times, especially since I live only a few miles away. I have always had a great meal and excellent service. I really love the eclectic decor and the funky vibe. On my first visit, I sampled several items including shrimp and grits (to die for), fried chicken (best I have had in Tampa Bay), ribs and my favorite menu item, peanut butter stuffed jalapeno poppers. The bartenders at Love's are some of the best in town. Be sure and try their all you can eat Sunday brunch, it's delish!

Had my bangs cut here a while back. The hairdresser went against my wishes and when I was about to ask her not to cut my bangs so far she got a bit defensive. I was too scared to complain. Result. My bangs start at the back of my head and everyone says it looks horrible. Other than that....cute salon. I was the only person in there. She was the only hair dresser there at the time. SO I cant really comment on anything other than my haircut. 
Was desperately looking for a salon to call home but this won't be it.

What a great hotel! We usually stay in the quarter, but this is just far enough to be away from the madness and just close enough that you can still walk to anywhere you'd want to go.  For much less than what we normally pay, we got a room about 3 times the size with a sitting area and kitchen. Our stay was very comfortable, and the staff was very accommodating (they even held our beer for us in the employee fridge after we'd checked out!). This is a great option for visiting New Orleans if you aren't there just to party and dead set on staying in the heart of the partying. We'll definitely be returning.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Dining at Bazil's is a little bit like a trip back in time.  Lights dimmed, faus Tiffany lamps, waiters running around all dressed in black.  It's a real treat. 

We came back after a few years absence, and found nothing had changed. The food is still very good, not perfect mind you, but just really very good.

We made reservations, which is something I would encourage you to do. I'm sure the wait wouldn't be too long, but every table is spoken for, so why take the chance.

Both their pasta and chicken dishes are our favorite. If you have a chance, sit in the bar area and enjoy life's characters. 

Enjoy!

The Dungeon.  Wow.  A "vampire bar" apparently, but i have yet to be bitten there.
Three different rooms, one in the front, one in the back-probably the orignal dungeon area, and then one up stairs that opens late and rarely.

Cool ambiance, check it out for a bit, it's probably exactly what you'd expect, it's pretty rad.  GOTTA check out the "Midnight Potion" for $4.  It's Everclear & Grape Kool Aid and it's amaaaziiiing.  It will mess you up, dude.  And it's yummy!  Careful, tho.  it sneaks up on you, just like a vampire in the night.

It's hard for me to believe that I did not post a review about this as I have stayed here at least three times. It is so handy being right by the airport and when I say right by the airport I mean it is the last driveway before you enter the airport. The beds are the comfiest you'll ever find and the pillows are soft and comfy too. My wife loves this place and sometimes I think she wants one of these kind of beds at our house. Her sister said I just want to move in. The staff is nice the rates are incredible and what more could a guy ask for. When I come through Tucson this is where I stay
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Ill keep this fast and simple. I love dunkin because i can get a good toasted bagel anytime of day with a delish side of their hashbrowns (ohhh so tasty). This spot it pretty close to my home its literally next to Hooters which i love as well. The only thing i would say is that where its set up its a bit of a pain. I say this because people coming in from the main streets (gandy or Manhattan) that are going into the drive thru literally block the rest of the parking lot. The drive thru goes a bit slow and wraps around to the entrances from the on coming streets. Thats the only down fall other then that very friendly and pretty fast inside.

My review from last year is no longer enough. Shinju might be my favorite place to go, in the city. It is quiet and friendly.  

While the service can sometimes feel a little slow, it's in actuality just un-rushed.  The sushi is delightful (assuming you like fusion rolls) and always presented well. 

There are some places that breed hostility.  You know, those restaurants you frequent when you're fighting with your significant other.  Shinju is the exact opposite of those. I have never had a bad experience or a bad time, here. I don't think it's possible to be unhappy in this tiny byo.

For one thing the lobby of club quarters hides ALL of it's flaws. The moody bitchy concierge. The small rooms with tiny bathrooms. And! tiny hallways. We stayed in one of the rooms behind the customer service desk behind the door that says EXIT. (Yes! there are actual rooms there.)

It's very convenient in location and for what we paid we also got a kitchenette, which came in handy, and a window! (not like another yelper). It was comfortable for the 3 nights we stayed.

Overall: It's appeal is something like 5 stars but the customer service is more like a quality inn. No bueno.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Being a former Gold's Gym member, this place is just great.  It's got a "lived-in" feel to it, and that's what I like.

I appreciate the free towels.

Yes, they do need to perform maintenance on their cardio equipment.
Yes, they seem to have just a jumble of equipment that's been collected (but at least it's organized by muscle group).

But I love it.  It has character.
Plus, they have no binding contract (like frickin' Bally's and Gold's), and the monthly price ain't bad, either.

If you ever need to leave, just give them a heads up and there's no problem.  If you ever come back, it's as easy as saying, "I'd like to come back."

Great place.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
The [gf] and I went here for lunch one day and found it to be a little lacking in originality. Seeing that the outside was very posh, and the insides are nice too; we expected a little more excitement in our meal. I had the burrito which was good enough but could have used a little more finesse in the presentation. There was also a lot of people with kids there that day, which I have no issue with - but it makes the place a little less intimate and exclusive when people are letting their kids run around all over the place. 

I am sure this restaurant has wonderful late night dinner but lunch didn't light a fire for me or my companion.

Decently priced, well-located, friendly staff.  Not ritzy or anything, but I didn't have any problems with noise or cleanliness.  The water dispenser in the hallways with free bottles was a nice amenity.

The biggest problem was the elevator situation though.  There was only one working at the time (I hope this has been fixed by now), and it took forever to catch it in the morning and evening.  

I live in Philly now so I don't think I'll need to come back here for a while, but I'd definitely recommend it to visiting friends (if for some reason I can't fit them into my place that is).
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This place is great - it would have gotten 5 stars if it weren't so hard to sit, if they weren't closed Saturday lunch and all day Sunday, and if they delivered outside Rittenhouse.

The sushi is great - the special is a great way to get people in the door, as we got in and saw the rest of the rolls and were sold. The special is a good deal but the rolls are small with more rice and less fish. Still, I'd order it alongside the specialty rolls.

The tuna dumpling is especially nice - thin pounded tuna wrapped around avocado. The texture (or lack thereof) was a but off but they're really good. I'd totally go back.

Sushi in the Plaquemines?  Yeah, it is there.  This would be a 4-star review if their prices were not as steep.

Reasons to go:  
1)  Clean store.  In this area, this will always be a reason to go if it is applicable.
2)  Food.  Not to bad on the rolls but I am comparing them to San Diego standards.

Reasons to avoid:
1)  Parking.  You are in the same lot with a popular pizza place as well as other successful businesses.
2)  Pricey.  It is not terrible, but the food is overpriced for what you pay for.
3)  Location.  It is next door to a place that sells good pizza... hard competition.

Nothing really too exciting about the bar area in my opinion.  It's functional and it's probably a quick and easy staple for lunch.  I just wasn't overly impressed as it looked like it hadn't been updated in quite some time.

I was greeted with a quasi polite server who didn't really project politeness but I know people have bad days and that's ok.  I ordered a ceasar salad with grilled chicken and it was fine.

I think this place probably use to be a top notch place but overtime it's lost is allure.  That's just my take on it.

I wish I was more impressed.  It was just fine.  I loved the location because it's literally across the street from the Arch but other than that I wasn't impressed.  Staff was very nice during check in and check out but there was just no WOW factor to the place.

Rooms were kept clean daily by the staff without any issue.  The rooms are refreshed but my biggest gripe, oddly enough, was the door hardware.  Let me explain.  The door handles on the inside didn't turn.  So when you shut the door it made for a very large SLAM sound.  That being said, I heard that all night long, ugh.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I really like Philly Car Share 1) as plan B for when my car isn't working and 2) using their pickups when hauling that sofa I purchased on Craig's List home.   It also rocks that they pay for gas, insurance, and maintenance.  There is a PCS right on my block but it is usually reserved but they have lots of locations so it is easy to reserve a vehicle at the last minute.  Many people do not realize that PCS is a non-profit, unlike Zip Car.  Plus my neighbor Larry Shaeffer is a co-founder of the organization which endears me to them even more.

The food was nice. I actually ate here two nights in a row, as I was in town for a conference. The Fettuccini Quattro Formaggi was a little too rich, too big and lacking a side. Second night Sicilian Strip Steak was good, nothing special. Nothing special but I would eat there again.

Now for the bar tender. He was horribly rude to all of us. I would never sit at their bar again. Trainwreck Saloon was a much better fit, as they were friendly. He treated us like we were children and the average age was 55 or higher. He complained that it was late, 8:00; he was understaffed and was so unwelcoming we left all 25 of us.

Truly as good as it gets. 
When I brought my Altima to GR on a Friday, Rick listened to me describe the problems I had been having with it and immediately started diagnosing it based on his experience. About two hours later, he called to tell me that his initial diagnosis was confirmed by the computer codes.  He assured me that he'd have the job finished on Monday.  True to his word, Rick called me mid-day on Monday to let me know my car was ready. Everything that had my concerned had been addressed. Fast, accurate, and great work!

They seemed honest with what needed to be done on the car and also supplied a $25 discount on services. One of the male employees was nice. However one of the female employees seemed not to be fully engaged. After $440 spent and waiting for over two hours, they failed to give me a print out read of my alignment. I had to wait an additional hour. Furthermore, they said they made an appointment for me yesterday for today at 1pm. They never did. However I did bring my car in at 12:50pm and they were able to start working on it at about 1:15pm.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Stopped here over the weekend. Not a good choice. 

Unfortunately, the food was not very good at all. Most of it looked like it had been sitting out for hours and had a film over it. I wanted to gag but was with a friend who will eat anything, so I kept my comments to myself. 

Thank goodness they had a salad bar so I could at least eat that, but that didn't really do much for me either, just iceberg and store bought stuff. 

They did have a cookie kind of dessert with powdered sugar all over it which was very good.

Tony's is my all time FAVORITE restaurant. I love being catered to with excellent food and service. I have been here 3 times since I moved to STL many years ago. I love everything about this place. In their old building they would go up the stairs backward, I always thought that was so cool. The wait staff is so attentive and the fact that everything is done table side is fun.

I wish I could go here more often, it is a pretty upscale place and costs big bucks to eat here. Tony's is a special place for special occasions, at least for me.

I really wanted to like this place, i really did. IMHO, the food was below average. I had the filled chicken breast and my friend had steak. The steak was to be med rare and came out well done!  Was sent back and came back out cooked medium.

 My chicken was OK but needed to be seasoned at the table. The clam chowder was thin and runny,  with lots of potatoes and very little clam, also pretty tasteless. The pot stickers had a very strong peanut flavor and the pork was under cooked. Service was slow. Don't think I'll be back anytime soon.

When people ask me what Nomad is like, I say "sort of like the bar in the Overlook Hotel from The Shining".  Well, that is without Jack Nicholson and Lloyd.

But there's something about Nomad that feels classic, like it's been here before.  The vibe, that amazing bar, the expert staff and those delicious cold drafts and perfectly created drinks.  Why would you ever want to leave?

I also had the chance to play a gig at Nomad, and the vibe was crazy, with folks from various walks of life making Nomad a great melting pot of fun.

I made my first stop to Kyoto today.  Usually I don't care about prices considering my dining choice, but for Kennett Square I thought the prices were up a little too high here.  Yikes.  My and my lunch buddy wound up forking over $80 for lunch?

Now, let's get to the food.  The quality of the sushi and sashimi was very good.  My buddy found White Tuna, which he said he never finds on the East Coast often.  I tried a piece and it was delicious.  Some of my staples, Tamago, Unagi and Spicy Tuna were prepared very well and fresh.

Service was good, but ouch, I'm still smarting a bit from that bill.

Met my college roomie here for lunch several weeks ago. We typically meet in this little riverfront section to have lunch, and we usually go to Iron Hill, but decided to branch out this time, and Timothy's had crab dip so and wasn't Joe's Crab Shack, so it won.

The crab dip was pretty good, as was the chips and dip they bring out. We both ordered crab cakes (even though I don't really believe in ordering crab cakes not in Maryland, Delaware usually gets a pass) and it was a poor choice. Dry, minimal flavor. Good fries, though.

Outside seating looked nice but was full.

I'll stick with Iron Hill.

You wouldn't believe how hard it was to find out the name of this establishment.  As far as I can tell, they did/do not advertise at all.  Which is sad, because I think it could have done really well this summer.  I'm worried it will have the same fate as Friendly's, Nelly Bly's, and all the other ice cream/frozen yogurt places that have tried to make it Downtown....

Anyway, this is just your standard, no frills scoop shoop.  The girl behind the counter was kind enough to let me read the actual tub to see if the flavor I wanted was gluten free.  I don't remember what I got, but it was yummy!

Please check it out and support local businesses!

Came to Makiman yesterday with a livingsocial deal. I have to say my experience this time was much better.  We got the McNabb roll, which was surprisingly twice the size as the one we got during my last visit. Perhaps it was a different sushi chef (or maybe they listened to their yelp reviews?! :)) Regardless, the rolls here were very filling this time. I also tried the salmon avocado roll and the white tuna roll, both of which were fresh and sizable. I hope these well sized rolls remain; I'll definitely be back!

The service was again very good.

The space is great for mingling and chatting up with friends. there are never enough bartenders here, and everyone is constantly waiting to get the attention of bartenders. ive been here once for happy hour in the summer, and was not happy with the constant waiting!  and ive been another time after my friends spam my email box with emails titled "free drinks at public house!!"  But upon arrival, getting the attention of a bartender is so tedious that it really isn't worth your time. ridiculous wait times seem like a part of the drinking experience at public house... i can pay for my own drinks and not waste my time. thanks.

Hmm, I've had four star visits here before but my last visit was a one or two star.  Generally I like the place because it's kind of tucked away and they have that recessed room down below in the back, which I really like in the winter, it's very snug and comfortable.  However, the last time I was there, I walked in and was immediately assaulted with the smell of a backed up sewer and a bunch of older, bead-clad tourists dancing to Night Fever.  I'm not making that up, in fact, the song has been seared in my head since then.  I'll be back for another go but I will wait until the weather is cool and I feel like being somewhere cozy.

I love going to Jason to get my haircut! He listens, will recommend what looks best with you features, and I am always happy with the end result. I would definitely recommend this salon to family and friends--and the pricing is phenomenal!

My mom and I use to get our haircut in Chinatown, but when Jason opened his own salon on on Washington Ave, we decided to follow him! Now, unlike Chinatown, we no longer have to pay for parking since the street parking and large asian grocery store across the street always have spaces available.

Came here for a Friday night dinner at 10pm so pretty late. Service was very friendly and came by with three meatballs they said we're complimentary because it was our first time here. I did caveat I had been here before but my husband's first time. When we got the bill they had charged us for the meatballs! A bit disappointing since the meatballs weren't great and cost $6 but it was the holidays so we didn't say anything. The burrata was really good and the food was good for a quick middle ground Italian spot. I would've rated 4 stars if not for the meatball trickery.

I have ordered delivery from here quite a few times and am usually pleased with the timing of the delivery and quality of the food. 

There pizza is not bad, compared to most pizza joints in Philly their pizza is a lot better. They also have 'Rustic Sandwiches' on their menu that are pretty solid. I have had both the buffalo chicken and chicken ceaser sandwiches and both were very good, came with fries and were under $7.00. 

They also have curly fries, which are freaking awesome.

Overall, its a solid delivery pizza joint that is reasonably priced. If you are looking for a cheap night in then def give this place a try.

Gio's is a new addition to the Maple Glen Shopping center and is owned by the same people that run the Jarrettown Hotel.

As stated in other reviews their Pizza is THIN crust. (I haven't tried the pizza yet)  On this visit my girlfriend and I split a Grilled Chicken Panini with honey mustand and Caeser salad.  The salad was a good size for $5.95 and the Panini was tasty.  The bread was fresh and the chicken was very moist.

Although Gio's was clean and reasonably priced they didn't have anything that makes me want to make a special trip to go there.

I gave Deterra another shot this past weekend.  We sat outside near the fire place.
I still stand by my first review.  This place is just way over priced for what you get.  I tried the braised short ribs.  The portion was very small for $28 and it was just above average in flavor.

One of the girls in my group had a plain thin crust pizza.  For $14 it was small and I would never get pizza here over one of the local pizza joints.

I really want to like this place.  The decor is fantastic!  I can't say that I will stop in again unless its just for a drink.

I really like this place and have been here a hand full of times. Its just that this one time I went and got shrimp tempura there they tried to pass off soggy day old par fried shrimp on me. I've worked in sushi restaurants before so I knew it the moment I saw it and tasted it. At least re-fry it? Nothing worse than cold un-crispy shrimp tempura. The rest of the specialty rolls I've had there are great I just hate when restaurants try to pass shit off on the guests. Seats only 8 people by the way if you go in there thinking you may get a spot you may be walking right back out the front door once you see the bar is full.

Changed my review since Zing completely changed their menu and mostly got rid of the tapas style dining and those loved tamales and so many others! Boooo! Service was ok. The portions are smaller for the price too. 
Previous review:
I love Zing! Great place for a large or small group! Sharing is the best part of the experience. Contemporary atmosphere and great service! 
Pineapple tamales are excellent and then we tried almost everything on the menu!! mmmmm SO GOOD! Lovely view inside or outside of downtown Indy!

My whole family enjoys this place.  It is always packed, so I recommend getting a reservation even if you are going within the hour.  That little trick kept us from being the poor souls sitting in the corner they call the waiting area. People get all pouty sitting there watchin others eat delicious sushi made fresh and still other people are being entertained by corny hibachi chefs. Watch out for the fire man!  (inside joke) Anyway, this hands down the best sushi and hibachi in the area there.  P.s. It is very tough to find a spot to park when it's ultra busy.

Pros:
-Convenient location
-Decent prices (on a lot of items, but not everything!)
-Friendly employees

I would never go out of my way to shop at this Piggly Wiggly, but when I'm in the area and need to pick up a few things, this is where I head.

Cons:
-Every time I walk in, there is a distinct, strange smell. I can't really describe what it is, but I know it doesn't smell very good.

-The store is pretty dark and dingy, and I get a little creeped out shopping there at night.

-Not a full grocery store selection. They didn't have fresh basil in the produce area, and their selection of frozen items isn't extensive.

It was ladies night, celebrating a birthday, so we selected a new to us restaurant within walking distance from our first stop at Tastings.  The waiter shared the specials, reeling off a whole lot of info... offering his honest opinions, which we all appreciated greatly.  We started with calamari which was good, but lacking salt.  The special was seafood with fresh made pasta.  I hear it was very flavorful, but I had the chicken penne with artichoke hearts and capers. Overall, a nice experience, but no wow factor, given the bill received.

My 'go to' dinner when I'm not in the mood to cook. I appreciate that you can send your order early, though I've never done it myself. I like the option to have a sandwich made as a salad if you'd like. 

If you sign up for text messages, you'll receive coupon offers. We use them all the time and appreciate any savings provided since they no longer doing Subway cards. They're also running $4.99 footlong specials right now on select subs. My daughter's favorite is the Black Forest Ham, which is on the list. 

Free cookie with purchase on Tuesdays!

The cauliflower rolls were SPOT ON!!!!!I had tried another place for dinner, it was really bad....so I wanted some good food! Pizza Delicious lived up to their name!!!!! But more than just delicious, it was totally unique!!! I loved that it was a guilty pleasure, but some what healthy!!!! I woke up the next day still thinking about the pizza roll from the night before, and wanted to make sure the evenings festivities had not swayed my vote. So, I warmed up another cauliflower roll and upon further inspection ******drum roll*** that roll is in fact DELICIOUS!!

Take your business elsewhere.  They were 30 minutes late picking me up and when I talked to the auto body receptionist about it, she said "They're probably short staffed because the last driver they sent over got arrested in our parking lot the other day".  Awesome!

This branch told me that my reservation wasn't until next week.. but I double checked with the branch that sent it over and they had the right dates on it.

Late for work and sporting a Hyundai Sonata with 22,000 miles on it.  Returning it tonight and taking my business to National.

Pros: Clean, bright store.  Friendly employees.  Fast turnaround on a moderately busy summer evening.

Cons: It was FREEZING inside and there are no tables outside.  Yeah, I'm a weather wuss but it ruins my ice cream experience when I'm already shivering.  Plus it was a tad on the expensive side.  I shared a large brownie sundae and was expecting a tower of deliciousness for $7.59.  Instead we were handed a large glass bowl that was only about half full.  

For the money, I'm probably more inclined to head to coldstone down the road unless I'm there to catch a movie.

Born and raised as a native southern Californian, my bar for delicious food was already set high.  However, as an honorary St. Louisan for four years (and starving college student), I was always on the lookout for great food at an average price.  Imo's was that spot! Ever had provel cheese? Neither did I...until I was introduced to Imo's thin crust-style pizza.  Breaking away from the norm of triangular cut slices, Imo's slices their pie in squares! 

The cheese is melted to perfection! You have to order one of their pizzas! To appreciate it, start off with a cheese pizza (if you're a college student they'll deliver it for $5!).

I finally went back and tried the yogurt again. This time I stuck to the original since I wasn't allowed to try too many flavors (I still don't like them for that!)

That being said, I did enjoy the original. It tasted similar to Pinkberry which made me happy. 

I love that they go by weighted amounts instead of sizes, which works out best for us who can't eat a lot anyway, or shouldn't have to pay for a large size when you only want a little.

Overall, I would go here if I was seriously craving frozen yogurt. I haven't been to any others in Saint Louis but for now, this satisfies the sweet and tart tooth just fine.

This is my neighborhood coffee shop, and man do I love it.  I was super excited to find out that Hubbard & Cravens is a local coffee company.  Their roasting facility is off 46th.

The coffee here is way less acidic than Starbucks so I can drink it all day long :)

I especially love the Carmilla Latte.  YUM YUM.

They also carry a variety of vegan and regular snacks, sandwiches, chocolate, etc.  I love that they carry Endangered Species chocolate which is also local to Indy.

And of course, free wi-fi so you can hang out, update Yelp and drink your latte.

The downstairs sister to Euphoria, I honestly prefer Creation Cafe. My only beef was that our menus (late late in the evening) didn't seem to contain the entree selections, so we ordered appetizers as our meal. Our BOGO coupon for entrees wasn't accepted. Grrr. Oh well. Maybe it's a ploy to ensure our return. And we probably will.

I ordered the chips with black bean salsa which was fantastic. I also had the quesadilla, and my friend ordered the nachos. Everything was delicious. The service was decent - even considering I arrived about 20 minutes prior to closing.

Okay, I'm rescinding my previous reivew.  How can this place have gone completely 180 in 9 months?  Woah.

Now Lulu's is a sushi/Asian fusion restaurant.  I'm not sure I get it.

We ordered the edamame, dumplings, squid salad, mackarel, King roll and a chicken teriyaki bento box.

Dumplings tasted oddly fishy.  Aren't they supposed to be ground pork?

They were out of the squid salad.

The mackarel was limp and kinda gross.

My friend found her roll inedible.

Oh, and we waited 45 minutes after ordering to receive this debacle - and WE WERE THE ONLY ONES THERE.

I'm never, EVER going back.

I really really really wanted to love this place.  It's SUPER close to my house, and convenience is my #1 consideration in a supermarket.

However, I found the prices quite high.  I suppose that being a small store, they probably have to have higher prices to keep all their people employed.  Still, when the Kroger isn't too much further away, and quite a bit cheaper on all my staple items, it's tough.

Safeway does have a better selection than the Kroger in Broad Ripple (which is tiny but CUTE).

I think this will probably be my emergency last minute grocery, and I'll make the trip to Kroger for everything else.

I had high high hopes for Dunkin Donuts.  Some friends of mine from the East Coast SWEAR by this place.

We stopped in there a couple Saturdays ago to pick up a dozen donuts for a group meeting.  We also wanted a jug of coffee.

The line was out the door.  The service at the counter was slow.  They didn't have enough coffee made to fill our jug.  We ended up waiting for almost 20 minutes before we had our order and could go.

And honestly, nothing was that great.  The donuts were average, the coffee was average.  And it was expensive!  It was around $30 for a dozen donuts, a box of coffee, and 2 large coffees.  Sheesh!

#1 or #2 for most authentic Chinese food in Nashville. Complementary soup was large portion when we did family style for 6 people. Sautéed sweet tea leaves and bok choi was tasty and delicious. Pork belly was a great cut of meat and the fat was buttery smooth. The chitlins with tofu could have used a little more spiciness but overall was well done. Bubble tea is also available and good.The roast duck should be avoided; overcooked and dry. Also more bone than meat/fat combination.

Overall, the food is excellent for the reasonable prices. I hope they keep it up.

Happy hour 4-7  rolls are $5-7
And there's about 7 rolls to choose from and happy hour drinks are American beer and sake only
This place was recommended to me by a coworker for happy hour ...but there was really not a true happy hour ..not like  I'm used to anyway . 
Service was slow ... One server for like a whole side of the place. Not her fault. But just saying. 
Sushi was decent at most. Tried. It. Still going back to soho sushi . Their happy hour has More to offer especially Japanese beer. 
Btw the calamari. Do not order. It's soggy and fatty . Not worth it.

Crowne Plaza Tampa is not a bad choice.  The room is spacious enough, clean, has a nice flooring.  They have a big shower stall.  The water system can be a bit noisy tho.  You gotta be careful with the door.  It is cheaply made and shuts really loud and could wake up the whole neighbor, if you don't try to close the door very slowly all the way.  There is no mini fridge and that was a bit of disappointment.  This place is not gonna wow you but if you are looking for a clean hotel around $100-140, then this place will do just fine.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I have never eaten at a Macaroni Grill so I came here for lunch when I was in the area.  The first impression was good.  Their server was polite and the interior was very classy.

However, the food was just terrible.  I ordered an alfredo pasta and my husband ordered some grilled shrimp on skewers.  My pasta was very bland and my husband meal was completely burned.  It seemed like the chef had no idea what he was doing.  

Maybe the food was so terrible because of the chef they had at the time of my visit.  I have no idea because this was my first time at a Macaroni Grill and I will never know.

I'm going to give this place four stars because it's here.  In Nashville.  I'm so glad that someone decided to go out on a limb and offer frozen yogurt that is similar to Pinkberry/Red Mango.  It's a gamble, but I think they'll do well.
The yogurt selections are plentiful and most are quite yummy.  The toppings are all fresh and delicious.  The environment is clean and inviting.
Sure, it might be pricier than Yogurt Oasis, but I wouldn't even think about setting foot back in Yogurt Oasis after having been there once and not inspired at all to purchase.  Krave rocks!  I will be back here often!!

I'd give Ralph's two stars for the food alone, but the atmosphere definitely brings it up to three.  As others have noted, it's full of history (it was founded in 1900; the menu claims that Frank Sinatra, Teddy Roosevelt, and many other notables have dined there) and it has a nice old-school Italian American feel.  The food arrived with amazing speed.  I had the gnocchi with marinara sauce; it was decent, but nothing special.  The house Chianti was pretty good; the coffee was ok.  It's not a bad spot, but I'd recommend Dante & Luigi's for the same historic and nostalgic value and far superior food.

Back home in LA, there's an establishment like Fro-yo on almost every corner. That being said, Fro-Yo does a pretty good job of being what it says it is. They have a nice variety of flavors (especially tart flavors) and they have peanut butter! 

The toppings are generally good, but I had to knock down this rating to only 3 stars because they never have raspberries! Maybe they will during summer, but it's the biggest bummer.

Also, their water cups are those baby dixie shot glasses. Barely enough for one sip.

I'm going to be living extremely close to Fro-Yo soon and I will probably be stopping by every day in the summer/fall to cool off :)

Great for airport food. The Neely's BBQ on the menu are same price as from takeout counter next door. Some people report having problems with wait time for food, but my half rack of ribs was out in the 10-15 minutes waitress estimated. Service was also fast and I was able to get check and pay quickly to catch my flight.

Ribs were OK and sides of mac-n-cheese, onion rings, and green beans were very good. Huge quantity and corn bread as well. I really couldn't finish so I'd suggest an appetizer and sharing a plate...

I DENOUNCE MY DUKEDOM FROM THIS JOKE OF A PUB.

Being that I apparently have two eyes, a mouth and a somewhat functioning brain... I can tell you from experience that this place only stays alive due to it's proximity to the Hilton Hotel (it is attached to).

The drinks are unbelievably weak and overpriced.
The service leaves much to be desired (though I am sure they try hard).
The food is greasy, bland and leaves me OTA (On the Toilet & Angry).

...I will fight it but sadly I am sure I will return due to convenience and long days :(

SOLID!!! 

I used to come here with my friends when we would ditch class in Highschool to go do illegal things and eat Cubans to cure the munchies.

SOLID!!!

Over the years the prices have jumped a little but the cubans are still crazy cheap. This place is authentic. Don't be scared. I think a cuban or turkey cuban will run you about $3. The bread is the best in the area..super buttery and flaky.

Call in your order so you dont have to wait. The crowd is mostly ethnic and they speak little english...thats how you know you found da spot.

FYI...CASH ONLY!

Let me start by saying that I am a Hilton Member and have been for years.

With that being said, I recently had a conference at the STL Renaissance Grand Hotel. (Essentially a Marriott location) 

The PROS:
The rooms were very comfortable and clean.
The Lobby and bar area was very inviting.
A full Starbucks off the lobby area.

The CONS:
Undergoing construction that was extremely loud at all hours.
Check-in was a complete nightmare. Both the wait for my room as well as the wait in line was totally unacceptable.

With all things considered, not a totally unbearable experience but something I will take into consideration when back in STL.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Any time we go downtown for a concert, or to entertain out-of-towners on 2nd/Lower Broad, we stop by Ichiban.  We joke that it feels like a bento-box inside - lots of little compartments on the ceiling, and the booths are sort of like little compartments or cubbies.

The sushi is always good; nothing too creative but it's all solid.  BEST veggie tempura in town.  We hit up the early bird special sometimes, can't remember the times but I believe I remember a shrimp tempura dish.  We always get great service here too!

I love roast duck. i do, i really really do.  So when i get a craving? this is where i go.  Fried wontons or dumplings to start then roast duck noodle soup.  The salt and pepper squid is good here too.  It's always packed but waits aren't too long.

Walk in, hold up however many fingers match your party size and hope they lead you on back.

It's cheap, fast and good.  My bf is chinese and he wasn't a fan, saying how chinese food in nyc is much much better but hey...i like it!! so i go.  Oh ya, their mango smoothies are DELICIOUS!!  i think once i got 2 (bad idea) but yes...GOOD.

definately not  a date spot, but if you want some warm food late at night, this wasn't too bad.  Good deal overall. Pick your pasta, pick your sauce, pick your side, pick your drink.  Lots to mix and match.  My hubby really like the Chicken Parmasean.  The lasagna was really cheesy that could have been melted a bit more. Cesar side ~ mediocre. I was definately turned off by the homelss guy that walked in and was staring at our food and grumbling angrily at us.  The employees must be used to it becuase they didn't come to our aid.

So, Melt is in a new location on Cherokee now.  Like their last space, it has a very relaxing vibe, much more so than most other breakfast spots in town.  They specialize in waffles, and although waffles aren't typically my thing, these aren't your typical waffles.  They offer both sweet and savory waffles.  And by savory, I mean options like brisket, bleu cheese, and caramelized onion waffles.  What a fine way to start the day!  They also have great coffee, chill tunes, pinball machines, and an attentive and outgoing waitstaff.  Oh, and adult beverages! Do yourself a favor and order a bloody mary.  It may be the best in the city.

Jacki's family basically worships this place and I have come to enjoy it quite a bit. Cannot rate anything but the pizza, because as I am never the payor I eat what is brought to the table and that is always pepperoni pizza. I have had a couple bites of some chicken tenders when Jacki's sister didn't finish them, a couple curly fries, and the garlic cheese bread. All seemed fine to me. I like the pizza a lot and wish I knew why the guy that just gave it such a bad review did so.

I am excited next time I go to get a salad with the Mayfair dressing and I have always wanted to order something else so we'll see if I am feeling bold next we go...

I recently went to a banquet in their ballroom, which was pretty nice.  The room was a great size for a medium to slightly large group of individuals. Great large staff to accommodate everyone. The food was actually good. I didn't have high hopes. They had a great fish and chicken plate and wonderful hot chocolate cake dessert. The location was pretty easy to find and accessible; right across from The Convention Center. Parking was good for me, but I can see it being a problem in the week or when large groups are visiting.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Went to a event here today, what a fabulous place. Its a small two-story hotel on Esplanade. So cute. Refreshing colors. The front has a wonderful lawn, pretty flowers, lots of seating. There is even a little fake cat sitting out front, that absolutely terrified me. 

The backyard area was wonderful! It was huge little ponds and stands all over! Great setup for parties and weddings during good weather. Spring time event would be perfect here. 

Minimal parking, in back twenty parking spots. You can find some parking in the area along Esplanade.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I never been a yogurt person, but I decided I deserved a treat and this was the location for it.  There were several flavors to try but both times visiting I went with Wedding Cake and Birthday Cake.  What I love the most is the fact that I can pick all of my own toppings. So I went a little overboard. You have to be careful because your yogurt must be weighed! Keep that in mind before you end up with one yogure for 15 bucks.

It's in an area with ample parking so no need to worry about that. There is no seating but you are close to the Lakefront if you want to enjoy your tasty treat in peace.

2 stars:
1 for location.
1 for bacon... not that it's particularly great bacon... just the fact that they serve it at all gets them a star.

My husband and I love a good divey diner. We love a good greasy spoon. We just plain love breakfast. But what we don't love is the constantly terrible, slow, forgetful, frazzled service. We can tolerate mediocre food... but not consistently bad service. Drinks come late, if at all. Food is often wrong or forgotten all together. I wish this place would step up their game.

It's 1:53 AM, and my group of friends are craving pizza at this point. I go to my Yelp app, and Tower comes up within walking distance. Despite all the bad reviews on service and the quality of pizza, we were able to pay and eat several slices of pizza within thirty minutes of when we arrived. Not bad at all! Perhaps it helped that it wasn't as crowded, and we were able to grab a table. 

By the way, it's cash only, and they had several pizza-by-the-slice options available: Cheese, mushroom, sausage, broccoli, and cheesesteak.

holy crap, am i jazzed about this joint!!

see, my bff has been crazy raving about this place for ....well, for several months, at the very least. me? i was the naysayer! saying nay, as i am loyal to la lupe! i am loyal! i do not stray, with my taco loving, sopes eating ways.....

well. all that has changed. i strayed! i couldn't help it!

i started out with the green enchiladas, and was stoked. unbelievably fucking stoked. good beans? hell yes. good rice, that ain't goopy or dry? hell to the yes!

i am making el hubbo try them tonight. convert, ahoy!

My original habit!! How I missed thee!!!

After living in SB for school for years, I moved back to L.A. and to my joy, they moved 2 locations down here, and they still have the same SB charm and flavor.

The lines are always long, so that's a good sign.

Back to this joint: I love the old-school feel to this place. Old town Goleta is a fun place to eat, away from the hussle and bussle of IV and the over-pricey-ness of Downtown SB.

They keep their menu simple, almost an In-N-Out feel to it. But that's a very damned good thing.

Decent food could be better though especially when it comes to consistency. Delivery is always quick and friendly. 
If the food was more consistent and better quality overall then it would get 5 stars. For the money and quality it's good enough overall. It was the first place I ordered food from and was great but it has been up and down quality wise recently.  I wish they would concentrate more on the products and have a little variety as well as some more home cooked/fresh food. Still recommended overall though.

Typical Subway....

Good food that you decide what you want on it and how you like it from the roll on. The service has been decent for the most part every time I've come here. Seem to be a slower overall then other subways I've gone to in the area.

Personally I go for the chicken teriyaki sandwich with extra meat, lettuce and onions. Service has been hit and miss. Sometimes the lettuce and onions don't look particular fresh though and I wish the manager would work to make this place better.

Overall you get a good sandwich with or without the extra meat for a decent price just expect to get it slower then other locations.

This is right around the corner from my house. They can always get me right in and have plenty of staff. 
The cheapest pedi is $25 up to $80. Be aware that the staff always want you to get the next expensive treatment by offering it to you 2-3 times (i.e.: Do you want this pedi instead? Do you want a flower on your nail? Do you want me to rub your feet for five minutes longer?). 
I think they do a good job. They get in there and get your nails clean. I went at 4pm today (typically when other nail salons are winding down and not doing their best work) and my nails came out great.

I was really impressed with this courtyard...especially after reading the mediocre reviews on here.  The staff was wonderful...from the valets to the front desk to the bartenders.  The all gave great advice on where to go and what to do.  You simply cannot ask for a better location.  Less than a 5 minute walk to Broadway...even in heels ;)  The room was clean and comfortable.  Nothing overly exciting as far as decor but not your standard Courtyard.  If you are looking for a great place to stay with friendly staff and an unbeatable location, stay here.  I know I will be the next time I'm in Nashville
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I've been going to Sean for a few years now, back when he was at the Chop Shop on Temple's campus.  When he opened up his own place I followed him there.  I absolutely love Snip.  The decor is really nice and the people who work there are a delight.

Sean is the best.  He knows just what looks good on me since I tend to be indecisive and vague on my request.  Now that I've been with him for a few years now I just kind of go in and say "Just make it happen"and he makes it happen.  Everyone who I have told to go to Snip has loved it as well.  I can't give it enough stars, always satisfied.

I've driven past the Rural Inn many times. I'd written it off as a generic liquor store that probably wouldn't stock the beers that I'm looking for. 

After reading the reviews and a friend recommending it to me, I decided to stop in. Initially your met with the "typical" liquor store offerings. Lots of inexpensive wine and beer line the walls and shelves. However they've got a great, albeit, small walk in cooler with tons of great beer at very competitive prices. 

If you know what you're after and happen to be in the area, Rural Inn has a great selection and competitive prices.

A departmental function led me to return to Sunset Grill. As always delicious and service was outstanding! Again I had the wedge salad with the beggar's purse; equally delightful! 

One thing that I kept noticing about Sunset Grill is the extensive wine list that literally goes on for two very full pages. I mean, where do they keep all that wine? Nonetheless I selected a white Ruffino "Lumina" Pinot Grigio '09. 

For dessert, mixed berry sorbet as my dessert but all the other desserts were begging me for a tasting.

I met some girls on Tuesday night for a post-engagement celebration. Located near Starbucks in Belle Meade Plaza, apparently this place has gone through several name transitions. The other rumor about this place is that they have what is known as "crack salsa" or salsa you cannot shake because it is addictingly delicious. Yes, I just made up a new word, addictingly. 

I'm not a Tequila fan but every one else in our party ordered the margaritas. Two for one Tuesday resulted in $5.00 tabs at the end of the night. The place is small but the prices are totally worth it. And yes, the salsa is pretty good. No smoking and definitely kid-friendly!

A truly resplendent dining experience. I think the Petruce Brothers have absolutely nailed it here, and have been three times in a month. The plates are so thoughtfully constructed. My one tip is to make sure to get a fork/spoonful of each piece of a plate to get the full experience. Every dish seems to offer a triplet of textures (creamy, crunchy, chewy, etc.) and a triplet of flavors (sweet, savory, sour) but you have to make sure to get it all together. The food based around a simple wood fired grill somehow ends up totally surprising as you go from dish to dish. I'll be bold and say this is my favorite restaurant in Philly.

I came here for the first time today for a pedicure.  I didn't have an appointment, but that was no problem.  There was only one other customer there at the same time as me.

After picking out my color, I was immediately escorted to my pedicure chair.  The nice, comfortable chairs offer massage and can be adjusted.  

Over all, the place appeared very clean.  The girl who waited on me took her time with my neglected Runner's feet.  Price was a few bucks less than I pay at my regular nail place.  

I'll likely be back to World Spa & Nails. If I can ever get these finger nails to grow, I'll try them for a mani.

I went here on Cardinals opening day this year.  I received and email about coming out to Gio's to enjoy opening day earlier that week so i thought we would check it out!
There were no festivities( granted it was pouring down RAINING) and there were NO drink /beer specials or food specials, we were even in the bar area.  Also, they did not have beer buckets, you had to buy individually.  I'm good with being an upscale place and all...but please don't go for the baseball crowd -especially on opening day if you can't deliver.  We were disappointed and left after 1 drink.

While on a work trip we were on the hunt for Starbucks, but found French Press Coffee House instead. We are fans of small local businesses so we decided that we would stop in. After the first visit (we made 3) we were hooked. 

Our supervisor had that café au lait and said it was actually made correctly (half milk/half coffee) unlike Starbucks which usually does 1/4 milk, 1/4 water and 1/2 coffee. 

My coworker had a caramel latte. She said it was delicious. They used real caramel, not bottled corn syrup.

I had the mocha. It was bitter, but only from the chocolate and not the espresso.

This was definitely a jewel on our trip.

Sushi is really good.  Hibachi is solid too, but hibachi is the kind of meal that people on the lower socioeconomic scale consider a vacation.  They become loud, embarrass  themselves and generally act like they were raised by wolves because one of the chefs might shoot sake into their mouths during his act.  There are a lot of affliction wearing T shirted people too, which takes away from the ambiance of any restaurant, Burger King included.  So all that sucks, but the food here is good.  Stick to the sushi area if you don't want to see a bunch of adult clowns act like adult clowns.

This place always has a line up from 11:45-1:45 (Mon-Fri) and I can see why. The 2 guys making the subs are really s-l-o-w-- twice, I've come in here over the noon hour and had to leave. Reason is, no progress in the line up and very slow working staff. These guys don't  have a clue how to hustle. I decided I would come back again at 11:30 the next day, and I still had to wait so long for the guy to make my sub, even with no line....in front of me. I only suggest coming in here before the rush,  you'll still have to wait, but not as long as usual.

Went here for lunch today with a group from work.  Just as my rating suggests it was just ok.

I opted for a lunch portion of pasta with a salad for $8.99.  The serving size was nice and the salad was larger than I expected (it wasn't huge, but larger than a typical side salad at other places).  However, the blue cheese dressing was kind of flavorless.  It wasn't horrible, but could have been better.  I had the baked 3 cheese penne pasta.  It was also just ok.  I love garlic and it had too much garlic in it.  

Overall, I would eat here again if I was in the area, but I would not drive out of my way to eat there.

The Good: They have an amazing selection of frames. As an avid collector of eye glasses (I have them in almost every color: green, purple, blue, etc ...), this is the only place I will buy my frames. They have designer frames from Sweden and Italy, and some very unique one-of-a-kind frames. Everyone always asks where I get my glasses!

The Bad: The service is horrible. It's always busy and the staff is condescending. I am the type of customer that likes to shop and choose without any help so this doesn't bother me. Regardless, I will keep coming back because their selection is truly unbelievable.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
I have been meaning to try this place for a while. I bought a Creative Loafing gift certificate. It was about to expire so I drove all the way across town. The Facebook page says they close at 9 p.m.. It was 330 in the afternoon. They decided to close early because of mothers day. Because really, who goes to a restaurant on Mother's Day to take their mother out? Genius move guys.

Fortunately I used the opportunity to have a meal down the street at Chihuahua's Mexican Restaurant.  Apparently they don't just randomly shut down their restaurant on a whim.

This place has taken a dive. The portions are so small and incredibly overpriced. Last time we were there I ordered the lamb and it was such a small portion, we laughed when they dropped it at our table. We laughed until we realized it was like $28. 

On a sidenote: we used to come in and were pleasantly greeted by the part owner and his daughter. Apparently he was in a near-fatal car crash and while in the hospital, the other owners fired his daughter and have made moves to force him out of the business while he was unconscious. 

Overpriced food and horrible business ethics. I wish I had four hands to give this place four thumbs down.

I wouldn't be able to find a phrase that describes this place than the "Meh. I've experienced better." that goes with a two star rating.

The food was decent enough, but not the best Italian I've had by a stretch. The wine was excellent, but they just had to pick out the bottles and purchase them, yeah? Also, the service on my last visit was so attentive as to be overbearing. I'd like to have a conversation with the person I'm there with, not with the wait-staff. Especially when they drop off a $150 check for a light dinner on a two top.

As a family of three, we were impressed with Homewood Suites. Here's why:

1) Rooms: It's in a historic building in downtown Indy and every room is HUGE with high ceilings. There's plenty of space for everyone!

2) Location: It's downtown and central to everything! The only downside is parking (valet parking is expensive!).

3) Food: They have a full breakfast every morning on the house and the staff are soooo friendly who work it. There's a waffle maker too!

4) Building: The lobby space is smaller than normal, but they do have a pool and gym. It's a nice facility. 

If you're traveling with small kids, they have cribs you can use.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Not impressed at all but then again maybe  traveling has made me a bit of a Diva. I like complete comfort especially when away from home. No restaurant on site but they have a cafe and the cafe is currently out of food because they are waiting for the truck. Then I get my keys and had to go back downstairs because neither work (I got in pretty late so this was more annoying than usual) and my floor stinks so bad. Luckily the room is big and ok so far. I wish they used plastic cups, I don't trust how they clean their mugs. I've watched that video. Lol ok I'm done being a DiVA
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
On my recent trip to Indy, had to book a last minute rental.  Dollar was the way to go.  Easy online booking.  My flight got in a bit later in the evening, but it helped not to have a line.  Other than the nice lady in front of me (that apparently had not rented a car in her life) I was in the vehicle and on my way in no time.

Vehicle return was easy - watch out tho since the new Indy airport doesn't really have a close gas station.  May be easier to do a pre-pay tank until they build more stuff around the new exit/terminal.

I always feel like I'm bothering them at the drive thru. Oh, I'm sorry, is that not why you're here?  I never, ever want to go to Rally's, but it's literally a minute from my house, and sometimes, everything else is closed/busy and you're desperate. This drive through (I've never been inside) always cements my self-hatred and the question "why did I think this was a good idea?"

I'm not an angry, judgey person, and I've worked in a drive through.  I know it sucks.  But c'mon, guys. You don't have to be so obvious in hating the customer.

For a small town feel and a great bakery make Landis one of my preferred stops for groceries. The produces is fresh and they carry some local products during the summer. Their meat selections is extensive with a lot of cuts you typically don't see in most supermarkets. Also, for a smaller type supermarket they have a lot of specialty items (i.e. chocolates, candy, ethnic foods).

Admittedly though the main draw for me is they have great donuts. Far better than the average grocery store. I've even been know to go out of my way on my drive home to pick up donuts.

Hmmm....what to say. There is nothing we could find exceptional about Salsa Mexican Grill. My buddy had heard the margaritas were their specialty. They're not. Watery and tasteless are the first adjectives to describe their margaritas. Food wise we were all pleased with our lunch menu items and did not leave hungry. I will say the place, especially for lunch, was reasonably priced. My chimichanga was crispy with moist chicken, so not too shabby. My closing remarks are that I am slightly intrigued as to what their best items are and would be able bodied and ready to go again.

I'm torn here between the reality of a really comfy bed and the cockroach that fell from the ceiling and landed on my husbands's hand. The cockroach wins. Overall this hotel has the feel of a Doubletree or Embassy Suites, either of which I'm guessing it was in a former life. The room was nicer than either the exterior and public spaces would suggest, with the aforementioned nice bed and an updated bathroom. None of it justifies the big price tag, which I would expect to pay at Hilton's better properties, but not here.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Unstained wood is the order of the day, Zama is bedecked with the stuff.  My fiancee and ordered: Ohitashi, one of the experimental rolls for charity, lettuce wrapped chicken and eggplant, John Dory Sashimi, Otoro, Uni-nigiri, ikura rolls as well as the Japanese style crudo and brussel sprouts.

Service was attentive, and was kind enough to nix the lettuce wraps when the lettuce turned out to be desiccated and limp.

A glass of wine rounded out the meal well.  The endless techno music was a little grating, but otherwise it was excellent.

Pluses: 
1) freakin' awesome light up skull cups
2) whiskey shot chair
3) electrical outlets AND charger plugs for cell phones

Minuses:
1) terrible dueling pianos. I thought we were watching some type of social experiment to see how long right minded people could listen to gut wrenching noise. I've really never seen "musicians" butcher music like they did at this place. Sad face.
2) very pricey drinks

Overall it's an ok place to visit. I can only imagine how much worse this place was before Bar Rescue. At least they've got a legacy going for them...

My best friend lives in the apartment above this place and we went on a double date here recently. To my surprise, it was outstanding food.

The service was a little slow, but if you're with good company that shouldn't matter much.

The space was very loud as two birthday parties were in what is a very small dinning room area, but once again if you're with a good crowd you'll be just as loud.

I got the osso bucco with wild mushroom risotto and it was out of this world. Soooo good.

I recommend this for anyone in the Conshohocken area. Don't forget to bring a nice bottle with you when you go.

I was so excited when told about this place! It's just a five minute drive from home and their beer selection is the best (unless you drive to Randall's, of course). They have a nice variety of hard liquor as well -- with all the fixings to make mixed drinks from the comfort of your own home AND for the fraction of the price at a bar. The one of the men working there was extremely helpful and knowledgeable. He was able to answer all my questions and even gave me a stellar gin recommendation! I'll definitely be back :)

After a little dress shopping, we ventured down to the food court and I knew immediately where I wanted to eat. 

Sarku makes each roll to order. Sure, you're probably going to have a wait a bit, but you're getting fresh sushi right in front of your eyes for a fraction of the price you'd find at any sushi bar in St. Louis. 

My nigiri was delicious, but I wasn't too keen on the service. They weren't friendly at all, but I guess if I worked in a food court in a mall, I wouldn't be too terribly friendly either. Overall, I would come here again. It's cheap, yummy sushi you don't have to drive to if you're shopping.

This place was not my selection, it was a default from a group travel arrangement from work.  I thought the place was more like a tiny grubby apartment than a nice hotel room.

The popcorn ceiling was very thick, and the room included not only a stove, dishwasher, microwave, full size refrigerator, but plates, cups, glasses and even leftover Tupperware! [YUK].

I pointed out to my co-worker that the room he was staying in had obviously been entered by use of crowbar force at some point in the rooms history.  I was just glad I didn't get that room.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: The ambiance of this place makes it more worthwhile than the food - the old bank interior, with super high ceilings and a preserved old vault - make it more interesting than the run-of-the-mill type restaurant.  Its location right on the corner of High Street and E. Broad (across from the Riverline station) makes it an easy stop as well.  We only had drinks here (twice) - the crowd seemed to be pushing 50 and maybe even 60 more the majority.  Good beer selection, excellently priced happy hour from 5-7, and an overall friendly atmosphere.  And really good french fries, especially when paired with beer :)

I like this location as it's not on a busy corner like most Starbucks! The space is very small so if there is a lot of orders- there is very little space to stand and wait for your order but I like that I can walk underground from my building to get here.
The staff knows my order and are always very friendly! I would not recommend having a meeting or working from here- there is literally 3 chairs in the window seat! But I'm a nice day you can enjoy your coffee in the large plaza outside and soak up some sun!

I hate ZING. I hate their name, I hate their ugly mosaic lights that are almost completely opaque and therefore functionless, I hate their terrible logo (there are plenty of competent graphic designers in town, please hire one), the servers have always been rude to me, they changed chefs and definitely traded down, and are no longer veg-friendly. 

The chef is ham-handed with flavors and uses dated ingredients, often repeating the same ones over and over and over throughout the menu. Totally uninventive, do yourself a favor and skip it.

first time here since it changed from madame butterfly.  upon entering the red lighting above the bar was hip and inviting.

seaweed salad had iceberg lettuce in the bottom and not cucumber.  i wasnt thrilled about that.

got a few rolls.  and i wish i wouldve written down what they were (i did post some pics at the time).  they were average and good.  hard to reach the bar set by ooka a few blocks away.  one thing it maru's favor is that the prices were slightly lower.  but the few more $$$ a roll is worth it for me at ooka.  (sushi snob i guess).

anyway, it wasnt bad but not good enough to tear me away from ooka.

This was my first restaurant to try during restaurant week and I would surely try this spot again for sushi I went for dinner and the fish was fresh as fresh could be.  I had  a salad, the pork dumplings, maki  combo and some of the tastiest desserts ever. Luckily these were bite size otherwise I may have rolled out of Zama.  I did try the cucumber martini which was very light and refreshing. The server was friendly and attentive. The space is nice and tastefully decorated. Parking could be an issue, I found spot around the block in lot.

I have stopped by Salvatore's a couple of times for a meal.  The sausage hoagie was well made.  It was thick crusty bread with a hearty sausage.  The sausage was hearty and spicy.  While a good lunch it was not especially outstanding.

Sausage and pasta was average.  The pasta itself was standard cooked okay.  The noodles were not pasty or hard, just a bit past al dente.  The red sauce was a a bit flat and lacked bright or spicy notes.  Perhaps the pizza is the better dish to go with here, I will have to give it a try next time.

I'd love to tell you that I fondly remember all of my trips to George's but the truth is that the only times I've been here have been when my craving for "drunk food" hits and I needs me some queso pronto!  

They always offer good service to drunk Kinsey.  The chips and queso are pretty good according to my snapchats the next day.  I like sitting in the window and people watching while scarfing my chicken quesadilla.  I don't think George's has a fountain machine, only canned soda which I don't like.

George's, one day maybe I'll visit you in the light of day, but until then this is all the review I can muster!

I stop here a couple times a week when I'm up early in the morning to bake cupcakes.  I always park and walk in because usually there is a huge line of cars waiting in the drive through.  Usually I am out of there before the last car I saw makes it to the window, so I am assuming that if you are in a hurry, maybe waiting in a line of 10 cars in a drive through is not the smartest idea. 

I like this DD, I don't eat donuts, but their bagels are good, and I enjoy the egg white veggie omelet flatbread.  Much better than a McD breakfast, and comparable in price.

What can I say?  It's Starbucks.  They do have some of the more friendly Starbucks employees I've encountered at this location.  I think because of its proximity to 465 and Carmel, there is ALWAYS a line at the drive-thru.  You will get much faster service and be much less irritated just parking and going inside for your coffee.  Trust me, you don't want to be stuck behind the Carmel soccer mom ordering her Venti 1 pump caramel, 1 pump white mocha, 2 scoops vanilla bean powder, extra ice frappuchino with 2 shots poured over the top (apagotto style) with caramel drizzle under and on top of the whipped cream, double cupped.

In person service was okay, but beware if you have damages.  I left my insurance information as required and they charged me a $500 deductible which was made clear to me - that part was fine.  A week later, another charge showed up on my account for ~$165.  The representative said that this was the excess amount from the damage, but this charge was made without any notification or bill sent to me.  Additionally, when I called them, it turns out that they had actually OVERCHARGED ME by $100.

Pay close attention to the billing.

Actually, 2/12 stars ...

We ended up here when our flight was delayed due to weather. The good news is that the room was only $69 (special rate). the bad news is that we were right off of the atrium with a pool and the chlorine smell was a bit much. all the rooms open onto this open area so it can get quite noisy at night, or anytime for that matter.

The room was clean but the bathroom (which was clean as well) was the smallest I have ever seen in a hotel. there is a shuttle bus to take you over to the Opryland Hotel (a huge step up from the Inn at Opryland (formerly a Radisson). 

A good port in our storm but not worth revisiting.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The only thing this place has going for it is its Downtown location and lack of fro-yo competitors nearby. Not much has changed since my original review.

PRICE? Still high but I guess that's expected of DTSP.

FRO-YO STANCE = There is a great variety of fro-yo bases as well as a new "featured" flavor that constantly changes. Unfortunately, the fro-yo dribbled into my cup as well as icy chunks of it. At least the flavor was constant.

FRO-YO TOPPINGS = It was very obvious the fruits (like the kiwi and berries) had been previously frozen and thawed... they were droopy and slightly mushy in appearance and texture.
Meh.

FOOD
This place offers typical sports bar food fare and at the typical prices. Nothing has really WOW-ed me. You also get the expected quality and taste of similar sports bars.  

AMBIANCE
It's always been a small crowd away from a ghost town--even on game nights! Please explain why! (It was suggested to me by a patron that--although good--the drink specials don't line up well with potentially busy times - like nonexistent drink specials during big sports nights) Plus it's hard to compete with the World of Beer nearby

SERVICE 
Servers are smiley, helpful, and have been great at describing and suggesting items for newbies.

This is a nice little place which is essentially a non-chain version of Cosi.  At lunchtime they serve a small selection of panini, wraps, salads, ice cream and smoothies.  The atmosphere and decor is modern and comfortable. They have both high and low tables and a few soft lounge chairs.  They may have free Wifi; I saw a few people with laptops.Off in one corner they have some toys to entertain the kids.

My wife and I enjoyed the food we had there. There has been a shortage of places like this in this neighborhood and they will probably do well.

Linda Jean's is a grill and pizza shop with table service, take out and delivery.  The menu isn't surprising - pizza, steaks, burgers, salads, wraps, etc. - but it is all fresh and well prepared.  The food my wife and I tried was a step above what you normally get at a pizza and hoagie shop.

So Linda Jean's isn't a destination, but if you're in the neighborhood, it's a good bet for a satisfying meal.  Anyone familiar with the restaurant that formerly occupied this location (Greenwood Deli) should note the Linda Jean's is a dramatic improvement, not least because they really cleaned the place up.

Still a great place for lunch, but Belle has gone more casual.

In a way, this is good (more affordable).

But it's sad to see that Chef Brian has removed some of the more ambitious items from the menu.

The burger stuffed with short ribs? Just a memory now.

The amazing fried chicken? Heartbroken to report that it has disappeared.

Apparently Belle does dinner once a month on Thursdays and some of these old favorites are resurrected.

Until then I'll just have to try to visit on Saturday (fried chicken tender and waffle day)!

Service is still lovely. The fruit tea is still spectacular.

We only picked this hotel because we had free nights to use, and this was the closest Category 4 Marriott to all of the action. When we first arrived, I was definitely a little sketched out by the location and neighborhood, but there are some pretty well-known restaurants close by (Cochon, Cochon Butcher, August, Herbsaint) and it was a pretty quick walk to the French Quarter. The staff was very friendly, rooms were clean and there were always cabs across the street waiting to take you to your destination.

If you want to be close to the French Quarter but need to save some money, this hotel is a decent alternative.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Reasonably decent prices for reasonably decent sushi. They're not really breaking any new ground on the inventive sushi front but what they do make isn't bad.
