It's a great spot for lunch (the lunch specials are good) or a casual dinner. If you're looking for a sushi date sort of restaurant I'd suggest trying your luck elsewhere. The between the music on the PA and the din of the adjacent karaoke bar the place can get kind of loud. So if you're looking for conversation with your meal you may find yourself a bit disappointed.

Little-known gem of a snoball stand on Jefferson Highway. There's a near-exhausting number of flavors available (including sugar-free options and a few real-fruit choices for people so inclined) and plenty of other snack options as well. I prefer Plum Street above all others but don't always feel like driving into the city just for a 2$ snoball. Sno Shak fits the bill! 

The line can get super long in the dog days of the summer but if you live here and are going for a snoball you already knew that was going to be the case. Luckily there's an awning around the building so you can wait in the relative shade.

It's convenient to run here for my emergency moments (ie: CRAP! I forgot to buy that ONE essential ingredient for my dinner recipe!) but it's just too expensive for me to make this my regular market stop.

However, I will say that the service here is quite enjoyable. The management definitely strive to maintain an aura of being your friendly neighborhood grocer. 

And while I haven't stooped low enough to consider delivery (I do live only a few blocks away)... they do offer it which is a nice plus if you want/need it ...

Absolutely the best Italian meal I've had so far in Tucson! Mid-meal I looked at my husband, sighed, and said sincerely "it tastes like happy memories, and love!" This food experience has left me feeling full,  not just in my stomach but in my heart. The owners are sweet, and attentive, and they help to make you feel so welcomed and at ease. I want to write on and on about this place, but it's something that you really should experience for yourself. If you go, try the lamb, they told me it's cooked for 4 hours, and is sooooooooooo tender.

A number of places are guilty of the "less is more pizza" where the meat is more of a garnish than an actual topping. If it's a vegetable topping then 9 times out of 10 it's loaded down. It would be a clean sweep for Slice in the World Series of Topping Rationing.

And I agree with most other gripers here. Blandissimo!

I have to give Slice some credit though... for...

1.being in 1 of the best alley strips in the city (Sansom)
2. friendly service
3. a Yelp promo soda (peace to the l33ts)
4. a pretty cool interior
5. obviously there are people who do like boutique pizza hence the 4's and 5's

Bad service today, server didn't clear 1 plate, hostess sat 9 people (including myself and my dad + 1 family of 7 people) with 1 chef section where the other section has 3 chefs with 3 people. Just totally stupid, the other chefs didn't come over and ask to help with orders the chef who was obviously overworked, had to ask. It was okay, but not a great experience. We had to ask for our check as we never saw the server after he brought 1 drink. I wouldn't return anytime soon based on this visit. to many better choices for AYCE!

This is a nice little gem on the Bench that I head to when I don't want to deal with downtown parking or driving out to West Ada. I usually opt for the eggplant parm - my go-to for any Italian restaurant.

They also have an excellent Ciopino seafood stew that my friend says is the best in the area. He's a soup guy so he should know. Although I think I like Bella Aquila's Ciopino better.

They do a Caesar salad the right way with a good dressing. Maybe it has anchovies like it should. Anyway it has the right level of umami.
 
Try out the berry dessert if you still have room.

Being a washingtonian,  I guess i am spoiled by the feast of late night take-outs and of couse the king of drunk food: JUMBO slice. This is one of the few places i have noticed in my immediate area open late night i decided to stop in (not drunk) and not very late to try it out. The service was friendly and fast and the pizza by the slice was cheap. However the pizza was lacking in the delicious factor area and i walked home not stunned but merely satisfied that i was no longer hungry. They are very creative with their pizza styles and toppings and i guess that makes up for the lack luster approach to their slices  of cheese.

Best Chinese food we have had since San Fran china town. Crispy pot stickers/ dumplings so so but everything else was fresh and outstanding. We shared the won ton soup which had the best broth and tastiest won tons ever. Chicken and mushrooms was so tasty as was the Mongolian beef - right mix of beef and onions. The house fried rice was so good with four proteins that my husband did not want to share. Service was quick and attentive. I had seen yummy house on yelp and we made a point to stop by for lunch when we were in the area.  Very glad we did and we will definitely be back.

Normally, I really like this place, but my meal tonight was a big disappointment. I started with a seaweed salad, which was good, and followed up with a dragon roll, which was not. The presentation was beautiful, the service was quick and friendly, but the quality of the eel left much to be desired. The eel, what little there was of it on the roll, was rubbery and not good at all. I managed to choke it down with lots of wasabi but was pretty bummed as I've had this roll here in the past and really liked it. I won't be ordering it again.

We stayed here for 1 night. Everything was clean and nice looking. We stayed in a 9th floor suite and it was plenty big. The cost of valet vs self park was the exact same. That did not make much sense to me. Nonetheless it was convenient and easy to access. The only issue we had was that the cleaning crew knocked on our door 4 times even after I put the "do not disturb" sign up. We had a late check out and found it pretty annoying. The stay came with a free breakfast, but we overslept so I can't comment on the food. I did notice they had a pretty decent beer selection.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Aviation grill is the restaurant lounge for the Airport Marriott. As a bar, they have a limited draught beer selection, decent wine selection and limited spirits. But you won't be dry. The menu has six entrees, a bunch of apps, and a few salads and sandwiches. The wings I had were very good, crisp with garlic and herb. The Korean short rib buns were a definite miss. The beef was well seasoned and the Korean gochujan sauce was adequate but, the light puffy bun was replaced by a deep fried piece unidentifiable bread. Worth eating but choose wisely.

I've had the pleasure of returning to Chambers after they re-opened for both lunch and dinner. Their burgers remain spot on. If you are a fan of fried pickles the pickleback burger is for you.

The new menu has a lot of great entrees. On my last visit I ordered the Shepherd'spie. Wonderful mixture of browned beef, vegetables in a warm gravy topped with mashed potatoes, served in a cute cast-iron skillet. 

The drink menu remains strong. The craft beer selection is top notch with a mixture of national and local selections.

While in-person dining may be done for2020, I cannot wait to return in the New Year.

For me the perfect fast-food burger combination is a cheeseburger with raw onion, pickles, ketchup and mustard. To achieve this you can order a quarter.pounder at McDonald's, a quarter pounder king at Burger King. To get the equivalent at Wendys you need to customize a Daves Single or Double, leaving off lettuce, tomato, and mayonnaise, adding extra pickles and mustard. The staff was accommodating and made the burger. Extra pickles translate into three small dill pickle chips, and mustard was not put on the burger but rather supplied in tiny packets. The result was an epic fail from a place that should be able to make a superior burger.

Came here on a Sunday early evening to hopefully watch some football on TV while enjoying some live music. Very disappointing.  For one, we were seated at an area, but then requested we could move to a table with a closer TV.  We overheard our first server getting really annoyed at the second server because she lost our table. Very unprofessional.

The food was plain, and worse it was cold. The gumbo was basically room temperature.  When I asked what kind of bourbon they had, our server started rattling off names of... whiskeys. 

The TVs were also pretty bad quality. Hardly HD (or even close to it).

Wouldn't come back.

You know what they say it the restaurant business....?  Location! Location! Location!  That's what Chill has going for it-- it's in the adorable Clayton/Wydown area.  Most of their customers walk here from somewhere nearby. 

The Yogurt is good-- but it's not the best in town.  They usually have around 8 varieties and probably 20 toppings.  The flavors and toppings are a little lacking. 

When the weather is warm, I love sitting on their patio tables outside.  It's definitely one of the best places to people watch.

My husband and I live down the street and have eaten here a few times. There is always a crowd! I think the food is pretty good but the restaurant seems a little unclean. I've always heard that the bathroom in a restaurant is a good indication of what the kitchen looks like. The bathroom here was pretty disgusting! 

I think they attract a crowd that wants super cheap (bland) food, large portions and cheap alcohol. If that's all your looking for--- you'll probably love the place. 

Bottom line, will we go back? Honestly, probably not. There are too many other restaurants in the area.

When I came back for 4th of July, I found that Nashville had been invaded by cutesy yogurt shops!

My Southern friends raved about Sweet CeCe's and the Cali-transplants were crazy about Menchie's. Since I've had Menchie's in LA, I decided to try out Sweet CeCe's.

Pretty standard issue yogurt. This is a good location although I was really missing inventive flavors - my flavor options were totally basic. Toppings were good... I could have used more fresh fruit and it would have been great to have mochi though.

While my favorite is still YogurtLand (not yet in the area), Sweet CeCe's is still a fine place to get your sweet fix.

This place is honestly awful, like spend the rest of the night with indigestion and your head in the toilet awful.  I am a fan of greasy run of the mill chinese buffet food from time to time but this place is just not worth it in my opinion.  The food here used to be decent a few years ago, but I went recently and it was bland, flavorless, extra greasy, and very fatty.  Overall a very bad experience and I wont be back anytime soon.  

Oh, and my favorite part of the place - the soft serve ice cream machine -  was broken when I went.  Two thumbs down

I wish Susan G. had said where the gym was lacking on convenience and function- if it's not convenient b/c you don't happen to live near it, that doesn't matter to other ppl reading these reviews. As far as I can tell, the Passyunk location has all the same weight/cardio machines, studio space, classes and equipment of the other locations, except for the pool that only the Arch St location has. I like the spaciousness of this location, and it is aesthetically more appealing than say the fitler or arch locations.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: I think the quality of this restaurant is 4 stars but the prices and the portion size gets three stars. I love sashimi but it is an expensive habit. If you are going to check out Sachiko I would advise you to order rolls to fill you up and the tiny orders of sashimi to savor the flavors. The staff here is also Japanese but the feel is not as traditional as Yamato.  I liked it and I can walk there, so they will see me again but only when I have an extra 50 to spend on myself for a sushi dinner. By the way this spot is in the Trader Joe's parking lot.

I went there one day before I hit the road and had a good experience. They began sending me coupons for $17.00 oil changes so I have been back. With my job I put 3,000 hard miles on my car every five weeks so price is important but it is the service that keeps me coming back. The owner is there all the time, he deals with his customers, doesn't try and sell me all this extra crap but does inform me of things that my mechanic husband needs to look at. They get me in and out in less than 20 minutes consistently so they have won my business. My time ='s money and they know that so they take good care of me.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: This is, as they say in Russia, liquor store kak liquor store. Meaning that this is nothing particularly special, but it still does the job. From the website, it appears that this store is relatively small compared to the other many locations in Indy. But they still have the basic staples. When I came in here, one of the staff members had just tragically died in a house fire a few days before (I'm sorry to report), but the rest of the folks on duty still seemed friendly and helpful. It's a good, solid little corner liquor store.

Well, it's...ok, I guess. It was packed when I was here, but I felt a bit young for the crowd. Most people looked more in the 40s range than the 20s. There was a somewhat generic band playing--nothing particularly memorable. I wasn't too impressed with our jalapeno poppers, either. Our drinks were fine, but they were just Blue Moons or something. In short, there isn't a whole lot to be said about this bar, but then again, there isn't a whole lot to do on the South side, period. If you're on the bottom end of town and feel like drinking out, I guess you could do worse than Jake's.

If I can find a deal, it will bring a smile to my face.
The gauntlet was thrown and I was in charge of a bachelor party. No more inflatable bouncing castles and sitting around the TV watching True Lies. It's the big leagues now and I need to make sure everyone is satisfied.

Great selection of liquor and beer to boot. Prices are very attractive (for the booze anyway. $2.50 for 2L of Coke, come on!) and they even compare their competitor's with a side by side comparison.

Bottle of Jose Cuervo, Jagger, Belvedere, and Crown came out to a cool $105.00. Not bad!

Stay thirsty my friends.

I've done a majority of my banking at this location not only because of its prime location in the suburbs but because of TD's excellent extended hours. Most banks only open until 16:00 or even 18:00 but with TD Canada Trust, most branches open until 20:00 which is a godsend if you're working late, running errands, or if you're like me, forgetful that you needed to make that large withdrawl of foreign cash.

After widthstanding two roberries, the staff are still committed to providing friendly service with a smile. They also have a mortgage specialist on site to cover almost all of their basic services.

Came here for lunch with a few coworkers, and it was okay. Nothing special, but then again, I came in knowing that this place wasn't going to be as good as other sushi places in St Louis. They do have a pretty decent special where you get a soup and salad, a roll, and three pieces of sashimi. Their sashimi was decent - not the best, but it wasn't terrible. I ordered the St Louis roll, which I actually liked.

I don't know if I'd necessarily come here again out of my own choice, but I wouldn't be opposed to it if someone else suggested it.

I love coming to this place even when I don't want coffee!  They get their desserts from Miel Patisserie and like many have mentioned, the atmosphere is amazing.  Don't forget the wireless internet available.  

I particularly love this place because their croissants are actually comparable to those from France.  They also had a time a couple years ago when they made crêpes on order on Wednesdays, again, comparable to those made in France.  I asked them why they stopped making them, and they said people weren't ordering them.  It made me so sad!  Anyway, I love this place. If you couldn't tell.

In a desperate attempt to fulfill a craving for some korean fried chicken (bonchon), we gave this place a try for take out on a Saturday night. I didn't hate it, but it didnt hit the spot like actual, authentic, bonchon would. To me, they just tasted like regular wings. The sauce was ok, but not what I was expecting. I would still give this place a try for other items on their menu..maybe. 

If you're in the city and looking for authentic bonchon..........i would just wait until the franchise opens (SOON) in Chinatown or make the drive to one of the Cafe Soho's. #JUSTSAYING

Well it was the Fourth Of July, and I thought the food was mixed, like the salads were decent, the steak good, my pasta dish so/so.  

Maybe Sunday is a lightly staffed night, because it took more than a hour for our food to come out.

Frankly, I was going to give them a 2 star review, but the staff was extremely nice, and I forgot my bag with all my important shit at an outside table, and when I came back a hour later, it was sitting behind the bar waiting for me.

I think the menu needs improving and the staffing could improve, but the guys there saved my day.  3 stars and a promise to return.

The hours, prices and doctors are fine, but I have had issues with the customer service side of things.

Their phone frequently goes unanswered.  Courtesy of reception staff is variable, especially when the waiting room is crowded.

I have previously ordered contact lenses that I was told would be shipped to my home, which never arrived because they were waiting for me in the store without notification.

Overall, the convenience of the location wins out for me, but I never expect things to go entirely smoothly.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text: I went to this small coffee shop while my sister ran some errands in the area. Its a small coffee shop with a great selection of hot and cold beverages. The have a small bakery section with pastries to devour with your cup of coffee. I ordered the Iced Mocha which was beautifully presented. Had the fresh taste of coffee and the chocolate they used had a nice sweet taste to it, didn't have that cheap chocolate taste. Prices were slightly higher than Starbucks, but still is a nice spot to have a cup of coffee on a rainy day.

We are currently staying at your Westin in St. Louis. We wanted to notify you that we were in room 373 in which the carpet and beds were covered in fleas. We had fleas hopping on our feet as we walked. The called the front desk who sent someone over to give us new room keys. The representative, who was very nice, had no idea why he was coming over. We called again to tell the front desk to make sure they were clear on the situation and all they told us that the room was now closed out. We were upset about the customer service until the manager called to express his concern a bit later and provided us vouchers due to our experience.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I made it to this subway one time.  I was so taken back by the owner (and he was happy to share that he was the owner) with how rude and impolite he was that I refuse to return to the store.
I just recently spoke to a friend that I learned had purchased a sandwich from the same story.  I shared my last visit there and my experience and he said he has had the same rude experience, but went there as it was one of the only healthy options in the area.  I was surprised to see things had not changed.
I go to Jimmie Johns across the street, quiznos two blocks away, or travel further to a different subway.

Higher Grounds is a large coffee shop with some food, coffee and desserts.
They are super low key and friendly inside.  
I have never tried their food, but I see people eating there in the afternoons.
Their coffee is pretty good and organic - a bonus!
It is hard to believe that this is the only coffee shop open before 8 that I can hit on my walk to work. 
Who owns a coffee shop and opens at 9?  Ridiculous.
Anyway, they allow pooches, so often you will find 2-3 dogs running about inside!
This is a cool place to catch up with friends or hang and read a book.

This is a cute little place on the corner of Liberty Walk.
They are BYO and I have gone for brunch and lunch on several occasions.  They have inside and outside dinning, and when we sit outside they always bring my sweet Nyla dog a bowl of ice water!

Their menu is limited - which makes it easier to pick what you want to eat anyway!
I just had the breakfast burrito last weekend with eggs, portabella mushrooms and Gruyere cheese...It was D-E-L-I-C-I-O-U-S!

The wait for food was a little long and, the service was fine, but not overly friendly.
Still, a great place when you are not up for the wait outside Honey's!

It's down the street from my house.  Thats really the only reason i go here. 
I hate the service, the unexpected fees, the miserable tellers,  the wait,  god its awful.   Dont go there in a Friday if you plan on seeing the light of day!   It's terrible.  
However,  its very convenient.  They have the penny arcade thing there.  One customer service rep, Tom,  is always very helpful.  If he is there, i usually wait until i can get him.  The other ones, at least from what i have experienced, are miserable and dumb.  
They will charge you for everything though. Beware.

Not too impressive.  They have ONE sugar-free flavor per day which is chocolate or vanilla.  Rah.  Hold me back.  Ridiculously overpriced and they literally WEIGH THE SPOON too. They sell their spoons at the same $7.85 per pound as their yogurt and toppings. How chickenshit is THAT?  Their yogurt is watery and flavorless and you can die of old age trying to get it out of the machine a spoonful at at time.  The floor was filthy when I was there, but there were plenty of kids (who allegedly work there) standing around talking to each other.  Go somewhere else--wayyyy not worth it here.

This review is not for the hotel, but for the hotel restaurant ML Prime, which does not have its own yelp profile.

Just to sum it up:  horrible service.  Friends made reservations, and we were still made to wait for a table for an hour.  We had to follow up with them 4 times before they finally paid attention.  Manager on duty smoothed it over with a free round of drinks.  However, the salad bar was pitiful and as far as my meal went, I could get better at any chain restaurant. 

Never returning, and I think if it weren't for my friend's restaurant.com gift certificate to this place, we probably would have never attempted to anyway.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I've been to Donnie Mac's a few times in the past year and I have been nothing but happy each time!  Most recently I ran over with a friend on my lunch hour.  We sat outside (DM's has some of the BEST outdoor seating downtown IMHO) and had a blast!  I've had sandwiches, burgers and hot dogs at DM's.. this past time I had their hand dipped corn dogs.. and OMG they are AWESOME.    I'm going after work in a couple of weeks, when I can enjoy a drink- three of us plan on tackling the Thunder Plate.  BRING.  IT. ON.

For a smallish space, La Tapatia is light and airy inside.  I found the chair a bit hard, but sitting in a booth would remedy that.  We had a group of 8 there for a birthday celebration.  I found the menu to be a bit pricy, even the lunch items- but my huevos chorizo was tasty. Tortilla chips a bit thick, but great bean dip.  I'm a 'spice weenie' so I'm not one to rate the salsa, but others with me found it tasty.    Service was swift, portions generous and served nice and hot.  Serviers were attentive and affable.  Such a successful first visit with a group merits a follow up!

Great location is the only positive. 
Check in was very slow. Took them forever to find our reservation even though I showed them the confirmation on my phone. 
They told me they were fully booked but would honor our reservation (somehow.)
The check in took about 30 minutes. 
The room is not a deluxe king as reserved. It is a small sized room with a queen bed. 
The room needs to be thoroughly cleaned. The air vent was filthy. I showed the front desk a photo. I have posted before and after photos. 
I do not recommend this hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Today was my first time visiting Roma after hundreds of drive-by's.  I was in the mood for pizza and drove from Medford to try them out.  I was not disappointed.  I got a slice of plain and a slice of chicken bacon ranch.  The plain was a perfect thinness for me with a crisp bottom, easy on the sauce, and a good amount of cheese.  The slice was HUGE!  The red sauce is sweet with hints of spice and no acidity.  The chicken bacon ranch had the same crispy bottom which made the huge slice easy to eat by hand.  I quickly moved my utensils to the side.  The staff was very nice, and the place is SUPER clean.  I shall be back!!!!

SURPRISE! Yummy House is good. 

It's true, the salt and pepper tofu is great. As is anything in XO sauce. The fried rice comes by the wheelbarrow-load. 

I would love to bestow Yummy House with the honorable Robert S. Five Star Review, but the seating situation kind of sucks. Yummy House is gaining huge popularity from the local dining community and should try to fit a few more tables in there to try to prevent the line out of the door or seating parties together. That shit's lame. They'd get much more business that we all WANT give them if they would make their capacity a little less incredibly finite. 

Still, go here.

I'll start by saying that I would give this place just one star if not for the cute setting. 

This by far takes the cake when it comes to horrible service. The over sized blond guy behind the counter slammed the iced tea down so hard that it spilled and didnt show a hint of an apology in his future behavior.  When asked for the manager he stated "im in charge, whats your problem"

New hope is filled with nice places, id steer clear of this place. Sure it may have a good location (its right on the water) but there is definitely a reason why this was the only place without a wait on a friday night.  Lesson learned!

I found O'Sake to be meh, overall.  It's a bit cramped, but they do have a decent sushi bar.  The service was very friendly, but the large, bright TV ruined any semblance of proper ambiance.  The place screams Japanese sports bar.

On to the food.  They do have a decent deal going on where you can choose two rolls for either $10 or $15 (depending on the type), which includes soup or salad.  Drinks are extra and are $2 for a can of soda.  The sushi was not really creative, my eel was slimy and old-tasting, the rolls were not tight and lacked flavor.  It's a good deal, I suppose, but I felt that the value was not spectacular at all.

I'm a huge fan of this place. I have been coming to Super Taqueria for about twelve years. Ever since their location was a few miles down the street near Damonte Ranch Parkway.

The staff is always super nice, helpful and the food delicious. Pretty darn authentic Mexican food at a great price. From the burritos to the tacos or enchiladas, all delicious food. They also have breakfast burritos which are especially delicious (I love their bacon since they use thicker slices) since I work around the street and can swing by and grab one for work.

Pro Tip: Order beforehand and then you can pick it up with a minor wait

We ordered from here the other night.  My kids wanted staples in the Chinese food world, such as orange chicken.  Personally, I am not a big fan of orange chicken.  So we ordered quite a big meal we ordered, crab puffs, pork potstickers, chicken lo mein, Mongolian beef, and orange chicken.  
I was displeased.  The orange chicken was gummy, the potstickers were bland.  The Mongolian beef was so greasy and covered in sauce that I felt nauseous.  It was unfortunate but we will not be ordering from there again.  
Unfortunately, the next morning I was sick from the food.  So,no more Panda Village for us.

I had to write an update we just went here on Sunday the day after Christmas with my mother in law.  Unfortunately our service was not good I was really disappointed by the food.  We had green corn tamales the first one was okay but kind of strange in a way we can't explain.  The second one was so bitter that you we could barely stomach it.
It was disappointing on top of it the sonoran dog my daughter ordered didn't come on the same bun it used too.
The place was really slow and it shows by the lack of service.
Too bad we enjoyed it much more last time.
Unfortunately I think this may have been the last time we go there.  Now onto new places.

I really really didn't like my experience here. The food was so terrible. I can't really compliment anything about it minus the fact the parking lot had spaces to park in an otherwise congested area. Service was hit and miss. Usually, I do not hold heavy expectations for Chinese food, but I held a higher standard here since it is more of a sit down establishment than take away. Quality was just a complete miss with all of our dishes from rubbery tasting beef to bone filled duck with little meat to be had. Just no... not worth my time or money spent again.

Good chinese take out at a fair price.

All your standard choices are available - chicken, beef, soups.   "Homestyle Bean Curd" is a wonderful (though not particularly healthy) vegetarian dish.  The veggie dumplings are cheap and very filling, too.

Seafood should generally be avoided here, but this is a good rule for all chinese take out.

Bonus - if you order $20 worth of stuff, you get free egg rolls and other fried goodies.  Though remember, $20 worth of chinese take out is a lot  of food; invite some friends.

I'm reviewing both the Fishers location and downtown as I have frequented both often when I lived in the area and now when I visit.  I love, love, love the pane granhcio, which I call "crab bread."  I always order the Tortellini Michelangelo or the Fettuccine alla Mariarosa.  The owner uses sauces that have been in his family for decades and really bring out the pasta dishes.  Service can be a lil off here and there, but the food is always consistent so I just deal with that.  Geez, now I'm craving crab bread!  Someone bring me some?!?! :-)

I love this Drury - they have updated this location yet again!  Brand new carpets, they extended and totally redid the breakfast/eating area - it is much bigger and so much prettier - tons of seating options, new bar area, etc.  In the rooms they also made changes to some of the furniture and decor - more importantly, new beds.  What I've always loved about this Drury remains the same:

1. Excellent location
2. Excellent value with the free breakfast and afternoon kickback meal
3. Free Wi-Fi
4. Free Long distance calls
5. Best customer service around.

I am still a Drury fan!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
E Sushi is the perfect family-owned restaurant in Apollo beach. Living in Waterset, there's limited options in the area. Chain restaurants aren't my favorite, so I love coming here to support. 

Each day there are various specials like ladies night or sake specials. We love the Asian pear and warm sake. 

Sushi favorites are the Phoenix roll and anything with veggies. The little likes that she can get her own sushi made to order and gobbles it all right up! 

We go here at least once a week and it's a favorite spot close to home!

I've recently discovered Grillsmith and their awesome happy hour!

We came here after work and were very pleasantly surprised. 

Service: our servers and the staff were more than friendly! They catered to our picky palettes and were super nice and cordial!

Food: I tried the beef steak tip eggrolls - yum! we also had their bruschetta and lettuce wraps which were both delicious. There were tons of appetizers and eats to choose from that were $7 or under!

We'd definitely come back again, as it's local and a great please to get together for happy hour!

I was able to try Moscato's at a friend's rehearsal dinner a couple of weekends ago. I'd not even seen or heard of it until then, and had walked past it many times - I missed a hidden gem!

Atmosphere:
Quaint and romantic, this little Italian eatery has a comfortable and homey feel. 

Food: 
Delicious! The noodles are all homemade and they take the time to cook each individual meal to your liking - I had the chicken Marsala with angel hair and it was yummy!

Service: the servers were all very friendly and made sure to take note of our separate likings and specific requests!

When in downtown St Pete, we definitely want to make a trip back!

I've been with Pyramid for about 5 months now and I can truly say that I am very happy with their customer service.  Their online banking is pretty limited but I can do what is most important and that is check my balance and use Bill Pay.  This particular location shares a space with Telco and all the ladies in there are very nice.  I love being able to walk into the branch and have the teller know my name. The place is always clean and there is never a long line when I go in, usually Fridays between 5:30pm and 6pm.  You can't really see the bank from the street, it's on the Northwest corner, in the Ross Plaza.

This restaurant is located in Center City and a few blocks from my office.  I think I visited many years ago, but didn't recall anything specifically about food, service, etc.  Well, this visit made up for my absentee mind.  I went for lunch with a friend and the first thing I noticed was the awesome lunch menu and most of them were under $10.   We decided to to get (2) dishes and share them, the portions were large and the food was ok.  

The staff were attentive, service was prompt and I think I will be back for many more lunches.

This location of Fine Wine& Good Spirits is my "Go-To" restock spot because it is super close to my house.   The location is large and usually well stocked.  The staff are helpful and offer suggestions at times based on what you are currently purchasing - I like that!  

I enjoy taking my time and cruising the for sales/specials when I am not in a rush.  I appreciate that they usually have the varieties of these new flavored vodkas; rums and whiskeys.  I usually find what I am seeking, so this makes this location a place that I find reliable.

Happy to find a cool dive bar in Chestnut Hill.  Places like this are hard to come by these days especially because most establishments want to cater to the "high end drinker.  Don't get me wrong, I like the gastropubs, along with great drinks that cost $15 or more.  

Sometimes you just want a shot of whiskey and a beer that costs less than $5 to take the edge off a hard day.  The local patrons are a diverse bunch and the place smells of cigarettes.  The bartender was friendly enough and we talked sports and local politics - exactly what you want in your dive bartender.  

Pros:  Cheap & Clean
Cons:  Cigarette smoke

Staff was nice and friendly, and if the facility was half as good, this would be a 4 or 5 star review, but the sound insulation in the rooms is terrible and you can hear everything in the rooms around you as well as the hallway. They seem to be mid renovation, as the room numbers were hand written notes taped to each door.

I didn't book the room for myself, instead the group bringing me in did, so I am not sure how the price compares to the other hotels in the area, but based on what I am use to, this place was lacking. The rooms were not bad and they did have wifi. The bed mattress could use an upgrade.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I was in Tampa for business, traveling solo, and just wandering around Ybor when I happened to come across Bernini.  Italian sounded good (my stomach was growling), so I thought I'd give it a shot.  I was seated right away upstairs, right next to the "vault" and by a window where I could people watch.  My server was quick and friendly, my lasagna was delicious, and the wine was refreshing.  Overall, a very good experience.  My ONLY issue (and it really doesn't matter) was that they forgot to bring me any bread, didn't even offer it until I asked.  But that's minor, and I still had a great meal.

This used to be a Church's chicken. I can't say I have ever stepped inside of a Church's chicken restaurant, but Rotolo's has done a good job at making this their own. Lots of updates to make it less... yellow.

The interior is a little small, but this place is never crowded, so it works. 

Friendly & quick service, great specials, and of course, free birthday pizza if you sign up for their online club thing.

This is a nice addition to the Westbank, as it isn't expensive gourmet, but it's definitely a step above fast food chain pizza.

So, here's the thing. It's FroYo. There are so many FroYo places everywhere now that I can't even bring myself to give this place 5 stars... even if it is Pinkberry. 

Yes, it's good. It's not life-altering, and it's not cheap. Most of the time it's really crowded, too, although we went early enough today that we didn't have much of a wait.

Still, it's super refreshing on a hot August day, and it's delicious, so it's worth 4 stars and will be a place that I visit from time to time.

Tip: Don't try to bring your cup of frozen yogurt onto the street car. They don't allow it.

You know... for fast food, Wendy's isn't terrible. Also, they don't mess up my order, which is nice since I order everything special (mayo = gross).

They just added some crazy Coke machine where you can apparently make 100+ drink combinations, as they now have 20 different Coke drinks to choose from, plus a ton of different flavoring options (vanilla, grape, peach, strawberry, cherry, etc). This, I am definitely a fan of. 

It's close to my office, so I frequent Wendy's once or twice a month when I can't think of anything better to eat. This is a good choice for a quick meal, or if you really, really want a Grape low-cal Lemonade.

The food is always good here.  I've been coming to Marco Polo for a very long time since it is around the corner from my grandparents' houses.  It's under new management, and has a new cook, but the atmosphere and the quality are still great - they haven't missed a heart beat.  

Today I had the sea bass over a thin potato pancake with string beans on the side.  My grandmother says they have that lunch special often, and it's always been great.  In fact, all four of us had that today, and we're licking our plates!

This is a great place to stay if you are in the Santa Barbara and Goleta area. The Pool is really well maintained and we enjoyed using the hot tub which surprisingly had no one else in it! The rooms are a little larger then the normal best western room and even had a nice seating area. The Bathroom was below average but when your getting a deal who am i to complain. One thing i really enjoyed was the Continental breakfast which was nicer then usual free breakfasts mostly because they have an espresso machine and i love me some coffee so it was a perfect match for me!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
After a quick lunch a couple doors down we decided to stop in and give Yo My Goodness a try.  We walked in and even though it was our first time in the set up looked familiar.  In my opinion familiarity is never a bad thing.  

We tasted several of the flavors but wound up going with the chocolate fudge brownie batter with some Twix sprinkled on for the added kick.  

It was a hot day and the cool goodness from Yo My hit the spot.  If I am ever back in the Groves and looking for something cool and sweet I'll stop back in and see if I can come up with another creation to fit my cravings.

This is the best liquor store in Indy, no question.

The staff is knowledgeable, friendly, and kind.  They know the "latest and the greatest" and listen to requests from their patrons.  Eric and Mike are our favorites; ask for them, and you won't be disappointed with the service. We mentioned a specific brewery months ago, and within one month's time, they had exactly what we were looking for---you can't ask for better customer service than that.  

Love this place, really.  We go out of our way for them.  It's worth it.

this was........... okay.   I got a vegetable noodle soup, for one. The portion was big but the flavor was far from it. The veggies and noodles were all fine but it was just pretty bland. For 2, I got another veggie noodle dish that was better but very long on the noodles and kind of short on the veggies. Its just not my style.  That dish also needed some help in the flavor department.  To their credit- the service was friendly and I saw the lady making the dishes fresh as they were ordered.  I guess maybe id give it a try again but with the plethora of options in the area for similar cuisine, eh...

First off, thank you Benjamin M. for informing me I live in the "third world," despite his making it out "alive to Yelp about it."  Is this thinly veiled racism helpful?  Why yes, Benjamin, it is!  Send my best to New Tampa.

Three Coins is solid local flavor.  It's an old fashioned diner, but more importantly a truly organic community center.  Everyone from the 'hood saddles up for Heart-stopping omelets, great coffee from Joffrey's, and service with a smile.  Not to mention cheap!  The pride of Seminole Heights!

BTW, how great are the waitstaff polos?  I want one.

I love this place in the summer when the patio is open upstairs. The indoor space is small but spread out well enough to alleviate any sense of claustrophobia. Typically it's a mid 20's - mid 30's crowd. Good music, interesting people, extensive drink menu. Try the Fred and Ginger. Gin-based...obviously. Fruity. Yum. 

Location is a bit out of the way from the rest of the Reno bar scene. But that can be a deifnite positive. 

Very social. Not a dark or dreary place. Upbeat and bustling for the most part. And ultimately I think that's what draws me here...good energy. =]

Not impressed, or even slightly happy.  Michael's was recommended by a friend.  I'm really glad he's had good service and is happy with this shop.  For us, $90 to replace a fuse and pull up a window that had fallen down and wasn't working and they duct taped it up.  A lot of recommended work for the next time which we were goofy enough to schedule an appointment for.  The window still needed a better fix than duct tape.  Got it in on time.  Nothing done that day.  Supposed to be done by lunch the next day.  Technician gone to lunch that day.  Still nothing done.  Done with Michael's Automotive.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Finally tried The Refinery, and we were very satisfied. We sat upstairs on the outside patio. It is covered, and they have fans, but the hot and humid of our summer was still dreadful. We had our little dog with us, so we suffered and survived.

We had a Sirloin Steak Sandwich on sweet Hawaiian bread with pesto and onion rings on it. It was pretty big so it was good for two people. We also tried their sweet biscuit debris. It's like funnel cake. It was served with blackberry preserves. Both were delicious. We are dying to try their dinner too sometime.

Great Great View!  That's about it!  Drinks were not good. We ordered Strawberry Mojitos, not much flavor or anything. A lady had a pina colada and that looked pretty and yummy.

We had a cool looking seafoot cocktail. It was different types of seafood in a martini glass. Great presentation but very small for the inflated price. Then again, we were in a touristy area. We also had salads with that. No big dealio. Our bill ended up being like 60. You know that drinks too always inflate your bill. It was a bummer for a pricey place, but sure did have a beautiful view!

No to the No. Service was eh, and food was bland. My enchiladas where like 2 second tossed together with barely any sauce or cheese, didn't event taste like enchiladas. There were a bunch of orders including a Molcajete, nachos, chicken fingers and fries, sopapillas and churros. all of it did not taste fresh or anything may just fresh from the freezer. There are just two varieties of margaritas lime and strawberry, that's it. but it tasted more like alcohol and less of anything else. yes, i know alcohol is good but a strawberry margarita is a strawberry margarita not a bottle of tequila.

Love La Michoacana!! I don't necessarily know if this is a chain or franchise or what. But the first time, I've been to one was in Chicago. They are very bright colored and have all types of fun ice cream flavors. They also have Mexican desserts and street eats and popsicles(palettas), fruit drinks, mango desserts. All kinds of fun sweet yummy desserts here.

Their ice cream can be quite unique like rice pudding and flan flavor. It's also sooo creamy.... my chocolate covered strawberry was sooo good!! I want another one. This is also in what seems to be a newer shopping plaza in Plant City!

Thanks to my coworkers I was able to try Amici's twice. 

I've tried a sausage pizza, white pizza, chicken wings, garlic knots, and potato ball. My favorites were the potato ball and the garlic knots by far. I'd definitely order those first.

I can't speak for pizza. Being from Chicago pizza is different. I've seen pics of Sicilian pizza which have sparked my attention. Maybe next time I will try it.

Amici's has been around for a while and now they have a new building. I've visited it before but my first impression was that it was extremely loud. So if I were to order on my own, I would take it to go.

Caramel pretzel was my pick of the day in a Yomo dessert treat rather than a big ol cup of fro yo. You can find this in the freezer. It is a frozen yogurt creamy popsicle and I loved the sweet and savory.

There are a bunch of different flavors and toppings, and of course sample it all. It's bright and fun inside, as well as the people working there are just as friendly.

Yogurt Mountain is totally a fitting name for this place. If you are like my hubby, you will spend at least an hour concocting your perfect yogurt mountain, and by that time, it will be a slippery melted slope, so don't take forever and enjoy!!!

I've been here a good number of times, and there is nothing but good experiences here. My last time here was today to get some cash. I wanted particular types of bills. One of the girls who I had seen there often is always so helpful. I hadn't used the fancy screen computer to request money before. She helped me out nicely with a big smile. She welcomed Mocha, my doggie, and she wished me a happy birthday. The computer system has all your information, so whomever developed their program made sure to add that special personal touch. It is a nice feeling. I love how modern this chase is, and I love the great customer service.

First time I was here I had the gnocci and was not happy.  If my friend did not ordered a pizza we probably would not have come back.  The pizza is very good and I have not ventured off to try anything else.  So I can only recommend the pizza at this point.  The service can be hit or miss but we keep coming back at least a couple times a month. - Update 11-1-10 - My friend and I are now addicted to their pizza.  The service has been great.  We go there at least once a week and they know our order when we come through the door.  I tried the spaghetti once, it was good.  I will update if I ever try anything else.

If ever a Starbucks needed a location makeover, the Paoli Starbucks was it. To actually have adequate parking at the Paoli Starbucks fulfilled a desperate need for them. 

But sitting here, I feel like they didn't quite get the seating area right. I've been in more comfortable Starbucks before. I feel like they missed an opportunity to add more comfort seating, instead they went with harder tables. They could have added more outlets for laptop use, but I don't see as many. 

There are a lot of improvements. But they could have done better.

The way I'd describe the food here is that it has a sneaky intoxicating flavor. 

It didn't appear that it was going to be like that. But tasting the enchilada was an experience like no other. It had a flavor I couldn't describe but made me want to devour it. Not too spicy but very bold in its own way. 

My wife felt the same way about the fajitas. They don't look too flavorful. But she raved about them. 

I loved the guacamole. I didn't love the rice and beans. But I'd forgive that for the enchiladas. 

Not a perfect meal. But a very good one for the most part.

I've been coming here recently to get some items cleaned and tailored.  This location has proven to be quite reliable.  

They've gotten out stains that I've asked them to.  They've repaired tears that i've asked them to.  They told me they'd have my suit ready three days from now when I need it.  

Prices are probably comparable to the competition, but I haven't done any comparison shopping lately.  This is a small location.  But, they're doing the job well for me, they're located around the corner from me, and in the end that's all I need from them.  They'll get the job done.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
This is one of those places I'd give 3.5 stars to. 

I liked everything I ate. Some of it fell short of the "I'm a fan" experience for me. But still better quality than a lot of Delco Chinese takeout joints. 

I was in an appetizer mood. Steamed dumplings had just enough flavor. Could have used a little more meat and less dumpling but that's a personal taste. Fried scallops had a nice sweetness and it's a quality deal with the fried rice. I even enjoyed a taste of the cheesesteak egg roll which was solid. 

The place is solid. Better dumplings might have gotten it the 4th star from me. But it's good enough.

Do they do an adequate job and get your clothes back to you clean and pressed? Yes

Do I want to give them my money in the future when there are other dry cleaners? No

Why you ask? They are not friendly. 

I read a few other reviews before dropping my clothes off and noticed that a few people mentioned that they were rude but I was hoping that they may have caught them on a bad day. I am guessing that good days or bad days their customer service could still use some work. I will be taking my business elsewhere next time.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
I have been here twice in two weeks if that tells you anything! 
This place is fantastic! In the previous reviews the commented on the appearance of the place and to be honest they are accurate. It is nothing to look at on the inside or the outside but to me it looks and feels very clean which is a huge plus for me! 
The menus.... yes plural.... are very self explanatory and everything we ordered was great from salads, to crab rangoons, to sushi! The prices are unbelievable and totally worth it! I will definitely be back and will be bringing sushi lovers with me!

My roommate and I went on a hunt to find a sushi place close to our downtown apartment. We had walked by Sushi on the Rocks plenty of times previously so we decided to stop in. The place was full so we had to wait. Once we got seated at the bar we realized the bar tenders were pouring sweat, apparently the air conditioner had gone out .
But back to the food- I ordered my standard- Spider roll. It was decent and my Philly roll was pretty good too. Nothing out of the ordinary. Overall I would say this place in OK. Would I go back for Sushi?? Probably not. But  I imagine its not a shabby place to grab drinks with friends some weekend night.

I don't know- just wasn't a big fan of this place. Salsa was average. The salsa fresca was tasty but boring and the other salsa was ridiculously hot. Our queso appetizer was a greasy mess of cheese, my $9 margarita was average and not worth $9, and the carnitas tacos that I had as a main course was slightly greasy and kind of boring.. Overall average Mexican food (I'm cursing all the amazing joints on the west coast that have turned me into a Mexican food snob). Where are the tasty cheap taquerias in Philly??

The plain exterior gives you no inkling of what waits inside. Modern, new, yet cozy.. The perfect coffee shop. Would the tea live up to it's surroundings? Unfortunately no.. I ordered a chai latte which left much to be desired in the chai realm. The foam with the latte was perfect, but the chai sorely lacked that wonderful spiciness of chai. My red velvet cupcake, although moist, was equally disappointing. There was something amiss with the cake and it just didn't taste quite right. This place is way too nice and inviting inside to not return, but next time I'm ordering something else..

Gia Nina's has something for everyone here... The pizza is about as good as you'll get... They have sandwiches also... But their dinners are what will bring you back if you're dining in.. It's a byob, and they added a live entertainer on the weekend nights that plays old Italian songs... The last evening that I was there, there was a dude there playing an accordian and singing.. lol.. yes, I said an accordian... I was entertained.. It kind of reminded me of a Mexican restaurant in Wilmington where a trio comes around with guitars playing and singing...

I wasn't in the mood for the usual cheese steaks, burgers, fries, etc when I got finished playing at Parx this afternoon. So I decided to stop in here for some tacos on my  way home. This is my second time eating here, and re food wasn't as good as it was the first time, but still not bad. The store from front to back has plenty of Mexican groceries, snacks, and pastries. The only downside was that even though the menu is in Spanish and English, ordering was a chore.... which made me wonder if I was actually going to receive what I ordered, or what they thought I ordered. 
Either way, I did enjoy the meal and would stop back again.

I won't stay at this hotel again for the following reasons:

-The lobby is a ghost town. The actual front desk is never staffed, you have to walk around the fireplace to the SPG desk to check in
-The maid is entirely inconsistent and doesn't pay attention to the DND placard or its absence
-The restaurant is overpriced. I'm a business traveler and it's not my money and it's still pricey
-There is always only one valet. They also accept call downs but don't get your car because they're so swamped

Just no. No thanks.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The best authentic local tacos I've had in the area. I've been searching far and wide. I tried this place on recommendation from a friend after moving form the city to within 15 mins or so and it did not disappoint. The search is over. If you want great authentic tacos, come here. 

Los mejores tacos locales auténticos que he tenido en la zona. He estado buscando por todas partes. Probé este lugar por recomendación de un amigo después de mudarme de la ciudad a 15 minutos o así y no me decepcionó. La busqueda se acabó. Si quieres tacos auténticos geniales, ven aquí.

I have a real soft spot for Happy Garden, even though I've been told it's not "real" Chinese food. To be honest, I'm not really sure what that means.

Happy Garden is a simple, family-owned restaurant located in Parkallen. What they lack in interior decor, they more than make up for in delicious food. Whether or dining in, or grabbing something for take-away, you're in for something delicious.

Faves at this place include the moo shu pork and the szechuan beef. If you want cheap, quick Chinese that makes you happy, you should try Happy Garden.

this is my first time at vons, since in the bay, its mostly safeway. anyways, i do like it, everything is easy to find. i was looking for apples and this guy graciously helped me and at the same time let me take a sample of their apple! he like cut a small piece out for me! what a nice guy/employee and that shows great service! Anyways, everything looks fresh, they categrozied things in good order so it wasnt' hard to find. it does get real busy with long lines at times! exit fairview to get here, they have good gas prices too!

The rolls were not alot. About 4-5 pieces for rainbow, hip hop, edomasa and spider. I was a bit dissapointed because for the price of the sushi, it wasn't that great. the highlight of this meal was the cucumber sumono salad! it was DELICIOUS. by far the best out of itsuki, sushi teri. I also liked their tempura green tea ice cream!! sooo good! i'd reccomend that! It was just so yummy in your tummy! Our total was about 90 bucks but that was EXPENSIVE. our waitress wasn't that nice but it was alright since it was a busy night. You know this place is legit when they are japanese!

Gourmet fast food. What a concept. I wish we had one of these in Nashville too (echoing Misty C.'s  lament). Wolfgang Puck's, even though it's a chain reminds me of the sandwich shops you see in New York City or in Europe, places you can go to get a good, healthy, unfried lunch. There are soups and sandwiches as well as heartier fare like mac and cheese and pizzas. 

It is a hybrid between a sit-down restaurant and fast food because the food is sit-down restaurant quality done quickly, and for a reasonable price. I wish we had more options like this downtown, where there's either fast food or expensive gourmet.

I've stayed here a few times now. I like the hotel a lot. The biggest downside is the lack of decent restaurants within walking distance. However, the rooms are large and clean and quiet. The staff is super helpful. You CAN get meals delivered to your room, a fact I learned only after a dinner acquired from a vending machine.
There is plenty of parking and free and fairly fast wi-fi.
The breakfast buffet is great and they have bigger than normal coffee cups, which saves a trip or two to the coffee machine.
I will be back!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This place is literally right down the street from our apartment, so I was surprised when my boyfriend sent me a link to this page and I had never heard of it before!  We ended up going there last night with his family and had a great dinner.  Good atmosphere- almost all the tables were full.  I had the mushroom soup and the Linguine Valentino- both delicious.  The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because it wasn't exceptional.  The dishes are very simple, but that's what makes for good Italian food anyway.  About $30 a head for appetizer/main entree plus BYOB, always a plus.

For all of the cute places offered in downtown Zionsville, I was disappointed that my first restaurant experience was here. With lively Friendly's across the street, that's where I really wanted to spend my evening. Even so, I was more than happy to give Zionsville Pizzeria a shot. 

Well. The pizza? It was good, but not great. The service? It was good, but not great. Not that this is a necessity, but apparently this place used to serve alcohol but that's no longer the case. Kind of a bummer, huh. Just not my favorite place. Sorry!

This is a cute restaurant right off Binford Blvd. that I'm surprised I just found this year! During my last visit it was lunchtime and I ordered their soup and sandwich combo -- chicken velvet soup and a chicken salad sandwich. It was incredibly tasty and was very affordable. Their bar area looked nice, so I'd like to try that out sometime soon. 

The only issue I found was that you couldn't really tell if this place was open or not as all windows were dark and it was a last minute "ok let's check to see if it's open" moment that made us take the plunge to walk in. 

Other than that - great place! Had a very "Sahm's Restaurant" feel to it.

Nothing special about this particular Chase -- it gets the job done. ha I find it hard to write reviews over banks simply because Chase, as a whole, usually does a good job of taking care of my beloved cash money. This Chase is close to work, so there have been a couple of times I have needed to run to the bank during my lunch hour. They're quick and efficient with whatever I request, so I thank them for that service! I've yet to have any issues with Chase and love that they are literally all over Indianapolis. I had to switch banks when I first moved here and Chase seemed like the right choice. So, here I am - still - a happy Chase customer.

I can't speak to the sushi because I'm not in a sushi mood during the winter, but I have come here twice with a couple of coworkers for lunch and they always get sushi- I trust their opinions. They know food.

I usually get the chicken teriyaki lunch special, which comes with a bowl of miso soup and some white rice. For $8 it's a nice, filling, hot meal.

My only complaint is the service. We've sat for 20 minutes before even having our order taken before. This is not the place to come when you only have an hour for lunch.

This is one of the rare pizza places in Philly to offer gluten-free pizza crust. Unlike Slice, this crust was a bit larger and thicker, so the pizza was actually pretty substantial. However, there's no vegan cheese, so you lacto- gluten-intolerant folks will have to go cheese-less or just suck it up like I did.

I went with the philly cheesesteak pizza (crazy impulse) and E went with a regular pepperoni. The regular pizza was fine. My pizza was also fine, but the crust was a bit on the pasty side. The chicken tender platter was probably the highlight - good tenders. All in all it was fine, but not terribly memorable.

I love the DJs that spin here. Unfortunately I feel like I'm the only one. For the most part people rather have their noses up in the air or worry about how they are going to cheat on their wives with someone 10-20 years younger than them than have a good time. Their loss. 

The DJs play some awesome mashups. Great stuff to dance to. Yet people rarely do. Although if you can manage to order a drink and ignore the yuppies you may end up having a decently good time.

I would give it a wavering three to two stars depending on the night. But Yelp won't let me.

A great little neighborhood pizza place. The pizza is a thinner crust that is very crispy and delicious. My favorite pizzas have been the Margherita and the steak and cheese. They frequently run of basil for the margherita, but you can sub spinach which is totally different but still good. 

I have only done carry out, they do have a few tables for dining in but only a few. 

Only knocks are that the breadsticks are pretty uninteresting and carry out orders usually take about ten minutes longer than they say to be ready.

they carry Fresh Corn on the Cob from My Dad's Sweet Corn, the best sweet corn i've ever tasted (& i've ate a Lot of corn) they also have FAB BOO BOO insulated bags (that keep things cold for up to 5 hours, can you say Chicago road trip) that zip (FINALLY) ($7.99)
you'll most likely find me in the Sauce aisle ( & not the liquor one) where you can find some of the most interesting combos
sorry to say they DON'T give bag credits
i'm a Bag Lady at heart, (before it was Green) i wasn't voted Miss Trash 1991 for nothing!!! LOL
LOVE their wrap around deli too
park on the roof if the parking lot is full !!!

Illy coffee ~ $14

Good people, good food.  Max and his wife started this place just a couple years ago and are doing well.  Large all-you-can-eat bar (20+ people) and tables with AYCE too!  Running special, buy one beer or sake, get one free. And with AYCE lunch at just $14 you can't go wrong (dinner I think $19).  Few new additions to the menu: deep fried upside-shrimp, yeah!, and hand grenades! Also, get a Godzilla roll or Caterpillar for lunch (don't see that everywhere).  Free apps with AYCE too: steamed muscles, miso, potsticker...etc. Try the 5-alarm, with habenjeros...if...you think you can handle it?!

Am I the only person to give this hole in the wall a mediocre review? 

I had just a "meh" experience here. I waited here forever with a friend to see what all the hype was about, and was disappointed. I got the spicy tuna roll, and it was waaaay too mayonnaise-y, and I could taste a fishy smell. Spicy tuna is the one roll that's supposed to be impossible to mess up, too.

Anyway, I don't think I'll be back. (1) It's not close enough for me to make any effort to get to it, and (2) I'd rather not wait for mediocrity.

Totally a delivery review since I have never been here in person. 

I honestly can't believe how many times I ordered food from here even after always being disappointed with everything they make. I was going through authentic Mexican food withdrawal and this place delivered to where I was living at the time. I remember their food was okay for when I needed a fix but most of the stuff was somewhat bland and the service was absent-minded and unprofessional. No matter how many times you ask for extra sauce they never bring it.

Prices are too high for what they actually give you. I won't order from here again.

I went for lunch and the service was really slow and not all that friendly..  The food was decent.  It wasn't anything to go running back for.  

I've eaten at many Italian restaurants around the world, but mostly in LA, NY, and Italy; and Vivace just doesn't hit the spot for me.  Perhaps it's one of the best Italian restaurants in Tucson, but since I travel back to LA every few months I'd rather just wait till I'm back there.

Based on food alone I'd probably give Vivace 3 stars(being on the generous side).  Factor in the service and the price they charge for the level of food being served I can only justify 2 stars.

Absolutely loved the food, ambience & service! But the desserts were the real winners of the night. We were able to get a reservation at one of the tables near the window so we had both an intimate experience but with plenty of natural light. The Scallops app & Spanish Octopus app were as beautiful as they were delicious. I ordered the duck breast which was super moist and perfectly flavored. For dessert we had the Peach Creamsicle pudding and the Sticky Toffee Pudding cake which were perfection. Would highly recommend and will definitely come back. And it's BYOB. All things awesome.

Was hoping for UNO or better than UNO za' but it's very close 

As other reviewers have mentioned..there is not place to sit down and eat..only an ordering bar with 4 stools mainly meant for waiting for your za' order not for eating at. 

We go the pizza to go anyhow. Took it back to the hotel. 

Was very tasty ! 

The one big bonus I have to give them is a large pizza that would easily feed 6 was only $18. This size deep dish would have cost $35 at UNO's. 

Very nice owner, family pictures plastered all over the inside. 

Nice little hole in the wall Chicago deep dish pizza joint.

Went on a Saturday, knew it would be busy and I was willing to wait but they had blocked off services because they were "too busy". The cap to my antena came off which HAS NEVER HAPPENED in any carwash. They were closed Sunday so I went Monday and they said they hadn't found it. Which I almost expected BUT then this guy came and LIED to my face about remembering putting the antenna cap back on my car. That's really what pissed me off. Shady business practices, will never bring any car there again and will definitely warn friends and family.

This restaurant is a pretty good rendition of the typical Mexican-American restaurant. They serve chips and a quasi-spicy salsa to start. The chips were nice and crispy without being too oily. I ordered the lunch special of chicken fajitas. They tasted great. I filled my flour tortilla with chicken, beans, Mexican rice, cheese, guac, sour cream and a little lettuce. The amount of sides they bring is perfect and will fill you up! 

The service was pretty good as well, perhaps a little on the "fend for yourselves" side, but nothing to complain about. All in all, a good experience.

We had another wonderful experience at Caffe Casta Diva last night...

The Salumi Platter is great.  Wish it came with some cheeses to make it a meat & cheese platter.  (See Mercato's Menu)

The New York Strip was cooked perfectly.  The potatoes with the steak were fried slices and lacked a little flavor.

The Scallops were unbelievable. Four large scallops on a bed of truffle infused Risotto.  I can't stop thinking about the dish into the next day.

BYOB!

Cash only :-(

Definitely go support Caffe Casta Diva.  You'll need to make reservations.

Don't get your hopes up or travel long distances to eat here.  This place is a normal Chinese Buffet.  The food is not bad.  They have a larger amount of Sushi than most buffets.  I was'nt to satisfied with it.  But that's me.  Mongolian Chicken is great,  General Tso's Chicken, thumbs up!!! It had a little kick like its supposed to. The chicken and broccolli was wierd tasting.  Basically this is a normal buffet that has pizza, french fries and fried chicken for kids.  Than the Chinese part thats pretty good.  Better than some buffets. They also have the grill where the chef will cook you up some meat/fish/vegatables on the grill.

This has become my go-to place for a one-on-one business lunch.  Incredibly unique menu with great variety.  Always a nice crowd.  Service is steady and friendly, bit slow if you don't have reservations as the front doesn't always seem on top of things.  Valet parking a nice touch.  Bit dark and noisy inside, however the decor overall I consider handsome and relaxing.  Historical reproductions line the walls, fun to read.  Small patio for outdoor seating will be nice in the warmer months.  Every visit I try a new menu item and have yet to be let down.  Truly a local gem with great character.

I bring my son here for his haircuts and the Stylists consistently do a great job. They maintain a computerized record of the clippers that were previously used, so there is no guesswork in trying to figure out what made the last haircut so great. The salon is tastefully decorated and I've never had to wait more than about 20 minutes - usually there is no wait at all early on a Saturday morning or weekday evenings. You can also use the computer check in service to reduce your wait, but I haven't found the need. They have lolipops for the kids after a job well done. High

Decent food for Wendys.  The sweet tea was far, far, far too sweet even by southern standards.  I threw 80% of it away.

Also, the above reviewer is wrong.  There are tons of options around the area which are both tastier and healthier than Wendys around the Vanderbilt University Medical Center.  Most run in the $8 to $10 range.  In the potentially tastier category:

1) Sam and Zoes (this one is a hidden gem) and just across the street.  It gets amazing reviews
2) Calypso Cafe (this one gets great reviews too) and its just down the road.
3) Chains like Applebees and Logans

The food is excellent, the service is attentive and South-Philly-authentic.  

Crowds at this no-rez institution can get pretty crazy, but Fridays are much more tolerable than Saturdays.  Arrive by 6 if you can to avoid a very long wait.

A note to the owners:  *PLEASE* consider some allowance for BYO, or at least upgrade your wine list to include some better selections.  A decent bottle of vino is a must with Italian food (if you're like me!) and the crap you offer (sorry to be so blunt... but crap is the right word) does not do justice to your food.

My opinion of this place has gotten steadily better over the years.  Been to many Italian BYOs and I have to say that the quality and consistency of the food and service at Trattoria Alla Costiera has improved to the point where the place is... well.. pretty darn good.

We last went with a fairly large group and weren't expecting much and we were all quite happy, especially when the very reasonable check came!

The atmosphere is a bit kitschy, but our friends dining with us who had just come back from two weeks in Italy were impressed by the authenticity of the kitsch!

Minor suggestion for improvement:  Play better music!

There was a line out the door!  They have implemented a new fee for lost receipts.  This kinda peeved me.  I always leave my receipts at the dry cleaner.  There was no mention of it when I dropped off.  

They also needed an ID card, I come in twice a week every week.  I was a little miffed about having to go to my car to get id since you pay at drop off.  Now I understand the line!      

When I got back and showed her "my papers".  She forgot about the fee.  Since I am a good customer and did not want to delay the ever growing line, I did not remind her about the fee.  :)
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Santa got my letter!  All mac and cheese?  All the time?  Really, what's not to love?  Unless you don't love mac and cheese.  In which case, reading reviews of Swallow seems like a waste of your time. 

The interior is beautifully grandma chic, and the service is friendly.  My friend got the Italian, and I got gruyere, asiago, and shrimp.  The plates are large and super delicious.  Not as good as my mom's mac and cheese, but what is?  The trade off is having mac and cheese of every possible design at your disposal.  Oh, and they give you free beer, if that's something you're into, which you probably are.

The hotel is right in the middle of everything. Rooms are not big but prefect for business travel. Easy check in and check out. Snacks, drinks and computers available in the lobby. WIFI for the room along with secured printing. Hotel is very clean and reasonable for costs. I was on the 11th floor and the noise from outside was amazingly loud. First general street noise then the garbage being picked up sound like it was right outside my window. Nice hotel for easy in and out, clean and friendly but they need to do some kind of soundproofing.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I try to like this location, I really do. But I don't believe I have ever gone here and not waited more than 10-15 minutes for a drink. While I understand there are busy times in the coffee business, I feel this location just can't quite figure out efficiency. Sadly, I waited 10 minutes in line to get to the register and another 20 for my drink. 

All came out fine. Thankful for that. If you're in a hurry and need a drink quickly, don't go here. 

*the app doesn't show this location as a mobile order location---at least it hasn't for me. Not sure why. *

I am a huge fan of sushi so when I have opportunities to visit restaurants with a wide variety of sushi, I make it a priority to get there. Ichiban is a cute, cozy place located in a strip mall on US 31 but don't let the location fool you. Once you enter, you are instantly greeted with a kind server who quickly takes you to your seat. The menu options are wonderful and you can see the sushi artists crafting your next roll in the front room of the restaurant. Everything is fresh and delicious....just as sushi should be. The kid's menu is great, too. You won't be disappointed in this favorite spot in town.

If you need a cheap, warm, sugary treat and you're in Center City, this is your fix. The coffee is acceptable but nothing special. I haven't been there on a week day, but I stopped in for coffee and a glazed donut on a Sunday afternoon. The trash was overflowing and as mentioned in other reviews, the staff seems to be hit-or-miss. But let's be honest: you're stopping in and getting your daily diabetes special, then heading out. It's not the kind of atmosphere where you're going to lounge around and people-watch.

This place in my opinion is just good. It's sold as a high end place, but compared to other remarkable Italian restaurants in Philly (I'm looking at you Vetri), I see it as one tier below the Italian restaurants I'm sure it's comparing itself to. The popovers were good, but not as delicious as I've had at Barclay Prime. The food itself is also solid, but again, it's a place that other people love, but for me, it is not going to be the first place (nor in top 10) that I recommend for people asking for a high dining place.

Greasy spoon alert ! This place is king of the chinese food greasy spoons. It's grimy exterior and location make this place a #1 stop for my greasy needs. I know if anyone has ever gone here they think (maybe even know..) that it's pretty gross haha. Regardless, the food is still good, and I always come back. It's cheap menu with endless options will fill your belly for under $10 bucks. My favorite to get here is the chicken cubes kai lan chow mein, I love the chow mein noodles here.. Perfectly crispy.  My only suggestion to squeamish folk is to wear a blindfold until you get your food.

HEADLINE: Great location, but poor cleaning crew and loud A/C unit in room

The hotel is perfectly located if you want to be close to the airport. It is literally a 5 minute walk from baggage claim. 

And the hotel looks nice and clean and the rooms are sizable and comfy.  

However, our room was poorly cleaned (there was used soap in the shower & newspaper in the trash can) and so we didn't feel the cleaning policies are up to snuff. 

Also, the heater in the room is unacceptably loud and makes for a horrible night's sleep. The hotel offers ear plugs for that issue instead of replacing heaters...seriously???
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I have been here multiple times, probably my favorite east side sushi joint. I always order the spanish mackerel - mackerel is not for everyone, but it is very fresh and well prepared here. I also enjoy the jalapeno/ blue crab roll, the Oregon roll, the spicy yellow tail and the yummy yummy roll.

Keep an eye out for the specials (they have them posted all around the restaurant on hand written signs. The only non-sushi items we've ever ordered was the chicken fried rice and seafood udon. Both were good but all around pretty standard.

The biggest upside is that this place is very central and easy to get to. However, its specific location is pretty shady. The consensus seems to be that this place is run down, smelly, dingy and shady (which it is). However, the key question for us central people; do you want to drive all the way up to Lee Lee's? Nope. Therein lies why I schlep down once in a while to restock on bulk kimchee, nori, Rousong, mochi, fish sauce, frozen packaged dim sum and various other staples in my kitchen. My advice is to stick with the non-perishable items.

Come during happy hour and the sushi is half-priced cheap. The half-priced menu rotates daily, making it one of the cheaper places in town. The atmosphere is nice with curtained booths and an indoor waterfall. 

The sushi itself is just okay. It's usually rather quickly made and the fish isn't the absolute freshest. Some of the rolls are better than others, and you should plan around this when considering what day to go. The service can be slow depending on how full the restaurant (which is typically on the "good roll" days). I agree with previous posters, this place is either a hit or miss.
