It's safe to say that Nico's is probably the only place that I actually hate. That being said, my family eats at various Nicos all the time - I guess it's a hit or miss sort of thing. . 

For me it is a big MISS... I dislike the burritos with just bland meat and beans - and then they charge you extra for all of the lettuce, salsa, cheese, sour cream etc, (that should automatically come with the burrito wtf?). The guac is also a pretty foul runny sauce (forget trying to find a real chunk of avocado in that mess). The tacos are bland and greasy and pretty much taste the same no matter what flavor you get. Blah

It's very centrally located, in SoBro.   Just 2 blocks from Broadway and all the bars, restaurants, and live music everywhere!!! Yet far enough to relax and unwind. The standard rooms and very nice and recently remodeled. We had a King bed (which was very comfortable) and lots of pillows. The bed sheets and covers where white cotton and very clean and soft. Our room also had an "L" shaped sofa and table. The bathroom was newly remodeled with glass showers and new fixtures!  They have free breakfast and WiFi. Room rates are a fair price but parking is an additional $32 per day.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
reviews on yelp made me question coming here. but having determined and acknowledge Nashville is simply not a "real" food town 
(sorry, it seems to be true!), i decided to keep it low key and hit a "local" pizza joint. 

 it was fun, lively, and the food was quite good. 2 for 1 draft beer "specials" actually are apparently always on.  The spinach salad was good, the ultra thin crust "happy family' pizza, great-- i didn't find the ultra-thin cracker-esque at all, as at least one other reviewer has suggested.  i thought it was quite good.  friendly staff was attentive though quite busy.  recommended.

Wife and I were on a spring break and we're staying at the Hampton inn at Metaire. The room was high priced though probably not for the area, but the room was worn, chair had cig burn marks and stain, bed cover had stains and the powdered sugar that I got on the carpet from the beignets I ate stayed for the two days before we checked out. The room had a musty odor. Even though we were on fifth floor, we were just level with top of interstate so view of downtown was interrupted constantly by traffic   Breakfast was traditional hotel fare.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Wife and I had a conference that was hosted at the Westin, so we booked a couple of extra days. I know all hotels do this but price swing of $89 to over $300 for same room kinda gets me. If I was paying $89 then this is a 5 star. When you get to the $200 range and up, then I expect more.

Room was nice and staff was accommodating. Vehicle Access in and out of hotel is a bit cumbersome as with many downtown hotels.

Room could use a deep cleaning and the hotel phone in our room did not work so we had to use cell to call front desk. And as with most hotels, you need better lighting in room and bath.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Wait-how has bacon not been put into a sushi roll before? It's on everything else and yet Fat Salmon is the first sushi place I've ever been to that has it as a roll.  Honestly, it gets 4 stars for this reason alone.

This is a cute little sushi bar.  It reminds me of a Japanese fast food restaurant with the cutesy character on the menu.  It is small though, so even at 8 on a Tues we had to wait 20 minutes for a table.  

I liked the variety of special rolls they had. Besides the BCT which had the bacon, I tried several others that were all reasonably priced and fairly unique.  It is easy to see why this is considered one of the best in Philly.

Let me say that I had no problems with service or price. The pizza just didn't do it for me. I was enticed by their commercial for the new "Zesty Jalapeno and Meats" pizza. Yes, I"ve eaten Papa John's before but was not a big fan. Guess what - still not. The pizza was hot but fairly bland, even for a "zesty" pizaa. And that sauce - way too sweet. It overpowers the rest of the pizza (and that is saying a lot when there are jalapenos on top!)
Bottom line - I'll stick with Peel, Pizza Hut, Joe's, and Pizza World.

The staff at Los Tres Amigos for our visit were not at the top of their game but at least we had a free show. 

It was a dark and stormy night, so maybe everyone had called in sick? We had to ask 3 times for my Diet Coke, and despite the better half asking for "No Lemons" we got LOTSA LEMONS!

I found my Seafood Enchiladas to be somewhat lackluster, and included more fish than shrimp.  The better half had the Fajitas which seemed pretty tasty.

If this *is* the service all the time, I can't imagine coming back.

As an average person I suppose my biggest complaint is that Yellow Porch is "Gourmet" all the way. Right down to the portions. Where my palate and wallet both more exotic, perhaps my rating would be higher. 

The food is delicious without a doubt, but I had a hard time not comparing the meal I ordered with the same portion I would get for the same price at J. Alexander's. 

The service was great, and we sat outside which was also a wonderful dining experience. 

At Dinner time it was pretty busy, so parking might be difficult.

Good food at what is essentially a sports bar.  Two major drawbacks though. First if you go at night and sit near the windows IT IS DARK. I literally had to turn the flashlight on my phone on so I could read both the menu and the check.  Second, if you order a sandwich, the sides are À la carte.  I was frustrated by what was basically "French Fry Gravel" but the waitress didn't charge me for it after I pointed it out. 

I absolutely enjoyed my sandwich though and i would come back, but I will make sure its in the light of day.

Stopped in on Saturday for the new Ruby Tuesday's Brunch. I would describe it as decent but pricey.  The REAL problem seems to be:  "Don't Be First".  The Brunch offers free biscuits with your meal, but they don't start cooking them until the first person arrives.. Which is great, UNLESS YOU ARE THE FIRST PERSON. I suspect Ruby Tuesdays needs to advertise a little better for the Brunch or lower the price a bit because for the entire meal, it was just my girlfriend and I.

The food itself WAS very good, but we spent an hour total waiting for all the courses to arrive and the bill at the end was nearly 40 dollars with tip.

Dropping a star from my previous review. They REALLY need to bring another wait person on weekend evenings. On our last visit, we waited for 15 minutes to get menus, and ten minutes later still no one came to take our drink or food orders. To add insult to injury of having to take our empty stomach elsewhere, we also lost some quarters on the bowling arcade machine. Apparently they had lost the ball/puck. 

Get your act together Melt and properly staff your night shifts! No thanks for that 30 minutes of my life you just wasted.

Wow! Worst Chinese delivery I have ever gotten.. period! 
I ordered the shrimp in chili sauce for lunch, with the hot and sour soup, and white rice instead of fried rice. I only got the fried rice and no soup! To add insult to injury, the shrimp was simply disgusting. It was overcooked beyond edibleness.. hard and chewy! 

I like to give restaurants the benefit of a doubt but this was so sub-par that I will not order from here ever again. Thanks Hunan Star for ruining my workday lunch! One of the few bright spots of the day that I look forward to....

I eat at Whole Foods A LOT.  I get coffee on the way to work, eat there for lunch, shop on the way home, etc.  And, when I travel for work and play, I often rely on Whole Foods to eat healthfully on the road.

But, the Franklin Whole Foods is NASTY.  One would expect the salad bar to have things like mixed greens.  Or cucumbers that aren't translucent.  Or for there still to be food on the hot bar, or sushi in the case at 7pm.  I expect an abundance of deliciousness should I try to eat at Whole Foods. Sadly, this location does not deliver.  At all.  I am going to have to start staying in Green Hills so that I can go to that location!

We went to dinner on a Friday night about 6:30. We'd called ahead and made a reservation not knowing if it would be busy or not. We walked in and were greeted right away. Staff was very friendly and welcoming. They brought us hot towels to freshen up. All we ordered was sushi and it came out very quickly. The Vegas Roll was IMO the best one. I also recommend the Caterpillar roll. I think the overall value was really good for our party of 6. We even got dessert afterwards. Reasonably priced.  We'd defintely go back again

Chips tasted stale. Salsa was heavy with cilantro, and seeing I have a genetic flaw that causes me to loath cilantro because it taste like soap, another ding. BUT, the chicken quesadilla was stellar.  Chicken was tender juicy and a flavor bomb, with some yummy cheese that wrapped it up in a warm gooey blanket.

My three other dining companions loved their respective meals of a burrito, tacos and some massive seafood, chorizo, chicken and meat bowl that stupid huge.  

Beer selection was garbage for a beer snob.  Margarita was a stiff one, I will tell ya that.

The biggest problem about Racanelli's is that the locations can vary quite a bit.  Probably my biggest beef with all the Racanelli's in general is that the employees frequently seem entirely disinterested in their work here.  

My favorite location, by far, was the U City location.  The unsuccessful attempt at a bar was its undoing, and I'm pretty sure it would still be successful there.  Alas... it WAS my favorite location until the guy who typically did the pizza there left... and opened some other place...

Durango can actually get pretty crowded during the lunch hour, but that would only mean that you get your drinks a little late.  It seems to have little impact on their ability to churn their food out to you.  

Their tongue tacos, fish tacos, and sopes are awesome.

The fish tacos are actually just stir fried bits of fish that's quite tasty.

Now seriously, I've probably mentioned beef tongue a couple times now.  It's beef.  Delicious flavorful beef.  No, you don't see bumps on it!  Give it a shot.  Durango's a great place to try it.

There really isn't any reason to come here anymore now that Hokkaido's busted into the scene... but this buffet was decent enough.  Pre-hokkaido days I thought the turnover was decent enough to keep the fresh stuff coming out, but then again, my strategy with MOST Chinese buffets is to stick with the chicken-on-a-stick and wings.  Those were solid and I couldn't complain about anything.  

I mean seriously, if I want real Chinese food, I'll go elsewhere.... like Hokkaido.

Hokkaido?  Isn't that Japanese?  It's a Chinese restaurant that just happens to serve some sushi.  Marketing!

You know the more I've eaten here, the more I like this place.  I enjoy the crust, the sauce, and the cheese.  I would go as far as to say that this is my favorite thick crust pizza place in St. Louis.  

Better than Pi?  Yeah.  I said it.

So stop on by if you want a nice robust crispy thick crust, tangy not so sweet tomato sauce, and thick mozzarella cheese at a good price and decent service.

I'm in the middle of a "review update" marathon so I recently wrote about how Spiros NoCo is legit because of the atmosphere.  Same goes for this place with their awesome booths and wood paneling.

Respect.

Good cut and value at $14 but over an hour wait and out of coffee by 9:30 AM on a Sat morning.  Forgetaboutit.  

You need to have more than a single barber working on a Sat. morning.  Like a restaurant not being staffed adequately on a Fri/Sat night.  

Either get here when they open on Sat or roll the dice on how long you will wait.  

A barber that is adequately staffed with upscale amenities would enjoy at least a steady business in the Clayton/University City area and probably rake it in if they had good barbers and advertising.

I just moved out to Nashville for a new job and was in desperate need of a clean up as my last barber jacked my shit UP. 

I found this shop on Yelp and when I asked my friend about Uncles he vouched for them. I booked an online appointment for 9:30 and the cut started at 9:30, pretty rare. 

Caroline was fanfreakintastic. One of the cleaner cuts I've gotten in a long time and she was a joy to speak. Gave me some recommendations for the area I'll be moving too and just pleasant all around. 

I'll be living a good 20 minutes away from here but it might actually be worth the drive. Cheers Caroline!

I like this place simply because it is easy for me to get to and is vegetarian friendly.  However, Koto is just average and could use some more fresh veggies atop the noodles.  The salad dressing is really good and the salad would have been too if it hadn't been premade and a bit frozen from sitting in the cooler.  There is an older guy that makes sushi and I can appreciate his hard work.  My BF said the sushi is pretty good.  If you are in the neighborhood, stop by, it's a cute hole in the wall.  Otherwise, eh, look somewhere else.

Happy eats,
TA

My husband and I were here for a private event so I can't really judge what it is like when it is open to the public for regular service. But I do want to comment that everything we had was delicious and they had a great selection of wines, including an amazing pinot noir (very sadly, I forget the name of). 

The restaurant is small and intimate, inside a bungalow. I would definitely return here for a romantic dinner out. The one and only issue we had was the tiny parking lot, we ended up having to park a few blocks away and walk over.

usually I leave this place wishing I had stayed home and cooked my own dinner.   it's weird because it should be totally awesome because there are several vegetarian and vegan options... but i have tried most of them and it was often mushy and/or lacking flavor.  

Their claim to fame is the vegan sunburger... and twice i went to try it and found that they were out of them for the day (that is why i ate the mush instead).   I did finally get one and i really liked it, but unless you call ahead and ask it's too risky to just show up and expect one.

Sadly instead of "A Full Plate" my friends and I call this place "Aweful Plate".

We stopped here on the final leg of our trip, to catch a flight home from Reno.  We chose it based on location and proximity to the airport and the reputation of comfort inn. The place was fine, no real complaints at all.  It is convenient.  They offered free breakfast--there was the omnipresent waffle maker, the agony of many comfort inn managers.  The breakfast is sufficient.  Bagels, muffins, toast, english muffins, cereal, fruit, juice and coffee. There were the processed scambled eggs, the thin bacon and the decent sausage patty.

The only odd thing was there was no pool there.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I had never been here, so decided to give it a try. Got 3 rolls to test it out...don't waste your money. The rice was too wet & there was too much sauce. Everything was sloppy and all the rolls tasted the same. This place is cheap, but that's all it has going for it. If you want affordably priced yet decent sushi, try Mikimoto or Sake Cafe during happy hour. I've had grocery store sushi that tasted better and was made with more care. I absolutely love sushi but I couldn't even finish the last three pieces because it was so bad. I had tums for dessert.

After 2 visits to SOTR, I am not impressed.  First of all, as other reviewers note...the place just has a funky smell to it.  Drinks are over-priced, sushi is so-so, and the server asked if we needed anything every 3 minutes.  We ordered vegetable tempura for an appetizer, and some of the pieces were still raw in the middle.  We ordered some various nigiri and a few rolls for dinner.  The fish pieces on the nigiri were the thinnest I have ever seen.  We definitely don't see a reason to come back here; There are several great sushi options on the northside including Asaka, Naked Chopstix, and Wasabi...

This is your typical Chinese take-out restaurant. They have lots of tables inside but most of their business looks to be take-out. They have the standard Chinese menu and the food takes like your average Chinese which is a-okay by me considering I've had way worse. The prices are really reasonable. If you're looking for high quality Chinese food but that will cost a lot more go to Gourmet Wok in Chalfont. If you're just looking for a typical Chinese meal that will satisfy your craving (and be easy on your wallet), you'll get that here for sure.

Went on a Sunday night expecting it to be slow...totally not the case. We were lucky to get a table without a reservation so keep that in mind.  It seems they also expected to be slow because they were grossly understaffed which made service pretty slow.  Remember to bring drinks because this is a BYOB (there is a great beer/liquor/wine store across the street). We ordered salads and 5 rolls...I would say all the food was average, nothing to write home about. There is now a new sushi place in New Hope that I would say is better than this place and given the poor service, I likely won't be returning.

Went out to Philly to watch my Braves play. My friend lives in Horsham which is not to far from Ambler so we hit Finn's up to meet with some other people. Cool looking spot with outside seating. This place would do really well in NYC.

The service was great. The waitress was really attentive of us. Cheap beer, outside seating and cool people make it a good time. I had better things to say I guess maybe because I'm not from the area. Being the only place open in the area I think people should have better things to say.

The decor is warm and inviting. I felt very comfortable despite the sterile greeting I received when I walked in the door. I ordered the pork sandwich with broccoli-rob and it was great: the pork was cooked to perfection and was really flavorful. I also really enjoyed the bun the sandwich was on. Next time I order this sandwich I will go no cheese and no broccoli-rob not because it didn't taste good, but because the pork was so well done I didn't need any additional flavors. While my food was excellent my overall dinning experience had room for improvement.

I have noticed that every time I pass by El Grande One Stop Supermarket it is packed. Being curious, I decided to check it out.  The store has a fairly large produce selection. Great place to look if you are looking for items sold in Hispanic countries.  They also carry a large variety of Goya products. However, I think the stores main draw is the meat counter. This is where the majority of the people in the store were gathered while I was looking around.  The meat  prices are reasonable but the stores meat counter didn't look very sanitary.

I recently moved her from Houston and I've seen several of these liquor stores.  This one happens to be conveniently located across from my new apartment complex.  They have a good selection but I find it odd that the prices at Racetrack are cheaper. Coming from Houston I am used to the liquor stores having the better prices on everything.  Including the beer and Lime-a-rita's.  Unless it was one of those small mom and pop jobs.  Oh well, it's the best liquor store I've found in my area so far.  BTW, if you haven't tried a lime-a-rita yet...you're missing out.

I go out to a restaurant to enjoy myself so when there is trickery involved I am not amused.  Another good reason to read Yelp reviews BEFORE trying a place out. This is something I did not do before trying Gallery Eclectic Bistro.  As the previous reviews warn, WATCH YOUR BILL.  I was almost overcharged 15.00 for something I did not order. Plus, the drinks were suppose to be buy one, get one...but I was charged for both before also bringing that to their attention. As former president George W would say..."Fool me once, shame on -- shame on you. Fool me -- you can't get fooled again."

I ordered a poke salad and miso soup to-go...again.  The miso soup was $3.50!!  Kind of expensive to me.  But, smartly, the soup is packaged in an insulated to-go cup, so it was easy to drink on my drive home.  If the weather was cold or if I was sick, the soup would have totally hit the spot.  

I didn't open my order until I got home and was really disappointed to find the poke salad was only grilled bits of tuna covered in a mayo sauce and some avocado, not my idea of a poke salad.  Where was the eel and seaweed?

Best burger in town. I love that this place is close to my apartment. The service from the staff are great and the prices are reasonable. This bar is not the biggest for large crowds, they have one tv and a really bad ass record player. The beer selection is unreal, a lot of beers I've never heard of. I'm not picky, I'll have no problem trying all of them out. They do have wine and liquor but the food is really good. Great veggie and cheese options, plus pickled veggies and spicy pickles. If your a big fan of a good old burger, this place has the best.

I loved this hotel but I think that was due to a combination of Alan at the front desk (above and beyond customer service!!) and knowing I was finally heading home to Detroit.

This hotel is conveniently located inside the Tampa airport.  I dropped off my rental car downstairs, entered the airport like I was heading to a flight then kept walking to the (not very well marked) hotel entrance.

Yes, the room was dated, but it was very clean.  The Marriott bed was amazing.  A bit of air traffic noise, but... uhm... you're at the airport.

Excellent rate at $109 too (when the Hyatt in Dallas' airport wanted $300 earlier in the week!).
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: It was OK, I'd go here again as it seemed to be the best choice in Terminal D. I got a large Yeungling (I'll miss that beer since it's not available in California) and a cheesesteak with whiz. The cheesesteak was pretty good and even big. I got another to bring home to my people and had the server wrap it extra tight. It held up and my people were happy to have it when I got home. I had a male server who was very nice and on the ball, but did notice that the female server seemed to be wandering and kind of out of it. Maybe that happens when you're exposed to jet fumes all day.

Palermo's has great pizza. The sauce is not sweet and fresh, the crust is crispy yet chewy. The white pizza is not greasy as you would expect for a white pizza. The dough under the cheese is not too chewy but also crispy. Sometimes its a little burnt but that is because the dough is so thin.

Their sandwiches are tasty too. Cheesesteaks, hoagies, and their falafel is delicious too. 
They recently renovated the dining area and it looks very upscale. I would recommend this place to any pizza lover since its so good.

This place is good but not great. This place has been here for as long as I can remember. They recently renovated I guess because of the Broad Ax tavern. 

Many hidden dining rooms, dark long bar, mostly decent service. Beer is cold and inexpensive. The food is okay, nothing special. Award winning ribs shouldn't have really won any awards but their burgers, cheesesteaks and other sandwiches are tops. Great happy hour and even when they are busy, service is still good. 

This is a regular place for me and it should be for you too

Its a hotel and you can stay there.

After a couple of stays here I find it is not bad. 

Its definitely more of a business traveler kind of place than a tourist kind of place.

Pros
The rooms have the essentials. The beds are quite comfortable.
The cafe isn't bad although it is a little foggy as to what comes with the room. Apparently its one entree and one beverage. Not a bad deal.

Cons
Hallways are a bit shaggy. NBD since I am not staying in the hallway.
Room cleaning dropped the ball on my last stay. The room was clean, but I found a bag from BK in my mini fridge ... eeeew!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
If this was my first time here, I probably would have given it three stars.  The drinks were ok for hotel bar prices and the ambiance is good.  However, they used to have daily drink specials and those are no more.  They used to have a specialty cocktail list, but they no longer have that.  Finally, they used to have a free (and totally addictive) snack mix.  No more.  :-(

Drinks are standard fare, the location is slightly intimate, not to cold or hotel-ish.  We ordered hummus and it was very oily and tasteless.  It was garnished with olives and we chopped those up for flavor, which helped.

We were very pleased with carry out from Root & Bone.  They offer a LOT of food for the price.  We ordered the family dinners - one spare rib and one fried chicken.  The fried chicken was nicely crunchy and well seasoned.  The mac and cheese was great and our family fought over it!  The biscuits were also tasty.  The spare ribs were probably our favorite, even though the meat was tougher than I prefer.  The flavor was out of this world, with a slightly spicy Korean style barbecue glaze. There are slivers of red jalapenos on each rib, so you can keep them on to amp up the heat, or pick them off to keep it mild.

Located in ClearView Mall, Stir Fry is a simple and easy Chinese takeout place. Came here for a quick snack and just grabbed some rice and spicy chicken. The rice was average, but still tasty. The chicken was good! It was spicy, but the spiciness did not linger in my mouth very long. It went away fairly quickly. I wouldn't really recommend coming here if you really really want a good Chinese food experience since this is just a food-court takeout place, but if you happen to be at Clearview and want something Asian then this is kinda your only choice. An OK choice as well. Also, they only take cash from what I remember.

Went here for the first time in about 4 years. Boy, has it gone downhill. Prices/quality were horrible compared to other sushi restaurants in the area. $13 for a large sake?! It's about $8 anywhere else. $15 creative sushi roll and received only 5 pieces... Strange and odd number. The sashimi was cut paper thin, however, it atleast seemed to be fresh. The music was BAD... Early 2000s pop hits playing loud over the speakers. The service was alright, not very friendly but attentive and prompt. I only went here for a Groupon and even another Groupon couldn't talk me into going back.

I eat for lunch...a lot. The special is a standard $11.95 for three rolls plus soup or salad. The rolls are decently sized, and tasty, though nothing that will change your life.

One thing I hate is that they charge for hot tea. It's a random pet peeve, but really bothers me.

I do also recommend the lunch bento boxes, as well as coming during dinner time and ordering special rolls.

It's a great addition to the neighborhood, there's no doubt. Worth a visit if you're walking nearby and don't want any of the other (less than savory) oiptions.

Listen - the pasta (at least most of it) isn't homemade, the sauce may be half can-based for all we know, and the place isn't the most beautiful, fancy or roomy by any means. But the food is good, the prices are right, and, for the most part, the service is enjoyable.

Sometimes they charge random corkage fees (a dollar each? or per bottle? huh? I'm confused), and sometimes the menu prices change on the daily, but I do like this place. It's nice to have a decent, inexpensive, Italian BYO option in my neighborhood, and the food rarely disappoints.

Overall, Tres Jalapenos is a fun place to go with a large group of friends. The food is definitely good, and is SO cheap that it's impossible to complain. 

The main issue I had was with the margarita mix. It really is awful. I've been to several BYOT restaurants, some fancy and some not, and this was BY FAR the worst mix I have ever had. It was simply lemon juice, and nothing else.

I will definitely go back and try Tres Jalapenos again, because it's an affordable place with fantastic service and a fun atmosphere. Hopefully they'll improve on their mixes though!

As far as Chinese good in Chinatown goes, there's nowhere better. I have places I prefer down the street for pho or dim sum, but nowhere competes as far as fried rice, hot and sour soup, chicken and scallions, etc.

The aforementioned hot and sour soup is the best I've ever had (I think) and all the other dishes I've tried have been great.

The service is fantastic, friendly and quick. The prices are fair and the place is surprisingly clean, like other reviewers have said. They're open late and more than happy to work with any food allergies or requests.

Just the best around!

I have only ordered delivery from Jay's, and the food has always been consistent. I would give the restaurant 3 stars, because the rolls are all fairly small and don't have much fish in them, but $10.25 for three rolls at dinner is really a great deal and definitely makes up for it. They have also been very fast with all deliveries, and exceptionally friendly.

I would not recommend ordering single rolls due to their size, though they may make the non-3-roll-special rolls larger (I highly doubt it). Just stick to the great special, and order delivery if you want; it's free (plus tip of course)!

Ahhh a great way to start your Monday morning...with a flat tire. 

Lucky for me Southern Tire Company is only about .25 miles away from my place. I limped in with a bad front left tire. 

They were very professional and they had my tire fixed by 10am. It was nice to know they fixed it so quick, but I was going to be at work until 4pm so it really didn't matter when they finished it. 

The patch job cost ~$30. It's a very new tire, so it was worth doing that. Not to mention a new tire would've cost ~$200. I was happy to pay ~$30!

I know I will be using them in the future for all my tire needs.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
This is my second time staying here. The lobby is decorated in tacky asian furnature and oversized vases. Looks like they all came from a chinese take-out restaurant. The rooms are fine, just what you'd expect from Holiday Inn. The breakfast was pretty decent. Didn't swim in the pool, but looked alright. There is a running path around a pond out back which was nice. They also had free beer downstaris in the afternoon! Really my only complaints are that there was no fast food within a mile, and that the rooms faintly smelled of mildew. Florida humidity I guss? 

Very close to stadium.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I've been to several nail places for pedicures and I really do like this place. My only issue is that none of the guys will do other male pedicures. I don't understand why. I have noticed it before, but the last two times they have been busy and I always have to wait (soaking in the water which is nice, but waiting). The guys will do other things after the finish a job and then sneak into the next female after me. And I'm left soaking and waiting. I don't really understand. Waited 27 minutes until a female was available to do my pedicure. Very annoyed. I feel sorry for the other guy who came in after me and now they are so busy.

Jax Kitchen is a wonderful little spot, trendy and casual with good food. When I first went I tried the gumbo. Probably not the best idea, being from the south,  but the gumbo was pretty darn good for being in the Southwest. We also enjoyed a 1/2 price bottle of wine... who doesn't love that deal? 

The best part, desert of course! The red velvet cake was simply the best I have ever had. I have a soft spot for red velvet and I try it at every cupcake or bakery I go to, but boy Jax is it for Red Velvet. So I'd suggest save room for desert!

My husband used to drive to Accent on Vision from Phoenix when we lived there for three years before we moved back down and I must say Dr. Zucker and the amazing staff are probably the reason for that. Dr. Zucker doesn't take himself too seriously and you feel like you're talking to a person not someone who wants to get you in and out. They have a massive selection of normal to designer frames and their sales staff is really good at helping you pick the right frame for your face.

Tip: They have a deal if you buy a years worth of contacts you get your glasses 50% off (frames, lenses, etc.).
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
We were super excited to try this place out the atmosphere is super cute and inviting. 
The food is delicious and I totally recommend it. 

We happened to have super crappy service. The kind of bad service you have to ask for the manager. 

Our server took our order and then never returned. We had someone different bring us our meal and then never saw a person again. We had to ask the hostess for our bill after a legitimate 25 minutes of no one coming by our table. 

The food is very good though. They have an early bird special 4-530 which is $12.95 comes with a house salad and bread. They have happy hour wine 2 for $7 and $2.50 bud light.

Their Sushi is ok, (the Korean food IS 3 stars worthy though). 

One night I was in the mood for sushi and went in on a whim. I walked in and there was 2 employees at the host podium both stared at me and after about 40 seconds I got, "um, are you waiting for a friend?" I laughed and said no that I was hoping to sit at the bar and grab a quick bite. For the rest of the evening the entire staff fawned on me like I was the saddest little diner they've ever had. lol.

Aside from how awkward it was just to grab a quick solo meal out, the sushi wasn't the best I've had so I've only been back once since.

Luzzara is a boutique coffee shop on east Whyte Avenue owned and operated by Sarah Jackson.  Sarah is a fantastic lady with an appreciation for coffee.  

Luzzara serves a variety of coffee's, italian soda's, and has, quite possibly, the best hot chocolate in town. Yes, it's bad for you - but try it with the whole milk, it's delicious.

She serves sandwiches as well as desserts, and visit on Friday's for a special cookie treat.

If you're in the area, this is a delicious coffee shop that you need to try.  You can also follow her on Twitter as @Luzzara.

I had high expectations when I arrived downtown to eat here.  After all, you Yelpers have made this the highest-rated sushi bar in Nashville!  The interior was dim, the mood peaceful, and polite chit chat could be heard over the background muzak.  
What about the food, you ask?  The food was good in a way that reminded me of places other than Nashville.  For sushi, that is a good thing.  The service was polite and non-intrusive.  I did not eat at the sushi bar but I will make it a point to eat at the bar the next time I am here.

Tucked away in a strip mall with a too-small parking lot, Ninja is an option for teppan yaki, noodles, or sushi.  It is bigger on the inside than it looks from the outside and the food prices are reasonable for this type of food.  There is a small sushi bar and a larger table area.

The evening I was there a nearby customer had impatient kids but the adults thoughtfully changed their order to take-out.  The owner is friendly and wanders the dining room greeting customers.  I would say it's the perfect place to eat before watching a move at Malco!

Great location, right next to Rumba.  We came here to have a drink while waiting for Rumba to open.

As I stood in line, noticed a fly inside the cake cabinet next to the counter.  It was going to town, taking turns landing on all the cakes.  I  mentioned this to the cashier, who opened and closed the door to the cabinet several times.  He did not reach in to try to get the fly out, and the fly ended up untouched and unbothered.

The cashier walked away and started mopping the floor.  I picked up my receipt from the printer as the buffoon cashier forgot to give it to me.

However, my drink was good and satisfyingly cold.

I have been to a few gyms other than this 24 Hour Fitness, & I must say, I feel very out of place at this gym. It seems to me that the majority of the men are there just to check the women out. The women (not everyone, granted, but the greater majority) all seem to be Caughlin Club types, you know, with the make-up & hair that nobody would have if they were to actually work out. The equipment is nice, the customer service varies, depending on who you get at the front desk. Lastly, the locker rooms are absolutely disgusting - be sure to bring flip-flops!
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
This place is the oldest Italian restaurant in Philadelphia...which is why it still has a good amount of clientele. 

Overall this restaurant is average. It's just average Italian food...the sauces are a little watery, the staff are a touch too casual, and the management likes to throw their weight around in the dining room. Unfortunately since it's the oldest restaurant, tourists will come here and miss out on some other true gems in the neighborhood. If I were to recommend an Italian restaurant in Bella Vista, this wouldn't be it.

I AM a regular at 13th street pizza, lovingly know as Gay Pizza or Homo Hut due to it's location. However, my check-ins don't represent that since it's usually 2:00 am and I'm "feeling the fruits of life" and forget to check-in. 

This place used to be great. They lost one of their best employees and now it's so hap hazardly run, that I don't enjoy making it my late night munchie spot.  If I was writing this review a year ago it would be anywhere from 4-5 stars, now I'm at a 2 with them. They know what employee left, and they know how shitty the service is now...they better make some changes quick.

This place has GREAT decor!  Like getting a haircut back when men were really men.  Checkered tile, antique barber chairs, straight-razor cuts, etc.  I went once...but the barber cutting my hair was whining like a bad wheel-bearing about working conditions there and where he used to teach.  So, for me, I likely won't go out of my way to go back but I suspect your experience may vary.  He might have been having a bad day, who knows?  And the price wasn't TOO high, given the location, amount of authentic decor, and such.  The owner shakes your hand a lot too.  Nice.

This is the gym I frequent since I live close to it.  Out of all three Gold's Gyms, I like this one the best because of its 24 hour open times.  The downtown location is decent and the NW location is huge.  I really don't see how some people have issues with a gym that offers enough equipment to target every part of the body in a workout.  However, I do understand how someone would opt for a lower priced monthly rate over a higher price another gym charges.  A gym is a gym.  Get in there, do your workout, then get out.  That's all there is to it.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I give this place five stars because the staff was so friendly and the food was so damn good and it was really priced fairly.  The Bloody Mary was a bit of a disappointment, but I survived worse.

I had grouper blackened and my husband had a steak.  Both were awesome. I was also really pleased to get a big, fresh spinach salad with my meal -- at a biker bar!?!  Excellent. 

Live entertainment, great atmosphere, reasonable prices and great food...it is a bit off the beaten path but do yourself a favor and find it. We had no wait at all at 7:00 on a Saturday night -- but I bet when the weather is nicer, that won't be the case.

I had a very good experience here.  This was a good meeting place too that was about mid point for me and my date (who lives north of Collinsville).  The parking lot was packed at 8pm on a Friday night and I almost couldn't get a spot to park.  

Service was immediate with chips and salsa and water.  The soda I requested along with my guacamole and Mexican hamburger dip (both excellent) came very fast.  I ordered soft tacos (very good) and she enchiladas.

Definitely one of the better Mexican restaurants I've been to.  Try them out when you are in town.

I'm pretty picky about where I get my Chinese food. I need a place that has a flavorful curry chicken, crispy and delicious egg rolls, good lo mein and fried rice, and good service. This place totally fits the bill. 

Not only is the food good, but the staff is always pleasant, and the prices are reasonable. We've only ever had a problem with our order once (our bags got mixed up), but they apologized profusely and we got our correct order quickly. It happens.

Is it the best Chinese food I've ever had? No. But, it IS really yummy and we like the friendly people who run it, so what more can you ask for?

I'm very happy with this McDonald's. A much-needed upgrade and construction of basically a new building was done. One thing that really needed to be done was done. They used to have only one toilet in the men's room and ladies room. Now there are two in both. The inside of the restaurant was completely remodeled including the lobby and the kitchen. There is a much better seating setup and it is a cheerful decor. They also have the self-service kiosks. Still have an nice staff. The food is good old classic McDonald's.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
I have tried. I really have. I have graced their bar stools a number of times but I have yet to shake the disapointment that inevitably  discends upon me on each visit. The draft is always flat and the bottled beer warn. (sin!) The parade of "food" I have received on each visit is all seasoned with a liberal helping of bland with a side of "if I wasn't drunk I wouldn't eat this" 

I realize that this review is a tad harsh but it will not effect the loyal neighbourhood regulars. They love this dive and will fill its register with cash and their guts with buckets of bland until the culinary gods see fit to smite it from it's corner of the burbs.

Good sushi but nothing that blew my mind. The place itself is tinnnnny so either pray  you come at an opportune moment or take it to go! Since I don't live in the city, I don't see myself venturing back here as there are many other sushi options to try. However, I think this is a good neighborhood sushi spot if you live in the area. There is a wide variety of specialty rolls! $10.95 for a more basic 3 roll combo is a decent deal too. My friend ordered some shumai as an appetizer and they came out in a tray that looked like the one I could buy from the frozen section of an asian market...so I'd say just stick to the sushi options.

Okay this place is great due to their selection of beers on tap. I love having a huge variety of beers to choose from from all around the country and world. They also have a 2 for 1 special. As a few other yelpers have mentioned, that means you buy one beer for yourself and you get one free no matter if you have another person in your party or not. Our bartender was very nice and had no problem striking up a conversation with her. The bathroom is gross here and you might have to worry about catching something.

This is the only place to buy eyeglasses unless you're Warren Buffett.  2 pairs for $80--they are practically giving them away.

Here's the best part, though: they're incredibly good at what they do and impossibly friendly.  I take all 7 pairs of my eyeglasses in for adjustments all the time and they happily do them for free.  Once they even un-tinted a pair for free with glorious results.

For an extra $10 they'll tint any eyeglasses you select, turning them into sunglasses or just orange-tinted glasses (which I enjoy seeing the world through).

Can't say enough good things about this place.  I'm in love.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text: Went here for the first time using a Groupon deal. Overall I was very pleased with the service and food. We didn't realize this was a BYO, so came empty-handed. However they happened to have some wine leftover in the back so graciously gave me and my friend a glass each of white wine. I ordered the mozzarella and grilled vegetable app, tilapia entree and chocolate torte dessert. Everything was delicious! Street parking was easy in this part of town and I would certainly come back again for a low-key Italian dinner.

Aahhh, Bourbon Rocks!  How they draw you in and you keep coming back!  During our first night here we were drawn in by the sound of Journey drifting out into the street.  The DJ's there were somewhat entertaining but I would say that it is the late night antics of fellow patrons that are the most entertaining. Does a booty shaking contest to Baby Got Back interest you?  That is the type of entertainment at Bourbon Rocks and the girls will find out that the hype dancers are pros!  They do have bathroom attendants which are best to be avoided.  Well worth a quick jaunt!

I came to Taqueria Durango as part of a meetup group.  I was very excited to finally have a date set to try it, because I kept forgetting it on my own.  It was positively a beautiful evening and we ate on the patio.  

I did not even look at the menu, I was determined to try the tacos, and had little interest in anything else. 

I still hold a warm spot in my heart for Cherokee Street tacos, but the carne asada tacos at Taqueria Durango are the best that I have tried.  The tacos de lengua, are still better on Cherokee.

Keeping my same stars, but just wanted to point out some updates.

1. Tony, the owner, read this review and asked if it was one experience that triggered my bad review. I appreciate this and respect his coming to me and wanting to find out how to make his business better.

2. I have think the new trainers are better than the previous ones. I have seen them working with clients to try new and more efficient exercises.

There are still things I'd like to see added or changed, but all-in-all I am there for the convenience factor.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Enjoyed my first then second experience at Ambrosia. 

Tip: call for reservations or go in when they first open. 

The peartini was my top choice out of the cocktails I had there. A little sweet but ever refreshing. 

Appetizers: goat cheese was AMAZING!  I'm not a mussels fan but they were delicious. Enough to share. Also the calamari was good. 

Rustica for dinner and I may not get anything else because it was THAT good. Lol. That was my only mistake. 

Chocolate cake for dessert? YES PLEASE!

Will be back and keep bringing friends.

Ho-Ho is our go-to place for Chinese takeout, and has been for over ten years. The prices are good, the food is good, and they always have coupons and specials. I love the hot braised chicken, which comes in a good-sized portion with plenty of rice. The crab rangoon and egg rolls are awesome. 

The restaurant itself that is very small, with only a few tables and a take-out counter that is very busy. I probably would not eat there because of the size. 

The people are very nice and we will probably keep going there for another ten years!

This place is SMALL.. When they say "sushi bar" just picture the sushi bar area, and that's how many ppl you can seat in there. You serve yourself the drinks which was odd, but I guess it's ok being sucha small place, I dont think they'd pay someone to just serve you the drinks since you order the sushi directly with the sushi chef. I do love how they don't have to write down my order nor ask me twice, and remembered exactly what I wanted (and we ordered $80 worth of food). Overall the sushi was pretty good.

Three stars for now cuz I have yet to try their sushi... So i would definitely be updating this again.

Ordered their Chicken Teriyaki lunch. It comes with a side of soup or salad. The meal also has four pieces of california roll, 2dumplings, rice, and duh, chicken. I have to say it was quite delicious. The teriyaki sauce wasn't too sweet (thank god). The dumplings were good.. For $9 or so, it was a decent size lunch. The staff all seemed friendly. Wish i had my Jefferson ID with me then I would've received a discount! lol.. Gives me more of a reason to return i guess =)

Handwritten note from room housekeeper left on desk. Get a balcony view -- it's worth it. Stellar dining options - a fine dining Italian, waterfront American casual, sports bar and some to-go cafes / snack bars. Customer service at front desk and concierge are spot on. They're running a tight and friendly ship. Valet service is immediate and on point. Bath and Body Works Aromatherapy products in bathroom a plus. Eco friendly and a gorgeous view. 

Wifi is $9.95 / day or $14.95 for high speed. 

One con: the business center is not 24/7 and also charges money to print.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Rick Bayless does it again!  Somehow his flavors and use of local freshness has made it all the way from Chicago. The only reason this Frontera Tortas doesn't get 5 stars is because it's hours are horrible. Closed 2 days a week and not open past 5? Impossible to get here when you're a working mom!

The chicken sandwich with avocado and arugula is a burst of smokiness with a touch of sweet and a hit of spiciness at the end. I don't understand how a sandwich can be so good. Thank you Rick Bayless. 

Tips:
Sandwiches for about $8, limited seating, salads and soups also offered. Amazing tortilla soup.

The location is convenient, the restaurant is almost never packed, and the food is fast and consistent. My boyfriend and I have been to Ginza twice and had a nice time with no complaints. He orders hibachi chicken since he's not much of a sushi eater, and he always leaves the restaurant with a full, happy belly. I order gyoza and a couple of rolls and have liked everything I've tried so far. 

The downside to this restaurant is luckily not with the food - but should you need to be the bathroom, beware. It's pretty gross. Just something to keep in mind!

I lovvvve this place! The atmosphere is so open and comfy! And the sushi is awesome!! Not too pricey at all and the appetizers are half off before 7. We got the fried calamari and it wasnt chewy like some others ive had. And it comes with this sweet sesame sauce. Yum. You can also get any roll deep fried for a dollar more. We took advantage of this and got a philly roll fried with the california and alaska roll. The salmon is so fresh and tasty! And service was soooo fast! I think we got our food in 5 minutes! 3 rolls in 5 minutes!! I love this place. Hands down. And our waiter was extremely helpful and friendly. :)

I really do love other locations, but eveytime I'm at this one the service is absolutely terrible. The last time I went there, a friend and I seriously considered dining and dashing.

Our waiter not only took forever to even wait on us in the first place (and it wasn't busy in the least bit). He also took awhile to pick up our food from the kitchen as it wasn't all that hot when we finally got it. Then he didn't check on us once before bringing the bill.

Needless to say, I won't be coming back here anytime soon

The condition of the hotel and the room that I had was fine.  The front desk service was professional and courteous.  However, there was NO window in the room!  I've been in many hotels and never received a room with no window.  But, the price is generally very competitive to others in downtown Philadelphia.  The hotel is in walking distance from Chinatown, the Convention Center, and other shops and restaurants.  If you're traveling into Philly on either Greyhound, Peter Pan or the Chinatown bus, this hotel is only a few blocks away.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I had dinner at the restaurant and it was delicious.  The menu is creative and the decor is festive.  My brother and I shared the Sopes Veracruzanos as an appetizer ... very good!  We also ate the Camarones Rellenos (stuffed shrimp wrapped in bacon) and the Enchiladas with ground meat.  For dessert, we had two kinds of tres leches cake, vanilla and chocolate.  I've had better, but it was still good.  The chocolate version was a bit too sweet for me.  The food overall is a bit pricey, but it was a special occasion (my brother's birthday).

Let's start with the positives.  The bedroom and bathroom were clean.  They could use a little remodeling/paint job, but it was acceptable.  There was a fridge and a microwave in the room.  They also had a safe that you could use (although you have to pay extra for its use).  The hotel is in a nice location ... in the midst of restaurants & shops and walking distance to tourist attractions.  The front desk was friendly.  Now the not-so-positives.  The elevator was not working during my stay (2 days).  And the television was not working properly.  Overall, it was an acceptable experience, but I don't plan to stay there again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I used to love eating at this particular location for little tokyo, until recently the customer service was just horrible. 

A friend of mine called in early to reserve a karaoke room for her birthday. The people there put us in a karaoke room with a broken karaoke system. The people working there even knew it was broken a few weeks earlier, but didn't do anything about it to replace it. We paid extra for the broken karaoke room and also received slow and bad service.We were also treated rudely for misunderstandings about the check

If you want to go eat at little tokyo, go to any other little tokyo location except here.

There is nothing special about this courtyard. Same template check in, same old menu meals, tiny sorry looking pool and gym. Room was dark and way too cold due to AC going crazy. Couldn't adjust for some reason. 
Floor carpet was so worn out and stained everywhere..was Peter North the previous guest!? 

Driving in was also pain, as the drive way access is really hard to find from the main highway, and if you come from opposite direction mine as well go back to Tampa and turn around. Not cool. 

Unless I can get a corporate rate I wouldn't stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
We went to serafina for restaurant week, and we enjoyed our food and service. 

The ambience is very nice and it's in a great location. we started w Vitello Tonnato (thin sliced veal tenderloin) and sliced prosciutto w mozzarella. 
we had Veal Scaloppine and Filetto Di Salmone for our entrées. It wasn't impressively good, but its quiet enjoyable. food are fresh and homie. Maybe a little on the pricy side but it's a great deal for RW. having Tiramisu &Chocolate Torta for desserts,  I think it's a good choice to try during RW.

This charming little restaurant off the main drag in Belleville is your basic family-owned pizzeria. The food isn't going to blow your socks off, but it is definitely good. Their house salad dressing (like most local pizzerias) is incredible. They also have a few really good family meals deals for a great price. If you are in the area and looking for something in a decent price range that you can count on to be good, you should try them out. Belleville is really trying to gain back their charm and appeal and its little mom & pop places like this that are helping do the job.

I know I throw a lot of shade at the Asian restaurants in Santa Barbara and am constantly whining about how few options there are. And I know everyone loves Edomasa because it's inexpensive(ish) and stays open late(ish). Good job...but, I'd kind of expect those things at a casual, college town sushi joint. I really can't get into the sticky tables and dim halogen lights. The sushi is okay, but unmemorable, and the menu is pretty basic. Don't hate me. I'm sorry, I really want to like Edomasa, but it just doesn't do it for me.

Shout out to my girl Ericka S. for putting me onto the legendary hand grenade! 

I would totally give this place 5 stars if I liked the drink more than I did!  It wasn't bad, the flavor was actually good (fruity) but damn was it sweeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeet!  I could actually throw a few more "ee's" in there, but I think you get the point ;)

Regardless, it is a necessary stop in NoLa and most likely you will get f'd up off of just one.  Unless you have "a drinking problem" and if so, this is a good one to have ;)

We went here for my birthday in January and we got in engaged that night! 

The food was decent, nothing spectacular. I had the pasta premivera dish with chicken and it was good but missing something to really make it mouthwatering. Everything was just "okay." Plus it's just one big room so it can get loud. We wanted a quiet romantic meal since I knew he wanted to propose but the table next to us was large and loud and within arms reach so it made it hard to talk and have our moment.

I don't think we will return except maybe for desert to remember our engagement.

Quick takeout Chinese food. I've been here twice. I haven't been disappointed, but I haven't been completely satisfied either. The crag rangoon is really good. a little sweeter than i'm used to, but good. Their egg rolls are really yummy, but a little too greasy. They also don't do a very good job of trimming the fat off of their boneless spare ribs, which results in a lot of gross chewy pieces. I definitely won't be getting those again. In the future i'll probably stick to the rangoons, egg rolls, and shrimp fried rice.

Ahh, I really really wanted to like this place. It has great reviews, I love sushi, and I had a Groupon! What more could a girl want? A lot, apparently. Admittedly, I'm pretty picky about sushi- and this sushi was SO bland. The rice had no flavor and the fish didn't taste fresh. As a matter of fact, it was slightly room temp, like it had been sitting out. I shouldn't have even taken the chance with eating lukewarm sushi, but I did... and my stomach paid for it the next day! I really had high hopes, but  after that experience, I won't be back.

I probably wouldn't have ever came to the Lobby Bar if it weren't for the Busted Blues band that was playing that night. (Discovered them at the big Yelptucky Derby and wanted to hear more!) Don Cesar is a very upscale luxury hotel, so of course their lobby bar has to match, and it does. Great choice for music. Our server was very friendly and helpful when we asked for dessert choices. Upscale means up prices, but you should expect such when coming to a place like this. Nice way to just chill and vibe out to the live music.

This place is a joke. I made an appointment online for a basic oil change and tire rotation for $20. I show up to my appointment and the guy tells me he only has full synthetic oil which is $50. Why in the hell would the website allow me to book an appointment at this location if they didn't even have the type of oil? Furthermore, he said they do this because there's a jiffy lube next door and needs to stay competitive. So you're worried about your competition instead of your customers?? Duly noted. Never again.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Food here is ok, not great not bad. Sitting outside is nice when it starts to get warm outside and probably the best sell of the restaurant. However, the staff here is absolutely terrible. The waiter's are slow and always seem to mess something up and Bici always seems to be out of something on the menu. On top of that it usually takes a long time to get your food. If you can live with bad service for a relatively inexpensive meal and the chance to sit outside on a nice day then this place is perfect. They also have delicious Sangria, probably the best thing at the entire retardant.

Fellas, this ain't a dive bar. For a detailed description on what a dive bar is please read my review on another mislabeled establishment.  http://www.yelp.com/biz/the-polo-lounge-reno#hrid:MUcA8HZNolgOlgMr-1iRQg/src:self

What makes me want to go out and drink, other than dealing with people all day long, is to experience a good bartender at their craft. I appreciate someone who takes pride in what they do. I think all the bartenders here are tip top. They keep track of your gamling, so if you're firing at the bonus poker you can get your drinks comped. 

Their dry rub chicken wings are the best!

Hands down the best sushi place in NOLA. The fish is always so fresh. I highly recommend the special fresh salmon and the baked salmon roll which is served with a mix of greens. The Hana special roll is another goodie and the service is wonderful.

However, my favorite thing they do is the BBQ EEL Sushi and the EEL roll.  The sauce they use on their eel is to die for.  Not to mention the "Hana Special Sauce" that is topped on many of the other wonderful rolls.  I've never had a bad experience there in the 15 years I've been frequenting it.  I couldn't recommend this place any more!

During the summer, my wife and I spend quite a few nights at Petrucci's.  They have a great variety of ice cream, and soft serve as well.  The selection of water ice is excellent, and the quality is way up there.  I usually get a regular sized vanilla soft serve cone dipped into a butterscotch shell.  

There is a nice play area for kids in the back, a ton of animals including cows, goats, roosters, and horses.  They also have an actual well that you can buy water from.  A farm in the middle of King of Prussia is a surprise, but it definitely adds to the charm of the place.

I ate at GG's this past Valentine's Day and the food was amazing and delicious. I had the Kobe meatloaf with garlic potatoes as my main entree. My BF had the ostrich which he said was okay and his appetizer was the duck and mushroom ravioli which he loved. The restaurant itself has an open floorplan and not a lot of privacy - was a tad noisy as it was Valentine's night. The decor seemed a bit drab but overall the atmosphere was romatic and the staff was very friendly. I would definitely eat at GG's again and recommend for a romatic dinner or social gathering. The attire is casual dressy as well.

If you are looking for a clean place to shop with good prices and no crowd this is the spot. Easy parking and good access. Don't suffer through the "Wal-Mart" experience and don't pay the high prices at Rouse's. Only negative so far is that if you bring your own bags and use self checkout they have not programmed the self checkout machines to ignore the additional weight of the fabric bag and you will get constant weight errors. I have talked with the manager a couple of times and the problem is supposedly being addressed.

I always wanted to come here but a gift certficate from Restaurant.com got me here. 

I must say that I had a pleasant experience. Their food was DELISH!....  I ordered the eggplant parm which was exceptional. I went a little different because normally I would order a alfredo dish. 

Also I'm not a huge fan of tiramisu from other places but their was great and not too much rum in it.

The wait time was long so I would suggest making a reservations especially on the weekend.

I will be back next week because now they have a promo if you buy $50 gift card you receive $25 back :)

Today, I had a horrible experience at this Starbucks. I'm going to call out the particular shift because I think Managers should know what their Barista's are doing. I was in around 11am on Sunday. The Barista started my drink, and another customers drink. During this time she decided to walk to the back..get a mop..proceed to mop the floor...and than put the mop back...Finally getting back to finish off our drinks...Really????? Horrible customer service Starbucks....While I will be back...I hope to get a Barista who actually cares about their Customers.

I know that writing a review of a gas station/ donut shop is a bit silly, but I just couldn't resist.  A few years ago, I worked at Franklin Mills and babysat in the area as well.  Since watching a 2 year old all day and then waitressing all night requires a LOT of energy, I would hit up this Dunkin Donuts frequently.  After the second time they would recognize me coming in and have my coffee waiting for me.  This alone was impressive, but flash forward 3 years and I stopped in the other day to find that the woman who works there still remembers my order.  It really doesn't get any better than that when you're looking for a fast caffeine fix.

Pine Street Pizza falls firmly into the category of food you eat before going to a club or food you eat after getting out of a club. as long as you go in with that in mind, you won't have any unreasonable expectations.

the pizza is extremely greasy. decent sauce and crust. really nothing to write home about.

the dining room is low fi, to say the least - it's actually fairly skeezy, with a revolving cast of strange characters passing through, including at least one or two cops. most everyone is absorbed by the big tv mounted throughout the place. if you're wearing your beer goggles, however, this probably won't matter too much.

In comparison to other 24 hour locations this one falls in the middle. The machines are plentiful enough and most are operational which is a plus. Staff is friendly and I do notice at least one of the staff members make a rounds here and again to check on the establishment.

The building at peak still leaves enough machines available to where you may end up waiting on a bench but if so not too long. Improvements can certainly be made here though all in all it's a solid gym, and there is virtually no excuse to stay away from the House of Iron.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Great little place.  It's the kind of place that can become "your place" -- that out of the way place that you fall back on.  There seem to be a lot of regulars.  It's very casual, very noisey, crowded, and very friendly.  Good selection of Italian dishes, decent specials, good service.  We've been there with a crowd -- try 6 visiting Mexicans -- as well as just the 2 of us.  It is almost aways my DH's place of choice when we want to do out for dinner on the spur of the moment.  

Parking can be a challenge.  Hearing your dinner partner's convesation can be a challenge.  Getting a good meal is NOT a challenge.

When you walk in, suddenly you are transformed and totally forget you're in a strip mall. There is a hip vibe and a friendly and accomidating staff. Tons of great beers on tap along with other fabulous wines and cocktails. The menu is wide ranging, so there is something for everyone (don't be swayed by the name). Most ingredients are locally sourced. You can taste freshness in each bite. You can tell the chef is amazingly talented. I've never had undeviled eggs til now, so different. Worth every penny. This is our new favorite in town! What took me so long to get here?

They have two flavors- chocolate or vanilla (no twist) at least not today. The menu is difficult to see. I'd highly recommend a menu on the outside wall. They give each customer one tiny napkin and no extras where you can get to them, so ask when you order. Several menu items were not available and the person working the window seemed to really hate his job. On the plus side, the chocolate and vanilla ice cream are pretty good. In general, I'm sorry to say, I think this tired old ice cream stand has seen better days. It could really use an update.

We had to leave Florida due to Hurricane Irma with our little dog, and Westin Indianapolis was one of the stops on our impromptu road trip. Comfortable beds, lots of green space outside to walk our dog around, friendly staff, and the bar has good food. I used to stay at another Indianapolis hotel by default, but they stopped allowing dogs, so this might be our go-to from now on. Minor down sides: The bar gets crowded--wish it was larger, and the Starbucks isn't a real Starbucks. But those are minor quibbles.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I ate here for lunch on a Monday. They weren't busy at all. The service was fast & friendly. I got the spicy tuna roll. It was good, not great. I don't care for when they shred the tuna in a food processor, it comes out with a baby food consistency. I also got the scallops with rice for 8.95. That comes with 4 regular sized scallops. They were cooked well, not squashy & not too firm. The rice is cooked well & full flavored. The veggies could use a few more minutes cooking. The yum yum sauce has an odd taste, almost like chewing on yellow school pencils. A nice place, but not on the top of my list.

So... I'm one of those "I like frozen yogurt becuase it tastes like ice cream but is supposedly healthier" people, and Frostbite is a shop truer to the yogurt taste than my liking. Even their flavors like "french vanilla" and "caramel" taste too much like yogurt. However, if that's what you prefer, than this may be the place for you.

Unlike other fro-yo locations, they are very hesitant to give samples- samples are the best part of fro yo! Yogurtland gives you like twelve sample cups so you can go to town... but I digress.

Family-owned and very quaint, the atmosphere fits the small-town feel of Freret st., but just not quite up to par.

This place is okay.  The atmosphere is average...colorful with Spanish music and lots of seating.  Service was fine, our server was nice and offered recommendations and options.  The food is well, on par with fast food.  It's not bad food, but it's not what you would expect in a dine-in facility.  I would say the quality of food is slightly better than eating at a Mexican buffet.  Again, not bad, just not the kind of place that makes you think, I can't wait to come back.  If someone suggests this place, skip it.

After a death in the family we reserved a room for the night at this hotel. When we arrived we were told there were only smoking rooms available. We had reserved a non smoking room. The person at the desk apologized and said that this keeps happening to people and she can't stop it...yet no one called to give us a heads up. We were a pretty late check in and at that point other places we had considered were full. They offered nothing to rectify the situation. If you're at all sensitive to cigarette smoke I suggest calling ahead and having them confirm that you're getting the room you reserved. Happy New Year to us.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This place is one of the good Japanese restaurants in Tucson. I did not try the sushi yet so my review is not based on that. The atmosphere is great, although I have to say that the waitress was a bit dismissive while we were there. We sat at the sushi bar but didn't order any sushi, and the sushi chef always seemed to be cheerful. The free plum ice cream at the end was a plus :). Will definitely have to come back for the sushi.

Try to avoid the Ramen (I swear it is just Maruchan with added spice and an egg).

4 for the food, but minus one star for the whole experience. The chicken here is yummy! and I definitely was surprised at the prices when I walked in. I thought they would be more like Pollo Loco's, so I was pleasantly surprised. I brought a picky eater with me and he liked his chicken burrito but said his tamale was just so-so (I was like duh, good tamales are across the street). I wish I could get them a 4, but the dining area was infested with flies and I had to swat them left and right throughout the course of my meal. Not fun. Definitely will come back for take-out though.

Food was okay, but the service was a mess. We went in for lunch and were the 2nd table there, placed our orders and received our salad and eggplant parm appetizer as the place filled up with more people we waited more than 45 minutes for our entrees. Many tables received their entrees before us, but some tables asked for their food to go because they couldn't wait any longer. The servers were crowding around the kitchen at some point waiting. I have no idea what was going on in the kitchen, but will never go back there for mediocre Italian food.

SO smoky! Iccckk!

Every time I have been to the Emerald, I have been dragged through the door. It's a typical smoky dive bar that usually charges a cover.

My last experience at the Emerald was losing my friends in the smoky haze and watching the rude girl covering the door call the cops on the Sake Bomb patrons next door for standing out front with their drinks. Lame.

Smokey bars are lame, grumpy bouncer chicks are lame and charging a cover is super lame. In my opinion, Emerald Bar needs to get with the times. I know a lot of people like the Emerald, but it's not for me.

Let me ask you a question; are you looking for watered-down martinis with tiny olives? How about mediocre dishes with a background of loud classic rock? Also, the prices are a bit higher than the fare would indicate appropriate.

Sounds great? Then the Landmark Americana is built for you.

Pleasant enough, and hardly awful, there is room for improvement. The very best part of Landmark is that they are close to several good West Chester restaurants , including the quality Star of India, and Mediterranean. Also a promising Soul Food shop, Moe's. But Landmark does have beer....

Good lunch place to take the grandparentals... quiet, quick, not too pricey. 

The shrimp and salmon lunch boxes were both teriyaki'd to perfection, and were served with a california roll, miso soup, salad, and rice. My sashimi was totally overpriced for the quality of the fish (then again, we are in Tennessee), but the lunch boxes were a cute, filling option that both gram and gramp seemed to enjoy. "Except for all that rice... what am I going to do with all that rice? I'd definitely eat that last." - Gramma

Not a HUGE proponent of chain restaurants, but Houlihan's does something that makes me want to come back, if for nothing else, happy hour. 

Prices are exceptional for happy hour, and the choices are abundant. The drink prices cannot be beat, and our bartender was charismatic and attentive. 

The actual food on the main menu, I could take or leave. At places where the genres of food are so scattered, I feel that they all just end up mediocre. I have tried the jambalaya and stir-fry- both meals I could make better in my own kitchen for a fraction of the price.

I went here for my friend's birthday because it is BYO. But when people say this place was small, they weren't kidding. I had a party of 15 and the place was very cramped. We barely had room to move or to eat.

The price of the food was definitely affordable... However the food was subpar. Here's the thing, Italian food is one of my favorite type of food, so when I tried the food here, it was very disappointing. I barely touched my plate which is rare because I love to eat. 

The service was just okay. Our waitress only came back to check up on us once and that was it. 

Overall, I'd have to say that I won't come back.

I went here after reading several reviews on Yelp and was pretty pleased. Everyone was really friendly and I love the small restaurant atmosphere. The mozzarella sticks were good, but nothing sensational. The pizza was pretty yummy. Lots of cheese and just the right amount of sauce. It also had oregano on it and the server didn't look at me like I was crazy when I asked for more oregano--- for some reason I have found that in the south pizza shops don't put oregano out for customers to use! So, all in all, one of the best pizzas I have eaten down here.

I prefer to purchase my wine and/or alcohol here because of the ease of convenience. There are designated parking spots for the Wine Shop so you don't need to valet park. The staff is friendly, helpful, and willing to quickly educate you if you need any assistance in choosing a wine. 

I also am happy I can purchase Bern's Steak House Gift Cards at Bern's Fine Wine and Spirits so that I don't have to deal with the hassle of running into the restaurant. 

Don't forget to sign up for their email list to be informed of their frequent tastings, special events, and sales.

Marble Slab is very expensive, but also very good. The ice cream is so creamy and smooth. I usually save it for a very rare treat. I'm not overly picky about ice cream anyway. I actually like McDonald's ice cream, and it's super cheap. 

I find that it's a better deal to take a small carton of Marble Slab ice cream home. They have different sizes of cartons, and I think the smallest one costs only $8, and it was much bigger than the Haagen Dazs or Ben & Jerrys that you see in the store. It can take a while for them to fill the carton, but it's well worth it, and you can pick any flavour you want too. I personally love the chocolate.

I really wanted to like this place more than I did. The sushi was good and the roll choices were nice as well. There was a lot of choices, but not too many. It still made it hard to pick between rolls. The reason for the -1 star is because about 15 minutes after we came in a group of about 10 people say down at the table. Our chef took over their table and getting her attention was very difficult. She acted annoyed when we asked for something more. She snapped at one of the employees to make us something and it was clear he was new and she continues to snap orders at the poor guy.

I would like to speak about convenience:

(Or lack thereof)
- In branch hours 10 - 5?  I guess that banker who died in England due to exhaustion really had a global impact.
- Supposed to be "credit union friendly" - yet when you try to make a withdrawal from their ATM and you have an account with another local credit union, the fee is $3.00
- Their daily withdrawal limit inside, if you have an account with a different credit union, is $500 - weak sauce

That just about sums it up - weak sauce.  Hughes doesn't charge any ATM fees for the same type of transaction.

I ordered the Sichuan Tofu.  On the menu, it shows two hot peppers next to this item.  This lead me to believe it would be at least moderately spicy.  Unfortunately, there wasn't as much heat as I hoped.  The service was friendly.  But since I ordered with a group, our food took much longer to be served.  The food portions were generous considering the price.  And not surprising, the quality of food was sacrificed.

If you're in the mood for Chinese, not looking to spend much, and aren't ordering in a group, Golden Chopstick should work out.

This is a quick and easy stop if you're looking to cold beer. The prices are good and I really like they're flexible and will let you buy a single beer or cinder. They also have a great selections of domestic and foreign beers and cinder. If you're looking to buy a full case, you're better off going across the street.  But if you're only looking for just a few bottles or cans, you should consider this spot. Also bare in mind that they're cash only. It's also true that this block can seem a little sketchy at times but I've never ran into an drama. And while the cashiers may be behind bullet proof glass, they're very friendly and helpful.
