We tried Sakura last night with some friends and really liked the food. We when got there it was packed which is always a good sign. Their parking lot is a nightmare I will say. We waited about 10-15 mins so that wasn't too bad but did learn they take reservations and will call ahead next time. The food was pretty solid. I had a Katsu don and loved it. Just wish they could do a curry Katsu don but it wasn't happening. My wife liked her meal and said it was pretty fresh. The service was meh. Our little old lady waitress was pretty grumpy but whatever. We will definitely be checking out Sakura again.

Interesting little spot for lunch. Got today's special, country fried steak, mashed potatoes, green beans and iced tea came in just under 10 bucks. Not much on Ambiance lol but food was hot and pretty decent. Staff not very friendly at all from either server to check out cashier. No smiles or how you doing from anyone. Not very welcoming and Nashville like. It is close to work so probably be back but they sure could do w some better attitudes. Just my humble opinion. Lots of other options within a couple block radius ...

Tabetha wrote a great review of this place, it is fine dining, the food is off the chart good, yes, it is not cheap but it is VERY good. The filet was around 30 bucks, one of us had shrimp and grits, and we tried each others, they were both VERY good. The bar b q oysters were the best in or around new orleans and we go there fishing every year and I also vacation some in New Orleans, been there many times, so know the cuisine. There were 3 of us, had a couple of beers each, the oysters and all of us had entrees and a couple of side salads...bill was 130, I didn't think that was bad at all for really great food and nice ambiance.

I had a selection of their standard rolls at a party my friend hosted.  He ordered and picked up.  The quantity seemed on point for the order. The quality was just average.  I mean, we didn't get an fancy rolls, but I judge a sushi joint on how it delivers on the basics as well - tuna roll, spicy tuna roll, california roll, etc.  Far from the best I've had in the city, but not quite in the bottom third either.

Oh, and we all found it odd that on a large take out order of sushi, they didn't include any chopsticks.

The only kind of "drinking and driving" I could ever recommend, speedy's make it easy to pick up a case on the way to the party or on your way home.  A key to making your trip successful is to know exactly what you want, pull up, pop the trunk, and place your order.  I've never managed to go when there wasn't another car following me in, so time is of the essence.  So why you may feel a little rushed, prices are comparable to other beer distributors, so at least you don't pay for the convenience of not having time to get out of your car!

Being one of the few places to grab a late night snack on Main Street apparently has its advantages as Main Street Munchies prays on the drunk and stupid!

After being dragged here by a friend, I noticed the clerks rip off not one but two obviously drunk kids on their food order.  No doubt part of me thought they probably deserved it.  When we finally order, they tried to overcharge us as well!  Since I could add, they quickly corrected their "accidental" mistake and we left with average quality slices of pizza.  I recommend you avoid Munchies at all cost, as I know I will!

Formerly the Sheraton, Hotel 201 by Marriott really does not live up to their standards. It is in dire need of a facelift/modernization. The rooms and common spaces are of rather nice size, which in this case leads to more a feeling of the space missing on expectations (and falling short of its potential). 

Having joined a friend for party of a conference, I can say the staff is sharp, friendly, and deserve better as well. I'm loyal to the brand, but would advise those who aren't to look elsewhere. And if you are, maybe consider another Marriott property until you hear of renovations.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Osaka is pretty solid for sushi.  I've gone for dinner a couple of times, and it's never crowded, the service is friendly and the sushi is delicious.  They do not, however have tuna tartar on the menu which I find odd and disappointing since it's one of my favorite items.  

I went last night and had the duck lettuce wraps which were fantastic.  The duck was perfectly seared with crunchy little fried leek strips and a pickled daikon slaw.  I also got a spicy tuna crunch roll which was great and only 7 bucks!

I hadn't been here since they updated the interior and got a liquor license.  They also now take credit cards and reservations!

The food is still fantastic, the service is great and the cocktails are amazing.  I especially loved the raw tuna tostadita- deliciously flavorful, crunchy tostadita, super fresh tuna.  The pork carnitas were also super flavorful and not dried out like some carnitas tend to be.  Also it looks like they're offering a happy hour now from Sun-Thursday so I will definitely be back to check that out!

Delivery was fast.  Came in just under 30 minutes, and I was able to order online and pay with my credit card.  

Decided to get the chicken scaloppine pizza with grilled chicken, mushrooms, roasted red peppers and mozarella cheese.  The pizza was just okay....everything tasted kind of bland and nothing really stood out.  The pizza also wasn't cheesey enough...the cheese ended about an inch away from the crust, the sauce didn't have a lot of flavor, nor did the chicken.  The pizza was thin an crunchy though and arrived piping hot.

A great selection of beer with a lot of cold cases in stock as well.  They also have tons of other beverages for mixers such as cases of seltzer, soda, and fentimans tonic.  They also have a big selection of seasonal beers and have tasting events occassionally.

However, they have been out of stock of Original Sin pear cider since the fall.  Bummer, but I think it is not the fault of theirs since I think there has been problems with the manufacturer.  The staff is always friendly and helpful and offer great advice when stocking up for parties.

Ugh, I get ass-raped by the prices here but yet I still go because I am lazy and it is only around the corner.  For a while, this was the only grocery store I was going to, until I realized that the price of tomato sauce really had not gone up to 9.99 a jar (and yes, it's regular tomato sauce that they sell at Shop-Rite for 3.99).  

On the plus side, they do have a fairly good selection.  They even carry things like seitan and I guess not shockingly, a large selection of Kosher food items.  The staff is always extremely friendly and helpful and the lines are never too long.

The inside is nice; no weird smells, festive Mexican music, large TVs, comfortable bar seating. There is also outdoor seating in the back which is pretty chill. The food is flavorful and authentic. I have had the tortilla soup and mole and both dishes were delicious. 

Regarding prices, comparing some common items you may be able to save a dollar or two at nearby spots, however Las Margaritias offers a different type of Mexican than Johnny Sanchez and Juan's Flying Burrito. Compare the menus, there are not similar. If you are squeezing pennies you probably shouldn't be eating out anyway...

With long lines and wait times are the surrounding restaurants, we decided to give this a try.  The immediate seating should have been our first clue that our dinner would be mediocre.  Upon entering we were consumed by a strange smell, like a recent cleaning solution had been applied liberally to the dinning room.  Our spinach dip appetizer was freshly micro waved and accompanied with bland chips.  My pecan crusted chicken was run of the mill.  The only saving grace was the coconut bread with an orange juice infused butter.  Next time I'll wait in line for a table next door.

Tried Anthonys today for lunch and was impressed. I also stay away from chains but after hearing 610 WIP rave about there pizzas for the past week I had to try them out. Drinks do come in bottles, which is weird and pricey if you are a big soda drinker ($2.50/bottle). We started with the salad with gorgonzola cheese. It was really fresh with just the right amount of dressing. The small salad was big enough to split. We then had a pepperoni pizza. It was great, possibly top 10 in my book. The crust was crunchy and light. The pizza itself had a nice crunch to it as it is cooked in a high temp oven. Give this place a try!

Sigh - I should have listened to Yelp.

Having just purchased a home less than two blocks away, I felt compelled to give the most local pizza shop a try during a day of pre-moving maintenance/cleaning projects.  I phoned in an order for a large plain pizza that was ready when I arrived to collect it ~15 minutes later.  The shop atmosphere was dingy and odd, but I don't really care about that for take-out.  The pizza was small, had a dry bread-y crust, and an overabundance of quickly congealing cheap cheese.  Fortunately, the thing was cheap, and not inedible.

Maybe their non-pizza items are better, but I am in no hurry to try them out.

Yes, I know everyone loves this place. I'm right along with 'em. Of course they have amazing and delicious burgers. I still think it's crazy and wonderful that none of their food is ever frozen. So why the hell am I reviewing In n Out? Two words; CUSTOMER SERVICE! Every time I go, especially to this location, every person I speak to is beaming from ear-to ear. They actually make me smile. Everyone is always kind and friendly and not once has my order ever been wrong. This doesn't happen much anymore, so if I can get the best burger ever, and feel great doin' it, I'm definitely coming back. I love In n Out!

Solid hibachi spot on Doylestown.  The place has a NYC feel to the inside which makes me feel sort of at home.  The food was very good, didn't try the sushi but after reading some of these reviews I will make sure I do next time around.  Was there with a group of six and the hibachi chief was very fun and entertaining.  We got plenty of food and was stuffed but the end of the meal.  The main bar looked like it could be fun for a Friday or Saturday night also, with TV's with the sports games on and good looking people standing around.  Will defiantly be returning to this place.  
Does get busy so parking can be tricky at times.

This is a fantastic Japanese restaurant and sushi bar right off of Rittenhouse Square.  It has a casual yet intimate feel (high-walled booths) and the servers have the perfect combination of spunky and sweet.  My parents and I enjoyed the edamame sampler (wasabi salt! yuzu salt!), tempura veggies and spicy tempura halibut.  The tempura was great, not too breaded or greasy!  We shared the sashimi and sushi sampler, which, with the three appetizers, was plenty for the three of us.  Definitely a solid sushi place and reasonably priced - I'd definitely come back!

I originally signed up here because it is right around the corner from my office. It is brand new - in a former ACME market. It is only $10 per month with no contract - that was enough for me to sign up without even seeing it. Ive been going for over a year now and stepped up to the "black card" membership which is only $19 a month - includes unlimited free guests. unlimited free tanning, half priced drinks. The free weight area could be bigger - there is def an over abundance of cardio machines - bikes, ellipticals, treadmills, ect. The majority of the people that go are either seniors or high school kids...no meat heads really.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Had a nice meal on a Tuesday evening.  I think our server was actually the owner, who was attentive and charming in an old world sort of way.  The food wasn't drop dead amazing, but very solid Italian fare.  (I especially enjoyed the grilled calamari appetizer!)  The dining area is VERY small, and a bit worn - could feel pretty crowded on a weekend night, but midweek it was quite intimate and charming.  LOVE the BYOB option - don't think there was even a fee for corkage (but not sure.)  Cash only - go prepared!

Had the pizza a few times and it varies but is usually pretty good. The Italian was the best one I've had so far, with a fair variety of tasty meats on top. Haven't taken advantage of it yet but they've got some good lunch specials from 11-3. 

Only thing that bugs me is how early they close. I made an order at 10 on a Saturday night, they're open until 11. I was waiting for my roommate to get out of the shower so we could go pick up our pizza when I got a call at 10:15 asking me if I could hurry up because they wanted to close up. Not a big deal since I'm close by but... srsly?

I like St. Louis-style pizza, so I like Imo's! 

I will have to say that I like Cecil Whitaker's pizza better than Imo's. Though Imo's is really good, sometimes the cheese and toppings can get kind of congealed if it's been sitting out. But I still wouldn't turn down a slice! I love that the mass of provel cheese melted over the pizza is thicker than the crust. Maybe you have to be from the St. Louis area to understand the awesomeness of this. 

Also, for some reason I just really love their salad. It always has a ton of provel, red onions and black olives. Their house dressing is also the best.

I completely agree wit Sean B.  The Sheraton Sand Key is past its "best by" date: the decor is outdated, the prices are too high, and you're merely paying for the opportunity to stay on the beach.  I stayed at the Sheraton for a conference, which was held in the Sheraton and in the Marriott across the street.  If I were to go back, I'd choose to stay in the Marriott instead.

On the other hand, the staff were extremely friendly and the service was pretty good.  But, that's not enough to make up for the lack of dining options in the area, and the expensive prices on property.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Way overhyped! We come to Reno all the time and like to check out local joints away from the the hotels.  This experience was just blah. Glad we called and made a reservation because the place is small and who knows how long AYCEaters will be hanging around. We, being the cheap Viets we are, did the math and decided a la carte was the better deal.  Yes, rolls are cheaper here but the portions are small to match. There was barely any fish on the orders that called for it. The food was not terrible; it just didn't live up to our expectations.  Nonetheless, if I were to suggest one roll, go for the Mountain Roll.

I would sadly like to update my review. My husband and I have been going here for years. It's always a special treat for us. We went a few months ago and I have to say I don't think we will be back. The service, which is normally stellar, was awful. We get better service at burger king. The food was ok, not up to the great standards we are use to. Due to the service being so bad we wrote them an email to let them know this waiter was awful, we never received any reply at all. Some kind of sorry would have been nice. Try al dente in moorestown instead.

Had a great experience at the Westin.  Great old building that has had a refurb inside.  Great downtown location fairly close to the trolly line which made it easy to get to the arch, city gardens, dinner etc.  Room was really nice, clean, and bright.  The workout facility is nice and the only downside compared to competitors is they don't have a pool.  I thought the breakfast was really well done although one day they were understaffed and service was really slow.  We didn't complain but they noticed, apologized, and paid for a breakfast.  A real nice gesture.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: i took my grandmother and little cousins here when they came in to town last year. It was an amazing dinner. For me. When I said good Italian, they thought pasta, sauce, breadsticks.... tsk tsk... This place had none of the standard "Olive Garden" flare, but instead had some authentic tuscan and Mediterranean food and plenty of awesome pasta, seafood, chicken and veal options. Great food for the dollar too. I'll remember to dress a little nicer next time I go. And I'll remember to bring a fancy bottle of wine.

The service was terrible!  I went here for lunch with 3 of my coworkers a few weeks ago.  The server said they were short staffed, but that should still be no excuse for getting our orders wrong.  The server only got 2 of our orders correct when she even wrote all our orders down.  She even refilled the drinks and returned the drinks to the wrong people.  The food wasn't even good.  I had a turkey wrap and the wrap was hard and overall wasn't good.  Even the french fries were horrible, they were dry and soggy...how can you go wrong with french fries??

I do not recommend going here and would not return.

I have been told by numerous native philadelphians that Ralph's is one of the best Italian restaurants in the city and is a must to experience. We did not think so. We started off with a grilled calamari appetizer that was soaked in salty red sauce. The amount of sauce overwhelmed the palate to the point where we couldn't even taste the calamari. I got the pasta bolognese with filet mignon tips. Again, the red sauce was very salty. The filet mignon tips was really just average quality beef. My wife ordered the black lobster ravioli which were decent but overly salty. We expected much more from the oldest Italian restaurant in the country.

Zama might just be my new favorite sushi joint in Philly. Granted I went with someone who knew Zama, the chef/owner. So we probably got some special treatment. But even so, a great all-around experience. Cool decor, friendly professional service, but with personality. But most importantly, stellar sushi - excellent quality fish, creative rolls, unusual sauces. We also had the tempura vegetable appetizer, a scallop appetizer, the wasabi salt edamame - all delicious. Even the desserts were fantastic - way beyond the traditional green tea ice cream: Fuji apple crisp, molten chocolate cake, creme brulee! We will definitely return...

Located walking distance to Bourbon, French Quarter and the WWII museum location is great. The rooms are so so so small but they have all the basics you need for a comfortable stay and clean room. Very quiet rooms for the area (not silent but for the area quiet). The breakfast was amazing that you get with Marriott platinum membership. Only real downside is the bar ran out of many items (cold brew coffee, pork sliders, canned local IPAs) so that is one area they need to improve on but otherwise great experience.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Living closer to another Dunkin' it was part of my routine to visit every morning. Sadly this is my new Dunkin as I have moved and that routine is very. The quality of the iced coffee here is very watered down compared to other Dunkins and even with a full staff they often still lock the lobby and force Hinton go through a long drive thru. The staff at this store clearly just want to take the easy way out. The sign outside says under new management- I would hate to know how bad it was before because as it is now it is pretty sad.

The quality of the donuts are what you would expect. Very sugary taste but that is the brand. Donuts are served hot and baked just shortly before. The drive thru could use some love. The ordering board has an annoying welcome to Krispy Kreme how many dozen can I get for you today. This is a recorded message that is not only insincere but very rude to the staff to have machine answer when the motion detector shows you pulled up. Krispy Kreme- value your staff more then trying to sell more the one dozen at a time and the service will be better in the end....

$9.99 for filet mignon + ravioli + some small side of veggies.  lets be honest, for under $10 for a decently cooked filet, is a steal.  it truly was cooked to order (as is not always the case especially with sub $15 steaks in casinos).  the ravioli, though initially i thought "what? 4 raviolis??" was definitely enough.  

for reno i'd say its one of the "classier" restaurants, in a pretty seedy casino.  the restaurant is sparkly clean, and the wait staff is definitely decent.  overall, i'd come back, this is a far better deal than any of the buffets in reno especially when you consider the price.

Considering the reviews about varying quality, I count ourselves blessed that the day we popped in - we thought this was some of the best froyo we've experienced.  The texture was right on, and the flavors full. 

However, the .59/oz price was startling. Across the country we've not yet paid that much - and have typically seen prices in the .39 - .45 range.  So for this, I demerit a star. 

The indoor seating options here are quite limited, and just a few people inside can make this place seem really crowded.

Great service and idea. Poor management leads them to slap a $15 monthly surcharge on us with little to no notice. Thanks but no thanks.. done

**Talked to them today, they are willing to refund the surcharge they slapped on all members, with a canceled membership.  I understand their circumstances..having their gas cards stolen en masse a year ago, and now struggling with the economy. Maybe I'll come back to them, I did enjoy everything about them and their car selections/locations..and they were earth-friendly.**

Random Japanese trivia for your day: Tsuki means "moon."  Welcome to Moon Sushi.  

A friend recommended this place for lunch and they really do have an unbeatable special.  For $10.95, you get three rolls plus the soup or the salad.  I ordered a salmon roll, yellowtail roll, and avocado roll.  Everything was awesome.  It's not the fanciest sushi restaurant I've ever been to (decor is lacking), but the sushi was rolled well and the fish was flavorful and fresh.  What more could I ask for?  Definitely will come back here.

Being the timely people we are, my bf & I arrived to Joe's Water Ice right before they were about to close. (But hey, the neon sign outside still flashed "Open" when I pulled into the lot!)

Joe's Water Ice is pretty good for what it is worth. We ordered a large "Joe 'Latti"...water ice topped off with ice cream. It was 4 bucks and it hit the spot. 

They have a wide selection of soft served flavors and a good choice of water ice as well.

There's two picnic benches off to the side for customers to sit and enjoy their treat.

I've come to this DD just about every day  for a good 5 months or so now and it's been smooth sailing so far.

This summer, one member of the staff remembered my semi-complicated coffee order and recited it to me every day as I walked in. So needless to say, it's a whole lot friendlier than most Dunkin's I've been in and their service isn't too shabby. 

The guy who owns the place, or at least manages the establishment is also great. He makes sure tables get cleaned and floors are swept and is open to inquiries about large orders and things of that nature.

I recently went to Derek's with my family for Mother's day brunch. While this was not my first time at Derek's, it was my first time there for brunch. I thought that the price was just a smidge overpriced for the selection of food they had. I have been to brunch at one of the nearby restaurants and as far as the selection, it did not compare. Derek's is also a few dollars more expensive than some of the nearby places. The food was good however, and the staff was friendly. Overall, I would go back to Derek's. Just not for Sunday brunch.

A real down home bar with a down to earth bartender.  CASH ONLY, their credit card hardware still hasn't arrived!?  I read the previous review from some months ago about the credit card stuff still not having been arrived.  It is still not there, as of the date of this review.  Our group came in to take shots of vodka, since we had reached the end of Chestnut street and were heading back.  This was one of our stops.  The bartender was born and raised in Philly so he knew all the ins and outs of the city.  We were there early, but it was still cool, but empty (nobody there).

I called ahead and it took only 15 minutes to prepare my pies because there was no one out, due to the aforementioned storm. I decided to go for the potato pie. The potato pie featured thin sliced potatoes, ricotta, rosemary, roasted garlic, and mozzarella. This is a bit of a change up from the potato pie by which all others are measured (La Rosa), but I was willing to give it a go. Well, it wasn't too bad. It was actually pretty okay, but no match for the current champ. Not enough garlic, or rosemary for my taste, and the cheese was good, but made it really quite rich. La Rosa wins on simplicity in my book.

Maybe I ordered the wrong thing, but I didn't really enjoy the food. 

The burger was a garlic bomb that I was hand in hand with for the next 4 hours. 

Fried mushroom app was poorly fried and the smoked gouda sauce was like creamy liquid smoke. 

The sweet potato bisque was just gross. It tasted like nursing home food. 

My wife ordered the farmers salad and it was ok, although the vegetable to lettuce ratio was way off. 

I really wanted to love the place as the people in there were very nice and attentive, but no dice.

I love the feel of this place!  I know some reviewers don't like the whole outside dining thing but I really enjoy it.  For the most part, the weather is great enough to dine outside.  However, I could do without all the noise from the street and the awkward parking lot but it's not too much to worry about when you're getting such great food.

All the stuff is delicious but I do love eating burgers so I'm easily satisfied. Everything is so tasty and pretty quick to come out after you order.  It's also very filling and they substitutions like fruit if you don't want to eat anything fried.

I really liked this bar. it's SMALL, so I would probably say don't try to go in there when it's super busy. we came on a saturday around 7 and it was nice. they have 1 bartender and a cool cocktail menu.

I got the "side piece" which was a tequila cocktail and it was phenomenal! the bartender was super friendly and accommodating to us the whole time. we really enjoyed our time spent in here, it was fun!

if you're looking for a low key bar downtown with good drinks, I suggest checking this one out. I look forward to coming back!

very nice stay from start to finish. the pricing was fair (we booked through booking.com) the room was spacious and clean, the view was beautiful, the water was hot. what's not to love? I would say the coffee situation was bad. I couldn't have a cup in the room, but that isn't worth complaining about.

we loved the bed- it was firm but not overly so. lots of pillows. the tv was a good size and had all our channels. the elevator was fast, and the valet was prompt and kind.

there's a reason that the grove is considered one of the top hotels in boise- it's exactly the service and accommodations we expected. I look forward to coming back!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
A solid stay for a Hampton Inn. This was oddly the most affordable hotel in the greater Nashville area so booked it. Nashville hotel prices are getting ridiculously high and staying out if center can save you some money. 

With this Hampton you know what your getting. A great bed, clean and decent pillows. However, pillows were getting worn out so not a great night sleep. I am not one to complain to try and squeeze out a free stay. But they need and upgrade on the lumpy ones I had. 

Breakfast was nothing great. Smaller selection than I have seen at others.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
My little Kia Soul doesn't have a spare, caught a screw in a tire I was going to replace after payday this Friday. Used fix a flat to get it inflated enough to drive. FIrestone won't repair a tire with fix a flat in it. (really not a fan of them but they were closer). Had them inflate it
Called American Tire. Sure, I will look at it.
Looked at it. Fixed it cheaper, showed me how I was in need of the two rear tires ASAP, offered to refund the cost of the fix if I came in to replace the tires after payday.
Will be back Saturday!!!!
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Always an easy go to for delicious Italian food when I can't get down to Florida for Dee's home made.  Good quality restaurant chain. Mall was busy but scored easy parking right outside and no wait for two. Our server Sarah was delightful. The portions are enormous so now we have a second dinner in the fridge.  I always go for the Chicken Parmesan and it was perfect. Would have been a 5 star review however the booths are starting to show their age?i normally sit at a lever table with the crew from work but just two of us in a booth.  Ours had both seats taped together and I got some tape gunk on my shorts. FIX IT!!!!!!!!!

The best thing about Yoko's is that it's always good. It's solid sushi that will occasionally knock your socks off. He gets in fresh local fish and makes pretty spectacular specials with them. I rarely order off the menu. They've got more traditional rolls and then American rolls with all the fixings. I don't know any of the rolls names off hand, which is useful, I know. But I don't really think you can go wrong.

If you're looking for a cool place to go, this is probably not it. It's not hip and trendy. The decor leaves you wanting but the food doesn't and that's what important.

Duckweed moved! It's no longer a cramped little place where the accident prone like myself are terrified they will knock something over and have the store collapse on their head! REJOICE!

The new space is gorgeous and the prices didn't go up! There's a juice bar and a limited menu. They've applied for their on-premise serving license for beer and wine. The beer and wine selection was solid at the other store but it's even better now!

When you're checking out avert your eyes from the ice cream cooler to your right. There is a salted caramel ice cream in there that is just begging to destroy your waistline!

This Hertz location's customer service has been nothing but great throughout the many times I have rented a car from there. 

On my last visit, I was ten minutes late after my drop-off time. I was prepared to pay the fee (unhappily, of course), but the employees immediately offered me the information on how to fix this. I was told that I should speak to the manager so he can make the adjustments. I would have asked, anyway, but to be told this information without me asking was pretty darn great.

I highly recommend this Hertz.

Of course we came back to give it another try, but same still holds true: The restaurant as a whole holds more patrons (than the prior location downtown), but I believe they must need more chefs (sushi chef AKA itamae) as it STILL takes WAY too long to get your order... especially if you order additional rolls half way through your first order!

Also we asked for advice from our server, and she didn't seem to have a clue about sushi nor Sake!! WHAT!!??

The sushi was tasty, as usual!! We love the variety and freshness we have had on a regular basis.

Cuisine would get 4 or 5 stars, but service is only 2 or 3 stars. And this isn't only during happy hour, I have found it to be at any time!! One can understand that sushi has to be prepared on the spot and if an order goes in right before yours, you are going to wait longer... but what about drinks??? Why did our drinks take so long when I can see the bartender isn't swamped? There is no excuse! Thanks for comping one drink for us, but why does this seem to happen every visit?

Must get the 'playboy' appetizer, really good.. and haven't had a roll I didn't like in our numerous visits!

To be honest, thus far I've only dropped off blazers, pants and one dress to be dry cleaned for work a few times but each time my clothes have been dry cleaned properly and ready and waiting for me, no issues. Most recently I brought in a dress that needed a strap reinforced and another piece with buttons replaced and both were cheap and no problem fixed. 

Service was decent too. 

Upon reading the other reviews, perhaps it's best to start with the basics and build your trust. :)  convenient location and will do next day if you are in a pickle.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
A nice selection bulk foods. I always buy my herbs and spices here in bulk. Once you have a container for things like pepper, garlic powder, etc. you can refill them with spices for just pennies. Most of the other prices in this store are great. The store is clean. The big problem is that sometimes they do not have enough checkers. But if you come in at the right times, very late night, or just get lucky during the day the lines are not too bad. The prices are worth the wait in my opinion.
One down side is that they do not accept credit cards, but they do take ATMs.

Dropped in on a Saturday night. Very busy but we were seated in about 15 minutes.

Tarantella is a fairly large place, it takes up two strip mall type store fronts. Decor is nothing special but fine.

Portions were huge as other Yelpers have reported if your looking for big plates. I had the Chicken Francese and it was just average, a little bland for my liking. The other dishes we had were good. The muscles and shrimp Fra Diablo had more flavor.

The owner and family are very nice. The staff was attentive. Tarantella supplies bread and salad with the entrees. It is BYOB which is also good.

First visit there was two years ago for a tire rotation.  I noticed they didn't even rotate the tires before I left and they then corrected.  WTF?  

Second visit was last week to fix a tire blowout (thx to a pothole).  They put a totally different tire brand and tread on the front without even asking me.  I spoke with the manager (Menendez or something)  and he said "it's fine" and acted like "no biggie"...this is a 2011 Volvo I'm talking about.  They really don't care at this shop.  Move on to Firestone down the road or to some other local dealer.  Done with Dobbs.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Never eating here again.  And if I do, I'm only going back for the bread.  Because that was the best part of my meal.

1.  The service - I sat at the bar and ate.  My server/bartender was extremely nice, but a little rough around the edges.  Not to be too snooty, but their uniforms were very...ununiformed.  

2.  I ordered the spicy ricotta meatballs and the crispy artichoke potato cakes.  Avoid these.  They both taste like cardboard.  I also ordered the calamari.  It was nothing special.  I could get the same anywhere...but better.

I don't know.  Part of me wants to give it another chance, but my stomach is not so sure.

B. Major Grade:  D

Shur Brite is a decent car wash.  I think there are a couple of better ones in the city, but this one manages to do a great job...on occasion.  One big plus about Shur Brite is that is locate right off of West End, near Vanderbilt.

Their prices about the same as other car washes in town and I usually just go for the most basic wash that they offer, which is usually good enough to make my car look nice and clean, I think

What I really like about this place is that it is so fast, probably the fastest in town.

When I think of Urban Market, I feel warm and fuzzy inside.  I love Urban Market!  This is pretty much the only grocery store in down town Nashville.  I usually pop in here during lunch for a quick sandwich.  They have a great selection of pre-made sandwiches that are gourmet in taste and gourmet in price!

It is a bit more expensive then most other grocery stores, but then again, it is the only one down town!  The staff here are really friendly and they have good coffee.

Oh, and do not forget to get a slice of their famous chocolate cream cheese cake when the bakery has it!  Very rich and decadent!

Nashville has so many Southern style restaurants it must be hard for them all to compete with each other.  Couser's does a pretty good job, but falls behind in a couple areas.  First, I must say the mashed potatoes are extra creamy and accompanied with the brown gravy they have, makes them even better.  The coleslaw is also pretty good, but too runny for my taste.  I like the atmosphere here, it is just nice and laid back, everyone takes their time.  This is not the type of place you want to go for a quick bite.  Okay the fried chicken is pretty good, but compared to the likes of the better known "meat & joints", it just can't compete!

My girls and I loved coming here to get drinks and dinner. They had the flights and larger martini glasses. It was fabulous....until....they replaced the martini glasses with smaller glasses but kept the prices the same. The drinks are also more "watered down" with juices. We were all disappointed because the food and drinks use to be great for a girls night out. Now it's just not worth it. It's a real shame too. I'm hoping they bring the larger glasses back and quit juicing the martinis down. They get two stars because the food is still great.

Not bad, but not great. 

Hey, the service is great. They actually didn't have power when we came, and they still sat us outside, were able to take credit cards via a Square reader, and could still make most of the menu. Can't complain about the service.

The sushi was just ok. There wasn't anything particularly bad about it or anything, but it didn't really stand out, either.

We'll come back another time, hopefully under more accommodating circumstances, and give it another shot. The prices were pretty good, as was the service, so it's worth coming back again.

I'm not a bar hanger...

So I cannot comment on the bar, which seems to get mixed reviews here.

I have to say though, the food is surprisingly delicious, I have had several lunch & dinners there and I always come back! The ribs are among the best in the area, first boiled (gets 'em tender & takes a lot of the fat away) and then smoked for a pretty long time. And they are really good!! Sides are good too. The boss seems to always be there, and the  waitstaff has always been exceptional, that is my experience. Remember folks, this is a local pub..nothing more, but it is a great example of it's kind!! Stop in for a casual meal..

Although the pricing of the vet isn't too bad, there are other concerns that I have. Each time I go, there is a long wait to see the doctor.  The front desk staff doesn't really know anything about animals, either.  Most recently, I was double charged (an extra $210).  When I called to take care of it, the people at the front acted like I made it up and had no idea how to fix it. She was also very rude! I couldn't believe how annoying she was.  It was sooo frustrating. When my year long wellness plan is over, I'm not renewing.

It's a little hole in the wall shop, but it's nice. The owner, Sunny, is a fireball and has no problem kicking out a rude customer. She's very creative, and always coming up with new nail designs. There are only 3 people on staff, so there can be somewhat of a wait on a Friday or Saturday afternoon. They have no problem doing kids nails too!

The prices are LOW $18 for a full set, $5 for eyebrows, $20 for a pedicure.  They don't rush, but aren't painfully slow either. If you want quality work with no frills, Sunny is the place.

Great place for pizza and drinks! I've been going here for quite some time but haven't gotten around to writing about them. This place gets bumping especially in the summer since they have a bocci court and they've won awards for their court actually. This neighborhood joint serves really great pizza and beer. I usually get this huge sandwich I believed named after the restaurant which has prosciutto, fresh mozzarella, tomatoes and roasted red peppers and onions YUM! I'm a SUCKER for fresh mozzarella. It's two meals in one. Great place to meet up with friends so check it out now that the weather is nice. Bonus plenty of parking.

Great place to grab a sandwich with no waiting.  Pretty generous portion for turkey with cheese or roast beef.  Nice touches include starting with a fresh, delicious roll, roasted red peppers, razor thin sliced onions, and well-paired cheese.  For $5.99 and ready made, you can't go wrong for the neighborhood.  Overall, the store is nice, with a lot of items, if you look hard enough.  They also tend to have some really good sales (esp. meats) so, have a look.  Fresh and reasonable produce and friendly staff, too.

This is one of the best places i have ever stayed.  The people were super friendly and the rooms were ridiculously big.  Not to mention you can get your free drink on with their complimentary happy hour from 5:30-730 thats a huge plus!  Free breakfast in the morning and not just your hard boil egg / cereal kick... You can chow down on freshly made omelets with all the fixings.   

Couple other things..

Free paper at the door was nice.
We had a nice balcony over looking the city.
Accessible to everything you need in walking distance.


Like Arnold said.... "I be back."
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
As with a lot of shops and services in this area, it's got convenience going for it.  Which, when it comes to a dry cleaners, counts for a lot.  But I've used other dry cleaners in other parts of town that I preferred over this one.  

Still, I'm not willing to drive 20 miles out of my way just to get a few items dry cleaned on occasion so Valley Cleaners it is.  It's close and it gets the job done.  The staff isn't particular friendly, the prices are a little unreasonable and the service is merely acceptable.  

It will do but I would like to see a lot of improvement before I add back any stars to this review.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Italian. 

In a city with a number of good Italian restaurants on the hill, this is actually one of my favorites.  Probably because it's local to me, and because it's still classic Italian, with a contemporary atmosphere.

Classic Italian fare, tons of pasta dishes, plenty of sauces, veal, chicken, and other meats galore.  

It's price tag is on the higher side, but definitely worth it.  Excellent wine selection to go with any dish.

Definitely a special event location, like an anniversary, graduation, or birthday dinner.  

Service was excellent, and the server was very knowledgeable about the entire menu.

The key to this place is knowing what to order because there really are a few duds on the menu.  Also, I think that the specials are the same every time I come here--with one very important exception.  They occasionally have veal osso buco which they prepare expertly.  I often call ahead to see if they're serving it before I decide to come in.  The mushroom appetizer is also very good and the lobster ravioli is the best I've ever had.  It's a great place to eat outside when the weather permits but the comfort of that osso buco keeps me coming back during the cold winter months.

I found out about the salon from Groupon. I made an appointment, and was squeezed in very quickly.  Sadie worked with me, listened to my ideas, explained what she was doing as she went, and managed to create a hairstyle using what I wanted and her own innovation.

I am extremely pleased with the results. She was friendly and engaging, and invited me to make comments even after she styled my hair, to make sure that it was what I wanted.

I can be shy when it comes to asking hairstylists for more once my hair is done, and she made me feel completely comfortable doing it, inviting my comments, and working with me.  

Great salon.

This place is cool.  I'm no frozen yogurt fanatic, but I pop in sometimes when I want a little something sweet.  Lots of different flavors & toppings, all are pretty good.  I like how I can get a small amount to satisfy my craving and not have to spend too much.. Being able to completely customize the whole experience is pretty sweet (get it get it?!?!)

It's always packed w/ high school kids.   Doesn't bother me... I guess they need some place to hang out.  Often there's no seats, so you just stand in a corner or step outside.

If you're looking for a quick, cheap, and good-tasting food... you'll probably have to look harder because you won't find it on the surface of Chinatown.  Actually, you'll have to look below it since it's located in a dingy underground next to a so-called "supermarket."

This place does live up to its name... and it is quite "tasty." My usual order is Beef Chow Fun. For $5, they offer generous portions. The only downside is that it can be a bit too oily.  

It's probably one of very few places in Chinatown where the service is friendly... and that's RARE!

Loved the dinner and had a wonderful evening, it is a Carrolton icon!  We started with Oysters Almondine.  My wife followed that up with the veal and I had the seafood medallions.  It was scrumptious and rich!  The portion size was large but not over whelming, but I felt full well into Sunday afternoon.  Our waiter was on the spot with everything with the appropriate amount of attention.  Never once did we feel rushed!  The restaurant is small, I would say tight.  Our 2 top table was right next to the bar.  It felt cramped but not unbearable.

I have been wanting to come to this restaurant.  The food is fantastic. We had the beer glazed pork belly. The sea food risotto and the branzino and for desert ,of course,Tiramisu. They offer a small portion of the risotto. I think that's smart because not everyone can finish a whole plate and leaves you room for more food. 
The ambiance is a bit too loud for my taste is hard to have a conversation across the table with out raising your voice.
The food took a bit too long to come out. We waited  over 40 minutes for our main dishes.
They only offer beer or wine. Which for me is a problem since I am not a big fan or beer and wine.

Scrumptious Pumpkin!  What a lovely place. 

Enjoyed a wonderful dinner at this little restaurant a few months ago.  The $40 5-course Prix Fixe is a supremely satisfying way to spend a Sunday evening, whether it's a special occasion or you just feel like pampering yourselves.  Everything I tried was carefully prepared and tasty.

Sunchoke-Hazelnut Soup was delicious.
Sweetbreads were crispy and tasty.
Smoked Quail was cooked just right, succulent and flavourful.
White Chocolate Goat Cheese Cheesecake was sublime.

Service was great.
Scrumptious food in a pleasant, intimate setting.  Cash only.  BYOB.

Hidden Pizza, you are breaking my heart.

I asked around for the best New York-style pizza in town, and this was one of the strongest recommendations. I was surprised, of course, to be recommended casino pizza, but it seemed like it might just be crazy enough to work, so we went. And it was so close. So. Close. HAUNTINGLY close. But it was just ... not ... quite ... right. :(

If you've never had real New York pizza, this is close enough that you can understand what you're missing. But it's not worth the hassle of hiking through a casino just to get to.

I have a problem.  I can't dance.  Luckily for me there's Sal's.  
I can't think of one time I've gone and not had a blast.  They always seem to get me drunk enough that I think I can dance, but not so shitty so that I make a complete fool of myself.  Just a partial fool.  Which is ok, because no one seems to care.  
They usually have good specials upstairs when something is going on, last night for instance it was free vodka/vitamin waters til 10.  
The staff makes you feel welcome and it's the only place I can say I've rolled a blunt on the bar and smoked it upstairs.

Yeah, I know what you're saying. "You go all the way to New Orleans and you get SUSHI"?? Well, this is possibly one of the BEST li'l sushi houses I've ever been too. Nothing fancy. Only a couple dozen tables but DAMN GOOD SUSHI! 

We ordered four different rolls. All came beautifully presented, prompt and oh so delicious. The salmon sashimi was fresh, firm and plentiful. Tempuras crisp, light, and hot. And the service was very friendly and attentive. 

Say what you will about going against the Creole gods. We'll go again to Sushi Brothers if the opportunity presents itself.

Man, I don't get it.

I've been here a lot since I work right down the street and while it's not an above and beyond experience I've never had problems.

My experience with the staff has been a-ok hence the three stars.  They have always been friendly to me I even remember one of the girls telling me how much she liked my purse one day.

Maybe there has been a staff shift I don't know but I like going to this subway.

It's always clean.
It's always been supplied.
Iv'e always received what I've asked for.

What more could I want?

I'll go again I am sure.

I freaking love Marble Slab. For one reason. 

CAKE BATTER

People say certain things are like an orgasm in their mouth. Well I'd have to say this is it for me. 

It's not in the I've got to go because it has to be loaded up with crap to taste good like another place I won't mention. It's in the simplicity of how good their sweet cream is before loading it down with tons of toppings/mix-ins. 

I lived in Lexington, KY for six years and I literally cried when they closed. 

One mix in 
Sprinkles
One sweet cream
Cake batter 

Do it 
Love it
Drool about it
Dream about it

Our room smelled of heavy bleach when we entered. It was so bad we had to open the window and it was freezing outside! So we cranked up the heat (this works well haha). The room was very small and the bed only had two small pillows. There is a coffee machine in the lobby (makes lattes, coffee, cappuccinos) which was very nice. They validate your parking if you park across the street at Liberty parking lot, so it comes out to $32 instead of the $48. Good central location in Center City. Wouldn't stay here again voluntarily.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Had a corner room with windows across all the walls. Pretty cool to see the skyline. The bed was ridiculously soft and comfortable. I fell asleep in probably two seconds. Very pretty and modern room. Super clean. Like super clean. The toiletries are mounted to the shower wall. It's nice because you don't have to worry about running out of shampoo, but something about the fact that someone could open and "contaminate" the soaps did cross my mind while showering. Can soap even get dirty?!?

Got this hotel using Hotwire. What a steal!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Tiniest restaurant I've ever eaten in, we were sitting at the sushi counter and we had a couple right next to us on both sides. But everyone was nice and respectful of "personal space." :)

Had the 3-roll special for $11 (salmon, eel, and futomaki). The salmon tasted like butter, so good! The eel left a lot to be desired. We also splurged and got a specialty roll: the volcano roll (spicy tuna and avocado). GREAT!!!! Ive had other specialty rolls here and they are all fantastic.  A good place if you want a really casual dinner or pick up. The sushi chefs are really nice!

From the Boot has three locations--Ambler, Lafayette Hill, and Blue Bell. For a while, I was going to the one in Lafayette Hill, but then I discovered this location in Blue Bell and realized it's closer, and honestly, a lot roomier inside. Extra star from me.

When I come to From the Boot, I'm here for three things:

1) The garlic rolls. My favorite.

2) Their arugula salad. Arugula, fresh mozzarella, tomatoes, olives, and pine nuts. It might be one of my favorite salads. 

3) Tiramisu. So good.

Oh yeah, and their pizza and most of their entrees are great too, but really I'm good with those three things.

Upon check-in I got "upgraded"....but somehow I ended up in a double queen instead of a king which is what I originally booked. So I called and asked to be moved to a standard king. Once moved, the standard seemed to be exactly the same as the "upgrade"....weird. But the room was nice and clean. 

The hotel restaurants are ok, the Brewhouse is the better in my opinion. The breakfast restaurant is a rip-off and the servers there keep asking if you are dining alone and then take F O R E V E R to get your a cup of coffee. 

It's ok...just not an amazing experience is all.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This review is based on my delivery order through GrubHub...

We ordered 5 rolls online, just standard like Alaska roll, Philly Roll, Spicy Tuna, etc.. and they arrived really quickly. When we opened them up I was shocked at how much there actually was! 

Each roll was like 7-8 pieces, so they were a little smaller (which I prefer cause you can fit one whole piece in your mouth) and there were a ton of pieces. I only got 2 of the rolls and was full at the 1.5 mark. 

The roll was fresh and they let me substitute white tuna for regular tuna (if you have never tried white tuna, its glorious!). I didn't even mind paying the $1.00 delivery fee!

La Viola has top quality food at Olive Garden prices.  Bring a bottle of your own wine to complete (or begin!) the evening.  A word of caution:  It does get cramped.  A reservation is strongly encouraged, otherwise, if you have a group of two, they'll sit you at a table that's bumped up against some other boneheads that made the same mistake you made.  Then it just feels like an awkward double-date.  So call ahead, make sure you have a group of four, and go during an "off peak" time and you'll have yourself some decent, affordable food in a simple, casual environment.

OK, first off, let me tell you not to expect a beautiful dining room.  This place is located in the basement next to the Asia Super Market, and it is dark and dingy and looks like it could be used as a backdrop for a dimly lit murder scene in a film, but....the food more than makes up for the less than appealing surroundings.  My go to dish is the Singapore noodles, full of spicy goodness and so massive I always get several meals out of it afterwards.  I normally get it to go, because I think eating in the dining area would only make me depressed.

The lines for the ATM are sometimes out the door, and the teller lines aren't much better!  The guard who works there is a little surly towards people when it gets crowded.  Avoid this place on Fridays because it only gets worse!  I used to come here to save time because it is closer to my office, but now I'll head over to the Broad Street branch.  I figure that with the time it takes me to walk over there, I spend even more time waiting in line at the Chestnut street branch.  Plus, the Broad Street branch staff are much nicer and the lines move more swiftly.

I was wondering what happened to this place!  I love KK donuts.  The plain glazed donuts remind me of my childhood.  Their donuts tasted so fresh and delicious!  I was thrilled when they opened up the Center City location because its super close to my office, but when I went over there to check it out, I found the location confusing, and it was hard to find out where the entrance was....guess many others had the same issue, because now its closed.  Its rare that I eat donuts, but  I'm sort of sad that I no longer have this option when I want it since I like KK donuts better than Dunkin's.

This is hotel is very "HIGH- TECH" Their elevators are quite intimidating in the beggining.
Love their gym on the 32nd floor. Breath taking views. Their pool is quite small but atleast they have a pool in the middle of CBD.
Location wise , you can walk to French quarter for around 10 mins . There are a few restaurants close around the area and a really great grocery about 5 minutes walk ( check this out!)
If you are here for business , this hotel is perfect but if you are here for VACA, get a hotel closer to French Quarter.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Great shop.  Everyone there does great work.  Young or old, they've got you covered.  Definitely a diverse crowd in there.  Quick turnover even when it's busy.  Wouldn't go anywhere else.  The only thing that made me do 4 stars instead of 5 is that it's cash only.  I know it's part of the charm and all ... but it's annoying to have to hit the ATM.  Not annoying enough that I would go anywhere else though.  They've got my business as long as I'm in Philly.

Did I mention it's only $13?!  Take that Center City.

I'll admit, I haven't been to Wilmington in maybe 25 years and I have nothing local to compare it to. That being said, we liked it. It's in a neighborhood, a corner spot. They are going for the old school Italian feel, something I am very familiar with. It was a little odd for a TV to be playing an R rated mob movie, but other than that, I liked the look and feel. 
Our server was friendly and good at her job. She made good recommendations and the food was delicious. If we find ourselves back in Wilmington, we would eat here again.

Awesome sushi spot! I love to try new locations however I pretty picky about what's offered as I am an extremely healthy eater. This place was happy to accommodate my requests and even made other healthy suggestions which I was delighted to try. I am back for the second day in a row....I will be returning again tomorrow. Yes! I am just that pleased. Feed me fresh, fast, simple, friend food in a cool atmosphere and I'm good to go. No need to fix what's not brokenI love this place it's my new favorite of the month

Sure it's an airport location with no extravagant leather sofas, industrial working tables are super cool baristas but it's an airport location...what more do you want but your daily dose served up just in time to board your flight outta this joint.

Located inside Terminal 1 just past the security checkout and next door to Dunkin Donuts.

Prepare for long lines but it moves pretty quickly if you know what you want and don't hold the line up ordering a tall cappuccino with a splash of soy milk, slightly shaken not stirred over a few cubes of ice in a grande up, half pump of hazelnut with a fan of whipped cream on top!!!!! STOP IT PEOPLE

Cheaper than Whole Foods and nicer than Winn Dixie but every few times we go there they overcharge us for something. Once they charged us $1.50 per potato instead of per pound. On several occasions things marked on sale rang up at the original price. Once they rang up cucumbers as broccoli, tripling the cost. So unless you enjoy donating money to a supermarket you have to either watch everything as it gets rung up or closely review your receipt. If you point out the mistake they will give you cash back at the customer service desk but oddly they never apologize...

I love Fresh Market! I need a larger basket to push around. I have really been hitting there little "Olive Bar" area a lot lately. The Ceviche and seafood salad are wonderful afternoon snacks or a full lunch. They have a great fresh bread selection. Their deli counter staff are always attentive and helpful and the quality of their fare is high. The meat counter seems always to have some type of special to get you in but then everything looks soo good I always buy more! It's a little pricey but it's worth the fast in and out Wow just like this review!

Good place (the only place) for a lunchtime sushi craving if you're already in Belle Chasse with time to spare.

I've been here 3 times for lunch. The food is all fine, I like that they serve root beer. The prices are definitely comparable or lower than Westbank sushi joints.

The sushi's just... meh. The fish itself has never been bad, but the pieces are different heights and there's always 1 or 2 pieces per roll that don't even stay closed on the way to your table. Never had that happen at a sushi restaurant before.

This is a restaurant in the Westin Hotel. And I would agree with anyone who would prefer to venture out into the Quarter to seek out food and booze. My wife and I used the restaurant twice on this New Orleans vacation. No need to go into the reason and we were happy.

The food is good and the service was even better. Bonita, Dedra, and Bernard made sure we were served properly and our glasses remained full. Whether that was with water or the good stuff. 

The food is on the high side but the portions are large. If you just don't wish to go out and need something to eat that will satisfy you River 127 is acceptable.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Love everything about this place!

Stopped here for lunch and got their lunch tray...for $10 you get 3 tacos and a salad or soup. Perfect lunch portion! I had the fish taco, spicy chorizo taco, pork pastor taco and the chopped salad. All of the tacos were bursting with flavor and everything was super fresh. The salad was great too with fresh avocado, coijito cheese and even crumbled up tortilla chips!

The decor is also very cool...very beachy chic. Service was also excellent. They have a system where you can put a card in a holder that signals the server if you need something. 

Will definitely be back when I need a taco fix!

We weren't impressed with the sushi (but we're not exactly "sushi people") and most likely wouldn't order it again. The 4 stars is mainly for the Ramen, which we're pretty new to but both thought was super delicious. We would absolutely go back for it. Prices are reasonable and service was good. Not the greatest ambiance for "date night," perhaps why we saw so many take out orders while we were there! Probably best suited for that or casual lunch. We'll definitely be picking up some Ramen here in the future.

They recently updated this Starbucks location. It looks brighter, more open and modern. I don't feel like it added any more seating space, but now there are lounge chairs and some booth spaces as well as a longer table to accommodate individual people working. The two-person tables are round and a bit small if you're both wanting to work on laptops or have books to spread out so keep that in mind. I do like the look of the space and they did fix some of those nasty potholes so the parking lot's improved since my last review.

Though the staff is nice, after two visits, I decided this place was not up to par. I mean they do have a good and varied menu; however, there are far better places for a fair price in the Nashville area. My main complaint with Fujiyama is that they have a poor selection of combos and their sushi is a bit on the pricy side. Though I will not argue their authenticity, I can get better at both Hanabi and Sonobana. Their lunch specials are also seriously lacking and even Ginza is better than them in this regard.

Now that I've gotten to know this place better, I find that it's a *great* place to watch a game! I come here less for the food now; I just prefer to slide up to the bar, chat with the bartenders, snack on tequila and guacamole (delicious, by the way), and watch whatever event catches my interest at the moment. Their 4 big-screen TVs are placed on the bar only, so this is not the best option for a large crowd. I just never expected a place like Borracho to become my neighborhood bar, but it fits the bill really well.

I really enjoyed my meal here. We were a large group, which was accommodated easily and quickly for a Friday night reservation. The staff was both friendly and efficient, explaining the specials and delivering our food very promptly. I just had a salad (womp womp), but I noticed that the portion sizes of my dining companions' pasta dishes were pretty huge. Everyone left satisfied and content, which is always a good thing. 

The atmosphere at Chiarella's is very homey. You really do feel as though you're in a dining room of a real South Philly Italian home. The place is just very comfortable.

Having read all the hype on Yelp, I must say that I'm slightly disappointed. The yogorino was good, though not the best frozen whatever that I've had. I got the Toblorone and chopped hazelnuts for my toppings, both of which were delicious. Don't get me wrong, everything was great, but I was expecting some life-altering experience that just never materialized. I would, however, recommend stopping in if you're in the neighborhood and aren't in the mood for Capogiro. The next time I go back, I'm going to try the gelato and do an update.

Great eye candy behind the counter, though. And the toppings didn't look bad either! o_O

I have never actually graced the doors of this joint, but I eat delivery from here more than I'd care to admit. I'm not sure if that will make this the fairest review ever, but like I said, I eat from here a lot. 
My order doesn't often vary, the lunch combo with spicy tuna roll and tuna roll comes with miso soup and a salad. It's around $10, an excellent deal any day of the week.  The tuna is always fresh and is delivered quickly.  Their bike delivery people aren't scary looking or smelling either, and in the FQ there is something to be said for that.

WHY OH WHY wont the northern suburbs get froyo....... *tear*

I love frozen yogurt and sweet ending is just like red mango, pinkberry, yogurtland, etc. if you've heard of those and/or tried them. You dispense what flavor and how much yogurt you'd like yourself and then add the toppings you want (healthy stuff like fruit or sinful things like chocolate)-weighing it at the end and being charged for how heavy it is. The pricing is the same as any other froyo joint, you'll be spending $3-$6 on just you.

They have seasonal pumpkin flavor right now!

I've been here three times but it's not a place I must go back to, only in emergencies when I don't have time for parking/driving in manayunk for Christie's ---wasn't particularly thrilled about the service but it got the job done in a pinch. If you're looking for the newest polish colors by (essie, opi, the like) you should opt for bringing your own OR just going elsewhere. Eyebrow wax wasn't worth it--she rushed through it & no clean up tweezing. Three stars bc it was clean & plenty of nail techs so no wait unless they're extremely busy (pssst come as early as possible if on Saturday)

Tampa has lots of other sushi restaurants that are better than this.  The sushi was mediocre.  I'm not a picky eater and I'm still not sure why I wasn't happy with the sushi but I've eaten enough sushi/sushimi combinations to know that it wasn't good.  maybe the temperature, the texture?  I was drinking water after each bite.  And probably worse - the service was horrible!!  I waited at least 10 minutes before I got my drink and another 10 min before I could get my order taken.   trust me folks.. lots of other choices with better fish in that area...

It's an update... so obviously something happened, right?

RIGHT! I haven't been here in forever... I'm so disappointed. The burrito was awful... the bottom half was just rice, a bean or two.. very little corn and spots of sour cream... 

After eating it, I actually wished that Chipotle had been open on 12th Street. 

The brownie made my day better. The manager (i believe) was so nice and attentive which made the waiting pleasant and not seem so bad. However, I'm sure I won't be back to that location for a while... just saying.

Chase is a national bank that works like a small business.  They are constantly improving their service.  I love this bank!  This location is close to my house, so I'm here every other week!  Fortunately I rarely have to go inside or through the teller drive-thrus because the ATM does everything I need it to!  I do most of my banking online, and I can deposit cash or checks and withdraw cash at the ATMs here.  I only go to the tellers when I need smaller bills, gold coins, $2 bills, or when the ATMs are under repair, which is a rare occasion.  The tellers here have never given me any problems though!

What a strange place. We went one day after work at about 6 pm. When we pulled up we thought the place was closed, then we went inside and really thought they were closed. It's a big place but we were the only ones there. 

Red flag? Maybe, but we persevered.

Good thing! The sushi was great, especially their special roll. The miso soup was different but had a good flavor. The crabmeat salad was tasty and fresh.

Service was good though I could have done without the loud pop music playing in the background.

My only question is...why don't more people go here?

I was never a big Mexican foodie... I am Italian and actually have family members that own Mexican restaurants, but never got into it. We moved downtown and love to eat out, unfortunately, there are few places to go. 

Anyways. Long story short, it's a great place to eat. I enjoy the quesadillas, chimichangas and Soft tacos, they are delicious. 

I think some of the reviewers are overly critical. You can't please everyone, but to compare the food to Taco Bell... Come on. Some of you take Yelp way more serious than you should.

I've been with this bank for yearrrrs!! when it was "Commerce" Bank but!!, today will probably be a FULL MOON, I called the main number #888-751-9000 numerous x's no answer, the call my main branch, Broad & Sansom, place on hold 15 mins. Eventually, hung up called back asked for the manager, said, he was busy, left my #..well, if, he called me, Obama called me. At this point, I'm thinking their's an apocalype (Walking Dead fan) . I did speak with Olga, said computers are down to call back later x30 mins. Believe I'm going to close this account & take my little $5.00 elsewhere.       toodles!

This place is so amazing!  So happy the empty haru place is finally something and not douchey! I used to live in old city and this is the best excuse to come back this way! The fried chicken and kale salad was awesome! Can't wait to try other items! Being from the south this is just what I need in Philly!! Our waiter (Harry) was so great! Definitely recommend if you come! Another man helped us as well, Todd, also amazing! And to the chef, if you are reading this- please bring back the okra!!! You will have my heart forever ! We will definitely be back!

I was not impressed!  I've heard such good things about this place but the prices are outrageously high for mac 'n cheese, large plate and a soda $16!  I got the pesto mac 'n cheese and there was just no flavor.  This place opened up about a year ago and the inside is already beat down, scrapes on the wall, mismatched colors on the walls, weird art, cheap furnishings.  Theres really just not much appeal to this place.  The nail in the coffin was that they carry PEPSI products.. YUCK!

What it has going for it: The staff was very friendly!

Super tasty cocktails, cool ambience, but most of all, an awesome experience!  We were listening to a jazz trio, and on this lovely night, with the doors open (in January! this Northeasterner was thrilled), in wanders another guy, who asks, "Can I join you guys?"  They said, sure, what do you feel like playing? Fast forward a bit, and we're up to three guys in the band, playing amazing music.  We liked it so much that we came back the next night... where we saw the same "trio" with only one of the same people.

Eh. I keep wanting to like this place more. I go back because they really have a good beer list. Nothing I've ever eaten here has blown me away. Decent burgers, okay pork and chicken cutlet. Menus is mostly sandwiches. Today we went and it took just as long to get our check and sign the credit card receipt than it did to order and eat our meal.  A little frustrating especially with a small child but this has been exception to the rule. I'll go back when I see beers I like on tap but not sure I go out of my way otherwise.

Delightfully average. The hostess almost seemed bothered by us being there. We were seated within view of the host stand and at least we weren't the only one to get the underwhelming welcome. 

Our server was George.  Incredibly personable and someone you'd just want to hang out with and grab a beer sometime. Good enough waiter and he was great with our toddler. 

Food was average.  Some small plates and desserts look amazing in writing,  but don't meet the expectations. 

Overall i wanted to like this place allot more but couldn't.

Wow, the reviews are killer on this place.  Having graduated from Penn, I went here fairly often for lunch and I never found it to be all that bad.  Service can be slow but the pizza is pretty good.  It's certainly better than most of the pizza joints in UCity, even if it's more expensive.

Don't go here expecting high end Italian or low end pizza.  It's a "classy" pizza joint, for what that's worth.  Paying $8 for a small pizza that is pretty high quality might turn off a lot of people.  Still, the quality is good and if you take it for what it is, you should be satisfied.

Went here for Restaurant Week, selected as it's a BYO and offered an additional fourth course. 
The first course, scallops, were cold and the second and third course, Bolangnse and Branzino were okay. The dessert, tiramisu, was obviously unfrozen and tasted watery.
Service was very young and awkward. A Penn frat rented the back room for an event, and there was a steady stream of young men, eh boys, lowering the median age of the restaurant staff and guests to about 18.
Won't be back. There's much better byo's in the area.

Had to update. Went back a few weeks ago and was so disappointed. Food was BAD, especially entrees. The pasta and soup were the best of the bunch. The creamcellos at the end are the highlight. 
Don't think I'll go back, SO many better restaurants on the Ave!!! Especially considering it's prix fixe and dinner took close to two hours due to slow service, even though there were only two other tables in the restaurant. Decor is dated as well. Don't want to beat a dead horse, but go elsewhere, unless they start a la carte and service improves.

I'm a byo-aholic, and went here to celebrate a friend's engagement. It is located on South Street, but don't let that scare you as South Street has a reality check on Broad Street, so you're safe from Flash mobs, and cheesy tshirt stores and Duck Tours.

Pumpkin is a big name in that neighborhood, with a Cafe and a to-go store all in Grad-ho.

The space is small, but this cute spot is great for a special occasion. To be honest, none of the food really stood out or was very memorable, but the cozy, candle lit atomsphere was very comfortable and would tempt me to come back.

I am really surprised this place has OK reviews, but mine is for LUNCH so maybe dinner is better. I had the buffet, so maybe I should just expect what I got because sushi buffet for $10? Is that ever going to be good? 

Eww. It was rather gross, though. The rolls have very little fish, if any, and most of them were fried. One even had imitation crab as the meat. I LOVE sushi and really just should not have tried such a thing as a sushi buffet.... what was I thinking? (Oh, I bought the groupon and need to use it on something.... )

I was overzealous in my first review.

The fresh meat is questionable. 

The sweet fruit is said to be so because it is overly ripe and going to rot in 24 hours. Look for the flies that are buzzing above the dying. 

The predictably cheap, 0.99 cents veggies are napa, cabbage, some varieties of bok choy, the occasional red leaf lettuce, and string beans. 

I have noticed that they do carry a decent selection of Asian species in a variety of price ranges. But rotting fruit? it's not even offset by the expensive price!

The problem with Derek's is that the food quality is inconsistent.  You could order a dish on Monday and it will be fabulous, but on Wednesday that same dish could be bland or over-seasoned. I have eaten here many times, and each time I leave feeling alright about my dining experience.  

They have an extensive wine list with something to please everyone. There are good deals on lunches, and dinner is reasonable. The service is always great, and try to save room for their wonderful deserts.

All in all, there are better places to get dinner on Main Street. If you're looking for drinks and some bar food, Derek's is fabulous.

My boyfriend and I ordered take out here because we somehow ended up with one of their menus. We actually chose this place over another chinese place because they had more vegetarian options and they just happened to have better prices too.

It was one of those situations where my dish was full of mystery flavors. (Hmm, salty, fishy...oh god.) You know, like every bite tasted different....until I finally took a bite that grossed me out so bad I couldn't finish it.

My boyfriend didn't seem to have this problem but his dish was spicy.

So yeah, I'm kind of turned off at the idea of ever eating there again.

In South Street life, there is one certainty: Dairy Queen is world's better than Rita's.

I like Dairy Queen. Ice Milk, while it creates a really unpleasant image in my head, has made DQ great for the duration of my life. I agree, Blizzards are the way to roll... in the Snicker's/Cookie Dough variety.

I'm not liking Cold Stone anywhere... but I will say that DQ needs to get their act together. This one can be pretty hella dirty... but it's one of the only places in the 215 that doesn't justify a $5 milkshake. 

It's ice cream people.

Okay, not the greatest pizza in the world. Rustica seems sophisticated on the inside, but this is really more of a grab-n-eat pizza place that happens to uphold Northern Italian pizza-making.

The only time I tend to go is in warmer weather, because there is a nice sized outdoor seating patio. The only problem... there's nothing to look at, just a sea of concrete. Still, this area is general is a bit slim on good eating, so Rustica won't disappoint, and the place fixes its face a bit for the dinner crowd... but I truly only find it appealing at lunch.

I don't hate the Marathon Grill nearly as much as my peers here, but I admit - I don't frequent them often.

The menu, I like... but you're always gonna expect it a few notches below the great writing used to describe it. I think much of Marathon's charm depends on the location. I like the spot @ 16th & Sansom, but wouldn't set foot on the one on 13th & Chestnut. People speak highly of the "Mar Bar" @ 40th Street too, especially for Thursday happy hour. 

I think these are a cute Philly chain, and I prefer seeing the block neon lettering than just another Ruby Tuesday's, TGIF, or other striped eyesore.

I bet this place was hop-ping when Reagan was pres.

Despite wonderful reputations in other cities (I've stayed in Pittsburgh, Orlando, Dallas), Philadelphia's own Embassy Suites just looks/feels tired.

The lobby is crowded and worn out. The rooms are given that tropical garb (dude, you're in Philly). The restaurant is trashy looking. With neighboring Four Seasons and the chance you can snag The Ritz or Sofitel on an online bargain, why settle?

For the money, Embassy needs to step their Philly game up. It's a good night's stay in a prime location, but compared to the reputation this company has, Philly's slacking.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
