Years ago, Quizno's never made a pound of sense to me. They charge $8 dollars to Subway's $5, just because they have a toaster. 

Now Subway has a toaster too, as does Wawa, and everybody else in 2007. So recently, a friend and I had little time, and everything was closed in the area, so he dragged me into Quizno's.

I was kinda impressed. You're still paying what you could be for a sit-down casual dining lunch, but the combo includes a decent cesar salad, a drink, and the sandwich selection is much better. After growing disappointment with Subway, I think I might've traded sides and become a Quizno's guy, when it comes to food done fast.

Located far enough from the tourist riff-raff is Beer Sellar, which just happens to be a bar in a cellar. Very misleading title, I know.

There's not much to say about this place, except that they have probably the largest beer selection that I've ever seen. I only stayed for one beer, but I really liked the atmosphere in there. It had the vibe of a bar that would have a ton of regulars that the bartenders all knew. It's spacious, has both pool tables and a jukebox, and also plays the games on TVs behind the bar.

Definitely a bar to check out if you're looking for a nice and laid back spot to drink.

Often disappointed. Their coupons are mostly nonsense. You get a free sandwich when you buy a sandwich, but not if you buy a combo. 

Their burgers are 'made with 100% real beef'. See the 'with' in there? that means that even though the beef is 100 percent beef, its not the only ingredient in the burger. 

Sure sounds like its only beef though. Weird. What else is in it? Why tell us that their beef is 100% beef? What else could their beef be? 

Their fries are not vegetarian and have wheat and dairy. So much for being potatoes, fried in oil.

The location is great and the staff are outstanding. From checkin to parking attendants, everyone was helpful and pleasant. Unfortunately, our room was near the elevator so I listened to the elevator bang all night. The carpet in our room was stained and disgusting. The service in the dining area for dinner was nonexistent. This was the worst service I've ever had. I expected someone to tell me I had to cook our meal myself. The waitress basically ignored us as long as possible and we had to ask for everything. I will choose another hotel for my next visit.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This is a super nice new location off Bruce B Downs near the Wiregrass mall. I do not have a checking account with them, but I do have a mortgage with Chase, which I pay by visiting this location once per month. I'm always blown away by how friendly everyone is and there's never a wait to see a teller. They seem to have a lot of new technology such as ATM's that seem to do as much as the tellers do, but the employees are what leave an impression. They are so nice and friendly, and I'm always greeted upon arrival and when I depart. I also like how you can park at the back and at the front, because it has double entrances.

My friend and I had an "oh goodness let's just get out of the city" moment last night, and we found ourselves at The Phil's .  I think I spent 45 minutes deciding what to get on their mile- long menu, but once my ribs arrived, oh man.  My dad is well known as an excellent rib cook, and I have tried many many delicious versions, but these were seriously great.  I didn't even need a knife, I could just slide the bone off the meat. Wow.  The place feels neighborhoody, our waitress was nice, and I would totally go back if I'm in the  area again.  Bonus points for crayons on the table for some pretty great napkin drawings.

Apparently the prices are cheap but it must be a joke that I just traveled across the country on a 9 hour trip and they have 1 PERSON WORKING. I get that it's late, but we will literally be waiting online for another hour and a half since there's 2 other people waiting. And did I mention that despite the fact that they obviously know that a lot of people reserved cars and they are all arriving on this flight, they still only have 1 PERSON WORKING!!??

Update, first I gave 1 star but I just upgraded to 2 cause after enough people complained they got some people from Avis to help. Still waited over 30 min.

I have been to Bertolini's twice. The place is just okay to me. It is good though. I expected better though. Twice I got the mediterrian salad, and enjoyed it! One time I had a virgin strawberry daqiuri, and somehow I had a fly in my drink. I'm usually don't make a big deal over anything, so I just let it go, and left the drink there. I did end up going again a second time. However, besides the salad, I enjoyed the soup very much. It was a special soup, a creamy clam chowder. The desserts there are good there as well.

Their selection of froyo is so-so, but their topping bar is def making up for it!! If you can think of it, I think they have it. From cereal to candy bars, from Fruit to cheesecake, they have it! I wish they had 10 or 15 more flavors to choose from, but they had what I like, so its all good, and I will be back! I had the birthday cake and the cheesecake flavors, both were really good. I used a little of a bunch of different toppings....Too many to list!! The divider they have was good to make sure to get the different flavors and compare them. Walking distance makes it a spot to visit often.

Not a bad spot for a roast beef sandwich but the experience could have been much better.
We came to this restaurant because Angelo's taste was closed on a Sunday.
I ordered the beef brisket sandwich. It was coated in a flavored spicy mayo and bbq sauce. However the meat was scarce on the sandwich and the meat was pretty dry. 
The pumpkin cheesecake shake, which I assumed was a holiday treat, was fantastic. 
It also took them a while to serve all of us. Not bad customer service, but a $10 price tag for a meal and a shake with dry meat is pretty excessive.

Ordered delivery for a large, thin crust, Hawaiian pizza, chicken wings, and lasagna. Delivery was on time (45 minutes - one mile) and the food arrived hot.

Pizza: Very large. Floppy, underdone, and doughy. Thin, flavorless cheese layer. Very small amount of utterly bland, sauce. Tiny bits of pineapple and ham. 

Lasagna: Small helping. Greasy. Bland. Watery. Very poor quality.

Chicken wings: Best part of the order. They were moist, good sized, and mildly spiced. Good amount of sauce. The ranch sauce was bland and had an off flavor.

Overall, very disappointing.

As an Ohioan, I'm super excited to have our ice cream represented here in St. Louis!

There are so many great aspects of Jeni's that I don't know where to begin! First, their menu changes, so if you can't find the flavor you're looking for, just come back in a couple weeks. Until then, try a new flavor you've never had before! Second, this is quality ice cream that's made with quality ingredients. Third, every flavor I've ever tried is super rich and punches you in the tastebuds! Fourth, if you're on a diet, you can feel good about the the small scoops or "half scoops" as they call them.

Stopped on my way home to pick up dinner as a spur of the moment decision. It was early for dinner so I waited in the car while one other person picked up her order. I overheard the older gentleman giving her some advice. When I pulled up to get my order, same guy remarked about my dogs in the car. I told him one was sick and he gave me advice on massaging his back to help his lungs. The food was pretty good, as I remembered from a visit a while ago. I've been wanting to go back but haven't yet. Maybe I'll ask for some advice about what ails me next time.

i really wanted to love this place..because the people there were so nice.. but the food wasn't the best i've had..

We ordered:

fried tofu
pepper chicken
dragon roll 
kamikazi  roll
shrimp udon 
beef dunburi

nothing really "wowed" me..the flavoring was just okay... the portions were small for the price..and the rolls were a little skimpy on the more expensive ingredients.. 

i would come back though if i was in the neighborhood and wanted some japanese food.. i guess this place just open.. so i think they're still experimenting..it has potential.. ..the decor and everything else look clean and nice..

My Mom and I ate here for lunch yesterday. She insisted I write a review because she doesn't "Yelp" and wanted this fine eatery to receive its due credit.

We split the fish tacos and tacos dorados. Then we each had a flan custard dessert (which we could have easily shared). Everything tasted wonderful, the fresh ingredients were in fact light and refreshing, and portion sizes were perfect (for two gals who love to eat mind you).

This place--so surprisingly cheap, especially for the area--has been added to our canon of homey, nourishing restaurants to go for no-frills, food-y food.

Just off the Courtney Campbell causeway is the Best Western Bay Harbor Hotel. It's tucked in an alcove off the road and houses Hogan's Beach. I was there because I was obtaining my CEU's for Massage, so we used their conference rooms. They were large but noisy since they were tucked up against the kitchen.  I can honestly say this was a huge distraction when you're trying to do some energy work. 

Over all, it's got some nice features, but a big drawback is the way their bathroom in the public area isn't kept up.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Not my favorite DD location.  I stopped here on the way to my HOS orientation. The hope was to get myself an iced caramel swirl latte. No such luck, it seemed that the latte machine (?) was broken. I think the woman meant the espresso machine, but I could be wrong.  

In any case, I asked then for a brewed coffee with caramel and cream, which would replicate the drink I was looking for. What I ended up getting was -not- that, but it was "almost' drinkable.  

The new coffee-creme donut is delectable though. I recommend that.

Date night, Apparently there are 2 locations in Oldsmar and I was at one while the beau was at another. While I waited for him to join me at this location, I ordered my hot chai Tea. Jonah was absolutely wonderful. He was personable and friendly and exceptionally warm. We chatted about how our names are different (my alternate Id) and how we don't often hear them, though mine is growing popular due to Anime. 

Once my order was placed, it took only a few minutes to have it in my hands so I could wait for Bruce to join me. I'd come back.

Stopped in for a wash before I headed out of state on a trip. I purchased their $20 unlimited, Note to self, download the ap before the month runs out. 

THe wash itself was pretty nice, the track is smooth as you're taken through the soap and brushes, and different color sprays as they hit your vehicle and take off the debris and road grime. 

Once you're blown dry and unloaded, you're able to go over and use the vacuums that are under a covering. The first one I pulled up to was very weak, as if clogged, so I moved to another unit and had far better luck. 

I'll be back.

Still new and working out the kinks. This is one of the harder DD's to get in and out of because of their location RIGHT in front of a mobile home park, adjacent to a Waffle house and some god forsaken construction. 

The crew is somewhat in need of training, however it depends on who you get. I've gotten excellent service and I've gotten some absolute horrible stuff too. I mean when you order a caramel swirl coffee and get something pecan flavoured you kind of want to cry. And then sometmes you don't get your flavor at all... Le sigh. 

Still when they're on the money, they're on the money.

I was wanting some Mexican. We'd stopped in here once before and were impressed, so we opted to try it again. 

The service is hit or miss, but the food. The food is the star of this place.

My husband had the enchiladas and I opted for the fajitas. Lets talk about portion size. The amount of meat I got with my fajitas was AMAZING. It would have fed 2 people, and I'm not even exaggerating, the sides they served it with Rice, beans, lettuce, pico, guac and sour cream were all top notch, but they skimped on the guac and the sour cream. 

Everything was hot, fresh and made to order. SO DAMN GOOD!

We opted to go here instead of our original brunch decision since they had a line out the door. When we walked in, the owner was having a chat with someone over either a job interview or some such, but we were pretty much dismissed, until the person behind the counter asked if we were placing an order for here or to go.. Clearly their dining room isn't used very often.  We opted for here. 

We sat down and waited for our Caprese salad, which was delicious, and then our Pizza. When it came out, the only thing I can say about it is that it could have been baked a tad longer but otherwise it was tasty. I enjoyed it.

A beautifully laid out Publix in the Fishhawk Ranch area of Lithia. It is large and neat, well lit with a large parking lot. 

We popped in to do some grocery shopping for my brother in law who is currently laid up due to an injury.  While things weren't in the usual places, like they are at our local Publix, but we were able to locate everything we needed, or ask an associate and find out where things were, with an offer to take us to them, which we declined. 

My brother in law did well this week, nearly everything on his shopping list was bogo, which Publix does quite frequently, making shopping at publix truly a pleasure.

I have to agreed with other yelpers.  My first impression of the lobby was very positive and as I walk back to take the elevator everything about this hotel starts to deteriorate.  The rooms are very outdated.  The bathroom is very small and the furniture other than the flat screen tv are from another generation.  The super thin walls is like sharing a room with your neighbor.  If it wasn't for the water park attached to the hotel I won't be staying here.  I hope they finish up the renovation quick.  I was lucky to get on the third floor.  Don't stay next to the water park unless you like hearing foot traffic.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Hertz had the least expensive car rental prices for the week we were in Tucson, and generally the experience wasn't bad-- but the car we got was super scuffed up even though they told us it was "brand new." We made sure to document the scratches and scrapes so that we couldn't be charged for it later. But when we were driving the car, the check engine light kept coming on with more and more frequency. We only had the car for two days! It would have been nice if the car had been in better condition from the start.

Is it amazing ice cream? No.  Is it cheap? No.  Do people line up around the block for it? Yes.

Why?  

It is a Seminole Heights standby.   It's been in the same place, serving basically the same menu since my parents visted.  It brings back fond memories of biking from Hillsborough High School when they were younger and they love to go back.  


They have shaved ice/icees (?) too which are good and are what I normally order.  

They also have a doggie ice cream that my pup enjoys and the people that work behind the counter are always friendly even when the store is extremely busy.

Love the food here! The bruschetta here is to die for and the lobster ravioli was absolute perfection. The service was very nice and our server was great and extremely helpful by giving us recommendations based on what we liked. Only funny thing that happened was that our to go order was switched with someone else s and we were given another tables leftovers. The crowd here was a little uptight but I don't really mind that. However, I felt I should mention that for readers who are intimidated by crowds like that. We will for sure be back!

Only went once, as part of a group dinner outing. We were expecting around 20 people so we made a reservation for that many, but as our group trickled in they REFUSED to seat us until all 20 were there. Don't most places allow you to sit as you arrive? Of course they do. But they were ultra-shady because they suspected most of our group would flake, which they didn't.

Then the place was ridiculously noisy because it's basically a place for frat dudes and sorority babes to get rowdy. SO noisy and loud, and then the food was a complete snooze for twice what it was worth.

Like I said. I've been here ONCE. Point made.

I'm bumping Old Point up to "respectable" (see my previous review).

I've figured out there's some really good food...& some not-so-great. But hey...some places don't have any really great food...making Old Point...respectable.

And the beer: well, draught selection isn't huge, but the choices are...respectable. Bottle selection is high, but they're a smidge pricey.

Most of all -- I've had really excellent service lately. That's beyond respectable...so good job Old Point!

And....loving the smoke-free-ness. Honestly, I never thought I'd see the day.

Like many Chinese places in Tucson, the quality depends on what you get here.  Some of the American favorites such as sesame chicken are downright embarrassing.  Other, also American faves, like Foo Young got high marks from my family.  The Mongolian Beef was just okay.  I stuck with noodles, as that seems to be the one thing that is consistently good here in Tucson.  The Thai Basil Chow Fun was very delicious.  I also liked the veggie fried rice, dry, but filled with an abundance of veggies.  Prices are high but portions are very large, feeding 2 easily.  Take out was fast, like 15 minutes fast.

This place isn't terrible, but it's not really good either. However, considering what is around the area in terms of sushi, it was alright. This is a Chinese-owned establishment that has a nice muted Japanese ambiance. I love their fish tank! Their service is excellent. Water was always filled, questions all answered and orders received promptly. The food is so-so. The rice is terrible, but the fish is not bad. I would get anything that is less traditional, it seems to taste better. Perhaps mayo helps mask the poor execution.

Food: It was okay- think of someone melting a ton of cheese on top of over-sauced noodles and it's pretty much the same thing. Just rotate the type of meat or pasta you use and change the name :). A bit on the pricey side for their quality of food and service. Also not sure if they're short on wait staff but our server took her time on almost everything. 

Ambience: I heard the Milano Inn is a classic in Indy and has been around for a long time. It's owned by an Italian family and has that Italian diner feel. Folks around were saying they come here more for the tradition than food really.

Cancun in Carmel is solid. I think I would probably give the food 3 stars, but I always get really good, friendly service when I go, so I bumped it up to 4 stars.

Most of the menu items are fairly typical of what you would find in a fairly authentic Mexican (Tex-Mex) restaurant trying to appeal to American (particularly Midwestern Americans.) Portion sizes are generous (I usually get 2-3 meals out of one order of fajitas), and the prices are reasonable. The prices are really great if you order one of the daily specials. There are even daily specials on the weekend, which is nice.

Ok, it is a Starbucks. If you drink coffee, you've been to a Starbucks. I typically don't write reviews for chains, especially the really big ones. However, what makes this Starbucks great is the service.

I have never had bad service at this Starbucks. There have been one or two time that something has taken longer than it should have. (Usually it is my son's Java chip frappuchino) However, they go out of their way to make it right and correct the issue.

The staff is always very friendly and typically speedy, even when they are really busy. This Starbucks is a well-oiled machine.

The staff are so very friendly, and not in that fake customer-servicey way.

Beer selection is banging'. This last time I came for a Growler refill and left looking like like I was hosting a party of 1,500 because I'd picked up two Growlers and 5 other bottles/cans. I always forget they have an awesome selection of non-Growly beers.

The last time I was there, the parking lot was overwhelmed with giant Jade beetles. A stranger and I cowered in fear for a good 10 minutes trying to get into our cars. I almost dropped my box full of beers!

Best sushi in Pinellas County - may be the best in the Tampa Bay area!  

Oh, but the blue lights... those intense, terribly bright, blue lights.  I don't know what Jimmy was thinking but I really wish he'd get rid of the lights.  On a positive note, he has some nice salt water live rock aquariums with live corals if you're into that sort of thing.

Even in spite of the BLUE LIGHTS, it's still our absolute favorite sushi restaurant in the area.  

If you go, you absolutely have to try the Triple Threat. That's my big tip for this review, and if he'd get rid of those blasted blue lights, I'd bump this up to five stars!

They have been open long enough now to really get their act together. They passed me on the list (I've been sitting waiting the entire time) and now I have been waiting 45 min because a party walked in. No sincere apologies for never letting me know this reservation was in place or offer to make the situation better. And, my best friend had to go to the doctor after they chopped her cuticles too low and needed antibiotics. I'm leaving 2 stars because I have personally always had a good nail job here but they need some serious lessons in customer service.

This is my first visit since they've oddly added the new "Subs n More" part to the shop, and I was pretty disappointed. Not only have they raised their ice cream prices, but the charm of the Sweet Cece's franchise has been absorbed and lost with this new weird low end sub shop addition. Staff seemed clueless, and could care less, and the toppings weren't well supplied. And, they didn't have the loyalty machine running so my points for today's visit are lost. I have been coming here every Monday on a regular basis for about a year and I won't be back. I'll drive farther for another location. Bummer.

I like Hard Rock Cafe. Yes, it's a chain, and it's busy and noisy, but it's fun. I appreciate that they have a good veggie burger, so there's at least one  option for vegetarians. I enjoy the music and memorabilia. This location is in a great area of New Orleans, so you'll be near Jack's Brewery and other notable places. In a city like New Orleans with lots of fabulous restaurants, this may not be everyone's first choice, but it's a fun place for a young crowd, and for a chain, they have some pretty good offerings.

I've been here a couple times now for lunch and I have yet to be disappointed. The prices are great as well as the quality. If you happen to be here on your lunch break my vote goes for the bento box.  You get soup, salad, shumai, a California roll, rice and that's all in addition to which bento box you choose. I'm all about variety when it comes to a good meal and at Akira they obviously feel the same way. It's never more than a $25 bill for two people from my experiences. 

The decor is modern and clean, comfortable seating, hibachi, and a sushi bar if you choose!  I'm happy to add this place to my list of quick, local lunch spots.

If you have the opportunity to watch Christian behind the bar, then for the price of a drink, you can have front row seats to the best 'dinner & a show' for its price. I watched this very talented mixologist mix 3 drinks while shaking 2 more (I swear, I saw it with my own eyes--and I wasn't seeing double!). He knows his drinks, creating some of the most delectable, original sips I've ever had. And he's a quick wit who's very generous with his drinky knowledge. I don't think I'll ever ask for a table again, opting instead to hang out at the bar.

I'm going to say what everyone has been afraid to say.  The place is NOT that good; you can get a better meal for less without the annoying "Let me put your napkin on your lap for you" worthlessness that comes along with paying way too much.  If that's what you're into more power to you, but I'd rather spend my money on something else.  All that having been said the two times I've eaten at Tony's the food was delicious, and if you're trying to impress someone shallow there isn't really a better place in St. Louis.

I recently visited Vaso's to see the brassaholics on a saturday night.  I was pleasantly surprised.  Great crowd mixture and large size acquarium to add to the rustic scenery!  The owner is a  new orleans original and appears to be pretty hands on!  They also serve food ranging from fried chicken to crawfish pies!  I sampled a few of the drummetts which were seasoned pretty good!  The bartender took a while to make my lemon drop martini but it was worth the wait because it had just the right amount of zing without being too sour!  It's a spot I would definitely return to listen to the brass bands!

It's hard to find a trustworthy mechanic these days! When I ran into car issues, I was going to head to my normal mechanic 20 miles away near my job. Thanks to Yelp, I decided to give this place close to home a chance. I'm glad I did! Sean was very down to earth, patient, and honest. Didn't overcharge & try to take advantage of clueless lady! It was truly appreciated & I will definitely be back! It's a small shop, so don't expect to sit around & relax ;) hahaha. I was thankful I lived close as it was just a stroll down the street for me!

I really like this chain, but this location was dirty and lacked enough seating for the amount of traffic they generate. Have enough chairs for your customers guys, its kinda important. The bathrooms were atrocious. Also, parking is a nightmare. I'll drive an extra 2 or 3 miles to find a place that has seating, parking, and is clean. While the yogurt is always good, this place was disappointing. I remember having lower standards when I was a starving student too, but taking my kids here was just too scary. Bummer.

Update: 
Guy on phone: Hello, thank you for calling Fritz's Frozen Custard, how can I help you?
Me: Hi, do you have anything without dairy, I have a little girl who is allergic to milk.
Guy on phone: Sure do, we make slushies.
Me: Wonderful, we'll be there in a little bit.
Guy on Phone: great, we'll see you then.

45 minutes later...

Me at counter: Hi, what flavor slushies do you have?
Girl at counter: Sorry, our machine is broken today.

To my 3yo daughter...I'm a suckie father. Thanks Fritz's for making me look like a dick.

I actually found Twisted on Yelp when I first moved to New Orleans.  It's slightly embarrassing to admit, but it has turned into one of my favorite places to frequent (that's including restaurants, bars, concert venues etc).  

Most of my male counterparts quiver at any mention of a "salon," but Twisted is laid-back.  Nicole gives the freshest of haircuts for a very reasonable $20. 

Most importantly, Nicole, Katie and the rest of the staff are some of the nicest people in the entire city.  I genuinely look forward to my monthly visits more for the conversations and updates on the best to-dos in the city.  Basically, they rock.

We had a marvelous dinner here with two friends. The food and the service were first rate. Our server was great -- friendly, good sense of humor, very professional, and he provided excellent suggestions and explanations. My mussels appetizer was superb and the lasagna was the best I've ever had at a restaurant in STL. Both were spicy, which I loved. Everyone else really enjoyed their entrees and desserts. The pappardelle with lamb ragu was fabulous. The bottle of Amarone complemented our dishes very nicely. Overall an outstanding experience.

This was a smooth process.  I presented the agent with my confirmation number and he gave me my keys. The agent just asked did I want protection I said, no I have insurance. He said ok.  Here your keys and enjoy.   The agent was nice and never tried to oversell me things. 

I ask for the GPS equipment which was a breeze to hook up. 

When I was leaving the rental car place the agent at the exit was courteous and positive.   The only thing I can say is the car was dirty on the outside but clean on the inside.

I didn't go for dreadlock weaves or funky color so maybe I didn't get the full effect of the 5 star reviews that I read about. My guy was nice but didn't give much feedback about my hair questions. I just went for a wash and blow dry and when he thought he was done he asked me how I liked it. It was fine until I saw a patch of curls that he missed so i laughed it off and he fixed that. I checked again and there was still curl that he missed. Maybe he was thinking about lunch or the upcoming parades but it was certainly discouraging to have to triple check someone's work as a first time customer.

My family and I frequent Yogurt Beach quite often.  We always enjoy the experience. The way it works is that it is priced by weight.  The more you put in your frozen yogurt bowl, the more expensive it gets. Be careful not to load up too much on the yummy candies/treats because it can increase the weight of your yogurt quickly. 

The staff is always friendly and professional.  We really enjoy our visit every time we visit.  Also, my kids love the surfing atmosphere.  It is always nice to visit the beach in the middle of a desert.

I know this is just a grocery store. However, if you are willing to search and go deeper, you will find a bevy of tastiness at your sausage link fingertips. Reason being, this particular Marsh's salad bar is EPIC! Seriously, I cannot overstate this enough. You can make a 3 TON salad filled with grilled or breaded chicken, every kind of lettuce under the sun, and any condiment on the planet for about $3.50 on a normal day. The lettuce is always crazy fresh and the number of choices available to you on the salad bar are baffling. Solid store, and super clean. Much love

Quick lunch here and overspent $8 for a wrapped burrito of sorts. Menu stated it had chicken but I only saw 3 or 4 small pieces. Mostly rice and partially melted cheese.

The only flavor was when I dipped it into the southwest ranch sauce on the side.

Tip to the restaurant staff: ask if it's a wrap or quesadilla. I wanted a quesadilla, got a wrap and couldn't wait for it to be made correctly due to short lunch at work. Also to-go orders should always have napkins included. Oh and chicken wraps or quesadillas that cost $8 should have more than 3-4 pieces of chicken.

I am not sure if this is connected to the Garcia's on Murfreesboro HWY96 or not, but if it is....please learn from that one.  I was very disappointed in the service and time it took to get my food. Usually you walk in and out of Mexican restaurants.  This lunch took me over 45-50 minutes and I could never get my waitress over especially to check out.  She never looked my way and I even tried to flag her down.  I finally left cash to pay for the meal and walked out and told the hostess....ridiculous service.  The food was decent but still not as good as the Murfreesboro Road one.

I really like this place. Very good for groups and a nice sit-down meal. The food is very tasty and very traditional. The menu is very big and has a lot to choose from. Make sure you try the hot tea they give you, it always sets the mood. The only down side about his place is that it seems to be run by only a few people. So if there are more than 3 tables, which that is rarely the case (especially on weekdays), be prepared to wait while the chinese server lady runs around and tends to everyone elses needs but yours.

Nato's is my families "go to" fast food Mexican quick fix.  The menu reads like a choose your own gastronomy adventure book. 

What really sets Nato's apart from the other Mexican food in Boise is their Menudo.  If you don't know what Menudo is?  Google it and then give it a try because this is he best I have ever had.  It is only served on weekends and they quickly run out...  wait, why am I telling you this?  Don't be eaten my Menudo!

Staff is incredibly friendly and the prices are extremely reasonable.

Thanks Nato's for your hard work, friendly service, tasty food, (awesome menudo), and reasonable prices!

Solid thin crust pizza and basic sandwiches.  I had the margarita slice.  A bit overpriced, but the economy forcing prices up.  Good cheese, tomatoes and fresh basil on a crispy crust.  

One issue, is a sign over the cash register advertised 2 slices and a 32 oz soda for $4.99, choose your topping.  I had two slices and asked for a soda and was charged $7.29.  I looked at the poor flustered guy and was too weary from long meetings all morning to bitch about the $2.  But, will be leery when I go back to see if prices fluctuate often.

Had lunch with a group and just to be quick, atmosphere, service and the drunken littlenecks, thai chicken pizza and the soups where great.

Not the best fish and chips, having both suffering from lack of crispness in batter and chips soggy from sitting under the soggy fish.  Second was the so called chicken gumbo.  The only thing that was gumbo like was the andouille sausage.  

The chicken was sodden with the puddle of oil in the dish.  Same for the orka and there was no rice.  Not sure what you would call the dish, but calling it gumbo should be a crime and would be if you were any where close to Lousiana.

I don't understand why there are so many 4 star reviews. This place is average at best. The last time I was here, I vowed that I would never come back. SIx months later, I wind up here on a Wednesday night with the worst opera singer I have ever heard. He ruined Andrea Bocelli's Time to Say Goodbye. I had to play it in the car to get his voice back in my head!. 

And to top it off, my pasta was mush. How the hell can an Italian restaurant not cook pasta al dente?

Now I can say, never again. Should I end up here again, it's shame on me!

I tried the lunch order of the tacos de asada - 2 chopped steak tacos served with pico de gallo, sour cream, and beans.  Overall the tacos were good.  It was good cut of steak that was well seasoned.  The soft taco shells only had the meat.  They appear to have cilantro, onions, avocado, and chopped jalapenos on the menu as side orders.  They could be a nice addition if I go with a taco plate again.  I'll have to check if the jalapenos are fresh or pickled.  I'll probably be going back to try some of the other dishes.  

They have a to go menu.

I frequently visit Santa Barbara and this is my most favorite hotel why? 

1. The customer service is outstanding! The housekeepers, car attendants, front desk, and other guests, they're all so incredibly friendly. 

2. Free parking and breakfast!! They actually do charge for parking...but totally worth it. 

3. GREAT location, right in the middle of downtown. 

4. The building and rooms are quite charming and clean. The building is pretty historic, without the creepy haunted historic feel. 

I don't know who manages this Holiday Inn but they're doing it, and doin it, and doin it WELL. Love this place, see yall this Memorial Day!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Best japanese desserts in St. Louis:
-Chocolate covered green tea cheesecake pops, I mean just listen to the sound of this, no explanation needed, must get
-Fried green tea ice cream, better than the one from The Drunken Fish
-Mochi ice cream was meh, I'm sure all the japanese restaurants around STL all source from the same generic box, just get it from Trader Joe's

Can't say much about the sushi since I've never ordered anything other than sweets here. Last time I was here, we just had two giant trays of chocolate covered green tea cheesecake pops and mochi ice cream, yeah, I know.

I hate to do this. I LOVE Krystal, especially being a Southerner. White Castle is better. It just is. I'm not sure what it is about those things, but they are just better. My wife and I actually did a little taste test. We visited both establishments and we both did a little blind taste test. Unfortunately, we both chose the White Castle burger over the Krystal. Id love to say that it went the other way, but it did not. WC is it. *Fortunately* Krystal still holds the monopoly on most of the southeast and we don't really have a choice. So, most dont even know there is something better.

This Springhill Suites is as nice an urban hotel as I have seen in a long time.  The design of the hotel is very European (reminds me of London) and the staff was very helpful with getting me around.

The free breakfast was about what I expected, coffee was good and available 24x7, and the room was very large with lots of room to spread out and get some work done.

They also were helpful in letting me check out late.  Used my Marriott points so not sure how the cost is, but I am going to be staying at more Marriott properties in the future, based on my experience with this hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Had a simple dinner with a friend: edemame to share, a vegetable roll for her, a shrimp tempura roll for me and an avocado roll to share.

The rolls were good, but nothing special. Our server knew limited English, so I tried to be as polite as possible, but we never received our edemame, so I asked for it to be removed form the check, and when our rolls arrived I was given an extra tempura, which I was told to keep for free.

A fine meal, but I was not impressed - especially after noticing that they have been voted Nashville's best sushi restaurant several years in a row.

This place freaks me out. 

They used to have a full food menu, and occasionally I'd get a cheesesteak. But then PA's smoking laws changed and they opted to drop their food output in favor of continuing to allow smoking indoors.

It's a grungy, dark, colorless Moe's Tavern inside, and on busy drinking nights you'll find the kind of people here who your parents told you not to hang out with in grade school.

Two stars for the pool tables. Everything else about it, especially when combined with alcohol, is like a bad dream.

My girls and I came here with their dad one night. It was really cold, yet they sat us directly by the door, which my bad for not asking to move, but still (restaurant was mostly empty, so it wan't because of space). Took the server 6 minutes to even greet us, which was irritating seeing as my 5 and 7 year olds were hungry and we wanted to order right away. I got the veggie fajita, and it was SOOOO oily. I know they cook it in oil, but this was awful. I've been here in the past (it's been a while though), and while not the most amazing, never this bad. I don't think I'll be back for quite a while.

I normally have a great experience at Champps, but my wife and i stopped by last Friday evening to enjoy some drinks on the patio. We first encountered a host that was a little rude. We finally got a buzzer and sat at the bar to wait for our table. An hour and a half later, the buzzer never went off so we decided to leave. I will say despite this snafu, the manager on duty, Amy was extremely apologetic and handled the situation very well. We'll chalk this up as not the norm, and be sure to go back to enjoy another meal.

A family member is a big fan. I've been here maybe three times, and I can say with confidence if you're in the area looking for a good burger to satisfy your needs, Cheeburger will deliever. Even as a vegetarian I found a nice portobello burger, or a veggie burger. The fries are food and so are the onion rings. Service was a little slow, but hey, it's a diner type place so expect diner type service. I'm not really into sweet things, but I expect if you are Cheeburger won't disappoint given their very large selection of sodas? I think it was ? Either way, good place.

Jules is a chain of thin crust pizza. I've come here many times and they always serve good food. The thin crust pizza is very unique thing, I had never seen it before. Their pizzas are rectangular, and very, very thin. Another unique thing Jules does is they do have gluten-free pizzas available when you request it, which is cool for people who have a gluten problem. Jules definitely gives a "trendy" feel about their food and restaurant. Their salads are all microgreens and they serve organic products and all the like. They are at least trying to be healthier than just another pizza place, and that and the taste earns Jules a four.

Without a doubt the best car wash in the area. Probably the best car wash in the country. I have had my car washed in many states. :) the facility is spotless and very comfortable to sit in while waiting. The equipment does a great job on the cars. The staff is awesome and every one of the "gets it". They know how to talk to customers, handle problems and be polite. More businesses should be run this way. Even if your car isn't that dirty you should go. Your car will like you for it. Have had a membership for months and love it.

I love this place. I actually was disappointed that at one point I lived in an apartment that was not within their delivery area!

We order from here at least once a week. Food is always good. They've only messed up once (but I've ordered from there a LOT) but immediately fixed it for me.

Pork & pineapple tacos are great and I love the tacos & flautas. And I have a friend who swears by the green enchiladas. If you want to spend a little extra money, splurge on the Camarones a la Diabla, which are fantastic but very hot.

Their online ordering system was awesome, I wish they'd get it working again!

Bennigan's (the chain) went bankrupt, but it appears an independent franchisee decided to try and keep the sad little flame alive.

Everything in this place is OLD and speaks of "no budget to update"...it's like a weird flashback ala 'Hot Tub Time Machine' to a time when there were Bennigan's everywhere. It is *almost* worth the 15 minute wait to get an overpriced drink JUST to check out the interior details.

Service, awful. Food, bland and consider yourself lucky to even get it. Beer...WARM?!?! Blech. 

Not a place I would recommend...

I'll refrain from parroting the dozens of other positive reviews and just confirm that this place rocks!

The parking lot is a joke though, and the staff is mostly very young and not particularly motivated - but the topping selection is mind-boggling and the yogurt is tasty.

Nice little self-serving pricing method they have (weight based) - since with basically one cup size you'll have a tendency to overfill 90 percent of the time. 

In the end, the cost is reasonable for what you get, if a little on the higher end. I'll be back to grovel at the altar of delicious goo, that's for sure.

I just cannot say enough about this place. If you want "the total experience" with your haircut and style, this is IT.

As soon as you walk in, it feels like you leave the outside world behind as you enter a relaxing place of beauty. Michael is a total professional and really goes above and beyond in every facet of the cut, color & style.

The prices are reasonable, the products top-shelf, and the service friendly and smooth...what more can you ask for in a salon?

I was shocked to be the first reviewer for the salon, it is well established and very popular...

In short: the perfect experience for mind, body and hair!

WORST THAN CAFETERIA PASTA!
I think I enjoyed the spaghetti they served in elementary better than the one I ordered here.

Only came here because it's close to work and yelp had decent ratings like 3.5 stars at the time. I order some kind of simple Penne pasta with red meat sauce. I only finished half of it because they gave a large portion and it just didn't taste good at all.

My co-worker ordered the Pasta with Pesto sauce and said he enjoyed it.

Wouldn't come back here again. I didn't even want to eat the left overs I got from this place.

I came here for lunch and had the bento meal as well as 2 sushi rolls. Their sushi is good but not great. I didn't order special rolls tho. As far as the bento lunch goes, i had the eel with rice, it was pretty good.  They also have the udon noodle soup where they put shrimp tempura inside the soup which doesn't really make sense to me because it makes the tempura soggy and the soup was bland.  
As far as service goes, it was good, no complaints. But there are so many other sushi restaurants in the city to choose from, this place is only satisfactory.

I came here for drinks only. That being said, I had the skinny bitch and was less than impressed because it was mainly coke, did not taste any alcohol. As far as the restaurant/bar, I liked the ambiance and atmosphere. It's actually good for a date night or just sit at the bar and catch a game.

I came back for brunch on a Sunday morning.  I tried their eggs Benedict, it was ok, not impressed. My date had the omelet which came out kind of dry. He also ordered Bloody Mary, but he didn't like it. Not much a spot for brunch, there are better choices in manayunk.

Food was fantastic and not overpriced! The seafood was really fresh, the staff was extremely knowledgeable and very friendly. The owner is awesome and very personable, we sat and talked with him forever! He even gave us a free cannoli! The place is really tiny but I think it makes it special, and the candlelight along with the Sinatra playing in the background made it romantic! The chicken bruschetta was to die for. The menu changes seasonally. Definitely a hidden gem on main street. BYOB which is also awesome and rare to find in a town with soooo many bars on the same street. We will absolutely be coming back here!

What to say about Landmark Americana? The environment? Nice. The food? Nothing remarkable, but certainly not bad. As another said, "Passably average." The menu? Wow, it is seriously boring. The prices? Not high, but somehow I walked away feeling we paid a bit too much for the quality of food and "typical" menu. The service? Again average. 

In sum Landmark Americana came across as a place that has decent food, but where you are somewhat disappointed as you walk out. 

2.5 stars. I don't think it 's somewhere I'd return.

Wing Wah is our Chinese take out "du jour." Are there better Chinese restaurants in the Philadelphia area? Sure, but around Wayne and Berwyn, I know of none better than Wing Wah. 

The food is always fresh, hot, and flavorful. It offers the standard Americanized version of Chinese cuisine, all prepared well. While I wish it offered more authentic fare as I can find in Chinatown area of Philly, it suffices for those those nights when no one wants to cook or go out for dinner. 

And the proprietoress is always welcoming and friendly.

The 0-2 sensor on my mom's car went out.  We took it to the local Car-X and recieved a quote of almost $600, plus another $80 bucks for the diagnostic.  Someone referred me my mom to Ralph's and they quoted her about $200 for the same job.  We made an appointment, and the car was fixed the same day.  I honestly cannot complain.  If you have to get your car fix, you want it done for a reasonable price within a reasonable time frame - and that's exactly what I got!  Now, it looks like a car repair place out of the 1970s, so don't expect a trendy lobby but do expect great service!

I was very surprised when I dropped by the Krystal drive thru last Friday night on my way back from Busch Gardens.  I was shocked by the quality of service which I have just missed from other fast food establishments in recent years.  Staff are fast, friendly and very polite.  I am lucky at other fast food places if I can get a smile anymore, let alone a thank you.

It has probably been 4-5 years since I last visited Krystal and this was a pleasant experience and I would definitely consider returning to this location in the future.

I've been here a few times and have been impressed each time.  One of my favorite things here is the outdoor covered patio in the second floor.  Outdoor dining is awesome and the ambiance they have set out here makes the dining  so much more enjoyable.

They have a fairly small menu as they rotate the items each week however I would say they emphasize quality instead of quality.  I had an amazing burger and my wife had probably he best marinated baked chicken she had ever had.  It was incredible how much flavor was deep within each bite.

Service was good and quick, friendly and attentive and we will definitely be back.

This is a great hotel option for NOLA, right in the heart of the French Quarter but still 2 blocks away from Bourbon St to avoid the noise or drama. You get all the good stuff about Marriott which are the consistency of having a good room, fitness, hot tub, clean, great staff and Starbucks on site. This is very moderate on pricing and knowing how long you will stay in your room in New Orleans anyway, this is a good lodging option. Final rate is 3.5 stars.

Tip: there is no parking but valet is available for $23/day.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The true old Italian Gravy House.  I'm not the True Old Italian as I had to embarass myself by admitting to someone that I did not know that Gravy was sauce.  Ouch!  I went down a few points on that one.

I've been coming here since my college days, and I think Villa di Roma has not changed at all except for the prices.  The food is consistently good, and the service, although brusque at times, knows their job.

CASH ONLY!  And it does get crowded at peak times, so be prepared to wait.  Full bar, desserts are awesome, and main meals can't be beat.  A regular place to come to!

I've brought my son here twice now, and the service has been stellar.  They give my son exactly what he wants, and he is happy.  It's also really inexpensive - $8 for a kid's haircut!

They have multiple stations, but I believe one of the barbers does all the children because he took my son ahead of an adult waiting to go.  Both times I've come there has been a steady stream of customers.

The place is clean and they have TV to watch.  I think the owners and workers enjoy what they do and they are a great addition to the neighborhood.

If I just did not buzz my head on my own, I'd come here to get my hair cut, too.

The name describes it all. This place is a moderately priced bistro that serves... Italian food. Beyond stating the obvious, I must say that I've enjoyed the food. Thus far, I've sampled the bruschetta, ravioli, chili chicken penne, tiramisu, and creme brulee, and have been impressed with all of the above. The creme brulee had a nice crunchy carmelized sugar crust, just as it should.

This place seems to usually offer a prix fixe menu for around $20, in addition to taking coupons from restaurant.com. Thus far, I've never gone here and paid full price. While not the fanciest Italian place, it really is quite pleasant.

This is our main branch location now that we live on the east end of Tucson.  It's not spectacular, but it's not terrible.  They've met our needs courteously.  Sometimes the wait can be a little long to see a "specialist", or whatever they call the non-tellers, to open or close accounts, etc., but it's not terrible.  The tellers are always very friendly.  I've definitely been to worse banks.  *cough* Compass *cough*.

Tip:  I prefer to park in the lot behind the building.  It is bigger and easier to navigate around.

I hate being constrained to a 5 star rating system.But Lillian's is a tough 3. This is a really good neighborhood restaurant. Nice selection on the menu. Lovely atmosphere, pleasant service. Is it great, no but it is very OK. 

There was an amuse bouche of a squash soup that was nice but not memorable. The butter along with the good rolls was a roasted garlic butter which was mild at best. The chowder was OK. I had a Turkey Croquet which was quite good and not something you see often. It was a little light on the sauce to my taste. 

This is BYOB. Something To be remembered. I'll most likely be back ,but my impression is resoundingly OK.

Pretty good!  The wait service is good, fast, and knowledgeable.  The wine selection could be better.  A little sad that there weren't a few more vegetarian options.  The tomato sauce was a little too salty for my liking, but that's about average.with restaurants like these.

The bathroom, however, is the only reason I'm giving this place anything less than four stars.  It was disgusting.  No hand towels or dryer.  Lots of empty toilet paper rolls all over the place--

I am very hesitant to go back for this reason.  

Also, I don't like going to nice restaurants and seeing TVs with sports games on them.

Maybe I'm biased, but I feel like Pinkberry offers more healthy choices in Fro-Yo versus SweetCeCe's.  

Don't get me wrong, both places have great Fro-Yo but Pinkberry wins in my book.  The quality of toppings and yogurt is distinguishable between these two places and Pinkberry tastes better and fresher.  

I still think Red Mango is my favorite Fro-Yo place, but I think I might have to wait awhile for that to arrive to Nashville.   But Pinkberry will make a smooth, delicious, and fresh tasting substitute in the meantime!

Yummy house is a clean, American style Chinese restaurant. They are good for some people, but being from NYC and being used to authentic Chinese food, Yummy house is not for me. If you like Chinese-American food you will probably like it here. 

Service is always okay, although some of the waiters do not know about some of the Chinese things you ask for that is suppose to go with some of the dishes. 

Parking is easy. 

Dishes are okay. They do use a lot of MSG in their and I always get a headache after coming here. 

They are across from Sanwa farmers market so it's nice to go food shopping after eating.

The owners really care about their customers! Someone fro Yokos reached out to us to discuss our experiences at their restaurant. We are planning to come back to sit down and eat soon. 

Since they wrote to us, I've ordered take out from them twice and the food has been excellent. They make the best quality salmon teriyaki (a little small, but I'll still keep getting it. Several other places overcook it or the sauce isn't right) and one time we were lucky and they gave us hamachi belly sashimi for take out. 

We have to go back to see how service is again. But the quality of the rolls, sashimi and cooked food is very good.

I read some of the other reviews before going, and was almost looking for reasons to not like Noble, but I couldn't find any!  Everything was awesome!  We had the oysters and gnocchi as appetizers, which were both very delicious.  The oysters come with little cuts of green apple that make them just that much more refreshing.  For the main course, we had the salmon and the swordfish. The salmon was a little basic (just slightly seared) but the swordfish was melt-in-your-mouth-fantastic.  A bottle of wine and a chocolate dessert to top it off, plus a Groupon for $25 off gets it 5 stars!

What was I thinking? Please forgive me for my prior 4-star rating. This is like a top 3 restaurant in New Orleans for me, and among the best pizza on earth. Get anything. Literally anything. It's all good (even the salads). But also garlic knots and pizza for ever and ever.

P.S. A higher marinara sauce to garlic knot ratio is super beneficial. Go for the double dip.

P.P.S. I managed to have pizza self control for the first time EVER and was able to wait for my pizza to cool off enough so I didn't eat it in molten lava mode and burn off my entire mouth skin.

P.P.P.S. Is there a name for the burnt bubbles in the crust? There should be.

The service gets 5 stars.  Like most pizza/sandwich shops they work their asses off.  The pizza is good(had better)  but I'm reviewing for their steaks and Italian sausage sandwiches.  Some of the best steak sandwiches are in the suburbs.  This is one of them.  They use Conshohocken bakery rolls for starters.  They make their Italian sausage sandwiches using loose sausage on the grill and chop it up to the right size.  The loose sausage gets a nice burn on the outside grilling with color.  Other places will par boil links which leave it mushy.

How do you say "Holy FRESH Batman" in Japanese ... without dating yourself? Because that's what I would say about Vic. I'd also say it's The. Best. Sushi. Joint. In. Philly! (No lie). The much vaunted tuna dumplings are worth the vaunting. The spider roll has crawled right into my heart (from my stomach). And the Sansom Roll... Makes my eyes roll (no pun intended!) back in ecstasy. The dining room is a counter that seats about 10 folks and a single table, so you'll be elbow-to-elbow. Expect a wait if it's crowded. If you're in Center City/Graduate Hospital, they deliver. Get you some!

I guess I'm not a fan (4 stars) because on a Saturday night, you cannot even order food after 11pm.  That's not late for a Saturday night on WASHINGTON in the heart of the CITY.  I'd think with all the lofts and the other establishments that I can get a meal this late on the weekend.

We almost had to beg for wings and a pizza because it was 10minutes til, but the kitchen went ahead and cooked our order...I saw others turned down though.

The food was ok, not exceptional (but I guess this goes to the late night meal).  The drinks however were good...I'd go back for that but I guess I'd need to eat somewhere else first :)

This is an old school barber shop run by new school guys. Those 90 year old barbers we had growing up weren't going to last but now there is a new generation. No self-respecting man should have to get a hair cut at a salon and Chad's team is here to save you from that.

There may not be many reviews on Yelp but this place is no secret. It started out in the same strip mall but they just keep growing. Prepare to wait in line on a Saturday. Once you're finally in the chair, they'll line you up in record time and send you on your way with a massage.

P.S. It's a machine, not some dude massaging you.

I have been coming here since it was Sammy's sushi bar up in the Walmart plaza.

The sushi is decent quality and prices are very fair. They have a variety of other Japanese dishes as well. While the wife and I generally get a few rolls and a miso soup, the kids love gyoza and the steak teriyaki kids meal.

At lunch, they have a 2 and 3 roll special. Same quality as dinner and a slightly limited selection (the full menu is available at full price) but the price is unbeatable and service is always fast.

The restaurant and even the sushi bar are very large so it never feels crowded even when it is full.

This seemed like a pretty decent sushi place overall. I had the Amanda roll which had some kind of spicy tuna and jalapeno on it which was real good and presented very nicely. The other roll I had was really interesting that it was wrapped in cucumber rather than rice or the seaweed paper. Inside was spicy tuna and I don't know what else but it was super good and very clever how they were able to slice a cucumber into a thin curled up shape that they could stuff with tuna and then roll up and slice into pieces of sushi. They had a huge menu of other things that looked good and I would go here again if possible.

Papa Murphy's makes some pretty tasty pizza -- and, in addition to being dirt cheap, it's made right in front of you. Skip the breadsticks (bland) and salads (looks like typical bagged lettuce) and create your own side dishes. I really like the "deLite" pizzas (ugh, that spelling) but everything I've had is good. These pizzas are basically foolproof.

Parking at this location can be a bit of a pain, as traffic is quite heavy in both directions on 62nd. There was no way I was going to be able to turn left to get back to Keystone, so I had to go through Broad Ripple to get back downtown.

Hate to do it, but I gotta give the Old Point 3 stars now ... of course, you can't beat the location. The beer list is great. Service is friendly. But ... the food. Meh. Today, I ordered the blandest chicken quesadilla I've ever had. Even the "salsa" was bland -- and I don't tolerate spicy foods all that well! My husband ordered one of the specials, a gordita, and was similarly unimpressed. Add in two soft drinks at $2.50 each (really?!) and our lunch was a hair over $30 with tip. 

It's a great place to sit on a warm spring day and have a brew or two. I just wouldn't make it a destination for dining.

OPT was the only place I could find that was open during the great ice storm of '11, when my car was frozen to the ground and my friend was finally able to escape her house to pick me up. The best Old Point story I have is when I was there with a friend; we realized TOTS had a show opening so I thought I would run down there to get tickets before we got our dinner. Well, I misjudged the distance and he was the recipient of many dirty looks while he ate his dinner while my untouched chili sat across from him.

Old Point has decent food and strong drinks -- and a small patio in the summer. I really couldn't ask for more.

I would probably give 3.5 stars if available. Food and ambiance very good. Service awful. 
We came on Saturday with a large party of 18. My father preordered a bunch of appetizers. It took 40 minutes for them to come out. What was the point of preordering in advance. 
Food was superb. Everything was tasty and cooked to perfection. 
Again, service was pretty bad all night. From getting extra bottles of water to other requests, we had to wait for a long time. In the beginning the place was empty too so not sure why there were no servers to assist.

I have lunch here with my mom occasionally as its pretty much in the middle of our places of employment. It's OK. Place is small and very dark. The servers are usually very sweet. The food is very cheap but pretty much a hit or miss. I got a shrimp caesar salad with 6 very large and tasty shrimp for only $7.99. But one time I got a personal pizza and I want to say that frozen pizza from a supermarket was better. It was very thick and completely raw in the middle. Pretty unacceptable from an Italian restaurant. 
There are other pretty decent options for lunch however so I don't discourage from trying it.

In retrospect, as a starving art student in University City, it probably wasn't a great idea to indulge in Ajia as much as I did. You get a lot for your dollar during the lunch specials, but otherwise it can be pricey, especially with the credit minimum. (Note: their ATM has a high surcharge, so it's best to take cash out beforehand).

That said, the food is quite good. I'm especially a fan of their teriyaki dishes. The service can be iffy if you plan to sit down, but they tend to be quicker if you order take out.

I'll give it a meh -- the other reviewers noting this is like a Chipotle for pizza are 100 percent correct.

The staff was super friendly and helpful, and the new place very clean and well set up. I just wasn't really blown away by the food. That's not to say it wasn't good, but maybe there's something to be said about recommended combinations. When left to my own devices, I'm pretty boring.

I will say the price is right and it's pretty darn fast -- so I won't put this place up against Bianco or Falora, but it's good for what it is.

The place is actually nice looking.   Very modern.  The have a cool fireplace. Nice lounge chairs.  BUT...

The bar tender spent more time watching TV than serving his customers. He also looks like a cereal killer.  The food is OK nothing special.  If you are stuck in a hotel and need a drink it will do.  

It is sad because this area is a dead zone for good food and drink and this place could be great with a little better management.

I come here once a year and will continue to as long as the hotel stays clean.

I got a membership to Philly Car Share because I no longer have my own car now that I live in the city. I'm on the $35/year membership plan, which is very reasonable. They have cars located on almost every block making it extremely convenient. They also reimburse you for gas so you don't have to worry about the rising prices! However, I do have to comment on the cleanliness of the vehicles, or lack there of. As a former member of Zipcar, I can confidently say that the vehicles are very rarely cleaned. Otherwise they have a pretty good system.

Penzey's is fabulous and I feel so lucky to have it right in my neighborhood. They have all the spices you can imagine, all at reasonable prices and they're pretty decently priced. The employees are helpful and good at answering questions. I bought sumac powder for some recipe and asked for suggestions of what else I might use it for and the cashier gave me several good ideas. 

I'm not sure what my favorite spice is from there, but if I were suggest ones for someone to absolutely try, I'd definitely get a jar of their cinnamon and any of their unique peppercorns. And my friend got their sweet curry powder and said that's worth trying too.

(Visited the hotel during Halloween 2009)

I did not experience the horror stories others have mentioned about this hotel. Yes - this wasnt the prettiest hotel ever, but it is a Holiday Inn after all. 

The location is great, right in Canal street and just blocks away from Bourbon. Royal street itself is actually quite nice as you continue walking into it. The rooms were actually very roomy - the bathroom was ok. Everything seemed clean - and the service was a bit intrusive in the morning, so I recommend you hang the dont disturbe sign!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
We usually love Sushi Teri, but last nights sushi from the Goleta Location just wasn't tasting, or sitting, right. 

We ordered the Pink Cadillac, the Goyo, the Omega III, Linden, and the Heart Attack Rolls.

The rolls were so big they were impossible to eat in one bite. They were falling apart immediately and the rice was dry and tasted almost stale. The fish wasn't as fresh as it usually is. Not sure if it was just an off night or what. 

The chicken teriyaki was as good as always though, so we were good there.

We obviously will give them another go before writing them completely off. Just hoping this was just a bad night!

Been taking Buddy here for the last 5 years or so. Their new offices look great and I cannot say enough nice things about Dr Clarke. Even Buddy is always glad to see her, until she whips the needles out!! LOL Anyway, I am very happy with the quality of service I receive. I've never had any problem getting an appointment nor have I ever had to wait an exorbitant amount of time once I've gotten to the office (i've read other reviews here talking about having to wait). I would gladly recommend Dr. Clarke and King of Prussia Veterinary Hospital to anyone.

Yes, I have become an Old Fart who is set in his ways. Been getting my hair cut at Mario's for 30 years now.  All the Barbers are very nice, very personable and judging by the steady stream of customers, very good at what they do.  Mario's is a Havertown institution that even though I moved out of the area a decade ago I still make the trek there every 6-8 weeks to get my hair cut. I've tried other Barbers, Salons, etc, closer to home but I always find myself coming back to Mario's. Nobody knows my hair better (and I am very thankful I still have hair to cut!!!).

I used to go to salons in Princeton, NJ, so the prices here seemed ridiculously low for such a nice place. $30 to cut my very long hair, and only an additional $10 for a full steam treatment, though the treatment used was not a particularly expensive one (I believe it was a mixture of Cibu International products).

My hairdresser (sadly I don't remember her name) gave me a lovely cut, with gentle advice to suit my face shape and hair texture, and was very attentive. Scheduling an appointment was very easy. I'll definitely be going here again.

I LOVE THIS RESTAURANT.  i come here to celebrate, or to mope after a difficult week.  the service is terrific!  they always remember my face AND what my favorites are.  it's affordable for the area.  being a BYO doesn't hurt.  i recommend reservations, but if you want to walk in, do it early in the evening.  the neighborhood crowd starts walking in by around 8pm most nights.  it's a fantastic place, but snug in seating.  what they lack in space they make up for in freshness of food and friendly service.  best italian for me in the city without a doubt.

I was once in the area during a windstorm and it nearly "Blue Indy" off the map. But anyway.

I love these little rentable cars that you drive around town. Brilliant idea. They're all over the place now, on several continents in a lot of major cities. It's awesome that they have come to Indy, but for the people of Indy that haven't experienced them in other places, let me assure you that the cars are usually better maintained than these Blue Indy ones, and that customer service is usually more reachable. Still, great to have them in Indy... but they need work.

Went here with a Groupon in hand to get my car detailed. They did a good job and I enjoyed the cats that were hanging around but it took 2 hours and there really is nothing around there in walking distance to do. The lounge area is pretty worn and not too comfortable for a 2 hour wait. Fortunately it was a nice day and they did have seats outside. Good thing I had my Kindle so at least could read! The owner was nice enough but had a tendency to complain, which was a little off putting but not truly offensive.

The staff is lovely and the drive thru is convenient. I once saw the drive thru line was super long so I decided to go in, thinking it would be faster. But they use the sticker system for orders, so it didn't seem to make a difference. 

Did find myself super annoyed that at 10am on a Monday they were out of the spinach feta wrap, along with other breakfast items. In my opinion there is no reason for that to ever happen. They should take a look at their ordering to ensure that doesn't continue to happen. It doesn't make sense from a business standpoint and they'll certainly lose customers to the other locations nearby

For a chain, Qdoba offers pretty decent burritos.  However, the service seems to be hit-or-miss.  I've had occasions in which ingredients were either left out or I was given a totally different burrito than what I ordered.  They also seem to be a little stingy on the toppings.  Personally, I prefer El Fuego down the street.  

On a side note, you can join the Qdoba Rewards club and earn points toward free/discounted items.  They e-mail you a "Buy 1 Get 1 Free" coupon for your birthday which makes for a pleasant birthday treat.

Hardee's is the red headed step child when it comes to fast food, it always seems to take a back seat to McDonalds, Wendy's and Jack in the Box. However I always forget that their food is actually better than all of the other options.

I stopped by this location while in a hurry and needed a quick meal. I opted for the Chicken Tender Sandwich, which was three chicken tenders with honey mustard, bacon, and cheese on a standard bun. The chicken tenders were good, not dried out like some places.

This location was clean with a friendly staff.

Sat for nearly 20 minutes after being seated before we asked who our server was, since no one was over since seating. To our suprise we hadn't been assigned one.   The restaurant was empty . However once we were assigned a waitress she was more than accommodating and apologetic, she even offered us free desert however we decided so she decided to comp our beverages.

Overall the food is better than Olive Garden, and not quite to the quality to some of the great places on the hill. Overall prices are a little on the high side, but then again they do offer cheaper options. Given a choice I would pick someplace else

Went here with my family a month or 2 ago. We choose the family style dinner/family special for 3 out of 4 of our party. I ordered the crispy orange chicken, the sauce was a perfect blend of sweet with spices. My mom ordered green mussels, great choice! Savory and melt in your mouth good.

The only downside was we were under the impression there would be unlimited rice, but we were only allowed 1 plate between 3 people, it was a little small of a serving between us.  

It was a nice dinner, and by the time we left, around 7, it was packed.

I had a few happy hour specials. Here's my view on each.

1. Calamari, perfectly fried to a golden crisp and came with a great dipping sauce.
2. Sliders, they were OK, the ground beef was a bit tasteless, and the fries DO NOT keep well. I would skip this.
3. Pizza, it was OK, but I will honestly say for the price I would rather have something from Domino's or Little Caesars. 
4. Saratoga chips, damn these are a winner. Came with buffalo and BBQ dipping. I wanted more, and more, and more!!!

Overall, a great little spot. The prices for the happy hour were relieving. I'll go back, every once and a while, especially for those chips!!!!!

Thorough exam-better than anyone I'd ever been to. Good service.Nice location. Pricey even with vision discount. Warning: tried to force me to buy lenses from them via a complicated scheme. (Note Under Federal law, opticians have to give you a prescription good for 2 years dispensable anywhere for contacts and glasses. Apparently if you write a prescription for something that the maker (inappropriately) only sells to opticians like them (and not to low cost chains), they can end run this pro-competive, pro-consumer policy.) Note: I bought from them anyway, even though I was annoyed. Recommended.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
Penske Auto now runs all Hertz locations in the area. 

All contracts are stamped: "Vehicle exchanges not allowed." This means if your car breaks down, you cannot exchange it for a working one at any Hertz location (like you could when Hertz owned the Indy locations). 

Also, the tolling equipment -- if used -- charges you $4.95 per day even if you don't use the toll booth. Read your contract.

This location is open Sunday -- a plus. All the cars are new--another plus.

However, renting outside Marion County avoids the 17% tax.

Still, renting here avoids the airport fees.

Had a nice Toyota Versa.

Disappointed.  Food was awesome, but the waiter kinda pissed me off.  He kept pushing specials and he would not let us order the apps separate from the entrees.  He suggested splitting apps up so we could share...we said no, but he did it anyway, then surprised us with an extra charge for it.  He offered to bring a side of pasta to share, we said sure.  He then charged us $28 for it (more than any entree). I don't mind the $, I just don't like being taken advantage of.  Service really slow too.  Parties of 6 or more pay 20% automatically, so we could not even leave a fair tip. If you go there, don't let John steer you off the menu.

Not bad at all for a quick chain pizza place. I prefer it to Pizza Hut or Domino's for sure, although I try to visit more local pizza shops. I ate this a lot in college, so it's quite nostalgic for me.

On Sunday night, I was able to get a large 3-topping quickly for around $10. I don't know what they're doing with these "Papadillas," which seem super weird, but stick with the pizza and you'll be okay. They're only allowing one customer in the store at a time and have contactless pickup and sanitizer at the counter.

La Viola is good, but nothing I'm dying to run back to.  It's a great spot when you're looking for a nice BYOB (white tablecloths, fancy ambiance) in Rittenhouse Square, but service can be brusque and some dishes are a miss (while others are definitely a hit).  The crowd tends to be on the older side, lots of lovely grannies, to accompany the 20-somethings who are looking for affordable Italian.  
They'll seat your large group, but expect to rub elbows with your friends on the left and right while waiters bumping into you throughout dinner.

Thanks to my afternoon host, Kaveh, for bringing me here. The flavors are fun and creative. It's great to see the "flavor-ologist" working in the back through this huge pane glass window. You can just imagine what crazy concoctions he's creating back there. 

I forget what I got - it was mocha something and really tasty. Not too sweet, which is often my problem with ice cream. Creole Creamery is a great place to recover from a hot day and hang. I've heard that on friday afternoons/evenings, the place is hopping with everyone from teenagers to college kids to families. Yee ha!

I had a wonderful time at Sansui this past Friday night.  We sat at the bar which was great because the sushi chef was very personable and made for an enjoyable experience.  

The sushi portions were pretty big and I really loved the Fire Fire Roll.  Their Inari contained a sweet root inside and wrapped around the outside which really added to the flavor.  

One downside, the Rock 'n' Roll was a little too fried compared to what I like and kind of mushy. 

Overall the staff was friendly, the food was great, and sitting at the bar made it even more fun.  I definitely recommend Sansui for a Friday night date with your significant other.

I tried the chocolate, original tart, and green tea for free at the grand opening. I am so glad I didn't contribute a dime to this terrible wannabe fro-yo place. This "stuff" was so gross and icy-tasting. Sweet CeCe's is THE BEST! It blows Pinkberry out of the water. They did have a good selection of toppings, but then again, so does Sweet CeCe's! I would rather have good yogurt (that doesn't come from a powder mix) and good toppings than have to settle for a lesser option. Sorry Pinkberry. 

Recommended for: people with no taste buds who want to feel like they're being cool.

Of the Marathon locations this one seems the least pleasurable to sit in. It's decor is funky, the service can be spotty, and the outdoor dining isn't so swell as Chestnut street gets really congested during the day. It seems to have been designed with lunch for business customers as it's top priority. That being said, I feel the place is very consistent. It is never going to be THE BEST place for most things, but I don't think it gets enough credit. They have a large menu which is all very reasonably priced. It's standard American fare.

I am giving Yogorino a 2/5 ONLY because I PERSONALLY prefer my frozen yogurt to be a less creamy. It wasn't horrible though... I still finished my cup. I prefer Pinkberry/Red Mango/Sweet Endings. So if you prefer creamier froyo, you will love this place! They also have different sauces if you like that as well. The other thing I did not like is that although the first topping is free... you pay 50 cents for any additional topping (I think? Correct me if I'm wrong please). I will not be returning. Staff was nice and service was quick.

A new place in the Bywater in the former site of the Bywater BarBQue, its a nice renovation with two patios and a big foot print. In my group we had three starters (the Lamb Lollys the standout), all good and four mains of which I three were excellent and one good (the good enough was the pecan encrusted catfish-the stand out for me was the sirloin tips).
