The deserts however where outstanding and a chocolate lovers dream, we have three of them and all were great. I thought the service was good and the place very well kept.

This upscale bistro is a recent find for me. The food generally was very good, the poached oyster starter was terrific and for a main I went with the pan seared drum fish, all very good. My only observation was everything seemed to my taste to be almost too salty, so when I return, I'll be sure to ask the chief to go easy on the salt. Some COVID observations, they really did not check for vaccination proof when we arrived and the whole mask thing here was hit and miss even among the staff. Parking is an issue and we ended up parking a few blocks away in a neighborhood.

I was visiting Santa Barbara and found a Groupon deal.  My family and I had the lunch special, two bento boxes and two sushi boats.  It came with miso soup (a bit too salty).  The bento box was a bento box with beef, salad, some potato thing and tempura.  My family enjoyed their food.

The reason for the 4 stars is the waitress didn't come around to refill our drinks until the end.  I get thirsty, so it'd be nice to have some more liquids during the meal.  It's a nice place near the beach, decent lunch prices.

This is the kinda place where everyone knows your name - 1. Because it is so small, you have to sit on top of the table next to you and 2. because if you aren't a regular, don't bother going. They clearly don't care to make you one either.

That said, the food is pretty great. My BF is a big Italian food fan and I think I saw him contemplating licking the plate. I am not an Italian fan so I went with the steak special and loved it. 

The upside is the food is great and price reasonable since it is a BYO, but the downside is it looks slightly better the 1995 Days Inn.

A clean... dive?! I love it.

My friend's south philly pals have been telling him that he needs to try this spot, so three of us made a drizzly trek down to south philly to check it out last night. It has a really nice interior, with bar seating as well as a cozy back room. Everything is clean and comfy and not cramped at all. The chalkboard beer list offered an awesome variety, so that we had trouble deciding what to try first. The bartenders are incredibly knowledgable, and the fact that they're quite attractive doesn't hurt either. Really good prices and friendly people. It was unanimous: three votes for "we dig it."

This was my second experience. The first one took FOREVER and during lunch that is not good. We ordered three different pizzas to split between our group and only one was decent. This second experience was worse. My guest ordered the Penne Pasta and I ordered the Mushroom Chibbata. Both were disgusting. The mushrooms seemed slimey. The garlic bread given pre-meal was very hard. The food was not tasty. I returned to work feeling sick to my stomach. I mentioned my experience to a co-worker and she said the only time they went there she went home nauseas too. We will not return again.

I fear sushi places outside of California. Primarily because they tend to douse the rolls with sauces or deep fry them. 

For my first visit, I played it safe and ordered a chicken teriyaki bento box -- substituting the CA roll with a spicy tuna roll. Much to my dismay, the roll had a mayo-based spicy sauce in it, and deep fried tempera batter in the roll as well. 

As far as the other items, the miso soup was bland, and the sauce on the teriyaki was watery. With that said, the service was quick, and the prices were reasonable. I hate to crush a place off of a first visit, so I'll go back.

I worked for Japanese companies for over 20 years. I've had sushi at any number of places across the United States ... in Atlanta, in New Orleans, in Manhattan and New Jersey, in San Francisco and Los Angeles. This little place, tucked in a strip mall at Harrison and Broadway is as good as any sushi restaurants I've been to and actually better than most.

I've had lunch at Ichiban a number of times and tonight I went for dinner with my wife (not a sushi fan, but it was my night to chose). Service was prompt and friendly. Portions were generous (particularly the sushi). My wife loved the teriyaki chicken and the tempura vegetables.

I like Lolita, but prices were not in par with the portion size that I am accustomed to. Folks, if your taking your significant other to eat on a date, this is a dope spot. But ensure you take an Uber, parking was way too difficult and expensive, more expensive than in NYC, sadly to say Philly. Seriously, take an Uber here and make sure to reserve a spot, because on Saturday, it gets packed. 
Service was good, a bit overbearing but friendly, with hints of pretentiousness which I despise, but tolerate. Go check out Lolita, it won't disappoint.

I came back here for lunch with a co-worker last week based on my suggestion from my recent dinner here a month ago.  Perfect once again.  Of course I got the tuna dumplings because they are heaven and my colleague agreed-- a must order.  We also got a few rolls to share and service was fast so we could eat and chat and get back to the hustle bustle of the office.  Since I wasn't drinking this time (I am the employee of the year) I asked for water and was directed to a self-serve station on the side wall.  Foam cups, tea-bags, hot water, and a faucet.  Yup.  This place is officially my dive bar sushi spot and I LOVE it.

I love the dining room in this place. High ceilings, beautifully painted walls and nice tables.

The sushi was fresh and hit the spot. Tempura udon was very tasty indeed. However, the agedashi tofu was nothing more than tempura battered firm tofu with an extremely bland sauce. Seriously, can't someone get agedashi tofu right??

I have to knock one star off for the service. It took around 25 minutes for us to get our check paid for and out the door. At least they were friendly.

Brad's rating (out of 5):
Price: 3
Food: 3
Decor: 5
Service: 2
Wild card: The solo, elderly diner who was pounding Kirin Ichiban and white wine.

I came here because reviewers said this sushi was better than my absolute favorite sushi restaurant in NJ, Mikado. Not so.

The decor is awesome. Nice bar when you walk in. Very clean with good customer service. They play music, seems like a hip spot. 

Now to the food; bland, bland, bland!
We ordered two appetizers. One being the salmon skin salad. Presentation was awesome. Looked delicious. Not so. Very bland. We also ordered two specialty rolls. Nothing to brag about. The food LOOKs good but the taste is definetly not as good as Mikado.

Prior to a group of poorly behaved children and negligent parents  partying in the breakfast area this hotel was decent. The girls ran up and down the third floor hallway screaming and banging on doors while parents got blitzed three floors below also drunkenly disrupting the entire hotel. The front desks response was I can't tell them to stop, really?? I'll try and shut the kids down but we can't tell the loud profane parents to stop?? There is a real management problem here, so prior to booking you might ask if any large parties of kids are coming in and avoid it like the plague.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
All I can comment on are the Cuban sandwiches that our friend bought from here. We found out that her father has been getting Cubans here for years and it has become a regular stop for a quick and easy lunch option.

I found the Cubans to be a little plain and the bread to be a little on the doughy side... more like submarine sandwich bread than Cuban bread and it wasn't pressed.

So maybe I'd call this a good try at a Cuban, but not quite the standard that exists and many other places locally.

I can't speak to the market itself as I haven't been there, but our friend still goes, so that may say something.

I'm considering calling Antonio's the best Mexican food in Reno. I really think it's that good. 

The tacos at this joint are so rad. Fresh full-sized tortillas (double), filled with very fresh and flavorful ingredients.

Can't speak for the carne, but the veg options are top class. I get two veggie tacos, one nopales and one rajas (no cheese), chips and salsa and a Mexican coke. Boom. Vegan heaven.

The fresh salsa is very good, but I would like it turned up another notch on the heat scale (it would be cool if they had a hot option).

Super friendly, and helpful staff. 

Sit outside on the patio and watch the Reno show, it's a good one.

This gym is kind of crap. Most people know that planet fitness isn't an actual gym since they don't even have squat racks because their members get intimidated. That's right if a member thinks something is too hard, they get rid of it. Gold star for everyone as long as you make it into the gym. 

But past all that the staff at this location is rude. Super unprofessional, they don't actually know the machines that they have there and they talk crap on the members. Yep, in the "no judgement zone" of planet fitness the employees judge their members. 

Anyway. If you're serious about fitness find a real gym.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: What a fantastic location.  We pretty much used the hotel for sleeping but it was a great base to explore the area from.  All of the fun bars are nearby as well as the Ryman Auditorium.  Printers Alley was seriously a block away and that was worth it right there.  If you are looking to be in the action and within walking distance of bars this is the hotel for you.  The rooms were large and clean, the check in service good and we experienced no issues.  The only downside I can see is that they do not have a parking lot or free parking.  I would stay here again if I am ever back in the area.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: There is ONE drawer in this hotel room. It is ridiculous. There is plenty of room for a dresser, but nope. Similarly the bathroom has maybe 1 square foot of counter (and then a weird thing glass ledge that's 5' long)-- yet there is air where another 1-2' of country could have been. A business traveler staying only a few night would not mind I guess. But we are here for a week long convention and it's incredibly frustrating. And this looks like a new renovation -- someone CHOSE this as a "guest friendly" solution. Epic fail.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Subway BREAKFAST
Tried the eggwhite on English muffin -- eh.

The muffin is not toasted, so it sort of ends of steamed - not the best taste for an E-muffin.  I opted for eggwhite -- and got to see the unappetizing pile of "white slices" in the container.  The ham was good, but overall pretty tasteless and soggy. 

The sandwiches at Starbucks are much better - or the old standby Egg McMuffin.  

Note - I don't like peppers or onions -- but maybe a "western" style sandwich would have more flavor that others would enjoy.  The "plain vanilla" was not worth it to me.

This was another location we chose after seeing it on Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives and it was another let down by Guy. 
There simply isn't anything special about the ice cream. It's good, yes. They have a ton of unique flavors, yes. The staff is friendly and the place is clean.But there isn't a "WOW" factor here. It's hard to say why this place gets featured on a nationally televised food show while others don't. Nothing about the place truly stands out. If I'm in the neighborhood and have a hankerin' for some ice cream, I'll drop by. Otherwise, your local grocery store will do just fine.

The Orange Couch coffee center also serves an New Orleans unofficial Apple store, the late Steve Jobs would be so proud to have an outlet in the South.  The lone Dell patron on my visit would no doubt soon be ejected for lack of creativity in her laptop purchasing decisions.

Frequented by a highly fashionable hip crowd, which the Dell patron appears to have overlooked, as she not only was not wearing plaid, a cool cap, thick rimmed glasses or skinny jeans, its a fun crowd nonetheless to people watch.  

Nicely prepared mocha, ice cream is served as well as moshi in a midcentury modern setting.

This one star is for the fried green tomatoes. The reviews for this joint must surely be written by sad tourists trapped into eating at one of the only early breakfast options in the area.

The cafe is short on charm, portions and care. For prices they charge, the hollandaise should have been better, or at least warm, the water for tea hot, the juice freshly squeezed and the pastry selection abundant (more than 2 cheap-looking varieties of muffins).  

Perhaps they should scope out what the rest of Nola restaurants are up to with reasonable prices and high quality local produce, hospitality and loving care in cooking.

A fantastic value at happy hour. Dishes like taquitos, albondigas, and tostaditas cost only $5 each. They're decently portioned (not bite sized) and reasonably authentic. You can easily make a meal or a nice group outing out of several of the dishes at once. Drinks are also quite inexpensive at happy hour, ranging from $3-6 for various options. 

The regular menu is far spendier, at least on the surface, but the range of options is far more varied, as are the ingredients. Service is engaging and personable, and the vibe is quite lively and social. One of many good options in this neighborhood.

A Midwest Dunkin is not the same as an East Coast Dunkin. I just don't know why. But still, when I need a Dunkin fix, this is where I usually end up. 

The people here are nice.  I have always had good service.  But, I am spoiled by DD in Boston - a Boston DD could have a line 20 people deep and you'd be in and out in 5 minutes.  At this (and other Indy DDs), I have been 4th in line and get my coffee 15-20 minutes later.

Update: Since I originally wrote this the Dunkin' app came out. Now I use "on the go" ordering and skip all those lines

The car wash is good. The up selling can be a bit much when they continually ask to add something - "you have a great finish on that car, would you like to protect it?"  I say no thank you, and they leave it alone.  (What I would like to say is, "my car looks like my toddlers took a rake down the side of it - what do you mean I have a great finish?")  

The people are always pleasant and seem to care about safety - for customers, employees and vehicles.

I would suggest getting a book if you are going to use the wash multiple times - you'll get 1 or 2 free washes out of it!

I love the pizza. We usually get the meatball. I have tried others but meatball is the favorite. 

They use organic or farm fresh when they can. I think this is hard to find in Indiana. I appreciate having the option. 

There is only one size. It's like a medium size so we usually get two for our family of four. That'll be about $27 before tip. 

I do suggest being careful on special orders like"hold the mushrooms" for carry out. I've had a couple times where the special order didn't happen. But, they made it right. The let me keep the mistake and made a new one. I even got a free drink while waiting.

This is easily located off on rt 30, great location. 

I order the chicken cheese steak and wings. The cheese steak was great, well cooked and cheesy. The wings weren't what I expected, they were breaded wings. The breading on he wings didn't really have a flavor, in my opinion I think they should have listed that the wings were breaded. Added a little hot sauce to give some flavor. 

I've had there pizza before and was great! 

They do offer a selection of takeout beer. 

They do take cash, credit or apple pay :)

I came back here on a Saturday night and ordered rigatoni in a sage-butter-parmesan sauce with grilled shrimp on top which was phenomenal. 

My friend had a pasta and seafood dish (it had scallops, calamari, clams, mussels and salmon in it) which was served in a lemon-garlic white wine sauce which she thought was delicious.

The only reason I won't up the rating is because their salads are always wilted and soggy which grosses me out.  In addition, their service is hit-or-miss and the night I was there, our waiter was completely out of it.

I went last night with some girlfriends for a late happy hour. I was excited to try a new wine bar in Mid-City. I got one cocktail, the 50 Grand, and it was pretty good. Unfortunately, the wine list wasn't as great as I thought it would be for a place calling itself a wine bar. It was no longer than a standard restaurant wine list. I got the 50 Grand, which was great. Since most of us were coming straight from work, we were a little hungry. Ultimately we left after one drink to get some food. 

Since this place is still pretty new, I'll be back to give it another chance. Hopefully they'll add some food options soon!

It smells HORRIBLE (slightly rotting meat). Its produce is often moldy. It's generally overpriced. Its cashiers are incredibly rude without any reason to. Its conveyor belts are always broken, and its lines are always long. One star for convenience, one star because sometimes it has good deals (and a surprisingly OK baking section).

But as an example of the quality of the Supreme's food, I forgot to look at my eggs ONCE before I bought them, and when I got home after treating them as carefully as I normally do, every single egg was cracked open and goopy. Gross.

Really nice little place with some very inspired food and very un-inspired service.

As the other reviewers have pointed out the food is fresh, local, organic with dishes that are satisfyingly prepared. The minimalist atmosphere does a great job of putting the focus on the meal and mirrors the fresh and simple approach. On our visit the service was also quite minimalist. Not rude or awful, just not really there...and not in the 'letting you enjoy your meal' way. We decided to just chalk it up to and 'off' night.

Wine list is a bit paltry for Santa Barbara County.

What a dump!!

An older hotel, converted from another chain.  Staffing is mediocre, and management is lacking.

Our a/c rattled throughout the night. The toilet flapper was partially functioning. There was an inadequate amount of toilet paper in the bathroom, and no additional rolls or additional facial tissue paper were provided. An we were in a VIP room on the top floor.  Hot water shuts down during the day, and we only had hot water during the morning!!

Hot (sic) breakfast buffet was cold, and poor quality of fruit.

We didn't test the wifi.  Parking is free in the rear of the hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: What a pleasurable dining experience!  While this is not fine dining, nor gourmet, it is quality, fresh, and ample portions for very fair prices.  Great for those looking for a casual dining experience, with kids, or dining out on a moderately priced budget.  Steamed calamari & eggplant involtini appetizers were $6.75.  A double house salad feeds 4 was $12.  Pasta dishes were great and are ~ $14.  Special baked fish of the day (branzino) was $22 (this was the only disappointment of the meal, as it was dry and of only moderate portion).  Corkage charge was waived for us, but it might be $10.  The other couple and we would definitely return!!

I want to preface this with the fact that I love La Colombe. I frequent the Fishtown location and would rate that location 6 stars if possible. The newest location on Independence Mall seems to be having a few growing pains. I was disappointed that my iced coffee was not served with a shot of espresso as is customary at all the other locations I've visited in Philadelphia. I also believe the price was higher than the other locations. Hopefully this will all get sorted out and my next visit will result in an update to 5 stars.

I was there for dinner with some friends and it had great ambiance for a casual get-together and reasonably priced.  The staff is very friendly and helpful.  My sister wanted a lemonade, which wasn't on the menu, and our server made it for her and didn't even charge us for it.  The server recommended a crab stuffed tilapia dish that I ordered, and it was fabulous!  Another member of our group ordered a steak and it was cooked perfectly.  There is nothing special with the way the food is made or presented, but it is just done right.  Good old-fashioned American food.

Overall, a cool place.  Atmosphere in the old converted bungalow makes you feel comfortable and at home.... almost like they've invited you into their home for a meal.

I've only had brunch here, never dinner.  The food was well prepared, fresh ingredients, but the portions weren't enormous.  If you're hungover and craving a filling breakfast, this probably won't do it for you.  If you're seeking lighter fare, Circles will probably be a good choice. 

I'm looking forward to having dinner there soon.  This seems to be one of those places my wife and I forget about for months at a time until we're randomly driving by.

A very busy place on a cold Sunday morning. This local coffee roaster is always a favorite of mine and this visit did not disappoint either. 

This was my first visit to this location and I love that there was plenty of off street parking. The inside was nicely decorated and bustling with people. I grabbed a latte to go and was able to get my order in promptly. I also noticed that the baristas were calling patrons by name, which I always think is great. 

My latte was tasty and I will be back when in the area. Thanks for a great experience!

I had a little time before an evening event began and didn't want to drive all the way home just to turn around and head back again, so I stopped in for an hour or so at Starbucks. Typical Sbux.. fast counter service and friendly baristas. The one thing that stuck out at me was the limited seating space inside. Lots of empty tables outside (like.. all of them because it's WINTER) but people were standing around waiting on tables inside. It was a nice enough day that had they had portable heaters outside, I think people would have been out there.. I know I would have been.

What's the deal with Sushi Restaurants in Edmonton putting so much god damn rice in their rolls?  Yea, I like rice but not 27 pounds (I mean kilos) in each freakin' roll!  

Mikado was good and I will probably return due to the lack of any better options around town, I just wish they wouldn't include so much rice.  I think my favorite roll has to be the lobster roll.  Even though its a million canadian dollars it is sorta worth it.  Their seaweed salad ain't bad either.  I also really enjoy their tea. 

That is all.

Why the hell won't you tell me my total before I get to the window and you start handing me my order??? It seems like they change the price they tell me every time I go here so that may be one reason... I wouldn't go here if I was in a hurry bc the line can get pretty long and they do take their time.  

Also, I have a love-hate relationship with one of the workers here.  She's always in a super duper cheery high-pitched happy mood and it freaks me out, sometimes irritates me, but I can't help but smile back.  She must be a robot bc she's always there no matter what time of day I go.

I came here for a friend's birthday and was thoroughly disappointed. The margarita mixes were ehhh, alright - nothing to rave about 0 and the food was mediocre. I am definitely a Mexican food snob, having grown up in LA, and this place tasted kind of bland. There are many different combos to choose from though...and they can definitely accommodate more people than Don Memo's. However, I would definitely pick Don Memo's over this place anytime. They have better margaritas and better tasting food. I would only return here in a group setting (when someone else was organizing and not me).

Week 1.  Got in line before 12pm on a rainy Friday and was number 3. Ordered The Angelo.  Waited 25 minutes.  Pie was smaller than expected.  Sweet sauce was tasty but too much sauce to cheese ratio - definitely not as pictured.  Cheese was also not the bubbly brown pictured - I think they rushed it.  Crust was right amount of crispy for a thin pie.  Not worth the wait and in person ordering in my opinion - but I am willing to give another try if they get a better ordering system and get past the early growing pains.

I am confused about the abundance of super high ratings here.  "Best italian on the main line...", frequently occurs in many of the other reviews.  Our meal was quite mediocre.  My husband LOVES pizza and didn't even eat half of it because it was so soggy and wet in the middle that he couldn't pick up a slice.  My pasta dish was ok, but I didn't feel the need to bring the uneaten half home.  I could hardly taste the anchovies and olives that were somewhere in my sauce.  Best italian of the main line?  We will keep searching.

Be prepared to spend a little more than you would at your "run of the mill" restaurant, because this is more than just that. What makes me give 5 stars is the food. I had the special that evening which was a pork tenderloin that was perfectly cooked. Not too tough, not too tender. The side were spinach and garlic mashed potatoes which didn't disappoint.

The building is in historic Soulard across the street from the AB brewery. The building itself is beautiful and it was nice enough outside to sit on the patio. 

The service was acceptable. I'll be coming back to try somethind different next time.

In my opinion, Nico's carnitas burrito is one of the most emotionally satisfying foods that one can obtain in this city.  It's extremely indulgent -- fatty, rich, and slathered in guacamole -- and reasonably priced at $5.39 after tax [UPDATE: Nico's raised the price of this burrito -- I'm not sure what it costs now, but it's presumably still worth it].  If you haven't had one, then you're seriously missing out.

Besides that, though, the food I've gotten from there has been pretty average; not bad, but nothing I'd be really eager to recommend.

I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at this hotel. The staff were very helpful and friendly. The room was confortable. I slept like a rock on the bed. My room overlooked the little lake (the ducks were very cute). I loved the outdoor seating overlooking the lake for lunch. The "continental breakfast" was better than any other I had seen--biscuits and gravy, scrambled eggs, oatmeal, and more. There was a coffee pot in my room. There was plenty of parking close by. And there was a fire in the fireplace on a cold night when I first arrived, which was wonderful. Wifi was free!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Very enjoyable, hidden gem.  We've lived near 16th and Locust for 18 months and never knew about Ernesto's.  

For a Center City BYOB, it was very spacious interior.  The staff was nice and our food was very good.  My Fettuccine Bolognese was outstanding and the two of us at our table devoured it. My wife's Orecchiette was good but not the best Broccoli Rabe we've had.  Our other friend had the Vegetale Napoleon which had a very cool presentation and she seemed to love it.  

Overall, we'll be back and it's a nice alternative to La Viola (which we like a lot as well).

i've heard so many great things about this place that i was excited to go. However, while I understand why people like it, i found the dishes overly complicated and overly salted. the best thing we had, by far, was the ravioli, the next best thing was the side of peas. When the side of peas is better than the 3 other things you ordered, um, that's a message. To me, this is a neighborhood place.  Doesn't come close to matching the unique complicated and complementary flavors of Helm and is leaning on salt to attract customers.

Pros: fresh produce, good selection of fruits and vegetables and some good prepared foods. 
Cons: no salad bar (that would a nice add). Most importantly the service for check out is non-existent. It's self service but often staff is standing around just watching you check out. Why not help out and pre-set a few paper bags? I needed help figuring out the check out and the person i flagged down was clearly annoyed that they had to help me check out. It would be a plus if they could add someone to the check out area who could be actually helpful.

Achieva has changed a lot over the years. Before they used to be the Pinellas County Teachers Credit Union. This was a fantastic bank. Wonderful customer service, great auto loan rates, the works. What you would expect from a local credit union.

A lot of this has changed in the last few years. It appears new interests have taken over and customer service has dropped dramatically. Fees upon fees now exist, and its worse than the major banks. $0.25 fee every time you use your debit card was the first big one.

I've since changed banks. I do not recommend them, as they do a disservice to the credit union name.

The mine shaft is great if your wife wants to shake her ass with her friends while you stand at the side, drinking blue moon and judging people. It's smoky and loud just as it should be. 

If you're not a dancer but have been dragged here, the people watching is top notch. My only suggestion would be to get a better beer selection. Judging by the patrons, I feel that would be a waste of money as most of the people there are either too drunk to care or don't enjoy good beer. 

I retract my request for you to get better beer solely for the maybe once a month I am there.

The Indianapolis Sheraton is pretty much on par with other Sheraton's across the land.

Great beds, nice sized and clean rooms. 

There is a roof top pool that overlooks the skyline and the circle. The only real thing I dislike about this particular Sheraton is the parking. It's a standard downtown parking garage with a $25 over night fee. A lot of others have similar parking, but I feel like this might be the most expensive overnight Sheraton parking I've had. 

If you're looking for a nice place to stay in downtown Indy within walking distance of pretty much all of downtown Indy, look no further.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Had sushi deluxe, seaweed salad, and got to pick off someone's stir fry udon.  The sushi was pretty fresh and portion of the fish to rice is alright, I personally would like more tho.  The seaweed salad is the standard stuff most Japanese places has and stir fry udon was pretty good.

The service was good, nothing too special but better than average.  

The inside is simply done, i think they're still working on more decor since they just opened up.  If you like sitting at the sushi bar, the place is pretty nice, it has 3 or 4 flat screens hanging behind the sushi bar.

BAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHH

Susan...that was great.

I cringe thinking about going to any Northeast bar....ESPECIALLY the ones located in Mayfair ie; Caspers, Pats. Casper's is basically a EFFIN REUNION for me. Everyone who went to Northeast, Ryan, Lincoln, Judge, HOberts, North Catholic (or any other type of Catholic establishment for that matter) or Dougherty highschools WILL be there. ALSO: Its a flocking zone for the suburb kids who think they are partying in the "city" to come and act like drunk idiots

:::::cringe:::::::

I have eaten at this Oishi about a dozen times. The sushi here is ok. They are a bit stingy with the servings. Shrug. The wine will always be old and taste like cooking wine. Just tell them to open another bottle. They will not be happy about it, but they will do it.

The thing that knocks this place down from 2.5 to 2 stars is the staff. I think they would be much more content if they could work as government bureaucrats. I have not had one server who seems remotely happy to be there. They all seem to literally dislike customers. It's a bummer eating there, but, as I said, the sushi is not bad.

The name is apt.

I love the fact that one can purchase beer here - and fun ones at that.  I'm not a beer drinker so it's nice to be able to stop in here for a few bottles for those times that my beer drinking friends stop by.

I also like the pre-made food section.  My partner and I enjoy cooking, but for when being a student as well as an educator gets in the way of normal life, it's great to have this as an option outside of delivery.

The store is wonderfully clean too!  I worked in a grocery store as a kid and know the common dirty areas and this one meets my white glove test :)

Wow... this restaurant is definitely all it's cracked up to be. Definitely order the cheese dip (FUNdido). It was a piping hot bowl of smoky, cheesy, spicy (but not too much) goodness! The Tacado salad with chicken was excellent with a giant serving of grilled chunk chicken breast coupled with excellent guacamole. The Numero Uno plate was also quite good... featuring a fantastic chicken soft taco. The service was friendly and very fast. Suffice it to say, it will be hard for me not to return to Taqueria Corona the next time I'm in Kenner.

Had an appointment, but unfortunately it was all downhill from there.  Rude and unfriendly service clerk that is an Assistant Manager.  He argued with me, and another customer for no reason at all.  Didn't let me sign quote for simple service, and the service wasn't completed, because he said the technician didn't know how to work on the car as equipped.  Didn't even bother to inform me, instead I was informed that the service wasn't completed after I returned an hour later.   I should have known after seeing the hand written sign at the counter facing the row of chairs for customers that prohibits eating.  Joke.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
I'll be honest - I prefer local coffee shops to chain ones, but sometimes, Starbucks is just so darn convenient.

This particular location is pretty awesome.  They have ample seating for people who want to read and/or study, including a long farm table, which is cool if you don't mind bumping elbows with the person next to you.  They also cater to the soccer-mom type, strollers and all.  

The staff is friendly and I never have to wait super long for my order.  Probably one of the best Starbucks in the city.

If you don't mind the smell of...well, I'm not sure what the smell is in this place, but it's not very pleasant, then Big 8 might be a tolerable experience.

My husband and I were on a mission to find a soda we had when we lived in California, Coco Rico.  After a few minutes, we found it located at the end of an aisle.  While the name is "Coco Rico," the taste and labeling are different than the good stuff we had on the West Coast.  My husband, however, thinks it's still delicious. 

If you're looking for something ethnic and can't find it anywhere else, Big 8 probably has it.

Decent food, average prices and perhaps best of all, online ordering.  The service is quick and I can't complain about the food.  Then again, I am usually eating it after a night of drinking, so anything tastes good after copious amounts of booze.

For real though, I've also had their food sober many times.  If you're too tired/hot/drunk to cook, Fuzhou House is a budget-friendly option.  

Oh and free delivery if you live within a 1 mile radius (I feel like since they have this option, it's only natural that I should take advantage of it, even if I can walk to the place in 3 minutes.)

Decided to go out on a limb and order sushi from a new place.  When it comes to sushi, I tend to be a creature of habit, so this branching out stuff takes some serious guts on my part.

Being that they have, like 50 rolls to choose from (seriously), I had a difficult time making a decision.  They have everything from my go-to rolls (Philly, shrimp tempura) to some crazier concoctions (pumpkin, crabmeat apple).  My husband and I found the quality of the sushi to be above that of most of our usual take-out places, although it is a bit pricier.

I'll definitely return and make sure that I come hungry!

Easy to find.  Here for business.

I was greeted by friendly staff at the front desk, and noted that most staff here are friendly, and will greet you when you are walking around the property.  I was asked several times, by various employees, if I was happy.  Very nice to see such good customer service.

The rooms are nice.  Typical Residence Inn rooms.  Clean and well maintained.

The food is typical here.  I do wish the breakfasts at Residence Inn had a little more variety.  Especially in the healthy foods area...  More/better fruit, some egg white options, etc.  But it was well supplied and warm.

I'd come here again if I'm in the area.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Not impressed.  I went to Pumpkin because all of Philly seemed to rave about it.  Even the ever pessimistic Craig Laban.  I guess that that all of Philly eats meat and is oblivious to tact because the menu at Pumpkin is predominately carnivorous (even fish dishes are infused with sausage) and the service is TACKY.  The waitress needs to go back to gradeschool to learn addition subtraction because she gave us the bill.  We paid.  She had the nerve to come back to our table to tell us she added incorrectly and that we owed more.  That, in my opinion is atrocious.

New in Sherwood Park.  Good food but weird ordering system.  The pastas were quite good and you could see the chicken and shrimp and spinach and their wraps and soup are tasty.  Prices around $14 to $18.  You enter and line up and look at a menu on the wall while people wait behind you, pressure.  You order then they give you a number.  Then you walk further and line up again to order your beverage and pay.  Then you sit down and they bring the food and beverage to you.  I guess you aren't supposed to tip... I don't know.  Staff were pleasant.  Ordering system is annoying but food is good.  So squeezes out 4 stars.

Ok place to have a drink if you are in the Bywater district.  It is an eclectic bar, not the cleanest or most modern, but it gets the job done.  
Like most other places in New Orleans, you will see pretty much every kind of person walk in here.  Everyone gets along and has a good time.  
Outside, you'll find two life-sized sculptures of the Blues Brothers. Great photo opportunity. 

This seems to be the only place in the Bywater area with the NFL package so I'd recommend it for watching the NFL Football games.  No food to speak of, just chips and a wide variety of beers and other assorted alcoholic elixirs to choose from.

Good place to watch the football game if you are in the Bywater district.  It has an eclectic bar, not the cleanest or most modern, but it gets the job done.  
Like most other places in New Orleans, you will see pretty much every kind of person walk in here.  Everyone gets along and has a good time.  
Outside, you'll find two life-sized sculptures of the Blues Brothers. Great photo opportunity. 

This seems to be the only place in the Bywater area with the NFL package so I'd recommend it for watching the NFL Football games.  No food to speak of, just chips and a wide variety of beers and other assorted alcoholic elixirs to choose from.

Service: SLOW, absent-minded, but polite? We waited so long for our drinks that I forgot we were eating there. My fiance's chilli was supposed to come before the meal but it came with the meal (that was the only good item out of the whole table i thought).
Food: My blue plate special bison bbq short ribs came luke warm which got sort of slimey as it got cold. I substituted mashed potatos with sweet potato and green beans with roasted asparagus. Those were OK and I can do a better job at home. The prime ribs that my fiance and his dad ordered were "good." We didn't want the dessert.

After hearing about the out of this world hot chocolate, I had to drag the Hubs down to try it out for myself.
And we were not disappointed.
The hot chocolate (and mochas) are made with a blend of different chocolate (and vanilla) sauces that is truly unique - just like Luzzara itself.
Sarah is really friendly and always has a smile ready.  She seems to truly appreciate every customer that comes in the door.
She also hosts different "event" nights, like a knitting club and information sessions presented by other local businesses on various topics.
This is a great addition to the community

went here to meet up w/ friends, even after reading the reviews. The food, eh. I liked that they offered boneless wings, (in addition to regular boned wings) and I recommend the chipolte dip for it-I dipped my hand cut potato chips in it. YUM! 
I had a Cesar wrap, it was tasty enough, and my companions had the bar pizza (looked pretty good) and the roast pork sandwich which looked and smelled great. the wine-a house pinot grigio was tasty. 
After wards we split a lovely brownie sundae which was probably the best part of the meal!

It's time for an update because Um not sure this place gets the credit it deserves. Yea it's in a strip mall on the outskirts of town but it's a gem! 

The sushi chef is amazing. Your plate will look like a work of art. I've been dining here for lunch for almost  5 years and it's been consistently good. 
The sushi , the regular and house special rolls, the lunch specials, the noodle salad, iced green tea, and service have all been great. 
The prices are reasonable and the hibachi menu too. 
The decor is very plain but the food speaks for itself. Located by the Rouses and Macalister's off Labarre and Airline.

It was a cold morning and all I wanted was a white chocolate peppermint mocha. I was on my way to school so I stopped at this location, no drive thru so I was forced to get out in the cold. It was a packed house.  I order my drink and they are out of white choc. Bummer. So I ordered a peppermint mocha=yuck. Tasted like dirt, not sweet and just when I thought they must have given me the wrong order, I tasted the peppermint on my last sip.  Never again will I waste my time getting out the car and paying $8 for a coffee and a danish when I can go to my local drive thru coffee shop and be way happier.    Lets remember why were NOT friends.

They have the best soft serve ice cream!  When I compared it to 2 other local snoball stands(caseys on w esplanade and another random one) I realized the difference!  My fav is strawberry cheesecake flavor stuffed with condensed milk on top.  My family gets choc soft serve with oreo mixed in and magic shell on top--can you tell they are choc lovers?  Big pieces of oreo are mixed in too.  They are generous with the syrup for the snoballs. We tried the hot tamales that were advertised and they were good too( you take them home and heat them yourself)  Im curious about their stuffed artichoke next.    I just wish they had places to sit outside

Went to Yoitomo for all you can eat sushi for $24.99. I thought this was a little pricey at first, but 5 appetizers and a dozen specialty rolls later I changed my mind. 

Our waitress was very sweet and seemed to come by like clockwork as soon as we finished our plates, ready to take our next order. The deep fried rolls were amazing. One that stands out is the "Mission Impossible". Deep fried roll with tuna and a spicy sauce on top. Wow! So yummy. The fish was very fresh, though I wish the ngiri rolls stuck together better. Atmosphere is okay. Modern and yet strangely outdated. The food definitely made up for this. Four stars!

I had tried Gogo before at a corporate event, and it was bad. I decided to give in-store a try before writing this review. 

The quality of ingredients is very poor. When I go for sushi, I'm expecting fresh cuts and sticky rice. That's about it. Gogo did not deliver. 

College students preparing sushi should be a give-away, but the proof is in the taste. The iPad ordering system is clunky for a user interface. The pre-programmed rolls are not the "classics".  

There are several better options for sushi in Nashville. I would rank Gogo at the bottom. 

The good: The students working there were very friendly.

Normally, I would have given this place three starts, but as Mike P. says, the hours are misleading.  The posted hours are not the actual hours they are open.  It's hit or miss at best. I stop by when I see the flashing light in the window that says open, there is a line, or there are a ton of cars. Why? Because that is the only time they are open.  The ice cream is sweet, creamy and everything nice, but it is not worth the pain of stalking it to see if you get lucky.  If you want to take your chances, it might be worth it.

I'm slightly confused by the reviews for this place. I think the prices are pretty reasonable for a supermarket that is one block away from Rittenhouse Square. I've found some pretty reasonable prices there that are comparable to a normal supermarket. Yes, some of them are overpriced but what do you expect for convenience. If you really want to spend less, go to Shop Rite in south philly. I also think the staff is friendly and they've always has a good selection. They're chicken in particular is actually very reasonable for a per pound price.

So, I ordered the three roll special expecting some pretty good sushi considering the reviews that it got on here. I have to say I was pretty disappointed. Spicy Tuna is my favorite roll of all time and their's was actually kind of fishy tasting and wasn't spicy at all. The Spicy Salmon roll was a bit better and the Shrimp Tempura roll was okay too but not very tempura like. I also got some pork gyoza which were pretty dry and were steamed not pan fried.  It was a good price but I don't know if I'd go there again, maybe to try the specialty rolls but I think I'll take my money elsewhere.

Went here with my sister and Dad and was seated right away on a busy Saturday night. We got a bunch of sushi, including some specials. It didn't take too long but when we ordered another order to satisfy us a bit more, we were given the small plate special on the house because they said the sushi bar was backed up; we hadn't even noticed that it had been a while! Their sushi was very reasonably priced and very good. They also have a bunch of asian beers which I love so I'd definitely go here again. BTW, if you're going to order the spicy tuna, order it crunchy, it's amazing. Their fish is super fresh too, not fishy taste at all.

The pros:
Generous Portions
Great Location (I'm bias since I live two blocks away)
Relatively inexpensive
Complementary bread with oil

The cons: 
Crammped 
Stuffy
Cranky and Poor Service 

This restaurant normally caters to large groups so it can get loud very quickly. As such, the staff tends to get impatient and cranky later in the evening. I went last Friday at 9:00 pm with a group of 8. Needless to say it took quite a while for the water and bread to be served. The food is tasty enough, nothing too earth-shattering, but not repulsive either. You also normally have leftovers which is always a plus.

Went about 2:30 on a Tuesday and we were the only ones in there. The food was quick and good. 

We had the quesadilla for an appetizer and it was yummy but quite cheesy. I had the ham and spring mix sandwich with a salad. Definitely amazing. My friend had the brie, ham, and apple sandwich which was equally good. Very fresh and quick. The bread was amazing on the paninis. A bit too greasy for my liking, but I'm super picky about grease.  For the normal person it would not be seen as greasy. This was definitely better than typical bar food. 

The waitress was nice and very attentive.

Never again. Not this Wendy burger and not any other one ever again either. I got a single combo w/ cheese & a jr bacon. About 15 minutes after eating this horrid meal I vomited all of it up in one painful shot. After that I wasn't mad anymore that the incompotent cashier had forgotten my side of imitation cheese sauce.

Years ago I love the super bar at wendys but once they took that away and Dave died this chain hit the skids. I can see them going belly up if they don't change their ways. It's a standards issue and wendys seems to have forgotten them along the way.

Place is okay. They were the only restaurant that was able to accommodate a large party on such short notice. I ordered the black spaghetti that other patrons raved about. It was pretty disgusting. I'm not sure why he had some a weird texture and almost tasted like plastic. I've tried many different types of spaghetti and this by far was the worst plate I've tried. My co-workers said their food was okay though. Maybe it was just what I ordered that sucked. If I'm ever in Nashville again, I'd give them another go. The drinks were on point as expected.

My husband and I planned a kid-free trip to New Orleans in October. Our suite was so perfect for us! The rooms were spacious and inviting. The courtyard was adorable and relaxing. The staff was friendly and accommodating. The location was very convenient! I liked being in a private hotel, not the traditional kind. I felt like I was at a bed and breakfast! I enjoyed having my morning coffee on the patio in front of our apartment. In the afternoon, I would sit by the pool and read a book or take a nap. The ambiance was pleasant overall!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
First visit to this establishment. Figured I needed to since most of the people I work with have been there and seem to like the fare.

The food was inexpensive, which is what I was going for today, and tasted good. It reminded me of a homemade meal. Not the kind grandma used to make, but more the kind that you and a group of your buddies would make.

Being my first time to Teutenberg's, I don't think it won me over just yet. There's a lot of different items to try out on the menu and I think I'll be back. Possibly, after a few more visits I'll raise the rating up to four stars. (I don't think it will hit five.)

It's a lovely hotel but they're determined to nickel and dime you to death around wifi access. The wifi splash pages doesn't tell you how much access costs, which might lead one to think it's free for hotel guests. Even a limited speed access is typical today. And charging guests to use a computer in the (FedEx branded) business center is rather chintzy. I spent a lot of time averting inadvertent spending disasters with my parents. 

Otherwise, very cordial and competent staff, spacious rooms, and excellent location.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Pretty good Mexican food- I am sorta a snob and think one of my first meals in California was Mexican- 
First off - prior reviews mentioned the service. Actually, I found our server- Araceli- quite attentive. Our food was delivered promptly and hot. 
Margaritas just ok- syrupy but not bad.
The fajitas were good- lots of steak onions and peppers. The flavor of the steak was good albeit it a bit tough. I am a guacamole snob and that was the downfall- overripe avocados? Old guac? Either way not so good. 
Would I come back? Lots of other mexican to try on nolansville road so ? 
But ---the place is crowded so clearly it is a popular spot!

Underrated burger alert!!

Randomly came into Pag's during a stroll around Doylestown. The menu wasn't super appealing, actually, so I just went with a cheeseburger. Legitimately, one of the best cheeseburgers I've had in a while! Tasted like a quality Big Mac! Patty wasn't too thick, bun didn't overshadow the burger and whatever sauce they used - YUM.

We were in the wine bar section - ambiance is really nice; def not very kid friendly (we had our son with us.) but staff was friendly and accommodating.

We will totally be back next time we are in the mood for a good burger!

The Landing is ok. It's really great for river views and gathering amongst friends, but if you're looking for great food - there's plenty of better places in New Hope.

I ordered the pear salad to start, it was lovely. My fiance ordered the calamari, they were sort of chewy and not fresh. For my entree, I got the sirloin special and it was nothing special, could have made it at home. My fiance ordered the fish and chips and was a little disappointed - the fish didn't seem fresh and the portion was a bit small. 

I wouldn't run back to The Landing for the food, but the views and ambiance are hard to beat.

My girlfriend and I are fans of "the groupon" (if you don't know what this is, send me a message and I'll hook ya up). We randomly decided to pick one up for Panini's having heard just about nothing about the place - we win! 

Panini's is exceptionally yummy. The service is down to earth and friendly - you truly feel as if they really appreciate your business. It's a little tiny (very NYC style) so it's not a great place to bring large groups or small children, but otherwise it's a no-brainer. 

Also, the espresso is devine. We were passing by a few days later and decided to just pop in for the espresso. Yumm!

Both times we've been to R Bistro we were there for beer dinners (one was 3 Floyds and the other was Brugge Brasserie) and both times the food and beer pairings were weak.  The staff was horrible, pretentious and rude.  The food was nothing special and quite honestly both times we left disappointed.  About the only thing that was good for both meals were the beers themselves - which R Bistro had no hand in preparing! 

Based on that I wouldn't come here on a regular night because of how poorly both dinners went.

I work within a stones throw of the Eiteljorg and like hitting up this place for a southwestern style meal that I can walk to without getting my car out of the garage.  

The Buffalo Chili is my favorite dish and I love the big chunk of cornbread on the side.  You can kick up the spice level with Cholula hot sauce or keep it on the mild side.  I'm also a big fan of the nachos (big enough to split) and the pulled pork sandwich is really good for museum food. 

Is this a great restaurant?  No, but it is a nice place for lunch when you're tired of all the usual places!

Great little hotel on the Gulf of Mexico with awesome beach space.  Our king club room was well appointed and cozy, but I had to hunt for the hairdryer (check the closet).  I'm a Starwood Preferred Guest so I'm used to staying in Sheratons, but this was the first time the hairdryer was in the closet!  

Our room had an awesome view of the gulf and the beach which made it perfect for a relaxing getaway for my husband and I.  I highly recommend getting the club option if you have it since the breakfast is included along with a happy hour.  

I would stay here again and would recommend it to my friends looking for a quick getaway on the Gulf!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
It's a dive bar and being New Orleans, smoking is allowed in this bar (so you non-smokers take note and don't b*tch about it afterwards). 

Came here on a Monday for King James and the Special Men; excellent, awesome show!! It was exactly the authentic New Orleans nightlife I wanted to experience. It was refreshing to see couples, young and old, making their way to the front and dancing together. I would never see that at home. Service was friendly but not overly so. It's a block away from Vaughn's and close enough to Bacchanal to make a night out of the 3. 

Free red beans & rice on Mondays (as is in the New Orleans tradition)!

Ordered delivery from here today. 

Broccoli with garlic sauce? Not bad but kind of bland (I requested it spicy).

Schezwan tofu? Not good at all. Tofu was soft and gooey. Very bland.

Veggie fried rice? No veggies. Tasted like oil poured over old rice. 

Hot and sour soup? Had substance in it with lots of veggies and tofu but it was so thick and slimy I was just confused by the texture. Oh, and very bland. 

Quick delivery time was nice. The fact that I spent $20 on food to last me a few meals but then threw everything out after eating half of one meal was not nice. And my stomach hurt for hours afterwards.

It's a Starbucks.

It met my expectations: friendly service, consistent food and beverage, free wifi, relatively clean, lots of outlets for electronics, and convenient location.

I had never been to this one, and it is a good choice for stopping while in South Reno. It is bigger than the one on Mt. Rose, there is LOTS of parking (it is in the Sierra Summit Mall) and when I went (early afternoon) there was no wait.

Nothing stood out as being outstanding. Nothing stood out as being terrible - hence "A-OK"

Being average is not necessarily a bad thing for a chain.

If there were such a thing as The Hall of Extraordinary Dive Bars, The Handle Bar would most definitely belong in it. Whatever hipsterity exists here is but a thin veneer, easily wiped away to reveal its true non-hipster, working class origins.

It's in a great spot too. Within the context of the rise of NoLibs and Fishtown, it's near the "center of things" yet simultaneously off the beaten path. I dig that. 

I've done my time on the dive bar circuit and this place quickly became a favorite of mine. If you like dive bars, you should check it out.

Get fu-shnickened and be sure to take care of your bartenders.

I gave them 3 stars because like real estate: location, location, location.  It was just steps from the street car lines and you can walk to either the French Quarter or Art District in minutes.

OK, I'll be nice, the rooms weren't that terrible either.  Although, they didn't get my room right (and after some fussing, finally reached a resolution) and the walls are paper thin it was at least clean and contemporary.  

Wifi should be free in your room, but it's not, it's $15/day.  Bed was comfy, breakfast was AWESOME.  The service I had was attentive and friendly.

Not totally sure if I'd stay here again, but not sure if I wouldn't.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Delicious food. Very high quality. Restaurant has serious time management issues. Wanted dessert and a coffee but was also on a bit of a time crunch. I wanted to leave between 730&745. Finished my meal between 645&7. Awsome, I thought, plenty of time for dessert and coffee, but no. I was wrong. I waited for over 35 minutes before I had to flag down the waitress for the check. Too bad, the dessert tray looked amazing when I walked in. Work on your servers time management please, and ill give you more stars. I will return, maybe sometime when I can spend more than an hour and a half there.

Colombo's is a smoking bar that is open until 3 am and no cover. They have a patio that you can sit out on. Some of the female bartenders are rude to customers, which turns me off from buying drinks from them. If you want to play music, you will be waiting for hours to hear the song you paid for. It's mainly a bar that you sit and talk with friends, no dancing. It's an ok bar to go to if you're in the area and don't want to pay a cover. But beware, if you plan on coming here as your last stop for the night, they do last call around 2:15 am.

I have conflicting view on Illuminare.  It is close and for the most part I have had some excellent food here (calamari is great).  On a few occasions I have had subpar food though.  The one major glitch that I have with this restaurant is the service.  It is pretty consistently not good.  I don't like to wait forever for my drinks, have my order screwed up, not get checked on after I have my meal, and wait forever for the bill.  But hey, that is just me.  The atmosphere is nice.  If they could make the food more consistent and beef up the service this would be an amazing place.

No complaints.  I stay here for work a few times per year, and the location never dissapoints.

I stayed on the first floor which has been re-done over the last year, so it smells new and looks nice.  The people working the property are all very nice.

What I like:
-  gym has new equipment, although limited
-  FREE continential breakfast
-  FREE internet
-  comfortable beds
-  rate out the door was like $165
-  big parking area, you can get close to the door, which is nice in the snow!

For what it is, and the cost - you can't beat it!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I've been going to Millenium for years now and they are a great nail place.  Even though I've moved from NJ, I still go there when I'm around.  Their work isn't always consistent but everyone does a pretty solid job.  They are quick and clean and everyone is really nice.  The waxing is pretty good too.  You can't beat their prices..$28 for mani/pedi.  

**note** they sell nail kits for $1 which include a buffer and a nail file.  You have to buy one from them but it's yours to keep and you bring it back each time you go.

We recognize it's a challenge on opening night but were excited about trying newest restaurant in West Chester. The restaurant has nice decor, large open kitchen, comfortable seating and great background music. We were surprised at how limited menu was, only  three entrees to choose from. Our party of four had all three, chicken, pork and tile fish. the presentation was beautiful, temperature perfect but lacking flavor. Also, the bread was sub par. Service was excellent. We will definitely be going back, hope to see expanded menu and/or maybe specials. We wish them much success .

My friend and I decided to go for a last minute sushi run and we decided to go here since it was close to where I was staying and my love for sushi.  I ordered the Spicy Tuna roll, the Philadelphia roll, and the Futomaki roll.  The service was fine.  The spicy tuna was ok.  The salmon in the Philadelphia roll was yuck - not fresh at all.
The Futomaki roll was even worse.  It was made poorly and just fell apart the second I picked it out.  Every single one of them did that.
I didn't finish my meal.  I was visiting from The OC and but I won't be back visiting that place again.  No thank you.

Bullet review :)

- Salad was just a glob of lettuce on the plate. Nothing was done - not even lumping the salad to the middle of the plate - to make it presentable.
- Pork had no flavor
- Plating / Presentation was non existent
- Desert was way to big (and also plated so incredibly poorly)

The whole thing felt like eating at a Denny's where the staff had checked out for the day. Actually, I've had many better meals at Denny's


....went here because of a restaurant.com certificate. Now i see why they signed up for that program..

I went to Eye Encounters to receive a much needed eye exam.  At my appointment, I waited for about 45 minutes before being seen.  When I went back to the exam room, I was surprised that the room did not feel very clean.  I was asked to use equipment directly on my face that I was sure had not been disinfected from the previous exam. The examining doctor did wipe down the equipment with alcohol at my request, but it still felt pretty gross.

I'd give this place one star, but I did have a positive experience with the women that staff the store. They were all very friendly and personable.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
I would absolutely give Little Nonna a second try, but I was not terribly blown away by my first visit.  We started with the garlic bread appetizer that had a lovely fresh garlic spread.  I thought this was delicious, but the bread came out very very dark, I would say on the verge of burnt.  

I had the swordfish entree as my meal.  I thought the fish was tasty, though a bit too salty and I found the accompanied vegetable proportions to be incredibly small. 

I really loved the environment. Our server was very friendly and attentive to our table.  There are absolutely other things on the menu that I'd want to try, so I'll definitely go back.

I've always said you can tell a good Mexican place by their carnitas. My carnitas were NOT good because the pork was all jacked up and hard around the edges. Everybody else loved their food and some dude even stopped me while I was walking here and told me how it was the best Mexican food he'd ever had.... 
My frozen margarita was priced right but it had big ice chunks in it which rendered it undrinkable with a straw. 

I'll go back and give it another chance but I'll stick to easy Mexican like tacos or burritos and enjoy a cerveza instead with hopes of writing an updated positive review.

If you know the Passariello's formula you know it's clean, the food is good and at a great value, and the service is excellent. This is the newest outlet. It's bright, roomy with some giant booths and well laid out. 
I opted for a proper dinner with my dear friend, though salads, sandwiches, and pizza are great choices here, too. She had Chicken Francaise,  mashed red potatoes and broccoli. All were delicious & the chicken sooo tender. 
I had Eggplant Parmagiana with roasted red potatoes and a cauliflower medley. Very nice!
It is not table service, but cafeteria-ish. That serves to ensure good food,... quickly. 
Enjoy!

I come to this 'bucks location because I happen to be on Racetrack a lot, but it's not my fave. If it didn't have a drive thru I wouldn't come at all.

For whatever reason this 'bucks doesn't make my coffee right. They always use more milk than espresso. I like my coffee to be robust, which normally I can get in a mocha or latte, but this location seems to skimp on how much coffee actually goes into those drinks...so I try to only get a tall when I come here. The bigger the drink the more milk they add. Yuck.

I prefer the one all the way on Anderson and drive out of the way at times just to go there.

After my 2nd visit I am a fan. My 1st cut was alright, but the second one is much better. The owner and sole stylist Hoa is an Asian woman who is friendly, pleasant, and does a great job. She washes your hair after the cut, which seems unusual, but includes a scalp massage. I guess this is an Asian thing, as I have only got this treatment from establishments run by folks of that persuasion.

The shop is very clean, the cut is $13, and does not take very long. I hope to make this my new go-to haircut place. Located on Broad St, between Morris & Moore.

Good old school S. Philly Italian-American food. 
You enter thru the bar to a no-frills dining room. Can get crowded around dinner time, so you may have to wait. Not much on atmosphere, but the service is good.

The food is really good. Gravy is excellent, as are the meatballs and the seafood dishes. 

I think the prices are a bit high for the portion sizes. The asparagus appetizer is great, but a bit steep @ $8.95. I really wanted to give them a higher rating. The pricing and the fact they they serve frozen spinach, and sub-par grated Parmesan prevented me from doing so.

Perfect for the college student who wants good Mexican and bring-your-own-tequila margaritas, but can't afford to go to Lolita. 

The prices are great - for $6, you can get a pitcher of margaritas (Lime, Strawberry, or Peach). I had the enchiladas mole, and while I was disappointed that they used corn tortillas instead of flour, for 12 bucks, you can't go wrong. The atmosphere is laid-back and casual. The wait staff was attentive and friendly, and the restaurant is great for groups. My friends and I will definitely be back.

I have to agree with the previous reviewers. The supermarket is dated and underwhelming. The best use for this market is when you don't have gas to get to the Giant, Wegmans or Weis. The only thing positive to say about this market would be the state store inside, but even that is disappointing due to its poor selection. Again, it's convenient. 

Even with all this and I might be able to shop there, but then you get to the cash registers, the cashiers are surly and unprofessional. I'm not sure how a place like this stays in business.

Just a not a fan of Subway's lately.  The service at this store is less than stellar.  It's pretty much just give me your money and get along.  The quality of the veggies is lackluster.. I'd hardly call anything in this store 'fresh' except for the bread.  The one thing this location does have going for it is that they move pretty quickly.  I stopped by at the tail end of the lunch rush and was able to get in and our in a fairly good time.    

Prices keep going up.. quality going down?   I'll pass for the near future.

I missed Champps when I moved.. and I'm happy to be back.  We not be here every weekend, but its always good when we do go.  I don't realize how big this place is until we get inside.  

Our server was attentive and took good care of us.  Their chips and queso is good.. The salsa that come with it wasn't my favorite, but worked.  

I got the cuban sandwich and was surprised!! It was very good.  The pork was cooked well and had great flavor.  The ham wasn't anything spectacular but it worked out just fine.  
The beer selection was OK but a bit expensive if I remember correctly.  

Overall a good experience.. we will be back!

I quite enjoyed the pizza from Charlie & Millies. I think it helps if you have a good idea as to what you are getting. The crust is a super-thin, cracker-like round unleavened crust. The best way to describe it is St. Louis style but with the traditional mozzarella instead of provel cheese. The sauce is on the sweet side. The place has been around forever so they are doing something right. I got takeout and they were quick and friendly. They also have really cheap draft beer prices for pitches for eating there. I will add it to my local Seminole/Largo pizza place list when I feel like a thin crust.

extremely disappointed with my recent visit.  

presentation - sloppy
taste - sloppy
service - slow and forgetful
wait - forever

it took a good 20 mins just to bring over a bottle of sake and this is with a reminder.  took even longer for the food to arrive... the seaweed was stale.. the rolls were small and loose.  we walked in around 8:45... i get it-- it's busy on friday.. but my whole meal lasted for a little over 2 hours.. definitely not what i was hoping for a quick easy meal.. 

will think twice before visiting again...

For the price, you really can't top this one.  Good neighborhood, clean room, descent breakfast (well what you'd expect for just over $100 a night), and walking distance from the capital building, Constitution center/Liberty Bell/ Washington Sq. Ritterhouse Sq., museums, and (if you like to walk a little further), the big building with stairs that Rocky ran up and danced around at in the first movie.  If you walk across the street and through the parking lot to the left, you'll find a couple of pretty descent bars, but if you're in town on a Friday or Saturday night, see my review of Bob and Barbara's before you do ANYTHING else.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I hadn't been to a Baskin Robbins in over 10 years. Let me tell you that the last flavor I tried was their Shrek featured flavor with chocolate covered pretzels. Today I decided to stop in and get an iced or frozen cappuccino type coffee drink to take a break from Starbucks. I figured the calories would be just about the same anyway :) 

Very pleasant experience. The store owner was able to explain all of the different coffee drink options. Of course I opted for the triple chocolately one (but that's just me :). Would highly recommend to satisfy your work week afternoon sweet tooth!!

I went for happy hour on a Thursday around 5 pm.  We went to the wine cellar area of this establishment.  They had half price appetizers from 5-6 pm.  I decided to try something new after my friend told me about an espresso martini the waterwheel has on their menu.  It was yummy and filled to the brim!  As an appetizer, I ordered the crab meat martini which is lump crab meat served to you on a bed of greens with marinated cucumber and onion slivers.  The crab meat was quite tasty --- you could tell it was a good quality of meat!  The bartender was attentive, polite, and helpful with suggestions.  A very enjoyable experience for my first visit.

good standard breakfast at a reasonable price. Sunday morning can best be started off with a veggie omelet or eggs benedict. Tasty and even though a few reviews here are complaining about the service we thought it was okay. Not a destination restaurant, but hey they can't all be, when you're hungry, you're just hungry- right? It was pretty windy the morning we went or we might have tried dining al fresco as it looked like a cool spot to catch some early morning traffic- you know those people that drive the wrong direction on the one way street - I love that!

Well it's Papa John's, so you should know what to expect. We got their jack-o-lantern shaped pizza for Halloween, because we're suckers. We ordered carry out, and it unfortunately took longer than expected. The other issue we had was that since it was a special pizza, it wasn't sliced. It was supposed to come with a pizza cutter, but we didn't get one. Maybe they were out? It was fine, since we have a pizza cutter at home. Unfortunately it was kind of frustrating, especially when our hungry family was ready to rip into that pizza.

I can't comment about much from this restaurant but I was at the Harry Potter Festival in Chestnut Hill this weekend and Stella Sera was offering butterbeer cannolis and they were phenomenal! The shell was fresh and crunchy, the filling had a slight butterscotch flavor from the butterbeer and it wasn't gritty at all as can happen with some cannoli fillings. If a restaurant can impress me with dessert, I'm much more apt to try it for a proper meal. :) Stella Sera has proven itself and we'll be back to try it for dinner! (And it's BYOB which I LOVE!)

For $14.99 a month I can't complain. I come in and do my bike/elliptical/weight thing. The ladies locker room has a sauna, they have a ladies only weight room, there is a cardio cinema, they offer Zumba classes and they also have a smoothie bar.

My only issue is the machines are broken a lot. Like more than they should be. Not to a point where I can't work out at all, but enough to be annoying.

If they would just spend a little money sprucing the joint up, I think this could be a great gym. Like I said though, for $15 a month I get what I need from it.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Decided to try Chill for a second time since a few of my friends have mentioned how much they like it.  I don't.  

Compared to Fro Yo in the Loop, Chill is cleaner, calmer and better staffed.  Their toppings are better and more varied.  Unfortunately, their yogurt sucks.  

Fro Yo's yogurt tastes like yogurt - creamy and kind of like ice cream, but lighter.  Chill's yogurt tastes like it is non-dairy.  Not creamy at all.  When it melts it looks less like melted ice cream than watery gel.  

I'm sticking to Fro Yo.

If you like Cuban sandwiches this is the place.  

I love the Cuban sandwich lunch anywhere, and have tried Cubans from Tampa to St. Pete, everywhere in between and around.  (There is a big Cuban culture here - Tampa served as a primary port before the trade embargo and it still flourishes with the roots from long ago)

 Every restaurant claims to have "the best cuban sandwich."  Caribbean Cafe is less talk and more action, and they get it right.   Go to this place, I defy you to find a better cuban anywhere, save Havana.  The value here is also great, get a sandwich and black beans and rice for under $5.  What a lunch!

I thought this place was going to be frou-frou to the max with those statues and such, but it's just like Acropolis. Knowing that I felt more inclined to go here since I'm usually in that area dressed in normal clothing. Food was pretty good. For apps got the Beef Carpaccio (delicious). For meal got the Crispy Duck. It wasn't very oily to my surprise. The whole thing tasted like Thanksgiving. Price is a bit high (nothing like Acrop). Overall though, I'm a fan. Will probably be going here more often since I know I don't have to get all fancy.

Pretty good. The place seems to fill up pretty fast on Friday, so make a reservation if you can. The concept of a changing menu is pretty nice. Of the three small plates we ordered, one wasn't anything to rave about. For the entree I got a Soft Double, described by the host as a vegetarian double down. It was pretty tasty. Overall, it seems like pairing is key with this place. 

Since the menu changes, this review hinges more on the drink selection, decor, and service. The place is a gem with great staff. I would recommend it to others to at least try. However, cider fans take note, there is no cider here :sadface:

When it opened, what set Noble apart were the chef's inventiveness and insistence on fresh, locally-sourced ingredients. While the top-shelf ingredients remain, the inventiveness has given way to massive overcomplication and loss of attention to details.

The chilled white asparagus soup I ordered tonight was lovely, but the risotto came out bathing in some appetite-destroying green liquid. (My overly-familiar server tried to pass this off as the way it is supposed to be, which was patent nonsense considering another person at my table had none of the Hulk juice around his risotto.)

This place badly needs to get back to basics.

i just had the rolls.  it's pretty good for around here, and especially if you haven't been to a big city for sushi in a while.  they give you a decent volume of food.  the fried (on the outside) rolls were not crispy, but at least the center wasn't cooked.  i didn't taste any fishy tuna, which is always my test of if the sushi if fresh.  they tend to load on the sauces, so it's not exactly subtle flavors that you're experiencing.  For close/proximity to home, I'd definitely go back.  But otherwise, see my review of Peter's for the Nashville area.

Met a friend for lunch and I only had an hour. The place was totally empty so that sort of made me nervous. We were told to sit anywhere and quickly loaded the menus on our phones. 
We each ordered the nigiri with a roll lunch item. I got spicy tuna and my friend got the tempura roll. Her roll came out within minutes. It was a really long time before my roll or the rest of the food came out. Like 20 minutes after the first. The food itself was decent. Nothing out of the ordinary but good. I had to wave the waitress down for our check as I had to be back at work. I'll probably go back again but only if I have more time.

The Ruby Tuesday in the Willow Grove Mall is hit or miss. Sometimes it is a good representation of the chain others it's a pretty poor experience. 

The restaurant is clean, the food is generally well cooked although not always and the waitstaff can often seem like they're just going through the motions. The salad bar is also not always kept up with, which considering the salad bar is what makes Ruby Tuesday unique against the similar chains, is problematic. 

There are a lot of chain dining options in the area, so you're probably better off going somewhere else.

This is one of the Courtyard Hotels that actually contains a central courtyard. Many of the rooms are ringed around the pool in the center of building. It can be both very nice and very annoying depending on whether you want to be part of the group by the pool or just want them to shut-up so you can get some sleep.
