The hotel is right across from the Willow Grove exit off of the PA Turnpike which makes it convenient for travelers. 

The rooms are pretty standard sized and were very clean. The pricing is also average. 

It is the best option if you're looking for a hotel in the immediate area.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
As an ABC (American Born Chinese) it's kinda hard to find a place with the right combination of the quality, price, familiarity with Asian hair, and the ability to communicate with the stylist in English. 

Sure you may be able to find skilled stylists or inexpensive stylists, but especially in Chinatown you are rarely able to find the complete package and that's where Perfect Cut Hair Salon comes in. 

Francis is not only skilled but provides a fluent option in Chinatown while maintaining low prices (Standard men's rate of 15+ tip) and higher quality.

For those lacking the ability to effectively communicate in Chinese, she's a lifesaver.

Okay, so I used to live 2 blocks away from this gem of a chinese restaurant, and it is hands down the absolute BEST chinese I have EVER had.... EVER...anywhere... and I've ate alot of chinese....I've had both the delivery and picked it up, and when it was delivered it was piping hot, and delicious! I cant speak for most of the menu items since I normally stick to general tso's chicken, fried rice and crab ragoon, but my word this stuff is awesome. So, if you're ever in the area, stop by...Its in an old pizza hut building.....

Sunday 3/10th- we arrived at Gallaghers 30 minutes before they closed- 
we were turned away at the door because "they had a wait longer than they were open".
We had drove all the way to Gallaghers-and we saw about 10 other people walk out too who were all extremely pi$$Ed- with good reason and said they would never go back.
I didnt even see any one waiting--- 
So note to Gallaghers- DONT TURN AWAY PAYING CUSTOMERS!! 
but we went to Farmers Inn in Millstadt and had delicious fried chicken, so if you get there and they turn you away too, keep Farmers Inn in mind! :)

Had a work meeting here for several days... Had all our meals privately served in the Lobby Restaurant and the food was great. Service was great. 

Hotel is completely new and clean in the lobby & meeting spaces. 

I was unfortunately staying at the Monteleone across the street, but I hosted all the meetings in this hotel as thats where my team was located.  We used several rooms & A/V and meetings planners were super helpful & were there when any requests came up. 

Would love to stay in this hotel when back In NOLA, but I can tell you for meetings and meals, they are great.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This is yummy pizza, though I wish it weren't quite so crispy.  The ingredients tast fresh and they are generally pleasant when you dine in.

As a bonus, they got the pepperoni right.  

Sometimes when you go for slices they have some weird shit... like they had a pizza with American Cheese the other day.  I didn't try it, but let's be honest, that's the kind of ideas you get at 3AM when you're looking in your fridge for a late-night snack.

Speaking of late night, this place could make a killing if they stayed open through last call.  It is infinitely better than Tower Style.

Also - had a slice of margherita yesterday - $3.30?  Really?

This location used to be the "gold standard" of Mickey D's, but since the regular morning crew has all quit or retired, the location needs some "sprucing up".  They recently renovated and redecorated, added kiosks, and removed the Redbox vending. They aren't keeping it as clean and fly-free as they used to. They encourage using the ordering kiosks with a credit card, but I prefer to order and pay cash at the counter. They need to hire more counter help. It's still cleaner than most in the area, but they need to up their game again.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: I usually love A & W I have had more then one issue at this location.The one evening I went I thought it was a little quick to get my food considering as quick as it came out it couldnt be fresh. I love poutines very much and thats what I usually grab if I work late and have not had supper yet.  Twice I had cold almost frozen cheese on my poutine.  The one evening I went I thought it was a little quick to get my food considering as quick as it came out it couldnt be fresh. I guess i'll have to stick to new york fries great poutines or a new a&w.

I don't normally jump the fun on reviewing anything but I just had the best steak tortas from here that I have ever had. Seriously, I didn't want them to end! We obviously came at a time that was slower, so it was pretty quiet and our food came quickly. The girl behind the counter was very sweet and a little shy. I wish I knew Spanish to make ordering more fluid (I don't see this as a negative, because if much of the menu is in Spanish you know you're getting some authentic delicious food).

Since I live down the street, I'm looking forward to coming again (and again) to try more of their food.

This is my neighborhood Starbucks and I frequent it often. Very often. Of course they can make every drink to perfection except the Flat White. It's supposed to be with steamed milk. Not a cappuccino or a latte but steamed milk.  I hate complaining about things but .... Why can't they make a flat white?!  The ONLY person that can a proper Flat White is Hannah. She ROCKS!  She's awesome!!  ....but she works mornings. So if I go on a day she's off or go later in the day, I shouldn't order a drink for my husband. Check out the pic of the drink we got today.

I loved my sushi, I ordered the crispy spicy salmon roll. It was good. I also order Steak and Shrimp from the hibachi  menu for my friend. I didnt care too much for it. Everything  was overcooked. The veggies was soggy and the steak was tough. She was pretty upset and i definitely  felt her pain. However the place was clean and the staff was polite, we ordered to go. Why they only received  3 stars because it was maybe two parties dining in. The food took forever. We basically wasted our whole lunch. I will give them another try for the sushi. BUT  I will stand clear of the hibachi. BTW the sushi is 50% off.. Dont know how long that will last.

Love Starbucks coffee and generally the service is pretty quick but this place is slooooow. The barista seemed like he knew how to make the drinks he just moved really really slow. There were only 5 not too special drinks in front of me and it took 17 mins to get mine. Every other Starbucks I've been to would have blown 5 or 6 out 10 mins faster. Based on the previous reviews this seems like a common complaint. Sounds like a new manager is needed. Do yourself a favor and walk the extra block the next Starbucks. You'll have your drink in your hand sooner even with the extra walk.

I'll keep this short and sweet. The food is good. Not O-M-G amazing, but good. The main reason why I wouldn't rush to eat here again is that the portions are simply too small for my liking, especially with the pricing of their dishes. I hate leaving a restaurant not having my fill, which sucks because everything else about this restaurant I would give a high rating.

Seeing that Seminole Heights still lacks on ample dining choices I will probably come back in the future to hang out upstairs and just eat a hardy meal elsewhere.

I was looking through a coupon mailer, and I found a coupon. I hadn't been to Sushi Time in about two years, so I thought I'd give it a go. I went for lunch and it was really only ok. The krab was off, that's for sure. It had a very weird texture, and that wasn't on account of it being krab, it just seemed like they were trying to offload it when they gave me a special I didn't even order that had a pile of crab in the middle. My friend liked it, but I wasn't down. Also, even with the dollar off coupon and drinks and a small tip, lunch was around $20. It just seemed like  a lot for something not that great.

Stayed here for almost a week during a business trip. The location is great. It's very close to Nashville's nightlife and a ton of restaurants. I did not rent a car while I was there, and I didn't need one at all thanks to the location. Every staff member I encountered was very friendly and helpful. The room (a regular double) was nice, but I've come to expect more from the Marriott brand. My biggest complaint was the high level of noise, despite their claim that the room had soundproof windows. Our room was also missing its hairdryer when we checked in, but the staff took care of that quickly. I would stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: My date and I were looking for somewhere to have dessert.  We happened into Serrano, on a Saturday afternoon.  It was nearly empty, and playing hits from the 40s and 50s.  The music was low enough that conversation could be had, but loud enough that we considered slow dancing to it.  The dessert was something chocolate - although I can't quite remember what.  It was FANTASTIC and we ate every bite.  I'm planning on going back this weekend with a friend of mine from out of town.  What an absolute gem this is.

I have found a new love - the 6-mini-scoop-sampler.  For $5.50, I had Salty Chocolate Almond, Mexican Hot Cholocate, A Chockwork Orange, Bananas Foster, Abita Apple, and Black and Gold Crunch.  

I sampled the Pear and Champaign Sorbet, just amazing.  The 'Chef' brought me back and I had the Fig sorbet right out of the machine - I could just cry.  My oldest found her bliss in the Black and Gold Crunch milkshake.  Our out of town friends were amazed at the creamyness of the sorbets.  We are regulars there and I have a new favorite.

Decent price, good service.  Parking lot is a looooooong way from the desk.  Car I got was decent (a Mazda crossover) but not great.  I'm sure I could have switched, but that would require two more times across that distance.  

Check-in and dropoff was easy.  Their gas deals are actually reasonable.  If I'd known I would use a whole tank, I would have taken their "we fill it" deal of $10 total, gas and service fee.  If you're just driving around town and will use less than half a tank, fill it yourself, but if a whole tank, read the fine print and take the deal.

Quick stop for dinner to go. Sweetie likes them, and you know what, so do I. Good sandwiches, good service. Prices are a little high, but for the quality it is almost worth it..

She got a cheesesteak and fries, and liked it. I tried the chicken teriyaki and some cheese bread. The sandwich was great- tender, tasty chicken, and lots of it, on good bread. The cheese bread was better than expected, just based on cheese bread at pizza joints, etc. Same good bread, and real cheese. The lemonade is pretty good. Service here was friendly and fast (though there is of course a wait while they make the sandwiches.)

BOOOOOO to Rittenhouse Market.

First, shame on me for being too lazy to trek to Trader Joe's and doing serious grocery shopping for a week's worth of dinners here.  Everything costs at least twice as much as at any other grocery store. So, that was MY mistake.

THEIR mistake was leaving out moldy blocks of Cabot cheese to pawn off on unsuspecting customers.  It was really, really frustrating to come home after dropping almost $100 on an astonishingly small amount of groceries, slice open the package, and see mold all over it.  It makes me queasy about the other groceries we picked up there.  This place blows.

This is a great option in Old City. The architecture alone is inviting- combining a historic building with soaring ceilings with an Ultra-contemporary new wing. 3 separate bars, including one on the 2nd floor offer different ambulances depending on your mood, the crowd and time of day. Upstairs bar good for searching sports if dining alone.  I had BBQ chicken thigh sliders which were a bigger (3) portion than I expected off the "small share" menu. Tasty. Everything looked good.  Prices very reasonable. Friendly service. Close to the Marriott Franklin Renaissance Hotel, the Monaco and the touristy stuff. Decent nicely priced wine selection.

After reading the reviews of this place, I was sort of shocked about how bad everyone's experience was. We went there around lunch time and it was packed, there were only a few tables available since the rest were taken, the take out line was at least five or six people out. I liked how when you walk in you have to go down steps (they do have a wheelchair lift for people not able to do steps) but they were reasonably priced too, good combination plates and friendly staff. I would return and recommend them. I have no tried their delivery service yet though.

My parents have visited this place often and they recommended we try them also. This is a very nice little "hole in the wall" Mom and Pop restaurant. I do like they have a salad bar and it was good! Their food was very tasteful also, and we did not have to wait long for it at all even though they were busy. They are out in a small town, so a lot of locals around that visit there. I wanted to get desert but was too full from eating them. Their staff is good at keeping your needs met and your drinks full. I would like to go back and try them again never time I am in town. The place was clean, smelled fresh and clean.

Select from reasonable bottles of Pinot Grigio or San Genovese, the amazing (and free) eggplant, olives and hot peppers with bread, house made chicken escarole soup, house salad with the best blue cheese dressing in the city, followed by any seafood on the menu (do not ignore the nightly specials). Other family favorites: the perfectly cooked steak, scalloped potatoes when offered, steamed clam appetizer (add the perfect garlic bread), panzanella salad when available, and a goblet of tiramisu for dessert.
This place is a treasure.

This subway is not much different than any other subway... except that they do not take American Express. It drives me nuts when I come across a vender, especially a large vendor like subway, that is so cheap that they will not pay the extra 1% to accept AMEX... especially since this is my card of choice, and on this particular day, was the only form of payment I carried into the store.  

It may sound crazy, but I likely will not go back to this Subway location for the sole reason of them not accepting AMEX. 

BOTTOM LINE: Does not accept American Express.

Let me start by saying that the first and only time I have eaten here, it was a much anticipated visit. I am a huge mac and  cheese fan, who isn't? So I figured this would be a no fail, delicious place that would keep me coming back. I am not sure that was the case. Though the mac and cheese was decent, I wouldn't consider it a place to have a meal. After eating the small portion, I felt that heavy, greasy feeling in my stomach. I may go back again, but wouldn't go looking to have a complete meal. Also, not a fan of the small, crammed dining space.

Tasty Place has one good thing: the salt baked chicken wings. Everything else should be avoided. My roommate brought home chicken wings, beef hofan, and salted fish pork and eggplant for dinner. Except for the wings, it was the worst take-out meal we have ever had. The beef hofan was bland and mushy. The pork in the salted fish pork and eggplant was dry and hard to chew. 

It is extremely irritating when you buy something from a restaurant only to realize that you could make it better yourself. How a Chinese restaurant with access to fresh groceries screws up food this basic is amazing to me. My advice would be to eat anywhere else.

Had my first Calzone from Basilico today and will be picking up a pizza to take home tonight.  They just opened yesterday in the old "Vita Bella" location in Oaks.  Brick oven pizza, pasta, Panini, sandwiches, salads.  Service was very friendly and the food was tasty.  

They are still in the process of opening...no take out menus yet, not even a register!  But they are open for business since 3.4.16.  They have made some minor changes to the interior and more to the menu.  I'll have to stop in and sample their chicken parm soon!  

Another good sign...they speak Italian in there too, so stop in and say Ciao!

I unintentionally ran over a nail during one of the recent snowstorms and had to get my tire patched. I dropped by after work without calling ahead, and they had it done within 20 minutes. At these places they usually only have stereotypical manly magazines (fitness, cars, hunting, etc.), but I was glad that they had some People so I could read trashy celebrity gossip while I waited. :)

They were really friendly, quick, and charged me around $35 to fix my tire. I'm not sure how that compares to others in the area because I didn't call around to check prices. A week later, my tire is still good.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Not a brewery and not a bar but some interesting version of a beer store that is like a bar but with much cheaper beer prices than a bar.  Interesting concept that offers an interesting selection of beer and ciders along with some wines and spirits.  They also have the rare to find in NOLA phenomena of an actual parking lot.  This place lets you run a tab and operates pretty similar to a bar except they close at 9 or 10pm depending on the day.  A comfortable spot to try out some new drinks and relax for awhile.

This place has decent Chinese food at reasonable to cheap prices.  The location has been multiple places and was most recently a vegetarian Indian establishment.  You can easily drive past this restaurant and not even notice it.  There has only been one person working the front of house during all my visits and it hasn't ever been crowded during lunch so this has been a quick lunch spot.  It's a pretty bare bones and basic place without a lot of atmosphere but that seems to be reflected in their affordable prices.

This is definitely one of the most neighborhood of all neighborhood bars.  It is just like a suburban house set amongst many other houses.  You won't be getting all rowdy and crazy in here but you can certainly have a calm and collected good time in here.  You definitely need to know where you are going to find this place and I've never seen it crowded.  When people move to Old Metairie and miss their nasty days at Snake'n Jakes they can come here for a clean and hygienic version of a hidden away neighborhood bar.

I've been in this store a handful of times and it has a much better selection than the Breaux Mart I'm much more familiar with on Magazine.  The location is a bit problematic depending on which way on Severn you need to go as the traffic is almost always terrible.  This grocery is very near Whole Foods so if you need items not carried there you can add Breaux Mart to your itinerary and complete your shopping in a more timely manner but items here are often more expensive than at Rouses.  They often have great prices and specials on beer.

The all you can eat deal is probably the way to go here as the rolls are pretty tiny.   I ordered the regular two roll lunch special that came with miso soup and salad and I was still very hungry and had to go to second lunch elsewhere to make a full meal of it.  The sushi wasn't terrible but it didn't get much above pretty mediocre at best.  It really didn't inspire me in any way that would really make me want to return.  A very average and bland kind of strip mall place like you might find in Anytown USA...  Have I mentioned I hate strip malls?

Man I'm not sure what has happened here.  I don't know if it was a bad day or a pizza oven problem or maybe the heat of August, as the margherita pizza has always been good here, but the one I got yesterday was just AWFUL!  The pizza was tough as leather and dry as the Mojave dessert.  I had a friend that had never tried it that I talked into getting it with me and they were very unhappy with the choice.  I really hope it was just an off day but it was like a completely different pizza than I've ever had from Pizza Delicious before as it was plain awful!

They have some really large lunch specials here that give you a lot of food.  The sushi has never seemed like the best quality but it has never been terrible either.  Nothing has ever really excited or inspired me here and it has all seemed pretty basic.  They do have a parking lot that is across the street and it can be a bit of an adventure crossing St. Charles at that spot depending on the time of day.  Overall a decent spot for lunch and a good value.  I live really close to this restaurant but I've only been for lunch so I can't comment on how this place is for dinner.

This is the nearest Chase bank to my house and its also my absolute least favorite Chase I ever visit.  There is invariably a line to use the ATM and frequently there are bums begging for money after you use the ATM.  Often the ATM is out of cash or broken for some other reason.  I do my best to avoid using this Chase branch and regret it nearly every time I do!  I much prefer the TWO Chase locations on Prytania right past Napoleon that have ATM's nearly directly across the street from one another.  This branch is in extremely sore need of more ATM's and they need to run the panhandling bums off!

This is an echo of the long time favorite in this Prytania neighborhood of Kyoto that closed due to the death of the owner.  They have a few of my past favorites from Kyoto like the Chirashi but the execution is not quite up to the same level while the prices here are certainly higher.  Sadly like so many things that were around before Katrina hit that survived and then faded away after the brief revival we had this seems to be a shadow of what used to be.  In the immediate area it is still probably the best sushi in the area but it definitely leaves me longing for what used to be and ain't there no more.

This is the bar of New York Pizza.  I like this place for the fact they offer a $5 pint and a slice special which is a pretty awesome deal.  There isn't a limit on this special and you can just keep eating and drinking as many $5 slice/pints as you want.  They also offer the full menu of New York Pizza usually so you can get some good options here if you don't feel like pizza.  Some nights they stay open late and other nights they just close when they want to close.  The inconsistent hours is the main thing that irks me about this place but generally its a good place to grab a quick slice of pizza and a pint of beer.

I was hoping the goat tacos would compare to the amazeballs delicious ones Johnny Sanchez formerly made but unfortunately these were nowhere close and the goat didn't have much flavor.  This was your basic Guatemalan joint and the tacos and fajitas were ok and decently priced but nothing really jumped out at me as being anything above average.  I was also a bit sad they didn't have a Caldo de Pollo on their soup menu.  So decent authentic food with slower than average service.  It is alright if you are in the area but I wouldn't make another special trip to it.  

WARNING: They also are all about some karaoke in here!!!

This is a glitzy new renovation of a corner grocery store that seems to primarily focus on selling booze, lottery tickets and a few grocery items.  They seem to have built quite a bit of infrastructure to sell prepared food items and to perhaps do po boys but it isn't functional at this point.  It is nearby my house so it is a convenient location to buy lottery tickets for me but I usually find myself going other places.  I hope they get the kitchen up and running to make a decent neighborhood eatery.  Verret's Bar and Lounge is right across the street so this is quite the developing spot at the moment.

Update 7/8/16 the deli is now OPEN!!!

For $15 + tip, you are supposed to get a scalp massage/shampoo, neck/shoulder massage, haircut, and blowdry. 

I got: painful shampooing, and LITERALLY a 30 second sholder massage. Also, my style request was pretty simple: layers all around. After she blow-dried my hair, I noticed she didn't give me layers in the back, so I asked her for layers in the back. Instead of re-wetting my hair, she cut my hair straight up DRY. So yeah, in the end, I got my layers, but it came with split ends from cutting dry hair.

I know i shouldn't expect much for a $15 haircut, but at least WET my hair, please.

I wish I could rate this place better.  I really do, the guys that run the place and the employees have been extremely nice to us when we have gone. The only reason I go back is that my son likes the pizza, if it wasn't for that I would never step foot in the place.  Super thin crust pizza, there is another, but I am not a fan of that either.  Don't get the sausage, unless they changed it since the last time it is basically a salt lick.  Overall unless you actually like Pizza King, this place will probably disappoint.  Worth a shot some people like this style of pizza. But I will have to pass.

Rented a sweet back in December when I came back to town for a visit.  Had an issue with the in room thermometer couldn't keep the room warm at all or it kept it too hot could not get it to a comfortable setting.  The cleaning of some of the areas was less than stellar, the bathroom had cobwebs in the corner.  

The free hot breakfast was nothing to write home about.  Some of the stuff was stale, or hot items were cold.  Etc.  Pool was heavily chlorinated, but I guess that is what you are going to get from a hotel pool.

Overall I would probably try out a few other south side hotels prior to going back to this location.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Americas most convenient bank can get crowded quickly and sometimes they only have one to two tellers. Drive thru can be slow as well but employees r nice and always apologize for the wait.  They are attentive to your needs once you get to them but the line can be frustrating, especially if you are running in on your lunch break or before a quick trip to Target.

The parking lot is kind of small and there is hardly ever a line at the ATM.  Also if you looking to see a customer service rep about your account, it's never really a wait.

Lebel Pizza is in my neighborhood its okay.  I mean the food is hot, delivery is okay, and the food is so so.  I don;t like that they cut their large pizza into squares but it is what it is.  My favorite item on the menu is the Buffalo Wings, I get them often because they are the only spot in the neighborhood that cooks them right.

Customer Service is okay, and their fish hoagies are okay, but nothing to jump up and down about.  If I need a quick meal or need to feed my daughters friends then I order from Lebels. Otherwise I skip by everytime.

The order through Yelp feature is what made me give this place a try. Ordering was VERY convenient and easy. Click your selections,
Pay through the ap and viola your order appears in a reasonless time.

My order was correct there was even a free Lo Mien in there. However the food was not that good. 

The beef skewers were dry and tough, the hot garlic pork had almost no pork, the egg
rolls were decent and the crispy squid was not crispy. 

I'll most likely give them one more chance purely for convenience and to be fair.

Like pretty much all car rental companies at PHL, this one is offsite with a shuttle service. Shuttle was fast enough. 

Enterprise always has very friendly service, but I feel like their check in process is a hassle. You have a person you talk to when you get in line, another one at the check in counter, and then a third person that actually gets you the car. When I rent from National or Hertz, I get an email with a stall number and the car is waiting with the keys in it- much better process. But, this was the cheapest for the car class we wanted and in the end, everything was satisfactory.

Relative to other Marriotts, this one is old and ghetto- they are in the process of remodeling, but the room I had sucked. It was also right next to the service elevator so every time one went by, I got to hear that- not to mention loud chatter in Spanish early in the morning. To top it all off- the construction was supposed to start at 9AM, but instead the hammering woke me up at 7- when I complained they didn't even give me a few points by way of apology. Lastly, the location sucks- there is nothing around but the hotel. I may try them again after they remodel, but first impressions are distinctly negative.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I love that the vacuum is included in a car wash starting as little at $3 but I always up grade to the $7 option. I don't have to worry about quarters. It's nice not to get wet trying to use one of the self service car wash options and then I'm not pressed into running around to beat the clock in the Florida heat ;-) 

Please add another location in Tampa! Specifically North Seminole Heights, I think off Florida or Nebraska...maybe Hillsborough   Somewhere. I'd definitely enjoy something east of 275, please!!!!

Charming Italian restaurant in an old house, not too far from the quaint town of New Hope. We came with a family friend who was very well acquainted with the restaurant staff and is a huge fan of the meatballs. (His only qualm with the meatballs is that they only serve 3 at a time!)

I was impressed with how crowded this restaurant got 2 days before Christmas, a testament to how popular this spot is in town! I ate the Octopus, Cavatelli, Fruit e Mare and a cannoli. My favorite dish was the cannoli. Though my dad wasn't a huge fan of the Fruit e Mare, I thought it did well as left overs with a lot of bread dipped in the rich tomato sauce.

I've been to this bank twice and the service is tremendously slow. You wait in line for far too long and then once you get to a teller, they easily become distracted with their coworkers or anything else beside yourself and your tapping fingers. 
Besides THAT- there is always ample parking, there is usually someone at the exit that tells you to have a good day or thanks you for choosing Chase. Also, be careful when pulling out of the parking lot as to not pull into oncoming traffic-there's a median dividing one lane from the other--OOPS!

It's hard to find good pizza in the burbs. I remember liking Palermo's as a kid, and tried it again pretty recently.  The pizza is good, not great.  But, in the greater lansdale area, it's still better than most that I have tried. They have a mediterranean menu as well.  The hummus is a HUGE portion, but pretty decent, on par with Sabra hummus.  Their falafel was also pretty solid. All pizza shops do the whole sub and grinder deal, but Palermos does it pretty well.  Eggplant parm sub was pretty amazing. At the end of the day, when I visit the area, and people are asking for pizza, I'll probably suggest Palermos.

Amore's Pizza has evolved over the years into a good selection of italian foods.  I rarely find something in this place unpalatable, and I always appreciate the speed of their service.

I bought their "6 Pack" special when I was in which was 2 slices of pizza, 2 bread sticks, and 2 garlic knots.  All of which were superbly made and very flavorful.  Their breadsticks were particularly enjoyable, having just the right about of spices to add that zing.

I also find the staff to be friendly, fast, and helpful.

The $2 off check in offer is also quite nice.

Wolfgang Puck Express is a great lunch or dinner spot. They have quick service, lots of options and good food. When you walk in take a moment to take a menu and it over. You place your order at the front counter, receive your table number and get your own drink- a server brings you the food. Most people like the mac n' cheese. It is good and I wouldn't turn it down. I should have it again before I make any official votes, but I still prefer J. Alexander's. Their Cesar salad is good, as is most of their sandwiches. You will be hard-pressed to not find something to enjoy.

Great customer service, however now that time has passed, I'm seeing issues with the alignment they performed. After getting brand new shocks, struts, and tires installed by my mechanic, I immediately took my car to Blatt to get it aligned.

Over time, my front tires have both developed premature wear on the outer edge. I looked back at the specs and I can see that they gave the front wheels a slight toe-out (note my car is rear wheel drive) versus being even. When bringing it back, they explained that they align to a "acceptable range" versus ideal state.

So, I'm left with new tires that are now wearing prematurely.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
This is a brand new place in Clayton, and i really like it for a casual night out with friends. Reservation are a must the outside patio is great. The acoustics are a bit off so go in knowing it is LOUD when it fills up. The appetizer portions and entree's are ample so you won't leave hungry. It is all locally grown product and the waiters/waitress's while they are a bit slow are very knowledgeable about the food and wine. Im sure their speed will pick up once they have had time to find their groove. The gnocchi was excellent and the braised ravioli is really a must!

NOT A DATE NIGHT DESTINATION... GOOD FOR THE MONEY..

Great food and service. Recommend the veal dishes. The raviolis are also good. The calamari was average. Next time I will go with a different appetizer.  It is BYOB which is a plus. Do not forget to hit the liquor store up. The atmosphere is OK. The tables are too close together, which makes it noisy and congested. The price point was about as expected. Typically I feel like BYOB's menu is about $4 more for an entrée than you would expect, which is the case here. Not a big deal as you know you are showing up with your own bottle. Recommend and we will back.

I have been to my fare share of authentic Mexican restaurants.  Cantina Feliz was good but not authentic, it is an upgrade...more of fusion.

The nachos as a starter were great.  Definitely big enough to have as your whole meal.  I was more excited about my squash enchilladas which were pretty great.  I was even able to add Oaxaca cheese on top.  I made a trip to Oaxaca, Mexico a few years ago and hadn't had Oaxaca cheese since.  It was great.

We had great service as well.  I wouldn't mind going back again.  The price was more expensive then I thought it was going to be.

Saw this place on the way to the shops in Santa Barbara and decided to check it out.

I ordered a coffee for my husband and I ordered a tea Yerba Mate with soy for myself. I was impressed that a cafe would even carry Mate tea and it tasted amazing.

The joint itself is really chill and quiet and has an artsy vibe to it, which gives it that cozy feel to it.

Overall the coffee and tea came to $5.5, which wasn't that bad. I don't know the exact breakdown of what it cost, but I'm assuming it was 1.5 for the coffee and 3.5 for the tea.

I definitely dig it and would stop by again when I'm in the area.

Happy Garden is a pretty good little Chinese food restaurant.

I was surprised to find the Happy Garden in the location it was. It's kind of out of the way and hidden but its rating made me decide to check it out. I went with a couple of friends and we really enjoyed the meal we had there. We received great service from the friendly staff and had quite a few delicious dishes.

One tip about this restaurant if you live in the area, if you order take out exceeding $40 (before taxes) then you will receive 10% off your order.

If you live in this area, check this place out.

I was really not impressed. The food and service were just ok. I ordered an appetizer of Chicken Chunks that were described as fried chicken chunks dipped in hot sauce. They were pretty much just breaded frozen chicken chunks with sauce dribbled on top. My side dinner salad was $4.99 and was just iceberg lettuce with purple onions and pimentos and cheese and a pretty small size for $4.99. With as many choices available in our area that have excellent food I will certainly not give this place a second thought.

Great food! I was very satisfied. I got a really nice steakburger, and a salad with an EXCELLENT homemade black cherry dressing. 
But I'm a little confused. The ambiance is nice and classy, low lighting, lots of wood, but the waiters are all wearing shorts and baseball caps. It's weird. I get that it's a bleed over from the neighborhood sportsbar thing, but it just sends mixed messages  about the dining room.
So all in all, a decent place to stop in, but not somewhere I'll be a regular. Unless you are looking for a nice bar to frequent, then its probably great.

By far my favorite (American) Chinese restaurant in St. Louis. It is a tiny little place that you can pick up from or they deliver if you live within 2 miles. Lucky me I live within 2 miles.

A family run business with excellent food. Can't say that it is gourmet  just your regular options. But often in Chinese food you get gross parts from who knows where from the chicken, but here you get large pieces of white breast meat. They offer a great lunch special for $4.20 before 3 PM.

Basically their food is fresh, stemming hot and cheap!

Kobe has always been our go-to place for sushi on the west end. It has always been awesome. Today we got a takeout order with our usual favourites (scallop roll, rainbow roll, hawaiian roll, dynamite roll, alaskan maki, spicy tuna maki) and unfortunately the fish was really subpar. I've never had to worry about freshness with Kobe, but our order today was disappointing. The scallop in particular tasted a little off. The salmon and tuna weren't fresh at all. Hope this was just a blip and not an indication of where things are headed.

Extremely accomodating and not at all what I was expecting.  The front desk clerk was AWESOME. He really went out of his way to ensure that everything was the way that I wanted, and or needed it. Traveling for business purposes is never easy but the Comfort Inn made it smooth. 

I thought staying at a casino would be better hahahaha yeah right. If I ever have to travel in this area again I will definitely consider this location an option. They even have a food delivery service that covers Chilis, BJ's, Claim Jumpers, and some asian joint. A pool would have given this 5 stars. But for now its a 4 1/2.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I love their selection of glasses, and the doctors are the best. I've come here for three eye exams and two pairs of glasses, and they've always done a very thorough eye exam and made sure you're comfortable with your prescription. I haven't had much luck with the staff, however. They've somehow messed up one of my orders, so it came in over two weeks late; they say they've left voice messages when I didn't receive any; and they've just not been very friendly through in-house service and over the phone. The doctors are great. In terms of customer service, I've definitely experienced better.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
Yogen Fruz has some really good frozen yogurt. Sometimes I feel it isn't up  to par but other times it is just amazing. I hate the lack of consistency I find here. 

Yogen Fruz is like a milk shake turned into ice cream. That is the best way I can describe it and it might be a little hard to understand unless you have tried it. They let you choose the fruits you want and the yogurt you want and then they put it in some machine that turns it into frozen yogurt. 

The outcome can be delicious or disappointing.

Mikado is WAY overpriced and there's nothing special on the menu that pulls me in. Actually, I shouldn't say nothing because I do enjoy the dragon eyes.. but I would never go to Mikado just to get them.

I don't know how fresh everything was because all of my rolls were tasteless. The decor is really nice. Probably the nicest of any Japanese one in the city, but who wants to pay for that? The service is so slow. They took forever to bring out our food and the portions were weak.

I don't think I would come here again.

I think this is a great place. They have an awesome selection of frames and in many colors. It is sometimes hard to find something perfect for yourself right off the bat but they have so many to pick from that you will definitely find something if you look carefully. 

The place is always busy so it is hard to get help sometimes but when you do the staff is really nice. They go out of their way to the extra mile for you. The prices are decent and you can sometimes bargain them down. Especially if you have been coming here for years.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
I am not a fan of country music but I find that the odd time I visit a country bar I end up having a good time. 

For the most part the crowd is made up of country music lovers. I noticed that there were people from many different age groups and they all seemed to be enjoying themselves. There was no attitude being kicked around here. The entire place is friendly and a nice change of scenery if you don't normally frequent country clubs. 

It gets extremely busy on weekends so you might want to get there early or you will be stuck in line for a bit.

it's nice to see Sherwood Parks night life slowly growing. This Overtime location offers much of the same stuff the other ones offer which is decent food and good beer. I personally think the one on the south side is slowly losing its appeal and not many people go there anymore but this location is quite popular.

At night it gets pretty packed with locals looking to enjoy themselves. They play good music and the service is good. Whether you come for food or stay for a drink the servers take good care of you and are really sociable.

It makes for a good night.

I didn't have the greatest experience at this Kyoto. I am a big fan of the one downtown and the one just off Whyte Ave so I was expecting much of the same from this location but I was disappointed. 

The service was decent but not as friendly as the other spots, but that's not what turned me off. The sushi here wasn't very good. It's possible they just had an off day but I'm not willing to risk going back. The sushi did not taste good, and the rolls were falling apart and lacked the proper taste as well. 

I would not recommend this Kyoto. The other 2 are amazing.

Sorrentino's is  way nicer then I thought it would be. It  is really fancy inside and very classy. The service is really good (they check your coats at the front). The coat check is something I have never seen before in a restaurant.

The food is delicious. I would recommend the Spaghetti all'Amatriciana, with spicy tomato sauce, pancetta and pecorino cheese. It was amazing and the portions here are very generous. 

I went into Sorrentinos without any expectations because I had never really heard much about it. It really surprised me though. I had an awesome experience here.

This hotel is located right on Whyte Ave and is pretty urban/classy.

The good thing about this hotel is that it is really quiet, considering that it's right in the middle of the Whyte Ave club scene this is pretty impressive. A lot of people like to get hotel rooms for their birthdays and throw parties and this hotel is perfect for that. You can pre-party here and then walk to the clubs and then head back for an after party. I think when they built this place they took into consideration that people might be doing this because I haven't heard of anyone getting complaints here when they are being really loud.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: After driving past for years, something about the "Party Liquors" name compels a visit.   It appears to be a former ABC/Jax chain and is about the size of surviving outlets of the declining chain.   Selection is about standard with a few hard-to-find specialties (e.g guava rum) , and a larger than usual supply of pocket-sized bottles/flasks.  Prices are about like other chains, other than Total Wine bargains.   The interior is clean and orderly despite being in a sorta rough neighborhood and lots of customers on foot.

A throw-back to the '50's-----an old-fashioned ice cream stand.  It offers soft-serve in 3 flavors, about 20 hard scoop flavor options, shakes and banana splits.   No burgers, fries, dogs or other non-frozen dairy. Unlike the '50s' the prices have kept up with the times.....2 small cones are about $5, and rising from that. The quality of the ice cream is ok...nothing special.

It is nice to see the mix of customers on a hot afternoon.....young & old, all races, vehicles ranging from Mercedes to rickety bike.   But not a melting pot if you lick fast enough.

A fine neighborhood bar....and not at all a dive.   Serves beer, wine, liquor with
 lots of specials, shooters and bombs.  BTW having a jagermeister chiller machine disqualifies a bar from dive status.   Also a fairly extensive menu, also with lots of specials and free hot app buffet on Fridays.  Strangely the bar allows smoking even with food....so they must sell oceans of booze.

Big emphasis on entertainment, including karaoke and pool table.   Did not sample the food but drinks were good, reasonably priced and served well. Made our escfape well before karaoke cranked up.

OK let me preface this with, I rarely write reviews but I just had to for this place. The food is absolutely amazing. I'm serious. Stop what you're doing and go here right now. It is quite possibly some of the greatest breakfast food I've ever had in my life and I've traveled the world. The service is also top notch. I had the best waitress I've ever had, I don't remember her name but she's from Colorado and I think there's a picture of her in the Yelp photos. I would request her if there's any way at all to do that. Either way this place is on the top of my list of great places to eat in the Bay area.

Great market. It's divided into two parts: organic/natural on the right & traditional/regular on the left.
The butcher kindly gave me whole fresh chickens rather than frozen Perdue ones for the same price which was really nice of him.
There is a very decent selection of cheeses from around the world.
The store is immaculate, organized & the staff is very happy to offer direction/help.
I prefer the natural side- excellent selection of just about anything you could want/need.
They also offer premade food to go as well.

The good parts of Gibson cafe would be it's location in Terminal C close to a bevy of gates, the decent onion rings, full bar, and friendly staff. The not so hot part (if you have read other reviews) is the burger. Lacking flavor compounded by the leathery piece of lettuce make ths a rather unpleasant mouth experiance. The presentation was nice but unfortunately didn't make up for the very meh burger. 

I'll try Gibson Cafe again next time I roll through, but will propbably give the nachos or the buffalo chicken sandwich a try (hold the lettuce).

Positive : super nice and courteous staff

Neg: about as smooth running as the Cleveland Browns. They are super nice but the staff has too many green members that need SR managers help on every thing. Everything took forever and even when I got there they didn't have my vehicle as they oversold it seems. 

Also I saw another customer who had to come back in bc the gas tank wasn't full and tag was expired. 

Nice is fine and all but give yourself an extra 30 minutes if picking up from here. Nice is good but will only pay for the bills for so long

Great italian food from a place I didn't even know existed.  Even with reservations, it took a while to get seated. The service was slow, but it doesn't help that I went on one  of the last days my Groupon expired!  

The staff seemed frantic and often times frustrated. However, I will not let this affect my rating because there were many patrons trying to use of their Groupons right before they expired. 

The Pollo Grigliato was amazing! I am usually not a fan of non-pasta dishes, but I would definitely order this again.  The portions were huge and being a BYO put the icing on the cake.

Every time i go here, something else is wrong.  First i show up at 11:02, and sure enough, they stop serving breakfast at 11.  No room to budge.  I might as well have been at McDonalds.
I figure i'll give them another chance, and go for breakfast at 10:00am, and they get everybody's cheese and meats mixed up.  oh, and there seems to be a hair in one of the omelette's too.

The last straw was, well, do you have netflix?  then watch BIll Burr: Let it go.  12 minutes in.  i wasn't even going to leave a negative review, because who has time for negativity, but bill did it so well, i had to share.

worst food I've ever had. There were numerous problems with this restaurant but the food had the be the most nauseating. I had an eggs benedict that tasted like it was taken out of a frozen food box and stuck in microwave. Their quiche tasted like it had already been chewed and was cold. Every breakfast item had a side of "potatoes" that could only be described as last nights leftover mashed potatoes thrown into a steam tray and had cheap american cheese sprinkled on them. Do not go here! You'd get a better meal from mcd's.

Coffee was overrated and not very impressive. Barista added whipped cream even though I didn't ask for it. This location is very small and felt claustrophobic at times. I also do not like their selection of music for purchase. Nothing wrong with the selection itself, but why would I go to Starbucks to buy a cd?

The pastry offered was a bit dry as well. The panini bread was dry and they seemed to skimp on the meat. Again, I'm at Starbucks to drink their coffee, not get a sandwich. If I wanted a Sandwich, I would go over to Safeway or Quiznos nearby.

This location has a drive-thru window and wireless internet available if you choose to use it.

Can I blame them for me ordering the wrong thing? Well I'll compromise and blame them for having a lunch bento box that didn't have any type of roll and for my stupidity of ordering that one.

There was nothing to rave about or cry about. I guess we did get a seat right away even though it was 12:30 noon on a Friday in South Common. Otherwise, 3 stars pretty much sums it up. I usually judge a sushi restaurant by the sashimi but since I didn't have that, much less a roll, it would be unfair to rate Mikado higher or lower based on some meat on rice and tempura. 

Remind me never to order a bento box again.

This was a very pleasant surprise.  I ate here while on the road for business, and had just experienced a streak of nasty, unhealthy, chain restaurant road eating.  Maybe that contributed to 5 starts.  Nevertheless, i ordered the Mango Summer roll, yellowtail w/ scallion, and tempura roll.  The latter of the three were fresh and the Tempura fried perfect.  The Mango Summer was quite the dish-- with this sauce that i can't quite describe, other than it complimented the roll perfectly.  

I ordered take out, so not sure on the service.  5 stars for the food-- definitely worth checking out.

OK, the Impossible Whopper is amazing! I've always loved that BK had a veggie burger (Morning Star Farms I think) and it was not terrible but didn't have much flavor. The Impossible Whooper is truly delicious and pretty under cover as plant based. 
The other and very noteworthy reason for this review is the customer service that is absolutely top notch. As a fellow review already noted there is plenty of fast food that comes with a side of attitude or just plain hostility in the area, so the A+ customer service was a wonderful surprise.  I mean, I got a genuine have a nice day on my way through the drive though!

I learned about the Italian Bistro from Groupon who was offering $40 worth of dinner for $20. Because I was going to see a show at the Kimmel Center, this place seemed like a convenient place to get dinner. Making reservations was really easy with Open Table although this restaurant does not offer any Open Table points. The food was really good, we had the warm crab cheesecake for an appetiser, our salads were tasty and I got the gnocchi with the Gorgonzola cream sauce. Soooo yummy and quite filling so there were plenty of left overs.

I love when a pizza place is open late, after midnight late because it proves I'm still in civilization.  Great to get a slice after leaving the bar/club/random night activities.  

Totally awesome gay pizza ( the place is nicknamed "the Homo Hut" ) that is creative in some of its special pizzas.  I stuck with white with broccoli and chicken but my friends got the mac and cheese pizza and I also saw some type of slice that had nachos on it.  The place gets crowded and has a doorman telling people when they can come in and asking people to leave after they get their slices.  This place is a fun way to end your night.

How all establishments begin. Nice. Clean. Organized. Orderly. All of the machines work. But give it time. Unfortunately, things don't stay nice in this area forever. But until then I'm jumping ship from the old laundromat I used to use (as of yesterday!). 

Everything in this place is clean and kept clean! Although, the machines here are a bit pricey I will pay for the added luxury of having them work properly. 

One suggestion however....they need to add more seating and folding tables. This place gets overcrowded easily and the parking is somewhat limited.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
I've only eaten here once, for brunch, so I base my opinion off a one time deal.  And a one time deal it shall stay.

Our service, for not a tremendously busy morning in such a charming atmosphere, was lacking in efficiency and friendliness.  I very much enjoyed the look and feel of the interior, aside from the aloof staff meandering about.  My meal, which consisted of an omelet, some home fries and toast, was much too elaborate for its own good.  Not to mention a bit overpriced for its mediocre quality.  I wasn't totally unsatisfied, but it left much to be desired, given its location, price and popularity.

I live a couple blocks from here, and it is great that I can get a decent healthy meal, at a decent price, so conveniently. Some interesting rolls, weird in their execution (too big), but quality as good as can be expected for So ILL. 

Probably should of made it only 3 stars, but they don't get all Sushi Nazi on me when I ask for sriracha and I can walk there. 

* Note - Global brew is upstairs and they really should leverage that. From what I heard, they won't deliver upstairs. Missing out on a natural opportunity. Very myopic and greedy - tripping over pennies and missing the dollars. Too bad too, because we get pizza delivered instead.

Not really great. Maybe Green Garden was so bad that in comparison Evergreen was looking worthy of a lot of praise (??) / I don't know what I was thinking last time I reviewed Evergreen so I wanted to update.
I used to like to order the mixed vegetables combo platter, but most times I ordered it, the mixed vegetables smelled kind of funky (rotten funky) and that kind of freaked me out so I haven't ordered from here in a long time. It smells so good whenever I walk on that block that I am occasionally tempted to stop in, but then I remember the rotten vegetables and keep walking.

This is my go to place for late dinners. They're open till 2 am. 3 am on Fridays and Saturdays. Small little place but the food is good and made fast. The guy run in the place can be rude sometimes but that's mostly because of the language barrier and super rude racist drunk kids that come in there and abuse him on his face and smoke pot in there. I would be grumpy if that were my place too. But the guy himself fails to understand English at times and occasionally messes up the order. Over all a good place to get late night Chinese take out and one of the very few food places open this late in west philly.

Pretty big humidor with a lot of good deals on cigars!  Olivia G series on sale for just over $4 a stick?  You can buy 25 of those cheaper than buying the whole box from Tampa Humidor on Busch.

The new store is fantastically clean and well-organized.  Not super tall aisles that you cannot see over, so the sections of the store (Beer, wine, chilled wine, liquor, etc.) are all very visible.  Plus, up in the front, they have a really good selection of cheeses and meats.

Ask about their ABC card point system.  Make sure you keep your receipt.

I don't think I've ever seen such a well-stocked DD before.  Walking up, my cousin said, "Boston Cream," and I replied back by stating a DD in a gas station is sure to be sold out of Boston Creams at 2 in the afternoon.  Everyone knows they're the first to go, but not at this DD.  Not only were they in stock, but in freaking BULK bro!  And yes, they were fresh.  In fact, everything was fresh.  I've been to a lot of DD in my day, and I've never seen anything like it.  Ordered up a medium iced coffee, a Boston Cream and hit the road.  They should all be like this.

Man, this place gets some rough reviews.  I don't get it.  It's an older style place, but with nice upgrades and a kick-ass bar & grille on site.

The rooms are spacious, the beds are comfy--more so than the Grand  Plaza down the street and for significantly less dinero.  I saw a pic of a bed bug in one of the reviews.  I checked our room thoroughly, and saw none, so thank goodness for that.

I really like the slight angle in which each wing sits.  It allows for a sunset view for all interior rooms with a balcony.

I enjoyed our short stay, and would gladly return.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This ABC kinda blows.  They do have a decent cigar selection, but the staff is a bit unknowledgeable and the liqueur selection is weak.

Two staff members had no idea what Galliano or Salerno was.  They had to look in their fancy computer.  Come to find out, no ABC carries these two. Also, of all the bitters in the world, they only carry one.  A good one, but still only one?  Hey ABC, in case you didn't notice, cocktails made a resurgence about 5 years ago.  Just sayin'.  What a joke.

We left and went down the street to Whiskey Willy's and they had everything we were looking for, plus more!

We all know Subaway is what it is; cheap products for cheap prices.  All their meats taste the same and their bread contains the same material that is used to make elastic.  Be that as it may, if you want a cheap sandwich with fresh veggies, then Subway is the place to be, and as far as Subways go, this one is fine by me.  It's a stand-alone store, clean, orderly and the staff is adequate.  My go-to sammich here is a custom one that I like to call the "turkey, bacon, Swiss."  No matter which location I order this from, it's always the same and satisfies my sammich craving.

They have a drive-thru here, but I've never been THRU it.

Went here with the ladies for Center City Sips Happy Hour event. Being a mild summer evening the roof top deck was packed and we were not allowed up. The restaurant has their own happy hour menu downstairs, so we decided to stay. We weren't too crazy about the Lady Belladonna; be sure that you like cardamon first, but the sangria was pretty good.
The sweet & spicy wings are more on the sweet side and very messy. The pork belly sliders were delicious, but I am a sucker for pork belly.
The staff was cold, but warmed up quickly. 
I am not sure that I would rush back for dinner, but its a nice HH spot if your around 13th st.

i love the old school charming hospitality of the maitre'd and servers here.  the food is good depending on what you get, and a standout is the fried artichoke 'rose of sicily' with prosciutto, basil, garlic, olive oil - yum!  my only complaint is that they're a little too quick to take dishes and glasses away before you're done.  if you pause for moment, your plate with disappear!  slow down or at least ask me if i'm done if there's still food on the plate or liquid in my cocktail.  the dining space is small and dimly lit so it's better suited for a date or close conversations than for a group.

I used to love Dunkin Donuts, but it's gotten expensive.

While their coffee is still amazing, they're turning into Starbucks (i.e. "Fivebucks") ... no, more like SIX-BUCKS! A small coffee and sandwich is their "combo meal" -- and it comes out to $6+ dollars? Are you kidding me? And I don't think the combo deal saves you any money as it is.

I don't know, man. Dunkin Donuts just isn't the same. I'd give it a 2, but the coffee is so wonderful and heavenly, so I'll keep it at a 3. Mmmm. There's nothing like a blueberry-scented coffee! :)

Lastly, they do offer free wi-fi. That's a plus.

Like most people have said, the fresh homemade tortillas for the win! I naturally went for the huevos rancheros since they are known for them. They to me were just alright. They were a bit to drenched in the ranchero sauce. It had good flavor and mild to moderate heat, but just overpowered the egg and the tortilla. The menudo here is good. But apart from the tortillas, the thing that has me coming back is the view. They do have a great view looking over the city. 

I think it is worth a shot if you are in the area!

Finally! I found my car wash! I don't know why not having a great place to wash my car was so distressing, but this place is taking all that away! I got my foot in the door by using their free coupon. When I drove up and looked at their services, I realized they were the reasonable prices that I had been seeking. Sometimes you will get service that is hit and miss with some of the younger employees not knowing some answers to questions. But the other times the service is perfect! They have free vacuums and I will be a loyal customer!

Well who knew that a girl who doesn't care much for sushi would start finding some sushi that she likes!? They start you off with some yummy miso soup and they appear to have fresh and quality ingredients. I enjoyed bites of Nigiri and Rainbow Roll.

As most people mention, it is a small place, so maybe go here a little earlier and get a seat while you can. This is not a place you come for an amazing experience, but the food makes up for it. The service was pretty decent for as busy as they were. The price was good for what you got.

Guess this place will have a soft spot in my heart for introducing me to sushi I actually like!

I wanted to like this place, as we were staying at the hotel. However, I just can't.

1) Food, except for the fries, were pretty tasteless and always served in styrofoam container. 

2) The service was just awful--they had one person working the bar and a fairly crowded area of tables. She walked right be me for at least 10-15 minutes before pouring me a drink.

3) Drinks seemed over priced, even for Saint Petes--the "special" was 4.75 cans of bud light.

Not the worst, but with so much competition, there are other great places to go within 300 feet of here.

I don't know why, but the bartenders always seem to be busy with anything other than waiting on the bar patrons.  They are either washing glasses, servicing the wait staff, re-stocking the wine and beer stash.  Anytime you have to wave your arms like you are trying to flag down an emergency vehicle in order to get attention, you would feel the service could be improved upon.  

BTW, the cavatelli in the duck ragu was nice, a tad bit salty, a tad bit small portion for the price, but faIrly tasty in it's own right.

I had no problems with this place like the other reviewers, and this is my first time.  A bit pricey, but car was clean and dried with no streaking, wheels were not bad, inside was vacuumed half-ass'd-ly but there was a strange smell inside when I drove away, maybe it was smelly, bad window cleaner...I am hoping, and not some bad cologne lingering from one of the many workers who seemed to be working their butts off.

Overall, I'll return.  Not as cheap as Fort Washington, but a little more thorough, and of course nothing tops a good car wash in the State of FL.  ;-)

OMG, have you tried their Red Velvet ice cream? Seriously? Red Velvet is my favorite cake flavor, and now they've made it in ice cream form. It's So good. I mixed it with white chocolate chips and whipped cream. YUM. 

I used to just get their Better Batter, Cinnamoo or Southern Peaches, all fine flavors, but I doubt I'll be going back to them. 

I usually only go to this location if I want to get some ice cream and get out. I don't usually wander around. It's in the middle of all the Green Hills Mall craziness, but a good way to deal with a sweet tooth.

I've been coming here since I first moved to Nashville. I've never actually gone there for anything other than their lunch buffet. I can't remember how much it is off hand, but I'm pretty sure it's under or right around $10 a person, without a drink. They have a decent sized salad bar, followed by a pasta bar of the usual suspects and then a rotating door of varies pizzas as well as garlic bread. There pizza isn't my absolute favorite but it is good. My real weakness is their garlic bread, its greasy and buttery and delicious! I definitely recommend it to any and everybody!

This is usually my go to Mexican for lunch since it's really close to Music Row and really cheap. Their queso is my favorite in town (white cheese, very creamy). The guac is okay but not my favorite (usually too heavy on the lime). It's always packed at lunch and people swear by their margaritas. Parking is hell. I love that I can get chicken fajitas with all the fixing though for 6.99. Service is usually good, but it can get pretty slow when their slammed. The only real problem I have is that during lunch the cashier line can get pretty backed up, so make sure you have enough time to make it back to work on time.

Good place to stop in for tacos.  Tacos are small, but tasty.  Chips are fried tortillas which I liked because 1. they're good 2. I don't eat an entire bag of chips before the meal arrives.  I don't have self-control when chips are around. 

Their soups are usually really good. Staff is generally friendly, but you can tell many waiters are inexperienced by their delivery.  

Outdoor seating is comfortable. 

Drinks were great. Margaritas are made fresh and properly.  I recommend getting a margarita with a little jalapeno.

This one is going to be a short and sweet review. This is my go to place when cooking something and need a good wine pairing. I walk in and go straight to the counter and BAM! They will not only ask what the main course is but the sides too. Then the price point I'm looking for. Never been let down with their recommendations. Of course I can never drink just one so I seem to always get another bottle of something. Lush???

They have a nice liquor section for the mixologist in the house. My only wish is that they had a larger High Gravity beer selection. Parking is a pain unless you are driving a Prius too.

Who knew Philadelphia would have such fantastic restaurants?!?!  

I am usually a patron of NYC restaurants, but I randomly strolled by this place with my lovely lady and had a glance at the menu.  Originally the plan was to get some dessert and coffee, but then the aromatics of the food just created what I refer to as 'the hunger force.'  We ended up sharing an appetizer and ordering the ravioli.  We did eventually end up having dessert which was lovely.  I would recommend this place for any random Sunday night.  I have realized that Market street doesn't look like the zoo on Sunday nights, so sitting outdoors is a fantastic option.

Cheers!

Good for a quick, easy meal or drinks after work. 
The menu definitely lends itself to lunch with lots of sandwiches and salads. Prices are really reasonable.  Service was friendly and quick.  Seating is cozy and comfy too, love that!  I hate uncomfortable chairs or restaurants that are freezing.  

It gets three stars not because the food is spectacular (had the Cobb Chicken Wrap, pretty standard), but because it was tasty and good for what it was.  It's not Bern's.  But it's also not $150 for a meal for two.

If you have been to one Honky Tonk bar you have truly seen them all, but hey we all like to be adventurous and try something new.

The band was pretty good; of course you know they work for tips and the moment you walk in the door and haven't heard a full song; they will come up to you and want to know if you want to tip the band.  Here is my tip; wait till I have heard a full song before you ask!

Bartender was efficient and had a decent pour; drink prices are average.  It was a little smokey; they had the doors open so that helped.

Not a big dance floor but hey when it's closing time you can dance where you want!

Great beer list, probably one of the best in the cherry hill area, and good attentive bar staff too.   But the menu needs a little more; not only does it seem limited, it also seems a little bland.    I understand the concept (farm to fork), after my second time eating here I'm just not that impressed; I had the burger which was like any bar burger and even a little dry and the fish and chips, which were mediocre in flavor and a tad too greasy.   Please F&F, keep the great local food concept, but a little more menu creativity is needed.

Very good sushi and like the other Megu location in Cherry Hill, there are several unique and tasty rolls and other sushi recipes worth trying.  Sunday and Monday nights offer a 30% discount off on most Sushi - be sure to ask for that.  
The new Megu features a posh, modern interior that is very clean and tastefully styled, however the Muzak elevator soundtrack does clash with the new mod look.
Service is decent and attentive but lacks experience and sometimes there may be a language barrier in communication.    We will try it again soon and update.

I'm from Pennsylvania, so in general, New Jersey liquor stores seem pretty super to me.  This Joe Canal's was no exception.  This particular store was very well lit with a decent balance of wine, liquor, and beer.  They have a lot of craft beers and when we were there, they had an area that focused on seasonal autumn beers.  In addition to a large selection of six packs and case at room temperature, they have a whole wall of refrigerated beer. 

The check out area was well attended and our cashier was very friendly.  Overall, just a quick stop in, but a great experience.

As far as car washes go, this place is on par with the majority.  They aren't going to rock your socks off with service or quality, but if you need to get your car clean, they'll get the job done.  The staff is nice and generally efficient.  They do a good job with wiping down the surfaces in the car so they're nice and shiny.  

I'm pretty particular, so I notice the little things -- they do not.  I've found that the cup holders sometimes still have crumbs and have found some particularly baked on bugs haven't been removed from the grill or windshield.  It's not a make or break for me, but I go with tempered expectations.

I am totally in love with this bar. From the handsome bouncer that greets you at the bottom of the stairs to check IDs to the friendly mixologists and awesome basement atmosphere, this place is a happy, intimate, low-light escape. The cocktails and liquor are seriously wonderful. They average about $10/each, and are best sipped from the beautiful stemware they are served in. This is a classy place, and although the price-point is a little higher (IMO) than the upstairs Reilly, it is definitely worth it to start your night here and head upstairs for a meal (and then to the patio for some cornhole and a beer).

YUMMY!!!!  I have just started to tap into the food scene in Philly and boy was I delighted to start here. The food was not only fresh/local, but the taste was amazing. My fiance and I went for restaurant week and I can't wait to try it on a regular night.  We started the dinner with pan seared scallops that was perfectly cooked and had the homemade gnoochi with fava beans and panchetta.  Seriously, the gnoochi melted in my mouth it was so tender and soft. 

I would highly recommend trying this restaurant out if you want a delicious meal in a young vibe restaurant.

They have vegan mac and cheese. 

I've definitely had better vegan mac and cheese, but not in St. Louis. So they get points for at least offering it - even if it's not the best on the planet. 

They have several options for different kinds of mac and cheese that include meat and other animal cheeses. And they all have little stickers that say "try it vegan." But when I asked if they have vegan chicken substitutes, they said no. They just use Daiya cheese and leave the other goat-style cheese or chicken off. oh well.

Conveniently placed McDonald's close to the highway and largely sized in & outside.  We used the drive-thru and were served in ample time and our breakfast.sandwiches and iced coffees were nicely prepared.  Only problem we found was that we had asked for ketchup and didn't find any in our take-out bags, so we had to drive around and walk in to get some...no packets available at the condiment/utensil area, had to wait behind ordering customers for an available employee to reach below the counter and hand me some.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: We enjoyed some appetizers outside at Britt's for a small in between lunch & dinner snack on a beautiful day after laying out on Clearwater Beach.  We ordered falafel & hummus, chips & salsa, creamy & warm spinach artichoke dip, crispy cajun calamari and popcorn chicken tenders, I think they were called?  Everything was delicious and we finished all of it while enjoying the shade under their umbrellas.  Prices were right on and scenery was fun, even the skateboarders holding up crude/inappropriate signs for all passerby to see.

Sushi on the Rocks sits in a really nice intimate space on the bar stretch downtown. It is actually a bar itself, and their martinis are off the chain strong. The volcano roll, dynamite roll, and negiri are among my favorites. Anything that comes to your table on fire is a win with me.

It would be 4 stars BUT: If you go during happy hour, make sure you order before the time ticks past. We sat down and waited ten minutes for friends, and after we ordered we were told we couldn't get the specials even though we were seated before the hour ended because "the computer changes and I can't ring it up like that anymore". That was crappy. Seriously?

We had been to Pizzacato at least 6 times in a 1 year span. We haven't been back in ages because they took their amazing meatballs off their menu. 

I'm writing now because every time we pass it we can't believe what disarray they've allowed their facade to turn into. Their windows are yellowing and cloudy, their branded over hangs are looking dull and worn out. These are not the signs of a restaurant that wants to attract customers. 

I would come back in a minute if it started looking as good as their food tastes!

Get a facelift.

This is a lovely restaurant . . . pleasant country inn ambiance, excellent food, and a very cheerful,  efficient staff.  

The dinner was paced beautifully, allowing us to fully savor each course without fear of something else approaching; also, our experience was heightened  by a couple of "surprises" from the chef . . . first an interesting, tiny antipasto, and later an "intermezzo" of citrus sherbet.

The only problem I encountered, if you can call it that, was that the entree was such a generous portion that I had to take half of it home.

I can heartily recommend this place to anyone who seeks fine dining.

less than average, chinese-american food.  ordered the veggie lo mein which barely had any vegetables...maybe 3 pieces of broccoli and 2 baby corn pieces.  a mess of a dish.  mu shu pork was forgettable...pancakes were dry causing them the break when you tried to fold them and the pork meat was extremely dry and hard.  the fried rice is a pathetic example of what fried rice should be.  the one shining light of the entire experience was the hot sour soup.  very hot and sour..perfect for a cold/rainy day.  

Is there any decent chinese food in Nashville?!

I brought my car in for a break inspection after noticing my breaks were making some noise when being used.  Bobby was helpful and said he would inspect them and call me back after the inspection.  I received a call in about an hr and he informed me that my brakes were getting close to needing a change but for the time being they were fine.  When do you ever get a call from a garage and they are not trying to sell you something??  

I'll need new brakes in a few months and I will definitely go to Ultimate to get the job done.

pluses:  doughnuts in lobby, rides back to work/home.

first come first serve - they open at 7am.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Upon first glance, the atmosphere seemed nice.  Then we were seated at the worst table in the house.  While it was far from packed, they wedged us into a tiny table with uncomfortable lawn chairs (no we were not outside) in between a mantel and another table with an arguing couple.  The food was good for the most part, however the service was not up to par.  The server was slow and inattentive.  When we wanted to leave, we actually ended up wasting an extra 15 minutes staring at our empty glasses because he was nowhere to be found.  We finally found someone else to bring us our check.  Not overly impressed and will likely not return.

This location has a problem with serving customers at the drive thru. I ordered the 2/$5 whoppers and when I got to the pick up window, he tried to give me a drink. I said I didn't have a drink. He leaned out and sneered at me and said "Are you sure, *honey*?" It was dripping with sarcasm. I picked up my receipt and said, "Yes, 2 whoppers, no onion or tomato." He slammed the window in my face, then returned and threw my bag at me. There was no reason for the attitude and people need to vote with their money by going elsewhere. There are plenty of places along Manchester Road to get food. This is not one of them.

I have to give this place three stars but only because I've won two free happy hours and I've attended three. I've never had a problem getting my drinks (we try to pace ourselves so we get 2-3 within the hour) and any place that provides me with free booze is "A-OK" in my book.

That being said, the atmosphere leaves something to be desired and the people who frequent Public House seem to really like to crowd the through-ways so it's difficult to walk across the room (let alone get to the bar). I wouldn't go out of my way to go to Public House, but it's not a bad place to enjoy a couple of (free) drinks with my friends every now and again.

Another good happy hour spot! Not too sure about how dinner here is but you're hungry after work for a solid meal and a brew I highly recommend this place.
