They offer really big salads (get the cobb salad) for 5 bucks and 4 dollar drinks. The salad is what keeps me coming back because you really don't need to eat much more for the rest of the night. The salad is very generous with a lot of chicken thats pretty tasty. You can come here for happy hour and feel like you don't really need to spend the next day burning those excess calories off at the gym.

WOW! Looks like alot of people hate this place. Well, as of yet, I have no complaints. Sometimes they'll have these buy 3 get one free deals on tires and if you ask me, that's the way to go. The mechanics all seemed pretty cool and fairly well-groomed and the waiting room was tucked away in the corner out of view of the counter guy so the next time my cable gets shut off I think that I could get away with lounging over here and watching a Robocop marathon or something. Hell, I could be in there for hours if it's a slow day.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Jacqui was wonderful and took the time to listen to what I wanted. She gave me a great cut at an affordable price. We talked about doing something crazy to my hair, but I said I get nervous to try something new on my first time at a salon. But after getting to know her and seeing that she was already doing a great job, I took the leap and went for bangs, which came out great. Overall, I loved my haircut and it still looks good weeks later. I'll definitely be going back. (Unlike Beehive, where they charged me for having long hair and took 1.5 hours to cut and blow-dry.)

Excellent beer and wine selection.  Nowhere as good As Rouses in Algiers but best in Marrero.

Has same fat , soft French bread as the sister store further down Barataria.  Labories.

There is a feature that makes this a little different, they sometimes sell closeout items in bulk,  like energy drinks, 2 for .88 or a box 'o corn dogs.  

You can order keg beer here too, but its not as smooth a transaction as Rouses.

Lotsa open cashiers available everytime I come.

Also has a growing Latin section....can you say JUMEX?  I knew that you could.

Really really wanted to be excited about this place... I had lobster ravioli and my partner had pappardelle w pork ragu. We shared the special salad. Kale Caesar salad. Meh. The lobster ravioli was more like crab Rangoon w tomato sauce. Lots of cream cheese filler. The pappardelle was pretty bland. The salad was really dry.
Re the alcohol. I'm sorry, any farm to table restaurant should have a selection of local beer. Largely AB beer tells me you are more of a chain.
Hope you can turn it around. The physical space is quite nice. Folks are friendly. Wish my tale was better.

My three friends and I decided to take a road trip from chicago to st louis for the blackhawks vs blues game this past saturday! The westin in conveniently located about 4 blocks from the scotttrade center. It's only about a 10 minute walk from the arch and right across from busch stadium.
The room was huge and so was the bathroom, and the beds were very comfy! 
They have overnight parking for 20 bucks which is not bad at all for hotel parking!
I will definitely be back next year for another hawks/blues matchup!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Wish I read reviews before I came... Think I was trying to give the the benefit of the doubt and was really hoping it would be better... It's not, I'm sorry to say. 

My tacos (traditional) were bland... (Carnitas, al pastor, steak) 
The guac that cashier and customers claimed was "the best" and very loved was not extraordinary... I definitely make better guac. It didn't taste bad. It was very creamy and had a good avocado flavor. You can tell it's fresh... But still, I was expecting more from the comments about the guac. 

The space looks like it would be nice for a party. They serve beer. 

The tacos tasted fine... But prob not coming back.

I'm not a huge fan of Maggie Moo's....  I got the rocky road and I thought it was super rich. I wasn't able to finish my ice cream (which is a first for me...) because it was just too much. I felt really sick after eating half of it.... My friends enjoyed their ice cream, maybe it's because my taste buds have been spoiled by Jeni's that they just can't eat ice cream from anywhere else... I do like that you're able to bring your ice cream home if you don't finish it though ! 

I might be back to give it another try, but I don't know if it'll be anytime soon.

The calabacitas plate was undeniably tasty; I hope this entree sticks around after Lent.  The beans, rice, tortillas, chips were all pretty bland, but the salsa bar was well-equipped to make them tastier.  The enchilada-style asada burrito scores points for good flavor and a $5 pricetag.  The shrimp cocktail and tacos were good, but not worthy of more descriptive adjectives.  It was a satisfactory, if unmemorable, meal.

Service was fast and friendly.  Their menu is limited and leans towards seafood, but they seem to have a few interesting specials.

The location is charmingly awful and the food isn't memorable.  Slightly below the mediocre threshold set by most sit-down Mexican restaurants in Tucson.  Beef enchiladas = meh.  Veggie burrito = pointless.  Chips flowed in copious abundance and the entrees were large, if little else.  Might be better if you ordered something more interesting than one of the lunch specials, but Leo's doesn't seem like the kind of place that is hiding talent... they just aren't very good.

But they are cheap!  Friendly, too.  Not that those are sufficient reasons to patronize a restaurant.

MidAtlantic is a great place to grab a drink after work. The bottled beer list provides a good smattering of Philadelphia brews that are hard to find elsewhere in University City.

The rarebit "Hot Fondue!" is incredibly rich, served with some of the best soft pretzels I've ever had. The strip steak was juicy and the bleu cheese fritters that came with it complimented the steak perfectly.

The staff is friendly and service is quick.

My only complaint is that the last time I was there, they were wasting tap room serving Lionshead. If I wanted a Lionshead from the tap I'd go to Mikey's.

Great sushi, but the place is SO SMALL! It's a BYOB, so I always prefer to dine in, but on the weekend nights I've waited upward of a half an hour. It's also not a "comfortable" wait. You can either stand outside if it's warm enough, or you can cram into the window "seats" by the drink fridge. They do, at least, have tea that you sip while you're waiting. 

I need a lot of sushi to fill me up, so I always order the 3 roll combo for $10.95. A great deal for the amount of food you get! The rolls were very fresh, and the last time I went, my friend and I sat right in front of the gentleman who was making our rolls, so it was fun to watch.

There was a large group of us - 30 to 40 - and they could accommodate us, which was nice, but overall ... meh ... there was a whole area of the restaurant without lights on - a little creepy. We ordered the sampler app and it was pretty terrible. If it was ever fresh, it was a couple days ago, or it was from a bag in the freezer. All the fried food filled me up, so I just ordered chicken tortilla soup for my meal. Thank goodness for that soup! It was super tasty - big chunks of chicken and avocado - yum. The giant margarita was fun, but I don't have plans to go back.

Great atmosphere, great service, great food - wouldn't change a thing. Definitely coming back. 

We had miso soup, edamame, a BBQ beef platter, the Las Vegas roll, Blue Crab roll, and the "Y" roll. Plus, a little surprise at the end with complimentary plum ice cream, which was incredible. 

The miso soup was the best I've ever had, the edamame was fresh and lightly salted. Even my husband who had a bad first sushi experience admitted that he genuinely liked the Las Vegas roll. And this was the first sushi place in Tucson I've been able to find a sweet potato roll ("Y"). 

You must come here.

Called our first time to make a take out order for dinner. My boyfriend ordered a very common lunch special that pretty much any Chinese place serves and the man who answered the phone was extremely rude telling my boyfriend they don't serve that, that my boyfriend was wasting his time and that we didn't understand because they "are authentic Chinese restaurant." We were finally able to place an order with that imbecile and immediately regretted it. We showed up and the place was a dump and the food ended up being very sub par. We will never return, and i can see from other reviews we were not alone in our experience there.

Never even knew this place was there, until I was looking for a place to take a client for dinner. The atmosphere was very nice -- great decor! But clearly I am the only person in town who didn't know this place was there. It was very crowded for dinner on a Wednesday evening. And loud. 

The menu was impressive and vast. The waitress was knowledgeable about any dishes we had questions about. The prices were a bit above my usual price range, and if I were to return it would probably be for a special occasion type meal, not just an average weekday dinner out. For just my entree and a glass of water, I ended up spending over $20 after tip.

Came here because next door was 1 1/2 hour wait. I needed something to hold my stomach before dinner. Seeing how crowded it was, it wouldn't be such a bad idea?! No, I was wrong. Just for a crunch roll, it took half hour to make. What's worse, it tasted not so good, and the aftermath, not so great either!!!!!! I won't go into details, but you get the picture. The rice was odd and tasted way too vinegary. Fish was not fresh and the tempera was not good. They topped it with lots of unagi to drown everything but still, did not make it taste any better.

Eh. Today I ordered a cheesecake brownie and a cup of coffee for an afternoon snack. The coffee had to be microwaved because apparently it had been sitting.  Okay fair enough I didn't want to wait to brew a fresh pot.  Both were given to me to go "to go" even though I wanted to sit down.  When I finished and was throwing out my single-use containers, I was asked how the brownie was. 
"It was okay," I said.  
"Excellent" the person responded.  
(Hmmm, okay is excellent?)
"It tasted like it had been sitting a little long," I told him. 
Crickets.

Completely overcharged.  $35??  And the haircut was fair at best.  Sylvio did a better job the last time I was there but this time he was busy .

I can't figure out how some barbers - despite specific instructions or requests which they seem to comprehend, still do whatever they want.  Do they think that the more they cut, the better value I am getting?  I really can't figure it out and this time, like others with other barbers, I was too pissed off to have this discussion.  Besides, what am I going to do, ask him to glue the hair back on?

Call me Forrest Gump for the next few weeks.

To fellow Yankees fans: this hotel does the trick if you're in town for Yankees Spring Training. Big parking lot. Walking distance to GMS Field. Many, many other fellow Yankees fans stay here. Hotel is comfortable. Decent sized room, pretty comfortable actually, and clean. Breakfast available. Patio, pool, and jacuzzi available. If you're in town for something other than Yankees Spring Training, I'm sure you can find a nice and better hotel in a more prime location elsewhere in Tampa. But for the purpose of Yankees Spring Training, this is the closest hotel and a good home base. GO YANKEES!!!!!!!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I've been to Bliss on a number of occasions over the past seven years or so, and each time I want to really like it, and each time I leave somewhat disappointed.  The food always seems just a bit "off" in one way or another.  I can't really say it's "bad" but just not what I'd expect, and not what really makes my night.  It seems that things are either over or under-seasoned, a little on the pedestrian side, not quite cooked right, or just don't taste as you'd expect or hope.  You'll have to try it for yourself and see if you have a different opinion...it might just be me.

Very convenient for the airport in Reno.  I got a room here via the hotels tonight app (and saved almost $40).

The staff were very friendly, my room was spacious & clean, they have a bar and a pretty decent menu.  The WiFi was quick and reliable, sadly I had to leave too early to try out their breakfast.

There was a flatscreen TV in the room (with an HD cable signal!) and a patch panel where you could plug in various devices via HDMI or VGA.

They have a shuttle to the airport which starts up at 4.30am (it isn't that far, but I have no idea how you could walk there!)
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I've been here several times now, and we like this vet better than the other two we've gone to.  The staff are all super friendly, and answer any and all questions thoroughly.  The place is very clean.  There is plenty of seating in the waiting area.  We had our dog neutered here, and everything went very smooth. He was ready to run, jump and play the very next day (keeping him calm the last week has proven difficult).

The prices are well within reason, beating most competitors in the area, but more importantly, they have earned my trust in carrying for the hairiest member of our family.

Really, realllly overrated.

Ever since I moved to SB my mom's been saying "we gotta go to the Habit,"  "we gotta go to the Habit," and so I did and it was not that great.

I came from my gym across the street and got a double with extra cheese, bacon, and avocado, no bun. I didn't try the fries or a drink. It was just really average and the meat was pretty dry. It didn't taste or look like it was any better quality than a burger from a huge fast food chain. And it took daysssss for my order to be ready.

Not worth the price or the trip out of IV. Just say no. And go to the Burger Bus.

I'm so disappointed; Bartaco used to be awesome, but... we haven't come in a while. This time we ordered a couple of pork belly, duck, and chorizo tacos. All were disappointing. The pork belly was dry and chewy (seriously it was tiring to chew). The chorizo was just some chopped up chorizo in a tortilla. And the duck was oily and didn't have any great flavor. The sides (plantains and corn) were still good, but that's not why we came to Bartaco. *heavy sigh* Time to look for a new fav taco joint... (oh, and no more chocolate mouse! Ouch).

My friend and I stopped in after an event at USF. It was late and pretty much anywhere serving food was closed, except for 3 coins and taco bus. So we opted to try something new. I was torn between a couple things on the menu, and the waitress suggested the French toast from my list. I went with it and while it was good, there was nothing that blew my mind. I also found myself wishing for real maple syrup as I always seem to do anywhere that only gives me "pancake syrup" as an option. Our waitress was fantastic, but the place is a total dive. I was reassured by the 3-4 cops that came in for their dinner break that night though.

Darrin can roast some full-bodied beans.  In fact, the bag I picked up had just been roasted by him that same morning.  You can't beat freshly-brewed coffee made from freshly-roasted beans!  

The coffee shop itself is simplistic, but I'm not going to be critical of the aesthetics, because most times I'm just grabbing and going.  As long as I have hot, strong coffee in my cup by the time I walk out the door, I'm good to go...and Darrin makes sure of it.  Try some for yourself the next time you're in downtown Zionsville.

The Bottle Shoppe has a solid selection of beer, whether it be a case of beer pong water or a coveted bottle of rarely-found Zombie Dust (you can only buy one bottle at a time if it's in stock).  I like knowing that I can go in and find my craft favorites but also walk out with a 6-pack of something I've never tried before.  Prices are a tad higher than what you'd get at competing stores, but when you're in need of something hoppy in SoBro or need a beverage to complement your Little Caesar's deal...look no further than the corner store on College and 49th.

Consider this my nomination for the following categories:

-Best CHEAP eats in Indy ($1.84/taco!)
-Best al pastor taco in Indy (It's so gooooooooooood.)
-Best hidden gem on Keystone Ave. (You've only driven by it 1000 times.)
-Best horchata in Indy (or as my husband calls it, "liquid churro")

One thing to note is that the tacos come with tomatoes, onions, lettuce, cheese, and sour cream.  I think next time I'm going to request just the meat, onions, and cilantro like a true Mexican taco.  Who knows - maybe that edit will have me nominating Taco & Burrito Place as THE best place to spend a Taco Tuesday in Indy!

The hotel is fine. The beds are comfortable and the rooms are clean. 
Was disappointed by the hotel restaurant, the food was sub par - the bartender said he had a bar hand in the kitchen. The bartender was also complaining that he was there later than he should have been. 
I sure of the restaurant hours but around 5p, the bartender said the kitchen was closed for the night. 
The gym was also a disappointment. The equipment was sufficient but there was a large puddle in the middle of the small room and all the machines were dirty.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Went here for happy hour today and it was fine, nothing special though. Starters were 50% off for happy hour and they had a selection of drinks available from $3 - $5. 

Service was friendly and well paced but food was too salty for my taste. I went with a group and we had the small cornbread muffins (complimentary), pork sliders, scallops, fries, some other small starters that I'm unable to recall at the moment.  Decor was very inviting and they have a open kitchen (love an open kitchen). 

I'll probably try this place out again at some point but I'm in no rush.

When we arrived there was no one at the front desk and it took quite a while for anyone to appear. I observed on several occasions the lobby was completely vacant. After we checked in I came down to ask a question but just eventually gave up. 

The ice maker on the second floor was broken (not the end of the world) but their complimentary breakfast was late. We had to skip it.

There was no bartender on duty. We had to wait quite some time for anyone to appear. When she finally showed up she apologized saying she'd been doing laundry. Huh?

I will say the staff I did encounter were extremely friendly and the room was very clean.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The flavor of the crab Rangoon was on good
The toasted ravioli nachos were tasty.
The smash burger was a hot mess like a whopper minus the meat was thrown in a box.
The loaded potato all the flavor was on the bottom of the box and none on the chips, we didn't eat it as the sour cream tasted off. *one party member didn't hold this one down so we tossed it*
The PBnJ fell flat. I had some jalapeño blue berry ham which I added to give it a pop. 
The Buffalo chicken has no chicken to be seen and mushrooms which we asked on the app to omit. 

The amount of protein and size for the value left me deflated rather than elevated.

Updating this review after several more visits.   There are so many options that I always have trouble making a decision.  

Piada choices include crispy chicken BLT piada, avocado piada, and a chef's special piada.   The Farmer's Market salad is colorful and delicious.  A Power Bowl features quinoa, red cabbage, and bruschetta.  

My favorites are the pasta bowls, and I usually end up building my own.  The pasta is always perfectly cooked, and I load is up with vegetables.  

The restaurant is always clean and employees are helpful and friendly.

YUMMMMMM i love yogurt so its hard for me to knock down any place i try... so now i sorta rate on how good they compare to others! :) this place had two good flavors i enjoyed and would get if i was here but i don't think i would have to run back to this place...I had the Dulce Le Lache and the Red Velvet Cupcake Batter which was good stuff!  

the inside looked just like all the others.. a bunch of yogurt dispensers, a toppings bar followed by syrup toppings a scale and register! sound familiar! haha

the hello kitty stuff is not here so i don't know why that is a photo...maybe someone brings thier own cup! lol

I will post an update after I've had a fresh square donut hot out of the fryer. I had some that were delivered fresh same-day, and I can't get excited about them.

The shape is novel. More donut per donut! 

The cinnamon sugar variety seemed to be a glazed donut with an added coating of sugar. Too much in my opinion - glaze or cinnamon sugar, not both. 

At the end of the day, these donuts are still donuts, and I'd gleefully eat 3 or 4 at a time. But if I had a $10 bill and other donut options in front of me I'd venture to try something else.

This is a no frills place for sushi and poke. They also have ramen but somehow that got left off the name. There are a few small tables for dine in but the majority of orders were takeout and delivery. I got the peach bay poke bowl which had salmon, tuna, avocado, cucumber, red onion, jalapenos, and poke sauce. There were a ton of jalapenos that made it soo spicy but overall it was delicious and a good portion. You can customize your poke bowl completely as well. 

It's a good spot for a quick and easy meal, nothing fancy.

Terrible. Wanted a quick in and out lunch while babysitting a three and four year old. Mostly I like Wendy's because they have a great menu with healthier options. This Wendy's, quite frankly, b.l.o.w.s. Their lines were backed up both inside and out. The bathrooms were so dirty, as were the tables. Our food took thirty-five minutes!! If we hadn't had kiddos with us who were hungry, I would have left but that was not an option. We did receive a refund after asking, at least. But were given no explanation and/or apologies for the long wait and delay. I will not be going back to this particulatar Wendy's again. Ever.

Another amazing evening at Trattoria Branica in Kirkwood!

Sam, the owner, was not there last night, but I usually get the two 8 ounce pork chops with some kind of delicious covering on them . . . yummy!  They came with new potatoes and also broccoli.  I believe it was $19.95 and work every bite.

The atmosphere is great - had dinner with two friends from out of town (total of six of us) and they loved the wine selection, great beers, and wonderful ambiance of the restaurant.

Highly recommend everything they have on the menu - perfect any evening!

We were here a couple of weeks ago and ordered the tasting menu for 55 dollars.  I rarely give 5 starts in any restaurant review but this was by far my best dinning experience in Philadelphia in the past year.  No complaints.  Everything was well thought out and delicious.  My wife and I picked different items in each section so we could try as much as possible - there were no bad choices.  Also, if you like bourbon and whiskey order the hammer.  It tastes like an old fashioned and is really delicious.  Top chef hype aside this is really a great place.

Deviled Eggs, Pork Wings, CannonBalls, Traditional Mussels and Grilled Chicken Salad.

We could have a whole meal just with the appetizers.

Next time I think we will pass on the pork wings.  They really were not very memorable, but the rest were good.  If you do not want your French fries soggy from the mussel sauce ask that they be put on a separate plate.

The menu certainly has changed from the old Winberies'.

We went on a Thursday evening and the place was extremely busy and loud.

We'll go back.
But it still is just an a-ok place.

Packed away in a tightly condensed parking lot, this is a Frys I find worth avoiding as much as possible despite it being convenient to my workplace. I have gone in here a handful of times and it is often crowded, which I suppose is great for business but it's just too much. It's your usual Frys, slightly overpriced items, not particularly clean. This one has a lot of household/kitchen items presumably for Christmas. I usually find the shoppers inside and out of the building rude and nearly get run over or pan handled each time I visit so I try to steer clear.

I love this place! One of my two favorite snoball places in the city thus far! Now, their customer service isn't exactly sparkling, but it's nothing deterring me from coming back. All of the signs look like rough drafts from an old science fair project, mostly handwritten and bleached by the hot Louisiana sun. That being said, I've never had a snoball here that wasn't delightful! They have MANY different sizes, all cheap! They also offer ice cream sundaes and different snoball toppings. I love coming here as it is close to home and also close to LaFreniere Park. It's not much to look at it, but give it a try!

I went here for Sunday brunch, one of my favorite meals.  They have a varied menu with options ranging across the typical omelet, french toast, or pancake spectrum.  I tried the veggie omelet which has onion, mushroom, spinach, and green peppers.  It comes with a side of potatoes and toast.  I substituted in the cinnamon roll, which was somewhat disappointing (and not a true substitute as they charged me without saying they would).  The omelet was delicious - the ingredients seemed fresh and the onion had gotten just mushy enough for me.  It was a nice place - not my favorite but still quite yummy.

I read through the reviews and was surprised at how different the experiences have been. We went while the Cats were playing and had a great time. My son and I played the bean bag game while we waited for our table. The lay out was nice and relaxing, especially outside. The two burgers that we ordered were perfectly cooked, and the grilled chicken sandwich was exceptional. The pico tasted homemade. It had a nice little bite. Our waitress was on point the whole time. Our drinks never went dry. I'm looking forward to checking out a happy hour. I do intend to go back, and only hope my experiences are consistently positive.

Location is fire!

But....the rooms were nasty.  For a million dollars, I wouldn't walk barefoot on their carpet..  Blacklight sea monkey discovery galore.

My man made the rez.  Due to a huge convention, the hotels were practically sold out. I quickly let him know he was not allowed to make reservations again. EVER.  

The room smelled like a old dirty powdered ass.  Probably due to a nasty smoker.   Also, we had no housekeeping for 2 days in a row.   

The lobby is great people watching.  Liquid courage and lots of fools.  

My advice, check out the location of this ho-tel and find something in the area that has better reviews.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I really wanted to like Las Bugambilias more than i did. The spot, right off Headhouse Square is much smaller than I had imagined, with a tiny bar up front that puts out a decent margarita. The cocktail list is awfully pricey though. 

The cochinita pibil wasn't available, so I had the enchiladas mole, which were really good. My wife's enchiladas verde were just as good. 

Our tamale appetizer was cold and crumbly however, a disappointment after it was recommended by our server. 

I'm not rushing back, there's too many other Mexican options, but Las Bugambilias is definitely a serviceable option. I was just expecting more.

I went with a Groupon. I had to ask a server who our waiter/waitress was, as we had not been approached for minutes. The stairs to walk up where we were seated were very steep. The service was the downside. Food was good. $8 for valet is steep for the neighborhood and type of restaurant. Street parking is available. My sister liked the house bread, but it was not exceptional to me. It tasted very standard and not fresh. We were placed with a family party full of kids and adults, which blended us in with my toddler niece. There was another section much quieter for people without kids. The escarole was delicious, as was the pasta.

The price is meh. The food is really good though. Their meatballs are so good. Their wraps are awesome as well. 

There isn't much to be said really. It is quick and healthy and compared to most quick fixes, it leaves you feeling good and alert rather than lazy and tired. 

I don't really buy into the calorie focus of the menu, but the food is "clean" and definitely light on the stomach. Still filling and hardy.

It is hard to get me away from the Panera next door, but I definitely been thinking about that wrap I had for a while now. Yum!

Overall this is a good standby for a quick lunch or easy dinner. Been here many time for a quick workday lunch. The service is always prompt and friendly. The restaurant is clean, well maintained and has plenty of Mexico-Americona decor.

As for the food you get plenty of for your dollar and the quality is always consistent. The chips and salsa the comes to the table when you are seated is ok but nothing specially. If you like your salsa anything above mild you won't be impresses. The Morales taco or barrito is a must is you haven' tried them before.

This review is just for pizza delivery. 

3-stars for the pizza being delivered in under the amount of time we were told on the phone, and a decent crust. Not more than 3, because the sauce was only so so and there was way too much spinach on the white/spinach pie and not enough garlic and ricotta (which we asked as an addition) and two large pies for over $40 is pushing it on being way too expensive for pizza, even in Newtown. 

I'd give it a try again and see if I like another type of pizza perhaps because I didn't mind the pizza dough.

Came here on a Sunday evening before any dinner rush. This was our first time trying this place. Sadly disappointed in both the (lack of) service and the poor quality of food. We sat at the sushi bar and neither of the sushi chefs acknowledged us yet they acknowledged others they apparently know and who possibly frequent their business. 
Quality of Food = 1 star
Quality of Service = 1 star
Value for Price = 1/2 star
Overall score =  1 star

Recommendation:  Don't waste your time and hard earned money here. Find another location that provides better everything.

I came here because the salad restaurant next door was closed. Everything on the menu seemed very well priced. When I first came here, they had worn down pictures of their food on the wall, I still appreciated it though because I always like looking at what I might eat. Now they have renovated and added a poke bar. 

I'm not a particular fan of the plastic takeaway containers when you're dining in but I guess that might be a cost thing? I didn't try any of their rolls. I got their chicken rice boxes. Their chicken is consistently dry/overcooked. But if you're in a hurry and on a budget, this would work if you're craving for Japanese food.

Mehhh. I wanted to love this place, but I really couldn't. Work took me here for a conference, and I stayed for 3 nights. The hotel itself is large, but the decor is so outdated and weird that walking down the hall of our room made me almost nauseous. 70s carpeting and weird lighting don't belong in 2015. The room was small, but fine, and our view was less than alluring (thanks, construction.) 

Also, there is no free wifi with your stay. I could write a book on how utterly ridiculous this is, but I'll just say this: if you are the Hyatt, you suck. Get your act together.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Very nice. Big open space for sitting and reading and drinking your coffee. Lots of tables available for people who want to hang out (and on a lovely Sunday afternoon, there were people working away and staying caffeinated at the same time), and a big variety of hot drinks and pastries to try. I chose an Egyptian chamomile tea (from their long list of tea offerings) and a chocolate chip cookie. Both were very nice. The tea was hot and very aromatic, and the cookie was rich and chewy and delicious. This was a pleasant experience overall.

Good salsa, friendly service--decent food!

AMBIENCE:  2.5 stars.  There are probably about 400 of these types of places in Tucson--strip mall Mexican food joints with colorful walls, etc.  

SERVICE:  4 stars.  Friendly, prompt lunch-time service.

FOOD:  3 stars.  Decent Mexican, but nothing great.  I had the lunch special with a shredded beef taco and a chicken enchilada--both serviceable but nothing I would crave.  The salsa is pretty darn good though!  Chips are mediocre.

OVERALL: 3 stars.  It gets the job done!  I would definitely go back!

This is literally the worst hotel I stayed at. The rooms were disgusting, the service was subpar and the overall experience was awful. When we got to our room, the toilet seat had stains on it and we had to ask for new blankets because there was blood on the blankets. They didn't come and change them right away, we had to wait for hours after we asked for them. Front desk was rude and dismissive to us as well. You couldn't pay me enough to stay at this hotel again. I will not be returning to this place and if you're reading this, do yourself a favor and book a room someplace else. If I could give this place negative stars, I would.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I live in Brentwood and have tried most of the Mexican places around me.  We stopped in to Mazatlan because we hadn't been yet and I was pleased.  It wasn't my favorite and I was a little disappointed they didn't have fish tacos, but the cheese dip was tasty and the margaritas even tastier.  We went on a Friday night and were sat immediately and had fast service.  I am unadventurous in what I will try, but I'm particular about my beef tacos and these were pretty darn good.

I'd recommend if you want something fast and relatively cheap.

no no no!  This place has the ability to be much better than it is.  The pizza itself just doesn't taste homemade.. I don't know if its the ingredients they are using or what but it's very bland.. and bland is not something I want when I eat my very favorite food.  The restaurant itself is very nice.. lots of space.. nothing in terms of service was offered when I went there.. Everything was ordered and picked up at the counter.. Matter of fact, the only thing I would mention in terms of service was the feeling of being rushed.  Not impressed.  Sorry guys.

I've been to Kiwi twice and I can't wait to go back. For anyone new to the concept, Kiwi offers frozen yogurt and all the toppings you could possibly want. The greatest thing is it's self serve. You can decide our much or how little froyo and toppings you want. You pay by the ounce, it's genius really. 

They have many flavors to choose from and toppings range from very healthy, like strawberries, kiwi, and various fruits to chucks of cheesecake and cookie dough. You can experiment with different flavors and toppings and have something different every time. 

I don't crave sweets often, but when I do I'll be going to Kiwi.

I haven't been to this place in forever but that's because they opened their new location but since this is the original home, I thought I'd leave a review. Sushi here is outstanding. Everything tastes fresh and unique. My only gripe would be when it was busy, they would forget our rolls or they came out very slow. I'd easily forget this hiccup in service after receiving some home made ice cream. If you're in the area, this is a good place to stop by. Otherwise the other Sakana is more appropriately staffed.

Hmm... I'm knocking them off a star. I don't know if it's me or the place but I swear the track on the car wash is quicker. Felt like I was in and out. The vacuums are hit and miss. Sometimes I have to move my car because the vacuum is kinked or not working. For all the business this place gets, I'd figured they'd fix those things. Nope, they spent it on the Volcano neon lights in the inside. Car wash pack is now 4 washes instead of 5. Still a better deal than most places but I'm not raving about this place anymore.

Why why why? Why do people get into the restaurant business and don't have the passion for it? My dinner here was a complete disaster. The only highlight was a friendly waitress. Otherwise it was horrible. My daughter wanted unagi... "Sorry we ran out of unagi." Ugh OK. Mind you, the restaurant wasn't even busy. Sushi took forever to come out and when it did, it was missing orders.  Normally I wouldn't mind this and just reorder what was missing but it was so slow, I just finish what we got and went to a real sushi restaurant to get my daughter her unagi.

Started with fresh chips and a generic salsa which may have been fresh or out of a bottle.  Too pureed to tell the difference and pretty mild.

Loved the swordfish tacos!  The spicy garnish sauce was great.

Great, friendly staff!

The Tortilla soup needs work!

Need an a la cart menu for sides.  Only option with tacos entree was soup or salad.  Why not offer refritos?

Dinner for 2 was $33 which is definitely a little pricey for StL Mex-Tex but you do get a cloth napkin and table cloth.

50% Off with Police, Fire, Military ID or uniform.

I'm giving this restaurant a 2 rating based on the food I had and not the atmosphere which was cool. I visited this restaurant on a summer Wednesday night when they have live music and an even livelier crowd. The atmosphere was fun and I enjoyed the fact that there was a lot of diversity in the customers (race, age, interests, etc.). My $5 Margarita was good enough but the Spinach Artichoke Dip was horrible and maybe the worst I've ever had. It was soupy and tasted like it had been frozen and defrosted right before being brought to me.  I would consider going back to try something else but I won't be recommending this place to anyone.

Last Friday morning my relatively new car (2014) started bucking like a bronco while I was crossing the Huey P Long. To add to my stress, I was supposed to be leaving Sunday to go on a toad trip and check off one of my biggest bucket list items. I was freaking out. I called CARS and Michelle told me to come on in. Within a few hours they had the problem fixed AND they were able to work with my schedule. It meant a lot to me to have such reliable and understanding people not only fix my car but get me on the road. Thanks to them I got lots of wolf hugs and kisses in FL instead of being stuck at home with a car that wasn't working.

I was super excited to find out that Sushi Land had baked rolls (Lion King Roll, Bay Scallop Roll), so I decided to order both. The reviews warning about the small portions were no joke! 
After getting over my initial disappointment, I decided to taste the darn thing. I thought, "Maybe something so compact can still pack a punch to my tastebuds?" Nopes, thought wrong. Tastebuds weren't even slightly roughed up. 
I know of a place where for a dollar more... you can get a normal-sized, bombass, flavor-packed Lion King roll. Just one minor catch, it's in CA. 
BTW, one additional star for the service.

I honestly wouldn't even rate this place with one star.  I ordered water because I didn't want soda and the server told me that I would have to order a drink if I wanted to take advantage of the lunch specials, it's not like the lunch "specials" are even that great.  The sushi was terrible, it was mainly rice and hardly any fish and it wasn't by any means inexpensive. I first came to this location when they first opened and I told myself that I would never again go but I figured several years have passed and maybe the have improved......NOPE!!! If you want good sushi go to On A Roll

Super frustrated and looking for a new vet. We have taken our pug puppy to Ada Veterinary Hospital 3 times. Once when we got her and she had diarrhea and then to more times for her first 2 sets of shots. Every single time they have charged us an exam fee. Then the last time they said they should have offered us the shots package which would have included all the shots and the diarrhea visit but because it wasn't offered at first they won't honor it. So we lose $100... Whatever... We still figured we would take her for her last set of shots... Well just went in and they wanted to charge us ANOTHER exam fee and a walk up fee plus the shots!!

So I'm kinda mixed on my experience. The crab and asparagus bisque was very tasty. The lasagna was so-so. The sauce was a pit tangy and the lasagna was not at all hot just luke warm. The Caesar salad was pathetic. Romain lettuce with some dressing drizzled. The service was less then par. The waitress was in a rush we had to ask for our beverages to be refresh TWICE and had to wait quite some time for her to come back to our table. I noticed we were not the only ones. And she proceeded to say how the younger wait staff just "play in their cell phones". I expected more. Maybe just a bad night but have to think about if I would come back.

To me it's just an average little restaurant serving up fast Chinese take out to the public. I randomly ended up here on day and decided to order some food before class. The food is pretty good, it was served fast and hot!

The location is clean and the service is friendly. I got sesame chicken with brown rice and was not disappointed. The small is actually a lot! I really appreciate that they serve brown rice and that's a reason I am a fan. 

If you're looking for Chinese and brown rice! Check this place out!

I had an okay time here. I went in to get a digital perm which never happened because my hair was "too fine". What a disappointment. It was the cheapest place that would do digital perm and also one of the only places that does digital perm in the area. They were pretty much rushing me in and out

I went to Bolsa in pinellas park with my mom and talked to them about wanting a digital perm but was told my hair was too fine to do it. The owner told me she doesn't know what they were talking about and told me that it would work on my hair.

I am currently a member of this gym and enjoy it. It's nothing compared to LA Fitness because it doesn't have as much space, room, classes, pool or sauna available but it also doesn't come with the price tag. 

At Youfit you have a choice of a $10 or $20 dollar membership. Of course, with the $20 dollar one you can have access to all Youfit locations, the tanning rooms and also bring a guest as many times as you want. The trainers are super nice and aren't pushy at all and the workers are nice (normally younger kids). 

I enjoy my time here because I can get what I need to get done and also have no complications with anyone.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
So big stars for the tasty treats, but turn a eye when it comes to service and looks. 

I tried the mango con chile popsicle and I'm addicted! I love the chunks of real mango and the spicy kick of the chile. It's so tasty... It's my new favorite! 

The horchata was also really good! Super sweet tho, too sweet for me but still tasty. It's creamy and spiced. Yum! 

I definitely would come back for their products and would try all the other flavors. I love real fruit bars and they do it right. You can try many different flavors. 

The service wasn't great. It wasn't much service at all. So don't mind it and get your goods and peace out!

First time & impressed, especially since this restaurant is housed in a damned truck stop! 

Our food was served on - duh me - skillets! Really cool & you can even buy a set (of 4)  as you check out for $20.

The buffet (only $12.99/pp)  looked lovely, yet fattening. 

We ordered off the menu. Pancakes & eggs
for the boy and me.  My girl
wanted lunch (we went at 11 am)  - chicken tenders, mashed potatoes and a biscuit.   She LOVED it! 

Two big "hotcakes" (just a tad sweet) w whipped butter - the eggs were GOOD! 

We'll definitely go again!

I'm trying to be as fair as I could here. . . the food was VERY good (went for lunch - I had a crab cake sandwich and my co-workers, chicken and portabello mushroom sandwiches and soup) but the service all but stunk (utterly S L O W and there were barely a handful of patrons) and the decor - dark and blah.  It's a real shame - as I said, the food was really good!  Hopefully Chef Ramsey pays them a visit or something!  I'd go back if I so happened to be in the area AND hungry but that's it - not a special trip unless I had another gift card like this time!

I needed a place to eat w/ my kids before a nearby appointment.  I hadn't been to this pizza place since it was Satellite (yummy!) when I was in high school eons ago . . . not happenin' as Luigi's for sure.  Don't know if it was b/c we ordered individual slices but the pizza was bland - my two types of white and I'm assuming my son's plain slice.  Their chicken bites were good and the fries didn't look greasy.   The guys hanging up front didn't seem too friendly - our nice waitress was the only saving grace.  Our lunch was almost $30 including tip - too pricey for this mediocre joint.  Won't be back.

Medford is a bit of a drive for me but its worth it. Id forgotten how delicious the food here is! 

I had the eggplant parm - huge "slab" plus a large side of fettuccine - tastes home made! 

All of my friends loved their dishes as well - one was a gluten free chicken selection. 

For $16.99 I had my fabulous eggplant & pasta plus a side salad. 

Rolls and bruschetta  (hello garlic!!!) were on the table too.  Meh.

Anthony, our server, was super nice & attentive. 

Decor is sweet but nothing to rave about (who cares!) 

There was so much food that I have leftovers - usually doesn't happen for me! 

Cant wait to go back!!!

This has got to be the best pizza place in the greater northeast. Incredible pizza. Since Da Vinci's is also Leonardo's bakery, these guys know their dough. Their pizza is some of the best I've ever tasted and by virtue of their incredible bread, their sandwiches are generally incredible. 

The prices aren't incredible, but they aren't much more than your average local pizza shop. The quality of product is definitely worth the price charged, anyway.

I'm shocked that there aren't already any reviews for this joint, I guess there aren't many yelpers in Feasterville/Trevose.

For the price the food is excellent.. 

The Chef Salad is HUGE and their house vinaigrette is awesome.

Definitely worth the 5 bucks. It eats like a meal and will fill you up.

They always have some really awesome deals on customer appreciation day and buy one get ones on XL pizza.

The provel cheese is the real deal - not that crap that burns to a crisp when it hits the right temperature for pizza... (can you tell from my other reviews I hate burnt cheese?) 

Order the chef salad and some garlic cheese bread and you'll be set..mmmm.....

This place is a broken down, unclean "motel". This is probably one of the worse hotels I've ever stayed at. The carpets were unclean, and had numerous cigarette burns. One of the pillows had blood on it, along with some suspect stains on the bed skirt. The tub and the tiles were covered in dirt and grime. There's no trash bags in any of the garbage bins. The hotel considers themselves "pet friendly", but there's no where to bring your dog, except on the side of the building where there's broken beer bottle glasses and a few other unsafe materials. I feel unsafe here, and unwashed. I would definitely not recommend this place to anyone.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: i just joined the 12th street gym...it's not my neighborhood gym but it is my gayborhood gym...spin class, yoga and cardio...this gym warms the cockles of my heart...the staff is friendly and helpful...you can actually find a quiet place to work out without feeling that your every move is being hyper scruntized...this is not to say that there isn't the occasional distracting bit of eye candy to cause you to miss a step or two on the treadmill... not that this has ever happened to me but well..um...what i am trying to say is that this gym is a keeper...
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: At 5:45pm, this Starbucks is dirty. The trash bins are overflowing and staff is checked out. One Male bearded barista was counting money as I came to the counter and after a minute never looked up, never acknowledged, so i went to the bathroom. After coming out there was a customer before me. I was next and I was still not acknowledged. I had to present myself to the barista, who only claimed he was waiting for me. It's the worst service I've ever received. I've never seen staff throwing away breakfast stuff already as customers are ordering. I will not be returning to this location.

I first went to Las Palmas during the very first week of my freshman year at Vanderbilt with my orientation group.  The lighting was a bit too dark.  Our orders got mixed up leaving me with a meat dish that had to be sent back.  It was pretty blah overall.  

Since then I've gone back a couple times and had varying experiences. All in all it usually ends up to be a non-special experience with good but not amazing food.  The prices are good for the portions.  The service seems to be fairly efficient.  Still, though, meh.

Something about the type of incense that was overpowering the room reminds me of my elementary school friend's weird mom who kept old newspapers and had a strange obsession with vintage coffee cups.  It made the experience a bit off-putting from the start.  The place is exactly what you would envision when you try to imagine a combination fortune teller's shop and coffee shop.  The light is a bit dim, the furniture is plush, and the ladies inside seem maternal yet standoffish. 

I ordered an iced coffee which was just the usual cup of coffee with ice.  It was only $1.70.

Sinkers is just what you need in a neighborhood liquor store. It has a large selection in a store layout that makes everything easy to find. It has a no-hassle staff who is always friendly at the register.  Also, it is one of the few liquor stores on gallatin that doesn't feel the least bit sketchy.

Due to the limitations of space they are lacking some brands and specialty liquors that I've sought, but not many.  They do make room for an oddly extensive collection of differently shaped tequila bottles which includes a gangster-style rifle if you're ever in the market for such a thing.

When I first heard about Decades I was so jazzed. An over the top 80's themed dance bar is the stuff dreams are made of.  Unfortunately, in reality Decades is just another crap downtown bar full of tourists and over-dressed local Casanovas.  

It was 80's themed, but in a really generic cheesy way.  The walls had paintings of 80's merchandise, but the whole downstairs still looks dreary over all.  There's a cover at the door which is obnoxious.  The atmosphere just felt a bit forced.  The crowd was awkward.  I'd much rather put on my Cyndi Lauper vinyl and dance around the living room with friends.

I absolutely love Samurai.  The main reason is their famous Choo Choo roll which is topped with strawberries, nuts, and a slightly sweet brown sauce.  I was hesitant about sushi with fruit, but am now a fan of all of Samurai's fruit-topped options.

The place is definitely small which can mean a bit of a wait, so come prepared.  Also, if you think you're going to be able to fit more than three of your friends at your table prepare for disappointment.  The bathroom is definitely a drawback size-wise as well.  It's quite a squeeze getting in and out so don't drink too much of the complimentary green tea.

Apple Market is a great grocery alternative when you just need the basics.  If you live in that part of town Kroger and the like are pretty far out and a lot more elaborate than necessary if all you desire is a frozen dinner and some produce (though it's not the best looking, the produce is still usually good enough).  The size makes it appear more like a convenience store than a grocer, but it definitely has the stock options of the latter so don't be fooled.

The prices are pretty cheap.  I definitely recommend tacking a stop at the Apple Market onto your trip to West End Liquors for mixers or snacks.

While this Wendy's is quick during lunch rush, and they only occasionally forget my sour cream for my potato...or the dressing for my salad...this place is a friggin' ZOO!

What truly makes it so crazy is the location. I would be curious to know how many car accidents occur in and around their parking lot on a monthly basis. 

Sheesh.

Yet, I still trek over from time to time for a quick, cheap meal when I'm in a hurry.

Tip: Exiting from the back of the restaurant via the one way to Powell is highly recommended.

As I mentioned in another Subway review, I am a believer that not all Subways are created equal. While this location does not earn the rank as the "best" Subway in my Nashville book, it's not far behind.

The staff here has always been friendly and efficient. Even when it's packed with hungry peoples, this team keeps the sandwhich-makin' a-movin' and a-shakin'.

Additionally, this location always seems to be very clean.

I do wish they sold my favorite salt n' vinegar potato chips, but to make it up to me, they sell Garden Tomato & Basil chips instead. 

"We're good, OHB Subway. It's all good."

My car was super dirty and needed some detailing on the inside so I bought the full service wash on Groupon. I had this really horrible red fruit punch stain (possibly some sort of concoction my brother made when he used to drive my car) on the inside and a coffee stain and they did a great job attempting to get them out...I kind of let the stains sit too long in the carpet. The service was awesome, the people there are really nice to work with, and my car looked great afterwards! Would definitely go back again!

Got delivery from here and ordered some lunch specials all for myself!

I tried the shrimp lo mein, Mongolian beef, and general's chicken. Each lunch special comes with your choice of soup, egg roll, crab Rangoon, and rice. It's so affordable!

The flavor of the dishes weren't too shabby! The lo mein was my favorite. The general's chicken was too breaded, but the flavor was good. I wish the Mongolian beef had more beef! I also enjoyed the hot sour soup and the egg rolls! 

Would definitely order from here again. Sometimes you just need that Americanized-Chinese food fix.

I loved it! I saw them on foodler but I lived too far away for them to deliver. So finally I got down there, which is pretty far out there, and I was a little worried it has.... character. It's not the prettiest place and I feel like theres a few too many chairs. The staff is amazingly nice I enjoyed talking to them because you can tell there geniunely nice people. The food? Was awesome my lasagna calzone wasn't very good but the actual pizza was phenomonal. I loved it. The cheese bread was good but eh Idk. The pizza is whats amazing about this place stick to it. Oh yeah they also have chicken parmesian ahhh yeah.

I didn't really want to go to another automatic car wash.  I thought this place was different.  I have yet to see any other establishments in the area that hand washes.  I knew coming here would be a bit more expensive.  I paid $16 for interior/exterior.  Since it is hand wash, it took longer for the service.  I think it's money well spent.  Plus, it's not often that I get the car washed.  It was nice of them to leave coupons in the car as well.  I would recommend this place.  Nice and friendly staff as well.  Oh they also offer oil changes if that suits your fancy.

I'm always on the lookout for great sushi in Tucson and I'm glad to add another to my top places! MY SO and his friend were in Tucson visiting for the day and so my coworker and I joined them here for dinner.  We ordered about 5 rolls to share and were pleased with all of them. I don't quite remember what all of them were now, but needless to say, all were excellent. We enjoyed the salads, endamame, and plum ice cream.  The restaurant is cozy and the waitstaff were friendly and always available to help us with any requests or questions. 

We'll be back to try more rolls!

I love White Castle. It gets five stars just for being open 24/7, which is essential since I always end up going there at like 2 am, whether I'm in town or just passing through. But the food itself is just awesome. They always get my food right (two double cheeseburgers, no pickles) and it's always hot and fresh.

The frozen ones you get at the grocery store are okay if you're craving and can't get to one, but nothing beats actually going there and getting the real thing. If you've never tried White Castle, you're missing out. So yummy.

We only stopped here on a road trip from New Jersey back to Washington, DC.  We were looking for a place to eat lunch and watch football, and someone at the gas station right off the turnpike told us to come here.  It definitely fit our needs!  I had the fried mozzeralla, which, was pretty good.  They bread it with a homemade mixture of bread crumbs and seasoning.  It was better than 85% of them mozzarella sticks I get at restaurants.  The staff was very very friendly as well.  I was thinking I'd be the first to review this place (it's located in a very, very farm/rural area) but I see that it gets rave reviews from other Yelpers!

Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice....well I know the rest.

Decided to give West End Wok a second try after a very lackluster first go.

The rundown...
Chicken Lo Mein - overcooked noodles and no spice.  Couldn't save it with a mountain of Sriracha.
Hot braised chicken- no heat and no sauce.  They use white meat which I can't stand but if you're going to use white meat, then you have to add sauce. More like dry chicken tenders.
Egg drop soup - ok.  nothing great, but not bad.

Still waiting for a solid chinese place in the CWE... for how long, who knows.  I guess when the competition is Hon's Wok there's no where to go but up.

A childhood favourite, likely due to the Spumoni. I mean who doesn't love Spumoni .... seriously it's just fun to say. Spumoni. 

Anyways, the Spaghetti Factory down town has quick service at lunch which makes it ideal in Edmonton's downtown business community. I've also been here for dinner and it's usually pretty busy!  The food is always good and the usually the service is too. I don't really have much to say about this place. I really do like the Spaghetti Factory, and it will always be a classic... I just think it's lacking a "wow" factor.

I'm not quite sure why no one seems to know the answers to my questions here but it is starting to get really frustrating. The branch manager is the only person I have spoke with that has been able to answer all my questions and know how to best direct me. Everyone else seems to answer incorrectly by giving me false information which then puts me on a goose chase to find out the correct information. The location however is convenient and the staff are nice. Hopefully they will step it up the next time I visit, or I'll just start making appointments with the branch manager.

I have mixed feelings about this Sobeys. It's smaller than most, but it's location is prime. I feel they don't have the selection that all grocery stores do, but I did go here on a Sunday night which is the worst possible time to grocery shop - do not do this, there is nothing fresh left. This Sobeys however does have it's redeeming qualities there is definitely more organic and local food, but there isn't a bulk section for flour or spices. Over all, I would have to agree with previous Yelpers that the prices are higher. Maybe I should give this location a bit more of a chance.

I frequent this liquor store a lot. No I'm not an alcoholic, it's just close to my home and grocery store. I shop here because of the convince but unfortunately they don't have the best selection. My main objective in life is to find the perfect wine to bring to wine club. While this store carries a variety of wines from different countries it doesn't have a lot when it comes to champagne, I think I found 2 bottles. The hard liquor selection is better, but there is also less variety compared to wine. I'll continue to shop here for liquor, but I don't think I will find my perfect wine here.

Looking for a place where there are tons of 18/19/20 year olds... this is the place to go. I'm lucky if I don't run into 3/4 of my graduating class at this bar, though I'm not sure why they are all still in the bar-star phase. The Ranch has tons of over-priced drinks and is usually at capacity which makes it impossible to find anyone. The dance floor isn't big enough and they play a mix between top 20 and country, so if that's what you're into this place is for you. I don't recommend it though unless you plan on getting at least tipsy. While I've had some good nights here I don't think I could handle this bar sober.

The staff here are exceptionally helpful and very knowledgeable about wine. However, the Canadian wine section seemed limited. It did seem like they had an agreement with some of the Canadian vinyards because they didn't have  a ton of variety and definitely lots from one specific vinyard. There was nothing from Dirty Laundry, and limited wine from Grey Monk which are two of the larger BC VQA vineyards.

The wines did seem a little pricey compared to what I normally pay for canadian wine but never the less I thoroughly enjoyed the $28 blend from Little Straw I purchased. I liked Vinomania, but I'm not sure how often I'll be back.

So far, this is the best Italian restaurant we've found in WC/ZH area. We had the Sergio special pizza, lasagna & spumoni. It was all delicious! But our server was not very good. She was more focused on her conversations with the male server, than her tables. The lady that runs the cash register wasn't the friendliest either. Maybe customer service doesn't have to be important anymore, once you've been in business as long as they have. If this is the case, it saddens me, because great service & great food combined are what will keep you here for the next 20 years. So, due to that I am only giving 4 stars.

Shredded beef Tesla Tacos. Nuff said!

Roscoe's Tacos fills an interesting niche in the Tex - Mex culture. It's BEYOND Taco Bell, but not a trip to any of your fave Mexican restaurants. What you get here is an addictive, fast eating, simple taco or burrito, drenched in one of several original hot sauces in a range of temperatures.

You come to RT's when you want to go on a crave bender. You don't come here when you want the traditional chips cum chimichanga charade.

Roscoe's is an Indiana original. There is nothing like it!

Met my good buddy there for a mutual b-day treat and we split six high quality rolls.  The standard fair was right on target (e.g. philly roll and dragon roll) and the more creative rolls (e.g. soft shell crab) really pushed me over the edge.  It's BYOB - we got a 6 pack of heineken for $11 @ the Locust Bar right next door (which is pretty good for that part of the city), which went perfectly with the fish.  It's a small restaurant that gets pretty noisy at peak dinner time, but I'll take lively over eerily silent any day.

Completely unassuming, but fantastic! 

I had salmon and white tuna nigiri, a spicy tuna roll, and a shrimp tempura roll. Excellent! The nigiri was slightly smaller than I've seen other places, but still a perfect serving. The rolls were prepared artfully with amazingly fresh ingredients. Of all of the sushi that I've had in the Cool Springs area, these guys take top rank on freshness and taste. 

The staff is very friendly; available, but not overbearing.

Because of its location, the ambiance leaves a little to be desired, but real foodies won't care in the least.

I really WANTED to like Mother's but they gave me no reason to like it......  We visited at an off time between lunch & dinner so seating was totally not a problem.In fact, we were the ONLY ones in the place on a Holiday Weekend - which I found a little odd. The service was super friendly but the food was quite sub par. The burger was little but "ok". The steak husband had - well - I kind of wish he sent it back b/c it was NOT "ok". There are so many other BETTER PLACES in New Hope. Don't go here so you can see for yourself - check out somewhere else b.c.  it is bound to be better than here.

Grande Margaritas.  How yummy!  And you can even get them flavored...strawberry, banana and the list goes on.

Recently I had a banana margarita and it was pretty tasty.  To be sure, I may have to go back and have a few more.

I ordered the tableside guac and the server pretty much didn't know the difference between chunky and throwing the avocados in the bowl! (So I took a star off for that. )  She was training another server and I hope and pray that she knows the difference and doesn't just make the chunky guac like our server did!  Yikes...

Other than the guac, , the service was good.  The staff was attentive and the food was excellent .

I normally do my own nails so I'm a little picky when it comes to shops. The place was SUPER small and staffed with about 4 technicians. They didn't turn anyone away even though they were clearly busy. They guy who did my toes told a customer he'd be with her in 5 when he hadn't even started my French tip. So let's say my pedi was rushed. They charge extra for salt scrub. My feet still had a rough spot and they weren't even that bad to begin with. The line on my French tip wasn't crisp. They played E news on the tv so that was nice. I paid $29 for a 10 min pedi and crooked white French tip.

I wrote at length about how much I liked Apothecary so I decided to see what the new place looked like.  Apparently, that whole block is now safe, popular, and popping on the weekends (who knew?).  Went there on a Saturday night and was seated within 10 minutes (score).  Drinks were great (nice martini) and food was very tasty (burger was good but apps were just OK, either way portions were nice).  Service was top notch (which is a gamble in that block).

Really looking forward to Spring when the outdoor area is open and can definitely give up that 5th star.

Run of the Mill AYCE Sushi.

The Sushi chefs were great.  Friendly and seemed to be enjoying their work.  I really like spicy food so the chef made me a couple on the fly creations that were all pretty tasty.  They use habanero peppers instead of jalapeno and it was a nice change.  Their menu is pretty standard assortment of cooked and raw rolls and nigiri.  I thought their nigiri was sloppy and not that impressive.  

The reason I'm rating it so low is the entire restaurant REEKS of fish.  Bad sign when it comes to any Sushi joint in my opinion.

I'm so confused about all this talk about great pedicures.  I booked this place for me and a friend based off yelp reviews and it was a bit of a let down.  We both recieved the most basic pedicure service with a hot water soak, lotion, and trimmed and painted toes.  There was zero massage, zero hot wrap, no filing or trimming cuticles or tending to calluses.  My heels actually left rougher than when I walked in.  I guess I should not have expected so much from a $28 pedicure.  

They were extremely nice, but I had a very hard time understanding them.  Again, the service wasn't bad, just very basic.

I moved from Slidell a few months ago and ive been looking for a good sushi place to eat at. Well i went here and i loved it. I got the Crunch roll and the crawfish roll. It was soooooo good and the service was nice. The actual location need a lil pick me up lol So two days later i was craving some sushi so i decided to place a order for pick up. I asked for spicy mayo to go and when i got there i noticed i was charged 1.00 for the spicy mayo. That was the only thing i didnt agree on lol But other then that i like the place....Two thumbs up :)

Below is a list of the items ordered at our table.  Everyone was very satisfied with their meal.  We come here often and we are always pleased.
Being from New Orleans, on this visit, I was not impressed with the Shrimp Étouffée, It was nothing like an Étouffée should be.  But I will be back.

Pulled Pork Tacos
Shrimp Bruschetta 
White Bean Artichoke Dip
Caesar Salad

Burger
Shrimp étouffée
Pasta Special
Salmon
Braised Short  Rib
Butternut Squash
Lancaster Chicken
Creme Brûlée
Bistro French Toast
Tiramisu 
Chocolate Molten Cake

My fiance and I were at Opry Mills during lunchtime, and we decided to stop by TGI Fridays for a bite to eat. The servers are very friendly, but the service is kinda slow. I ordered the chicken tenders with fries, and asked for a side of ranch dressing...it was forgotten about and the waitress didn't ask me about it until I was nearly done eating my food. The food still tasted good though.

The environment was nice and clean, but I did notice after finishing my food that the fork I received (which I didn't use) was dirty.

Hopefully the service will be a little better next time we are here.

Dapper's a great salon. Er...it's actually a barber shop and, as such, it caters to men. 

That said, Josepha cuts women's hair and she does a great job of it. She's given me my best cuts in Tucson. Plus, it's super fun to watch the skillful and sexy barbers give guys a close shave with a straight razor. 

P.S. My survey answers re: price and appointments are relevant to WOMEN only. As I understand it, men should NOT make appointments and men's cuts are very inexpensive. Women's cuts cost significantly more but it's worth it.

Coyote Wore Sideburns is a decent straight-to-the-point haircutting place. It's kind of like a nice guy with a good job who doesn't really play mind games or ride a motorcycle or challenge you intellectually or have too many tattoos or too many women on the side. 

And that's 'A-OK!' 

There's absolutely nothing wrong with direct and uncomplicated. However, the clever girl must be pro-active with a nice guy to make sure her needs are met. Go to the salon with ideas about how you'd like your hair to look, and I'm sure they'll be more than accommodating and helpful.

Love the location, perfect place to come to before hockey games and events etc. 

Beautiful room, beautiful staff, and some interesting drink specials ... however, the service is extremely, extremely slow. 

Took about 17-20 minutes to be acknowledged,  then another 15 minutes to get two basic drinks.  Not cocktails, just pour out of the bottle drinks. 

Give yourself an extra hour if you plan to have a  drink, and like the gentleman sitting beside us warned us, you'll be hard pressed to get two. 

The friendly staff & sexy room is what makes you come back.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
So I have not been to this actual establishment. Instead, I visited the food truck version this past weekend at the Tomato Arts Festival in EastNasty. After my friend suggested we try some, I just went for it. 

The options were limited but interesting at the food truck version. I went with the salted caramel and a sweet corn with black raspberry. I know... the second one sounds terrible, but it was so, so divine. 

I highly recommend you give this a try and suggest you don't get discouraged by the unusual flavors.

The least ghetto McDonald's in the area. The only other one is over on broad. No thanks. Overall it's fast and accurate. I never had a problem here. Then again I am not a commuter and also never came here with the rest of the drunks at 2am. It does have a preponderance of homeless people who harass diners for a " dolla yo so I can git a hamabuga". 

Don't give them any money. McDonald's takes food stamps when you are homeless. They want to buy drugs. You're not helping anyone when you give them money. 

Oh the fries are hot and fresh. 

-1 Star for the low lives and skells in the vicinity.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Second time visiting was a vast improvement from the first.  The first time I waited FOREVER for my coffee...this location was extremely busy during both of my visits where I went inside to order.  The line moved quickly and the barista was very polite.  We had a bit of a longer than anticipated wait for our coffees but I think that is do to them focusing on the drive thru line.  I feel they could be a bit more organized and the place could be a bit tidier but my coffee was delicious and the patio outside relaxing.  I hope they keep up the improvements as I'd like to keep coming back.

Finally stopped in at a time where there wasn't a crazy line and ordered two pizzas, cheese and pepperoni. Very friendly cashier. Clean, casually chic interior. The pizzas smelled great and I couldn't wait to get them home. We were very happy to see the generously sized slices and hearty amount of pepperoni. The cheese pizza was a little under-cheesed, the sauce and crust were the overwhelming elements on that one. The pepperoni  pizza was great though, with the tangy sauce adding the perfect foil to the salty meat. Definitely will be back for the pepperoni pizza.

I can't tell you what the rooms are like. I can't tell you if the bed is comfortable or if the shower is hot. I can't tell you if there's a tasty free breakfast or if they have a good channel selection. 

I can't tell you these things because despite the fact that we had a reservation, they gave the room away and when we showed up after a long drive, we were turned away.

Don't worry the fellow said, this happens all the time.

It happens all the time? Now as a general rule, if you find yourself saying that something happens all the time, it's probably a good sign that you're in the wrong business.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I have been waiting to go to La Viola ever since a friend told me it was their favorite BYOB in Philadelphia. I went there on a Wednesday night after leaving the Academy of Music. I had pasta on the mind the second I sat down in my seat at the ballet so I couldnt wait to get dinner, get my big spoon and my fork and start twirlin away at some spaghetti. 

Service was top notch. I ordered the special which was the Stuffed Chicken with fontina cheese, spinach and roasted reds. mmm mmm mmm. delicious. My fellow diner got spaghetti with shrimp which was also amazing.

Very reasonably priced. I can't wait to go back!

I got dragged back by a friend who was in a karoke contest.  We stopped in for dinner first and since it was a friday in lent, being the good Catholic boy that I am I ordered the fish option off the menu.  It was called cod sea dogs, which were basically fried cod in the shape of a large hotdog.  There were two of these along with fries, and they were very tasty.  

The service here is pretty good and the crowd was a bit better this time, and the PBR option for beer was way cheaper than budweiser.  I had a bit better time out there the second go around.

Been craving doughnuts for about a week. Finally decided to stop at DD while running errands. Sadly typical DD. Donuts not particularly fresh tasting. They don't make any doughnuts in house. I was told a few years ago by an employee the doughnuts come from Ohio, that may have changed. Service not very friendly at the drive thru. Didn't recieve a thank you and I was handed a half closed box. I can't wait till Krispy Kream gets back in town it will give DD someone to look up to that knows how to serve fresh in house dountuts.

Between 630-730 Sunday night Crust was almost empty. When we pulled in the parking lot we weren't sure they were open. We sat in the dining room and our server was the bartender , when he could pull himself away from the football game on TV. It is not true for all bartenders but in my experience they can't tend bar be a server and watch TV and be attentive to customers. Hummus was off tonight. Not nearly as garlic and kind of dry and thick. Strom Calzone was very good with a nice thin crust. Marinara for dipping was very watery but had a good flavor. Not our best experience at Crust but also not our worst either.

my tire blew out on rt 42 and it was difficult to get the lug nuts off at another place then i had to tow it to sts. They worked tirelessly  to get if off and i knew the rim may have to be scrapped so while they where working on that i went looking at the junk yard for the rim  found it and they charged me a reasonable price . the bolts  things that the tire sits on had to be replaced . Scott was very informative and through with letting me know what they could do and the several options as he progressed with the work so we where always on the same page i will be back soon!
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: This is a one man shop and being that I like to support local businesses I figured I'd give it a try.   I told the barber exactly what I wanted.  When he said he was done I looked in the mirror to see that this was probably the worst shaped haircut I ever had received. I asked him to shorten the sides and his response was "I did what you told me, I'm not going to keep on cutting and cutting".   What barber doesnt do what you asked?  I left without giving him a tip he was so rude and did such a bad job.   Not to mention the place was dirty-he hadn't swept up any hair all day.  I don't particularly like walking on peoples cut hair.

This is not a review on the sushi.  I had a few bites of my friend's order and it was just average compared to the sushi bars in SF, CA.  

However, the Korean owners sure made a good Beef Bulgogi!  It was just a tad on the sweet side of the dish but it was near perfect.  The Hamachi Kama was also pretty well done.  Those are two pretty hard dishes to do well, so judging by that, the rest can't be that bad.  Thumbs up from me.  

Plus, free edamame and green tea ice cream are always a welcomed bonus.

Why are so many Japanese restaurants in Tucson owned by Koreans?!  Also, what is up with the lack of Chinese cuisine???    I'm perplexed.

Back when I went to Jay's I had no idea Philly had so many greater sushi restaurants.

Went in with my girlfriend, the location is quite small. The service was slow and the prices questionable for the quality. We ordered 3 rolls: Black Dragon (5/10), Romantic(6.5/10), and Spicy Tuna(3/10). Nothing to write home about.

I truly hope that since then, Jay's Favorite Sushi has picked up its act and started to produce some higher quality sushi. The location is really prime and I'm always in support of a sushi establishments survival.

Straub's could use some remodeling at the front entrance/cashier area. The location across the Chase Park Plaza and nice Central West End neighborhood makes me think that at one time, this place had more gourmet options, but due to the economy, the selection of fine foods has decreased over time. However, there is still a nice deli, bakery, and cheese selection and quite a bit of imported sweets and savory grocery items in the aisles.
