In addition to this location, there are three more locations. I have heard good things about Straub's deli and baked goods so when I return to St. Louis, I stop by the other locations as well.

Great downtown location next to the Arch. Nice, modern, spacious, comfortable rooms, ours had a view of the Arch made this AAA Four Diamond hotel a fairly pleasant stay. We scored a good deal on hotwire.com for around $90.00 (tax included). The downside is the lack of attention to detail. The coffee maker was filthy and had white growth in it. The tub was filled with dirty water and debris floating in it. The hotel sports bar is lively and has reasonable food and drink prices. On Sundays, the hotel sports bar has $5 build your own Bloody Mary! Yum, yum! Overnight valet is $26.00. Public parking is available--see hotel website for details.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I felt like I was cheating on my regular place. 

I went here because my schedule was tight and I needed a place that was close to my office.  But, they did a decent job, the price seemed on par and the turnaround time was okay, so I'm happy to have a back-up place.  Their attention to detail is not quite what I'm used to, though: for example, the linings in a couple pairs of my wool pants were pressed kind of twisted.  They worked themselves out after wearing for a bit, of course, but it was a little annoying at first.  So, not bad...more of a 3.25 or so than a three, and they're still newish, so maybe...?
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Fast, efficient, and reasonable. Went in (without an appointment) around 8:30am. Oil change and tire rotation in about 30 minutes! Suggested some things that needed to be fixed, but gave me no pressure to do anything I wasn't going in for that day. For my Dodge Dakota truck, it costs me $37 (with tax and labor) to get a basic oil change and tire rotation. I was able to watch the entire time as their waiting room looks out into the bay. Great service, women friendly (you know how that goes sometimes!) and reasonable prices. Ask for Tony!
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: We have been to the Countryside Mall location in the past but we thought to try this one out.  We were there when they first opened and got the buffet.  There is a mini-salad bar with a choice of Greek or Caesar salad with choice of dressings.  For hot food, there was pastitsio disguised as lasagne, stuffed shells, Italian sausage, Buffalo wings and some very good pizza.  We had a choice of 4 different types: cheese, pepperoni, sausage and a veggie pizza.  Saving the best for last, they had wonderful baklava for dessert.  Under $20 for two people, you can't beat it!

I know, I know, this restaurant gets a lot of grief from reviewers because it's supposedly not authentic, blah, blah, blah. Well, we went there last night and had a pretty good meal.  We started with the white queso and chips. For entrees, we had a couple of their combo dinners.  We had customized our orders and they delivered on what we wanted.  The food was hot, fresh and the chips kept coming.  For the money, we had a good Mexican-ish meal.  Oh, it was Tuesday 'All You Can Eat Tacos' night and the place was packed!  If you haven't been there in awhile, go by and give it a try.

I stopped by to indulge one of my guilty pleasures:  a sausage, egg and cheese croissant.  It was fresh and delicious.  The staff all looked new and enthusiastic.  Management was there as well to oversee operations.  The remodeling of this location came out very nicely.  It had been quite a run down location with a persistent roof leak. Now, it has a more mid-century feel, inside and out.  They now have a TV in the dining room.  Unfortunately, it was tuned to FOX entertainment news.  The TV station made my breakfast not so pleasant...too much vitriol for so early in the morning, I guess.

Another favorite of mine & my honey's!! love their food - we always get the chips & pico de giuo (did I spell that right?) - that is soo good! & I get one of 2 things - either the black bean soup (minus the cheese - although that is really good to keep in) but I will add chopped avocado (side order) - yum!! my other fav is the Carne Asada taco mmmmmm!!! My honey gets the taco salad & always enjoys that - or something else that is smothered w/ cheese - looks fab (& hey melted cheese - for real - YUM-O!!) the staff are great - really friendly!!!

I only go here for the kids most of the time(since reading Fast Food Nation 10 years ago) and all I can say is WTF is up with this Mcdonalds? Sometimes their service great and sometimes its downright awful! The double drive-through is hit or miss and today I had to ask the person behind me to back out from behind me so I could LEAVE. Three cars ordered and went thought on the outside lane while the car in front of me and I waited and waited. After five minutes of this, I left. Another thing that they used to be really bad about was not putting everything in your order. 

On the + side, the staff is usually very friendly.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: This place is great for studying and I am really happy to have found it. The set-up and decor is great- you can sit on a couch or spread out at a table and the music is normally pretty decent too. Nothing extra special in terms of food or drinks, but you can get snacks if you're hungry and I have tried a couple of the baked goods too. Everything is decently-priced, but my only gripe is that it's cash only. I am a sucker for anything peanut butter and the best thing is that you can get a peanut butter latte here, which makes me a happy camper.

How aptly named this place is! I read about this place online before I visited Nola and I am so excited that I made it out here. The space is super nice, very clean, light, and open. I got a slice of cheese and a slice with mushrooms and pancetta as well as a beer on tap and ate them in the backyard. Thin NYC slice perfection!

Everything about my experience was perfect, from the service to the decor (including the fact that you can put Sriracha on your pizza!). My only complaint is that I wish they were open later because I would have loved to have a late-night slice! Regardless, I loved it here, and you will too.

Jake's is a typical neighborhood bar.  I ventured in once in a while only because it's conveniently located to my house.  Inside, one will find things somewhat dark and smoky with some pool tables in the back.  The food is typical American pub fare, but no dish is truly remarkable.  The service is adequate, and the patrons are the usual working-man and friends catching a game on the TV. 

 If the juke box is on, then it's probably playing Nickelback or a country song.  Parking can be an issue on the weekend and during sports games.  Basically, if you're in the area and don't feel like going to Broad Ripple or downtown then stop by.

Walked in not knowing what to expect but felt somewhat assured when I saw four customers waiting ahead of me. Obviously repeat customers. I had the opportunity to watch the barbers at work for the 20-25 minute wait. Professional, friendly, and they knew what they were doing.

Joe was my barber, and he was every bit the master barber. Turns out he is a stonemason as well, and he gave me tips on restoring a retainer wall at home.

All in all, a great deal. Old school style and quick. I'll be checking out their Jenkintown location as well. 

[They are located in the Suburban Station Concourse, not very easy to find but worth the search.]

Desk staff aren't very friendly, but the valets make up for the front desk demeanor.  As a HH Diamond member I have never received an upgrade at this hotel.  In fact, last time they put me in a room that faced a brick wall!!  The room prices are reasonable, but the parking pricing is a bit over the top.  Really like the room where breakfast is served and they do an exceptional job for a Hampton Inn.  On balance, this is a 3 1/2 star place.    Location is perfect if your headed to the Quarter (and who isn't?).
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Honestly surprised by the bad reviews, but they're a bit outdated perhaps. Forewarning - I probably wouldn't be clamoring to return just cause the prices are exorbitant and the selection is a tad underwhelming - but lemme tell you something about the chicken salad sandwich. Shit was BOMB, hence why it warranted a review. Fresh and flavorful large pieces of chicken, eensy bits of celery and carrot, green onion, red raisins (not the promised golden ones), walnuts, and arugula, all perfectly dressed in not too much Mayo. But the best part was that fantastic whole grain sourdough. Soft and warm but still crispy. Yum.

One of a kind!

Downtown isn't ideal for me but this place is worth it. I was initially looking for a place to get a slight beard trim and saw that they have very reasonably priced beard and hair packages ($35). So i gave it a shot.
They have a very easy to use booking system on their website. I booked with Chadwick who is an awesome guy who did a great job on my hair and beard. He also cleaned up my neck and cheeks with a straight razor. 
The shop is easy to get to and there is some street parking in the area. 
Has a great old time barber shop feel and they play some great tunes in there.

Had Subway for lunch today and forgot to check-in... so checked in later! 

I love their spicy italian subs, with double meat... and the creamy sriracha sauce that they have. Sometime I get them hot, sometimes cold. But they are always delicious. 

The staff at this location are friendly and willing to do whatever it takes.  They had to find the sriracha in their cooler, since the apparently don't get many requests for it. It was appreciated! 

Location is clean, and looks like they keep it up.  A good lunch if you are in the area!

Best Sashimi I have had in Tampa, and really glad to find this place. Fish is fresh, firm and very delicious. Served in beautiful plate settings, and with plenty of wasabi and pickled ginger. The Tri-Color Sashimi plate (Maguro, Hamachi, and Sake) was a nice portion, almost too much!  Had a serving of Toro also, since my girlfriend had never had it... and I wanted to see what the quality and portion was like. It was delicious, but I thought the portion was a bit small for the price.

Service was wonderful also.. very attentive and friendly staff!

Highly recommended!

Wow... Marco's really blew it tonight. I ordered my "usual" online... Pepperoni Magnifico with sausage and bacon added. In the attached photo... the top pizza was what I usually get. Tonight the bottom pizza is what I got. A pepperoni Magnifico without pepperoni, lol! I called to let them know, and yes... they gave me a store credit for the pizza. Said they were training new people. I was really surprised... of all the pizza places I have ever eaten at, Marcos has been the most consistent. So hopefully I can update my next review with it being back to 5 stars! If not, there are a lot of pizza places, right?

Went for a special date night with a gift card from my family. Decided with my fiancé to order the chef's tasting menu without the wine pairing (we were having drinks and decided to just enjoy the food) 
Each course that came out was better than the next. Started off with some pork offerings and  then had the egg custard all of which were dynamite. My favorite part of the night was the steak course which was cooked to perfection.  The dinner ended with a lemon custard which was delicate, and tasty and tart and a wonderful end to a wonderful meal. 
Would definitely go back to enjoy another meal if I was not leaving town. . .

only three stars here becuase even though they are quick , the food seems rushed and sometimes doesn't come out all the way wrapped - I would rather sit in a long line at the one next to the base and get good quality and drive a bit farther  than go to this one by my house and have to feel jilted .... 3 stars until the food is better qaulity.... (what am i saying this is fast food) until they take their time and not rush the packaging of the mostly processed bad stuff for my body that i shouldn't be eating anyway....
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
this place is really , really out of the way. in fact if you leave from the fair grounds and head south.....far south , like the mountains get a lot bigger south  you eventually come to a stop light and a brief glimpse of civilization! 
the road runner market ...... which has stock of gas, water, and jerky of all sorts..... and an ATM.... but no money in this ATM..... on fair weekend!
 I would hope to have either been able to get money out or cash back but neither was available here.... so 2 stars for you buddy... I drove a long way and only got some bottles water and jerky......

Cold weather and I saw 3 Avis buses, 3 Enterprise, 2 Thrifty and Sixt and by the time Hertz finally rolled around I was not thrilled.  Every other airport I have rented from Hertz is the 3 to everyone else's one.  Then I picked up my car and was 9 deep leaving to check out - no Clear expedited line so another 20 minutes out of my life again.  Needless to say not my favorite experience and I am President's Circle with Hertz.  Staff was friendly at the exit but took way to long for me to get to the agent, and way way , way to long for the Bus to pick me up.  Room for improvement here in their process.

Location and staff are top notch - very professional team and exceeded my expectations.

The hotel is older but solid in comfort, safety and convenience.  Wish they had a full size coffee maker though as I travel with my own coffee and those tiny cup makers wear me out as I drink 8 cups first thing in the morning.

Only thing I dislike is the Fitness Center - the treadmills are somewhat dangers as your front feet are prone to hitting the front of the machine and possible losing footing.  The wi-fi also does not perform well in that area which makes an hour run seem longer.

I would stay here again and kudos to the Staff
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Sat at the bar and the server was more interested in texting every 5 minutes and talking to other workers than serving - which is the norm here based on other reviews.  

Had to flag her down after a few minutes and ask for a menu and a Diet Coke - after that the drinks were refilled and the meal was fine.  Had a bleu cheese burger and it was alright though the burger had virtually no seasoning the cheese compensated for it.  

It is airport food that is standard fare - next time I will eat at Cheesburger Cheeseburger next door or the Taco place - nothing to write home about here but apparently to the server it is text book worthy.

Covid has removed most of the benefits of staying at a Marriott but the proximity to the airport and check in is well worth it.  The staff is friendly, the hotel takes Covid precautions and you can walk to the ticketing in minutes.  They have adjusted pricing to reflect the reduced services so well worth the value for travelers.  Concierge Lounge is closed, restaurant seating is closed, and the gift shop is open occasionally.  The only thing I don't like here and other hotels as well when they do it is to pump in perfume smells into the common areas.  It immediately causes my allergies to kick in and I start sneezing and eyes watering.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Stopped in for a late night snack last week. We chowed on the Ultimate Spicy Tuna Roll and Nogales Roll. I loved the spiciness of the jalapeno in the Nogales Roll. The tuna roll was good as well. I appreciate that the bottle of beer they served me was ICE cold, just the way it should be. 

The service was average at best. Not very personable, but adequate for the most part. The interior of the restaurant is nice. Though the drink menu located on the little "A" stand on the table was dirty, torn and wrinkled up from water stains. They really should keep these fresh. It gives a careless impression.

For my purposes, this place is perfect. Quick, cheap, and pretty delicious. I get takeout here often, and the staff is always courteous. I have never done delivery, I probably never will. My order is always ready in 10 minutes, and I have never had a problem. This is honestly some of the best Chinese takeout I've ever had. Most often, I order chicken fried rice. I typically do not feel poorly after eating it, and I'm someone who can be very effected by greasy food. I gotta say, I'll miss this spot when I move.

I like this location because it is really convenient location to meet for business with Carmel, Zionsville, and Westfield people.  The parking situation can be a bit tough with the other businesses that share the parking lot.  There is plenty of seating as this is one of the larger Starbucks that I have been too.  Since I spend so much time in coffee shops, I will admit that I am hyper critical of Starbucks and unless they wow me, they get average marks.  This would be another one that met expectations and with that I am pleased.

I am a sucker for good coffee, and there are very few local options that I have found, so I end up defaulting to Starbuck, but that does not mean settling.  This particular location could benefit from some more seating, or maybe some different arrangement of seating, but all in all, it's adequate.  I didn't like that I ordered the Narino 70 cold brew on their menu, because it's on their menu, but "they don't sell that here" was the response I got.  That was frustrating as I don't like false or dated advertising, hence the three stars.

I have to agree with reviewer Kirstie N about the love hate relationship.  I tend to Love them a bit more than not though.  I have had awesome and the next can have the WTH is this drink effect.  That aside, we were homeless here last week, no motel, and no job to go to with the customer messing it all up, so we sat for 3 hours in front of this Starbucks without getting kicked out :-)  We kept going in and buying drinks as our outside table 'rent'.

Staff here was great, and yes, the drinks here were awesome this day

I kind of left here saying "meh". The waiter wasn't rude, but he wasn't very friendly either. For example, when the plates arrived, he just put them infront of us without saying a word. I got the mediterean pasta and it didn't have much flavor. However, I got the chocolate sushi for dessert and it was probably the most unique and yummy dessert I've had in a while. Another good thing is that the bottles of wine were priced really well. So, I'd say 3 stars with the dessert and wine, but 2 if it were dependent on the service and food.

Rita's is pretty awesome.  Their Italian ices (or "water ice," as they call it in Philly, where Rita's originates) are excellent.  Cold, tasty, refreshing, treats include both ices (think of powdered ice that's flavored with fruit, chocolate, or vanilla flavors), custards, or blended desserts with candy pieces.

I've been several times, and the counter people are always very friendly.  They're patient and let me try any flavor I like.

It closes in the fall, then reopens in the Spring, but during warm (or hot) weather months, it is a wonderful way to cool off.

I've been to this Dunkin Donuts multiple times, and the vibe I always get is that they'll get to me whenever they're good and ready.  I'm always waiting for them, they never acknowledge me when I come in, and I'm waiting even though there's no one in front of me.

My understanding is that Dunkin Donuts was in the area some time in the past, left, and then returned.  If this is the experience I'm always going to get (and good service at Dunkin Donuts is hard to come by), then I'd just as soon they leave again.

The wifi is decent, but the coffee is nothing to write home about, and I think the donuts are overpriced.

I like City Fitness for a number of reasons. First, it's on my way home from work, so I don't really have an excuse not to go. Second, all I do is cardio (I do weight training at home), and I like that there are TVs on all of the cardio machines. It makes working out that much more bearable. There also are a ton of machines, so I can always do what I want with almost no wait.

There's a parking lot, which is super helpful.

It's also cheap, they have enrollment specials all the time, keep an eye on the website!
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Delicious sushi with less rice and more fish. Most places have a very similar style menu but not this place. Their menu features new ingredients that can't be found in town.
The location is out of the way which could make it a problem for those willing to drive from Sparks and South/Mid Reno. The Restaurant is big and spacious with comforting interior design. At night the place lights up with beautiful neon lighting. Also, the nice fountain inside soothes the mind. From talking with the owner, He constructed most of the interior himself instead of paying contractors. Very impressed.

We ordered some sushi takeout from here and it was prepared as perfectly as if we were staying for dinner at the restaurant.  We used to have a favorite sushi place 40 minutes from our house, so it is wonderful to know that there is incredible sushi just down the road in King of Prussia.  The fish is fresh and the presentation is impeccable, which resulted in some serious deliciousness.  Looking forward to sitting down at the restaurant for my next sushi fix.

 Now if only I could find good wings around here.

After I wrote my previous review, I was contacted by Joe from Landmark who apologized for the experience that we had, sent us a gift card to the restaurant and asked us to give them another try.  We did that tonight and it was like eating at a new restaurant.  The first thing we noticed was that they removed the crab dip from the menu and had quite a few new items.  Our server was friendly and attentive, the food was delicious, and we had a lovely and relaxed night out.  I'm impressed.  This was the first time in my experience that a restaurant has listened to the customer and made changes for the better.  We will return.

My husband and I visited on a Friday night and had a great experience. We walked in without a reservation although it was early. Our kids ordered from the kids menu. One had the pasta dish and the other had chicken strips. Both meals were HUGE and one could have easily fed them both. The pasta dish had some of the best red sauce I've ever had. I had the garlic hamburger with a side salad. The homemade salad dressing was delish, and the burger tasted like it had been grilled and not fried. My husband had the fried chicken and it lived up to it's reputation.  Simply delicious. We will definitely go back!

There are some tasty mexican eats inside this hidden gem.  You'll have to search them out and explore a couple times.  Make sure you try the tres leches cake and don't be afraid of trying something new.

On the weekend they have roasted lamb or goat that is fantastic and I'd recommend it. 

Burritos aren't bad and worth a try.  My family likes their enchiladas. I've have their 4 or 5 mini tacos and have enjoyed those.

I'm sure you'll like this place next time you are in town.

This is a great place to go with friends and bring your own beer and wine and enjoy the service and atmosphere.

Solid Hertz location...I always seem to luck into upgrades here.  The crew that checks you out when you return your car are always friendly, professional, and efficient.  I would give them another star, but as previous Yelpers have mentioned the wait time for the bus can be brutal....15 minutes seems to be the norm.  Not sure what the deal is.

The folks at the counter can be a bit salty.....I have witnessed at least one incident with another customer per visit.  However, they have always been great with me.

Dined here last night..The Overall atmosphere was quite dull..Although I'm a fan of all the little pictures of Goats all over the place..Our Waitress was amazing and very attentive. She was happy to recommend some dishes on the menu..We tried the Goat Quesadillas and Fried Goat Cheese appetizers..both were good..and finished off the meal with the lamb burger...which was not bad either...the house made potato chips that came with the lamb were quite amazing...Overall, not a bad spot, but the vibe is off here and maybe it will get better as more and more people get to know about this place...

I decided to stop by Jeni's on Sunday afternoon to see if it lived up to its hype. I am pleased to say it definitely did. 

I had the White House Cherry - which had cherries, white chocolate and pistachios in it (side note : pistachios are definitely making a comeback...i called it). and a half scoop of the Whiskey and Pecans...both ice cream flavors went together perfectly. I also tried the grapefruit frozen yogurt - amazing. I will need to come back with friends to be able to try more flavors. 

very impressed.

I don't see myself getting too worked up or excited over dry cleaning.  However, this place has become my go-to.  The employees are friendly and always ask me if I need my clothes back by a certain day.  It's a funny question because I usually forget or get too busy and don't pick my stuff up for weeks!

Everything always looks great - I've never had issues with poor service or poor cleaning.  I even took a jacket in with a rip on a seam, and they stitched it up for me because I'm not talented enough to do stuff like that on my own!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Time for an update!  I've been using JJ's for YEARS and they've gotten even better lately!  They installed new software that makes it even more convenient to do my dry cleaning.  I set up an account, and now when I drop off my dry cleaning, I get a text when it's ready, and they automatically charge my debit card when I pick it up, so it's as quick as possible!  I see they offer pickup and delivery, which is also great.  Not necessary for me because I live close and do my shopping at the Smith's in the shopping center, but also a great feature.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Alright, it's a Dunkin' Donuts, but who doesn't love a donut?
I like the bavarian creme best.  I have to say that I'm not happy with the amount of creme in the donut, it's like a tiny dab that I have to take 2 bites from each direction to get to it.  And it's the star of the donut!

The coffee is good.  Dunkin' coffee has always been really good.  That's why they sell it in the store too!  It's that good!

But, it's a Dunkin' Donuts, it's definitely consistent with any other Dunkin' Donuts.  But, it's convenient and it's not $5 for a cup of coffee!

Quick and cheap.  Delicious large breakfast burritos, usually.  It is what it is.  Sometimes we just go across the parking lot and take out food from El Molinitos if we want items with chicken.  I do not like the chicken (burritos or enchiladas) at Nico's.  My wife really likes the carne asada burritos.... lots of meat, ground beef tacos okay too, but any other toppings (cheese, guacamole, sour cream, etc. are a la carte... extra and a little expensive for this type of carry out restaurant).  Staff could be friendlier and learn to smile.  Also need to improve on the nachos... much better elsewhere.

I've lived in Boise for more than 30 years. Louie's has always been around. They moved into Meridian about 10 years ago. I grew up in a large family so it was very seldom that we ate out. When we did we would go to Louie's for pizza. At the time, I thought it was terrific.

Going back to Louie's after all these years I think my expectations were set way too high. In reality, this is Boise Italian food. The menu is based around bland average food. The portions are large but the taste is bland. 

If you want a pizza and exceeds the quality of Pizza Hut this is your place. If you're looking for fine Italian dining don't stop here.

The reviews for this place are all over the place. Some loved it and some had horrible things to say. I decided to give it a shot and come to my own conclusion. 
Yes, the place was empty on a Friday night. But the service, food and experience was great. The burrata cheese with roasted beets app was absolutely delicious.  My friend & I both ordered pasta and enjoyed our meals so much, we both ate every last morsel, so I think it's safe to say we enjoyed our experience. I is a bit on the expensive side though.

I've tried this place twice based on recommendations. The ambiance is nice, prices are reasonable, service was excellent,  but the food --- not so much. The food was barely OK. The pizza was soggy and too many topping --I basically just at the cheese and toppings. I always consider pizza a "safe" selection at an Italian place --- not so much/  My colleagues ordered ravioli and only got 3 lobster ravioli in the lunch portion. The lunch menu was also served with salad but it still was a bit of a shabby portion for grown men. The taste was just ok. We all left underwhelmed and  bit disappointed.

Whoah. $28 for a 2x4" salmon steak w/ a few stewed cherry tomatoes on the side? No way...no way! I was expecting a hearty salmon filet with some decent compliments on the side, instead what I got was something as pretentious as you would expect from 'American Psycho'. The waitress reeled off the specials and changes to the menu, clearly not caring whether or not we were listening. She took FOREVER to bring our drinks, then was still snooty throughout the meal. All in all, for a beer and the salmon I ended up paying $43.00 for a meal that reasonably should have cost $27.00. Wasn't pleased, definitely not going back.

Ruby's Seafood Festival is on right now.  A whole host of different seafood entree to meet anyone's expectations.  As a matter of fact, Brandon Z., our waiter, suggested an entree that did not even hit the menu officially until later this month.  I enjoyed it and they prepared the steamed veggies just as I like them.  Great evening with friends and their salad bar is now complimentary in addition to your meal.  Big plus.  For me, the salad bar at Ruby Tuesday's is a find in itself as it features better ingredients than you normally discovery.

Mike Express Car wash rocks!  

The service and staff are always on top of their game.  It is best not to hit them during peaks times as they speed the car wash conveyor up to rush you through.  If you are not satisfied with the quality of your wash, they will run you through again for FREE.

This location is always top notch though.  One instance, I was driving a truck that had over sized tires on it and they moved me to a bay for FREE, since I could not drive through the tunnel.  

Mike's Express sells great car wash packages and I always buy the "6 washes for the price of 4" book or the "unlimited monthly" wash package when it is promoted.

I was hoping this location would improve when it was bought and changed to Giant. Sadly, they still have the longest lines and fewest checkouts. It's the exact opposite of the larger store in Willow Grove. 

So, it's a grocery store chain, with all the good and bad that brings. This location includes a coffee bar, hot food, cold deli, floral, etc. 

I'll continue to visit this Giant. All I can say is, I'm glad for the neighborhood to still have something in the area -- even if it's no better/ no worse than the chain it took over.

This is an all you can eat place that at $27/adult isn't bad.  But if you ordered from the regular menu, you come to realize just how mediocre the quality is.  Maki rolls are OK, but mine were so cold they had clearly been premade and sat in the fridge.  Oyster ponzu was missing the ponzu and the coating was really heavy - like an A+W onion ring. 

So if you are really hungry and want to eat several plates of rolls and greasy tempura then this is for you. Granted sometimes that is just what you're craving. But avoid the squid.

This is a welcome addition to the northeast, serving both sushi and a wider range of Japanese-inspired dishes.

The beef tataki is lightly seared and cut thicker than the raw version of this dish. The sauce was a nice blend of citrus and acid.

The rolls were tight and there are some unique combinations of flavours.  The noodle dish we had was very salty.

Overall, it was a good meal. I found the presence of large, bright televisions disturbing to the quiet, clean room design. So unless I am in the area, I am not likely to go back.

Located in a sad, dated little strip mall in Brentwood, this place came with a decent reputation.  It did not deliver.  The bento box meals were quite expensive so we opted for ordering rolls and some shared plates.  The oyster ponzu was the best of those, with the gyosa the best deal.  The tofu kara age was too soft and the bowl too deep which meant it was swimming in sauce.

The barbequed eel was tightly wrapped and tasty.  The salmon skin roll was messy and tasted a bit off. Nigiri was OK.

There is better sushi to be had in the Park.

Hadn't been back for a while and was happy to see it was actually better than I remembered.  Arrived on a hot summer night and the place was packed.  But they quickly cleaned a table and we were soon enjoying Jarritos sodas and a yummy chorizo and melted cheese starter.  I stuck with the chicken enchiladas and they were very good.  Rojas sauce had great flavour.  Son had the large, grilled pork tacos and loved them.

The chips served with a tasty salsa (which was different from our last visit) came from a bag, but were crunchy and not at all greasy.

Great dinner for under $40.

This place is the epitome of a great hole in the wall find.  From  the  70s vintage floral upholstery  to the back entrance off the alley, it undersells it self and sets you up for a great surprise.  The food is good -- not fancy, not at all pretentious - but good. 

A group from work made the trek on the coldest day of the year and we were rewarded for our efforts -- the chicken hot pot was the best example this dish I have ever had.  The seafood dish with shrimp, scallops and squid was very generous for the price of about $10. The beef in black bean sauce was nice and spicy.  

I will certainly return, but only with adventurous companions.

Have been to this place four times. The first time we were so impressed.  The melted cheese and veggie starter was great.  We also shared the grilled meat dish which was a generous mix of various meats served in a stone chalice.  Very tasty. I would have given a five star review after that visit.

Our other visits have been less impressive. We treated family friends one night and were not impressed by how the vegetarian options are so limited and there was no willingness to adapt enchiladas or tacos with veggies.  Fajitas were a messy plate of grilled meats, no veggies or cheese. 

So I would go back but with much lower expectations.  Too bad.

We came in with a reservation and were seated about 15-20 minutes after the reservation time. This feels like and old time place that doesn't care about the food quality. Our server was friendly and any questions she couldnt answer she found out for us. We had a good time while we were there because the company we were with but the drink was meh as well as the food. No attention to detail on food presentation and the salad was Olive Garden quality. It's just not my type of place. If you enjoy divey, old time feel, then you'll like it here. If not skip it and you'll be happy you did.

Salam Market is a great place to experience something unique. This Mediterranean/Middle Eastern place is a great lunch spot to enjoy. The one thing that I would recommend is the schwarma. I usually order double meat (beef and chicken) and spicy. I am not one who really likes spicy foods but with Salam Market's schwarmas you can't go wrong. The service is fast and easy and they are extremely friendly. If you have never tried felafel's or schwarma before, I would go here for your first time. I don't think you will be disappointed! The homemade hummus is great as well and is much more fresh than the hummus you see at the grocery stores ;)

This is a perfect place for a quick, delicious meal.  A simple atmosphere, kid friendly, and fresh food make for a nice lunch or dinner.  I highly recommend the flautas, cheese enchilada, and cebollitos, however, everything I tried was really good.  
  Recently, I noticed they are building a Carrettas near by. Ugh. 
  I truly hope people will not overlook T. Corona because the food and service are A LOT better here.  I gave 4 stars because it is not the fanciest place, they could step up the decor. That being said, it is refreshing being so very simple. It's definitely my go to place to satisfy a Mexican food craving on the fly!

CASH only!

I hit up China House based on their Yelp reviews.  I was driving home from the airport and wanted to try a 'new to me take out restaurant.'  The woman who picked up the phone was easy to talk to and she advised me on what was best to order for what I was describing to her.  I got beef lomein and one spring roll.  The food was delicious and full of meat.  It was also a good temperature...very hot (warmth).

This is definitely a take out place.  I wouldn't recommend eating in unless you were in a hurry.  There are two tables in the take out area.  The interior of the restaurant is very run down looking.

I can unequivocally say that I am not a Drury Hotels fan nor any of their off brands for that matter. 

Staying at the Pear Tree Inn is like taking a step back into time and not in a good way, more like a trip back to the early 80's to a Howard Johnson or a Ramada Inn. 

Besides the garish 1980's look in form of carpet, cheap furniture, brass lights and mirrored closet doors they only change your linen every 5th day. While I am as environmentally conscious as the next guy, 5 days seems a bit excessive. Additionally it does not seem to reflect on the price compared to better chains such as to the adjacent located Marriott or Crowne Plaza.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Brunch!  With a capital B.  Come hungry.  I mean, really hungry.  There is so much selection and yumminess - that you may need to fast ahead of time.  Also, it isn't cheap, so be prepared.

The Bloody Mary bar was quite nice - as was the selection of smoked fish, grilled veggies, and amazing small desserts.  I actually was very impressed with the quality of the desserts.  Often the table of desserts at brunches like this are only so-so, but this brunch brought it.  There was a lot more to be had - crepes, omelets, small plates of meat, etc.  I just ran out of room in my stomach.
  
Service was fantastic.

Queso dip, margaritas, and guacamole were five stars.  Enchiladas, rice, and quesadillas were about three stars.  Weird ladies room (thank goodness it locks!) earned one star.  This place was looking alright and I would go back for the guac, ritas, and queso alone until...the manager refused to let us combine the buy one get one margarita special!  Apparently this special applies per person - the person who orders the full priced rita has to end up drinking both, can't order two then give the second to your date.  Ummm, what?!  Bummer.

I stopped in here needing a simple polish change on my fingers and toes.  The nail salon was clean and had a lot of designs to choose from.  Their color selection was so so, lots of reds and pinks but some funky colors.  So my nails were painted then dried under a fan with UV light and they looked great.  Unfortunately they chipped the next day.  One nail has the polish come off in a big sheet while the others got chips at the corners.  I didn't do anything to cause these chips - no dishes, cleaning, etc.- so I blame it on the base and top coat they used since the polish I brought was my own.  Bummer!

This USED to be our go to breakfast joint. It was your typical, towny diner. If you came here a few times, they considered you a regular. The staff is friendly, and the food was consistent and good. Now, flash forward to November of 2013, they completely renovated it from the decor to the food to the prices. I'm so disappointed. I want my average omelette and cup of coffee, not some fancy spinach eggs Benedict and cappuccino. If I wanted that, I would head down to Main Street to Winnie's. The service is super slow and the food is just average, especially for the price.

I've been coming here on and off  for a few years, and the quality seems to be dropping every time.

It is very over priced now, and not the same prices you see online.

The taste is not as good as it used to be either, and the portions seem smaller, definitely not the same as 3 years ago..

Our server was unavailable for long periods at a time, and not very attentive. You couldn't find him if you needed a refill, our food took a while coming out, and waited again for our check.

I think today's experience has resulted in it being my last  trip here. Unless they make some serious changes, I don't think I'll be spending my money here.

I tired liking this place, we came in at 8pm. (Wife & Daughter) on a Monday night for some dessert but everything I ate was way too sweet. The glaze was too thick and the selection was just all donuts with cereal on top.  Maybe I'll try going in the morning and seeing if they have a better selection. The place was very clean and the Employee were attentive. It had plenty of room for big groups and also had a kid/children's play wall with chalk and letter which is a plus for my toddler to keep her busy so I can try the donuts.

Splendid, yes. Unique, yes. Worth $2 per half scoop? Not sure about that. I mean it was good and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Judging by the line, Nashville considers the value worthy of the price. But when you consider the scoop price, I would guess a half gallon of Jenni's to run north of $50. I'm becoming more doubtful that we actually are in a recession.

Anyway, the homemade, freshly pressed waffle cones made my triple scoop of vanilla bean, whiskey pecan, and salty caramel delicious. And in the end a really nice, indulgent treat to ano already indulgent day.

Although in a strip mall, this upscale, yet medium casual Italian dining restaurant features some incredibly flavorful dishes. Service has been consistently attentive and the salads and entrées have always been exceptional. Perfect for dinner groups of 2, 4, 6, or even take out from the bar area. Nice wine selection. Reservation may be required for peak hours on Friday and Saturday evening. Very nice addition to this corner of Ladue Road in Ladue/Clayton area. Very central location, lots of easy parking! Hill-style Italian.

Location, location, location.  That is what this hotel has going for it.

I did not stay overnight, but came for a conference for the day.  Although there are some repairs in progress, this place is really looking its age.  The lobby level is reasonably modern, but the conference levels and parking levels are really old.

Plus, the whole building is round, so navigation around the confernece center labyrinth is a challenge.  How about some signage?

Nice location -- attached to the airport terminal itself -- but otherwise nothing special.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I went here with a group of friends for my best friends birthday in March. The food was great and that wait staff was very pleasant. I ordered some sort of pasta. I loved that they didnt over cook the pasta like most Italian places. Big plus. There food was good but not the kind of place that I crave going back to. For sure one of the best places I've gone to in the city but not the absolute best out there. Another plus is that it is really reasonably priced. If you are looking for an affordable genuine Italian meal definitely look into La Viola!

Ive been coming here for about 8 years, about 1x a month. I have had some problems with some of my cuts but nothing to cry about. The salon owner sometimes misinterprets what you want, so you have to ingrain and tell her exactly what you want and keep reminding her. There are people who review and say she is political which is true. Most people should keep their politics to themselves but hey i want my hair cut.. so i'll endure it a little. She is also very religious and will talk your head off about jesus.. either you take it or leave it. If you dont want to endure jesus or politics, go somewhere else. For me, i just want my hair cut.

one of my late night spots. After coming up to Chinatown for for all these years, we just like to go with the flow. I found this place because it was one for the few that is opened super late without a crowd of riff raff like Davids. 
Pro: the food variety is great. you can get Chinese, Malaysian and from what i can see Taiwanese. 

Con: it could be a little cleaner. this is one of those places where they just wanna go home, or just serve you it's not as clean as say Bon Chon Or Shiao Lan Kun

Extra Tip: get the fried puffs. they are dumplings but just not as oily. Avocado or the curry chicken i would make the drive up for. definitely.

its a great local gym!!...definately not ballys!...or la fitness, the prices are waaay reasonable good parking. near 2 supermarkets, and the neighborhood is ultra accessible, and clean! though this is not the place for the muscle man or triathlon girl...if you wanna work out in a friendly environment, with friends(get the black card for that) do it!! the membership is reasonable and if you can catch it, (like I did I signed up for a $1 and got the black card...over a year ago) the prices isn't bad at all......so try it, if all else fails leave....and its only 59 to opt out, or find a friend, try it (again black card!) and see for yourself!!
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
The first time I dined in, and the pizza/salad were satisfactory (the cheesy-ness was especially good on the pizza the first go-around).  

However, today I ordered take-out from this Pie of ill-repute and the pizza was just plain bland and cardboard-ish - the cheese severely wanting, the crust brick-ish, and the toppings almost mute (admittedly, I did not choose any of the more expensive "gourmet" toppings for this unit).  

Such insipid food would be acceptable if a medium pizza with toppings cost $10, but it was $21 for a medium (14").

I wanted this place to satisfy my take-out needs.  Sadly, moving on to a higher pie.

This place looked great driving past and I needed my van washed bad! I first noticed that it has a very short driveway so if there's more than 3 cars in line, your car will be sticking out into traffic. Poor design. Because my van was pretty dirty, I went for the $20 wash. The worker guided me through and should have seen how dirty my front hood was. When I came out, I drove away, thinking all was good. A couple miles to my next errand and when I exit, I see how dirty my van still is. Even the windshield had spatters on it.

I'm just visiting and was directed here by the hotel personnel. The front smaller loader cost $3.50 and all the dryers were free! Things got clean and I only needed to run my dryer load twice (though I guess I could have used two dryers at once). When I got there mid-morning it was busy but cleared out by noon. There was one gentleman watching and cleaning up the place. TV, detergent available for purchase, change machine, lots of laundry carts, comfortable chairs and tables, and it was clean! Also, if you pull up to the curb, someone will help you unload!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: We came in for lunch on a Saturday and got the tuna tataki appetizer, the Godzilla roll, and the spider roll. The tuna was very flavorful, and a decent portion for an appetizer. Both rolls were bigger (longer?) than I expected. The Godzilla roll had SO MUCH stuff in it, maybe too many flavors going on for me. I really liked their version of the spider roll. It was tasty and the asparagus had a nice crunch to it. Service was quick, we were on our lunch hour and had time to spare. Space seemed on the small side but there is an outdoor patio. Prices were okay.

I absolutely love this place and it's staff.  
It's small, tucked away behind a bank and a car wash.  They are a small shop with a limited amount of items that they offer but what they lack in quantity they make up for in quality and the personable staff.  The staff knows what they are talking about and will actually remember you with genuine smiles and they offer tastings of their wares on Friday's.  The pricing is on par with other liquor stores.
They have taught me a thing or two about alcohol and even introduced me to my new favorite vodka.
If this is in your area, I say go.

As other reviewers have mentioned about the attitude of the folks here, they have huge attitudes here. Reserved for a Jetta, then they say they'll put me in a Chrysler 200 or Dodge Dart. Then became defensive that our reservation was not until 2 hours later so they do not have much for us now... It was a bit too combative for me. Id rather not give enterprise any business with this attitude, ill take the airport shuttle up north and give SIXT my money. Much much much better service with no attitude. Same price.

First thing to teach employees is how to handle food!  Multiple employees were touching face and hair and then touching food.  One guy was scratching his arm pit and then grabbed a tray of donuts!   Disgusting!  
If you still want a donut after that there are no signs to tell you what's available.  No one knows how to work the coffee maker and the donuts themselves are overworked and off putting.  The icing was done lazy and gives a messy appearance.  Low level donut shop with no special flavors that should probably be closed from too many health code violations.

Gave it another try and added a star.  Large sashimi this time and the fish was fresh but nothing sensational. Accompanying rice (costs extra) would have been much better if it was sushi rice instead of warm regular rice. I would have given it a  3 1/2 if I had the option, but then they forgot some orders for some of my friends and likewise for water and sticks but then service is pretty haphazard here as everyone notices.  Popular place.  Always crowded.  I liked it better this time. Maybe I'll add another star next time.

Update: 

 Chirashi , bleh, same as last time, very little good fish in it.  Added uni to the chirashi, but it came as a sushi with a tiny amount of uni and big chunks of rice, and the uni was not that great anyway; various celebrated "specials", like "fatty tuna", which looked more like canned salmon, rolls, etc.  Even the edamame was tasteless.

This place isn't horrible, but it's not good either.  I don't know of any good sushi restaurants in Tucson, not since Sushi Ken (formerly Sushi Ten - that is the REAL Sushi Ten) moved north.

Actually I haven't been here in years, long before they remodeled, but Heather F's great review reminded me of a time.  I once left behind something quite valuable in my room, and when I went back the desk man told me the maid had turned it in.  I thanked him profusely, but cheap bastard that I am I didn't leave a reward for the honest maid. I wish I did.  I wish I could go back in time and do things right.  I always think of what I should have said and done years too late. 

PS The trick with that Motel 6 was to get a room on the far side of the railroad tracks because the trains blast their horns all night long.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Overall, a decent place for sushi. I ordered some nigiri as well as some rolls, and the fish was decently fresh. However, this place is definitely not for those seeking more authentic Japanese - the rolls, while decent, were very Americanized (names such as Mickey and Donald duck rolls appear on the menu) and the rice was packed a bit too hard. 

Service was very quick and attentive - our dishes arrived very swiftly after ordering. 

Depending on how much you expect to eat, it may be cheaper to order à la carte than go for the AYCE.

Wasn't the best experience.   It started out well. Our server came and got our drink and food order.   Our food was brought out by a different server, I had a cheesesteak ordered hot peppers on the side along with the pickles our friends had ordered sandwiches for which needed tweaking.  I ask the girl if she could get me hot peppers and our table the pickles.   It took SO long my sandwich was now cold our friends were looking for another drink.  All in all the service was bad.  Portions were way to large.  Don't think we'll be back.

This place is OK. The prices are pretty cheap.. 8.99/3 rolls for lunch + salad and 9.99/3 rolls for dinner. Not too bad. However, my spicy tuna roll was rancid. I couldn't eat it. I got my order to go or else I would have sent it back. My salmon/avocado and veggie rolls were great, though. The ginger dressing on the salad isn't the normal one you get at most Japanese restaurants, but it was very good. Since my bad experiences here, I've been ordering from Machi Sushi Bar, which is much better. Do not go out of your way to eat here. I don't think I'll ever be able to order that spicy tuna roll again...

This should really be 2.5 stars. My husband and I stayed here for our 1st wedding anniversary while we had dinner at  Morimoto. Check in was quick, parking is discounted across the street, bed was comfortable, and the hotel is in a fairly good location to a lot of places nearby. However, the rooms are small, the bathroom looks a little worn down and barely cleaned, and the water for the shower barely stayed warm. They don't even have room service. They just have a menu of different restaurants nearby that you can order from.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
We decided to try this place for breakfast. Something differente'. $40 later, we were not wowed. 

The Egg White Omelet was passable but incomplete. It needed something, perhaps fresh Basil or fresh jalapeno, to give it some zing. Egg whites are so good about absorbing flavors. An opportunity was missed. The serving was too small for the price as well; a side of  potatoes would have been perfect. Instead, limp flavored whole beans and lettuce garnish.

Chorizo was ok, but won't set the world on fire. Same with the Huevos Rancheros. Tortillas were not as fresh as we would have liked.

This place is not on our list of places to visit again soon.

I realize that it was my fault for falling into an obvious tourist trap called "Italian Bistro"(!), but it was a Friday night, we were starving and everywhere else was packed.  This place had open tables to spare.  The food was bad, first of all, and I'm not all that difficult to please.  It was all very heavy and generic; calamari made me queasy and  don't get me started on the red sauce.  And the prices were honestly insulting for the quality-- $18.5 for gnocchi with sauce and $17.50 for a glass of Kendall Jackson?!  Learn from my mistake and stay away.

Delicious. I am not a connoisseur of Italian food, but the dishes are well prepared, the menu is short and sweet, wince selection is decent. Do make a reservation if you are considering of going on the weekend. Their new location is one of the best looking restaurants in the city. They have a large private room which I recommend. The carciofi, tortellacci and the seafood stew were all very good. I would return and recommend for first dates and any other dinners you want to impress someone but not sure what exactly they are into. Weird, I know, but true. 

Food: 4/5
Service: 4/5 - Service at the bar is great!
Location: 5/5

Terrible. Just terrible. I think the big draw of this place is the "all you can eat" sushi. We didn't get that. What we got was a bad table right in front of the servers station plus a lot of inquisitive servers who kept wondering how soon we can order, eat, and leave. I think they're used to getting people in and out of the place quickly. The sushi was very bland with no flavor. Even the spicy rolls had no kick. The other Sushi House in Willow Grove is much better. My son was a lot more generous and gave this place 1.5 stars.

I know good pizza. When I walked in that's what I was expecting for how they were advertising. With gluten free and free range meat options, I definitely expected a little more. While the food looked sumptimous, it didn't taste the same. Perhaps mediocre at best. The thin crust was thin but not as soft as I would've liked. The ingredients also didn't seem as fresh to me. The quality just simply fell short of my expectations. I felt like low pricing was their major selling point, it was only 8 bucks for two slices and mango white tea. Still I'd prefer go to CPK pay a little more and get a better pizza.

I wanted to love this place....but....

We reserved our room months ago. Specifically a double room because there are four of us. When we checked in they put us in a King room with a sleeper. EW. It was terrible & they were "full" so we couldn't switch rooms. The pool is VERY small. It only mattered to us, because that was a big selling point with our two little dudes. The last negative was that there was no hair dryer. Seriously?

The pros were that the hotel is very close to restaurant choices & Dutch Bros. The "Courtyard" area was nice to sit outside for a bit. I have mixed feelings about my stay this weekend. :(
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Two words, don't bother, if you want some North-woods ambiance, then please go check it out but only for drinks.  They spent allot of money inside, looks great, kick-back kinda place, but the food is horrible.  I had a chicken sandwich with some type of avocado spread, it was, I thought, suppose to be real avocado, very bad and the bread stale.  It's a must see, great big family of Sasquatch to greet you outside, great look, but.... it's all about the food, if you don't get it... you will soon be closing your doors..

Here's looking at you, Casablanca. You're a great place where hungover Caroline can enjoy a bacon, egg and cheese Casabagel (if I can roll out of bed before the 11am breakfast cutoff). Your wifi helped me write a paper. Your drip coffee helps me study (especially the 50 cent refills). I like your assortment of magazines and the comfy armchair section. I like your rotating art displays. I like that you're walking distance from my apartment. 

Wishlist: Ketchup on the Casabagel. Eggs past 11am. More electrical outlets.

This place looks pretty scary from the outside, but it's actually alright (although I will agree with other reviewers who said they might not trust the chairs enough to get a pedicure here).  I got a manicure and the man who did it was VERY meticulous.  He went over any spots he got on the skin with a brush dipped in polish remover and was extremely precise.  The manicure also lasted a good length of time.  Pros: Quality, price; Cons: Physical appearance, selection of polish shades-- they have nothing trendy, mostly just reds and pinks, which is a BIG con for me, since I like my bright nails!

Just ok. I don't hear well and noise level on Friday night made it difficult to enjoy the dining.
The service was friendly and efficient but the food was just not memorable. Shared two appetizers. The eggplant wrapped around asparagus with melted cheese was good but the red sauce was bland and lacked character. The sautéed calamari was pretty boring as well.
For my entree I had scallops with risotto. This was a big letdown. Scallops were fishy, really big and not enjoyable. The risotto was very creamy and ordinary.
Oh well. Has potential but just not anything special. And it's a BYO that is not cheap with the tab at $100 for two people.

Fantastic food and great service made this a 5 star night. James and Chris worked the kitchen with artistry and very also great to speak with. For appetizers really enjoyed the  grilled squid, main courses loved the scallops and chicken, desserts warm chocolate cake with mint ice cream. Everything from start to finish were fresh and creatively prepared with hard to find ingredients and local/organic sources.
Diane was great server and hostess. Knowledgable on food with recommendations (dead on) and good conversation. Add this to your must list. Very small which helps with you enjoying food with memorable flavor and perfect plating and taste!

Greeted well and was seated promptly. Server checked in right away and took our drink orders. Apps were bruschetta, fried mozzarella and calamari. Bruschetta was grossly under seasoned and the calamari was under cooked and a little rubbery. Entrees were steak panini, manicotti and sea bass. Steak panini was the worst steak sandwich ever. The steak or the veggies were not properly seasoned and was extremely bland. Manicotti was just ok. The sea bass lacked seasoning and the lemon taste took over the dish. Very disappointed as I was excited to try this restaurant.

So, I decided that I wanted to try out City Fitness and I figured being a former Ballys member it wouldn't take much to be better! So, I got a 1 week pass to City Fitness and it wasn't bad. I like their cardio equipment because you have your own TV to watch while working out, which is really nice. You can workout an entire hour watching The Devil Wears Prada. 

Its a nice place to workout and there is plenty of room and help if you need it from the staff. I only wish they had a steam room or hot tub! That could just complete the picture! :) 

Lets hope in their new location when they decide to span out - there is a steam room and a hot tub.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Food is as good as the scenery. If your planning a day at Cheekwood you definitely need to stop on by. 

I wouldn't go out of my way but I wouldn't not go to Cheekwood without grabbing lunch there. If you didn't call ahead expect to wait. Not a lot of room parties of more  than 4 or 5 are probably a bad idea. 

I had a salmon sandwich, girl friend had duck. They were both awesome. 

Bottom line if you're in the neighborhood stop in but don't go out of your way. Also don't expect to be in and out quickly but it makes for a good meal.

This is not a place for a romantic dinner. The food is definitely close for comfort. Tried "the Hill" Mac n Cheese with Salssicia, Provel, and marinara sauce. They offer breadsticks, but they are nothing to write home about, tasted like they were just thawed for the day. If you think you are going to go into this restaurant and try something other than the Mac n Cheese, you're out of luck cause that's really all they have on the menu. For those lactose intolerant, there is free Lactaid by the counter. 

Overall, the food is good, but I think there is much hype behind this place, something I would expect out of a foodcourt at the mall.

12/31/2019: The manager/shift lead Orlando was very unprofessional, I stopped in to pick up an Uber Easts order and he tried to grabbed my phone out of my hands and when I refused he said I need to see the order, I tried to show him the details and he said I need to see the whole order so I tried to read it to him... he attempted to take my phone again and I said shit man I've told you the name, order number and read you the customers order.... He then refused to fill the order saying I was disrespectful but he was the one that that was disrespectful and stressed out from the store being so busy. Very disrespectful man!
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
We just returned from a weekend visit to New Orleans where we stayed at Prytania Park. Great location one block off St. Charles and the trolley line. Five minute trolley ride to Canal Street which gets you one block from Bourbon Street. A hop to Magazine Street for a day of great shopping. 

The room was clean and fresh. But the bathroom and fixtures desperately need updating. Peeling wallpaper, some small holes in the tiles and walls. The rooms have been updated with flat screen TVs and some furniture.

Great location! Great price! We'll stay here again!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Having a meal with two vegetarians and two meat eaters can pose a problem for most restaurants.  A Full Plate was the exception.  The place is eclectic with a variety of choices for all diners.  We shared two fantastic salads, a watermelon and feta, and the fried green tomato salad. Both were fresh and very tasty although i would have preferred a bit more feta on the salad.  The lunch entrees were also extremely creative and well prepared.  They also serve beverages in huge mason jars.  The iced tea was great.  The service was friendly and prompt and the food excellent.  Definitely a winner!

This was the first time I had been to this car wash. Generally I go to the place on Oracle, but this was on the way home and our car needed a wash. 

The attendant that helps you get there was missing when we got there and then was a little too pushy in upselling. 

We ended up getting their wildcat special which was $25 and wasn't worth it. The car is clean and the inside was wiped down, but that is about it. 

The reason I gave it three stars is that the inside was nice. It was clean, bright and airy. Not a bad place to have to wait.

100% authentic Italian food - the owners and his family are from Italy, so you know this spot has to be good. Coming from New York I have high expectations for Italian restaurants and Anthony's does it right. I'm happy that this place exists in Downingtown and I think that it should get more recognition.  It's very obvious that the owner takes pride in his restaurant, he is constantly cleaning and checking in on patrons waiting in line. I would say that Anthony's is definitely better than any other local Italian restaurant in this area.

I really wish I could give this establishment 0 stars.  Due to convenience I ate here again (for a 4th time) with a girlfriend despite my previous negative experiences. 

I knew I should've turned around and walked out after the host showing our table  bolted ahead of us, realized he forgot us, turned around and had to come back which was an awkward experience.  But that doesn't warrant a zero star review...

What does is that my girlfriend and I both got VIOLENTLY ill from their sushi. We both ordered spicy tuna rolls.  I was sick and throwing up for 4 days afterwards. 

Never again will I come here!

This is one of my favorite Italian restaurants in the area. Great service, large portions and authentic Italian - American taste. It's hard to come by good pizza in Pennsylvania but Pomodoro does a great job!

I stopped in this weekend and ordered a spinach calzone that was perfectly doughy, warm with stretchy cheese. I ordered a medium and it was huge! I can't even imagine what the large size looks like. My husband's chicken parm was great - the marinara sauce here has a sweet taste, which I prefer over a more acidic sauce. Tiramisu was sweet, chocolatey and great way to end our meal. We'll be back again and again!

better than the one on 12th and girard mainly since 9am and everything is ready to order( girard location not so much )

full selection of breads,sandwiches and never crowded (when i go anyways) 9-930am.

the dude, sandwich maker doesn't seem the happiest and talks a lot of s*it under his breath while making sandwiches but the hell with it, the sandwiches taste good. i'll take the hatred for a fresh sandwich anyday of the week. Dude gets the order right 9 times outta 10 but if its a big order don't expect the sandwiches to be labled. he looked like he wanted to jump the counter and do some mortal kombat type beat down when i asked last time

This is my idea of a great neighborhood bar. The bartender is welcoming, you get a nod or a smile from the other patrons, the drinks are cheap, and best of all, the food is terrific. Let me wax lyrical about Jimmy Chips. Ahhh...they are a cross between a potato chip and a French Fry. Slivers of potato fried to perfection, accompanied by Cheese Whiz and sour cream.  Like numerous menu items, they are named after one of the regulars who invented it.  Burgers are good, meatball sandwich excels, and grilled cheese on a pretzel roll is another star item. Conshy's finest!

I had nothing but praise for this place previously but the past few times the service has been terrible.  First they got my drink wrong.  Then they brought the appetizer with the main meal and wouldn't take our meals back until we had time to enjoy the appetizer.  And then my chile relleno was child...colder than room temperature.  When I complained, instead of quickly offering to take the item back the manager appeared annoyed at the very suggestion.  The server did apologize but blamed it all on how busy they were.  There were perhaps 4 other tables between him and another server.  I won't bee going back for quite a while.

It's clean and new.. But if you like an old fashioned workout you may find yourself frustrated with the options.. theres no lat pull down bar, and very few attachment options for machines.. and no wide smith cross cable or decline bench..I almost stopped going altogether.. But after going to the spring garden location (a much better, traditional gym) I decided to stay.. The SG location feels like the flagship and the GH feel like the "express" version... I wish they stayed open later and had longer holiday hours.. It does the job& is a block from my house, but I much rather workout at the SG location..
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I've purchased kegs and many cases from this place but they are clearly not focused on customer service. 

After being ignored by 2 employees (owner and son) when I asked about a limited run beer which other places are selling for $8 less a case the rep stated the price and said "well do you want it or not?". 

I will over pay for a good experience however today was the last time I'll ever deal with those guys. 

Remember if you create a wonderful customer experience people don't mind paying but when you act like you're the only game in town they will not.

Absolutely delicious place in Collingswood.  Like everyone else, I get nervous because it is never crowded when we go.  But the food is shockingly good.  And the person who didn't like the fried chicken, I have no clue what happened to your order.  But the first time we went there I had it and it was perfect.  And the cole slaw was amazing.  We have gone several times and have had most of the menu and nothing has been even the least bit disappointing.  Awesome food, awesome prices.  I hope it sticks arounds.

The food here is great, don't get me wrong, but it's a premium priced place that should knock me out every time I go. The first time I went was when they were in the city, and I loved it. Knocked me out. But the last time I was there (in Clayton), I wasn't wowed. It was good, and did the job, but for $100+ a person, I expect a little more. I am a huge fan of the other Niche restaurants (Pastaria and Taste are favorites), so I'll probably go there for 1/3 the price. 

Note: Yelp says it is only $$$, but it is clearly a $$$$ place--the chef's tasting menu, which I highly recommend, is $100/person.

I would zero stars if it was possible. You cannot get into this place to rent a vehicle unless you are coming on a shuttle from the airport. They claim to have a parking lot if you want to call it that, way out in front of the place. It holds about 4 cars in this "parking lot". When I walked up to ask the woman how to get in, she was very rude and said this is the airport location meaning you can only rent a car coming from the airport. The whole thing was ridiculous, but they were extremely rude on top of it.

I was here at the beginning of August and was so impressed... here are some highlights:
1) Location - Right on the beach!!  Beautiful beach!!
2) Service - The hotel staff is amazing... I've never been to a Residence Inn with such a fantastic staff. Everyone was so friendly and helpful

Drawback
- Elevator situation... the only drawback of the hotel... not enough elevators for everyone, so just be prepared for a wait... no big deal, just be prepared.

Thank you Residence Inn Treasure Island for a fantastic getaway!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I really would have expected a little better quality food from JW Marriott...but both my wife and I agree the food for a brunch was no better than what you would get at a Holiday INN....wow we both were shocked. Even the staff were not on top of their game. We didnt stay in the room here but we are very hesitant to recommend to our friends to stay here here if they cant even get the food portion of the business straight..especially for the price you pay!......I say think twice before trusting in a name and believing its all High Class, because its a cover just to get your money!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Came here for the opening night and had an AMAZING time! I loved the decor of the place... How open and welcoming it was. I really hope it becomes a dance hall after restaurant hours because the open space is so inviting! The pasta dish I tried here was also incredible. The cheese melted perfectly in my mouth and I'm still curious what type of tomatoes or seasonings were used because they definitely had an interesting kick to them! Will definitely have to return and try the food before I move out of Philly soon!

Ordered from here on a Yelp review recomendation.  I have had some recent frustration with our normal go-to Chinese food place.  Overall it was OK, nothing to write home about-but maybe a few notes on Yelp
I would not eat AT the store front.  It is next door to a cigar business, and yuou can smell it.The last thing I want to smell while I am eating is cigars. YUCK!!!
The Pheonix shrimp had a good spice level, but, as with most Chineses food store front locals, it was drown in sugary he eggroll and crab rangoon had an odd earthy flavor to it. The search continues...

For the Franklin area, this is one of the better establishments.  The bigger concern here is consistency.  First two times, they deserved a 4-5 star ratings, the remaining 3 times, it was a miss.  It seems like they "let it go", and not in the Frozen Elsa way that's fantastic. 

Pros:
-Good portion sizes
-Fair pricing
-Nice variety on menu including AYCE sushi lunch buffets

Cons:
-Location is out of the way
-Freshness of fish is a hit or miss
-Service can be a hit or miss

Overall, if I don't feel like driving all the way across Nashville, this place should stomp my cravings for now.

I was happy to see this location in my neighborhood completely rebuilt a while back and had high expectations, but those hopes didn't last long.

They ALWAYS cut me off when I'm ordering, rip me off on drinks (see pic), and leave out parts of my order. I never bother fixing those problems because I know I'll get a rude attitude in return! The only good thing about this place is that the new building layout makes more sense and moves more quickly than the old one.

I'll only go here out of necessity from now on.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Markley St, Norristown, PA
Great service and drive thru. And a cute Indian guy took my order. You know why people like chains? Because they know what they want n dont need to think too hard or make a decision over small things like coffee and dont need to be too surprised as they know what to expect. Thats why chains typically do well. People dont always have the energy to figure out if a store is selling something they want when they are out shopping and get exhausted and need to fuel up their bodies. By the way...the Decaff was a tad bit sweet. I just needed something hot. Usually dont like that much sugar in my decaff.

Finally had dinner here last night with a couple of friends after wanting to come here for years. The four-course dinner was excellent! Each course was clearly prepared with care. I highly recommend the beef tartare as an opener! Filet mignon with mashed potatoes and oxtail was worth the up-charge as was the spaghetti with king crab. My only criticism is that I actually felt like four courses (plus an amuse bouche and popover) was a little too much and too rich. Otherwise, would highly recommend and eat here again.

For a sushi place in Montecito, I was expecting MORE. All the employees were very nice and accommodating. I noticed they were quick to clean tables once customers left BUT they are definitely understaffed. My boyfriend and I came by during my lunch and it took 25 minutes (after he ordered) to get our first roll. The spicy tuna was also not spicy at all and it had a really weird consistency. It kind of made me sad considering I work 5 minutes away and when I need a "sushi pick-me-up" I was hoping this would be my "it" place. I'm super disappointed...

This place has become our family favorite for Italian.  We eat here several times a year, and the food and service are always very good.  The specialties of the day are excellent, and I go with one of them about half the time, otherwise I almost always have the ravioli aurora.  My younger son alternates between pizza and fettucine alfredo.  When his brother is home, he always gets the margarete pizza.  And my husband usually orders one of the specials.  All the entrees come with house salad, with Italian dressing on the side, but they also have a creamy Italian.

Eight of us took Mom for her birthday to only be let down. We love BOYB, the food was very tasty, the service was ok. Not crowded, but noisy! The portion sizes were very out of whack. Caesar salads were ok, but were tiny. Some of the dishes were smaller than tiny. The veal was wonderful, more than 2 minuscule pieces would have been nice. My nephew, growing 15yo, ordered ravioli, unfortunately he left hungry. Contrasted by Mom's pasta was a huge portion. I love that they are trying to do Italian upscale, but the $$$$ to portion size is out of balance. My way of saying, overpriced...way overpriced. If $$$$ is no object, its great.

Dr. Baker does a fine job....the opticians...not so much!!!!  Last year they screwed up my contact order, lied to me about a rebate offer and then were rude to top it all off.  Jolene the OM did help me through all the mess and it eventually all was taken of.

This year I'm surprised I went back, but I gave them a second chance.  They are still VERY rude especially when you tell them you aren't ordering contacts through then because I can get them fir half the cost at visiondirect.com

Needless to say, I don't think I will be giving them a third chance.  :(. Sad because they have convenient hours for working people.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping
