text: Quiet little neighborhood cafe with extensive tea, bubble tea, and coffee options near a school. The crowd in the afternoon includes some cultured neighborhood kids.  Three sitting areas: front room, back room for slightly bigger groups, and an outdoor sitting area. Tried their "green tea cupcake" because of the reviews, but I thought it was just okay. Iced coffee was good. Nice quiet place to meet up or study.  With the breeze, there was an unsavory odor that seemed to blow through that just didn't suit me.  That and the ok green tea cupcake were the main reasons why I gave the place 3 stars instead of 4.

So my very first time here, by pure luck I was getting my hair cut with Heidi. I've never walked out of a barbershop or salon and didn't feel the need to mess with my hair!! Seriously. Never
My hair is a mess, it has 5 or 6 cowlicks and is thick and wild, this hair cut was perfect.
Heidi did exactly what I asked her and more, she took her time and made sure I was happy along the way
The shop itself is super cool, played the guitar in the corner while I waited, they offer you beer or drinks which is awesome, at 10 am, I was tempted but also knew how the rest of that day would go.
Great shop, great people!! I have found my barber shop!!!!!

20 min prior to closing I laced a "to go" order to be picked up. I walked down from the Hampton Suites, 0.3 mi. from the hotel. Upon arrival, my order was ready and waiting. 
Back at the hotel my friend and I were quite pleased with our order of Miso Soup, Salad with ginger dressing which was thick and delicious. Seaweed salad can be hit or miss.  Im happy to report this one was a hit. I had Yellowtail Nigiri and a roll. Fully satisfied client here. 
The place is small, could use a good scrub down and a facelift but I'd definitely order from here again.

The past few months of nothing but successful visits warrants Sushi Cafe a bump up to five stars. I appreciate their extensive menu more than ever now that I'm allergic to wheat. About half of their maki rolls are naturally gluten free! Staff let me know that the eel and eel sauce contain wheat, so they modify rolls accordingly. They also offered to substitute any shrimp tempura roll with steamed shrimp. They are extremely accommodating and careful of allergy issues. 

Sushi Cafe still provides the freshest and most flavorful sushi in the new Tampa / Wesley Chapel area. I just wish I could take this place home with me to the west side of Tampa!

Meh. Average food at high prices for Tucson. I should mention that I have only paid to eat here once (the first time, when I went with a friend for her birthday). Every other time, it was because someone else wanted to go, or for some work party. 
I once had some good baked mostaccioli and a decent spaghetti with basil, tomato and garlic. This place also served the worst calamari I have ever eaten, dried out manicotti, and the service was usually not good at all. You would be better off going to the place behind it in the same shopping center (La Dolce Vita) - better food, prices and service.

Just ate here a couple of hours ago, and I must say, it was pretty good! I had a carne asada taco and the small quesadilla, and my friend ate the #11 combo, which was a cheese enchilada, ground beef taco and a chile relleno with rice, beans and sour cream. This was the first time I've tried a chile relleno, and it was really good. They had a help-yourself salsa bar with chopped onions and hot peppers, too. None of the salsas were great, but they weren't bad, either. The service wasn't very good, but there was only one waitress, and the place was totally full. I would go back, especially considering the fact that our bill totaled only $13!

Under new ownership since Labor Day, this place is terrific.  We ordered the sushi/sashimi boat for 3 people, a rainbow and spicy tuna roll and bulgogi dolsot bimbimbap.  Overall, the food was very good.  The sushi/sashimi boat and rolls were fresh and made with excellent sushi rice.  The portions were generous and it was delicious. 
My son really enjoyed his bimbimbap (it's a Korean dish of rice with mixed vegetables and marinated beef).
The service was prompt and very friendly. If you want a really good meal, this is a great choice!

I had the farm and fisherman sandwich/salad combo.  I got the half tuna melt and salad.  It was literally a one slice sandwich with a juicy tomato.  My parents had the crab cake sandwich.  Their sandwich was on a brioche bun and they loved it.  It was tall with a fluffy bun and thick but properly cooked crab cake.  My wife had the tuna melt too with fries.  The fries were crispy and she loved it too.  The only "downside" for my meal was my chopped salad.  I found it to be somewhat bland.
BUT, the meal overall was very good and service was also very good.

stayed last week... nice room but small. great location within walking distance from everything. staff was great besides the night manager who barely spoke english and couldnt understand a simple request... deer in the headlights stare, as she was the night manager. rooms  separated from the lobby where the ice machine is located. room states in writing, if someone complains of noise, you would basically have to pay for their room as it wont be tolerated. 2 of the 3 rooms were loud and security warned us 3 times to lower the volume.  no extra charges as the written agreement was apparently a scare tactic. overall a descent hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This Pizza Champ pop up is the best New York style pizza I have had outside of New York.  It may be the best pizza in St Louis that I have had. We got a sausage pizza, which comes with red peppers and onions, and we got an cheese pizza with onions and mushroom conserva.  The crust was perfectly crisp with the right amount of chew. The sauce was rich and tangy, and the cheese/topping ratio was perfect.  I had never heard of mushroom conserva, but it had a great texture and incredible flavor.  And I have leftovers for lunch tomorrow!

I just moved to town so I was excited about trying this place - I have not dined in, but I ordered Togo and was completely let down. I ordered edamame and that was the best of what I ordered, which says A lot. I ordered sashimi tuna and it was only one overpriced piece that was not fresh. I ordered a side of hibachi shrimp and it was 6.95 for maybe 8 max really small shrimp. Then I ordered a cucumber salmon roll that was weirdly soggy and the cucumber was not rolled right and falling apart. I would like to dine in and if my experience is different I will certainly change and edit my review.

Our usual pizza places were closed so we decided to give Original Venice Pizza a shot. I picked up a pepperoni pizza and mozzarella sticks. Sticks were good, nice and crispy with a marinara sauce with a good consistency (not too watery or two chunky). The pizza was good. Dough was thin and crispy, pepperoni a bit spicy but not too hot, sauce was tangy and a little spicy, and the cheese was a bit light. Pizza was slightly overcooked but not bad. This pizza was better than a lot of pizza I've had in my time but not one of the best, it's good but not great.

First time stayiNg at this property. Have stayed in many different Garden Inn's. RealLy like this one. Rooms are laid out the same as the others but with a more modern feel. Bigger TV and large walk in shower, no tub. Free breakfast at the restaurant for Gold and Diamond members. Nice pool and fitness room. The best feature, the rooftop bar. Daily happy hour specials and decent food. Target across the street, big shopping center across the street, and an Albertsons a couple miles away. Would stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This one is going on the Biscuit List, not because they had the greatest biscuits but because of the gravy. It was rich and flavorful - better than the gravy at the Nashville Biscuit House. Now if you could just combine the biscuits from there with the gravy from Charlie Bob's . . . . Anyway, I was also impressed with the hash browns that Zim had - he chose the toppings and they made this great custom dish for him. So if you are looking for hash browns that go beyond the basics, this is your place. 

Overall, a good basic breakfast spot with very friendly service. The other items we had - waffle, eggs, etc - were all fine.

it's possible, of course, that they just had an off night, but the impression we get is that there's a been sea change in the kitchen.  (there's evidence of this, too, for omnivores, as seen on the new "philosophy" on bistro's menus.)  in any case, yes, we're still delighted that there are vegetarian options on the menu, and the service was quite good, but the quality of the food is what really let us down.  we'll be writing much more about this very soon.  in the meantime, please accept our sincerest apologies, vegheads, if our previous endorsement mislead you.

There is nothing special about this establishment. The decor is ok but lacks any kind of vibe at all. The waitstaff are not overly helpful relative to suggesting anything at all that might make the experience special, The fish was presented in a fairly attractive manner. I'm not sure what they did with the white tuna but it wasnt right. The rice was not well prepared and frankly that's the test of a good sushi chef. I wouldnt go back because I can get this quality at Genuardi's. See my previosu review of Morimoto for a review of great sushi.

After all the nice review this place has, I want to know what went wrong when we went there.

The green tea came in a beautiful pot, and tasted like grass. Pretty sure they were trying to stay as true to the tea ceremony as possible here, because this stuff was nasty. 

I ordered an assortment of sushi. Every freaking piece was slathered in wasabi. Seriously?! I can't stand wasabi, I have a very sensitive stomach, and trust me, my sinuses were cleaned out by the time we left. There was no way I was paying twenty bucks for a dinner and not eating it. 

I left with heartburn and very peeved off.

Let's be honest- it is really hard to find good and somewhat authentic Chinese food in Nashville... but hands down, Hong Kong might be the best we've found so far. 

The food is your standard Chinese take--out. I also appreciate that some of the chicken dishes are already made with white meat.  

The dinner specials are pretty good. It's a ton of food for under $10 (which includes an entree and bowl of soup). 

I've never had a  bad experience. We usually just carry-out so I can't speak to the delivery service, but I know the people are always pleasant when we call! Give them a try!

This place was not so bad. The first time we went here the sign said it was open but it was not. The second time it was though! Its priced decently and the staff was friendly. The interior is really nothing to look at. We choose to take our food home.
My husband and I both got burritos. The ingredients tasted okay. By the time we got home everything pretty much was mushed together so I could not really tell what I was eating. I did not care for how the tortilla tasted. It kind of fell apart. 
I did like the chips and salsa though. I like my salsa spicy and this one was pretty strong.

I was invited to dinner here by some friends. The waitress was extremely attentive and friendly. I ordered the filet mignon which was $20.99 medium well. It came back rare... so I asked for it well done and they came back.... with it rare AGAIN. So they give me my steak and its burned sooo badly it is barely edible. Pretty sure that was the cooks way of getting revenge? By the time I got my "dinner" everyone else was finished. They only took $10.50 off of my meal. I really wish I could of taken that $$ and gone to Benihana!

I was at Caffe Valentino for my bachelorette party this past weekend. The food was delicious, and it was very classy. The menu is easy to understand. Definitely a reasonable price, portions are a tiny bit small but it was still tasty and satisfying. I'd like to add that the servers were very kind.

However, it really took forever. We were there at 8 PM and didn't leave until 11 PM. The food just took so long to come out- I'm sure that's because we were a party of about 15, but perhaps consider this before coming with a huge group if you have a time crunch.

I am not a smoker, so tend to not go to smoker's bars. But I enjoyed Lana's so much I didn't seem to notice!

We stopped in here on one of our "let's only go to places we haven't been before" date nights and stumbled into Lana's after seeing it is so popular on Yelp.

Della was super friendly and funny. We went in for one beer, but stayed for 4 because we were enjoying the conversation with Della and two regulars so much. 

Plus, it's very refreshing to find a dive bar in Florida that not only doesn't have MAGA blasted everywhere, but actually has a "Trickle Down Economy Tips" jar.

Having moved from Brooklyn, I was skeptical I could find Mexican as good in Philly as I had in Sunset Park. Que Chula Es Puebla is easily the best I've had in the city. As others said, yes, it's not the prettiest place (and looks a bit scary from the outside) but when you make al pastor tacos this tasty, you can serve it in a cardboard box and I'd go there. Aside from the great tacos--shredded chicken was also fantastic, though shrimp was a bit overcooked--the prices can't be beat: $6 for three, well-stuffed soft-shelled meat tacos. We brought our own alcohol, too, so we left satiated and happy--and just $8 poorer each!

It's a family style place with family style food.  The staff is very friendly, helpful, and attentive.  It's as far from pretentious as a place can be and they aim to please.   The portions are mega-huge and food coma inducing.   Just imagine a much more skilled Chef Boyardee as your uncle, whipping up something good for you to eat after soccer practice.   It's got those hearty, familiar recipes without getting too crazy with creative menu innovations that are nice to look at but don't always work in the mouth.  This might just be my favorite Italian joint in SB.

I go to Rowan, and since I turned 21 7 months ago, Monster has been my first choice for beer / liquor. They have a huge selection of beer, wine, and hard alcohol. Their prices vary with the quality of alcohol. You can go in, buy 2 40s for $4 bucks and call it a night, or  walk out with top shelf stuff, and everywhere in between. They are also generally cheaper than their Glassboro competitors.

They also have a smaller section for juice, soda and other party supplies, as well as other alcohol related accessories. Definitely the only place you'll need to go for alcohol in Glassboro.

Well it's about time a decent pizza place opened up close to meadow point. I ordered 2 small pizzas one was a Saint Louis style which is a very thin crust and the hand tossed which is similar to a New York style crust. Both of them were poo pretty tasty. We had the meat lovers hand tossed and there was so much meat you could hardly see the cheese. It looked like bacon, ham, sausage, hamburger and pepperoni. Excellent. The thin crust was pepperoni only and again you could hardly see the cheese. The sauce was very good as well. I think our favorite is the thin crust. Looking forward to try other things there.

This has become our go to sushi restaurant lately. It's the closest to the house, the food is good and the staff is awesome. I can't ask for more than that when a sushi craving hits. Last time we were there the waitress put jasmine petals that she grew in her garden in the water our glasses. Super sweet lady. I think she has been in there every time we've stopped by. 

I still usually order the same boring rolls but they are good every time. I haven't noticed the smokey flavor I mentioned in my first review since so it must have been a fluke. One of these days I'll get more adventurous and try some of their specials!

For some reason, I keep coming back to this place whenever I'm in Philly.  Nothing is particularly amazing, maybe except for the huge colorful sombreros they give out to birthday folks and the fried ice cream which I tried once.  The burritos are pretty okay, but the enchiladas are kind of chewy and strange.  The last time I was here, we were dehydrated from the saltiness of the rice and beans. Some accident must have occurred in the kitchen because that stuff was SALTY.  But they do have a wide selection of dishes, and my friend swears by their tamale. I dunno, maybe I'll give them another chance and try something new next time I'm here.

Being a vegetarian, I am usually limited to basic veggie rolls when I go to a sushi place. It's not bad but it wouldn't hurt to have some variety. 

Well fat salmon has that variety! This place has the most amazing vegetarian rolls. I always get the lipstick trays and old school roll but I am looking forward to trying a lot more as I go back. 

My friends who aren't vegetarian love the sushi over there but even they order the aforementioned veggie sushi rolls.

Love this place and will be frequenting and trying more rolls

Not a spa. By far the worst mani I ever had! No one has hurt me more doing my REAL NAILS in 19 years! Now they are all broken peeling off the shellac after a week!!!!! I'm new in town and my regular place "popular nails Carlsbad ca" would take their time and soak my nails gently file with fine emery board NOT the black for acrylics! This older lady from Tampa at this location did my nails. Unfriendly, slow, and rough! OMG rough and now my real nails are all broke and short! I thought this was going to be a nice place because of reviews! BS! Nice punch card, not, I'd rather punch the lady that ruined my natural nail.

Not a spa. By far the worst mani I ever had! No one has hurt me more doing my REAL NAILS in 19 years! Now they are all broken peeling off the shellac after a week!!!!! I'm new in town and my regular place "popular nails Carlsbad ca" would take their time and soak my nails gently file with fine emery board NOT the black for acrylics! This older lady from Tampa at this location did my nails. Unfriendly, slow, and rough! OMG rough and now my real nails are all broke and short! I thought this was going to be a nice place because of reviews! BS! Nice punch card, not, I'd rather punch the lady that ruined my natural nails! I'm so angry!!

Terrific barber shop! Consistently very good cuts and straight razor shaves (if you just get your hair cut they also use a straight razor on your neck). 

I always leave feeling good and happy with the service. I've been to the shop now about four times and really like it. It is a small shop (two chairs) and I definitely recommend making an appointment. Jamal (owner) is very friendly and I've only seen Diego for my services. Diego is the man! He's very detail oriented and friendly. 

It is on the high end cost wise but for the level of service and care, it is very reasonable.

The food here is pretty good, not the best ever or worst ever either.  

I have a tendency of getting the chicken parmesan or the chicken marsala. Both are ok.. My main issue is the red pasta sauce with the chicken parmesan.  It's kinda tasteless. When you warm up your leftovers it doesn't warm up well. The penne pasta is always so watery which in turn waters down the sauce. Constantly having to ask the server to please have the kitchen staff drain my pasta well before plating my dinner.
Their soups and salads are very good as is the bread!

Since the rehab some months ago, the huge glass windows give you a lovely vista of the Gallatin Road.  There is free Wi-Fi and in the early morning it can be quite soothing.  The bright yellow chairs and vinyl booths are sunny and optimistic.  Today we headed in to try the McFishbites that we had seen on the Telly the night before.  Blimey what a winner.  they really did taste like the fish sandwich but in a round bite size form.  soft and fishy and lovely.
Service is A-OK - not as efficient as the Mighty Fesslers Lane branch but we will be back for more mcbites soon
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Another we could be anywhere in the US middle of nowhere breakfast diner....Pablo and I split the pork chop breakfast, two pieces each, an egg each, hash browns each, a biscuit each and sausage gravy, coffee and Tax = $11.
Filling, tasty and of course gut wrenching later.  Service was pleasant and good, quiet and soothing, now if only there had been some Elvis Christmas Song in the background.  As another reviewer said, no arugula here folks.  There is a bar around the other side of the cash desk, with twinkly lights, and yes there were four people sitting there at 9.30am.  Liver on Thursdays fellow Liver fans.

I hate to rate this place so low because the staff if super friendly and helpful but in todays food environment the quality just has to be higher.
The pizza prices are as high as other places in the area that have better quality crust and ingredients. The crust tastes and feels frozen and the pepperoni is light on flavor.
None of us liked the chicken wings as all the sauces tasted like a mix of BBQ and wing sauce.
The place may be worth it during buffet hours but at regular price there are just too many better choices.

THIS LOCATION NOW OUT OF BUSINESS
Went here on a monday night when it was pretty empty and depressing. Loved it! Small, dark and cramped, with barely enough room to fit the pool table. The bartender was a plucky older woman named Fran. She poured us nearly clear drinks ($6 well) and tolerated our silly behavior with just the right amount of attitude. I've since heard that Paseo Nuevo (trendy shopping area) had to be built around it because they refused to sell...which only adds to this bar's cred in my book. Sad to say, however, I recently glimpsed the bar on a Friday night and thought I saw a collegey crowd spilling out...

I wish this place was better. I would much prefer to patronize this place than any of the chains. However the fact of the matter is that this place sells old ice cream. You know what happens when you put ice cream in your freezer and leave the top half open for weeks and the ice cream gets this disgusting taste, it tastes like the freezer and it gets ice crystals? That is what the ice cream here tastes like. Old and yucky. And you get to pay 5 bucks for that privilege. But I do love an old fashioned retro scoop shop. Too bad they don't care about the product here.

Yoko is one of the better sushi/Japanese restaurants in Tampa, but that's not saying much, because the sushi/Japanese in Tampa is not that great. This restaurant in a larger city with better Japanese/sushi would get 2 stars max.

Actually, I think Soho Sushi is better than Yoko. But Yoko has a more extensive menu and has great desserts, etc.

One thing about Yoko is, it SMELLS BAD in that restaurant. If you are one of those people who is smell-sensitive, you will know what I am talking about when you go here. I think the place needs a paint job, new carpeting, etc.

Came in for a fill and pedi with my 
 daughters along, who also got mani/pedis for our vacation the next day.  First I was very disappointed with the polish choices, with most of the OPI colors dried out or in outdated or winter colors, I was left with a sub par brand.  The polish was then slapped on and not applied carefully.  My daughters cuticle is sore where the technician was too rough.  By the second day of vacation all of our polish has chipped and even my acrylics are completely dull and the color is worn off along the edges.  Unfortunately, I will not be back.

I used to frequent this place often and always ordered the same thing : a mixed of vegetables with cheese fried like an omelet. The main cook liked me and allowed me to order this for about 4 or 5 bucks. They have a nice selection of pre-wrapped snacky foods, and the pizza is not bad at all. 
They have bathrooms but they are not the cleanest, they have take out, delivery, and sit down area. I don't go anymore because I stopped walking by on my way to work. Would still consider stopping in for a bite if I got hungry.

Swung through on my way back to work from an off-site meeting.  Decided to try the new pretzel pub chicken - it's interesting.  There's a lot going on between the chicken, muenster, salad blend, honey mustard, and cheese sauce.  Was sort of like a full course meal in each bite.

However, $7.91 for a small combo. Ouch.  And traditional fast food chains wonder why fast casual is taking all of their business?  I'd much rather go to a Panera type place for $8.

Oh, and I'm already ordering a small combo.  You could skimp on the ice a little bit and actually fill my drink up.

1. Love that this place is so close to my work!

2. First time i went here it was amazing!! And second and third! Their donuts were so moist and amazing. They had so much flavor ! 

3. There is sooooooooooo much sugar in them.. you can barely eat a whole donut.

4. The apple fritters are to DIE for

5. The fourth and fifth time i have gone, the donuts have been soooooo dry :-( i went today after work and i wasn't impressed with the selection either. I threw away half my dozen because the donuts just tasted like they had been left out all day :-(

I am a long time Chapala supporter of all the locations around the valley. Went to the Vista location this weekend and was very disappointed. I feel like they are cutting corners on portions and food quality. The Chili Colorado looked thinned out and lacked flavor. The Carne Asada was very greasy and a little tough. The quality of ingredients did not seem up to par for what you usually expect at Chapala. The chips also tasted like the oil needed to be changed out. I hope it was just a bad night for them because it is one of the few places in the valley where you can expect consistent quality and service.

If this is the best Nashville has to offer, then I think we're all in trouble.  Well, I know I am anyway.  The appearance of this place is worn and rough, suggestive of a haunt that has stood the test of time because the focus is squarely and entirely on the art of sushi.  Substance over style.  But the sushi here just doesn't measure up.  The nigiri was barely passable.  The shrimp crunch roll (which I never get, but came with my order) was made with tempura crumb rather than tempura shrimp, sans eel sauce.  Major disappointment after reading so many good reviews.

Dropped in for a quick bite on a Wednesday night for the first time. Restaurant appeared very clean and orderly. Waitress came out to introduce herself a few minutes after I sat down. Better than average beer selection. 

The waitress brought a basket of rolls and a plate of spiced olive oil to dip the rolls into. 

I ordered the rigatone, it was served hot and I thought spiced just  right. There was more than I could eat.

The check was very reasonable and the waitress was pleasant and attentive.  I would say this place was A-OK.

Over all the food is pretty solid, for take out Chinese style.  My biggest complaint is with anything they have to fry.  More often then not they really need to change their oil.  

We've all but given up on eating any kind of egg roll provided to us with a combination platter because they just end up being soggy and taste of old oil.  On the rare occasion we do get a "dry" egg roll they are fairly tasty.  On the same note the "Chinese Doughnuts" consistently taste of won ton and grease as they fry everything in the same vat.

They're by no means bad, but they don't blow any of their dozens of competitors out of the water.

I know this place is a staple on Mass Ave because it holds an amazing location but man...I just don't get it.  They serve OK beer with a mediocre selection and have pretty awful food.  Maybe awful is a strong word...I'll just go with very bad.

The chips they use for nachos and chili are like the big generic round tortilla chips....yuck....and their sandwiches are equivalent to things you can just throw together at home.  If you lived ON mass ave and wanted to stop in quickly for a beer...fine....go for it....but food here? ugh no way.

Really solid pizza joint right inside the mall.  Fresh ingredients and cooked to perfection made for a wonderful meal.  My wife and I split the margarita boat pizza (don't judge me).  Great tomato flavor, fresh cheese, basil, and great leoparding on the bottom made for a great thin crust pizza that had the right amount of pillowy crust. The beer was cold but many of their kegs were kicked so the selection was underwhelming.  For the price and the limited drink options, I'd have to say that this place is A-OK... if it's sunday and Chick-Fil-A is closed, I'll consider coming here if I don't mind spending a few extra dollars.

Great rooms and I love the lobby bathroom.  I mean its so serene like sitting in a victorian era cave while a baby deer laps guava nectar from your shoulder blades.  I withhold my constitution and then fortnightly I visit these green pastures and unleash my "harvest".  Nothing compares to my six hour otherworldy adventure in the annals of the hotel lobby where sweet vessels of relief venture up from my bowels to my spine and break like sweet waves in the form of goosebumps on my jawline.  
Great customer service too!   Would reccomend!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I've been here a few times and really it's just whatever. I like that the patio is really big but you better get here early to claim a table. I like that their mixed drinks are actually served in a glass, not a plastic cup. Pours are usually strong. I dislike that you can smoke inside. I dislike that there is only 2 toilets and 1 of the stalls is so small that my knees hit the wall in front of me while sitting on the toilet. I'm not THAT tall. When I've been there I've actually seen a pretty diverse crowd but for the most part it's college aged kids. Not my fave place, but not the worst either. It serves it's purpose.

Quick assessment: It's the Hand Grenade bar.

They're 100% worth trying, and were way better than I'd expected - it reminded me of Smarties, and wasn't particularly strong. The bar is pretty wildly decorated (but was empty every time we passed). Standard procedure: order a HG and leave the bar immediately to walk Bourbon Street and people watch. Our hotel balcony was just across from the Tropical Isle balcony, which led to some fun "We Are - Penn State" chants with some Bros during our trip.

Order a hand grenade, for no other reason than to be able to tell people you had one.

Great store with plenty of healthy options. Prices can be ridiculous but I always go back for healthier options of meat, healthy types of bread, good coffee and some specific non-dairy products or ethnic goodies like Indian or Japanese products. I also love their selection of spices and sweets, nuts.
The only product that I can never find there is cardamom seeds for my Indian cooking. Can't find it anywhere in FL.
I do not rate it with 5 stars because Whole Foods in my Favorite store with wider selection of everything.

Pretty average Chinese take-out (you can dine in, as well). The egg drop soup was horrible, but for the price of $1.75 what do you expect? It was just bright yellow broth with egg pieces and lots of corn starch to make it look (and taste) glue-y. We didn't even eat it. Fried rice was ok and chicken with vegetables was a bit bland. However I liked the fact that it was lots of veggies in a dish and used only white meat. The price was really good $5.25 for smaller portion (but it's big enough to share). It's not one of the best Chinese food I have had but if you want something fast and cheap, go for it.

Cheap, tasty, quick, satisfying, clean, efficient service. I like it! Reminds me a lot of the quick family meals my family had during my childhood in Chinatown Calgary. Ginger beef and sweet and sour pork have their place and time (e.g. 3am after a night out) but that's the Chinese equivalent to a Big Mac. Taipan Cafe is for when you're not in the mood to cook but want better than fast-food. There are dishes for the uninitiated (green onion cakes, chow mein, wonton noodle soup) and for those who grew up eating congee and BBQ duck at Popo's (Grandma's).

So, I literally live a couple blocks away from Hiro... and I've only been once.. BUT my first time is definitely a precursor to many more trips to come. 

Had the sushi and the chicken dumplings YUM! Definitely yummy!! Had a cocktail as well.. I'd say they make their drinks nice!!

LOVE the atmosphere... definitely a bit different and edgy! And that's always a plus when you're eating good food !! 

On a side note.. it's not in the best part of town.. especially with the club next door.. so I'd be careful if you're there out late at night!

Actually 3.5 stars. 

Good casual place to go with a group of friends. We were excited about the BYOT, but the watermelon margarita mix we got was kind of bland. I appreciated that it wasn't sickeningly sweet, but we ended up needing to add salt and lime to the mix to make our drinks taste better. 

The food itself is pretty decent - unless you're married to the idea of flour tortillas, get the tacos and quesadillas "traditional style" with the corn tortillas. Both the shrimp and the pork were juicy and flavorful. They have a nice portobello option for your vegetarian friends too.

My kinda bar! Very small and narrow, artsy 'dive' bar (get it?) with super friendly staff, lots of fun shots, bombs, drinks and great variety of fancy beers and of course, cheap PBR. Super duper smoky - shower AFTER the bar yo! Bands play in the small back room and start late a la Detroit garage rock scene. Good mix of customers ranging from ska kids, dogs, hipsters, way too dressed up singles, and middle-aged peeps. Always super busy on the weekends - you need to drink to not have a panic attack smooshing through the crowd ;)

Day/time of visit: weekday lunch
Atmosphere: casual, sports bar

Looks like a typical sports bar, imagine it's packed and rowdy on event nights, lunch was low key. Started out with some fried green beans - these were great and the accompanying ranch wasabi dipping sauce was awesome. Ordered a club sandwich and coleslaw side - club was nothing special and coleslaw was boring (kinda wished I had ordered fries or homemade chips and gone whole hoggy ;) Prices are reasonable for the quality/quantity/type of food. 

Would revisit but it's not going to be on my 'favs' list.

I have been to Yapple three days straight now! I think this place is better than Sweet Ending or Phileo Yogurt, so there is no need to go into the city to get good frozen yogurt. The flavors are amazing, I have three flavors that I love here the green apple, blood orange, and the chocolate sorbert. There also so many toppings to choose from, I love the little balls filled w mango/orange flavor those things are so good and I haven't seen it any where else. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants some good frozen yogurt!

Oh how we love this place!

Great meal tonight. I ordered the Maccharoni and my wife ordered the scampi. We were lucky enough to have Chef Chris come to our table and talk with us about our meal and even told us how to make it at home. I had to give him a hug in thanks for the delicious meal and for being so cool. 

Later a friend introduced us to co-owner Steven who was very gracious and seemed a genuinely nice man. He is the kind of person that should run every restaurant - really makes you feel welcome & special.  We can't wait for our next visit. 

OH! Make sure to try the Petite Petite red blend for your wine pairing - so good.

The staff was pleasant when we checked in & out.  The other thing was they were pet friendly.  Which is always a bonus for anyone traveling with pets!  
There's only one main elevator by the lobby so, if you have a lot of items or are handicapped, hopefully there's not too many people during your stay.
The room was mediocre but the bathroom was questionable.  The bathroom in our suite was fairly large but was not planned out properly.  The repairs were also very visible.
Lastly, the breakfast buffet was $15 if you weren't a club member so, sign up for that or you'll have to fill your $15 worth!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The issue here is that this is the best place in the area, but if it were near Temple's main campus it would be very mediocre. Having said that, its still good and cheap. 

The people who work there are really nice. You get a lot of weird people in there, though. Its usually pretty busy, as its the most popular place around. 

About the menu? They have the same as any other chinese takeout place. I happened to like their beef dishes a lot, while the chicken ones weren't that great. Don't waste your time with eggrolls or wonton soup because they don't jack inside.

Good sushi in Nashville is hard to come by, so when I saw this place was rated 5 stars, I had to try. 

I was not disappointed. The service was wonderful and friendly, the atmosphere relaxing and the sushi... Wow. It was AMAZING! Honestly the best I've had in a loooonng time. 

I split the Shiki roll, Godzilla roll and mango shrimp roll with my husband and they were all perfection- Godzilla being the overall favorite. 

Do yourself a favor and get here asap for an experience your heart and belly will thank you for.

If work downtown and you're grabbing lunch, it's always a choice between expensive upscale restaurants and down-n-dirty lunch joints.  DuJour offers something smack in the middle.  

Choose between panini, salad, sandwiches or flat bread (a personal favorite) -- all of which will put you in the $7-12 range.

Best of all, the menu is fresh -- both from an ingredients perspective as well as meal choice.  They do a good job of putting pleasing twists on standard fare like turkey BLT or tomato-basil-mozzarella.   

I'll back for lunch 2-3 times a month.

Since I discovered this place sometime last year, I've become a regular.  This is a coffee shop that offers a menu of various freshly cooked foods.  Some foods are the same each day and others change according to the preferences of the chef.  I always get an egg sandwich with sausage, egg, and cheese on a bagel, and it is consistently the best egg sandwich I get anywhere.  The shop offers a comfortable environment with plenty of tables, a couch, and art on the walls.  It is an independent family owned business with an individualized touch.  I recommend it, and I disagree with other reviewers who were critical.

I went in to this location today to grab some lunch for me and my bf. I had a coupon they sent out in the junk mail, it was a 2 Mottza burger, 2 drinks, and 2 fries kinda deal.

So I had asked her if I could change one of the burgers to a chubby chicken burger..thinking it would be no big deal....Apparently, its a huge deal for them, and there was a big spiel as to why they couldn't allow that. OK; so fine 2 mottza burgers it is. 

Except for that when we got home and opened them it was 2 teen burgers..in double teen burger wrapping. Well done, well done.

I have several chemical peels (all prepaid for) with this place..so every few week's I go in..so I call today to book an appointment and because they've put up a LOAD of deal on the deal websites..they don't have any appointments until mid January! 

I mean these treatments are meant to be relatively close together to actually do anything..so now it will be 2 months between treatments. There's no point even getting them done now as there will be no effect :(

The girl on the phone gave me the big spiel about it being a Christmas rush..well if you flood the deal sights than there is no room for the rest of your customers. Very disappointed.

I had one of the limited time specials (Jerk Chicken) as well as a small salad.  I wasn't a fan of the salad dressing (Vinegarette, thickened with corn starch) they offered, but the macaroni and cheese was pretty good.  The macaroni and cheese was served on something that resembled a small, personal sized cast iron pan; portion size for the macaroni and cheese regular size was a bit small given the price ($7-8), but filling.  I'd go back to try the other flavors when/if I get a craving for macaroni and cheese.

This place is legit!!!  I happened to be on a truck, for work, driving a route this particular day. I didn't pack enough food for the energy I was exerting and needed to find a bathroom and a quick bite to eat Togo. Big Fred's looked so inviting with the diner type theme AND it had parking for a large box truck!  The options all looked delicious. (Did I mention I was starving?). I asked about the fish sandwich and was assured it was breaded in-house. ~Ding. Ding. Ding. Ding. Right answer!!!   It was SO delicious!  I highly recommend this place for the homey feel and the fresh food.

The miso soup was great, very flavorful. The portions were very big we ordered several rolls and definitely had leftovers. The tuna-tuna roll was good, the mango was a great flavor combined with the tuna and ponzu sauce. The spicy tuna crunch was great too. The waitstaff was fantastic, couldn't have been friendlier or more attentive. The rock shrimp tempura was bland, there wasn't enough flavor to the shrimp and not enough sauce but the presentation was beautiful. Everything was very fairly priced and I will definitely return.

This place is ok but nothing special.  Cheesesteaks, chicken sandwiches, strombolis, pizza.  Maria's Special Cheesesteak has provolone and broccoli rabe.  It's pretty good and different than you'd see at most places (Tony Luke's offers the same sandwich) so that's why I went from 2 to 3 stars.  Sandwiches are around $7 so you can stay around $12 when you add drink and fries.  I'll be back but it's not a place I'm jacked up about.  
One note on the fries: they are the right kind of fries (non-coated) and they are properly cooked (not undercooked or reheated/overfried).  This was another thing that got them the 3rd star.

Consistently dirty, bad food and service. Unfortunately, my kid likes this dump and it's on the way to school, scouts and the movie theater. 
   Food is always gross - eating area and bathrooms always dirty - employee attitude is always apathetic at best and they are not too smart...
   This is not a new thing - this has been the same at this location for 12 years. I travel across the country weekly and I have eaten at hundreds of Wendy's locations. Most are pretty good. This one is not. The owners either never visit this location or they have no pride. Either way, the result is the same. Terrible.

I came to Bubble Buzz for the eggies (a treat I first experienced in Vancouver), but I was a little disappointed. My previous experience with eggies was a light crispy sphere that broke off easily and had a little bit of chewy batter in the middle. The eggies here were dense, heavy, and tough. The mango bubble tea that we ordered was really tasty (thick and not too sweet), except the sago were undercooked. 

I won't go out of my way to come back, but it's a nice place to stop by if you're in the neighborhood.

i love this gym! i'm a proud member. they offer a LARGE amount of yoga classes, which is wonderful :)  love all the teachers, love all the classes i've ever taken. what i love about this gym, is it is all ages friendly... meaning someone who is sixty+ can take a class with a twenty something year old, and everyone feels comfortable at their own skill level.  everyone who attends the gym is super nice and friendly. i've met so many wonderful people from the neighborhood and beyond.  love the staff. they're always very very helpful.  it will be hard if i ever have to move and leave this gym!  it's that great!
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Let me preface this review by saying I grew up on La Hacienda. Quesdailla Verde, Vegetarian B, and Enchiladas Haciendas are dishes that will always be with me and my reminiscent stomach.

However, La Hacienda is much like El Rodeo and El Jaripeo in that they cater to people who want a certain type of Mexican. This is food is more authentic than taco bell, but very unoffensive. It's good food and it serves its purpose. 

I'll come here when I crave chicken nachos or margaritas. Otherwise, It's La Parada time.

Had a great brunch with about 25 other friends at Harvey's today . . . they are awesome.  We were able to make reservations and reserve the back room with picnic tables.

Harvey's has been around a long time and is consistent.  They make everything from scratch and have the best dressings and food.  I love the breakfast potatoes on their Sunday brunch, fried veggie app, and almost all their sandwiches.  The fires and potato salad are awesome too.

It is kid friendly and always packed.  They have a bar and lots of regulars.  The price is right as well.  Cheers!

The actual 3.5 average of all the reviews is appropriate. Like many reveiwers are initial reaction a few years ago was that we would never return. The Prussian mentality of the wait staff was entirely unacceptable and the no substitute policy just added to the insult. We returned at the invitation of friends and things have improved, but only marginally. The staff is friendlier, but is reluctant to split checks, good restaurants do this with a smile. They were out of the special by 7:30 on a Friday. The food is good ,but not that good and still no substitutions. Not our first choice when we are in Indy.

Had dinner here on Saturday night, after a great day at the Zurich golf tourney.

I ordered veal saltimbucca, it was very good, and just the right portion size. I tasted the swordfish special, and my friends pasta dish - both were first rate.

Service was quite good, and the waiter had excellent knowledge of the menu. We were impressed. Things arrived at a slightly less than average pace, and this was perfect for us on this night, as we had a lot to catch up on with our friends from Mandeville.

The restaurant was packed, the bar was busy, and we had a nice time.

George's is locally owned and operated and it just keeps getting better and better.   For you beer lovers, there's Bells and other crafts on tap.  The last time I went there solo I tried the tasty  fish tacos and they were very good and a great value.  George's features a good, solid menu.  I've been there several times for dinner a few times with friends.   One time, we had a hankering for Sangria for some odd reason, and they were happy to oblige us: what a nice surprise!  I hear it's a great place for gatherings, too.  George's is in the top of its class of mid-range, all-purpose restaurants.  It will be interesting to see how it evolves.

Went there last week because we haven't had sushi in a VERY long time. WHAT a disappointment. You would think that being so close to the ocean there would be good seafood. Unfortunately we have yet to find it. The sushi was ok, but we have have had much better back home in Tucson (the middle of the desert), and the appetizers were extremely small.  The service was the only thing we are willing to applaud. 

The waitress' wear Kimono's, which is cool. But our waitress was really attentive and checked on us constantly. So I guess we are still on the hunt for good seafood. Raw or cooked. Will not be going back and wouldn't recommend it.

The service is excellent and the staff was friendly and helpful. But when I'm getting dropped off by a friend or picked up, where do they park? There doesn't appear to be any parking and I see other customers with the same issue. I've seen people park on the side on the frontage road (which is dangerous, I don't recommend it), or next to the return gate. When I asked an attendant where they could park, they always point to a lot near the front that must be employee parking becuz it's always full. With such a big lot, you'd figure they could find another spot for them to park.

I would give Sakana 5+ stars if I could. This is hands down the BEST Sushi ever!!! You don't need soy sauce, instead just enjoy the fabulous flavors and sauces on the plates. The rolls are big, colorful and loaded with flavor!!!! Each one looks like a piece of art. Must trys are: Tuna Carpaccio Volcano, Grilled stuffed calamari, TNT roll, Red Wine eel roll and the Tofu Cheese cake. 

The restaurant is small, but always worth the wait!!!! Everytime we are going to pass through montecito on our way to SB we stop here! Service is always great too!!

Generally this restaurant would get four stars but today's Ita hard to even give it three. The restaurant is totally understaffed but I guess their attitude is - "you've got no where else to go tonight as all the other restaurants in town are closed for Christmas so just be thankful you don't have to cook". The service is totally lacking tonight as we ordered edamame and it never came out. The food did not come out together which means one person got their food at a time. Suggestion - avoid this place on Christmas

I am Japanese, born and raised in Japan. I'm picky about Japanese restaurant. Tokyo Restaurant had good atmosphere and great service. Menu is somewhat limited, but the food was "good enough" to be called Japanese. We had sashimi and sushi combination platter. It didn't come with salad or soup. Salmon was very very delicious. Rice was a little hard. The worst part is the price. I have paid this much and more for sushi and sashimi before, but I didn't eat anything worth that in this restaurant. This was a good restaurant, but not a good value.

What's to say. This is not a gourmet or craft or boutique donut shop. It's a branch of a chain of nearly nationwide donut shops. The best you can say for this place is that it is reasonably consistent with other DDs. Pretty good hot coffee, fair selection of commonplace donuts. Specialty drinks and sandwiches also available.

Staff is friendly enough. Seniors get a 10% discount...(thank you).

Drive through gets jammed early morning as the rush to the office gets underway. 

Yes, we'll stop again....but only because my grandson likes their jelly-filled Munchkins (donut holes) and....they're about the only donut joint in this part of town.

Sam is a complete loony tune. He tried kicking us out for no known reason but we insisted on staying. Once we started swearing at him he became a lot nicer and told us that Katy Perry was getting a divorce. He is well versed on all Hollywood drama. He yelled at a lot of people in the very short amount of time that we were there. Our food cost 8 dollars each and he told us that if we left him a tip we weren't allowed to come back. How's that for a complete lunatic. This is the best place in nashville. I'll be back tomorrow.

1. only takes cash
2. has one bathroom
3. serving sizes are way too small 

You figure if they are only taking cash, they could use all the blanketed tax money on another bathroom.  The server said the pasta servings are appetizer portions but offered to upgrade the serving to entree portions by doubling the price.  When we got our pasta it was still a ridiculously small portion.  The food was not good enough to override all the cons about this place.  Only good things are byob and server was nice.  Plenty of other byob italian places in the city that blow this place out of the water.  Would not come back.

Could be a nice place if the sushi options had more variety. Especially during lunch time. I had AYCE and there are not that many long rolls to choose from and most of the choices were deep fried or had tempura item inside. I very much prefer fresh fish, so wasn't taken away. The plus - rolls were cut into small one-bite size pieces, which are easy to maneuver without making an ungodly mess. The fish seems fresh, nigiri was very nice and surprisingly large size.  
The place is clean and service is very attentive and polite, but not in your face. Might go back for dinner if in the area, but will not go out of my way to eat there.

Stumbled upon this place this weekend looking for a quick lunch.  We got here at the right time as it was pretty open when we arrived but quickly filled up and was full when we left.  Service was fast and friendly on my visit.

I ended up having the fajita quesadilla with chicken and it was a good lunch portion and priced well.  It came out fast and unlike some places the quesadilla wasn't soggy in grease, which made it all the better in my book.  They have various weekday and weekend specials that I'll be trying out in the near future.

Finally got a chance to check out the infamous Bartaco earlier this week.  I was shocked that there was a 30 minute wait at 8pm on a Tuesday night, but it happens.  Once seated, the server we had was very attentive and explained the concept to us.  We had orders of the cucumber salad, black beans, chips an salsa, and I ordered the Chicken Rice Bowl for my entree.  The tacos on the menu are mini sized as are most items on the menu.  It makes for a great way to try a variety of different items.  Overall the flavors of my food were great and I will definitely be back!

We stumbled upon this bar while walking around the French Quarter and deciding we needed to get a drink to beat the afternoon heat.  The sign out front advertised a 2 for 1 specialty cocktail happy hour so we stopped in.  It seemed to be a newer place given the appearance of the inside of the bar and only a couple of regulars seemed to be occupying the stools at the bar. The bartender was friendly and took care and time in crafting our cocktails.  I had the Pimm's cup which was a balanced mix of flavors and a refreshing treat.  Overall a great place to stop in for drinks day or night.

Stopped in here with a group of friends on New Year's Eve as we were staying out at the beach that night.  We were really appreciative of how their staff was easily able to accommodate our reservation for 12 and even let us have their semi-private front room area just for our group.  The Sangria we ordered for the table was served at room temperature sans fruit so we were all a bit mystified by this.  Otherwise, most people enjoyed their meals.  I tried the Margherita Pizza and was not disappointed.  Overall a quaint place to have a meal if you are not in the mood for bar type food or seafood while out at the beach.

I used to be an intern at a nearby office and one day, my manager took the whole department out for lunch here. My co-workers said this place is usually quiet (one recalled one occurrence where she and her husband were the only customers around). Not the best, yet not the worst Italian food I've had. Interning in the suburbs where lunch options are very limited (compared to my colleagues who get to intern in the heart of Philly's skyscrapers forest/food truck jungle), I don't really have anything to complain about Bertucci's.

I had to wait for an hour, but I'm telling you Joe is worth the wait. I just wanted to cut my hair short without any clue of which style. All I knew was I wanted it to be short and Asian, if you know what I mean. I've heard about Joe being so awesome in handling Asian hair, so I came in and told him do whatever you think looks good on me. He was so patient and asked my feedback as he worked on my hair. I was very satisfied at the work he did. Even after a month after the cut, people around me haven't stopped complimenting my hair, thanks to Joe. He wouldn't expect you to tip him, but please, the guy deserves it.

This is a solid, consistently good sushi place that is decently priced and a great option for lunch or dinner (great lunch specials, btw). The quality of the sushi is really good - maybe not quite as great as Morimoto, but pretty darn close and way less expensive. And I think it's just as good as pricier sushi places, like Zama or Raw. The vibe is also modern and pretty, and the service is super friendly and efficient. 

Highly recommend this place if you're looking for something nicer than Mizu or Vic's, but you don't want to spend a fortune for sushi.

Thin beds, musky smell, no gym beginning of Nov 2018 due to a flood.

If you're platinum member the lounge is a great place for breakfast, apps, and amazingly DESSERT!!! The lounge is also decked out with tons of fresh fruit and amazing Harney & Sons tea.

Beautiful lobby. Elevators can get packed. Rooms are decently sized. Clean sheets, great workstation with plenty of outlets and media plugs. The toiletries smells like old people though, that rice bran oil I think. Parking is a dangerous game on Wednesdays and Thursdays. I'm not sure where you'd park if the first two rows are taken.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I don't know what happened on this night, because I see the other positive reviews, so I want to keep it nice here cause I'm in a good mood today. But I'd expect this type of sushi if I was to make sushi at home while drunk. For example the avocado roll, consisted of a chunk of avocado pushed into the center of some mushy rice and slapped on a plate. I don't think the avocado ever met the blade of a knife. Needless to say there was no-need for a to go box, because it only should go in the trash. On a positive note, the people there were very nice

Way overpriced for food that was good but wasn't great. Party of 6 came out to close to 200 dollars. 3 of the ones in that party were children. I mean come on, 17 dollars for chicken Alfredo and a little over 20 dollars for cheese ravioli?  It's a disgrace to charge that much for something so very simple. If you look at the money signs it states there are 2 when clearly it should be marked 4 because of their prices. Don't try and drum up your business by charging outrageous prices but by offering great food at reasonable prices and you'll get more than enough business.

This place was one of those places you really don't want to tell anyone about because you want to keep it your little secret but I thought why not share it with everyone else. Well first off the food is authentic, you have maybe 3 or 4 older ladies cooking in the back, just like grandma does and boy is it delicious. I would sit here and tell you specifically what to order but honestly I do believe everything they make is good. Definitely make it your next Mexican food stop. (Don't be confused when you first go in the front door, it is a Mexican grocery store in the front just keep walking to the back and you'll find it.)

My first time here in years, and it was okay. The place was not busy, although it was early, probably around 5:45 pm; and the service was attentive and good. We got two different rolls and sushi. I was a bit disappointed with the eel, it lacked the flavor that I'm accustomed to when ordering that dish, and the rolls were also good, but not exceptional. I thought they could've turned the AC a little cooler because it felt rather stuffy and warm in the dining room. Over all, nothing to jump up and down about, but still a good experience.

This place is pretty expensive but you do get what you pay for. The foods are very well presented and have a variety of complementary flavors. The food is just really well done and it's a joy to eat. We started with the sweet potato pie and shrimp starters then moved on to the duck and beef short rib entrees. Finished with chocolate and olive oil cakes. I also had the Japanese Matcha. The total bill including tip was $150, but I would go back again for special occasions. I would say this is one of the nicer restaurants in Media. Oh, and service was very professional - top notch.

Samarai is a little hole in the wall place with friendly service and delicious aromas filling the air. I ordered the Shoyu Ramen, which comes with pork and vegetables. I was happy with the amount of vegetables, and the pork is also a good size. The broth is good, but my heart belongs to another Ramen place in town, so it's hard to live up to my favorite. However, I did enjoy my bowl of Shoyu Ramen, which left me satisfied and full. I'll definitely come back to try other items on the menu. It's nice that there's even an outside booth for additional seating. How often do you get to see a booth outside? :)

This was my first time to this location, and every In-N-Out feels pretty much the same.  Great customer service!  Our server was friendly and helpful.  The restaurant was clean.  I ordered the cheeseburger, animal style, with fries and a side of the Special sauce.  It took less than 10 minutes for our number to be called, as the place was pretty packed.  I forgot to tell ask for no bun, and went back to the counter and asked for lettuce in lieu of a bun.  I was given a generous amount of lettuce, and pretty much had a salad, as I dipped it with my extra sauce.  I love how the French fries are made from fresh potatoes.  Yum!

The place has a weird vibe. They have chic booths and seating but the decor is off. There are columns, arches and weird tuscan-esque walls; it doesn't really flow. The menu follows suit, with a variety of random and pricey choices. We had the cheesesteak egg-rolls for an appetizer and they were pretty good, but I've had better. Ordered a burger and carved roast beef sandwich, they came with fries that were extremely salty. The sandwiches were okay, but not really worth the price. If I eat here again, I would like to be drunk enough to enjoy the bland food. The waitress was very nice and the beers were delish.

Was staying at the hotel across the street and needed to grab something quick before we got ready to go to the airport. I saw a sign indicating that they were offering off 2 sausage biscuits for $2. What a great deal! Yes, it is just McDonald's. But I LOVE their sausage biscuits. Especially with the grape jelly. It was a CRAZY run across the major street to get to the store. Overall, it was quick to order and get my food even though there appeared to be a morning rush. Everything tasted great. Happy customer.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Are you kidding me??? This place is the best sushi around. I just love the hand rolls and Jimmy turned me on to a raw scallop hand roll that melts in your mouth. So I get it every angle time I roll into this place. Tonight I got takeout for the first time and just had to finally write a review. 

Go here and you wi t be disappointed. Be smart about what you order, ask lots of questions and don't order something with things in it you don't liked, like cream cheese or mayo... You get the point.  Tell them what you do like and they'll point you in the right direction. 

Get the tuna sashimi platter too!  It freaking rocks!!!!!!

The Short: Decent food, too many TVs

The Long: I guess I was expecting a rustic feel, not a sports bar.  I hear that some people enjoy watching sporting events (ha!) but that's not me.  Other than that, the feel of the place is fun!  The staff was friendly without being in your face.  

All the food and drinks were good, but I do have to rave about the Sasquatch Burger.  My husband ordered this behemoth - giant burger with grilled cheese sandwiches for buns - and it was awesome!  If you are hungry or have someone to share with, get it. 

Great location and good energy, we'll be back!

This place is what customer service is all about!  The folks at this branch are so kind and personable!  I have rented here about 5 times and almost every time I go in without a reservation and in 10 minutes I drive away with a rental car.  And since it is just south of center city the place is never crowded.  I am not sure if it is the manager there, but there is one guy who is there every time I have gone and its always such a pleasure to chat with him while I fill out paperwork and he takes my info.  If you need a rental with no BS this is the place!  They also normally have really nice cars.

I really don't know why we went here in the 1st place but it just was the only thing in the complex that was not fast food, it looked fine, until we walked in pretty drab which is most Asian food places.  The waiter was more concerned about sitting and reading the paper than he was about serving food.  I can kind of understand his concern or lack there of.  The food while edible was about as good as a can of Chung King that has been on my parents pantry shelf since the age of Disco (the early 80's for those of you too young to know).  I would try to avoid this place unless you like marginal food.

Pretty much my favorite dive bar right now. The bar tenders are awesome, and while youd think the crowd would be a bunch of uptight blue collar dudes, they are actually awesome. Every time I go here the few regulars cool as hell and will buy you drinks if you arent a total asshole. Ive gotten more drunk here than almost every other place in the city because the atmosphere just lends itself to drinking. 

Jukebox is awesome too, it only accepts old 5$ bills which is hilarious and its fun to put on 13 minute metalcore songs and not have anyone complain.

Buy union

Simply the most gorgeous liquor store in Philly Center City. It has a wide variety of options and did have Pappy on offer (for about an hour) once it came in! 

It hosts several wine tastings so be sure to stop on by - taste some wine and stare at the sheer abundance of liquor and wine on offer. It almost measures up to Total Wine in Cherry Hill ... but I suppose it's better than having to trek all the way to Jersey for a good bottle (I suppose that is technically illegal by Philly standards as well *wink wink*).

This was our second time coming for the lunch prix fixe. First off, they would not honor our living social deal (which was fine). The more egregious error(s) had to do with the fact that there were lobster shells in the lobster risotto ... the stuffed chicken was well overdone ... and the breadsticks were stale. The salads were pretty good and the gelato was excellent! I will be willing to give Bliss another chance since the first time around, the dining experience was much better. But hopefully we won't run into this problem again. Service was very good.

Classic 3.5 star type place. Service started off slow, but different than other pizza places where you can request what you want. Basically, like Qdoba but for pizza. Pizzas come out quick once they're in the oven (maybe 2 minutes) and were pretty tasty. 10" regular size is about perfect for one person, maybe slightly more.

Sweet italian sausage as a topping is really good, as was the fresh mozzarella. Sauce was just OK. Prices were reasonable given how many toppings you could potentially order. If they can get the logistics right, could be very popular.

Solid meh. Was here for a conference and did not stay overnight. The conference was geared toward design professionals and I was surprised that the hotel was not better designed. In the ladies room, for instance, there was no one in the stalls next to me, but the automatic toilets were flushing with abandon. What a waste of water. Parking layout seemed extremely awkward and difficult to find as evidenced by strangers asking me where it was. On the plus side, it is a convenient location and the fresh food was good.  Grateful for the Starbucks in the lobby, but canned soda was $2 each, which seemed exorbitant even in the city.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Update to my earlier review. We called several times asking for a manager even called corporate several times and have never received a call back. The deductible has since been paid as well as claim by the person who caused accident insurance company. We had to fight the $500 charge with our credit card company. TOTAL disrespect from this location. Buyer beware! There are other locations that I would consider renting from before booking. As you can see from my Yelp page it takes a lot for me to give someone a poor Yelp review but the customer service was SO bad at this location I had to let others know to avoid a major headache!

Seriously not a great spot. I HATE giving bad reviews but this place is run so poorly I feel people need to be aware. Dunkin is a chain so you have typical expectations and this location is way below the expectations. This is our 3rd time being disappointed. They usually get order wrong, ie wrong donuts provided. The last order our jelly donuts were literally smashed as if the guy at the window did it on purpose. This time there was no jelly in the donut...it's our last visit. To the owners...please give your employees some more training. There are some nice girls that work there so this is not pertaining to all...but your losing customers.

Good go-to neighborhood gym. Has all the basics, never have a problem getting a cardio machine, facilities and equipment are clean and well kept, the industrial quality of the space (exposed brick, tall ceilings, open plan, etc) make this place a good gym.  The reason it doesn't get four stars is it lacks some of the amenities that many other city gyms have - locker rooms don't have steam room or saunas, in fact the layout of the locker rooms is small in comparison to most gyms, the classes aren't anything to write home about, and it can be hard to find a space to do floor work or free weights during peak times.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Our friends recommended this place after they tried it for the first time. We bought  groupon for this place and by far, this is the best hibachi we've been to in the area. It's better then Bennihana. The only negative thing was that we were celebrating a friend's birthday so I called to reserve a room, but they ended up sitting other parties in the same room. We went on a Friday night and it was pretty busy. I would definitely recommend making reservations. They also have a full bar here. The food was delicious and not too greasy like most chinese/hibachi places. It was a little expensive, so I wouldn't go back unless we had a Groupon or deal.

Called ahead. Was told I could be be taken immediately. Got in my car, drove to this destination. Somewhere within those two sentences of actions they had filled up so much I had a 20 minute wait. What in the heck. Just got a gel manicure, and the person doing the manicure for me changed not one but two times. At the end of it, I had no idea who to give the undeserved tip to! My nails came out sloppy and the sides were left completely unpolished. The only thing I liked about this messy, low-class looking salon was the amazing selection of gel polish colors. My usual salon only has about 10 gel colors to choose from. This place has tons!

Its located in Clay Terrace that has a huge parking lot in the pack. The atmosphere is very much family style but can be a lil romantic for your Friday night dinners. They have a patio on the side which is great during summer and perfect for people watching. 

They have a variety of menu. They even have a pretty good gluten free menu which is a plus. They can easily substitute some items in your meal to accommodate your diet.

Don't skip on dessert though. For gluten free people like me, their creme brûlée is a must have!

If Chipotle had a brother from another mother...that will be Piada. The layout is pretty similar and the decor is more contemporary. It's a perfect place to grab a quick lunch and definitely on the cheap side. The portions are great and a good selection of meat for your salad, wrap or pasta. 

There's an Italian soda station that's refillable which I think is great. My fave aqua panna is also a main staple. 

I will skip the cannoli chips next time though. Overall, it's a great and cheap place for lunch or maybe a take out.

It's your neighborhood hibachi place. Locals like this place and you'll see walls and walls of polaroids of people who have celebrated birthdays there. It's actually a package where you can get a dessert, birthday song, and Polaroid for about $5. 

This place is famous for their ginger sauce that you drown your fried rice with. It's pretty solid. You can't skip on their playboy roll where the whole thing lights up on fire. 

There's a kids menu, decent selection of sake and they also have a bar. There's plenty of parking, service is fast and price wise is right.

I've never seen my hubby be so giddy about a frozen yogurt place. Coming from LA, we had our fair share of yogurt places including Yogurtland and Pinkberry who started the craze. However, this is exceptionally different since he likes the variety of toppings offered. He also liked the quality of the yogurt, the decor, pricing and location.

My hubby has a weird sense of taste so he got the vanilla and pomegranate berry flavor with weird combination of toppings (nerds, nilla wafer, cherries, sprinkles, strawberry). I'm sure our punch card will be used quite often.

This place is the real deal. Be prepared to call ahead in advance. It's quite small inside and people typically line out the door. 

Asaka is Japanese owned and actually frequented by local Japanese folks so you know it's legit. The entree selection is quite extensive for a small place.

I ordered the grilled squid with sauce, grilled salmon collar, gyudon, tempura and a maki. They were all delicious. The place is priced so right and even has a happy hour. 

Plenty of parking outside, has a kids menu, good selection of sake, carries Japanese beer and good service.

The pizza is not terrible, but it's not far from it. It has some resemblance to dare I say frozen pizza. The meatball sandwich is good though. It didn't help that the pricing was high for what you get too. The girl at the front desk had a hard time understanding my order as well. I don't get the 4-star rating they have. I will say that the four TVs are nice if you are dining in, but they play odd stuff  (ie. it's the baseball playoffs and they don't have it on???) It's close to the theaters so that helps a bit if you are planning to watch a movie. Irritating that they kicked me out at 8:30pm.

If you are planning an event....This is the place! Ive been here for a number of events, Yelp, Charity, etc. It is always a fun night. The last time was for a charity that used TPepin to cater and it was damn good. Not foodie good but who expects that at an event but surprisingly good food. The space itself is huge; unless your expecting 300-500 plenty of room for all. Decor is beautiful, large bar at one end. They have a stage with access from behind. There is a ton of parking. If you need an event space this is it.

This is definitely a sushi favorite.
Their special rolls are amazing! It's made well and when it comes to your table, it looks great and tastes like it! I don't know who their sushi chef is but he creates miracles!
It opens for lunch and then closes to reopen for dinner. And although, street parking is a bit difficult to find, this place is probably my number one in the city for sushi. The ambience is very modern and it can be a little quiet at times even though there is conversation going on. Great for couples and small groups.
Recommended this place to friends and they all said they loved it. It's worth to try this place at least once.

This gets 4 stars and not 5 simply because of the prices. I know it is a local and family owned business, so it is almost impossible to compete price wise with the big box stores. Nonetheless, I continue to shop here for my at home bar. The selection is incredible (they must be really good at Tetris because I have no idea how all of that fits in a tiny location) and they have everything you could ever think of. I've gotten some great recommendations from the staff here and really enjoy stopping by. What a fantastic business.

We stayed here again!!! We got a bigger room than last time and it was really nice, lots of space and a fridge :). I wish they had a pool here but other than that you probably wouldn't have to leave the hotel for anything. I love the Red Bar in the lobby area. All the staff are super nice, from the Valet to the housekeeping crew! I like the fact that I saw the same faces in the short amount of time that I was there and they said hello and had small talk, and this is w/ housekeeping and the bellman...not the lady who answer's the phone Mrs. Wills....that's just her job.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Good food and service in trendy Seminole Heights
Fresh and tasty,  we shared several small plates, starting with the Salade Lyonnaise, very good version of the French classic, then the Brussels sprouts, they were cooked perfectly but unfortunately too salty, the pork belly on corn bread was yummy and the lobster and wild mushroom risotto delicious and full of flavor, a must try. We paired our meal with a good white Vouvray and finished our meal with a semifreddo ganache dessert. Overall a great meal and evening among an interesting crowd. Special thanks to Gem our server, she was knowledgeable and courteous.

I've been living in Santa Barbara three months now and have been to Willie's 3 times.  I'm happy to say I've found my barbershop.  Each time I came out with a long crew cut I was more than satisfied with. Gilbert and Willie are both great guys and they've been doing this forever.  I've had my hair cut by both of them and they're both skilled in what their trade.  $20 bucks and 20-30 minutes of my time (even during the lunch hour when I typically go) I came out clean cut, looking fresh and ready to take over the world.

Oh lord...Decades. How do review you? You are the best and worst in all of us. You are the one word that sums up how my night went. You are drinking more than I should, dancing as if I knew how, and stumbling home with less than half of the friends I came with. I don't know how you do it, but I'm not even mad. I love you for all that you are, and forgive your transgressions. You are my quazi-monthly escape from even resembling a responsible adult. Keep doin' what you do (but charge less for the shots if its not too much trouble).

The Andouille  Sausage Benedict was scrumptious. Nice helping of crawfish is on the dish. The hollandaise literally and figuratively topped it off. I ate this dish in tiny bites to savour the experience. Their NOLA roast coffee is nice accompaniment as is the fresh OJ. The menu has some interesting sounding options and they always have a few daily special editions. On weekdays there is a hard stop of 10:30 for breakfast, but on weekends it's all day. The prices for the elaborate dishes are commensurate with the ingredients and prep time.

I like the Pinkberry idea. Tasty frozen yogurt topped with fresh fruit, chocolate, coconut, whatever you fancy. I visit them when I am out west, and in NOLA. There is one uptown on Mag, which has some outdoor seating in the suburbs. This one is right smack downtown at the intersection of Canal, Peters and Tchop. Its across from the Shops on Canal, in a high pedestrian traffic area which makes for some good people watching. This place has a little gated garden with seating. It's a perfect place to have a refreshing break on a hot afternoon.

Well, Expedia didn't accept my review probably because I mentioned that the price being advertised on the street was way less than what I paid for my reservation. I found that same thing in Las Vegas, though.
As far as Flamingo goes, it seems like a fairly cute place, pink and nostalgic, but the upkeep could be better.
