It has a kitchen and coffee maker, but no coffee cups or plates or utensils of any kind. The Bathroom door had a problem closing. No iron or hair dryer. We borrowed both from office. If you go there, look in the fridge, we forgot 4 Newcastles.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
eh....it's the lesser of two evils. it's a convenient market for last minute stuff but that's about it. the produce section may be one of the worst ive ever seen from a market in north america.  veggies are in their latter stages.  the prices are a bit on the high side as well for common things like poultry. but black people love their chicken so why discount it right?
very unprofessional employees but i find it amusing. 
if you're looking to do go grocery shopping this is not the place. if you want something a little more than a 7-eleven this will do

My respite from the overwhelming mound of laundry across the street at the laundromat.  

I come here to enjoy a cappucino and read while my laundry tumbles and tumbles.  

Ample seating in and out. Free wi fi. Great/friendly staff. Fine choice of teas and coffee; but none of that silly crappucino stuff.  They have a corner selling little soaps and sassy memo pads. (Unfortunately, the soaps aren't natural but very cute packaging). 

Overall a great place and love that you could sit here and enjoy the overcast yet warm days on the Mesa.

This is is my first nail place and so far, is the best (of the two i've visited).  It's clean and has a cute blue colored motif.  (Looks A LOT like Sakura in San Jose Japantown).   The receptionist is a little rude b/c i was a walk in and didn't have an appt.  But I was seated promptly and two people helped me one with my mani and one with my pedi.  

Pluses: I like the set up, both of my technicians spoke english, and good selection of nail polish. 

Negative: pricey, sort of hard to find and not exactly the "best" mani/pedi.  Total price is $54 including the tip.

We headed to Super Cucas on a Sunday afternoon and I drove right past it.  This location is sort of hard to find, hidden right before the over pass.

I ordered the veggie tacos and it was pretty good -- the only weird thing is that the tortillas were on the bottom of all the veggies making it impossible to actually eat a "taco".  The portion was pretty large.

My friends ordered a carnitas nachos -- very good with guacamole and sour cream, and a pork plate which was pretty good too and it was also a huge portion.  

The price was affordable and the taste authentic.  Overall, it's not a bad choice if you're hankering for mexican food.

I haven't actually eaten in the restaurant so this review is based on my take-out experiences.  It is really easy to call in an order, find a parking spot near the restaurant and the order is right and ready to go by the time I get there.  Although, like another review, they didn't answer my call on a Thursday night so I went elsewhere.  

I've had the veggie roll, edamame, and fried tofu (not sure if it was the tofu steak or fried tofu).  These items have been good and taste fresh.  I'll re-review when I get the chance to eat at the restaurant.

The hotel room was very nice and very clean. The bed was extremely comfortable and my bay view was very nice and calming. I was there for a trade show and I was able to get a nice comfortable rest every night.
The hotel is across the street from the convention center which makes it very convenient. 

They also have a nice spa where you can get facials, etc. Unfortunately I did not try it but their prices looked reasonable. $95-$110 for facials.  They also have a nice terrace where one can sit and read next to the bay. 

Over all very pleasant experience.  Nice and professional staff. You have to valet the car though and its $18/night.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
A very modern hotel in both decore and age.  The decore is not my style/preference but it was acceptable.

Fitness is well equipped but the TVs didn't have the same channels as in my room. 

Never found my bed to be overly comfortable and I'm not sure why.

Staff was always friendly.

There's a club room on the 4th floor.
 
In a quiet neighborhood and a very convenient location to explore downtown New Orleans.

This is a general complaint for most hotels im finding... I prefer using the stairs but found that they are not easy to access, locate, and move between floors.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The ambiance and music really added to the mexican type atmosphere. Rustic, trendy and charming and a place not to miss. Service was great and dishes were well explained.

 The chips and salsa were great - fresh chips, great salsa with a little kick, and free refills of both. 

Can't beat the happy hour, the Margaritas are light but for the price it's worth it. We had the usuals of tacos and Enchiladas and rice, they are good and never fail to fill one up. 

Just wish some Mexican restaurant around had some white queso! 

Chicken salad is one of my favorites.

Amazing. Best waffles I have had in STL. I wish it was open more days out of the week. During the several times I have eaten here, I have loved everything I have ordered. 
Be prepared to spend some money, especially if you double up the order, which I recommend if you are very hungry.
like so many of the other businesses on Cherokee Street, it really has a lot of character and an appealing, unique ambiance. The decor really gives Melt a character of its own.
Love this place
Ps: wake n bake, little piggy are two of my favorites thus far.

This location is okay, but pales in comparison to other Aldi locations. I believe it's mostly constained by the limited size of the store and parking. The cashiers are exceptionally expedient, however, and they would put most cashiers at Schnucks to shame for speed and quality of service. My biggest issue is the lack of selection and frequently out of stock produce. I usually find myself buying what I can at Aldi and going elsewhere for what was out of stock, not carried, etc.
BTW, this location does not stock any alcohol.
I again want to reiterate how great staff is...my big complaint being lack of selection and inventory.

We have a good ol' time here!

A honky-tonk it is not. Just a smoky bar with lots of beers and half-decent eats. Been to trivia here a couple of times on Wednesday nights and we always have a great time. One night, the the bartender wasn't super knowledgeable about the drafts (couldn't tell a lager from a wheat beer) which is kind of important at a bar called the Beer Seller but it happens. Parking is usually decent if there's not anything going on downtown b/c you can park off of Gay street for free. 

A great place to hideaway from the rest of the downtown madness.

This is some of the better pizza we have tried in the area. It's pricey for what you get, considering that it is very thin and not very cheesy. The pizza itself is pretty tasty, but I feel like I can find something even better and for a better price. I'm a cheese fry fanatic and theirs left something to be desired. I like my fries to be just plain old fries, these were coated, which I hate. The cheese was good wiz, and was just plopped on missing many fries. In addition, there is no delivery. Overall this pizzeria was acceptable, but not amazing.

The building & staff...
This place is very small and very cute. We rolled in about 5 minutes before they closed on a Saturday SoHo party time fun, but she was very polite. We made a little bit of a mess pouring our yogurt into the cups (she'd already cleaned), but she was still cool, so they get an A+ for service.

The food...
I wish I could give them a 5, but I just didn't enjoy the yogurt. If you're into fro yo, you'd probably like this. They have A LOT of flavor options and many toppings, but it's a bit pricey.

This Dunkin, like many of these stores, is a bit of a mess in the mornings. I don't know if it's a staff scheduling issue or what, but they just don't seem to handle being busy all that well. Going inside to avoid the drive thru line is a terrible idea because your order gets messed up and the wait is an eternity. 

However, getting good via drive through is a relatively safe bet that your order will be correct. But even that's not safe. 

It still gets three stars because Dunkin's coffee is so tasty. It's their service that sucks.

I've been passing O'Bistro for over a year, assuming it was an overpriced restaurant. I finally went in and was pleasantly surprised that it is not! Granted, there are expensive dishes, but there is a wide range cost-wise. 

My friend ordered the pot roast, and I ordered a cheeseburger with macaroni and andouille sausage as the side. The pot roast was tasty and included perfectly tender meat.  The burger was cooked to order, and the macaroni was so good!

There is a full bar with some choices in craft beer and a wide assortment of wine. The wait staff is nice, and the place is clean. I'll definitely be back!

Trains pass through the night and even on the 21st floor with the beautiful floor to ceiling windows you might want your earplugs. Rooms are so air tight doors click with HVAC. 

Banquet food is fantastic!! Service is consistently outstanding from the food & room service folks to the bar and valets. The Nashville mayor has turned lobby check ins into a political stand off if masks aren't secured but that's a politicians fault. 

.5 mile from the Strip is a short fun walk. The views are great. 

If the ownership was smart they'd hand out free earplugs.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I really like this place.  All I've had here is sushi. Because I love sushi and they have a great selectjon, priced from 5 to 10 dollars per roll.  I've eaten here about three times since moving to the area a month ago.   Service is usually efficient. The food tastes wonderful.   

Addressing other reviewers comments, they do usually have the kids here. Can't imagine how boring it is as a kid to hang out at your parents restaurant all the time! It never bothers me seeing them there.  

Also, they have to go menus.  You can call an order in and it will be made ready for pick up!!

Sushi Land reminds me of a small Japanese den. Intimate, cozy, warm Sushi bar you see all the time on TV. The only thing I feel is missing is a drunken Japanese business man hitting on my wife. 

I like the place for the decor, but also the way they arrange their seating area. It is just the right amount to move and feel comfortable, but also perfectly so you do get that communal feel without feeling like someone is eaves dropping. 

I would say there isn't a particularly exotic or adventurous menu, but then again it is main line and that should not be blamed on Sushi Land but the general lay of the land.

This casual pizza place is a convenient location inside a strip mall. You order up at the counter. We came on a Friday summer night and they offered us a complimentary glass of wine! We started with cheese fries. The crinkle cut fries came out piping hot with cheese whiz. My boyfriend and I then split a half-BBQ chicken, half-plain cheese pizza. 

I'm a bigger fan of brick-oven pizza with a slight bite to the bottom of the crust. This is a doughy, chewier crust. The flavors of the BBQ pizza were good, and my boyfriend quickly regretted his plain half. The service was pretty decent. They do a quick takeout, too.

Excellent service and food.  I visited the restaurant with a large group of friends and the staff took great care of us.  I had the gnocchi, which was cooked perfectly.  My wife had penne with broccoli and oil.  The broccoli was steamed just right and the garlic and oil was very tasty.  I also thought the pricing was reasonable given how well the food was prepared and how large the portions were.  I plan on visiting again to try all the other things on the menu that looked good.  Also, they are many vegetarian and even a few vegan options.

This is our go-to restaurant in our neighborhood. Period. We go there when we need a quick bite, and when we have out-of-town guests to have a leisurely meal. The food is always great, the service is friendly, and the atmosphere is upbeat and homey. 
Don't miss the fish taco! It's my absolute favorite. My typical order is one of these, an order of rice and beans, and a house margarita. And, after years of eating there, I just tried the flan. WOW! It's so tasty; fresh, creamy and vanilla-y, with the most fabulous caramel sauce. I highly recommend it!

This is an OK pizza joint although it's not in the same league as Flying Pie. The service is fairly good and friendly and as a bonus they do serve half pitchers of beer if you go by yourself and don't feel like pounding a whole one.

The pizza is good but nothing special.  They have your typical pizza joint salad bar with your choice of iceberg lettuce and ....well, iceberg lettuce.   It's got a "Family" vibe to it and is usually packed with noisy ill mannered bastard children whose parents think it's cute to ignore their tantrum throwing spawn. Aaaahhhrg!  Someone shoot me! More beer....

If you're looking for really decent Japanese food, this is the way to go.  My friend and I stuffed ourselves full of tapas and our $60 made perfect sense based on how absolutely full we were. The Dragon Eyes (fried salmon roll) and sushi pizza were absolute hits. 

The service can be slow and the booths don't allow for much privacy, but there are are separate rooms that can likely be reserved (I'm not sure, but it seemed the groups eating in them had reservations).  

All and all, I would definitely go there again and would love to introduce others to this restaurant.

If you have to be around 10th and Locust for any hospital visit, walnut street theatre trip, or visit down jewelers row,Fat Salmon is an awesome spot for lunch. I was seated promptly around 12:05 and by 12:15 I blinked and the place was swamped. I ordered off the lunch menu which provided either a soup or a salad, and got a spicy tuna roll two pieces of nigiri and 2 pieces of Nigiri for 11 bucks. The roll was significantly large in size and the nigiri already had wasabi added to it. (Always look for this for authenticity). The service was overly friendly prompt and the place was clean. Excellent spot for a high quality low price lunch.

The hotel is right across the street from the Arch. Very nice. Hotel was clean and room was always kept nice. Lobby was large and open with bellman always ready to help. I did have a king size room but no view of the arch. that was a little disappointing. Shower was great, plenty of pressure and with the giant head. Bathroom was big enough for one might have been a little cramped for two. Nice extras in the bathroom, brand name toothpaste, cotton balls and q-tips. Bed was very comfortable. All in all a nice room. there is self-parking and valet but i did not use those. 3 blocks from the Busch stadium and there are several restaurants nearby.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Good sushi/ramen for Tucson, would be pretty mediocre in a bigger city. The staff were all friendly and the ambiance/decoration were really nice. We got pork buns (a bit meh in execution, but so much better than most others I've had here), and then some pretty standard nigiri and rolls (salmon, tuna, yellowfin + spicy tuna and shrimp tempura rolls). All were good. Prices were reasonable ($25 each for 2 people). I'll probably be back if I get a craving for sushi, but not really a place I'd go for a special time.

DIRTY and BAD FISH!!!!
I went to Mikado about a year ago to try it out and was REALLY disapointed! Nothings worse then craving some good sushi and being semi-disgusted by it. The fish had NO flavor whatsoever and the rice was sloppy. To not gross anyone out, but when I was waiting for my takeout order one of the sushi chefs sneezed on the sushi bar and disregarded it! UGH.... I don't know about anyone else, but the inside was a bit dirty and it is a big turn off when places have carpeted floors, esp. seafood places!

Word to the wise... don't waste your money!!! Very, very disapointed.

Heard so much good things about this place...HUGE let down. Sucked.

ONLY GOOD THING WAS THERE Salt and Pepper Chicken Wings..those were great.

Got the beef spare ribs..they were horrible..also orange chicken horrible...attempted to return the orange chicken(tasted worse than the ribs so I decided to return that one considering it was the cheaper plate you think I could return it or exchange it) WRONG! you cannot get a refund or exchange it for another food,the lady was nice enough to take.... 2$ off the bill -_-.... I will not be going back

This is a very poor hotel.  I have to say that I have NEVER been in a Westin that is this ugly.  The room when I checked in was totally crazy, all the drawers were open and the bed was unmade. The bathroom lights were all on and it seemed off. I asked the desk staff via their 1979 telephone (I could hardly hear them) for a room move.  They moved me across the hall..not much better.

The service was poor, we're having a corporate event here and they messed up nearly every part of it. The person organizing the event is at whits end with this hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Il Forno is a nice casual restaurant in the Jasper Gates shopping Centre. I came down here for lunch, got a seat right away. Inside it's rather spacious, and quite bright a cheery. It's a little to bad the only view outside the window is a parking lot, but that's unfortunately the downfall of many restaurants in Edmonton. I had a pesto pasta with anchovies, that was a little salty (to be expected with the anchovies) but pretty good. I gave Il Forno three stars not because it's a bad restaurant, it just isn't the best Italian restaurant in town. Still if you're in the area and looking for a place to eat Il Forno is a good choice.

Pac A Deli does in deed have everything I ever need. It's great since there isn't many other places nearby to pick something up quickly on my way home. I do find it quite pricey though and tend to only go there when absolutely necessary. Also they only take credit cards if you spend over a certain amount. And since I don't go there to pick up several items I never meet the minimum and thus have to pay cash. They are very nice and considerate there and are always fast and friendly. I just don't go often for the credit card minimum and the prices.

This Anytime location has a great NW set up in the new Tangerine Crossing area.  It's rarely crowded, has brand new equipment, and the all the cardio machines have personal TV's on them.  They also don't skimp on the channels, which is nice.  Another bonus, is this location has a TON of classes to take, as well as their On Demand classes.  Kraig the TRX trainer is the best!  Aside from being able to work out 24/7, this location strives very hard to keep the gym clean, which I appreciate very much.  Finally, a great caveat is that a membership here allows you to access any Anytime gym around the world.  Get healthy Tucson, and workout Anytime!
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I love coming here for pizza. The slices are huge! It's always comical to watch people try to walk out the doors carrying a full pie. The pizza is definitely better than some places in the area, but it certainly isn't the greatest slice I've ever had. 

The place is usually always busy and even with the upstairs seating area, there isn't really a lot of places to eat your slice after you get it. In warm weather it's not an issue, but in the winter it's a big inconvenience. 

I usually just do a plain slice, pepperoni tends to be on the greasy side, even for pepperoni.

I'm a big ice cream fan, living pretty close to Handel's Homemade Ice Cream in Berwyn. That's the place all other ice cream shoppes measure up to for me. Bruster's is very good! I've tried many flavors, and gotten a waffle cone to go. 

I really liked that they will mix two flavors in a pint for you, and perfectly put the flavors side by side in the pint. Some of their flavors didn't come close to being as good as versions I've had other places. Their Graham Central Station doesn't even come close to Handel's. Their caramel Twix flavor was good, but barely had any Twix in it. 

The next time I'm in the area I will be back again!

There are many Imo's within the City and even further away but this one is my main location. They're quick and friendly, but most importantly the quality of the pizza is always spot-on. My one complaint is that the quality of the lettuce in their salads can be poor most of the time. But this is something I've found at every Imo's I've been to.

Sure the pizza's great and if the lettuce is good the Imo's deluxe house salad is where it's at with their house dressing. Don't count out their sandwiches like the meatball or my favorite, the Special sandwich. If you ask nicely they'll even serve it hot (toasted).

It's your typical Dunkin Donuts but the line moved really slow the morning I was there and they screwed up my coffee order. They pretty much have the same menu items as any other Dunkin Donuts but looked like they had a smaller selection of donut varieties. I also use Passbook to pay for my meal and for some reason, they couldn't scan it so I had to sit there and read the numbers to the cashier and waited for her to write it down and then punch it in. Next time I'll get my coffee from somewhere else in the airport.

The car wash itself was OK and about typical of what you would expect from an automated car wash--never as good as what you could do yourself at home. What I didn't like about this place was cash only and no towel dry. I was unfortunately not headed straight home and by the time I did get home, I could easily see water spots on my vehicle. There are other car washes in the nearby area that do as good of a job, but also take credit cards and towel dry your vehicle. There are also vaccums on-site if you want to clean your interior yourself.

The food was OK and I did enjoy my chicken enchilada with mole sauce but I did not like the chips. The chips are on the thicker side and some of them were a little chewy. Both of my kids went with basic cheese quesadillas and my one son didn't eat much of his because he didn't like the way it looked with cheese coming out of the quesadillas. The waitress noticed and asked what was wrong and after telling her, offered to make him another one. I thought that was very nice as there was nothing wrong with the original quesadilla--I just have a very picky eater.

It's a typical Starbucks and I always feel like I'm an idiot when I'm trying to order coffee here! I just don't get all the lingo that I suppose coffee aficionados use! Still, staff is friendly but I do find the service to be a bit slow at times. I find their coffee to be a bit on the pricey side and a bit stronger than I usually prefer. I do really like their hot chocolate! Still, this is a clean Starbucks with available indoor and outdoor seating along with a drive-thru. The parking lot is not overly big and during busy times, you just need to be extra careful.

I usually come to this Starbucks because it's in my neighborhood. I must say the location is nice sice it's right on Harrison. However, the inside space is quite small, even though there is plenty of outdoor space (which is really unpleasant during the summer months).

I must say though that the staff is really friendly. I remember one time I went there, I wasn't sure what I wanted and the barista guided me in the right direction.

All in all, this is a good place to come to study, catch up with friends, or just get your daily caffeine fix.

I've only come here a couple of times so this probably isn't that useful of a review, but I do like this place. It kinda reminds me of F&M's of downtown.

They play really good music.

I hear they are known for their Flaming Dr. Peppers, which I have yet to try. Hopefully I can come back soon to get one.

The one thing I don't like about this place is that there is a cover, which is pointless to me since I'm pretty sure it's 21+ to get in. The cover is probably the one thing that has prevented me from coming back more even though it's not that expensive of a cover.

Fritz's is delicious.  More options than you could possibly need.  I've never had anything that wasn't good.  Whether you just have a hankering for some clean custard, or you need a unique sundae/conrete, they have tons of options.  

Sometimes in the summer the line can seem annoyingly long but the workers have a good system that moves the line fast.  

Just a tip, save a few cents by paying cash as they charge a very small fee for credit card purchases.  But it really is a minimal fee.  Maybe .30 to .50 cents per transaction.  

PS I like it better than Ted Drewe's.

The New York style pizza crust is disgusting. Its clearly frozen pizza dough. Chewy and bland & resembles styrofoam. That's not a problem if you are getting it from the gas station next door, but when you are paying $27 for a pizza with 3 toppings, you expect more. What they are pulling off is borderline robbery. Won't even get into the cheese, which  tastes like Best Choice brand mozzarella from Rouses. 

The deep dish must be delicious for this place to be highly rated. Do not order the NY Style pizza from here.

Their 3 star average seems spot-on to me.  We have ordered takeout and eaten in occasionally over the years.  The interior since they moved from the old location is really nice.  The menu is typical pizza, cheesesteaks and pasta dishes.

Pros:  large portions, delivery, large parking lot and kids menu

Cons:  pasta dishes can be very oily yet sandwiches dry?  Dinner for a family can add up quickly for what is basically a glorified pizzeria.

But all told, this is a nice local business that I wouldn't hesitate to recommend.

Quality food at one of the most popular spots in town.   It's definitely not cheap, but at least it's all fresh and tasty.    You can byob for eat-in dining & they do both takeout and delivery as well.    On Monday nights there is a good prix fixe deal (4 courses @ $20).

Favorites are the chicken Caesar salad and the amazing house salad with house balsamic dressing.   
Pasta entrees are also very good.    They have both expensive items like steak or seafood lasagne and the usual cheesesteaks, pizza etc.   I have to admit to a bit of sticker shock for south jersey but it's reliably good.

Not the best Asian market on Wash Ave.  Possibly the worst.  But it's convenient if you are getting some grub at Nam Son.  The aisles are very cramped, and the fish section is not appealing.  I also found the produce to be very close to its end life, even considering the prices I would recommend heading elsewhere for fresh fruit/veg.

The prices are good, but the selection is sorely lacking for Korean & Japanese items (my benchmark).  Overall, I'd say stop in only if you happen to already be at this shopping plaza.  Otherwise, head over to the other side of Broad for better experience.  Sorry!

Delicious. Great food, quick and efficient service. I had the shrimp chimichanga and my husband and the Pollo con Tocino (chicken, onions, cheese dip, rice, beans, tortilla shells) and he loved it. A bit pricey for queso dip but it's very good cheese dip. The environment is a different Mexican ambiance, very modern.
They've only been open 3 weeks and it was pretty busy for a Wednesday and they said it's been busy since they've opened and they have had repeat customers, which is always encouraging to hear.
The back parking lot is a little strange and awkward and dark.

I am an Enterprise Plus Platinum member, I rent from Enterprise all over the country. Occasionally I rent from this location as it is near my home. The Glen Carbon location has the rudest, most unfriendly, unorganized staff of any location I have ever rented from. They have forgotten to pick me up, they have not had cars available, they stand on the other side of the counter to check you out but never look at you or acknowledge your presence. It's unreal. If it weren't my home base, I would never use this location again.

A great (hidden?) gem in the heart of Old City. It's a great place to hide out and read for a bit on a blustery Monday morning. 

The staff was really friendly, easy-going, and helpful. I ordered a coffee and a breakfast sandwich. Instead of just reaching into the refrigerator to get a pre-made sandwich, the guy behind the counter, assembled it fresh and served it up nice & hot. 

There's PLENTY of seating, and when I was there, it was pretty empty and low-key. If I worked in this area, I would stop by for a quick breakfast, an afternoon coffee, or a sweet treat.

A solid Double Knot satellite location inside of Franklin's Table food hall on Penn's campus.

The menu is pretty varied, with rolls, sushi, sashimi, rice bowls, and combination boxes. 

I ordered a Yellowtail Scallion Roll and Salmon Avocado Roll, plus the pickled cucumber salad. Everything was fresh and tasted great. I especially loved the pickled cucumber salad. 

Service was super friendly and easy going. On my next visit I want to try one of the rice bowls, or combination boxes (which from the looks of it is A LOT of food - but you get a good sample of the menu.)

Low-key, no-frills sushi spot that has a wide selection of affordable rolls.

My partner and I came in on a Friday night before an event we were heading to. The space is pretty tiny, but has a few tables.

I wish I was hungrier, because I would have loved to check out the 3 roll special - a really good deal.

I ended up ordering a seaweed salad (which was so-so) and a tuna-avocado roll, which was decent.

The service was okay. Not the friendliest in the world, but satisfactory.

I'm not sure I would come to Tsuki again for dine-in, but maybe take-out if I'm in the area!

I've heard a lot of good things about Lucky's General Tso's Tofu ever since I was in college. I finally ventured into the Baltimore Ave take-out spot this past Friday for some quick, easy, delicious Chinese food.

I went for the Sesame Tofu Combination Platter (always a good deal) and my boyfriend ordered General Tso's chicken. The food was probably better-than-average, with flavorful sauces, and tender chicken/tofu. 

Behind the staggered plexiglass counter, the man who took our order was really nice. A few different people came in and said hello to him by name. Clearly a favorite of many neighbors - which, i think, is a good sign.

How have I never visited this store before? It's pretty awesome! Their bulk snacks are intense... and pretty tempting. I find it extremely hard to say no to blueberry yogurt covered pretzels or cherry yogurt covered pretzels, if I'm being honest. You will find a lot of gourmet, natural and organic items as well.  The produce is nice and there is a good selection. Unique items you might not find elsewhere. Nice coffee selection as well. If this store was closer to I know of be spending a lot more time and money here. And I'd probably be okay with that.

Why do I continue to go here? It's 5 minutes from my house and in a pinch it has kept me alive. The service here is hit or miss. Mostly miss.
 Don't go inside!! You will just lose your faith in humanity from the staff and customers. I once saw this woman in a wheelchair arguing they had gotten her order wrong but refused to return the wrong food. She continued this scam for the 15 minutes I was in there.
 The drive thru can be very crowded and the staff hardly mumbles a greeting. I would suggest not to order from of the higher end things like McCafe drinks and check your bag before you leave!
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Worse staff ever! I usually go in here in the morning because its right by the trains. The lack of order reminds me more of a deli than a fast food joint. It's not there fault its crowded but it is there fault for not using the order numbers right on the receipts. So you're always guessing is that my egg mcmuffin that the lady just ran away with. The cashiers definitely don't want to be there and mumble. On top of that you may have to wait for 10 minutes for just a egg mcmuffin and coffee. Service is horrible I started just being 10 minutes late for work and going to the one on Walnut instead of going to this McDonald's I pass every day.

As far as coffee, it is very good but not great. Much better than Starbucks. But the best coffee in the area is High Point Cafe, hands down who also make their pastries and food on teh premises. I like the layout of Chestnut HIll Coffee and you can definitely get some work done but I don't find the atmosphere very friendly. The owner is very obnoxious and pretentious. Baristas are hit or miss when it comes to friendliness as well. I also wish they had better pastries and more of a variety to eat. The pastries aren't always fresh.

Clean and semi-empty on July 4 during their limited opening hours.
Got the $3 frap promo of Double Fudge Bar for me and Caramel Waffle Cone for the friend.
The Caramel waffle Cone was too sweet for my liking and same with the Double Fudge Bar.
Such have stuck with my usual Green Tea Frap, but this is the point of these $3-Frap promo=for you to try something out of your comfort zone.

Anyway, the milks were empty and I placed them at the Starbucks counter and notified the staff to replaced them. After 30 minutes, they did no such thing. At least they have nice tables where you can do your laptop work, but no plugs near the tables.

Beautiful, clean and nice hotel. I would've given it 5 star except... they didn't deliver my breakfast. The breakfast slip was still on the door the next morning. I think it's because the slip is brown-colored and the door is brown... so it's hard for staff to see. 

Otherwise, the hotel is in a prime location to the convention center a short walk to the French Quarter. It's got really nice restaurants near by too. 

The rooms are spacious and clean. It has a really nice rooftop pool and jacuzzi. Crawfish Benedict breakfast is delicious!... all for 159$ weekdays.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This is probably my most favourite Boston Pizzas in Edmonton. I have been to many, but this one is the one I come back to. Partly is due to the fact that I grew up in the area. I like that it is near West Edmonton Mall, but not in it. 

I prefer the lounge side to the restaurant, mostly for the wait time and partly due to the noise that is children. The restaurant can't help bad parenting. The food is always great and the service too. I don't know that I can say I have ever had a bad experience. It is consistent. I like that.

I am always nervous going into a new salon. Part of it is personal anxiety and the rest is that I don't know what the environment is like. I have been to many salons with snobby attitudes and that is not what I found with Shadified. Really helpful staff and though it was busy and the music was up, it was an overall great experience. The stylist, Stacey, listened to what I wanted and kept checking back with me to make sure we were on the right track. Greatest cut that I have had in a long time. 

They offer a lot more services than just cut and colour and gift cards, which is originally what got me through the door. Definitely going back.

Not great tonight. Came for my daughter's 18th birthday.  Not many customers but service was below average. Ordered 2 appetizers. One came out as expected. The other came out much later with our dinners. 

5 of our 6 dinners came out together.  The last was more than 5 minutes later.  The manager came and offered to take that entree off our check.  That was reasonable.

Got a free desert for the birthday girl. Our server sang to her and that was nice. 

No complaints with the quality of the food but just not a good enough experience with so many better options in Nashville.

Loving this quaint Italian restaurant just off of Rittenhouse Square!

It's an intimidate little place that gave our group of 6 just the right amount of attention. I thought the pastas were prepared perfectly and seafood was fresh. It's an older clientele so the place is relatively quiet for being a BYO. Definitely my favorite BYO so far. 

The prices seemed reasonable relative to other Italian restaurants in the area. Cash only though so come prepared.

Awesome little spot. Unique/inventive menu items make this an A for me.

This place is a great spice shop. They always have what I want and if they don't they order it. The mixes (ex: "black and red" or "rib rub" or "spicy chilli") tend to be spot on also! Very friendly staff, and decent prices considering you get a glass shaker (or, you can opt for the spices in a bag). More variety than the grocery store (duh) and less expensive. They have a good turn around so the spices are always fresh. They get a lot of orders via catalog which is how i think they really survive. I have to admit, thats how I do most of my shopping.

After baseball games at Collier Park, we stop in to g et quick sandwiches as a healthier alternative to fast food. Usually get there 30 minutes before closing. each and every time we arrive, most of the food is either empty or put away. The food that is out looks past it's prime.  The people working are put off by late comers so I am paying for a sandwich that has below average food quality made by someone who doesn't want to be there.  This could be there busiest hour of business with over 100 families leaving the ball park at the same time! Hint Hint!

AWESOME. All of the Barbers Here are on point! Dennis Redmond is the owner and also happens to be one of the Nicest Barbers Ever. They offer a wide range of services for men such as hair cuts, shaves, Detailed hair designs, & More. Ladies do not be Afraid to go in here they offer Great Services for Women too, Jessica Martin is the Woman to see. My husband and I both use The Boulevard and Neither of us have ever been disappointed. The staff here are all Friendly and professional. The Prices are Reasonable. The Team here work's hard to keep their customer's happy and Looking sharp. I wouldn't be caught anywhere else.

The service was decent but the food wasn't to our liking. The Lollipop roll is way smaller than anywhere I've had. The pieces are cut unevenly - some thick, some thin - and are swimming in the vinegar dressing. As for the Salmon Skin handroll, the skin is chopped up into tiny pieces that makes it impossible to dip it in the soy sauce because all the pieces would fall out. We've had it where the skin is long pieces. The Sunomono only has 1/2 the seafood as at other places. The only thing that is decent is the Crunchy roll. The sushi here is not good enough for us to return.

I'm a huge fan of Bernini's happy hour! Where can you get virtually every entrees on the menu at half price?! The food here is really good too!!! If the half priced food during happy hour is not enough to bring you here, there's also the $2 Finlandia martinis. I'm totally serious!

Bernini is in centrally located Ybor with delicious food at good prices, great atmosphere, full bar, spacious, and decent service, it really is a great place for any occasion, especially large groups. A couple of times I've organized girls night out here. We always got good service and good food. I highly recommend Bernini.

This is a nice and clean place.  Has the coffee shop feel with bright colors.  They are fast and efficient.    Seating is indoor and sparse with seating along the window and two booths.

I ordered the Southwest Steak Burrito combo. It comes with hash browns and medium coffee. I have to confess I always know what I want with coffee but it was refreshing that it comes exactly the way you order it. I expected the burrito to be bigger. It had nice combo of steak,  egg, cheese, and peppers.  The hash browns were lightly seasoned and would make a good snack on their own.

Enjoyable stop.

Four stars only because, well.... This McDonald's is always nice & without incident. We often use & abuse the drive thru for cookies (3 hot fresh chocolate chip for a buck?! YEEE!) and I have been known to swing by on busy weekend mornings for a nice, greasy, satisfying breakfast. My cutie adores him a sausage biscuit! And so he shall have one! Sometimes I will bring my people at work breakfast & the staff here is always happy to serve up my order with individual bags, per my request, so that I can deliver to individuals.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Came for lunch with a friend and fell in love with Red Elephant!

The Line Up:
Soup/ Sandwich combo- French Dip & French Onion (Bonjour!)

We both ordered identically and inhaled our lunches! Savory, delish...nice portions & we were both interested in more (Oliver Twist? Please sir...more?).

Customer service was grand! The gentleman (manager? owner?) who took our order welcomed us, asked about our previous dining experience and thanked us for coming in. He then came by the table later to see how we were enjoying our meals & this place was hopping. 

Throw in the 100 choices drink machine & we have a go-to for lunch from now on. Yeah!

I just found my new barbershop.  I've been in Tampa since 2012 and it seems as soon as I find a decent barber/stylist, they transfer.  And far too many shops are living off reputations (and low price ads) they no longer deserve.  Today I got the best haircut I've ever had for $15.  I was so impressed I left a $7 tip.  On a Monday, when most of the "elite" barbershops are closed, the Elite Barbershop is open.

Updated review.  Inconsistencies in barbers and price increase have me shopping for a new barbershop.

The staff was great, the owner however was the one who hosted our table and he was not friendly what-so-ever. Everything was dirty, EVERYTHING, tables, seats and the bathroom was absolutely disgusting. We received only part of our order which we didn't realize since we got it to go. The rolls are small, the fish seemed to be going bad so we didn't eat everything and threw about half of our rolls away. Another thing that was quite annoying was their rice, it literally fell apart when we tried to dip it in soy sauce, so our soy sauce cups were FULL of rice when we were done. So disappointed, so we are sticking with Cafe Mochi down the street!

This is my go-to Italian restaurant. I always get the Drunken Gnocchis - which come in a creamy vodka sauce with parmigiano cheese for $16 (dinner price.) The servings are large, which is an important factor to me. I haven't had the pizza, but my boyfriend says it's amazing. 

The staff has always been very friendly and the service is great! I suggest making a reservation.

The inside of this restaurant is gorgeous. It's so cozy and comfortable, yet roomy and spacious at the same time. Such a neat looking restaurant. 

I highly recommend this place!

Came here on a whim. First time. Yikes! The least expensive entree is $16. Most average $19-$23. The tight space makes it extremely loud; can hear everyone's conversation and when someone laughs it echoes through the whole place making you pause your conversation. Food: meh. Fried calamari was bland, as was the marinara sauce. Our chicken dinners certainly not worth the price paid in terms of portion size. Pasta extremely garlic-y. Plates were plated a-la 1990s with garnish all over the edges. App+2entrees+waters=$65

Please don't make a Cafe du Monde mistake, and think that this is how the famous fried dough should be prepared.  In years past, they were better. Now they are but a shadow of what they used to be.  Hidden under an enormous pile of confectioners sugar, the standard three to a serving still stands.  But what is supposed to be a tender, airy, pillowy soft interior, with a crispy outer shell, has turned into a tough, dense, blob of dough.  Quantity vs. Quality rears its ugly head again.  A small coffee shop turned into a gigantic empire.  And all went kaput.

Overall: Little neighborhood bar and grill. Nothing more, nothing less.

Food/Drinks: The food is nothing special, typical pub food but it's not bad. Then again, I don't set the bar too high when it comes to places like this. There are drink specials almost every night so that's a plus. 

Atmosphere/Service: Everyone that works there is nice and attentive, can't beat that! It's in a little strip mall in the middle of the Bellevue neighborhood called "River Plantation." It flooded back in May of 2010 so I'm happy to support businesses on the rebound!

Overall: Fresh and delicious fruity treat!

Yogurt: Creamy, cool, fresh flavors. I usually go for the fruity options (favorites being pomegranate & mango) and add fresh fruit on top. I haven't tried lychee, but I've heard great things about it. The salted caramel flavor yogurt is an interesting flavor, though not one of my favorites.

Toppings: There are toppings-a-plenty but most are fresh fruit. If you aren't into fruit for dessert, there are a couple other options.

Cost: About $4; the difference between this place and Sweet Cece's is SC is based on weight and Pinkberry is not.

review for late night bar scene-

i was here for a night out on the town with the girls. there's a nice outdoor patio and heat lamps-convenient for chilly weather. the lamp near us wasn't working so the bouncer changed the propane tank and made sure we were comfortable. the dj, drinks (~$8) and dancing were great! it's a more dressed up crowd in their mid 20s-30s. it is very loud/not conducive to conversation (inside at least) and there is only one bathroom stall. 
but overall it's a good spot for singles and the staff are nothing but accommodating.

This USED to be the best.... I don't know what happened. I got the best ($12) wash. My expectation was a clean windshield. After THREE trips through the wash... I had to clean my windshield when I got home. The staff was nice enough, I guess, to let me go through again. But the last two trips weren't the wash I paid for. No wax and tire shine stuff. Just the basic. So I wonder if it washed off the good stuff from the first trip. 
My car wasn't super dirty. Just some dead bugs. 
If you're too lazy to so spray your car with water- this is a great alternative. If you want a clean car, I suggest somewhere else.

Great place!  Reservations can be made online from their website, and it looks like they're necessary because the place filled up quickly.  The waiter recited a detailed list of specials from memory, and provided excellent service.  The regular menu (which is also available at their website) is comprehensive.  I had the caesar salad and rack of lamb, both of which were delicious.  

Parking was a little difficult, but I don't know Collingswood well so perhaps there was some local parking that I didn't find.

I'll definitely be back - this was a great find.  Thanks, Yelp!

A small joint tucked away in a strip mall that serves great food and reasonable prices with good service. That means we will return. I think this location used to be Ziggy's and it seems like a similar menu. 

I had the bison chili which had just the right flavor and the perfect mix of meat and beans. We also sampled the Humus which was Awesome served with a side of feta, olives and tomatoes. The veg was offered a wonderful plantain filled burrito that she could finish. All this for under 30 bucks,

You can have a full meal, a sandwich or just a salad all is OK at the Zinc Cafe!!

Get there early it fills up quick

Started to consume my dish, Grouper with XO sauce, only to discover a crispy dead black fly in my dish. They were initially apologetic and offered to replace my dish. However I opted to not eat anything coming out of their kitchen. When i asked about the meal being comped, the manager refused. She gave us a lot of attitude, and made no change to the bill. Seriously!?! We left highly disgusted with the experience. You'll never find me in there again.

So, eat there at your own risk and watch for the flies.....

We stayed here over a weekend and the place was packed with weddings and drag queen(?) convention.  Even with all the hub bub they made our stay very pleasant and enjoyable.  We enjoyed all the activity in the hotel and did not have any noise problems at all.  The staff was friendly and accommodating.

Even with, what I would think, was a high occupancy level there was plenty of parking in the lot.

Our room was very acceptable with nice amenities - mini fridge and a coffee maker.  The bathroom was okay but could be updated.  It's definitely showing its age with cracked tiles, old fixtures and counter tops.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This is our usual take out place when traveling through Smyrna. We have stopped here multiple times. The service is always very friendly but the food is pretty mediocre.  

On our most recent visit hubby ordered the chicken enchiladas. When we picked them up they were covered in mole sauce. He would have preferred a green sauce but they didn't provide us an option. I had the chicken quesadilla. They were fine. A large portion but pretty bland. I was glad they provided a cup of salsa to spice them up a bit.

In the past we have ordered sides of guacamole. It is top notch.

A decent option if you want something other than fast food.

This is an unexpected little bar that has a decent Happy Hour!  The only place I've been on a Friday night where you get an entire bar to yourself to have good conversation and watch Comedy Central.  

We split a quesadilla and it was pretty good, perfect for two people to split and filling enough that we didn't need much else.  We drank Blue Moons, they have a limited draft situation.  

One downside is that the bartender sometimes has to run room service for the hotel so she'll leave here and there, but she's pretty quick.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I just need to take a moment to tell you about how this is my favorite M&T Bank!  I switched to M&T from Wells Fargo and frequent TD everyday for work but neither have that personal touch like these guys.  

The hours may seem inconvenient to most but they are always open during the times that I am in center city and the lines are very rare and quick.  It IS smaller than the other banks (both space and staff) so call to make an appointment if you need to really talk to someone (very easy and plenty of open slots)

They also allow friendly dogs!

It's a tiny but mighty supermarket in Rittenhouse that is convenient to the type of people that live around it.

They have a pretty awesome deli section in the back where they make sandwiches, hoagies, salads, and all sorts of other stuff.  The fresh-made sandwiches are only like a dollar more than the pre-made ones and I find it worth it.  The sushi is also pretty good - ate it for two years and never got sick!

The cashiers range from anti-social to very pleasant.  No coupons!  And they do have signage not to talk on your cell phone while making a transactions.

We were shuttled over to the Staybridge when the Courtyard Marriott 5 miles away was overbooked - definitely considered this an upgrade!  The staff were wonderful and pleasant to interact with.

The coffee area was clean and well-stocked.  I was not a huge fan of the continental breakfast as the meats were really unappetizing and the waffle batter was really thick and did not make good waffles.  They did have a lot of good healthy options like fruit and granola!  

Our room was clean and homey and overlooked a cemetery.  It was a little weird but actually a decent view!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Pretty decent place to get sushi in the neighborhood. Their regular rolls are good: spicy tuna, sweet potato, and their avocado and peanut rolls.  If you find yourself here, try their Godzilla and Crazy Friday roll. I've tried some of their appetizers as well--their vegetable tempura and calamari was just okay. I'm a little curious about their sushi pizza appetizer. Will try that next time I'm in.

It's a very small place so sometimes I'm shocked at how long it takes to get our food. They are also BYOB, which is a plus. Overall, there's not much to complain about this place. They have decent prices and decent food.

Just got back from dinner here with the boyfriend. We wanted to check this place out because of the Groupon we purchased back in December.

The boyfriend got the Bi Bim Bop with Eel that also came with a salad and soup.
I got the NE Viking Roll.
Both dish were pretty satisfying. =)

The dishes here were pretty spicy but pretty good so I think I would come back again.

Oh, and all the waitress and waiters were pretty young which I don't know why but it surprised me. Our waitress was nice though. =)

There were actually more people than I expected to be there.
And parking was hard to find!

My mom loves this place! She says the fish is fresh and she likes the options.

Her favorite is the Play Girl (cucumber, avocado, spicy salmon with more spicy salmon)

Mine is the Eel Dragon (cucumber eel, eel, avocado crunch, sauce, scallion, masago)

The people working there are very friendly and you get your order pretty quickly.

The only thing I would say is that they have a lot of repeating tempura options and a lot of them seem to be the same. I am not really a tempura for sushi fan so I would like to see more raw options and this would get a 5 star from me.
It is on my top 3 favorite sushi places though!

Good flavors? limited
Quality for price? yes
Competent service? yes
Clean joint? yes but crowded in the extreme
Real beers? oh yes!


For an airport bar, this was fantastic. The necessarily crowded tight fit and necessarily limited menu (it's an airport) are all that keep it from being truly oerfect. Great beer list for an airport, better than most non-Philly bars, airport or not! Good fries, decent enough service (if a tad slow). The prices were nowhere near as high as you'd think for a captive audience...barely over Philly market numbers. Thank you!!!

My wife and I finally made it to Villa Barone after living in Collingswood for 2 years. The restaurant has an old school charm to it. It was nice to get bread and olive oil as soon as you sat down. Our waiter was very courteous to us, and was there to answer any questions about the menu. He also went over some specials that were not on the regular menu.

I decided to get the bass stuffed with crab meat specal. The bass itself was cooked well, but could of used more salt on it. There was a decent amount of crab in the entree though. Not a bad spot if you don't want to pay an arm and a leg for Italian food.

The ambience is like a retirement home cafeteria. We sat in the upper part past the bar (which was tended by a sort of bored/rude woman). Our waitress was nice, and had a slew of "tonight's specials" to remember, and she recited it with only a little trouble. The meal was good, but for 2 people, I paid $67 for 2 "Recession Specials, and 2 beers total, including a 20% tip. I thought it was a little on the higher side, although their presentation of the dishes was nice. A solid restaurant, and I feel you won't be disappointed, but I feel it is a "nice" restaurant only because Chestnut Hill proper doesn't really have a ton of restaurants.

Tasteless food and a too loud atmosphere makes El Boraccho El Yucko in my opinion. We were seated directly under a speaker and we asked the waitress if they could turn the music down a little and she said "I can always ask" and they proceeded to turn the music up. 
My chicken chalupa was bland and tasteless and had pieces of bone and gristle in it. My husbands tacos were tasteless also. The waitress buzzed by our table so fast while asking if everything was OK we couldn't even stop her to order another drink. Complete waste of a drive downtown.

I was in a group of 3 and went here for the first time a few weeks ago. I usually had gone to Ninja in the past. 

The service we experienced at Hana was amazing. We did have a mix up in the order when I ordered chicken teriyaki and was presented with chicken tempura. When told about the mistake, the waiter immediately brought it back to the kitchen and I had my correct meal within minutes, and they apologized for the mix up.

The quality of the food was fantastic. The sushi did sometimes fall apart, but it was delicious and well presented and very quick. I can't wait to go back again.

We rode the train here from our hotel and it could not be more convenient.  Got off and it was on the same corner at the exit (eastbound)

The food was good.  The garlic bread was a little weird, had to smear our own garlic onto the butter.

The place was almost dead since we ate dinner early and slow, which is never a good combination.  Strangely they started seating people closest to what ended up being a large party of around 20 people.

The food was good but the menu was confusing in retrospect.  they have a price for the size we ordered but every single topping was extra and our waiter didn't tell us this.

3 Stars, Down from 4

Arby's is a chain whose specialty is roast beef sandwiches.  Note that this is pressed beef, not beef sliced off of a roast.  While still fast food, Arby's is a nice alternative to greasier offerings.

Like most Arby's, this location is generally clean and inviting.  The service at this location used to be well above average for fast food establishments, but recently has disappointed (hence the downgrade from 4 stars to 3).  Our most recent visit involved multiple mistakes in our order.

This is one of my favorite Italian restaurants.  I have eaten at this location very many times for lunch, and my worst service experiences were still reasonably good: Generally, service is fast and friendly.  The food is rich and tasty.  Personal favorites: any of the penne dishes, and the eggplant parmigiana.

One minor annoyance: When the server asks if you "like olives", they are asking if you want to buy a plate of seasoned olives as an appetizer.  The olive dish is tasty, just be aware that this not complimentary.

Puerto Jarocho is a small Mexican restaurant / bakery.  Authentic Mexican food is served (mostly tacos and tortas) for relatively low prices.  Ask to see a menu: the one on the wall behind the register is incomplete and is posted without prices.  In summary:

Great:
tacos (we've tried asada, bistec, al pastor, chorizo and carnitas)
cemitas

Very Good:
pastries, tamales

Mixed:
There is seating, but it is limited to just a few tables.
The physical restaurant itself is typical of authentic Mexican lunch spots: Clean, but not fancy.

I have been bringing my pets to North Hills Vet Clinic for the past three years. Dr. Baggett is very personable, on schedule with his appointments, and always allows enough time to thoughtfully answer any questions. He's very gentle with my dogs, and his calm demeanor seems to put them at ease. When I had to take my dog to a day camp that required vaccination records, the vet's office had them printed and waiting for me in minutes for no extra fee. The patient rooms and waiting room is very clean and modern and well maintained, and beautiful black and white photos of the patients (including my pets) are featured art in all the rooms.

Yuck! Hate this place. Went like 3 times but disliked it. The cover is $20 but if you get on the guest list it's $10. I went twice when I was 17-18 because Friday's are the underaged nights where high school kids can get in (or under 21). Everybody that was there looked like there were from the Jersey shore. EVERYBODY. Went back again when I was 21 and figured it'd be better because I wouldn't have underaged guys hitting on me but it was just as bad. Creepers everywhere. Over priced drinks that were just ok. They have valet parking which is like an extra $20.

Wouldn't really recommend this place unless you're in the mood to be sleazy.

My fiancé and I visit this location every time we visit my in-laws. Over the past 3 years the service has never changed. There are usually 5-6 employees working but there is no sense of urgency. It takes 3-4 times as log to get our drinks than the Starbucks standard. The employees are all over the place and do not seem to have any specific assigned station to keep the store running smoothly. If there was another Starbucks closer, I would be more than happy to avoid this one and drive a little further for better service.

I prefer to stick to local spots, especially for ice cream, but Jeni's is just so good! It gives you the same vibe as a local place and I haven't been disappointed with a flavor.
Unfortunately, the days of sampling flavors is gone (writing this Apr 2021) but if you see one you like you probably won't be disappointed.
Oh, and make sure to get a waffle cone. They're super buttery and sweet and are a treat on its own. 
Staff is always friendly and service is quick.

Only con is parking might be a little annoying.

The yogurt here is fantastic and probably my favorite frozen yogurt. I pretty much crave the cookies and cream and peanut butter yogurt night and day. Im also a huge fan of their happy hour special where you can fill a cup as high as you like for $5.

The reason why I am giving 4 stars instead of 5 is because the people who work there are pretty flightly. Half of the time when I walk in there it is empty with no employee to be found. So I get my yogurt, stand by the register screaming, "HELLO?? Customer here!" for several minutes while my yogurt melts.

Ok Pizza - bit $$$
Ordered 2 small pizzas to taste a variety: The Windy City White (no sauce, ricotta, provolone and mozz) & the Godfather Special. Didn't really care for the Windy City White as the ricotta cheese threw me off but my friend loves cheese and he LOVED it. I preferred the Godfather special, quality toppings, thin crust, great!! Both pizzas were a bit on the greasy side but other than that it was fine. Would have liked some bread & dipping sauce before our meal but nothing was offered. Surprising for an Italian joint. (price range: $$ our bill was $37 kinda spendy for 2 small pizza pies)

Terrible place to bring your pets, the staff is incompetent and SLOW! 
They take their dandy time and constantly come up to you and ask you if you need to be checked in even though you've already been sitting there for over half an hour and they should have gotten the hint that you were already waiting to be seen. 
They also take forever to take a payment and ask you to hold while they fiddle away looking for your records, it shouldn't be THAT difficult. 
I've never had a problem with Dr. Smith's office next to dominos, these people are just terrible at their job. Save yourself some frustration and go someplace else.

My family decided to give In-N Out one more try and I'm happy that we did. The burgers were cooked perfectly! I love a classic tomato, lettuce and onion burger and they did a great job yesterday. A little too much onion for our taste, but we pulled off enough to customize them! Why only an upgrade to 3 stars? The fries. They weren't cold and limp, but rather dry and flavorless. At very least, they could salt them when the fries come out of the fryer. If only they could deliver better fries, I would have easily given them 4 stars.

My friends and I came here for restaurant week.  I ordered the Ricotta Gnudi, Amish Chicken, and Sour Cream Pannacotta. 
The Gnudi was DELICIOUS.  I was debating over this and the chick pea fritters, and while the chick pea fritters were good, I'm so glad I chose the gnudi.   The chicken dish was good as well but nothing "special".  The chicken was cooked well.  The added pumpernickel was good.  But just felt like an average chicken dish.  The sour cream pannacotta was good.  My friend did rave about the chocolate cake option. 
Overall, not bad. not great.

Whenever I need lunch at City Centre West, I always head to Famous Wok. Why? Because of their awesome bourbon chicken. There isn't actually any bourbon (I asked) - it's just barbequed chicken thigh pieces in a Chinese honey-soy sauce marinade. It tastes very similar to my dad's barbequed chicken - yum! Goes great with the shanghai noodles and broccoli-veggie medley - ask them to drizzle some of the bourbon chicken sauce on everything. Prices have gone up for this 2-item meal though - without a drink, it comes to $8.00, a little steep. Beware - cash only!

OMG. Came here for Sunday brunch. FINALLY!! A Sunday brunch that truly delivers.  
The boyfriend had the scrapple and egg sandwich minus the bread...he raved!
The kid had two eggs and bacon...she couldn't even finish it all. 
I had the bread pudding French Toast. O.M.G. Seriously the best French toast I've ever had....
Our table shared the Chorizo Sausage Gravy..I can still see our three forks crashing into each other as we fought each other for another bite. 
Service is impeccable.  
Bravo!
WE.WILL.BE.BACK.

Friendly staff? Most definitely
Overpriced? You betcha

I go here for tea for my mom mostly because it features interesting flavors. I wouldn't go for any one else due to how overpriced the place is.

I was here on Sunday just to get a few ounces and the sampling was delicious. However, the person we had definitely did not know too much. Turns out it was one of her first days. Bless her though because she was very sweet and encouraging. In a few weeks with her enthusiasm, she will definitely be a great asset for them.

If you are a tea fanatic, come here. If you are so-so on tea, I'm sure you can find better options out there

I've never been to Sahm's Place and tried it for the first time this weekend.  It was so much more than I expected it to be!  The menu options are all delicious sounding and include a lot of local ingredients.  Everything was so fresh and the service was maybe the best I've ever had!  Shoutout to server Molly...she was amazing and very friendly!  I got " Ryan's Current Edition" with some fries and it was the best patty melt I've ever had.  I consider myself a patty melt expert because I've grown up eating them.  I plan to go back time after time to one of these mouth watering burgers!

Homemade waffle cones. Finished. That should be all you really need, but in case it isn't the ice cream is also incredible. Probably the best you will find in town and worth the parking hassle of the CWE. A flavor for every taste and palate. Sampling is highly encouraged and despite there often being a line, no one is rushed and somehow everyone moves through quickly.  I recommend a waffle cone with a milky chocolate bottom scoop topped with the brown butter almond brittle. Despite numerous samples I always come back to it.

This is a small dueling piano bar on bourbon st. The piano players we watched on Thursday were awesome! They were fun, funny and played really well. We didn't order 'drinks' here but the beers were cheaper than most other places we went. 

The waitresses are not cute and one girl wore a white corset that obviously did not fit her.  Apparently it got redone by bar rescue so I doubt Jon Taffer would be pleased if he saw it now. I will say though that they were really nice and checked on us often.

Would definitely come back for the awesome piano players!!

This review is for this location and may not necessarily reflect my view of the McDonalds company. 

I like this place and this is my usual goto location because it's close to my girlfriends house. I have had great experiences with the people here 99% of the time, the other 1% I attribute to one of us having a bad day. 

I have yet to go inside but they do have an indoor play place for kids.

The drive though service is usually quite fast. In the AM 8-10:20 there could be a couple cars in the line but they move em through quick.

Did you know mickey ds sells bags of ice too?
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
I though I had already written a review of this location. the drive through is quite slow and the line can extend into broadway, if that happens go to the next street, make 2 rights and you are in the parking lot. if you go inside it is just as fast, if not faster then the drive through. 

they also messed up my order once, wanted an iced americano, got a hot... not too pleasant on a hot day but I had a test to get to so I couldn't even get a new one. To be fair it was busy, and I dont think the barista was fully listening.

although I like within walking distance and have been here many times so im still commin' back

After Sabrina's Cafe, dropped by with my nephews and they were going nuts. 

So many different flavors of ice cream/frozen yogurt and then you come over to the toppings section and you just are overwhelmed with the selection. 

The kids definitely loved it and and had a blast. 

Service was great. The gal behind the counter was sweet and very nice. Nothing else really to review about the place because you serve yourself and then pay at the counter. It's just all up to you whether you make a crazy good bowl of Frozen Yogurt.

If I haven't been to the grocery store outside the city due to not wanting to lose my street parking spot...... I'm forced to go here. They have last minute items you need. Is it in bad condition, no? But expensive, yes. 

I am still trying to hone in on when exactly their produce deliveries arrive during the week because sometimes you show up and there are a lot of items that seem like they've been rotting, and some days you come in with everything looks fresh and newly stacked as if it were Whole Foods' little brother. 

I'll still be going there but the amount I spend there doesn't go unnoticed. $$$

i really like the decor of the place. The menu was like a novel, so many things to choose from. While we were reading over the menu we order the chips and salsa and a side of guacamole. Salsa was like water and guacamole had no taste. Finally I made my mine up combo #11 burrito, taco and a enchirito. Everything taste the same. I never had a burrito with just  flour and meat, if it was even meat at all it kinda taste like dog food. I guess you would say this was authentic Mexican food. I guess when I am in the mood for Mexican i will go to taco bell. The staff was very friendly and the service was fast.

Went on a busy Friday night and the line moved with ease. It was our first time but it was pretty easy to figure out what to do. I wish MD had casual dining pizza options like this!

Staff was extremely pleasant, prices were just right, and the options were unique and fresh.

I got the Kennett Square and the herb butter was super good. Boy got the Mexique and it was on point. It was a lot of food for the cost - love that it's BYOB, and their eclectic sodas were a refreshing surprise. I'd go here a lot if I lived in the area!

Food was pretty good. Nothing spectacular, but good. Their ads say they are rated one of the ten best in Tampa.. ummm.. no. The lobster strudel was "interesting" and the tuna was pretty average.

Price was not bad for this kind of restaurant.

Addmitedly, my recollection of the service in this restaurant-in-a-hotel will be slanted a little to the negative side since one of the first things our waiter did was stab me in the hand with his pen. I'm still pretty sure it was an accident. They were also quite slow on an uncrowded night, not what you'd expect for a more upscale place.

Bacco has a great atmosphere to take your family or your counterpart for dinner, especially on the weekends which I believe is when they have live music. The food is great and service is pretty good considering how busy they get on the weekends. Highly recommend making reservations or pray there will be a table available. Been here multiple times with my wife and our families whenever they come to town. My parents live in NY and they rave about this place so we come here every time they're in town. So many different entrees, starters and desserts to choose from, not to mention a long wine list as well.

I honestly expected this to be an exceptional hotel, but I was disappointed. Reserved a king bed room, was given something else. Found the room to be dirty and dated. Talked with a wonderful concierge, Arielle, about local attractions. She happened to ask about the room, and we politely expressed our concerns. She did a fantastic job finding us another room that met our needs, and came with a fantastic view. We did find the new room to be dusty but cleaner than the original. If it weren't for her help this would be a different review. 

The hotel staff is wonderful, luckily I can review the restaurants and bars independently.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: the arbys roast beef jrs are good but I like to make them deluxe to add lettuce/tom/mayo and add a packet of the arby sauce! I kind of wish the price was a little better though. Occasionally I get the curly fries w/ranch to dip them in or potato cakes. The jamocha are the bomb and have been for years! I also love their $1 apple or cherry turnovers! Not the cheapest food but never disappoints. I once tried the brisket sandwich, yummy but too expensive for me. Then again it is better than spending that much on a crappy burger somewhere for just as much:)

great job replacing 4 low profile tires on our Eclipse and a reasonable price. They had to replace 2 or 3 studs on the back left tire for some reason they were broken off. They told us the brake was bad and after a while, it did grind and wear down because we couldn't afford to repair it but will soon. Strange how this happened after replacing the studs though. I wonder if it may have been related somehow. Btw, the only reason we came here to replace the tires is that R&G didn't have used ones at the time and we had a bad experience going to a Discount Tire which I'll write about from just before this
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
I really love this place. It's so casual, so friendly, and very much local. The atmosphere is kind of like a beach shack with an old Florida feel to it. The service I received was very friendly and personable, and I can bring my dog too which is a huge plus.

The beer selection is pretty typical, but the prices are excellent. I am a big fan of the buffalo shrimp, but the menu has a lot of great options. There are plenty of TVs for watching sports, and seating is available at the bar or at the patio tables.

This is a great place to relax with a few beers.

We had reservations but still waited over 15 minutes and the hostess was not honest about how long the wait would be.  After waiting for a while, we asked how long the wait was. She told us she was clearing a table soon but another 5 minutes later, we asked someone else how long it would be when he told us that the table we were waiting for just ordered dessert... Which would have meant another half hour wait. Not sure why they would overbook and not be honest about the wait time. Anyway, we definitely did not stick around...

Pretty disappointed because normally the food is delicious but not worth a 45 minute wait WITH reservations.

The Mona Lisa Lounge is a hidden gem! We signed up for the Swamp Ultimate Adventure and stumbled into the Mona Lisa on a Bloody Mary recommendation. Boy we're we in for a treat...The Bloody Mary's were amazing! The bartenders became great friends in matter of minutes. After we finished the tour we came back to grab some ice cold beers for $1.25!! The owner Tony was so kind and treated us to fresh crawfish. Tony and his team made us feel like we were family and made our experience amazing! Definitely check this place out!!

I was a little disappointed as this location didn't have very many games. Just corn hole .. which is fine but I was expecting more since the other locations have lots and I had promised my little cousin a game of life size jenga. .
 This place was so hard to find. .The one sign I saw was at the very bottom of the publix sign and it was covered by bushes. It took me 2 times to even see it to begin with. There's nothing from 54 that indicates a wob either especially in the day time.  
Other than that typical wob with a nice big patio and plenty of beers.

Hmm I've been here before but my review seems to be missing :-( I know it wasn't a bad review because I love this palce. The first time we came we both had strombolis and they were delcious. We also had the little pizza pocket type things as an appetizer. .. sorry I can't remember the name but they are so good.
We came here again and had them too:-) we made a reservation but we showed up early and it may have been the owner but this seriously nice man got us a table right away and we were seated it was super nice of him.
The food and service were amazing and everyone was satisfied. We will be back.

This place was really tasty when I first started coming here. But lately I feel like there has been a decline in the quality of the foods prepared. Salads and sandwiches have been sub par. The lettuce doesn't seem as fresh and the meats have been having a not so fresh taste lately. I tried to address it with their staff and they just brushed me off. I probably won't go back. I'd have given it three stars just for the past pleasant experiences but the way they brushed off a customers comment just struck me as careless.

I love mac and cheese, so I had to try this place out.  I like the concept and they do stick to only mac and cheese for the most part.  Three varieties of salads are available and also bread sticks, but I only had mac and cheese.  We ordered the Buffalo Chicken and the Bacon, Bacon and both were tasty. Being served in a skillet is a nice touch because the mac and cheese comes out piping hot and stays hot. 

I think the place is a little overpriced.  We had 2 small orders of mac and cheese and 2 sodas and the bill was $19.XX.  I will go back, but the fad may be over by the time I think of it again.

I've heard of this place in passing, but hadn't ever stopped in.  It's a tiny place - has the bar stools up front that other reviews have mentioned, with some booths - though I'm guessing the place only holds 20-30 people, max.  

We stopped by at around 1pm, and there were only 3-4 other people there.  I ordered a cashew chicken salad wrap and potato salad.  The wrap, stuffed with a basic chicken salad (mayo, onion, celery), lettuce, cashews and craisins, was grossly underseasoned, as was the potato salad.  

The service was above average, but I'm not sure if I'll be a repeat visitor.

My daughter and I tried this spot Friday night. It was hopping at 10pm and rightly so! It was a bit tight moving around and deciding what to get with the crowd, but I expect it's fine most of the time. I loved the Cherry Limeade and Lemon Icebox Pie flavors, unique and delicious! The staff was friendly and offered me sample cups when we walked in, despite the crowd. The Mochi wasn't fresh, that's my only complaint. Oh, and they had hot caramel as well as some dessert sauces I hadn't seen before, including lemon zest, and white chocolate, and marshmallow sauce. We signed up for text message coupons, and we'll go again soon.
