The food was really really good we had a past It didn't look pretty on a plate but it tasted good the service was really bad we're waiting at the bar no one came up to the head to ask the host to give us wine and drinks  waiting for water actually had to go back and ask for water so I don't know its family owned business. I would probably come back here for the food but because of Service I don't think so because we're paying so much money to have a good experience and in all honesty the service sucks maybe owners should hire more people. I wish the best of luck

Ok selection. Better then the one it replaced. The line is always way too long and the people behind the counter don't know anything about booze or common human interactions. Rude. Rude. Rude. I was looking for Pernod and after explaining it, spelling it, and disc ribbing the bottle, the lady behind the counter still had no idea what I was looking for and didn't want to help me find it. Long story short, they were out of it and I wasted 20min explaining to a 65 year old woman a very common liquor. It's near my house so I will keep going there for easy stuff, but risk the ticket and go to Jersey when you will need to talk to the sales people.

The check in process was easy and welcoming. Soon as I check into a hotel, I always ask the front desk staff their advice on how much time to allot for the return trip to the airport = Deanna was at the Front Desk and immediately gave me helpful advice and offered to book a taxi for me. Return transpo - done and with no effort on my part. This is just one of the reasons I love Holiday Inn Express hotels. 

This property is newly renovated and open as a Holiday Inn Express and they've done a great job. The location is convenient and as I'm likely to be back in Indianapolis on and off, I'll be staying here each time.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Being my first time at Koi, the sushi looked good, but I was in the mood for soup, so I ordered the tempura udon. The soup itself was pretty tasty, with nice, chewy noodles. It had a different flavor than other places, a little more salty and citrusy, but it hit the spot. The tempura was served on the side with Japanese seasonings and lemon sprinkled on the plate. The deep fried portion was extra crispy  and not as light as I prefer, but still good. It included a nice mix of sweet potato, broccoli and shrimp. Overall a good meal, but a bit pricey for decent food.

Booked a king room (225) at only $66 with tax. Nice setup with tables, a separate bath and sink, and what not. I don't remember if there was a fridge and microwave. It was a bit more modern than the pics booking websites have so the set-up may have changed in all rooms, as well. 

Moving on, I know it's a budget motel, but, I do expect linens without burn holes and cleaner floors. 

Otherwise, the bed was comfy, the room had a flat-screen, and there is variety in going to party and eat including room service until midnight.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Went here more recently for my youngest sister's 8th grade graduation. We were seated downstairs this time. Food was great as expected and the dining room was actually comfortable,though, it was also a little cooler than the last time I went.  I got fried calamari for an app and a salmon special for my meal which was served with asparagus. I still am noticing issues with the service, though. They can take a little longer than expected when getting things (I.e. the beer I brought in and paid for)and be rushy, still. It's not too much of an issue, but, can be annoying.

Love this place. It's a BYOB spot with really good food and plenty of it. If you're looking for an Italian restaurant that has good pasta and plenty of it, this is your place.

Stay away from the specials. They're often times more expensive then anything on the regular menu and while tasty, not worth the extra coin. My wife and I go here and order the pasta such as their puttanesca or penne ala vodka sauce. Honestly if you take a bottle of wine and order the pasta, you'll leave full, satisfied and with leftovers for less then $30!

we shared the chicken teriyaki.  It was two pieces of chicken breast with sauce dumped on top.  I could have made it at home in a few seconds.   I did enjoy the salad with the ginger dressing.  Dressing was very good.   We also shared 4 rolls.  the rainbow roll was really good but other rolls were just okay.  Bill was 63.00 with only one glass of wine.   And could have eaten a cheeseburger an hour later.   I feel like i have been a littel disappointed the other 2 times i have eaten here as well.   And still hungry.

Usually the food is great here but not so much this past visit. We did get a table outside which was nice since all of the other restaurants had a wait.   Service was a little slow.   Shared a margarita pizza which looked fantastic but then when we tasted it the sauce tasted like it was out of a jar. Also tried the Kentucky Bourbon wings.  They were a little over cooked and the sauce was sweet with out much flavor.  We actually had to ask for a side of the regular hot wing sauce to dump on them.  They were super sticky as well.   Probably won't run back anytime soon.

A better follow up experience today.  Mr. Shula, I'm a hostage at the hotel so you have a captive audience.

So, I stopped by for a quick lunch.  Took a while to get a server but once that happened, she was attentive.  Ordered the Chicken Sandwich (I know it's a Steak House but they don't have lunch sized portions).  It came in a reasonable amount of time.  Brioche bun was good, tomato and onion were fresh.  Butterflying the chicken seems to make for a better sandwich but the breast was cooked well none the less.

Better experience but wish they had a lunch specific smaller option on the steaks.

This is a conveniently-located cleaners, near Publix.  However, I've received spotty customer service over several years of use.

Sometimes, they start closing shop before the published 7:00 pm cutoff.  The lady who works there pulls in the rubber hose you run over in the drive-through that rings the bell inside to alert them that a car is there.  So more than once, I've shown up at 6:45 pm...and sat... and sat... and sat...  If I have to get out of my car an knock on the glass, it's not really drive-through and I would have just as soon parked and walked in.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
The service is poor.  They were messing up drinks left and right, including mine.  I realized it wasn't right, I realized there was a small line at the pick-up end of the counter.  There were two others in front of me waiting to get their drinks fixed.  It feels like the drive-thru gets the priority here.

It seems like everybody working there had on a head-set, so when I tried to address the drink-mess-up with the barista, I got the blank stare that says "I'm not listening," because I assume the head-set was talking.

This place has a great location, so I guess it survives in spite of itself...

Fell on the place second night open. Packed already!

Guacamole and queso fundido for a very good start. Guacamole was well-made but not incredible. The queso was *really* good- nice and crispy on the edges with a little body left in the rajas.

Enchiladas (chicken) and tacos (carnitas) to follow. Good quality, not enough quantity, and no sides included. The "salsa roja" was reminiscent of tomato gravy, though. :-(

Margaritas to stay hydrated. ;-) They were good clean drinks, nothing spectacular.

Decor was really good, as was service, especially for being slammed their second day open.

This place is out of the way for us but every now and then we'll head over.  The food is great - I tend to stick to the machaca and eggs.  I've also tried the chorizo and that is good too although of course the homemade tortillas are the star of the show.  They have fresh squeezed juices including a limeade that I love!  The decor is nice and open and prices are cheap.  The only bad part about this place is the service I agree with another reviewer that it's either great or awful.  Luckily the food is good but we'd probably be back more often if everything was good.

For the most part I do not opt for fast food but every now and then you just have to and In-n-Out is usually a reliable go-to.  Unfortunately lately it's been hit or miss and while the last visit was a miss I can't say I'd never go back.  Everyone makes mistakes and I just hope this isn't the new norm.  When I ordered dinner - all cheeseburgers - the meat on our burgers was unusually thin.  I basically got a lettuce burger with a smear of meat.  I still think this is the better of the fast food options and of course service is always friendly and quick.  Hopefully next time the lettuce to meat ratio will be reversed.

Blegh this place is terrible!  I helped my sister move in here and at first everyone was very friendly and accommodating - of course.  Once she moved in she could hardly get a response from the office when she needed anything.  Worst of all she had mice in her apartment!!!  So disgusting!  And they didn't even bat an eye when she told them, let alone jump to help her.  They eventually had Truly Nolen come by but it took several visits and lots of phone calls to fix the problem.  To top it off the pool area is very rundown and the pool itself never gets cleaned yet the grounds are meticulously groomed weekly.  Not a good complex to live in.

Villa Barone is a nice Italian restaurant in the center of Collingswood.  Definitely BYO, my favorite part of Collingswood.  

I've been here several times.  The food is good, not amazing.  My main problem with the food is it's all so heavy, laden with creamy sauces.  It's hard to find anything light for a summer evening.  My husband has also had the brick oven pizza, while okay, it doesn't even compare to a place like Tacconellis.

The decor is a bit dated, I feel like my grandmom opened a restaurant.  However, we have always had exemplary service, and the food is reasonably priced.

I have only done dine-in here and only the by-the-slice specials.  I love some great plain cheese pizza and it also gives me a good chance to evaluate the sauce, dough and cheese at a new place.  Best NY Pizza did not disappoint.  Well-seasoned sauce with a good balance of sweet and tangy and a crisp crust that had me eating every last crumb of the crusts.  Great place to stop in and grab a quick bite while out running errands or if you're just crazing some good pizza.  I don't know if it's super authentic or truly New York style, but I know it's good and sometimes you just need a big, slightly greasy slice of NY style pizza.

This is my go-to car wash. They do a great job, and they do it quickly.  I like the system here. You pull into the lane outside and you are greeted by someone who helps you pick which wash you want. Then you go inside and pay and wait in a comfortable area.  It's located in a busy area but it's pretty easy to get in and out of the driveway.

Make sure to check all their specials. I'm pretty sure they have ladies day, senior day and some other great promotions.  Pretty much my entire family uses this car wash.

Ok I didnt go here but I called to make an appointment for my grandma to get a perm and a trim. The lady that answered the phone said they don't make appointments and then when she realized that said a body perm she told me that they only make appointments for perms and that they couldn't do it this week because they are having a hair cut sale and she didnt have anyone that could perm her hair. They told me they werent busy so I dont see what the problem was. Isnt a perm and haircut more money then just a haircut? I wont be going there. Good thing I called first.

I came here Friday night with two friends, with an open mind despite the bad rating on here.

It gets two stars for its ambiance (full of 20somethings and relaxed) and its service (our waiter was good). My friends also enjoyed their lobster ravioli. As for my food, however, I could not have gotten a blander "fungi pizza": putting maybe 3 whole mushrooms across a piece of bread covered thinly with tomato sauce does not pizza make. Probably the worst pizza I've had in Philly, unfortunately, and it's not even cheap!

This is one of the best hotels I have ever been to. I stayed here for two nights and it is absolutely fascinating. I plan on returning just to enjoy both the view and the atmosphere of the hotel. The rooms are extremely inviting and offer all the comforts of home living. The bathrooms are nice as well. As far as the facilities, the restaurants are great and so is the convention area. It is nice that one can basically walk throughout the walkways that are attached to the hotel, and never go outdoors. The hotel was extremely nice and I highly recommend it. If they have any specials and you are in the area, take advantage of them! A+ hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
What a gem! 

After spending a gorgeous day at the lake, we rode the Harley on in for some craft beer & lunch (used yelp location to find)...glad we did!

Bartender knew his stuff and boy, did they have some great beer on draft & in bottles! After ordering an Ithica flower power (draft) & a Firestone Walker Union Jack (bottle) we ordered some lunch from a great menu. A variety of bar food & healthy options, we got the avocado salad with grilled shrimp, asparagus & green beans & an avocado BLT with awesome waffle fries. Wow, superb! Fresh, great flavor, really money!

Definitely stop in if you're in the area...great, great place!

Love this place! It's a go to for our family, usually for take out. We love their rolls, and the udon is a mainstay as well. Their service is usually quite good, and they get you your food quickly on the takeout end of things. It's not the least expensive place, but it's high quality and quite good considering it's in StL. The parking is a bit tough since it's right on South Grand, but you can usually find some street parking along the side streets.

There is a quick spot you can park with your hazards for takeout at the corner.

Super tasty food.  Every last dish really outstanding. This place defines ambiance. Every little thing has been carefully purchased, made, and placed. To be plain it just feels good to be in there. There are a bunch of little rooms and at first feels funny and disjointed but once oriented feels like an old family members home.  The bar is ok.  The bartenders seem stressed out and there are stickers on the fruit in the garnish bowl, eww. They are new and there's always things to work out with a new place opening so hopefully will just get better and better. Eat everything!!

If this place didn't sell Starbucks products and have the Starbucks logo all over the place, I'd confuse it for a local, neighborhood coffee shop.

The building itself is pretty small and there isn't much seating space, but it's cozy. It's my place for a coffee treat so I'm not sure what's like during the work rush, but I've never had to wait too long to place my order or receive my drink. The sugar area is always clean. 

Not sure how this place will hold up once all the new Granary residents are moved in and there's a whole new set of foot traffic, but for now it's a pleasant experience.

You are in Chinatown and it's late in the evening. You pull up your Yelp app to see what's still open for eats. Look no further before heading to Ho Sai Gai Restaurat. 

So this review is based on a late night experience, but good is good. I trusted my gut and went with the beef fried rice. It was on the best beef fried rice dishes I've ever had. The beef had plenty of flavor and was tender. The fried rice epitomized what fried rice should be. 

We popped in for take-out and didn't have to wait all too long either. 

If I liked them late, I bet I'll like them at normal hours. Can't wait to explore their menu.

The Atrium is the only straight up bar in Terminal C. It looks like a sad extension of the rest of the airport. There's absolutely no character to this bar and it just looks like a waiting area. 

My glass of mediocre pinot noir ran about $8 before tip. I would have considered a beer, but the selection was a tiny selection of Abita. I was totally Abita-ed out at that point. 

It's the only full bar (I believe Zatarain's has a few beers on tap) so this your best option for sitting and drinking. This epitomizes a 2-star rating. Meh. I've experienced better.

At least they gave me a glass of water upon request versus charging me for a bottle.

I went to this Target Optical for an eye exam and new glasses. Dr. McAleer was great. She was friendly, knowledgeable, and took the time to answer my questions and suggest a solution to my complaint about progressive glasses. The staff were great too - Omar and Jennifer were very friendly and helpful. 

There's a nice selection of glasses, including some that are more affordable than the well known big brands but that are still fashionable.

It's a busy place, so probably best to make an appointment in advance, and the online booking is very easy. I'd highly recommend this location!
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
OK. I will preface this review by saying I have lived here for 3.5 years. You move here for one reason: its cheap. And, it is. And, none of my complaints are ruining my life... but the apartments are what you pay for. 

The pools are maintained, but always packed.
The location is in the upcoming neighborhood of sobro, but on the wrong side of College.
All the doors/walls/etc are thin and weak. You hear EVERYTHING.
My roommates car was hit and run by a resident, and the office staff did little to help the police.

Its a stop gap for a cheap place to live. But, at a certain point, YOU WILL PAY for comfort. This place will drive you to it.

Smelled like carny pee!

So, my girl and I go into this place for a quick dinner on a weekday night.  The minute we walk in the place smells like carnival pee ruminated in a corner somewhere.  We sit down hesitant for obvious reasons.  Our server was rude to say the least.  We decide to try just an appetizer in order to test the kitchen.  We order the "homemade" hummus with veggies.  The menu stated homemade, but that could not have been further from the truth.  It tasted take pureed hummus from a can.  Needless to say, we will not be back.

I really wish lucky goat would carry skim milk. On several occasions they have either not had it, or worse handed it to me and then I realized that the expiry date had passed. I can imagine that I am not the only person that doesn't like whole milk or cream in my coffee. It just seems to me like skim milk should be a staple at a coffee house and it isn't here. Other than that, the service is always friendly and they have a nice assortment of fresh pastries. It is for sure a welcome addition to the neighborhood.....if management reads these reviews....please consider having fresh skim milk.

I was so excited to see the defunct Jolly's piano bar taken over by this charming pub with a great menu.  This is located right near my home and I think that they have done a great job reinventing this spot with a well thought out and diverse menu and outdoor seating.  I went with a group of people on a Friday night.  Although the food was good and the portions were ample the service was just horrible.  I mean 25 minutes to get a draft beer horrible.  I know that this is a new place and it takes a while to work out staffing kinks.  I so hope that they do since I can not wait to go back for the $19 all you can eat crab legs!

I dig this place! I work right next door and seriously, when I get to the point in my day where I feel a murderous rage coming on, I know that I can always head over to Bravo to watch "Real Housewives", get a great lunch and B.S. with the guys for bit. It really is a highlight in my day! 

I love their turkey subs, super fresh and always hit the spot :-D They have a sweet variety of slices to choose from and their pasta is so naughty. So much for that diet :-( - but screw it! 

Go to Bravo, eat pizza, smile!

Revised review:

Thank you, Louise's for contacting me about this issue! It says a lot about the business when you care enough to correct a situation. 

Our next visit was top notch! Great food, good service.... Everything I expect Louie's to be. We'll be back.

******

Oops. I asked for a table away from the live music (it was too loud) and we were seated at a table in the corner. Must have been forgotten because that was the last contact we had with the waitstaff. Even though the table next to us was served we sat there with our menus and nothing else - not even water. 

We left without ordering.

I think this must be some sort of mob front because there is never anyone there and the good is downright awful. We went there once to satisfy our curiosity but will never be back. I don't mind a little worn decor. In fact we seek out little holes in the wall but the food cannot make up for anything. I always think of the South Park episodes with City Chicken and City Beef, said with a bad accent. You know what I'm taking about. It's so easy to do mediocre Chinese take out, they are all over. You really have to go out of your way to be so bad.

Ordered a chocolate shake, this is what they send out. The first one had chocolate on top and was vanilla the rest of the way. I said that didn't look like chocolate so they made another one, this time no chocolate on the top. It's clearly not mixed at all and they didn't bother to even fix it. They just sent me home with 2 half chocolate half vanilla shakes. The manager was the one to make them too. They need to take 30 seconds to mix the shakes instead of sending customers home with a vanilla shake and some chocolate syrup. This is just shitty effort to send out not just one but two unmixed shakes, even after I sent the first one back.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
Sapori, Sapori, Sapori, I APPRECIATE YOU! 
We've been coming to Sapori for years. Date nights, girl nights, work dinners- always a great time. The environment is cozy with lots of detail to the decor. 
The staff is always extremely knowledgeable and friendly.

Over the years, we've tried so many things and I honestly cant say I've had anything bad. What stands out most is the Portobello in goat cheese as well as the INSALATA DI FICHI E PERE. 

For entrees, you HAVE to get the Bronzino. SO fresh, so delicious. 
My husband gets a variety of things while we are here and he always enjoys his meals. 

Sapori is a Collingswood must!

The wings were mediocre.  Maybe it's my fault for not knowing what to expect from all the exotic wing flavors.  The chicken was hot and cooked through, so that's a plus.  The fries were better than mediocre, but not fantastic.

Our server was pleasant, but with our being one of only TWO tables in the entire place, it was incomprehensible how long it took to get our food and also to have our drinks refilled.  There is nothing I hate more than having to look around for a server hoping to make eye contact -- especially when said server is not anywhere on the floor for extremely long periods of time.

Stopped by on my way to the office. I ordered the waffle sandwich. New and looked tasty. I'm sure it probably is fresh, but the one I ordered with sausage I would say probably wasn't very fresh. The Maple waffle sandwich did not taste like it had any Maple. I could smell the Maple however. The color did not look like the picture in menu either, but a lot of times when ordering fast food it doesn't look like the menu pictures. Taste was really bland and the hash browns even tasted a little old. Service was good. Very friendly and was quick.

Did drive-thru. I'll start off with drinks. As i know some may feel that it's not a big deal, but my husband and I drink different sodas. Depending where we are I usually get Dr. Pepper the husband gets Coke. Drinks handed to us and we don't even know which is coke vs Dr. Pepper because we weren't told nor was it marked. Got home and unwrapped my chicken sandwich. All that comes on it is lettuce and mayo. My sandwich was pretty dry. Hardly any of either. My husband looked up from his Texas Whopper and said "doesn't look anything like the picture". My thoughts EXACTLY!

Just wanted a simple burrito. I had to ask for black beans, which was a bit weird. I asked to have lettuce, tomatoes, onions, pico sauce, rice & guacamole in it. 

Instead I got a shriveled burrito, wilted lettuce, no tomatoes, pico or onions, then they charged me $2 for guacamole. The only thing in the burrito was chicken beans and cheese. Like one review said, you can make it better at home. If you must find mexican food this may work. It's not authentic and it's sub par. My waiter was ok, nothing special but he brought the food out atleast.

We were in Tucson for a wedding, staying at the Westward Look, and had a nice, pre-wedding get together (with the bride-to-be and groom) at Gold. They do have aces on the view of Tucson, which is worth something, but the food was middling. I can't honestly remember what I had (granted, it's been ten days), and if you it runs these prices (about $75 per person wiith drinks and tip) it should be more memorable. The staff was great, the scenery lovely, the food average. I'm torn on the overall rating - I woudn't run any one off from going to Gold, just know what you're getting when you book.

We got a pie of plain from here today as they did not sell slices. We have been used to thin crust wide slices that are often sold near college campuses in New Jersey.  That said, the pizza here was too greasy and cheesy. The extra grease does make the crust tastier but even having a slice (not too big ...comparable to pizza hut slices) is enough, and I usually have 3 slices a meal. The flavoring was slightly spicey but it was difficult to taste the tomatoes because the cheese was too thick. Maybe I am more of a sauce (than cheese) person. Anyway, it seems like this may be comforting after a night out but for a regular meal it can be too much.

I like Portofino, but I think it's pretty pricey for what you get.  That said, I had their salmon special last night and it was really delicious.  The service is excellent.  I can't say enough nice things about our server--she was helpful and cheerful and knew exactly when to check on us and when to stay away.  The bartender was great, too; I waited at the bar, but didn't want anything to drink at that point--I was hanging out waiting for my friend.  She gave me a glass of water and lots of nice, friendly conversation while I waited.

Came here for the re-opening in first to second week.  Seems very similar to previous Winslow except now you have to wait to be seated.  Menu seems similar type of food.  Brunch menu I was not impressed with.  Long Wait for seating.  Not much of a wait area to sit in either.  It gets crowded fast at entrance.  They Should have a designated wait area for to-go coffee orders at barista station.  While waiting for coffee you feel like you are in the staff and others way, lots of dodging happening.  The best thing I had was the cortado from barista.  I would not return here, just as I felt when I came prior as it was Winslow's home.

I just tested Leo's today, brought there by a friend for a business meeting. It's not El Charro Cafe, but it's a good cantina with very decent prices, tasty food and fast service. I ordered their chicken fajita tacos, and the chicken was nicely cooked, with plenty of onions and peppers in the soft taco shell. My plate was about $9 bucks with tip, very reasonable. The chips were nicely crip, not overcooked, not greasy and not too salty.The salsa was good, home-made, rather picante. Overall, a good meal at an affordable price. I'll go back if I'm in the area.

Stopped in for the first time after the Gasparilla parade. It is a cute little restaurant. We ordered a nacho to snack on before heading home. The nachos plate was smaller than expected, but delicious. It had the perfect amount of refried beans, quest, guacamole, lettuce and Pico de Gallo. The chips are freshly made here and tasty, however the nachos only had about 6-8 chips so we had to ask for more.  Our server was doubling as the bartender today and did not check on us. If the service were better I would give it more stars. I will definitely give it another try though because I thoroughly enjoyed the food.

Great, cheap, filling breakfast! Pancakes are fabulous, maybe the best in town. Thick and fluffy with a nice flavor. Sausage patties are flavorful and just greasy enough. My family likes to come here for breakfast when we are in St. Pete. Everyone always comes away full and happy. They now take credit and debit cards. 

Even on a busy morning service is quick and with a smile. Servers are good about refilling coffee, etc. Don't expect anything fancy (syrup is served in the bottles it came in) but it is good food at a good price.

Dropped off a years worth of dry cleaning because I was too lazy to go to my regular place and this was right next to my gym. Very friendly service. Easy drop off and pick up. I dropped off 11 items (3 dresses, 1 pant, 1 skirt, 6 tops) and my total was about $81. I'm not sure where that fits in the dry cleaning world but it seems on the pricier side to me. That said, I am willing to pay more for convenience and customer service. As I picked up my clothes, the owner introduced himself and the cashier gave me a coupon to use on my next visit. I was happy to learn they also do alterations. 

I'll be back, Al Capote's!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: We went there with two friends who go regularly. It was definitely meh. We had hummus and mussels as appetizers and those were far better than the entrees. My veal special was over cooked and over-flavored. The desserts were unrefined and huge in proportion. The clientele is a mix of family with young screaming kids and over 50 year olds I guess if your idea of good food is snickerpie, (we were reminded that it got voted best homemade dessert on Mainline Today), than it's ok of a restaurant. All in all, it's over rated and over priced.

Sushiland seem to be popular with the college crowd and it's easy to understand why. The price is cheaper than the other two surrounding sushi places- Samurai and Fujian mountain. The owner is a Korean single guy who is friendly and eager for business when he first opened ( he gave us free sampler rolls ). However, with his success, he is a little less friendly. We have been back with our kids many times but I think the quality has suffered a great deal. The sushi is definitely mediocre but what do you expect out of Philly suburb. None of the japanese restaurants are owned by actual Japanese - they are either Korean or Chinese.

We`ve had the pleasure of dining at the Rockford for both brunch and dinner services. 

The food is excellent quality and is priced right on par with your typical Moxies or Earls type restaurant. Servers were knowledgeable about the menu (and even the music being played)

Both times, we were seated promptly. The restaurant has excellent items to offer for brunch, wok, grill, and appetizer sections of the menu. A lot of interesting flavours and small but delicious spins on typical fare such as the sauce for their ribs. 

I would definitely go back there again!

Craving for some sweet stuff on my way back from Bloomington to Indy, I am excited to try out this frozen yogurt place and I was disappointed to find they don't have the white peach flavor which was my favorite so I had, strawberry, vanilla and orange flavors. Compared to Red Mango, I'd say their yogurt is watery than creamy. And as for the titbits that you get to add into your bowl, they prolly have the same variety as Red Mango. 

The environment though is spacious, clean, refreshing and modern looking. But I'm here for the food, not the atmosphere.

After exiting the car wash my brand new WRX had scratches on the bumper and sharkfin roof antenna that I know weren't there before. Management didn't seem at all concerned when I politely informed them that they should check their equipment because something is awry. I didn't even ask for anything to be done about my car because most of the scratches should buff out, but they seemed annoyed by me telling them their equipment is scratching cars. It's too bad because I really like(d) this car wash. I guess my $12/week would be better spent elsewhere.

Our family stayed in a three bedroom the Tuesday before Thanksgiving.  We had so much fun playing in the court yard.  My kids crushed the ping pong, corn hole and foosball.  "The Hub"  had all of the essentials that we needed.  Beer and wine for the adults and pies and cookies for the kids.  I love the idea of being able to purchase a quick meal from the to go area and go up to your room and cook it.  The rooms were so nice.  King beds for everyone.  We went on a walk that night to go to dinner and also the next morning for breakfast.  It is so close to everything and so much more of a better deal.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Very unusual and bold menu featuring lots of British/European highlights. If you like the idea of fat on toast, guinea hen, bubble and squeek, this might be for you.  The food preperation is on point, but it was regarded as overwhelmingly bland by just about everyone in our large party of 6. Seems that it lacked seasoning....which of course British/European food is not really known for though. 
As one member put it, it was interesting, a nice experience, but not sure that I'd want to go again anytime soon.
Service was acceptable, although even the servers were a bit confused by what entree was what......desserts were the best part of the meal.

I called for an appointment for Friday, so when I got there I was told that the special only ran Monday thru Thursday and the special was expired? They suggested Yelp was the actual contact that places the specials and Sears can cancel them, any mis information was Yelps deal!  Charlie (SM) went ahead and honored the special and in doing so I purchased some oil treatment to add to my oil change! A shout out to Charlie!!  So buyer beware.. call and confirm (which I did) but make sure its a manager and not a mechanic and get a name to put with the special.  Charlie also mentioned that when a coupon special has been used to much they cancel it.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Sept 30, 2012

My cousin and extended family in Tucson are regulars here, their favorite go-to place for great Chinese food. We just had to try it!

A group of about 15 of us went and they connected about 4 tables to fit us all. At one point we pretty much had the entire restaurant to ourselves, it seems they do a lot of take-outs.

Food was very good, however I do believe we have just as good (if not better) Chinese restaurants in the LA area.

Staff were friendly and attentive to all our requests. Definitely the best meal I had during my 3-day trip of Tucson.

I just returned for a late brunch with some out of town friends. The brunch menu was more veggie friendly (I had the yogurt and granola but that was only one of two or three good options). My friends, both carnivores, enjoyed their sandwiches a ton (especially the home made chips). I also had the iced jasmine tea which was really good.

Again, the service was great. Our waiter even got the kitchen to give us the opportunity to order off the brunch menu even though we were about 30 minutes past the cutoff time.

This place gave me the best manicure of my life!! Today's Nail Salon is owned and operated by a very sweet family of excellent nail technicians! I got a gel manicure from the daughter, and a regular pedicure from the mom. Both were excellent, fast, and really relaxing. However, the manicure was (is) next level. It looks beautiful and really sharp, but it has lasted me without a single chip (I shit you not) for TWELVE (12) days!!! This includes an eight-hour day of cleaning. 

I would highly recommend getting a manicure and pedicure here. This is the best gel manicure of my life, and everyone should experience this sort of joy!

I've eaten at this restaurant several times and not once have I been disappointed.

Lobster Bisque, awesome.  The lobster is really there!
Eggplant Parmesean, awesome.  The appetizer portion is large enough for 2 - 3 to share.  Very enjoyable.
Lasagna, it's huge!  I've enjoyed this a few times.
Crabcake appetizer, taste very good.  Lump crabmeat in the mix.  You only get 1 and it's not very large, so don't expect to share this.
I always have the Wedge Salad with the Garlic Asiago Dressing.  That dressing is the absolute best!

This location has been here since I was in high school and that was more than 20 years ago.. the sad thing is that it looks the exact same.  In desperate need of a facelift.  Anyway, the food is what we really care about and this Imo's does take care of your pizza craving.  I always walk in and place my order here because in prior years phone orders didn't seem to make it to well.  Anywho, I was quoted 15 min, but unfortunately it took about 30 - 35, I think they forgot to put my order in.  I did leave with a fresh hot pizza and my toppings were correct, so at the end, it was good.

The 4 star is significant because as compared to the other liquor stores in the area, this place is my "go-to".  Now, having also visited the Jefferson and Manchester stores, this location falls in line behind them.  
In general, this place does offer the best selection of spirits and it's a great feeling when I randomly pop in and there's a sample tasting in progress of some type of libation... Yes, I'll partake.  My thoughts are that their prices are reasonable, but can be a few bucks higher on certain items compared to competitors.  I'll still choose Randall's because I enjoy the layout of their store and the overall appeal.

So... this place isn't bad. Its just ok... Like the review states - I've had better. Maybe the 70's feel lends to the atmosphere, but I found it to be dark and oldish? The service was great! The food, was just alright. I had the chicken parm and fettuccine Alfredo. My boyfriend had the fried shrimp and fettuccine Alfredo. The fettuccine was ok, it had a garlicky taste at the beginning and then became bland. For 5.00... not worth it at all! Chicken was bland as were the shrimp. So... it was just ok. Probably wouldn't go again. The sangria wasn't that good either. But it was a nice night out. Overall... We've had better.

Yikes...um...its a Chinese food joint...in a strip mall...next to a ShopRite...and one bite of their food and that reality comes shining through. We ordered vegetable lo mein, spring rolls, a roasted pork egg roll, vegetable egg fu young, and dumplings. Everything tasted like old oil. No zip, no spice, no sweetness or saltiness. Just...there. Veggies in everything were pale. Dumplings were gummy. Egg fu young was burnt and tasted like grease and therefore hit the trash almost immediately. Just not worth it. That and the staff at pickup were pretty crabby and ungrateful for the business. Don't bother.

If you like to hear your neighbor sneeze, enjoy being yelled at by drunk people from the courtyard, appreciate the ceiling falling down on you while you shower then this is the place for you!  And don't forget that this is located behind a commercial park!  
The staff was polite and helpful however that is about as far as the positives go.  Since the human element is a big part I gave it 2 stars instead of 1.
Hyatt should consider certain room upgrades in 2017: 1) USB ports should be everywhere, 2) I should be able to access a guide on the TV, 3) internet should be faster than 1.5mbps.
I would not stay here again in the future.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Nailbanger Here Again;Recently this Restaurant offered a online coupon deal I could not pass up. We went during Happy Hour 4-7 and 8 to Close,and they had 1/2 price appetizers, and $3 Drink specials. This place was busy, but we were seated right away. They serve mostly Pub type food. Lots of Burger Choices. Other Reviewer`s commented on Poor Service, that was not our experience at all. We had extremely attentive service in the Bar Area. The Food and Drinks were very Good. Prices were average. I would not recommend the Desserts. They have plenty of well lighted Parking at the Foothills Mall.

You don't get what you pay for.
Took my car in today and paid $9 extra to do the undercarriage and when I checked it was bone dry under there. You could see the sand/salt  or whatever it is they spread on the roads here in winter, 
Went back and talked to the guy about it and when he looked he asked what that was under the car.... 
They finally got the settings right on their machine and when it went through the second time it was all gone. 
Makes me wonder how much extra they make by up selling services and then not providing them for the customers. 
You have been warned about this place.

Awesome lounge in the back corner of the Hilton, was starving after drinks and 360 was a little too popular for the simple meal I wanted quickly so we went off to eat here. Very comfy, very cosy, intimate lighting makes it nice for anyone wanting to have some drinks and eat. The food was surprisingly very good! Had the pulled pork nachos and tried some of the wings. Drinks were tasty and strong BUT had a lot of ice...don't do me buddy lol. It was kind of empty for a Saturday night compared to more of the social traffic being in the front. Staff was very nice. Wouldn't mind coming back but ok leaving it at a one time experience.

Eh. It was okay overall I guess.  When you walk in you will love the foyer. The front lobby is decorated way better than the rest of the hotel.  Front desk service was always friendly and so was the housekeeping staff. Though they did forget to make up my room during one of the days I stayed there.  I was happy that the room had a microwave and a fridge. The beds were average spring mattress, not anything special.  It was clean I guess, but I would suggest not laying on the top cover. It was a decent price for the type of room I guess.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The best place to eat in town. 5 stars!!!! And here's why...

Food:
DELICIOUS.  It is fast, the noodle soups can come as little as 3 minutes, while the rest will probably be in front of you in 5 to 10 minutes.  I usually get the something with roast duck because theirs is no doubt the best in town.  I also love the snow peas leaves dish, it's so flavorful!!!!!!!  My friends also love the rice dishes, vegetarian dishes, and other small dishes.

Service:
Fast and friendly.  And the place is clean, which is definitely more than you can say for most restaurants in the area.

Price:
Cheap, and the food is still delicious!!

Location was great for the venue across the street which is why we were there.  The breakfast is really good for being complimentary.  If it wasn't for all the "guests" that come into the hotel and stuff their plastic sacks with the food, I would have enjoyed it.  the staff is weird.  I don't know what I expected but they are just plain weird.  I saw one staffer doing her home laundry on the washer and dryer that is for guests.  Another one was stuffing her purse full of food to give to her family at the back entrance.  Not really the experience we were hoping for.  Won't be back.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I decided to give this place a shot because it's close to my house. The first time I got a pedicure with a hot stone massage because they were having a deal and the second time I got a mani/pedi. I liked the guy I had the first time better than the lady I had the second, but she wasn't bad. Next time I'll skip the manicure just because they never last more than a day for me without getting ruined but that's probably just a personal problem.

The prices are good. I don't remember what I paid the first time but I believe the basic mani/pedi was $32 which isn't bad at all.

Heavy air. Stale smoke and beer. The sandwich was very light on the meat and mostly bread. Nothing exciting about the taste. The low fat potato salad was pretty good, although it was just potatoes, herb, and mayo. Overall the restaurant seemed to use cheap ingredients sparingly and the prices were high. My server was excellent and attentive. Take note - they didn't make a good initial impression with the sign that delegates bicycles to the back parking lot or the lot across the street.  If you use a wheelchair or other assistive device you can get in but it will require help.  Two stars is generous.

Top 2 worst pizza I've ever had. I ordered two pizzas this past Friday night; one plain, one "italian sausage". The sauce was way too sweet; it tasted like tomato paste slathered onto dough that felt like it wasn't completely done. The "italian sausage" was, no joke, sliced up hot dogs. I love pizza and am in the mindset that even bad pizza is still pretty good, but my wife and I couldn't bring ourselves to eat more than a few slices and had to end up throwing the rest out. I can actually feel myself getting angry thinking about this pizza again.

I went here last week with a few friends for my girlfriend's birthday.  It was a really rainy night, so the place was pretty empty, so I'm not sure how the service is on normal nights, but we were treated extremely well and promptly.  Without even asking or mentioning that it was my gf's birthday, they overheard us and sent over a complimentary tequila shot for her.  I had the shrimp quesadillas and they were very good.  The chips and salsa were amazing as well.  Everyone at the table loved their food, with one of my friends never shutting up about how good her tacos were.  I will definitely be dining in/ordering from here again.

The sushi here is delicious and fresh, and the 3-roll special is perfect for dinner. But the reason I'm reviewing is because the service is excellent. Prime example - they have a $10 credit card minimum, and I was two dollars short of that the other day and didn't have enough cash. Rather than making me go get cash or buy enough to get up to $10, they said I could give them the difference next time. Not too many businesses, especially in a city, are that good to their customers. I made sure to come back the next week and give them the $2!

They've got an escalator past that . . . eh.

Their produce department, in particular, is frequently under stocked and out of  the most basic things.  I can't put my finger on it but there's something strange about the way it's laid out maybe the aisles are longer and fewer than normal or something. I just know I end up walking around a lot scratching my head looking for stuff when in other Publix stores I can go right to what I want. On the other hand Publix fried chicken is always awesome and the escalator is cool. It's also the only grocery store around here that has a parking garage so if it's raining you can stay totally dry.

I'm a loyal Hilton Honors Member and Hampton is usually my hotel of choice. This location is not a "Hampton Inn & Suites", but it certainly lives up to Hampton standards and the friendliness of the staff and decoration of the lobby/breakfast area are slightly better than other locations. 

The rooms are fine. I usually say, "yay this is a NICE Hampton" when they have free mouthwash in the bathrooms. Don't ask why, but some locations that spend on the mouthwash do things a little nicer. This location did not have mouthwash so I can't give it 4 stars...
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Two stars for dining, four stars for happy hour, so I'll average it to three.

Service is pretty bad.  The food is mediocre.  It is cheap during happy hour though!  They do $5 glasses of wine from 5-7 each weeknight.  The pours are generous.  It makes it worth stopping by.

I with they could improve their food and service, cause this place has a lot of potential due to the location.  Unfortunately, when the new restaurant opens up in the old American Eagle store, I expect The Saint James to go under just like Plate did.

I went here to get acrylic nails and was very disappointed!  The ladies did not speak English (well, not really), so there was a huuuuuuuuuuuge communication barrier.  The nails were put on very thick so they started to peel after just a few days (although they did look good right after they were put on).  When I went to get my nails fixed/filled today (at another salon, of course), they commented on the hack job and had to charge me extra to correct the peeling.

I really want to think that the ladies who did my nails are not the normal staff at VIP nails, because if they are, I can't comprehend how this place is still in business.

Petruccis is a cool ice cream shop located in the township park and petting zoo. In addition to selling ice cream, petruccis offers hot dogs and other novelities.  I'm a huge fan of their milk shakes, and I always make sure to stop and look at the animals while I'm there.  They have goats, chickens, bunnys and some other livestock.  They also have a nice nursery where you can get plants, as well as limited mulching supplies.  

They have a punch card for frequent ice cream eaters that gets you free ice cream after 10 visits!

It pains me to write this, since I've had okay experiences with this shop in the past on my other vehicles.  Today I messaged them wanting to get my 1982 Chevy C10 head gasket done.  The 250 inline 6 is a VERY simple engine - should be a 6-8 hour job that any mechanic can do.  They did not provide any quote, and I was told "Hi, thanks for thinking of us but unfortunately we do not do head gaskets".  

2 star rating says, "meh, I've experienced better", which in this circumstance is 100% accurate. 

Not sure if incapable of repair, too busy, or just lack of willingness, no further explanation was provided.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: This gym is not bad for the beginner to intermediate gym-goer.  It's a decent size and very clean.  The staff is very friendly and the fact that it is open to members 24 hours a day is nice.  It does have a limited number of cardio machines and also only 1 set of each of the free weights which could be a pain during busy times.  They have only 1 kettlebell and do not have a couple of basic equipment needs like a decline bench or a regular chest/bench press but they do offer a couple of spin classes/week.  So, if you like small gyms, this is a pretty good one.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I enjoy raw fish and seaweed as much, or more than, the next guy.  So when an officemate informed me that we were headed to a new sushi place for lunch, I was pretty excited.  I grew even more excited when I learned that it was reviewed favorably by Craig LaBan. 

I got the small maki and sushi combo, which comes with a California roll, six pieces of sushi and a Miso soup.  The sushi was good, but not great.  The soup was sub par.  It was much less sock-like than some of my other miso soup experiences in Philly restaurants (which will remain nameless), but after a few spoonfuls I really didn't feel like eating any more of it.

Really just meh for me, consistent with reviews I had received from friends but I wanted to check it out for myself. On taco night, the portions were meager for the price and tasted...I dunno...store bought? The service was kind of schizophrenic, vacillating between rude and extremely friendly/attentive. Made me feel rather uncomfortable. The decor is cute but in a contrived Williamsburg, Brooklyn kinda way. I do like the fireplaces, I think they're a nice touch. Not particularly inclined to go back but the views here are so polarized with some very positive ones that I would give them benefit of the doubt and try again...

The weather was not our friend that day, but I have a feeling if it wasn't stormy and cold, the rooftop view of the beach and the easy access to walk right up to water would have made this place gorgeous. I was a little turned off by the lack of options when it came to wine. It was just basically Sutter home in a bottle, which is the lowest quality you can get. It was basically a beer bar. Also as far as food it was wings and corn dogs, of all things. I wasn't super impressed. However, you couldn't beat the location and the oversized chairs were really cool, and given if it was a beautiful day I may have warmed up to this a bit more.

Ok what's up with these reviews. In my humble opinion, it is the overpriced fast food of Mexican. Think McMexican. Well I would prefer to have my mcmoney back. There was no one in front or behind. I told her at the counter I was glad because I had never been there before. She said have you ever been to a Mexican restaurant before? Really? They got the order wrong. Two people, two combo plates. No special orders, and its wrong. My bottomless pit son, even he said eh. They don't have fresh brewed tea, just the funky machine stuff. I don't know. It was just a bit of a let down.

Well since my last review things have gone downhill. Four times in a row when we've gone in for a quick dinner they have been out of unsweet tea. Now we're talking 530 in the evening so there are a few hours before they close. It's one of those restaurant machines that you stick a teabag in and click the start button. They always say that they're out. But the last time that I asked the young man up front said he had to ask his manager and when he came back he said the manager said no. Well then I say no. No to giving you my money if you don't care about your customers. If he got on here and apologized then I might go back. Other than that bye!

I'm a big fan of the great wall, I go here about once every month or two. They have the same stuff all the other chinese take out places in the area have, but the quality of the food is higher than the others. The prices are reasonable and the owner is seemingly always there and is very friendly as are the girls who work the front counter. 
I never get chinese food from anywhere else anymore, cause great wall is the best around. Give em a try, especially if you usually go to that other place down the street in Ridley Park.

Wow... Tokyo express locations have gone downhill since the first few opened years ago in Edmonton.  The maki rolls I ordered were huge.  For $9 they would fill you up for sure.  However, they lacked flavour.

The teriyaki chicken bowl here was pretty standard except it seems like they are making the chicken pieces smaller and smaller every time I visit any of the Tokyo Express locations.

The person taking my order looked pissed off, not sure if it's because he isn't getting any at home or because he's working at Tokyo Express.  Regardless, he needs to learn to smile or at least not look upset.

Tony's is a local Italian joint in the beach town of Carpinteria... Let's just say the food is the only thing saving this place from a 1 star review. The atmosphere is not appealing to any sense, and the service is awful. I don't think I can stress enough about how bad the service at this restaurant actually is, it completely takes away your attention from everything good about the homemade food. If your looking for somewhere cheaper to sit down and eat in Carp and don't care about customer service whatsoever, then I recommend this place for the food... and only the food.

We were thrilled when El Guero Canelo opened on 22nd so we didn't have to drive across town to get a great Sonoran dog!

I like the one with 1 hotdog while hubby likes the Sammie dog with 2 hotdogs. I make a big enough mess with all the fixings that come: bacon, beans, mayo, mustard, onions, salsa, etc...with jalapenos, grilled green onions, radishes, cucumbers on the side.

And then add a couple carne asada tacos or burritos or caramelos with ice cold Mexican cokes and you've got yourself a great meal!  And you didn't have to drive to Nogales to a food cart to get it.

Enjoy!

My friends and I had a great experience at Ralph's Italian Restaurant.  Laura was working at the front of the house, she was pleasant and very accommodating. Michael was our server, he knew the menu extremely well and was helpful while we were picking wines, appetizers and our main course. The bread was fresh from the Sarcone's bakery next door and the food was all perfectly cooked classic Italian. We also really liked the old school ambiance and vibe of the restaurant. We all had a great night and would recommend Ralph's to anyone looking for good South Philly Italian.

Gratzzi is a very pleasant restaurant to visit. It sits just behind Publix in downtown St Pete. Don't dare park at Publix though as you will be towed. 
I've only had drinks here (as I am the happy hour queen!), but the food looks and smells amazing. The bartenders and servers are very pleasant. The well drinks and house wines are cheap and decent on happy hour. Great atmosphere. Very nice decor and very clean.
I would like to eat at Gratzzi soon. Maybe one day I'll have a date and go! All in all a cute, intimate atmosphere with great service.

I freaking love this place! This is my new favorite NoLa hangout spot. It is a large yard on Tchoupitoulas (go figure) that features tons of outdoor seating, TV's, some yard games, and sometimes food vendors. They have an outdoor bar that is dog friendly and an indoor bar with a small food counter. The indoor area is impressive with high beams and an open floor plan. The food counter has typical bar food. But there are sometimes food vendors outside. 
I love their Frose. It is strong stuff. They have a huge selection of beer and liquors. 
Plenty of parking as well. You definitely have to check this place out!

This is a dive bar through and through.  Even though smoking is not allowed in the main bar area, you still can catch a wiff of smoke from the outside seating area.  Yes they have craft beers but their selection is not too extensive but they offer all the main staples you would expect from a dive; PBR and the likes.  I've eaten here twice and the food was always good.  I asked if their wings were breaded and told no, but they are, just as a heads up.  Their happy hour prices are great and available on the weekends.  All in all, a great little place to get a decent meal and a cheap drink.

I wish i remembered everything i ordered so i could relay it all to you... but i don't.

Here's what i can tell you, everything was pretty much amazing. We had probably 4 different orders and it came out beautifully displayed on a large platter. I've heard they do a sushi happy hour? or something? i plan on looking into it further because i need to come here more.

The establishment itself is adorable. Small on the inside, bright pink walls, a lot of windows so it's nice and bright. The patio looks awesome but i haven't given it a try yet. 

If you're in the south grand area, check this place out.

I completely and utterly love the Fresh Market. It's fantastic! It has very unique items and it's only a one minute walk from my home! 

Unfortunately, I can't attend more often because it's pricey. I will hop over there to get something for dinner like sushi, calzone, quiche, etc. They have amazing salads: baked potato salad, artichoke, Mediterranean pasta, cous cous,  all kinds. And they have an Olive Bar of all kinds of olives stuffed that you can think of! :) 

Life Goal: Make enough money that I can shop at the Fresh Market regularly...

Hands down the best Italian BYOB in Philly. We have had many family celebrations here, birthday parties, grad parties and a ton of family dinners here so maybe I am a bit biased. The owner here is a magician, the Broccoli Rabe, Fettucini Ai Tre Funghi, Veal Saltimbocca and the Gnocchi here are the best I have ever had and that is saying a lot because I have been to Italy and have dabbled with a lot of other Italian restaraunts here in Philly and elsewhere. The deserts are excellent as well, I would recommend the Tartufo.

I'm a partner so I know the standards and I'm usually pretty understanding since I know what it's like. But the minute I walked into the store the girl on bar had an attitude with another customer. The store wasn't busy and I was the only one waiting, the Barista at the register didn't acknowledge me. I probably waited a good couple minutes before being greeted. The guy didn't give me my discount after I told him I was a partner.... luckily I mobile ordered my other drinks. Even then I didn't even drink my caramel macchiato because it was gross.

Very disappointed in the staff here. Their parking lot "detail" treated me like a criminal. I went in and asked a server to speak to the manager. He refused to let me talk to a manager, but the manager heard me ask a second time. I tried to explain the lot attendant's poor attitude, but the manager told me to hurry up and get to the point. So I did, and the manager told me the parking lot guy didn't have to treat me with respect. What kind of a business says that to a potential customer?  

They must stay in business by not allowing the staff to talk to the public. Shameful. You've lost my business for life.

Some minor issues with staging. I ordered chicken yakatori as an appetizer, three normal rolls, and a deep fried roll. I got the Philly & crunchy rolls first, then the dynamite roll, followed by the yakatori, and finally the deep fried Gold Point Roll. I didn't care for the flavor of the Gold Point roll, but that sort of thing happens on occasion when you try something new.

In response to a question, I can't quite put my finger on what i disliked about the Gold Point roll. Possibly the flavor of the oil it was fried in. It just didn't taste sushi-like to me, if that makes any sense.

I wish I had seen the "yelp deal" before I had lunch here yesterday! sheesh....anyway,  decent food and excellent service by the new guy, Ed.  I ordered the sausage/fennel/red pepper wood-fired pizza and it was excellent. My friend ordered the bbq pork sando with a side salad, and we shared everything. I've had better versions of "pulled pork" sandwiches, but it wasn't terrible.  The large side salad was pretty good, too.  I'll give them another try, especially with the Yelp dollars deale-o!  Very nice atmosphere, but I imagine it can get crowded in the bar area during happy hour.

Little Alex's is super cute - I love the ease of ordering at the counter and having your food brought out to you. I've only been once (with return trips likely in my future...) and split a couple Raja Tacos with my sister. These are solid - good tortillas, nice melted cheese, cooked green peppers, and cilantro. I added the pico de gallo and their "hot" salsa (and Tapatio, duh). The tacos are solid. I had some serious food envy for the guy sitting next to me, who was crushing a massive burrito covered in some enchilada sauce. I'll be back soon!

Like I said... It was really freaking good!

JRb

The service was great, but unfortunately, could not make up for how old and outdated the hotel is... they upgraded us to an executive floor, but the decor and overall cleanliness of the rooms were below average.  The bathrooms are so small, you can barely close the door -- the toilet and tub are crammed together... the toilet was so old that the handle broke off with the first flush.  This hotel needs a major overhaul -- they state that the executive floor rooms have been renovated recently... umm, I don't think so.  The rooms are still really dingy.  Stay somewhere else, even if you have to pay a little more per night.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Great local bar to hit up after work, as well as on the trip home from town... it stays open until 3 AM!

The staff is great- in fact drop dead gorgeous (Ahem- Jamie)  And for the ladies..there is the "dreamy" Adam..  

Great conversations, excellent drinks and fun people to hang out with, watch a game and to get your drink on.

One drawback- the smoke.  Plan on leaving without deniability if your on  a covert drink mission as it will permeate every ounce of clothing your wearing- hence the reduction of 1 star.  

All in all this a is a regular hang out.  At least once a week.  (More if Jamie is working)

Laid back, cheap drinks, but nobody was in there on a Saturday night.

We walked in just to do sake bombs, so we didn't stay long at this bar.  It is pretty dark so I couldn't see much, but I would describe it as a dive bar.  I was surprised that there wasn't anyone there other than us.  We ordered five sake bombs and they were $5 each.  The bartender was really nice and walked us through doing it.  After we did our shots we moved on.

I would come here with friends, but I probably wouldn't come here expecting to meet people.

I wouldn't say this hotel sucks. But I definitely wouldn't stay here again if I had a choice.

First of all, all the native Boiseans (is that the right word?) I know, WORSHIP this hotel. I think they all must have had their senior proms here or something. And from the looks of it, the hotel hasn't been updated since the Class of '79 celebrated here.

Hotel looks like something out of the Loveboat. Really old stuff, super spread out. I got lost trying to find my room. I hate hotels with outbuildings.

I go where the Hilton points are, but frankly I prefer the Doubletree Club across town. Same cookies, better hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Decor - A little dated with lots of stained glass

Service - Formal but friendly

Food - Tons of food!! This restaurant mainly has dishes with a cream sauce...if you prefer tomato sauce based dishes, go across the street to Laroccas.

The off menu escargo is to die for...I mean any cooked with tons of butter and garlic can't be bad. Included with dinner is a anti - pasta course, soup, entree and pasta side dish. Trust me, theres enough food to feed you for a week.

The place reeks of old school Italian, and I dont mean it in a bad way. The dishes aren't novelle or fusion, but pays a nice homage to traditional dishes.

How things have changed.  So I know competence, consistency and quality aren't hallmarks of fast food restaurants.  This location, however, fails cataclysmically on all fronts.  

Avoid at all costs.  If you enjoy coming back twice to correct your drive-thru order, this might be your place.  

Nasty, greasy food (even by fast food standards).  Milkshakes taste sour like expired milk.  Slimy, soggy lettuce.  All vegetables of questionable freshness.  Burgers so sloppily put together, as if each ingredient was thrown from across the kitchen.  

No.

If you can get past the somewhat bizarre hours, this place is worth going to. It's got a really cute design. Some of the space is a little cramped especially in the corners where they try to fit two or four tops but it's a really cozy feeling. The sushi is consistently good and definitely beats Kampai Sushi across the street. Service is attentive and I love the pitchers they give you whenever you order iced (green or reg) tea. They also serve mochi ice cream for dessert (they jazz it up with some fruit and chocolate designs) that I love. Great place to go that is on the Northwest side of town.

I needed a quick meal and wanted to try somewhere new so I stopped in for lunch.  This place is a little confusing in terms of the protocols associated with ordering and getting your food but it is worth trying to figure it out.  

I went for the chicken souvlaki - nice sandwich all around.  I opted for the plain (as opposed to wheat) and instantly recognized the style from some of the middle eastern places where I've eaten - not like a gyros pita but larger and thinner.  Add some hummus, lettuce, tomato, feta and tzatzki sauce and it was pretty dang good!

The comparisons to Subway rang true for me as so frequently commented on by others.

I have been going here for 5 months.  Always ordering delivery... Some of the best sushi I had on the main line until recently.  I don't know what is going on... But the rice has been chewy lately.  I have asked them on three occasions to please use fresh rice when making my sushi. Especially since I'm paying almost $40 a meal. They told me they had a rice problem and it was faxed. But last time I ordered it was chewy almost on the side of stale. This is very disappointing. I don't know if I'll be ordering from here anymore. Unless they get better rice. No one wants to pay $40 for chewy sushi.

I used to come here a lot more often when I went to high school across the street and lived around the corner. I stopped in yesterday with my sister while visiting our mom on this side of town. They've remodeled since I used to come here, but I'm not sure when that happened. It definitely looked better and the sandwiches are typical Subway sandwiches. I wasn't overly impressed with the service, but it's better than the people who used to work here a few years ago, for sure. I'd stop back in if I'm ever wanting Subway while at my mom's, haha.

We stopped by in the drive-thru with my nieces who were visiting. We wanted something sweet (me and the girls) and my husband wanted coffee. At the time--they might still have this on the menu, but I don't know--they were running some special of two donuts and a medium coffee for $1.99. It's been a few months since then. Needless to say, the deal was either old and they didn't take it down OR the cashier didn't know the menu.

We got to the window and it was $5-something for two measly donuts and a medium coffee. Not worth it, but especially not worth it when their menu said it was supposed to be at least half that. No thanks.

Pretty good! I took my parents here while visiting them in FL, as it's one of their favorite go-to places. It's not much to look at - in a strip shopping center, not very plush on the inside, but oh my goodness does it smell good in there!!

Everyone was happy with their meals, but the bread was the big winner! Each dinner entree came with a salad and a large piece, border-line loaf, of delicious bread, complete with marinara dipping sauce. It was so tasty we just had to request more!

It you're looking for a casual Italian spot in this area, give it a try!

Best pizza in Philly.  Thin crust.  Amazing sauce.  

My parents started going here when they were dating in the 70s.  They brought us later on when we were kids and we loved it.  We switched to Vince's (same recipe) further up the boulevard because it was way closer, but we always thought Charlie's was better - sorry Vinnie!

I don't live nearby, but I'll occasionally stop in for a pie and love bringing people who have never been.  The place is the exact same as it was when I was a kid!  Yeah... it could use a major makeover, but I get the feeling the owners/staff like it just the way it is, and so do I.

All you can eat sushi for 21.99 on the weekends? Perfection. The quality of the sushi was just ok and not amazing but you cannot beat the price. 

It was a clean restaurant. The service was pretty good. Our second platter of sushi took about 30-40 minutes to arrive though (our first was about 20 minute). I recommend getting appetizers because those came out in about 3 minutes. Appetizers are included in the all you can eat price!

I will definitely go there again. Although it's not the best sushi or best quality I've had, when you're craving a lot of decent sushi, this is the place to go.

I have to say the food was very good, but I was there with a group of fifty.  We had a limited menu to choice from, and coffee and tea was included in our dinner free of charge.  When dinner ended we were not asked if we wanted coffee.  Although the waitress was told we wanted coffee she just disappeared and when I found the manager, a rather rude woman who's name I didn't get tried to double talk her way out of including it with dinner and no one tried to retify the situation.  I will NOT be going back there.

I visited the Flying Pig Taphouse last weekend.  It was the initial meeting place for a fundraising event I was involved with through a charitable organization.  

From the outside, this place appears very nice.  You step in to a very clean establishment, with very friendly staff.  They seem very attentive to everyone's needs.  

I personally am not a beer drinker; so this isn't quite the pace for me.  However, they have a very extensive beer selection, both on tap, and in bottles.  The prices are average for other like establishments in St. Pete. 

All in all, a nice place to visit.

First I will say that I appreciate their ability to use fresh and organic foods. Outside of that I'm just not a fan. We got the Meat #1, which I admit wasn't bad - and the cheese #3, aka the Brooklyn Pie. There was nothing "Brooklyn" about this pie; in fact if a place in Brooklyn sold it, I'd be willing to say they'd be closed before too long. I found it incredibly flavorless with far too much sauce.
Again, the meat #1 was fine, but it wasn't enough to make me want to come back. Plus, call me old school, I like round pies. Nit-picking I know, but yeah.

In a way, Madison's feels a lot like a very college-popular Boston pub.  Maybe it's the woodsy atmosphere, and the fact that you can swing around on your chair and be talking to new, also slightly inebriated patrons, in a fairly friendly and low-barrier kind of way.  The free peanuts are also a nice touch, even if the Joyce has had that game covered for a while.  

I actually had a much better time here than I would have thought.  But I also came during the Sunday 6pm lull, which I imagine is a long stretch from weekend nights.  I think it was the recessed neon shot bar at the back that tipped me off.

On this one particular morning, I ordered at the drive-thru.  This location has 2 drive-thru stalls, so try to pick the shortest one to get through the line the fastest.  The line seems to move pretty quickly in the morning when drivers are usually just getting a cup of coffee and a sandwich to go.  My bagel was the perfect temperature, the cashier was polite.  No problems!

In the past, when my order was not ready upon arrival at the pick up window, I have been asked to pull ahead for them to bring it out to me.  When my order was delivered minutes later, I was also given 2 coupons good for free fries or pie.  Not an inconvenience at all!
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Just meh....I really like their breakfast. My favorite is their biscuit and gravy. The milk gravy taste just like my grandmothers. The lunch was not too good today. I got the chicken tenders and onion rings... the chicken was chewy and rubbery and the onion rings were super greasy. Popeyes is much better for chicken tenders. My husband got one of their cheeseburgers and there was so much mayonnaise that it was literally falling out as he tried to pick it up.Yuck. I will stick to Hardees for the breakfast and skip the lunch.

I went to this gym for about four months and then I quit at the end of last year because of the smell. You might think well gyms are going to have a certain smell to them and I agree however what I don't like is that the ventilation was truly inadequate for the gym's size. Consequently the Smell was far too ripe far too often. In addition, there was too much pressure to pay up charges to utilize the full gym. I think everything in the gym should be available to you, if no one's using it, and that's just not the case here. The customer service was OK for the most part but the gym alone doesn't warrant the pricing that they charge.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Not gonna be a super long review, but I can definitely say Sushi Garden has really upped itself in customer service and quality.  I always come here for AYCE sushi and appreciate that they don't go overboard on the rice to "fill you up faster".  The fish is really good quality and always tastes fresh.  They have other specialty rolls that I wish were included on the AYCE menu but for what it's worth- I'm still a fan!  

Our server (I want to say his name was Nick or Mike) was also incredibly attentive and friendly.

I definitely prefer this one to the other location on Country Club.

Hertz has been good to me as a business traveler. No issues picking up my car, upgrading with the free gold choice (I usually rent intermediate), or returning the car. I've rented cars here three times for 5 days straight each time, and total would always be around $208. I've had a Toyota Corolla S with 14k miles, Altima with 40k, and Camry with 45k. They all ran smoothly, had clean interiors, and everything worked. Only thing I would say is clean the wipers, because it's dangerous driving in the rain when you can barely see the windshield.

It's cheap and they have the basic facilities I want, but to some degree you get what you pay for. For example, they open at 8 am on Saturdays, but as I'm writing this review at 8:32 am, the place is still shut down with no sign of opening anytime soon. People are waiting outside for them to open, and I've watched about 8 people get in their cars and leave, or drive up and then drive off. So, I got up early on my day off, motivated to get a workout that I pay for monthly, and they're not even professional enough to keep their own hours.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
My husband and I discovered Wasabi on the last day we were in Reno. After eating here we both wished that we had found this place earlier.

$15.95 for all you can eat sushi during their lunch hour. What a deal!! The Hamachi and Saba nigiri were so delicious. We also had a bunch of maki's. My favorite were the Lion King roll and the Viagra roll. 

The sushi chef was super fast in making all of the sushi and he provided excellent customer service. 

We will definitely be coming back to this restaurant the next time we are in Reno.

Ok, I must have missed something with this plate. I tried the Asada and the chicken, and they were ok, but they weren't so mind blowing that I felt like I ever had to go back. The meat on the Asada was super dry. The  chicken at least had some onions and flavoring in it, that one was ok. The guava soda I drank with the meal was the highlight of it for me! I did like the toppings bar but there were no labels on everything so I really had no idea what I was putting on my tacos. That would have maybe helped me know what I was creating!

It wasn't bad by any means, but I doubt when I visit again I'll make any extra effort to go.

First, their menu board in the Drive-Thru says their Large coffee is $1.89, but when you get to the pay window, they're charging $1.99. I called it to the attention of the clerk three different times but they have not corrected their menu board. 

Then, this morning I went through again, and all I'm getting is a large black coffee, so not too complicated an order, and again I paid their $1.99 plus tax, but the gal at the window gave me a medium. I didn't even realize it until I got home.
