Will find some place else for my morning coffee.

My family took me to Ooka for my birthday seeing as how I love sushi. The environment is well designed and clean and the service was fast and curteous. I ordered an assortment of their special rolls and was not dissappointed. The rolls were well balanced and the meat was perfect, the spicy scallop roll was particularly noteworthy. Others in my family not as occustomed to sushi ordered teriyaki that arrived promptly and very hot, they assure me it was excellent. Overall no complaints and good times were had. Great Japanese joint.

It gets the car kinda clean. This is only an exterior wash place. $20 for the ultimate. While lines can be long they do seem to move at a good pace. Just don't expect the cleanest car. It is the old style heavy material that doesn't really clean the back side of our SUVs. I need to find a touchless laser place. Any recommendations? Don't want to drive to Fishers to the only one I'm aware of. But I have to. Last time I took my wife's car through and the back wasn't as clean as I'd have liked. So down a star as the Fishers touchless is now my go to (esp when on a Costco run).

Marsh closed up and now a Kroger. The food court is impressive but not why we came here. Prices are okay for downtown. But as big as the store is (you want to see a small store hit Needlers on 320 N New Jersey St) the choice of stock is not great. They did have Finlandia grassfed butter so that is okay but it is also pricier than Kerrygold. [edit to update I found the Kerrygold in the specialty cheese section. Do not know why they do not stock all the butter in the same area. Not even the same side of the store.] I will shop here for the Kroger organics and to get some variety from Needers. An okay store for the space.

#312

This is a great Italian option just east of Center City in Philadelphia. It fits right into the standard "great little restaurant" category in Philly - small restaurant, tables close together, seems to be family-owned, and GREAT good. I was here for dinner with a friend, and it was exactly the right atmosphere for that kind of meal. Friendly atmosphere, good service. It's not a BYO, which is a bit odd for this kind of restaurant in this area, but whatevs - it's still good!

As always in Philly, no parking. Best bet is walking or uber.

Apparently it's a tough location. New chef, new but similar menu. Food is delicious, the whole fish being my favorite. We have gone often since the new chef took over, and are alway supportive of a neighborhood gem that is open late (ish).  
               The food remains solid and consistent. The bar service (we sit at the bar) has dropped precipitously to the point of this evening's travesty. (no reflection on the waitstaff)
                While eating hangar steak and whole fish (at the bar), the bartender mopped with pine-sol and bleach, and completely ruined our meal. Not a good pairing. Hope to hear feedback.

A friend and I tried this place on Saturday and it was fantastic! I was a little worried when we went in because we were the only people in the place, but the service, food, and atmosphere were great! I had the dancing eel roll and the dynamite roll. Both rolls were well prepared and great tasting. The sushi chef came to the table and talked to us and he was very knowledgeable about sushi. The prices are great here as well. Many basic rolls such as Spicy Tuna and California rolls were around $5. I was glad to find a sushi bar in Lawrence and I will definitely be returning!

Still 5 stars! Since my first review, I have returned 2 more times (recently) and have been delighted each time. On my family's most recent visit, we all had an absolutely delicious dining experience. The bread,.flat bread pizza, fried mozzarella, linguine Alfredo, salmon and steak were all prepared with great attention to detail. Flavors were exquisite! Finally on to dessert, where a limoncello cake, a cannoli and special cannolli creme chocolate cake were all delicious! We will return and hopefully, bring some more along with us next time!

I ordered a hot sandwich and the sauce was awful.  The bread was good, cheese was barely there, meat cooked ok but grizzly in parts, not trimmed or pounded. 
Sauce out of a can or a jar would have been better! 
Also there was a really loud guy at the bar who kept talking like he knew about cars, but he didn't. Anyone who says they know about Mazdas would never make the statement that a Miata has a "Rotary engine", unless of course it was a custom job. Just an example of the clientele. 
I may try the pizza in the future but it will definitely  be a while before I return.

I have a hard time giving this hotel more than 3 stars. I stayed here 3 nights. Check in was efficient but they did not offer me a bottle of water or a welcome bag. I think they should do that for first time guests. The room was mostly clean but the towel bar broke and the fridge would not turn on. The bed was ok and I had a room with a balcony, and the fresh air at night 2as nice, but the noise from the road did wake me up a few times. The bistro has a limited number of items and I did not eat there as a result. The staff was nice if not aloof.  Oh and -- NO HOT TUB!  Save your pennies and stay at the Hilton Garden Inn instead
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
eh...will have to try it again.  I got the special (veal chop) and it was covered in a glaze that tasted like marmalade jelly.  I felt like it should be on a piece of toast served with bacon and eggs, not my $25 veal chop.  But, the veal chop would have been great without it so thats just like, my opinion man.  

The prosciutto appetizer was pretty amazing, we could have ordered 2 of those and been good to go.

When I opened the menu I expected the prices to be about $5-10 more than they were.  Great service and big portions.  Im looking forward to trying it again.

as an avid fan of fast food, I have been to many of the different restaurants and chains the city has to offer, Mcdonald's has been in my eating habits for more years than I care to say. While each location is run differently, this location is also run badly. 

the service is slow, the employees rude,and consistently the food is bad. on many occasions  I have stated I wasn't going to return. but only do because of hoping it getting better, but it never does.  I think this location needs to do us all a favor and close. 

Do yourself a favor, don't use this location, you will only leave  aggravated..
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Tried the hibachi not the sushi. Might be good for sushi per other reviews. Two meals were listlessly prepared with indistinct flavors. We were the only customers on a week night. Perhaps that should have been a clue. If not for the nearby wine shop the meal would have been a complete waste of time. Two stars because food was fresh, hot, and right-sized portions, and place was clean. You might like it though so don't be afraid to try it. We are going to check out other hibachi offerings in the area before trying this one again.

Delicious sushi...but when we came in around lunchtime on Monday entire case  (I assume for sushi) was empty ;( 

They had ONE pre made rice ball pack and ONE something spicy with lots of mayo on top (pre made) 
It didn't look inviting... 

Honestly, I'm a sushi-sashimi Freak but there was nothing to eat! 
- Ok - so we sat and ordered salmon lovers special and spicy tuna and nigiri and that was super delicious!...but - the portions were TINY (6 pieces (Itsy-bitsy) and after paying $35 I was hungry!!!!!

It's way too expensive for take out and lack of ambiance 
I will come back but not very soon

I really enjoyed Felicia's! The crust is very crispy, towards the end of the pizza but ooey-gooey in the middle where all of the cheese congregates. 

We got the Pomodora Romano which was incredibly sweet.. so much so that we couldn't eat more than one slice. I really wanted to like this pizza, but  the sweetness of the carmelized onions was overpowering and there wasn't enough prosciutto to give balance as a sweet/salty dish.

 The Portobello & Roasted Garlic pizza was delicious! Tons of garlic flavor, tomotoes and portobello's. I will definitely go back again and try a few other selections.

The brunch was pretty good. I've never gone to this restaurant for any other reason except by suggestion from our real estate agent - who suggested their Sunday brunch. They have stations with different foods including their salad bar (I didn't check that part out). The omelets were really delicious - made fresh to order in front of you, they had different waffle options with toppings, a lunch-y station, and their lovely chocolate fountain with a lot of other food as well. All in all, I would come back for another brunch, though for other meals probably not.

I used to dine at this restaurant frequently, however the last two times they denied me the opportunity to eat all you can eat. I typically only order an appetizer, two nigiri, and two to three rolls. I did not and could not understand why I was being discriminated against for à la carte only. I've always eaten everything that I've ordered. I will no longer be dining at this restaurant. There is no way that I'll be convinced otherwise. Shame on Sakana for allowing such actions. If you offer all-you-can-eat, then follow through with what is advertised.

Gorgeous views from the room, cute gym w cardio machines, cables and decent size free weights.  I had wonderful workouts! And definitely deserved breakfast buffet afterwards: omelettes that we got served in probably less then 10min, hot foods like sausages, bacon, french toast etc, good selection of fresh fruit, berries, greek yogurt. Good service all over, from housekeeping and front desk, to waiters and all. At our breakfast buffet we had Debbie as our waitress, she's always with a smile, accommodated our special requests and got us what we wanted (omelettes cooked w no butter/oil, add avocado etc). Nice vacation  spot!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Maybe if I had not heard such good things about this place it would have been better, but I was very disappointed overall. 

First, it is way too expensive. I am willing to pay for truly great pizza, but this is just so-so with some very fancy toppings and for that they charge way too much. My friend and I split a salad and a pizza and each had a soda and that came to over $30 for our lunch. Sorry, that's just way too much especially for a place that does not have waiter service. 

The ingredients are definitely fresh, but the dough is nothing special and the sauce had no particular flavor. 

Save some time and try other places!

Damn, whats with all the one star hate? 

I have been to this bank several times and I haven't really encountered that many problems. The customer service is alright. The only thing that is kind of tricky is the entrance and the exit  part of the trip in the bank.

I do realize that this is a mega corporate bank and they are prone to problems. But I will tell everyone from personal experience that they are not nearly as bad as Chase, or Regions bank. Those banks gave me way more problems than this one ever did.

In short good customer service and great convenience. Not really deserving of so much chain scorn.

While I will admit that this is not my favorite Rouses they do have certain things that I like. The best thing they have is the prices on their merchandise. They are cheaper than Win-Dixie down the street but they lack the selection of their competitor.

If you want to go to a better location check out the Rouses on Airline Hwy in Metarie. The problem I have with this particular rouses is that it has more of a closed in feeling to it. It just doesn't seem the same as all the other Rouses I go to.

In short its alright to check this one out if you live in the Mid City area. But still not my favorite Rouses Location.

The only reason I am giving this place 2 stars is because of the fantastic customer service. I stopped here a couple of years ago just out of curiosity. The host was incredibly friendly, the waitress was incredibly attentive to my needs. It was a clean and very beautiful restaurant.

Now for the bad part. I ordered the food which was not very good at all. The bread was very stale and the pasta I ordered was pure garbage. Of couse the bill wasn't something I wanted to see either. $52 for so called "food" not even fit for a dog, and that was before the tip!

In short great customer service! But very bad, over priced food.

Tucked away into a far corner of the UC district in Philadelphia, Ajia definitely delivers some great food, although the experience is tempered by the disappointing service, as remarked by other Yelpers.

Showed up on a Saturday evening, and it was about three quarters full, with a decent atmosphere around the place.  The infamous grumpy waitress was our server, although I have to say that I genuinely did try to give her a chance before coming to my conclusion.

Either way, ignoring the service, the food was great and the prices were really good for the quality.  A nice (ethnic) joint in Philly that serves good, authentic food.

Jalapeño appetizers are to die for! I recommend you try them if you like spicy food. 
The list of AYCE sushi rolls is short but everything tastes fresh and amazing. The chefs take their time and pay attention to details. The presentation is as appetizing as what you're being served. 
The service is friendly and attentive, you're always being asked if there's anything else you need and your drink is topped off constantly, something I really like. 
Good family atmosphere and also good if you're planning on going on a date. 
Try this place if you're a hard core sushi water, you will not be disappointed!

It was fine. I went on a Monday night during happy hour, so the sushi ended up being reasonably priced and was of a decent quality; however, I would not be willing to pay full price for it.

The service was really slow but mostly friendly, though we almost didn't get part of our order. Had to bug the waitress about that.

The worst part was that it took us about 15 minutes after our table was cleared to flag someone down to give us our check. The hostess had passed us by in a rush several times until I was able to get her attention, and she told us she had assumed we were waiting for dessert.

I had a pretty good experience here. Showed up 15 minutes after opening, and there were already a few people waiting for their orders. Looks like this place gets some decent business.

Placed my order and was quoted 10 minutes of wait time for a cheese pizza, crazy bread, and buffalo wings. It ended up being an accurate estimate.

Food tasted pretty good. One breadstick was really tiny, but I wasn't keeping track of whether it was one of the eight I was supposed to get, or if it was an extra. The wings were generously sauced and had a good kick to them.

The employee who took my order was also nice.

I was excited to try this place while on vacation to see my family.

I'm going to keep  this short and sweet.
I am all about "hip" farm to table restaurants. 

I LOVE supporting local farms and businesses. 

It's a possibility that I am spoiled living in the pacific north west- where places like this are a dime a dozen and therefore need to execute the food on their menu properly.

Fried chicken should never be soggy. Even with gravy. 

My husband said his burger was super tasty.

So for that I give you two stars instead of declaring a "citizens arrest" for soggy chicken breading.

Well, it's a chain so it's really about the service, which sucks!

The first time I ordered online.  I went to the restaurant and it took them 45 minutes to find the order.

The second time we got delivery and were missing 2 items that we were charged for.  So, their delivery driver went home for the night (at 8pm).  Fine, refund the money or credit the account.  No, they didn't want to do that.  So, cue disputing the charge with the credit card company and a Yelp review that hopefully encourages you to go elsewhere.

Going to be a bit conservative on my review.  I was there on 7/3 and it was busy.  Really busy.  And it was hot.  Really hot.  There seemed to be a staff of five at most.  The bartender, one waitress, and the cooks (possibly three).  I went because I had purchased a coupon of some sort.  

The food was good.  Well priced.  Nice selection of beers including some that are not that common.  But...the service left a LOT to be desired.  If I didn't have additional coupons, I'm not sure I would give this place another shot.  But I do, and I will, and I will report back.

I think this place is just ok. I have friends who rave about it and I'd be willing to give it another shot, but the goat cheese and mushroom pizza finished with arugula was just average. I did like the taste of their sausage, but the pizza snob in me just refuses to accept the concept since I'm used to pizza in New York and Jersey. For a few bucks more, you can go to a place like nomads or get an entire pie from a decent shop. It was fast and you can pile it up with toppings, but those two characteristics aren't very important to me and are the reasons for the average rating.

I am a beer geek extraordinaire and monster has an awesome selection of beer. Hops and Grapes probably has less brands of beer than this place. The beer wall is probably 400ft long! I just wish they had a better make your own six selection. However, if you ask if they have singles of a certain beer they'll let you take a bottle from a six pack on the shelf. Anyway, they also have a nice wine and liquor selection, but Hops and grapes probably beets them in this category. The staff is cool an always willing to help.

Great liquor store! Great selection of wine, beer, and spirits. I think monster beverage down the street might have a slightly better beer selection, but you would only notice if you're a beer fanatic. If you feel like splurging, they have some cool vintage bottles of wine and some nifty spirits I can't find other places. Also, they have an impressive walk-in humidor if you like cigars. They also wine tastings every fri, and you can order some of there wines on there website. I've never ordered online, so I'm not exactly sure how it works, but the option is there.

I am just absolutely in love with this place! My husband and I have our date nights there as much as we can. But don't be fooled, kids are definitely welcome! We took our daughter there for Sunday Brunch and the place was full of families! The food is outstanding and we have always had great service. The atmosphere lends itself well to everyone, whether you want a casual dinner or are celebrating a special occasion! This restaurant is exatly what we have been looking for in this rapidly growing part of town!

Only went once, when I first moved to Brandon, 6 years ago.  I was missing NYC pizza and was told about the place.  "It's amazing, the best pizza in Tampa.  They have a double stack pizza that's awesome!"  Ok, that set the bar pretty high.  Ordered a large pie and when I got there, they'd accidentally made it a double decker.  When I got it home (just 5 minutes away) my wife and I dug in.  "Dug" is the right word.  Sloppy, soggy, drippy, falling apart.  We'd have done better to go at it with spoons and straws.  Never went back.

I KNOW you can do better.  See my other reviews for the best pizza joint in Tampa.

I like the flavor of this tea but expect to throw 4-5 tea bags away and clean up all the tea off the counter and floor.  The design is so tight it leaves no room for the rest bag to not be torn when opening it. I called to suggest since the phone number is wrong on this pouch is to redesign it to avoid the tea bag being torn when opening. I tried shaking it to move the tea bag down, however the bag is fragile and pulling it out of the tight pouch it tore. 

The person on the phone made it about me doing this or that and not about customer satisfaction. Sorry Whole Foods won't be buying this brand of tea again.

Went to Taipan earlier this week with some colleagues from work.

As far as Chinese food goes in China Town I'm pretty happy with the food that they provide.  The portions are large and the lunch for 2 could easily serve 3.  I've been a few times now and I keep trying new dishes and I'm never disappointed.  They are consistent and everything is flavourful.  We're always out before the lunch hour is done and the service is decent.

The restaurant is nothing fancy but it's a great lunch spot if you're downtown and in a bit of a hurry (even for groups of up to 6).

I'll be back for sure.

Trenton has great local coffee houses, but it's also nice to have a good brand name coffee chain right downtown. 
This location is in a nice corner spot. The interior is warm and welcoming, as are the baristas (Tony is our favorite). There are lots of cozy seating areas as well as tables for larger groups and meetings. 
The display cases are well stocked with a variety of food choices, even at 3:15pm.
The wall murals reflect the historic and governmental significance of the city of Trenton.
They are also open until 7:00, well after the state workers have departed.

Fabulous location.  Very friendly and efficient staff.  We got a rate on Priceline that was so low I am embarrassed to tell you, but our room may have reflected that.  We were in a handicapped room right off the elevators.  The handicapped shower flooded the entire bathroom every time we used it.  The people coming and going from the elevator were so loud they could wake the dead.  Like I said, we had a VERY low rate, and the location was wonderful, so we put up with these issues.  If we had paid more, we probably would have asked to change rooms.  We would return, especially if we could get a screamin deal on Priceline.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
My first experience with bubble tea was about eight years ago. I wasn't impressed. A friend suggested I give it another shot, so we mosied on over to Bubble Buzz. 

Instead of a milk-based tea, I tried a fruit-based one. It was delicious! The folks at Bubble Buzz use fresh ingredients to concoct what I'd describe as a cross between a Booster Juice and a Slurpee. 

The drink I tried was a mango fruit tea with sago and lychee pieces. It was light tasting and not too sweet. 

The service was great, and the place has a really clean, bright look to it. I will definitely go again.

I only wish that I frequented this place in the past while traveling with this job the past 7 years.  Since the run is almost over I may not make it back again. But I do want to recommend this sushi restaurant. The chef was super friendly and talkative although I struggled a bit with his English.  He gave me a sampler appetizer and it was wonderful. An assortment of all the raw fish and cooked octopus. Even included some eel. Wow, delicious and a very nice gesture.  
Finally, I would have absolutely went full 5 stars if the carpet condition and cleanliness was better.  All in all, no doubt I will try to stop again if I can.

We were treated like royalty here, as were our two dogs! This hotel was super pet friendly, they provided a dog bed, bowls, and treats for my dogs and only charge us $50 for the both of them.  I room was nice and beds were comfy. The only real down side to our stay was the bathroom echoed, so when you used the restroom everyone "heard" what you were doing. Other then that this place is amazing!  I also love the location: close to the metro train (we took it to see the arch), down the street from our concert venue, and across the street from nice restaurants.

WE WILL BE BACK!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Okay in retrospect it did not warrant 4 stars. It was only preferred by virtue of its proximity. In the half year I've been nearly a mile away, I haven't gone back. Truth is there's plenty of cheap, fast (delivery), and tolerably well-executed even if basic (i.e. not stunningly fresh quality raw nigiri/sashimi, or highly innovative rolls) Japanese places in the city. Places like this are of best benefit to the people nearby, it really isn't worth the trouble of traveling to as a destination. As such, I guess I can't really call myself a fan.

Okay I love deals,love to find great deals for my son and I to try out.

Living Social is an awesome find but Cheeseology is even better. 

What better place to have a  "Mahookieday lunch" with a little skillet of mac n cheese to your very own liking.

My 13yr old and I hit them up today for lunch and I'll just say I'll return again and again.

My son had the Buffalo Chicken and I Shrimp Scampi with bread crumbs,I also had a salad with cranberries,blue cheese and walnuts it was to die for good.

"Mahookieday"~ A day just for a Ma and her kid to play hookie from school and concentrate deeply on that mother-child bond.

I love Shop N Bag!  I like it much better than Fresh Grocer (which is kinda dirty and the produce isn't yummy and has very few meat alternatives).  Produce is great.  Some organic things.  For people, like me, who have dietary restrictions (vegan), I've found their selection to be great.  They have like 4 kinds of tofu and every type of non dairy milk you could want.  And talk about ethnic food selection!  There are so many foods I'd never heard of til I starting shopping at Shop n Bag.  I try to get something I've never had before every time I go.

I just ran in here really quick for a pack of beef hot dogs, buns, and potato salad to bring to a BBQ while visiting family in the area. It seemed clean and so were the restrooms. The lady the the deli helped me out with recommendations on the deli sides and was very nice and helpful. The hot dogs were the most expensive I have seen in the country and totally caught me off guard. Other than the outrageous price for that I like this store I can't speak for many other products because I went in here looking for specific item's. I did go to a Rouses earlier that day and liked their store a lot better it just seemed to have more and looked nicer.

I went here to see what all the hype was about, I was not impressed. The scene was filled with a bunch of Philly posers who wanted to pretend they were in NYC. The food was ok; not good or bad, just ok. The service left a lot to be desired. We couldn't get refills on water the waitress was busy, one dish was cold and needed to be reheated, then we had to wait for the check because the waitress was too busy. Meanwhile, the manager was giving us dirty looks because they were busy and he wanted our table, but we had to wait and receive and pay our bill.

I will not go back.

The sushi was great, but the place was small and crowded. The menu has a more authentic feel than other Japanese spots since there was no chicken teriyaki or shrimp sauce on the menu. The unagi (eel) was flavorful and cooked per perfection. I also suggest the Vandy roll (fried on the outside with melted cream cheese oozing out!) Ok sake selection, perhaps a little overpriced ($15  for a bottle drink smaller than a beer). I would not suggest going right at 7 PM if you are claustrophobic. But if you are looking for just plain old delicious sushi in Nashville this is the place to go!

I have to agree with Sara V, this would have been a 5-star, but the RC drops it to a 4-star. (Coke over Pepsi please, by the way....)

We went here after a co-worker recommended the wings and we were very impressed. There are about 10 flavors of wings to choose. We had four varieties -- original, tequila lime, "pit wings", ancho chile.  All were delicious, large, juicy, not greasy. And they are a great deal at 50 cents each! 

We also shared a basic burger. It was your basic burger, but delicious... very flavorful, juicy with good quality bun and fresh lettuce and tomato. 

Service was excellent and helpful. 

We will definitely be back!

I don't understand the negative reviews. Our meal was FANTASTIC, service was superb and I have nothing but good things to say.  I liked the small plates style for this type of food.  They even added on an extra taco to our order to be sure everyone at the table got one.  My father in law commented on how nice it was to have Mexican food presented in a way that wasn't just slopped on a plate.   The only reason it's not 5 stars is the portion size for the guacamole.  It's smaller than what I'm accustomed to for that price, but that's not to say it isn't worth it!

We wanted something light to eat and came upon this sushi spot.  It's a tiny place on a small street in Philly.  I came with my gf and we order the 30 piece platter.  It came with 15 pieces of sushi (variety), 2 rolls and 1 special roll for about $32, i think it's a tad expensive.  The sushi was good though, fish tasted fresh and they made it for us in a short time.  This is a small place, not much seating, maybe about 6 at the sushi bar and a couple of tables around.  It's more of a take out place.  It's a decent place.

I love this place. Great ambiance, very nice and knowledgable employees. I'm usually at the bar for happy hour (available M-F from 5-7 pm) - which is great. $5 glasses of house wine, 1/2 off they're rotations seasonal cocktails. I remember when around the time opened the happy hour wine was a rotation of different wineries...now it's just always Corbett Canyon (or something like that), which is decent for a drink special. 

The pizzas are amazing, my favorites are the  Margherita and the one with short ribs. The hand cut fries are scrumptious. I have been a couple times for regular dinner but really do just prefer going for happy hour.

So we loved so much we stayed on our way home. Not as impressed.  The mirror's back light only partially works and flickers. Mostly just staying off.  The bedroom looked clean, but we are at the end of the building and this time it's rather noisy. There was one towel that was dirty. I grabbed it and put it on the floor so my kids wouldn't try and use it. 

The front desk clerk wasn't helpful. He told me what flor my room was on, but that was it.  We had to figure out the rest.  

There was cat litter in the elevator.  Perhaps to help with a spill.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Went to get French gel mani/pedi. Was very sloppily done. the shiny coating was all over my skin as well as nailpolish on the skin. the French line wasn't even..one was clearly wider then the other. Had something pointy sticking up on nail that I kept telling her about and she kept saying it would go away when she put coatings on but it didn't. DIDNT get a mini foot/leg and hand massage that all other nail salons do for you. very disappointing. not to mention the air conditioner didn't work on a very hot day.

Made reservations. They could not accommodate us inside. We sat on the deck which turned out to be fine. Our waitress was mediocre . not bad not good. And she should have asked to refill our drinks. I got the fish tacos that were very dry. Only a teaspoon of sauce was put on them so I had to ask for more. Instead of boring lettuce and tomatoes they should use a Caribbean type slaw like other places do.  Now, I have been here through the years and I don't think it's a bad place to eat. So I would say the food is decent, service is mediocre including the bartenders. Nice atmosphere.

We decided on Sbraga for a big bday dinner party on a Saturday night. There was about a 15-20 min wait with reservation, but that can be expected with a crowd of 12. We went with a 3 course meal and dessert for 49.00, but with drinks, it was a ton more. The food was excellent and plated very well, but the portion size was tiny. The service was good and atmosphere set the tone. This is an excellent place for a small dinner or dinner date to impress the lady. Be sure to grab some pre-dinner before the actual dinner. Otherwise, you'll be left with a loud stomach and empty pockets. Absolutely pricey for the portion size.

Normal starbucks just located in roswell, new mexico.  Maybe area 51?

Not too far from Slu's campus it is under the UFO looking thing.  I keep my eyes peeled for Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones to stop a bug from taking off with the galaxy.

They have a drive thru.  I would have expected some kind of delivery system, but maybe it costs too much to fly that saucer?

Some people need their fix at starbucks every day.  I don't know if I'd trust little green men with my brain chemistry or risk prolonged contact with the unknown.

Proceed... with... caution!

Car is dirty outside, especially side mirrors. Waited over 15 mins at airport for shuttle while watching Budget, Enterprise and Avid steadily go thru. One bus crowded so that people were standing next to driver. Driver did not announce Gold Membership and we got off in error as we saw Hertz on building. Girl at desk was so rude and made us feel like idiots.  No apologies, no offer to help us.  We walked to other building and it was a mob scene. Kiosk helped but because employee was in a different state she couldn't tell us where the lot was. Guy at booth was very helpful as we left lot. Next time we are using Enterprise.

Not a bad spot. I like the wide space, different from other coffee shops in the city. And they serve La Colombe I believe, which is never a bad brew to serve. I wasn't too impressed otherwise. The barista was not very friendly, and there are not many places for ac outlets. It's a shame I didn't like it too much because other than Euphoria in the Piazza, there are not many other places to choose from for your coffee fix in Northern Liberties.

I'd come back but I probably would be reluctant to do so. Heads up: CASH ONLY.

Cousin's is the place to go if you live in North Philly. I take this joint any day over Fresh Grocer. 

The only complaints I have is with the produce (which is expected considering it is COUSIN'S after all) and the hours (like many others have said, they have awful and inconvenient hours post-5pm).

That being said, I can get most essentials here and for much cheaper than anywhere else. 

This is only a two minute bike ride from my apartment so there's no reason not to shop here. Matter of fact, I'm headed there tomorrow.

When it's too cold or you're feeling to cheap to go to Trader Joe's, Cousin's is the place to head to.

I stand by my original review of nastiness. The service is horrendous.  They have been bullying me to try to make me change my review. I will not. I know what nasty fish smells like, and this place had it when I went. 

This place used to be my favorite in Belle Chasse.  I took everyone there.  Today the fish was awful it was smelly and had a stringy film over it.  They insisted it was fresh.  It was not.  I didn't even finish one whole piece.  They refused to replace it or take it off the check. I will not be back.

I know what sushi should taste and smell like, this is not it.

This is a touristy dive bar. It is filthy for sure. The crowd is fun, and the house band late night is talented. They play the same set list regularly, so you know what you will get when you go in (usually) They have the ability to read the crowd and can keep the party going.  
They throw in alot of hair metal, and take requests. They even managed to crank out a nice rendition of Sara Smile when my husband asked. 

I'm not sure what the bartenders do with all that alcohol because they cant seem to make anything I ask for. Some of them have specialty drinks, this is a gamble. Stick with the basics, and you will be fine

Is there a way to give ZERO stars ??? This hotel and frankly Marriott Bonvoy Elite services customer service is about the least customer service oriented I have yet to find in the hospitality industry . They did zero - except to insist they were. Right on every count and to lie and procrastinate in terms of getting back to me despite countless attempts on my part to reach out to them . You would think I'm asking them for a piece of gold rather than a simple sorry . Please don't stay here and frankly perhaps no Marriott hotels - bed bugs , falls on water - I can only imagine what one would deal with with a real tragedy !!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I really like this Starbucks location. It's definitely a neighborhood spot for East Franklin. If you love nearby it's quite likely you'll run into a friend. Typically it's easy to get in and out within 5 minutes. It does get very busy during the early morning hours. 

It's a great location to meet a friend or colleague unless they are full which happens more often than I'd like. This is a criticism I have have most Starbucks. There's never enough seating. 

The staff is always very friendly and courteous. If you like Starbucks coffee, I would recommend this location.

Typical fast food fare. In Green Hills there really aren't many traditional fast food options. There's Wendy's, Krystal, and McDonald's. So, it really depends on personal preference. 

Personally I'm not a big fan of Wendy's. There are far superior burger and sandwich options nearby, albeit at a premium. However, the location of this Wendy's keeps it on my lunch rotation. I typically get the spicy chicken sandwich. I've never been a fan of their burgers or fries. Unless this is close to your home or office or you just like the dollar menu, I would highly recommend looking elsewhere for lunch.

Not a happy camper in the beginning but I got a great deal in New Orleans at the Airport on Hotwire. After my debit card situation was cleared. I was taken care of. 

Disclaimer: *If you have a Louisiana license and you are using a debit card, they will not allow you to rent unless you have a Major credit card. Apparently, people with Louisiana licenses don't return cars...* 

I live in Miami now, went to Louisiana to visit and had a LA license and a debit card = not a happy camper...but it was cleared once I had to prove I lived in Miami...

Dropped in to this location with my mom after getting our nails done at the salon a few stores down for a late Mothers Day; neither of us had tried this place before and thought we'd give it a go.

It's a self serve type situation where you get to pick what size (there are 2), what kind of frozen yogurt, what toppings and pay a certain amount according to the weight.  I liked that I had the opportunity to choose & give a small try of them before committing to a certain kind.  

Overall, I was pleased with what I received and would definitely drop in again if I'm in the area! :)

Most grocery stores are pretty much the same, but I have to say I actually enjoy this one a bit more than the others; one big difference is they have a "nut bar" with such a variety and they seem to be quite a bit more well stocked.

I've found that the employees seem to be abundant and friendly enough; willing to provide assistance where needed, etc. 

The only downside to this location is parking, as it can be a bit tricky simply because it's in the strip mall area with so many other businesses; during Farmers Market season, it is hell to find parking.

I'd be back if I'm in the area!

Consistently good. This is one of my go-to places. The food has never overly wowed me, but has never let me down.  The chef usually has some type of fish as a special, which is usually very good.  The rack of lamb with pesto risotto is one of my favorite dishes in Nashville.  A good wine list and overall reasonable prices  Small, cozy and dark -- I suggest making a reservation.  Never had a bad experience; the staff is delightful.  One complaint is that they need an improved ventilation system. It often becomes smokey from the kitchen and really bothers my wife's eyes.

Just returned from staying here for a work week.  Clean, well-run hotel at a fairly convenient location.

Very good breakfast buffet and the room was perfect-exactly why I try to stay at HGI anytime I travel for business.    Staff was friendly and check in process was as fast and easy as I can ever remember.

Only cons were water pressure in bathroom sink was non-existent-suppose I could have said something to have it fixed but not exactly a deal breaker, and the noise from nearby US 31.  If I return to the area, would ask for a room not on the west side of the building when booking, that's all.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Place was so ghetto and disgusting!! Would never come here again. I was there because it was closest to the school I was interviewing at. The indian guy gave us attitude and couldn't understand him. He first gave us one double when I booked two double and then charged us additional $60 bucks. He also gave us smoking and gave us attitude for wanting non smoking. So noisy here. Walls are thin. Bathrooms are dirty. I felt dirty sleeping on the beds. The free Breakfast consisted of bread, juice, and cereal. I wouldn't doubt if it was expired.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Had a coupon for a $10 medium pizza, how did my bill come out to be almost $14? Oh well anyway the pizza was a little bit better than average, the toppings tasted pretty commercial. The crust tasted good and the sauce tasted pretty good as well. But the Greeks I remember which I have had a put their fishers location was 10 times better than this one. So they must not be doing something correct here because it's the same place, it shouldn't taste this much different. So in closing if I go back here again it will be to the one up in fishers. 2.5 stars. I wish yelp let you half stars too, my experience was in between two and three stars.

Had a coupon for a $10 medium pizza, how did my bill come out to be almost $14? Oh well anyway the pizza was a little bit better than average, the toppings tasted pretty commercial. The crust tasted good and the sauce tasted pretty good as well. But the Greeks I remember which I have had a put their fishers location was 10 times better than this one. So they must not be doing something correct here because it's the same place, it shouldn't taste this much different. So in closing if I go back here again it will be to the one up in fishers. 2.5 stars. I wish yelp let you half stars too, my experience was in between two and three stars.

The food quality itself is four star, but every time I go here the service is not good. The last time we went to woman who waited on us clearly did not wanna be there, she had a huge huff and puff about my kid trying two different flavors before he picked his out. Then when I went to use the coupon they tried to argue with me and tell me that they gave me bigger scoops than a coupon would allow me, OK? I told you exactly what I wanted, exactly which was printed on my coupon but now I'm not allowed to use it? It's right in my neighborhood and my family loves to go here, so I probably still will continue to frequent it if that means anything.

Lets me start off with that I just moved to New Orleans in the last month. 
My car made it on a trailer safely with no new dents or scratches.  It didn't last 20 minutes in the parking lot.   A large cart with children's "police" labeling was left after banging my car and leaving a fairly large dent on the drivers door.  
Two, yes two, employees saw it happen when I asked them.  They were busy on their cell phones taking their break.  At the time nobody was collecting carts either because of the rain!
I will never go to a Rouses again.

I went to this Sushi place last night and had the all you can eat dinner. The food was exceptional. The rolls were fresh and the fish seemed very fresh. 

The decor is very comfortable, you can either sit at the bar or down at a table. Compared to other sushi places in Reno, probably the most quiet atmosphere. 

The prices for all you can eat were 20.00 a person. It was good value for dollar spent. 

The service was exceptional at this place. They had our drinks out to us very soon. The sushi took a little bit long to get out to our table, but the quality was exceptional.

My family have enjoyed this place for the past few years now even before Katrina. The food is delicious and the staff are friendly. The menu is huge, so you can always find something to eat. I don't recommend going here an hour or so before they close, because the food is awful around that time. I understand people wanna hurry up and leave, but that shouldn't be the case. I just had to point that out in case someone want to visit that place around closing time. That's the only reason I didn't give it 5 star.

Try their ice tea it's great!

This location would have gotten 5 stars but they don't offer the veggie patty, so 4 it is. It's always nice and clean in here and never crowded. I can always get a nice booth to sit in read in during my lunch hour. I pretty much always get the same thing, the veggie delite, because besides breakfast subs it's the only vegetarian option. 

I would recommend going this month because all of the footlongs are only $5 and you can get the $2 add on that includes a drink and chips. Also, the new jalepeno cheddar bread is fire!! Definitely worth a try!

Pretty sure we just found our new local go-to place for Japanese food now that Numa is closed. 

Came here out of curiosity after nabbing a Groupon. The sushi was great quality, service was prompt and friendly, prices were VERY reasonable, and the variety of rolls on the menu is dizzying. 

We got ... a lot of food. Something like 6 rolls, additional sushi a la carte and soup -- and the bill (before groupon) was only $60. You cannot beat that. (That it's a BYOB helps.) 

We'll definitely be back. Likely often.

Long story short:
They were very professional, organized and swift every-time I've requested list of apartments or anything else.
They were on time for every appointment and always pleasant but not pushy.
I was using other agencies at the same time and some of them were rude over the phone and/or would not show up for scheduled appointment.
Guy who was helping me in my search for the apartment was Jon.
I recommend you give them a try and compare them to other agencies in the city (like I did) so you can see for yourself.

I'm adding a star for good customer service. Before I could get a chance to call in regarding the issue in my review, Josh from Sears reached out to me to try and make things right. Long story short, due to them not having the European codes or add ons or whatever (since everything in my car is controlled by some type of computer module), they were unable to straighten the steering wheel, but they did verify the alignment, and accommodate me for the inconvenience. Although they were unable to rectify the issue, I do always appreciate it when a business makes the effort.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Here's the truth. I am not a burger snob. As long as it's a burger made fresh with decent meat, I can be pretty happy. And In N Out makes me veryyy happy. Let's face it...instead of going to McDonalds you can come here and get a meal for the same price but fresh. Never any problems with customer service always good burgers and their fries are crispy. You hear that, Five Guys? CRISPY. Anyways its good on a day when cooking dinner isn't a viable option or you just don't want to spend big bucks at a restaurant.

Doesn't deserve one star. My mcdouble was dry. Ends were dark brown of the patty , the cheese was old, there were no onions on it. Sorry to say although I'm new to the neighborhood I won't be returning.  Why sell food that's not fresh, especially why sell food that's been in the heating lamp for a couple hours or more. That's restaurant suicide these days, yes it's fast food but it still needs to be fresh. I would not recommend this location.  Apparently the owner doesn't care much about his customers.  Look at all these bad reviews.  Obviously something needs to change
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
This location is ok, but I think the West Chester restaurant has better food.
Service was great, but Calamari salad was disappointing. The calamari were rubbery and not hot when the salad came out, and dressing was on the heavy side.
The sausage , peppers and onions sandwich cam on a very good housemade roll.
However , someone put some king of aioli sauce on the bread instead of "gravy" like I 'm used to. The sausage was ok, but lacked taste.  Maybe it's my imagination , but I think the W. Chester location does a better job.

For lunch I thought it was fine.
Hot dog came with either slaw, fries or chips for 9.99. It had good taste , but the dill pickel could have had a little more snap to it.
The mussels are offered in both white or red sauce. It was a good sized portion of mussels that was offered with fries on top or chips. The mussels and the broth was very good, the fires could have used more seasoning.
All in all for lunch I think its fine. The service was friendly and attentive. They have their own lot and it's convienent if your're around K of P mall.

I wanted to try this place and it was a nice day to sit outside, so stopped in and had lunch.
Service was prompt and pleasant. Lunch menu is basically either pasta or pizzas, although I did find a burger on the menu. The burger came out as ordered, bun was fresh, the side of fries were lukewarm and not very well seasoned. The Caesar salad was odd tasting. It had a very heavy taste of mayo in the dressing. They do offer other salads for lunch, but to me their prices are on the high side. 
Good ice tea with a nice flavor to it.
It was ok, but there's better spots around Rittenhouse for the pricing.

The intersection of Whyte and Calgary trail as a few coffee shops nearby; Starbucks, Second Cup and the great Block 1912. I like to go to Second Cup to write things and get some stuff done when I need a change of scenery. That and there are too many distractions at home.

This one is okay. Nice enough but without the homey feeling like the one at Oliver Square. The food and beverage consistency is the same. Really nothing more to say than that since the experience was merely okay. Nothing great, nothing bad; just run of the mill.

I had a date nite with my girlfriend from collage. 
She said the roll is very good, but I am more sashimi lover.
She had roll with spicy sauce and shrimp tempura roll, I didn't take a bite, but looked like pretty decent. 
I had chirasi bowl served with miso soup and salad on the side. Its really hard to find a fine chirashi don around center city area; I always go to NY just to have chirasi don.
I could say that fat salmon is pretty good for their chirasi, and wish that they could cook the tamago little sweet.. 

The highlight of the meal was tempura ice cream!!! Love it :)

We came here on a Thursday evening. Didn't see security and the patrons were your average take out people. This was my first time at this location although I've been attending the one on Upper State for over two decades.

Our food had special orders (no tomatoes for example). It was ready quickly and exactly like we ordered. I don't recommend the new ranch bacon fries however. It's very short on the dressing.

Another plus: they have cherry Coke on tap. It's one of the few places that has this, and drinking it from a can just doesn't do it. 

I will be returning here for sure.

Food is very good. Very fresh. Plates arrive with the most beautiful presentation, very artistic, done with great care.
 
Always gone during the day and it wasn't very busy. Was seated right away.

The low rate is based on the service. It wasn't terrible, it was just completely without polish or refinements. Didn't match the elegant food at all. Dragging feet, snappy replies, not very attentive for an empty restaurant, plates kinda slammed on the table. Teaching and training some basic etiquette in service is greatly needed.

Elegant food with fast food service...

My cousins and I went to Nashville for a bachelorette and we wanted to have a fancy farewell dinner where we could dress up and have wine and a nice fancy meal. This place did not disappoint! It was a group of 11 ladies and we had out own private room which was perfect! 

The drinks were yummy, everyone had different ones but I had one called the Lady Gaga I believe and it was very good. All of the ladies complemented me for picking a good place because they all loved the food. I can vouch for the spaghetti and the pizzas. Go there for a fancier type of meal, you won't be disappointed!

This place is good - just not knock your socks off good - or the kind of good where you dream about something on the menu. Their outdoor patio, though, is reason enough to go and celebrate a beautiful day. I ordered the ooey-gooey sandwich (gouda, goat cheese, spinach, and bacon). Nothing named "ooey-gooey" can be good for you - but you can bet that it will be tasty and this held true. I liked that you can opt for field greens instead of french fries. It seems to be a popular place among the IUPUI and hospital campus crowd. I'm also glad to see that it brings people down to the canal.

Great food? No. Good food in a hurry? Depends on what you order on the menu. I like that they will actually make something extra garlic or extra spicy, rather than giving lip service. It is the best take out Chinese in Bellevue, although that is not saying a lot.

Personally, I like their szechuan beef and garlic chicken combos. Both come with an eggroll and pork fried rice. And both are around $7 - $8 (in 2014), which is reasonable.

And to Scott G (yes, I know him), this is hole in the wall take out Chinese. :-)

Goodyear has always done a great job for me and believe me they've had my older car many times over the past 10 years. Whenever I need major car repair or just maintenance, I know I can trust my car to these mechanics. Their terrific letting me know what has to be taken care immediately versus something I can wait a few weeks to correct. They work as quickly as possible and usually turn my car around in a day or two, if parts are available, for major issues. My husband's truck was just there today and again, we were very happy with the service.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Old Point Tavern has the best patio in downtown for the past 30 yrs., in my opinion, to watch the daily hustle & bustle and I love people watching here. Of course the experience is heightened by decent pub food and drinks. The hot dogs, chili, nachos and several sandwiches continue to be staples along with a few healthier options incorporated over the years.

The bar selection has grown and kept pace with the demands of its clientele. Old Point appears to continue on focusing on what the customer wants while maintaining the successful menu items.

We have a history of good experiences at this location. We do mostly on-line ordering with in store pickup. I use their delivery service more in the winter time. The staff is always friendly to us and we've only had one incorrect order which they corrected quickly. The pizzas are hot, not overcooked or dried out. The brownies is one of our favorite side orders along with the wings.

Papa John's has great coupons and specials with some revolving around the Pacers  and other teams. We especially try to take advantage of the 50% off when they hit our emails.

Overall, we're very happy with this location and our orders.

We (party of 14) went to Anthony's for lunch on Sunday. We were pleasantly surprised.  The wait staff is a little shorthanded, but she did a great job.  The food was very good--we were all very happy with it.  We had dishes ranging from Veal Parmesan, to Chicken Marsala to Lasagna and everyone was pleased.

I think the pizza is a little bland--for my tastes.  It is good and not too greasy, so I like that, but they could put some flavor in their sauce or dough.  

I would recommend you try it out.  We hope it stays around, but for some reason Italian restaurants here in Lithia haven't discovered their "niche" yet.

The salad is a meal in itself; simple lettuce, tomato, cured olives and grated parm cheese with a vinaigrette dressing and a thin veal cutlet that covers the other half of a dinner plate. All fresh and tasty. Along with the bread and fresh marinara sauce, little room is left for an entree but do it anyway. Light fresh sauces and perfectly done pasta make each dish a pleasure. Small menu but well done overall. I'll be back as often as I'm looking for a great meal at a fabulous price. The Frank Sinatra music in the background made the mood mellow.

Cansecos on Esplanade is one more reason to love my neighborhood. The staff is super nice, and for a little corner mini-market, the selection is top notch. The prices are a little high for some stuff, yeah, but if you watch the specials, you can get some stuff cheaper here than in Rouses. It ain't Walmart, dats-fer-shur, but the quality and sophistication here is high, and the staff and the management are tippy top. Plus, they have one of the best lunch specials in Mid-City. I should keep it a secret, but there you go. I grab lunch there at least twice a week.

I prefer this establishment because this one is a lot more organized and their Shelves are always stocked. Their check out lines are not as long asyhe  Winn Dixie close to Louisa St right before you get to the Danzinger Bridge.  This place just looks like hou will find what you need.  Also please be mindful that Wi nn Dixie is kind of pricey so definitely grab you a wonn Dixie card and get your sales or save on gas at participating Shell Gas Stations (not every Shell does the winn Dixie rewards so just asks).

i enjoys the hand rolls here whenever i come here to eat. i came and ate here two years ago and they really gave me a good deal for like 32 rolls. i remember the snow-crab rolls being all delicious, and when ate here a couple of days ago they were the same fresh and delicious tasting rolls i remembered.  I love the atmosphere because it's mostly quiet and warm. My waiter made sure my glass stayed full and i stayed satisfied, so he deserved a great tip.i had ordered the snow crab roll and their crunchy roll and i was very satisfied. Great place!!

I always go through drive thru cause it's convenient to grab and go before work. Based on drive thru experience ONLY! Its ok. I love the frozen coffees and flavor variety.   Not a bad wait time either for drive thru so thats cool. I have had a rude drive thru worker that have made feel blah and I'll tell myself I'm done with them, but I'll come back and get an awesome drive thru worker! That makes me feel like I gotta ti p big!. Its hit and miss with customer service so that's why I give the three star instead of four. Overall pretty good coffees hot and or cold, and I really enjoyed my creme bruele frozen coffee .

Took out dinner yesterday, the seafood delight. Taste is good.  Menu says scallop, lobster tail, shrimp, but disappointed that I didn't see any shrimp.   Lots of vegetables but not much seafood.
Oct 2015 update:  Agree with Brian M there are no really good Chinese restaurants in Phoenixville / Kimberton.  Shrimp egg foo young, chicken with vegetables, egg drop soup, seafood delight all just okay; I like their white rice (I'm Chinese).  Price to value just okay.  People there are meh, busy not at all friendly.

Went for a mid-week lunch with my gf.  Easy to find in the middle of a mall, but was surprised it was a grocery store.  Restaurant was in the back, half dozen tables, with Univision on a large flat-screen.  Open kitchen, 2-preparers, giving you a home-cooked feel; people are nice.  Lots of menu choices, many looked promising.  Mostly hispanic customers, also promising.

However, the food was mostly disappointing.  I had the Enchiladas with mole (chicken was tough), tortillas tasted flat, good refried beans.  My gf had the huarachi, looked good, but it was not very tasty.  Strawberry shake was good.  $23 total.  Wouldn't go back.

A new favorite. 

I'm always looking for a new lunch spot and Joe Natural's has become my new favorite. With options for half-sizes and a reasonably priced menu Joe Natural's is now my go-to. I recommend the Beth's Favorite, a roasted turkey sandwich with cranberry sauce & brie. Opt for the half-and-half and get the Mediterranean Salad with hummus, red quinoa, marinated artichoke hearts, lolives, mixed greens. 

Don't forget to grab a gluten-free chocolate chip cookie, the best cookie I've had in Nashville. The best part was the speed of the service. They had our food ready before we had a chance to sit down. 

Excellent all around.

Gratefully this place has gone out of business and is CLOSED.  My only concern is for the fate of that sushi chef's rough trade assistant.  What piece of raw fish will his filthy finger nails come into contact with next?  Will this unfortunate young Asian hottie be left to wander the streets of Baja Arizona in search of fresh sea food?  Will he be forced to move from massaging mackerel to fondling father-figures in Old Pueblo's next M2M massage parlor?  Will he find a "girlfriend"  from his homeland to administer the mani-pedi that he so deserves?

4 tacos for $4 .. 2 beef crunchy, 2 chicken soft.  great value .. plus a big side of chips and salsa while u wait . i added a side of guacamole and sour cream b/c that's how i roll .  Awesome deal .. keep in mind, Taco Bell charges $1.19 for a crunchy beef taco half this weight made from who knows what .. and $1.79 for a chicken taco that's even smaller ..  anytime us see Yelp reviews that are all 5 star and 1 star u know it's somewhere in the middle ..for me,  food 3 star (good) , service 4 star, value 5 star .  Avg rating 4 star

Good place to get your fix for some good beer, on draft and bottled.  You can buy beer to go in bottles as well and you get a discount for taking it with you.  

The actual space looks like your typical chain, so -.5 stars for that (I would prefer a more unique atmosphere) and another -.5 stars for the lack of food options, you can bring your own food or order from Moe's or Pizza Suprema II and they will deliver to you.  I would prefer some sort of bar bites, but I realize that would require more work on their end and obviously they aren't into that.

The chinese food here is really good.  You used to get a bit more and it always seems like when I order a special they are out of something related to it.  Last time Betty got here around 6:30 and they were out of green beans for their XO special.  Wha?!  Oh well.  Their S&P (insert food item here) is great and you have to love the fact that it is BYOB.  So bring the cooler!  Betty always gets the spicy seafood and tofu hot pot.  Last time it wasn't very spicy though.  Still one of the better places to enjoy some chinese in the bay area.  Just don't come for an upscale atmosphere, go to their bistro for that.

Oh my.  If I wanted to waste hours of my life away I could've come up with many better venues, Brass Tap, Cigar City, etc.  Visionworks...not so much.  I came here in support of Betty and her blindness, as she was filling her eye glass prescription.  After perusing the selection which was OK, we sit down to go over the insurance details, figure out her contact lens situation and all that really fun stuff.  

Long story short the girl who helped us did not really know what she was doing when calling the insurance company or even how to bring things up on the computer to get things through.  It was absolutely painstaking!  Go elsewhere.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
This is a nice place to go for the ambiance. The patio is nice, the interior is well done, and the vibe of the place is great. The service was average, and the food is average to below-average. I had the Cuban, which was quite bland. Wife had the chicken nachos, they were ok. Nothing to write home about. We wanted to try some ice cream, but the gentleman serving the ice cream was unpleasant, so we ended up skipping. I guess my hair was not long enough for him or something. 

In summary, we might come back for a dessert or some coffee. We won't be back for a meal. Food was average at best, and service was close to the same.

Really liked this place. A cozy little place for dinner. We tried the tacos (fish and pork, I think) and the hamburger. They were delicious!!! We'd been recommended both and couldn't choose so we did both and split it. Great choice. The hamburger was mouth watering. The tacos were very tasty - I particularly likes the fish tacos. 

Great service and nice drink selection. I'd never been to Recess next door before, but this appears to be is smaller, more casual counterpart. Nice, relaxed place - small, but we had no trouble finding a seat. Would go back.

A few problems to begin with; the price is outrageous, prepare to spend hundreds if you got a party of 4 or more.  The waiter is very unfriendly, most of the times anyways.  There isn't enough waiters.

Why did I give it a 4 star then?  The food is just THAT GOOD!  This restaurant serves one of the best Chinese foods I've ever eaten.  If you are in the area, don't miss out, you have to try this place.  

On a positive note, the restaurant is huge, you won't feel cramped up like you would eating in China town.  They are also very generous with their portions.

I always trust Mike's with my car. My car is 12 years old, but she shines like new. Mike's recently rolled out inexpensive monthly unlimited options, and I jumped right on that! I get the Your Choice with Clear Coat and Wheel Bright. I usually have to wipe extra water off my car and between the seams, but I like to do a little bit myself. I am never disappointed. 

This location is pretty good. Compared to others around town there isn't as much space outside to detail, so if it is busy you might just have to wash and go. The staff are always friendly, and they seem like mostly UIndy students. Top notch scores for the wash in this location.

This place was pretty good. I went on Saturday for lunch/brunch with my fiance and parents. I got the Salmon Toast & Arnold Palmer. I loved that the toast was served on a thick slice of bread. I tried some of my mom's breakfast potatoes which were seasoned very well. They have an assortment of creative lattes such as a cookie dough latte which I would want to try next time. The inside of the restaurant was adorable as well. My only small issue with this place is that they said that there was only outdoor seating available when I saw several inside spots. Maybe those spots were reserved for people with reservations.

I came here to see a metal band i had never heard of before. What i got i was more than pleased with. The staff here was amaze ball friendly and the bands were top notch. Its a small cozy venue but it is very well done. I have never been here before but most definitely will be back because of the people and the feel of the place. I havent been in a place where I can listen to live music thats local and global at the same time yet inexpensive and friendly. I didnt know what to expect because of the mixed reviews on here but in all honesty i have nothing bad to say here. It was most definitely a pleasant suprise for me

Always loving coming home and eating at the Tavern.  Not the hippest place but so homey and inviting. You get a very mixed crowd form the great-grandparents to their grandchildren.  Couples and families fill the room.   There is something on the menu for everyone.  The starched white table cloths  make the dinning there a treat.   Our favorites are the soups, burgers, turkey club, flounder florentine, veal parmigiana, Greek salad   and don't miss the mussels. Always best to make a reservation but walk ins are always welcomed.

If you can avoid this Marsh, please do.  They do have an alright selection, but the staff make you feel like the last person in the world they should have to talk to.  When I asked the guy at the deli if the potato salad was $2.49/pound because I couldn't see the sign, he said "probably."  I asked for a pound; he gave me 1.2, didn't ask if I cared if it was over, didn't say thanks, nothing.  I was very pleasant, and I hate when, as the customer, I try harder to make it a pleasant experience.  The liquor prices are also outrageous for a grocery store.

I have gone to this Marsh 3 times.  Today was the last.

The dryer at the house went out, so it's just easier to come do all the laundry. Tried finding a place that wasn't so crowded and stumbled across this place. It's the new way of washing I guess you could say. You down load the app, enter the washer or dryer # and it charges to your credit card. No need for quarters. The big washers you can wash 4lbs for $5. The dryers are only $1.50 for 40 mins. It's nice and clean. They have charging stations for your phones, and free WiFi. They have a drop off to have your clothes done for you, just not sure how much that is.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: I have tried this carwash a couple times and I just can't write too much that is good. The first time I came here the carwash put soap on my car, but did not rinse it. I came back again today and paid for the $15 option. I know it's pretty price for an automatic carwash, but thought it was wash pretty good. Well it didn't. I could have gone to one of the $5 automatic carwash and had a much better job. I actually have gone to the $5 ones and had a better job. The only good thing I can say is the vacuums are really good. And they have a floor mat cleaner. Other than that, I say go to a cheaper automatic carwash. This one is not the place

Personally I think all Reno sushi is more or less identical.  I can't imagine their sources for their ingredients aren't exactly the same place, city wide.  Which is to say that it's all decent, but makes it hard for any of them to be exceptional.

But given all that, it seems like there are one or two places that try and pile the rice onto your rolls and nigiris in order to minimize costs.  Sakana is not one of these places.  Sakana is a good place.  Good food, good employees, good service, good apps, etc, etc.

I've been going to Nail Expo for some time now.  It's just down the street from my parent's house, so its a great place for my sisters and I to go.  The staff is all very friendly and I rarely have to wait for service, even without a reservation.  I just went yesterday and found out they had moved a few doors down from their prior location.  Since they moved, they have gotten what appears to be all new pedicure chairs and the place has a great, clean environment!  Plus, they have Shellac / gel manicures.  I was in and out in about 30 minutes yesterday for a Shellac manicure and my nails look amazing!

The service was very good.  Unfortunately, I didn't enjoy one dish.  The broccoli rabe was far too bitter for my liking.  I know broccoli rabe is bitter by nature, but it was pungent.  The bruschetta was so oily. The spaghetti and meatballs were cooked wonderfully, but had an extremely surprising, and unwelcoming smokey flavor.  This restaurant could be pretty great, with the romantic ambiance....However, the food and drinks seem to be trying way too hard to be different.  Everything was VERY fragrant and SALTY.  I don't get the amazing reviews?  I suppose the food and drink could just not be my taste?

Great customer service! They were so helpful and kind! Greeted us with a smile and were very helpful with our flat tire and oil change! They were able to service my car in a very timely manner with a great attitude! The service work was done without adding any extra expenses or inflation of cost. They even gave me a discounted rate better than the coupon I was using. The only issue I found was finding the location with my gps. Its off of Doyle rd and Lancaster Ave. the sign on Lancaster is too small. Otherwise I would give it 5 stars!  It is a gem of a find! They are so helpful!! Go see Anthony! He's great!
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Been wanting to try this place and finally did. We were the only people in there. The decor was a bit too fancy and wanna be pretentious, but who cares. The real issue with my place is the yogurt. It's very similar to the Chill Yogurt across the street. Watery with a powdery taste. The toppings, like across the street, are off-brand candies. No real Reese's or anything you'd expect. I guess I'm spoiled with Sweet Cece's, but the yogurt is not great quality. I wish them well, but I don't see them lasting here.

This is one of my favorite car washes. It's always open even when it's freezing out. Usually there is an attendant on duty if you have any issues. One time the bay with brushes ripped off my back windshield wiper, so the owner gave me a bunch of free car washes. FYI- if you go thru the one with brushes, tape your back window wiper!
I prefer the brush free one, but a lot of the times the line is long. There are several do-it-yourself bays and best part, vacuuming is free for the 2 drive-thru bays. So for $5 you can get a decent car wash and free vacuum.

First time back since the debacle. And i was a Jeni's loyalist prior. No more buckeye state, akinosie chocolate and biscuits and jam. Seriously!?! Those were the best flavors! I opted for brown butter almond brittle and basic milk chocolate. It was not good. Couldn't even finish it. My husband and I couldn't quite put our finger on it, but the consistency has changed considerably, and I don't mean in a good way. The only thing I enjoyed was the waffle cone fortune cookie. Line not as long as 12south, but I don't foresee coming back voluntarily, and that's a shame. If it ain't broke...

It's pretty rare that I give a place like this 5 stars... but I find it hard to find fault with Phil's.  The service is always good, the most relevant sports game is almost always on, and best of all the food is always top notch.  They have TONS of choices on the menu, and although I haven't gotten past their burger cuz I love it so much, I have never seen anyone complain about the food.  The portions are so satisfyingly large, I make it a point to plan my Phil's run ahead of time, and not to eat anything else that day.  If I time it right, it fills me up for the entire day.

Go check out Phil's.  I assure you, you will not be disappointed!

Billing, billing, billing. The place almost operates like a Payday loan office or a Ponzi scheme. I accidentally let my credit card on file with them expire, and they charged over $30 in finance charges (note that this was IMMEDIATELY after the due date for monthly membership). It is also impossible to cancel, and you have to provide a WRITTEN NOTICE 60 DAYS IN ADVANCE just to cancel ANNUAL AUTO RENEW. Really terrible corporate monster, avoid like the plague.

The gym itself is OK, but very few classes and no pool.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: It's a little surprising to me that this place is such a dump.  Crown moulding rotting in the bathroom from moisture, tile that looks like a vagrant laid it, AC is marginal even in October, Restroom door has holes in it.   I've never seen a commercial building with this poor construction outside of Mexico.  6am is too early for breakfast?  Avoid this place.  The Comfort Inn in Dickson last weekend was far nicer and cost less than half as much as this Holiday Inn Express.  A dump for $200 a night.  Seriously?
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Solid 3.5 stars but due to extremely slow and inattentive service, I went with 3. This place always seems to be busy and they consistently have great food so I understand why. We typically try to sit at the bar & that usually equates to good/decent service. They are one of the few places in St. Louis that offer grilled artichokes and they are my favorite. One of the main reasons we go! They also have delicious sushi and their burgers and French dip sandwich are always tasty. I would recommend sitting at the bar, if possible, as our experiences in the dining room have never been that great.

This is a traditional old-school Italian restaurant. They offer some Italian staples--arancini, speidini, pastas and what not. I tried the fresh fish of the day--which they get in that day and offer different preparations. The tuna was okay, a little over cooked but good. They had a delicious artichoke and shrimp appetizer with a creamy spinach sauce over it and it was sooooo good. Bartender makes strong drinks and they have some affordable Italian wines on their menu. Cute little space that seems to have a strong regular following. Service was also excellent. Not my favorite Italian place here but definitely good!

Great lunch spot. They offer a nice special where you can choose 2 rolls and either a Miso soup or house salad for $10. Not a bad deal! Popping in for lunch at noon on a Thursday, most tables were full. Lucked out and got a 2-top in the back by the windows. Our waitress was attentive, kept our iced tea full, and delivered our check promptly. I am not a raw sushi kind of lady so I went with the simple crunchy and shrimp tempura rolls. Both done well. The ginger dressing on that salad, man I think I would dip anything in that stuff, so tasty! Overall, a smallish restaurant on the edge of the CBD one block off Canal Street that is worth visiting.

The quality of the main restaurant menu has declined since chef  Brown has left. Today with great anticipation I ordered a Cobb salad thinking that I would get 5 star quality service however much to my dissappointment I had a salad that was  of common quality.  The bacon bits were not homemade and the cubed chicken tasted like it had been frozen and thawed.....Mr. Brown I definitely miss you quality cuisine Your replacement is not  as great as you were as a chef.

I used to go and have the Ahi Tuna dish, however this is no longer part of the menu. I am greatly sad that this change was made.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I do NOT recommend this location ever. Regardless how many cars are in the drive thru (1-10) it will always take FOREVER to get anything. I could've ordered a drink and it would've taken 20 minutes. Since I live close, I see cars consistently waiting in the drive thru, not to mention there is limited parking and no room for more than 10 cars to be waiting as it backs onto Keystone. I've seen fights and customers/employees yelling at each other, random people parking in places they shouldn't park. This whole establishment is awful. Worth it to drive to another Wendy's, out of the way, to get the same food.

I can't believe that I've never reviewed Nicey! I love this place so much! The amount of flavors is neverending. I get so overwhelmed when I'm in here because I legitimately want to get about 12 popsicles at once. The staff is always friendly and enthusiastic and they store is adorable. They offer chocolate dipping for an extra charge if you're trying to "treat yourself"! I'm more partial to the fruitier options because they are made fresh and local!
