I showed her a few pictures of styles that I liked, and let her do her thing. She rocked it! My hair looked great(as did all the other girls whose hair she did), and I got tons of compliments. If I'm ever in STL area needing any hair styling, makeup, etc. I will be looking her up again!

This Holiday Inn Express is tucked away off of Bruce B Downs. Stayed here April 9th in one of the suites. 

The hotel was nice and clean. Then we got to our room. The door would not close properly. They couldn't do anything about it at 9 pm at night. They didn't seem to worried about it since it was able to lock. It wasn't secured though like a normal door. 

The air conditioner made an awful rattling noise. I had to get up in the middle of the night a couple of times to kick it to shut it up. 

Wouldn't stay here again. Figured it was too good to be true with 5 stars. At least my kids enjoyed the pool.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The brilliant staff ended up giving me someone else's takeout order the other night. Of which, I couldn't eat. I called and they told me they would give me credit for the chicken quesadilla. I went in today and collected and asked for a side of rice and beans for the inconvenience their fine restaurant had cost me. She refused.

I told her I would never eat there again if she didn't. She refused. Pretty stupid losing business like that. The food is largely mediocre anyway, and only convenient if you happen to be shopping at Vons.

Awfully run restaurant and staff. Be advised.

Ho Wah? Oh no! My wife and I tried this place the other night and it was quite possibly the worst Chinese food I've ever eaten with terrible service to boot. Our crab rangoon appetizer arrived after the entrees, and they were tiny, overfried and tasted more like bad fish and rancid cream cheese than of crab or even imitation crab meat. Our food in the dining room was served on paper plates... to go boxes were Styrofoam that broke in half once you folded the lid. After this experience and others, I can say there is no good Chinese food in B-burg. Just a gross experience all around.

I tried it this morning and will absolutely never go back.

I get better service from the kiosk at Target in West Clay. I was coming to work from a different direction this morning and not only did they not care when I told them their Thanksgiving blend tasted horrible, but the cashier completely drained my Starbucks card and screwed up my rewards when I was trying to buy my coffee with a card for my wife.

The barista was rude. Not my fault the place is so loud and you can't hear well. I've only recently gotten into the Starbucks experience, but I know it's not supposed to be this.

I've only recently gotten into Starbucks, and while I have a favorite location to go to, it's near work and I thought I would try this location near my home so I could enjoy my drink during my commute instead.

For this location, they never have skim milk out and the baristas fill the coffee to the top. I have a very simple brewed coffee order and just ask for a little room to add my milk, and they can't seem to comply.

There are better locations on the west side than this one (Avon, Brownsburg). This one is usually not busy in the morning, which probably should have been a tip-off.

Compared to my usual sushi spots in the city, Zama is definitely trendy and the menu options/prices reflect that. My favorites were the Wasabi Tuna roll and Japanese 75 martini. The roll was super tasty, but not as spicy as I expected from something with wasabi in its name. 

I'd been here for lunch in the past, but this was a first for dinner. Their specialty rolls all sounded good, but I'm not sure they were worth the higher prices when there are so many other awesome sushi places in the area. You're paying for the atmosphere here which was fine for our girls night out.

Great place!    Fausto's Bistro is an Italian restaurant that serves authentic Italian food.    

I ordered the Friday lunch special:  Seafood Pasta.  It had a large amount of crawfish tails, shrimp, a few oysters and 4 crab claws.  The cream sauce was light and full of flavor.  Yum!  I ate it all!  My BFF ordered a meatball poboy that was delicious.  He inhaled it!    

We both ordered a small cesar salad that was so-so . . . would try another salad next time.     

The staff was very friendly.

We will certainly return!

We come to this Starbucks once or twice a month. It's a matter of convienence vs preference. The service is so hit or miss, mostly miss. Today, my drink was made the wrong size and the barista huffed at me and was snarly about remaking it. I've found most of the baristas are lackluster about customer service and much more interested in chatting with each other or friends.  This location is frequently crowded with students studying or working.  The drive through tends to move fast and is usually pretty busy. The drinks and food is up to the normal Starbucks quality

Sake Sushi is such a gem! The service is unbeatable and we tend to have the same incredibly happy and fun lady serve us each time we go. She makes the experience even more pleasant! The sushi here is so, so good! It's really phenomenal and makes me question why I haven't been going here for years. My favorites are the Crunch roll and the Osaki roll for sure! I have also had the volcano roll, which is also yummy as well as the Red Dragon roll. You truly can't go wrong! Great service, amazing sushi at great prices, and a nice atmosphere!

Location.  Location.  Location.  The hotel is on Bourbon Street, on the calm side of Canal.  You can literally stumble back to your room, it's a straight shot.  We had our adult children with us & I felt comfortable with them being out late.  The hotel lobby & elevator are secure (you must use a key to get in) and it was VERY quiet at night.  Breakfast is decent for a complimentary deal & the rates were extremely reasonable.  Definitely stay there again.  Oh, and it's not on a list of haunted hotels so that was a bonus for me!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Here on the SE side of Indy, we now have two real choices for donuts. The city standard of Longs and now Jack's. 

Jack's does a great job of making their donuts. They are very large and very good. I have noticed that they have a lack of variety like Longs and almost always are out of chocolate covered donuts. My favorite one that they make is the the apple fritter. 

The have ultra fresh donuts but my main issue (not complaint) is a variety of everything.

And they accept credit cards. Long's won't and that works for them, but on some days, you don't have cash!

I tried China Moon for the first time last night and they did a great job. First of all, I placed my order online and my food was ready when I went to pick it up about 25 minutes later.  It was still nice and warm.  The staff was very friendly and likeable.  I had Kung Pao Chicken, Wonton Soup, Fried Rice, and Wontons and all the food was very good.  I was impressed that the Kung Pao Chicken was actually spicier than I expected. I love spicy food but most places don't make the food spicy and hot enough for me.  When I want Chinese take in the future, I'm going to China Moon.

This is currently the best auto repair shop for air-cooled Volkswagens in Tucson. Bob has years of experience and is one of the few people left in the state of Arizona who will still take the time to rebuild your engine - moreover, he does it with care, replacing every gasket with German parts wherever possible. He'll also do custom work and is skilled at tricking out your VW to make it more comfortable and a smoother ride. He's trustworthy and good at diagnostics, and everyone in town has a nice word to say about him.

This neighborhood Italian grub and bar hosts a nice set up inside. I would say they're probably over priced for a small local nearby place, and personally I prefer the food at Fratelli's, BUT this place is close, convenient, and what really makes it is a dark, romantic interior, whereas compared to Fratelli's nearby you are eating on what may be a plastic checkerboard table cloth concealing a picnic table underneath. I've never had a bad experience, and it's a nice go-to spot if a craving for Italian staples happens to hit out of nowhere.

I wasn't sure what to expect with the new ownership taking over and practically razing the interior of an old favorite spot, but I think we're gonna be ok. We've lost the pool table, but we've got dollar beer. We've lost some regulars after the initial closing, but we've got flame-licked burgers. The trade-offs at this place are alright with me. On every other Thursday they offer bike-night Jack burgers for 5 buckaroos which  pretty much outshine most burgers in the area by simply arranging really fresh ingredients with spot on cooking technique. Still like the place, hope it holds up!

This place is ok in a pinch. Why only in a pinch? Well, with Trader Joes and Aldi springing up everywhere it's easy to see that even Hannaford store brand stuff isn't the right price, or any better quality than the cheap stuff. Why such a disconnect? Why is it so difficult to compete? Well one tip for this place, is that they hide large sale bins in the back near the restrooms if you need a brief escape from the small, $8.00 bags of trail mix. There are a few finds in there, sometimes utensils, sometimes soups, sometimes matzo ball mix. Is it worth having to shop in a bathroom hallway? Probably not.

Had a late family lunch today. Party of 4. Chicken tortilla soup was delicious,  as usual. Service was quick and friendly. My entree, steak and fries, not so much. Been coming here for 3 years, today was my first disappointment.  I ordered my ribeye medium. It came out with its customary fries and salad. Steak seemed alittle cold to me. After eating a few bites, I saw that the steak was raw. Not just rare, but literally uncooked. Server didn't come around for awhile. Bu the time he did, I wasn't hungry anymore and just returned the meal.

If you're craving Italian this is an excellent option. We opted to order via DoorDash and the food arrived so fresh and hot.

Would definitely recommend the bruschetta. For take out they provide the tomato and onion topping on the side, so your bread is not soggy. The bread is a focaccia like pizza crust drizzled with a delicious balsamic. 10/10 would recommend.

Maybe pass on the mozzarella sticks, as they don't hold up on delivery. I'm sure they taste great fresh though. 

The Alfredo with shrimp is excellent as well. Very flavorful and doesn't seem too heavy like most alfredos. 

Highly recommend if your in an Italian mood.

New to Greenwood, HotBox Pizza is what you expect from a pizza place 
   
They feature some unique pizza combinations, with plenty of options for toppings. HotBox has a great online ordering system for those too lazy to pick up the phone. Their delivery time has been very reasonable and within 30 minutes almost every time. Their prices are comparable to other pizza places, although when customizing your pie it may get a bit pricey. 

There's not much to say about HotBox, for those looking for reliable pizza, this is the place for you. The pizza is pretty good, although it may not be as "unique" as other pizza places in town.

I was eager to try Sam's sushi after reading the reviews and he did not disappoint, but his food did. He was ornery and kicked out a few kids who came into the restaurant being somewhat loud and trying to order something not on the menu. He proceeded to tell them to get out and locked the door behind them. And it was 3 o'clock in the afternoon.

I can appreciate ornery individuals, but his sushi was mediocre at best. The sushi had a tremendous amount of mayonnaise all throughout whatever roll we ordered. The taste was overpowering. But you get what you pay for...

I used to come here a lot before I stopped eating cheese and dairy. Now I go and get pasta and bring my own vegan cheese. It's a fun place to dine at. It isn't uncommon to see celebrities, if you're into that sort of thing. The outside dining area is great and the inside, sorta romantic. Decent but sometimes moody service, but overall a good experience. Their thin crust pizzas are incredibly tasty. This place can get pricy in a hurry ... especially their fresh fish dishes and specials. In spite of the fact that there are three great Italian eateries at that particular intersection, Via Vai is my favorite all around.

To be honest, I'm not a real big fan of Bourbon Street, so I was quite pleased to find this place on the corner without having to walk down Bourbon. 

From Jackson Square just head north on Toulouse street. You can't miss the bar on your right side at the corner of Bourbon. 

The drink is quite interesting. Very sweet, very green, and pretty high alcohol content. Not sure I would have wanted another. Perhaps if it was 95 and sunny, but at a comfortable 80 & in the shade, one was just fine. 

Definitely a must stop when in town though.

Great atmosphere and a buzzing South Philly location, but to me this is middle of the road Mexican, made by Gringos for Gringos. It just lacks that south of the border authentic flair, that could take it to greater heights. 

The fresh made chunky guac and house made tortilla chips were the highlight of the meal; don't order here without it. To drink, the coconut mojito should be your goto cocktail, refreshing and pairing perfectly with the Mexican fare in front of you.

This place is a great night out, but food wise it's clear this ain't quite Cali and for darn sure not quite Mexico. 

Más o menos

-SZ

I've been coming to Sonobana for years (when it used to be called Benkay).  They have the best Japanese food in Nashville, by far!  The servers are generally nice and attentive.  It's a long wait for the sushi bar, but it's worth it.  They have really yummy ginger salad dressing that they also sell in the small grocery store next door.  The free green tea is also an excellent addition to your meal.  Honestly, because of the long wait for food, I usually get take out.  

Must try: lunch special - "Special Box" assorted sashimi over rice.  It's a great deal and a lot of food!

Vegetarian eats: Vegetable Roll #2

First time here with my best bro of 30 years. First off we sat at the bar to watch the chefs at work. They were lots of fun and lively. Needless to say we were a hand full. Despite that they were great. We try about everything and they even created a few special hot rolls for us not on the menu. They were great hosts including the manager. Trust me we were a handful. Regardless they were gracious and loads of fun. After about 3 bottles of saki and a few other drinks we departed. The food was excellent and the service was excellent as well. The prices were reasonable and the chefs were very creative. You cannot go wrong if you like sushi!

Eaten here quite a few times in the past year, and every experience has always been good.

Service is fairly quick, and servers are always polite.  Food has always been a good value.  Nothing special about the place - it's a very basic Mexican restaurant.  Happy hour drink specials are pretty great - $1 drafts and $2.50 margaritas!  Chips and salsa are always great, and food tastes fresh!

It's never very busy, and it's a reliable place to always get a good inexpensive meal.

Parking is very easy, though turning left out of the parking lot onto Lebanon Pike can be a pain due to the amount of traffic in the area.

I don't really know what to say about this place.  My dogs like coming here.  The staff is always friendly.  The vets are knowledgeable. The pet plan is great deal, too.  The problem is that I always feel like they are trying to up charge us. I am not sure I truly trust the vets, and I generally end up calling my sister in law (who is also a vet, though out of town) for a second opinion.  The head vet is almost always willing to help answer questions and put us at ease too.  We've been bringing our dogs here for several years, and have not had any major problems.  They are happy and healthy.   I'm just still unsure.

Probably my favorite sushi in uptown. I've eaten at 95% of the places in the area and this is where I always prefer to go. (Sushi Brothers and Kyoto are alios pretty good but for different reasons each). Hana is always fresh and consistently delicious. I adore their mango salmon and no-name rolls. If you like crabstick, the Hana special roll is a killer. I especially like places that start you off with the noodle salad and the actually MAKE their miso soup instead of using instant. The service is always prompt, water glasses always full, excellent to-go packaging. I'm a fan!

This store is not one of my favorite ABCs.  I found the layout to be odd, and their selection seemed surprisingly limited.  I was looking for vanilla vodka, which just about every vodka company makes, and could only find Absolut Vanilia.  I must have gone back and forth in the vodka area 4 or 5 times looking for any other brand.  And you would think a worker in the store might have been like, 'hey, can we help you find something?', but no, nobody cared. 

So - this store is good for basics, but not the interesting or unusual.

Party atmosphere?  Not at all.  Just a very basic liquor store, that will usually have exactly what you need as long as you are not looking for fancy.  They had probably 10 -15 different flavors of vodka, including both the Stolichnaya (Stoly) Iced Cake and Stoly Vanilla I was looking for.

It is an older building, worn down inside, but still clean.  ID is asked for if you use a credit card, and they also charge a small fee if you pay with credit card or debit card.  The parking lot is in front of the store, but it can be a little tricky to get out of, even with the traffic light at the entrance.  I would recommend going during daylight hours.

In the 6 months since I first reviewed The Beverage House, Billy has perfected his business into a craft beer mecca. He now has over 300 craft beers in his store too many to mention here in this review so, I have added his website so you can check them all out in one spot. www.thebeveragehouse.net

They still have a large selection of wines from around the world too.

Check out his prices for those who are looking for good prices on tobacco products also.

Yes, 5 stars for The Beverage House. It's as good as it gets!

Who knew? Right here in Largo there is a gem of a store selling beer and wine. 

The Beverage House, has a great selection of craft and specialty beers. Beer from local, domestic, and international breweries.

From our local breweries like "Cigar City" and "Florida Ave" to Belgium and German beers and many others from across the USA. 

They also have a good selection of California and international fine wines.

If you don''t see what you're looking for, mention it to Billy (the owner) and he'll get it for you. Billy is very personable and engaging, stop in and say hello.

www.thebeveragehouse.net

The two girls working the front desk March 1 at 2pm are the most glum dour front desk staff I've ever encountered. They obviously hate their jobs.  Anti-motivating for sure.  Otherwise all other staff have been pleasant. The facility at any location is a total dive and defines ghetto. If that's your thing you don't even know what I'm talking about. It's not even that cheap.  If you like old equipment and people who make bowel movement comments and jokes in loud voices in the locker rooms you should sign up now to be with your peeps
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Typical Aloft property - good location, basic amenities, mainly catering to a younger crowd. As a platinum SPG member, I got upgraded to a room on the top floor (17th). The room was a good size but had an adjoining door, and the neighbors were pregaming very loudly. I guess I'm officially old when I start complaining about the damn kids. Free WiFi, efficient front desk; the front desk staff even called me a cab (considerably cheaper then Uber during a storm/surge pricing). Hallways were maze-like and like someone else said, the lobby is freezing. The Halal Guys is walking distance for late-night eats.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I really hesitated to come here because the reviews were so mixed but my friends said her family really likes it. Well if you are used to eating banquet pot pies or Marie Callender's and that is your caliber of food then you probably will like this place. I ordered the Thai peanut quesadilla. I question whether there was any meat between the grilled tortillas, I don't know what they use for peanut flavoring but it fell way short of my expectations. It falls apart in your hands and is very messy and really wasn't even worth eating.

Thank you, Yelp.

I had a nail in my tire, checked Yelp, found that Ian's was well regarded, took my car there, and was back on the road in an hour (there were a few people ahead of me).  They didn't try to pull any sales-oriented bullshit, they just fixed my tire and remounted it and I paid them $25 and drove away.

My impression: a busy shop with lots of business (a good sign) and lots of competent guys running around, working hard.They seemed to have a large selection of tires as well, although that's not what I was there for.

A good experience. I definitely recommend them for tire and wheel-oriented stuff.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Totally remember why Dunkin Donuts disappeared the first time. Always out of what you want. Then why be open so much of the time if you have nothing. It's basically a coffee store. And the donuts are so meager and lacking in flavor. I mean geez, can you actually glaze the glazed donuts. Update .....I was stupid enough to go back and it was even worse. The Croissant Donut which they sell at a premium price $2.50 is awful. It was cold, as in we took it out of the freezer. And my once beloved butternut donut is now just crunchy on one side and mediocre at that. So sad that they are successful.

I realize this is "just a car wash", a chain retail car wash at that.  Yet it was an extremely cold day and the guys meeting you outside were having fun with it.  I just wanted a basic car wash to get the salt off the car and said I would be back- probably in a few days after the next snow.  As you'll see from the photo, satisfaction or a rewash, no need car was clean.  I liked the pace thru drying the car as it seemed a little slower on a freezing day so probably better for the cars.

Either way, if you are on the west side, don't be intimidated by the line- the manage it well and your car will look great!

This place is run by an Eastern European couple who are very friendly.  The decor is a bit wild but very different and cozy in its own way.  I've been there a few times and enjoyed it every time.  The food is quite good and can't remember ever having something I didn't like. In fact, we had our rehearsal dinner there for our wedding, we like it so much!  Guests we had, contacted me later because they didn't remember the name of the restaurant and they wanted to go back and recommend it to others. Recommended!

Three of us came into Cinderella on a Friday evening an hour before closing time desperate to get our nails done after a long week. They took us with no hesitation and did a fantastic job with all of our nails. $40 for mani and pedi combo is not a bad price, especially with the added massage. I would love it if they added booze into the mix and offered some champagne/wine while getting pedis done. All the girls seem to know what they're doing and take their time. I was particular impressed with my manicure looked like gel even though it was not! Last almost two weeks before even chipping a little, very impressive. I will definitely be back!

This last visit, we had our favourite server.  He made our evening experience such a HUGE improvement from the prior visit.

It's nice to be able to walk in and not have to wait for a seat.

That Halo roll... I know the sauces don't agree with me, but it's SO absolutely delicious - we ordered two this time. Kissed by a torch, the flavour changes oh so subtly, and it is remarkable HOW fantastic it was.

Again the shrimp cone wrapped in soy sheet  with the mango was good, but they have made me better. 

Now I know which server I want next time I visit.

Service was good, however my Insalata de Mare (Salad with seafood) was just ok. Bland. The scallops were plentiful and correctly cooked, but the shrimps were very over-cooked and tough, the mussels were cooked properly, but a little fishy smelling "off". Got some grit in one. The shells were too tough & couldn't be separated to use as scoops for the flesh. 

Over-dressed, I forgot to ask for the dressing on the side.

Not a single gluten free dessert on the menu, no sorbetto, no fruit or zabaglione. Disappointed.

Service was good, food delivery was timely. That saved the rating a star.

Ok for quick service, microwave heated food.  Had the chicken and steak combo and it came out in less than 3 minutes.  Tasted good. The one down side was that they were constantly cleaning the restaurant. Someone was continually walking around with a broom and dustpan, sweeping right next to us while we were eating.  The bus person comes around with a rolling cart full of dirty dishes to clean a table. They don't empty that cart until it's overflowing.  They just go from one empty table to another.  Quite gross.

Visited this restaurant during restaurant week, and was not all that impressed. It took nearly 2.5 hrs for our dinner, for 2 people, eating soup and pasta...

We were seated on the ever so awkward and cramped porch, which has no heat and is very drafty. Many of the dishes had cream sauces that were bland, and all started to taste the same after a while. The cannoli cream was so overly sweetened with confectioners sugar, we barely ate ours. Not authentic Italian as far as I'm concerned, and we will not be returning.

I've been here several times because I live close. I love the rewards program. I get $1 off almost every time I go. I use to think this was the best fro-yo until I tried a really good place off of Prytania. Now Orange Leafs flavors don't have enough flavor for me. I still go because its a quick fix for my craving. The staff is wishy washy and if you want to try something, they hold on to those little cups for dear life. My other spot gives you a handful and let you have at it! All in all... It's ok for what it is.

I used to live in the apartment building above this place.  It used to be my go to Sushi resteraunt long before I got on Yelp. 

I was there the other night.  25 minutes in I had to ask for my appetizer and gave them 5 minutes or I was walking out the door (note, they were not really busy at all).   

My appetizer amazingly came out 4 minutes later.  Was good and the Sushi was good as well.  Nothing to write home about or to overcome my disappointment in the service.  

Given the number of Sushi places there are in the area, I won't be going back.

Let me just say it's a beautiful place once you get past the rudest & most disrespectful girls at the inside entrance demanding a cover charge.  The owners & management are extremely cool & professional.  My recommendations are to past the professionalism on to the Frontline Staff as the girls collecting cover charges need to at least learn to pretend to like the people coming into the establishment.  Aside from typical rude staff the food & drinks are great.  The atmosphere is awesome for all types of gatherings.

Service department review: It was my first time bringing my 14-year-old car here. They are a very busy dealership with their service department. It was car after car, but they have three waiting areas, and they seem very organized, which I appreciated. I was given a rental free because my car needed more than $300 of work (that's what the coupon said), and my car was fixed and ready by closing that day. The work was as costly as any other dealer, but other than that, I have no complaints. I waited a few weeks to review in case any problems arose, and nothing did.

If your looking for low priced, quick Chinese take out this is the spot.  The general Tso's I got from there was average but their combinations are about 2 bucks lower cheaper than other Chinese full serve restaurants in the area.  The hot and sour soup was one of the best I've ever had but the noodles with that came with it weren't the fried ones but were non greasy and stale.  The cold sesame noodle appetizer was a good change of pace but for some could seem underwhelming although very much worth four dollars and change.  Finally the Hunan beef was standard.

Went here right after I moved into the area.  Was happy to have a beer distributor that carries good stuff so close.  Walked in was and looked around for a bit and noticed that the domestic cases were more expensive than most place by at least 10%.  Got rocked on a case of Leinkugel Summer shandy cans for $35, which is way more expensive than anything else.  When I went in no craft cases were labeled with prices, not sure if that changed in the following months, but there are literally a half dozen places in the area with better prices and selection.  Haven't been back.

This is a poor example of what a good pizza restaraunt could be .the pizza is soggy undercooked and bland.I enjoyed pizza from around the world this is the worst by far.The service is good,5.50 for a salad that consists of lettuce and a tomato slice is even a worse slap in the face. If you enjoy flushing money down a toilet this is the place to go.I tried to give it a chance but you can't fix what is beyond repair.If you like pizza that is undercooked and sits in a bed of water on a plate then this isyour new home  ciao

We've passed this place many times while riding our bikes, and would always say we should try it. Well, last night we did. We ordered a pepperoni and a porchetta. 

We were surprised at how flavorless each one was. We never add salt to anything, in fact if we have a complaint about salt at a restaurant it's always because something's over-salted. But the pizzas from Square Pie had to be salted. The pork had absolutely no flavor. The sauce on the pepperoni was poorly seasoned. 

We were really disappointed and I can't think of a single reason why we would return.

Disappointing.
The good: Service, private booths, and kitchen decour. 
The bad: Unfresh and pregrated Parmesan. The  focaccia seemed stale. The Mahi-Mahi was overcooked. The truffle fries didn't taste like truffles at all.
The Ugly: Adding mayonnaise to salmon tartar.
Of note: The bone marrow dish was the best thing during our 4 course tasting menu(which was supposedly "adventurous"), and I definitely had better.

Bottom lines: 
1. I would have been very upset if I didn't have gift cards.
2. I won't be back.

Service was excellent. The place looks nice and has a nice bar that screens sports on multiple tv's. I had the burrito ranchero off the lunch menu for under 10$, my wife had the chicken fajitas, around 9$ also off the lunch menu, and we had the quesadilla chorizo for 7$ from the appetizer menu. The burrito was served with rice that was fine, but the burrito itself lacked any defining taste even with the jalapeños inside. The guacamole was bland. The fajitas were decent. The chicken was under marinated and slightly over cooked, so it came out kind of dry. The quesadilla was good. Probably won't go back there, although the service was excellent.

It's a shithole. I cannot be more truthful in that regard, but as I look over it, I can't help but think "But it's *our* shithole!" No other place in Manayunk quite does what they do...perhaps for good reason, but they are the only ones nonetheless.

It's dirty. The food is greasy. I honestly don't know if they pass health inspection. Whenever I'm in a state to go there I rarely care. They give me what I need, when I need it, which usually is something hot, salty and greasy. They have no illusions about what they are, which is probably for the best. I don't think I'll ever love the place, but I can't deny it's value.

I went there once and Billy cut my hair.  I have to agree with another poster that I was NOT impressed.  He spent most of his time talking about how much money he made in New York and how he was coming down to New Orleans as if it was charity for him to get stylish hair to the area.  He honestly spent 75% of the time talking about himself and not listening to what I wanted.  My haircut turned out mediocre.  I would have rather paid half the price elsewhere to get the same if not better job done.  Nothing special.  This place is pricy for New Orleans.

The food here is almost indescribable. Melt-in-your-mouth, two-bite sized, magic creations plated on lines of delicious and flavorful sauces.  

I guess it's sushi as in fish but there is no fishy taste (Yay!). We only show up here with friends that order for us so I'm sorry to say that I cannot even tell you what I eat here. 

Waitstaff is efficient and friendly - it is not a quiet romantic place where you decide you want a 2 hour dinner- they get you in and out quickly.

It's worth the wait like others have said - the key here is drive a van and have a few cocktails within while you wait:)

There isn't a better place in the area for sushi. The service is unbelievably fast and the quality of fish is pretty great. However, the most amazing part about Vic's is that they have a $10 special...3 rolls of sushi of your pick for only 10 DOLLARS. I honestly couldn't believe it! 

The place is BYOB and great if there are less than 4 people because it is cramped. Really its the best for take out/delivery. 

Along with the $10 special I order a miso soup and seaweed salad.  Enjoy :)

On a side note, if you stray away from the special I highly recommend the Fantastic roll!

Update - we went back only a few weeks after our good experiences and it was like there was a completely different chef.  The food was terrible - even the Mahi tacos, which we had loved on our previous three visits.  The avocado cream was brown.  The fish had been marinaded in something dark brown and cooked to death.  We tried a tostada-type dish (don't remember the name) and it had so much siracha that it was inedible.  Our waiter didn't seem to notice.  When we said something, he just said "yeah, it is hot."  WHAT HAPPENED ZING?  If your chefs cannot duplicate your signature dish, you have a chef problem and a management problem.

Disclaimer: I am rather picky about sushi and used to dining in San Francisco, Napa, and Los Angeles.

This place is okay.  The service is the best part of the experience: attentive, friendly, polite, and unobtrusive.  The fish is fresh and the variety fairly typical.  The rice is bland and fails to enhance the fish, which is the major failing point.  The all-you-can eat is a great deal, although the nigiri portions are notably small.  I may stop by again when in Reno but I certainly won't come looking for it.

I am writing this review for the new Yummy House on Hillsborough Ave. Went for lunch today and boy, what a surprise! A  whole different environment than the original Yummy and dim sum is served everyday from 11 to 3!  it's a more upscale restaurant, almost too much for the area considering that it's not a very safe neighborhood.

Ordered a few dim sum dishes, beef strips in black bean sauce and house fried rice. EVERYTHING was yum!!

The only thing that spoiled the food/environment was that they were playing Kenny G's xmas CD! yup, xmas music!!

Fairly new place on the Rittenhouse Square area.  There are tons of small sushi places all over this city, most of which are alright.  Honestly, we tried this place because of one menu item, the tuna pizza.  This item had become a favorite after trying it at Morimoto, and this is a very respectable version, for half the Morimoto price.

Other food items included various sushi rolls, the best of which was the spider roll (soft shell crab).  Mmmmmmm.  

Definitely a repeat visit location, next time I'll remember its a byob.

I was disappointed when we tried Sushi on Oracle tonight...wishing that we had gone somewhere else.  First of all it is disorganized.  No one checked us in to wait for seating and because it is so small we had to wait outside in 100 degrees plus temps. No one cleaned a spot on the sushi bar for us until we asked.  No one served the complimentary Miso and soy beans until we asked twice.  We have eaten sushi for decades but we still like to see pictures that show us how EACH restaurant makes their rolls.  No pictures and an extremely limited and boring sushi selection.  As my daughter said...this is white girl sushi - bland.  We won't be back.

Ichiban is a quality Japanese restaurant. The pricing is average and the food is good. The service here was just okay, because the staff wasn't very personal, but they got the job done adequately. My party especially liked the appetizers that we ordered (Beef Maki Maki & Fried Scallops). Their sushi boats are a bit more expensive than at other restaurants in town, but it was an impressive array of food. The atmosphere is quite nice and there is a tatami seating section which gives you the option of sitting cross legged or regularly (helping  out the tall folks).

The best car wash on the west side in fact on in a side of town in Indianapolis they do the inside, the outside, even have a nice fresh a variety of air fresheners to scent your car. I highly recommend that you like them on Facebook so you can receive discount coupons. They are located right in the heart of Speedway right down from the motor speedway track. This is one car wash that is worth the drive I can guarantee you will leave a lot cleaner than you drove in, they vacuumed the inside have a great new cleaning facility and also even hand dry your car from top to bottom.

In my experience, a maybe somewhat better than mediocre Chinese take out place.  The service inside the restaurant has always been friendly, but I'm a little disappointed that they don't deliver to the southern half of Bargersville (south of 144) where there are many homes.  The food quality used to be better several years ago.  I wouldn't consider it one of the best.  Not bad food by any stretch of the imagination, but if you want outstanding Chinese food, go to China Garden at Southport and Madison.  It's worth the drive!

I decided to give them a try. I usually go to Classic Car Spa on Grant. As i looked at what Royal's top car wash included, I asked the guy do you clean the inside. He said they vacuum and "wipe" off the dash. I asked what about the rest. I was told the $25 wash was the best to get. However, I could not use my 50% off coupon. 

I said forget it and drove to my usual wash, 5 min away btw. Out the door, $10.99 with a coupon. I shouldn't have to pay close to $30 for a "good" wash and clean for the inside. 

I highly recommend The Classic Car Spa on Grant and Tucson.

Hope that helps.

Well, having a Groupon is what brought me in for the first time to this shop. They did what they were supposed to do, change the oil.

However, the Service from the guy at the counter was so horrible, I don't think I'll be going back. He barely talked to me, and at the end when I was asking him questions about the bill, he made me feel like u was stupid for asking them.

He handed me the keys, said thanks and walked off, so I guess we were done. No feedback about the car, how the oil was nothing. Just thanks then turned and walked off. I think I'll pay a little more and go back to Pep Boys.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Such great doughnuts. I came here for the warm glazed. After we ordered ours, I noticed my glazed wasn't warm. I went back up and talked to Cheyenne hooked it up.

She was nice enough to say new ones were coming out, and she would get us a couple more. She didn't have to do that but she did just to take care of us.

Update : 3-
Service still great. The Doughnuts are still awesome. I was so full and had to have a green glazed. 

Update 4 stars. 2-16-20

We came in 20 minutes before close and the doughnut were good as usual. Yes the choices were limited.  Next time we will have to come earlier.

Well when we first got here, I used the bathroom to wash my hands. Wow, it was sooooooo dirty. The dining room needed to be cleaned so bad. 

We ordered 2 Big Macs and some how Jaime's came out cold. She went back up and they were happy to exchange it. The Servers were very nice, hence a 2 stars instead on a 1 star rating.

At the end, I went up to order 2 apple pies, the gal said were out and making more, it will take 10 minutes. I waited 15 minutes, went up and the guy forgot to drop my pies. I know mistakes are made, but come on. Again, the gal was very nice and gave me a refund. 

I think we will just go somewhere else in the future.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Delicious taste of homemade Italian goodness. We stopped in for a late lunch and wanted to try as many dishes as we could. We had the eggplant stack, the meatball salad, the four cheese gnocchi and the spaghetti and meatballs. We definitely couldn't finish everything, but it was really hard to stop eating the gnocchi! They were super soft and hand made to perfection! The gravy was perfect and the meatballs are well-seasoned and very generous! The staff are extremely friendly and we even got to meet the owners mother who was so sweet! Scalessa's is a definite must-try restaurant near Trolly Square! What a perfect lunch!

This little spot is a gem and I'm so happy it's in our neighborhood! The sausage and polenta was delicious and the ingredients were so fresh. Our group of four tried the Salsiccia, Fungi, and Melanzane pies. All of which were amazing. The dough has the perfect crisp on the outside and light and fluffy in the middle. To top it off it's a byob. I think the only negative is that the restaurant is a little small, but we just found out they are moving across the street to the old Cochon location. This will be our new go-to place.

-cheap sushi. 
-Good hours
-Terrible staff
-The to go order phone is constantly ringing. It's a terrible environment. Really annoying. It's the low pitch that carries and the server carries it everywhere bother everyone. 
- place isn't dirty but also isn't clean
-too dark
-awful staff
-short staff
-just all around bad servers. 
-didn't offer me a glass for the beer
-waited 20 minutes for them to clean off one table to seat 2 people
-The annoying phone ringing the whole time. This ruined my meal more than anything.

This place is one of the pricier laundry mats I've been to.  For a regular sized load it's $4, for a large load it's $6.  And another $4-5 to dry.  90% of the driers are taped so you can't use them and have been like this for weeks.  Tread lightly because the ones that aren't taped, may or may not dry.  Please be sure to use the restroom because theirs doesn't always have TP, paper towels.  People in here are always complaining but nothing's changed much in the while I've been here.  At least now I've gotten to know which machines are good and which are bad.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Really enjoyed my first visit here and plan on returning! All of the staff were friendly in a very genuine way and not a forced friendly like you experience at most salons now a days. Angela my stylist was very open to what I wanted color wise and cut wise. I unfortunately left a hairstylist recently that I saw for almost a year because he ignored what I wanted for my hair color or even my cut. I'd say lavender purple he put in dark purple, I'd say I want my curls short so chop them down, he heard just a trim. However that wasn't the case here! She listened and delivered! I'm so excited to go back in a few weeks to get a touch up and a trim!

This location was great for the New Orleans Jazz fest and is not too far from the Bourbon and shopping.  Parking is easy and the door hosts are very helpful and friendly.

The check in was a nightmare as they had messed up our reservation, but it was easily fixed. We were staying for work though and got stuck in horrible inner rooms.

Had it been money from my pocket, i would have saved $50 and would have stayed at our avorites in the actual quarter and would have had better rooms, better views, and free authentic morning coffee.

The wall were thin.  Avoid rooms 204-206 as they are right by the gym and very very loud.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Stopped in this subway for a quick dinner after a workout. The place was clean enough. There was a worker sitting on the ground while reloading the chips. I do think that's a bit unnecessary. You can easily refill that while standing. It bothered me a little more so because that's where the line started. 

The man working behind the counter was friendly and helpful! It wasn't the fastest sandwich I had had made, but I really enjoyed that the worker was nice and took the time to listen to what I was wanting and carefully put it all together.

This place wasn't what I expected! They do a mix of popular US dishes and dishes from Mexico. It's a nice variety, especially if someone in your group prefers traditional items rather than Mexican dishes. Our waitress was very nice and helpful with the menu. The place had plenty of seating. It also had a stage area with photo props to take pics in. 

Our table got the queso blanco appetizer. Always a good choice! I wasn't super hungry so I got the Chicken nachos appetizer as my meal. They were so good! Definitely recommend, you get plenty which is nice.

Attempting to park in this gym's parking lot or around this gym is a nightmare. We missed our first class and ended up taking a class an hour later because we couldn't find parking. We had a groupon pass but this is the first gym to pounce on us immediately as we walked in for a tour and sell talk. The gym itself was packed; people were everywhere, which explains the parking lot although my guess is most people live or work in the area. The gym is just too cramped for me. We barely found locker space. While class was enjoyable, I wouldn't fight for a parking space to get there every week.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
My husband and I love, love, LOVE this place.  It's directly across from the Budweiser factory, so it's super easy to take tourists there for lunch or dinner, and it's very reasonably priced.

The calamari is the best I've ever had. Period.  

My complaint are that it's always cold in there, no matter the season, and you must have a reservation on a weekend.  I showed up at 5 pm on a Saturday and no one was there, but apparently they had reservations through 6:30.  We sat at the bar and were seated about 45 mins later, but at 5pm??  We thought we were being the early birds.

Nico's!  In the true test of a Tucsonan you must choose between Los Beto's or Nico's, I'm a Nico's girl.

I am a happy #1 breakfast burrito girl with bacon, egg, cheese, and potato wrapped up in a huge tortilla.  They have lots of other breakfast choices as well, sausage, chorizo, and machaca.  The burritos are hot, served with red or green salsa, and with locations all over town you are never far. 

This location is not 24 hours and does not have a drive through.  The dining room and bathrooms are clean and service is fast and polite.

This place was great - amazing service (seriously top notch), great food & a good vibe. Highlights were the lasagna, eggplant rolls, stuff long hots & MY GOD THE DESSERTS WERE UNREAL (and I'm not a dessert guy). A very good sweet red sauce on all the dishes. 

Funny thing is, if you live in Center City & have a car, this place is easier to get to (factoring in parking) then most places in Center City. 

Only downside was, we went on a Sunday and the bread tasted like yesterday's Amoroso's re-heated in an oven.... to get to the next level, you need fresh bread IMO. 

HIGHLY recommended.

One of two La Quintas very close to IND, this location provided me with a reasonably-priced, spotlessly-clean clean room presided over by a very friendly staff.  I'm reducing the review from four to three stars -- which is still not bad, to be sure -- because the treadmill in the fitness center was flimsy and lame and because the breakfast was meh, even by the standards of free continental breakfast.  If you're looking for a quick, nice place to pop through while on the road or in town for the weekend, I recommend this place.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: It was nice to have a cold treat on a hot summer day but Ice & Cream wasn't all that great. They claim to make homemade ice cream and it's totally not homemade. I went with quite a few people and we all ordered different ice cream flavors. The flavors we're decent but had that "fake" flavored taste. The ice cream wasn't horrible but you could totally tell their ice cream is made someone else and brought in. It's not made in house. We had Chocolate, Cookies n' Cream, Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough, and Strawberry & Banana ice cream flavors.

Fat Catz was a vibe! We stopped by during the middle of the day. We heard some music from the street while walking by and decided to drop in. I'm glad we did. The day we went they had a band playing and they were killing it. The lead singers name was Joe but I don't remember the band name. They were playing old school songs and jamming out. Everyone in there was rocking and singing. They certainly moved the crowd. We sat until it was time to go to our activity. We sat for about 45 min - 1 hr. For it being about 12:30-1:00 pm during the day, it was certainly a mood!

Great smooth coffee we have been looking for! I did get an iced coffee with the brown sugar cinnamon ...and it wasn't overly sweet but I didn't taste the flavor. My husband confirmed it was slightly sweeter than his. He just got iced coffee with milk. I ordered the strawberry pop tart. It was good. Sweet...looked like they just use strawberry jam. It's a small place with seating. A number of small tables...and bar seating. I think the prices were reasonable too. 

Place is in the same parking lot as hot tuna. Sits next to a dry cleaning place. 

I look forward to returning.

My wife and I went for dinner before a show at Tin Angel on a recent cold Friday night.  Pros: service was attentive, restaurant was cozy, and dinner was promptly served.  Cons: my wife's burger was dwarfed by the bun, her fries were lukewarm, my braised short ribs were ok but the portion was way too small and I had to have a second meal when I got home.  I got the feeling that ownership is more concerned with profitability than focusing on the quality of the dining experience.  All-in-all, there are much better places in Philly to combine dinner with music.  Go to Johnny Brenda's instead, where the entire experience is on a higher level.

Placed an order online and it had not arrived in the stated time. I called the location and was told their system was down and that they were just processing those orders. Also told they could not tell me when the order would be delivered. 
Maybe its me, but that is not good customer service. Someone should have called those order and explained the delay.

UPDATE
I was contacted by management. They apologized and corrected the service I received. I understand the process of online ordering now and will probably just call my orders in from now on.

The food is what you expect from Carl's Jr.  Tasty but way too salty. 

I think the drink guy might be speaking English but I am not sure. I think he is refusing to give me another drink refill. Not even if I pay for it. I thought I was minding my business after eating lunch. I guess he is too busy with his other duties of standing around the drink machine doing nothing. 

Fortunately, McDonald's is a couple of blocks north and Habit (which is actually pretty good) is a couple of blocks south, so it is not hard to find a place where people want to work.

It was late. I wanted pizza, but didn't want to walk far. Olympia II was right there.

We headed inside, ordered and were instantly handed hot slices. There appeared to be no warm up process involved. The slices were just ready and waiting. Is this a thing? Have I just not noticed? ...Maybe they were sitting on something hot. I don't know. It was late, after all.

Anyway. The dough was a little, um, rubbery? But the cheese was tasty! I really enjoyed the cheese. And I was super hungry. All the gin-and-tonics and what-not. They caused hunger. Thus: food! It did the trick and I didn't get sick, so I'd recommend.

I bought a Groupon in November and finally was able to use it last night.

Upon leaving the restaurant, my boyfriend and I were in pain, and not in the best of ways.

The four course dinner was just too much, with too little flavor. The tomato sauce tasted like it came fresh from a can at Wegmans. The spaghetti with the chicken parm was a little soggy. I wasn't a fan of the creme brulee. The caesar salad was great, so I'm glad I spent the $2 to upgrade from the house salad.

In all, we likely will not be back. To succeed as an Italian restaurant in this area, the food has to be phenomenal. There's just too much competition.

Jet Rock offers an above-average airport food/drink experience. Their prices are fairly high, which should generally be expected when flying. But for one last meal of local comfort food before leaving the country for a long while? I'll take it.

I ordered a couple fancy craft beers and a fried chicken sandwich. The sandwich needed mayo to taste better but overall wasn't bad. I also enjoyed the beers, but the pricetag makes me sad.

It's unlikely I'll return any time soon, but I do recommend this spot to other travelers passing through. Service is fast and friendly, which is always appreciated while on a deadline to reach the gate.

Yikes. My experience today wasn't nearly as bad as the other posts. I walked in after already chugging coffee at home and still failing at successfully waking to acceptable daytime levels. DD is my last resort place these days. Stuff makes me jittery.

It was pretty empty despite the morning hour, and I ordered my large coffee and muffin. Staff member was friendly enough/efficient. Muffin was good. Coffee succeeded in waking me up for a little bit pre-caffeine crash/causing extreme jitters.

Pretty standard DD experience overall. It's in the strip mall between Westmoreland and Allegheny on Broad. Lots of other convenient chains surround it.

Just like most typical Subways, but the only main difference is that the seating space is smaller compared to the other location on Speedway. The staff were friendly, but a little busy due to the fact that I came here on National Sandwich Day. If you forget to add a sauce, they will accommodate and add the sauce in a cup that you can take out with you. Don't forget that if you want a meal, you can either get a bag of chips or 2 cookies. 

Check online for daily specials, or sign up for their newsletter/emails to get coupons and deals on meals.

This is a great little place. You can design your own pizza with a wide selection of sauces and toppings many of which are fresh and healthy. The Caesar salad was also fresh and delicious. Pizzas are baked in a matter of minutes so you don't need to call in an order to have freshly baked pizza made to order. The business is family owned so staff are friendly and helpful. Don't be fooled by the lack of curb appeal, as it's right next to a dry cleaner in an ugly strip mall. Dine-in facility could be spiffed up a bit but for carry-out or a quick lunch break this place can't be beat. I'll definitely be back!

Delicious home made ice cream, very creamy and rich, and taste natural as well.  They also have some interesting flavors, like root beer, tiramisu, lavender honey, lemon blueberry and more.  Their small cup is about $3.50, which is like half the price of the fancier nitrogen/thai ice cream rolls, with comparable taste, so I totally love this place and make it a point to visit whenever in town.  

My favorites are coffee - rich coffee flavor, and tiramisu - very boozy but not enough espresso in it.  But they are honestly all delicious.

Like many others, this is not a hotel we would have chosen, but we ended up spending a night here because of a flight delay. 

Good things: Room is spacious, there is a microwave as well as a fridge. Bed is comfortable enough. They have free shuttle to and from the airport and we didn't have to wait long.  Overall staff is nice. 

Bad things: The room is rather old and dated. I won't say it's dirty but with old things sometimes no amount of cleaning can make it look bright. 

I don't know if this hotel would have survived if there's no airline sending stranded travelers their way.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The best sushi in town, actually the best I have ever had, and I eat a lot of sushi in a lot of place.  The staff is great, but the food.... WOW
It can get a little busy around the normal 7/8 as they don't take reservations.  So be patient, it is well worth it. 
The Champagne Fluke Caviar Sashimi is out of this world!
If you sit at the bar, Nowri (owner) & Teru (forgive the spelling) are great guys, and if you ask, the can make crazy stuff up just for you that's not part of the normal menu.  As others have said, if I could go over 5 stars, I would.

DON'T order the uno bruschetta, me and my bf thinks thats a shameee to italian food. it was a tasteless whole slice tomato with tasteless wet mozzarella cheese with too much basil on bread.. that is soo sad. brushcetta should not even be like that...  it just seemed lazy. my bf also ordered the mahi mahi which was recommended and he said it was not a good taste. i did enjoy my blue cheese salad very much and the bread and olive oil, that was probably the best. i did like that they had many egglplant variations and chocies for vegetarians.. to sum it up, it just wasnt worth the price, my bf would rate this restaraunt as a one..

I went to sorisso, and I ordered the vegetarian lasagna. The lasagna was interesting because it  was large, had a white sauce instead and had lots of cheese but the whole thing was smothered in the same flavor so it just became bland.  My friends ordered a spicy marinara pasta plate, it was basically spaghetti with marinara sauce on it, that's all with barely any spice. The food were dinners that you could have made yourself. I was hoping to get garlic bread with my entrees, but what I expected is nothing like other Italian restaurants or even chain stores, those places are better. I guess I shouldn't expect a lot more out of IV.

Cooks Liquors is a great little liquor store with a pretty impressive craft beer selection and an equally impressive wine selection. The staff is friendly and is always willing to offer some suggestions. They even have some tasting events. 

Cooks went above and beyond this weekend when we needed a keg for our party. After a few phone calls back and forth with the owner, a sixtel of Yards IPA was waiting in their fridge for us, ready to be enjoyed and regretted by all of our party guests. If you don't see what you want or you want to get a keg, just ask! They are more than willing to see what they can do.

Wild Fields is like the middle child in the neighborhood finding its identity. Big food Publix a block away and natural store Richard's across the street make this a pretty darn good corner for shopping. Produce, meats/fish, prepared foods, wine and cheese are the strengths of Wild Fields. 

Wild Fields has tremendously good prices for produce. Pantry foods are expensive if they aren't on sale. Really, you can get all your shopping done fairly affordable between Wild Fields and Richard's without even having to go to Publix.

I agree with the rest of these reviews...the SLOWEST drive thru I have been to in my entire life!! I'm not kidding. I pulled in at 205p. I drove off w my order at 225p. I have no idea why it took so long bc each window I was asked 'what did you order?' with no explanation of why they didn't know or have it ready. When I got to the handoff I was given my drink w no straw. Then the rest of my order a few minutes later. Good thing I checked the bag bc no straw in there either. Fries were good. Sandwich tasted off but not sure why. 
Will NEVER stop here again and neither should anyone else. The employees just don't care about service.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
All ratings on a scale from 1-10:

Restaurant cleanliness 6
Bathroom cleanliness 2
Food quality 7
Food taste 8
Speed of service 5
Quality of service 3
Restaurant ambiance 3
Parking 4
Menu selections 4
Charging me $2 for white rice (after eating at probably several hundered if not a thousand different Chinese restaurants in probably hundreds of cities, this is THE ONLY. ONE EVER TO CHARGE ME FOR WHITE RICE). And she offered it to us AND it's not anywhere on the menu that it's $2 extra. TACKY. And the score for this; negative 30!

Total score - 3

All you can eat lunch was a pretty good deal. Fresh and tasty salmon. Huge selection to choose from. Warning - the crab I had in two rolls was actually Krab (imitation crab). Chewy and made the two rolls rather unappetizing. 
Servers were very nice and all items cane out quickly. Right in the heart of downtown Boise so limited parking but worth a little walk.
I'll be back, but am now aware to avoid anything on the menu that lists"crab" as its not true crab meat. I guess they have to cut somewhere if they are offering all you can eat sushi for $18 (lunch).

I feel bad giving a bad review but I really was not a fan. We got a square plain - the pizza sauce was very fishy. I know places put anchovies in the sauce but I feel like it was over powering. The cheese is good and the crust also good but seriously could barley eat because of the sauce. Also got a circle pizza just with cheese. Again, crust was good but the cheese was not, almost tasted like the cheese on NY dollar slice shops. For the price of the pizzas, the hype and the order process- I was expecting much better.

I've been to red cat a few times.  The 4 star rating is factoring in their pedicures. They are great!  I definitely will continue to go if I just want a pedicure.  

On the other hand, gel manicures here only last me about 4 days max. I would rank them about a 2 or 3.  They do a nice job and the shoulder massage is awesome, but unfortunately it's not worth the money when the gel chips or starts peeling after 3 days. I also don't use my hands more than normal and normally gels will last at least a week if not longer. Unfortunately I won't be back for manicures.

Clean and spacious rooms. The staff was super helpful and friendly! Problems with checking in, our room was supposed to be ready at 4 however 4 came and went so we went to dinner then checked in when we returned. We had a balcony room which was both lovely and incredibly loud. The trolley line sounds like it is barreling down the middle of the street and the street noise is loud. Saying that, aside from waking up occasionally, l am a pretty good sleeper but I would get a room
In the back of the hotel if I stayed there again. They did allow us a little bit of a late check out so we did not have to store our luggage.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Great boutique hotel. The rooms are clean and beautiful. I loved the exposed brick and cement in the rooms. The rooms are uniquely decorated with a voodoo like decor that is very New Orleans! It is a quiet area, so your guaranteed a good nights sleep.

The hotel is located in a great area in the warehouse district. Its easy to get to and you are surrounded by plenty to see, do, eat and drink. The beds are comfortable and again you will get a good nights rest. They have a small gym with a few cardio machines and a weight rack, which is nice. They also have a snack and bar area, which is helpful.

Book this hotel, you will not be disappointed!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The bacon board and fried green tomato BLT were enough to get me to want to return. But everything else was more average. The biscuits and gravy were enjoyable as was the chicken and waffle. The corn souffle had no flavor and sour cream on top made it even worse.... AND I LOVE LOVE sour cream. 

Staff doesn't wear masks while Omicron barrels through the land. I watched the woman setting a table put her fingers inside each and every glass as she set it... My server was great and attentive, but a bit too close and chatty considering covid.

Anyway, cute space and vibe, but wouldn't return until after the pandemic slowed back down.

The modern building exterior and the impressive website made me curious about this place which is why we tried it a few weeks ago.  We had made reservations as we went on a Friday evening, but turns out we didn't really need to as it wasn't as busy as expected.  The waitresses were like ones you'd see at Moxies.  Although the interior was modern, it had a feel a bit more casual than expected.  There were also kids there too.  Food was alright, nothing ground-breaking, but still good.  I'm not sure if we'd go back though because from where we live, Moxies or Earls would be comparable and closer to us.

Great gym. I used to work at 24 hour fitness which granted me access to the ultra gyms so I am kind of picky when it comes to picking a place to work out. I've tried Fisher's health and the local 24 hour but neither felt like a good fit. Golds on the other hand has everything I need. Good equipment, free weights, group spin, and high end cardio machines. Wish they were 24 hours but the hours listed are good. It's never really packed which is a huge plus compared to places like the UCSB Rec Cen. My only gripe is that it is kind of expensive but all gyms around here average 60-80 bucks a month so I guess it's standard for the SB area.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Our current favorite Mexican joint. Totally authentic, super fresh. They made the guacamole to order, the burritos are massive and flavorful. My only complaint would be that we were there on a 2 for $5 Margarita night, and I have a pretty good allergy to alcohol and I downed two of these with no reaction. This tells me that there was hardly any alcohol in it at all, which is fine by me, since I only paid $2.50 for each one, so I feel like I got what I paid for, lol. At any rate, we go here whenever we crave Mexican.

Upscale gastro-pub fare with a nice assortment of non-local crafty type brews on tap. Mooses Drool on tap. Props for that! (...and the 4th star). Soft pretzel for the appetizer, grilled fish sandwich pour moi & BBQ chicken sandwich for her; both with YUMMY sweet potato fries. Focus is on the bar with lots of TVs, Yeah, it's a sports bar. But the food is definitely above par (in fact, way above par). This is the 3rd restaurant at this location. The original was a chain that crashed as a result of the crash in '08, the second was a local Greek restaurant. I hope this place sticks..

dinner w/ Lynette,Amy & Bill. first thing i noticed is the ceiling height. me being 6'6" i could mot straighten up. its in a basement of a house. 
a little disappointed because one of the reason we went was for the 'hand made home made' Toasted Raviolis. they had run out. grrr. the pizza is really good. it has a smokey flavor because of the brick oven! the hand made sausage is good AND they have GREEN OLIVES. what a rare find. 
Meghan was our server & she is great. 
we will return,
1. call ahead for the T Ravs.
2. Meghan is working.

What's happening to Distrito?  Are they trying to save money or dumbing down on flavor for their non flavor/spice seeking customers?  The pork taco is now tasteless and the veggie enchiladas have changed also - less spice, blander.  We used to love this place but they are going in the wrong direction, in our opinion.  It started when they changed the churro dipping chocolate - used to be a spicy chocolate but evidently it was too spicy for some kids.  My advice is don't be generic, don't be just another run of the mill Mexican restaurant.  Be what you used to be!  Flavorful, spicy and different!

Had the pleasure of dining here last Saturday, was by far the best restaurant I ate at while in Nashville. We arrived a few minutes early for our reservation and were promptly seated. Upon hearing it was our first visit, we were presented with prosecco for a toast. The cocktails were promptly delivered once ordered, the cheese plate was incredible. I had the filet, the wife had the cod, which was the special. Both were unbelievably good, as was the crumb cake we had for dessert. I highly recommend this establishment and will be eating here next trip to Nashville.

We went here because it had a 4 star rating from a lot of people, but we were very disappointed. We were asked 3 times in the first minute if we were ready to order, but we had to ask for them to bring us water. We ordered the sashimi deluxe plate - the fish itself was not dry and not fresh, and they gave only a cup of rice for the whole plate. When they refilled water, after we had to ask for it, they didn't add anymore ice or anything. The tapioca balls in the bubble tea were just big clumps at the bottom of the glass. The rolls we got just had the sauce unevenly splattered and weren't good quality. Overall bad service and mediocre sushi.

There was nothing wrong with three coins but then again there was nothing real great about it either. It's not really in the best part of town but it's a 24 hour diner hard to find in lowly old Tampa. So for a local place to eat late night breakfast, it's a good location. Just nothing real special about their food or service. I've been to much better diners in Lakeland. I can't even tell you what I had because it was just another breakfast meal for me. Again I'm not saying there was anything wrong but nothing really for me to remember or make not of.

The service is very good and the staff professional.  I also like the atmosphere tremendously.  The only negative is they don't take appointments.  So, if you're a busy mom and professional on a tight schedule, it can be very challenging to get in.  

They do have a "Call Ahead" policy.  You're asked to call in about an hour - 30 minutes ahead of time so they can put you on a list.  But, when I called in and showed up when expected (actually 5 minutes early) I was told that I'd have to wait another 45 minutes.  As you can imagine, I didn't like that outcome.

I called around to get some quotes for hemming a dress. All the places said they couldn't do that without seeing the dress in person. Fair enough. I didn't bother with Master's because they were two weeks out on any alterations. 

I took the dress to Sarah's A List, Josephine's and Classic Cleaners. The pricing came back at $25 to $40 (seriously overpriced). I went with Classic Cleaners and am really happy with the results. I made sure she understood that I wanted a professional looking hem and that is what I got. I've had skirts and coats messed up before and it just baffles me when the hem lines are wonky.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Been  here a few times and I'm still confused...is this a Mexican restaurant or a sports bar?   The ceiling shelves are still lined with football helmets from the previous owner-sports bar and  a few sombreros on the wall.  Food and service are really good  but there is no ambience.  The ice machine is  making a very loud industrial sound which doesn't help.  Get rid of the football memorbilia, change out the loud ice machine, add some Mexican flair and turn on some music!  Owner is so sincere and means well but he really needs to create a fun Mexican atmosphere to take this restaurant to the next level and make us want to come back!

So we wanted sushi for dinner and were driving into NJ from Philly to catch a movie and saw Osushi on Yelp with pretty good reviews. We were not disappointed!! Their special rolls are fantastic! Very unique! And they were delicious. The staff was very friendly as well. Also the decor is amazing... You can tell they put a lot of effort into setting this place up! We will be back very soon. :)


3/31/17 update!!! We come here EVERY time we go to see a movie now! We are here today for my husband's birthday and as always Osushi has delivered phenomenal service and impeccable sushi. We drive 40 min from Philadelphia because it is really that good

The past 2 times I've visited China Pan, it's just been ho hum. My excitement for it has waned.

Today the things that were supposed to be crispy on the outside (spring rolls, sesame chicken) were soggy--and dishes were crusty (pepper chicken) that shouldn't have been. 

The water tasted like dish soap but my server ignored me. Fortunately, I happened to have my own water with me.

The hibachi grill was still pretty decent but the chef wouldn't even make eye contact with me so I could specify sauces. The raw mushrooms also had not been cleaned!

Ohhhh welllll....

Philly Car Share is terrible and I recommend staying away.  They overbilled me $40 and now, their customer service people are non-responsive.  They do not return phone calls, and it is impossible to get a live person in billing.

They USED TO BE terrific.  Clean cars, low prices, a great community feel.  They are no longer terrific.   They are now AWFUL.  Their cars are filty and in terrible condition, their prices are high, and their billing practices are unethical.  It's a shame.  I'll be using Zipcar from now on.

Wow this place was absolutely awesome. Great bartenders! Great outfits, such a great period place. Well made Old Fashioned.

The bar is not too big not too small, just the perfect size. We didn't have to wait long for a drink even though there were a few people there for drinks.

They had old movies paying behind the bar and of course the music, the live band that was there was so great.

There are so many bars in NO, but 21st is a must stop, it really should be on the walking tours. If you have 1920 type clothes and like to dress up as well they will appreciate it.

What makes a perfect dive bar?

Old, musty smokey smell - CHECK
Floors and walls that haven't been updated since the Reagan administration - CHECK
Sports on TV while music blares from the juke box - CHECK
Being served a Coke and Malibu in an ale glass with a "bendy" straw - CHECK! CHECK! CHECK!
Entertainment in the form of dog-eared early 80s boxes of Trivial Pursuit cards placed across the bar - CHECKAROONI
Pringles as pretty much the only dining option - (crunch) CHECK
The bartender coming out on the floor to join you as you regale other patrons with your best and funniest stupid-people stories - FO SHIZ!

Seriously.

#RainbowMufflerLargoFL
Rainbow Muffler 185 So. Belcher Rd., Largo FL 33771
727-535-3011 ask for Bri or Paul  - tell 'em we sent ya... Well worth the drive to Largo!!
... took my Nissan Frontier in for several issues - were handled properly, professionally with ultimate refreshing customer satisfaction! Great trustworthy breath of fresh air - folks to do business with, recommended highly :-) :-)
Thank you Paul, bri, Sean and Nate!!!!!

6/21/3016
Took the Nissan Frontier in for a issue with a flange, Nate took care of the problem pronto and professionally!! Thank you Bri, Nate for the Fast Courteous service:)

Saw the name of this bar while grocery shopping across the street and just had to visit for a quick drink. This is a very small, divey type bar with an attentive bartender. The people I assume were regulars were friendly and, although they didn't serve food, there is a pizza place and a Chinese food place right next door for an easy munchies fix. 

I was surprised to see a man getting beaten up by three others a few months ago while driving by on my way home from work - doesn't really seem like that kind of place (but I guess all bars have potential). Credit cards not accepted.

We love the Red Key. It's the perfect neighborhood bar. The service is friendly and welcoming. The decor is a perfectly preserved retro time capsule. My husband loves the old 45's in the jukebox. The food is pretty good, too - yummy burgers and perfectly cooked grilled cheese. They also have tenderloins and BLTs. Tons of chip options to choose from to go with your sandwich. Apparently the potato salad is awesome, when they have it. I'll have to try it one day! They also have a good selection of beers (in cans and bottles) and liquor. It's cash only, but they have an ATM if you need it.

I shop here pretty often because of that God awful soda tax we have here in Philadelphia. We don't buy soda as much as we used to but when we see a great deal, we jump right on it. Out of all the Acme stores I shop, this one has the best selection of deli salads and fried chicken! I would love it if the store updated and added beer and wine like most of the other locations only because in this area, there really isn't anywhere else to buy it. Cashiers are always helpful and available to help. No complaints here.

Stopped in here after a few Scotch drinks at Irish Pub. To my dismay, their kitchen closed at 11and I'd arrived a shade afterwards. So I was "forced" to drink on an empty stomach... Oh the horror. My drinking partner mentioned this place was open til 2am. So here I am.  Place was empty. I ordered two slices of greasy pepperoni. It wasn't the worst pizza I'd had but damn sure wasn't the best by any means.  Just pizza you'd get when nothing else is open or available after drinking to your hearts content. Pizza was lukewarm and the crust tasted like burnt paper. Two stars for being open after the bars close.

I'm not sure what all the hype is about for this place. Yes, it's a super cute joint with awesome service. However, I wasn't very blown away by the food. I had the grilled calamari, gnocchi with shrimp and tiramisu. The grilled calamari tasted a bit bland. I had to sprinkle a decent amount of salt to taste anything. The gnocchi felt overcooked and I got exactly 3 shrimps on my plate. The tiramisu was delicious though, although way too small for the price. Even though the food was just okay, I really enjoyed the wonderful service and complimentary orange shots.

This obscure Chinese restaurant is located right off of Ulmerton. If you aren't prepared, you may miss the entrance. The aesthetics are just one notch above a hole in the wall. The food is ok.The service is quick and friendly. 

There is nothing exceptional on the menu though. You will find your standard takeout type fare such as General Tso's chicken, Egg Foo Young, and Chow Mein. We like to order take out from here when we are too lazy to cook. It is fast, convenient, and good enough for a weekday dinner when all you want to do is feed the kids and send them to bed so you can crack open a bottle of wine and forget the day.
