My dad had some kind of sea food pasta and it was good.   I would of liked this spot more it more if it was a byob.  For northeast Philly location, it can really get pricy.  If im in the area, I would definitely come by here again.

Not my normal stop, but I was driving by and it was convenient to stop here and stock up for a football game at home.

Excellent beer selection and I like how virtually all of it is inside of coolers already chilled.

Vodka selection was good too, and some prices on certain brands and flavors was surprisingly low.

Did not think as much about the limited variety of wines in this location. Also had to really search hard for some chocolate and there was not much to choose from that was better than what I could buy at a CVS.

Employees were aware of customers and quickly opened other registers to get us out the door, which is always appreciated.

Our family have been patients at Pritchett Eye Care since Dr. Pritchett was actually practicing his trade at this location (I think he is busy running his small empire of offices across norther Nevada these days as I haven't seen him in years).  The doctors here are always thorough with their exams and they have a wide range of frames etc. to choose from if you do need glasses or contacts.  I do like that they will work with you to let you know what your insurance covers so you can make informed decisions when ordering your glasses.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text: Airplanes landing and taking off SO FREAKING LOUD all day and night make it impossible to sleep. I was on the third floor on the front side of the building and I was woken up about fifteen times through my one night stay. It is deafening. Sounds like the plane is going to crash into the hotel, no joke. Other than that, this is a pretty standard red roof inn. Our room did not have any towels when we arrived which makes me question the depth of service from the housekeeping staff. When we received replacement towels, this stain accompanied them.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I've only eaten in once or twice - I usually grab a to-go order from the bar.  Danielle, the bartender, is wonderful.  She's pleasant, courteous, attentive and quick.  Food comes out speedily and well packed for travel.  My favorites are the fried mozzarella, petite crab cakes and the apple walnut spinach salad, though their specials do not dissappoint either.  The food is always in large portions.  Conveniently located off Broad St, a short walk from the Walnut Locust stop.  Love it and eat there a few times a month.  Defintely check it out!

Started with garlic knots- they charge you individually and tasted like plain bread, not buttery and full of fresh garlic like I had hoped.  Nothing special.  Ordered some wings, they came out a little under done for my liking but we're still edible.  I had ordered hot sauce on the side and the server forgot it.  I don't know how seeing as we were the ONLY table in the restaurant.  Next we had the meat pizza- it was ok- I felt like the ingredients tasted cheap and the pizza was covered in grease.  Better places in the area for pizza.

It's very rare that I would write a review for a big chain restaurant. However, this specific location does an exceptional job at everything. The service was extremely courteous and they are extremely thorough. My family can be a little special. A lot of adjustments. No this no
that and for that I am sometimes embarrassed. However, they were spot on all three visits. I have a closer location, but the service of this establishment is worth the extra distance. We are quick to say when a business messes up, but it's important to give a kudos when they excel.

The decor in the lobby is great! The hallways are a little dated, good thing I don't sleep in the hallways.  The rooms aren't the best I have ever seen but the bed was comfy and the sheets were fresh.
  The breakfast was good, and the restaurant staff was super nice.  Actually I didn't meet a staff memeber that wasn't nice, from the shuttle driver to the front desk manager.

I don't think I'll stay here the next time I come. I could have booked the same price with nicer rooms.  

Oh and guys... can you fix the ice machines!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
First can I say that I didn't try anything I didn't love... and I tried ALL the flavors. Jenis wants you to try everything. I was handed samples I didn't ask for "you like this..oh you will love this." The staff is amazing. 
The chocolate tastes just like a brownie even has the same texture. The lavender ...oh geez....so good. I finally made a choice. Mango, passion fruit, and lavender( I didn't day I chose just one).

OMG I can't believe I forgot to tell you about the coffee ice cream ..... bits of esspreso...Yep that's a wrap folks...its just amazing here.

Went there recently during a week night - the only way to get a table. The climb up with the elevator was fascinating! But the view from the top was a let down that evening as the last floors were in the clouds. We ordered the sea urchin and the sea bass served with fennel. The food was excellent and they had an extensive wine list. This said, the restaurant space on the 59th floor is a huge, impersonal, space, meaning that the restaurant felt cold. The noise level was quite high from music played on the bar level. I'll go back because of the food

Went her yesterday night: definitely blown away by my meal. Me and my fiancé both ordered sushi here and were pleasantly surprised with our experience. I ordered the Devil and Bloomingdale rolls while she got something like the Spicy Dancing Kani and KK rolls? Both of hers were awesome and while both of mine were good themselves, the Bloomingdale was easillllyyyyy my favorite. The best part of the experience is the presentation as well. They deck out the plates with all sorts of LED lights, sauces, leafs and cool stuff. Would recommend this place to anyone

Side note: they have 43 specialty rolls to choose from...43!!!

Really good chicken Caesar salad. Crab cake sandwich is also really well made. These are the only reason we stop in. Unfortunately on a Saturday at lunch time there is a wait and it is almost impossible to get a table. We were with our daughter otherwise sitting around the "bar" would have been just fine. The waitresses do not seat you and this really makes for a miserable time finding a table. The service is quick. 

It is so tight it quickly gets annoying and I like to think I'm more patient than most. If you are feeling particularly patient and want a good salad, hawk a table!

Sparkling new and stuffed to the brim. 

They sell a few local products like Frittle and Broad Ripple Chip (yay!). They also source a lot of produce from farms in Michigan, which is nice to keep it in the Midwest. 

They sell sushi, as well as made-to-order Mexican foods, pizza and more. There's also a create your own salad bar. 

The people we interacted with were friendly and I liked the size of the grocery: Big enough but not overwhelming. 

You can park in the garage on the east side of the building for free and access the grocery from the garage.

Why my family loves this place: 

My grandma is hard of hearing and there's an amazing back room where our whole, large family can meet for a peaceful, Christmas meal together. It's large, so people can move around/switch seats to talk and the babies can run around without disturbing anyone. The lighting is dim and peaceful, and the service is always attentive.

You can choose menu options for everyone ahead of time (which is what my grandma always does) and then we pick between those. My favorites include the filet, salmon, mashed potatoes, chopped salad, and apple crisp.

Who knew they have great quesadillas? We were on Mass Ave on a Friday night and every place was crazy-busy. However, we were able to walk right in here and order instantly. There were even some available tables and the servers were friendly and got our order quickly. 

The food came out fast too and our portions were large and worth the money. I got the chicken quesadilla and it had corn and beans and onions and cheese in it. Super delicious.

 I loved the speediness of this place because on the weekends, Mass Ave restaurants can take hours to get sat. They also had a fun, seasonal & spiked drink menu.

Stayed here for a work accounting symposium. The location is directly across from the arch but at the time we were there, construction was being done so in order for us to visit the arch we had to walk a couple blocks down. No biggie. Very close and walking distance to the stadium as well.

I like how there was an extensive list of items the concierge would be able to provide if you forgot anything (hello, aquafresh whitening toothpaste) or if you wanted to borrow something (foam pillows). I enjoyed the flavored water provided in the lobby during the afternoons and the BBQ restaurant in the lobby was good too!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Well, it's a Chase Bank. So every time I'm here there's always a line. They're constantly busy- from simple transactions to account opening etc.  There is an ATM inside if you don't feel comfortable using one of the 2 drive up ATMs.  Last time I was there, a staff member was assisting customers / showing them how to use the new ATM which is very user friendly.  There are usually only 2 tellers working so if you need to see a human- be prepared to wait about 10 minutes.  Every time I have interacted with a staff member they were very friendly.  So overall- good service, just be prepared to wait.

I honestly think this maybe the cheapest place to eat on campus. The breakfast bowl is only $3.99 and includes puree, 2 poached eggs, a pita puff, and 3 toppings. I never was able to find anything that is filling and costs less than $5 in Tucson and near the U of A, unlikes those near ASU. The panda express here costs $6.20 while a chinese food bowl near ASU costs $4.50 for way more than that and I could eat for two servings. Anyway done with the comparison. 
I totally recommend this plus. Although I never ordered the expensive items on the menu because what kind of wraps costs $7-8.

I went here a few weeks ago and called in my order.  The woman who took my order indicated that it would be ready for pickup in 15 minutes.  I arrived at least 20 minutes later only to find out not only was it not ready, but I had to recite my order 2x.  I finally picked it up at least 20 minutes past the time she indicated it would be ready.  I complained to an older Italian looking guy with white hair but suspected he was just a driver.  The lady was very rude, dismissive, and unapologetic.  I don't think I will return.  The food is good, but not great to deal with rude, inattentive, and uncaring customer service.

Gave me a mid-sized Kia K5 (replaces the Kia Optima) for the full price of what Enterprise considers a "full size" vehicle.

 "Only" $103.33 for 24 hours to rent this vehicle that didn't include the $50 insurance. Expect to be heavily pressured into buying these expensive insurance products. I was even asked for my insurance company, insurance contact information, insurance policy number and insurance deductible amount to intimidate me in buying the $50 insurance add-one.

Oh and they require a $400 deposit at the time of the rental as a "hold" to protect the vehicle. It's all about the money here and not the customers!

No complaints here, this place is what it is, and everyone already knows, lol. I have eaten inside and used their drive thru window, and most of the time they get my order correct and to me in a timely fashion. 

I usually am there during off peak hours, so maybe that helps me too, but normally the drive thru has been pretty quick getting my food, and I even order my burgers without onions, which takes them a few extra minutes to make fresh. 

I like when they have the 2 big mac's or 20 chicken nuggets for $5 deal. Now I think it's 2 egg mcmuffins for $4, and they serve breakfast all day long now too.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: The owner (Willie Lopez) really knows his customers! Due to calorie counting, I haven't splurged on Italian food as much as usual, so it had been nearly a year since I was last here. Willie asked me right away if I would still be ordering my usual...Alfredo pasta. How did he remember that?? It's because he cares about his customers and the repeat business. I've also had their pizza & chicken parm. Both were excellent. La Prima does not deliver, but that doesn't seem to keep people away. If it's that good, and you want authentic NY-style Italian food, chances are that you will make the trip to pick it up.

I'm new to the area and love that I get to try out new restaurants. When I saw that Balducci's was near to my apartment, I was excited to give it a try!

The ambiance was a bit divey, but it is underground so that's expected. The service was good and pretty prompt. The menu is a little boring. We asked for recommendations and were told to try the pizza. So we ordered the deluxe on thin crust.
It was ok. The sauce was sweeter than I'd like in my pizza. Overall, not much to write home about, which was disappointing considering a large of this pizza was $18. Probably won't be craving this nor coming back anytime soon.

I love the price of half-price happy hour sushi! The quality is middle of the road: not coastal, not grocery market. The service at happy hour is slow, but it is happy hour and always seems to be super busy. The cooks and servers can only move so quickly when they are sat 5 tables in 5 minutes. If anything, they need to hire a proper host, not just what seems to be a buser that finds a minute. As a former server, I know that can just ruin the rest of your service timing. Just bring a good friend or loved one to chat with while you wait the 30 minutes to get your food, and enjoy each other's company and the inexpensive fare!

*** WARNING ***
THIS IS NOT A WASH N' ROLL LOCATION ANYMORE. Not sure who owns it, but if you go here, here is what to expect:

1. Employees look like they are meth heads and are on drugs.
2. NONE of the employees wear a mask.
3. When you enter, there use to be 3 entrances, and now they're down to 1.
4. They went from 20 vacuum spots, down to 6.
5. All vacuum spots are now right next to each other.
6. They changed all the hoses from 20' down to 10', so you can forget about cleaning out your back seat or back of your SUV.

Food was just ok.  We started with an order of the gnocchi which is good, however ordering the half Gorgonzola and half marinara sauce, I thought it would have been served on two different plates. NOPE.  Just plopped the sauces one to the left side, one to the right side.  The two bled together and ruined it for me.  The chicken al forte was again, OK.  It stated there was crab meat atop the chicken along with mushrooms...mushrooms yes, crab meat no.  For a BYOB it's ok.  A nice plus is they accept credit cards.  Would I go again? No.

I was hungry for tacos and Tacos A La Diabla fit the bill. Fair prices, prompt service, and hot food.  This restaurant did not set the bar higher than any other local mexican place, but met those expectations exactly where I had planted them. I feel like everyone has that one local Mexican place they went to growing up; this could be that. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to get there, but if in the vicinity might drop by if a particularly strong salsa craving arises (they did have an excellent cilantro to tomato ratio).

"Meh" would describe how I feel about this place perfectly. Definitely not my first choice for late night, but now that Pat's & Bobby's just closed there aren't too many options especially for cheesesteaks. The quality of steak definitely is below average at best. Service is blah and my friends have gotten incorrect orders before, but you just want to get in and get out as quickly as possible because it is a late night joint. They're definitely preying on all the drunkies that come in, so I can't blame them for that. I'll pop in to get a 6-pack but other than that, not worth it for the food.

Chef RJ is downright royalty (can you say James Beard winner??)and we are so lucky to have him, his talents and his team in Germantown. I've only visited during the early post-Quarantine, so things are not set up as they usually are. But I was lucky enough to chat with the chef, and sample many of his offerings via take out. BLOWN AWAY.  Fresh oysters, homemade squid ink pasta with mussels and clams, veal Parmesan, burrata, chattily cream cannoli, a variety of flat breads... such elevated Italian! 
Saint Stephen will be high on my list to revisit as we exit the stay at home restrictions. Can't wait!

Okay so I've been to Mama Bear's twice now and I would go back a third time. If your scene is raunchy dive bars then this place is for you 5- stars. The bartender, an older woman, is beyond nice and will make you feel at home as she teases you throughout the night. 

Then again I give this place a 3-stars because it is not my scene and the place is tiny and very out-dated. I definitely wouldn't bring a girl on a date here but if a buddy and me want a cheap beer and are in the area we may stop in. 

If you're open minded give this place a chance. Don't knock it till you've tried it!

Only place with vacancy while driving from Florida to Indiana.. At first glance it seems nice but as we walked in the room I noticed a really dirty and sticky floor as well as mold in the bathroom and a broken mini fridge. 
The free breakfast was a joke. The eggs had so much salt I could not even swallow one bite of it. The sausage and grits looked very undesirable. 
I will say the bed looked sketchy but we did abed bug search and it seemed clear. I could not get a good nights rest but my hubby our driver did and that's what's counts.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: First of all, I waited in line for 20 mins to place my order. Ordered 8 donut holes and a bacon egg NO CHEESE croissant, yet again with another 15 mins for my food, got out to my car and realized that I was given a bacon cheese NO EGG croissant so I had to go back in for them to remake it after debating on them making the correct one or not the first time! Woth no apologies or anything I can say we will NEVER BE back to this one again! Even management was all cool and collective when everyone that was in the lobby had to wait just a much time as us, JUST TO ORDER!  Ridiculous!!!!!! #notadunkindonutfananymore

I loved it here!! I went on a Sunday, which is when they do their chef's tasting menu and it was worth it! I think it's only $45 for five courses! Including a dessert!!! IT'S ALSO BYO! I mean what more could you ask for? Nothing in my opinion.

The portion sizes were actually not that small. They were on the smaller size but after five of them I was definitely satiated. The atmosphere is warm and inviting. It is extremely small so make sure to make a reservation before going. The staff was friendly and overall it was a really enjoyable experience. This is on my "Mmmhmmm List" and I can't wait to go back again.

3.75 stars 

I've had only take out sushi from here twice. The quality is very decent, but a little pricey. However, I feel like most special rolls had some type of mayo sauce or tempura/crunchy stuff (not my preference). That said they have a few rolls that use soy bean paper rather than rice which is pretty cool (and tasty!). Also, great rice to fish ratio (not too much rice!).

Love the seaweed salad. 
Spicy tuna tartar cold appetizer was good but maybe too much mayo?
Salmon avocado was delicious! 

Steven Sashimi Roll - enormous. Huge. Very good

I'd like to review.... alas they don't open till 9 am.   My son's school is right down Jefferson and I thought I'd pop in, do a bit of work, conf call, etc., but noooo.  I was denied by a CLOSED sign at 830 am.  Conf call couldn't wait.... had to rush home thru a jillion stop lights/signs.. as there is no quick way from this joint to anywhere pretty much.  Disappointed. And wondering why a coffee place wouldn't be open during morning coffee time. I know its a different kind of place... but still.  Those of us that love coffee love it at 8am as well as 11 pm.  And 3 pm.

The service her was very good it's pretty small for a Chinese buffet but the food was good, no real complaints. They did put slices of cheese on some sushi and it seemed strange but their food was quite palatable. They have a very good hot and sour soup and their crab rangoons were delicious. I do however wish the green onions for the soup were changed more often, they were kinda of dry. They had a great selection of food, something for everyone. I really liked their pineapple chicken as well. Also very clean.

Let me first say that I have not yet been to a Starbucks that wasn't super busy but this one is ridiculous.   However,  it is to be expected because of it's close proximity to the Westgate Brandon Mall, the AMC movie theater and the I-75 exit.  When they first opened they were extremely slow getting orders out, especially for the drive thru.   I thought I might run out of gas while waiting.  They have gotten a little better with time but still too slow.   Keep in mind the location if you plan to go to this one.   You WILL wait.

I stopped at the first Tropical Isle I saw without realizing it wasn't the original smh.. i ordered my hand grenade frozen and at first it really didn't taste like much, not that it was bad, just not much flavor. Although it felt like it burnt my tongue. It was bizarre. As we walked around New Orleans it started to melt and get stronger and stronger. Once it was completely liquid it was so strong that I couldn't even drink it. I poured out basically half of the grenade portion of the cup. Oh well, I can say I've had one now.

It's a barn full of liquor, what else can you ask for? Yes, this is in a real converted barn, and it carries all sorts of assortments of wine, liquor and beer. In fact there's some pretty decent craft selections there, including a large display of bombers. Also there's a florist attached, ya know, just in case you want to take some flowers with that wine along to your significant other.  It's not as big as some other booze shops in Jersey, but it's worth a look if you're in the area, otherwise you'll have to drive to the more populated Mount Holly.

This is my new go to Mexican restaurant. I've never had anything bad here and they have a wide variety of options on their menu.

I suggest enchiladas with tomatillo sauce, delicious! Also just an FYI their quesadillas are tasty but also kind of tiny. Their burritos on the other hand are huge. 

Would be five stars but I find their dine in situation to leave a bit to be desired (one time it was blazing hot with no air conditioning and one time we were totally forgotten about when it came time for the check), however their food is great so you should try some take out.

So, in my humble opinion, and having tried all the pizza joints on Brownsville road, this is by far the best one in the area. The crust is typical Neapolitan, nice and fluffy, and the cheese is usually plentiful. I love their sauce, which is sweet (I feel that pizza sauce must be a by sweet to counter act the cheese's saltiness instead of just adding a ton of acidity). Their prices are a bit better than their competitors in the area too. Overall, if I'm in the mood for pizza, this is my go to place. Haven't been disappointed yet. Wait, I take that back. Their fries aren't too good, but still, their pizzas are great!

I'm really very impressed with the selection here. I'm not nearly as impressed with the price, but where else can you get such a huge selection of foreign beer? There's not just your usual Belgians and Germans either. I was happy to find Japanese, Russian and even some Lithuanian and Polish bottles to choose from. There are even some Quebec based brews you can find here (Du de Ciel sticks out) that I haven't found elsewhere in the Philly area.

I'll be back just for the selection alone. You won't find anywhere with more inventory in the surrounding areas. I'll cringe when I see the high price but try to remind myself it's worth it.

The service at National is exceptional. I rented a car here on my 21st birthday and, contrary to popular opinion about how dealing with car rental agents can be pushy and uncomfortable, I was met with personable customer service and a knowledgeable staff. I told them what type of vehicle I needed and the rental agents not only helped me make my reservation but also guided me through the process and fine print of renting, something important to me as a first-time renter.

If I recall correctly, I believe I was assisted by a manager named Doug. Very helpful.

I had a wonderful stay here for my conference. Clean and sophisticated with helpful and courteous staff. I like the direct enclosed bridge walkway from the hotel to the Indianapolis Convention Center. I arrived late Sunday night from the airport and checkin was a breeze. It was hard to relax after such a long day on the road. I requested some camomile teabags from the room service and they promptly brought me 1 for each night! I enjoyed the nice views from my room on the 28th floor. I was close to the elevator but it was remarkably quiet and peaceful.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
My experience here is hit or miss. I've eaten here thrice. The first time was great. Excellent carnitas, very good refried beans, a tasty soup and outstanding chiles rellenos.

The second time, the pork enchiladas seemed like leftovers. The mole sauce was good, but room temperature and the enchiladas were soggy in places and dry in others. I guess it depends on who's preparing the food.

Third time - back to being pretty good. 

Maybe if you get there when they're busy, the food will be fresher. When it's good, it's very good and very reasonable.

I have been sitting on my eyeglass prescription, hunting for new frames.  Had gone to a couple of places and could not find anything so I thought I'd pull out YELP and I founf this place in South Reno.  Boom!  Found 2 pairs of frames that I had in my hand ready to do the deal.  

I was seen right away, but alas, found out that they are not covered by my insurance until April.  Boo hoo.

But I will be back in April.  Fast service, great selection.  The prices are far better than any other optical shop I've been in.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
2 week stay at this hotel.  The one thing about Marriot Hotels is that they have pretty much the same layout and no matter what city you are in, there is some sense of commonality.
Not too happy with the fire alarm tripping at 1 AM.  It was hard enough getting use to the time zone change.
And to top it off, in the morning there was a cockroach in the the bathroom.  But I was too tired to react or step on it.  I told it to go on it's merry way and not to hide out and come back to Reno with me.
I suppose this hotel met my needs for a place to stay close to work.  Not sure if this would be my choice of hotel for fun and games, Tennessee vacay.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
So far so bad......  2 hours since our reservation.  One hour since ordering.  We got our appetizers and they were good but NO water NO bread.  We are just sitting here waiting.....WHY?!?!?!  We are through our BYO wine, we are prolly going to get a PPA ticket b/c we had a 2hr spot.   Really disappointed so far.

UPDATE:  After getting our food, we all really enjoyed what we got.  The only snag was the pesto.  Very bland and dry.  The rest was great.  The owners were very sweet and apologized profusely about the wait.  It could have been handled better from the start, but we all have bad days.

We had our 6.5 month old puppy spayed at Bonnie Doon Vet Clinic on Wednesday, as our vet clinic does not do this. Dr. M Siddique did a thorough exam beforehand, and when we picked up our pup, she was happy and her lesion was minimal. She's healing well. All the staff were very friendly. The next day, the clinic manager, Ji Youn Lee called to check up on our pup and offer any helpful advice. It was a good experience, considering the circumstances. I would recommend your slay/neuter at this clinic for sure. 
Also, the clinic is the cleanest vet clinic I've ever been in, it was immaculate.

Cheerful, efficient crew at this Crew welcome you with smiles. I have the monthly pass for $31 so I don't wait in line making it easy in and out and you can use at any Crew Carwash. 

The facility is sparkling clean and the wash water seems cleaner than other Crews that I visit. My car comes out sparkling clean. They still offer complementary wipes and bags with your visit. 

They have vacuums for an extra fee for cleaning inside the car. I like that two people can vacuum at the same time with the vacs on both sides of the car. The vacuum is $2 for 8 minutes. 

The lines get longer later in the day so I always visit early.

It's a cold snowy day here in Philly aaaaaand of course, I trekked it all the way to my favorite pizza spot in the northeast. *cue krusty krab pizza song* 

Today was a really good mario's pizza day. My pizza was perfect in the way the crust was thin but not too crispy, the tomato sauce was flavorful and sweet, and the cheese was so deliciously ooey. I added all the essential flavors and spices to make my slice just right when it came out. As usual, their pizza was fresh out of the oven and ready to be chowed down, NY style ;)

Whatever you're doing, put it down and go to this place immediately. Get the homemade tacos. Get all of them and pick your favorite. They're amazing! These tacos are served in a homemade tortilla, each meat is perfectly cooked and not greasy, over spiced or anything bad. Each is served with cilantro, onion and a lime wedge which only brings out the flavor even more. Also, try their red or green hot sauces for extra kick and flavor. 

Ok so the decor is very much like a typical Mexican place, but very humble and not flashy. The staff was friendly! So happy to have a great place in Smyrna like this one!!! We will be back!!!!

We had a great dinner, we ordered a bunch of dishes from the menu and shared them all. We loved every dish we tried except for our last one which was the grouper cheeks, it was still a decent dish but the flavors were not there for us like the other dishes. The lamb was incredible and was one of my favorites of everything we tried. The Foie gras was also super amazing. The atmosphere is great and service is impeccable. They have beer/wine only no liquor drinks which was fine with us. Great place in seminole heights.

I am giving this place 3 stars mostly because of the bad service we received. Our server was not nice and completely ruined our fun. We waited 1 hour for a table and then finally get seated and we are all happy and excited and our server is mean. Really not cool. 

The tacos were good, my favorite was actually the cauliflower which is pretty different but that one had the most flavor. Chorizo was ok and the Mahi Mahi was good. 

Plantain appetizer was ok, nothing special and their guacamole was also ok, neither were great. 

Drinks were rather pricey, service was not great but the tacos were good.

I used to love this car wash. However, when I visited this week, their prices had doubled! I figured I'd give it a try and hope the service would match the price. I'm disappointed sm to say it didn't. 

The employees spent quite a bit of time on my car, and I'm very happy with the vacuum job. That said, there were tar deposits all over the side panels, no one even tried to wipe the spotty wax off the windshield, and the mirrors and inside of the windshield are now covered in a streaky, oily film. I won't go back.

Came to treat my husband to a sushi fix and left rather disappointed. We were the only other customers in the building and it took quite some time to get our food which was rather bland and lacked freshness.

 We ordered (along with sushi bar) a cucumber salad (not bad), a vegetarian roll, and the teriyaki chicken dinner which came with mere morsels of overcooked chicken with a glaze thrown on. We got the fried banana and green tea ice cream to split, the banana was far too ripe and the green tea ice cream was like a tinted vanilla. 

Service was friendly but not very knowledgeable of menu items and the sushi cooks look miserable and in pain.

Not a very nice HIEX. Rooms were dated and bed was old. The tv was a flat screen but no hi def channels. The area where it is located is a little shady looking. Especially with the comfort inn right next door that shares a parking lot. 

The night I stayed there it was not very full. I lost Platinum status this year (soon to get back) but am currently Gold.  I asked for an upgrade to a king but front desk said their policy is to upgrade only Platinum members. No issue with that just good to now if you are IHG gold.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Everything was okay until the end. I finished eating my food, closed up, I put a napkin over my drink, and went to go handle something real quick with my flight. I wanted to come back for alcohol and some snacks but she gave up my seat to someone else. I walked around the bar to find another seat and there wasn't another seat available. So I asked my waiter Sarah if she gave up my seat. She said yes, you were all done with just a water sitting. Simple bar etiquette states napkin over drink means the customer is coming back. However, she just assumed I was all done.

Breaux Mart is a small local grocery store. Prices are comparable to other grocery stores and if you hit a sale you may just get a big bargain. 

They have a hot food bar and a salad bar that looks really good and is 7.99 a pound. #notimetocook

The vegetables and fruit look fresh and are displayed very nicely. 

The fall and Halloween decorations are really nice this time of year. #gotobreauxmart

There is a nice deli also with a variety of meat and cheese. 

Ok you can't be in the New Orleans area and not have alcohol. The entire center section of the store has all of your alcohol needs. #nolaencouragesdrinking

The service is really rude, waiter just reached over my girlfriend's shoulder to grab the soybean bottle to refill, when he came back, he just left it on the table like without say anything like we are air. So we stopped him and said this is inappropriate, you should say something like can I take this bottle. And he said "This is my job, what's you expect me to do, oh my god?".
Are you kidding me, he said OMG to us like we did wrong. So I complained this to another waiter, he just like I will talk to him, that's it, nobody take this seriously.
Okay, fine, good luck shogun, this will be my last time here, worst experience ever.

Wow!! Went here on Saturday night! The place was packed! Had a reservation for 9pm and said we could be seated a little earlier. We tried getting drinks at the bar and the bartenders we just rude.. Said that they would get out orders and never did! We told the hostess and we sat down in their "lounge" area and they finally sent us a server! Anyways best part of this place is the food, hands down!! We shared the Brussel sprouts, the buffalo cauliflower, pretzel bread and the ravioli. It was amazing. I'm definitely coming back but, hopefully next time I get better service while waiting for my table!!

Do you want to read what I have to write for you today?

The breakfast is good in the past today. Hard boiled eggs, dice them up, add hot sauce, a spoon full of gravy, and all of it in a plastic bowl. For your second course, get hungry, because it's omelette time with six pieces of bacon. Make sure to get an extra napkin to soak up the grease. To complete the balance, the cheese croissant and cinnamon roll were not up to par. Take a good banana, orange, and two yogurts for your lunch and enjoy the bailout today. Have a good day today.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Adorable little cafe in the middle of Citrus Park Mall. Delicious coffee and a mean espresso here made fresh to order. They even have seating in the middle of the mall next to their station, which provides a little respite from the hustle and bustle of the mall.

For those of you who like to enjoy a little snack while you enjoy your beverages, they have a nice selection of desserts and sweets as well to go with your drinks. 

Nice touch to get away from the usual starbucks at the mall when you need a pick me up.

Having H-Mart just below your restaurant where fresh ingredients are always available helps this restaurant provide really good and fresh sushi.  The fish is fresh and the rice is the right consistency and flavor.  

I would say that the portion size is pretty big and the hand rolls are a little bigger then I am used to, however the different flavors and sauces that they provide are delicious. 

Don't expect a great seating and ambience unless you like the cafeteria style seating in the best food court in town :-)

Buyer beware: "No commitments" means a $58 buyout fee if you want to cancel. Ordinarily I wouldn't mind so much, but that's PF's whole thing, right? No commitments? That's the whole reason I joined. 

Of course, no one ever mentioned this when I joined. I was under the impression I could cancel anytime, like it says on every single commercial and billboard you guys have out there. 

Blatantly lying to your customers is pretty crappy, I don't care how nice your gym is. I have no idea how you get away with this kind of false (or at least very misleading) advertising.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Used to shop there, will never go there again. Bought wine and a bunch of other groceries. The wine didn't make it into my cart. When I got home and put my groceries I realized it wasn't in my possession, immediately went back. Instead if making it right, rude mgr looked back through video, showed me video of the back of the bag boy  moving the wine, but it didn't really show him putting it in the cart. It was $18. Like I would lie about $18? I was treated like crap and will never go back. That's at least $500 a month gross they won't get from me.

Decided to stay here for my birthday this past year. Bumped up my opinion from 4 to 5 stars. I had a bath tub this time.. Sweet relief. One of my favorite things has always been a big luxurious bathroom and this one is great. 

One thing I'd like to add is that I had the delicious breakfast buffet downstairs. It was so good. Loved all the fresh fruit. 

This is the best place to stay when going to a Cardinals game, especially if you have seats on the first base side - VERY close walk between that stadium entrance and the hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
We LOVE Kampai. I lived in Hawaii for the first 22 years of my life and my boyfriend lived in Japan. We both agree this is the best sushi/Japanese restaurant in STL. We always get our standard favorite selection and then add an extra new dish each time we go. That being said, everything has been good. The sushi is fresh and flavorful. We go here all the time and the service is consistently GREAT! Honestly the best service out of any restaurant I have ever been to. I do not know the name of the waitress who always helps us but she is fantastic. 


I would give Kampai 10 stars if I could.

Hands down best sushi and Japanese in STL.

We got an amazing room with amazing views of the Riverwalk.

I would highly reccommend this place if staying in Tampa. The hotel is hip and new, they had a full bar with a DJ spinning during the weekend. Coffee is complimentary and the staff couldn't be nicer. 

We arrived wicked early and randomly our room was ready. This was a blessing seeing as though we got up at 2am for our flight.

A central location, close to everything and no matter which way you walk, you will find something interesting and/or delicious.

The pool overlooking the riverwalk and back patio is incredible. I cannot say enough good things about our stay here.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The pizza was surprisingly good. Why the 2-stars you ask? The woman inside (I assume the owner) was EXTREMELY rude. As I was observing the prep area, she angrily asked "what are you looking at?" Then she sneered at me!

I was caught so far off guard I was rendered speechless. 

On my ride home I came up with come- backs such as;
"I'm looking to see if your nasty a** washed your hands."
                      Or
"Damn B, why you all in my grill?"

Unfortunately, I'm not that swift under pressure.  

It took serious coaxing from my friend for me to try the slice.  It's a damn shame it was so good.  Its a damn shame......

This Starbucks is always slow in the drive through. Today, I waited 10 minutes (normal for the drive through). I ordered a latte, which is obviously a hot drink. For some reason the woman added ice to it. I saw that on the sticker and so I asked her if there was ice and she said no. I left the drive through and took a sip and the drink was cold. So I had to drive all the way back around the block to get back in line. The drink also had whipped cream when I asked for no whipped cream. I went inside and politely asked her to make me a new one without ice. She did, but with a very unfriendly attitude. No apology or anything. She must be new.

The place is inside of the sandwich place The Three Pickles which was surprising. I was kind of exited to try this place but I'm kind of disappointed. First the miso soup was served boiling hot, we had to wait 10min to drink it, then the food took pretty long to arrive for 2 rolls in a place with only 4 other customers, but I don't mind waiting for good food. The rolls were good but not amazing, and definitely not worth $16. We paid $40 without tips for 2 miso soup and 2 rolls. If it was amazing I would understand, but amazing is not the word. Good yes. But so overpriced...

Absolutely outstanding service.  Stayed here for four days and received great tips on dining and things to do from the polite and friendly staff.  

Four members come to mind that deserve mention.... Kenisha and Danielle were always polite and greater us at breakfast. 

Kendra McGee and Flojo Zantt were always pleasant and fun to see she coming back in at the end of the night. 

People make the place... And there are good people here. Now let's see if we can get them to lower their bar prices to something more reasonable, for those of us who like a night cap.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
What's not to like about this place? The food is good, I am an Arizona native and I'd put this place near the top of my list for Tex-Mex that I've come across in the mid-west. The chips came out to our table warm every time they were replenished. The salsa is a little plain, but I'm assuming that's just so that they have a broader appeal to the average stl resident. We also caught the tail end of happy hour, so we got the $3 frozen margaritas, which were good, but I prefer them with a tiny bit more kick. 

All in all, this place has great food, in a clean atmosphere, but falls just short of that 5th star.

Cute & Trendy hipster vibe inside the place with unusually interesting flavors. They boast all natural ingredients (no high fructose corn syrups,etc.) which was the draw for us. I sampled about 6 flavors ranging from a very subtle vanilla bean to a tart lambic ice cream with no dairy. We went with the dark rum chocolate (rich flavor) & the brown butter brittle. I plan to go back and sample some more flavors. They serve it in a way where you can get 2+ flavors. For example, the small is $6 & consists of 2 scoops (real scoops, not oversized ones) & you get 2 of the same ice cream or 2 different flavors.

Stopped by for drinks and an appetizer, so my experience is limited but even from that limited experience I can tell that......The place is expensive!!!!!!!!!!!!
3 beers, 1 glass of wine, 1 iced tea, 1 club soda (they don't have normal sparking water....) and 1 appetizer (including taxes and tip): 75$???????
The appetizer was not great....the bell peppers had so much garlic that we couldn't eat them, the Parmesan was ok (after all it is a cheese, comes in a package) and literally 1/2 grilled artichoke split in 2...

This is the absolute worst Baskin Robbins ever. Ive been three times. The first time, they were out of bananas for the banana royale. The second time, service was terrible. Employees stood around talking while people waited to be served. Then I was told they were out of fudge. I wasn't told until AFTER my ice cream was made. The last time I went (2 weeks later) they were still out of fudge and this time also out of lids. Now if you are out of lids, you should tell people that before they order! Also, how are you out of fudge for two weeks?!  I completed the survey on the receipt once and requested a follow up. It never happened.

This is a price performer. Good solid food served by friendly waitresses. Hang with an old timer at the counter to take it up a notch. 

Those posts that warn you about the neighborhood or proclaim their misgivings about eating in a rough neighborhood have never ventured beyond their suburban safe houses into the real world. Real people eating real food in a real neighborhood - That's Three Coins Diner. You have nothing to fear here other than your own worries and insecurities. 

Stop by three coins any time. You'll be glad you did.

This is one the better A&W locations in the city. They have some good staff that don't have serious attitudes. The breakfast can be  pretty good for a fast food place. The eggs are cracked fresh unlike the fake eggs at other places. They will make them to your preference of scrambled, over easy, sunny-side-up etc. The toast and bacon are decent. Coffee refills are free. There seems to be many regulars that come by and reminisce about the old days at A&W when girls on roller skates served the burgers to the trays on the doors of the old cars.

This is the former Adam's Mark hotel in St. Louis.  The location is great, the views from the roof-top pools are spectacular, the rooms are spacious, and the mattresses are hard as rocks!

Don't get me wrong, I like a firm mattress, this was ridiculous.  My fiancee, who prefers a softer mattress, woke up in agony when housekeeping came pounding on the door at 7:00am!  The decor was also quite dated, and I referred to it as 'old school snooty'


We would have to think long and hard about coming back here without some significant improvements.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Service is nice and the area is clean. Photos on here are clearly not taken by customers, but I do think they are pretty representative of the hotel. I'm quite annoyed that they skimped on giving lotion because it is quite dry here and I forgot mine. Also, it's  $2.50 for bottled water??

The restaurant in the hotel is a bit pricey, but at least it is good. Still not quite worth the price, but it is worth the per diem. 

Pool was a bit dirty, but I liked that it was open til 11pm.

Had no issue with my room, nice and clean. Lots of nice and bright lights for the night time. Iron leaked water, but worked. 

All in all, good stay
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice...you will not. 

It was cheap? I paid more than I wish I would have. 
It was good? Not really. 
It happened? Yes. 

I just can not find positive adjectives for CWP's pizza. If you like dough and sauce and cheese, these are certainly the ingredients. Flavor takes a back seat, unfortunately, and anyone looking to enjoy a meal in the CWE should look further than CWP. 

I do not have anything horrible to say about the establishment, but I would be lying if I rated this place average or anything higher and so I will lend my less than stellar review here.

I brought my son (13 months old) here for his first haircut and I could not be more pleased with the experience.  Jonathan, who has been cutting my husband's hair for years, did a fantastic job.  He was quick, efficient and, most importantly, treated my son with kid gloves. Being that this was his first experience with a haircut, I feel that it was positive and pleasant enough that he will not be afraid of future haircuts. And that is so important in a barber for me and my family.
Empire barbershop is clean, the staff is friendly, professional and inviting, and the pricing is extremely reasonable.

Not as delicious as the original location in Brooklyn, but pretty close to it.   I was happy to hear the franchise was hitting the Tampa Bay Area, An establishment with a supreme reputation and an even better "secret" sauce.  Oven fired pizzas are not heavily present in the North Tampa area, I'm especially pleased to have Grimaldi's only minutes from my neighborhood.  
The restaurant is fairly large and adequate for accommodating larger parties.  The bar is pleasantly inviting and splits up the dining room seating.  The Sangria was tasty but not their forte. Pizza was just how I wanted with extra sauce and perfectly layered mozzarella cheese.

This used to be Fess Parkers Red Lion Resort which had great service and went way out of their way to provide excellent service. How the mighty have fallen. Called for reservations was on hold for 15 to 20 min. Called the hotel and explained I wanted to make reservations. Was told to call back and be patient.  Called back waited 30 min on their reservation line, no answer. Called back spoke to the person at the front desk and still no help. He would not take a reservation. Omg his answer was well wait on hold if you want to stay here. Really. At least Motel 6 answers their phones will take a reservation and they even leave a light on.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This place is awesome, I don't know why I never gave a barbershop a try before. I'm very particular about my hair, I know my blades, I know what I want, and I don't want small talk. This is very much a guys place, great music, beers if you want it, awesome atmosphere. Justin (Knux) cut my hair for the first time a few weeks ago, it was the greatest thing ever. Having my hair cut with a straight razor over a blade was not only refreshing, the cut was so much better and didn't leave me to come back sooner. Getting my second cut today, it's been a month, usually I have to get it cut every 3.5 weeks.

What can I say - subway is subway.  Since it is a chain there is a consistency in the quality of the ingredients and the selection. So in my opinion the only variance between different subways are their location and their staff.  The staff here is friendly and keeps a very long line moving right along.  They are always pleasant, fast and efficient.  This location has a large college crowd as do most places in this area with the proximity of Webster university.  So if you are in Webster and want a subway, give this one a try!!!

Diet? I'd rather have tacos!

My family has relocated to the south side, so I'm always on the hunt for a good place to meet and try new things with them. My cousin was on the prowl for Mexican and neither of us had tried this place so we thought we'd give it a spin! Of course we got margaritas because...come on, it's a Mexican restaurant! And though a bit sweet, they were the perfect Friday evening wind down drink. I got the arroz con pollo (my Mexican go to!) and it was cooked to perfection! 

This place is bigger than it looks so bring the crew, there's plenty of space!

Justin has created a wonderful little place that was perfectly needed on Georgia Street!

With big competitors like Starbucks and H&C right down the street, Georgia St Grind has done a great job of setting themselves apart! Justin is always so friendly and makes a point to chat with every customer, a truly customized experience! I'm a HUGE fan of the chai latte, it definitely is my favorite in the city and a special treat each time I order. 

Remember, this isn't the place for a meeting or sit down coffee experience, it is a drop in and grab a cup of Joe to-go. Just what downtown needed and super excited to keep coming by!

Popped in for a walkin pedicure.  I usually plan ahead and try to make an appointment at my usual spot, but this was a last minute - lets see if I can find a spot type day!!

Glad I found LUXE - they were accomodating and I didn't even wait!  I ended up choosing a jelly soak deluxe pedicure - it had a few add-ons over the basic, but wasn't the most deluxe.  Overall it was a great choice and the polish looked great at the end I added on nail art to my big toes - the technician did a nice free style flower design

I liked how quiet and cozy this place was. The sushi was rolled in slightly bigger sizes which I loved and their menu had a good amount of options: bubble tea, vegetarian rolls, tempura ice cream. 
The service was friendly but the waiter had to come back to ask us a couple of things which could have been avoided if he wrote it down. It seems to be a family-owned smaller business which is always nice.

Overall, i'd come back bc of the convenience of the location and still a very good option for a little date night.

Not sure how this one got passed the filters, but Broad St Car Wash and Broad Street Car Wash are one in the same.  

They both do a very good job cleaning my vehicle of all the ashiness that covers the sheet metal (polymer) after snow and salt get finished turning the wheels into a ghost. 

If I had to choose between one or the other, I would probably choose Street, as St implies sainthood, and I doubt that this "Shine On Line" operation is on the short list for canonization. 

Although, there are times I thank the Almighty for creating this automated wonder of the world.

Made a return visit after an hiatus of almost 2 years, and was pleasantly surprised to find the house redecorated with more comfortable seating and brighter lights. 

Accompanied by a teenager and his mom, I again realized that American fast burgers are very popular.  I tried one of their discount double burgers and fries, and found that while they were no match for Five Guys or that ilk, they were still decent and satisfying.  Watching the young guy wolf down his Double Baconator was eye opening. He was totally into it.  Oh, and the fries was ample and crispy.  

Time for an upgrade. 

No apologies!

The was a reason why this BK was practically empty when I stopped in for a quick breakfast the other day.  

The Biscuit for my sandwich was hard and too small to enclose its contents.  It appeared to be a tube biscuit that had been made earlier and left in the open air to dry out, and then microwaved just before sale.  It rehardened quickly and was a crumbly mess to eat.  Just not very good, despite the fact that the rest of the ingredients seemed fresh.  

Given the competition across the street, it is difficult to see how this place survives. Maybe their burgers are better, but I won't be back to find out.

I came here late afternoon to meet up with a friend and to study and I did not regret it. This place has a really refreshing environment with store front windows that allow copious amounts of light to radiate into the front of the store. I love the location where it's at in Old City  but it seemed rather busy when I got there. They ran out of cold brew, which was the first thing I tried to order, so I got their iced latte instead. I loved how light the taste was especially because I'm personally just not a huge fan of an overwhelming, heavy coffee taste. Perfect for a day with great weather.

Really good wood-fired pizza! I'm excited this place has come to to our neighborhood. We ordered takeout and it took all of 15 minutes to walk there and it have it coming out of the oven and ready for us to take home. The flavors were on point but I will say the bottom crust was a little too soggy and my toppings just fell off which was kind of a bummer but I'm hoping that gets worked out. I also think it would be nice if they could list their pricing online. Other than that, it is really tasty and the customer service is great! Welcome to the neighborhood!

#189

Yes, it's just a Dunkin Donuts. This location is ok, they don't mess your order up. All their donuts taste the same. Is it me? The best thing in DD are the bagels.
Today I went in to try the Cronuts which DD does not call Cronut. They are Croissant Donuts. The only thing resembling a croissant is that you could pull it apart in layers. Tasted like any other DD spud. It was kinda cakey but nothing resembling a croissant. Individually boxed and priced at $1.99 each....I don't think so. Gimme that bagel instead.

When hunger strikes and you're about to start a marathon of running around doing chores what's the answer? My guilty pleasure, Mickey D's filet o fish. Always good. This particular location is an extra busy one, cars always seem to be wrapped around it but the drive thru was fast and efficient and I was on my way in a jiffy. The staff was great, everyone was happy to see you and it showed. The coke was cold, the fries hot and the fish sandwich had just enough tarter squeezing out, perfect. This is one of the best run McD's I've ever seen.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
This is the location that obviously didn't get customer service training. This is a super busy spot but hey, it could be much better. Don't expect any hello, thank you, come again, don't come again, get lost, or whatever. This is exactly what Ray Kroc had in mind when he opened Mickey D's up....blank stares. Time for Ronny boy to send one of his inspectors to check this location out.
Having said all that, the egg, sausage and cheese McGriddle  is a nice breakfast alternative. Very tasty but not cheap at over $3.00, but they are good. 3 Stars and that's pushing it.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Has everything you need to get a great workout but there are too many simple improvements that need to be made. There's always a constant stench next to the  30-45lb dumbbells. There is a severe lack of clips for olympic weights. Most of the pegs for pulley machines are detached. There are leaks in the ceiling when it rains. Not too much for air circulation. Only half of the bolted down benches are in front of mirrors. And the benches that are bolted down are pretty basic none of them are fully adjustable. The rest of the machines are all pretty old but work fine for the most part, some could use some lubricant.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Went for a late brunch today with two close friends. I made a reservation on open table, and we were seated as soon as we walked in. Service was perfect. I ordered the buffalo chicken biscuit- which was excellent. The gravy has sausage and the buffalo sauce has just enough kick! My two friends each ordered burgers, which they devoured so I'm going to take an educated guess that the burger doesn't disappoint. We also ordered red velvet french toast stuffed with cream cheese filling for the table. It was delicious! Just the right amount of filling and sweetness to balance out the meal. Highly recommended, and I will definitely come back.

I rented a suite here for my birthday (about $300 for the night) and had a fabulous time...until I realized how thin the walls are!

Let's just say - my neighbors had a very *exciting* morning and would not stop having a *exciting* morning. The Walls were so thin that I had to go into the other room to continue sleeping to not hear all the *excitement*

Also - parts of the floor were sticky and didn't seem mopped when we arrived, that is a little disappointing.

I wish I had tried the breakfast (I love complimentary breakfast) but I was just to ill in the morning to try to figure out where food was located
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
One of the few low key good bars with good food I will miss in Reno! Love the fish tacos!

There is a dearth of bars that aren't noisy and obnoxious in the south Reno area. 

I hate sports bars in general because sometimes I just want good conversation while I enjoy a good drink - Bistro 7 offers the latter!

Both Will and Case are great bartenders and fix solid cocktails with the ingredients at hand. If you are looking for higher end bourbons this isn't the place because after all it primarily is a wine bar.

Given that it IS a wine bar, I'm so impressed that I could get a decent cocktail here! Thanks guys!

Used to go here all the time for great sushi.  However, one day as I was getting some left-overs boxed one of the boxes they gave me had a dead cockroach in it.  Immediately I felt disgusted and expressed concern to the front desk/staff.  However, instead they tried to "reason" with me and tell me to ignore it, followed by random angry Japanese being yelled directed at me, and I'm not one to make a scene so I kindly said I will not be returning.

If you're not grossed out however, the food and place are GREAT!  Just hard to get that image out of your head after a while =/ yuck

My husband calls this restaurant a "little hidden gem."  Located on the first floor of the Hilton Hotel, this is a great place to go for a great meal before a baseball game. Because it is a Hilton, you know the food will be good. 

This time we decided to share the wings with lemon pepper sauce.  Very tasty appetizer.  After that, we shared the turkey sandwich (I forget get the name but it had club in it) with French fries. It was a great sandwich and one a half along with some fries filled us up nicely.  Our waitress was attentive but not overbearing  

Would I come back here again?   Yes definitely.

Gio's is an Italian restaurant within walking distance of Busch Stadium so it is a great place to grab a lunch or early dinner before the game. 

We walked in and were seated right away and our drink order taken.  After looking over the menu and hearing about the specials, I chose the taco salad and Majordomo opted for the wedge salad. (Don't worry. He got a hot dog later at the ballpark.). 

The wedge salad was good and my taco salad was good also although I would have liked to have had a little cheese on it.   Both of us were members of the clean plate club. 

Would I come back here?  Yes, when we are down here for a game.

As a LA girl who is a self-proclaimed foodie, Jason's Toridasu was a pleasant break from our college dining hall. Jason is very welcoming and just an all-around cool bro. He offers superb menu suggestions, despite his salad diet (he lost five pounds, aka he looks good)! His miso soup is by far my favorite on the Mainline--not too salty or too watery. I had the spicy salmon roll, which was pretty good, not mind-blowing amazing by LA standards, but better than that of other Mainline sushi options. I will definitely return!

This a Canal's with a moderate variety of alcohol - definitely better than your nearby, independent no name liquor mart, but there are Canals with an even more extensive selection than this.

The prices are typical Canal's prices - the cheapest you can find. 

The staff has always been unnecessarily unfriendly to me. I get this often as a young girl from older women, and the staff here is composed of older women. (It's not my fault you are wrinkly, stop treating me like a criminal.) The men are much more friendlier to me.

Overall, three stars for average.

Not sure how this hotel even scored 3 stars. I'd give it a .25 star if I could, for having a decent lobby, everything else was lacking. 

First of all - there is no bottled water anywhere in the hotel. Not even the standard bottle of water they leave in the room. Nope. Were dying of thirst all night. No vending machines either. The AC was running all night. The pillows were midget sized, and the water in the shower took 20mins to heat up. Also, I could hear every move, breath, and door open from the room next door. So intimate.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I ate in at the Moorestown location with my coworker on a Sunday night.

It was pretty empty, which I didn't mind. The Mexican wrestling masks kinda freaked me out. The decor in general is all over the place. I was confused.

I had enchiladas, cornbread, and a mango juice. 

The cornbread... OMG. Super buttery, and delicous. Please, please PLEASE try it if you go.

I love Mexican food. So I can pinpoint authenticity, or commercialized Mexican food when I taste it. These enchiladas were not authentic, but it was a great stab at it.

I would go back, and explore the menu some more.

This is amazing. The owners, Jason and Cricket are so personable and awesome. Started with the scallops- amazing, and the short ribs-Whoa. Get them both. Then to the Middles- got the foglio pasta and the bacon meatballs. The homemade pasta itself was the best I've ever had, the polenta under the meatballs was like a heavenly cloud. And for dessert we got the black pepper pound cake, which other than the scallops, was my favorite dish. You can't go wrong, everything is magical and wonderful. I can't say enough good things. Wow.

I got my car washed here for the first time today. While it was a good car wash I was disappointed that the vacuums at the end of the automated wash cost extra. The cost of the car wash itself was eight dollars. The cost to use a vacuum afterwards was an additional dollar, and machines only take quarters. Unfortunately, I did not have quarters on me, and there was no one available to help me get change for a dollar, so I left without getting the inside of my car clean. I have seen similar car washes in the area that cost less and include vacuuming.

1. Variety
2. Fresh
3. Trendy ambience

Consumed: (In order of preference)
Lost Rainbow
Dancing Vampire
Miss Sake Bomb
Spicy Tuna Crunch
Shrimp Tempura
Alaskan Roll

I love sushi and hailing from Seattle, where there's always fresh seafood, this place is comparable! The sushi was very fresh and I really liked the variety of choices. The Lost Rainbow was my favorite. The texture and flavor was top notch. Dancing Vampire came closely second with the crunchiness and kick of chili flavor. Mmmm, I'm really inspired to embark on a sushi making adventure.  

Also, their rolls come out in sixes, go in a group of 3 or 6--perfect for sampling.

When I went to the bathroom during my most recent visit to Undertow, a girl who was walking out said to me, "My advice: hover!"  This pretty well explains this spot, which is what I would call a "beach dive."  The drinks are cheap, and although it's not the classiest bar on the beach, the deck above the bar offers some excellent views of the ocean.  The service was a bit slow while I was here, but I've stopped by for three years in a row while on vacation at St. Pete Beach, so I would say that it's worth checking out!

Ordered the old fashioned from this place and some wings with two different sauces. The pizza was pretty solid, different then the normal Sicilian that I am use to but I would get it again. The wings were okay we got zesty garlic and the garlic parm and both were alright, with the zesty garlic being a good deal better. Wings themselves were not that bad; decent meat on them and maybe a little more fried then I like but not terrible. Overall this place seems pretty solid to get some take out from. They were quick on delivery and food was all A-Okay!

Came in for lunch and had their 3-roll lunch special for $13.  This also comes with a choice of soup or salad (I went for the salad).  I also ordered the yellowtail/scallion, eel/cucumber, and red snapper rolls.  The red snapper and yellowtail were very good, with lots of fish.  However, there was just something missing from all three rolls.  Maybe it's because I really enjoy the bigger rolls with lots of fish combinations.  But, these were good enough that I will definitely come back for dinner one night to try their specialty rolls.

FOOD - Gotta be honest, I think I just ordered the wrong things here because the fish in the counter glass looks amazing.  I ordered the 3 rolls for $11.95.  I got eel and cucumber, spicy yellowfish with apple, and the asashi roll.  I enjoyed the spicy yellowfish but in general, I was underwhelmed by the sushi.  I also usually order "specialty" rolls that usually include a lot more fish.  

SERVICE - Great.  We brought wine and saki.  They warmed up the saki for us and poured it into proper saki serving pieces (I don't know the proper wording).  Food was brought out in decent timing.  

CONCLUSION:  Would go back and try different food.

Suffice to say that the grenades are a must! Bartenders here were pretty cool! My friend spilled her drink and they made her another at no cost! What an awesome and nice service. I had other drinks that were made really well. I left feeling just right after 3-1 deal. This location in particular is a bit bigger so they have live music you can listen to. They also have an awesome upstairs area with a great view. Overall, great experience with awesome service. Talented band too. Came in on a Wednesday afternoon, not too packed.

Americanized Chinese made to order. Don't take American express though. Run of the mill Quick in-and-out Chinese eatery. All of the other places are similar to this one, same paper menu, same menu board with the same pictures, and same meal combo deals. If you're looking for good Chinese food you're better off going to a sit down restaurant, but if you want some quick, hot, and vaguely Chinese food these places are fine. General Tso chicken is better and sweet and sour chicken, and get lo mein instead of the bland fried rice.

There are a lot of different make your own salad/pizza places around the city. But I haven't found a place that allows unlimited toppings for a fixed price. I've probably been here more times than I've been to the gym since moving to Philly and each time I get more than 10 different veggies, a meat, and at least 3 types of cheeses on my salads. Thank you snap kitchen for enabling me to continue my gluttonous habits at an affordable price. ily

FYI: This location doesn't sell packaged meals like the other ones do - only fresh made salads and pizzas.

I used to be a HUGE fan of this place but over this past year, the quality of service has changed a lot. A simple order can take an unnecessarily long and at my last visit - the guy making my salad was focused on everything else but my salad. The quality of the ingredients is also at most mediocre. I got a grain bowl and the quinoa has an odd smell to it, so that will be my first and last time getting a grain bowl from here. I think a pizza covers some flaws up because it is cooked, but it's hard to hide the lack of flavor/ freshness in a salad/ grain bowl.

There's an old saying: "you get what you pay for". If only that was true for Sushi Shop. The prices are just a bit cheaper than a sit down restaurant but the quality is  fit for a shopping mall. Jiro this is not. 

We ordered the chicken meal. Eight tiny pieces of what I hope was mostly chicken. They messed up the sashimi order and gave us the wrong stuff. Ten hours later and no one had food poisoning so that's good news. 

It must be owned by the government since it took 25 minutes to cut raw fish. 

I recommend going to mikado or japonais or ichiban instead.

How the mighty have fallen. Giuseppe sold this place and it's been downhill ever since. Their pizza is decent - beyond that, they altered the recipes for all of the other items on their menu, and in some cases they flat out ruined them. Seriously. It takes a pretty bad eatery to mess up chicken noodle soup, but congratulations, guys, smashing success. 

It's truly heartbreaking to see a place like this that's been in business for decades swirl down the drain such as this. And advertising cheap beer isn't going to help. Go to Tosco's instead. There's a reason why they have a full parking lot on a Monday and Via Roma is dead on a Friday night.

It was just ok. Our waitress was Savannah. She seemed out of it. I don't know if she's shy, having a bad day, or hungover...but took way too long to get greeted, get drinks, and we had to ask for refills after our food came. We got the pick 5 which was great. We devoured it. I got the parmesan chicken and it was kind of sour/bitter tasting. Hostess stand acted like we were a huge inconvenience, and the restaurant was barely half full. There were 6 of us. Shouldve just pushed two tables together and been ok with it or put us at a big table. Womp.

Food is ok. Our service was really, really bad. My mother was in town visiting and we had to flag our waitress down to get our check. Waitress I noticed had been double sat, but was too busy giving the hostess a dirty look rather than asking us what we wanted. She was so short with me and my mom then overly flirtatious with my boyfriend. (I guess she thought he would be paying and not my mom HAHA) I ordered a margarona and it was AWESOME. Food took a long time to arrive and we were full of tortilla chips so couldn't enjoy it much. They were pretty busy and I'll be back but hope to get another waitress..

Downtown location is a 4, room itself is a 3.5, ballrooms/conference rooms are a 4. The actual hotel rooms in this hotel are a 3.5 because they are on the small side, the bathrooms are tight on space and could use updating on the shower tile and door frame (mine was peeling which meant the door couldn't fully close - this was fine since I was staying alone).

The lady working at reception was really nice and gave me a room with a beautiful view of the arch, the trade off was that it was quite far from the elevator. So keep that in mind when you are choosing your room location!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This is one of my favorite Subway restaurants. It's immediately obvious that the people who work here take great care of their customers because they greet the regulars by name and ask after their families.  People are happy to come back again and again because of how they are treated. Although the workers here don't know my name they recognize I'm a regular and I'm always greeted with a smile. They make great sandwiches too! 
Definitely 5 stars for customer service which says a lot for this Subway! Keep up the good work!

The place looks nice, friendly staff. The menus need replacing and are taped together. But the food is great. Got the Oishi Roll and would recommend it. The chicken katsu was good too, though the katsu sauce tasted a bit like BBQ sauce which wasn't bad, just different. The miso soup and gyoza were both excellent. Also got the non-specialty spicy salmon roll and that was good also--very fresh--but not spicy. Maybe they just gave us the regular one instead. Was still good, though. I'll definitely be going back.

Frozen yogurt, aka "froyo" is a fun treat for people of all ages. The price for froyo depends on what you put in your cup because it is based on weight. There are typically plenty of toppings and flavors for froyo, including chocolate, strawberry, mango, and original tart. This location changes out their flavors at least once a month I believe. My favorite is when they have the more fruity flavors such as taro froyo. 

Toppings also come in variety. Toppings include mochi (my favorite), fruit balls (ones where the ball pops with fruity syrup when you bite into), brownies, chocolate candies, and even fresh fruit. You can't go wrong with froyo!

I have been here a couple of times, and I'm surprised that there are such mixed reviews.  I'm not sure what people are expecting at this casual pizza joint, but I think they have it nailed.  

Each time I've gone the service is very good, but I must say that could be because it's never been as busy as some of the others reviewers are commenting.  The pizza is always delicious and comes out pretty quickly.  One time my friends and I had a conversation with the manager and he bought us a round, which was super nice!

A full plate is a charming little place. I don't get why people are writing about "hipsters" and "vegans" in their review. Obviously these kinds of people will eat here, this is northern liberties, get real. Anyway, there's great food options for both vegans and non vegans. I really like the vegetarian pulled pork. The sauce is great. Their wraps are great too. As far as service goes, it does get chaotic if busy. However I've been there several times when busy and I've never waited to come across bad service. It's BYOB which is cool but because it's so tight and busy I wouldn't say you'd want to sit and drink there for long.

My boyfriend has had his hair cut from this place twice (though I'm usually the one that has to book his appointment for him), but he's seemed pretty happy with his service the two times he's been. We live around the neighborhood and decided to give this place a try. Very nice and clean on the inside, and the stylists and receptionists always seem nice and friendly. They also play great music and offer you a drink during your service as well (and by drink, I mean some big boy whiskey). Boyfriend always gets just a haircut and pays $30 for it (but don't forget to tip, ladies and gents). Thanks, ModMen!

Been craving for their lavender flavor ice cream so we head over here after our brunch. I got the lavender and salted caramel ice cream, so delish. They only thing I have a complaint about was that our server didn't wear gloves when scooping our ice cream. When he was grabbing a spoon for my ice cream, the spoon slide from the ice cream and touch his hand that was holding my ice cream cup and he still handed to me without asking if I'm ok with it or he can replace it. At a time like this, we all should be taking precaution to stop the spread of Covid.

A friend of mine posted that she got her macaroon king cake over here so on my way to a parade I decided to go and grab one but they were out of it so I end up getting a lemon blueberry chantilly king cake. The King Cake has blueberry preserves and lemon curd filling topped with a whipped cream cheese icing topped with fresh lemon slices and sliced almonds. The king cake was good but not compared to my favorite Chantilly King Cake at Bywater Bakery. I really didn't care too much for the brioche-style king cake. It taste kind of doughy. I like mines soft. But each to his own...

Worse customer service. My nephew who is a picky eater wanted Spaghetti so we stopped to grab some while doing some shopping. We were the only ones in line. Only two workers. A black guy who only gave us a look but never knowledge us. The white guy who was busy doing something and finally looks up and asked if we need help.
