I gave him my order and he got the other guy to take our order. Not once did he smile or even thanks me throughout our interaction with each other when he gave me my food or receipt. I would never come back with that kind of service. They were not even busy...smh

I've checked in a few clothing items here once and I happen to like this laundromat. Yelpers had great reviews for Modern Laundry and I based my decision on people's positive experience.

I actually believe Modern Laundry is more equipped than most laundromats. This location has wifi. The vending machines have a variety of well-known snacks and beverages. There's a media section that appears to be designated for children. The section features tv programming for children. 

There is always more than one attendant on duty. I remember the staff returning my missed call within minutes!
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Starbucks is one of my favorite places to go. Usually I go to the Smyrna location which is rarely a bad experience. I have tried the Mt Juliet location at least 5 or 6 times now and it's a bad every time.. so today I ordered a "venti caramel cloud macchiato"... 
she never told me my total.. and when I look over to my fiancé handing me my coffee I got a "tall plain caramel macchiato".. didn't get a receipt or anything. Not happy. I would have been more understanding if they were busy..but we were literally the only people there.

For fifty five a person you get wine, which we quickly titled welch's and then 5 courses. The appetizers were bland and poorly fried (turn up the heat on the cooking oil).  The soup was so bland we began adding parmesan cheese. The entrees were better, slightly more flavorful, as was some of the pasta in the pasta trio. Although the marinara was plain. The overall experience is like stepping back into time, with the plates from Niagara Falls and the endless pink (walls, bathrooms) and the accordion player with his straw hat. One of those places you go to once that makes you thankful for,good company.

Located right next to the convention center this is a great location and good hotel if you need something near downtown.  There is a full service Starbucks in the lobby so that is a huuuge plus.
Why did I only give this hotel 3 stars?

1.  When you order room service and request no cheese on the hamburger and it shows up with cheese on it AND the receipt even has typed right on it "no cheese" you have to assume the kitchen just doesn't care and the order wasn't checked before delivery.

2.  There is no easy self parking.  I wish I had known this as I would have booked elsewhere.  I hate having to valet my car.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
5 star chicken!  Good food. 2 star dining. Maybe 1 Star.  Not a great place to dine in. 

Absolutely love their chicken!  Love love their chicken!  

So I get the food to go!  Today they included a roasted chili!  Yum. Love the chicken. Nicely seasoned or marinated. Nicely cooked, like over a fire!  Love the salsa that comes with the chicken. Usually love the beans. Today there was too much water (juice). Tortillas are good. 

Ate everything before I could take pictures. I guess the next time. There will always be a next time...since I love their chicken!!!

Picked up a to go order and they didn't have the very best customer service even though they weren't packed. I was so excited to try this place because of all the reviews and the pictures, but I guess I'll try to original place or maybe no order to go? But that really shouldn't matter. Very skimpy on the fish and rice was SUPER dry (so dry that it was very hard to chew).

Update: currently sick in bed with food poising because of the sushi here. I didn't even finish my entire order since it was really hard to eat.

After driving by frequently my husband and I decided to give this place a try and we were impressed. The atmosphere was great (no TVs anywhere!) and the staff was friendly. They offered complimentary hummus and pita bread as well (not sure if it was a special or not). The pizzas were delicious with quality ingredients.

The only suggestion I would make is to leave the processed parmesan cheese on the table to fast-food pizza chains. The parmesan that came on our pizza was amazing, and I would much prefer they offer that instead of shelf-stable options on the table.

Having ate in and ordered delivery I will say that Kabuki Sushi doesn't score high on my list. While I think certain dishes are very good like the Gyoza, California roll, and the Hibachi entree; a lot of the other food I've tried isnt anything to write home about. The shumai is mushy and taste pre frozen. The miso soup is just ok. For the price, I hate when still feel quite hungry after spending close to $50 for 2. So I may come around again if im really desperate for the Hibachi entree but it won't be for a while yet.

Disappointment! The menu is very small & overpriced. My husband ordered steak tacos for $9 & they were tiny & nothing on them at all except the meat. And you don't get any sides. Also the women's bathroom smelled like something had died & they were trying to cover it up with too much air freshener. The male server was ok he really pushed the most expensive items on the menu. We won't ever go back to this place.
DO NOT go here if you want good Mexican & a larger selection of food. They say they are not "tex-mex" & therefore don't have burritos & quesadillas, etc.

Before I start, on food alone, I'd give this place 4 stars.  We shared the calamari and fig salad apps, gnocchi and hanger steak mains, and an affogato to finish.  Everything we ordered was tasty and came out quickly.  The portions were big too and we left stuffed.  The pricing was also very affordable.

The service wasn't bad, but wasn't great either.  It took a little while for our server to greet us after we were seated.  We also had to ask for water.  

Otherwise, this is a nice BYOB with great food.  I'd recommend to friends.

I saw the many ads in local Florida Chinese newspapers which is why a coworker and I stopped here during our lunch hour. Not sure what the hype is about, I suppose it's because Tampa doesn't have many authentic Chinese offerings (I'm from Orlando). 
We ordered the grouper casserole and the Singapore rice noodle. Both of which are normal staples of mine at other restaurants. The fish was soggy and the noodles were really soggy too. Not impressive. Combine that with the fact that it took us 20 minutes to get our food. Will try again, hope it's better next time.

These little burgers are always a better idea than they actually are. We ate here late night before heading back to the hotel. The drive through was packed. 

The burgers are simple. They have meat, cheese, onions, pickles, and bread. I'm not sure how they make them, but they always turn out soggy and not that great. 

Came here bc of the movie and honestly, the frozen ones you get at the grocery store are a better consistency. I recommend trying them for the experience, but I def will not be returning for seconds.

During Covid ordered takeout . A mixed tempura (shrimp and vegetable) appetizer, NOLA specialty roll and a basic tuna avocado roll. The food was ready when I arrived 30 minutes later. Staff were wearing masks and the food was nicely packaged. The restaurant is actually quite sizable and nicely decorated inside. The NOLA roll, containing tempura shrimp, snowcrab and spicy crayfish was substantial, fresh and tasty. The tuna avocado roll was simple and basic, but fresh. The tempura batter was a bit heavy and somewhat disappointing. The staff are friendly and I will return for more specialty rolls as the restaurant is conveniently located.

With a name like pizza delicious...well you expect it to be delicious. But I guess a name like Pizza Pretty Good isn't quite as catchy. 
It's not bad at all but not my favorite in town. The toppings they offer are non-inventive especially for vegetarians. The service is good and efficient though. And it was nice to see they added an outdoor seating area next door to bratz y'all. I just get mine to go though. 
One thing I noticed after left was they added a 20% tip to my order and I had tipped them as well so they got tipped VERY well. No idea why they tipped themselves for a walk-in takeout order of one pie. So that left me pretty salty.

This Italian restaurant was one of the best I have ever eaten at. The service was very prompt, and the waiter was very friendly in explaining the menu. The food portions were humongous, with a side pasta being enough for a second dinner. The Eggplant Parmesan was very flavorful, and the Eggplants were cooked to perfection. The Fettuccine Alfredo was amazing, with the Alfredo sauce having good consistency, and the pasta tasting fresh. The bread before the meal was also cooked well. Overall, I'd recommend to anyone looking for Italian food better than Olive Garden and reasonably priced.

The Eurotrash tasted nothing like Nutella, they might have to change the name to just plain old trash. Just kidding, but being serious, if you're looking for that Nutella indulgence, I do not recommend the Eurotrash. I'm giving it four stars because of the service and because even though it was flavorless, the ice cream was very creamy and my bf's order was pretty good...overall, cool place, will go back to try a different flavor. For now, I'm going to continue buying the Nutella jars and pretending it's ice cream.

Came here with a fellow Texan after finding a Groupon. It was great. They had a bunch of options and everything we tried was so good. Tender and full of flavor. Great drink options including sodas in bottles. 

I got a BBQ pork tamale, a chipotle beef, and a green chili chicken. I couldn't tell you which one was my favorite because they were all so good. And my friend and her son, who grew up with homemade tamales courtesy of her grandmother, also really liked the food. 

The restaurant itself was clean and the service was good. Overall a great place for lunch. You can also order in bulk for family gatherings.

The only thing I ever order here is the hot and sour soup. It is so delicious that I order the large and eat the whole thing. The large soup is less than 4 dollars. I think that is an absolute steal. It is always very busy so it seems like they have a large customer base. However, it is always very hot in there. I'm not sure how people actually eat in. The staff is quick but not very friendly. The location is very convenient. It is located a few doors down from Publix. It's very easy for me to pop in and grab my soup!

We had a reservation for a group of 9 at 5:30 PM on a Thursday. Our table was set and ready to go when we arrived and we were seated right away. It was not too busy but filling up fast.

We ordered drinks and the bruschetta and fried calamari appetizers which were delivered in a timely fashion. The appetizers were very tasty.

The group of us ordered a wide variety of entrees which were delivered in a timely fashion. Everything looked and tasted very good.

Overall this was a good experience and we were well taken care of.

One of my favorite places to get a manicure and pedicure.  I've tried places that are closer to me and I always end up coming back to here.  They always do a wonderful job and make me feel comfortable.  The girls here are super friendly and they have something entertaining on the TV.  They really spend the time to cut my cuticles and make them look perfect.  
During non-busy times it's easy to be a drop in, but during busy times is easier to make an appointment, that way you aren't waiting too long.  I even trusted them to do my wedding nails.

I remember Philly Magazine voted Franzone's Pizzeria as one of the best pizza places.  It won because of the sauce and since my favorite part of pizza is the sauce, I made it a goal to try Franzone's Pizzeria.  
When I finally got around to trying it, I loved it.  Franzone's has the best sweet sauce.  Since the pizza is mostly sweet sauce, it is easy to eat more than a couple of slices.  When I'm really hungry and I'm craving sweet sauce I get my pizza with pepperoni, so it is really filling.  
Franzone's Pizzeria is worth trying even if you just do it once.

I indulged in the Chocolate cake for a dessert. It was delicious.  I think my friends thought this was the best dessert after trying all the others. 

I have been to this restaurant many times. I am never disappointed.  I have indulged in the $2 Martinis for happy hour. They are delicious! I also like their half off menu items for happy hour.  I also enjoy everything they have to offer on the menu. I have had the pasta dishes, duck dish and many others and never left disappointed.  

I would recommend this place to anyone who is in the area or who has never tried. The owner also owns Bernini's down the street which is also a great choice.

Amazing spot for great drinks and live music. Yes I know you're in New Orleans and there's literally music everywhere you go but this place has good quality jazz and swing music. Small location so it can get pretty packed but its part of the whole experience here. We ordered a round of whiskey sours which has to be some of the best I've ever had in the world. Yes in the world. They just do it right here. I love that they'll also have some retro/vintage films playing in the background most of the time. 

Its worth checking out this place to get away from the crazieness of bourbon street. I come here every time I'm in town. Its a must for me.

I have tried lots of nail shops in Edmonton but never took the time to write a review. In all honesty none of them were worth it till now! 

This location is very new. The location is small but the place is so clean. My nail tech was so detail orientated and her tools were spotless. I feel sometimes reluctant to use fast drop in nail salons but this one is very well maintained. No nail dust insight. I got a gel removal, manicure and gel polish. My nail tech was so thorough and got every piece of cuticle and buffed/shaped my nails perfectly. I 

will not hesitate to go back in fact and rebooked for 2 weeks from now!

Food was not great. Went with my family party of 6, bill totaled over $1k  and the food came out cold!!! I literally reserved months in advance (late Sept 2019 for 12/30/19other than the actual gorgeous views in and outside of the restaurant nothing else was impressive. I think  if the Chef spent less time walking our food around the table than taking back to the kitchen to plate it and brought it back 10-15min later it prob would of been served warm and not cold!!! Not impressed at all other than again the view.

Just opened! Was going to go but ended up ordering takeout. The sushi here is good! About as good as Kei around the corner or Vic's downtown. Had the tri- color sushi entree (3 tuna, salmon, yellowtail) and the 3 roll dinner. Both came with miso soup or salad (as all sushi entrees should). Fish was very fresh and tasted delicious. 

Def fairer priced than Kei, which does not include soup/salad with their entrees. Also a bit more spacious with more modern decor.

Overall, another good sushi addition to the neighborhood- can never have enough good sushi!

I thought the Hyatt was supposed to be pretty nice. At least for the price, it should've been. My bathroom had pubic hair on the floor and in the tub, so I called the front desk and someone came up and cleaned it again, but all they did was push it around so I had to pick it up with a Kleenex and throw it away. My pillowcase had a few small stains on it. For breakfast, I went to the restaurant on the first floor and they gave me oatmeal that was barely warm. All in all, not a great experience. The 2 stars is for the view and the gym was good.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
This place was simply amazing! I am a vegan, and my server was incredibly accommodating to my diet! He let me order a special hummus appetizer, which was delicious. I highly recommend getting some of their pita because it is so warm and fresh. For my meal I had the cauliflower panini, and it was incredibly tasty and unique! Great portion size too. I had sorbet for dessert, and my server allowed me to put grilled peaches on top!

This place is so fresh, and the service and atmosphere are exceptionally above average. Though the location may seem odd, since it's in a strip mall, this place will NOT disappoint!

They know how to assemble a side dinner salad for one thing. Limited selections on beer but a couple  of local Yards selections on hand.

My club sandwich although ample was a bit on the dry side but overall not too bad. Pricing is airport hotel lopsided with one beer and a sandwich at $30.

Ambience is nice for a place like this and bar is happening with sports on TV's. If on an expense account you might not be able to dine as you usually do but it works for being "trapped" in a hotel on the airport grounds.

Yep, it is a Courtyard. Stayed in them hundreds of nights. This one is a decent location and the only choice left when anything is in town for the weekend.

Same motif pretty much everywhere so the people make or break it.

Free parking, the obligatory Starbucks and Bistro for coffee and limited eats.

Beds are decently comfy and the blackout curtains to hold day at bay rock.

Not too far from downtown and couple of minutes from Lakeside Mall and Morning Call for beignets.

More than one visit and most likely more to come.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Using the aisle to bypass all the hassle and most of the online reservations making process: 4.5 stars

Trying to use the app or calling a location or the "customer service" folks is a 1 star at best.

I will round up to 3 here overall. The gulf between the two is amazing to me. Suffice it to say if you need to change anything or get any help from them other than the website using a PC, forget it. 

Not enough yet to make me search elsewhere but they should strive to make changes and getting phone assistance easier. Been like this since I can remember. For years.

We had dinner here last night and found the food to be very good BUT the noise was just unbearable!  They cram so many tables in that the back of my chair was up against the chair of the table behind me ( I wonder if they were in compliance with the fire code). 

To make matters worse, not only was there the noise of all the people talking, they had a person playing the guitar throughout the evening.  

It was a shame that a restaurant serving real good food made the experience unpleasant. 

WILL NOT BE RETURNING!

Well maybe I picked a bad day to eat here. When we sat down the first thing I noticed was a dirty plate on our table.  Our waiter took it away and never came back with a clean one. 
Next, our appetizer came out (meatballs) which were cold.  They took them back to the kitchen, and finally brought out hot meatball.  I nevertheless thought that serving meatballs would be so difficult. 
Our pizza came out and the crust was burnt.  Eating carbon is not a pleasant experience.  
Finally, our waiter kept coming over to see if there was anything he could do but he never did a thing.  

I don't think I'll be returning.

The Public house should really be called the private house because it is truly a hidden gem of the midtown scene. I'm quite fond of all the bars around midtown, but public house I am especially fond of. It has a unique atmosphere which makes it feel cozy inside. The music isn't very loud and it is dimly lit.There is also a good amount of seating to make having conversations much easier than in most bars. Other pluses: a fairly decently priced and decent amount of beers on drafts which seem to be rotated out frequently. And, my friends drunk ordered pizza there and the bartender didn't even get mad.

We brought our tortoise to Adobe and they did a great job of nail trimming and gave a ton of extra info on caring for our pet. And then we started taking our dog Apple to Adobe a few months ago and they were in the midst of a remodel. The new office is very nice. They are very reasonably priced (especially compared to La Cumbre where we took our last dog). They also took care of our bunnies nails and even had a nurse who had owned her own bunnies and gave us some helpful tips.Very nice people that seem genuinely happy to be there. Highly recommend.

A delicious surprise but not unexpected. I read "Joe's Pizza" took over this place but I was still reticent but today I thought, why not? The delivery man was nice and the pizza came on time. 

I ordered a plain pizza which came hot and thin crusted and a cheeseburger hoagie because I haven't ever seen that on a menu up here in Philadelphia. The pizza was yummy and so was the cheeseburger hoagie. The pizza dough seemed lighter with a thinner crust than from Joe's (we both love thin crust pizza). Frankly we all enjoyed both items and I recommend you try this place because everything came hot, fresh and on time!

Not impressed. This place used to be good. First of all it took us a while to get seated, then when we did sit, the waitress was extremely slow bringing our drinks, and even brought the garlic knots we ordered before we had drinks. Then, when the pepperoni pizza we ordered FINALLY came out, it was covered in grease. Maybe I'm biased because I just came back from NY where I had REAL NY pizza, but I don't think this place is as good as it used to be. I can't attest to its sandwiches though, because I haven't tried them.

It gets the job done! Good location in downtown Indy. Comfortable, clean beds. Staff was friendly - not amazinggg, but they did their job. My room was located on the 17th floor and had a gorgeoussss view. I uploaded pictures, so take a look! :) Especially at night when the lights lit up on the Soldiers & Sailors Monument. Parking was $25/night for self-park. Wifi was only free up to a certain GB. I got a room with 2 double beds - pretty standard. It's not superrrr close to the stadium...I think about a 20 minute walk? Or maybe I'm just a slow walker...
Otherwise, it was close to lots of bars/restaurants!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I cannot tell a lie, as a mostly non-Spanish speaker, I was a little intimidated by the location and store front. Mi Espanol es no bueno. . . But the reviews drew me in, and me gusta!!! I'm so happy I went in! 

I ordered corn tortilla tacos - al pastor, carne asada, y chorizo, with extra cilantro - 2 of each. They were so fresh, hot, amazing. So good. I look forward to going back again and trying not just one of the other many taco variations, but also some of the daily specials. (The day I went in they had shrimp and fish specials as well as ceviche.)

Excellent food, good prices, you can definitely trust the reviews.

We came in looking for a cup of miso soup and some sushi.  The place was pretty busy, only 1 two-top available.  But that doesn't excuse the slow service.  Being from out of town, we didn't realize we had to write down our orders on the slip on the table.  We ordered two cups of miso soup and a couple of rolls.  The sushi came out before the soup and it only appeared when we asked for it.  This place isn't the best sushi I've ever had, but it's reasonable.  If service improved, I'd probably still only give it a 3.

All in all, this is a pretty good Burger King.  It's clean, roomy, and nicely decorated (as fast food places go).  It has the Coke freestyle machines.  There's a play area that kids seem to enjoy, though I'm obviously not eligible to play in it (Ageism!  Heightism!)  There are also a some computers there for customer use, so if you don't have one, or if yours dies unexpectedly, you can go there, buy a burger and check your e-mail.

The food and service are probably about what you'd expect... No glaring shortfalls there.

At landmark, the food, while the types of items that you'd expect from a bar, is always very well prepared.  They have a pretty solid beer list, and their cocktails are very good.  It's a nice looking place, with comfortable seating.  The service is pretty good. This place could be one of my favorite bar/restaurants on the mainline, except that it's just a little bit too slow, and just a little bit too expensive.  It's not terrible in either regard, but if they dropped all of their prices by $1, and shaved a couple of minutes off of the wait time, that would take them from pretty good to great.

I am giving this a 5 star review because the 1 and 2 star reviewers are hopefully long gone! It's really more like a 4 just because it's Starbucks, but I would like to defend the employees. I have found most of them very friendly. They don't know my name but they seem to know many people that come in around 9ish, which is when I pop in a couple times a week. The music is at just the right level and the ONE time they flubbed up my order, it was super busy and they more than made up for it. One of the managers knows who I am and even though O don't called by my name, they make me feel welcomed here and that's what I like.

I had a recent service experience here that I wasn't too happy with. I had my car taken in for a few minor things I needed checked out/fixed. 
Long story short: Apparently a couple of the things I thought were potential issues actually weren't...great, right? Definitely, except the borderline passive aggressive way in which it was handled left a bitter taste in my mouth about their customer service. 
Four stars for now because I've taken my car here before and it's been a pretty decent experience in the past.

My husband got a hair cut yesterday from a nice lady with big big earrings 
I loved her 
She was so fun 
She loved that I was from Las Vegas, my clothes, my Swarovski Crystal Uggs. 
She was excited to meet a "real Vegas girl" 
It was funny
She cut my husband's "fine baby hair"
And i started laughing
It was a dominant African American clientele, so when they give cuts to them the hair is more coarse
So they tend to be "heavy handed" normally

My husband is white, didn't complain at all. 
Looked good. 
There was plenty of parking 
And and it was a cool shopping plaza. Lots to do.

We've been to Petrini's probably 4 times now and we are never disappointed.  It's close to home and really feels like home cooking. Friendly service staff all around and hearty old-school Italian food. We've had the pizza and they are always good. Tonight, I had risotto with chicken - a great tasting and fully filling portion for only $9.95. Incredible!  OK, so the garlic bread is t the best, but I shouldn't eat it anyway!  This place has so much retro style and it's just plain and simple - honestly good food. No frills. No attitude. Just a spot on dinner joint that we will keep coming back to.

I sincerely love this place.  In under 10 minutes, and for under $10, you can get a pizza topped with whatever your heart desires.  As little or as much as you want without judgement.  That includes cheese, protein, veggies and finishing for an honest $8.  And these aren't some crappy canned foods.  Everything is fresh and delicious.  I really can't say enough about this.  It's my perfect lunch.  Some days I eat the whole thing.  Other days I eat half and save half for the next day.  The people working there couldn't be nicer to boot.  It's a classy operation thru and thru.

My toe still hurts from where the nail tech cut it back too far on the sides. It stung when she put on the alcohol solution before she put the gel polish on. This place is usually better for me than this, but it depends on who you get. The water in my foot bath was way too hot at first and then too cold after she tried to adjust it. The polish looks alright and I hope it lasts but the pain is not worth the lower prices. You get what you pay for. I was going to get a manicure too but I didn't want anything to happen to my hands after that.

Toscana is kind of hit or miss in my opinion, and of course how you feel about it depends on your preferences for Italian food. If you like it Americanized - heavily sauced, lots of cheese and cream in huge portions - you'll probably be thrilled. If you're looking for authentic Italian food, however, look elsewhere. I tend to stick with the grilled steaks and meats, which they do quite well, but avoid the Cedar Plank Salmon at all costs unless you like dried out fish that tastes like wood. Calamari and other appetizers tend to be very good and filling.

One of those branches that I have never been inside besides their drive thru.  I don't know why but never felt like walking into this particular location hahaha.  I don't know if it's because it's right on a very busy street or every time I'm here I'm just too lazy to walk in.  Anyways, the drive thru area is very spacious and you definitely have enough space around so you feel comfortable driving into each lane. I have never encountered any delays nor traffic during my visits (maybe I've been lucky) so I'm pretty happy about that.

This is 100% the place to go when you're so hungry you can't see straight and you want comfort food.  Just go up to the counter, ask for a chicken teriyaki with onions and a cookie.  Devour.  Enjoy your food coma.  However, you can't do this more than like once a quarter or you'll be a junkie with a big ol' belly.  Service depends on who is working, but generally it works best to call ahead.  Their fries are good, too, but you'd better be starving to even mess with those.  The cookies are worth every melty morsel of butter, sugar, and chocolate.

What's better than great company? Great food! Fat salmon exceeded my expectations. I came here for date night and the atmosphere was super cozy and romantic. The menu is vegetarian friendly and has pictures showing each item. 

We ordered the avocado roll, old school, and sweet meadow. All three were amazing, the combination of sweet and spicy was perfect for my palette. Definitely the best sushi I've ever had. The sushi is made fresh to order and you can taste the freshness in each bite.

I will definitely be craving sushi every week and will be back at fat salmon soon.

I had a little bit of time in Old City to grab a quick coffee and Yelp reviews led me here. I wish I had more time though because the inside has such a cozy atmosphere, especially the back area. Seems like a great place to get work done for a few hours. 

The coffee was super tasty, a bit overly hot initially but even the drip has great flavor. Also the Irish soda bread (only $3!) is made in house and it's a wonderful hold-you-over-for-a-bit snack. It's dense as soda bread typically is but the butter helps nicely with that.

I try my best to love this Starbucks, but the drive-thru and the parking lot kind of kill it for me.  I do have to give the staff props because they are so friendly and consistent with their service.  This is my daily Starbucks because it's on my way to work and I don't have to go out of my way, which is awesome.  I have thought about changing to a different location, but since I moved to Tucson this has been my go-to place, and I can't seem to make a change.  If the drive through/parking lot is empty, give this place a chance.  The staff definitely make up for the crappy location.

I had a solid experience at Crazy Sushi. The sushi was good, but I think they only do the three roll special for lunch, not dinner. I ended up getting three rolls: the spicy tuna, the Philadelphia, and the spicy crunchy salmon roll with gyoza on the side. 

The spicy tuna was a little soggy at the top, but everything else was fine. I do have another spot in the city where the sushi is just as good, but they do an all day three day special. I will say that I am impressed with the sheer size of Crazy Sushi's menu though, and some of the other specialty rolls caught my eye!

This is a terrible experience. We've been standing in line for 45 minutes and none of their employees have apologized for the wait, or explained why they are moving at a snails pace. I'm a very patient person, however they grabbed a group from the back of the line and pulled them aside to check them in before all of the people in front for no reason. Mind you there is a gold member check in that if they were of a "certain status" they could go to instead. These employees seem lost, GO TO ENTERPRISE INSTEAD!!!!

I had seen this place for a number of years but had not ate there yet.  My friend and I were there on a Saturday night and they were busy.  We sat out on their porch which was enclosed which was great since it was raining outside.  Food was good....only issue was that that the original drink I ordered, Moscow Mule, was too sour so I got a Manhattan instead.  I didn't notice this until later but they still ended up charging me for the Moscow Mule even though I couldn't drink it.  That is why I felt 4 stars was appropriate in this situation.

They reach for mediocrity and fail, but the good thing is you won't remember what you ate at this generic American-chinese-place-that-pretends-to-be-Japanese. The entrees come with a sad salad of lettuce and maybe a mushroom if you're lucky. Edamame was undercooked and undersalted. Best ingredient is chicken - surprisingly high quality, but most of the rest of the ingredients were blah. I prefer Wabi Sabi, part of the same genre, although its nothing special, either. Call it "good if you've never eaten anywhere else in your life".

I have stayed at the Crowne Plaza in Downtown Indianapolis a few times for various conferences.  The location, comfort, and cleanliness of this hotel is great! I also love that when it is cold you can walk through indoor paths to get to Circle Centre Mall and other downtown favorites! 

My only warning to people planning on staying here, it is an active train station.  I  woke up a few times throughout the night as a train would be passing through.  On the other hand, my co-worker who I often travel with was not bothered by the noise.  If you are a light sleeper, you may want to consider staying somewhere else.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Above average sushi in a confused atmosphere with lackluster service. 

I can't fathom why this upscale-appearing restaurant decided to dress the rich, red walls and smooth jazz with brown paper on the tables, but they did.  There are other contradictions as well, such as the lackluster service that took far too long. 

The sushi, on the other hand, was the star of the show.  The Tampa and California rolls were well executed, and a bargain at their happy hour pricing.  

This restaurant has amazing potential, if they can address the minor but irritating issues.

This place really likes dill. I mention this because it can be found in quite a few dishes, sometimes a bit unexpectedly. I sort of like the local, smaller-scale, kinda hipster vibe here, with the hand-crafted burgers and so on...can't say I loved it, but neither would I call it bad. It was mostly just there. Burger was acceptable, but nothing particularly striking and nothing I would drive past a Five Guys to get. Definitely a step above the fast food chains, but altogether absent on the wow factor side of things.

Warning: It's Cash Only

Glorified Diner

This should not be called an Italian restaurant. Their are no descriptions of what the dishes have on them just names. The prices make it seem like you're going to get a plate larger than your head and take home leftovers, but no leftovers here. My fettuchini Alfredo had the cheese separating from the other sauce elements, making it very odd and lumpy. Waitresses were confused about whether or not they were out of things. My boyfriend and I left and both said never again.

I have eaten here three times! In the realm of cheap Chinese food, there is no contest to be had. 

For $6/($8 during dinner hours) you can get a relatively generous portion of a main entree, rice, egg/spring roll and your choice of soup. 

That's crazy!!! 

Unlike other cheap Chinese food places:
The meet is fresh , each piece is separate, the flavors are unhealthy, but accurate to what the dish is supposed to be. Rice is not dry; and the Wonton soup is surprisingly good.

In it's price bracket, this place is a clear winner.

This review is purely for Delivery.

Sushi-to-go is about as bad of an idea as eating Tide Pods. But, sometimes the craving is simply too strong. 

Thankfully there is an answer. 

I have done the dirty work and have ordered from several Sushi places through Uber Eats.

In its budget price range of 15-20 per person
-This place has ok sized rolls (some places have these micro rolls) 
-No off or worrying flavors.
-the rice is good
-fresh veggies with a crunch. (no brown avocado)
-fish is tasty and not ...weird.

If you are on a budget and in need of decent sushi this is your best option.

We come here because we get coupons in the mail which is good! I mean who doesn't want a discount right? My son gets his haircut here & we are pleased everytime. I like that you can do online check in & they tell you how much waiting time you have, I can get use of my remaining time & not waste than when you do walk in & you don't know how long you'll be waiting (though you can still do it). His hairdresser is pretty good with what she does, it's cool too that they have a record of his past appointment that it's pretty much based on that, he has the same haircut anyways.

Let me just start by quoting my friend on this place, "The espresso tastes like candy."  And, it just gets better from here.  NEVER have I had a cup of coffee so delicious that adding milk or sugar to it would be an outrage.  

If you are a coffee lover, you will not be disappointed.  The place is very hipster with their coffee roasting, but definitely not snobby.  The baristas do a great job of explaining the process to newbies to coffee like me :)  It's a quaint little coffee shop that was not highly trafficked on the saturday morning I went there.  Overall, a wonderful time and I need to go back soon.

This is an affordable decent hotel located centrally to all the main venues such as Jackson square, bourbon street, and cafe du monde is only a few blocks away.

I booked the interior room without a window and it actually wasn't too bad. The room was a decent size, came with an in room safe, 4 lamps,  and the bathroom was also updated.  

My only complaint were the pillows were a bit stiff or maybe I just weren't used to the pillows since they made my shoulders ache after a few nights rest there.

All in all, I would stay here again if I visit new orleans.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I gave this place four stars (even though quality wise it probably deserves a 3) just because I have a special place in my heart for the lunch runs we did here when I worked at the travel agency around the corner. It's not-the-best-omg-amazing sushi, but it is solid, edible, and cheap. Also, it's BYOB but I don't recommend this place for a cozy, intimate BYOB dinner night with your S.O. It's more of a "get boozy with your girlfriends post-work dinner" or boozy lunch with co-workers kind of place, as the inside is not super nice, and the tables are kind of rickety. But the staff are so, so friendly and accommodating.

Bro! These guys are the Truth and nothing but it so help me god. Not only did I get an awesome fade but I felt very comfortable there, as if I were amongst very good friends. The hot towel service, their specialized beard service and their great customer service is what sets them far apart from any other shop in the bay area. Chago has done an amazing job in finding good barbers brothers who are just as dedicated as he is in giving quality hair cuts and providing excellent customer service to work along side him at Chagos Barber shop. 10's across the board!

Um...let's see. They clean my ties that get stains on them from my leaking car window. They made sure the job was done right (told me that they needed more time for one of the ties to make it shine). The prices were not clearly listed (though they are written on a board to the left of the cash register). While they are a bit pricey, the cashier told me about some ways that I could get coupons to bring down the price a bit. Will I shop around for somewhere else? No. They are right next to my place of residence and I don't really dry clean enough to care.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Dunkin Donuts it's place you pick based it's nationwide name brand and it's local convenience. Location becomes a huge factor in what DD you'll be going to, ideally you'll be able to find one along your travel route. 

If this is the Dunkin that happens to be along your route, keep driving. The horror stories from this location should be enough to keep you away. But if it isn't -you'll get to experience their rude and slow customer service right away. 

As with any DD, you'll find all the DD staples here; donuts, coffee, breakfast sandwiches, etc. If you are a DD regular- get the app and start building those points!

My mother has been raving about this Auto Shine Car Wash for awhile now. I finally decided to take my car in and see how they did, and I was pleasantly surprised. 

With a coupon from a mailer, I was able to get the outside of my car washed, and the inside wiped down and vacuumed, for just $6.99. The best part- no surcharge for a SUV! They did a great job washing the car, and spent extra time after the wash getting any specks of dirt that were missed. 

Keep in mind, this isn't a bells and whistles place. There's no comfortable lounge to wait in or shopping area to look thought- it's just a car wash. But a good car wash.

Had a great dining experience. Dinner for 4, and everyone enjoyed it. They don't have a separate gluten free menu, but lots of gf options. Had the arugula salad -very tasty and large portion size. Had the cauliflower app- very tasty, gf and size to share. Split the rigatoni as the main meal. (I swapped the rigatoni for the gf penne) it was fantastic. Only suggestion would be to offer more gluten free dessert options. The only option was the pans cotta. We didn't get it. Our friends got the panettone bread pudding and loved it. Overall a great dinner!

The Detroit style pizza is good not great it tasted a lot like little caesars  making me question the quality of their ingredients. Spray oil, is that what the initial taste is? Meh...

Atmosphere is takeout style. Nothing fancy, although it is new, clean, and social distancing is encouraged. Paid public parking lot off to the side definitely doesn't inspire.

Up to date POS system so electronic payment is easy yet grubhub had no timeslots for the day I ordered, phone in  resolved that problem.

Based on flavor and price 3 stars is a bit generous so 2 stars.

I rent from Hertz quite a lot with business travel.  My one complaint is the speed of the bus to and from the terminal.  I always see multiple other busses from other companies before I see a Hertz bus when arriving to PHL.

When I drop the car off, they're always pretty speedy, but Friday afternoons they definitely have more people working.  But the bus - again, they must have to have it packed to the gills before they slowly make their way to the terminal.  I'm only lucky that I normally leave out of terminal A.

The lobby has been updated since many of the pictures - its very impressive.  I checked in, got in the elevator and was pretty stoked for my room.  When I got off the elevator on the 11th floor, I was disappointed to find that the lobby renovations didn't make it past the first floor.  

My room was clean, large, but I was really hoping for more of an updated look.  

I left early in the morning for a flight out of PHL and was greeted by an army of geese.  I was almost afraid to walk through the 15 birds but I had no alternative.  Watch where you wheel your suitcase because those geese are frequent visitors to the entrance of the hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I can't complain about the appearance of the hotel since they appear to be doing some minor renovations. It's the housekeeping that got under my skin. If your still in your room when they come around and are unable to clean it then it doesn't get done! We would tell them at the front desk and they assured us it would be taken care of but it rarely happened. The one time they cleaned the room but left us no towels. On our way to a concert we told them and was told it would be taken care of. When we got back still no towels. We had to call the front desk to inform them of the problem. Finally security brought us the towels.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Great gluten free experience. I informed the staff of my wheat allergy and that I can't have tomato sauce (due to my severe reflux), and they were super accommodating. They recommended a few pizzas with olive oil and different meats and/or veggies. I chose The Mayor. My pizza came out quick and was delicious. I asked the server to find out the base ingredient and she communicated from the chef to me that they use rice flour. I will most definitely be back on a regular basis, as this is a great option considering my new dietary restrictions. Thank you, Theos!

I had high hopes for this place & maybe I will give it another try at some point. 
The layout makes it feel fairly crowded when busy with people. 

The worst part of my visit was the smell- it was awful. I asked a couple ladies who seemed like regulars about the smell & was told it has always smelled like that & it is most likely their "new wood smell" but I didn't get that from the smell- it was really rough & I just couldn't shake it, I was very ready to get out of there & breath. 

I had heard great things about the ownership, bartenders, & drinks so I really wanted to like this place but just didn't.

Presto Pasta has been in Santa Barbara for twenty years, and they are still going strong.  I finally got to visit there new location and it is very nice.  Since the one out at the Calle Real Center closed a couple of years ago, I have really not eaten there.  Now that I have gone back and tried it, it was good.  I had the Fettuccine Alfredo with Italian Sausage which was very good in both taste and on the wallet.  There new location is just across from Ralph's Supermarket right off of De La Vina Street near Mission Creek.  I will definitely be going back to this place in the near future.

Went there on a Saturday for dinner; won't be going back. We started off with the gyoza and spring rolls which were not that great. The menus had pictures, instead of descriptions, not a fan of this since there are "different" sushi rolls and you can't really see what's in the roll. The waiter was not very friendly; he was not welcoming or even attentive.  Our sushi was ok but we've definitely had better; the place was completely empty when we were there; and the hours are strange so I highly recommend calling before you go. Overall a mediocre experience you can definitely have better service and sushi somewhere else.

Great variety of flavor. This place totally disrupts my diet plan.
Note:
1. they offer half scoops. So for 1 scoop, you can choose two flavors, each for a half scoop.
2. Some of the sundaes I had are not as good as the pure ice cream: the sky scraper is way too creamy--too much caramel and chocolate syrup, and not enough ice cream. The cookie monster is better, but still too much crunches and whip cream for a decent ice cream bite.
 
The only reason I didn't give the place a 4 star is that it's cash only. Seriously, considering the business flow, go get a credit card swipe.

We love Main Street Animal Hospital. I originally found this veterinarian through recommendations on the Doylestown Facebook page from locals. Since getting our puppy in February, we have had various check-ups and appointments with all three of the vets at MSAH and we love all of them - Super helpful, informative and caring. The people at the front desk are extremely friendly and helpful as well. We have had nothing but great experiences. The building itself is really nice - Modern, updated and they have separate entrances/sides for dogs and cats. Highly recommend!

Great area to unwind after the St. Pete beach sunset and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere in here.

Drinks aren't cheap at the bar, but we also brought down our own drinks, from our room, and sat closer to the lobby area on our own.

There was a very good mix of people at the bar and at tables and on our first night Saturday, there was live music in the bustling lobby. 

The seats are very comfortable and decor is interesting to look at. Definitely take some time to visit the lobby bar if you stay here. One of the best lobby bars I've seen and fantastic service.

Ok I don't know if we was just late for our arrival for our pizza but when we did receive it. The pizza did not look like a Imos pizza just look like sauce and meat no cheese at all .  I'm not a big fan of your pizza only because you never get it right. I've wrote a review on the one downtown location in my city and I have no idea what's going on in these restaurants! Wings are always good if you get them well done  well I'm from here and I hate your damn pizza might as-well close down dominoes do it way better ! Sad to say this but you gotta get it right ! I'm tired of this ! And every experience I Will post 

Thank you !

I order from here all the time, but I have only eaten here twice and both times they were understaffed. However, the pizza here is not overly greasy which I appreciate. The rice balls here are soooo good. Every time that they have them in, I order them. I would also suggest trying the potato pizza if you're looking for something different. Other than the lack of grease, the big draw for me here is the sauce. It has a very vibrant red color to it and it has a very nice balance to it.

I can honestly say that for as many times as I have ordered from here, I have never had a bad pizza from this shop. Will be ordering again.

We came here for a conference and were very comfortable with our stay.  The view of the arch and the location- super close to the stadium are unbeatable.  Seriously, this is the best view in St. Louis!  The restaurants were good and there's a full Starbucks in the lobby area so you'll always be well caffeinated.

The rooms were clean and the staff were very helpful. We had to split our room three ways, which I'm sure is a headache for staff but they handled it gracefully. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying downtown...oh ya, parking is a block away and only $8 a day!  For this girl, who has had to pay $20+ a day, that was a bargain!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: This Starbucks location is the gold standard.  I have been to many others in Nashville and in small towns and far bigger cities, and this West End location provides the friendliest and speediest service and most consistent quality. Have I gotten a wrong order once or twice in my history of going there at least 2x/week for years and years... yes, maybe so, but really... what do we expect, fellow Nashvillians, if our vehicles are lined up for a block and half on West End and we get thru the line in ten minutes.

Popped in with some friends for a hot drink. I didn't realize this is one of the older Second Cup locations in the city and has recently had a bit of a makeover. 
Like most Second Cups they serve a decent tea or coffee, and they have upped their food offering since my last visit. It's not just sweet pastries, it now includes bagels, sausage rolls and even wraps. 
There are a few tables chairs, one long table for larger groups, a cute fireplace with cosy seats and he best thing is the mural toward the back with iconic spots around the Oliver area.

Pretty good location in the King of Prussia area. Dined in for dinner and went with the seaweed salad and miso soup to start. Both were your standard fair and nothing spectacular. 

Decided to get the yellow tail jalapeno appetizer, a spicy tuna hand roll and ikura (I had to order two pieces). These were good as the yellowtail had a citrus dressing that was more lemon then the typical yuzu combination that seems to be the norm. It was a nice change.

The roll was not overly spicy but well made. The ikura was fresh.

Service was nice and the prices were reasonable.

The coffee here was just okay. It's attached to the hotel so the prices are probably reflecting the conveniently longer hours. 

The significant other and I ordered the cappuccino ($4) and latte ($4.50) in a tall, though it was the only size from looking at the menu. Their coffee blend was rather good pretty plain. My latte just needed some additional milk to make it slightly sweeter, but it was good overall.

Killebrew Coffee isn't a super large coffee spot. The booths were cool since they had outlets on either side. There were also some bar style seats facing the street along with a few regular tables and chairs lining the wall.

What an interesting bar.  Total locals dive, tucked into the Navarre neighborhood (often confused for Lakeview).  It's the kind of place that everyone knows everyone's name, but none of them recognize faces because it's so dark and likely everyone's so drunk!  

They have some high tables and the bar, dart board and some tiny TV's.  They give away free crockpot food occasionally and they do a mean trivia night.  There's an awesome juke box inside too. 

The beers are cheap and mostly everyone sits outside and smokes and uses the inside to grab their drinks.  

Plenty of street parking!

Really enjoyed HQ! The house drip is AMAZING. I usually go for something darker but this sounded really good. They were helpful in finding me something I was in the mood for. My fiance enjoyed a tasty hot chocolate and a blueberry muffin. They also carry Dozen's Gluten Free baked goods (allergy note: most had almond flour/paste). I live downtown and ventured out to Sylvan Park; I wouldn't normally, but I was tempted to try this new place using a Scoutmob deal. The space is small and cozy but comfortable. I will most definitely be back.

The food here is amazing. I know, you think i am already trashed or out of my mind, but, 1. I don't drink. and 2. the food really is amazing. The Delmonico Steak is a generous portion, and always cooked perfectly, and very inexpensive. They make their own scalloped potatoes, Their not out of a box! Fresh potatoes in a velvety smooth cream sauce. It is so good. My wife always gets The Horse salad. and by always I mean 6 times in the last 3 months! They make food for our kids as well, cheeseburgers, chicken fingers, grilled cheese. I love it there. Go in with an open mind and an empty stomach. you wont regret it!

Wish I could rate "0" stars. A good friend of mine, the sweetest and most professional person, was recently harassed by an employee named Amanda. The police were called on her and her family, because she communicated issues her family encountered during her stay. Unwilling to address the concerns, Amanda told her to LEAVE the hotel if she was unhappy. She then called the police to have my friend, her husband, and children removed from the hotel. She said she was threatened by the opportunity to resolve a customer's complaint. Amanda should be removed from her post, and Wyndham needs to address this situation EXPEDITIOUSLY.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Wow! Really nice, brand new car wash located on SR 54. You can pick an a la carte service or a pre-selected wash ranging from $10-$20. After you go through the car wash you're able to stop and use the complimentary microfiber clothes with glass cleaner, super suction strength vacuums and a air brush that literally blasts those tiny crumbs in those hard to reach spots right out. The kids really enjoy the car wash because of the different color lights... almost feels like you're at a rave, which the kids know nothing about but still... it's fun lol This car wash does get busy, so go at odd times if you want to be in and out.

[596]

Today was my first visit and I was very impressed.  This location is on busy Oregon Avenue in Philly.

There are two drive up windows.  Inside had a kids playarea which my son loved.  There are tables and counters to sit at which is nice to have a choice.  Looks like it was renovated recently.

The drinks are self serve.

First time experiencing.......   kiosk for ordering McDonalds food. 

Dave was very nice and helpful.   The cashier was very nice.

All around great experience.  I'll definitely be back.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
This was one of my favorite spots a few years ago when I moved here.  They closed and remodeled which was desperately needed. The new restaurant is huge and beautiful with plenty of seating.  

The prices went up which I expected so we didn't come as much.

Ordered a cheesesteak with provolone and  fried onions and the sandwich was really light on the steak.  When i opened the sandwich there was too much empty space for me ESP if I see the bread.   It's just ok and would be better if they were generous w the meat 

Will I be back? Not sure

To me it's just "OK"

I didn't find any of the yogurts I tasted amazing.  I did love the concept of the store
 
Tons of topping to choose from.

It's a self serve place and you pay by the ounce.  There are two sizes.  The "small" is huge and the "large" is even bigger.

I filled up about 1/4 of the small and my son did about 1/3 of the small and it was $8 total.  Felt a little pricy to me.  He enjoyed it especially the gummy frogs.. lol

The décor is really cute and colorful.

Plenty of parking in this strip mall.

Will I be back?  Maybe If I'm in the area.

[557]

I saw so many positive reviews so I must have  came on an off day.   

Parking is tough due to the shared lot with Applebees.   Inside there were tons of empty trash boxes in the aisles.  I suspect unpacking but I didn't see anyone unpacking.   There were only 2 registers open and the line was over 20 deep (see my pic).   So I waited on a long line next to trash.   

Staff was nice once it was my turn.  I guess the "NEXT" that kept hearing would have been nicer with "next customer please" or something not so short.

They did have a guy in front with wine samples.

I will not be back.

Holey Schmidt has a Voo Doo donuts vibe. Donuts didn't look fresh or appetizing but after taking a bite out of it, they were soft and yummy. However, just standing back and watching, none of the tables are clean, there are two counter employees - both switching back and forth to cashier and two or three in the back making the donuts. Seems a bit understaffed for their opening weekend. 
Although they had yummy donuts, there were few selections. Perhaps they should get ready and bake a batch before their most popular selections run out for their next few guests.

Complete waste of money.

Equipment was only partially functioning but there was no signage to alert anyone to this.

My car is not clean and it did not get dried off either.  I may as well have had neighborhood kids just point a tepid trickle from a garden hose at my car. At least I could have spent my $10 on somebody actually doing some work.

I'd have called somewhere to let them know of the problems but they don't even put their phone number on the receipt -probably don't want to be responsible.

Save your money, don't go here.

This place may look like a hole in the wall, but it's one of our go-to favorites for take-out near Tower Grove. One of the biggest factors for me when it comes to Chinese food is that, at some places, the meat is not good quality. It's good at China King. From shrimp lo mein to chicken with cashews to Mongolian beef, it's been good. The portion sizes are huge for the price, so it's a good deal all around. Occasionally we've had an order with too much oil, which is why I gave four stars instead of five, but overall, I'd recommend China King.

Dr. Gary Puglia did great work on my cat. Paul is an indoor/outdoor cat and somehow gashed his stomach badly. I brought him in, Easter Sunday morning, and by night time Paul was ready to go home with strict orders and the cone of shame. Some special attention had to be done with Paul and he is doing much better now. The stitches come out today and the cone can finally come off. He will have to wait a bit longer to go outside again though. The location and staff are very nice and my family was lucky they were open.

I really like how this tiny joint is tucked away behind a strip mall, so unassuming and genuine. The owner helped me order and was very accommodating. There were some Japanese guys enjoying the Udon which smelled delicious by the way, and an older couple having a late  dinner even though the place would probably close in roughly 30 minutes. I placed an order to go, I had the Spicy Tuna Don Buri Volcano style. It was delicious. It was a huge serving as well, I had to split it into two meals. How did I not discover this place sooner? I cant wait to try a number of different things on the menu and I will definitely be back.

I waited a long time to go here because there are a lot of other (better looking) places in downtown.  But I'd nearly run out of new places, and it was time to give UC a shot.  As I suspected, I haven't been missing much.  I ordered a burrito, which was lukewarm at most, and it was otherwise bland.  Three things brought this from a 2- to a 3-star experience.  The first two are the the chips and salsa, which were free and great.  The third was the size of my burrito.  After the massive burrito and the chips and salsa, I left UC full -- and, for me, that's an exceptionally rare feeling.

I don't know a lot about cars, so I can't answer the most important question (are they finding unnecessary repairs to make?).  But I can say a few other things.  I've gone to McGee twice and both times were pleasant.  The people inside are very nice.  I paid $170 for a new tire on an SUV and that's with a $10 discount from Yelp.  (Be sure to use that.)  Also, it's located in downtown, so you can leave your car there and go to work.

In sum, I've never had to spend too much, they've always been pleasant to do business with, I've never had any problem with their work, and the location is great.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Family takeout night! We ordered a variety of items including: tacos, quesadilla, enchilada, and the Alambre platter. They were very nice in the restaurant and the food was pretty good too. It didn't stay hot for too long in the styrofoam so the quesadilla was pretty congealed with all the cheese. The tacos were a hit and a good deal of food for $9. Enchiladas were solid and the Alambre platter with pork, cheese, peppers, and onions was also tasty but it didn't translate too well for take out. The chips and guacamole were delicious!!! Would I order again? Maybe if I was dining in.

Just wanted to say the biggest thank you to Dr. Avery, Kerri and Laura (and all others involved) for taking such good care of my baby, Bane. He has had a stressful long few weeks but I am so impressed with how they handled him before, during and after surgery. Even though he was a big baby, I cannot thank you enough for making this process as stress free as you possibly could. And for making us feel comfortable leaving him in your hands. I'm sure Bane will be excited to see you all at his check up in two weeks.

I originally thought the Wellness Plan offered would be really beneficial, however I soon realized that you don't save as much as advertised. The selling agent also did not explain the hidden cancellation fees & contract. I've decided to stop going after my last visit where nothing was explained when picking my dog up - Not the invoice, diagnosis on issues nor medication. I was handed a bag & my dog - The vet never came out. I will go somewhere more official moving forward & am currently in a battle to cancel the Wellness Plan.

Have ordered here three times and this place is terrible.  The lady that works the drive through is rude and makes it seems like she's doing you a favor by getting your food.  Last time I ordered it took her nearly ten minutes to approach the window.  She gave me the burrito after I paid and didn't even say thank you.  Normally, I'm not too picky about service, but this place has the worst service ever.  To top it off, the food is not even that good.   Think microwave burritos and that's what you're getting.  There are much better places to get a late night Mexican fix in Tucson so save your money.

Overview: 2/10 service, 3/10 food, 5/10 ambiance 
Would not recommend. 

To be honest this place is mediocre at best... The service was really slow and the chef was on his phone right in my face! He didn't even answer me when I tried to get his attention.
The food was fine I guess...
Overall I would not recommend this place. If you're looking for somewhat authentic Japanese food look elsewhere! As an American, I spoke more Japanese than the entire staff combined. There's plenty of great food in Santa Barbara so just go somewhere else.

Nothing great, nothing terrible.  Came here for lunch, sat in their "sundeck," which is really just another room but has a lot more light then the tomb that is their main seating area.  They have a big menu, plenty of options for every taste.  I ended up with a cajun chicken sandwich and fries.  It was good - not great, but acceptable and reasonably priced.

It's the type of place that could be an old reliable.  You don't know where else to go, want a quick inexpensive meal that doesn't need to blow your socks off, you come to Harvey's.  But it's not a location if you're looking for a spectacular meal.

Pretty much a "to go" only coffee place with just a couple small tables outside during nicer weather days.  Didn't see any indoor seating.

The place seems like it is a beverage only shop as well since I didn't see anything on the menu to munch on.  I simply got my standard black drip coffee and it was okay, not fantastic.  It was served right on the edge of being to hot to drink, but I managed to not burn my tongue, so they get a good rating for that!

Friendly and quick service around lunch time, so good ratings for that too!

Review #2584

In 2016, this local eye care business hired artist Justin Olson to create a colorful mural on the outside of the business.  The artist depicted the face of an eye glass wearing person on three sides of the building.  To fill out the rest of the space, vibrant colors are swirled including silhouettes of eyes.  As you drive by this place on Shelby, the colors draw your attention to the building...that is if your vision is good enough.  If you have trouble seeing it, maybe you should stop in....and maybe somebody else should drive! ;)

Review #1890
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
Do NOT rent from this enterprise. You will be better off renting from the budget in church street.

1) the staff is horrible. The staff that is not serving customers played around at the counter so loud that you can't hear the one that is working with you.

2) they gave you false information about your credit card insurance trying to make you buy their insurance.  The way they presented it was confrontational. 

3) they told you to return the car at 8am in the morning. But their location would NOT even open until 9am. Not only I was waiting outside for an hour outside their location, I saw another customer had the same thing happened to her.

Me and my girlfriend came here for a night out. Every table in the place except ours was given bread. Every table except ours was given service. I really hope others have a better experience. When we left visibly in a bad mood some male employee came outside and threatened me with violence and told me if I didn't leave the street (Waiting for an uber) he was going to do this that or the other. Because my girlfriend and I are rational human beings we walked down the street and waited for our Uber. Overall terrible service, terrible employees, and just a hint of racism.

Wow I'm quite disappointed.   I came here a couple of years ago and the food was fantastic. Now it's very bland. I had the pork tenderloin with apple chutney, potato cakes and veggies. The pork was cooked well but flavorless. The chutney was like they put a dollop of applesauce on the pork and called it chutney. The potatoes very bland as well. No flavor of salt and pepper...nothing.   Portions were very small...left still hungry. The staff was very nice...met the owner as well. The atmosphere is nice and comfortable. Wish the food could have met with the same praise.

A friend and I wanted to get the night started with a fish bowl. They have one flavor of fish bowl, so not much choice there. It was $10, and the pros about this location was that they take credit cards as well as cash compared to other places on Bourbon Street that are cash only.
The drink itself was okay. It was more ice and juice than alcohol. That was pretty disappointing, to be honest. It was an okay try but I would recommend skipping out on this drink and getting the hundreds of other drinks offered on Bourbon Street.

Stopped by for a quick bite during my layover. I ordered the Big Fish Filet sandwich (with cheese added and a small fries. This is usually my go-to order at Burger King! For airport quality food, it was pretty good and nor too different from other chain locations.
I took off a star because the seating area wasn't very clean, the floor was somewhat sticky, and the line got crazy long after I ordered and there was still only one person at the register.
Good spot to stop for food but they could definitely use some improvement on appearance and customer service.

I see a lot of negative reviews here but I had a quite different experience. I found the staff friendly and chatty, and my exam was thorough and efficient. I had come in to get an exam and glasses and got both. My insurance covers a limited range of frames but I was pleased to find something I liked among them. It took about a week and a half for the glasses to come in.

I'd happily recommend this place and in fact have already to some coworkers with the same insurance. It's not the fanciest eye place I've ever been to, but I'll go back.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
I'm crazy for Crazy Sushi! Sorry, I had to. 

They have a great lunch deal, where you get "Any 2 Rolls and Soup or Salad" for $8. The any 2 rolls doesn't include the special rolls, but there are still plenty to choose from.  I've tried most of them - not mind blowing, but they always use fresh ingredients, and they're consistently good! 

Added bonus: Pretty fast delivery. I was on crutches for a while and got delivery 1-2x a week during that time.  I only work a block or so away, but it would often only be 30 min from the time I place my order to delivery. 

Definitely worth checking out if you work or live nearby.

This Dunkin is new and it's not your average Dunkin. It's super slow and the quality is off. Just my 2 cents. I hope they improve.

Update: this Dunkin' just seems worse whenever I go to it. At this point, I will just goto any other Dunkin' on the way to wherever I am headed because this place is slow and the order is often wrong. The staff here should be forced to see a "day in the life" at any other Dunkin' location around basically during the morning rush in order to see how the franchise is supposed to operate. There are usually plenty of staff too, so I am bewildered how slow and backed up it gets.

If I could give this place 0 stars I honestly would. The most ridiculous thing I've seen happened to me tonight. I pulled up around 10:40 and the Baskin Robbins lights were off and the worker was just standing outside kissing her boyfriend. I am absolutely astonished to what I just witnessed and find it truly unbelievable that I pulled up twenty minutes before close and this is what I see. Are you kidding me? The girl had the audacity to give me a rude look and tell me they are closed 20 minutes early and just go back to kissing? Very unprofessional and disappointing experience.

Scam of a business do not go! I went in with a Tricare referral and they tried charging me $99.99 for an appointment that was specifically for contact lenses. They never once mentioned the cost for contact fitting at all. Mind you they were the ones that contacted me to schedule this appointment. They refused to give me the prescription to contact lenses and only gave me one for glasses which I did not go for. When I asked to speak to someone they said I wasn't the only military member that has had this problem. So apparently it's an ongoing issue with this place.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text: I was not impressed with this place whatsoever! The ladies were nice however their work is horrible. We asked for regular pedicures and they charged us $25 for his instead of $23 and since I got French tip they charged me $35 instead of a normal $5 up charge and for my daughter's hand and toes I don't even know what they charged us. Their nail polish wasn't the best, it seems like they added stuff to the nail polish because they had to add several coats of the white nail polish to make the color more noticeable and they don't put a final coat just the clear and it's only one coat. Needles to say I will not be returning to this place.

Wow! Looked back at my reviews and our last visit, and only visit, to Luciano's was over three years ago. We did try their new place on the river and had a great experience.

Anyway... Had lunch today at the Orchard Street location. We were seated immediately and our wait person was there almost as fast. AND she was fabulous - her name was Jennifer and she knew her business. She was warm and friendly and made us feel welcome. The last time we were here had a bad experience with one of the waitstaff - not this time!!!!!

Five stars for the food - 6 stars form the service. Thank you, Jennifer, you made our day so much better.

I would give no stars if possible. My mom and brother went in to get my brother a haircut about 230pm today. The hairdresser had the poorest customer service. Not a hello or how are you, the girl seemed more interested in her phone and showing whatever was on her phone to the other hairdresser. She did not speak to my brother at all during the time she cut his hair. Extremely rude. I know it is an $8 haircut place but please girl learn to be a little more cordial with your customers. Unfortunately they did not get her name but if she reads this, I'm sure she'll know who she is. Just plain rude.

I may be a little bias because the H&C on 49th is in my neighborhood, and I'm a sucker for local joints... But that aside, this place is pretty killer. 

Warm modern fireplace, lots of comfy yet cozy seating, local art on the walls... And of course, the best coffee in town. Literally. I love walking down for a latte, or stopping by on Saturday mornings for a cup on my way out. 

They have all types of "milk" for all likings too, huge win in my book: soy, almond, etc. 

And recently, I noticed smoothies made with traders point yogurt- so of course, I had to grab one...  And it was delicious, a little pricey for the small size, imo.

Sushi Ten USED to be voted the "Best Sushi in Tucson." This has seriously changed. I think the change in management contributes to the difference.

I visited Sushi Ten a couple weeks ago, not knowing of the management change, and discovered new inexperienced sushi chefs. These chefs did not even know how to slice nigiri sushi, which were presented in pathetic tapered strips. In addition, service was horrendous. Two of us ordered "all-you-can-eat-sushi", 45 minutes later got half of what we originally ordered and asked for the rest, but after waiting another 30 minutes, eventually left and only paid for one order of "all-you-can-eat."

Oh Lorddddd. I wish I read my fellow Yelpers' reviews before pulling in the drive-thru line. I was making good time on my morning commute and decided to grab some breakfast since I was early by 20 minutes. 

I ended up waiting in the drive-thru line for about 25 minutes for a mobile order. Do yourself a favor, order via the app, and just walk inside the store and pick up the order. Do not get in the drive-thru line.

When I got to the pick-up window, I could see a bunch of employees inside, like any regular dunkin donuts with a drive thru. For some reason, this one is just not a very efficient operation.

I was once told the incorrect time for an appointment and I showed up at the time I was told, which was apparently 30 minutes late.  The stylist was very angry and gave me an attitude. The attitude was unacceptable, especially given that it was the salon's mistake.  The stylist put a foil on my hair & then proceeded to tell me that it was my error & not the salon's error. Then, she took 4 hours to do my highlights while chatting with her friends & taking several cigarette breaks. It was a horrible experience.

Went here for a double date in which we didn't have reservations for a Friday night. The gentleman told us he wouldn't be able to seat us until closer to 8:30. Which we said that's fine and that we would go down the street for a drink. He took our number and ended up texting us a lot sooner and have us a ten minute heads up. Super nice!

Then our dinner and waitress was wonderful. We wanted to share a bottle of wine but didn't want to pay out the wazoo (as the place has GREAT selection from $30-1,000 bottles). She recommended an affordable wine which turned out great. 

All of us loved the food.

Nothing special. I haven't been, but apparently it's just a wannabe Frankford Hall. Called ahead to ask if they had happy hour, but only upon arrival did they tell us that happy hour prices are only inside Opa, not the beer garden. Pricing was quite expensive especially since we were expecting happy hour prices.

I actually can't drink because of health reasons, so I was excited to see the Jenga and Connect 4 sets to play games with my party, but the Jenga set was incomplete and hard to set up/clean up. Maybe invest in a couple of new sets?

Got take out here using a grub hub 10% off promo - this restaurant is pickup only! 

Service is good - I ordered the chimichangas and I asked for everything separately, and they accommodated accordingly. The portion was ginormous- I was ridiculously full after one chimichanga, and I still had a whole other one left along with a full plate of retried beans and chips and salsa.

Price was 14$, but I think I got my money's worth. The food was deliciously messy; the guacamole, melted white cheese, grilled chicken all blended together beautifully. (Looked kinda gross but tasted amazing)

This is THE place to take any european car in Indianapolis.  I've had two Mercedes, meticulously maintained by Euro Motorworks.
