Love the vegan and vegetarian tamale options here. The vegan blue corn is my favorite. The veggie curry tamales are good? But they leave my tastebuds a little confused so I'm not sure how I feel about them. My friends love it though. 

They offer takeout and also frozen tamales for purchase.  All the ones I have tried have been delicious.  I did try a seasonal pumpkin tamale a few years ago and it tasted like Fall. Mmm, still dreaming about those. 

I am always disappointed by their sides and salsa. The chips are not my favorite and the salsas are a little bland and watery. I'll stick to only tamales in the future.

A Gem of a place in open view on one of the corners of mass ave.

We visited mass avenue on a busy Friday night needing to get a quick meal, and old point tavern really didn't disappoint.

Plenty of places to sit in a nicely open small bar, however they also have a wonderful selection of food.

We went for the cheesy chicken tacos which came out piping hot within 10 minutes of ordering. 

An excellent place, with parking right outside, however it is paid parking which is often full right on the street. I would recommend not planning to park right outside , we just got very lucky that a car was pulling out as we were arriving.

Modern Mexican culinary experience  -  The venue doesn't have an ethnic feel, and it definitely lacks character. The food, however, is excellent. Salsa is fresh and tasty. Sure it could be slightly more spicy for me, but I enjoyed the salsa. Pico de gallo was fresh and retained the taste of the ingredients. Chile relleno was filled with chicken, mazella cheese, and surprising morsels of pecan inside the relleno. Brilliant, I say!! I like authenticity of ethnic food, but I loved the twist that Garcia incorporated. Well done!!

The pool is nothing like it is in the photos and to top it off no pool side service. The rooms are nice and the staff was accommodating. However you could stay at a Hilton garden inn for half the price and have the same experience. I vacation quite a bit and part of my enjoyment is pool side service. I only stayed one night and canceled the rest of my 4 night stay. I ended up at the Weston down the street. Corey was the manager and apologized for the inconvenience which was kind. If you are looking to relax by the pool do not choose this hotel!!! Other than that my stay was splendid.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
One of the best places to get sushi in Nashville.  My favorites are the Caterpillar roll and the Playboy.

I've ordered sushi to go for lunch many times.  One time I ordered and then something came up and I couldn't make it to pick up my sushi.  I called and told them and they said no problem.  The next time I went to Samurai, I asked to pay for the sushi I ordered a week ago and never picked up but they wouldn't take the money.  Very nice staff!

The atmosphere is more like a "hole in the wall" type of place.

Highly recommend!

Took a white suit here yeah it's a white suit I know. It looked pretty much the same all the stains were still there.  And they pressed it really hard it looked horrible look like a napkin that was left in a pocket. I didn't complain I walked right out the door went to a different cleaners on College Avenue and they laughed and fixed it all up for me stains are gone the wrinkles are almost out. This place has dead flowers in the windows cobwebs hanging from the ceiling stains in the carpet. I should've known better
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Please keep in mind that I have only been to this place once.  The menu said the Garden Burrito included Cauliflower and Carrots rice and beans.  I got the non dairy version (no sour cream).  The burrito was mostly rice, no Cauliflower and no carrots.  It had some lettuce, tomatoes and red cabbage but not enough to warrant calling it a garden burrito.  Service was fast and the man at the counter was pleasant.  If you order the Garden Burrito I would just make sure you confirm the contents before leaving the establishment.  Not a horrible experience but I'm not likely to go back

I live right down the road from this car wash and there aren't many options on places right on this stretch of 19. I've gone here multiple times but it appears things don't improve with time. I purchased their Superior Wash last visit, which runs around $26, plus a tip for attendants. You'd expect an awesome job for a price that steep. They did a decent job on the inside, but don't make much effort on nooks and crannies. The outside was a total disaster. I had to ask for the towel to finish the job myself. I'll be driving further out next time to a place that can deliver.

This is a hidden little restaurant in an unsuspecting location in the middle of a plaza so its really easy to miss. I've eaten here twice and the food was great both times. Their bruschetta is good but it's on tiny little crostini instead of bread so portions are so small! Their chicken lentil soup was prob the best I've ever had. The prices are fair and the restaurant is small but cute. I wouldn't agree with the reviews saying its THE best Italian since blah blah blah, because there are better Italian restaurants in the Tampa area, but I will give it credit for being a good option in an area with very little variety.

Get thee to Andiario stat. First off, the restaurant is gorgeous. Decor is understated, seats are spaced out nicely, and the open kitchen is subtle. We were lucky to snag a Friday night reservation for a weekend we happened to be in town for a wedding, and I'm SO glad we did. Service was prompt but not annoying. We had heard such great things about the pasta, so we tried the approach of 2 pasta dishes, 1 protein, and then 1 dessert, splitting a bottle of wine. The menu changes frequently but everything was so delicious. I can't recommend it enough!!

This is my favorite sushi restaurant in Tampa. The prices are beyond reasonable (my favorite roll is the cold roll for $8.75 and it is amazing) and the service is always fast and friendly. You get a lot of food for such a good price. I ordered asoup, salad, specialty roll, sweet tea, and split an 8 piece appetizer of gyoza all for just $16. The sushi tastes super fresh and was tender, and they were generous with the amount of fish and veggies inside of the roll instead of just stuffing it with rice. My friend always gets a massive order of hibachi for just $12. I come here probably twice a month and have never been disappointed.

I've read mixed reviews about sushi brothers but decided to give this place a try since it was so close to my house and I am very disappointed. I am by no means a sushi snob. All I need is a spicy tuna roll and simple eel roll and I am happy. I enjoy restaurant sushi, grocery store sushi, and hospital sushi. I never thought you can have a "bad" spicy tuna roll until now. I ordered the spicy tuna roll and eel roll from here. The spicy tuna roll was SUPER SALTY. It was inedible. I could not finish it. The eel roll tasted very artificial. I would've been better off getting a spicy tuna roll at rouse's.

Had this for the first time and I was very disappointed. I had a spicy tuna roll, a yellowtail scallion roll, and a special eel roll. The spicy tuna was way too mushy and had a very odd consistency and didn't taste fresh at all. The yellowtail scallion roll had no scallions, and the yellowtail was not chopped up, just a big hunk of yellowtail. The special eel roll was just eel and cucumber (not very special...). The prices were not bad so that was a plus but the sushi was obviously not very fresh and it kept falling a part whenever I picked it up with chopsticks. I won't be eating here again...

Great little sushi spot located on a quiet street with a huge menu and great sashimi! 

I ordered the sashimi appetizers, edamame, and two special rolls. The food was ridiculously cheap for how good it was. The sashimi appetizers was around $8.95 for 12 pieces of sashimi (tuna, white tuna, salmon, and yellowtail). The two special rolls were very tasty, but I didn't enjoy the sauces on them. The banana tempura/spicy tuna roll in soy wrap was fantastic. Huge roll for only $6.95, unbeatable. The salmon sashimi here is also thickly cut and fresh. 

The waitress was really polite and checked up on me so many times. I'll be back!

I'd never gotten a chance until this location opened, and...WOW! I'm super impressed. The waitstaff is great. The restaurant is clean and comfortable. The food---phenomenal. I love their salads, and they're so big that they, easily, make two meals. They even serve Stag on draft. My only suggestion is to add more heat to the Buffalo Chicken Pizza. It's cheesy and delish, but there's not a ton of buffalo flavor. For me--I'd just ask them to pile on the "hot"! Everything I've ordered or tasted from someone else has been to die for. You must check this spot out!

Hand made tamales using fresh all organic masa were delicious.  Quick serve walk up and order, friendly service, nice atmosphere inside and a great value. We really enjoyed! We also liked the chipotle, habenero, and jalapeño hot sauces made with organic ingredients, so we bought a bottle of each to go. I'm glad I found this spot using Yelp's reviews. Also, visit the Tucson Tamale website which is interesting too! Oh by the way, they ship tamales anywhere in dry ice, so keep it in mind, cuz, I will! Cuz, I do not cook-up tamales "en mi casa!"

This is a pretty property and the room was fine. For the price I prefer a suite with 2 rooms. Had one incident where I made it to the top floor back side only to find out my key had stopped working. Infuriating. One of the side doors was out of order. They kept one of the side gates to the U shaped parking lot closed and locked. Maybe for security but also annoying. Lastly, and not so much the hotels fault, but there is road construction going on at the highway directly behind the hotel and they start bright and early with heavy equipment and back up sirens. When I return next month, I probably won't be staying here.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: It's small size and portions make you feel full and cozy.  That being said, make a reservation or your chance of grabbing a table will be as small as the place itself.  I've been here for restaurant week but also outside of that, and what I respect about this place most, is that the quality of the food remains consistent and reliable no matter when you walk through the door.  Do yourself a flavor and try the blood orange margarita as well as the guacamole with bacon.  The tacos and the tostadas are equally satisfying.  Weather you grab a table or a drink and a bite at the bar, the service is phenomenal.

This place is Philly's best kept secret or judging from the number of reviews here maybe not. Here's what you need to know: it's small, they don't take reservations, they're a byob, they do take out, they're delicious and fresh. If you're coming in for awesome sushi, you won't be disappointed, if you're coming in for thrills and fancy decor well, this may not be the place for you. Me personally though, I love the decor, or actually the lack of thereof. Except for a wall of photographs you won't see any adornments. The focus is on the rolls and the guys behind the counter making your delicious dinner. I'll keep coming back for that.

Much better this time around. Once again, Mardi Gras brings me back into town! I actually didn't mean to stay here again (everything was booked except here and Four Seasons) but I'm glad we did. 

Hyatt beds are like the clouds you imagine Snuggle, the laundry bear, would sleep on. The best sleep happens here. Our room setup was different from our last room and everything seemed in good order. 

My only gripe would be our room neighbors. Party weekend means party people. Our room reeked of marijuana horridly.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I heard about Loren & Mari from an IndyStar article and loved reading the story of this family-run business, so I grabbed a friend and came here for an early lunch. I'm glad a local restaurant took over the space where a chain used to be.

I liked, but didn't love, my healthy green quesadilla. I think it's hard to stand out in the Mexican food market, and I can't say my dish was overly memorable here. I did like the chips with salsa, guac and queso - but chips and salsa are not free. 

That being said, I would come back here to try some more dishes.

PSA: Dunkin' Donut Happy Hour is every day (I think? Don't quote me on that) from 3-6 p.m. Get a medium iced coffee or tea for only $1 (plus tax, but still). A lot more affordable than Starbucks and IMO better coffee. I don't like coffee that much, but I enjoyed the iced coffee with caramel swirl (swirl is better than syrup, trust me). 

The lady at the counter realized we were all getting happy hour iced coffees, so she took all our orders at once, brought them all to the counter and then we paid individually (#productive.) 

Also, a drive-thru exists if you don't feel like leaving your car.

Pros:
+Location in downtown Indy.
+Easily accessible parking garage for quick in and out shopping trips.
+Bright, clean and new.
+Looks to be decent selection.

Cons: 
I went with a friend to get balloons for our friend's birthday. We approached the floral/balloon counter and no one was there. After two minutes, we asked the help desk if someone was coming. They were no help. After almost ten minutes of waiting, an employee finally said "Do you need help?" She was nice and helped us, but took a looong time. It was like Mr. Bean in Love Actually at the jewelry counter slow. 

Customer service is lacking but otherwise is a decent store.

I thinks it is expensive for what it is. The parking is not good, we parked on the street, we found after you can park for 2 hours in the parking structure. The service is very good and attentive.The wine selection limited to italian wine which is not my favorite. My wife complained the eggplant tomato sauce appetizer was " sweet" and in fact it was. The mussels were good. I had asparagus with risotto and the bolognesa, and my wife caesar salad and  chicken marsala and again she complained to me about the sweetness of the food, like added sugar.The ambiance was good.

This place is nothing. This place is nothing special. It's your average neighborhood pizza place. Everything on the menu is just alright. Only usually order here, because it's close by and deliveries fairly quick/ under an hour. They're going to couple times that we had forgotten her order on GrubHub and had the nerve to be super rude about it. Once they gave us hot saucs instead of hot sauce with are boneless wings( seriously). Once I ordered a mushroom pizza for lunch, and the pizza came with about four mushrooms on it. Really hit or miss with this place.

So service was fast and the food was good. However, when I went to get my drink the floor was super sticky. Which I mentioned as I was leaving. Also, as I was trying to enjoy my meal before driving back home, I heard the employees yelling in the back about another employee who had been on their phone. Number one, if you have an issue with an employee direct it to them. Number two, you should not let any guests hear you yelling about issues with other coworkers. I came there to enjoy my lunch peacefully. Not to hear employees scream about their coworkers.

What a wonderful clinic!!!! The focus is truly on pets. I came in as a walk and was greeted within seconds (by Ronnie) and given the paperwork necessary to get my dog's heartworm test/pills. I was able to go back with her, and there were 4 vets in there (maybe 2 of them were students) and they were all helpful and informative! One of them even reminded me to ask about a rebate... saving me $50! I can't even explain how grateful I am for this clinic... definitely will be back! ***oh I just want to add: I was in and out in less than 40 minutes!!!!

The dining area was about half full on a Tuesday night and yet the wait for the food was incredibly long - over an hour for the entrees.  I must have contemplated several times making my way across the street to the Olive Garden to get me some Tour-Of-Italy along with some free salad and breadsticks.  

As an app, the warm crab cheesecake is can't miss.  For entrees, the Tuna Livornese was passable with an ice cream sized scoop of linguini.  My fellow diners enjoyed the Salmon and Lobster Ravioli.  However when it was all said and done, the wait just killed the dining experience.

Went on  Friday night around 8 PM....place was packed.   Went upstairs for a beer and was called about 20 min later with a table for 2 downstairs.   The place is cramped.  Not exactly an intimate date spot, but when you're dining a few feet away from Mr Greg Gumbel himself, who cares?  Went safe with the Lasagna and Chicken Parm and was happy overall with the selection.  Large portions, decent taste.  The sauce wasn't anything special.  It's an average restaurant with good service but really what you come here for is the nostalgia and to say, "I've eaten at the oldest Italian restaurant in the country."

Stayed here for work for a couple nights, and it was my first time in NO but man were the people who work here surly and no interest in helping anyone who might be staying here. Worst part was an alarm was going off at 12am-2am both nights I was there and I called the front desk to see if they could do something and the response was 'nope'. It was probably in a crawl space because I checked it out and it wasn't in a room, so seriously where is this POS alarm that is going off? I would smash it like Bruce banner if I had found it.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I tried Jims for the first time today. A lot of people have recommended them, and it's very hard to find good pizza in South Jersey. Unfortunately, my search will continue. We did pick up for our order and were within the 30 minutes we were told. It's about a 10 minute drive from our home and we ate as soon as we got home. The two pizzas we ordered tasted like they were microwaved and were very congealed. It was also barely warm. We also had 10 mild wings that were barely warm, tough, and looked undercooked. Our two orders of fries also tasted like the grease they were cooked in. I will not go here again.

Shop is tiny, be ready to know what you want! While  you certainly can sample it can feel awkward if anyone else is there due to how small the space is. I had pomegranate blueberry ice cream with dark chocolate chunks and whipped cream. It was outstanding!! My go to is always vanilla so I went way off the charts with this and was glad I did!! My wife had peanut butter and mocha in a cup with a sugar cone on the side and was equally pleased! We each got a small, 2 scoops, it was plenty!!! 
One note: toppings aren't listed anywhere, probably would've gotten some if I knew what was available. There was no way to tell.

The coffee is good. However, we bought a box of coffee today (enough for 8 people or so) and they said it did not come with cups or sugar. One girl said you had to purchase the cups for $3 and some change. The other girl working there said she gave cups with it for free and there was nowhere listed on the menu for cups to be bought. Personally, if I buy a box of coffee, I want cups to go with it. If you are going to charge me for cups, I will not be purchasing my coffee from you any more. That is the dumbest, cheapest thing I've heard in a long time to try to charge people for cups.

The food was convenient, but, they charge you to deliver. I am a great tipper, but, get irritated at nickel and diming.  The food was good, but, pricey. We ordered for dinner and I didn't realize how large the portions were, so, the portions were commiserate with price, but, I wasn't told over the phone that I wasn't ordering a combo, so I was a bit surprised when everything was priced separately. I.e, rice, egg roll, etc. I wouldn't have ordered it all if I hadn't been asked....hence, thinking it was a combo. 

It is convenient location wise, so, I will likely order again.  The food is good, but, not great.

Hubby had a half day, so when I picked him up, we were hungry for lunch!

Came across town, and didn't realize there was an Arby's right here!

We were planning on trying the sushi, but decided on Arby's.

Drive they was long and busy.

They were actually fast on putting our order together.

Downside: No straws or or napkins!

We checked the bag and I had to run inside.

But the dining area was closed?,.. no I wasn't going through the drive thru!

I called, and they came outside and apologized.

Just check before you leave the window!

Wanted to go out for breakfast, but nothing was open at 6:15 in the morning.

By this time, of driving around, decided to just grab a coffee and donut.

Asked the cashier if there were any cake donuts with maple and peanuts, and heard "NO"!..

So rude of a drive thru... decided to get maple bars and coffee.

$7.10 later, the maple bars weren't bad. The coffee was actually hot, and had the right amount of cream and sugar.

As I was watching thru the drive thru, none of them had masks or gloves on, and one had really long hair (maybe needed to be put up)?..

I liked the coffee but the attitude has to be better!

Had to do some shopping at Raleys,
and it was almost lunch time.

Called in while I was shopping.

Ordered the cashew shrimp lunch and the schezuan egg plant with chow mein.

Order would be ready in 25 min...

Enjoyed the beautiful day looking at the snow peaked mountains..

Walked over and there was one table being used.

Waited another ten minutes for the order.

$19.92 for two lunch combos, included soup, and vegetable egg roll, fortune cookies (dogs love them)..

Better than expected and will certainly try another lunch in the future.. just order ahead.. or be prepared to wait.

Glad I stopped and ordered.

Not sure why this place has good reviews but coming from a sushi fanatic- it was awful. There are places down the street from this place that were AMAZING! The sushi was gross and didn't even seem to be edible- my husband and I took a bite and we didn't finish it. The fish was not fresh and didn't taste right, as well as the dishes were not cleaned. The service was so awful too! The waitress was not nice and wouldn't help us at all, and would go to someone else. Never going back- not worth the sickness we had the next day from eating at this place.

This is the closest Starbucks to my house so I am here a few times a week. 

I like that they never mess my order up. I always get soy milk and my lattes so they ask me if I still want whipped cream and I say yes. The whipped cream is always there. (Many other Starbucks still don't put the whipped on) 

I was a bit disappointed when I had my dog in the car and asked for a puppychino. They gave me a little shot glass of whipped cream. They used to give them in the bigger cups. I was willing to pay for it so I was confused.

A bit pricier, but remember "price is what you pay, value is what you get." In that regard, this place definitely offers a lot of value.

From dining experience to the food itself, everything here was top notch.

I had the Ahi Tuna and it was amazing, and I was with a (fairly picky) party of 4, and they all enjoyed their meals as well. Even the organic chicken offered a really unique flavor.

Selection of drinks really compliments what's on the menu, and the servers are quite knowledgeable. You can tell a lot of thought was put into the customer experience and it shows.

Overall, well worth it!

I really wanted to like this place as it is so close to home.  However, when a local Mexican restaurant doesn't make things from scratch it really bothers me.  We ordered guacamole which was cold from having come out of the fridge.   Fresh made guacamole is warm not ice cold.  The chips were good but not homemade.  The two complimentary salsas were so spicy they were uneatable.  We shared an order of the steak sopas.  They were okay, but nothing I would rush to come back and eat.  
Unfortunately, we are probably crossing this place off our list

Cute place with friendly service.  We came here for lunch as we had a local flavor deal.   The place had a few customers but was empty for the most part.  I ordered the wedge salad which was okay.   Nothing special about it.   I ordered the mussels for my lunch. I do not care for large mussels so they were just okay.   My daughter ordered the fettuccini Alfredo which she said was fine.   Our server was very nice and let my daughter try different gelatos.  
I might return again and try dinner if I had another local flavor deal.   It was fine for a $15 lunch.

I like to come to this place every week the staff is really nice and they have helped me with my questions about washing  I like to do laundry and do some homework I'm a sbcc student I decided that I would bring my laptop and get some work done as I tried to connect it re routed me to the cox page it seems like they didn't pay their bill  so now my plans have change my laundry was getting done so I couldn't stop the cycle but once it finishes it am taking off cause I have to get work done I'm not coming back until it gets fixed  and it's sad cause its advertised on the window....
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Great sushi! I've been to sushi brothers a bunch of times and have always been very impressed by everything I've gotten! I especially love their special rolls, which are good sized for the price! Some great rolls are the saints black and gold roll (with mango yum!) and the LSU roll! I love that they give you a complimentary clear soup with your meal! Make sure you know that they give you a free soup, since I one time made the mistake of ordering a miso soup, which was huge and $5!! Definitely recommend! One of the best sushi places in the city!

Food -- 4 stars
Price -- 4 stars 
Service -- 4 stars
Atmosphere -- 4 stars

I wasn't too impressed. The menu was a bit confusing. We kept waiting for the loop on the tv to come back around so we could see the flavors of waffle cones. We ended up asking and they offer red velvet and lavender. That's pretty cool. We didn't see them use the nitrogen machines at all. I'm actually pretty confused. My daughter had chocolate ice cream with strawberries. They just plopped the strawberries on top and handed her the cone. Nothing fancy. 

The floors were sticky and the prices were high. I dont see the appeal.

Even for diner food nothing really stood out for our party of four.  

The prices are good but not great and the food quality just seemed cheap. To me, the flavors were bland.  I did enjoy my corned beef hash but the white gravy had very little flavor, the potatoes were bland as well.  I will say service was great and the establishment stayed busy the entire time we were there with patrons coming in and out frequently. This diner is open 24/7 so if you find yourself in the area late night in a need of a quick bill this might be a good option but I would not drive out of my way to get here.

This place has been my go to for a couple years now. Most of the time it's pretty good and decent for the price. Lin is the best tech there. Within the last couple months, they hired someone who is awful & it seems I get stuck with her when I go. The pedi is crappy & the mani is worse. I get a basic mani with no color & the paint job is horrible. I didn't know you could screw up clear polish but she did. There are a lot of bubbles and the entire nail isn't even painted. I will be finding something else close to my place.

Edit- not even 6 hours & now my toenails are chipped.

I'd only come to this place if I absolutely had to. Cheesesteaks are pretty good. Pizza isn't the greatest, sandwiches are mediocre. 

The reason they get one star rating is their service. One of the women who works the phone and takes orders is cool, outside of that RUDE. The main taller young guy is ridiculously disrespectful to his workers and it's so horrible to witness. I've seen him curse and yell at his cooks in front of customers. It's sad. 

I wouldn't support this place with people who can't even love their own people. Not okay with me.

Good to catch a game, or as I did, attend a fantasy draft. The food is not anything particularly special, typical sports bar menu of sandwiches, salads, burgers, fries, etc. Some items are loaded with salt or are too dried out. The space is large and open which is nice as opposed to some other dark and dingy sports bar I have been in. The service is nothing above and beyond what I would expect of a sports bar. They're quick but not there to really enhance your experience. It can get loud in here during games.

3 of us came here on a Tuesday evening for their infamous 4 course Foie Gras tasting menu. Easily one of the best meals of my life! It was my first time trying Foie Gras and I couldn't have asked for a better experience. The service was great, and the food was absolutely delicious. The portions were generous for Foie Gras (and the fact that it was only $45 for 4 courses was really a steal). I was really impressed with the creativity behind each course and how everything went together. Aside from the meal, this is a great, intimate BYOB spot!

I've been here before and the food was good. Not phenomenal but good. Came back for a second time to take my family and tried to make reservations. She said they do not take reservations and we hung up. We waited for an hour to be told 2 people were ahead of us. Then 20
Mins later we asked and 5 people were ahead of us. When asked how that is possible she stated when people "call ahead" they skip the line. Why would someone calling ahead skip other people that had been waiting for over an hour. Several groups left after being told the same thing. Very poor customer service. Call ahead wasn't even mentioned on the call.

Here is my fun night with Luca Pizza tonight! I placed an order and was quoted 45 minutes for delivery at 6:45 PM. It's 8:35 PM and still haven't received my order. Instead of whoever I spoke to on the phone apologizing, he argued with me about the time I placed the order. Claiming that his system shows that I paced the order at 7:23. That would be that the order was entered almost 30 minutes after I placed the order. Zero customer service and complete disrespect. Will never order again! Sad that this place was a cherished childhood memory.

This was a great little ice cream place we stopped into this weekend while in NOLA. We were all craving something sweet after touring the Garden District and I remembered that I had book marked an Ice Cream shop someone told us about during our last visit this summer. Turns out we were only a couple miles away.

Loved the fact that they made the waffle cones fresh and had a number of flavors to choose from. I loved the Coquita (a coconut flavored ice cream with some liquor) and the banana pudding was very good too. Micah (my 14 year old) loved the butter pecan.

I tried Maggie Moo's Ice cream from their food truck the other day while it was in Shelbyville at tractor Supply. I had never tried their ice cream before, but had heard many good things about them. The ice cream was ok, but not as good as I had hoped. I was a little bummed that they only had about 5 or 6 flavors, but can't really fault them much for that because it was a food truck after all. I decided on butter pecan because I didn't feel like cotton candy or plain chocolate, Vanilla, or mint chip. In all reality, not trying to bash them in any way, but I think I'll stick with Baskin Robins or Blue Bell next time

Fro Yo is a great alternative to the other dessert places in the CWE. When I'm not craving cookies, Tutti Frutti is the place to go. They have a decent selection of flavors and even have soy options. Fantastic array of toppings, great sauces, and they can even make coffee drinks or shakes! 
Get their punch card-only takes 10 to get one free! Bring friends and go crazy. 
They have a really nice section of tables outside, which is perfect during the summer
Props to management on hiring selections-every employee has been so nice and cheerful each time I've been in. 
And they get bonus points for making it easy to recycle spoons!

We ordered from here recently. Good, cheap chinese food and fast delivery. It really is cheap.  I got one of the chicken combinations platters that came with rice and an egg roll and it was something like $6.50! Now, it's not the most amazing chinese food i've ever had. But, it's not bad at all and is obviously a great value. I have ordered from other chinese places in the area and the price difference was huge. I will definitely order from here next time i'm craving some chinese and don't feel like spending too much.

I came here for the first time in a long time for lunch not too long ago. I would describe it as average. It has a nice and relaxed atmosphere. I ordered a lunch special that was reasonably priced which came with pasta and a salad. It is a nice plus that this place is a BYOB, but they don't really have anything to drink at all. I don't drink soda and couldn't find anything to drink besides water. Service was kinda slow, but our waitress was friendly. Overall, this is a solid place to eat but nothing to write home about.

Went here for the first time the other week. I was a little skeptical to try it because I was mad about peace a pizza being replaced but my friend recommended we go there. The layout of the place looks very different than before but in a good way. You get to make a custom personal pizza but I did one of the signature ones. I got the BBQ chicken pizza which was very good. My only complaint was that there was way too much cilantro on it, like more cilantro than cheese. But, this could be easily fixed next time. Prices are pretty reasonable. Staff was very accommodating and friendly.

Came here before a night out with my friends to pick up some liquor. The store itself was nice and clean. The selection was about the same as all the other PA liquor stores. However, the girl at the register was so rude! I worked retail back in college, so I totally understand how some people treat the employees like they are beneath them and how much it can suck. But, that isn't an excuse to be rude to nice people for no reason. I don't think she smiled once, and she didn't say like "have a good night" or anything. She really was miserable and my friend commented on it too, after we left. Unacceptable.

An OK Japanese and Asian fusion restaurant (with some Thai dishes) on the edge of the French Quarter with good service. Funky unique decor with changing lights under the bar. 

Their hamachi kama (grilled yellowtail collar) was a success if a tad bit too salty. They offer soy sauce on the side. It should be salt and pepper. They should not salt the fish so much. Instead, grill it to bring out its flavor. Then, let the guest add salt and or pepper at the table. 

Their seafood soup was quite bland (the soup base has no taste). Their fried calamari appetizer was terrible: rubbery, not tender, tasteless.

Heather is hands down the best stylist I've ever had. She is attentive, she listens, and takes her time. She will also be very honest with you about your options given your hair texture. Heather has been cutting my hair for a few years now - we've gone through several variations of 'rock bobs' and pixies. She is always able to find the balance between my inner rock star and my professional life. I am so thankful that she opened her own place - an entire salon that exudes her positive and peaceful energy! Aside from being the most talented stylist ever, she is an amazing human. I cannot recommend her highly enough.

This restaurant is by far my favorite place in Nashville. Easy. 

My first trip here was impromptu when a reservation was lost at another place. And they won me over right away. The staff is incredible. Professional, yet personable. They show that they care about the food the serve and that they care about your experience. 

The food and drinks are excellent too. Every time we go were blown away with our food. They use some locally sourced ingredients and meats. 

If you've never been, make it a priority. It's excellent. You won't be let down.

solid sushi restaurant that is part of the food court located on the 2nd floor of the H-mart.  Their sushi tastes above average and they do a good job presenting the sushi, which makes it look even more delicious! Prices are comparable to other sushi joints around philly.  

Random side note, they cannot serve hot tea here because according to the bylaws of the food court, the restaurant right next to them already sells tea, making them unable to sell any...for anyone who loves drinking hot tea with their sushi, heads up!

At this Dunkin donuts location, I had a bad experience with their donuts.  Got the Boston creme and Krueller donut which we both very dry and tasted like they had been out for more than a day.  Seems like Dunkins skimp out on the creme given my Boston creme only had one good bite full of creme...otherwise my friends get coffee here often and it is pretty solid in terms of consistency as other Dunkins.  

This place is conveniently located right next to the 8th street market frank ford line and can get packed with people in the morning and rush hours.

Stopped in Sump Coffee for a monthly "brunch" outing. The food options are limited, but the coffee and tea options not only varied but interesting.

The place has two rooms wih the exposed brick and wood look. One wall had skull wallpaper. Overall rather masculine in appearance.

I had a plum ginger iced tea from the seasonal menu. It was more plum than ginger and I was happy about that. Delicious and only $3. 

I also had a poptart-like (only better) pastry. It was good but I'd like to try something else next time.

Pros
--$2 wash in average (small) sized machine 
--Relatively quiet
--Funny business name

Cons
--No cards on machines. 
--ATM minimum withdrawal is $20 and $3 fee.
--The doors to the dryers don't stay open when loading and unloading! They slowly close on you! You have to reopen the door as you load or unload OR you have to hold it open with one hand. Very irritating, especially if you end up hitting your head. I tried the dryer next to mine and it did the same thing. :( 

The dryer door issue is why I will not be back.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Four Strings closed their kitchen shortly after my first visit. That's right: no food to be had. Why?? All that delicious cheesecake, gone. 
My friend and I walked in around 3, when it opened. There were leftovers from some party that had just ended on several tables. No greeting at first. I was concerned we were trespassing on a private event. Nope. I asked for a menu and realized my famished friend and I would have to go elsewhere. 
I'm really disappointed but grateful this happened with a local friend and not someone I had drive an hour or more.

Went here for the first time recently. 

Prices are average-ish? $2.50 to wash a large load. But $1.00 for 45 minutes of dry... that's a bit high.

Estimated time to wash: 25 minutes. Actual time: closer to 50. I don't know whether I just got a bad machine or if these are the slowest washers ever.

It took over 45 minutes to dry the load, so I paid $2 to dry. :(

Place looks cool with ancient couches and wood paneling. Antenna TV channel was playing Maude and Archie Bunker's Place. Like being in my parents' basement in the early 1980s. 

I feel like $6.50 and two hours for one large load was not quite worth it.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
Perfect location 1 1/2 blocks off Bourbon Street. Close enough to the action but far enough from the mix. Quite hotel connected somehow to The Ritz so you could use amenities from both hotels. Must be the same company.
Seemed a little musty at times but the buildings are very old and humidity was very high.
Rooms were comfortable and spacious. Every room a suite so you have a separate living room area.
I like the little refreshment areas they all have so you can grab a beer, soda, snack or whatever on your way up to your room. Very convenient.
Anything in the Marriott family seems to be a safe bet.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I will never understand the hype around Jeni's. Yes, it's good ice cream. BUT it costs about an arm and a leg to get a scoop of it. I can walk down the street to Kroger and get a gallon of ice cream that's JUST as good for the cost of a kiddie cone at Jeni's. I would much rather do that, and then I can eat it in my room alone and enjoy my life in the best way possible. I will give it to Jeni's though, they create some interesting flavors. Now I have some inspiration for the next time I head over to Coldstone Creamery.

Service was fast and friendly enough. But we ordered five drinks - four simple iced coffees - that were all not filled up (about a half inch or more below the lid). 

The iced Cloud Macchiato was like 3 inches down and barely cold within a couple minutes. The picture I posted has NOT been drunken out of. The foam didn't last at all. That was a $6 drink. I've ordered these drinks before and they aren't like this. The Cloud Macchiato does have the foam go down, but only after you start drinking. Not so fast on it's own. 

Both of these issues aren't normal so I wasn't impressed.

So horrible. While I was drinking and roaming in NOLA in the French quarters area in the afternoon, I walked past this place thinking "when doesn't pizza sound like a good idea"... especially when you're drinking and need a snack! I guess if you are at this place it's a bad idea. The staff wasn't that friendly. The pizza tasted like it was made yesterday (maybe just earlier that day) and had been sitting in a warmer for hours upon hours until it withered away to some kind of "food" that was no longer edible. Highly disappointing for a quick grabbing slice. Go anywhere but here.

It's a standard Hilton. Good check in with friendly front deskers who kept it moving. Room was a bit less shiny and newish than a lot of Hilton's it felt like. Rather small work out area, but high quality Precor Equipment. I made a boo-boo and made my reservation for one day less than I thought. Called and fixed it after extending online. 

The front desk agents booked me for my same room without any trouble. I would have stayed at the Doubletree next door since I like things a little more laid back, but DT had those cookies that are so good and I'm trying not to eat sweets.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Best cut I've had in Philly - and what a steal!

This place is right on Broad Street - deep in South Philly. The vibe is chill, and the place is clean. There is one main stylist who also is the owner and I usually can find parking right in the area or in the middle of Broad Street without much of an issue.

I usually show the style that I'm looking for on my phone and she delivers consistently! 

Also there's always a fresh wash after the cut! You're not going to have to risk being a hair piñata after leaving since it's taken care of before you exit - looking fly and feeling fresh! 

Recommend this place highly! 

FYI:  cash only!

Despite finding other location of Sake pretty enjoyable, I often struggle to find the same enjoyment with this spot. It is often convenient and we keep going because of that. And sake is always a great spot to feed the whole family when sushi is the request. But the service and execution at this location often lacks. On my last visit the problem was with our tuna tataki. While the tuna was of good quality, it was sliced way too thick for tataki and not seared enough. That sort inconsistency is what make this location lose a star over other Sake Cafes.

Okay have not been to a barber shop since I was single digits and my dad who was military insisted I go and get crew cuts. So it's been a long time. 

I had a need for a beard and brow trim and read good things about this place. 

When I entered it seemed a little chaotic but I was sitting for no more than three minutes when Anthony came out made eye contact and wisked me to his chair!  The rest must be all caps. 

FANTASTIC WORK, SERVICE, PROFESSIONAL DEMEANOR, BEST BEARD TRIM EVER. 

Thank you!  I WILL be back!

Good sushi but terrible service. If you're really craving for sushi, you're going to have to wait a long time to get it and sometimes you don't even get what you order. 

You write on a piece of paper what you want and every time, they always 'forget' certain sushi rolls. The waitresses are horrible. They don't check your table if you need anything. To eat here, you have to have a lot of patience.

The price raised to $20.95 on weekdays and $22.95 on weekends. So you're spending about $25-$30 when you come here.

Came a second time for dinner with two others and each got the premier omakase. I had made a reservation online through resy. 

Got there on time and was promptly seated. Everything was great and tasted super fresh. The rice could have been a little tighter though as a couple of times the pieces fell apart, but the quality of the fish and seafood was great. 

I would recommend early or late instead of the middle as the place was super full around 7, and our meal felt kind of rushed at the end which kind of ruins the experience. 

But all in all, I'll be around probably more for lunch as the food here is pretty good :)

Came here after moving to this side of town. Also saw this was on dive, drives and diners. I love fried chicken so when I am craving this guilty pleasure. This is a great place to go to.  They have a unique menu as well. Such as jalapeño poppers stuffed with peanut butter.  Never tried it.. But sounds good. The only reason why they didn't get a perfect score..: the side dishes they serve aren't very appealing. I would have to say.. They are just OK..

But I do return for the great tasting, juicy fried chicken.  Just wished they would up the sides.

Pros
  1. Easy process is you purchase through hotwire. 
   2. Will be greeted with a smile. 
   3. In and out. 
   4. Informative. 
    5. Garage attendant is accommodating. 
    6. Hours of operation are reasonable. 
     

Cons. 
  1. Associate is extremely talkative with the neighboring company. 
   2. Upsale tactics 
   3. Vehicles run poorly. 
   4. No longterm customer deals. 
    5. Vehicles are not that fuel efficient. 
    6. Person that checks the car out of the parking area is often missing. 
    7. Establishment is dingy. 
     8. Feel like this is the bottom of the barrel.

We love Dr. Hart. He has a very calming demeanor with our two dogs, a border collie mix and a husky/boxer who is typically very nervous around new people. Loved Dr. Hart the first time he met him! Reasonable prices and the ability to schedule a little bit later into the evening is very nice too. 
Dr. Pagan is also a competent vet, but my dogs prefer the calming presence of Dr. Hart. However, if your dog is high energy and loves excitement, Dr. Pagan would probably be best. Two ends of the spectrum, different strokes, etc.
My dogs went to him when I was a kid, and as an adult, I will continue to take my pets here.

We ate there 2 days ago. The restaurant was not busy by any means at 6:30p on a Sunday night. It still took us close to 40 minutes to get our entries. I got the create your own pasta, I asked for Pesto/Alfredo, the pesto was Overwhelming, I was finally able to get a side of Alfredo sauce after waiting another 5+ minutes and it was like pouring straight heavy cream over my pasta. I also got roasted mushrooms and one of the mushroom stems was longer than my fingure. It was Gross! Upon leaving the restaurant we found our waitress outside smoking a cigarette. Disappointing to say the least.

I love this gym! It's open 24/7.  It's very clean/organized, the staff is friendly, the equipment is in good condition, and there is a wide variety of machines.  There is a private exercise room with a large selection of video on demand workout classes that is fantastic.  Even the other gym patrons are pleasant and respectful.  The only downside is that they really only have one set of  each size of dumbbells and sometimes there can be a little bit of a backup.  I'd suggest getting a couple sets of the lower/standard weights to ease congestion in the free weight area.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
My sister and I had dinner here yesterday. We each ordered a two-tamale plate ($7.99), which comes with two sides. We split everything, so we each got half of four different kinds of tamales. The best one was the chile relleno tamale. The tamales were not at all spicy, but there is a salsa bar with hot, medium and mild salsas as well as jalapeño slices and pico de gallo, so you can make them as hot as you want. I especially liked the Mexican cole slaw side dish.

This is an order-at-the-counter type of place, nothing fancy and very affordable.

In comparison to all of the other amazing beer gardens in Philly, I'd say Drury falls short. It's small, in a dumpy alley (without the charm of McGillin's), and slow/unfriendly service. 

I don't mind stopping in for happy hour, given that I work nearby, but it's not somewhere I'd go out of my way to spend a night out. They have a decent beer selection and it's relatively cheap but I can't speak for the food (though, I've checked out the menu and there aren't many options). If you're in the area and looking for somewhere to have a drink outdoors, I'd recommend heading a couple blocks down to Graffitti Bar!

It was a nice clean hotel.  Great location.  It seems like the hotel ran out of money before they totally finished the concept.   They were supposed to have "naughty" and "nice" rooms but all the rooms are the same.   Cool lights in the hallway.  Wierd that they would use blacklights in the bathrooms for night lights.   Cool effect but is a black light in the bathroom really the smartest thing to do?  They haven't finished stocking the minibars, no interactive TV services and room service menu was just the scaled down restaurant menu delivered to the room.   Good work out facilities.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I used to frequent this location and always found their beverages and staff to be above average. I miss the big, comfy chairs and parking has always been a pain unless it's right at closing time. I stopped in at this Starbucks twice last week and was given terrible service on both occasions. I'm know people aren't perfect and can mess up a drink order, but I actually watched the drink being made with the wrong type of milk BOTH times, asked about it, and was lied to by two separate staff members (or "partners", if you will). Please, have some pride and dignity. Customers aren't as stupid as you may believe them to be.

I have been going to Lee Garden for years- ever since I was a kid. They are by far one of the best Chinese restaurants in the area. Their noodles (lo mein, ho fun) have just the slightest taste of garlic and are delicious. I have ventured on to some of their other dishes- my favorite probably being the Amazing Thai Chicken (a bit spicy but definitely worth trying). Their appetizers and soups are all winners- especially their hot and sour soup and cheese wontons. The restaurant is small, but not cramped, and has enough room to bring your family or a few friends. Definitely a great place to go to eat out, or to get takeout.

Reading the reviews, I came across many yelpers complaining about the layout and the size of the space. THE EMPLOYEES CAN NOT CHANGE EITHER ONE OF THESE SITUATIONS. If they could change this, I'm sure they would in a heartbeat. 

Anyway, service has always been great for me! In the morning, it could be absolutely dreadful, due to the line. However, the employees try their best to stay chipper and calm in these hectic situations. I could NEVER be that chipper in the morning, so it makes me appreciate the service even more.

The coffee place that I come to every single morning before work is now getting a 3 star review, instead of the 4 that I have previously.

I received my vanilla HOT latte today. It didn't take long to make and the line didn't take a long time this morning. However, I took a sip of my coffee as I was  leaving and it was cold. How could this possibly be!? 

Dunkin, I have dealt with the long lines, the long waits for my coffee, when there is not enough flavor or sugar in my coffee, etc. I never thought that I would have to hope that you guys manage to make my HOT latte HOT, rather than cold. 

Ugh....

OMG........classic Italian at it's best.

I must start with the awesomely, delicious drinks. I love, love, love their chocolate martini's, even at $13 a pop and don't sleep on their white russian's at $7.50 a glass or so. They're well worth it. Ohhh and the long island isn't bad either.

 A few MUST try eats: the Meatballs (don't sweat the $10 tag), the Caesar salad, the chicken spedini and ooohhhhh that tortellini!!!! Of course I'm a sucka for bread and butter and they deliver. It's  an absolute heavenly accompaniment to sop up their various rich sauces. 

I can't wait to return, looking forward to going through the menu dish by dish.

Worst customer service ever. I was moving and I needed to cancel. You have to go in person to cancel, and every time I went the owner was always "out of town" and the people working at the time didn't know how to cancel someone's membership. I went FOUR times! None of the staff were properly trained on anything. I ended up moving and having to drive an hour back when I finally got a hold of the owner. He was not even apologetic and continued to try to get me to keep paying and stay. I ended up paying for like 3 months that I didn't use. He does not know how to run a business and I do not recommend this location to anyone.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I try to stay away from reviewing chains unless there's a good reason. So for this, I have a good reason. 

I'm going to keep this short: if you pick up a sandwich and stuff starts to fall out before you take a bite, it's not a good sandwich. 

Second info: I don't care if you're a young teenager working at your first job, you give me attitude I'll give it right back. If you don't want to listen to me, I sure as heck don't have to listen to you. 

This location might be convenient but is not the best. It's not exactly the cleanest either.

Disclaimer, while I have been here a few times, I've only had two items and I've never actually been inside.  That being said, their food is delicious! Calling and ordering is easy and quick, like the average Chinese store they take about 10 minutes for pick up.  I've only ever ordered shrimp friend rice and chicken wings, so that's all I can speak to.. it's delicious.  The wings aren't as big as I would like, cause they are really really good, but I'm not gonna complaint, at least I know they aren't steroid filled.  Oh and they have homemade lemonade.. aka liquid sugar in a container, the pink and the regular.. Score!

I've gone here a number of times and have never had to wait long in the morning for my coffee... to me that's a BIG deal. :) The employees are a hit or miss...some get the cuustomer service and drinks thing right some...not so much. I get plain coffee, and so far its been just fine... i will say the outdoor seating is nice.  This one, doesn't have much for interior. We usually get our stuff to go anyways and the drive thru, though always packed, seems to work just fine. I've been to  nicer dunkin locations, so that's why I'm giving this a 3star.

I came here with a friend and was a bit surprised when I entered the bar. I had seen it several times out of the corner of my eye but had never gone inside. I was impressed by how big it was inside and how it had a nice cozy feel. Although I had imagined something along the lines of a Bud Lite and Miller Lite only bar which had led me to avoid it for years, I was impressed by their broad range of craft beers. It seems like a cool place to hang out for a drink if you're in the area. I would however keep good track of your spending, as some of their beer prices are quite high.

The greasy spoon of St. Petersburg. Extremely cheap. I came here for years and saw the same faces over and over. I especially loved coming in high school. My usual was one (very large) pancake and a side of home fries. Sometimes the pancake is too dry or too buttery. Sometimes the home fries are cooked perfectly and other times there are several burnt ones. Is the food horrible? No. Is it an awesome breakfast joint? Not so much. But it's decent and cheap, so you can't go erin is that's what you're looking for.

Quick summary based only on the sushi, soup, drinks, and salad...

Soup and salad were very good. Nothing spectacular, but still not bad. 

Sushi was good, but I felt the price point was higher than other places where I've had better sushi. 

My fiancé and I had the jasmine tea. It was literally a jasmine tea bag thrown in a pot of boiling water. If I wanted that, I wouldn't have bothered ordering it. 

Overall, decent place and I've heard the hibachi is good, but I feel there are other places to get better quality sushi at better prices in Pinellas County.

My friend and I recently came here for a late night bite after a concert when it wasnt too busy. We immediately commented on how much we liked the atmosphere and vibe. The staff were super courteous and on point to make sure we understood how to order, since it was our first time there. We ordered the chips and guacamole along with a variety of tacos. The chips and guacamole were fresh (bonus points for the warm chips), and I always love chunky guacamole. My favorite tacos were the tuna (in a lettuce wrap) and the shrimp tacos. We will definitely return again!

I can't get enough of this place. It's a foodie's dream come true when it comes to enjoying twists on classic dishes. I'm not a meat eater myself, but friends and family have told me their burgers are excellent. I've personally enjoyed their shrimp po boy on more than one occasion. I've been dying to try their fried mac n cheese, but they ran out the last time I was in. 

For dessert, you can't go wrong with anything. So far, I've had the berry cobbler and fried key lime pie which were both delightful. 

Great good, good service, and extremely reasonable prices. You can't go wrong with a night out here!

Great place for food and serious cocktails in the French Quarter. Restaurant is small, but very hip. Everything we ate was excellent. The wIne list is very good, but the real drink stars here are the delicious cocktails as it is very hard to find good cocktails in NOLA.

Only downsides were our waiter sucked (but we didn't let that dampen our spirits), and also we had to wait 15 minutes to be seated even with a reservation and some empty tables - may have been a ploy to get us to drink more (it worked).

However I'm glad to see that NOLA is finally getting a hipper dining and cocktail scene.

I love T!!! I've been seeing her for almost a year now and she's awesome. She's such a sweetheart, always super flexible, so fun to chat with, and so on!!! I'll always recommend her as well as any of the other ladies that work here. They are so much fun to be around and I always leave loving my nails.  T introduced to me the dip powder and it's awesome. It's so much quicker and looks just as good. :) the salon is so pretty as well and in the perfect spot for midtown. I really like how there in only a handful of stations, so it's not over crowded.

After careful deliberation we had booked this hotel. After a good experience at another Hilton hotel, we decided to become HHonors member to avail points on our stay. This stay was off the same standards as the one we stayed at Chicago. 

The staff were super nice. Being a Honors member, we were given cookies as a welcome snack. The cookies were good ! We would leave the room in a mess in the morning and by the time we came back, it would look like how it was the first time we came in. 

This hotel is aptly situated in a way you can get to French Quarter with ease on foot. 

Bottomline: Will stay here again and super staff !
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Basically these places are just for quick, cheap haircuts. I feel like it's always a crapshoot going to one of these chains, you either get someone OK or someone that doesn't know what they're doing...more often than not, it's the latter. 

My haircut probably lasted 4 minutes, and while she at least didn't screw anything up, it was a pretty lame attempt at a haircut. Maybe if she spent a couple more minutes on it, she wouldn't have missed the loose strands of hair or the uneven sideburns. I'm a fan of the old-school barber shop and will definitely take the time to locate one before my next haircut.

Mehhh...not horrible...but not good either.

We live near here, less than 5 blocks away.  But, we rarely go.  The food just isn't compelling enough to beckon you to come back.  I'd much rather drive the 10 minutes to go to Danny's Wok, or go to Shangri-La.  But, I didn't want to pay cash, I didn't want to spend a lot of money on dinner, and I really was too tired to go anywhere else, so Spring is where I went.

Don't get your hopes up.  They'll never be a place that lives up to your expectations.  But, if your lazy, really don't want to put out any effort...this place will give you a modicum of sustenance.

Absolute worst sushi place I have ever visited. Rudeness and the sushi was awful. I always try to give restaurants another shot, but this one is not getting any more of my time or money.  When I go to a restaurant and feel like a burden, that is not a good thing. The nigiri tuna was good, the salmon was good but the slices of lemon were way to thick and the snapper was tough and chewy. My daughter ordered a couple of rolls and they looked more like rice rolls then sushi. Not coming back. Atmosphere was uninviting.

Any car wash that cleans my car and gives me a great deal is pretty much on the top of my list. You can pay $11.99 for a great wash that is buy two get one free!  You can't beat that anywhere in town and the personnel are so friendly and greet me with a smile. I always support businesses that give me a deal and a smile.  The great thing about this car wash is that the garbage cans are right next to your car and they have hoses on both sides of the car port. My car always comes out squeaky clean with the basic car wash.  Thank you Metro for offering such great service.

My wife and I rented one of the townhouse styles apartments. The property really shows well during the tours and for the area you can't beat the amenaties: pools, play area, gym, restaurants , etc. Now to explain the three stars instead of five stars. The property isn't as well built as it appears. You notice quickly the floors aren't as well built or the fixtures are pretty cheap and washer and dryers are not the newest ,etc. The staff was friendly and personable overall, but they will give you hidden charges once you leave so beware of that. I would stay there for a temp stay not over a year if I had to choose a place in the future.

My inlaws reserved a vehicle through Advantage about 4 months ago. They confirmed the reservation a few days before their trip, then flew down here from Canada. When they got off of their plane and arrived at the car rental, they were told that Advantage had *no* cars in stock.

What sort of company accepts a reservation, and confirms it - and then does not have the car in stock? Their mess up meant my inlaws had to go to another rental place and spend an extra $500 to get a car that day.

The Advantage employees were very rude and unhelpful. We will never use this company again.

We stopped by after a soccer game to get a quick bite and first of all the place is a filthy mess. There was food all over the floor and people just walking over it including the waitresses that were bringing the food out. It was so disgusting. I asked and employee if they could please clean it up because it was grossing me out and 10 minutes later she showed up with a broom and swept the floor. As for the food, all I can say is that I have had way better. It was edible but nothing out of this world. I am sure I can make better at home but this was convenient because we were in the area. Will think twice about coming back here.

A drive thru experience that I still can't figure out.  It's a typical Starbucks, and I've placed this order 100 times and never had this happen.  I ordered venti coffee.  The person on the other side of the sqwak box asked if I wanted cream and sugar.  I said yes, 4 sugars and cream on the side.  I get to the pickup window, and they give me the coffee and the cream in a cup like always, but she tells me they already put the sugar in the coffee and asks if that's ok?  Um, no that's not ok.  I don't get how one ingredient gets put in the coffee and the other comes on the side.

Upon first impressions Piada reminded me of Chipotle. The feel of the restaurant is casual chic. You order behind a glass counter which allows for transparency in your food preparation. Everything was extremely clean and organized throughout the entire place. You have three entree choices : piada, pasta bowl, of a chopped salad. The Piada is a rolled, stone grilled wrap. You have the option to create your own or choose from their list of flavor combinations. It's an incredible value for the price and you won't be disappointed by the quality of the ingredients. I will definitely be back to try other menu items.

We were driving by after church and noticed they were open for business and brunch at that We shared the County Line salad with a delicious, juicy addition of fried chicken breast plus a side order of buckwheat waffles with cheddar cheese and bourbon maple syrup! The portions were large enough to share plus we had to sample the amazing waffle ice cream sandwich with Nutella ice cream with toasted hazelnuts and dark chocolate syrup. The decor and ambience were so cheerful and bright! The service was also spot on! My granddaughter's new favorite place for brunch!

Went here for valentines day (well actually 2/13) and I was very pleasantly surprised. Doesn't look like it is very special on outside (in strip mall off mcdill) but very authentic northern Italian cuisine! Everyone who works there speaks Italian and the food is out of this world. Strongly recommend the osso bucco with risotto. The server said they cook it for 24 hrs and it tasted like they did!! Not to mention the sauce which was very simple but perfect to compliment the rich veal. The polenta and sausage appetizer was very good too! Definitely will go back!

So, the inside of your room really isn't bad. I read a lot of reviews that had me really nervous about staying here. Once I got there, the room was clean. I brought my own blanket and pillows because of other reviewers saying how filthy the room was. I would have been okay sleeping under their sheets until I saw the prostitutes. Yes, there are prostitutes. They pretty much minded their own business but I would suggest bringing your own bedding. I'm not sure if I would stay here again. It's pretty cheap so I probably would. It's about an 10 minute drive to all the fun stuff.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I checked this place out for the first time this past weekend.  The location is easy to miss due to being tucked between some large restaurants off Mass Ave. 

The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming.  There was a live musician playing the piano.  It was definitely loud.  The drink menu is extensive.  I had an Old Fashioned.  It was good. I guess, based on reviews, that I'll be going for a mule next time!

I should have looked at reviews prior to visiting this place.  I had NO idea there were more floors!  Now I know I will be returning.

We've been strictly ordering their food as takeout for dinners and have yet to be disappointed. Wonderful sauce flavors and large serving sizes (which we feel justifies the price and leaves us with several days of left overs from a single entree per person). The Cioppino is an incredibly large serving of seafood with a lovely light but flavorful sauce. The chicken milanese is to die for -- amazing breading and texture. The staff are always pleasant and quick when we come to pick up our order. We will definitely continue to support this lovely local restaurant.

I used to stop here when I would drive in the mornings to work. Used to being the key word. One weekend I stopped both Saturday and Sunday and they were out of coffee. Any coffee. On BOTH DAYS. Another time stopping here, I got an iced coffee that the server didn't feel like securing the lid on, which promptly ended up on my lap after I got back on the road. On the way to work. 

Honestly, the city of Temple Terrace should just bulldoze this atrocity and put up something useful. Like, oh I don't know, any other place of business. Or some trees. I think that trees would be more useful here than this dump.

My mother and I have been here twice now. Our first experience was unique and believe it or not we had the same server the next time a few months later. Again we had the most mellow red head lady she is very calm and a little awkward but very helpful. We liked how dead the restaurant was and definitely don't eat here  if you're in a rush I recommend. Food is amazing. Bang bang shrimp as an appetizer or pasta is great. Also mango pecan salad is delicious. Had 2 for 1 wine as well and for 3 people and only $52 not bad for  Sunday Funday. The best place at the mall to dine.

I think the reviews are harsh.  I always judge a Mexican place by the tamales.  Tamales are an old school art.  These are on point.  Salsa is great, food is good.  I see people complain about the wait.  They *might* be making this fresh.  Fresh takes time.  We are always in such a hurry.  Put down your phone and a have a conversation with your companions. Life will wait.  Have a tamale.  

The best Mexican I ever ate was in Mexico.  This is a solid 3.  Probably the best in Hendersonville.  Wish I had pictures.  We ate it   all.

We normally love Macaroni Grill and brought some friends from out of town.  Our server Emily was sweet, helpful and attentive.  Sadly she was the best part of the meal.  The food was less than mediocre.   Gummy pizza dough, super acidic salad dressing, flat alfredo sauce.  It was such a disappointment.  The gluten free pasta was good and Emily helped me create a allergy friendly sauce which I deeply appreciated.  We live in the area and will probably not be back.  Emily, your skill exceeds the food.  Thank you for taking good care of us. 
Emily receives 5 stars... the restaurant sadly, receives 1.

The hotel was pretty nice- nothing over the top, but on the surface it "looks nice". The rooms are modern and have flat screen tv's. The only downsides: toilet did not flush, there was no hairdryer in the room, there was no "visitor's guide" and worst of all...the sheets felt like paper! Very rough and not soft at all. Bed was ok- covers were not very "fluffy". For one night, it was a nice stay and not that expensive. Breakfast was ok too--cold cereal, fruit, yogurt/granola,coffee,waffles, make your own breakfast sandwich (already cooked bacon and egg circles).
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: First time at The Big Cheezy and it definitely lives up to the hype. First, Excellent customer service, Thomas who took my order greeted me immediately when i walked in with great enthusiasm and he's extremely knowledgeable about the menu. Now about the food: i ordered the Original Pairing which is a simple grilled cheese and tomato basil soup. The soup is only okay but the sandwich is awesome! Perfect portions, neither too small nor too large. Clean restaurant, cool music and free wifi! This place is winning on all levels.

Great drive thru car wash close to my job. They provide many options at various price points which are appealing to me, you can pay with cash or card, and the free vacuum area is awesome (never broken vacuums or low suction). The wash itself is seamless and nice with pretty multicolor suds. At the free vacuum area, there's two types of vacuum handles to reach every space in your car and the mini duster gun is great for getting tight spots such as the dashboard and gear shift. Rich's Wash Dat makes washing your car less of a chore.

The food is DELICIOUS. You cannot go wrong with a Red Chili Burro. I ask for an extra tortilla because 1) the tortillas taste so goood and 2) because there's a lot of meat stuffed in those burritos! The customer service isn't the best, they are always very busy between take out orders, the people dining in (no wait service), and the multiple call in orders. My suggestion would be to keep a menu at home or in the office and always call in your order. Be prepared for a good wait if you don't, the food is really worth the wait though!

The place has a really cool vibe and was recommended to me by many of my friends. I was told to either try the grenade or the shark attack. The shark attack was definitely too sweet for me and had barely any alcohol in it. The bartender was also not excited to attack the drink for me so it did not feel as special and it felt like a basic and overpriced drink. The grenade though was awesome. I love the sweet yet salty flavor and preffered the liquid version but my boyfriend really liked the frozen version. Great place though and awesome music!

I found out they have an AMA discount so tried this place out the other week to get an oil change. It is a small location but there is ample room in case of a line-up. They have 4 bays and the day I went there were about 6 people lined up ahead of me. It didn't take too long from start to finish and the staff were very friendly and did not try to push add-ons or extras too hard. They do offer them them and also note what they have recommended to you in the invoice so you have a note in case you want to do it later (or yourself).

With Covid everyone was wearing masks and you get to stay in your car.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Way too expensive. I went here because my usual coin car wash on Calgary Trail was closed. There I can do a quick wash and wax for $4-5. At Em's you have to buy tokens which cost $3 for 3 minutes. I bought 4 hoping I would have leftovers. Nope. A quick wash and wax I would normally pay $5 for just cost me $12. 

On the plus side it is a nice new building. It also wasn't too busy when I got there. My usual place sometimes has a line-up. Em's is also a big, clean facility and warm inside in winter. 

If you want cheap and quick this isn't the place. 

Personally I need to find a cheaper back-up car wash.

Nice place. But my food was really BAD. I had a simple Teriyaki Chicken for lunch. It was two thin half chicken breasts on a piece of lettuce. It had no color -- looked like it was boiled or something. One piece was so tough that it was completely inedible. The other was just blah. So I spent $14.50 for a lunch I didn't even eat half of. I didn't send it back because I figured the "good" piece of chicken was their best and I wasn't even eating what I had of that already. The people were friendly and the service was quick, but I still have no desire to come back.

I was pretty unimpressed. After reading all of the reviews it was very disappointing. My sister and I went in for mani/pedi's. Our pedicure was ok but my problem came with my full acrylic set. These nails she put on are crazy wide. They make my actual fingernail look extremely fat. Not to mention to tried to charge me $5 extra for a clear coat of nail polish on top of my nails. Wth is that?  Since when do we charge for a clear coat on top of pink and whites?!  Needless to say nail salons are a dime a dozen and I won't be returning to this one ever again!!

It has been a LONG time since I've gone through a drive through car wash. 

This was such a good experience and so fun to take my 4 year old through. They've got the lights and the colored soap - all the fun things! She asked to go through again right when we got out.

Plenty of affordable options ranging between $10-25. 

The customer service was fantastic. Salina was extremely helpful and even went out of her way to grab a little beach ball for our little one. Truly made it an enjoyable EXPERIENCE, not just going to get the car washed.

Recommended. Their version of Chicken Kara-age is very good, it's on par with Izakaya Tomo. The Black Dragon Roll is one of the best sushi rolls I've had in a while, I think it's just as good as Japonais Bistro's TNT Roll. Service is good, very attentive. What I don't like about this restaurant is the interior and ambience. I'm not sure what this restaurant looked like before the renovation but i feel they should have considered adding windows to bring natural light inside so you don't feel like you're in a storage room when eating.

An unexpected pleasure on a rainy Monday night.  Wasn't in the mood but was convinced to go. She knows better. Was glad I did. Nice vibe in the bar. One warning. If it is cold outside the tables near the front windows are cold - ask for a booth or a table away from the windows. Food has always been good here. This time I had the special - a small filet. It was prepared just as I asked and was very tasty. My wife had one of then several fish options on the menu and she gave it the thumbs up. Prices are  not cheap but decent considering the quality of the food.  One of the better places in Brownsburg.

This place was so close to us and with awesome ice cream places far away from me, I was so excited to try it.  There have been lines at a lot of locals go here.  There are a lot of flavors of Hershey ice cream, not Hershey chocolate, but it reminds me of some places I used to go at the jersey shore.  

So I've battled the lines, got to take my order and the staff kinda messed things up.  It wasn't exactly what I wanted and kinda hard to get them to fix it.  Then they were out of small items.  I'll stick to making the far drive to places that make their own.

Granted it is only Wendy's but this one is by far the worst I've ever been to. I ordered a number one with a Coke and yes I understand this is a very complicated order but they made me sit there for five minutes because the fries work done there was absolutely nobody in the entire store and they completely forgot I was sitting there

Oh I forgot to add that this was drive-through with nobody in front of me and nobody behind me I would stay far away God only knows what they're doing or how they're making the food

I really like this place, it's probably my favorite Mexican restaurant in Philadelphia. I do wish they had a larger variety of taco types though, as I don't really like fried chicken or fried fish that much(2 out of their 3 taco types).
