categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I usually use the drive through at this location so my review can only speak to that... the items are not consistent, one day they make your order perfect the next day they tell you they ran out of ice once you get to the window to pay and after you have sat in the line up for 20 minutes, and another time you may get your drink completely wrong. Also, the staff here is not friendly or polite. So if you want to take a chance then go to this location. If you want to get a delicious drink from a friendly barista go to the many other great Starbucks  around town.

This place is an embarrassment to the McDonald's Corporation. If this location is a franchise McDonald's should take it back. Food on the chairs, look at the trash on the floor (right at the front counter) and no ice one of the machines. I am surprised that the Lower Merion health inspector hasn't shut this down. The workers are doing the best that they can with their limited education, but come on turn down the hip-hop music down to an acceptable level. Music is supposed to be BACKGROUND and not here to entertain the workers. The McDonald's in Rosemont is amazing- maybe they take a lesson from them.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Two stars for atmosphere and service.  We LOVE Italian food and this restaurant was very disappointing.  Several friends told us that the fish dishes were excellent.  We weren't in the mood for fish, but wanted Italian comfort food.  I had eggplant parm which was totally overcooked, mushy and charred.  If it wasn't for the burnt taste, it would have had no flavor at all.  The husband had spaghetti & meatballs.  He, too, thought they had no flavor and the meatballs were mushy and tasteless.  We won't be going back.

Food is above average.   It's obvious the owner has his very very young children working there.  They are too young to understand customer service and be thankful customers like myself come in and spend $30-40 a time so they can afford to buy their kids the iPods and tablets that seem to be more important then helping me pay my bill.  With the owner just standing there.   No one really cared if I was there or not.   Well this was the last visit I will make there.  I will explore other options from here on out.

I am giving this place a 3 star for now but am intrigued enough to give it a future try. It is certainly a slightly different style of food from most Mexican restaurants. I had the enchiladas which were good but could have done with just a tad more heat for my taste. My wife had a dish that seemed to have chewy soggy tortilla strips in a green sauce that was not nice at all. Sadly our server was on her first day and spoke very little English and did mess up our orders a little. Other people in the restaurant were very enthusiastic in their praise if the food so hopefully on my next visit I can give them a higher star rating.

The food was plentiful and tasty. My carne asada was overcooked and had no seasoning but everything else on the plate, beans, rice was delicious. The chips and salsa were excellent with homemade pico. The guacamole was spectacular. I took a drink of my fountain Sprite to wash down a bite and tasted mold. I looked at my tortillas. Nope. Took another sip of Sprite and realized it was the drink. I let them know. They gave me my choice of a drink in the cooler. I chose Mineragua. I hope they fix that. Was very unsettling and unmistakable. My husband also Loved the chips and pico.

Overall a decent hotel. Typical Hampton Inn. The breakfast here was lacking from the normal places. The staff was good. The room had a few issues from wear. The beds and room were clean and comfortable. The a/c was a pain because they must have a sensor for when people are in there and moving. My room got warm at night. The internet was slower and unsecured.  The first nights we stayed there the front desk clerk was very helpful. The second time we came back there was a different girl that acted like we were a problem until the first lady recognized us and help out. I would stay again though.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Wow, I can't believe there are no 5 star lucky's reviews...so here goes. Lucky's General Tso's tofu is delicious, and currently $3.65 for a portion that feeds 2 people. You just can't beat that. You can find enough spare change in your house to get a meal there, and they're open till 2am on weeknights, 3am on Fri and Sat. Seriously. If you want gourmet food, go to Whole Foods in South Philly and you'll quit whining and get the same amount of their take-away for $25. What Lucky's lacks in ambiance it makes up in special sauce.

Wasn't impressed. We ordered steak and something and my husbands steak had about 2 oz of fat. My steak had a lot of fat also. Inside is beautiful.they just need to work on the food. Kids complained the portions were small.we have ordered steak and something ect. Before at other Mexican restaurants and never got fat. But here both of our steaks had a lot of fat. Don't waste money on steak meals has a lot of fat can tell it's cheap cuts and really thin...won't eat here never again. I have one child who loves any Mexican food but refuses to eat here again..

We came here twice, both times their sushi was terrible and overpriced. One roll in particular was made of "tuna, salmon, and [another fish i can't remember]" and it literally looked/ smelled liked canned tuna wrapped up (not the good quality tuna either...). Once I got a "chicken and broccoli" dish and it was comparable to a take-out Chinese place (which i thought was good but not worth their price). Maybe we just kept picking the wrong things on the menu because the table next to us had sushi that looked really good. I don't think we'll be back though.

Dive looking, but good food and a clean kitchen. They have the best chicken tacos made with 2 homemade corn tortillas, onion  and cilantro, you add the salsa from the fresh salsa bar (really good). The chicken burritos and chicken nachos are also very good. The best chicken enchildas verde (4) made with homemade  corn tortillas and served with rice and beans. They also serve burgers and fries. The people are friendly (bring Lucy back, please). It's out of the way, but worth it, and the owner appreciates your business.

Went there the other night. Food was good (not the best sushi I've had but a good selection and some rolls I've never seen) but waited an hour from sitting down until rolls were brought. They did have an almost-full dining room and some folks waiting for take out, but there was really no acknowledgement about it, when we had two antsy and hungry kids with us. I guess if there was some acknowledgement and/or apology I would've felt better about it. It was just super slow service from the moment we sat down until getting our check.

I love the atmosphere, service,oysters, and drinks here. I want to love the food- I've tried twice. It's just too much for me.. too many weird flavors put together on some dishes... some things were plated weird (burrata (which is not good), tartare..) I like they experiment with different flavors but I really don't like any of it- the oyster mushrooms on the fall menu taste like a fall candle. You will see a common theme on these yelp reviews- they always seem to be out of something- that happened both times I visited. I wish they would tone it down and work on their menu.

Ordered 2 pizzas. One was fine. The one with pepperoni was rancid. Smelled and tasted awful. Called to let the store know and the girl who answered: (1) didn't apologize; (2) said could give us a credit for later use; (3) would charge us another $2.73 to re-deliver another pizza; and (4) that re-delivery would be there in about one hour to one hour and ten minutes. Terrible customer service. Worst part is, I don't feel confident that they were going to check that the pepperoni in their store was rancid! Never ordering from here again.

Great All-You-Can-Eat sushi! 

Fresh and Yummy Fish, Fantastic Variety (see below), Super Friendly Staff, Very Accommodating Chef, and Great Price! 

AYCE Included 1) UNLIMITED appetizers: (edamame, seaweed salad, baked mussels, and more), 2) UNLIMITED NIGIRY and SUSHI Rolls (Made to order, modified upon request), 3) UNLIMITED Dessert (ice cream, fried ice cream, mochi ice cream, banana fried ice cream); 4) Sake (this month's special)!!!

Much better than the Peppermill's OCEANO AYCE; Circus Circus's Kokopelli's AYCE and Atlantis' SKY BAR AYCE sushi.

We Loved it!

What ever happened to my favorite Burger King at Veterans and Transcontinental?  It dirty as heck - floors, condiment station, tables, parking lot and even the trash cans.  I actually glad they made my order to go because I doubt  those are clean when all else is not.  There not even music in dining area.  Thats not lazy, thats no clue..  They used to have an American flag out front but its just an empty pole now.  They place could care less, ss long as they get paid.  And a small dized Whopper Combo is $7.50?

Such. Good. Ice cream. I'd definitely recommend the mini trio - three "half" scoops of ice cream, but it was definitely enough to split between two people and you get to try more flavors! The best of all was the lavender ice cream, unlike any other lavender ice cream I've ever had! we also got the intellgenstia coffee ice cream and the buttermilk peach and both were fantastic! Have as many samples as you want, because some of them I definitely didn't like, but that's the beauty of samples! Wish there were more of these around the country.

I love dunkin coffee, especially the new cold brew, but their reward system is atrocious. Went to redeem my free drink reward and they said I had to print it, they couldn't scan it off my phone like any other business. They print it out on the receipt that you're expected to keep track of or email it to you but then say to print it off. 

No longer will I go out of my way to get to dunkin (I'm from Chicago where there's one on every corner) I'll just go to the Starbucks down the street where I can do everything off my phone.

I implore everyone to try Mae's Chinese across the street on Harrison behind the Circle K. Mae's environment is much more welcoming, cleaner, not musty, and more light. Their food taste so much fresher and not greasy or oily. Plus Mae's prices are much more reasonable. The owners at Wei's are so rude when something goes wrong. Everyone else's fault but theirs. We tried Mae's, my family and I love it! Been going there for months now and have yet to be disappointed. if you make the change to Mae's,  you will not be sorry.

What a disappointment.  We had a 6pm reservation for party of 5.  By 6:18 we had been served our entire meal. Sushi appetizer was served with soup and salad. As the waitress was leaving, the Hibachi cook immediately came in and started cooking. He Put chicken on the same time as steak...that meant chicken finished well after steak was served. There were only 2 other guests, so not like the place was overly crowded.  After scrolling through other honest reviews... rushing customers out the door seems to be the norm.

I absolutely loved my first experience at Kink Salon. I went in to see April for a full balayage, cut, and style, and am very happy with the outcome! Aside from the great service, I had a wonderful time chatting with April. My hair takes a long time to work with and I've noticed in the past that most stylists rush through it. Not April! She stayed an hour and a half late just to be sure my hair was absolutely perfect. By the end, I was expecting to pay close to a million dollars considering all of the time and services that went into it, but I was pleasantly surprised that the price was completely reasonable. I will most definitely be back!

Maria Pappone's Grilled Aged Provolone Cheese Sandwich:
(Thick cut aged provolone dipped in egg batter and grilled. Served in an long roll. Add sweet or hot roasted no charge.) This was delicious.. a little too heavy for one person.. if you have a fellow sharp prov. lover in your life, share it. I got both sweet and hot on the side. They gave good portions of both. Mac and cheese bites were delicious, and the french fires are mcdonalds shape, and yummy. (but you need to add salt) Fast delivery, friendly polite driver.

This place has always had poor service but had still managed to be my favorite place in Brownsburg to eat, until the last couple of months that is.  Poor service can be tolerated with great food but sadly the food has turned into inedible, grease covered, zero flavored having slop. I have no idea what happened to this place but stay very clear unless you love utter frustrating for slop. You will easily wait 20 minutes to get you bill when you're done eating. I'd say my family and I averaged 1-2 times a week here for a long time. My last 2 times I didn't leave a tip and I always leave a tip.

This is a relatively older property that has been really elegantly restored. Nice beds, floor,  bathroom, linen, etc. They provide goat milk soap that's my favorite. I ended up staying in two different rooms because the neighbors in one room were making noises late at night and I complained. The moved me to an even nicer room looking over Tampa Bay. The rooms have the biggest, cool-looking table lamps I have ever seen.

It has a pool and a mini pier to enjoy. Staff is friendly and accommodating.

I would definitely stay there again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I took my car in today for an oil change and state inspection. Online appointments and weekend services makes this place a plus but the customer service my husband received when dropping off and picking up was outstanding. 
They recommend a few things to make my car run better but didn't act like it was "absolutely necessary or I'll break down" crap that other service centers have done to me in the past. 
We have our "go to" car guy that we've relied upon for years and will continue to do so but for oil changes and inspections (that's closer to our new home) I now have another place I can go to that I trust. Great job guys!
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: So, I'm amazed that these people are in the service industry. The treat people like crap. We ordered crispy tacos for a family of five 3 weeks ago. Tonight we called and they put me on hold for a LONG time. They finally pick up the line to tell me they don't "do" crispy tacos. I said we just ordered them 3 weeks ago. The woman says they may start doing them and did I want to speak to the owner. I said yes. On hold for even longer. Then they hang up on me. Then they don't pick up my call- as I thought *maybe* the slow woman disconnected us accidentally. Good riddance Tres Jalapeños. Adios.

Perfect neighborhood eatery.  Fresh spinach salad with a blueberry dressing...looks weird, tastes great.  Service was a little unorganized but so friendly that we didn't care.  Portions not huge but everything is tasty.  They were shucking oysters and we couldn't help but wonder if those were some of the last ones we'd see for a while.

Take the ferry over from Canal St. and it's a 3 or 4 block walk.  Kids will love the ferry trip and Aunt Leni's kids menu and desserts.  There's a playground for little ones next to Aunt Leni's.  Beer and wine for the grownups.

Closed Monday & Tuesday.  Sunday brunch has eggs benedict.

Very mediocre food quality and taste. Not too bad, but not great either. Quick service. I was a little concerned with hygiene, but did not get sick from eating take-out from this restaurant.
The food tasted like there was something missing, but couldn't quite point out what. Just a little less flavor than other Chinese restaurants. 
The location is somewhat hidden from view on Church Road.
I'm not sure I would order take-out again from here, unless I'm starving and every other restaurant in the area is closed.

This Giant in Broomall is the best Giant. Their bakery is better than even standalone  bakeries. A wide selection of everything from fresh danish pastries, croissants, bagels, cookies, cakes and breads. I also like their meats/butcher section, deli and produce. This store also has an organic section where I find some of things I need, when I don't have the time to stop at Whole Foods. The store is always clean and the staff is helpful. Way better than other Giants in the area, as well as better than any Acme or Shoprite. I also like that this Giant is open from 6am to 11pm, so you can go at odd hours and avoid crowds.

Outstanding. Interior is dated but well maintained and very clean. Nicely decorated. Service was friendly, helpful, and attentive without being intrusive. Food was remarkably good. The churasco steak was as good as any that I have had at a high end steak house. The steak fajitas were also outstanding. It's the first time that I've had tender steak in fajitas at a Mexican restaurant. Also, the guacamole maya was delicious. A meal in itself. The only negative is the very limited parking - both in front and behind the restaurant. Will be back again, and again.

I live near by and was craving sushi so I thought I would give it a try. Boy did I pick the wrong night They had one waitress working and she was way overwhelmed for the 6+ tables that were seated, she forgot half of my order so I was sitting there for quite some time. When my crawfish roll came out the crawfish was bad. I mean like sitting in the freezer for  a looooooong time. The owner/mgr not sure which, was very nice and removed it from the bill with no problem. I also feel like they need some massive updating. It feels very dirty in there and dark. Just wasn't a good experience The two stars was for the Miso Soup and the Sweet Owner/mgr

convenient location, cramped and dangerous parking lot. comprehensive selection-with no prices listed- arranged haphazardly in cramped aisles with no one in sight to help you find anything. drove over an hour on the basis of their websites assertion of 'in stock' on a highly rated seasonal (once  a year) beer...upon arrival was informed 'it'll be in next week' and 'we only get four cases anyway so we sell it by a lottery'..'but the website said'...'i just work here, i'm  not the owner'....and i just shop here and will never be back....

My boyfriend and I stayed in a studio room with our two small dogs. The hotel is very pet friendly and will often give the dogs treats when going in and out of the hotel. The kitchenette came with all of the necessities (pots, pans, silverware, plate, bowls, toaster, and much more). The living space was big enough for the two of us and the dogs. Nice size closet and very spacious shower. Everything was clean and well kept. Housekeeping comes by everyday and will do any servicing needed in the room. If you need anything after they are gone the receptionist at the front desk is always friendly and willing to get anything else for you.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I've been here twice, and that will probably be it for me. The donuts are okay but nothing special and the price is very reasonable, but the service - blah. Both times I walked in I was treated like I was bothering them! I didn't think anything of it since I stopped the first week they opened and figured they were exhausted, but there was no reason for it this second (and last) time. They were not overtly rude but didn't greet me, just sighed, asked what I wanted, boxed them up and as she turned said a blunted "have a nice day." Looks like my new go-to place will be District Donuts - pricier but they are ridiculously nice and helpful there.

Perfectly serviceable manicure.  No bells and whistles (hot towels, nice smelling lotions), but they did a nice, quick job for $10.  My nails and cuticles are neat and the polish was applied meticulously.  Great for a quick manicure on a work night.

I'll probably go again when efficiency is the name of the game as I'm in the neighborhood.  When I have more time, though, I'll seek out a place with a few more amenities and spend a few more bucks. 

I didn't get a pedicure, but the pedicure chairs looked older and a little sad.  Not sure I'd risk it.

What a disappointment!  For so long I have waited to try this adorable, charming place.  It came with such high recommendations.  Unfortunately the first bad sign was the LOUD music!!!  I could not hear my dining companion. I could not hear the waitperson's dialogue.  I am a  professional musician with very GOOD ears....and this was HORRIBLE.  I would have left immediately, but my companion was so looking forward to this place.  The food - overly salty. Nothing special. This place is another example of Emperor's new clothes.

All the women that are cashiers are always in a bad mood and not friendly. It's like they are mad they have to check people out. Never a hi how are you. Poor customer service. I got pizza from the deli and stood there while two employees just stood there and didn't even come to ask what I'd like. I ordered two slices of pizza that were very small and greasy for $5! Plus the guy used his hands to get the pizza off the tray. Not sanitary at all! I keep going here cause I live close but I think that will be the last time.

OMG-We ate dinner at MidAtlantic last night and had the best meal.  We hadn't eaten there in a while because we usually aren't in that part of the city but now I would make a special trip to go there.  We ate outside which was lovely on the first cool evening of the summer!  Our service with spectacular...as good as any 5 star restaurant and all of our meals (there were three of us) were outstanding.  We had the chicken which was juicy and served with wonderfully prepared veggies and hamburgers were perfectly prepared (medium rare) on homemade rolls.  The bread basket was filled with more delicious homemade bread and biscuits.

This location is terrible and it's been that way for a while. I'm always rushed going through the drive through. And I always have to check my bag because this location always forgets something I ordered every time I go there. Seriously like every time. I've also had times where my soda had no syrup in it because they forgot to change it. And they didn't change the syrup so I could get another one. I've also had instances where I've seen cockroaches on the floor inside. Overall one of the worst bk's ive ever been to. I only go because of the convenience.

I've been here about 4-5 times. I really liked my first haircut here so I decided to return, but the later visits have not been as impressive as the first one.  I don't speak Chinese so I just showed him a few pictures of how I wanted my hair to be cut, and he always assured me saying "no problem, it will look good on you," but my hair rarely looked like the pictures. He pays attention and takes his time to cut and style, but I was not fully satisfied. I can't really complain for a $18 haircut, but I'm not sure if I would go back.

This was our second attempt to like this restaurant but alas it was not in the cards.  We came here several months ago and were scared off because the food was soooo salty.  Well tonight the food was much better but the service was not.  Our server was indifferent at best and even surly.  He was clearly overwhelmed as they were very busy.  That does not excuse them for ignoring us or having such an indifferent persona when they remembered we were here, even though we were only a party of two.  We watched several parties show up, wait patiently, get ignored, then leave.  We will not put this on our
 favorite restaurant list.

Where is it considered normal to have your genitals visible while waiting on customers? Well,the answer is here. Now don't get excited. This is not something anyone would want to see. A black female with her zipper down . You could really see a lot. Smh. Discusting.  Seems like the lady Indian manager was afraid to say anything    She needs to go .Pronto. The manager may want to call the police before firing her. Sickening animals. NEVER AGAIN. LOST MY APPETITE I WAS ABSOLUTELY STUNNED. NEVER SAW ANYTHING LIKE THAT

Loving this Safeway more and more! I never used to shop at Safeway as I preferred a competitor. My husband converted me. They honestly have the best bakery. Never disappoints. Produce is very fresh good and good quality products offered. They do have some harder to find items but not all. I wish their deli was a little more thorough with cheese selection and variety. 

I would have given them 5 out of 5 however when you hit the deli for a signature cafe sandwich it is such a HUGE inconvenience for the staff and they let you know it with attitude.

Maybe it was just a bad day, but our recent experience and first time at the 29th street location was a disappointment.  Previous visits to the 22nd street location were always positive.  The waitress was pleasant.  The food, however, was not.  We were not offered the standard peppers and onions; the chips were stale and mostly small, small chips; my whole talapia was burned to a crisp; and the other meals were just passible and cold.  There were no other patrons in the restaurant.  Overall the quality did not match the prices.  "All good things must come to an end."

Decent, but not great, food. It's good enough to get us to stop in for lunch a few times a year. They do have one stand-out item, their table salsa. It's not a fresh salsa at all. It's strip sauce! If you grew up in a SoCal beach town in the 60's-70's, you'll recognize it immediately as that same wonderful concoction found in a squeeze bottle on the counter of every strip shack on the beach.  SoCal kids love strip sauce!  If you want a more traditional table salsa, ask for some pico de gallo and mix the two together.

Way understaffed. Only one customer service representative in the downtown main branch. I had to wait one full hour to correct a mistake they made last week. Although the representative was capable she was swamped. People called and after putting them on hold had to ask to call them back. When I left there were three people waiting and a fourth had walked out and gave up. Not everything can be done on the web and if there is a mistake in person is sometimes the only way. All financial institutions are after fee income, but this one forgot about service.

Nice pool.  No hot tub.  Don't get a room on the second floor.  The exterior corridors make noise every time someone walks by.  Two face towels had stains that didn't come out in the wash.  The rooms have a shower, toliet, sink and closet all behind one sliding partition - a real negative if you're rooming with someone and they are in the bathroom so you can't get in to the closet or the sink.  The retrofit of the shower into a former bathtub wasn't done very well - the shower pan bounced up and down a bit.  Friendly service, easy parking.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Well Alrighty then. Flew out of Philly this past Sunday. So my husband and I shared the "Cheesesteak " so where do I begin? Cheesesteak was awful! Like the worst that I have ever had in my whole life and I'm born and raised in Philly. Imagine chewy meat that you have to break with your teeth and fingers each bite on a cold roll with cheese wiz slapped on the roll..... I really felt bad for the travelers who get this as their only cheesesteak experience.  On the upside service was great. I saw the wait staff walk the floor frequently to take orders and find seats for passengers. They get a A plus. Food gets a F.

I just finished my excellent 2 for $20 dinner at Ninja. You pick an app, 2 entrees and miso soup or salad. Thanks to  Yelp, I also got a free spring roll. Edamame is the other free choice, but we picked it as our appetizer. Its a great deal for a nice dinner. Service was  polite and attentive.  I give it 4 because the edamame was overly salted,  the salad is the still wet iceberg lettuce with too much dressing. Its a nice ambience, the statement stairway chandelier needs to be dusted. I will go again for my reasonable neighborhood byo. Its not the best Japanese, but thats not what to expect in NE Philly.

I'm so disgusted and feel incredibly sick right now. I ordered three rolls to go and sadly all of them were terrible. The fish isn't fresh and the cooked rolls literally taste like someone deep fried it in old oil and let it sit out for hours. Not fresh at all. I'm usually not one to complain but this experience was terrible and a waste of my money and excitement. I was really craving sushi but I will not be back to this place. It's my second time eating here. The first time was okay but very slow service and this is my first time getting take out. Just never again. I would've ate fast food before I go back here.

This was our first time at Amani's and it was delicious. Our group of 4 split calamari and it was cooked beautifully, very tasty with the edamame. Some got salads, one got the crab and corn chowder and one got the pork belly, all were great. For entrees, we had the salmon, lobster ravioli, Long Island Duck Breast and the Braised Short Rib Bolognese. All entrees were wonderful. For dessert we had the blueberry pudding cake and Pear Ginger Crème Brûlée, again, everything was perfect. The staff was very attentive and our food was cooked exactly as requested. Would highly recommend and can't wait to go back.

Great Steaks! Both the Bison and Beef were excellent. Very cool atmosphere and a very friendly staff that seemed to go out of the way. There was a bit of a snafu with my order though; I got the wrong steak at first, but a new one was quickly brought to the table-- which was WAY under cooked. The manager got involved and personally made my steak the correct way and without hesitation, compted the entire meal. It was good to see a restaurant admit to and correct a mistake, that is why I will be back to Ted's on a regular basis. The apple dessert was excellent also.

Let me start off by saying this place is a good value for a hibachi buffet. Having said that, I will not voluntarily come back here. The food is mediocre, and the service was slow. The sushi was loaded with rice and limited on the fish/filling. The hibachi was just so-so. I asked for my steak to be rare, and got steak that was well done and it was very chewy. Granted they were busy the night I went, but having to wait so long to get served each coarse and even longer to get the bill was enough to make me never want to endure the experience again.

This Asian market serves those of us who cook Asian very well.  It is stocked with items you would find hard to get in traditional Chinese grocers even in large cities.  For example it has blachan (Malaysian shrimp block) and the Malaysian shrimp paste or ha ko.  It also has very traditional Chinese sauces that sometimes are omitted in the Asian/Vietnamese grocers such as thick dark soy sauce.  Ellen Woo is very accommodating in stocking items if you let her know what they are.  I find this store very adequate.

I've been a member since 1997 but I might change credit unions.  I don't like the new drive-thru service.  I needed a thousand dollars to give someone, I asked for hundreds but the biggest bill you can get from that machine with a live person screen (if I wanted to talk to someone's face, I'd go in) is a 50.  And you can't get an envelope to put money into.  So, without parking, turning off the car, getting out and going in, waiting in line, getting what I WANT from my financial institution, getting back in and starting the car again to leave, I left stuffing a wad of bills into my purse.  Not cool.

I don't like giving bad reviews but my wife and I were recommended to try this place for good fresh Chinese food.  We went for lunch and I was a bit wary that the lunch was priced quite cheaply (I don't recall exactly how much but around $5).  My food was, quite frankly, horrible.  It resembled fried batter (I'm not even sure if there was any meat in it) covered with goopy sweet sauce and was absolutely horrible.  My wife's ordered green chicken curry and it was slightly better but not much.

Maybe it's better for dinner but lunch was one of the worst restaurant experiences I've had in Tucson.

Great happy hour! Beer is cold and they have a great selection! Burgers are great. 
They need to work on the appetizers. Nobody likes burnt bacon on the poppers.  The bacon should be nicely browned and crisp. The new happy hour menu is kind of a rip. The potato skins are $4.00 and literally you get two skins cut up into several pieces. I can go to a half dozen places in town and get a full order for 6 dollars or even less during happy hour. The wings need to be fried longer so the skin is crispy not soft.  I have to agree with some of the other reviews on food taking way to long. It's hit or miss sometimes.

The first thing you see when you walk in are 1980s-esque security cameras. The "security" asks you not to bring any bags in and you have to leave them at the front. 

The produce is OK. Sometimes good, sometimes bad. Most of the items are general junk food. The thing this place does right is some foreign items but there are better places.

Overall, the supermarket is pretty depressing. Empty shelves, incorrect prices, slow service, rude security and owners. It smells like a dirty, burnt hotel room.

If only Trader Joe's replaced it...

This is the second time we had an order that was screwed up. The first time or several months ago when we ordered a calzone and they left out half the ingredients we requested. This time, I got the veggie flatbread which was essentially pizza without the sauce, the crust was so thick, not the way a flatbread should be. My daughter got the chicken chipotle panini and they forgot not only the coleslaw and pickle but also the Chipotle sauce! Our meals tasted good enough but they were not as expected or as listed on the menu.

Needless to say, we are not going back. This place used to be good but it's completely unreliable now.

Three of us walked into the St. James and the greeting was  friendly. Seated at a very comfortable booth then greeted again and served a yummy roll. To be quite frank and to the point....Server very attentive. Appetizers chosen, which included, the frank in the blanket,  generously presented and  tasted quite good. Caesar Salad with Shrimp, Chopped Salad with Chicken,Crabcake Sandwich and a side of the Brussels Sprouts..Fantastic..  Desserts, Pecan Pie and the Bread Pudding. Fantastic. Try it yourself, we will again and probably for Dinner.

Consistently get the wrong order in drive-thru.  Need to repeat order at the order station because servers are having three other conversations with other people so thecan't hear accurately.  Please please listen to the customer in the drive thru instead of talking to other employees at the same time.  Ordered a bagel with cream cheese today, got to my desk to eat it and no cream cheese.  Coffee is way over sweetened when i ordered the complete opposite.  Like wtf it's not that hard.  You just lost my daily order.

Food was great and so was the bartender and staff.  I ordered their amazing Chicken Parm and cooked thin and crispy like they do.  However, no pasta came with it.  Asked for a side of pasta and it was a $12 up charge...for a side of angel hair pasta?  Since when did Chicken Parm not come with pasta and since when did a side order of angel hair cost $12??  I understand making a dollar, but for what it literally costs in time to prepare and for the pasta itself, how can you possibly charge people that kind of money?  It is like ordering fajitas and being charged for sour cream, cheese, guac, etc.  Too many other places to go here in Philly.

I won't go back a third time. I've had two bad experiences at WTCW. First, the automated car wash bay took my money but then didn't work. There's no workers onsite and the phone number on the door goes to a fax machine!?! Went back another time and used one of the self-wash bays; this time no soap!!! (of course, after I had already paid I found that out.) So my car got a rinse off, not a wash. Also, the water pressure was inconsistent to where it really didn't do a very effective job at even rinsing off my car. Better options just to the North and South of this place so I won't bother with this place again.

Not like Chicago pizza at all. Sauce not spicy.More like sugary sauce from a jar. No pieces of tomato. Peperoni had to be searched for. We love going to Pizzeria Uno (Due) or Ginos East when in Chicago and read the reviews for this place and went in with great expectations. So disappointed. Gave it a star for prompt friendly service. But it was Sunday and almost empty. Pizza crust like bread and doughy. Not crunchy and golden like real Chicago pizza.We were informed that cheese was not put right on the crust before we ordered.  That's why in Chicago, your cheese never slides off your pizza.

I had high hopes of this place but it failed. If you make an appointment in advance be prepared for constant reminders to be on time. Emails, texts, and a call! Only to get there early, wait, wait some more and the hair stylist isn't on time. 
Also, there's not a place for parents to sit while your kid is getting services. Which was a minor annoyance. 
The hairdresser was nice, not overly engaged. She seemed like she wanted to get the encounter over ASAP. Everything felt rushed. 
For the price your child could go to a nice salon and get treated a little better AND be on time.

If I could give this place less than a star, I would. The crowd was enormous and there was only one cook and one lady on the register.  When they finally called our order it wasn't even actually ours.  Another 20 minutes and we got our food, which was completely  terrible. The burrito was oversaturated with salty grease,  the taquitos (or beef and cheese tacos as they called them) were hard/ had an odd favor, and the tamales were dried out on the inside but covered with too much sauce on the outside. I will never,  ever,  ever go back.  I rarely leave bad reviews but this one is well deserved and then some.

This is what a grocery store looks like before it dies.  The entire stores just feels dark and somewhat dirty.  The prices are incredibly high - sometimes as much as 2-3 dollars higher than the Giant in Flourtown.  Over the past couple of years, the produce selection has been getting smaller and smaller, and just yesterday, many items appeared to not be in stock.  I've never seen more than 1-2 checkout lanes open, and recently, even some of the self checkout lanes have been closed.


Unless you just need the convenience of going to this Pathmark, stay away and opt for a much more pleasant shopping experience elsewhere.

Worst food ever went there Saturday evening,the chips were ice cold ordered the caso cold as well,advised our server he said ok and walked away,asked the server the name of a drink he had to go and ask someone then when we asked him what was in it he said how would I know.No comparison to Casa Garcia the parking lot is always,  busyhow I can,t imagine.I actually think Taco Bell  would have been better,advised the staff of our experience they just shrugged their shoulders and said ok!I give them two months at best save your money restaurant not clean at all!

Very impressed with the level of service and willingness to help here. I have a kegorator with a smaller CO2 tank than normal which makes it difficult to fill. My go to distributor can't accommodate this. Javie's was more than willing to get it filled for me and call me when it was complete. ETA was originally 2 weeks, but I got a call in 4 days saying it was done. They also ordered me a keg and got it delivered ASAP.

Great selection, very friendly staff (Hannah), and customer focused. I will be back often!

Going downhill fast...seems like there is a new manager every other month...when I moved here last year, the staff was more engaging and friendly. Now, you can barely get a hello, phones are never answered and maintenance is now subpar. Regretfully, I opted to sign a lease for another year and have had to go to the office twice to sign, only to be told the first time, that another agent had my lease and would be placed on my door. Today, that agent had no idea I wanted to sign. Save yourself the hassle and go elsewhere.

We move to Palm Harbor a few months ago, we used to frequent Sushi Alive, yummy. . Well I read some really exceptional reviews for this place so we had to finally try it.. we order about 6 rolls from the menue, and I noticed a few of the sushi from the reviews were not available. . But I was less than impressed, I thought the presentation was lacking in creativity and most were quite bland for my taste. We spent over 100$ and ended up giving 1/2 of it to the Cat. Can't say we will frequent this place. But the waitress or owner, if that is who she is, seemed nice.

I only get the Nino's Supreme and I like it very much.

I've tried their other pizzas, wings, pasta, etc from Ninos and they are not good AT ALL.
The ingredients on the Supreme seem pretty to be of good quality to me but all of their other dishes taste really bland to me.

They just renovated this location and they seem to go through staff pretty frequently.... So it looks like they are trying to improve the brand but they still have a long way to go.

In the meantime I will continue ordering my Nino's Supremes

I have only used their tailoring services. They take all their alterations to their plant to be done by a seamstress. Although the price is pretty cheap the quality is not good. I had a sleeve shortening job done for a shirt and when I closely inspected the sewing work I noticed several places where the string was coming out.

The people I spoke with on the phone were average in service but the actual seamstress was very kind and easy to work with. I may try them again but right now I prefer paying a bit more for quality.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Sadly, very disappointed... I was here last summer and had a great time...decided to take the family (4 adults) two weeks ago and it was like night and day...bad. They don't take reservations...ok no problem so we waited. We were told 30 mins...we were seated an hour and and 30 mins later. Ordered drinks, an app, and food immediately...my drink was wrong, and the app was never entered...the service was poor at best. Food was average. I'm hoping that it was just the beginning of the season....don't know if I'll be back.

Just trying to make an appointment was a painful process during which my appointment was deleted.  I double checked to make sure my appointment was booked on the correct day and time, because my initial phone call did not leave me with confidence.  I was told my appointment was accidentally deleted.  I found it difficult to communicate with the person taking appointments and the unprofessional attitude carried throughout the appointment. 
Without going into details, I'll simply say I will not be returning and would suggest others beware.

So first, what I liked: there is more seating, and seating that is more comfortable. Some of the lunch items have transferred from Vicia and are good, but I do think the price point for the amount of food you get for some items is an issue.

My main issue is sadness over what was lost with the old version of the restaurant. I miss the quiches, the kinds of scones they had, the varied food items you could get to go. . .  They were a go-to for me for affordable brunch catering, and this is just to let people know that all that is gone. It's fine. But I think we lost something substantive with the new ownership.

This is my favorite Sushi spot in the area, outside of Morimoto's in Philly.  Order the Kani salad and thank me later (it's not on the menu. spicy crab salad. I add octopus to mine, because it works, but it doesnt need it). Their sushi is very fresh, the sea urchin is awesome and their yellowtail is spot on. The rolls are very delicious as well. You really can't go wrong with any of the Sushi. Their Hibachi is very good too. All around a great spot, but it's small, so get a reservation and/or get their early. Parking is an adventure as well. Also plan to spend $$$ if you're hungry!

Returned to Vivace's 5/24 and were again disappointed. The kitchen has lost its mojo and has become all too inconsistent. The veal piccata was fine but the Branzino were flavorless. The sausage and pasta was also bland. The risotto side dish was watery 
and undercooked. Ever since they moved and expanded the food quality has slipped and slipped badly. I am distraught as Vivace's use to thrill their patrons  with exceptional fare. No longer. Two things have not changed , the absolutely superb service and their great deserts.

This Mcdonald's does not withhold to Mcdonald's standards.  Do yourself a favor and drive on by.  It will be a waste of time to stop anyway, because they irregularly on a regular basis only take Cash.  They say its because they are resetting their system, but its at a different time all the time.  Very inconvenient.  If it was that it would be daily and at the same time daily. That's not the only problem, the sodas taste like they have cross contaminated the lines.  Diet coke taste like bubble gum, fruitopia Taste like  sparkling fruit juice.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Bring the family or friends with you! These are big portions, good tasting, perfect heat/spice level for me.  We had the Mexico City Quesadilla and Pangea 'chos (everything)...these two fed three out of four of us. And we ordered a kid's quesadilla with chicken-also good for kid portion. Indior seating accomodated plenty. (Ask for help on the soda varieties-they have different names for what we are used to). Tip! Order extra sourcream.  We paid for more twice!  Highly recommend. Only thing that would make it better is outdoor seating-it was beautiful today.

I think Budget and Avis deliberately harassing customers to upgrade to bigger car and charging twice as much. So be careful not to be convinced by their sweet talk and stick to your original reservation. Double check your paperwork before leave their lot. They tried to push me to upgrade to bigger car when I refused they tried to give a mid size car as same prize of original reservation, which was a full size car. I was exhausted after 7 hours flight along with my family. But I acted calmly and were able to outrun their scams. Hope this message will help you . Thanks.

We stayed here because we got it on Hotwire for $80 for one night. For the amount I paid, I'd give it 4 stars. However, if I had to pay the full $160, I wouldn't be impressed. Bed was uncomfortable, pillows were terrible. The hotel looks nice but it seems like they spent more effort on making the hotel rooms look cool, modern, and hip than actually making it a quality hotel. Location was great. Parking was an additional $50, after tax, which is ludicrous. I even asked for a discount because we were there literally 13 hours, and they weren't able to provide a discount.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Quite possibly the perfect business model to fail if it wasn't for a sequestered clientel?  We visit New Orleans often, and it is an activity of ours to bet on how many beers or ingredients they are out of.  Bartenders rude and swearing. It's almost comical, we sit and listen to patrons asking for draft beers and mixed drinks and getting responses "can't do that".  They said "No mules", to at least 5 people as we sat for about 30 mins today.  2 out of 4 taps not working. What an absolute waste of opportunity.

Pros - delicious food, friendly staff, cool ambience

Cons - the place is tiny and therefore it feels very crowded, and the music was quite loud you have to almost shout to hear your friends talking

We ordered 6 out of the 7 Smalls and they were all very delicately seasoned. My favorite was the foie gras. We also ordered the charcuterie and cheese tasting platter. They were quite cheap with the slices of bread, we kept asking for more. 

Overall a very pleasant dining experience. Will come back and bring friends from out of town.

Six of us were there this weekend.  We all had been regulars (maybe five visits per year), but with this last visit, I am fairly sure none of us will be back.  Unfortunately, all the couples ordered the off menu beet salad.  Someone must be nuts.  $14 for a salad that has two thin slices of beets, maybe one leaf of lettuce cut up, and a few candied nuts!!!!!!  We complained to the server and he basically ignored us.  That's fine, they made a big profit on the salad, but they will never see us again.  (Also, the cut way back on the items offered on the diner menu and jacked the prices since our last visit.)

This place served it's purpose... But for the price- it should've had a refrigerator & a microwave at least... & a room safe...???  I can't remember when I've stayed in a hotel room that didn't have a fridge last, & that includes a HoJo... Pretty bad... Beds were comfy tho. This place looks like a 1950s hotel that's been remodeled. All doors on balcony, either inner or outer, pretty sure the inner courtyard used to be open-now enclosed with pool. Who wants to swim in a pool in the cold AC??? Very nice decor, but need mini fridge in room- a must have.  Don't scrimp on the essentials!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
First time at Santa Fe Mexican Grill.  Service was pleasant.  Food was very good. Had grilled chicken with green peppers, onions with white cheese.  The chicken was so tender. Loved the refried beans. The only reason I only gave it 3 stars is because when the bill came we were charged $17.50 for a pitcher of Bud Light.  The menu price said $9.90.  When we questioned the bill, the waitress explained they had recently changed their prices.  When we asked to look at the menu again, she failed to show us a menu with the "new" prices.  Our cost of the pitcher was adjusted.  Please look over your bill. 
I felt we were being taken advantage of.

This is one of those out of the way places you'd never know existed except by sheer luck. I was lucky to have found it because the food is excellent. I have had the seafood pasta dish and it was the best I ever had. Their pizza is to die for. The only reason this is getting 3 instead of 4 stars is the staff and owner. I got the feeling that I was annoying the wait staff when asking for something. The owner has that I don't care if you eat here or not air about him. They do takeout which is what I do now as opposed to dealing with the staff issues.

A few years ago I bit into my roasted peppers AND a fish hook. The staff could not have cared less, pretty much insinuating I brought the hook with me to put in their food. They didn't even take the dish off the check, even though I wouldn't eat it or anything else after nearly having my gums impaled. I'll never go back & have advised others to stay away. Not even an apology. I should say there was a lot of blood & they couldn't wait to get me out of there (after paying the full bill). Rude does not even begin to describe that staff.

NOTE:  A reservation does not mean you won't wait 20 minutes or more on a Saturday night, which was annoying as there is really no place to wait. Once we finally were seated, we had a nice dinner. Great traditional Italian food, hearty pasta and sauce, fresh shrimp, attentive staff.  It is fun to watch them work. Fabulous bread.  And they gave us a free order of (very good) bruschetta to make up for the delay, which was very thoughtful. Very closely packed, to give it the real south Philly feel.  BYOB, which keeps the bill reasonable.  We took  a LOT home with us -- enough for a full lunch for everyone on Sunday!

Huge rooms at an awesome price.  Super nice staff and great views.  However, I had my car burglarized there overnight.  My back door window was shattered.  I got the hotel/maintenance manager involved and he found the TIPD number for me.  Then, he walked away without a care in the world.  My job is customer service, no one offered me a credit for another night stay or were sympathetic.  I will not stay here just because of the way they handled the situation.  I will be staying at the Hyatt in Clearwater next time I head this way.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Pains me to only give 2 stars because I've had GREAT experiences at other Vetri restraurants.

Pizza was ok, had the marinara and margarita.  Thicker crust isn't my style but I new that going in.

My beef is with the service and prices.  The bartender lady wasn't friendly at all.  They charge $9 for a glass of red wine that couldn't have been more than 3 oz. and it came in a plastic cup.  The woman at the counter were a tad friendlier.  

If I'm in the mall, yea I'd probably stop in again but I wouldn't make it my sole reason for going like I did over the weekend.

Sat down and ordered a bento box and some sushi for dinner.  The sushi was excellent, but the tempura shrimp was just mediocre.  

Instead of tempura sauce, they drizzle some kind of sweet teriyaki ish sauce on top, and they left the shrimp on top the hot rice, so it was no longer crispy by the time it got to my table.

The sushi on the other hand had nicely seasoned rice, and the sashimi dinner came with much more fish than I pictured.  Their light sushi soy sauce is bangin.

Food prep was a bit slow.  Took almost 30 mins for my food.  But overall I had a good time.

"This hotel is awful" - my husband upon entering the room. Yes, it's awful. It smells like mildew, the tiles are old and dirty, the molding is worn and darkening around a scummy tub... Outdated carpet, noisy toilet and AC unit kept the dog up and barking all night, the food is left out with no way to keep perishables cold- the milk and hard boiled eggs were warm. I will say the bed was decent and appeared clean but the pillows were kinda weird. I was surprised because we stayed at the other LaQuinta nearby and it was pretty good; clearly they are not all held to the same standard.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Hailing from the tropical isles of Hawaii, I've had my shares of exquisite sushi.  Ergo, when my friend suggested Sam's Sushi Bar for a quick dinner, I did not harbor any particular predilection toward Japanese cuisine in Nashville. However, given the persuasion of Sam's Sashimi Specials and Unagi rolls, I can't particular disparage his culinary skills. The idiosyncratic and seemingly cantankerous man certainly has a character, which many of the other reviewers have referenced, but I don't find that to be a hindrance to my dining experience.

Take out lunch was a decent value.  Flavor of the food was all there (General Tso) but it was a weak amount of chicken compared to rice.  Again the flavor was probably some of the best I've had in years, and recently I have been struggling to find a good "Bad" ("bad"= Americanized Chinese) spot.  I usually venture into the city if I want real taste of China. Wonton soup was on point, the wonton wrapper was very thin and not doughy at all.  I work in the area and rarely order out for lunch but I would try something else to see portion size before I say value isn't there.

The hotel itself was fine.  The poor bartender.  Management has not set her up for success. I ordered champagne, she had to go to the cooler for it. My husband ordered a glass of Cabernet, which was on the menu. After 10 minutes of looking, they didn't have it.  They were kind enough to comp. the glass they did give him.  He then asked for another round and asked "what do you have?"  She said she had a Merlot but no corkscrew to open it. I felt sorry for her, it's not her fault.  But the management needs to provide her the basic tools. I felt bad for her. She was delightful!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Thick crusted pizza that is somehow light and almost like pastry.  It produces a giddy feeling, not unlike that you feel eating fresh baked bread right out of the oven.  The crust is an integral part of each delicious pie, not just a sad conveyance for toppings.  Thin crust just seems so Kate Moss after this...

The appetizers and pasta dishes elevate the menu above most pizza places.  Rumor has it the meatballs may soon be recognized as some of the best in the city.  The concept is worthy of Cochon's chef, and is an authentic nod to the Sicilian pies of Brooklyn.

These guys continue to hit it out of the park.  Offering good burgers and great service, this location of Five Guys is recommended.

Protip: as it will likely strike you as being dry and uninspired, avoid getting a plain burger; the bacon cheeseburger is the way to roll here.  You don't need fries, either, as free peanuts are available to all.  When both of the foregoing are combined with a complementary cup of water, you'll be betting a better meal for the same price than you would at McDonald's, Wendy's, A&W, Harvey's, Burger King, etc.

While the tacos here don't seem to be quite the same as they were several months ago, that could be my mind playing tricks on me.  What isn't the same and what needs to change is the complementary snack that they bring to you before your meal.  Previously, Mexico Lindo used to bring to you a small plate of totopos/nachos/tortilla chips at which one could pick until your main course(s) arrived.  No more.  Now some pretty gross wheel-shaped corn puff things are produced for you to try.  They aren't the best.  Six-year-old me might have liked them, though!

Well, this is annoying.  So, someone complained and had my review of this establishment removed because they claimed it "did not appear to describe a firsthand customer experience".  What a load of nonsense!  I ate here and the food was very underwhelming.  In fact, it was kind of bad.  I stand by my assertion that you're likely to find the food served up by Panda Hut Express to be to your taste only if you enjoy bad small town American/Canadian Chinese food restaurants across the land and I continue to suggest that you pass on this place if you know better.

just paid US$99.50 for a regular bottle of Blanton's which is usually US$66-72. They also have their own label single barrel from Blanton's just for Lukens.  Also, US$99.50 ! Strange.  Called, but they stuck to their story, both the same whiskey and the same price. Then why the different bottle?
Lukens has a great selection, but so does ABC, Total Wine and Universal, they have more rare Bourbons than any other store.  I just think Lukens' staff is not well trained nor very welcoming. I'll make a circle around their stores

This place is unbelievable! They have a prix fixe menu that's $25 for 3 courses. I went with my family and we had the crab cakes risotto, the scallop and shrimp papardelle, tiramisu and coffee. The bread was oven hot and crispy, served with olive oil and butter. My mom had clams and scallop pasta and my aunt and uncle had the chicken parmigiana. The service was excellent, and the prices reasonable. I suggest making a reservation or you'll be waiting. It's BYOB, so be sure to bring a bottle of your favorite. I will be returning soon.

Took my tiny little convertible to have it washed. I know the front inside needed a serious vacuuming. But to get my car back with exterior still dirty. My top of my that never leaks was dripping water !! Brake dust on the rims and my tiny trunk not vacuumed is ridiculous. I went back to ask for my money back and the rude manager refused to do so. I was angry told him it was B.S. asked for the owners card he walked away and never returned. He hid from me and I was told by another employee I could get a card for a free wash. Why would I want another wash from them?  This place is a joke with a worthless unhelpful manager.

Food, real good
Service, real mediocre

I've been to Grillsmith multiple times, usually on Wednesday for the all day happy hour. However, we usually get hassled about getting the specials when we don't sit at the bar. Last time the waiter told us the specials were no longer available. 

Hmm....All day happy 4-11pm, yet at 8pm happy hour is over. Interesting....

The food is great. Simple, well made and served on enormous plates. Everything is bigger in Texas, I guess.  

I've tried all the appetizers and never been disappointed. The Salmon bruschetta is my favorite.

Go during happy hour, get the apps and 1/2 drafts beers and enjoy.

I realize being a fast food restaurant I shouldn't be too picky or expect much. This review is based only off of their drive through, I have been through the drive-through a few times and each time I am sitting at The menu waiting for someone to come over the speaker and take my order. Finally somebody comes on to take my order but they are interrupted by another employee who was chiming in to take my order. Food is food. Timeliness of order is not bad once you place the order. I will avoid going here again.

The drive thru takes an eternity to get through.  When I got to the counter to pay, I noted how long I had been waiting (just for a tea!).  The girl who was there said "it's happy hour, so it going to take a long time."  Does the manager not know that it's happy hour?  Can they bring in extra staff?  I should note that it was last day of a month of every day happy hours, so they should be prepared by now.  I usually get this attitude from anyone working at this location.  I don't go on a good day, it will ruin my mood.

Three stars is reasonable. Their food is at best okay. Why? It's not, in my opinion, anything close to what I consider Chinese. The owner/some employees seem (but I'm no expert) to be Vietnamese. No problem with that but it kind of shows in the taste of the food. Also, I that may explain why there is Vietnamese spring rolls and Pad That (a Thai dish) --- in a Chinese place?? I have enjoyed dishes in Shanghai and Beijing as well as in Hong Kong so I may be quite critical - sorry.

I guess one can enjoy the food but it's just not fitting the flavor profile I am used to eating.

I can tell why they named their store Five Star Pizza. The quality of their pizza and chicken wings and everything is amazing! It's delicious! I'm very picky about where I get my pizza from.. I didn't really want to try their pizza at first because it wasn't a name that I was familiar with .. but it was worth trying anyways! Everyone was nice and very accommodating. Service didn't take very long. Customer service was great. I love this place! I highly recommend this to all pizza lovers and to all non pizza lovers. They're going to end up liking the Five Star Pizza.

It was the hardest phone call I ever had to make. Sheila allowed me to ask as many questions as I needed to. She answered every question with knowledge and compassion. She allowed me to sob as long as I needed to. When I was ready, she explained what was going to happen. When I was ready, she performed her task with the greatest of care. My sweet baby for more than 15 years passed over without a bit of pain. It was a most peaceful, loving, and compassionate act. If I could, I would rate Sheila as many stars as there are in the sky. 

Paula H.

We live close and have been there a few times and it's been ok. Went in last week for lunch, I had the lunch special pizza and wife had the lasagna special. Pizza tasted like one of those cheap frozen pizza's, no taste from anything. Got some extra sauce just to give it a little flavor which cost an extra $1.50 for a very small amount. The lasagna was a small serving, wife said it was just ok. Bill came to about $20 which was not a good deal. Told server food was not very good, and she didn't seem to care. Won't be back.

The service is good.

The decoration of the café gives a feeling of "Europe"; in other words, if you are the kind of person who cares a lot about "the beauty of a restaurant", this is a right place.

There are some sort of special elements in their breakfast dishes (e.g. some dish uses spinach instead of lettuce; "English muffin" instead of muffin); but I would not say that the taste of dishes in this place could give any unique experience to customs, compared to other café places. Nothing special & nothing terrible. Anyway, it's still a qualified place for a decent "standardized" breakfast.

The place looks a little shabby on the outside. I think the bar in the front might be abandoned, it certainly looked so to me. Rooms look a lot better on the inside. Clean. Service is nice, staff is friendly. The breakfast was hot: sausage,eggs, etc. muffins, yogurt and juice(mostly prepacked food or processed food as one might expect.)

Loud people around outside pretty late. cops were there the first night. People hanging around outside the rooms on the ground floor. Overall, I was not impressed even with the low price. I guess you get what you pay for with lower prices.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: In town for business and stayed at a nearby hotel. Decided to order a pizza from a nearby pizza place. I'm sorry to say this was one of the worst pizzas I've ever had. I watched them make the pie and instead of hand tossing the dough it went through a dough rolling machine. The meat topping was very sparse. The pizza was cooked in a conveyor belt broiler type oven and was under done. The crust tasted liked raw flour and wasn't even close to done. I'm from Philly and have great Italian pizza joints all around me. I hope for everyone's sake there's better pizza in Harvey, LA somewhere.

I started calling for an appointment and the woman who answered was not very nice. Despite my questions (first haircut in the US) she kept on repeating what time I wanted to go. Whatever.

I arrived just in time (I didn't want any problem after the phone conversation) and they sat me right away. The woman who did my haircut was nice and helping, as I didn't know which were "my numbers". I explained myself and she did her best, which finally was quite near what I wanted.

I can say the result was nice, and that I will come back. Ok, the fact that it is three blocks away from home helps, too.

We decided to have a date night last night and we had not been to Hal'a in a while. It did not disappoint. They prawn appetizer was so good.It was in a sweet a spicy sauce. My husband had the ribeye and I had the spicy sirloin tips and a side of asparagus .It was truly one of the best steaks we have had in a long time. Kudos to the chef! Our waitress was very good and the hostess Made us feel right at home. Wine selection and full bar was a plus. I would defiantly recommend this place! We have tried my new places downtown and this is way better!

My hubby and I went for the first time last night, November 2013, a Saturday.  We live in the neighborhood and my hubby  is a snob and thinks you need to leave our area to get good Italian food.  I saw a coupon  in the mail, so I suggested we give it a try.  He agreed with me.  We had an excellent meal and were happy to have such a good place so close by.  I would give them 5 stars but the coffee was terrible and they had no hot tea.  They need to fix that fast.  They have breakfast too, so get on the coffee fix please.    We will go back soon and I highly recommend Roma for the dinner entrees we enjoyed.

Ok so this is where you want to go if you want to stay in center city and don't care for el Rey or el vez. If you're looking for lots of melted cheese or refried beans and the basics go here. I was surprised by how much I enjoyed the chips and salsa. Very good. It appears that you can bring your own liquor (and beer, but they charge a 'corkage' fee). They do serve wine and beer if you aren't a big drinker or didn't make it to the store beforehand. Seems great for large groups even though I wasn't part of one. Combination platters aren't cheap- about $12-13. Overall- I wasn't disappointed but I've been to better.

The service was wonderful, our server was so nice and she was paying attention to us the whole time though her section was busy. Everything came out in a reasonable amount of time. The food was on the good side of mediocre and was a tad overpriced considering. Husband had the osso bucco and I had the penne with vodka sauce. Both came out hot and looked great, cooked properly, just not the best we've had. The place is clean and well lit, good for a date or a family meal, and again, the service was really great.

We have been going to this place for several years, even when they were a small place in Kennett Square.    This is NOT a chain, but a family owned place.   We recommend ordering what they call "chunky salsa" and the Quac for the chips - really good.   The place has become more commercialized after if moved from Kennett but the food is still good, and now they have a liquor license.    Some of the special dishes are the seafood soup, Molcajete in green sauce and the Tex Mex Fajitas Moroleon style are very good.

This is by far the WORST store in town! Employees tell me how bad they are treated by the comapany and by store manager Terry. The chicken is HORRIBLE! The deli is disgusting and have seen pictures from employees showing how filthy it is in the back! Produce is always moldy or beyond ripe. The bathrooms are worst than a highway gas station!! They are never clean, never have paper towels, never have toilet paper, never have soap...I cant believe Jon Flora has let his company get to this...Walmart...here I come!!

The food here is good - but the dining room is so small you're practically sitting on top of the people next to you. Also, it's incredibly noisy so you can barely carry on a conversation with the person you're with. On top of that, we were seated next to the kitchen, and I kept on getting bumped by waiters walking back and forth. I like to relax when I go to a restaurant, and it's really just not possible at this place due to the noise and close quarters. I guess some people like small, noisy, cramped BYOs, but this place just didn't do it for me.

So...as  i normally do...PROCRASTINATE...needed a hc bad...called fringe..of course Jessica is booked up(my bad...my fault) still wanted a hair cut...the next day Irma was available at the time I could actually get up there...Holy Shit...do you believe in fate ...meant to be...everything happens for a reason?? jessica was booked so i could meet Irma=) SERIOUSLY tho...this cutie can cut some hair!! and can actually stylt it so i DON'T have to go home and redo it...plus...bonus she can shampoo too...sweet!! my hair cut by the is a serious sexy bob...not aline... not crooked ...thx Irma...muah!!

Maybe I'm too picky about cleanliness but this place is gross. I also understand having a family run business but twice I've been seated toward the back by the sushi bar... The last table, both times, was covered with coloring books, ipads and take out from fast food.. With what I assume are the owners children and the wait staff dropping by and snacking with them. Just not my idea of a relaxing dinner. Plus the menus, tables, etc are sticky and gross. This used to be a favorite of ours. Sad too see this happen.

Ack!  I live two miles from this place and will NEVER go back!  The decor is nice, the building historic and the Coke was good.  That's where it ends...

I waited about 20 minutes for the most tasteless Maryland Crab soup I've ever had.  Then waited another 50 minutes for one sad looking plate of food.  Ordered the shrimp skewers.  Overcooked mushy shrimp, dried-out cold potatoes and flavorless veggies.  The waitress offered free dessert for the wait.  I turned it down.  Just what I needed, more bad food!

They sat us at a table near the bar.  Man was it LOUD!  Never again!

Everything was going great until we got sprayed with beer by the bartender for a second time!!  Our group was very accepting of the bartenders apologies the first time one of us got hit by an what appeared to be a broken beer tap. For all we knew he had not idea it was going to happen.  The second time it happened the guy was obviously aware of the situation.  He told us he was sorry and if we didn't like it we could leave.  The correct answer would have been to either shut down that tap or at least warn us before pouring from it.  I couldn't imagine spilling stuff on my customers, I would be out of a job by the end of my shift.

My hubs and I eat here A. LOT. I have my definite favorite (grilled salmon sandwich), but try other things when I'm in the mood. We've always had very good food with very good service - the waitress who has worked there forever is so sweet and kind (and she recognizes us, every time); she really makes the experience. In our experience, it's a solid choice when we want to eat out but can't decide on a place in NW. They have a little bit of everything - fancy dinners, burgers, salads, hot sandwiches. We're big fans.

went to fill a friends growler. great selection of growler fills. a good diverse although overpriced selection of bottles and cans. 
the guy at the growler bar did not greet me at all i had to find the menu on my own he was busy telling a customer that he has to tip him there because if you tip when you pay at the register he wont get it. (maybe he would get more tips if he provided service and wasn't to cool for customers. )
the owner at the register ignored customers while texting on his phone he actually told the woman ahead of me to wait until he was finished. after her he went back to texting while i waited to pay! i will never go back.

My girlfriend and I stayed overnight for a little date night between the two of us. Rooms were nice and clean, i liked the high ceiling and view in our room. We dont get to go to the city much as we used to and didnt really have anything planned until a helpful staff member Joseph Crismond gave us some great restaurant recommendations and told us about some other places to check out in the city. It was nice hearing about these places from a person who spends time in the city as oppose to a website. Nice hotel, friendly staff, we plan on staying again on our next date night.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Wow, I am surprised by the reviews. We love Pat's Pizza and think it's the best place in Downingtown for pizza. Their pizza is thicker and not paper thin. 

Their sandwiches are well stuffed and rolls are soft. I have had their salads and they are large.

My husband thinks they have the best Italian Stromboli and this is his fav.

The restaurant is clean, clean, clean! It's kid friendly and has two TV's inside (usually CNN or ESPN  on).

The service is friendly and the manager always is nice. 

For a pizza and sandwich shop, this place gets a high rating from me!

It's not bad, it's not great.

My biggest complaint is so many freaking onions! Really, this place will have you thinking China only has meat and onions. So many onions. I mean, if onions are your jam, I got the place for you. They also didn't take out the digestive tract in shrimp.

But the green beans are awesome! Crisp tender and oily but not too much. I would be happy to eat green beans with seasoned meat all day.

In the other places I've lived this would have been a 2. But it's 'Chinese' in Nashville so what can we do?

Wine selection is good but seems to be over-priced. Hard liquor selection is very, very sparse.

Staff is always turning over, I feel like I never see the same people twice. EXCEPT for an elderly man who is an asshole. I've had the displeasure of dealing with him a few times. After the last, never going back. Also, bottles are dusty as hell. Rotate those things (as a side note, I've been privy to more than one customer complaining about corked bottles).

There are a few wine and spirit shops in this areas, use any one of those.

Two stars for location only.

I recently ate dinner here and the ambience is lovely. 

Unfortunately, the food is not. I ordered a crab cake sandwich and sweet potato fries. Both were only luke warm. The crab cake was covered with an unusual substance. I needed to ask the server what it was as neither myself nor my knowledgeable companion could determine what the smooth covering was. For reference, it is Ritz cracker.  The sweet potato fries were soggy and bland.

On a positive note the staff were attentive. There is a nice selection of beer on tap.

I have never left this place without feeling up-sold, fast talked or held hostage. I can't complain about the quality of the product or their work. The one exception is a  recent repair on which I dropped a grand on a coolant system issue, which included $60 in labor for "Flushing," only to have old coolant all over the engine smoking and making a lovely aroma for me and the other motorists fortunate enough to be around me. However, I do continue to pay the stupid tax for their convenient location and hours of operation.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: Visited the restaurant shortly after first opened and didn't have good experience - had to wait an hour and half for table for 2, then 30 mins for drinks and just to order, then the food was just meh.  Thought would give another shot tonight ordering thru Bitesquad but same bad experience - they took over an hour to prep my food and when finally delivered the order was missing items and cold. Never again Grand Hacienda - don't think your going to last very long in St Pete with this level of service and there are much better places to get Mexican food!

I know it must have been tough to make the quick move from Vandy (near my work) to Murfreesboro Rd (near my home) but somehow they've maintained the same quality and great prices I had come to expect.

Their new location was an O'Charleys and most recently an outpost for Boltons next door to Horus Kabab near the corner of Murfreesboro and East Thompson Lane. 

Great sushi and ramen are difficult to find in this part of town. And the switch from an eat-out-every-meal Vandy crowd to this hidden spot will be difficult. For the sake my own selfish sushi needs PLEASE VISIT KENS SUSHI!

this place. OY. very very inconsistent, which is a total shame b/c its so cute inside! 
I've been here maybe 5 times. only 2 out of the 5 were good experiences. The last time I was here, the polish the girl used on me seemed to be near empty. When I said something about it, she put some solution in it and kept going. She probably rubbed my arms once over with lotion, and then went on her way like she was in a hurry! (Mind you, there wasn't a line at this time of day). My nails lasted 2 days until they started chipping. So, theres that.

Today was the third time since dunkin donuts opened in this location that my husband and I have tried to patronize this business. For the third time we were told they didn't have donuts. Perhaps the franchise should consider changing its name to dunkin croissants or dunkin bagel; considering they never seem to have donuts. In an attempt to salavage a wasted trip we ordered two coffees that tasted burnt. 
The only saving grace this location has is the lovely drive thru attendant that was very sweet.
