Very expensive for what you get, especially considering how stingy they are with the meat - my sandwich barely had any turkey on it and had big sections of bread without cheese either. Definitely not better than I could make myself at home. Cheesy tots were kind of soggy and not very flavorful, a grainy cheese topping with some spices that just registered as "mildly hot" and not much else. I hate wasting food, but if I hadn't been sharing them they probably wouldn't have been finished. I remember the food truck versions being better in all cases.

My wife and I went there for lunch. Being vegetarians, she had the Mediterranean and I did the 4-cheese. Now, if you want to create a restaurant based around something as simple as mac & cheese and charge $8 for a small dish of it, the execution and flavors had better be perfect. Unfortunately the food was all around mediocre. While I would eat it if a friend gave it to me for free, I could create something better at home in the same amount of time it took to drive there and wait for the food to be cooked. So, overall, I would not recommend spending the time or the money on this place.

A great family restaurant. Great meat and veggies that they are well known for. They also have been the best burgers and sandwiches around and the onion rings are the best. Norman Couser and his wife are still involved but not like they used to be. Many days you will see them there with smiles on their faces and a thank you for coming. The servers, all friendly and willing to please are glad to wait on you. You may get a hug from one or two of them before you leave. I highly recommend this place if you want good home cooking,friendly service in a warm atmosphere.

Stopped here for the first time the other night. What a great experience!!! We were in Morrisville planning a retirement party that will be held at this restaurant and thought we would stop for dinner on the way home. What a nice surprise. Amy our server took us through the specials and was very attentive. I had a Ceaser salad, very good and pasta with sausage and broccoli Rabelais. Delicious!! The wife had the salmon special with lump crab meat and declared it one of the best meals she has had in a long time. I don't know why it took us so long to go here, but we will be back. Give it a try, you won't be disappointed.

Yeah, whoever decorated this place had REALLY interesting taste. Christmas tree lights, and not so clean windows. The bathroom stinks. I swear, there was a kaka stain on the wall near the urinal that had remained there through 3 years of my eating there (no kidding). The food from the menu is good (The Sesame Chicken is the best in town). The buffet (which is not offered every day now) is regrettably a tad smelly. The Tsing Tao beer is awesome. Come during Happy Hour. The waitresses are nice and the overall service is good. It's worth the stop.

My family loves this place. It is truly one of the best restaurants in the Willow Grove and surrounding areas. Reservations are almost always a must especially towards the weekend. The staff is very friendly and attentive to kids and my kids love the attention they get. My wife is a sushi snob and claims that this is one of the best (next to Blue Fin in Plymouth Meeting). I am not a big sushi fan but we tend to eat here a lot. The only downside which I can see is the parking lot which tends to be a bit chaotic especially around the side of the building.

My husband and I have a love for sushi. We would drive from San Francisco to Reno and spend our weekend for sushi. We used to go to Sushi Pier, until we found out Minato. They have those Donald, Mickey nigiri and the egg shooter that sushi pier has, and more. I simply just love their hand rolls, especially the Amy and Playboy. Really flavorful and unique. They also have the marvelous mussels. Oh, and save some room the tempura ice cream. The last time I was there I had 2 of them :).

Really really hope they would have a branch in the bay.

time to change personnel and get this restaurant back to where it had been a few years ago. Bar is a lack luster environment, with BAD bartenders who cant keep up  with orders on an average day leaving the bar unclean between patrons . Left the restaurant tonight on a Thursday @ 9 and all but 1 or 2 tables was occupied and  all others were still dirty after patrons had left. BAD morale, Bad customer service, BAD family management (2 exceptions).\. Time to get back to basics and take this business seriously..

My daughter-in-law when in for 4 new tires, they insisted that her car, a 2016, needed an alignment.  She said no but they insisted, she agreed but requested proof from the before and after alignment reports.  They only provided the after and when she argued the validity of the service Jeff, the manager, said they would put it back on the lift and take it out of alignment.  My daughter-in-law said no and that there wasn't a reason to pay the extra $100 Jeff, assumedly caught in his lie, caller her a bit@h and asked her to leave.  We're headed to the West Chester police station tomorrow to file a harassment report.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
I'm allowing 2 stars because the other locations are MUCH better. First off they don't have free parking after 6pm. ($5) Second they had two employees working and no one was wanting to come help us when we wanted to try one of the flavors. There were only 4 of 8 flavors working. (The other were "out of service"). If you go to any other location they have what's called "Weigh and Pay". Not knowing this location was different we all got little helpings and were charged full price for the large instead of how much we got. 


SUMMARY: If in Nashville go to Green Hills, Brentwood or Franklin. Avoid 21st.

I beg to differ on the service. It's fair.  The Sunday bartender seems to be more concerned about football results rather than doing his job.  Do patrons come there to hear his post game of the over rated Phila Eagles?  No.   There's a time and a place for everything. Food is outstanding despite the half arse service  The owner and or manager, or whatever youngster who was in the vestibule should thank patrons for coming when they leave.  Not just have them walk out with no acknowlegment.  Rude and he should know better than that.  They take people for granted when money is flowing into their pocket.

My mom used to take me here when i was little and i recently started going here again as an adult. Still exactly how i remember it, and that's a good thing. a few chinese buffets i've been to have been a little sketchy and dirty but this one is usually pretty clean for the most part and its always nice and quiet and ive never had to wait for a table. the food is always great and if something runs out they are quick to replace with a fresh batch. i don't really have any complaints except that the lady that you pay up at the front always seems a little unfriendly lol.

Stopped in again tonight and - Ohmagosh - the Wildcat - Sin on a Plate man - the best ever nachos on fries I've ever had.  The meat is so good.  They were worth blowing the diet for (albeit a couple weeks worth),  Mix that with Moose Drool on tap and pretty decent bartenders and I had to up the rating a full star.  Wings were star quality as well but had to bag those up - couldn't eat a full serving of both - even after calling in reinforcements to help.  Sinful portions but a great place.  Good beer, good food, good service.

This was a busy place around noon time on a Monday.  They had a counter and a few bar stools.  There's also a separate line to order.  I wish they had a sign stating that so I didn't waste time.  Ordered 1. Roast duck & cha siu on white rice and 2. Roast duck & won ton in noodle soup.  The roast duck were very fatty and not much meat.  The cha siu was flavorful and tender.  Won ton skin was very thick and could use some good seasoning in the fillings.  There were only a few bean sprouts in the noodle soup instead of green veggies.  I will try sitting at the counter next time hopefully I'll get better looking meat.

Stayed here on a day it was 90 degrees. Went to check in and was told the pool was not operational. At 3:30 in the morning the air conditioning started making a squealing noise had to hit it to get it to stop but it would start making the noise again a few minutes later so turned it off.  Got up next morning and turned on tv to watch the news, cable wasn't working!  Worked fine night before.  Vending machine on our floor was out of order so went to desk to see where there was another one. Lady said there isn't anymore but we have soda here we can sell you for $3 a bottle!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I went here last week with my sister. I had the steak which was good. My sister had the chicken which she said was alright. The problem was that she ate over half the chicken until she realized the thicker breast part was raw! We showed it to our server and all she said was "sorry about that" and took it away. In hindsight it was our bad that we didn't ask for the manager. But when you're charging $20 for a piece of chicken--come on! The place did salvage a star from me for having a good wine list but I still feel they're overrated.

I honestly don't know what has happened to this dunkin donuts in the past year or so. This used to be one of my go to places, but now it has really gone down the tubes. Every time I go weather I go in the store or through the drive through I end up waiting way longer than I should for my food/drink regardless of weather or not theres a line. Every other time I go through the drive through they get my order wrong. I used to stop here almost everyday on my way to work/school and now I hardly go to this location any more. Definitely would not recommend.

Staff is great. The hotel was undergoing some renovations on some floors when I last visited hence the lift had some building material litter in them. The location is great as it was close to my office and close to restaurants and Wegmans. the breakfast was pretty decent. The hotel is very close to the highway so was woken up numerous times at night when trucks were thundering past. The air conditioning is also very loud on both occassions I stayed there. Cannot continue staying here due to disturbed sleep so staying at a hotel further away from the highway.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I love Meglio's, but I just got CRAZY sick / food poisoning from one of their chicken cheese steaks.  My wife and I ordered delivery and our food was there within ten minutes, which I guess should have set off an alarm, but we were just happy to have our food so quickly.  

I got violently ill for 24 hours (I'm starting to feel a little better now); I had given my cat a piece of the chicken and he threw it up in the middle of the night, too.  I recommend going there in person to get your food.  We're going to be staying away for a little while, though.

This place is incredible. Their food has always been perfect. Fresh ingredients. They also deliver which as all of know. Lunchtime is always limited in time. Assorted very tasty sandwiches and very awesome soups. Within an hour or less "hot and very tasty food" arrives. We have also gotten delicious dinners. We have eaten at their location in Cherry Hill several times. They only issue is parking in that shopping center. Hit or miss. All about timing. Either way. This place is worth a visit. Eat in or delivery!!!!!!

-1 definitely agree. I have been to this location maybe 3 times. Would not recommend ANYONE to go here. You will be disappointed. I hate to say this but when I walked in today I was not greeted when I walked in. Ordered a #9 w a milkshake to drink & a bag of chocolate chip cookies. I am then informed that there is no ice cream after placing my order. I got a refund of the cost of the milkshake. My food became ready it seemed to quick to good to be true. I go to leave no cookies in the bag, my burgers are cold cheese not even melted. Just save your money & do not go to this location. Customer service & food is trash....!!!!
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
We went on a Friday night at about 6:30PM and it is almost empty. By the time we left at about 7:30, it was still less than half full. The decor was generic, the large screen TV and the rock music made it feel like a sports bar rather than a pizzeria. 

The menu was on the expensive side, pizza for $16-$20 and pasta at about $19. We tried two pizza and it was fine, nothing too special. The Kobe meatballs  was greasy and bland. 

Service was fine.

We were not impressed by Avero, it was not terrible, it's just okay.

I've had good quality work done here, but the wait can be very long-- as in, 5-6 hours for basic maintenance tasks-- and they do not tend to say up front if it will be a long wait.  Most of the people are extremely nice and helpful, but one woman in the office (who appears to be in an owner/manager role) is really nasty and obstructs the good service of the other people.  I believe the mechanics are honest.  I would say, this is probably a good place if you need a complicated repair, but for basic maintenance, it would be best overall to go somewhere else.

I'd been hearing rave reviews about their brunch from friends and finally got to try it out a few weeks ago. I was not disappointed! The atmosphere is really charming and rustic and our server was just the right amount of attentive without being pesty. The food was awesome. I am so surprised at others' bad experiences because we both thought the buffet was great. I'm taking another friend back next weekend. Everything was fresh and replenished, even after 1PM (we got there late), and very tasty. Standard brunch fare, no real surprises, but everything was really good and the dessert table was amazing. I can't wait to go back!

Food was good, but we thought it was overpriced.  Salads are extra and run $7-$8.  Tables are extemely close.  I wish restaurants that do daily speciaks would either print them out in insert into the menu, place on tables or have a board for them.  Knowing the price helps also without having to ask.  We did have to ask for a second basket of bread after the bus person and waitrewss walked by several times noticing it was emply.  The restuaranmt was not busy when we were there,  It was early on a Friday.    Water was refilled promptly.   Not sure we would go back.

I stayed here last week for a work mtg.  The hotel was clean and the staff very friendly.  Location is great and near restaurants, shopping and a gym.  However, I stayed on the 9th floor and it was freezing in the hallway.  Honestly, it felt like there was no heat on in that area of the hotel.  My room was also extremely cold.  I set thermostat on 80 degrees and with covers still was cold.  I do not think the heat was operating right.  My colleague shared that he had the same experience.  What a shame because otherwise it is a great hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Wonderful location. I love the open space and the beautiful Probat roaster. Great interior.

Service was great. Barista pulled the shots for my cappuccino a little fast, apologized for the wait(which wasn't long), adjusted his grind and pulled another with better timing. (Coffee geeks will understand). Just goes to show that they care about serving the best espresso drinks possible.

I love their coffee for pour over and straight espresso shots. I'm hoping they will develop another blend that compliments milk based espresso drinks a little more. 

I am excited for this new location, I hope it will be sucessful

My friends and I were in Nashville over the weekend for a concert, and chose this location via Priceline due to its location. It did not disappoint! The lobby has been nicely updated and was very inviting. Unfortunately, the front desk is small (only allowing 2 workers to check in guests at a time) so there was a small wait upon arrival. However, the front desk staff were very pleasant, apologized for our short wait and quickly got to work. While it's obvious that it's an older property, the rooms were clean and fresh and the common areas were well kept.  We'll definitely be choosing this location again!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Solid donuts. These are cake donuts, not yeast like most of the bakeries around.  They are airy and kind of crispy, pretty awesome. The set up reminds me of the fractured prune, except the donuts aren't hot when the toppings are added. I actually prefer this set up, because you don't end up with a sloppy mess of a donut and melted toppings. We got a box of 9 donuts, called the niner and they were good. I enjoyed the samoa and my husband was happy with the caramel apple pie. We will definitely add this place to our regular breakfast rotation. Great addition!

These people are terrible!!!!!! They have the worst customer service ever!!! I lived at many apartment complexes in the past (in this & many other countries) & never had so many issues as at this one. In addition, they are the biggest liars, they said they were only going to do a soft inquiry on my friend that I referred to live there at, & my friend told me they ended up doing a hard one (which nobody appreciates because they could have just been honest). Please save yourself time & headaches with this apartment!!! The infrastructure is really bad, needs lots of maintenance & again, nobody is friendly nor helpful!

We had lunch at this Arby's location yesterday (May 6) - ordered combo meals for 2.  The sandwiches took a long time to get, but finally they called my name and I walked up to get them.  Then they told me that no one had made the fries or onion rings.  So they took the sandwiches back and began to make the fries/rings.  Finally got it all, but the sandwiches were now pretty cold and tired.  The store just seemed to be in chaos...like there was no manager on duty.  Lots of customers were standing around waiting on their food and it was taking a long time to get anything!

Check in is 3pm.  At 4pm I arrived and waited 45 minutes in line to get to the check-in desk which was absolutely insane.  I've never had to wait in line to check in like this in my life.  When I finally get to the desk the y tell me that no rooms are ready so I have to wait around for another hour before I can actually check in to my room at 6pm.  The staff was unsympathetic and made ZERO effort to make up for the inconvenience.  I was really shocked by the poor level of customer service here, especially considering how overpriced this place is.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Many meals here, never again!

Slow service. Our main course arrived 1:45 minutes after our arrival. We had to have it boxed up.  Manager Mike actually blamed US for ordering an appetizer!

There were only 5 tables in the entire place with customers and they could not handle it.

The final straw was the 2 employees smoking outside as we left, the actually told us to,"get the f$ck out of here".

So sad as this used to be a good place. Obviously service is not a priority anymore!
Avoid at all cost! There are much better places in Indy nowadays anyway...
#milanoinn #badservice

HORRIBLE SUSHI! and i MEAN it!
this place has been sending fliers to our building in CBD for a couple months now and we decided to give it a try, so we did (WHAT A MISTAKE)... O.M.G! the roles were the tinniest roles in THE ENTIRE WORLD. I wish i would be only that. They tasted HORRIBLE. I never near this place ever again, ever ever ever! we ordered 3 different roles and they came in a tiny tiny little box as small as a pencil case. if you dont believe me, order your sushi once from there and you learn your lesson!

Very disappointed. I ordered Mongolian beef, which should be cooked with green onions, seasoned with sesame seeds. Mine was a mash of over cooked yellow onions and tough strips of beef. The garlic shrimp dish was chock full of vegetables and only 3 shrimp. Very little garlic flavor. Hot and sour soup was also very weak in ingredients and flavor. This is what I usually use to treat a bad cold, but this wouldn't stifle a sniffle. I'd really like to see a really good Chinese restaurant in Edwardsville. It's been a 20 year wait.

I ordered a filet o fish for the second time at this location(8500 Henry ave.)  thinking it would be better this go around, but I was WRONG. The sandwich was below room temperature and the fries tasted like leftovers. The look I had on my face you would've thought I was having a stroke. I was extremely dissatisfied once AGAIN. It was at that moment I knew I had F**ked up. That location has given me TRUST issues with all McDonalds everywhere. It should be demolished and used for a parking lot. It doesn't deserve any stars IMO. But it won't post my review unless you give it at least one star.‍
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
January, 2017, Breakfast...Solo...9/9:30 AM
* They specialize in a "all-you-can-eat" buffet.
* Waitress, pleasant, seated me into a booth(nice).
* Looked over the menu...ordered(not the buffet).
* Waitress returned, 6-8 minutes later with..."I am so very sorry".
 -I said..."what are you being sorry about"?
 -Reply..."We are OUT of EGGS"...Whaaat
 -How can you RUN out of EGGS when you "feature" a breakfast buffet???
WHERE is the clueless/idiot manager??? Send someone to the nearest 
supermarket/store w/some $$...until breakfast hour is over... DUH!!!

The food was basic Mexican fare. The problem I have is they have a margarita and a ultimate margarita. The ultimate is $7.99 after our first round the waiter came back with a smile on his face and said here I kick this up A bit for you. So we had three kicked up margaritas and two regular margaritas and he charged us $10.99 a piece for all five.  I would call that a rip off! He made no mention of upgrading the strength with a cost involved. That should have been our option as some of us did not appreciate a stronger drink.

I go in here a few times a month with friends, the food I give 4 stars , the rolls and sandwiches (hot & cold) I give 5 stars. The owner & attitude in this place keeps it from being great which is why I didn't give it 4 or 5. 
Every time I'm in there the owner is either bad mouthing someone or just flat out rude to customers.

I've asked relatively general questions, like a menu question or something pertaining to my order & I get nothing but rude answers or 1 word answers. 

I got back because the food is good, not as much as I would if the owner wasn't a stuck up A-

It's a typical Americanized Japanese restaurant targeted for the general public.

I was expecting a bit more on traditional taste and freshness due to the high rating on yelp, but it's not really that much different from other generic Japanese restaurants near by.  I can understand that sashimi slices, though thick and somewhat fatty, may not be fresh since the fish market is not nearby, but the udon soup base also lacked depth. 

I haven't tried the soba noodle, so I'll reserve my final decision to go up or down a start until later.

Not very many cars to pick from in the lot. I had asked for Sirius/XM, but did not get it (although I was charged for it). I also discovered during the return that I was charged for pre-paid gas, which I specifically declined.  The guy checking me out after picking my car was less than enthused, and it took way to long discussing the radio and gas situation.  I knew he did not get it right.  The good thing is that upon returning the car I was referred to the manager, who was able to credit me back the gas and radio charges.

I have gone to this place several times.  It is very good no doubt and I assume because the ingredients are fresh? that that is the reason why it is pricey.  But I WILL NOT be going back there because this place cheats you!  If you scoop off the top portion of your yogurt (in a cup) you will see that they rip you off.  And this has happened on more than one occasion.  They don't fill up the center.  Basically you pay all that for them to rim the cup but not fill it.  It's good but don't go there unless you demand they give you your money's worth or unless it doesn't bother you to pay more than three dollars for air!

Finding the Creole Creamery was like finding heaven on earth!  So many flavors to choose from and so little time.  

The Black and Gold, in honor of the New Orleans Saints, features chickory flavored ice cream with bits of chocolate.  It was so good that I wolfed it down so fast that I got back in line and tried another flavor.

The staff is incredible, so helpful and clearly enjoy their jobs serving up ice cream that puts a smile on their customers' faces.

A little of the beaten track but a visit to this place is a must while in New Orleans.

We went to Avalon Pasta Bistro for their Sunday Supper at 5pm. Since it seemed family friendly (and it was early for dinner) - we took our toddler with us. The food was excellent and the service was fantastic. We ordered 2 small plates and 2 large plates for 2 adults and our son was given a generous portion of pasta and meatballs for free! (Kids under 5 eat for free on Sunday nights) It was definitely enough food for us. The complementary sangria and beer were a nice touch. We will definitely come back here whether it's for a quick family meal or a longer date night out.

Ordered a Large Pepperoni Pizza w/ Green peppers and onions, and sausage on one half, a cheesesteak, zucchini stixs and mac & cheese bites last night for dinner.

The delivery took over 1 & 1/2 hours to get here, the pepperoni pizza came with no pepperoni but with the green peppers onions and sausage on half (bizarre way to screw it up). The pizza was stone cold and soggy, cheese steak was cold and so were the apps. After reheating everything, it wasn't even that good, certainly not worth the amount of money i paid for it. Will not be ordering from here again.

I ate lunch here. Nice, clean restaurant. Good service. No wait. No complimentary chips and salsa.  They were on the menu, but if u dine alone, it's often too much, and doesn't taste as good leftover.  Menu had fish, chicken, beef tacos. 3/order. No combo platters... I'm not sure what restaurants have against combo platters that allow customers to try a variety of items. I ordered fish tacos. Fish a bit overcooked. Taste pretty good. But TINY. And no side dishes. I was hungry afterwards. I ordered tiramisu for dessert. It was filling, I only ate half. Not sure of I will return.

Do NOT stay here! My family checked into this location and after getting settled and pulled back the bedspread there was blood ALLLL over the white sheets. I grabbed my 6 yr old off the bed so fast. I called the front desk and explained. A man showed up and never even asked or suggested we move rooms. Instead he showed up with new sheets and said he's talk to housekeeping. What?!?!

Since most places were sold out we made it though the night totally disgusted and I refuse to ever set foot into a La Quinta Inn ever again, let alone this one. Worst experience ever!!!

Doesn't even deserve a star. Likewise it's old and rundown inside. Stay away.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: I just visited this business as I've not in some time.  I was seriously expecting a fantastic experience and I was absolutely not impressed at all.  $69.99 for a super sub par experience.  After the wash I went across the street to wegmans.  As I closed my door I noticed a dirt spot as big as a shoe.  I took a rag and rubbed it off.  How could this happen after I just paid for a hand wash and was told the price is equivalent to a mini full detail? I beg to differ.   I won't be back.    Go to Medford Wash on Stokes Rd.   A definite better wash.

My boyfriend and I used this dry cleaner to get some formal clothes cleaned before a wedding. We were happy with how quickly the clothes were cleaned, but not happy with the quality of the cleaning. My boyfriend had a suit dry cleaned and it looked worse after they cleaned it than it did before. Whatever they used to clean the garment wasn't fully removed so there was gunk in every little crease and fold. Additionally, the lapel looked jacked up. Very disappointing as it was a nice suit and we didn't notice it in time to take it somewhere else to have it fixed before the wedding.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: Well I am moving out of the area and need to cancel my membership.  Not easy thing to do here.  I have to appear at the gym an they fill out a cancellation membership form or I can send in a letter.  Anything to make it more difficult to and time consuming to cancel.  Plus two months membership fees and a $25 admin fee.  So over to $80 just to leave the gym.  I hope my next gym is better at treating their members than Zone.  The cost of leaving was well worth being gone from that gym.  It's in the contract I can here. Just be reasonable with your members. All I ask.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Was excited at the opening of a hotel just off campus from Penn and even encouraged my parents to stay here when visiting me after checking out the hotel's restaurant for brunch with fellow students... My feelings have drastically changed since being asked to leave a virtually empty lobby while quietly studying there after dining. Surprised and frankly disappointed that hotel staff went against both its namesake and location straddling university campus in shoving respectful students out of its lobby. What a shame--will not be coming back.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This has been tough day for reviews. This Florida on the water eatery rates high if you want to experience yesteryear Florida - nothing very fancy but an interesting experience.

Atmosphere    75   Run down, but on the water
Service           70    For a local place not very friendly
Food               75    Rustic Floridan eats
Value              75    Pricey for what you get

If you want the old Florida experience without driving to the shore, you might like this eatery. Otherwise, there are a ton of better places to eat on Tampa Road.

This store front gem of an eatery well deserves its Tampa Top 50 rating.
Its the original Yummy House hence, pretty much a Chinatown setting.
But, oh, the food is right on.

Atmosphere           75       Very ordinary interior. Its original!
Service                    80       They did the job
Food                        95        An a+ eating experience
Value                       85        The food quality outweights everything else.

If you like Chinese food and are tired of the buffets, go out of your way for this restaurant. Its Yummy!

Eclectic it is. Located in Tampa's International Market  restaurant area it is a very ordinary, albeit nice looking,  eatery. The menu offers an array of unorthodox entrees but from our sampling it was like someone experimenting at home.

Atmosphere        85       New, trendy modern.
Service                 60       Nonexistent
Food                     75       Curry was okay. 
Value                    75       Really nothing special.

Just too many choices in the area to have to settle on this restaurant. Keep walking and try something else.

Boy, am I in the minority on this top 50 restaurant. I had a veal lasagna that was God awful. It was loaded with chopped veal and hamburger helper and was still frozen in the middle. Need I say more. Day off for the cook.

Atmosphere          80     Interesting  new Europe decor
Service                   75 ;   Just too many tables for the young lady
Food                       70     Wooo ! What I had was not good
Value                      80     Fair prices for Italian food

Hey, the reviews on this eatery are all good. I had a bad reciped dish on the cook's off day. If you are adventurous try the place. Everybody else can't be wrong.

Becker's is a place to go to if you are out of options.  I have been there about 8 times now and I keep hoping for a tasty meal.  Unfortunately that is not the case.  Each time the food has been bland and uninspired.  If you like wings avoid ordering them other than the wing special on Wednesdays.  They charge you $8 for eight wings.  In my book a dollar a wing is a complete rip off.  I have never paid so much for less than a dozen wings.  I live close by and really want this place to be good but it falls way short.  Try the Old Bethlehem Road Hotel just up the road.

Beyond the classic atmosphere, adorable niches of vintage 40s/50's retro collectibles lies a fantastic experience waiting. My server was Lydia. The meal was perfect. Simply put. My spaghetti and meatballs was more than a I bargained for. 3 huge meatballs and a mound of sauce draped pasta gave me an excited twitch in my stomach. Post dinner the hazelnut cannoli is not too be missed. It tasted like Ferraro Roche candy but better and mini. Oh and btw, the cleanest bathroom in Philadelphia. All in all I will be back. As a baker and pastry chef of 16 years I am always happy to pass on fabulous restaurant when I find it.

One of the best restaurants I've ever been to! The customer service was impeccable from start to finish. Our waitress was so well informed yet non-intrusive and very sweet and helpful throughout our meal. Everyone in the restaurant is polite, accommodating and extremely welcoming. We enjoyed the four course option and it was so fun to get each course -- all of which were so flavorful, innovative and beyond delicious. Especially the salmon sashimi and the blue fish. The wine was fantastic as well. I highly recommend this restaurant for anyone in the area!!!! GO GO GO!

This is a truly outstanding omakase experience and adds to the growing list of top end Japanese restaurants in Philadelphia. Better yet, you can now get NYC quality meals at much more reasonable prices. 

The meal starts with a few composed dishes, and moves on through sashimi, nigiri, a handroll and several surprises before ending with exceptional renditions of transitional tamago and dessert. The sake pairing is very generous and reasonably priced. 

Seared tilefish, toro handrolls, exquisitely fresh uni and wagyu short rib. These were just a few of the perfect bites we enjoyed tonight. We'll be back very soon.

Never had an issue with this location..I think they are top-notch, BUT the last time I rented, I signed a line that they have added about no dogs in the cars.

What?
I was put off and don't want to use this company now. How about anyone with a cane..that might scratch your car up. I assume any actual damage done by a dog or a human would be an insurance issue. The outright denial of having a dog in their cars bothers me enough to write this, and again, not want to give them my money. Change that policy, Enterprise, please.

Horrible food and service- do not go- only people in retaurant and took 10 minutes for waiter to come over. ordered wine another 10 minutes for him to tell me selection was not available-

Main course took 45 minutes to come- ordered special and it was almost inedible- Chicken was so overcooked a dry left it on plate- 

while waiting for check busboy came over and put bread on table 

do not go -rip off- not saying anything about obnoxious rude owner- who ripped me off on bottle of wine when they were on brandon Blvd-

Great experience here and I wasn't even working out! My dog was rolling around in the grass to cool off and the owner (I think) came out and asked to say hi. I mentioned my dog (a pot mix)was a skittish rescue and she understood. She has one of her own. Unafraid, she offered water and let us inside. She told everyone who passed that Trista was a rescue. Everyone was careful and she even let A GUY pet her!! It was so nice to be around people who weren't afraid,  who listened, who gave my little girl a chance :)
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Excellent, traditional style pizza. The meats they use are fantastic, especially their thick-cut ham. My wife and I order from here frequently and have never been disappointed. Their lunch time buffet is a great deal: 6 bucks for all-you-can pizza and access to their stellar salad bar (and this coming from a fat guy who doesn't like salad). We also LOVE their parmesan garlic monkey bread and order that every time.

The owner is a real nice guy. Always makes sure you're taken care of. I can highly recommend this place to anyone!

Don't stay here if you want an easy experience or a good night's sleep. We arrived for check-in 3 hours after the appointed time and it still took 45 minutes to get our rooms ready. About 7 pm the halls began to smell like marijuana. Someone was smoking "pot" and our room reeked of it. They were unable to accommodate us anywhere else. The whole night teenage kids roamed the halls, speaking loudly and using profane language. The only reason you should stay here is if you wanted to school your kids on the hard knocks of life. My four kids were thoroughly educated. Very disappointed that Marriott has their name on this hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Typically National is great. Unfortunately the Phila experience was less than that. We rented in the winter, during an extra cold snap (high was around 20). During our trip there was a small snow storm. I was incredibly disappointed to find the windshield washer fluid was actually just water. If you've ever driven during a snow storm and not been able to use your windshield washers, you know how challenging this can be. 
Additionally, I was surprised and disappointed to see an hour and a half rounded up to a full day charge.

Just were there with 6 people. We sat there for 20 minutes and got no help so we asked for bread. They gave us a spread that was bland & never told us what was in it. We had to ask for olive oil. Everything we asked for the waiter gave us a look like we were really put him out. They didn't have pepper on the table or offer us pepper or Parmesan. It was bland except appetizers were good. It took hours to get served and then they added 20% for tip. I guess he knew he would get 20% no matter what. We were upstairs and most tables were downstairs.

I have eaten here twice and the first time the food was delicious.  The portions were generous and the food was savory.  The sushi lacked flavor but was well made and easy to eat.  After enjoying my first visit, I decided to get sushi to go..............................big mistake.  The take out sushi must have been made by the less experienced chefs as it completely fell apart.  It was no better than sushi that sits in the grocery store all day, definitely made me question its freshness.  While I may dine in in this restaurant, I am never ordering out ever again from here.

We have generally enjoyed the service/food at Fratelli's over a long period of time.
The other night, not so much.

The waitress knew us and was, as usual, very pleasant, 
The kitchen sent us another table's food, which was immediately corrected.
The waitress offered us dessert as compensation.
It was a hot night and we were eating outside.
We didn't touch either of our salads.
We asked to take home the salads and half our meals, declined (free) desserts.

At home, we discovered about three lettuce leaves in the box that should have contained two salads--obviously not OUR salads.

The next day, I emailed the restaurant.
No response.

There are no fountain drinks here, at least the last times we visited, and they charge a lot for the bottled beverages. 
I don't eat any gf foods anymore, but my husband does, and he said he won't buy their donuts  at this location anymore because the ones he has tried from this DD tasted old, not fresh. Maybe they are fresh early in the day, but when we have gone it has been later on in the evening. On the other hand the staff is nice, and the coffee is top notch.
It is a cute little restaurant that is nice to sit down and visit with a friend over a cup of coffee.

If you work and want to be told an 1 1/2 and then wait 3 then come on in. They say Tire Discounters but only have 1 tech installing tires... 7 bays and 1 tech. Professional staff. 
Just drive one more exit and go to Discount Tires. Always friendly and professional. They give you a time and it's done. I have had multiple cars done there but was close to this store so I ran in. 
Oh yeah and only 2 tires (not 2 options... actually 2 tires) that fit the vehicle in stock. Please do yourself a favor... go somewhere else.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
So it's 83 degrees fahrenheit (28 degrees celsius) on a lonely Sunday afternoon. I drove by and impulsively decided to go in for the Lavender Honey - a flavor that I had tried and loved a few months ago. Unfortunately, they didn't have it. However, the server suggested that I try Honey Wildflower. AND am I glad he did. It was sweeter than I wanted but it was quite delicious. Less subtle than the Lavender honey but it was some good ice cream for a hot day. Loved it. Will probably go back in an hour for another scoop.

Yum.

And who can't love their motto? Eat Ice Cream. Be Happy. Sounds like a recipe for a good life to me.

Not sure where the low rating originated. We've had nothing but super gracious service and good food, for fast food.  Occasionally our drive-Thru drink orders get mixed up when we order several so some re-training there might help accuracy. But food is fresh and good appearance. Service is friendly and fast. Store is clean inside and out, including rest rooms. Mornings are our usual visit time and drive-Thru line is fast despite high volume. We feel this is the best McD in the area, especially around The Pyramids area
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: When you first walk into the hotel, its impressive. Its very modern and looks clean. That kinda changes when you get to your floor. Once the elevator doors opened I knew that the downstairs was a facade. There were stains on the floor everywhere, including a large red one in my room. The room itself was fine but my floor was a nightmare. I was alone and actually scared thanks to a rowdy group of people that kept slamming doors and yelling at each other. Then at 12:15am someone actually started pounding on MY door. I was terrified and not well reseted to catch my 6 am flight.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I'd give 3.5 stars if I could.  They accommodated us as a table of 10 on short notice around 8 last Saturday night which I really appreciated!  We'd waited for a table at the Palms across the street & finally gave up.  (Turned out we could talk better since the Palms had live music start up not long after). 

The servers were attentive & worked to brings drinks/bread quickly as we had little ones getting hungry.  The calzones were a hit, I had a burger I enjoyed.  Others had pasta dishes and were pleased.  Did not try the BBQ.  A locals, laid back spot & I'd go again.

Went there last night and did not have reservations, apparrently it has become so popular now you need them on weekends. The owner was nice enough to seat us even though it may have caused a proble. The food was excellent eggplant was great as was the spaghetti and meatballs. Everything made from scratch so if they run out of something it is not available.


great to have a private owned italian restaurant in Brandon, and we ate a little faster than usual so as not to disrupt his reservation schedule, great place

Don't be fooled by the little hole-in-the-wall appearance! Go in and give it a try! It's so quaint, they also have a full bar area in addition to the restaurant area, and the food is unbelievable! I got the sausage Genevese. I don't even know what to say... it was so delicious! And the meatball appetizer was the hit of our table. They are perfect and an absolute MUST! On the way out I noticed they sell their marinara sauce, and some other items, so of course I had to buy a quart of their sauce.  I would definitely go back again and again. Bring cash - it's cash only.

A little better from a service perspective than previous visits.  Our server was capable and fairly attentive.   His one service failure came from him telling us he would get the TV changed to a sporting event we requested.  We asked three times to no avail.  He never even offered an excuse.

The biggest problem came from a private event that we're hosting on half of the patio.  They had DJ blaring music that made it almost impossible to hear each other.  The servers had to yell to be heard.  Either shut the whole place down for a private event or turn the music down.

Had a group of 16 people for a party for lunch today and what a great experience! I emailed with the event manager for the past month and chose a menu of two apps, three entrees and desert. We were a little confused when our waitress took our drink order but never gave us menus, but soon the food started rolling out. Everything was served family style so you were able to sample a little bit of everything. I cannot tell you how good all of the food was! And the best part was they boxed up all of the leftover food so we could take it home. If you are looking for a great spot to have a group I highly it, everyone will be raving about the food!

You have to remember that this is a location that you get what you pay for. You only spend $2.25 per article for dry cleaning, and $1.49 for laundering shirts. I have read complaints on the location, but you should use this location when your clothing has already had a "good life" but you still want to wear it. I take my khakis, old sweaters, and old shirts I still want to wear for work/play, but realize it is not my best things.

Keep that in mind. It fills a niche on price I am very happy it fills.

I would give it 5 stars for price, but quality and service is just not there, and should be no stars.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: First time there and last time.  We went in during the Italian Market Festival.  First of all they get you with being cash only.  Who does cash only when their entrees are like $20?  They are like we have an atm.  Give me a break place is too cheap to accept credit it's the cost of being in business.  So the food is pricey as the portions were pretty small.  The food was alright...nothing to write home about.  My friend then came in to joing us and she wanted to order something and the waitress actually refused to serve her.  The waitress overall were pretty nasty and not nice.  I don't recommend this place at all.

High value lodging, for location and quality. Rooms nice, but overcrowded with furnishings. Drapes and blinds don't really close against the street noise on Friday night. Breakfast buffet large, but loaded with salt. Deal-breaker: the League's forceful notions of "patriotism" and "American presidents" appear to be strictly limited to the male icons of one political party -- and not the party that looks out for the staff that work at the Inn.Portraits of recent GOP politicians would made any real American patriot (as opposed to nationalist) gag. Someone should remind them that "Abraham Lincoln crushed the conservatives of his day."
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Ordered a quesadilla that was supposed to come with chicken on it and since I'd read reviews before ordering that had said it comes with hardly any cheese I paid for extra cheese. Quesadilla came with hardly any chicken at all, hardly any cheese at all, and the cheese was not even the least bit melted. Also asked over the phone while ordering (just to clarify) if the quesadilla came with guac, sour cream, and salsa and the man said yes but none of them came in the box when it got to me. Way overpriced for what you get. Will not be ordering here again.

They card everyone.  And I mean EVERYONE.  If Barbara Bush came and sat down to tell Sarah Palin to stay in Alaska (this review will become obsolete in about a month, I'm just planning ahead), they would card her before they served her a drink.  Seriously.  Maybe it's a Tennessee thing, or maybe it's a guitar-shaped bar thing.  

The service.  Meh.  The food.  Meh.  The drinks.  Meh.  

You know what?  I have experienced better.  What knocks this place up a star is that the food did come out quickly with a full restaurant, prices weren't bad, and I got to read about the history of Gibson guitars.  That's worth it.

I love the drive through at this Starbucks. I realize that sentence makes me sound like the laziest person alive, but I'm typically on my way to a friend's house whenever I swing by this location and the drive through is just too convenient to pass up. Everyone who works there is super friendly from my experiences and the line moves quickly. They even plug your drinks with those little green plastic things so there's no spillage. I just wish there was a more convenient way to get out of the parking lot, instead of having to drive back through the strip mall lot.

Of all the Philly Fine Wine & Good Spirits stores, this one is definitely up there among the nicest and most organized. Occasionally I have had some luck with getting decent recommendations from staff members, but more often than not I have to do some iphone research from the aisles. 

The woman who was sampling wines from CA on my recent visit was knowledgeable not just about the wines she was pouring but also other wines in the store. The cashiers are fast and friendly. 

It's still not as good as the stores in New Jersey but it's an improvement over other FW&GS locations.

So a pitcher of margaritas will set you back fifty bucks. However, said pitcher of margies lasts for quite some time and has enough kick to get three girls pretty tipsy. Highly recommended. 

Our crew also shared an order of guac, which I thought was overpriced and under-portioned at nine bucks. My tortilla soup came in just under seven dollars and was delicioso. 

While I thought the prices were on the spendy side, the quality of everything I tried is enough to get me back for dinner sometime. And you know I'm going to be hitting up those happy hour margs in the very near future.

Its far from my first choice to shop for groceries. But Rittenhouse Market can be a good mish mash of conventional, organic, and local items; albeit oftentimes on a more expensive pricetag than most other grocers as others have alluded to. But I suppose that's the price to pay in supporting the little guys these days, and the amicable customer service and reliability of being able to locate some harder to find items can make it worthwhile.

The produce section is always fresh and well maintained. and the butcher and prepared foods sections are spot on for a tinier store.

I've been there two times and was not impressed either time.

My last negative experience there (dinner) was so bad that I gave an absurdly low tip (which I don't do often). Service was slothlike - I was there for lunch months ago and noticed the same thing - and we waited almost a half hour for a seat after being told we didn't have to sit long. While waiting, one of the staff remarked (in Chinese) to their coworker that they were surprised we were sitting so long. Comments aside, the sushi was okay but not worth the wait. Avoid.

This Starbucks is conveniently located right before you hop onto the Pennsylvania Turnpike in Plymouth Meeting. Parking's easy. Their staff were friendly and fast, making it easy for us to pick up a caffeinated beverage before heading on a long long long drive. Like many regular Starbucks, there's seating and a restroom for customers.

If you HATE Starbucks, why are you reading this?
If you LIKE Starbucks, this one is just like the others except folks don't seem to hang out here - it's mostly drivers who need a fix for their commute.

Perhaps it was the dishes we ordered, maybe it was the darkness of the restaurant, but my dinner date and I were supremely underwhelmed and unimpressed with Bliss. From the appetizer, to our entrees, to the dessert, Bliss was not bliss (sorry, I couldn't resist) - all bark and no bite. The high prices didn't help me warm up to the average fare.

Positives: Our server (Evan) was good and our bartender (forgot her name) was also friendly. Of course, the interior is nicer than my photos portray, I only had a point-and-shoot on me that night...

For what it is, where it is, this is a good Travelodge.

It's spitting distance from Chinatown and the Reading Terminal Market, and across from the Convention Center - when I was there, there was construction across the street, but that's hopefully not going to be there forever. This motel's next to a homeless shelter, but it's not like you're spending quality time here, right?

Free Wi-Fi and a complimentary breakfast will win the hearts and minds of any budget traveler. Bed was average. Our bath fluorescent was super dim (read: like a horror movie), but it was clean, and shower pressure was decent.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Location, location, location. The best part about this hotel. Near touristy Art Museum destinations, this Embassy also has ready taxi access.

I've been here enough times to appreciate their lobby, but their elevators drive me batty. They take forever: there's only two - as far as I can tell - and they're prone to high-traffic. On my way up, the lift stopped five times for staff and guests.

At least their suites themselves are decent. They're more than a bit aged, but the beds are quite serviceable. Not that I ever get much sleeping done here. Or partying. (You have to sign verbiage to that effect when you check in.)
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I went here for lunch with a small group (7 people). We opted for this place over another in the area because it has more seating. The lunch specials were reasonably priced. A bowl of udon and three pieces of sushi?? How did you know my usual order ??? (although I usually go for a whole roll as I don't usually have a "value meal"-like option)

I've had better udon elsewhere, but it was still very good. The sushi was fresh, but not the best I've had. The service was good and they didn't mind making substitutions. The dishes were very pretty. And a little bowl of miso on the house to start the meal? What a pleasant unexpected surprise.

I had a terrible experience staying here, from the time I checked in (in a lobby that was semi-under construction) to the time I checked out. 

The only thing that saved my experience here was them giving me a whole bunch of extra Starwood points (after a lot of phone calls and emails). 

The poorly appointed rooms are far from spotless and the building is just old...with the comfortable bed being the saving grace.

I'll never stay at this location again and caution you to heed the warnings in the negative reviews. They all are mostly accurate. Look somewhere else when coming to Philly.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Cooler than ice cold!

I was extremely impressed with this venue from the moment I walked in. The decor is pretty much flawless, all the way down to the intentionally black and white TVs over the bar.  Just when I thought it couldn't get any better, I was taken up to the patio on the roof!  I got a little bit nostalgic, as it reminded me of the good old days when we would go to Deux Gros Nez (formerly down the street) as teenagers and climb up on the roof.  

Love the vibe here!  It is definitely my new favorite Reno bar, one of the first places I will be sure to bring my friends to when we visit Reno.

The service is exquisite and the wine list AMAZING.  The price is steep, but what can you expect from a restaurant that wins the coveted five-diamond AAA award?  It is also a restaurant that consistently snags the DiRoNa Award.  

After my dinner there, I understood why.  The proprietor came to my table and spent 15 minutes chatting with me in depth about the red wine that I had picked out to accompany my meal.  He even offered to show me around the town, as it was my first time in St. Louis.  (Tony, you are the best!)  This is real, warm Italian hospitality at it's best.  The bill made me flinch, but it was a dining experience of a lifetime.

Hmmm, I regretted coming here. This is a great place if you're on a budget and want to pay $10 for three rolls. Not a great place for authentic sushi. I got the platter and none of the rolls or sushi really impressed me. The service was almost non-existent and I never got a refill on my water. I felt sad because I could have chosen another sushi place, but since it was raining, I got kind of lost in this unfamiliar city. Ended up at Vic Sushi bc it had decent rating on Yelp. Well, yah...I should have guessed people rated it so highly bc of the price of the food, not bc of the quality of the food.

I wish I could say I loved this place, because I like places where I can consume a pitcher of margarita and not be very far from home, but I can't.

We kind of liked this place when it first opened, but it seems to get worse and worse every time. Chips are always stale, beans never taste fresh, fajita veggies seem like they come from a can, food is never more than lukewarm, and server is usually nowhere to be found after food is brought to the table.

On a positive note, the carnitas aren't bad, but that is all I can really think of.  There are too many better options that are worth the extra time driving to get there.

Even though i'm still dreaming of a Chinese restaurant that delivers to my house (which is apparently in the middle of nowhere), if I'm in the mood for take out this is the place I'll go. It's not super awesome (I'd give it 3.5 stars if I could) but it's better than China Panda. The food is always ready within the amount of time said(usually 10-15 minutes) and has WAY more flavor than the food at China Panda.

My favorites here have to be the wonton egg-drop soup, lo-mein and cashew chicken.

If you're in the Bellevue area and haven't given this place a try or haven't in a while give it a shot next time you're in the mood for Chinese.

Really nice place to stay! Their parking garage was full and we had to park really far away. This was bad for us because we read online they are pet friendly and they are NOT actually pet friendly unless it's a service animal. Our poor kitty had to sleep alone and it was hard to access her to check on her even few hours.

Other than the pet and parking issue it was a lovely stay. Our baby woke up early so we had breakfast delivered to the room hot and ready with just a phone call. There was room for the pack and play in the room. 

Not a bad stop off, it was very close to everything so you can walk around downtown.

I would stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
What can I say? Like the song says:
We got winners, we got losers
Chain smokers and boozers
And we got yuppies, we got bikers
We got thristy hitchhikers
And the girls next door dress up like movie stars

Hmm, hmm, hmm I love this bar

Sits on the peaceful Alafia river for those who want to sit outside and enjoy the weather. You can get food at the snack shack from Chef Paycheck. And on every Wednesday afternoon starting around 4, chicken wings for everyone. Unfortunately this brings out the broke folk and seniors but, alas, nothing is perfect.

I'm so sorry if this is your local watering hole. 

Unless you're drinking the nightly/weekly/monthly special, brews are not cheap. And not an impressive selection.

They had 312 on tap, but it was $7.75 A PINT. Crazy! 
 
This place is your most basic, your most bland. The epitome of a suburban strip-mall bar.

The bartender was nice. And the crowd was interesting. I'll give you that.
But the music was HORRENDOUS. The food order (appetizer sampler platter) took half an hour, kid you not. And it was late and not busy.

But don't mind me. I'm just an out-of-towner, passing through.

I rent from Hertz all over the country all of the time and the one thing that I can expect from the location at the Philadelphia airport is that their buses come very in frequently. In fact so infrequently that you will save yourself 30 minutes or more by simply walking through the parking structure and playing Frogger to get across the street into the Hertz parking lot. I would suggest this tip for both arriving and departing if time is of the essence, or if standing out in the rain or cold is not something that sounds like fun.

Being Avis Preferred is one of my favorite things about renting a car. I highly suggest that you get in on that! Special lane for picking up your vehicle. One signature and you're on you way. It literally took me less that 3 minutes at the counter. 

Normally there is a Preffered section near the front in whatever rental car facility, but this one in Boise still had me hiking down rows to find my car in its space. Ones found however, no gates bar you from getting on your way. 

The cars to choose from are always in good repair and ready to go. This location was no exception. 

Easy return, no stress.

I feel like I got very little from the Renaissance Hotel for how much I paid. I was disappointed that they charge for Wifi and the room was expensive. 

Another reviewer mentioned a AAA discount. We asked and they said they didn't offer that. We also did not get any chocolates on the bed or anything like that. 

We were staying in Philadelphia on our road trip for 2 nights and could have stayed here for that second night. We switched to the Aloft hotel up the road, even closer to the city and got a better deal and way more perks.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
A bit of history....the name comes from the 21st Amendment to the US Constituion which repealed the 18th amendment declaring prohibition. Legend has it this place was owned by the mobsters, Carlos Marcello and his partner Diamond Jim Moran. Definitely look at the old pictures on the walls!

These guys serve excellent drinks from house made ingredients and real herbs. The live music was a nice surprise and they do actually close at 4AM. We had a large group and ran them out of some of their finest high end whiskies. They came up with alternatives and the group thinned as the night wore on.

Great fun and a wonderful time!

I ordered a $13 driver, and they got me a $40 taxi. Not ok, never ok. Train your people. Why would anyone want to spend that much for a shitty cab, when they can get a nicer car or share a ride for $13. Its not like its a nice cab. 

Anyway, rooms were so-so. Staff was bland, dry, and not helpful. My key stopped working and I was blamed and it took them forever to help me. 

Also, check in took forever. Shouldn't they have enough people working so there aren't 5 people waiting in line?

If I had my choice, I wouldn't stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: First time in Camden. I had to travel down to Camden for work. My client highly suggested this place when I told her I wanted to try a local cuisine. Panzarotti is similar to a calzone. For one price, you can get as many toppings inside your panzarotti. There are about 15 to 20 toppings to pick from. I thought the panzarotti was good but it didn't hit the spot like I thought it would. I was turned off by the amount of grease that was dripping from the panzarotti. It's just one of those food you have to try at least once.

I just left here after being embarrassingly pulled from a machine because of a billing issue. The clerk has me follow them to the front desk because of a balance. I was charged 2x this month and PF needs to get their billing/accounting shit figured out. You charge $23 a month and you think it's ok to just approach people and do that? 

Have you accounting department call me. I don't need to speak to the manager of this gym. Hearing my feedback about how embarrassed I was isn't going to do anything, so don't bother.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Easily the best dining experience I've had in (or outside of) Philadelphia.  I went on a Tuesday night (tip: they have seasonal 4 course tasting menus every Tuesday) for my birthday and hit the jackpot with the foie gras tasting menu.

Started off with a delicious amuse soup from the chef.  Moved to a ridiculously velvety yellowtail and shaved foie appetizer, and had pan-seared foie as my entree.  Pan-seared foie was cooked perfectly.  Service was watchful but not oppressive.  Well worth the 15 minute drive from Philadelphia!

This was a pretty cool dive bar. It kind of has a punk rock vibe (think a red and black motif with a bunch of weird decorations), but nothing pretentious. Bartenders were nice, and the crowds were chill and friendly. Like most of the bars around, this bar was a pretty large space, and they have a huge patio for those who want to chill outside. 

However, omg... the bathrooms (or at least the women's bathroom) is the smallest bathroom ever, ahaha. I think the bathroom, which rooms two stalls and a sink, holds room for what should be a good one size bathroom. I thought it was inconvenient, but a little cool for the creativity of space haha.

If you hate smelling like an ash tray at the end of the night, avoid going here. Avoid going to any bar on Division if you don't like or care to be around smoke. Otherwise, pretty good bar--always has a decent crowd. It's a typical bar, though. But I don't smoke, so after a night hanging out at Red Door, I woke up the next morning and everything in my room smelled like cigarettes. 

Find the hole in the floor. And when you do, just go stand by it and you'll get a good laugh at all the drunk girls that will get on all fours just to look through it. Hah!

Was with some friends and they asked the bartender for a beer for a non-beer drinker (me). Jared gave me a couple to try and I ended up with one called Sweetwater Blue. It was really really good. I wasn't sure what I was tasting in it, exactly--I knew there was a fruit taste--but my friend realized it was grapefruit. It was great.

Best bathroom on bourbon street. Super clean, but don't think you'll stop and use it without being a paying customer or you'll pay $5 for the privilege. I didn't see any soap, so take hand sanitizer.

Expensive. They charge a $200 (refundable) deposit, which I have never been charged at Hertz or Enterprise. They gave me a hard time about the insurance as well. I only used this place because it was recommended by the conference arrangements committee for the conference I attended, and there was a discount that made it slightly less expensive. I won't bother with Advantage again. Instead I'll stick with the more reputable companies I've used in the past (Hertz, Enterprise), since they seem to be more up front with their customers.

Whatever Fat salmon is...it is defiantly NOT Japanese! 

Take away the swanky lighting, the modern decor, and you are left with sushi that is reminiscent of any food court sushi at your local shopping mall.  

Start with the sushi bar that is so high, you can not see your chef, and he can not see you.  Any proud Japanese sushi chef will want to interact with you and see your expression when you bite into his masterpiece.   

It is so hard to find authentic sushi when traveling, and yelp is certainly no help. 

If you like a roll factory then Fat Salmon is for you.

Whenever I have family visiting from out of town, I always recommend they stay at this Comfort Inn location.  For those that are sticklers for good customer service, you will not be disappointed.

When my parents stay here, they always bring me back warm cookies, fruit, and other complimentary goodies that are given to them.  
Also, since this is a newer hotel location the rooms are not yet old and busted.  

Definitely not a place to stay if you do not have a car.  Yes, there are many conveniences located just across the street, but no one crosses this area of Gandy on foot (that is a death wish).
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Disappointing. Entered the restaurant where someone was chain smoking and it filled up the entire outdoor area plus inside the restaurant. I tucked myself into a corner to avoid the smell which somewhat helped. Restaurant's menu is your average sushi bar restaurant options. Server didn't hear my order correctly (darn masks) so the wrong order came out. No biggie. My correct order was brought out promptly but sadly the rice had no vinegar so the flavor was bland. The food is plentiful however the fish is not very fresh. The salmon roe was rubbery. Boo.

$6 super tasty veggie burgers, solid $3 fries and a rockin' beer list? I'm so thrilled my friend moved to South Philly and not too far from this spot.

The service is solid, the folks that work there are attentive and nice. The customers? Generally more dude-based but that's not big deal.

They decorated for the holidays but in general the place is nice and dimly lit, the bench tables in the back were perfect for my friend's birthday get-together, and I can't wait to visit again in a week.

Hey Fountain Porter, keep on keeping on.

We arrived at around 8:30pm on Saturday night.  We were promptly seated by the hostess outside. 5 Min to have our drink order taken and 10min to receive.  The server seems to be very distracted and non-attentive as he was inside most the time rushing about, yet we didnt see many people inside.  Our beverage glass ran empty many times and food was slow to arrive.  

The food quality was great though.  

Poor management is going to run this place into the ground. I do not blame the server, he seemed to be over worked.  You can get the same food with better service at Cheesecake Factory with consistent service.

Stopped by for a bite at lunch, it was packed inside and they proudly display their yelp certificate at the front. I was excited to think I randomly picked a hidden gym but found it mediocre at best. I was with a group of three and the food delivery was spaced out so nobody ate at the same time. The tempura tasted soggy and we were not fans of the dressing on the salad. The window coverings seemed like an attempt to make you forget you were in a strip mall eating lunch but in turn made it dark and claustrophobic feeling, add on poor ventilation and we were ready to be on our way. It wasn't horrible but we will likely not return.

This location only provides drive thru service. The Starbucks app states drive thru and in store service for this location. You can imagine my frustration when I walked about 1.2 miles from my hotel, looking forward to a warm venti coffee and a chance to earn some stars, and the in store was closed. 

Granted, I was planning on getting in a nice walk today, but it would have been great to know ahead of time that this Starbucks was limited in service. So I guess the one star is for the local person who decided to close the Cafe and not coordinate that with corporate.

I ordered the Chile Verde burrito today. I said no rice. My burrito was a huge disappointment. It was 90% bland whole pinto beans, 5 % chile verde, 5 % cilantro & pico do gallo. I didnt care for the chips and salsa either. I opened the burrito and ate the 7 small pieces of meat and threw my burrito in the trash.

My friend ordered the breakfast burrito without rice or beans. Her burrito was ok.

Esau's, a different restaurant, was my initial choice. Esau's is closed on Wednesdays. 

The gentleman that took our order was nice.

That's all I can say.

Food: Good (I rather like the specials with the baked cheese)
Service: Quite good
Drink: Full bar
Ambiance: Nice
Value: Good, if you have some coupon
Summary: If you are in Eagle and craving Italian, its a pretty good choice.

From our last visit:
I like the family style salad
The bread with olive oil is always appreciated
I enjoyed my baked pasta covered with cheese.  i am sure that any sane person would think it had too much cheese.  Perfect for me.
My wife's chicken was well cooked.
My son liked his spaghetti and meatballs.
The creme brulle was large and delicious.  Glad that we were willing to stuff ourselves to try dessert one time.

At first glance, this place looks great!  ...and then you step into the elevators and the mask falls off. Don't get me wrong, I'm a sucker for vintage, but this isn't vintage,  it's just "dated." Nasty carpet, rusty, moldy, worn out, minimal and basic (at best) bathrooms. Not as painfully over priced as some, but too bad the developer didn't put his (a female developer knows where to spend) money into the parts that count the most. Such a shame. This property has so much potential with the right developer at the helm.

I love this place.  Great ice cream, shakes and hotdogs!  Just be prepared for some extra sassy service.  Middle aged blonde female has more bad days than good.  Saw her get frustrated at some point with everyone ordering.  Even the 8 year old boy in front of me when he politely asked for a lid on his ice cream.  "Be sure you ask for a lid when you order your ice cream next time [over exuberant eye roll]"  I'm sorry if a smile and CUSTOMER service is too much to ask for.  Ice cream really does make me want to scream when ordering from this lady.

Our friends were craving a nice Italian meal and Moto really delivered.  I'll definitely add it to my rotation for Nashville visits.  

The service was very good and they were able to accommodate removing meat from things for my vegetarian husband. Everything we tried was delicious, especially the side of brussels sprouts which was large enough to share, and the one of us who got wine was very impressed.  If you see the vanilla passion fruit dessert on the specials menu, definitely get it. In addition to tasting amazing, it has edible gold on it. FANCY!

Spent the night here on a weekend trip from Phoenix to Chiricahua. Nothing too fancy about this place (outside of the lobby area which is pretty nice) but it suits its purpose in providing a place to sleep for the night. Breakfast is $5 if you stay at the hotel. The hallways are something reminiscent of hotels frequented in my childhood (something about the smell brings me back), but the rooms are definitely more updated/renovated. As it serves its purpose and isn't too pricy, I could see myself booking a stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: On our way back from the museum and shopping, we were a bit hungry, so we thought we'd stop at Squeeze In for a nosh, but there was a crowd waiting. We decided to stop into Sushi 7 and have a couple rolls. The place was not busy, but it still took a while for our first rolls to come. The first roll was okay, but the others were not so good. The tempura batter was not crisp, the fish on the rolls was cut so thin, you wouldn't know it was there. If you like rice, fried in batter and covered with mayonnaise, you might like this place. If you like sushi, go someplace else. The AYCE at the Atlantis is $3 more, but so very much better!

Okay, so let's be realistic about what this business is and isn't. It isn't a place where you get the best pizza you've ever eaten, and you sit in a restaurant with glorious ambiance and revel in what an awesome food scene Reno is. 

What it is, however, is a great place to pick up a $5 (or $8 if you splurge for the deep dish, which I highly recommend) pizza if you just can't stomach the idea of cooking dinner or if you've had a few brewskis and late-night pizza is all you can think about. 

Grab it to go, take it home, and watch the newest episode of The Good Wife while you eat more pizza than a person should in one session. 

That is all.

Very very old and outdated, but clean.  Well clean enough I guess... I found lots of dust around the mirrors and desk.  It was kind of noticeable so I'm sure Housekeeping saw that.  

Not too far from downtown Philly.. about  20 mins on a Saturday night.  I only stayed here because I had a free nights stay with the Marriott for my Rewards Points but I would not stay here on my own free merit.

This place had the quickest and friendliest check in ever by the way. I simply walked up to the counter, gave them my last name and he handed over the keys and gave me my room number with a smile :)  It was appreciated!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Not a bad spot, but it's in a fairly busy part of town. They do have a shuttle that goes within a 2 mile radius of the hotel. 

Surprisingly the restaurant at the hotel is pretty good!  The BBQ chicken pizza was very good. Aida at the bar make a heck of a chocolate martini!

The rooms were just ok. They don't have any suites which kind of sucks when you have status and are used to upgrades.  The room wasn't super clean when we arrived, but we needed adjoining rooms, so I didn't ask for a switch. 

I would probably stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Good view overseeing the stadium. Spacious room. Love all the layout with clean new bedding and huge bathroom. Service is good that they were fast to deliver the slippers we needed. We ordered room service, it was fast too and they can accommodate your need like.. i only want half dozen of the wings and they did so. Might be bc they only have the boneless ones while I originally wanted the bones.
 Food itself is just so so. We were there on a Thanksgiving night, hence we won't bother to look for a restaurant opens that night. You need to pay extra for parking though. And there's no laundry onsite and they sent us to Hilton next door instead.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: The Jet Rock in terminal B is probably one of my most favorite airport bars. I would even go to the Jet Rock if it was not in an airport. The all glass location allows you to watch the weather, planes arriving and departing, your gate, and all kinds of action at the bar. The bartenders and waitresses have always been efficient, fun, and make great drinks even if the place is jammed packed with travelers. There are tons of beers on tap (I think 48) and they know how to make a spicy Bloody Mary. Jet Rock, you rock!!!

I was in town visiting family and needed to find a gym nearby. I found this gym via Yelp and decided to stop by around 9:45 am to get a day pass. I definitely recommend calling ahead since the staff doesn't arrive until 10am. The price for one time day use is $10, which is normal for gyms. The facility is clean, but very small compared to the gyms I am accustomed to back home in Los Angeles. If I were to do my leg workout the equipment wouldn't be sufficient enough for me and space is very small. I would only recommend this location if you are doing cardio or light weights.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers
