text: Saw them on Food network and thought it would be a great place to go. First, the people were very friendly and helpful, but I can't base a review only on the service. I was excited when I saw them cooking homemade tortillas. I had the special of the day, two chicken tacos, cheese enchilada, and beans. The chicken tacos were flavorless and bland. The enchilada was mediocre, but the enchilada sauce was tasty. The guacamole appetizer was OK, felt like it was missing a little kick. Overall I just wasn't impressed. Maybe I just hit them on the wrong day.

Idk. Any joy I get from visiting this Starbucks diminishes at the annoying light that takes forever wish I could chose a different way out, but not so.  The store is nice and quick, an friendly, everything I enjoy about the brand, its just I don't want to visit because of the hassle to get out of there.

What this intersection needs is a pretty round about. That way everyone keeps moving and doesn't have to wait forever at that damn light.

Maybe I'll go again and try to get out another way. Ughhh. Im getting old !!!

It's clean.
Breakfast is free, but I've never had it.

Not sure about amenities here as I came for work. We held meetings here and the staff is just super. Everything needed for the meetings was as it should be, there were never any issues.

Staff was available and responded to every need quickly and courteously. 

I do use apple products and had no issues with wifi while staying as an overnight guest.

Because of the loyalty program, I was able to request 2pm late check out. 

I CANNOT TELL YOU HOW HAPPY THIS MAKES ME!!!!!!!

LOVE LATE CHECK OUT!!!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I have never stayed as a hotel guest here. Rather, my company held seminars here and used the meeting room space. 

Since I was leading the seminars, of course I am concerned that everything runs smoothly as possible.

I have to say, the staff was really quick and responsive to making sure everything was organized and set up as needed.  The meeting room was spacious, and the temperature and lighting was perfect.

I cannot tell you how many venues have rooms that are difficult to manage temperature wise, and how this can easily distract a meeting, but no problem with that here. . .

and yes, the pool area is really nice.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The area is grim, but it's walking distance to Broadway. The hotel itself is fine but really needs a coat of paint and a bit of a sprucing up because from the outside and afar it really looks very grim and depressing. 
It's not an incredible hotel but the rooms are not bad. There's a sad breakfast you can get as well. 
The prices are high for what it is, I was surprised how much it cost, but being downtown Nashville there aren't many options. 
It's okay and if there's nothing else in the area, it's fine but it's not the best of the line, obviously.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
So a friend of mine stopped in for lunch and I couldn't make it so he brought me a to go order, what a great friend!

The B.L.T. was supposed to have six slices of bacon but mine only had three, the tomato was not very good but of course it's not the season so I can't ding them too bad. The bad part was the bread was just a bit stiff. My sister has eaten there and liked the food, I just didn't feel as though they made much of a effort, I mean it's a B.L.T. how can you mess that up?

Horrible? No, but I've had better.

Can I be okay with this branch of this money sucking entity?  Yes.  I truly have to keep in mind what environment this location is in.  I am used to quite sterile bank personnel, but being that this is New Orleans, people in there are smiling and taking it easy!

Good customer service aside, the people inside makes sure they get the people in the lobby moving through quite quickly so they can get to their personal task at hand.

You rarely see 2 atms side by side so close, but that is the type of place you are at when you come here.  This place is friendly and convenient...even though they work for an evil, evil sort!

It's good-cheap chinese food... As long as you have your expectations in check before going in, you should be satisfied.

I go here about once a month for lunch and usually get either shrimp, chicken or veggie lo mein or sometimes general tso's chicken. I like all of those... they are consistent and good for the price. You get a lot of it too.

I also like the hot & sour soup.

Service is generally good and friendly... sometimes at lunch they can be a little slow due to all the take-out orders.

The interior is as plain as it gets, but it works and I have no problem sitting in there and having lunch.

Took my Jeep Compass in just now to the automated car wash and it ripped my spoiler off. The system guides you to give you and indication as to when you are in place for the wash to start. I moved into position until the system gave me the ok. Once the machine started washing it seemed to be ok and then I heard a loud noise and wondered "what the heck was that?". To my astonishment when I exited my vehicle (after pulling to the side of course) the spoiler was hanging on the side of my car and had been ripped out.

Tooooooooooooooooo fun!  The only thing I really did not like...was the bar catered to the "I just turned 21" or the "It is a Bach/Bachette Party" as far as choices in alcohol.  And the dirty old men in there really DO NOT care that you are with someone hahaha.  But the bar itself is so awesome.  The dark alley walk way into the courtyard and the TV Monitors so they can see people approaching...the hidden bars in different rooms...and we sat in the Cage...Yeah we did!  I wish they would have been playing better music.  The Gwar era is over.  Now some Type O Neg, Primus, Tool, I appreciate and then you can sign me up.

So do not go here and expect a life-changing meal. Go here because you are starving and need a quick lunch. Or maybe you just want to sit and chill with some friends....or your kids.

I have come here twice and ordered the lunch buffet...unlimited pizza, salad, and drink for like $7. The salad bar is pretty decent. Usually I HATE when they serve iceberg lettuce...but they made up for it with all the "toppings" AND the awesome bread sticks. If those come out of a box, I might have to raid their freezer some day. No problems with the pizza, it's on par with my mediocre expectations.

This may be my favorite spot and it's all because of Ryan the bartender. He was in rare form when the group of ladies I was with stopped in. It was a non-stop barrage of awesome. He has to be one of the funniest bartenders I have ever encountered (keep in mind I drink a lot) and he totally made our night. 

There was also a fantastically friendly gentleman that played the spoons and provided a very cool looking knife to cut the material off of my friend's shirt. Between these two amazing, funny, and very good looking guys we were kept laughing, dancing, and flirting. 

This place made not only made my night, but it made my entire vacation.

This hotel served its purpose...clean, nice accomodations near the quarter. We stayed there during St. Pat's weekend, so the price was seasonal..i.e. expensive! However, it was clean, nice exposed brick walls, and it is right by the quarter. Parking was $25 which is average price, but I was told it does fill up, so if you get a spot stay parked. We did not get up early enough for breakfast. We did have to wait an hour for our car to be brought around from valet, but that is because we waited to check out at noon, so leave plenty of time to get your car.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
A friend of mine recommended this place to me and I'm so glad! I was looking for a place within the neighborhood that could do some wheel repairs rather quickly since I was leaving town for the weekend. I called on a Wednesday and got an appointment for the very next day. Dropped off the car in the AM and everything was done by the time I was leaving work. Not to mention, the pricing is very reasonable. 

As soon as I hit the highway that weekend, my car felt like a brand new car! No more vibrations and rattling at highway speeds. Gave me great peace of mind throughout my whole trip. I'll definitely be bringing my car back there in the future.

Dammit i wanted to be number one on this review.  This new bar kicks ass. it will kick more ass in the summer when their deck opens.  Great calave location, nice mix of people, great drink and beer menu, no smoking...thats nice, no food.

Interior is very cool retro/modern lounge. They kept the original Society Cleaners signs in there.  I dig people that value nostalgia.  White vinyl booths and lots of private space make it a great place for a small group of friends.

Bartenders and staff are friendly and fast.

Cant miss here.  I will frequent this place for sure.

My 9th grade English teacher was Mr. Petrini, one of the original owners. The brothers sold it in the late 90's but the current owners have kept the original menu. An entree, plus a salad and garlic bread for $10?! Awesome!!! And the quality is great, obviously homemade sauces and fresh pasta.  Honestly, this place is the best kept secret in SB...well its not really a secret but whenever I've eaten there its never too busy. Just the regulars that the wait staff know by name. I must try to go more, so they'll learn mine :-)

A friend had mentioned that this place had a really good beer selection. We went after dinner one night and were disappointed that the selection was really pretty average. But what was worse, the bartender was horrible. She was flirting with some douchebags down from us, and literally walked by at least 4 times while I was looking right at her. My girlfriend had time to go to the restroom and come back even! What's worse, the rude bartender had ugly hair extensions and really awful fake nails, according to my girlfriend. We never got served and just left. So, beer sellar loses all respect from us. Shame on you!

I have been to Cafe Napoli for lunch and evening cocktails/dessert. The ambiance is elegant and professional. The tables have white linen and there is a great round window to watch people walking by outside. The prices are very reasonable for lunch, especially for the quality of the food. The prices for dinner are a little high.

I had the Penne Con Broccoli which has an excellent tomato cream sauce. My friend had a cup of the Ciappino soup, which was also excellent. They claim their tiramisu is the best in the city, I felt it was average.

It's been a long time since I've dipped my toe into the B&R ice cream cake game and the quality has definitely slipped. We ordered a strawberry ice cream cake and it was ok. The Ice cream was actually really good and I loved the frosting, it wasn't too sweet. 

Unfortunately, the cake portion was very lackluster. The cake was dry, flavorless and not spongey enough for me. I know the cake needs to be dense to support the ice cream, but dayum it was like a brick. 

I might be back in the future, mostly for a coffee milkshake and a cone for my son.

What can I say about Mickey D's that hasn't already been said a million times over? 

Maybe this, we have lived in Mt. Juliet for 8-months now and we've eaten here three times. Every time we eat here they forget the Happy Meal! We have to remind them every single time about the missing item. We hand the receipt over, get a confused look and then pull into one of those "whoopsie" parking spots to wait for that little red box. Going home with a screaming child, only to find out that his meal is MIA, yikes. 

SIDE NOTE:
The chicken nuggs? Still on point! Pink slime or whatever, just give me all the nuggets!
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: I would say just by looking/walking around in the French quarter area, the hand grenade is the most popular drink around. So with that said I had to go to the source and try one. The place is super popular and of course packed. I must give them a point for being somewhat healthy (in their terms) and offering the hand grenade in a skinny option, but of course I went for the original. The drink is strong but extremely too sweet. Overall the drink wasn't good to me and the bar overall is just like any other on bourbon street. I guess it was worth a shot though and a check on the New Orleans to do/drink at place.

The worst Italian food I have ever tasted . I ordered shrimp scampi with spaghetti. What I got was a bowl of olive oil and a few spaghetti my shrimps were just okay . We also chicken parm sandwich and I was so upset that I got chicken strips with  cheese that was hardly melted  and sauce that was ice cold . A chicken parm is  done properly with a full cutlet melted mozzarella and sauce on a toasted bread . I have gone here twice and both times the food was just horrible.  I gave it 2 trys I wont be back . It's not even worth doing a second review.

This is an above average Renaissance in an ideal location for me. Its close enough to walk anywhere in the CBD or French Quarter but just far enough away to give you some relief from the Bourbon Street insanity.

Check in was smooth and staff were all friendly. The room was clean and comfortable. The housekeeping looked rushed and sloppy but that's my only small complaint. There's a gym and a pool on the roof. The bar downstairs was nice and relaxed. 

The rates were on the higher end (compared to other hotels nearby) but not a bad value. I'd stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Americanized Japanese.  I used to come here a lot before I expanded my sushi palate. i.e. sashimi or nigiri. Now, I know better.

If all you've ever tasted is the Cali Roll, the sushi is alright.
The hot items never tasted quite fresh. Hot food may or may not be contained in tin pans heated by a hot water bath. 

If you like japanese cafeteria food you should come here.  One plus to this review, the downtown location is probably the best out of all your sushi teri options.  

Sushi teri to real japanese cuisine is like panda express to real chinese cuisine. It doesn't compare to the real deal.

I came in slightly after the lunch hour so it wasn't as busy. As I entered however, there was no one hosting me even though the sign asked for a host to be seated. I sat myself to the bar instead and no one was available. I waited around 5-10 minutes to get serviced. Menu was available via QR code. 

I ordered 3 tacos (barbacoa, carne asada, al pastor). Meat was quite dry and didn't have much flavor, especially carne asada. The hot sauce was pretty good though and it definitely helped the taco with flavor. It's street taco sized and there aren't much toppings on or varieties, which I find a bit pricey for its size and variety.

This was my husband's and my first experience with Jeni's. I jumped head first and ordered a scoop of Gooey Butter Cake in a sugar cone. It blew my mind and I was instantly transported to a child like state, ice cream dripping down my hand, carelessly enjoying every gooey cake filled bite.

I was given a very generous scoop. So much so I couldn't finish it all and my husband and I agreed to share a scoop next time (maybe).

The only reason for the 4 stars and not 5, is while their creativity and quality cannot go unoticed, I still want classic flavors like rocky road or chocolate chip which I won't be able to get here.

Open 24 hours! White Castle definitely does not compare to the "gourmet" sliders that are becoming more and more popular, but it is very good late night food.

I actually like the chicken and fish sliders more than the regular burger sliders, though those aren't bad either. The burger meat is really thin, but you get what you paid for since they're super cheap. Their sweet potato fries are really good, but the cinnamon dipping sauce it comes with is too sweet--just eat the fries by themselves.

Just come if you want pretty good meal food as a snack.

Here's the thing about Cavanaughs 's, the food is fine.  It's at least as good as most of the other places on Market St.  Atmosphere is really nice--well above average and their prices are reasonable. My only quarrel, and it's a fairly significant one, is that their staff is kind of rude and non-accomodating.  I have always noticed it but today I was denied a very simple change to a pasta and then 2 people next to me were  denied a four top in a half empty restaurant.  It's not enough to keep from coming back.  They should work on server attitude though.

Hm. I'm gonna preface this by letting you know I'm from Chicago. So I come from the land of pizza generously adorned with lots of cheese and a hefty amount of tomato sauce. And also crazy thick, buttery crusts! But I am open-minded and even enjoy other pizza styles. 

Lorenzo's slices are impressively large. I think part of the fun is seeing how many slices you can finish (I made it to 1.5). And figuring out the best method to eat it (I like to roll mine into burrito form). So it does make for a good group activity. But I felt the absence of tomato sauce and, really, just flavor. I'd probably eat it again though if I were really hungry.

I've never heard of Pizza My Heart, but all of my norcal friends told me that this place was a huge chain up north! My roommates and I decided to give it a try one day, and I was definitely left content. The cashiers were super friendly in describing the types of pizzas they had and what the pizza of the day was, and one even took the time to tell me about his personal favorites. I got a huge slice for roughly $4, and was left satisfied and full. I'd say that one slice is comparable to two small slices of pizza. It's definitely a place that everyone should try at least once!

Just had another tasty dinner at sezmu recently. My girlfriend (who had never been to sezmu) and I went for her birthday.

As usual, we drooled over the menu. There were a ton of new things we hadn't tried before so we were excited. Everything was wonderful. Even got two dishes with fiddleheads, one of my favorite seasonal exotic vegetables. a couple of delicious amuses kept us intrigued between each of our three courses. I enjoyed my sorbet dessert as a light finish to our feast..

Service was unimposing and subdued. A wonderful way to celebrate my girl's birthday.

Planned our only dinner on the trip around Kokopelli's!  Open at 5 for dinner and we were seated by 5:05 on a Friday night.  By 5:30, every seat was filled.  We got our fav sushi chef Godzilla, who had us swimming in food.  We actually started with mussels and salmon skin hand rolls to start with.  We usually wait until later but we are usually too full to enjoy them.  Midway through our sushi bonanza, she gave us some grilled gama (hamachi collar).  Very tender and tasty! We had our standards but the 49er roll was very light and had a nice citrus flavor.  Also liked the melody roll.

Rolls were small and had too much rice in them. They were not any better than the sushi from the Whole Foods deli down the street. Their CA rolls just uses a solid stick of imitation crab instead of the mix. Tonkatsu was too dry. Sauce was not katsu sauce but different, so was the veggies that came with it--does not taste Japanese at all, although it wasn't bad.

Coming from the west coast, this place is clearly subpar for any decent sushi restaurant back home. Might be ok by local standards but was a pretty disappointing meal IMO.

I think I've written two reviews ever. This is the only time I've ever ordered coffee and then simply just...never got it. Took so long (45 minutes+) that I had to leave. And this happened more than once. The people that work here are obviously incredibly stressed and overworked. It's not their fault. But I also know that enough of these terrible ratings going through will eventually cause somebody at a higher level to add staff or make some changes and hopefully help what is unequivocally the worst location I've ever been to in my life. If you work at this place, I'm sorry.

Meh.   No A/C was on, limited wine selection but a lot of locals hang out here.   No food, so if you're hungry they direct you to the burger monger next door.  

There is a another place in the same strip mall - Cuvée 103 that has a great selection of wine so I was thinking it would be a little competition but no.  It might be a good place for beer drinker.  Mostly standard beers and limited liquor selection.


We cane in around  5:30 and all the covers were still on the liquor bottles so it mist be all beer locals.  Not my style.

After getting 'access denied' to La Super Rica over on Milpas (long ass lines) we hustled over to Goleta to see if any of the other legendary places were less crowded. In my mind, I juggled the pros and cons of Cal Taco versus the Habit. Honestly, I always thought they were the same place (Char Burger anyone?). 

Anyways, I had a Char Burger with chili and an order of rings. Man o man, I really, really, really missed this place. We used to pile eight guys into my friend's little '79 Mazda GLC and drive over here for lunch. Good times in SB can always be found at the Habit.

Everyone said we needed to try a Grenade while out on Bourbon Street. I saw everyone walking with a green bottle. I asked someone, and they said Tropical Isle was the place to get it at. It wasn't crowded, just a bar, and I ordered 5 on the rocks (he said it'd be stronger) and one frozen. They weren't too expensive, about $7 each, and you get the souvenier of the bottle and a plastic grenade inside. :) They were tasty, but reminds me of midori sour? And we did not get faded by them at all? The frozen is incredibly too sweet, I'd advise not to get that one. Just dissapointed as I was hoping to get annhilated by one of these bad boys.

Highs:
-uni was pretty fresh

Lows:
-The Chirashi Bowl i ordered looked nothing like the ones in the pictures on Yelp. I saw only about 4 different kinds of sashimi with about two pieces each. 85% of the bowl was just the rice. Not only was I disappointed about the lack of variety of sashimi and the EXTREMELY SMALL PORTIONS, the sashimi wasn't too fresh and the rice was a bit mushy
-poor service- i had to wait forever for the waitress to come to my table so I could ask for a check. There seemed to be many waitresses for the size of the place but none were very attentive/helpful

This is overall an ok average Japanese restaurant. It 's not the best or worst either. But the problem is the service speed. If you make any additional order or extra service you have to be very patience. I went to this place three days in a row. Today I waited more than 20 minutes after I asked for the check so I had to go to the cash register to pay because the waitress never bring me the check. It looks like they are good people and trying to provide good service. But they really need to improve the overal priority management.

Great location, but not a classy place to stay.

We booked the French Market Inn when last at JazzFest.  It was one of the few hotels who would take only a two-night booking.  The location in the Quarter is fabulous, and the building is interesting.  But when we arrived there was no room at the inn (not even the one we'd paid for).  We were put for the night in a room being renovated.  It was raining the next day and we had to wade through puddles to get back to the front desk, through a maze of outdoor walkways.  

Will I stay there again?  - only if it's the only choice near the French Quarter.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Well i don't know where to start.  One thing this place is always packed!! This is my first time having Starbucks...yeah it's true why you ask well probably because i hate the smell of coffee so if it wasn't for a gift card i would have never tried them. Like i mentioned its always packed so we walked in the service was perfect i ordered a blueberry muffin and a Apple juice it came out nice and warm and was damn good. I can honestly see why folks are crazy about this place I'm just not into all the coffee and lattes it's just not my thing and for the record i almost died from the coffee smell while waiting for the order lol.

This location is one of only two McDonald's in the downtown/Quarter area. It is the bigger and busier McD's of the two. 

This McD's for years was run-down, had poor customer service, and long wait times. Within the past two months it got renovated and now it is totally updated. It isn't a complete eyesore anymore. The employees seem to be happier and friendly. The lines move more quickly. The seating is more comfortable and even the lighting has been changed. Vast improvement over what it used to be like.

The food, however, is still the same. Nothing new. Nothing amazing.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
A Full Plate is a neat little spot to find an eclectic array of meals; Fried Green Tomato salad, Catfish fingers, Crab Cake Sandwich or a Fried Egg BLT.

I had the Monster wrap with chicken.  The veggies were fresh the chicken was tasty and the sauce was excellent with just the right amount of spiciness.  

The drinks are served in a large mason jar which is great if you drink a lot during meals.

Although the menu is diverse, it is small.  I would very much like to see a few traditional items on the menu to even things out a bit.

Late Night Delivery...

Shared a pie with the bartender at The Raven Lounge. Believe it was the BBQ Chicken.

It was decent I suppose. I was stuffed after 3 slices (which is probably equivalent to 3/4 of a "regular" large pizza. I'm a big boy what can I say.

Didn't really taste the BBQ Chicken, and there really wasn't that much chicken, but it did what it had to do... which was eliminate the hunger pains.

Would I order the pizza before I drank my 3 pints of Guinness? Probably not... would I post-alcohol infusion? Hmmm... if I was feeling lazy, sure why not.

When I'm on the road in Tucson and need to do a load of laundry, this is my go to place. It's always clean and and the machines have never failed to work. It's $2.00 to do a load in the washing. Detergents are sold for .75 cents and the dryers start at 25 cents. 

The hours are from 5:00 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. and they ask that you not start a load after 9:00 p.m. 

The great thing, on the left side of this business is the Crying Onion Cafe and on the right is Sports Grill & Bar. What more would you want when waiting on your laundry?
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text:
The classic Italian menu is simple but delicious.  I didn't have a chance to try the special menu, but many items sounded delicious.  

I had spinach ravioli with meatballs.  The plate had 3 BIG ravs on it with 2 good sized meatballs; the sauce was a basic marinara.  The meatballs tasted homemade and were moist and firm, the sauce was simple and delicious with nice seasoning and a few chunks of tomato.  The ravs were well filled and cooked to perfection.  

Next on my list to try is the Bolognese from the special menu and the gnocchi from the regular menu.

We got the "super nachos" although they are not so super. They were just chips with canned nacho cheese, some strange chicken meat, packaged watery guacamole and watery sour cream. Not appetizing at all. We also ordered a bean rice and cheese, but somehow they added carne asada. My son at it and didn't complain but it looked pretty bland to me. If they changed their nachos I would give this place another try. Nachos are a staple but I've had better at a hospital cafeteria. Get real cheese, BEANS, fresh guacamole, tomatoes, salsa, sour cream. Make it like that and then you have some thing "super".

Y'all .. let me preface this.

This is a 4-star spot, if you don't have to wait.

If you are waiting more than 20-30 minutes, it's like a 2-3 star spot. Because you will be starving by the time you sit and you won't be able to hear the person next to you.

I've eaten at Bar Taco plenty of times in other cities, and I just don't know what it is about it, but everyone flocks here for food that is...good and fine, is it the price point? Certainly not the service that is hit or miss (more hit recently hence the 4-stars).

I'm also giving it 4-stars for the amount of gluten free availability that is on this menu.

For my first visit to this little place I was totally wow'd. I walked into great smells and cooks singing and a very simple menu. This is a cool spot. The young lady behind the counter is very pleasant. The staff was all super and me with the picky way I eat they were all very accommodating. The corn tortillas are fresh made and boy oh boy does that make a difference. I had Taco al Pastor and Taco de Chorizo. Then I could not resist the Campechana Fries(Fries covered in Pastor and Asada). I had a very nice lunch and very much look forward to trying more things off this awesome menu.

I like this gym because it's near my house, has good hours and friendly staff, and has great yoga classes. I like the friendly living room atmosphere. I like how I see the same people regularly. However, it's not the cleanest gym in the world (I wouldn't call it dirty, but it could use some work) and the equipment isn't superior - the dumbells don't come in less than 5 pound increments; the barbells don't come in less than 10; and they don't have elliptical machines with arm motion. Also, the sales staff is a little pushy. That said, I'm happy with my membership.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: Breaux Mart has been our neighborhood grocery for years now.  Even with the new competition down the street, it is the store we go to for the weekly shopping or just popping in for a quick purchase.  They did respond to the competition.  The store has been remodeled inside and out and there has been some changes to the products they stock.  One big plus for me is that I seldom have a long wait in line. The store is clean.  They always have a fair amount of help in store.  It is locally owned, not a national chain.

Apparently the store has been around for about 30 years.  I had been to the St. James Cheese Company in the past and didn't realize the store was only a couple of buildings away.  That's my loss.  I did discover the store when I had to pick up some wine I had ordered after a wine and food pairing dinner my wife and I had attended.  The Wine Seller has a nice selection of wines covering quite a few different price points.  Before I picked up my previous order, I added a couple bottles of Spanish wines I was interested in trying.  The service was excellent.

We've been eating here coming up to 7 years now.  If anything, the food has gotten better.  I can't say I have a real favorite.  I'll select pasta dishes from all over the menu.  I like the idea that they have both small and large plates for most of the pasta dishes, to suit my hunger.  If pressed for a favorite, then it is probably the veal parmesan.  My wife's favorite entrée is the eggplant parmesan.  Over the first part of last year, I don't know how many times she sent me here to pick up an order of the eggplant for her.  I'm glad that they are now open again for inside dining.

This hotel is absolutely redunkculous! Absolutely jaw dropping decor with beautiful, massive structures, like a 3 story tall giant mirror, white drapes hanging from a high ceiling, a fancy restaurant to the right, a pool table and a giant chair all in the lobby. The left is a bar with a Bohemian taste and live bands during the night. Never been to the rooms, but just the lobby visit and having a drink at the bar makes me want to stay here every time. Also, they're facing Canal and about a block away from Bourbon. Amazing!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I will come here just for the outdoor patio. It was nice to be able to hang out with friends in the outdoors. Okay, I guess I should add that this is a late write up so really, I went before we were not allowed in (Mardi Gras 2020).

The main reason for losing a star was because service was a tad slow. I expected to be slower considering there were a lot of peeps but during Mardi Gras, I would think there would be more bartenders. 

I only drank beer while here. The prices are decent so that is another plus.

Restrooms are clean and functioning (that's important during Mardi Gras). ;)

I mean, there's nothing WRONG with this Hertz location. It's just your typical, sh*tty service. Maybe it was just my first trip back to the East Coast for awhile, but the last thing you want after a red-eye from San Francisco is attitude from the car rental people. 

Attitude, of course, that you get after waiting in a 45 minute line. At 7 AM. 

The car was fine. An Impala, that was a tank to drive and park in downtown Philly. It had a GPS in it, which we didn't ask for, use, and sure as heck didn't pay for. 

The car rental came from Priceline, so it was cheap. Otherwise I'd use Avis because their President's Club makes it a nicer experience.

Huge property with all the amenities of a luxury resort.  Decor and furnishings are a bit older and beds can use newer, firmer mattresses.  Pool is decent sized and you can certainly get some exercise in doing laps.

Hotel is located across the street from the beach, and within a mile of the Santa Barbara pier (not quite walking distance).  You will get woken up by the commuter train running opposite side of the beach side.  Tracks are pretty close.

For the Tesla and EV owners, there are plenty of EV chargers on site.  Pretty convenient for those making the drive back to Los Angeles.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I spent a few days at the Hyatt Regency for a conference, and had a great time. Service is on point, and the restaurants available are pretty good too. I especially like the space they have in the Empire Ballroom - it is very clean, spacious, and professional.

However, it can be downright confusing to navigate this place. If you want to get to the entrance from the back of the hotel, you need to go to the third floor, then back down to the first. Also, if you want to use an elevator, you need to go to the terminal first, rather than the elevator itself.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Always glad to support local family owned businesses. The super yummy homemade ice cream, and garden district location doesnt hurt either.

Locals, celebrities and tourists all love Creole Creamery. From classic vanilla and chocolate to lavender honey and ginger spice everyone will find their perfect ice cream flavor. 

Their famous Tchoupitoulas Sundae challenge (8 scoops of ice cream, 8 toppings- finish by yourself get your name on a plaque) is something I have never done myself, but have shared with friends. 

This old fashioned ice cream parlor is great for families, date night, or general gluttony!

I really enjoyed my time here. I had just come out of hermit mode and was to catch up with two of my favorite people. I chose Bistro Daisy on a Friday night. It was a bit last minute, but I managed to get reservations near their opening time. Everything was great; the drinks (mixed and wine), the food, the ambiance, the noise level (which I'm usually complaining about), and the service. We stayed nearly from opening to close, and they never made subtle suggestions that we should leave (e.g. ceasing to fill our waters) and allowed us to keep drinking at the table, even though it was a busy Friday.

Will never go back there. I have just moved to this area and have been trying difference salons to find a good place to go to so I gave this place a try. I thought by having the owner do my nails I would be guaranteed a good manicure.
Horrible!!!! a little kid could do my nails better. the gel polish was all over my fingers and he tried fixing it by adding layers and layers!!!! no cuticle cleaning and a drop of lotion for moisture!!! then he had the audacity to say " I didn't charge you for repairing you broken nail!" 
Will never go back. I have yet to find a good nail place around here!

Who needs gambling money??? I do I do!!! ohhh well these ATMs only spit money from your own accounts =\ I guess I get none.

Located in North Western Sparks, you can cruise in and hit the drive up or the walk up ATMs. Either way you will get to quickly grab some cash and continue on with your day. This used to be a thriving merchant area, but its now almost all fast food joints, grocery stores, and thrift shops around it. 

Regardless of all of that, this is a fairly well designed location to get some cash and roll on with your day...

Went on a Friday or Saturday night, don't remember, but it was empty besides a couple there...First time having penguin's frozen yogurt so i thought ok, something new. When i went in, i saw there was no one @ the counter...the counters were messy with toppings ALL over the place...I waited there for almost 10 minutes and still no service...there was this girl in the back but i couldn't get her attention, dunno what she was doing, finally a guy came out to help...gave samples...ok...so i decided to get taro, which was interesting... but i wouldn't go back to this location...

Took my ferret here even though it was totally out of the way. It's in the outskirts of the city and I live very central. But not only were their prices better than anywhere else, the staff on the phone very really kind and knowledgable. They were able to get us in same day and if you have a sick pet, you know how valuable that is.

Everyone we interacted with was so friendly and upbeat. I really liked the energy there. I love how the vet did not rush through and spent a lot of time explaining. There was a great rapport between Carat and the vet, clearly this guy loves animals. Would highly recommend this place. Worth the drive.

Oh, La Viola. I have such fond memories of you - multiple Valentine's and anniversary dates were spent here while my husband and I were in college. This is a charming but tiny BYOB with absolutely heavenly Italian food. Not only that, the prices were surprisingly reasonable but this may have changed in the three years I've been gone from Philadelphia. I wish I could comment more on it more, but alas, I've left the City of Brotherly Love. We could use more BYO's like La Viola out here in the Whale's Vagina (San Diego).

I am giving this place a 3.  They have forgotten to put my toppings in on two occasions (I have no idea how), but considering I've been here 40 or so times, I can't complain too much on the messing up twice. I go here the most only b/c it's right by my house and I'm too lazy to drive to Sheridan's.

They aren't stingy w/ the toppings and they are right below Fritz's for taste.  

Go here in the summer for the YUMMY raspberry or strawberry cheesecake concrete and in the fall for the pumpkin!  Totally worth it!

WARNING:  Hit the bank beforehand, they do NOT take credit cards

I went in about 5 min prior to closing, because when I  are out to my car to run errands, I noticed my tire had a huge bubble. 
I knew I couldn't drive long on it so I hauled it over to Tire Discounters. They were so kind and accommodating, despite my showing up at the last minute. 
There were still quite a few people in the waiting room, and it did take about an hour and half to get me out of there, for one tire, but the service I recieved from the guys was great. 
I knocked a star off of this rating because they didn't fill my tires (which I then had to go do myself). Which is a pretty common courtesy.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
Can't give this place 4 stars since I didn't stay in a room and didn't get past the lobby.

Definitely the nicest hotel in the area, as far as I can tell.  There's a Gold's Gym in the hotel!  And there are some condos available, which is like the Boise version of say, the Four Seasons SF which has Sports Club LA and residences.  But still a stretch.

Poor signage on the hotel, but the distinctive art installation on the corner of the building clearly defines it.  I think it's a representation of the rivers there?  Lobby bar looked super nice too.  Fully stocked and there was plenty of comfy seating available.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I came here for lunch, craving some good classic italian food and this is just what the doctor ordered!  We sat outside and started off with a cocktail, the moscow mule which they just introduced to their menu.  It came in a copper mug and I thought it was very refreshing.  I skipped out on an appetizer and went straight to a lunch special.  I got the spachetenni which are pasta filled sacks of fontina cheese and prosciutto.  They tasted so fresh and paired with a fresh basil sauce.  This plce had good service and totally worth it for the fresh pasta!

Stayed the night here while visiting a client and I'd consider it above average for a mid level hotel chain. They have nice, spacious rooms with a while sitting area with couches which is just such a huge perk rather than a studio type hotel room. The bed was comfy and gave me a good night of sleep in a time I was struggling to sleep consistently. 

The service was friendly and there was a breakfast downstairs that had some nice, basic offerings. Also, I'm pretty sure some like really aged old WWE guy was pulling up when I left? The people I was with recognized him anyway lol.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
It's dark and cozy, which is really all that matters. The ambiance is perfect for a late, rainy night--modern and artsy, with lots of dark woods and reds. 

Having just come from a workout at the SBCC track, my cohort and I decided to replenish our glycogen stores with a nourishing snack of creme brulee. Just one. With two spoons. Very delicious. He also really enjoyed the glass of port that was recommended to him by our waitress. We were so satiated afterward, there was no need for dinner. But perhaps we'll be back to try it.

As much a museum of manly men stuff as it is a barber shop and personal grooming boutique. I didn't get a shave or haircut (and frankly the $50 gave me sticker shock even though I am grom L.A. - I can get a REALLY GOOD barber to give me a REALLY GOOD cut in Hollywood for $35 with tip). I did like the space though and looking through their collection of really old shaving ephemera. Plus I found a pair of cufflinks with secret compartments I have put on my permanent wish list. 

Drop in and look around. Though I would probably get a cut elsewhere- I can't imagine this is the going rate around here.

2nd visit today was much better!  I got the 101st rolls which consisted of tempura shrimp, crawfish, avocado, eel sauce, spicy sauce and crunchies.  One roll was about 10 slices, so it was huge, plenty for one and big enough to share. 

I told the sushi chef I was now a fan since I have found a fav.  He gave us seaweed salad with cucumbers which was really delis too!

If you go and are not impressed, then go again and have something different. I think their specialty is special rolls not just your everyday sushi or rolls.

My boyfriend and I were looking for a late dinner place around 10:30 and our hotel receptionist recommended Restaurant Roy. The ambiance is really cool - dim, intimate lighting and lots of cool art and decor to look at. We ordered a reasonably priced bottle of wine and shared a seafood entree. We came the weekend after Christmas so they were out of bread and pasta, which explains the 3 stars vs 5. We also got the last creme brulee, the only dessert they had. The service was good but I was a bit disappointed with this place because half the menu was unavailable.

This is located in the back of the Holiday Inn. It is a great location being right on the water. We were surprised how good the food was. We ate there a bunch of times during our stay and had family join us and they thought it was great too. I thought breakfast was a little pricy but lunch and dinner was priced right. We will be back. The reason for lack of one star is the band on Friday night and Saturday night was not good at all. Very corny duo. Daytime was great. Also there were a lot of smokers at night. I don't like smelling smoke when I'm eating and there were a few kids around.

Worst. Restaurant. Ever. So, I decided to continue my quest to try all the local places, and prefer to eat non-chain. I am not sure where to start, but this place looked great on paper. Over 30 years, or something, established, local, good selection, etc. The veggies I had (fried okra, green beans) were just plain bland. The fried chicken was blah. The plating was on hard plastic plates...plastic old cups for the tea. I saw several people come in and leave. The interior is blah and decorated horribly. The service was lack luster and slow, adding to this review of not just the food - but the service, too! Never will go back.

Great hotel!
In town for a wedding, and this hotel was where all of the guests were staying. Definitely appreciated the lower rate!

New hotel, the guy at the front desk said it was built in 2014. Room was super clean, decorated simply, and the bathroom was large, clean, and stocked with plenty of towels. There's a fridge (!!!!), microwave, and coffee maker in the room.

Plenty of parking, free breakfast in the morning, free wifi if you're a HHonors Member, spacious lobby, and even a little snack area to buy goodies.

If you need a place to stay in the area, this is a good one.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The food a good, it is REALLY good. I had one of the best udon there, ever.

But, I'm not sure if it's related... after having a half bowl of delicious raw salad (and this is probably my fault since this is peak romaine e-coli season) ... I had two full days of diarrhea. Took me out a full week. I don't blame the restaurant though, I was fully warned on the news.

Regardless of my illness, the food was really great, and I'd just say, as long as you eat everything cooked, you simply can't go wrong at this restaurant. Recommended.

I don't know if we got the reject room, or if all the rooms are reject rooms but:

1) the toilet wouldn't flush. We asked like 3 times for them to come fix it.
2) the faucet at the sink was broken (only the cold water handle worked)
3) we are skeptical of how clean the shower was
4) the cabinets were falling off the hinges
5) 1/3 of the elevators were out of service
6) the breakfast was......pretty bad. Maybe I should move this up to like number 3 of egregious violations during our stay. It was.....not good.

The free happy hour was good tho, lol
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
This location is fantastic.  Yelp keeps prompting to me to review this location, but I just realized I'll never be coming to this location again....because my parents no longer live in Montgomeryville. Still, that makes me sad, because this is one of the better PF locations I've been to.

The location is big, not too crowded, and has AIR CONDITIONING THAT WORKS.  I've been to so many planet fitness locations that are stuffy and gross.

I really like this location.  Wish more PF locations were like it.
(-1 star because I don't think they have stair masters? At least I don't remember seeing them any time I was there...?)
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text: My office comes in here every single day. Multiple times a day. We happen to come in on a Sunday, when Pricilla who is normally our 10/10 Starbucks barista was off shift. Ordered what we always do, Nitro Cold Brew, light sweet cream. Got our order, and noticed the cold brew had way too much cream. Politely mentioned it to the barista and instead of making a fresh one..... dumped half my coffee out into the sink and added more cold brew. Said "that should be okay". Not your best work Starbucks. I would expect a fresh cup with the right amount of cream, especially with all the business we consistently give.

We were so excited to find this place after a long day at the Expo Center around the corner. Bar food, beer, dimly lit, sign us up. However, very similar to another review, the bartender/waitress was less than remotely excited to see us. I believe we were actually an inconvenience to her (2 of us). I ordered chicken wings which come plain, mild, hot, or suicide, when I asked what happened to medium, I was informed that the hot was super hot and that I should just do that and not worry about medium. I did. They were saucy, but there wasn't a flame to be found. Disapointed.

I would give it a try again, but would definitely skip the wings.

I loved this quaint hotel! Location was perfect, dozens of eateries, shops, and bars within walking distance. I loved the character this place had, with its classic NOLA architecture and beautiful inner courtyard. Just a heads up, parking is not included. You can choose the hotel parking for $38 for 12 hrs, or there is a public parking lot right across the street. Staff was very helpful and friendly.  Me and my sister stayed one night and we are certain the place is haunted! They seemed to be friendly though
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The place looks pretty busy so that can be a sign of good service and or good value for the service. I got my eye exam at a different place so I can not give opinion about that. But I ordered my lenses here because they would take my insurance!! BOY, four weeks later and I am still waiting for my glasses. Not to mention they got it wrong the first time! Every time I call (not that they should be calling me the customer) they give me a different story about the delay with my glasses. 
So they are busy and guess what? May be that is why my glasses are late too. I think someone forgot or misplaced my glasses. WHAT A MESS of a place.
categories: Eyewear & Opticians, Health & Medical, Optometrists, Shopping

text:
The room was very spacious and the aesthetics was nice. The air conditioning is very quiet, which is good for some, but not for those that sleep with a fan. 

The customer service was great, but the valet parking was $28/day. You don't have many parking options, you are stuck with that option.

The location is in the center of everything, so all of the attractions are within walking distance. 

They offer a free continental breakfast, but the fruit wasn't the best. However, they have a nice variety so you are able to get the whole family full. I loved the oatmeal, personally. 

Overall, I'd recommend this location.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
UGH FOOD IS SO TERRIBLE.

CHOW HO FUN: made with cheap thin noodles that look nothing like Ho fun that you otherwise will find in all Chinese restaurants. Noodles were dry and they all stocked together. I stuck my fork in and the whole portion lifted up.

SWEET AND SOUR CHICKEN: Blend and over fried (brown color) versus the light fry crisp you will see in ANY other decent Chinese restaurant.

CHIPS/FRIED NOODLES: the cheap kind, soggy as hell.

Overall it was just bed. I would recommend either Jin  House or Rich City for lower price point and WAY better quality.

I have been a customer of Chuck for years.  When he told me he was buying Nick's with his wife Marie who worked at Nick's for years, I followed down to their very old school shop.

Chuck is a great barber and does a good job every time.  Chuck and Marie are modernizing the shop bit by bit - WiFi, big screen TV, a Keureg coffee machine, and updated decor all bring the old school with modern features Nick's into the first rank of area barbers.

I have seen Marie's work and she is a top rate barber too.

I think that Nick's is the go to place and at least, IMO, it's well worth the trip from Cheltenham!

I usually want to explore a city when out of town, but my husband opted to stay in. Nourish is on the second floor of the Westin and has ample seating and great staff. The server recommended so great local beer by Quaff On (Busted Knuckle) and I ordered the vegetarian pasta and my husband ordered the cheeseburger. The pasta was quite tasty and filling. It was chocked full of veggies and the sauce had plenty of flavor. I went back the following evening just  for drinks and the bartender then was nice too. It's also a great place for watching sports. I'd recommend it.

Yelp and fate led me to Menagerie one hung-over morning. I know next to nothing about Philly - I was in town for a bachelorette party. I got a little nervous when I realized I was in the historic cobblestoned streets parts of town, because touristy areas are rarely home to great coffee, but Menagerie thankfully proved me wrong. It was a very cute cafe, sunny, quiet and surprisingly uncrowded for a Sunday. I got a bagel and a much-needed, very delicious pour-over coffee, sat at a large table in the back with a few other folks quietly reading. Ah - it was lovely. Thanks Menagerie!

Such a pain to get through to traffic. Parking was also a pain. We found parking not too far away and it turns out that this hotel is affiliated with them so instead of paying $44 a night, the hotel stay will get you $38 night. The lobby was very nice. The staff is also very kind. Now, on to the room - It was small. It also smelled like someone cooked fish in it. The room was clean, just didn't have a pleasant smell. 

Now, on to the positives. They have Davio's Italian restaurant, A standard Keurig coffee maker in the hotel room, free coffee in the lobby, a fitness center and free launderette.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I just moved back from LA and have really been missing street tacos and in general food Mexican food. Since today is Cinco de Mayo I gave el Limon a shot. I'm happy I did! It curbed my tacos craving and I was impressed! I order 3 tacos 2 steak 1 tongue and dice and beans. 

I will have ti say the Lengua was one of the best I have had. Seasoned just right and cooked well! The tacos are pretty hefty and filling. The rice was nicely seasoned and oh boy the sauces just hit just right! 

Thank you for the great food to celebrate the holiday! Viva Mexico!!!

The food is absolutely amazing. Probably the best Italian food I've had outside of Italy itself!

Family feel with great service, everyone makes you feel very welcome. The menu is small but they will make anything you'd like, and one of the many daily specials is always a good option.

I would deduct half a star if possible since the physical space is less than ideal... it's small so try to sit near the middle or rear of the place because a seat closer to the door takes away from the experience. 

Overall this is a highlight in the Tampa area.

To be fair, I must mention that I was completely drunk by the time I made it to Beer Fest. It's located on Bourbon Street, which is generally a bad sign... but as I remember it is a tad nicer that the rest of the places around there, some of which can be quite dismal. It's a beer bar: they have a good selection of microbrews on tap, which was nice. It's not particularly cheap, but still reasonable. Order in a plastic cup (which come in several sizes... we got the larger one and weren't able to finish it...), and walk around the neighborhood.

I cant say enough about this place! Its never that crowded for lunch and the service is amazing. ITs so clean and usually doesnt have that not so fresh fishy smell. (no one likes that) The sushi is so fresh and good! I have never tasted anything unsavory. The miso starter is great and the eel is extremely tasty. The booths are big and its just a classy joint. The only thing i dont love is the large boat the food comes out on if you order a lot. its meant to be cute but i could leave the boat and just take a plate.

A BonVoy hotel in a nice, central location.  It's just a few short blocks from Bourbon Street and walking distance to the Casino as well.  The staff was super friendly and accommodating (never a problem to bring lots of extra towels).  There is a cool pool table in the lobby and the decor is modern.  The rooms are a bit on the small side, but it's NOLA, no need to spend too much time in your room anyway.

The sexy bar is a hidden gem.  Good drinks and they serve food in the bar too.  It was never crowded and it was sort of nice to get a drink without the huge crowds.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Stopped in on s Friday night and this place was jumpin ! Very very busy even with a reservation in place we still had to wait about 20 minutes. All of the staff was in top form and working hard to take care of their guests, food coming out all looked great. We had miso soup, 5/6 cut rolls and some yuzu to drink. All of the fish tasted nice and fresh and everything we had was on the better side but nothing really stood out ? Our server was great and we will be back at some point. Definitely worth a try and better than most sushi places in the area.

The two stars apparently mean "Meh. I've experienced better." And that's exactly how I felt about lunch at Villa Barone. It wasn't at all bad, but there is better Italian food out there.The gnocchi was chewy and tasteless (is it ever anything else? maybe I've set my hopes to high for this dish) and the ravioli was good -- but then, I rarely have bad ravioli.

Service was fast, but we were one of two tables in the entire restaurant. And while I know that wait staff are required to be on the floor and attentively watching diners at all times, it's really unnerving when three or four of them (and a hostess) stare at you.

Construction is the pits.  So is the manager who either doesn't knock at all, or didn't knock loud enough for guests to hear when he's doing room checks.  Props to him for taking my yelling at him like a man...but geesh did that give me the heebies at the time (this all went down in May).
For a Airport-adjacent location, it's not a terrible place to stay.  Big comfy bed, nice flat panel TV, free wifi, and even windows that open.  Might not be terrible after construction.

The ladies at the front desk were awesome.  Friendly, sweet, and very sympathetic to what was definitely the weirdest thing to ever happen to me in a hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I can only comment on my food which is kinda off the menu. Anything vegetarian is not vegan. Vegetarian soup has a chicken base. All vegetarian options are chicken based or fried. 
I was so hungry and didn't have much time however this place hooked me up with STEAMED vegetables and tofu for $5.00 I added lots of soy sauce and was able to function the rest of the afternoon. Dish consisted  of a lot of tofu, broccoli, bock choy , onions (too many to my taste) carrots, green bell peppers and 1 mushroom. 
Friendly service. Clean area. 2 outdoor tables.

We spent two nights there and other than ending up in a handicaped room our room was fine. Though I had requested a smoke-free room due to our late check-in (7pm) only smoking was available. It didn't smell too bad and the view was nice. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. The hotel does have parking available for an additional $26.00 a day which after shopping around seemed like a great deal. The hotel has a small but clean fitness area and an indoor pool. The location was great walking distance to everything! The front desk could have been friendlier and though the hotel advertises they have a concierge, they don't.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I selected Payless Car Rental last week instead of my regular enterprise, and it was a big mistake. I prepaid the $35 two day rental online, which was supposed to include all taxes and fees. Nope. My rental ended up costing me $115 total. Why? Because I opted for pre paid gas ($27) and the rest was "taxes". So I was charged over 100% in "taxes". When I questioned them on it, they told me they would give me a partial refund on the prepaid gas since I called them to ask. Never happened. They are liars and cheats and they will end up charging you more than double and blame it on "taxes". RENTER BEWARE! Go to enterprise instead!

The friendly staff was the highlight here. The rooms are dated and tired looking. My room was clean but everything is visibly worn.

The address here is the same as the Hilton, confusing any Uber, Uber eats or Lyft. So factor that in. Despite adding direction notes, it was a daily challenge getting my ride on time.

No food (dinner) options at the hotel. The breakfast looks and feels like a free breakfast. The Hilton next door has a steakhouse I wouldn't recommend to anyone.

Overall it was okay. I'd definitely look into other options closer to downtown before staying here again. This was booked on short notice for a work trip.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
The rudest, most careless woman works the phone there. I have frequented this place several times and lost my expensive Rx sunglasses. The lady answering the phones was not interested in helping me whatsoever and got extremely annoyed as I asked her questions. She acted like it wasn't her job to help me.  

I asked for the manager but I don't think that's who I spoke to. The "manager" was as inept. If he was the manager, he has no business being a manager. He barely apologized for the way I was treated and was no help at all. Don't go there if you want actual customer service.

For years i used the service and loved it ... even one year i paid for upgraded membership which help me that year and when i did not need the paid membership i turned it back to FREE.. then in April i get a e-mail telling me that my membership will be rolled into a paid membership or i can leave ... well ... i left that month.. Even if then offered me a yearly paid membership  25-50 a year i may at that time paid it to keep my membership but this or that .... i think not .. they need to look at where the members are going (ZIPCAR)

I absolutely love it here. The indoor and outdoor spaces are perfect for loud and fun group settings. No table service but the cheap drinks make up for the constant trips to the bar. I have to rave about the food for a second. Bar food is usually whatever in my book and I rarely order quesadillas because well, a bad quesadilla can ruin your night. But there's is not to be missed. The chicken is slow cooked and divine. Perfect for sharing. The tots are crisp and delicious. The portions are huge! And the service is quick. I'm only taking off a star because the location is a bit sketch. They do have parking though.

Breaux Mart is very close to my house. I do enjoy supporting local so I do shop here often. I think they have a great selection of New Orleans favorites... blue runner beans, hubigs pies, every flavor of Tony's imaginable. That is a major plus. The deli looks like it has some good options for meat eaters. The only negative is that it is so expensive to shop here. Things you would find at Rouse's are generally double here. For such a small store, they have a great selection of wine. That gets major props in my book. Overall, I will continue to support but I might save buying toilet paper and conditioner for Walmart.

After my first night on Bourbon, all I wanted was a taste of home, and I definitely found it here at Pinkberry. My friends & I found that it was right on the way back to our hotel, so we stopped by before closing, and the staff was so nice & stayed open a little bit later just for us. I also stopped by on one of the hotter days when I was in New Orleans, and had exceptional service. I feel like the portions are larger here than they are in California [no complaints], but the flavor & everything is exactly the same. I mean, what else can I say about Pinkberry that hasn't been said before?

I am in LOVE with Rough at Sea, which has a creamy sea salt base mixed with candied pecans, almonds, pistachios and a honey swirl. I literally asked to taste two flavors- Rough at Sea and the bee/honey one. My eyes went wide and I said "that one. I'm getting that one". I did ask to do a single with the two flavors which I'm glad I did, but that salty/sweet combination is perfect. 

4/5. I need to figure out whether or not my local ice cream places in the Bay Area serve anything like it, otherwise I might need to figure out how to make it myself!

If the food wasn't so good, I would not put up with the rude attitude that seems to come from behind the counter. I placed an order for tamales and saw people come and go, while I waited and waited and waited some more. I asked how much more time it might be and was told they go in numerical order. That is great, but you had passed my number 4 people back. The women at the front argued with a woman about whether or not she ordered a chicken taco or flauta for several minutes and then proceeded to go through all the orders to find hers. 

Yep...like I said... the food is good, but the employees make me want to find a new spot asap.

Why does your phone number not work during business hours? Are your business hours wrong? Are you under staffed due to the current situation? 

I believe my cat has a UTI and tried to call Friday late afternoon. Your website allows to try to make an appt but no one got back to me to let me know if I have an appt on Monday. 

I really liked the vet who saw my cat last winter. I hope she can see him soon so we can get the answers needed and I can stop covering my bed with a tarp and making her sleep alone. My goal is to have her seen Monday, but no matter when she is seen, I hope she can get help and I can get my questions answered.

Located on the north end of the canal this place has an beautiful view of downtown Indy from it's outdoor seating area. The food is just as good. If you like pulled pork, you've got to get the Southern Style BBQ Sandwich. And, it is definitely Southern - served up with a helping of creamy coleslaw and pickles right on top of the pulled pork. This sandwich is sure to please the heartiest of appetites - it did mine! Served up with a side of homemade sweet potato fries you are sure to get a flair for the South. Delicious!

We went to Upstares at Varalli during restaurant week.

I have to agree that it may not serve authentic Italian cuisine but is definitely up there when it comes to service and food. We ordered the stuffed mushrooms(must try!!), the house salad, pasta primavera and a tarragon chicken. The meat was tender and cooked well. The veggies were fresh and so was the pasta. 
We ordered the tiramisu and the bread pudding for desert. The tiramisu was okay but the bread pudding was delicious!. 
The service was quick and prompt. We got a good table with a nice view of broad street

Tennou is probably the best sushi joint in the Westbank.  The food here is fantastic compared to all the other sushi joints in the Westbank!

My favorite appetizers:
-Baked Salmon. It's perfect. Just the way I like it. It always has the right amount of eel sauce.
-Beek Tataki. I love the onions they top it with. Other sushi places don't always give onions.
-Hamachi Kama.
-Green Mussels are good. 



My favorite rolls are:
-Hawaiian Roll
-Tennou Roll
-Crunchy roll with cream cheese added. 

I've tried various things here. These are my all time faves!

Monday night 6/25 at around 8:57pm I pulled up to the drive through after a hard gym session and needed some caffeine to get me home. I was greeted by the most genuine, friendly voice asking me how my day was and what I would like to drink. Later on, I was told her name is Elizabeth (blonde ponytail working the drive thru)...and I just have to say THANK YOU FOR YOUR AMAZING CUSTOMER SERVICE. If only every Starbucks was like that...I didn't feel rushed even though I asked for future when they closed and she said 9!! Oops...once again thank you for the great customer service!!

Very similar to any of the other newly built or renovated Sprinhill Suites that are out there, and this is a very good thing. These places are always clean, usually has a shower (NO TUB!), free breakfast, nice atmosphere, free Internet, HDTV, good AC, parking garage and nice staff. This place is right off the highway so it is easily accessed. It is in an area with a bunch of shops and restaurants so you can get the stuff you want quickly and easily. The rooms are very fairly priced for the quality of experience you will get. I will definitely stay here again when I visit STL and need to stay west of downtown.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Really solid hotel. The rooms are really big with really high ceilings. Of course there is the amazing Westin heavenly bed. The bathroom has separate shower and bath which is really nice. The staff was very nice during the stay. The room service staff still hustle for a tip even though it is built into the price of the food. I'm already paying 30-ish dollars for a meh burger you dont need a tip. The elevators have leather walls but the creators failed to foresee that they would be easily defaced so thats worth a laugh. The location is close to the ballpark and train and other downtown type things so thats nice.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: Eh. This place usually gets the job done but when they mess up, they mess up bad. I've gotten lots of cars that reek of cigarette smoke. I've refilled my car and still gotten charged for fuel. Showed up and they do not have my reservation, I've showed up and I have 10 cars reserved for some reason. Huge pain to make any changes to your reservation. Calling this location you have to wade through infinite phone options and usually do not get a person still. Shuttle drivers are ok, sometimes a little to pushy with trying to take your bags, etc. But most of the time they are pretty cheap and you can just get your car and go.

I came here for Fiestas last Friday (and other downtown SB nights as a UCSB undergrad) and it was fun!

The pros:
+Music was bumping and the DJ even played like 3 Spanish songs in honor of Fiestas :)
+Not too crowded but party people filled it up
+Bathroom lines were short
+$10 cover charge (assuming other clubs were $20+)
+One of my friend's met the owner and he was an awesome guy who resolved an entry problem

The cons:
-Drinks were overpriced which is funny since Madison's is known for cheap drinks but I guess it's for the spirit of Fiestas lol

I would come back again when I wanna go start off a night of mayhem in downtown SB :)

Live music, cheap eats...what more do people want from an airport restaurant?  My kids were entertained while we ate peacefully!  Basketball was on the screen to distract the big kid from his phone for 1 hr.  That is priceless.  Now to the food.   It was decent.  Of course the hot chicken can not be compared to real Hot Nashville chicken such as Hattie B's.  The salmon and chicken strip was good too.  We are all our food.  Let's recalibrate since we are at an airport.  Service was quick and easy with the service buttons at the table.  Enjoyed our meal here between or connecting flight.

The actual rental process here went smoothly - our car was ready when we arrived, and it only took a minute to check it back in when we were leaving Boise. It's located on-site at the airport, so if you're flying into Boise, the place is very convenient. 

I agree with the previous poster, though, in the actual comfort level of the car. We had some kind of Chevrolet, and it was really uncomfortable. There are cheaper cars made that don't leave you with a backache after driving around... but it does seem like Enterprise just wants you to spend as much as possible.

Disappointed. Yoitomo is one of the few places in Boise that offer all-you-can-eat but it limits you to one order of Yellowtail (Hamachi) and one order of Fresh Water Eel (Unagi) per person. Also the "eel" (aka unagi) sauce they put on some of their rolls is a bit over-powering than most places. The rolls would taste better without it. 

What really irked me was when I received my second order of nigiri. The size of the rice under each piece of fish grew to almost double the amount.

Lastly, what kind of sushi joint doesn't have hand rolls on the menu?

All I had on this trip was the Chirashi, a bowl of sashimi (slices of the chef's choice fish, usually consisting of yellowtail, tuna, and salmon amongst some other fish) over sushi rice, so this isn't really going to be a complete review. The menu was quite extensive so it would be unfair to grade this place on one dish.

Positives: The fish appeared to be fresh, the yellowtail was almost perfect, and the dish was filling. 

Negatives: The rice seemed a bit bland and some of the fish slices were a bit cold.

I will return to try out the cooked dishes. More later!

Please do not order from this place. Their delivery drivers are adding $10 tips to peoples orders for themselves and the manager of this location is aware and said he knows which driver it is and he told him before to stop by writing $10 tips for himself on peoples receipts. Question is why is this person still employed? Secondly, why is the manager still employed when he is aware of what this driver is doing? 


I had to go inside this place to get my money back s and witnessed them not even using gloves while preparing the food!

Tried this with a groupon for the first time last nigh.  Never again.  The poorest service I've ever had in the city: ignored upon entry- took forever to be seated in an empty restaurant. It then took forever for someone to take our order... at which point, they got it wrong. I had to wait an additional 20 minutes for them to get the right order.  The starter came after the mains (I had to remind them to bring it) and it took forever to get a drink..or a napkin...or...anything. 

Food was so-so. Not terrible- not that good. Only 4 shrimp on the shrimp tempura dinner... Bi bim bop in hot stone bowl...served in a tepid bowl. 

Never again.

Most of the food is really not good, but you just have to be strategic about it. The teriyaki beef on a stick, eggs rolls, crab Rangoon were all very good. The rest was mediocre at best. The prices are awesome, but not low enough to make me want to each mushy flavorless fried rice. We'll order from them again, but we will be sure to only buy food they are good at making.

Personally, I would advise them to dial back having so many options on the menu until they can master a handful of dishes. Then add more options. I mean, the rib meat was so tough it's like how do they even let that out the door without being concerned about losing customers.

We were in the heart of Chinatown last weekend. My boyfriend wanted hand drawn noodles and I was  craving an egg roll and some pork lo mein. The menu was very extensive and the gentlemen who took our take out order was super nice. But really $2.79 for an egg roll? I found most of their items to be overpriced. I was underwhelmed by the food that I didn't even keep the leftovers. I think if you are going to charge more than your competitors the good should have more flavor. $33 later...for three egg rolls, beef teriyaki sticks and lo mein is a bit much when you can get most other places for $20. I likely will not be back.

Hey, it's a laundromat.  There seems to be enough parking and there's some nearby not he street as well.  It's $3 a load, but you get a free dryer with that.  The staff is friendly and responsive. As a bonus, some gal comes around selling tamales, and some dude was selling cologne out of his trunk in the parking lot.  And there's some pinball and video games, as well as a bookshelf.  Well, the bookshelf had only one book ("Tommyknockers" by Stephen King, but you get what you pay for.  All in all, a solid laundo experience.
categories: Dry Cleaning & Laundry, Laundry Services, Local Services

text: It's Okay.  I had steak and ribs combo.  I ordered the steak medium-rare and got rare.  The outside of the steak was too charred for my taste.  So charred that it gave a bitter taste to the steak.  Ribs were okay as well.  The sauce had a similar char to it, so I'm guessing it was hit on the grill or popped under a salamander for warming.  I missed the tang that you find in most rib sauces.  The Mac and cheese was good as was the Ceasar salad.  Service staff was friendly and the interior was very neat and clean.  I'd love to come back and watch a game at the bar.  Great bar area.

Super far away from the French Quarter. It's approximately a 1.3 mile walk to Café Du Monde. Unfortunately, it's not close to anything cool or hip. While the lobby and first few floors are remodeled, this hotel has a very old 70s vibe. It's extremely crowded and the people flow of this hotel is poor for a conference. The exhibit hall which is the bottom floor of this hotel has a very low ceiling and is extremely dark. It's a decent played place to stay if you want to be far away from the French quarter. However, not a deal for conferences.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I recently stayed here for a business trip and loved this hotel. Beautiful lobby with great lighting. Super friendly and courteous front desk staff. Great hotel rooms that offer a nice break from the traditional Marriotts and Hiltons. Right in the heart of downtown Indy and within walking distance to everything. 

As a runner, it was centrally located by great running paths (e.g., canal system, bridge near the zoo, etc.). I must have looked like a sweaty mess when I ran back, as the front desk offered me bottles of water right away. Overall, really pleased with the excellent customer service. Worth staying at.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
I don't really like going to generic places to eat (IDK a pet peeve of mind) but at the airport (PHL) what can you do. Anywho, my friend and I walked up to the counter to look at food, everything always looks shiny and semi perfect...a little too perfect if you as me...but I didn't go into this expecting the best pizza i eva had. 

In short the service was very very nice, super friendly staff, and the food was okay. I'd eat there again. (I purchased a stuffed steak pizza) - All the veggies in the pizza were very fresh and that was another plus.

I went here on a Saturday after I'd passed the restaurant Friday. (I was drawn in by the crowd - and the urban  vibe it had in the small town of maple shade- neon lights and so on)  I was greeted by smiles and very generous service. The selection was great and the pizza was very good. (I just ordered the plain slice b/c I feel it was necessary to start with the basics.lol) It taste very good and I'm so happy that such a great pizza restaurant is sooo close I can eat there whenever I want to. (I use to drive like 20 min to grab a slice from my favorite pizza spot) 

I'll soon be a regular at this place (:
