The service was very good but we are not fast eaters and someone kept coming up to us and asking if we needed boxes.  

Felt sorry for the staff that had to clean up after a table of 3 mothers and 4 children.  The mothers were talking and having fun while their children threw food and things on the floor. Didn't care the least when one of the servers would stop to clean up the mess.  Hope they tipped well!

The first time I ever visited this restaurant the employees were fighting and arguing with each other. This was a little less than a year ago. I never really wanted to give them a chance again until now that I no longer order from the local Pizza Hut. I placed an order today and I'll definitely give them FIVE stars! They came in a timely manner (about an hour) my food was hot, fresh, and yummy! The wings were not the best but that's not the employees fault, corporate just needs to update the quality of their chicken ! Thank you papa johns employees!!! Will definitely be ordering again!

Good location!! But I'm not sure what was going on this weekend,may a lot of birthdays etc, however I had to switch room due to noise, I'm all about fun however my child was with me, and if she complains about not sleeping it's a problem, call down because my neighbors were loud, security and and they turned the music down, but started again, ended up changing room, much better, but a went to lobby huge fight broke out and my baby was with me, " not a good look" 
Then Sunday morning another fight broke out with a female and young male such a nice hotel but too many young unmannered kids check in that makes this place worse, sorry not sorry
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: We held a rehearsal dinner with 50 guests at Fratelli's on a Thursday night.  Our guests were heavy wine drinkers so finding a BYO establishment was important to our wallets.  The planning process with John was very easy and he let us drop off 24 bottles of wine the morning of the event.  While we did not have a dedicated "private dining room", our area was essentially separated from the remainder of the restaurant.  Our guests really enjoyed the food and the service was very good.  We are extremely happy that we chose Fratelli's to host our rehearsal dinner!

FInally got around to visiting Fiesta Chicken after a friend's recommendation. I ordered the Chicken Burrito and nachos. I'm from San Diego and thus extremely critical of Mexican Food. The burrito was a good size, the chicken was seasoned well and tasty. The orangish salsa I had with it was a great degree of spiciness and had a great flavor. Great burrito.

The nachos were good not great. Chips were a bit stale but even stale, the chicken, beans, cheese and salsa made them alright. 

Highly recommended. I'll be back.

Great location in Brentwood TN for our visit to CMAs in Nashville. The hotel and rooms are in great shape and appears to have been refitted recently. The front desk staff was great even though as a Gold Honors I did not get upgraded or was allowed to used the exec lounge. The hotel room suites are very nice and roomy. The breakfast food was very good so kudos to the chef and staff. The breakfast servers were somewhat challenged to handle even though there were very few customers. All in all a great visit to this hotel.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
what can i say about Derek's? we celebrated a friend's bachelorette here the other night. for me, neither here nor there, and probably would not have been my first choice for a fancy special occasion dinner. service= exceptional. wine list= delightfully extensive. food= nothing to get too excited about and expensive. decor= could use a little makeover. 

my main advice... Derek's...please! step into the twenty-first century by taking the ".99" off the end of your menu prices. seriously. if i order the $23.99 salmon, i'd rather be charged an even $24. if i order the $7.99 creme brulee, i want to pay $8. after all, who are we trying to fool?

An overnight trip to New Hope/Lambertville brought us into Walker's to grab a bottle of champagne for after dinner. Though Walker's has a decent selection (given there aren't many choices), it's pretty pricey, especially for a small-town liquor store. Laphroig rang in at around $62 and they had Van Gogh Vodka going for $33. 

Very friendly staff and a convenient location does make this a great option for out-of-towners in need of booze. Just be prepared to fork over a little more than you are used to shelling out.

Cuban pork sandwich - 8.50.  Pretty juicy and flavorful.

Thunder Chicken pizza - 14" 18.00. The menu said fried chicken, but it was simply chicken strips on top of the pizza. Wasn't that excited anymore when the pizza arrived...the sauce was good & it was extremely cheesy.  You can tell that the dough was hand-tossed b/c the pizza came in a weird shape, but it tasted good.

Our server was kinda ditzy, she was all over the place.  Came here on another night just to get a beer to-go and the bartender was awesome.

Valet scratched my rental car and took forever for someone to address. This caused us to get late charges for the rental car and miss a scheduled tour. Room had no ventilation and was humid the whole 3 nights. Air conditioner blasted from the ceiling onto my face every 10 minutes. Breakfast downstairs was understaffed and waited 10 minutes without service; I just said forget it and left without getting an order in.  My worst stay at a Marriott-related chain; and I'm a platinum member with them. Would not recommend this hotel at this time. Spoke with the GM Daniel and will update my review if he follows through as he said he would.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Ok I think my daily sushi cravings are over for now, thanks to Moshi. I can't really tell if the sushi was bad, or if I just wasn't in the mood for what I ordered. 

I usually wouldn't order what I did, but something propelled me to. I got the spider roll and the shrimp tempura roll. Knowing that it is an insult in Japanese culture to leave food on your place, I ate it all. But I wish I hadn't. I was stuffed, so full and not it a good way. It made me not want to order anything fried again for a long time. 

So I don't think that the food is bad, I just think it wasn't what I wanted.

I had a nice dinner here with a friend and we had to wait over an hour to get a table. In the end we ate some sushi rolls and the black cod and enjoyed the meal and atmosphere. 

If you're after some great Japanese food in Philly this is one of the places to go, but don't get your hopes up, the food isn't that different to other Japanese places and you're going to be paying a premium for sushi in Philly for some unknown reason. 

The service was pleasant and professional but for the price tag and the wait you could catch a bus to New York and eat a better meal!

Friendly staff and some of the best white pizza you can find in this town. If you're looking for a quick and cheap meal that could stretch for a snack later, get the six-pack deal. It's all the starch that you could want in both pizza and various garlicky breads form. Curly fries are also one of my favorite things about ordering here. This is a staple of the American foodscape that sadly goes underrated. It is our just as residents of this fair town to make sure Arby's isn't the only place that offers curly fries.

I ordered the Chef's Special ($16) for lunch which included miso soup, a spicy tuna roll, and several generous pieces of sushi. The photo I took shows nice looking food, but I thought the fish was dry, slightly warm, and not particularly pleasing to the mouth. 

On the other hand, the woman that served me was polite, very personable, and obviously liked her customers, me included. If I were to return, it would be almost entirely because of her. 

They offer cooked dishes, too, so don't let my review discourage you from giving them a visit.

The things I like most about this La Quinta are its rates and that it is directly across the street from (what is now poorly named) the 1-800-ASK-Gary Amphitheater. The AC is better than some economical hotels since it has an actual thermostat.  They also have hassle-free WiFi. 

The beds are comfortable, and the towels are average.

My one complaint is that none of the electrical outlets near the desk or bed (at least in this room) are accessible without moving furniture or crawling under tables. These are essential to have access to for people traveling with laptops and cell phones.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Excellent service from Markee automotive. Brought my car in fearing the worst (head gasket problems) but turned out to have no major problems. They found a few other minor things that needed repair, and suggested some late-mileage repairs (timing belt, etc) it was due for.

Nothing was done without my permission, several things were done without charge, and everything was performed quickly and expertly. Great work, which should come as no surprise as I learned these guys were from Ultimate Tire and Car Care, which was previously my shop of choice prior to its untimely demise.

It was probably only good because we stopped by after walking a few blocks in the hot sun. The worker could have been a little more courteous. I was unaware that we were not allowed to take a spoon 'YET.' I took a spoon to try the flavor and she raises her voice saying, "You can't have a spoon yet!" If we weren't allowed to have a spoon yet, then why were they out in the open near the cash register? Put them away if you wanna be tight with the spoons. Sheesh! Oh, and as I am getting my toppings, she could not stop staring me down. Seriously? In my head, I'm thinking, "What is her problem?" I felt so uncomfortable, not cool.

Rooms here have been recently remodeled as part of the transition from the Ramada into the Four Points by Sheraton.  It's a 5 story building, so if you want the most quiet rooms (remember, this is Bourbon Street, so don't expect too much), ask for something on the 5th floor.

If you want a balcony overlooking the street (read: you're a bead-tosser), ask for something on the 2nd to 4th floors.  All Bourbon Street-side rooms have a balcony over the street.

Internet is free here and every room comes with two half-litre bottles of water per night.  Coffee is Four Points-standard, so head to CC's to grab your post-hangover joe.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I have rented cars twice from this location and it is now my go to Reno rental. I am so sad that so many people seem to have had a bad experience. I have never had anything but friendly, honest service AND unbeatable prices. I feel like with most rental car locations you either getting a deal with terrible service or you are paying an arm and a leg and getting great service. I have never waited in line longer than 10 minutes which isn't bad at all in the grand scheme of things. They have great deals, great cars and great staff.

The place is very artsy & quiet, which I liked because I could sit for hours and get some work done. The downside was...that it was boring & not a good place to people watch unless you're sitting outside. 

I really enjoyed the coffee, but when I first went in and asked for a triple non fat vanilla latte, he looked at me like, 'whaaaah?!' but i didnt care because he was gorgeous & I stood like a baffoon grinning at my stupidity for asking for such a ridiculous drink (duh!) 

However, on my second trip, the lady was on it & didn't look at me like a yuppie freak speaking Seattle-talk.

Interesting unique flavor creations. Unfortunately, I have nut allergies and this place seems to be worse than most other donut shops about keeping the stuff with and without nuts separate. I've been eating donuts my whole life and it's extremely rare (perhaps one in a hundred) to ever have an issue of contamination, but at this place it has happened two out of the three times I've come and I've gotten pretty sick. I can't risk it anymore. It seems they don't care much here, or perhaps their non-contamination practices are not effective because I keep getting sick. Plus, they never keep their tables and floor clean. It's always a mess.

Stopped in here for lunch when we were in town for the day.   I had the sushi and chicken teriyaki lunch, and my daughter had the chirashi, which is one of her favorite dishes.My nigiri was fresh and the chicken teriyaki was flavored with the right amount of soy sauce, sugar, and the other miscellaneous ingredients that go into making a good teriyaki sauce.   

I didn't get a chance to try her chirashi, but she said it was really good.

You'd be amazed at the sports memorabilia on the walls.   Owner must be a real sports fan.     When we go to Tucson again, we'd like to return and even try out their dinner menu.

My daughter ordered spaghetti & meatballs and the meat was horrible.  I even tasted it to make sure.  I ordered the Mediterranean salmon with jasmine rice and green beans.  The salmon was delicious, but the sides were overwhelmingly salty.  When I told the manager about our food issues, he wanted to defend the meat and thought my over-salty sides were simply an uneducated palate on my part.  To his credit, he did offer to replace the items, but it was too late for me by then - I was irritated.  The worst part was when we got the check, it was wrong!  Ugh.  

This chef will NOT be going back.

if i'm ever in santa barbara and need another football fix on a sunday morning and a beer, i'm going here. it's just off the UCSB campus, so it's probably a popular watering hole for the local kids. there was a couple handful of folks when i walked in to catch the game. my friend was doing a seminiar presentation thing for the students of color conference....but my packers were playing =)

the bartender was awesome. he did the funniest brian wilson entrance impression ever, he's a giants fan lol. fun crowd, there's food, decent bar. 10 buck minimum if you paying with plastic. have fun.

I did not have the negative experience that many Yelpers here are describing. I came here with my family before we hit the slopes for skiing and we ordered 5 Sausage McMuffins. No more than 5 minutes after we ordered, we got our food and was ready to go. The cheese was not fully melted on the sandwiches, and while this sucks, this is consistent with other McDonald's that I've been too. 

Scott's negative review from 12/2/2014 because he was charged for extra dipping sauces is a bit unfair in my opinion. This particular McDonald is not charging customers more than other McDonald's. Other McDonald's will charge you as well for extra sauce.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: Oh, Magnolia... you seemed so nice... We stayed here on Labor Day weekend and overall had a lovely time. The employees were all friendly and helpful. You can tell they've been well trained and are striving to be a proper 4*. Where Magnolia suffers is that it even though it looks completely renovated, they only put lipstick on the pig. The walls are so incredibly thin you'll here everything your neighbor does... and, I mean, EVERYTHING! I spent most of the night laying awake wondering if they'd ever go to sleep.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I've eaten at Marathon Grill a handful of times and I always like the food.  The menu has a wide selection of brunch items, and I've never been disappointed; the eggs are good, the homefries are good, the multigrain toast is good.  I've never really had to wait either, which is a plus, since so many of the brunch spots in this town get so packed on the weekends.  However, my most recent visit was a little lame; the coffee was not very good, the waitress was inattentive, etc.  All in all, it's a place to go when you want a good breakfast fairly quickly, but at the same time, it's not the kind of place you need to make it a mission to go there.

The food I had at Portofino was decent, but I was largely unimpressed with the service.  When I asked for suggestions about the menu, the waitress replied that "everything" is good.  I realize I was one among a large group, but she was terribly unhelpful.  Also, I kept running out of water.  

As for the food, the salmon and tuna carpaccio was palatable as an appetizer, but my friend's calamari was better.  For my entree, I ordered linguine with calamari in a tomato-based sauce.  Again, the food was mediocre.  Plus, my friend's caesar salad was forgotten, and the staff had to be reminded to serve it.

The Margaritaville Shrimp was quite tasty.  After that, things went downhill fast (food-wise; however, the service was good).  I'm not sure how a restaurant on the waterfront of the Gulf of Mexico has the nerve to serve frozen, undercooked flounder, but for the answer to that riddle you'll have to ask the management here.   I typically love stuffed seafood anything, but my dinner here was bad enough that I couldn't finish it.  

Also, the crowd at the bar was loud and kind of rowdy (and not in a good way).   I found the behavior of some of the patrons to be distracting and disturbing.

BYOB place. Very cosy. Nice upscale decor but once you sit down, you don't get the pretentious feel you sometimes get in NYC. Everyone around us was having a good time and drinking away! We actually got two free glasses of red wine for next table. 

Waiters are pretty friendly. The menu is straight up Itailan; price is perfect for your wallet. We ordered homemade gnocchi with tomato and Parmesan cheese, salmon with fettuccine and orchenette with sausage. Each dish is delicious and great portion. 

The only downside is this place is cash only. So make sure you come prepared!

I recently went to Happy Nail during a trip to Boise. I stayed at the Doubletree, whose parking lot conjoins that of Happy Nail and a few other businesses. 

It was empty when I walked in, and I was very pleased to find 2 very welcoming Vietnamese ladies and a wide selection of OPI polish. 

I expected it to be a little cheaper than it was ($15 for manicure, $30 for pedi-- you can get a discount if you get a combo), but the lady who did my manicure was so meticulous about getting rid of all of my cuticles that I really did not mind the price in the end.

The good part- For starters, you can't beat the $2 martinis!  Our service was excellent and our waitress easily handled our party of 6.

The bad part- I had to send my first filet back because it was cooked way beyond well done.  The second one was served at the right temperature but just lacked any kind of flavor at all.  One other person at our table had the filet as well and had the same opinion- just no flavor at all.

-The kids enjoyed their pizzas and I tried a piece and it was great- nice thin but chewy crust, good cheese and toppings.

I'll probably go back for happy hour and the pizza but that's about where I'll stop with this place.

This bar had my favorite drink on Bourbon Street.  The Resurrection was amazing. Chances are a person would probably only need one to feel the effects of the drink.  The bartenders were awesome and during my week stay they actually remembered my group the next time we stopped in. (Still not sure if that is a good or bad thing).  Either way it was an awesome place to stop into.  They have dueling pianos as well as a chair where you can have an attractive woman pour shots down your throat if you are into that sort of thing

This place is pretty hit or miss, and I think I had a miss day.

On the weekends it gets really loud and there may be a wait to get to a table. So beware.

The slices are huge but expensive. I always have pepperoni. When it's fresh the crust is slightly crispy with ooey gooey cheese. The first time I had it, it was the best pizza I've ever had. I don't eat pizza often. But with more trips the magic wore off. 

They do offer other menu items like friend chicken, jalepeno poppers, and meat pies. I haven't really tried them though.

I will still continue to go here, especially when I have a really good buzz. It's really good drunk food.

Came with some friends during our snowboarding trip.

A plus for their sushi buffet, as I love sushi and don't like to pass up all-you-can eat ones. However, this place disappointed me. I mean, I still left feeling satisfied, but somehow, I felt that they could have offered better quality fish, but for the all-you-can eat, I won't complain. Also, the sushi chefs were very nice and accommodating to my group.  

I probably won't return to this when I'm in Reno again, just because there are so many restaurants there that I haven't tried.

For a quick and easy hotel right in the middle of Philadelphia, this place is awesome. It's in the downtown area so it's within walking distance of alot of shops and places to eat, plus it's within a quick drive to alot of tourist spots.

The staff is friendly, the rooms were a nice size, the beds were comfy, the bathrooms were clean, the parking lot seemed pretty safe... and the view from my room gave us a nice look of parts of the city to boot! 

This place probably isn't as nice as the Hilton, but for a Holiday Inn Express it gets a high 4 stars from me.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Nothing too exciting. The seaweed salad was unbelievably bland.  The rolls all sounded pretty imaginative and delicious... They were pretty good, but not spectacular. The sake was not good. The service was okay, until about 9:50 (they closed at 10). The waitress started ignoring us, and when she brought the charge receipt she hung on us until we signed, then took off. Not a great experience. I can't think of any reason to go back, especially not when there are so many other great restaurants in Indy (including other Japanese restaurants, like the other Ichiban, which is amazing).

Beautiful modern hotel right in the heart of down Indianapolis. There's a little league on one side, a connecting bridge to the convention center, a mall, theater and a bunch of restaurants in walking distance. 

The hotel is clean, service is great, beautiful view, Starbucks on the 2nd floor and an Italian restaurant inside.

The room is spacious with view of down town.  The shower is new and has spa like sprout. The only thing though they don't give us room slippers or other amenities you get when you travel overseas.

Oh and you will meet all kinds of people here as most people are here for convention.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: We've used them extensively for repairing our cars and they've always been honest and upfront. They'll tell us truly what's wrong with our cars even when it's something we don't want to hear.  They guide us with what the necessary repairs are and repairs that aren't quite as necessary.  We've been very pleased with them and have recommended them to many of our friends.  And they always seem to be busy, so that's typically a good sign.  I'm not sure what happened with the first reviewer as that's been quite different from the experience we've typically had.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text: One word, Bland. I used to be a fan until I tried the other mexican places in the area. Yes they have variety but everything tastes the same. When i eat mexican food i expect the whole dish to taste great, the rice and beans at this place need a lot of work. which is weird because i thought those were the easiest to make. maybe Im being to picky but if Im going to pay $10 for a burrito i would want the rice and beans to be at least halfway decent and not make me sick. If you have a weak stomach do not go here!

Of all of my favorite foods I'd have to say that Sushi / Sashimi is my favorite... and having gone to some of the best Omakase in the US, Hawaii, and Japan its quite a stretch for me to give this place four stars.  I admit the quality of the meat isn't quite as great as say Sushi Ota, or a few of the places that I refuse to write reviews for...it most certainly is a steal at around $20 for all you can eat sushi and $30 for all you can eat sashimi!  It is quite an amazing experience to be able get as much sushi as you could possibly want.  If you happen to be in Reno and are a sushi lover be sure to check this place out!

Credit where it's due.... the shift manager was extremely apologetic about the crappy car and issued me a reasonable credit for my trouble. He explained -- in a roundabout way -- that Hertz isn't staffing his location adequately to get underserviced cars out of the fleet proactively.

I think it's a nationwide problem given the counter staffing at every Hertz I've seen... but again, not something the local manager can fix. He did take care of the squeaky wheel and will fix the squeaky brakes on the car I rented.

I won't be joining Hertz's premiere program, but I will use my credit for a personal rental in the future.

Heard good things about Penn Station so I was looking forward to trying it out. Overall, it was a decent sub sandwich. Nothing particularly special, but it wasn't bad either. I can't say that i'll be back, but a combination of hunger and unwillingness to spend a lot may bring me wandering in some day again.

This location in particular had a great atmosphere with very friendly employees. I'd say that the atmosphere made the experience more enjoyable than the food itself.

Oh, and skip the lemonade. It was pretty terrible.

Noble opened to lukewarm reviews, but months of tweaking have created a satisfying neighborhood bistro.

The autumn soup wasn't especially creative, but a well executed version of a now classic dish. My duck was excellent -- rich, most and not at all fatty. The cabbage pairing was delicious.

Service was friendly and adequate. The downstairs portion is better suited for drinks than dinner, so request a table upstairs if you can. 

If you had dismissed Noble because of earlier performance, give it another chance. I did and I was pleasantly surprised.

Coming into Nashville without hotel reservations isn't always a good idea! But found this Hampton Inn at the Hickory Hollow area.  Better pricing but may had been due to pool being closed.... Fine for us!
Front desk was friendly and easy check in service.

Our room had no view and no tub, just a shower only! Very clean but need to update the night stands to have usb outlets so you can charge your phones next to your bed!

As usual, a very comfortable bed as only Hilton properties promise!!

The breakfast buffet seemed not as appetizing as others I have had before. However,  many other guests were eating without complaint.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text: This has been one of my favorite meals since I've moved to Nashville. They have a diverse menu with everything from $12 pasta and burgers to a $35 steak, so there's something for everyone. It's a good place to experience "modern Nashville"( for lack of a better term)- it's in the midst of Hillsboro Village, but cozy and with a strong "sophisticated southern" flair to their dishes. Their wine list is good and their desserts are ridiculous- butterscotch habanero bread pudding with white chocolate sauce? Yes, please.

One of best places to go for water ice in south jersey. I look forward to them opening every year, and would most likely go all winter long if they were open. They have a variety of water ice flavors, including sugar free, and also soft serve ice cream. The girls behind the counter are always friendly and on the ball. The line can get relatively long in the evening, but it moves fast. You can sample any of the flavors if you can't make up your mind. I am fan of mango, strawberry, or vanilla chip, and usually request 2 flavors in my serving.  Rita's doesn't even stand a chance when comparing the two brands.

This is a category 3 Marriott property which puts it in the average category.  By the outside visual and location, I think the rating is spot on.  

However, I have to note the outstanding service I received on a recent brief stay.  From the front desk at check in to the staff in the restaurant and the concierge lounge and the shuttle drivers, everyone, without exception, was courteous, attentive, competent, and went above and beyond in more than one occasion.   The level of service I received was on par with the much more upscale brands.   Kudos to management!!
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: I ate dinner there with another couple for the first time this week.  The decor and atmosphere were amazing!  I was very surprised that the dining area was so spacious and that they offer seating outside.  The food was amazing!  Best Italian food I have had in a long time.  Well worth the visit! The appetizers were fantastic - especially the mussels.  I had veal for my main course and I could cut it with a fork it was so tender.  Dessert was equally good and so was the coffee.  The only draw back was that the waiter was a little slow in keeping up with our table.  Other than that it was a perfect evening.

We ordered the sashimi platter and had the *BEST* super white tuna (escolar) EVER.  It was so smooth and buttery.
I have tried and failed to find a similar quality in various Chicago restaurants.  

I feel lucky to have experienced sashimi nirvana....  especially since my friend has been back to the restaurant on multiple occasions, and she says that the fish there has not been as phenomenal. 

Also, this place is currently listed on Restaurant.com, which is why we went here in the first place.  If you google up a 50% off code for the site, you could possibly pay $20 for a $100 gift certificate to the place.

I really enjoyed my self though it was a bit expensive. ($115.00)

The GF ordered the Clams and Linguini which she found too salty. I would assume anything from the sea is salty but that's my opinion. 

I had the chicken something something. It was glazed in a very tasty port and came with with Rice which I thought was very good. 

The place is small but close to Bath if that's where you will be staying. 

Get in by 6:30 or wait  or do what we did and make reservations the night before. 

I doubt if we will go back as it was way too much money for what we usually look for on any other day but New Years Eve.

One Hoot!!

So I am pretty torn here.  I love the cardio cinema.  The people who work there are generally friendly and helpful and the people who exercise there are nice.  However, I am horribly upset about the hot tub, steam room, and shower area.  It needs to be scrubbed!  And often!  Not good at all.
A friend and I had a complaint about a movie that was really offensive, playing in the cardio cinema.  I received an email reply that informed me that they "proudly showed this movie."  And that was it.  There is a list of movies that members can add requests to-but it seems pretty rare to me that the list is consulted.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
I love sushi and this place sucked! For one the place was empty and the server was standing right next to me the entire time we were there. I can eat a fair amount of sushi and after ordering the crystal shrimp roll, I turned to my friend and was like what the F are we doing here? If I was not on a time crunch I would have went to my fav place but the wait was 2.5 hours. Never will I come back here. Your fish was not FRESH
I have been going to the Sky bar at the Atlantis for years now. This place does not even come close.

I was looking for a good place very close to my hotel in Clayton, and this was about a block away. My boyfriend and I got there just as they were opening. I got a regular burger with cheddar and he got the leather bottle chicken. The burger was excellent, and the cheddar was a huge scoopful of soft cheese! Very flavorful and sort of unique. The leather bottle chicken was good too. The fries were nice steak fries. We also got a cookie that had just been baked that was pretty decent. The service is good as well.

We came here after my father-in-laws wake for a family memorial dinner.  

It's located in a strip mall, and very tiny but they accomodated our family of 15 very well.  

We got the spicy calamari crema to start and its a fried calamari in a spicy alfredo sauce with artichokes.  To me, it didn't have much flavor until you add a little dash of lemon.  

The portions of food were huge and they were happy to alternate recipes for some finicky eaters.  

The food is just ok, but the atmosphere and friendleness made up for the food.

Everyone and their Reno luvin drunk unlce always extolls the food virtues of this small sushi joint in Circus Circus, so the wife and I during our stay at the Silver Legacy. was already pretty full with all the food i ingested so we didn't get the all you can eat option. We had the ala carte menu and ordered the spicy california roll, the rainbow roll, tekka maki, and also the fried cali roll. The fish was very fresh, and boy they were generous with the fish, I mean, that tekka maki had more tuna than rice, and I was just like..wow. glad we went here, and will most likely be back next time we are in the poor man's vegas

I agree this is a fantastic authentic mexican restaurant.  The chips green salsa, and Guacamole are to die for.  The taste is like no other mexican restaurant I've been to.  We also ordered the ceviche.  It was light and refreshing.  We then ordered the chicken flautas.  The chicken was a bit skimpy in the flautas, but was very tasty.  The only negative for us is the service.  It takes awhile to get anyone's attention and if you want another beer, you probably need to get it yourself.  And don't expect them to remove your dirty plates.  But you know......that's how it is in Mexico.  I love the place.

This is my first time staying at this HI Express, and wish now I would have stayed elsewhere.  The rooms are clean and large, but the walls are paper thin - you can hear an entire conversation in the room next to you...especially at 4am.  The wireless internet is spotty and you have to sign in quite often.  The breakfast was horrible, not worth even stopping to try.  The TV signal is also questionable - if you like to watch TV, don't stay here.  Being an ex IHG manager and a Platinum Priority Club member, I had higher hopes for this hotel.  There are plenty of other hotels in the area, and I would highly recommend you stay somewhere else.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: A friend and i are driving home and were craving for some chinese food. This was the closest to where we were. The staff were very friendly staff and made the effort to get to know you or maybe it was a slow night. We had the mushu chicken and shrimps with mixed vegetables. When the shrimp with mixed veggie came out, it was definitely prawns and not shrimp. They were huge! Definitely worth 11.95! wrap for the mu shu was warm when it came out. Ingredients were definitely fresh. If this place was closer to me,  i would definitely come back.

Pizza in Metairie is sadly lacking compared to the more diverse choices in New Orleans, but I am always happy when I go to Sbarros in Lakeside Mall. The portions are generous and I love the mix of sauce and cheese. Even if it is greasy its everything I'd expect New York style pizza to be!
By far the best Mall Pizza I've ever had and it's reasonably priced!
I do wish they would serve Coke products instead of Pepsi and their side dishes are only "okay" but when in Metairie I always try to get people to eat at the mall with me!

A great location in downtown Santa Barbara. Just off of the busy and trendy State Street but close enough to the action for me. Be aware that this place is located on a one-way street so if you're unfamiliar with the area use the GPS.

I my opinion a good mix between value and quality. I've had better sushi and teriyaki but it seemed to cost me a fortune. Portions are plentiful especially if you go with a combination plate.

Great casual atmosphere and the outdoor seating is a great option and there isn't a drop off in the service. There are a few other locations in the SB area but this one seems to be my favorite.

Out of the four AF locations I've been to in the area this was my least favorite. There are no benches or hooks in the bathrooms, which makes it awkward to change clothes or even shoes - no toilet lid either so you are left to sit on the bare seat or stand up. Also no coat rack so you have to roll up your coat and stuff in into one of the cubby holes. I also didn't see many people cleaning the equipment and I agree it did not smell that great either. The only thing that was good about this place was there were a couple of pleasant staff members.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
Decent bar on the ground floor of the Hyatt.

Drinks are good, food is good and better then I would have expected.

Only downside was I went out the lobby door and was standing quite a ways away from the door. I lit up a cigarette and the a-hole security dude came out yelling at me like I was a child. I moved farther away and was practically standing in the street and he kept yelling. I ended up walking away from the bar at this point simply pissed off.

respect must be earned and not demanded because you have a shitty job as a hotel night security guard

Came here on a holiday weekend that was very busy. We were seated in the bar area. Got the Tagliatelle con Funghi Misti and that was pretty good, nice mushroom flavor and noodles were good. Husband got the ravioli stuffed with prime rib. There were only seven of them, and they were small so we both thought it wasn't much for the price we were paying for them. Overall, I'd say that everyone seated at the bar loved the bartender. That's probably where all the reviews are highly rated for. He's very engaging, personable and makes you feel at home.

this was by far one of the saddest 24 hour fitnesses I've been to.  their equipment is pretty old, and they don't have any weights in the 2.5 lb increment.. actually, i lie, they had one set of 7.5 weights.  some of their cardio equipment could use some upgrades as well, the stair masters didn't work so smoothly, and made weird noises.  it looks like they had a pool, but i didn't check it out.   i think i'd be bored  coming to this gym on a regular basis due to the lack of variety... i'm glad i was just visiting.
categories: Active Life, Fitness & Instruction, Gyms, Trainers

text:
This sushi place is totally adequate and definitely hit the spot while I was visiting Feasterville. My husband and I were a bit taken aback at the half-off prices. We assumed they were happy hour prices but apparently it's all the time?! I think places that do this are a bit strange.

We ordered miso soup, edamame, and 3 sushi rolls. We couldn't finish it all. The edamame was a bit overcooked and the rolls were just ok -- nothing to write home about. I would try another sushi place in the area before returning to this one.

So-so at best.

Starting with the starter bread--it was fine, but not any better than from a grocery store. It also took 30 min to get after the server said "it'll be right out".

I had the bruscetta and a chicken-wrapped-in-pasta dish (I unfortunately forget the name). Again--I would have rather had the equivalent meal from Costco across the street.

Two good things: 1) They aren't massively overpriced my meal was $20 before tip. 2) The ambience is nice.

Final verdict? Based on this single visit, there are better places in the area (e.g. Hollister Brewing Co, which has about equal food but awesome beer).

As far as lower-end hotels go, this place is nice.

As far as hotels/motels in the Days Inn franchise go, this place is a palace.

Indoor entrance to the rooms, which in itself is a huge plus. It is four stories and does have elevators. There is a fireplace in the lobby and apparently on mondays they have a movie night.

The rooms are very clean, microwaves and fridges in every room.  Housekeeping is a bit aggressive but I'd rather that than they not come at all.

There are a few things in walking distance, including a pretty well priced pub across the street.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
Seriously good sushi at a seriously good price. I'd give it 3 1/2 stars really.

I mostly get the lunch special, which beats almost any other sushi place in the city. However, as has been said here already: the service is pretty dismal. 

Basically, it comes down to this: if you are someone who doesn't care about service, this is a five-star spot. Almost anyone would give it 5-stars for takeout, I believe. If you are someone who *only* cares about service, and is not interested in food, it is a one-star place. For everyone else, it falls somewhere in between.

I went here for lunch, right at 12 noon, and the service was quick. The restaurant filled up and got busy closer to 1215pm. 

All of the food was great. I had miso soup, the sashimi lunch special, and green tea ice cream. The miso was fresh and flavorful. The fish was great. The green tea ice cream about what you would expect, good. 

The portion sizes (and correspondingly the prices) were odd. Compared to lunch specials I have seen in New York at similar establishments, Moshi Moshi's sashimi lunch special was slightly more expensive and much smaller portion size. The ice cream was pricier also, but a huge portion.

My girl and I went here for a late lunch last weekend.  The inside dining room was full but it was suggested that we check out the back patio which was enclosed and heated.  The view outside was great and the outdoor bar was a perfect fit as the dining room seemed a bit too stuffy for us.  Along with our great view of the river and bridge we had steamed cockles with a white wine butter sauce and a rueben which we washed down with some draft beer.  The cockles were great and the sauce even better.  My only wish is that I had more bread to soak up the sauce.  The rueben was also very good with a great marbled rye and very tender cuts of meat.

This is the second time our family have stayed here and I always love my stay because it's decent and close to many things.  It is pet friendly, which is what we need because we have a 3lb yorkie.  The room with two queen beds and a den, the staff are very helpful.  I couldn't give a 5-star rating because the bathroom lock was broken, the blow dryer and some of the outlets were not working. Overall, we will come stay here whenever we are in town, hopefully we get a room next time that has those working things.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I was here on a rather busy Sunday afternoon 50F in January so the lines were 2-3 deep for self serve and out onto Kingshighway for automatic. 
the good: change machine, soap and wand all were in good working order.  paid $2.50 for about 6.5 minutes of self serve wash time. opted out of taking a go at my car with the vacuum but they all seemed to be working. 
the bad: the layout of the place when crowded is challenging to navigate when crowded, even in my sub compact car. it sits on a postage stamp of a lot. 
overall I'd be back but this isn't anything super special as car washes go.

We stopped in because we had 2 free drink coupons.
The, all I can call her is crazy, Manager Lady wouldn't take 2 coupons at the same time even though there were 3 of us and I was ordering other items.  She made me go into another line with one of the coupons.
I have no idea what planet she lives on, but every other McDonalds we have been in with these free coupons hasn't had a problem with taking them.
Needless to say, we won't be slumming it to this McDonalds ever in the future.  We will stick to the ones in the nicer areas of the City.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text:
The produce section ain't half bad and they had a killer sale on kombucha the day I stopped in. There is also a half-decent selection of tortillas, some of which are tucson-made. But that's just about where the positives of this location stop.

Maybe I like really weird foods but I couldn't find any kefir, let alone any brand or kind of yogurt besides one. The fish looked really old. There was no almond butter to be found. And the breads in the bakery looked stale. 

In the end we still managed to get a full grocery run together but missing some of our beloved staples.

A simple dining environment and friendly service put this restaurant on the trajectory for success but the food, for the most part, brought it down.

The dish that impressed me the most was the spicy salmon donburi (surprisingly!!!) - a generous heap of fresh sashimi, seasoned well, on fluffy rice. I could eat this on a daily basis.

What put the drag in my step was the oily and tasteless gyoza bento and the bland veggie sushi rolls. Not into any of it.

I don't know that I would go on my own accord but if someone dragged me back, I would order my salmon bowl and avoid all other dishes at all costs.

I really enjoyed this restaurant. I ordered the Fettuccini Di Mare, the seafood was cooked to perfection. I'm excited that a great Italian restaurant has finally made it to South Edmonton. Unfortunately the service was quite slow. I had to flag the waiter down to order a second glass of wine - and my water glass was never refilled. I guess they may be short staffed as a newer restaurant. I would definitely come here again the food was worth the wait.... Depending how hungry I am. I probably would not have been a happy camper if I was starving. I found the mark up on the wine to be quite high.

Guide to NOLA Grocery Stores

"I need paper towels/toilet paper/beer/cheap wine/candy" = Winn Dixie 

"I need cereal/milk/eggs/bread/King Cake" = Rouses

"I need produce/kombucha/delicious pastries/organic anything"= Whole Foods

"I need to shop somewhere with a fancy name" = Robert/Breaux Mart

Winn Dixie gets one star knocked off because the staff is TERRIBLE and could not care less about your needs. It also gets another star knocked off for lackluster selection. All in all, if you need something very basic and prepackaged, you can get it at Winn Dixie.

First time here so wasn't too sure what to get so I ended up getting the sampler which included...chicken caprese, lasagna, fettuccine alfredo, garlic bread, choice of salad and a drink.  Man!! that is alot of stuff and it only cost 12.40 with tax.  I get to go, jump in the car and I'm starving and the smell is fantastico.  Get to the room and start eating like a maniac and can't believe how good everything is.  THEN...

as soon as that initial starvation wore off I realized everything is just 'ok.'  Nothing is stellar and nothing was bad.  I give 4 stars for value for nice food.  I would go back again.

After being turned down at other locations for having a large party or the wait was too long, we finally found this restaurant while walking through philly. This place is spacious and great for large parties. We didn't have to wait long for a group of 7.

The food on the other hand... 

1) Crab cakes - very heavy with mostly mayo inside. I was expecting more herbs, crab, and greens inside.

2) Stuffed mushrooms - very flavorful with the sausage. Probably the best thing I had here. 

3) Salmon - had absolutely no flavor and dry. 

Definitely not my first choice nor would I come back to dine here.

I'll have a mani/pedi please!

This is the best nail salon in the city! What a great, clean place to come and relax. A friendly and detailed staff is just a tiny bit of the goodness that Beautiful Nails offers. Their massage pedicure chairs are fabulous and their products are celebrity spa worthy with minty smell and exfoliating scrubs - for the few extra bucks, I recommend getting the spa pedicure.

They carry only professional nail colors from OPI and whatever color you want, they've got it!

Go, relax, enjoy, Beautiful Nails

Unfortunately, I have to update my review of Chinese Village for the worse after a couple of very bad experiences there.  I will NEVER dine here again.  Last time we ordered, two of us were very sick for a couple of days.  The food was not fresh or well prepared...most of the rice was dried out and almost like it had never been cooked.  I don't know what changed.  Beyond that, they randomly decide what days they will and won't deliver and the woman that answers the phone is one of the rudest people I've ever dealt with.  They are just not worth visiting.

where do i begin.....
the food was trying too hard to be amazing that it became strange. the tastes were a jumbled concoction that did not sit well on my tongue. the lamb was excellent, but the almond jellied SALAD? come on... i think after they changed the chef and owners it sadly started to decline. if they didn't try so hard and simplified a few things, then well it might rise back to its former glory days. it was expensive too! (around $60 per person). i must say though the cornbread in a flowerpot was truly yummy. bring your own wine and good friends to make your visit better. 

cons: strange eats. $$$.

OK, so I can choose the size and type of burger I want, then I choose the bun, the cheese and all the toppings?  Yes Please...

And the fact that you can your soda with their special syrups, make mine cherry please.

The Fries are hand cut, with the skins on...and they were amazing...and don't get me started with the onion rings...they were very good.

If you're looking for a pretty good burger, a lot of options and a really good experience from the waitstaff, then I would go here...

I think that I'll be back at some point...I only wish that I could get a burger cooked less than Medium....

One of my favorite places to grab a po-boy (their shrimp and oyster poboys are out of this world...) or a muffaleta (as a native New Orleanian I think this one is better than central grocery's in the quarter) .  Cheap seafood anything and fried anything.  Only downside is that is that most of the food is very greasy.  But then again you are eating poboys (or really good muffalettas)  right outside New Orleans.  It should also be noted that the muffalettas are served hot with melted cheese (delish) compared to the cold ones you will find in the quarter.

Fresh and delicious sushi can sometimes be difficult to locate in smaller cities (especially those that aren't close to a coast). Luckily this is not an insurmountable challenge, and Cafe Mochi proves you can get good sushi in St. Louis.

The restaurant is in a cute space, and it looks like they have a nice outdoor area for when the weather is conducive. The nigiri was tasty and fresh, and the rolls were delicious and (very importantly) well constructed.

The service was good, and prices are reasonable for the quality. Definitely check them out if you need sushi in the Lou!

Check-in was hectic. The elevators were very slow (and only one of three seemed to be functioning.) The bathroom seemed to have been recently renovated, but there was no vent fan or lighting above the tub/shower, and it was very cramped. There were no desktop electrical outlets, and the only outlets I could find were hidden behind furniture -- extremely inconvenient. The lounge had about as much atmosphere as a family restaurant populated with grandparents. The only upside was that it was much cheaper than staying in the city.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I was in Florida on vacation a few months ago and was visiting my parents. I was craving Mexican so I found this place in Zephyrhills. A group of about 6 of us came here as it had better reviews than other Mexican places in the area. 

The services was okay.....the food was good. But what stunned me is that they charge  $1 for a chips/salsa refill. I mean, really?? Who does that!?  The certainly cost them a star or two in my review. 

I'd probably go back here for dinner as the food wasn't bad. But I think it's ridiculous to charge for chip refills.

Deducting one star because the 'sell' was very obvious and uncomfortable. We rented an intermediate SUV and ended up selecting a Kia Sportage. Other SUVs that we could have chosen  from include: Jeep Cherokee (not the big nice one) and the Jeep Patriot. The car was super clean and well taken care of. The process to return the vehicle was very easy.

Note, if picking up from airport, go to ground floor inside the airport to find your rental company. You'll check in and pay, then you'll be sent for a walk. Not too bad, but don't expect a shuttle.

4 stars because I was just super excited to be here!!!   My first...  I was snapping pictures from my camera phone like crazy, from the posters on the wall, to the menus (yes, the menus...), to the burger container, to the burger, to the bag...  Yes, even the White Castle sign (it came out white....).  Had a blast with the 42 center burger and even asked for a clean bag to take home!!  Yes, the workers were looking at me funny - but my colleagues played on with 'she's from japan'...    I can't recall the burgers much - they were warm, with itty bitty grilled onions...  I had 2.  =)

My wife and I ate here on one of our trips to STL to see a Cards game. We ended up here after checking out the casino. Since I grew up i STL I had to have the toasted ravioli and my wife had a burger. She loved the topping bar in the other room. I remembered that they had a special for a 24oz red bull and vodka. This was a nice place with tons of Cards stuff hanging on the wall. We were there during the afternoon and we were the only people in there. I wish I could have hung out with other Cards fans but maybe next time. I think the next time we go see a game we will eat here as well. I kept one of their cups for a souvenir. 

Peace Out,
MZ

We had a lovely time here. 
The beds are comfortable and rooms are modern and clean. 
The staff are friendly, attentive and kind. 
But...it is noisy (and not just bustling city noisy).
Of course we could hear the music coming from outside, that's to be expected. We didn't expect to hear our neighbor's TV through the walls, or the sound of normal decibel conversation from the hallway. The walls are thin. 
Also the bathroom door is on a track (like a barn door) so if the peace of a private bathroom is something you require, this is not the hotel for you. 
We probably would stay here again.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text: Terrible. Just terrible. Took my car for a routine oil change less than a week ago. Then, my 'check engine' light comes on randomly. I take it in to find out the issue, but also try to understand why it occurred AFTER I left with no explanation given. They keep my car for over an hour to tell me that two small clasps that keep the muffler together need to be replaced at a staggering $739.00 with tax!! With more than half the cost attributed to labor! Honestly, you could go anywhere else and not get estimates at a third the cost of not more and you may even get an honest answer! Quite literally, 'steer clear' of this place.
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
This hotel is actually pretty nice. It's been recently renovated.I didn't really have any issues as from the others.

We chose this hotel because it was right next to the cruise port and offered a cruisers package. With a night stay parking is included as well as two breakfast tickets. Breakfast means you get to pick one menu item from their menu. 

We picked eggs bacon and toast. All were pretty good for what you get. 

The hotel ended up being only 2 blocks from the port!

The hotel has a nice pool in the middle, a fitness center with several treadmills, and a business center right in the lobby which offers free internet.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
We had some super tasty things at our table and some not so great stuff.  I loved that there was vegan/vegetarian stuff, and a girl I was with is gluten free so the menu options were great.  
The service was slow and the place was empty (strange) - although our server was nice.
My plate was good, my Aunt's pot pie was good, but the pizzaS (which comprise a large part of the menu) were burned.  I want to give it more stars because my dish was tasty... but I just can't.  And it was so empty I am surprised they can continue on if tonight is indicative of the normal pace.

Man this is the only Starbucks with a drive-thru for many miles and the girl that has been at the drive-thru window (Lauren) is terrible. I say this because the last three times I've been through the drive-thru she has been at the window. Every, single time, she cuts me off and I have to let her know I have more to order... Every single time she gives me attitude when this happens and every single time she gets one of my drink orders wrong! I've never had an issue with any other employee or anytime I've gone inside. Lauren doesn't belong at Starbucks, wrong attitude and wrong drink orders... Disappointing.

Y'all. No. 

The Vegetable Egg Roll was incredibly greasy. It was as if it had actually been injected with grease. 

The Crab Rangoon was way too sweet. Even if I liked sweet Rangoon, this would be too sweet. 

The Shrimp with Mixed Vegetables was just awful. The veggies were cooked too soft so everything was mushy. The overcooking was likely to cover the fact that these veggies were not fresh. The broccoli was yellow. There were brown spots on the carrots. The sauce was the worst component of this dish, though. It was flavorless and goopy. 

Overall, not a good experience. Avoid.

don't get your hopes up, this is a hotel bar - nothing better, nothing worse. drinks are what they are. "thursday happy hour" meant a dollar off my ten dollar app, probably a similar discount on my $7 drink...

the food - actually, let me take back my last comment, is kinda worse.

"beef flatbread with tenderloin tips" = the equivalent of "steak" at a subway restaurant, in a squarish flour tortilla with a sprinkle of red onion, a cheese not worth remembering, and a flavorless pico. lame.

the crowd last night was nice to look at though ;) but that's just cause the right conference is in town...

This is a cute lil spot. And I do mean little. The sushi is decent, not too much rice, so you don't get stuffed off rice, but the favors are cool. My issue with the spot is the size. There is only one 6 seat table and a sushi bar. You almost have to order to go or go either alone or at a good time. I took my 11 y/o lil cousin & he enjoyed himself, so I enjoyed it as well.  We got 6 rolls and sushi for 49.00, which I thought was a great deal! This spot is like a down home sushi spot, if there ever was one...styrofoam cups & all. Don't go for the frills, go for the sushi & enjoy the swift service and the yummy rolls!

We had a wonderful Valentine's Day dinner. The food was fabulous. The atmosphere was perfect. Best view! Watching the sunset and then the lights come up on the city is always amazing. But what made the evening was our server Matt Santos. Rarely do you have fabulous food and and outstanding server. Matt was the busiest server in the restaurant and he still took time to discuss food and wine and have a fun conversation. He was absolutely delightful. I highly recommend La Vecchia and when you come, ask for Matt and tell him Alice and Fred sent you.

Decent but what else is new? A standard Sheraton, cheaper than other Philly hotels (I got $119 per night, even at the last minute), comfortable and good service, but on 17th and Race. 

Con: I happened to go on Model UN weekend. Disaster! Under-21 kids everywhere, prepping for conferences and asking where the party was, getting off at the Lobby floor, M floor, Ballroom floor, and every floor from 1 - 6. I was on 26. Sigh. 

Pro: they gave me a free breakfast coupon and a rubber ducky in my Platinum Guest gift bag (!)
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
yummmm I'm a white castle fanatic, and anytime I'm in the same city as a white castle I make a visit.  That said, this particular one was sort of sad.  Sad location, sad workers, sad burgers with soggier-than-usual bread.  But mmmm I still love em and I'd definitely come back.

Usually I just get the absurdly cheap cheeseburgers with that tasty sweet pickle and oniony goodness, but I also like the chicken rings, very crunchy and light onion rings, sort of crappy fries, and the perfect made-to-order oozy gooey MOZZARELLA STICKS.  The epitome of fast food.

A good and honest mechanic is hard to come by, especially in Philadelphia. 
Andrew and Willie are the old school friendly and attentive mechanics that you just don't find anymore. You're not going to find a plush waiting room with great magazines and a flat screen TV or espresso machine but you will find friendly, courteous, and polite guys that will explain what is wrong and provide options. 
I'm in the process of selling a car that is an absolute lemon and I have been to A&W on several occasions unfortunately and no matter what part of the city I may reside, I will always bring my cars to them for now on. Wonderful Shop!!!

I'm not one who's big on Mexican food, but this is where my friends had taken me on my first night in Tucson. It's wasn't bad, but it didn't make me want to join a mariachi band either. The waitress was cute if that counts for anything, Ashley I believe her name was. The service was on point this night, the food came out in a timely manner and was hot, and they were good about making sure our drinks were filled. They do offer $5 meal specials a different one for each day of the week. There is also a scaled down version over at Tucson Electric Park.

I thought this sushi place was decent. The taste of the rolls were good and I liked their movie themed specialty rolls. The only problem I had was their rice was too sticky and it stuck to the plate which made it hard to pick up with chopsticks.

I really liked the decor and the restaurant was nice and clean. The service was okay. I liked how friendly the sushi chefs were. 

I'd like to come back to do their all-you-eat menu which seems like a really good deal. 17.99 for lunch and 24.99 for dinner I believe and is available from opening to 2pm and from 5pm to closing.

I love the staff here because they are friendly and all, but I absolutely hate the drive-thru window here. It took me about 25-30 min to get through the drive-thru the other day. How can it take so long to prepare food and give it to your customers in a timely fashion? I've been to other McDonald's locations and I would go through the drive-thru in less than 2-3 minutes. What's the excuse here? This is very disappointing! I highly advise anyone to go to this location, unless you plan on wasting your time sitting in line and wasting gas. Honestly, if there was an option to give zero stars, I would give that rating in a heartbeat.
categories: Burgers, Coffee & Tea, Fast Food, Food, Restaurants

text: There is NO WAY IN HELL that this is a real business. This is thee definition of a "front business." I want them to leave my neighborhood so at least someone of legit business can move in there. If you walk in to order food they look a little surprised that you want to order. The place is extremely dirty. One time I came in and there was a full trash bag sitting on one of the table tops. At strange hours of the morning and night there is always a uhaul or the recognizable purple mini van loading and unloading boxes out of there. Get your fake business out of my neighborhood!

If you're staying at the Grand Sierra Resort, need a quick bite to eat, got the drunchies, or your party wants different things, look no further than Cafe Sierra.

Always satisfied me when I was hungry and just needed to curb the pangs.  I like the simple things like the breakfast menu, burgers, pizza, and soups.  Most of the other gourmet foods like the taco salad or asian menu were usually subpar.

My favorite and go-to item that I order every time is their buffalo wings.  I don't know why, but I crave them every time I stay here.

Instead of going to the nearby Hilton Luna which is consistently good but never exciting,  I decided to take some business colleagues here for a change. With only a few people at the bar,  the noise level was high, speaking to the bad acoustics. I always like it when the server comes to take your order by saying "Yeah?" and the orders needed to be repeated several times because of the noise. The appetizers, chips and wings, were good, the salads as well but the entrees were all over salted to make them borderline inedible. I'll stick to Luna in the future.

Oh boy. This place is a doozy, Judge. They don't/won't put on the Angels division game because the Cardinals aren't playing. A really drunk guy left to drive himself home. Everyone yelled at him, he yelled back, then drove anyway and everyone went back to drinking.

The food is bland. Better than airport food, but not great. 

Bud' products here, so don't go execting good beers. 

You'll be surrounded by 50-somethings drunk beyond karaoke, and mesmerized by high falutin' technology such as iPhones. Really.

Anyway, it's more fun than sitting in the hotel in Fenton, the world's most boring city.

I'm highly disappointed. I've been coming here for a year or so and my toddler and I love it. Went in the other day and we were asked to leave because my two year old wasn't wearing a mask. She left crying unable to understand why she wasn't getting the ice cream I promised her. 
Governor Wolf's mask requirement applies to children over two and excludes those with health issues who are unable to wear a mask. There's no reason why I shouldn't have been able to spend a few minutes in this shop to get my kid some frozen yogurt. 
Tried emailing the owner(s) and never received a response. Gonna find somewhere else to go when we want some froyo.

Too bad.
Just moved into area and was looking for a good car wash. They did a good job washing car.  I actually considered the "unlimited car wash" option.  The next day I pulled into a restaurant and opened my coin box only to find my $5 bill missing.  Self-tipping is great for them, unless they ever want repeat business.  If I can't trust them with my money and coins, I can't trust them with my car.  I guess this is their "Royal" treatment.  Sad thing - I was going to email owner privately so he/she could deal with employee theft, but they offer no contact information.  So long Royal.

Visited: July 30th, 2011

Oh White Castle.....it has been two years since I've been there. I first enjoyed it when I had it in 2008 in St. Paul, Minnesota and went back in 2009 when I was visiting family again. I was excited when my boyfriend's brother took us there when we arrived in St. Louis (the closest airport to Mt. Olive, Illinois). I once again was devouring the little sliders. I truly love this burger place and wish it was in California, but the White Castle chain is only in the midwest and east coast. :(

All 4 of these stars are for one thing and one thing only.

WELL PRICED LIVE UNI. 

It was so good we made sure to come back the next day and we werent even hungry. Unfortunately they didnt get any that day.

Fun tip - eating sea urchin from its spiny body whacked in half - compels kids of people walking by to barrage their parents with questions along the lines "whoa what are those people eating!?!?!" to which their parents respond with hilarious awkward replies along the lines of "keep walking, its not polite to point, its probably sea urchin"... good times.

These yogurt buffets seem to be the latest trend. Yo My Goodness follows in the same vein as Fro-Yo. What I did like was that they were very helpful in letting you sample the different types of yogurt. The decor is especially bright - it looks like giant highlighters went to war over the wall color.

Bottom Line: If you like yogurt over ice cream then this place is as good as fro-yo, but nothing super special. It's sometimes very loud with kids, but a convenient next door dessert bonus from Robust and Jimmy Johns.

Coffee:
good, but not great. The espresso didnt have much crema and thought it lacked flavor

Price:
normal

Location:
the spot itself is different than most coffee vibes, especially for N.O. It may get old, not sure since I am just a passer through....but like the different feel.

Needs:
more knowledge of coffee and what they are brewing. Every barista should be able to say - where it's roasted, where the beans come from, how fresh they are and how many seconds it takes to pull a good shot....this place lacks that. Nice folks, just not 'coffee heads'

*free wifi is nice.

I use to love White Castle.  I never lived near one so every time I took a trip I'd try to find one on my route.  I stopped by this one going from OHIO to MISSOURI.   The Burgers were gross, I couldn't believe how horrible they were.  I ordered six thinking I was going to enjoy them and only ate two.  I should have made a complaint to the manager but I was so grossed out I just wanted to leave.  Lucky for me I found a Culver's not too far down 70.  Because of this, I'll probably never eat White Castle again.

I see a lot of positive reviews so maybe they had an off day or something, but still, I don't see my going to any others ever again.

I gave this subway a one star, strictly based on the service I received.  The restaurant was clean, but the sandwich artist was stale.  

The gentleman must've been the franchise owner or a manager, he had white hair and was a bit older than the standard 28 year old employee.  He was rude, did not greet or thank me for my business.  The gross part, he wasn't wearing a hair net and he reached into his pocket with gloves on before serving the next guest.  He was also very disrespectful to the girl running the register.  Boo for this dude.

My star rating is low because this is the smallest and busiest Starbucks I've ever been to. At any time you would expect to find a working person get coffee you can expect the line is out the parking lot,  across the street, and backed up to the light. I can't imagine how much business they are losing simply because of that. If they opened up another location in the area that would greatly help. I'm also not sure if they changed their to go cups but mine are always leaking! I have coffee stains all over my car :( Fix the location problem, fix your cups and I'll be a happy camper

Geez. This is my Imos. We order at least once a month, but more like weekly. We ordered delivery yesterday- pizza was warm and the extra dressing I paid for wasn't there. We I have a friend in town that wanted Imos tonight. I called and tried to order. In the middle I was hung up on. Called back phone just rang and rang and rang. Hung up tried again. The same. Finally get through to get halfway through then transferred? Then the guy thinks I'm another person. Yeah, I'm done. If you can't even take my order, you probably aren't gonna get it right. Super sad. Just lost a life long customer.

I have always heard that if you are in New Orleans you must try a lucky dog. Depending where in New Orleans you are you might worried to try one. I think I was safe getting one at the airport terminal. The young lady was working her tail off. Long line but she was moving fast. 

The hot dog was good. I went for the 1/4 lucky dog but I think the regular one would have been just fine. Good dog good flavor. At the end of the day it's a hotdog. 

I failed to take a pic of the dog since I was in a hurry to try it.

I'm a total poke fan so ordered the Special Poke and was super pleasantly surprised when I got the platter of amazing fresh fish!  See pic. A good deal for dinner with miso soup and salad. The corner restaurant borders on a walk street of other restaurants and bars and the Edwards theatre. Red walls and an Asian cook along with paper Japanese fans and lanterns and loads of Japanese posters make it a very Asian flavored place.  Nice young atmosphere.  The poke prep was the most interesting to me as I'm from Hawaii and poke is a staple. I did miss the Hawaiian flavorings though.

Great location. It's tucked away between a residential area and the freeway. Easy to get to from the back roads or the freeway.

The front desk area smells like chlorine; it's near the swimming pool which I didn't visit. Some evenings I returned to the hotel and the front desk greeted me and other times they ignored me.

There is a breakfast buffet ($8.95) and you can have food (pancakes or omelets) made to order. Wifi is complimentary with Hilton Honors membership.

My room was clean as was the refrigerator. The rooms have individual kcups and Target is close so you can go there to get some pods at a reasonable price.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
The food was really good, but there were a few things that spoiled the experience. We didnt have a reservation, but they had a table, so we sat. They didnt pay any attention to us. It was like we were second class. We ordered our drinks and asked for water. Well, we asked for water 4 times. Our drinks took until our entrees came. We ordered guacamole, which was great, but it came with a handful of chips. We asked for more, but were charged $2 without being told. Dont give us 5 chips then! The dessert was okay, but it said chocolate cake, but had no chocolate, but apparently was what we ordered. 

Its a cute place and great for happy hour.

Excellent service, great pices, gets you all your deals, won't screw you over. Could handle my being neurotic. Got away with a full synthetic oil change, rotatii, alignment check, cleaning of corrosion onbatteries, and checking the cables for looseness for $24, had my own oil from Costco, didn't have my own filter, used corporate site for coupons. Make an appointment, quite the wait once it is a good place and many folks come here. They say make an appointment for under an hour guaruntee.  I was an hour and a half, even at 9 am
categories: Auto Repair, Automotive, Oil Change Stations, Tires

text:
We went here on a reco from a friend while we were visiting for the weekend. 
The one star is for the ambiance (outside).  The service was beyond awful - the bartenders were more interested in flirting with each other and checking themselves out in the mirror than making any money.  And considering the place was dead I don't think it would have been that hard to offer some table service. 
The menu requests that you be patient because the food is "made to order"  (as opposed to)...  
Bonus: you also get a free side of sketchy characters hanging around to check out the bartenders checking themselves out.

Beautiful store. Horrific service. Just waited in line for 28 minutes to get a bento coffee only then to be told there was no half & half by a dread headed barista who was to busy singing and cracking wise to his coworkers to do it politely. Called the manager as I left. She told me cream was on the way and told me she "understood" when I mentioned the lack of customer service. 

Sorry. Was really glad to see this place open but will gladly wait in line at one of the 5 others Starbucks within a few blocks before I return to this one. Apparently, it's more of an open mic comedy store than a real Starbucks.

Super hipster spot on the outskirts of downtown Tampa. We walked in through the kitchen entrance (at least it felt that way) but were immediately welcomed and brought to our table. Wine prices were fair and the food was delicious. The standout was surprisingly the buffalo cauliflower with blue cheese slaw appetizer. Two weeks later, I'm still thinking about it. The fish special was delicious. My only gripe was that the quail was too heavily breaded. It was tough to find the meat through all that breading. Other than that, the food was stellar and the service was on point.

Not great but not terrible. Live music on Tuesdays was nice. Friendly bartenders / waitresses....

But, for what is probably more of a business hotel, the desk area in the room was conspicuously devoid of outlets. I had to unplug the coffee maker under the table to plug in my laptop. 

#firstworldproblem? Probably, but problematic nonetheless. Also, no outlets that reached the nightstands by the bed.

The clients I went to visit complained about the same issues and said they switched to the Hyatt nearby instead. #diva
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
Would have been 2 stars and great service took them to 4 stars.  The hotel is very nice with a pool and all of the amenities.

Our room was big and comfortable.  The would have been 2 stars comes from the fact that our air conditioner barely worked in 95+ degree heat.  And the light in the bathroom flickered.

The management got the light fixed and provided a fan after my wife complained.  The said they would "make it right".

Well, "make it right" turned out to be a complimentary stay!  Excellent service recovery.  I'm a fan.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel

text:
I don't know why I'm bothering to review this place. It's a business hotel, and business travelers will continue to book here. In case you care, though, it sucks. When I ordered room service, it took two and a half hours (and three angry phone calls) to arrive. Then they tried to charge me for it (twice - once on arrival and once on our final bill) despite having told me it would be comped. 

Decor is dated, water pressure in the bathroom is terrible, and there are some alarming clanging noises coming from inside the elevators. My boyfriend booked this one, but rest assured I will never darken its doors again. NEVER AGAIN THE SHERATON TIMES.
categories: Event Planning & Services, Hotels, Hotels & Travel, Venues & Event Spaces

text:
If you happen to see sushi chefs wearing gloves to prepare your sushi I would think twice eating there. So I really did cringe when I saw sushi chefs wearing gloves at this joint. If you want to know why read this article here: https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2015/nov/12/why-i-want-my-sushi-prepared-with-bare-hands

Tiny California rolls lacked flavor -  very little crab meat and giant piece of cucumber.  Might as well call them cucumber rolls instead.

Chicken teriyaki was so dry and chewy. How could they even get this wrong?

I'm sorry to say but overall not a good dining experience and will most likely not return.

The worst Dunkin Donuts in the world.  Or at least in the Top 5. I wanted a bagel with cream cheese but the guy making the food didn't want to make it. I sat waiting for a long time. Finally I was asked what I'm waiting for and then yelling came from the guy in the back saying he didn't want to make it. The manager tried to force him to make it and then I said No I do Not want him to make it. Please refund my money. I did get a refund but it's unbelievable that guy still has a job or at least disciplined and told to go home. Manager didn't even say a word.... Not coming back here.
